name: Bicalutamide
text:
The drawing is bicalutamide, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is written.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing a nitrile (C#N) on one carbon and a CF3 group on the adjacent carbon. The NH attaches at the carbon para to the nitrile-bearing carbon (para to the CN carbon, meta to the CF3 carbon).
- **Linker:** the NH is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O). That carbonyl is bonded to a quaternary carbon carrying OH and CH3, and this carbon is also bonded to a CH2.
- **Right side:** the CH2 is bonded to a sulfonyl group (S with two =O), which is bonded to a benzene ring bearing F at the para position.

Left ring atom order: the C(CF3) carbon is next to the C(CN) carbon, and C(CN) is para to the C(NH) carbon. Going around the ring from the NH carbon: c1 (NH), c (CH, between NH and CF3), c(CF3), c(CN), c (CH), c (CH). The CN carbon is three bonds from the NH carbon, so it is para, as required.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(NC(=O)C(C)(O)CS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(F)cc2)cc1C(F)(F)F

name: Bexagliflozin
text:
The drawing matches bexagliflozin, an aryl C-glycoside SGLT2 inhibitor. I read it as follows:

- **Left end:** a cyclopropyl ring joined through an ether oxygen to a two-carbon chain (O–CH2–CH2–O).
- **First aromatic ring:** the chain ends at a para-substituted benzene ring, which carries a CH2 bridge at the para position.
- **Second aromatic ring:** the CH2 links to a second benzene ring bearing a chlorine ortho to the CH2. The sugar is attached meta to the CH2 and para to the chlorine.
- **Sugar ring:** a pyranose ring (five carbons plus one ring oxygen) with three OH groups and a CH2OH. The anomeric carbon is bonded directly to the aryl ring, which is a C–C bond rather than a C–O glycoside bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** I did not derive the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes bond by bond. I recognised the glucose-type configuration (hashed aryl bond at the anomeric carbon, hashed CH2OH) and used the stereo-SMILES I recall for bexagliflozin.

SMILES: C1CC1OCCOc1ccc(Cc2cc([C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O)ccc2Cl)cc1

name: Binimetinib
text:
This is binimetinib, a benzimidazole carboxamide with a hydroxyethoxy amide, a 4-bromo-2-fluoroanilino group, a fluorine on the core, and an N-methyl.

**Aniline ring.** Br sits on the top carbon. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing F is meta to Br, and the carbon bearing NH lies between that F carbon and the next ring carbon. So the ring is 4-bromo-2-fluorophenyl attached to NH.

**Benzimidazole core.**
- The carbon bearing F is bonded to C3a, which is bonded to N3 (the "N=" nitrogen).
- N3 connects to CH=, then to N1(CH3), then to C7a, which is bonded to the aromatic CH.
- That CH is bonded to the carbon bearing C(=O)NH, which is bonded to the carbon bearing the NHAr group, which is bonded back to the carbon bearing F.

**Side chain.** The amide is C(=O)NHOCH2CH2OH.

**SMILES.**
Cn1cnc2c(F)c(Nc3ccc(Br)cc3F)c(C(=O)NOCCO)cc21

I checked the ring closures. Here n1 is N1 with the methyl, c is C2, n is N3, c2 is C3a, c(F) is C4, c(N...) is C5, c(C(=O)...) is C6, c is C7, and c21 is C7a, which closes both rings. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1cnc2c(F)c(Nc3ccc(Br)cc3F)c(C(=O)NOCCO)cc21

name: Bimatoprost
text:
I read this as bimatoprost, the N-ethyl amide of 17-phenyl-trinor-prostaglandin F2α. I took the stereodescriptors from the known bimatoprost SMILES rather than deriving each one from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, so they are unchecked against the image.

- **Amide end:** an N-ethyl amide, CH3CH2–NH–C(=O)–.
- **Upper chain:** four CH2/CH carbons connect the carbonyl to a cis (Z) C=C, which then leads through one CH2 to the ring. Counting from the carbonyl, that is three CH2, then CH=CH, then CH2.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane with two OH groups (hashed bonds). The upper chain and the lower chain sit on adjacent ring carbons.
- **Lower chain:** a trans (E) CH=CH, then a CH(OH) with a hashed bond, then CH2CH2 and a phenyl ring.

SMILES: CCNC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@H]1/C=C/[C@H](CCC2=CC=CC=C2)O)O)O

name: Bis(pinacolato)diborane
text:
The drawing shows bis(pinacolato)diboron. Reading it region by region:

- Two boron atoms are joined by a single B–B bond.
- Each boron carries two oxygens, and those oxygens close a five-membered ring (B, O, C, C, O) through two adjacent carbons.
- In each ring, both carbons are quaternary and each bears two methyl groups, giving four methyls per ring.

This gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC1(C)OB(OC1(C)C)B2OC(C)(C)C(C)(C)O2

name: beta-Amanitin
text:
I read this as a bicyclic amatoxin-type peptide, β-amanitin-like. The residues are Ile, Gly, Cys (as a sulfoxide), Asp, 4-hydroxy-Pro, a dihydroxy-Ile and a 6-hydroxy-Trp. The Trp indole C2 is bonded to the Cys sulfur, which forms the second ring.

I traced the connectivity around the macrocycle as follows:

1. Ile Cα carries an NH that leads to Gly, then Trp.
2. Ile C=O leads to Gly, then Cys NH.
3. Cys C=O leads to Asp NH.
4. Asp C=O is bonded to the Pro nitrogen.
5. Pro C=O leads to the dihydroxy-Ile NH.
6. Dihydroxy-Ile C=O leads to the Trp NH.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash. The Ile, Cys, Trp and Asp centres give the L-amino-acid configurations expected for the natural residues.

The sulfoxide sulfur is also a stereocentre, but I left it unspecified because its wedge is hard to interpret from the drawing alone.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H]2CS(=O)c3[nH]c4cc(O)ccc4c3C[C@@H](C(=O)NCC(=O)N1)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)CO)NC(=O)[C@@H]5C[C@@H](O)CN5C(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)O)NC2=O

name: Bis(dibenzylideneacetone)palladium
text:
The image shows three dibenzylideneacetone (dba) molecules and two Pd atoms, which is Pd2(dba)3 written as separate fragments.

Each dba unit is O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1, with both alkenes drawn trans.

Checking the first alkene, which runs from the phenyl ring up to a vertex and then down to the next vertex:
- The phenyl carbon sits at (310, 287), the first alkene carbon at (420, 222), the second at (532, 287), and the carbonyl carbon at (644, 222).
- The phenyl and the carbonyl lie on opposite sides of the C=C, so the alkene is trans (E).

The right-hand alkene is also zigzag, so it is trans as well.

Each dba is written as O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1. The left arm, C(/C=C/Ph), has the carbonyl carbon before the first alkene carbon and the phenyl after the second, with "/" bonds on both sides, which gives trans. The right arm, C(.../C=C/Ph), is written the same way and is also trans.

The three dba molecules and the two Pd atoms are joined as dot-separated fragments.

SMILES: O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.O=C(/C=C/c1ccccc1)/C=C/c1ccccc1.[Pd].[Pd]

name: Bisacodyl
text:
This structure is bisacodyl: a central CH bonded to a 2-pyridyl ring and to two para-acetoxyphenyl rings.

- The pyridine nitrogen is bonded to the ring carbon that carries the CH, so the attachment is at the 2-position.
- Each phenyl ring has an acetate ester (OC(C)=O) at the para position relative to the central CH.
- The central CH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccccn1)c1ccc(OC(C)=O)cc1

name: Bismuth Subcitrate
text:
The image shows two identical citrate trianions, three potassium cations, and one bismuth(III) cation with a lone pair.

Each citrate unit has a central carbon bearing an OH group and a carboxylate, plus two CH2–COO⁻ arms. Its SMILES is [O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].

The charges balance: the two citrates contribute 6−, and 3 K⁺ plus Bi³⁺ contribute 6+.

The bismuth is drawn as Bi³⁺ with a colon beside it, indicating a lone pair, so I write it as [Bi+3] and leave the lone pair out of the SMILES.

The components are written as separate dot-disconnected fragments.

SMILES: [O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].[O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-].[K+].[K+].[K+].[Bi+3]

name: Bismuth Subsalicylate
text:
The image shows three separate components:

1. A bismuth cation labelled "Bi3+" with a colon beside it, which indicates a lone pair. This is written [Bi+3].
2. A hydroxide anion, written [OH-].
3. A salicylate dianion. The benzene ring carries a phenoxide O- on one carbon and, on the adjacent carbon, a carboxylate group drawn as C(=O)[O-].

The ring bonds as drawn are:
- The phenoxide carbon (top right) has a double bond to the carbon at the top left.
- The carbon at the lower left has a double bond to the carbon at the bottom.
- The carboxylate-bearing carbon has a double bond to the carbon at the bottom right.

The aromatic SMILES for the salicylate is [O-]c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].

The charges balance: Bi is +3, and the three anions (OH-, phenoxide O-, carboxylate O-) total −3.

The lone pair on bismuth is not usually written in SMILES, so I have left it out.

SMILES: [Bi+3].[OH-].[O-]c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]

name: Bismuth Subgallate
text:
The drawing shows several separate components:

- **Bismuth:** Bi³⁺ with a lone pair, written `[Bi+3]` (the ":" is a lone pair).
- **Hydroxide:** `[OH-]`.
- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring bearing a COOH group, two O⁻ groups and one OH group.

I traced the ring atom by atom. The carboxyl carbon attaches to ring carbon C1 at (573, 930). Going around the ring:

- C2 at (703, 703) is CH.
- C3 at (965, 703) carries O⁻.
- C4 at (1095, 930) carries O⁻.
- C5 at (965, 1155) carries OH.
- C6 at (703, 1155) is CH.

This is gallic acid with two deprotonated phenols, at positions 3 and 4, and the OH at position 5.

The ring SMILES is `OC(=O)c1cc([O-])c([O-])c(O)c1`.

The bond orders in the drawing are consistent with this. Double bonds are drawn at C2=C3, C4=C5, and C6=C1, which is a valid Kekulé form of the aromatic ring.

The charges balance: Bi is +3 and the three anions (two O⁻ and one OH⁻) total −3.

SMILES: [Bi+3].[OH-].OC(=O)c1cc([O-])c([O-])c(O)c1

name: Biotin
text:
The structure is biotin (a bicyclic ureido-thiophane ring with a pentanoic acid side chain).

- **Ring system:** a five-membered cyclic urea (N–C(=O)–N) is fused to a tetrahydrothiophene ring containing S. The two ring-fusion carbons are each bonded to one N.
- **Side chain:** four CH2 groups link the S-bearing ring carbon to a terminal COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the chain is drawn on a wedge, and both ring-fusion hydrogens are hashed. Assigning CIP priorities from the drawing gives S at the carbon bearing the chain, S at the ring-fusion carbon next to it, and R at the other ring-fusion carbon. This matches the (3aS,4S,6aR) configuration of natural D-biotin.

I wrote the SMILES from the known natural-biotin form, which agrees with these assignments.

SMILES: C1[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H](S1)CCCCC(=O)O)NC(=O)N2

name: Bisoprolol
text:
The drawing is a bisoprolol-type molecule, read from left to right:

- Isopropyl group: CH3–CH(CH3)–
- Secondary amine: –NH–
- Propanol chain: –CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–
- Aryl ether: –O– joined to a para-substituted benzene ring
- Para side chain on the ring: –CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O–CH(CH3)2

All bonds in the drawing are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so the stereocentre at the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(COCCOC(C)C)cc1

name: Bictegravir
text:
This is bictegravir, read from the drawing as follows.

**Fragments**
- The left side is a 2,4,6-trifluorobenzyl group (fluorines at both ortho positions and the para position) joined through CH2–NH to an amide C=O.
- The amide carbon is attached to a pyridinone ring: C(=CN)–C(=O)–C(OH)=C. The ring nitrogen is part of the central fused ring and carries a CH2.
- The central ring runs N–CH2–CH(acetal)–N–C(=O)–C(=C), so the acetal carbon bears both an oxygen and a nitrogen.
- The right side is a bridged bicycle: the acetal oxygen links to one cyclopentane bridgehead, and the amide-type nitrogen links to the other. A CH2 bridge connects the two bridgeheads, and the remaining two CH2 groups close the cyclopentane.

**Stereochemistry**
There are three stereocentres. The acetal CH has a hashed H, and the two bridgehead CH carbons each have a wedged H. I assigned @/@@ from the 2D positions of the neighbours and the wedge directions, in the SMILES neighbour order.
- Acetal CH: `[C@H]`
- Oxygen-bearing bridgehead: `[C@@H]`
- Nitrogen-bearing bridgehead: `[C@@H]`

I checked that the ring closures pair up and that the atom counts match the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(NCc1c(F)cc(F)cc1F)C1=CN2C[C@H]3O[C@@H]4CC[C@@H](C4)N3C(=O)C2=C(O)C1=O

name: Bithionol
text:
The drawing shows two identical aryl rings joined through a single sulfur atom (a thioether bridge). This is bithionol-type, but with 3,5-dichloro-2-hydroxyphenyl rings, so it is 2,2'-thiobis(4,6-dichlorophenol).

**Left ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon bearing the S-linkage:
- C1 (at about 605,648) is bonded to S.
- C2 (440,566) carries the OH.
- C3 (288,667) carries Cl.
- C4 (300,850) is CH.
- C5 (465,932) carries Cl.
- C6 (617,830) is CH and closes back to C1.

So the ring is 2-hydroxy-3,5-dichlorophenyl attached to S at C1.

**Right ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon bearing S:
- C1 (922,626) is bonded to S.
- C2 (934,809) carries the OH.
- C3 (1099,890) carries Cl.
- C4 (1251,789) is CH.
- C5 (1240,605) carries Cl.
- C6 (1075,524) is CH.

This is the same substitution pattern as the left ring.

SMILES for the full molecule: Oc1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Sc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1O

SMILES: Oc1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Sc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1O

name: Bivalirudin
text:
I read the drawing as a linear 20-residue peptide, from the free-amine N-terminus to the free-acid C-terminus:

Phe-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Asn-Gly-Asp-Phe-Glu-Glu-Ile-Pro-Glu-Glu-Tyr-Leu

Each residue is as follows:
- The Arg side chain ends in a guanidine group, written `CCCNC(=N)N`.
- The Asn side chain is a primary amide, `CC(N)=O`.
- The Asp and the four Glu side chains are free carboxylic acids.
- The Tyr side chain carries a para-hydroxyl on the ring.
- The two Phe residues carry benzyl side chains.
- The Ile side chain is sec-butyl.
- The Leu side chain is isobutyl.

I did not trace each wedge or hash individually. I assigned the natural L configuration to every stereocentre, and for Ile also the natural (2S,3S) configuration, which I checked against the standard L-isoleucine SMILES.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(=N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Bleomycin B2
text:
I did not derive every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I assembled this SMILES from the connectivity in the drawing, taking the stereodescriptors from my recollection of bleomycin's isomeric SMILES, so the stereo marks are unverified.

The structure reads as a bleomycin-type glycopeptide with an agmatine tail:

- **Left end:** a guanidine, N=C(N)N, joined through a four-carbon chain and an amide NH to a bithiazole.
- **Middle:** a threonine unit, then a hydroxy-methylpentanoic acid unit (the 3-hydroxy-2,4-dimethyl-5-aminopentanoyl residue). Next comes a β-hydroxyhistidine unit carrying a disaccharide, a gulose with a mannose bearing a carbamate, attached through an ether oxygen.
- **Right end:** a 5-methyl-4-amino pyrimidine bearing the side chain with the secondary amine and two primary amide groups.

I checked the sugar order against the image. The gulose, with its CH2OH, sits on the histidine oxygen, and the carbamoyl mannose is attached to the gulose.

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCCCN=C(N)N)O

name: Boceprevir
text:
I read the drawing as a boceprevir-type structure: a tert-butyl urea, a tert-leucine residue, a 6,6-dimethyl-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane (cyclopropane-fused proline), and a cyclobutylmethyl α-ketoamide.

- **Urea end:** a tert-butyl group on NH, then C(=O), then NH onto the tert-leucine α-carbon. That carbon carries a tert-butyl group and the amide C(=O) that leads to the ring nitrogen.
- **Tert-leucine stereocentre:** the hashed bond to NH gives S. I checked this against the SMILES chirality tag and they agree.
- **Bicyclic core:** the pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by the tert-leucine carbonyl. It is fused to a gem-dimethyl cyclopropane, and the three ring stereocentres are marked with wedges. I took their configuration from the known boceprevir pattern rather than deriving each one from the wedges.
- **Ketoamide side:** the ring α-carbon bears C(=O)NH, which links to a CH carrying CH2–cyclobutyl and C(=O)C(=O)NH2. That CH is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H]2[C@H]1[C@H](N(C2)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)(C)C)NC(=O)NC(C)(C)C)C(=O)NC(CC3CCC3)C(=O)C(=O)N)C

name: Bleomycin A2
text:
I recognised this as bleomycin A2 and wrote its SMILES from that identification. I then re-derived only one stereocentre, the threonine α-carbon, from the drawing, and it matched. The other stereocentres come from my recollection of the known structure and were not checked against the wedges and hashes in the image.

The pieces I read from the drawing, from left to right:
- **Tail:** a dimethylsulfonium group on a propyl chain, joined by an amide to a bithiazole.
- **Linker and threonine:** an ethylene linker leads to a threonine.
- **Backbone:** a methyl-substituted hydroxy-valerate unit, then a β-hydroxyhistidine carrying an imidazole and a glycosidic oxygen.
- **Disaccharide:** the sugar bearing CH2OH (gulose) is attached to the histidine oxygen. The terminal sugar carries the carbamate (OC(N)=O).
- **Pyrimidine end:** a methyl- and amino-substituted pyrimidine with the asparagine-derived side chain and the terminal diamino-amide.

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCC[S+](C)C)O

SMILES: CC1=C(N=C(N=C1N)[C@H](CC(=O)N)NC[C@@H](C(=O)N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C2=CN=CN2)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)OC(=O)N)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC5=NC(=CS5)C6=NC(=CS6)C(=O)NCCC[S+](C)C)O

name: Boric Acid
text:
The drawing shows a central boron atom with three single bonds, each to an OH group. This is boric acid, B(OH)3. There are no charges or stereochemistry to record.

SMILES: OB(O)O

name: Bocodepsin
text:
I read the structure as a 16-membered macrocycle with a thiazole fused into it and a valine thioester side chain.

**Macrocycle** (going around the ring):
- The thiazole C2 carries a CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2 link.
- That leads to the ring CH–O, which closes through the ester O–C(=O) to the ring valine α-carbon.
- The valine α-carbon carries an isopropyl group and an NH.
- The NH is bonded to C(=O)–C(CH3)2–NH–C(=O), which returns to the thiazole C4.

**Side chain:** the ring CH–O carries a CH=CH–CH2–CH2–S–C(=O)–CH(NH2)–CH(CH3)2 chain. The double bond is drawn in the trans zigzag, so I wrote it as E.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes using CIP priorities.
- The side-chain valine α-carbon (hashed NH2) is S.
- The ring valine α-carbon (hashed isopropyl) is S.
- The ring CH–O carbon (wedged vinyl) is S.

I then chose the @/@@ symbols in the SMILES so that each centre comes out as S.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)SCC/C=C/[C@@H]1CC(=O)NCc2nc(cs2)C(=O)NC(C)(C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)O1

name: Boron tribromide
text:
The drawing shows a central boron atom (B) with single bonds to three bromine atoms (Br). That is boron tribromide, BBr3. No charges or stereochemistry are shown.

SMILES: BrB(Br)Br

name: Boron trifluoride
text:
The image shows a central boron atom (B) with single bonds to three fluorine atoms (F). This is boron trifluoride, BF3. There are no charges and no stereochemistry.

SMILES: FB(F)F

name: Boldenone
text:
The drawing shows a steroid skeleton (four fused rings, 17 ring carbons), and I matched it to boldenone by reading it region by region:

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with C1=C2, a C3 ketone (C=O) and C4=C5.
- **C10:** a hashed methyl group, which is the 19-methyl.
- **C13:** a hashed methyl group, which is the 18-methyl.
- **C17:** a hashed OH on the five-membered ring D.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** a wedge H at C9, a hashed H at C8 and a wedge H at C14.

The molecule is drawn mirrored left to right (ring A on the right, ring D on the left), which swaps wedges and hashes. Once that is accounted for, every stereocentre matches the natural configuration: 8β-H, 9α-H, 14α-H, 10β-methyl, 13β-methyl and 17β-OH. This is 17β-hydroxyandrosta-1,4-dien-3-one.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the drawing. I wrote the SMILES from the standard testosterone SMILES, changed ring A to the 1,4-dien-3-one, and relied on that to carry the natural stereochemistry.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O)CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]34C

name: Bosentan
text:
This structure is bosentan.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Central pyrimidine:** the ring atoms are C4 (bearing NH), N3, C2 (bearing the pyrimidin-2-yl group), N1, C6 (bearing the OCH2CH2OH group) and C5 (bearing the aryloxy group).
- **Left side:** C5 carries an O linked to a benzene ring, which has an OMe on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.
- **Right side:** the NH is bonded to S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to a para-tert-butylphenyl ring.
- **Bottom:** C2 is attached to a second pyrimidine ring through its 2-position, so this ring has an N on each side of the attachment carbon.

SMILES, written in order:
- Sulfonamide: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ncccn1

Check of the central ring: c1 (C4, bearing NH), then n (N3), then c(...) (C2, bearing the pyrimidinyl group), then n (N1), then c(OCCO) (C6), then c1 (C5, bearing OAr). The ring closes properly.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ncccn1

name: Bleomycin
text:
This is bleomycin A2, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Left end:** a dimethylsulfonium on a propyl chain, linked through an amide to a bithiazole.
- **Middle:** an ethylamine link to a threonine residue, then a methyl-hydroxy-valerate unit.
- **Histidine unit:** a β-hydroxyhistidine whose oxygen carries the two-sugar disaccharide, with a carbamate on the terminal sugar.
- **Right end:** a 4-amino-5-methylpyrimidine carrying the diamino-propionamide side chain.

Stereo is written only at the centres drawn with wedges or hashes. The sugar rings have plain bonds, so they carry no stereo marks. The imidazole is attached at the carbon next to the NH, as drawn.

SMILES: C[S+](C)CCCNC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1csc(n1)CCNC(=O)[C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)c1nc(nc(N)c1C)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC[C@H](N)C(N)=O)[C@@H](OC1OC(CO)C(O)C(O)C1OC1OC(CO)C(O)C(OC(N)=O)C1O)c1[nH]cnc1)[C@@H](C)O

name: Bosutinib
text:
This is bosutinib.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Quinoline core:** the ring nitrogen sits at the top and is bonded to a CH. That CH connects to the carbon bearing the nitrile (C#N), which connects to the carbon bearing NH (C4).
- **Benzo ring substituents:** the carbon at position 7 carries the OCH2CH2CH2-N-methylpiperazine chain. The adjacent carbon at position 6 carries the OMe.
- **Aniline ring:** the NH-bearing carbon is flanked by a Cl-bearing carbon on one side and a CH on the other. Going around from the NH carbon: C1 (NH), C2 (Cl), C3 (H), C4 (Cl), C5 (OMe), C6 (H). This gives the 2,4-dichloro-5-methoxyphenyl group.
- **Side chain:** propoxy linker to the piperazine N, with the other piperazine N carrying a methyl.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CCCOc2cc3ncc(C#N)c(Nc4cc(OC)c(Cl)cc4Cl)c3cc2OC)CC1

name: Bortezomib
text:
This structure is bortezomib. I read it in four parts.

- **Left chain:** an isobutyl group (CH(CH3)2–CH2) is attached to a stereocentre that carries B(OH)2 and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH connects to a C=O, which connects to a second stereocentre bearing a benzyl group (CH2–phenyl) and an NH.
- **Right end:** that NH is acylated by a pyrazine-2-carbonyl group (a 1,4-diazine ring joined through C=O).
- **Stereochemistry:** both stereocentres have one wedge bond to the CH2 substituent, so the implicit hydrogen points away from the viewer.
  - The boron-bearing carbon has priorities N > CH2 > B, which run clockwise on the page, so it is R.
  - The benzyl-bearing carbon has priorities N > C(=O) > CH2, which run counterclockwise, so it is S.

SMILES: B([C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)c1cnccn1)(O)O

name: Bolasterone
text:
I read this as a 7,17-dimethyl-substituted testosterone-type steroid (a 4-en-3-one with a 17-hydroxy-17-methyl group), with methyl groups at C7, C10 and C13. The stereo marks come from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing.

**Skeleton**
- Ring A has the C3 ketone (C=O) and a C4=C5 double bond.
- C10 and C13 each carry a hashed methyl.
- C17 carries an OH and a wedged methyl.
- C7 carries a wedged methyl.
- The ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn explicitly: H on C9 is wedged, H on C8 is hashed, and H on C14 is wedged.

**Stereo assignment**
I worked out each centre from the 2D coordinates and the wedge or hash on its substituent, then converted to SMILES neighbour order:
- C17: @
- C13: @
- C14: @@
- C9: @
- C8: @
- C7: @
- C10: @

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures (1 to 4) and atom count against the drawing, but I did not check the stereo marks against a reference structure.

SMILES: C[C@]1(O)CC[C@@H]2[C@]1(C)CC[C@H]3[C@H]2[C@H](C)CC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C

name: Boro-Scopol
text:
I read this as scopolamine: a phenyl hydroxymethyl acetate ester of a tropane-type bicycle that carries an epoxide.

**Side chain.** A phenyl ring is attached to the stereocentre. That carbon bears a CH2OH on a wedge, a plain bond to the phenyl, and a plain bond to the ester carbonyl C(=O)–O. I worked out the wedge as `OC[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)O…`.

**Bicyclic core.**
- The ester oxygen is attached to a ring carbon with no stereo marking, so it gets none.
- That carbon connects through two CH2 groups to the two bridgehead carbons.
- The bridgeheads are joined by an N–CH3 bridge.
- Each bridgehead is also bonded to one carbon of a C–O–C epoxide, and the two epoxide carbons are bonded to each other.

**Stereo marks.** The bridgehead hydrogens are on wedges. The epoxide hydrogens are on hashes. I assigned `@`/`@@` for each centre from the drawn geometry, using the neighbour order in the SMILES.

I wrote the SMILES with ring closure 1 for the ester-bearing ring, 2 for the nitrogen bridge, and 3 for the epoxide. I did not run this through a cheminformatics tool, so the validity check was done by hand.

SMILES: OC[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)OC1C[C@@H]2[C@H]3O[C@H]3[C@H](C1)N2C

name: Bradykinin
text:
I read the drawing as the linear nonapeptide Arg-Pro-Pro-Gly-Phe-Ser-Pro-Phe-Arg (bradykinin), written from the N-terminus to the free C-terminal acid.

- **N-terminus:** an arginine with a free NH2 on the wedged alpha carbon and a guanidine side chain, `N=C(N)N`.
- **Pro-Pro:** two proline rings, each with a hashed alpha carbon.
- **Gly:** a plain CH2 between the amides.
- **Phe:** a benzyl side chain on a wedged alpha carbon. I checked this centre by hand against the wedge geometry and it comes out as L-Phe.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Pro, Phe:** a third proline and a second phenylalanine.
- **C-terminus:** a final arginine ending in COOH.

I assigned the other centres as the natural L-amino-acid configuration, which is consistent with the wedges and hashes shown, but I did not check each one individually.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)O

name: Brigatinib
text:
This structure is brigatinib, and I read it region by region from the drawing.

- **Pyrimidine core:** the ring atoms are N, C(H), C(Cl), C(NH-aryl), N and C(NH-aryl). The Cl sits on the carbon next to the CH.
- **Left aryl group:** the NH at the 4-position of the pyrimidine attaches to a benzene ring that carries a P(=O)(CH3)2 group on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.
- **Right aryl group:** the NH at the 2-position attaches to a second benzene ring. That ring has an OMe ortho to the NH and a piperidin-1-yl group para to the NH.
- **Piperidine and piperazine:** the piperidine is substituted at its 4-position with a piperazine, and that piperazine carries an N-methyl group.

I wrote the SMILES in this order: Clc1cnc(Nc2ccc(cc2OC)N2CCC(CC2)N2CCN(C)CC2)nc1Nc1ccccc1P(C)(C)=O.

Checking the connectivity against the drawing:
- In the pyrimidine, c1(Cl), then c(H), n, c(N...), n, and c1 bearing the NH closes the ring. That matches.
- In the right benzene ring, c2 (bearing the NH), then c, c, c(N-piperidine), c, c2(OMe). The OMe carbon is adjacent to the NH carbon. The piperidine carbon is para to the NH carbon, which fits the drawing, where the ring carbon bearing N is opposite the NH carbon.

SMILES: Clc1cnc(Nc2ccc(cc2OC)N2CCC(CC2)N2CCN(C)CC2)nc1Nc1ccccc1P(C)(C)=O

name: Brexpiprazole
text:
This structure is brexpiprazole-like, but the quinolinone is linked through a butoxy chain and there is no vinyl group, so it is closer to a brexpiprazole analog. The pieces are:

- **Left side:** a benzothiophene attached through its 4-position to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Linker:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries a chain of 4 CH2 groups, which ends in an oxygen.
- **Right side:** that oxygen is bonded to the 7-position of quinolin-2(1H)-one.

**Benzothiophene.** The thiophene ring is S, CH, CH, then the fused carbons. The carbon next to S is a fusion carbon (C7a). The other fusion carbon (C3a) is bonded to the CH=CH. The benzene carbon adjacent to C3a bears the piperazine, so the attachment is at C4.

SMILES for this part: c1cc(N2CCN(...)CC2)c2ccsc2c1

**Linker.** Counting the chain from N: the bonds run N–C, C–C, C–C, then C–O, giving 4 carbons. This matches the picture, with vertices at 630, 705, 787 and 862 before the O.

**Quinolinone.** The ring is O=c1ccc2ccc(OR)cc2[nH]1. The oxygen-bearing carbon is bonded to a CH on one side and to a CH adjacent to the fusion carbon (C8a) bonded to N. That places it at position 7.

Combining the parts:

O=c1ccc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc4sccc34)cc2[nH]1

Check on the benzothiophene: c3cccc4sccc34 starts at C4 (the attachment), then C5, C6, C7, then C7a (c4) bonded to s, then the two CH carbons, then C3a (c34), which closes to both C4 and C7a. This is correct.

SMILES: O=c1ccc2ccc(OCCCCN3CCN(CC3)c3cccc4sccc34)cc2[nH]1

name: Brimonidine
text:
This is brimonidine, a quinoxaline bearing an imidazoline ring.

**Imidazoline ring (left):** The ring is CH2–CH2–N=C(–NH)–NH, closed back to the first CH2. The carbon on the right of the ring is double-bonded to the ring N at the lower left and single-bonded to the ring NH at the top. It also carries an exocyclic NH that links to the aromatic ring.

**Quinoxaline (right):**
- The benzene ring carbon attached to the exocyclic NH is adjacent to the carbon bearing Br.
- That Br-bearing carbon is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon, which is bonded to the lower N.
- The pyrazine ring runs N–CH=CH–N between the two fusion carbons.
- The upper fusion carbon connects to the CH=CH part of the benzene ring.

**SMILES:** Starting from the Br carbon: Brc1c(NC2=NCCN2)ccc2nccnc12. Checking the ring closures:
- c1 is the Br carbon.
- c(NC2=NCCN2) is the carbon bearing the amino group.
- cc are the two benzene CH atoms.
- c2 is the upper fusion carbon.
- n, c, c, n are the pyrazine atoms.
- c12 is the lower fusion carbon, bonded to the Br carbon and closing ring 2.

Atom by atom, this matches the drawing.

SMILES: Brc1c(NC2=NCCN2)ccc2nccnc12

name: Bremelanotide
text:
Reading the drawing region by region, I get an N-acetyl-norleucine attached to a cyclic hexapeptide whose ring is closed through an Asp side chain and a Lys side chain.

- **N-terminus:** acetyl on the Nle nitrogen, then Nle (a butyl side chain). The hashed butyl bond reads as L (S).
- **Ring:** Asp, His, Phe, Arg, Trp, Lys.
  - The Asp side-chain CH2–C(=O) forms an amide with the Lys side-chain NH. The four labelled "C" atoms in the ring are the Lys (CH2)4 chain.
  - Lys carries a free COOH at the C-terminus.
- **Side chains:**
  - His is an imidazole attached at the carbon next to the NH.
  - Phe is a phenyl.
  - Arg ends in a guanidine, N=C(N)N.
  - Trp is an indol-3-yl.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each alpha carbon from its wedge or hash bond and CIP priorities. Nle, Asp, Lys, Trp, Arg and His come out L. Phe comes out D, because its CH2 bond is hashed.

The SMILES below was written to match these assignments and checked against the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCC)C(=O)N[C@H]1CC(=O)NCCCC[C@@H](C(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2cnc[nH]2)NC1=O

name: Brinzolamide
text:
This structure is brinzolamide, read as follows.

- **Ring system:** a thiophene is fused to a six-membered cyclic sulfonamide (S(=O)(=O) bonded to N). The N carries a 3-methoxypropyl chain (CCCOC).
- **Thiophene substituent:** the thiophene carbon next to the ring S carries a primary sulfonamide, S(N)(=O)=O.
- **Stereocentre:** the ring carbon bearing the ethylamino group (NHCH2CH3) has a hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - Seen from the front, N (bottom), the ring-junction carbon (upper left) and the CH2 (upper right) run clockwise.
  - For the SMILES neighbour order N, H, ring-junction carbon, CH2, this gives `@`.

SMILES: CCN[C@H]1CN(CCCOC)S(=O)(=O)c2sc(S(N)(=O)=O)cc12

name: Brincidofovir
text:
I read the molecule as the hexadecyloxypropyl ester of cidofovir (HPMPC), a cytosine-based acyclic nucleoside phosphonate.

- **Alkyl chain:** counting the zigzag vertices from the left end gives 16 carbons, so a hexadecyl group. It is joined through an ether O to a three-carbon propyl linker, which ends in an O bonded to phosphorus.
- **Phosphonate:** P carries one =O, one OH, the ester O from the propyl linker, and a CH2 that leads to an ether O.
- **Stereocentre:** the ether O is attached to a stereocentre bearing CH2OH and a wedged CH2 that connects to the cytosine N1. The wedge is the only stereo marking in the drawing.
- **Base:** cytosine, with a 4-NH2, a 2-C=O, and a C5=C6 double bond.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are O > CH2OH > CH2N > H. With the implicit H pointing away, O → CH2OH → CH2N runs counterclockwise, which is S. I encoded this as `[C@H]` with the neighbours written in the order O, H, CH2OH, CH2N.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCOCCCOP(=O)(O)CO[C@H](CO)Cn1ccc(N)nc1=O

name: Brilacidin
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrimidine-4,6-dicarboxamide whose two amide nitrogens are each bonded to the same substituted aryl group.

**Core:** the pyrimidine has C4 and C6 carrying the C(=O)NH groups, with C5 as CH between them and N1/N3 flanking C2 (CH).

**Each aryl ring** has these substituents, with the ring-carbon neighbours in this order:
- the carbon bonded to the pyrimidine amide NH
- a CH
- a carbon bearing CF3
- a CH
- a carbon bonded to NHC(=O)(CH2)4–N=C(NH2)2 (a 5-guanidinopentanamide; I counted four CH2 groups between the C=O and the guanidine N)
- a carbon bearing O-pyrrolidin-3-yl, which sits between the two N-bearing carbons

**Stereochemistry:** each pyrrolidin-3-yl ether carbon is drawn with one wedge or hash bond to O (a hash on the left, a wedge on the right). The priorities are O > C2 (the CH2 next to N) > C4 > H. Working through the geometry, both centres come out as R. In the SMILES, `O[C@@H]1CCNC1` encodes R for each.

SMILES: NC(N)=NCCCCC(=O)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(NC(=O)c2cc(C(=O)Nc3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(NC(=O)CCCCN=C(N)N)c3O[C@@H]3CCNC3)ncn2)c1O[C@@H]1CCNC1

name: Brevicidine
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing as a lipopeptide with a depsipeptide ring. I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash by working out CIP priorities.

**Sequence, left to right:**
- A 4-methylhexanoyl chain acylates the N-terminus.
- Residues follow in this order: D-Asn, D-Tyr, D-Trp, D-Orn, L-Orn, Gly, D-Orn, L-Trp, L-Thr, L-Ile, Gly, L-Ser.
- The macrocycle closes through an ester between the Ser carbonyl and the Thr side-chain oxygen. The ring atoms are Thr Cα, Thr C=O, Ile, Gly, Ser, the ester O and Thr Cβ.

**Stereochemistry:**
- Thr has the L-configuration (2S,3R) and Ile has the L-configuration (2S,3S).
- The ornithine side chains are plain aminopropyl groups, so only the α-carbons carry stereo.

I checked the SMILES for ring closures (digits 1 and 2 for the indoles and the tyrosine ring, digit 3 for the macrocycle) and for the atom count against the drawing.

SMILES: CCC(C)CCC(=O)N[C@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H]3C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O[C@@H]3C

name: Brivanib
text:
This structure is brivanib, and its single stereocentre is drawn with a hashed methyl bond.

- **Left ring system:** a 2-methylindole (N–H, methyl on the five-membered ring). The benzene ring carries fluorine next to the ring-fusion carbon, and an aryl ether oxygen on the carbon adjacent to the fluorine-bearing carbon.
- **Core:** the aryl ether oxygen links to C4 of a pyrrolo[2,1-f][1,2,4]triazine. Its pyrrole ring has a methyl at C5 and an O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH3 ether at C6.
- **Stereocentre:** the carbon bearing OH has OH drawn up, CH2 to the lower left and CH3 hashed to the lower right, so the hydrogen points toward the viewer. Priorities are OH > CH2O > CH3 > H. Going OH → CH2 → CH3 appears counterclockwise from the front, and with H toward the viewer that reverses to clockwise, giving R.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** in `C[C@@H](O)CO...` the neighbour order is CH3, H, O, CH2. The `@@` tag encodes R for this order, so that is the tag used.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O)COc1cn2ncnc(Oc3ccc4[nH]c(C)cc4c3F)c2c1C

name: Brivaracetam
text:
I read this as brivaracetam, (2S)-2-[(4R)-2-oxo-4-propylpyrrolidin-1-yl]butanamide.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- On the left is a primary amide, H2N–C(=O)–.
- Its carbonyl carbon connects to a stereocentre. That carbon carries an ethyl group drawn on a wedge and is bonded to the ring nitrogen.
- The ring is a five-membered lactam: N, C(=O), CH2, CH and CH2. The ring CH carries a propyl chain drawn on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Side-chain carbon:** the priorities are N > C(=O)NH2 > ethyl, with H pointing back. Tracing N (upper right) to C(=O)N (upper left) to ethyl (down) runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S.
- **Ring carbon:** the priorities are CH2–N > CH2–C(=O) > propyl, with H pointing back. Tracing down-left to up-left to right runs clockwise, so this centre is R.
- I checked that `[C@H]` for the ring carbon and `[C@@H]` for the side-chain carbon in the SMILES below give R and S respectively.

SMILES: CCC[C@H]1CN(C(=O)C1)[C@@H](CC)C(N)=O

name: Brevetoxin B
text:
I read the drawing as a brevetoxin-type polyether, working ring by ring from the left.

- **Left end:** an α,β-unsaturated six-membered lactone with a methyl on the C=C, fused to a six-membered ether ring.
- **Middle:** two six-membered and two seven-membered ether rings (one seven-membered ring carries a CH-methyl), then two six-membered rings with angular methyls.
- **Eight-membered ring:** an eight-membered ether ring containing a ring CH=CH. I wrote this double bond without cis/trans marking, since it sits inside the ring.
- **Right end:** two fused six-membered ether rings, then a six-membered ring bearing the hydroxyl and a CH2–C(=CH2)–CHO side chain.

Stereochemistry is assigned from the wedges and hashes at every drawn centre. I read each centre from its 2D coordinates and converted to @/@@ by hand, so the descriptors are the part most likely to contain an error. I did not run the SMILES through a parser.

SMILES: CC1=CC(=O)O[C@H]2C[C@@H]3[C@@](C)(O[C@H]12)C[C@@H]4[C@@H](O3)C[C@@H](C)[C@@H]5[C@@H](O4)CC[C@@](C)6[C@@H](O5)C[C@@H]7[C@@](C)(O6)C[C@@H]8[C@@](C)(O7)CC=C[C@@H]9[C@@H](O8)C[C@@H]%10[C@@H](O9)C[C@@H]%11[C@@](C)(O%10)[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](CC(=C)C=O)O%11

name: Bromperidol
text:
The drawing is a bromo analogue of haloperidol, with Br in place of Cl. I read it region by region:

- **Left ring:** a 4-fluorophenyl group attached to a ketone carbon (C=O).
- **Chain:** the carbonyl is followed by three CH2 groups, ending at the piperidine nitrogen. That gives a 4-carbon butanone unit, C(=O)CCC–N.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring containing N. The carbon opposite N carries both an OH and a 4-bromophenyl group.
- **Right ring:** a 4-bromophenyl group, with Br para to the attachment point.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry in the SMILES.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccc(F)cc1)CCCN1CCC(O)(c2ccc(Br)cc2)CC1

name: Brodifacoum
text:
This structure is bromadiolone-like but without the hydroxy group: it is the coumarin anticoagulant difenacoum, specifically its brominated analog, which is brodifacoum.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Coumarin:** a 4-hydroxycoumarin with the benzo ring at the top right, the ring oxygen, a C=O, and an OH on C4. C3 carries the tetralin substituent.
- **Tetralin:** C1 (attached to coumarin C3) is bonded to CH2, which is bonded to CH (C3 of the tetralin) bearing the biphenyl. That CH is bonded to another CH2, which joins the aromatic ring.
- **Biphenyl:** the tetralin is attached to a phenyl ring that is para-linked to a 4-bromophenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is included.

SMILES written from the coumarin end: O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1C1CC(c2ccc(cc2)-c2ccc(Br)cc2)Cc2ccccc21

SMILES: O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1C1CC(c2ccc(cc2)-c2ccc(Br)cc2)Cc2ccccc21

name: Brompheniramine
text:
The drawing shows brompheniramine: a dimethylamino group on a two-carbon chain, leading to a CH that carries a 4-bromophenyl ring and a 2-pyridyl ring.

- Dimethylamino: N bearing two methyl groups.
- Chain: N–CH2–CH2–CH, where the CH is bonded to both rings.
- Bromophenyl: a benzene ring attached at one carbon, with Br on the carbon directly opposite (para).
- Pyridine: attached at the carbon next to the ring nitrogen (2-pyridyl).

The central CH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CN(C)CCC(c1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccccn1

name: Bromfenac
text:
The drawing shows bromfenac: a central benzene ring carrying three substituents on adjacent carbons.

- **Carboxylic acid arm:** a CH2COOH group is attached to the ring at the lower-left carbon.
- **Amino group:** NH2 is on the next ring carbon, adjacent to the CH2COOH carbon.
- **Aroyl group:** the next carbon carries a C(=O) linked to a 4-bromophenyl ring.

Reading the SMILES from the acid end: OC(=O)Cc1cccc(C(=O)c2ccc(Br)cc2)c1N

Check against the drawing:
- The ring carbon bearing CH2 is bonded to the carbon bearing NH2.
- The NH2 carbon is bonded to the carbon bearing the C=O.
- The remaining three ring CH carbons close the ring.
- The second ring is para-substituted, with Br opposite the carbonyl attachment.

SMILES: OC(=O)Cc1cccc(C(=O)c2ccc(Br)cc2)c1N

name: Bucillamine
text:
The drawing shows N-(2-mercapto-2-methylpropanoyl)-cysteine.

- **Acyl part:** a quaternary carbon carries two methyl groups and an SH, and is bonded to a C=O. That carbonyl is joined to an N–H, giving CC(C)(S)C(=O)N.
- **Cysteine part:** the nitrogen is bonded to the α-carbon. This carbon bears a hashed CH2–SH bond (going away from the viewer) and a COOH group. The implicit hydrogen therefore points toward the viewer.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities are N > CH2SH > COOH > H. In the drawing the sequence N → CH2SH → COOH runs counterclockwise. Because H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is R. This matches L-cysteine, written as N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O.

SMILES: CC(C)(S)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O

name: Brivudine
text:
This is brivudine, (E)-5-(2-bromovinyl)-2'-deoxyuridine.

- **Base:** the pyrimidine-2,4-dione ring has an N–H between the two carbonyls and is attached to the sugar through N1. Its C5 carries a bromovinyl group, and the vinyl double bond is drawn trans (E).
- **Sugar:** the five-membered ring has an ring oxygen, a CH2 at C2', a hydroxyl at C3' and a CH2OH at C4'. It is a 2'-deoxyribose.
- **Stereo:** the drawing shows a hashed bond from C1' to N, a wedged OH at C3', and a hashed CH2OH at C4'. Taking the implicit hydrogens as pointing the opposite way at each centre, I worked out the chirality tags as C1' `@`, C3' `@` and C4' `@@` in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)N([C@H]2C[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O2)C=C1/C=C/Br

name: Budipine
text:
The drawing shows a piperidine ring with a nitrogen carrying a tert-butyl group. The carbon at position 4 (opposite the nitrogen) carries two phenyl groups.

- The tert-butyl group is a central carbon bonded to three methyl groups and to the nitrogen.
- The piperidine ring has N plus four CH2 carbons and one quaternary carbon, which is six atoms in total.
- Each phenyl ring is drawn with alternating double bonds, so each is a normal benzene ring.
- No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)N1CCC(CC1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Bumadizone
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Butyl chain:** four carbons run from the right edge down to the CH, which is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo.
- **Carboxylic acid:** the CH carries a C(=O)OH group, drawn at the top with HO and =O labels.
- **Hydrazide:** the CH also carries a C(=O) group bonded to N. That N bears a phenyl ring and is bonded to an NH, which in turn carries a second phenyl ring.

The molecule is 2-[(N,N'-diphenyl)hydrazinecarbonyl]hexanoic acid.

SMILES: CCCCC(C(=O)O)C(=O)N(c1ccccc1)Nc1ccccc1

name: Budesonide
text:
The image matches budesonide: a pregna-1,4-dien-3-one steroid core with an 11-hydroxyl, a 17-hydroxyacetyl group (C(=O)CH2OH), and a 16,17-acetal bridged by a butylidene (propyl-substituted) group.

I took the ring-junction and ring-carbon stereocentres from the drawn wedges and hashes, matched to the known budesonide configuration. The acetal carbon, which carries the propyl chain, is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo.

SMILES: CCCC1O[C@@H]2C[C@H]3[C@@H]4CCC5=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]5([C@H]4[C@H](C[C@@]3([C@@]2(O1)C(=O)CO)C)O)C

name: (+-)-Bunitrolol
text:
The drawing shows bunitrolol: a tert-butyl group on an NH, which is joined to a CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O chain, which is attached to a benzene ring that carries a nitrile ortho to the ether oxygen.

Reading the structure region by region:
- The tert-butyl group is a quaternary carbon with three methyl groups, bonded to the NH.
- The chain runs NH, CH2, CH(OH), CH2, then O.
- The aromatic ring is attached through that O at one carbon, and the adjacent ring carbon bears the C≡N group.
- The CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1ccccc1C#N

name: Bupivacaine (USAN:INN:BAN)
text:
The drawing shows bupivacaine, built from three parts.

- **Piperidine ring:** the ring nitrogen carries an n-butyl chain, drawn as four carbons. The ring carbon next to the nitrogen is bonded to the carbonyl carbon.
- **Amide:** the carbonyl carbon has a C=O and is bonded to NH.
- **Aryl group:** the NH is attached to a benzene ring that carries a methyl group on each of the two carbons flanking the attachment point (a 2,6-dimethylphenyl group).

All bonds in the drawing are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so the stereocentre at the ring carbon gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CCCCN1CCCCC1C(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Bryostatin
text:
I read this as a bryostatin-type macrolide (it matches bryostatin 1) and wrote the SMILES by tracing the macrocycle atom by atom.

- **Macrocycle:** it runs from the lactone C(=O) through the ring oxygen to the carbon bearing the CH(OH)CH3 group. It then passes a CH2 to the carbon bonded to the ring O, and on to the hemiketal carbon C(OH) and the CMe2 carbon. After the ring C=C it reaches the tetrahydropyran carbon, and it closes back through the CH2, CH(OH), CH2 sequence next to the lactone.
- **Left ring:** a tetrahydropyran containing the OAc-bearing carbon, a gem-dimethyl carbon and a hemiketal C(OH).
- **Lower ring:** a tetrahydropyran carrying the exocyclic =CH–CO2Me.
- **Upper side chain:** a carbon bearing the octa-2,4-dienoate ester, attached to C(=CH–CO2Me).

I could not reliably assign the wedge and hash stereocentres from the drawing, so I left the chiral carbons without stereo marks. I included only the E geometry of the dienoate and of the ring alkene. The exocyclic C=C bonds are left unspecified as well.

SMILES: CCC/C=C/C=C/C(=O)OC1C(=CC(=O)OC)CC2CC(C(C)O)OC(=O)CC(O)CC3CC(OC(C)=O)C(C)(C)C(O)(O3)CC4CC(=CC(=O)OC)CC(O4)/C=C/C(C)(C)C1(O)O2

name: Bupranolol
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Left end:** a tert-butyl group (a carbon bearing three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- **Chain:** NH–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O, with the OH drawn with a plain bond.
- **Ring:** an aromatic ring joined to the chain through the ether O. The ring carbon bearing O has an adjacent carbon bearing Cl (ortho). The ring continues CH, CH, then a carbon bearing a methyl, then CH, and back to the carbon bearing O.

Numbering the ring from the O-bearing carbon as C1:
- C1 has the O.
- C2 has the Cl, at the upper left of the ring.
- C3 is CH (top).
- C4 is CH (upper right).
- C5 has the methyl (right).
- C6 is CH (bottom).

The methyl carbon sits on the ring carbon at the right, which is para to the Cl carbon. The ring is therefore 2-chloro-5-methylphenoxy.

The CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cc(C)ccc1Cl

name: Bryostatin 1
text:
This is my reading of the drawing: a bryostatin-type macrolide with three six-membered rings (two tetrahydropyrans and one more pyran ring). The stereo tags (`@`/`@@`) were assigned by eye from the wedges and hashes and may contain errors. I left the two exocyclic C=C bonds bearing the methyl ester groups without cis/trans markers.

**Macrolactone and substituents**
- The lactone C(=O) sits next to a CH2, then a CH(OH) (wedged OH), then another CH2.
- The 1-hydroxyethyl group, CH(OH)CH3, is on the carbon bearing the lactone oxygen.

**Ring A (six-membered, oxygen-containing)**
- It carries an acetate on one carbon, a gem-dimethyl carbon next to it, and a hemiketal carbon bearing OH.

**Ring B (tetrahydropyran)**
- It has an exocyclic =CH–CO2Me group.
- A trans CH=CH links it to a C(CH3)2 carbon.

**Ring C (six-membered, oxygen-containing)**
- It has an OH on the carbon next to the oxygen and a ring carbon bearing the exocyclic =CH–CO2Me.
- The adjacent ring carbon carries the (2E,4E)-octa-2,4-dienoate ester, O–C(=O)–CH=CH–CH=CH–C3H7.

SMILES: O=C1C[C@@H](O)C[C@H]2C[C@H](OC(C)=O)C(C)(C)[C@@](O)(O2)C[C@H]3CC(=CC(=O)OC)C[C@H](O3)/C=C/C(C)(C)[C@]4(O)O[C@H](C[C@H]([C@H](C)O)O1)CC(=CC(=O)OC)[C@H]4OC(=O)/C=C/C=C/CCC

name: Bromocriptine
text:
I read this as bromocriptine and wrote its SMILES from the drawing. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash bonds and checked the SMILES atom order against them.

**Ergoline half (left)**
- An indole-fused tetracyclic core carries Br at C2 of the indole, next to the [nH].
- The ring nitrogen bears an N-methyl group.
- A carbonyl is attached through a hashed bond to the ring CH. It forms an amide with the NH that leads to the right-hand half.
- The ring CH next to N is drawn with a hashed H.

**Cyclol/peptide half (right)**
- A quaternary carbon bears an isopropyl group, the NH (hashed bond), the ring O and a C=O.
- That ring O links to the hemiaminal carbon, which carries an OH (hashed bond).
- The hemiaminal carbon is also bonded to the proline CH (wedged H) and to the N of a diketopiperazine-type ring.
- The pyrrolidine ring is closed through the proline N.
- The leucine-derived CH carries an isobutyl group on a hashed bond.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H]1C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2[C@]3(O)O[C@](NC(=O)[C@@H]4C=C5c6cccc7[nH]c(Br)c(c67)C[C@H]5N(C)C4)(C(C)C)C(=O)N13

name: Bupropion
text:
The drawing shows a tert-butyl group on an NH, which is attached to a CH carrying a methyl group. That CH is bonded to a C=O, and the carbonyl carbon is bonded to a benzene ring.

On the ring, the carbonyl-bearing carbon is at the bottom left (995,875). Moving up, the next vertex is (963,627). Cl is on the vertex at (1163,476), which is the next one along. Cl is therefore two ring atoms away from the carbonyl-bearing carbon, which makes it meta.

The CH has no wedge or hash bond, so I have not assigned stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(NC(C)(C)C)C(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1

SMILES: CC(NC(C)(C)C)C(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1

name: Buspirone
text:
The drawing shows buspirone, which I read region by region as follows.

- **Pyrimidine:** a 2-substituted ring with N at the top and N at the bottom, attached to the piperazine through its C2.
- **Piperazine:** two nitrogens, one bonded to the pyrimidine and the other to the chain.
- **Chain:** four CH2 groups link the piperazine nitrogen to the imide nitrogen.
- **Imide ring:** N–C(=O)–CH2–C(spiro)–CH2–C(=O), a six-membered glutarimide.
- **Spiro ring:** the spiro carbon is part of a cyclopentane, which gives 8-azaspiro[4.5]decane-7,9-dione.

No wedges or hashes appear in the drawing, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=C1CC2(CCCC2)CC(=O)N1CCCCN1CCN(CC1)c1ncccn1

name: Busulfan
text:
The image shows busulfan, a butane-1,4-diyl bis(methanesulfonate).

Reading the drawing from left to right:
- A methyl group is attached to a sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens (a sulfonyl group).
- That sulfur is bonded to an oxygen, which connects to a chain of four carbons.
- The chain ends in another oxygen bonded to a second sulfonyl sulfur, which carries two double-bonded oxygens and a terminal methyl.

I counted the chain carbons along the zigzag: the bond from O goes up to C1, down to C2, up to C3, then down to C4, which bonds to the right-hand O. That gives four carbons.

The SMILES is CS(=O)(=O)OCCCCOS(=O)(=O)C. It has no stereocentres, so no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)OCCCCOS(=O)(=O)C

name: Buprenorphine
text:
I read this as buprenorphine, a bridged morphinan skeleton. I identified it from the drawn groups and checked the SMILES against them:

- The cyclopropylmethyl group is attached to the nitrogen.
- A phenol OH sits on the aromatic ring, next to the furan-type ether oxygen that closes the bridging ring.
- A methoxy group is on the wedged ring-fusion carbon.
- The side chain is a carbinol carbon bearing a methyl (hashed), an OH, and a tert-butyl group. The tert-butyl carbon sits on the long vertical line, with three methyl ends.

I wrote the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes as I read them. I took the SMILES string itself from the known isomeric SMILES for buprenorphine rather than deriving each @/@@ from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]([C@H]1C[C@@]23CC[C@@]1([C@H]4[C@@]25CCN([C@@H]3CC6=C5C(=C(C=C6)O)O4)CC7CC7)OC)(C(C)(C)C)O

name: Butalbital
text:
The drawing shows a barbiturate ring (pyrimidine-2,4,6-trione) with two substituents on the quaternary C5 carbon.

**Ring:** C5 is bonded to two carbonyl carbons (each with =O). Each carbonyl carbon is bonded to an NH, and the two NH groups are joined through a urea carbonyl (C=O).

**Substituents on C5:**
- An allyl group: C5–CH2–CH=CH2. In the drawing, the bond from C5 goes to the CH2 at (437, 642), then to the CH at (443, 393), which has a double bond to the terminal CH2 at (231, 262).
- An isobutyl group: C5–CH2–CH(CH3)2. The CH2 is at (485, 960), and it connects to the CH at (240, 910), which carries two methyl groups.

This is the structure of talbutal-type barbiturates, here with isobutyl in place of sec-butyl (that is, 5-allyl-5-isobutylbarbituric acid).

SMILES: C=CCC1(CC(C)C)C(=O)NC(=O)NC1=O

name: Butanilicaine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying a Cl on one carbon and a methyl on the other carbon adjacent to the ring carbon that bears the NH. That NH is bonded to a C(=O), which is attached to a CH2. The CH2 connects to an NH, and that NH carries a straight n-butyl chain (CCCC).

Reading the ring: the carbon bonded to NH sits between the Cl-bearing carbon and the methyl-bearing carbon, so the substituents are 2-chloro and 6-methyl on an anilide.

I traced the chain from the NH: the bonds run to the first carbon at (1030, 787), then (1157, 700), then (1297, 767), then (1424, 680). That is four carbons, so the group is butyl.

SMILES: CCCCNCC(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1Cl

name: Butenafine
text:
The drawing shows butenafine, a tertiary amine with three substituents on the nitrogen.

- **tert-Butyl group:** a quaternary carbon on the left carries three methyl groups. It is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Benzyl link:** the benzene ring is joined through a CH2 to the nitrogen.
- **N-methyl:** the nitrogen also carries a methyl group.
- **Naphthylmethyl link:** the nitrogen is bonded to a second CH2, which attaches to the naphthalene at position 1. That carbon sits next to the ring-fusion carbon.

The SMILES below follows this connectivity. It has no stereochemistry because the drawing shows no wedges, hashes, or double-bond geometry.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(CN(C)Cc2cccc3ccccc23)cc1

name: Butaperazine
text:
The structure is a phenothiazine core with a butanoyl group (CCCC(=O)–) on one benzo ring and a 3-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)propyl chain on the ring nitrogen. This matches butaperazine.

**Butanoyl group.** The chain runs CH3–CH2–CH2–C(=O), and the carbonyl carbon is attached to an aromatic carbon.

**Substituted ring.** The carbonyl-bearing aromatic carbon sits at about (290, 747). Its neighbours are the carbon at (425, 747), which bonds to the carbon at (488, 863) next to N, and the carbon at (222, 860). From there the ring continues to (290, 977) and then to (421, 979), which bonds to S.

So the ring is C(acyl), CH, C(N), C(S), CH, CH. The acyl carbon is therefore meta to the N-bearing carbon and para to the S-bearing carbon.

**Check of the acyl position.** The ring atoms in order are:
- a1: C(acyl)
- a2: CH at (425, 747)
- a3: C–N at (488, 863)
- a4: C–S at (421, 979)
- a5: CH at (290, 977)
- a6: CH at (222, 860)

The acyl carbon a1 is separated from a4 (C–S) by a2 and a3 on one side and by a6 and a5 on the other, so it is para to the C–S carbon.

**SMILES.** Written starting from the acyl carbon: CCCC(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN4CCN(C)CC4)c2c1

Reading the ring closures: c1 (acyl carbon), c (a6), c (a5), c2 (a4, bonded to S), then S, the second benzo ring c3ccccc3, then N bearing the side chain, then c2 (a3), then c1 (a2). This gives the correct pattern.

SMILES: CCCC(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN4CCN(C)CC4)c2c1

name: Butylphthalide
text:
The drawing shows 3-butylphthalide (3-butyl-isobenzofuran-1(3H)-one), read as follows:

- **Chain:** a straight chain of four carbons (CH3, CH2, CH2, then the ring carbon). The vertices at (75,840), (260,943), (443,835) and (630,938) are the first three chain carbons and the first CH2 of the butyl group, and the attached ring carbon is at (812,829). That makes butyl = C–C–C–C, with the fourth carbon being the one at (630,938), so the ring carbon is the fifth carbon from the free end.
- **Lactone ring:** the ring carbon at (812,829) bonds to O at (829,620), which bonds to the carbonyl carbon at (1040,572). That carbon carries a C=O (O at 1120,375) and bonds to the aromatic carbon at (1148,752). The ring closes through the aromatic carbon at (1008,912) back to the CH carbon.
- **Benzene ring:** six aromatic carbons, two of which are the ring-fusion atoms.
- **Stereochemistry:** the bonds are all plain, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CCCCC1OC(=O)c2ccccc21

name: Buserelin
text:
The image shows a linear peptide, pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Ser(tBu)‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt, which is the sequence of buserelin. I read it residue by residue.

- **N‑terminus:** a pyroglutamic acid ring (5‑membered lactam with C=O), joined by an amide to the histidine.
- **His:** an imidazole attached through CH2. The substituted ring carbon is bonded to the NH and to a CH that leads to the ring N. This gives the ring SMILES `c1[nH]cnc1`.
- **Trp:** an indole attached through CH2 at C3, with an NH in the ring.
- **Ser:** a plain CH2OH side chain.
- **Tyr:** a para‑hydroxyphenyl group on a CH2.
- **Ser(tBu):** a CH2–O–C(CH3)3 side chain. This is the only residue whose side‑chain bond is drawn as a hash, so it is D, while the other residues are L.
- **Leu:** an isobutyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a propyl chain ending in N=C(NH2)NH2.
- **C‑terminus:** a proline carrying a C(=O)NH–CH2CH3 ethylamide.

Stereochemistry follows the wedges and hashes, which match L‑amino acids except for the D‑Ser(tBu).

SMILES: CCNC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](COC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1[nH]cnc1)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1

name: C.I. Acid Orange 52
text:
The image shows methyl orange, the sodium salt of 4-[4-(dimethylamino)phenylazo]benzenesulfonate.

- On the left, a dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- That ring connects through an azo group (N=N) to a second para-substituted benzene ring.
- The second ring carries a sulfonate group: S double-bonded to two O atoms and single-bonded to O⁻.
- Na⁺ is the counterion, drawn separately.

The azo double bond is drawn without a clear cis/trans depiction, so I added no stereo marks.

SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc(cc1)N=Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Cabazitaxel
text:
The drawing matches cabazitaxel, the 7,10-dimethoxy taxane (docetaxel core). I recognised the scaffold and wrote the SMILES from that, taking the stereodescriptors from memory of the known compound rather than deriving them from each wedge and hash in the image.

Features I checked in the drawing:
- **Core:** the taxane skeleton, including the oxetane ring bearing the acetate, a tertiary OH, the C=C bearing a methyl, and a gem-dimethyl group.
- **Substituents:** a ketone, two methoxy groups (one at the top of the eight-membered ring and one on the six-membered ring), and a benzoate ester.
- **Side chain:** a Boc-protected phenylisoserine ester, with the NH-Boc, the OH and the phenyl group all present.

SMILES: CC1=C2[C@H](C(=O)[C@@]3([C@H](C[C@@H]4[C@]([C@H]3[C@@H]([C@@](C2(C)C)(C[C@@H]1OC(=O)[C@@H]([C@H](C5=CC=CC=C5)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)O)O)OC(=O)C6=CC=CC=C6)(CO4)OC(=O)C)OC)C)OC

name: C.I. Acid Blue 90
text:
This is a triarylmethane dye, a sodium salt with two sulfonate groups and one iminium cation.

**Central carbon.** It is double-bonded to a ring carbon of the upper quinoid ring and single-bonded to two aryl groups: a para-phenylene bearing NH-C6H4-OEt, and a tolyl ring bearing the amine.

**Quinoid ring (top).** Starting from the carbon double-bonded to the central carbon, the ring runs C(=N+) … as follows:
- C1 is attached to the central carbon (C1=C central).
- C2 carries the methyl group (the "C(C)" at the left of the ring).
- C3 is CH, double-bonded to C2.
- C4 is C(=N+).
- C5 and C6 are CH=CH.

The ring SMILES is C1(=C(central))C(C)=CC(=[N+](CC)Cc2cccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c2)C=C1.

**Iminium nitrogen.** It carries an ethyl group and a benzyl group whose ring has the sulfonate at the meta position.

**Lower tolyl ring.** The central carbon attaches at C1. The ortho carbon carries the methyl, and the carbon para to C1 carries the N(Et)(CH2-C6H4-SO3-) group.
- Ring atoms: c1(C central) c(C) c c(N...) c c1.
- Reading the drawing: C1 at (815,1040) is attached to the central carbon, and C2 at (903,1010) carries the methyl. C3 at (968,1070) is CH, and C4 at (953,1158) bears N. C5 at (868,1187) and C6 at (800,1127) are CH. So the methyl is ortho to C1 and the N is para to C1, which is consistent.

**Left arm.** The para-phenylene ring is attached to NH, which is attached to a C6H4 ring bearing OEt at the para position.

**Assembled SMILES:**

[Na+].CCOc1ccc(Nc2ccc(cc2)C(=C2C=CC(=[N+](CC)Cc3cccc(c3)S(=O)(=O)[O-])C=C2C)c2ccc(N(CC)Cc3cccc(c3)S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc2C)cc1

Check on the quinoid ring: C2 (=C central) is followed by C=CC(=N+)C=C2C. The ring atoms are C1(=central), C=C, C(=N+), C=C2(C), which gives 6 atoms. The methyl-bearing carbon is adjacent to C1, and the ring bonds around it are C(=N+)–C=C(C)–C1. In the drawing, C2(methyl)=C3H, C3 is bonded to C4(=N+), and C5=C6 are the other side. This matches the form C1(=central) C(C)=C C(=N+) C=C1, so I write it that way:

C(=C1C(C)=CC(=[N+](CC)Cc3cccc(c3)S(=O)(=O)[O-])C=C1)

SMILES: [Na+].CCOc1ccc(Nc2ccc(cc2)C(=C2C(C)=CC(=[N+](CC)Cc3cccc(c3)S(=O)(=O)[O-])C=C2)c2ccc(N(CC)Cc3cccc(c3)S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc2C)cc1

name: C.I. Direct Blue 53
text:
I read the image as the tetrasodium salt of a bis-azo dye built on a 3,3'-dimethylbiphenyl core. This is the trypan blue skeleton, assembled from the drawing as follows.

**Central unit.** Two benzene rings are joined by a single bond. Each ring carries a methyl group ortho to an azo (N=N) attachment, and each azo group sits para to the biaryl bond.

**Naphthalene ends (identical, drawn symmetrically).** Each azo group connects to a naphthalene carbon that is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. Going round the other ring of the same naphthalene:
- The ring-fusion carbon next to the OH carbon leads to a carbon bearing NH2.
- Next is a carbon bearing a sulfonate group (SO3⁻).
- Next is a CH.
- Last is a carbon bearing a second sulfonate, which attaches to the other ring-fusion carbon.

**Counterions.** Four Na⁺ balance the four sulfonate charges.

I wrote the SMILES from these connections and checked each ring closure and substituent position against the drawing. No stereochemistry is included, since the drawing shows no wedges or hashes and the azo double bonds are drawn without specified cis/trans geometry.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].Nc1c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c2ccc(N=Nc3ccc(cc3C)-c3ccc(N=Nc4ccc5c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c(N)c5c4O)c(C)c3)c(O)c12

name: Butorphanol
text:
I read this as a morphinan skeleton (butorphanol-type), assembled from the drawing as follows.

- **Aromatic ring:** a phenol with the OH at the right. The ring carbon below the ring-fusion CH2 is bonded to the quaternary carbon at the bottom.
- **Nitrogen:** it carries a cyclobutylmethyl group (CH2 attached to a four-membered ring). It is also bonded to the CH that has a hashed H and to a CH2–CH2 chain leading to the quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it has a hashed bond to a ring CH2 and is part of a cyclohexane ring.
- **Hydroxyl-bearing carbon:** it has a hashed OH and sits at the other end of the cyclohexane ring, which is four CH2 groups long between the two ring carbons.
- **Stereocentres:** there are three, at the CH bearing the hashed H, the C–OH carbon and the quaternary carbon. I assigned each from the hashed bonds and the positions of the neighbouring atoms in the drawing.

SMILES: Oc1ccc2c(c1)[C@]34CCN(CC5CCC5)[C@H](C2)[C@]3(O)CCCC4

name: Cabozantinib
text:
The drawing shows cabozantinib-like connectivity, built from these pieces:

- **Quinoline core:** 6,7-dimethoxyquinoline, with the ring N at the top. The 4-position carries an O linking to a para-substituted benzene.
- **Central benzene:** para-disubstituted, with the quinolinyl ether O on one side and an NH on the other.
- **Linker:** that NH is bonded to a C(=O) on a cyclopropane carbon. The same cyclopropane carbon carries a second C(=O)NH group leading to a 4-fluorophenyl ring.

Writing the SMILES from the quinoline outward:

COc1cc2nccc(Oc3ccc(NC(=O)C4(CC4)C(=O)Nc4ccc(F)cc4)cc3)c2cc1OC

Check on the quinoline: the N-bearing ring is n–c–c–c(O)–c2 (the fused carbon)–…–c2 (the other fused carbon, bonded to N). In my SMILES, `c2nccc(O...)c2` closes the ring correctly. The benzo ring's CH next to the N-bearing fused carbon (the carbon at about (285,657)) is bonded to the C-OMe at about (228,743). The other OMe carbon at about (273,837) is bonded to the CH at about (378,843), which is bonded to the fused C4a. So the order is COc1cc2nccc(OAr)c2cc1OC, as written.

SMILES: COc1cc2nccc(Oc3ccc(NC(=O)C4(CC4)C(=O)Nc4ccc(F)cc4)cc3)c2cc1OC

name: Calcium Chloride
text:
The image shows three separate ionic species and no bonds: one Ca²⁺ cation and two Cl⁻ anions. This is calcium chloride, CaCl₂, written as disconnected ions.

SMILES: [Ca+2].[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Cabotegravir
text:
I read the drawing as cabotegravir and wrote the SMILES from the labelled atoms and rings.

- **Left side:** a 2,4-difluorobenzyl group is attached through CH2 to an amide NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) group.
- **Centre:** the amide carbonyl sits on a pyridinone ring that carries a ring C=O and an OH, and the ring nitrogen is shared with a second ring.
- **Right side:** a second ring contains a lactam C(=O) and a CH2, and it is fused to an oxazolidine ring (N–CH(CH3)–CH2–O–CH). Both rings share the nitrogen and the CH.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are two stereocentres, the hashed methyl carbon and the hashed-H ring-fusion carbon. For the methyl carbon, the H points toward the viewer, and the other three groups run clockwise (N, then CH2O, then CH3) as seen from the front. Reversing that gives S, which matches the known (3S,11aR) configuration of cabotegravir. I took the ring-fusion carbon's configuration from the known cabotegravir structure rather than deriving it separately from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CO[C@@H]2N1C(=O)C3=C(C(=O)C(=CN3C2)C(=O)NCC4=C(C=C(C=C4)F)F)O

name: Caffeine
text:
This structure is caffeine, a xanthine core with three N-methyl groups.

Reading the drawing atom by atom:
- Six-membered ring: N (top left, bearing a methyl), C(=O) on the left, N (bottom, bearing a methyl), C(=O) at the bottom right, then the two fused carbons.
- Five-membered ring: the fused carbon attached to the top N is double-bonded to the other fused carbon. The top fused carbon also bonds to the ring N= (top right), which is double-bonded to CH. That CH bonds to N (right, bearing a methyl), which bonds back to the second fused carbon.

SMILES: Cn1c(=O)c2c(ncn2C)n(C)c1=O

Checking this string against the drawing:
- n1 is the bottom N-methyl, followed by c(=O), the bottom-right carbonyl.
- c2 is the fused carbon attached to the right N-methyl.
- c(...) is the fused carbon attached to the top N-methyl, and it carries the branch n c n2C. Here n is the ring N, c is the CH, and n2C is the right N-methyl closing ring 2 onto the first fused carbon.
- n(C) is the top N-methyl, and c1=O is the left carbonyl, which closes ring 1 to the bottom N.

Everything matches the picture.

SMILES: Cn1c(=O)c2c(ncn2C)n(C)c1=O

name: Calcium Levulinate
text:
The image shows calcium levulinate dihydrate, which has these components:

- Two levulinate anions. Each is CH3-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-O⁻, written as CC(=O)CCC(=O)[O-].
- One Ca²⁺ ion.
- Two water molecules.

I read the top anion as: CH3 at the top right, then C(=O), then CH2, CH2, and C(=O)O⁻. The bottom anion is drawn the same way.

name: Camostat
text:
The drawing is read from left to right.

1. The left end is a dimethylamide: CN(C)C(=O), with the carbonyl carbon bonded to a CH2.
2. That CH2 is bonded to an ester oxygen, which links to a C(=O) and then to a CH2 on the first benzene ring.
3. The first ring is para-substituted. Its other substituent is an oxygen that forms an aryl ester with a C(=O) attached to the second ring.
4. The second ring is also para-substituted. Its far substituent is N=C(N)N, a guanidine group drawn as N=C(NH2)NH2.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=O)COC(=O)Cc1ccc(OC(=O)c2ccc(N=C(N)N)cc2)cc1

name: Cabergoline
text:
I read this as cabergoline: an ergoline core with an N-allyl group, a C8 acyl-urea side chain, and a dimethylaminopropyl arm.

**Reading the drawing**
- The indole NH sits on an aromatic ring fused to the tetracyclic ergoline core.
- The ring nitrogen carries an allyl group (CH2–CH=CH2).
- The carbon on the ring carrying the carbonyl group (C8) bears the amide C(=O)–N(CH2CH2CH2N(CH3)2)–C(=O)–NH–CH2CH3.
- Three stereocentres are drawn with wedges or hashes:
  - C8 has a hashed bond to the carbonyl carbon.
  - The carbon next to the ring nitrogen (C5) has a hashed H.
  - The ring-fusion carbon (C10) has a wedged H.

**Stereochemistry**

I worked out each centre from the drawn geometry, taking the hashed or wedged H into account. The SMILES is written in the order C8, then C10, then C5. That gives `[C@H]` for C8, `[C@@H]` for C10 and `[C@@H]` for C5. I did not cross-check this against a reference SMILES for cabergoline.

SMILES: C=CCN1C[C@H](C(=O)N(CCCN(C)C)C(=O)NCC)C[C@@H]2c3cccc4[nH]cc(c34)C[C@@H]12

name: Calcium Gluconate
text:
This is calcium gluconate: one Ca²⁺ ion and two identical gluconate anions, each drawn as a six-carbon chain.

**Chain connectivity (each anion):** a carboxylate carbon (C=O and O⁻) is bonded to four CH(OH) carbons in a row. The chain ends in a CH2OH group.

**Stereochemistry:** I read each centre from the wedge or hash on its OH, taking the implicit H as pointing the opposite way. Neighbours are ordered as in the SMILES (preceding carbon, H, O, next carbon).

- C2: OH hashed (back), so `[C@H]`.
- C3: OH hashed (back), so `[C@@H]`.
- C4: OH hashed (back), so `[C@H]`.
- C5: OH wedged (front), so `[C@H]`.

Each anion is therefore `O=C([O-])[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO`. The full formula is two of these plus `[Ca+2]`.

SMILES: [Ca+2].O=C([O-])[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO.O=C([O-])[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Camphor
text:
The drawing is camphor (1,7,7-trimethylbicyclo[2.2.1]heptan-2-one), a bicyclic ketone, and I read it as follows:

- **Bridgehead C with one methyl:** the carbon at the top (about 862,555) carries a methyl. It is bonded to a ring CH2, to the carbonyl carbon, and to the CMe2 carbon.
- **Gem-dimethyl carbon:** the carbon at about (747,960) carries two methyls. It is bonded to the methyl-bearing bridgehead and to the CH bridgehead at about (1097,1191).
- **CH bridgehead:** this carbon is bonded to the CMe2 carbon and to two CH2 groups. One CH2 leads to the CH2 at about (1425,931), which connects back to the methyl-bearing bridgehead. The other CH2 (about 678,1210) leads to the carbonyl carbon.
- **Carbonyl:** the C=O carbon is bonded to the methyl-bearing bridgehead and to the CH2 at (678,1210).

All bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC1(C)C2CCC1(C)C(=O)C2

name: Candesartan
text:
This is candesartan, drawn as the 2H-tetrazole tautomer.

**Benzimidazole part.** An ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O) is on C2. C2 is double-bonded to N3 and single-bonded to N1. N1 carries the CH2 linker to the biphenyl. The fused benzene ring has the COOH on the carbon adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N1, which is position 7.

**Biphenyl part.** The CH2 is attached to a para-substituted benzene. The other para position joins an ortho-substituted benzene, which carries the tetrazole.

**Tetrazole.** The ring atoms are C5, N, NH, N, N. C5 is double-bonded to N, which is single-bonded to NH, then to N, which is double-bonded to the next N, and that N is single-bonded back to C5. So the ring is C1=NNN=N1 with the H on the second nitrogen, written c1nn[nH]n1 in aromatic form.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Ethoxy-benzimidazole: CCOC1=Nc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1
- Checking the tetrazole connectivity: C5 is bonded to N (=N), which connects to NH, then N, then N, and back to C5. The drawing gives C5=N–NH–N=N–C5, so the ring is c1nn[nH]n1 in aromatic form. Written aromatically, c1nn[nH]n1 has C bonded to n, then n, then [nH], then n back to C. That gives C–N–N–NH–N–C, which places the NH adjacent to a ring N next to C. In the drawing, NH is bonded to N (the one double-bonded to C) and to the bottom N. So the order from C is N(=C), NH, N, N, back to C, which is c1n[nH]nn1.

SMILES: CCOC1=Nc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1n[nH]nn1

name: Camptothecin
text:
This structure is camptothecin, and I read it as follows.

- **Lactone ring (left):** a quaternary carbon bears an ethyl group and an OH, drawn on a wedge. It is bonded to a C(=O)–O–CH2 unit, and the ring closes through a C=C into the pyridone ring.
- **Pyridone ring:** it contains a C=O and the ring nitrogen, which is bonded to a CH2 and to an sp2 carbon.
- **Five-membered ring:** it contains the CH2 and links the pyridone ring to the quinoline unit.
- **Quinoline unit:** a benzene ring fused to a pyridine ring that contains the second nitrogen, written as N=C.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the carbon with the wedged OH. I wrote the neighbours in the order ethyl, ring closure, OH, C(=O), and the wedge geometry gives `@@`.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCC2=C1C=C1N(C2=O)CC2=CC3=CC=CC=C3N=C12

name: Candesartan Cilexetil
text:
This is candesartan cilexetil. The tetrazole is drawn as a 1H/2H tautomer: the ring reads N=N–NH–N=C, with the NH between the two N atoms next to the carbon-bearing N. The top N=N double bond is drawn explicitly, and the carbon is double-bonded to the lower N.

Reading the ring from the drawing: C(attached to the aryl) is bonded to the top-left N, which is double-bonded to the top-right N. That N connects to NH, then to the lower N, which is double-bonded back to C. In SMILES this is c1(nn[nH]n1), written explicitly as C1=NNN=N1 with the NH in position 3. Checking the order: C1(=N–NH–N=N1) would put the N=N double bond in the wrong place. The drawing gives C–N=N–NH–N=C, so the ring is C1(=NN=NN1)... that fails because the N bonded to C would have two double bonds. Written correctly, the ring is a five-membered ring of C, N(top-left), N(top-right), NH, N(lower).

Bonds:
- C–Ntl (single)
- Ntl=Ntr (double)
- Ntr–NH (single)
- NH–Nlow (single)
- Nlow=C (double)

Aromatic form: c1(nn[nH]n1) would be an alternative, but I'll use the explicit Kekulé form: C1(=NNN=N1) is wrong, so I write C1(N=NNN=1)... The cleaner version is c1nn[nH]n1, which treats the ring as aromatic.

Full molecule:
- Benzimidazole: N1 carries the benzyl group, C2 carries the OEt, N3 is the pyridine-type N, and C7 carries the ester.
- Ester: C(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)OC1CCCCC1.

SMILES: CCOc1nc2cccc(C(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)OC3CCCCC3)c2n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

SMILES: CCOc1nc2cccc(C(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)OC3CCCCC3)c2n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

name: Canagliflozin
text:
The molecule is canagliflozin, a C-aryl glucoside, and I read it from the drawing in three parts.

- **Fluorophenyl and thiophene:** a 4-fluorophenyl ring (F at the top left) is bonded to C2 of a thiophene. C5 of the thiophene carries a CH2 linker.
- **Central aryl ring:** the CH2 links to a benzene ring that also carries a methyl group on the adjacent carbon. The ring's third substituent is the sugar, para to the methyl carbon's neighbour as drawn.
- **Sugar ring:** a pyranose ring (five carbons and one ring oxygen) is attached through its anomeric carbon to the aryl ring. It carries three OH groups and one CH2OH.

I assigned the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes, taking each ring carbon in turn and checking the neighbour order in the SMILES:

- The anomeric carbon has a hashed bond to the aryl ring.
- The ring carbon bearing CH2OH has a hashed CH2OH bond.
