- The two OH groups next to the anomeric carbon and the ring CH2OH carbon are wedged.
- The OH on the middle carbon is hashed.

This gives the SMILES below. It matches the known canagliflozin stereochemistry as I recall it.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1Cc1ccc(s1)-c1ccc(F)cc1)[C@@H]1O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Cangrelor Tetrasodium
text:
This structure is cangrelor as its tetrasodium salt. I read it region by region.

- **Purine base:** an adenine-type core carries a 2-(methylthio)ethylamino group (CH3-S-CH2CH2-NH) at C6 and a 3,3,3-trifluoropropylthio group (S-CH2CH2CF3) at C2.
- **Sugar:** a ribofuranose is attached through N9. The drawing shows a wedge at the glycosidic bond, a wedge at the CH2 carbon, and hashes on both OH groups. This matches the D-ribose pattern of adenosine, so I used the adenosine stereo pattern.
- **Phosphate chain:** the 5'-O is linked to P(=O)(O⁻), then to a bridging O, then to P(=O)(O⁻), then to a CCl2 carbon, then to a terminal P(=O)(O⁻)O⁻. This gives a dichloromethylene bisphosphonate group.
- **Counterions:** four Na⁺ balance the four negative charges on the phosphate groups.

SMILES: CSCCNc1nc(SCCC(F)(F)F)nc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=O)([O-])OP(=O)([O-])C(Cl)(Cl)P(=O)([O-])[O-])[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O.[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+]

name: C,C'-Dimethyl N,N'-(tricyclo(8.2.2.24,7)hexadeca-4,6,10,12,13,15-hexaene-5,11-diylbis(1H-benzimidazole-6,2-diyl((2S,3aS,7aS)-octahydro-1H-indole-2,1-diyl)((1S)-1-(1-methylethyl)-2-oxo-2,1-ethanediyl)))bis(carbamate)
text:
I read the molecule as a [2.2]paracyclophane core carrying two identical arms, one on each benzene ring.

**Core.** The two benzene rings are joined by two CH2–CH2 bridges, one at the top and one at the bottom of the drawing. Each ring also carries a benzimidazole substituent next to one of its bridgehead carbons.

**Each arm.**
- The benzimidazole is attached through its 6-position, with N1 as the NH.
- Its C2 is bonded to C2 of an octahydroindole (a cis-fused cyclohexane–pyrrolidine, both ring-fusion hydrogens drawn as wedges or both as hashes).
- The octahydroindole nitrogen is acylated by an L-valine unit whose amine is capped as a methyl carbamate (NHC(=O)OMe).

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes, and both arms come out with the same configuration:
- The octahydroindole C2 is S.
- The two ring-fusion carbons carry cis hydrogens.
- The valine α-carbon is S, as in L-valine.

That is why the same arm SMILES is used twice.

**SMILES check.** I assembled the string as `core(ArL)(ArR)`, using different ring-closure digits for the core and the arms so they do not clash. Atom counts and ring closures agree with the drawing.

SMILES: c1c(c4cc5[nH]c([C@@H]6C[C@@H]7CCCC[C@@H]7N6C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)C)nc5cc4)c2ccc1CCc3c(c4cc5[nH]c([C@@H]6C[C@@H]7CCCC[C@@H]7N6C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)C)nc5cc4)cc(CC2)cc3

name: Canfosfamide
text:
I read the molecule as a glutathione-like tripeptide, γ-Glu–Cys–phenylglycine, in which the cysteine sulfur is oxidised to a sulfone. The sulfone carries a 2-hydroxyethyl ester of a bis(2-chloroethyl)phosphorodiamidate (a phosphoramide mustard).

**Regions read from the drawing**
- **Mustard end:** a P=O phosphorus bears two N(CH2CH2Cl)2 groups and one O–CH2CH2–SO2 link.
- **Cysteine unit:** the sulfone sulfur is bonded to a CH2 on the cysteine α-carbon. That carbon carries an NH-acyl group and a C(=O)N amide.
- **γ-Glu unit:** the cysteine NH is acylated by C(=O)CH2CH2CH(NH2)COOH.
- **Phenylglycine unit:** the cysteine C(=O) is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to CH(Ph)COOH.

**Stereochemistry (three wedged centres)**
- **Glu α-carbon:** NH2 is on a wedge. This gives `CC[C@H](N)C(=O)O` when written from the chain side, which is the L configuration.
- **Cys α-carbon:** the CH2 is on a wedge. This gives `C[C@H](NC(=O)...)C(=O)N`.
- **Phenylglycine α-carbon:** the NH is on a wedge. This gives `N[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)O`.

I checked each centre by viewing it with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer and reading the order of the other three substituents.

SMILES: O=P(N(CCCl)CCCl)(N(CCCl)CCCl)OCCS(=O)(=O)C[C@H](NC(=O)CC[C@H](N)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: Canrenoate Potassium
text:
I read the drawing as potassium canrenoate, the open-ring carboxylate salt of canrenone. I did not derive the stereo descriptors atom by atom from the wedges. I took the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the known canrenoate structure, and the drawing is consistent with it:

- **Ring A:** a 3-keto group (C=O at the right) conjugated with a C4=C5 double bond.
- **Ring B:** a C6=C7 double bond, so the A/B system is a 4,6-dien-3-one.
- **Methyl groups:** bold wedges at C10 and C13 (the β-methyls).
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** a wedged H at C8 and hashed H atoms at C9 and C14, which matches the natural steroid configuration.
- **C17:** a bold-wedged OH and a –CH2CH2–COO⁻ chain.
- **Counter-ion:** K⁺.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1C=C[C@@H]3[C@@H]2CC[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(CCC(=O)[O-])O)C.[K+]

name: Cannabidiol
text:
This drawing is cannabidiol (CBD): a 5-pentylresorcinol ring joined to a 4-isopropenyl-1-methylcyclohexene ring.

**Regions read from the image**
- **Chain:** a plain pentyl chain (five carbons) is attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Aromatic ring:** six carbons, with an OH on each side of the carbon that carries the cyclohexene ring (a resorcinol pattern).
- **Cyclohexene ring:** one ring C=C bearing a methyl group, and two adjacent stereocentres.
- **Isopropenyl group:** a C(CH3)=CH2 group attached to the second stereocentre.

**Stereochemistry**
- The hashed bond from the aryl carbon to the first ring stereocentre puts the aryl group behind the plane. I assumed the narrow end of the hash sits at the stereocentre, as is usual. This gives `[C@@H]` for that centre.
- The wedge from the second ring stereocentre to the isopropenyl carbon puts that group toward the viewer. This gives `[C@H]` for that centre.

SMILES: CCCCCc1cc(O)c([C@@H]2C=C(C)CC[C@H]2C(C)=C)c(O)c1

name: Canrenone
text:
The drawing is a steroid skeleton with a 3-keto-4,6-diene in the A/B rings (the C=O on the right, two ring C=C bonds along the bottom). Two methyl groups sit at the ring junctions (C10 and C13), and a spiro γ-lactone (O–C(=O)–CH2–CH2) is attached at C17. This is canrenone.

The structure is drawn flipped vertically relative to the usual steroid orientation. Inverting the wedges accordingly (10-methyl and 13-methyl β, 9-H α, 8-H β, 14-H α) gives the natural steroid configuration. I took the stereo descriptors from the known canrenone SMILES rather than deriving each centre independently.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1C=C[C@@H]3[C@@H]2CC[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]45CCC(=O)O5)C

name: Capecitabine
text:
The structure is capecitabine, read region by region:

- **Side chain:** a straight five-carbon pentyl chain is attached to an O, which is attached to a C=O. This is a pentyl carbamate, written CCCCCOC(=O)N.
- **Base:** the carbamate NH is on a 5-fluoropyrimidin-2-one ring. Going round the ring: C4 (bearing NH) is double-bonded to N3, then C2(=O), then N1, then C6H=C5(F).
- **Sugar:** N1 is bonded to C1' of a five-membered ring containing one O. C1' has a wedge to N, C2' has a hashed OH, C3' has a hashed OH, and C4' has a wedged CH3. This is a 5'-deoxy-ribofuranose.
- **Stereochemistry:** wedge on N, hashes on both OH groups, and wedge on the methyl match the natural D-ribo arrangement, so I used the known capecitabine stereo-SMILES rather than deriving each @/@@ from the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCCOC(=O)NC1=NC(=O)N(C=C1F)[C@@H]2O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O

name: Capmatinib
text:
This is the structure of capmatinib-like compound (imidazo[1,2-b][1,2,4]triazine core with a quinolin-6-ylmethyl group), and I read it region by region from the drawing.

**Left side.** A methyl group is attached to an NH, which is attached to a C(=O). That carbonyl carbon is bonded to a benzene ring. The ring carbon next to the amide-bearing carbon carries F (ortho to the amide). The ring carbon para to the amide carries the bicyclic heteroaryl group.

**Central bicycle.** I read the atoms as follows:
- C2 is the carbon attached to the benzene ring.
- N1 is bonded to C2 and to the bridgehead N.
- The bridgehead N is also bonded to C(a), which carries the CH2 substituent.
- C(a)=CH–N=C(bridge) completes the five-membered ring. The ring atoms are bridgehead N, C(a), CH, N, and the bridging carbon.
- The bridging carbon is bonded to the N of the six-membered ring.
- The six-membered ring runs: bridgehead N, N, C2, CH, N, bridging carbon.

**Right side.** The CH2 links C(a) to quinoline position 6. In the drawing the CH2 attaches to a benzo-ring carbon that is one carbon removed from the ring-fusion carbon, which gives the 6-position.

**SMILES.** Writing the connectivity out:
CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)-c1cnc2ncc(Cc3ccc4ncccc4c3)n2n1

Check of the bicycle in this SMILES: c1 (C2) – c (CH) – n – c2 (bridge) – n – c – c(CH2Ar) – n2 (bridgehead) – n1. The ring-2 closure runs from the bridging carbon to the bridgehead N, and ring 1 closes from the bridgehead N's neighbour N back to C2. This gives five-membered ring atoms c2, n, c, c, n2, and six-membered ring atoms c1, c, n, c2, n2, n1, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)-c1cnc2ncc(Cc3ccc4ncccc4c3)n2n1

name: Capivasertib
text:
I read the structure as follows:

- **Left ring system:** a 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine, with the pyrimidine C4 bonded to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** C4 carries both an NH2 and a C(=O)NH amide group.
- **Amide nitrogen:** attached to a stereocentre bearing a 4-chlorophenyl group and a CH2CH2OH chain.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 bond at that stereocentre is hashed (pointing away from the viewer). The priorities are N > aryl > CH2CH2OH > H. Viewed from the front, N → aryl → CH2 runs clockwise, but the implicit H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is counterclockwise. That makes the centre S, which is written `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order below (N, H, CCO, aryl). This is consistent with the drug capivasertib.

The piperidine C4 has two identical ring branches, so it is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: NC1(CCN(CC1)c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCO)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Caprolactam
text:
The drawing shows a seven-membered ring. Its vertices are:

1. NH
2. a carbonyl carbon bearing a double-bonded O
3. a CH2 at the bottom right (around 790, 1115)
4. a CH2 at the bottom (around 393, 1207)
5. a CH2 at the left (around 75, 952)
6. a CH2 at the left (around 75, 547)
7. a CH2 at the top (around 393, 293), which connects back to NH

That makes 7 ring atoms: N, C(=O), and five CH2 groups. This is caprolactam (azepan-2-one).

SMILES: O=C1CCCCCN1

name: Capsaicin
text:
The drawing is capsaicin, read as follows:

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group (a CH carbon with two methyls) attached to a C=C double bond.
- **Chain:** after the double bond come four CH2 carbons, then the amide C(=O). That makes an 8-methylnon-6-enamide chain.
- **Double bond geometry:** the chain is drawn as a regular zigzag across the C=C, so the double bond is trans (E).
- **Amide:** the carbonyl is bonded to N–H, which is bonded to a CH2.
- **Ring:** the CH2 is attached to a benzene ring. The OH is para to that CH2, and the OCH3 sits on the adjacent carbon, meta to the CH2.

SMILES: CC(C)/C=C/CCCCC(=O)NCc1ccc(O)c(OC)c1

name: Carbachol
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary ammonium cation with a chloride counterion. This is carbachol chloride.

- The nitrogen carries a positive charge and has three methyl groups plus one CH2CH2 chain.
- The chain continues through an oxygen to a carbonyl carbon, which has a C=O and an NH2 (a carbamate).
- Cl⁻ is drawn separately as the counterion.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CCOC(N)=O.[Cl-]

name: Cantharidin
text:
Reading the drawing:

- **Anhydride ring:** a five-membered ring O–C(=O)–C–C–C(=O), with both carbonyl oxygens drawn as double bonds.
- **Quaternary carbons:** the two ring-fusion carbons each carry a wedged methyl group.
- **Bicyclic core:** these two carbons are joined to two bridgehead CH carbons. The bridgeheads are linked by an oxygen bridge and by a CH2–CH2 bridge, which gives a 7-oxabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane. Each bridgehead H is hashed.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned @/@@ at the four stereocentres from the wedge and hash geometry, and I used the mirror symmetry of the drawing to settle the left bridgehead, where the direct calculation was marginal.

SMILES: O=C1OC(=O)[C@]2(C)[C@@]1(C)[C@H]3CC[C@@H]2O3

name: Carbamazepine
text:
The drawing shows carbamazepine, which is a dibenzazepine core carrying an N-carboxamide group.

- **Core:** A central seven-membered ring contains one N, two fused benzene rings, and a CH=CH bridge.
- **Substituent:** The ring nitrogen bears a C(=O)NH2 group, drawn with O at the upper left and NH2 at the upper right.

The SMILES below traces this: the amide group on N, one benzene ring, the CH=CH bridge, then the second benzene ring closing back to N.

SMILES: NC(=O)N1c2ccccc2C=Cc2ccccc21

name: Carbazochrome
text:
The drawing shows an indoline core: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring.

**Five-membered ring.** N-methyl nitrogen, a CH2, and a CH bearing OH, then the two fused aromatic carbons. The N-methyl nitrogen attaches to one fused carbon. The CH(OH) attaches to the other fused carbon.

**Benzene ring.** Going around from the fused carbon bonded to N (call it C7a):
- C7a connects to an aromatic CH, then to a carbon bearing OH.
- Next is a carbon bearing the N=N–C(=O)NH2 group, then an aromatic CH.
- The ring closes at the other fused carbon, C3a, which is bonded to CH(OH).

**SMILES.** Starting at the methyl group: CN1CC(O)c2cc(N=NC(N)=O)c(O)cc21

**Check.**
- N1 carries the methyl, bonds to CH2, then to CH(OH).
- CH(OH) bonds to c2, which is C3a.
- Then the aromatic CH, then the carbon bearing the azo group, then the carbon bearing OH, then an aromatic CH.
- The last atom, c21, is C7a. It closes the benzene ring to C3a and closes the five-membered ring to N1.

The ring order matches the drawing. C7a is bonded to a CH, which is bonded to the C–OH carbon. That carbon is bonded to the C–N=N carbon, then to a CH, then to C3a.

The stereocentre at CH(OH) is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is specified.

SMILES: CN1CC(O)c2cc(N=NC(N)=O)c(O)cc21

name: Captopril
text:
The drawing is captopril: a proline ring with the nitrogen acylated by a 3-mercapto-2-methylpropanoyl group, plus a free carboxylic acid on the ring carbon next to the nitrogen.

**Structure read from the image:**
- The five-membered ring has one N and four carbons.
- The ring N carries a C(=O) group. That carbonyl carbon is attached to a CH bearing a methyl and a CH2–SH.
- The ring carbon adjacent to N carries a COOH group.

**Stereochemistry:** there are two drawn stereocentres.
- The methyl-bearing CH has a wedge to the methyl. Working through the geometry gives `C[C@H](CS)C(=O)N…`.
- The ring CH has a hashed bond to the COOH. Working through the geometry gives `N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O`.

This is the (S,S) form of captopril.

SMILES: C[C@H](CS)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Carbazole
text:
The drawing shows carbazole: two benzene rings fused to a central five-membered ring that contains an NH.

**Atoms:**
- The N–H sits at the top of the five-membered ring.
- The N bonds to two ring carbons, one at (527, 660) on the left and one at (972, 660) on the right.
- Those two carbons are joined to the bottom carbons at (613, 921) and (887, 921) respectively, and the two bottom carbons are bonded to each other. This closes the five-membered ring: N, C, C, C, C.

**Left ring:** (527, 660), (260, 603), (75, 807), (160, 1069), (429, 1127), (613, 921).

**Double bonds in the left ring:**
- 527–260 is double (inner line drawn).
- 75–160 is double.
- 429–613 is double.

**Right ring:** (972, 660), (1241, 603), (1425, 807), (1340, 1069), (1071, 1127), (887, 921).

**Double bonds in the right ring:**
- 972–1241 is double.
- 1425–1340 is double.
- 1071–887 is double.

Both rings have three double bonds and are aromatic, so the SMILES can be written in aromatic form.

SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)[nH]c1ccccc12

name: Carbidopa
Calicheamicin
text:
This is my reading of the drawing, built region by region. It looks like a calicheamicin-type enediyne glycoside carrying an iodinated aryl thioester, an N–O glycosidic link and a methyl trisulfide. I derived each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the image, and I did not run the SMILES through a parser.

**Fragments, from top left:**
- **Amino sugar:** a tetrahydropyran with NHEt (wedge) and OMe (hash), attached through an anomeric O (wedge) to the next sugar.
- **Central sugar:** carries a 3-OH (hash), a 4-NH (wedge) and a 5-methyl (hash). The 4-NH is bonded to O, which links to the third sugar. Its anomeric O (hash) is bonded to the aglycone.
- **Third sugar:** a 2-deoxy sugar linked through O to the NH. It has a 3-OH (wedge), a 4-S (wedge) and a 5-methyl (hash).
- **Aryl thioester:** S–C(=O) on a benzene ring bearing, in order around the ring, two OMe groups, an O-sugar, an iodine and a methyl.
- **Fourth sugar:** a 6-deoxy sugar with two OH groups and one OMe, attached to the aryl oxygen.
- **Aglycone:**
  - a cyclohexene ring with an NHCO2Me group, a ketone and a tertiary OH (wedge);
  - a 10-membered ring containing C≡C–C=C–C≡C;
  - a quaternary carbon (no stereo drawn) bearing the S–S–S–CH3 chain;
  - a CH2–CH= unit that closes the six-membered ring.

SMILES: CCN[C@H]1CO[C@H](C[C@@H]1OC)O[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)[C@H](NO[C@H]3C[C@H](O)[C@H](SC(=O)c4c(OC)c(OC)c(O[C@H]5[C@H](O)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O5)c(I)c4C)[C@@H](C)O3)[C@@H](C)O[C@H]2O[C@@H]6C7=C(NC(=O)OC)C(=O)C[C@@](O)8C#CC=CC#CC6(SSSC)CC=C78

name: Carbenicillin
text:
The image shows a penicillin-type bicyclic core with a carbenicillin side chain, which I read as follows.

- **Core:** a β-lactam (the four-membered ring with the C=O and N) fused to a thiazolidine ring (the five-membered ring with S). The thiazolidine carbon next to S carries two methyl groups, and the carbon next to N carries a COOH.
- **Side chain:** the amide NH is attached to a C(=O) group, which leads to a CH bearing both a phenyl ring and a COOH. That CH is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Stereocentres:** the three ring stereocentres have drawn wedges or hashes. I checked each against the drawing.
  - The S–CH carbon has an H wedge and is `@@` in the SMILES.
  - The carbon bearing the hashed amide N is `@`.
  - The carbon bearing the wedged COOH is `@`.

  These match the natural penicillin configuration.

SMILES: CC1(C)S[C@@H]2[C@H](NC(=O)C(C(O)=O)c3ccccc3)C(=O)N2[C@H]1C(O)=O

name: Carbon Dioxide
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon labelled C with an O on each side. Each C–O connection is a double bond, so the molecule is carbon dioxide, O=C=O.

SMILES: O=C=O

name: Carbutamide
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is NH2. The other is a sulfonyl group (S with two =O) bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) that carries a second NH. That NH is attached to a straight n-butyl chain of four carbons.

Chain count: from N, the bonds go to C (1080,690), then C (1205,730), then C (1300,643), then C (1423,683). That is four carbons, so the chain is butyl.

This is carbutamide.

SMILES: CCCCNC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(N)cc1

name: Carbocysteine
text:
Reading the drawing gives S-carboxymethyl-cysteine (carbocisteine) with one defined stereocentre.

- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH.
- **Stereocentre:** the alpha carbon carries an NH2 on a hashed bond, so the NH2 points away from the viewer. Its implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **Chain:** the alpha carbon connects to a CH2, then to a thioether sulfur, then to another CH2.
- **Right end:** the second CH2 is bonded to a second carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH.

To assign the stereo tag, I viewed the centre from the H side (toward the viewer). From there the carboxyl, CH2 and N substituents run clockwise on the page. Written in the order carboxyl, H, N, CH2, that arrangement corresponds to @@. This matches the L-cysteine configuration.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H](N)CSCC(=O)O

name: Carfilzomib
text:
This drawing matches carfilzomib, a tetrapeptide epoxyketone, and I wrote the SMILES from that recognition and from my memory of the published SMILES. I did not independently re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the @/@@ marks rest on that recalled structure.

Reading the drawing from left to right:
- A 2-methyl epoxide (three-membered ring with O) carries a methyl on its quaternary carbon and is bonded to a ketone C=O.
- The ketone is attached to a leucine-type residue (isobutyl side chain) through its NH.
- Next comes a phenylalanine-type residue (benzyl side chain), then a second leucine-type residue (isobutyl).
- The next residue is homophenylalanine, with a CH2CH2-phenyl side chain.
- The chain ends in an acetamide, C(=O)CH2, attached to the nitrogen of a morpholine ring (N and O across a six-membered ring).

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@@H](C(=O)[C@@]1(CO1)C)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCc3ccccc3)NC(=O)CN4CCOCC4

name: Carbetocin
text:
I read this as a cyclic peptide analogue with a thioether ring and read it region by region.

**Tail (left):** Gly‑NH2 (`NCC(N)=O`), then Leu, then Pro. The Leu isobutyl group is `CC(C)C`.

**Ring (clockwise from the Cys carbonyl):**
- The Cys residue is attached to the Pro nitrogen through its carbonyl. Its side chain is CH2–S.
- The sulfur carries a three‑carbon chain, `SCCC`, ending in a C(=O) amide, so the ring contains S–CH2CH2CH2–C(=O).
- The next residue is Tyr(OMe), with a 4‑methoxybenzyl side chain.
- Then Ile, with a sec‑butyl side chain.
- Then Gln, with a CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
- Then Asn, with a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
- Asn closes back onto the Cys nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry:** The wedges and hashes at the Leu, Pro, Cys, Tyr and Ile α‑carbons, and at the Ile β‑carbon, are consistent with the natural L configuration. I checked the Leu and Tyr centres by working out the CIP chirality directly from the drawing. For the Gln and Asn α‑carbons I assumed L and did not check them against the wedges. I wrote the SMILES with the matching @/@@ tags.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H]2CSCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc3ccc(OC)cc3)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N2)C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Cariprazine
text:
The drawing reads as follows, region by region:

- **Left end:** a dimethylurea, CN(C)C(=O)N–, where the NH is attached to the cyclohexane.
- **Cyclohexane:** a six-membered ring substituted at positions 1 and 4. The NH sits on one carbon and the ethyl chain on the carbon opposite.
- **Linker:** a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) from the cyclohexane to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two nitrogens, one bearing the ethyl chain and the other bearing the aryl group.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring attached to the piperazine N at one carbon. The adjacent carbon carries a Cl, and the next carbon after that carries a second Cl, giving a 2,3-dichlorophenyl.

No wedges or hashes appear in the drawing, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=O)NC1CCC(CC1)CCN1CCN(CC1)c1cccc(Cl)c1Cl

name: Carboprost
text:
I read the structure as a 15-methyl prostaglandin F2α skeleton and assigned stereochemistry from the drawn wedges, hashes and double-bond geometry.

**Carboxylic acid chain:** COOH is followed by three CH2 groups, then a cis C5=C6 double bond and a CH2 (C7) leading to the ring.

**Cyclopentane ring:**
- C8 carries the chain, drawn with a wedge.
- C9 carries OH, drawn with a wedge.
- C10 is a CH2.
- C11 carries OH, drawn with a wedge.
- C12 carries the lower chain, drawn with a hash.

**Lower chain:** a trans C13=C14 double bond leads to C15, which bears a wedged methyl and an OH. C15 is followed by a pentyl group.

I worked out each @/@@ label by looking at the three-dimensional arrangement around each stereocentre in the drawing. I did not check the result against a reference SMILES.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@](C)(O)CCCCC

name: Carglumic Acid
text:
The image shows N‑carbamoylglutamic acid (carglumic acid), drawn as the (S)-enantiomer.

**Connectivity**
- A chain of two CH2 groups carries a terminal carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) on the left.
- The central stereocentre carries a second carboxylic acid on its upper right.
- It also carries an NH that is bonded to a urea-type carbonyl, C(=O)NH2.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only wedge runs from the stereocentre to the CH2 of the chain, so that CH2 points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away.
- The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H.
- Viewed from the front with H at the back, N (bottom) → COOH (upper right) → CH2 (left) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- Written as `OC(=O)CC[C@H](NC(N)=O)C(=O)O`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, N, COOH. I checked this against L-glutamic acid, `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O`, which is also S. Moving N to the CH2 position is one swap, which turns `@@` into `@`, so `@` is correct here.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC[C@H](NC(N)=O)C(=O)O

name: Carisoprodol
text:
This structure is carisoprodol. I read it region by region:

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group, CH(CH3)2, attached to an NH.
- **First carbamate:** the NH is bonded to a C(=O) that is bonded to an O, giving the N-isopropyl carbamate.
- **Central carbon:** the carbamate O connects through a CH2 to a quaternary carbon. This carbon carries a methyl group (the short bond drawn down), a propyl chain (the three carbons drawn up and to the right), and a second CH2.
- **Second carbamate:** that second CH2 is bonded to an O, then to C(=O)NH2, giving the primary carbamate.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the SMILES has no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)NC(=O)OCC(C)(CCC)COC(N)=O

name: Cardiolipin
text:
I read this as a cardiolipin: two glycerol units joined through a central 2-hydroxyglycerol bridge by two phosphates, with four identical linoleoyl chains.

- **Chains:** each acyl chain is C18 with cis double bonds at C9 and C12. I counted one carbonyl carbon, seven CH2 groups, the first cis C=C, a CH2, the second cis C=C, and five terminal carbons.
- **Phosphates:** the left phosphate carries one P=O and one O⁻. The right phosphate carries one P=O and one OH.
- **Bridge:** the central glycerol has a free secondary OH, drawn as CH(OH) between two CH2–O–P groups.
- **Stereocentres:** the only stereo shown is a wedge at each acylated glycerol CH.
  - Left centre: the wedge is on the CH2–O–P bond, and I read it as R.
  - Right centre: the wedge is on the CH2–O–acyl bond. By CIP priorities (O > CH2OP > CH2O-acyl) and the drawn geometry I get S, so I encoded S as drawn.
- **Unmarked centre:** the central CH(OH) has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)O[C@@H](COP(=O)([O-])OCC(O)COP(=O)(O)OC[C@@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCC)COC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCC)COC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCC

name: Carisbamate
text:
I read the drawing as a 2-chlorophenyl ring attached to a stereogenic carbon that bears an OH, a CH2–O–C(=O)NH2 carbamate chain and an implicit hydrogen. This is the carisbamate skeleton.

**Structure**
- The benzene ring has six carbons, with Cl on the carbon next to the one carrying the side chain (ortho).
- The side chain is CH(OH)–CH2–O–C(=O)–NH2, a carbamate ester.

**Stereochemistry**
- The OH on the stereocentre is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. The implicit H therefore points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are OH > CH2O > aryl carbon > H. The CH2O carbon (O,H,H) outranks the aryl carbon (C,C,C) because O beats C at the first point of difference.
- On the page, OH (top), then CH2 (lower right), then aryl (lower left) runs clockwise. The H faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, which gives counterclockwise, i.e. (S).
- In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` with neighbours in the order CH2, H, O, aryl also works out to (S), so it matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)OC[C@@H](O)c1ccccc1Cl

name: Carmustine
text:
The drawing shows a urea core, C(=O), with two nitrogens attached to the carbonyl carbon.

- The left nitrogen is NH and carries a CH2CH2Cl chain.
- The right nitrogen carries a second CH2CH2Cl chain and an N=O group, so it is an N-nitroso nitrogen.

This is carmustine (BCNU). I read it as ClCCNC(=O)N(CCCl)N=O.

The SMILES is valid, and its atoms match the drawing one for one. There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry to encode, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: O=NN(CCCl)C(=O)NCCCl

name: Carprofen
text:
This is carprofen: a carbazole bearing a chlorine and a CH(CH3)COOH group.

**Ring system.** The left ring carries Cl, the central ring contains the NH, and the right ring carries the propanoic acid substituent. The carbazole is numbered with N at position 9.

**Atom coordinates from the drawing.**
- Left ring: C-Cl at (227,632), then (378,593), then the fusion carbon (487,705), then the fusion carbon next to N at (446,856), then (294,895), then (185,783).
- Central ring: (487,705) is bonded to (645,698), which is bonded to (700,845), which is bonded to N, which is bonded to (446,856).
- Right ring: (645,698), (745,577), (899,603), (953,750) bearing the side chain, (854,871), and (700,845).

**SMILES.** Writing from the Cl-bearing carbon: Clc1ccc2[nH]c3cc(C(C)C(=O)O)ccc3c2c1

Checking the connectivity:
- c1 is C-Cl.
- The next two aromatic carbons are (185,783) and (294,895).
- c2 is (446,856), bonded to [nH].
- c3 is (700,845), followed by cc(...), which are (854,871) and (953,750), the latter bearing the side chain.
- The following two carbons ccc3 are (899,603) and (745,577), then the fusion carbon (645,698), which closes ring 3 with (700,845).
- c2 is (487,705), which closes ring 2 with (446,856).
- c1 is (378,593), which closes ring 1 with C-Cl.

The side chain is CH(CH3)C(=O)OH, and the stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: Clc1ccc2[nH]c3cc(C(C)C(=O)O)ccc3c2c1

name: (-)-Carnitine
text:
The structure is carnitine (3-hydroxy-4-trimethylammoniobutanoate), drawn as a zwitterion.

- **Left end:** a quaternary N⁺ carries three methyl groups and a CH₂.
- **Chain:** the CH₂ is followed by a CH bearing OH on a solid wedge, then another CH₂, then a carboxylate C(=O)O⁻.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the CH(OH), and the wedge puts the OH toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are OH > CH₂N⁺ > CH₂COO⁻ > H. Viewed from the front, OH (bottom) → CH₂N⁺ (upper left) → CH₂COO⁻ (upper right) runs clockwise with H at the back, so the centre is R (L-carnitine).
- **SMILES chirality:** for `C[N+](C)(C)C[C@H](O)CC([O-])=O`, the `@` tag corresponds to R, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)C[C@H](O)CC([O-])=O

name: Capreomycin
text:
I read the image as two separate capreomycin-type cyclic peptides, so the SMILES has two fragments joined by a dot. I assigned the stereochemistry by hand from the wedges and hashes. One uncertainty: for the bottom molecule's ring-bearing α-carbon, I assumed the wedge's narrow end sits at the stereocentre.

**Top molecule (Ser-type ring):**
- The macrocycle runs through a ureido-dehydroalanine, a residue with a CH₂NH side chain, a serine, a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid and a cyclic guanidine residue.
- The side chain on the CH₂NH is a β-lysine unit: C(=O)CH₂CH(NH₂)CH₂CH₂CH₂NH₂.
- The cyclic guanidine is a 2-amino-tetrahydropyrimidine ring.
- The ureido C=C is drawn with the ureido N trans to the ring NH, which I wrote as E.

**Bottom molecule:**
- It has the same skeleton, but the serine CH₂OH is replaced by CH₃, giving an alanine residue.
- The ureido C=C geometry is drawn the same way as in the top molecule.

I worked out the CIP configuration at each stereocentre from the drawing and converted it to @/@@ for the atom order in my SMILES. The result is S at every stereocentre except the cyclic guanidine ring carbon, which is R, in both molecules.

SMILES: NC(=O)N/C=C1/NC(=O)[C@@H](CNC(=O)C[C@@H](N)CCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](N)CNC(=O)[C@@H]([C@H]2CCN=C(N)N2)NC1=O.NC(=O)N/C=C1/NC(=O)[C@@H](CNC(=O)C[C@@H](N)CCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)NC(=O)[C@H](N)CNC(=O)[C@@H]([C@H]2CCN=C(N)N2)NC1=O

name: Carnosine
text:
This is L-carnosine (β-alanyl-L-histidine).

- **Imidazole ring:** The ring carbon bearing the CH2 is bonded to the ring NH and to a CH. That CH leads to the ring N, then to another CH, and back to the NH. This reads as `c1cnc[nH]1`.
- **Side chain and acid:** The CH2 links the ring to the α-carbon, which carries the COOH group.
- **Amide chain:** The α-carbon's NH is acylated by C(=O)CH2CH2NH2, the β-alanyl unit.
- **Stereochemistry:** The α-carbon has a wedge bond to the CH2. The priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. With H pointing away, the sequence N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S. This matches the L-histidine configuration, written as `N[C@@H](Cc1cnc[nH]1)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: NCCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1cnc[nH]1)C(=O)O

name: Carteolol
text:
The drawing shows a tert-butyl group on an NH, which connects through CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O to an aromatic ring. This is carteolol.

The ring is a 3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one, with the lactam NH and C=O on the right side of the structure.

Ring atoms, reading around the drawing:
- The benzene ring carbon bearing the O substituent is at the lower left.
- The adjacent fused carbon at the bottom connects to CH2, then CH2, then C(=O), then NH, then the other fused carbon.

Chain: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2NC(=O)CCc12

Check of the ring closure: c1 (bearing O), then c, c, c, then c2 (fused, bearing N), then N, C(=O), C, C, and c12 (fused, closing to both c1 and c2). This is consistent with the drawing.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the stereocentre carries no stereo label.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2NC(=O)CCc12

name: Carmegliptin
text:
I read the molecule as a 9,10-dimethoxy-benzo[a]quinolizidine core. A lactam is attached at C3 and a primary amine at C2. The lactam is a 4-(fluoromethyl)pyrrolidin-2-one joined through its nitrogen.

**Core ring system**
- The benzene ring carries two OMe groups on adjacent carbons.
- It is fused to a CH2–CH2–N bridge, so the nitrogen is a tertiary ring N.
- The ring-fusion CH (C11b) is drawn with an H wedge.
- The saturated six-membered ring runs C11b, CH2, CH(NH2), CH(N-lactam), CH2, N.

**Substituents**
- The NH2 is on a hashed bond.
- The lactam N is on a wedge bond.
- The lactam ring runs N, CH2, CH(CH2F), CH2, C(=O). The CH2F is on a wedge.

**Stereo assignment**
- Each of the four stereocentres was assigned from the wedge or hash directions and the 2D neighbour positions.
- I converted these to @/@@ according to the neighbour order in the SMILES string.

**Check**
- Ring-closure digits were reused correctly, and every atom and bond order matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cc2c(cc1OC)[C@@H]1C[C@H](N)[C@H](CN1CC2)N1C[C@@H](CF)CC1=O

name: Carvedilol
text:
This structure is carvedilol: a carbazole joined through an ether oxygen to a 2-hydroxypropyl chain, a secondary amine, an ethylene linker, and a 2-methoxyphenoxy group.

The drawing uses plain bonds only, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo marker.

Reading the pieces:
- **Carbazole:** the NH sits in the five-membered ring between two benzo rings. The lower benzene ring carries the ether oxygen at the carbon adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon, which is carbazole position 4.
- **Chain:** the ether O connects to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then NH, then CH2CH2, then O attached to the aryl ring.
- **Right ring:** the aryl ring has the O–CH2 substituent and, on the neighbouring carbon, an OCH3 (ortho).

Writing the SMILES for the carbazole: c1ccc2c(c1)c1c(OCC(O)CNCCOc3ccccc3OC)cccc1[nH]2

Atom check:
- The ring c1ccc2c(c1)... is the top benzene ring. Atom 2 is the carbon bonded to N, and c(c1) is the fusion carbon bonded to the other ring.
- That fusion carbon then connects to c1, which is the lower ring carbon C4a. This carbon is bonded to c(OCC...), the carbon bearing the ether oxygen, as in the drawing.
- The ring continues through ccc to c1[nH]2, the carbon attached to N, closing both rings.

SMILES: COc1ccccc1OCCNCC(O)COc1cccc2[nH]c3ccccc3c12

name: Cediranib
text:
This is a quinazoline bearing three substituents, plus an indole joined through an ether oxygen. I read it region by region.

**Indole part.** The 2-methylindole has an NH. C2 carries the methyl and C3 is CH. The fused benzene ring carries F at C4 and the ether O at C5.

**Linker.** The O at indole C5 joins quinazoline C4.

**Quinazoline part.** C4 is bonded to N3, then C2 (CH), then N1, then C8a. The benzo ring runs C8a, C8 (H), C7 (O-propyl chain), C6 (OMe), C5 (H), C4a.

**Side chain.** At C7 the chain is O–CH2CH2CH2–N(pyrrolidine).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Indole: Cc1cc2c(F)c(Oc3ncnc4cc(OCCCN5CCCC5)c(OC)cc34)ccc2[nH]1
- Check the indole: c1 (C2, methyl), then c (C3), c2 (C3a), c(F) (C4), c(O…) (C5), cc (C6, C7), c2 (C7a), [nH]1. The ring closures are consistent.
- Check the quinazoline: c3 (C4) n (N3) c (C2) n (N1) c4 (C8a) c (C8) c(OCCCN…) (C7) c(OC) (C6) c (C5) c34 (C4a). C4a closes to C4 (ring 3) and to C8a (ring 4), which is correct.

SMILES: Cc1cc2c(F)c(Oc3ncnc4cc(OCCCN5CCCC5)c(OC)cc34)ccc2[nH]1

name: Casopitant
text:
I read the molecule as a 4-(4-acetylpiperazin-1-yl)piperidine with an aryl group on C2 and a urea on the ring nitrogen.

- **Piperidine core:** the ring nitrogen carries a C(=O)N(CH3) urea. C2 bears a 4-fluoro-2-methylphenyl group on a hashed bond. C4 bears the piperazine nitrogen on a hashed bond.
- **Piperazine:** the other piperazine nitrogen is acetylated (CH3C(=O)–).
- **Urea side chain:** the urea nitrogen carries a methyl and a CH(CH3) group. That CH has a wedged methyl and a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** working through the CIP priorities from the wedges and hashes, C2 of the piperidine is R, C4 is S, and the side-chain CH is R.

SMILES: CC(=O)N1CCN(CC1)[C@H]2CCN([C@@H](c3ccc(F)cc3C)C2)C(=O)N(C)[C@H](C)c4cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c4

name: Carumonam
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below.

- **Oxime side chain:** a carboxymethyl group (HOOC–CH2–O–) is attached to the oxime nitrogen, which is double-bonded to a carbon (N=C).
- **Thiazole:** the oxime carbon carries a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring and an amide carbonyl, C(=O)–NH.
- **Oxime geometry:** from the drawn coordinates, the oxime oxygen lies on the opposite side of the C=N bond from the thiazole. I encoded this as `O/N=C(/c1...)`.
- **β-lactam ring:** a four-membered ring with a carbonyl carbon, a ring nitrogen bearing SO3H, and two CH carbons. The amide NH is on one CH (hashed bond) and a CH2–O–C(=O)NH2 carbamate is on the other (hashed bond).
- **Ring stereocentres:** working out the chirality from the hashed bonds and the implicit hydrogens gave `@@` for both CH carbons as written in the SMILES.

SMILES: OC(=O)CO/N=C(/c1csc(N)n1)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N(S(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H]1COC(N)=O

name: Catechin
text:
The structure is a flavan-3-ol: a catechin skeleton with a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl group on C2 and a 3-hydroxyl on the heterocyclic ring.

**Skeleton read from the drawing**
- The left benzene ring carries two adjacent OH groups (a catechol unit) and is attached at C2.
- The central ring is a chromane (dihydropyran): ring O, C2 bearing the aryl group, C3 bearing OH, a CH2 (C4), and two fused aromatic carbons.
- The right benzene ring is fused to the central ring and carries two OH groups, meta to each other, at C5 and C7.

**Stereochemistry**
- C2 has a wedge bond to the aryl ring. With H pointing back, the priorities O > C3 > aryl > H give a clockwise sequence, so C2 is R.
- C3 has a hashed bond to OH. With H pointing toward the viewer, the priorities OH > C2 > C4 > H appear clockwise, which reverses to S. So C3 is S.
- This is the (2R,3S) configuration, i.e. (+)-catechin.

**SMILES check**
In `O[C@H]1Cc2c(O)cc(O)cc2O[C@@H]1c1ccc(O)c(O)c1`, I worked out the chirality tags by permuting the neighbour order. The `@` on C3 gives S and the `@@` on C2 gives R, matching the drawing.

SMILES: O[C@H]1Cc2c(O)cc(O)cc2O[C@@H]1c1ccc(O)c(O)c1

name: Cefaclor
text:
I read the drawing as a cephalosporin (cefaclor-type) skeleton. It has a β-lactam fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring that carries Cl and a carboxylic acid. The 7-amino position bears a phenylglycyl amide side chain.

Stereochemistry comes from the three drawn stereo bonds:
- The side-chain carbon has a hashed NH2, so the NH2 points away from the viewer and the implicit H towards the viewer. This gives `N[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)...` in the written atom order.
- C7 of the β-lactam has a wedged N, giving `N[C@@H]1C(=O)...`.
- The ring-fusion carbon C6 has a hashed H, giving `S[C@H]12`.

Connectivity check: C7 is bonded to the amide N, the lactam C=O and C6, and C6 closes onto both C7 (ring 1) and the lactam N (ring 2). The sequence N–C(COOH)=C(Cl)–CH2–S–C6 completes the six-membered ring.

SMILES: N[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N2C(C(=O)O)=C(Cl)CS[C@H]12

name: Cefazolin
text:
The structure is cefazolin: a cephalosporin core with a 5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-ylthio-methyl group at C3 and a tetrazol-1-ylacetamido side chain at C7.

- **Left ring:** 2-thio-substituted 5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazole, with the S–N=C pattern as drawn.
- **Core:** a dihydrothiazine fused to a β-lactam, with the carboxylic acid on the ring carbon next to the ring nitrogen, and the lactam C=O next to C7.
- **Right ring:** a tetrazole attached through N1 to the CH2 of the acetamide, written `CN4C=NN=N4`.
- **Stereochemistry:** the two stereocentres are the ring-fusion carbon C6 (wedged H) and C7 (hashed NH).
  - At C6, the priorities are S > N > C7 > H. With H toward the viewer, S→N→C7 runs counterclockwise on the page, so the true sense is clockwise, giving R.
  - At C7, the priorities are N > C6 > C8 (carbonyl) > H. The same reasoning gives R.
  - This is the (6R,7R) configuration of natural cefazolin.

SMILES: CC1=NN=C(S1)SCC2=C(N3[C@@H]([C@@H](C3=O)NC(=O)CN4C=NN=N4)SC2)C(=O)O

name: Cefadroxil
text:
This is cefadroxil, a cephalosporin with a 3-methyl dihydrothiazine ring fused to a β-lactam, a carboxylic acid on the ring carbon next to the lactam nitrogen, and a 4-hydroxyphenylglycyl amide side chain.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Ring system:** the six-membered ring contains N, S, a CH2, and a C=C bearing a methyl group and the COOH. It is fused to the four-membered lactam, which carries the C=O.
- **Side chain:** the amide NH is attached through a wedge bond to the lactam carbon. The amide C=O leads to a CH carrying NH2 (hashed bond) and a para-hydroxyphenyl ring.
- **Stereocentres:** there are three, at the wedge-bonded lactam carbon, the ring-fusion carbon (hashed H), and the side-chain α-carbon (hashed NH2). I assigned @/@@ at each from the wedge and hash geometry.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)O)N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@H](N)c3ccc(O)cc3)[C@H]2SC1

name: Cefamandole
text:
The image shows cefamandole: a cephem core with a (1-methyltetrazol-5-yl)thiomethyl group at C3, a carboxylic acid at C4, and a mandelamide at C7.

**Connectivity**
- The tetrazole ring has an N-methyl on the nitrogen next to the carbon that bears the S–CH2 group.
- The CH2 is attached to the ring alkene carbon, which is double-bonded to the carbon carrying COOH. That carbon is bonded to the β-lactam N.
- The β-lactam has a C=O, a C7 bearing the amide NH, and a C6 bonded to both N and the ring S. The ring S is connected through a CH2 back to the alkene carbon.
- The amide N is acylated by a CH(OH)–phenyl group (mandeloyl).

**Stereochemistry** (read from the wedges and hashes)
- C6 has a bold wedge to H, which gives `[C@H]` in the order I wrote it.
- C7 has a hashed bond to the amide N, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- The mandelic carbon has a hashed OH, which gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: Cn1nnnc1SCC1=C(C(=O)O)N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@H](O)c3ccccc3)[C@H]2SC1

name: Cefiderocol
text:
I read the structure as a cephalosporin (cephem) core. Its substituents match cefiderocol.

- **Side chain on the 7-amino group:** a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl group on a C=N–O oxime, with the oxime oxygen attached to C(CH3)2–COOH.
- **Cephem core:** a β-lactam fused to a six-membered S-containing ring that carries a carboxylate (COO⁻). The 3-position CH2 is attached to a pyrrolidinium nitrogen (N⁺).
- **Group on the pyrrolidinium N:** an N-ethyl chain ending in an amide NH–C(=O) to a 2-chloro-3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows a wedge on the 7-position C–N bond and a hashed H on C6. Both centres work out as R by CIP priorities, which gives `[C@H]` at C7 and `[C@H]` at C6 in the SMILES below. The oxime C=N geometry is not specified in my SMILES (I did not assign E/Z).

SMILES: CC(C)(ON=C(C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(=C(N2C1=O)C(=O)[O-])C[N+]3(CCNC(=O)c4ccc(O)c(O)c4Cl)CCCC3)c5csc(N)n5)C(=O)O

name: Cefcapene pivoxil
text:
I read this as cefcapene pivoxil and wrote its SMILES from the drawing region by region.

- **Side chain:** an ethyl group on a C=C, with the other alkene carbon bearing a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring and an amide C(=O)NH.
- **Alkene geometry:** the ethyl group and the amide carbonyl sit on the same side of the double bond. The carbonyl carbon (O,O,N) outranks the thiazole carbon (N,C,C), so this is the Z isomer. In the SMILES it is written `CC/C=C(\C(=O)...)C1=CSC(N)=N1`.
- **Bicyclic core:** a cephem ring system with a β-lactam C=O, a ring S, and a ring C=C. The ring C=C carries a CH2OC(=O)NH2 (carbamoyloxymethyl) group and the ester carbon.
- **Ester:** the carboxyl is esterified as C(=O)OCH2OC(=O)C(CH3)3, a pivaloyloxymethyl group.
- **Stereocentres:** the amide N on C7 is drawn with a wedge and the H on C6 with a hash. Working out the neighbour order for each gives `N[C@H]1[C@H]2...` as written.

SMILES: CC/C=C(\C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(COC(N)=O)=C(N2C1=O)C(=O)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C)C1=CSC(N)=N1

name: Cefdinir
text:
This is cefdinir, a cephalosporin antibiotic. I read it region by region.

- **Bicyclic core:** a β-lactam (the ring with the C=O) is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring containing S. The dihydrothiazine ring carries a vinyl group and a carboxylic acid on its C=C.
- **Side chain:** an amide NH on the β-lactam carbon leads to C(=N–OH), which is attached to a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Ring-fusion carbon (bonded to S):** the hashed H gives the R configuration.
- **Carbon bearing the NH:** the wedged N gives the R configuration.
- **Oxime:** in the drawing the OH and the amide carbon lie on the same side of the C=N bond. That makes it the Z oxime, written `/C(=N\O)/`.

I checked both stereocentres against the CIP priorities. The SMILES encodes the same (6R,7R) configuration as the drawing.

SMILES: C=CC1=C(N2[C@@H]([C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)/C(=N\O)/C3=CSC(=N3)N)SC1)C(=O)O

name: Cefepime
text:
This is cefepime, a cephalosporin, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Left side:** an N-methylpyrrolidinium ring (N⁺ with a methyl and a CH₂ link) is attached to the C3 position of the cephem core.
- **Core:** the bicyclic β-lactam/dihydrothiazine system has a ring S, a C=C bearing a carboxylate (COO⁻), and a β-lactam C=O.
- **Side chain:** an amide NH links the core to a C(=N–OMe) group that carries a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Oxime geometry:** the methoxy O lies on the same side as the amide carbonyl carbon, which is the Z configuration. I wrote this as `CO/N=C(/thiazole)C(=O)…`.
- **Ring-fusion stereocentres:** I took the two stereocentres (wedge on the ring-fusion carbon, hash on the carbon bearing the NH) to be the natural cephalosporin 6R,7R configuration. I wrote `[C@H]1[C@@H]2` from recall of cefepime's known SMILES and did not re-derive the chirality tags from the drawing.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/c1csc(N)n1)C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@@H]2N(C1=O)C(=C(CS2)C[N+]1(C)CCCC1)C(=O)[O-]

name: Cefoperazone
text:
I read this as cefoperazone, a cephalosporin, so I matched the drawing against its known structure rather than deriving every stereocentre from scratch.

- **Left end:** a 4-ethyl-2,3-dioxopiperazine ring, joined through its other nitrogen to a urea carbonyl, which links by NH to the side-chain stereocentre.
- **Side chain:** that stereocentre (hashed bond to the NH) carries a 4-hydroxyphenyl ring and an amide carbonyl.
- **Core:** the amide NH (bold wedge) attaches to C7 of the β-lactam, which is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring containing S. The ring-fusion carbon has a hashed H.
- **Ring substituents:** the ring carbon next to N carries a COOH on the C=C. The other alkene carbon carries CH2–S–(1-methyltetrazol-5-yl).

I did not independently verify the stereo tags (the side-chain @ and the two ring-fusion @@). I took them from the standard cefoperazone structure, which has the 6R,7R core and D-configured side chain, and they should match the wedges and hashes drawn.

SMILES: CCN1CCN(C(=O)C1=O)C(=O)N[C@H](c1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]1[C@@H]2N(C1=O)C(C(=O)O)=C(CS2)CSc1nnnn1C

name: Caspofungin
text:
I read the structure as a cyclic lipohexapeptide of the echinocandin type, with a 10,12-dimethyltetradecanoyl side chain. I wrote the SMILES by following the ring and the side chain atom by atom, then assigned each @/@@ from the drawn wedges and hashes.

**Side chain.** It is a C(=O) followed by 8 CH2 groups, then CH(CH3), CH2, CH(CH3), CH2 and CH3. The two methyl-bearing carbons are drawn with one hashed and one wedged methyl.

**Ring, in order from the acylated carbon:**
1. An alpha carbon carrying the NH-acyl group, then CH2, then CH(OH), then CH(NH-CH2CH2-NH2), then the ring NH.
2. A 3-hydroxyproline (N-CH2-CH2-CH(OH)-CH alpha).
3. A 4-hydroxy-homoornithine unit, CH(CH(OH)CH2CH2NH2).
4. A dihydroxy-homotyrosine unit, CH(CH(OH)CH(OH)-C6H4-OH).
5. A 4-hydroxyproline (alpha-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-N).
6. A threonine unit, CH(CH(OH)CH3), which closes the ring back to the first alpha carbon through its NH and C=O.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)C[C@H](C)CCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](NCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)CCN2C(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)CCN)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)[C@@H](O)c3ccc(O)cc3)NC(=O)[C@@H]4C[C@@H](O)CN4C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC1=O

name: Cefmetazole
text:
I read the structure as a cephamycin-type bicyclic β-lactam (it matches cefmetazole), working through it region by region.

- **Tetrazole:** a 1-methyltetrazol-5-yl ring. Its carbon is bonded to S, which links through a CH2 to C3 of the dihydrothiazine ring.
- **Dihydrothiazine ring:** S–CH2–C(CH2S-tetrazole)=C(COOH)–N, fused to the β-lactam at the CH carbon (C6, carrying a wedged H) and at N.
- **β-Lactam:** the ring has C6, C7 and the C=O carbon, plus N. C7 carries OMe and an NH-acyl group.
- **Side chain:** the amide is NH–C(=O)–CH2–S–CH2–C≡N.

**Stereochemistry:** C6 has a wedged H, and C7 has a hashed bond to NH.

- At C7, the SMILES order is O, C8 (carbonyl), N, C6. With N pointing away, C8→O→C6 runs counterclockwise on the page, which gives `@`.
- At C6, the order is C7, H, N, S. With H toward the viewer, C7→N→S runs clockwise, which gives `@` for this neighbour order.

SMILES: CO[C@]1(NC(=O)CSCC#N)[C@H]2SCC(CSc3nnnn3C)=C(C(=O)O)N2C1=O

name: Cefixime
text:
This is a cefixime-type cephalosporin. I read it region by region.

- **Bicyclic core:** a β-lactam (N, C=O, and two CH carbons) is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring containing S, a CH2, and a C=C. That C=C bears a vinyl group on one carbon and a COOH on the carbon attached to N.
- **Side chain:** an NH–C(=O) amide is attached to the β-lactam CH carbon through a wedge bond. The amide carbonyl is joined to a C=N–O–CH2–COOH oxime ether, and that same carbon also carries a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Stereocentres:** the NH-bearing carbon has the wedge, and the S/N-bearing ring-fusion carbon has a hashed H. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@@H]` for the NH carbon and `[C@H]` for the ring-fusion carbon.
- **Oxime geometry:** the oxime O sits on the same side as the amide carbonyl, which is the Z (syn) isomer. In the SMILES this is written as `C(=O)/C(=N\O...)`.

SMILES: C=CC1=C(C(=O)O)N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)/C(=N\OCC(=O)O)c3csc(N)n3)[C@H]2SC1

name: Cefotaxime
text:
The structure is cefotaxime, a cephalosporin, and I wrote the SMILES from the drawing region by region.

- **Bicyclic core:** a β-lactam (C=O at the top) is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring containing S. The ring N carries a carboxylic acid on the adjacent alkene carbon.
- **C3 side chain:** the other alkene carbon bears CH2–O–C(=O)CH3, an acetoxymethyl group.
- **C7 side chain:** an NH–C(=O) amide leads to a C(=N–OCH3) carbon, which is attached to a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.
- **Ring stereocentres:** the wedge on the C7 amide N and the hashed H on C6 fix the two ring stereocentres. I took them to be the natural (6R,7R) cephalosporin configuration and used the standard cefotaxime SMILES for that, rather than assigning each @/@@ independently from the picture.
- **Oxime geometry:** the OMe oxygen lies on the same side of the C=N bond as the amide carbonyl carbon. That carbon has higher CIP priority than the thiazole carbon, so the oxime is Z, and the SMILES encodes this with `/C(=N\OC)/`.

SMILES: CC(=O)OCC1=C(N2[C@@H]([C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)/C(=N\OC)/C3=CSC(=N3)N)SC1)C(=O)O

name: Cefilavancin
text:
I did not read every stereocentre off the image independently. For the vancomycin core I relied on my recollection of vancomycin's isomeric SMILES, so those centres are unchecked against the drawing.

The molecule is a vancomycin–cephalosporin conjugate with three parts:

- **Vancomycin aglycone and disaccharide.** This is the glycopeptide core with its vancosamine–glucose disaccharide, the N-methylleucine at the N-terminus, and the Asn side chain.
- **Linker.** The C-terminal carboxylic acid is converted to an amide, –C(=O)NH–CH2CH2CH2–O–N=, which carries the oxime.
- **Cephalosporin.** The oxime carbon bears a 2-amino-5-chlorothiazol-4-yl group and a C(=O)NH group on C7 of the cephem. The cephem has a pyridinium-methyl group at C3 and a carboxylate at C4.

Stereochemistry that I worked out from the drawing:

- **Oxime geometry.** From the bond directions, the O–N oxygen sits on the same side as the C(=O)N group and opposite the thiazole. I wrote this as `O/N=C(/thiazole)`, which places the oxygen and thiazole trans.
- **Cephem centres.** I mapped the C6 and C7 configurations from the cefotaxime SMILES onto my atom ordering.

I checked ring-closure labels and valences by hand, but I did not run the SMILES through a parser.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H]([C@@](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@H]2[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O[C@H]2OC3=C4C=C5C=C3OC6=C(C=C(C=C6)[C@H]([C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@H]5C(=O)N[C@@H]7C8=CC(=C(C=C8)O)C9=C(C=C(C=C9O)O)[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C1=CC(=C(O4)C=C1)Cl)O)NC7=O)C(=O)NCCCO/N=C(/c%10nc(N)sc%10Cl)C(=O)N[C@@H]%11C(=O)N%12C(C(=O)[O-])=C(C[n+]%13ccccc%13)CS[C@H]%11%12)CC(=O)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)NC)O)Cl)CO)O)O)(C)N)O

name: Cefotetan
text:
This looks like cefotetan, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Left side:** a 1-methyltetrazol-5-yl group, joined through S–CH2 to the dihydrothiazine ring of the cephem core. The ring carbon bearing this CH2S group is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the COOH.
- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to the six-membered S-containing ring. The carbon next to the lactam C=O carries OMe and the NH, and the NH bond is hashed.
- **Ring-fusion carbon:** it carries a wedged H.
- **Right side:** the NH is acylated by a 1,3-dithietane-2-carbonyl group. The dithietane is 4-ylidene, double-bonded to a carbon bearing COOH and CONH2.

For the two stereocentres, I assigned the C7 (OMe/NH) and C6 (H) configurations from the hash and wedge geometry. The dithietane CH and the ylidene double bond are drawn without stereo marks, so I left them unspecified.

SMILES: CO[C@@]1(NC(=O)C2SC(=C(C(N)=O)C(=O)O)S2)C(=O)N2C(C(=O)O)=C(CSc3nnnn3C)CS[C@H]12

name: Cefoxitin
text:
I read this as cefoxitin: a cephem core (β-lactam fused to a dihydrothiazine) carrying a methoxy group and a thiophene-acetamido group on C7, a carbamoyloxymethyl group on C3, and a carboxylic acid on C4.

Substituents and ring features, region by region:
- **Left:** a thiophene ring attached at its 2-position to a CH2, which connects to a C(=O)NH amide.
- **C7 (β-lactam carbon):** bears OMe, the NH (drawn with a wedge), the C6 carbon, and the lactam C=O.
- **C6:** bears H (drawn hashed), S, N and C7.
- **Dihydrothiazine ring:** S–CH2–C(=C)–, with a C=C to the carbon bearing COOH, and N closing the ring.
- **Right:** CH2–O–C(=O)–NH2 on C3, and the COOH on C4.

I assigned the stereo marks from the wedge and hash geometry. At C7, the wedged N points toward the viewer, and O, C8 (lactam carbonyl), C6 run counterclockwise, which gives `@`. At C6, the hashed H points away from the viewer, which gives `@` for the written neighbor order.

SMILES: CO[C@]1(NC(=O)Cc2cccs2)[C@H]2SCC(COC(N)=O)=C(N2C1=O)C(O)=O

name: Cefpodoxime Proxetil
text:
I read this as cefpodoxime proxetil, a cephalosporin prodrug, and worked through the drawing region by region.

- **Left side:** an isopropyl carbonate, (CH3)2CH–O–C(=O)–O–, attached to a CH(CH3) carbon. That carbon is bonded to the ester oxygen of the carboxylate (the "proxetil" group).
- **Bicyclic core:** a cephem. A dihydrothiazine ring (S, CH2, C(CH2OCH3)=C, N, and the S-bearing CH) is fused to a β-lactam ring (N, C=O, CH–NH, and the S-bearing CH). The carboxylate ester sits on the ring alkene carbon next to N, and the methoxymethyl group is on the other alkene carbon.
- **Side chain:** an NH–C(=O)–C(=N–OCH3) amide whose imino carbon carries a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring.

**Stereochemistry:**
- At the S-bearing CH, the H is on a wedge. Checking the neighbour order S, H, N, C7 gives @@.
- At the CH–NH carbon, the NH bond is hashed, so the H points toward the viewer. Checking the neighbour order C6, H, N, C8 gives @.
- In the oxime, the amide carbon and the OMe are on the same side of the C=N bond, which is the Z geometry. It is written as `/C(=N\OC)`.

The SMILES below was checked atom for atom against the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)C1=C(COC)CS[C@@H]2[C@H](NC(=O)/C(=N\OC)c3csc(N)n3)C(=O)N12

name: Cefozopran
text:
I read this as a cephalosporin: a 7-acylamino cephem core with a 2-(5-amino-1,2,4-thiadiazol-3-yl)-2-(methoxyimino)acetamide side chain. It carries a carboxylate at C4 and an imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazinium group on the C3 methylene. This matches cefozopran, but I built the SMILES from the drawing.

**Side chain.** The 5-amino-1,2,4-thiadiazole ring is attached through its C3 to the oxime carbon. The methoxy group on the oxime nitrogen points to the same side as the amide carbonyl, so it is trans to the thiadiazole. That gives `CO/N=C(/C1=NSC(N)=N1)C(=O)N...`.

**Cephem core.**
- C7 carries the NH on a wedge bond. This gives `[C@H]1` in the SMILES order N, H, C8, C6.
- C6 carries a hashed H. This gives `[C@H]2` in the order C7, H, N, S.
- The ring is closed through the β-lactam N and C=O (`N2C1=O`).

**C3 substituent.** The CH2 is bonded to the cationic N of the imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine. I wrote that system in Kekulé form, with N⁺=C at the fusion carbon: `[N+]3=C4C=CC=NN4C=C3`.

I checked the SMILES atom by atom against the drawing.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/C1=NSC(N)=N1)C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(C[N+]3=C4C=CC=NN4C=C3)=C(C(=O)[O-])N2C1=O

name: Cefpirome
text:
This looks like cefpirome, a cephalosporin, and I read it region by region.

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a dihydrothiazine ring. The ring carbon bearing the CO2⁻ group is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the CH2 substituent.
- **C-3 side chain:** the CH2 is attached to a pyridinium nitrogen. The pyridinium is fused to a cyclopentane ring, giving a 6,7-dihydro-5H-cyclopenta[b]pyridinium.
- **C-7 side chain:** an amide, NH–C(=O), leads to a C(=N–OMe) carbon bearing a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl group.
- **Oxime geometry:** I worked out the geometry from the drawn coordinates. The OMe is on the same side as the amide and opposite the thiazole, which is the Z (syn) isomer. In SMILES this is `CO/N=C(/thiazole)\C(=O)`.
- **Ring-fusion stereocentres:** the amide-bearing carbon has the NH on a hashed bond and an implicit H. The adjacent carbon has an explicit H on a wedge. Working out the chirality from the drawn geometry gives `[C@H]` for the amide-bearing carbon and `[C@H]` for the ring-fusion carbon.

The SMILES below was written to match the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/C1=CSC(N)=N1)\C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@H]3SCC(C[n+]4cccc5CCCc45)=C(N3C2=O)C(=O)[O-]

name: Ceftazidime
text:
I read this as ceftazidime: a cephalosporin core with a pyridinium-methyl group, a carboxylate, and a 2-aminothiazole side chain. The oxime carries a C(CH3)2–COOH group.

- **Oxime geometry:** the oxime oxygen sits on the same side as the amide carbon and opposite the thiazole, so the C=N is Z. I wrote this as `O/N=C(/thiazole)\C(=O)N`, which puts the oxygen cis to the amide carbon.
- **Ring stereocentres:** the wedge and hash on the β-lactam carbons match the natural (6R,7R) configuration. I took the `@` markings for these two centres from the known ceftazidime SMILES (recalled from memory, not re-derived from the drawing), not from my own assignment.
- **Charges:** the pyridinium nitrogen is N⁺ and the ring carboxylate is O⁻, so the molecule is a zwitterion with a free carboxylic acid on the side chain.

SMILES: CC(C)(C(=O)O)O/N=C(/C1=CSC(=N1)N)\C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@@H]3N(C2=O)C(=C(CS3)C[N+]4=CC=CC=C4)C(=O)[O-]

name: Cefprozil
text:
I read this as a cephalosporin skeleton, which matches cefprozil, but the propenyl group is drawn trans, so the SMILES describes the E isomer rather than the Z form of the marketed drug.

**Ring system**
- The β-lactam (four-membered ring) is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring that contains S and N.
- A carboxylic acid sits on the ring carbon next to N.
- A propenyl group is attached to the ring carbon next to the CH₂–S.

**Propenyl geometry**
- The methyl and the ring carbon lie on opposite sides of the C=C, so the double bond is trans (E).

**Side chain**
- The β-lactam carbon carries an NH–C(=O)–CH(NH₂)– group, and that CH bears a 4-hydroxyphenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned the three stereocentres from the drawn wedges and hashes: the ring-fusion carbon (H hashed), the β-lactam carbon bearing the wedged NH, and the amino-bearing carbon (NH₂ hashed).
- All three come out as `@@` in the SMILES below.

I did not run this through a SMILES parser.

SMILES: C/C=C/C1=C(N2[C@@H]([C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)[C@@H](c3ccc(O)cc3)N)SC1)C(=O)O

name: Ceftizoxime
text:
I read the drawing as ceftizoxime, a cephalosporin with a 2-aminothiazole side chain.

- **Side chain:** a 2-aminothiazole (ring N, S, an NH2 on the carbon between them) is attached through its C4 to a C=N–OCH3 oxime carbon, which carries a C(=O)NH amide.
- **Oxime geometry:** the methoxy group on the oxime nitrogen sits on the same side as the amide carbonyl carbon. That carbonyl carbon outranks the thiazole carbon in priority, so the double bond is Z.
- **Bicyclic core:** the β-lactam (N, C=O, and two CH carbons) is fused to a six-membered ring. In that ring the sequence is N–C(COOH)=CH–CH2–S–CH. There is no substituent on the ring CH2, so there is no acetoxymethyl group as in cefotaxime.
- **Stereochemistry:** the NH-bearing carbon has a wedge bond and the ring-fusion CH has a hashed H. I assigned the stereo tags from the known natural (6R,7R) configuration of ceftizoxime rather than deriving them from the wedge geometry, so these two tags are the least certain part.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/C1=CSC(=N1)N)\C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@@H]3N(C2=O)C(=CCS3)C(=O)O

name: Celecoxib
text:
This structure is celecoxib.

- **Pyrazole ring:** N1 carries the 4-sulfamoylphenyl group. N2 is double-bonded to C3, which bears the CF3. C4 is the CH. C5 carries the 4-methylphenyl (tolyl) group and bonds to N1.
- **Right-hand ring:** a para-substituted benzene bonded to N1 and carrying S(=O)(=O)NH2.
- **Lower ring:** a para-substituted benzene bonded to C5 and carrying the methyl group.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1cc(nn1-c1ccc(cc1)S(N)(=O)=O)C(F)(F)F

name: Cefuroxime
text:
This is cefuroxime, a cephalosporin, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring (S, CH2, C=C, N). The ring carbon next to N carries a carboxylic acid, and the adjacent alkene carbon carries CH2–O–C(=O)NH2 (a carbamate).
- **Side chain:** the ring NH is acylated by C(=O)–C(=N–OMe)–(2-furyl). The methoxy-oxime is Z: OMe sits on the same side as the amide carbonyl, which is the higher-priority substituent on that carbon, and opposite the furan.
- **Ring stereocentres:** I took the two fused-ring configurations from the known cefuroxime structure, which I recalled from memory, and did not re-derive them from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing. They are consistent with one wedged N–C bond and one hashed C–H bond.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/c1ccco1)\C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@@H]3N(C2=O)C(=C(CS3)COC(=O)N)C(=O)O

name: Ceftiofur
text:
I read this as ceftiofur: a cephalosporin core with a 2-aminothiazole, a methoxyimino group and a furoyl thioester on the side chain.

- **Left side:** a 2-aminothiazole is attached through its C4 to a C=N–OMe group. That carbon is bonded to the amide C(=O)NH.
- **Oxime geometry:** in the drawing the OMe is on the opposite side of the C=N from the thiazole, so I wrote it as `CO/N=C(/C1=CSC(N)=N1)`.
- **Core:** a β-lactam (the C=O at the bottom) is fused to a six-membered ring containing S, CH2, C(CH2S…)=C, and N. The C=C carbon next to N carries the COOH.
- **Right side:** the CH2–S–C(=O)–2-furyl thioester.
- **Stereocentres:** the two ring-fusion carbons are the only ones with wedge/hash bonds.
  - The carbon bearing NH has a wedge to NH, which I wrote as `[C@H]1`.
  - The carbon bonded to S has a hashed H, which I wrote as `[C@H]2`.
  - I derived both from the drawing rather than copying a known SMILES.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/C1=CSC(N)=N1)C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(CSC(=O)c3ccco3)=C(N2C1=O)C(O)=O

name: Cefuroxime Axetil
text:
I read this as cefuroxime axetil, working through the drawing as follows.

- **Core:** a cephalosporin bicycle, with a four-membered β-lactam fused to a six-membered ring containing S. The ring carbon bearing the carboxylate is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the CH2–O–C(=O)NH2 carbamate.
- **Ester group:** the carboxylate is esterified with CH(CH3)–O–C(=O)CH3, the 1-acetoxyethyl (axetil) group. This carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Side chain:** the 7-position carries an amide, NH–C(=O)–C(=N–OCH3), attached to a 2-furyl ring.
- **Oxime geometry:** the OMe on the oxime N lies on the same side as the amide carbonyl and opposite the furan. The amide carbon outranks the furyl carbon in priority, so this is the Z oxime. It is written `/C(=N\OC)`.
- **Ring stereocentres:**
  - The S–CH carbon has an H on a wedge, which gives `[C@@H]`.
  - The carbon bearing the NH on a hashed bond gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC(OC(C)=O)OC(=O)C1=C(COC(N)=O)CS[C@@H]2[C@H](NC(=O)/C(=N\OC)c3ccco3)C(=O)N12

name: Celiprolol
text:
This structure is celiprolol, drawn without stereochemistry.

**Reading the drawing, region by region:**
- **Left side:** a diethylamino group (N with two ethyls) is bonded to a C=O, which is bonded to an NH. Together these form the urea N,N-diethyl-N'-aryl.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring carrying three substituents.
  - The urea NH is attached at the lower-left ring carbon.
  - An acetyl group (C(=O)CH3) is on the upper ring carbon.
  - An O-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-NH-C(CH3)3 chain is on the next ring carbon, adjacent to the acetyl carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is written.

**SMILES check:** CCN(CC)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1
- The ring atoms are c1 (bearing NH), c, c, c(O...), c(acetyl), c1, which is six atoms.
- The urea-bearing carbon sits meta to the acetyl carbon, since the acetyl carbon neighbours c1 through the last ring atom. In the drawing the acetyl carbon is adjacent to the ring CH, which is adjacent to the urea carbon, so this matches.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1

name: Cephalexin
text:
The drawing shows cephalexin, which I identified from its overall structure. Reading it region by region:

- **Core:** a cephalosporin bicyclic system. A four-membered β-lactam ring (N, C=O, and two CH carbons) is fused to a six-membered dihydrothiazine ring containing S, a CH2, and a C=C.
- **Ring substituents:** the C=C carries a methyl group on one carbon and a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen.
- **Side chain:** an amide NH on the β-lactam ring is acylated by a phenylglycyl group. This is C(=O)–CH(NH2)–phenyl, with the phenyl ring drawn as a benzene.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing has a hashed H on the ring-fusion carbon, a wedged amide N on the adjacent β-lactam carbon, and a hashed NH2 on the side-chain carbon. I did not assign each centre from the wedges independently. I wrote the stereodescriptors from the known cephalexin configuration, (6R,7R) with an (R)-phenylglycyl group, recalled from memory.

SMILES: CC1=C(N2[C@@H]([C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)[C@@H](C3=CC=CC=C3)N)SC1)C(=O)O

name: Ceftriaxone
text:
I read this as a cephalosporin skeleton with a methoxyimino aminothiazole side chain, which is the ceftriaxone structure. The SMILES below follows the drawing region by region.

**Core.** The bicyclic β-lactam–dihydrothiazine has a carboxylic acid on the ring double-bond carbon. A CH2–S– linker leaves the neighbouring ring carbon.

**Triazine ring.** The linker sulfur attaches to a six-membered ring: C(=N–C(=O)–C(=O)–NH–N(CH3)–). This is a 1-methyl-5,6-dioxo-1,2,5,6-tetrahydro-1,2,4-triazin-3-yl group.

**Acyl side chain.** The β-lactam NH is acylated by C(=O)–C(=N–OCH3), which carries a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl group.

**Oxime geometry.** On the drawing, the OMe oxygen sits on the same side of the C=N as the amide carbonyl and opposite the thiazole. That makes it Z, written as `CO/N=C(\C(=O)...)/Th`.

**Ring-fusion stereochemistry.**
- At C7 (the carbon bearing NH), the hashed bond puts N behind the plane. With neighbour order N, H, C8, C6 this gives `[C@H]`.
- At C6 (the carbon bearing S), the wedged H points toward the viewer. With neighbour order C7, H, N, S this gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CO/N=C(\C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(CSC3=NC(=O)C(=O)NN3C)=C(N2C1=O)C(=O)O)/C1=CSC(N)=N1

name: Cenobamate
text:
This structure matches cenobamate, (R)-1-(2-chlorophenyl)-2-(2H-tetrazol-2-yl)ethyl carbamate. I read it as follows:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with Cl on the carbon next to the ring carbon that carries the side chain (ortho-chlorophenyl).
- **Side chain:** a stereocentre bearing the aryl group, an O–C(=O)NH2 carbamate, and a CH2 drawn on a wedge. The CH2 is bonded to N2 of the tetrazole.
- **Tetrazole:** the ring runs C=N–N(CH2)–N=N–C, which is a 2H-tetrazol-2-yl group, written `n1ncnn1` when attached through N2.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - The priorities at the stereocentre are O > CH2N > aryl > H.
  - The wedged CH2 puts H at the back.
  - O (right) → CH2 (lower left) → aryl (upper left) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.
  - In the SMILES below, `O[C@H](aryl)CH2` encodes R.

SMILES: NC(=O)O[C@H](c1ccccc1Cl)Cn1ncnn1

name: Ceritinib
text:
This is ceritinib. I read it region by region.

- **Left side:** an isopropyl group is attached to a sulfonyl, S(=O)(=O). The sulfonyl is bonded to a benzene ring, and the carbon ortho to it carries an NH.
- **Pyrimidine core:** that NH attaches at C4 of the pyrimidine. C5 carries Cl, C6 is CH, N1 is the next ring atom, C2 bears an NH, and N3 closes the ring.
- **Right side:** the C2 NH is bonded to a second benzene ring. Going around that ring, the carbon bonded to the NH is next to a carbon bearing an O-isopropyl group. After that comes a CH, then a carbon bearing the piperidin-4-yl group, then a carbon bearing a methyl, then a CH that closes the ring back to the NH-bearing carbon.
- **Piperidine:** attached through its C4, with a free NH in the ring.

SMILES: CC(C)Oc1cc(C2CCNCC2)c(C)cc1Nc1ncc(Cl)c(Nc2ccccc2S(=O)(=O)C(C)C)n1

name: Centanafadine
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane carrying a naphthalen-2-yl group on the quaternary ring-fusion carbon.

**Ring system.** The left part is a five-membered ring made of NH, a CH2 on each side of the nitrogen, and the two ring-fusion carbons. A cyclopropane CH2 bridges those two fusion carbons.

**Substituent.** The quaternary fusion carbon is bonded to a naphthalene ring. The bond is attached at the carbon next to the ring-fusion position, which makes it a naphthalen-2-yl group.

**Stereochemistry.** There are two wedges:
- The naphthyl bond on the quaternary carbon is a wedge, which gives `[C@]` in the SMILES below.
- The H on the other fusion carbon is a wedge, which gives `[C@@H]`.

I assigned `@` and `@@` by working out the neighbour order around each centre and the viewing direction from the wedged substituent. I did not run the SMILES through a toolkit, so the chirality marks rest on that manual check.

SMILES: N1C[C@]2(c3ccc4ccccc4c3)C[C@@H]2C1

name: Cephaloridine
text:
I read this as cephaloridine, a cephalosporin. The fused ring system is a β-lactam joined to a six-membered ring containing S, and the groups on it are:

- A carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]) on the ring carbon next to the lactam N.
- A CH2–pyridinium group on the neighbouring alkene carbon.
- At the β-lactam carbon bearing NH (drawn with a wedge), an NH–C(=O)–CH2–(2-thienyl) amide.

Stereochemistry comes from the two drawn stereocentres:

- The ring-fusion carbon bonded to S has a hashed H. Its neighbour order in the SMILES is S, H, N, C7, which gives @@.
- The carbon bearing NH has a wedged NH bond. Its neighbour order is C6, H, N, C8, which gives @.

SMILES: [O-]C(=O)C1=C(C[n+]2ccccc2)CS[C@@H]3[C@H](NC(=O)Cc4cccs4)C(=O)N13

name: Cephalothin
text:
I read this as cephalothin: a cephalosporin core (a β-lactam fused to a dihydrothiazine) carrying an acetoxymethyl group, a carboxylic acid, and a thiophen-2-ylacetamido side chain.

- **Left side:** an acetyl group (CH3–C(=O)–O–) is attached through a CH2 to the ring C=C, and the other alkene carbon bears the COOH.
- **Core:** the ring nitrogen is shared by the four-membered β-lactam, which has a C=O, and the six-membered ring, which contains S and a CH2.
- **Side chain:** the amide NH–C(=O)–CH2 is attached to a thiophene ring through its 2-position.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are two drawn stereocentres.
  - C7, bearing the NH, has a wedge bond to N. With its implicit H pointing back, C(=O), N and C6 appear clockwise from the front, which is `@@` in the SMILES order below.
  - C6, the ring-fusion carbon, has a hashed H. With that H pointing back, N, C7 and S appear clockwise, which is also `@@` in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: CC(=O)OCC1=C(C(=O)O)N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)Cc3cccs3)[C@@H]2SC1

name: Cetirizine
text:
The drawing shows cetirizine, read region by region:

- **Aromatic rings:** an unsubstituted phenyl ring and a 4-chlorophenyl ring, both attached to a single CH carbon.
- **Piperazine:** the CH carbon is bonded to one nitrogen of a piperazine ring.
- **Side chain:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2CH2–O–CH2–C(=O)OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: OC(=O)COCCN1CCN(CC1)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Cephaeline
text:
This structure is cephaeline, an emetine-type alkaloid. It has a benzo[a]quinolizidine unit carrying two methoxy groups and an ethyl group, linked through a CH2 to a tetrahydroisoquinoline. The isoquinoline ring carries one OH and one OMe.

I read the drawing as follows:
- **Left aromatic ring:** two adjacent OMe groups, fused to the ring containing the tertiary N.
- **Quinolizidine core:** N is shared by two rings. The ring-fusion carbon bears an H wedge. The adjacent ring carbon carries a bold-wedge ethyl, and the next ring carbon carries a hashed CH2 linker.
- **Right ring system:** a tetrahydroisoquinoline with an NH. Its C1 carries the linker CH2 on a wedge. On the aromatic ring, OH sits next to OMe, with the OH carbon next to the aromatic CH that follows the ring carbon attached to the CH2CH2.

I checked each of the four stereocentres against the wedges and hashes by comparing the viewed rotation of the neighbours with the SMILES neighbour order. All four agree with the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1CN2CCc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc3[C@@H]2C[C@@H]1C[C@H]1NCCc2cc(O)c(OC)cc21

name: Chloral Hydrate
text:
The drawing shows a two-carbon chain. The left carbon is a CH bearing two OH groups. It is bonded to a right carbon that carries three Cl atoms. This is chloral hydrate, 2,2,2-trichloroethane-1,1-diol.

Both OH groups are on the same carbon, and no wedges or hashes appear, so no stereochemistry is needed. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: OC(O)C(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Chlorambucil
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an N,N-bis(2-chloroethyl)amino group, with N attached to two CH2CH2Cl chains. The other is a chain of three CH2 groups ending in a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH).

Counting the chain from the ring: the ring carbon attaches to CH2 (935,575), then CH2 (1025,672), then CH2 (1153,643), then the carboxyl carbon (1243,740). That is three CH2 groups followed by COOH, so the acid is a 4-carbon butanoic acid. This is chlorambucil.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCc1ccc(N(CCCl)CCCl)cc1

name: Cerivastatin
text:
I read the molecule as a 3,5-dihydroxyhept-6-enoic acid chain attached to a substituted pyridine.

**Chain.** From the left: a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O), then CH2, CH(OH), CH2, CH(OH), then a CH=CH double bond joined to the ring.

**Stereo.** Both OH groups are drawn on hashed bonds. For each CH(OH), looking from the viewer's side, the left CH2, the OH and the right-hand neighbour run clockwise, with the implicit H pointing toward the viewer. Written in the order "preceding carbon, H, O, following carbon", this gives `@` for both centres. The CH=CH has its two chain substituents on opposite sides, so it is E (trans), written `/C=C/`.

**Pyridine ring.** Going around from the vinyl-bearing carbon (C3):
- C3 carries the vinyl chain.
- C2 carries an isopropyl group and sits next to the ring nitrogen.
- N follows C2.
- C6 carries a second isopropyl group.
- C5 carries CH2–O–CH3.
- C4 carries the 4-fluorophenyl group.

**Check.** The SMILES has the pyridine closed (six ring atoms, one N), the phenyl ring with F para to the attachment point, two isopropyl groups, one CH2OCH3, and the carboxylic acid at the chain end.

SMILES: OC(=O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)/C=C/c1c(C(C)C)nc(C(C)C)c(COC)c1c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Chloramphenicol
text:
The drawing shows chloramphenicol.

- **Aromatic ring:** a para-substituted benzene carries a nitro group, drawn as N⁺(=O)O⁻.
- **Side chain:** the ring attaches to a CH(OH) carbon, which is bonded to a CH carbon bearing a CH₂OH group and an NH.
- **Amide:** the NH is acylated by C(=O)CHCl₂.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon has a wedged OH and the second carbon has a wedged CH₂OH. Assigning CIP priorities with H pointing away gives R at the CH(OH) carbon (OH > CH(N) > aryl) and R at the CH(N) carbon (N > CH(OH) > CH₂OH). This is the (1R,2R) configuration, so I used the known stereo SMILES for that isomer.

SMILES: C1=CC(=CC=C1[C@H]([C@@H](CO)NC(=O)C(Cl)Cl)O)[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Chlordecone
text:
I read the drawing as a ten-carbon cage with one ketone carbon and ten chlorines, which matches the formula of chlordecone (Kepone), C10Cl10O.

I labelled the ring vertices and traced the bonds between them:
