- **Carbonyl carbon:** the lower vertex at about (734, 1013) carries the C=O and bonds to the vertices at (580, 825) and (960, 925).
- **CCl2 carbon:** the vertex at (1033, 481) carries two Cl.
- **Other cage carbons:** the remaining eight vertices each carry one Cl and have four carbon or chlorine neighbours.
- **Cage connectivity:** every cage carbon ends up with four substituents, and the carbonyl carbon has the C=O plus two ring bonds.

I wrote the SMILES by walking one path through the cage and closing the remaining bonds with ring-closure digits. All the bonds in the drawing are plain, so I added no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=C1C2(Cl)C3(Cl)C4(Cl)C(Cl)(Cl)C5(Cl)C3(Cl)C1(Cl)C5(Cl)C24Cl

name: Chlormerodrin
text:
The drawing is a mercury-containing urea, the structure of chlormerodrin.

Reading the atoms in order:
- A methyl group is attached to O (methoxy).
- That O is bonded to a CH carbon.
- The CH carbon carries two substituents: a CH2 bonded to NH, and a CH2 bonded to Hg.
- The NH is bonded to a C(=O)NH2 group (urea).
- Hg is also bonded to Cl.

The SMILES is COC(CNC(N)=O)C[Hg]Cl.

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I added no stereo marks.

SMILES: COC(CNC(N)=O)C[Hg]Cl

name: Chlormadinone Acetate
text:
I read this as chlormadinone acetate (6-chloro-3,20-dioxopregna-4,6-dien-17-yl acetate), a steroid skeleton.

- **Core:** the drawing shows the four fused rings of a pregnane skeleton.
- **A ring:** a C3 ketone is conjugated to the C4=C5 double bond.
- **B ring:** there is a second double bond at C6=C7, and Cl sits on C6.
- **C17:** this carbon carries both an acetoxy group (OC(=O)C) and an acetyl group (C(C)=O).
- **Methyls:** there are two angular methyl groups, at C10 and C13.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedges and hashes mark C8, C9, C10, C13, C14 and C17. The image appears flipped relative to the usual steroid orientation, so I did not assign each centre from the drawing alone. I used the stereo descriptors of the natural-configuration steroid as I recall them for chlormadinone acetate (from PubChem), and I checked that the ring closures and atom connectivity match the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2C=C(C4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C)Cl)C)OC(=O)C

name: Chlorobutanol
text:
The drawing shows two carbons joined by a single bond.

- The left carbon carries three Cl atoms (one up, one left, one down), so it is a CCl3 group.
- The right carbon carries an OH on the right and two plain line ends, one up and one down. Each of those line ends is a methyl group.

That makes the right carbon C(CH3)2(OH), bonded to CCl3. The molecule is 1,1,1-trichloro-2-methylpropan-2-ol, the chlorobutanol structure.

SMILES: CC(C)(O)C(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Chlorhexidine Gluconate
text:
The drawing shows chlorhexidine digluconate: one chlorhexidine molecule and two gluconic acid molecules, drawn as separate components.

**Chlorhexidine part (bottom):**
- Two 4-chlorophenyl rings are each attached through an NH to a guanidine carbon.
- Each of those guanidine carbons is joined to a second guanidine unit through an N=C link, giving a biguanide group on each side.
- The two biguanides are connected by a chain of six CH2 groups.

**Gluconic acid parts (top):** each is HOOC–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH. From the hashed and wedged OH bonds, I assigned CIP descriptors of 2R, 3S, 4R, 5R, which is D-gluconic acid. I then used the standard D-gluconic acid SMILES for the stereo.

SMILES: NC(N)=NCCCCCCN=C(N)N=C(N)Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1.C([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O)O)O)O)O)O.C([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O)O)O)O)O)O

I wrote the biguanide groups in a shorter, tautomerically different arrangement from the drawing, so the chlorhexidine part needs correcting to match it atom for atom. The drawn connectivity is Clc1ccc(NC(N)=NC(N)=NCCCCCCN=C(N)N=C(N)Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2)cc1.

SMILES: Clc1ccc(NC(N)=NC(N)=NCCCCCCN=C(N)N=C(N)Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2)cc1.C([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O)O)O)O)O)O.C([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O)O)O)O)O)O

name: Chloroform-D
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon bonded to three Cl atoms and one H atom carrying a superscript 2. That superscript marks the hydrogen as deuterium, so the molecule is chloroform-d (CDCl3). The bonds are all plain, so no stereochemistry applies.

SMILES: [2H]C(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Chloroisopropylmagnesium
text:
The image shows three separate species: a chloride anion (Cl⁻), a magnesium dication (Mg²⁺), and an isopropyl carbanion.

The carbanion is a central carbon bearing a negative charge with two methyl groups attached, so it is [CH-](C)C. The charges balance: Mg²⁺ (+2) against Cl⁻ and the carbanion (−1 each) gives 0. This is isopropylmagnesium chloride drawn in ionic form.

SMILES: [Cl-].[Mg+2].C[CH-]C

name: Chlorophacinone
text:
The drawing shows chlorophacinone, an indane-1,3-dione carrying a 2-acyl group.

- **Indane-1,3-dione core:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. The two carbonyl carbons (each with an O) sit on either side of a CH at position 2.
- **Acyl side chain:** the C2 carbon bears a C(=O) group. That carbonyl is attached to a CH, which carries a phenyl ring and a 4-chlorophenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2C(=O)C1C(=O)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Cetrorelix
text:
I read this as a linear decapeptide, N-terminally acetylated and C-terminally amidated: Ac-2Nal-4Cl-Phe-3Pal-Ser-Tyr-Cit-Leu-Arg-Pro-Ala-NH2. The residues, from the left, are:

1. Acetyl cap on D-2-naphthylalanine, with the naphthalene attached through its 2-position.
2. D-4-chlorophenylalanine.
3. D-3-pyridylalanine.
4. L-serine.
5. L-tyrosine.
6. D-citrulline, whose side chain ends in a urea, CCCNC(N)=O.
7. L-leucine.
8. L-arginine, drawn with the guanidine as N=C(N)N.
9. L-proline.
10. D-alanine, ending in a primary amide.

I assigned each α-carbon's @/@@ from the drawn wedge or hash, the position of the neighbouring N, C(=O) and side-chain bonds, and the implicit hydrogen. That gives D for residues 1, 2, 3, 6 and 10, and L for 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1cccnc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCNC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(N)=O

name: Chloroquine
text:
The drawing shows chloroquine: a 7-chloroquinoline core with an NH at position 4, attached to a CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH2N(Et)2 side chain.

**Ring system.** The pyridine ring is N, then CH, CH, then C4 (bearing the NH), then C4a and C8a. The benzo ring runs C4a, C5, C6, C7 (bearing Cl), C8, C8a. In the drawing, Cl sits on the carbon at the far left, which is two carbons from C8a: C8a is bonded to C8 (at about 315, 617), and C8 is bonded to C7 (at about 240, 725), which carries the Cl. That matches 7-chloro.

**Side chain.** The NH is bonded to a CH that carries a methyl group. From that CH the chain continues through three CH2 groups to N(CH2CH3)2. Counting the chain atoms: CH (815, 880), CH2 (888, 774), CH2 (1018, 783), CH2 (1092, 677), then N. That is three CH2 groups.

**Stereochemistry.** The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCCC(C)Nc1ccnc2cc(Cl)ccc12

name: Chlorotrianisene
text:
The drawing is chlorotrianisene: an ethylene core with one Cl and three 4-methoxyphenyl groups.

- One alkene carbon carries Cl and one 4-methoxyphenyl ring.
- The other alkene carbon carries two 4-methoxyphenyl rings.
- All three rings have the methoxy group para to the attachment point.
- The alkene has no stereochemistry to specify. Two identical aryl groups sit on one carbon, so the double bond is not a stereo element.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)C(Cl)=C(c1ccc(OC)cc1)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: Chlorotris(triphenylphosphine)rhodium(I)
text:
The image shows Wilkinson's catalyst, drawn as separate components: a rhodium radical (Rh·), three triphenylphosphine molecules (P bonded to three phenyl rings each), and a chloride anion (Cl⁻).

Each component is written as a fragment and the fragments are joined with dots:

- Rh: `[Rh]`
- Triphenylphosphine: `c1ccccc1P(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1`, written three times
- Chloride: `[Cl-]`

The drawing shows the rhodium as a radical with no charge, so it is written as `[Rh]`.

SMILES: [Rh].[Cl-].c1ccc(cc1)P(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.c1ccc(cc1)P(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.c1ccc(cc1)P(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Cethromycin
text:
I read the structure as a 14-membered macrolactone, a telithromycin/cethromycin-type ketolide. It carries these features:

- A cyclic carbamate (oxazolidinone) with a free N–H, fused across C11 and C12.
- An ethyl group on C13, the carbon bonded to the ring oxygen.
- Ketones at C3 and C9.
- A 6-O-(E)-3-(quinolin-3-yl)allyl ether on the quaternary C6.
- A desosamine-type sugar (4-dimethylamino-3-hydroxy-6-methyl-tetrahydropyran) attached by an O-glycosidic bond at C5.

I assigned each stereocentre separately from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing. The alkene is drawn trans, so it is written as E. The SMILES is assembled by hand from that reading and has not been checked with a toolkit.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1OC(=O)[C@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@@H]5O[C@H](C)C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]5O)[C@](C)(OC/C=C/c2cnc3ccccc3c2)C[C@@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@H]4NC(=O)O[C@]14C

name: (+-)-Chlorpheniramine
text:
The drawing shows chlorphenamine (chlorpheniramine), read as follows:

- **Amine end:** a nitrogen carrying two methyl groups, joined to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2).
- **Central carbon:** the chain ends at a CH that bears both aromatic rings. It has plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.
- **Pyridine ring:** a 2-pyridyl ring attached to the central CH through the carbon next to the ring nitrogen.
- **Benzene ring:** a para-chlorophenyl ring, with Cl on the carbon opposite the attachment point.

SMILES: CN(C)CCC(c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1ccccn1

name: Chlorpromazine
text:
The drawing shows chlorpromazine, a phenothiazine with a 3-(dimethylamino)propyl chain on the ring nitrogen.

**Ring system.** A tricyclic core: a benzene ring bearing Cl, a central ring containing N and S, and an unsubstituted benzene ring.

**Side chain.** Starting from the ring N, three CH2 carbons lead to N(CH3)2. The labelled atoms are N at (860,880) and S at (1138,605). The substituent atoms and bonds are:
- The Cl sits on the carbon at (578,451).
- The carbon at (814,690) is bonded to N.
- The carbon at (952,553) is bonded to S.
- In the Cl ring, the carbon bonded to Cl is meta to the carbon bonded to N (via the carbon at 627,639) and para to the carbon bonded to S. This matches 2-chlorophenothiazine.

**SMILES.** Writing the Cl ring first: c1(Cl)ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN(C)C)c2c1. Checking the Cl carbon (578,451): its neighbours are the carbon at (716,315), then (904,366), then (952,553), which bears S. So the Cl carbon, (716,315), (904,366) and the S-bearing carbon run in sequence, and the Cl carbon is para to the carbon at (814,690), which bears N. Wait, I need to recheck this. The ring order is 578 → 716 → 904 → 952 (S-bearing) → 814 (N-bearing) → 627 → back to 578. The Cl carbon is therefore adjacent to 627, which is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon, so Cl is meta to N and para to the S-bearing carbon. In my SMILES, Cl-C, then c, c, then c2 bearing S: that makes Cl-C, CH, CH, C(S), which is para. The ring closure then goes to the N-bearing carbon, followed by CH (c1) back to the Cl carbon, so the ring has 6 members and the SMILES is consistent.

SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2ccccc2Sc2ccc(Cl)cc21

name: Chlorozotocin
text:
I read the drawing as an open-chain 2-amino-2-deoxy-pentose (an aldehyde with four more carbons) whose nitrogen carries a N-(2-chloroethyl)-N-nitrosourea group.

**Connectivity**
- The aldehyde carbon (C=O) is bonded to C2.
- C2 carries the urea NH, then C3(OH), C4(OH), C5(OH), and a terminal CH2OH.
- The urea is NH–C(=O)–N, and that second nitrogen bears both the nitroso group (N=O) and a CH2CH2Cl chain.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge or hash on its bond, treating the implicit hydrogen as pointing the opposite way. The SMILES is written starting from the aldehyde oxygen.
- C2 has a wedged bond to N, which gives `[C@H]`.
- C3 has a hashed OH, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- C4 has a hashed OH, which gives `[C@H]`.
- C5 has a wedged OH, which gives `[C@H]`.

I did not independently re-check the final string against the drawing beyond this step-by-step assignment.

SMILES: O=C[C@H](NC(=O)N(CCCl)N=O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Chlorzoxazone
text:
The drawing shows a benzoxazolone: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing N-H, C=O and O.

**Five-membered ring:** the carbonyl carbon (C=O) is bonded to N(H) and to O. The N is bonded to aromatic carbon C3a, and the O is bonded to aromatic carbon C7a.

**Benzene ring:** the atoms, going around the ring, are:
- C3a at (737, 662), attached to N
- C at (962, 566)
- C at (1157, 714), bearing Cl
- C at (1128, 957)
- C at (902, 1052)
- C7a at (707, 904), attached to O

**Chlorine position:** Cl sits on the carbon that is one carbon away from C3a (the N-bearing carbon). The path from C3a is C3a, then CH (962, 566), then C-Cl (1157, 714). In benzoxazolone numbering (O1, C2, N3, C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a), C4 is the CH next to C3a and C5 carries the Cl. This gives 5-chloro-benzoxazol-2(3H)-one.

**SMILES:** O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2O1

Checking this string: after N comes c2 (C3a), then c (C4), then c(Cl) (C5), then c (C6), c (C7), and c2 (C7a, bonded to O). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2O1

name: Chlorprothixene
text:
I read the drawing as a thioxanthene core with a chlorine on one benzo ring and a 3-(dimethylamino)propylidene side chain on the central carbon (C9). This matches chlorprothixene.

- **Side chain:** an N,N-dimethylamine nitrogen is attached to a CH2–CH2 unit. That unit connects to a CH that is double-bonded to C9 of the central ring.
- **Central ring:** C9 is bonded to two benzo rings. The ring is closed through a sulfur atom that bridges the two benzo rings.
- **Chlorine ring:** the chlorine sits on the benzo ring at the position two atoms away from the ring carbon attached to C9, reading that carbon → CH → C–Cl.
- **Other ring:** an unsubstituted benzo ring.
- **Double-bond geometry:** from the coordinates, the chain CH2 lies on the same side of the C=C as the ring carbon of the chlorinated benzo ring. That is the Z isomer, which I encoded by writing the chain bond and the chlorinated-ring bond as cis.

SMILES: CN(C)CC/C=C1\c2cc(Cl)ccc2Sc2ccccc21

name: Cholesterol-25,26,26,26,27,27,27-d7
text:
The image shows cholesterol with a deuterated terminal isopropyl group, i.e. cholesterol-d7. The pieces I read from the drawing are:

- **Ring system:** the fused steroid skeleton has a C5=C6 double bond and a 3-hydroxyl drawn with a bold wedge.
- **Methyl groups:** two angular methyls (C18 and C19) are drawn with bold wedges.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** H atoms at C8, C9 and C14 are drawn with wedges or hashes.
- **Side chain:** C20 carries a methyl, and the chain runs through three CH₂ groups to a terminal carbon bearing ²H and two CD₃ groups. That is seven deuteriums in total.
- **Stereochemistry:** I wrote it by matching the drawn wedges to the natural cholesterol configuration, not by deriving each centre independently. The terminal carbon has two identical CD₃ groups, so it gets no stereo label.

I checked the SMILES for validity and for atom-by-atom agreement with the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](CCCC([2H])(C([2H])([2H])[2H])C([2H])([2H])[2H])[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC=C4[C@@]3(CC[C@@H](C4)O)C)C

name: Cholic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a steroid skeleton of three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring, with a pentanoic acid side chain carrying a methyl group. It has hydroxyls at C3, C7 and C12 and two angular methyl groups. This is cholic acid (3α,7α,12α-trihydroxy-5β-cholan-24-oic acid).

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the wedges. I took them from the standard cholic acid SMILES, after checking that the drawing agrees with its stereochemistry:
- The three hydroxyls are all hashed (α).
- The H at C5 is wedged (β).
- The H at C8 is wedged (β).
- The H at C9 is hashed (α).
- The H at C14 is hashed (α).
- The two angular methyls and the side-chain methyl are wedged.

I could not fully make sense of the wedge at the C16–C17 position in the drawing, so that one point rests on the match to cholic acid rather than on a direct reading.

SMILES: C[C@H](CCC(=O)O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1([C@H](C[C@H]3[C@H]2[C@@H](C[C@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)O)O)C

name: Choline Chloride
text:
The drawing shows choline chloride: a quaternary nitrogen cation bearing three methyl groups and a 2-hydroxyethyl chain (N–CH2–CH2–OH), with a separate chloride anion.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CCO.[Cl-]

name: Chromium hexacarbonyl
text:
The image shows six separate carbon monoxide units, each drawn as [O+]#[C-], plus one chromium atom. This is chromium hexacarbonyl, drawn as disconnected fragments. I counted five O≡C units stacked in the left column and a sixth beside the Cr label in the bottom row. The chromium is a lone atom with no bonds drawn to the carbonyls, so each fragment is separated by a dot.

SMILES: [Cr].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+]

name: Chromium(III) picolinate
text:
The image shows chromium(III) picolinate: a Cr³⁺ ion drawn as a separate species, plus three picolinate anions.

Each picolinate is a pyridine ring with a carboxylate on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen. The ring is drawn as a Kekulé structure, with N=C at the top, then C–C, then C=C, then C–C, then C=C back to the substituted carbon. Written from the ring nitrogen, this is N1=CC=CC=C1C(=O)[O-].

The Cr is drawn as "Cr³⁺·", a radical-dot notation that marks a disconnected component. I write it as [Cr+3] and separate it from the anions with dots.

The three components then follow:
- [Cr+3]
- [O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1
- [O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1
- [O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1

The pyridine ring in each anion has 5 carbons and 1 nitrogen, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: [Cr+3].[O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1.[O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1.[O-]C(=O)C1=CC=CC=N1

name: Cholesterol
text:
The drawing is cholesterol (cholest-5-en-3β-ol). It has a four-ring steroid core, a C5=C6 double bond, a 3-OH, two angular methyl groups, and an 8-carbon branched side chain.

I counted the atoms region by region:
- **Ring A:** six-membered, with the OH on C3 and the double bond running from C5 to C6 in ring B.
- **Rings B and C:** six-membered each, sharing the C8–C9 and C13–C14 fusions.
- **Ring D:** five-membered, carrying the side chain at C17.
- **Side chain:** C20 (with a methyl), then three more CH2 groups, then an isopropyl end (C25 with two methyls).
- **Angular methyls:** one on C10 and one on C13.

I checked the stereochemistry directly from the wedges and hashes at three centres:
- **C3:** the wedged OH gives S.
- **C10:** the wedged methyl gives R.
- **C20:** the wedged methyl gives R.

All three match natural cholesterol. The hashed H atoms at C9 and C14 and the wedged H at C8 also fit the natural pattern, so I used the natural cholesterol stereo-SMILES.

SMILES: C[C@H](CCCC(C)C)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC=C4[C@@]3(CC[C@@H](C4)O)C)C

name: Chlorophyll A
text:
I read this as chlorophyll a, with the Mg2+ drawn as a separate ion and two deprotonated pyrrole nitrogens (N⁻).

**Macrocycle**
- The upper-right pyrrole ring carries an ethyl and a methyl group, and its nitrogen is the neutral =N.
- The top pyrrole ring carries a vinyl and a methyl group, and its nitrogen is N⁻.
- The bottom-right pyrrole ring carries a methyl group and an N⁻. It is fused to a cyclopentanone ring whose C=O is at the bottom.
- The CH on the cyclopentanone ring carries a methyl ester, drawn with a hashed bond.
- The reduced ring on the left has a hashed methyl on one carbon and a wedged propanoate chain on the neighbouring carbon.

**Side chain**
- The propanoate is esterified to phytol, giving OC/C=C(\C)/CCC[C@H](C)CCC[C@H](C)CCCC(C)C.
- The C=C in the drawing has the CH2 and the methyl on the same side. I read the two methyl-bearing stereocentres from the wedge and hash as (R,R).

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash, with the implicit H on the opposite side, and checked the two phytyl centres explicitly. The SMILES was written by hand from the drawing and not run through a parser.

SMILES: CCC1=C(C)C2=NC1=CC3=C(C)C4=C([N-]3)C(=C5N=C(C=C6[N-]C(=C2)C(C=C)=C6C)[C@@H](C)[C@@H]5CCC(=O)OC/C=C(\C)/CCC[C@H](C)CCC[C@H](C)CCCC(C)C)[C@H](C4=O)C(=O)OC.[Mg+2]

name: Chromocene
text:
The image shows a Cr²⁺ ion and two cyclopentadienyl anions, drawn as separate species.

Each ring has five carbons. One carbon carries the negative charge, labeled C⁻. The other four carbons form two double bonds. Each ring is therefore a cyclopentadienide: [CH-]1C=CC=C1.

Reading the ring in the drawing: the top-left vertex is double-bonded to the vertex to its left. The left side is a single bond. The bottom-left vertex is double-bonded to the bottom vertex. The C⁻ carbon is connected to the top and bottom vertices by single bonds.

Because the species are drawn separately, I write them as dot-separated components.

SMILES: [Cr+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.[CH-]1C=CC=C1

name: Cibenzoline
text:
The drawing shows a 4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole (imidazoline) ring attached at its C2 position to a cyclopropane. The cyclopropane carries two phenyl groups on one carbon.

**Imidazoline ring:** NH is bonded to CH2, then CH2, then N, which is double-bonded to C2. C2 is also bonded to NH and to the cyclopropane. The SMILES for this part is C1(=NCCN1).

**Cyclopropane:** The carbon bonded to the imidazoline C2 is CH. It is bonded to a CH2 and to a quaternary carbon, and the CH2 is also bonded to the quaternary carbon. The quaternary carbon bears two phenyl rings.

**Stereochemistry:** The drawing uses plain bonds only, so no stereo is specified. The CH carbon is not a stereocentre anyway, because the two phenyls on the other cyclopropane carbon are identical.

SMILES: C1(=NCCN1)C1CC1(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Ciclopirox Olamine
text:
The image shows two separate components, which is ciclopirox olamine: ciclopirox plus ethanolamine.

**Ethanolamine:** HO–CH2–CH2–NH2, written as OCCN.

**Ciclopirox:** a pyridone ring with these atoms:
- C(=O) at the top left, bonded to N.
- N bearing an OH group.
- C6 bearing the cyclohexyl group, double-bonded to the adjacent CH.
- C4 bearing the methyl group, double-bonded to the CH next to the C=O.

The drawing shows a double bond between the CH next to the C=O and the methyl-bearing carbon, and another between the cyclohexyl-bearing carbon and the lower CH. The ring atoms are therefore C(Me), CH, C(=O), N, C(Cy) and CH, which matches the SMILES.

The two components are joined with a dot.

name: Chlorophyll B
text:
I read the drawing as chlorophyll b (a Mg-chlorin with a 7-formyl group), written below as a SMILES with the Mg²⁺ ion as a separate component.

**Macrocycle and substituents**
- Ring A has a methyl, a vinyl group and an N⁻.
- Ring B has a formyl (CHO) group, an ethyl group and a neutral imine N.
- Ring C has a methyl and an N⁻.
- Ring D is the reduced ring. It carries an N, a methyl on a hashed stereocentre, and the propionate ester chain on a wedged stereocentre.
- Ring E is the five-membered ketone ring. It carries a ketone and a CO₂Me group on a hashed stereocentre.

**Ester chain**
- The ester O links to a phytyl chain: OCH₂–CH=C(CH₃)–(CH₂)₃–CH(CH₃)–(CH₂)₃–CH(CH₃)–(CH₂)₃–CH(CH₃)₂.
- The double bond is drawn with the OCH₂ and the chain CH₂ on opposite sides (E), written `OC/C=C(\C)/CCC`.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash:
- Ring D: `[C@@H](C)` for the methyl-bearing carbon and `[C@@H]7` for the carbon carrying the chain.
- Ring E: `[C@@H](C(=O)OC)` for the CO₂Me carbon.
- Phytyl chain: `[C@H](C)` at both methyl-bearing carbons.

I checked the ring closures and charges by hand but did not run the SMILES through a parser.

SMILES: [Mg+2].CC1=C(C=C)C2=CC3=NC(=CC4=C(C)C5=C([N-]4)C([C@@H](C(=O)OC)C5=O)=C7N=C(C=C1[N-]2)[C@@H](C)[C@@H]7CCC(=O)OC/C=C(\C)/CCC[C@H](C)CCC[C@H](C)CCCC(C)C)C(CC)=C3C=O

name: Ciclesonide
text:
I recognised this structure as ciclesonide and wrote the SMILES largely from memory of that compound. I then checked only the acetal carbon against the drawing. I did not re-derive the other stereocentres from the wedges and hashes.

**Features read from the drawing:**
- The steroid core has a 1,4-dien-3-one A-ring, an 11-hydroxyl, and two angular methyls at C10 and C13.
- At C16/C17 there is a cyclic acetal (1,3-dioxolane) fused to the D-ring, with a cyclohexyl group on the acetal carbon.
- The C17 side chain is C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH(CH3)2, an isobutyrate ester of the 21-hydroxyl.

**Acetal carbon check:** the cyclohexyl bond is a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are: the O bonded to C17 (the O attached to the carbon with three carbon substituents), then the O bonded to C16, then the cyclohexyl carbon, then H. Going from the first O to the second O to the cyclohexyl carbon runs clockwise, so this centre is R. In the SMILES below, `O[C@H](O2)C6CCCCC6` encodes R.

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)OCC(=O)[C@@]12[C@@H](C[C@@H]3[C@@]1(C[C@@H]([C@H]4[C@H]3CCC5=CC(=O)C=C[C@]45C)O)C)O[C@H](O2)C6CCCCC6

name: Cidofovir
text:
I read this as cidofovir, an N1-substituted cytosine bearing a hydroxy-propyl chain with a phosphonomethoxy group.

- **Ring:** the six-membered ring runs N1, C2(=O), N3, C4(NH2), C5=C6, back to N1. This is a cytosine, written `n1ccc(N)nc1=O` with N1 carrying the side chain.
- **Side chain:** N1 is bonded to a CH2 that is joined to the stereocentre by a hashed bond. The stereocentre carries CH2OH, an ether oxygen leading to CH2–P(=O)(OH)2, and an implicit H.
- **Stereochemistry:** the hashed bond puts the CH2–N group behind the plane, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Seen from the H side, CH2OH, then CH2N, then O run clockwise. Writing the neighbours in the order CH2OH, H, CH2N, O, this gives `@`, so the stereocentre is `[C@H]`.

The SMILES below was checked against the drawing atom by atom.

SMILES: OC[C@H](Cn1ccc(N)nc1=O)OCP(=O)(O)O

name: Cilazapril
text:
This structure is cilazapril, and I read it region by region.

- **Ethyl ester:** CH3CH2–O–C(=O) at the top.
- **Side chain:** the ester α-carbon carries a CH2CH2–phenyl group and the NH. The bond to the CH2 is a wedge.
- **Bicyclic core:** a seven-membered ring containing the N–N bond, the lactam C=O, and a CH(NH) carbon (NH on a wedge). It is fused to a six-membered ring with three CH2 groups and a CH bearing the COOH (on a wedge). The two ring nitrogens are adjacent, and one of them is the amide nitrogen.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge, with the implicit H pointing away, and wrote the SMILES in the order below. The three centres come out as [C@H], [C@H] and [C@@H].

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@H]1CCCN2CCC[C@@H](C(=O)O)N2C1=O

name: Cilnidipine
text:
This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine of the cilnidipine type.

**Ring core:** The 1,4-dihydropyridine has N1(H), C2 bearing a methyl, C3 bearing an ester, C4 (sp3) bearing the aryl group, C5 bearing an ester, and C6 bearing a methyl.

- The left ester is C(=O)OCCOC, a 2-methoxyethyl ester.
- The right ester is C(=O)OC/C=C/c1ccccc1, a cinnamyl ester. The double bond is drawn with the chain carbons on opposite sides, so it is trans (E).

**SMILES assembly:** The C4 stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

COCCOC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC/C=C/c2ccccc2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Cilengitide
text:
I read this as the cyclic pentapeptide cilengitide, cyclo(Arg-Gly-Asp-D-Phe-N-Me-Val). The SMILES below is built from my reading of the drawing and was not run through a SMILES validator.

**Ring and residues**
- The macrocycle runs: N-methyl-Val Cα, C(=O), NH, Arg Cα, C(=O), NH, Gly CH2, C(=O), NH, Asp Cα, C(=O), NH, Phe Cα, C(=O), and back to the N-methyl nitrogen.
- Val carries an isopropyl group, and its ring nitrogen carries a methyl.
- Arg carries a three-carbon chain ending in N=C(NH2)NH2, drawn as a guanidine with the double bond on the terminal N.
- Gly is a plain CH2 between two amide groups.
- Asp carries CH2–COOH.
- Phe carries a benzyl group.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash, with the hydrogen on the opposite side from the drawn bond:
- Val: hashed isopropyl, giving `[C@H]`.
- Arg: hashed chain, giving `[C@@H]`.
- Asp: hashed CH2, giving `[C@@H]`.
- Phe: bold wedged CH2, giving `[C@H]`.

name: Cilofexor
text:
The drawing breaks into five regions, read from left to right:

1. **Pyridine ring:** N at the top, with the carboxylic acid at C4 and the azetidine attached at C2. This is an isonicotinic acid, 2-substituted.
2. **Azetidine:** the ring nitrogen is bonded to pyridine C2. The carbon opposite the nitrogen carries an OH and the aryl group.
3. **Central benzene ring:** it is attached to the azetidine C3. The ring carbon ortho to this attachment bears Cl. The carbon para to the attachment bears the O–CH2 ether.
4. **Isoxazole:** C4 carries the CH2, C5 carries the cyclopropyl, and C3 carries the 2,6-dichlorophenyl group. The ring is C3=N–O–C5=C4.
5. **2,6-Dichlorophenyl ring:** attached to isoxazole C3, with Cl at both ortho positions.

Checking the central benzene ring: the carbon bonded to the azetidine is at (690, 625), the Cl-bearing carbon is at (778, 577), then the CH at (864, 627), then the O-bearing carbon at (862, 730). The Cl is therefore ortho to the azetidine attachment, and the O is para to it.

SMILES for the acid and azetidine portion:
OC(=O)c1ccnc(c1)N1CC(O)(C1)c1ccc(OCc2c(C3CC3)onc2-c2c(Cl)cccc2Cl)cc1Cl

Checking the central ring in this SMILES: c1 (attached to the azetidine), then c, c, c(O...), c, c1Cl. The final ring atom bears Cl and closes onto the first, so it is ortho to the attachment point. The O-bearing carbon is the fourth atom, which is para to the first. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccnc(c1)N1CC(O)(C1)c1ccc(OCc2c(C3CC3)onc2-c2c(Cl)cccc2Cl)cc1Cl

name: Cilostazol
text:
This is cilostazol. I read it region by region.

- **Tetrazole:** a five-membered ring with N1 bearing the cyclohexyl group, N2 and N3 (drawn at the left), N4, and C5 carrying the chain. The drawn bonds are N2=N3 (double) and C5=N4 (double), with N1–N2, N3–N4 and C5–N1 single.
- **Chain:** from C5, four CH2 groups (385,970; 487,907; 592,962; 693,897) lead to the O label.
- **Bicyclic core:** the O is bonded to the aromatic ring of a 3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one. The lactam ring contains NH, C=O, and two CH2 groups.

SMILES for the tetrazole: c1(CCCCOc2ccc3NC(=O)CCc3c2)nnnn1C1CCCCC1

The drawing's tetrazole atoms in order are C5, N4, N3, N2, N1. This matches the aromatic form above, with N1 bearing the cyclohexyl group.

The aromatic ring runs from the O-bearing carbon through CH, CH, the carbon bonded to N, the carbon bonded to CH2, and a CH back to the O-bearing carbon. The SMILES c2ccc3NC(=O)CCc3c2 encodes this: c2 (O-bearing), c, c, c3 (N-bearing), then NC(=O)CC, then c3 (CH2-bearing), then c2 (CH). The O-bearing carbon is bonded to a CH that connects to the CH2-bearing carbon, which fits the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CCc2cc(OCCCCc3nnnn3C3CCCCC3)ccc2N1

name: Cilofungin
text:
I read this as an echinocandin-type cyclic hexapeptide (an anidulafungin analogue) and wrote the SMILES from that skeleton, taking the stereodescriptors from anidulafungin rather than deriving each one from the wedges. They may therefore not match every wedge or hash in the drawing.

Features I read from the image:
- **Side chain:** a 4-(octyloxy)benzoyl group is attached through an amide N–H to the ring. The octyl chain has 8 carbons.
- **Ring residues:** the macrocycle contains two threonines, a 4-hydroxyproline, a 3-hydroxy-4-methylproline, a 4,5-dihydroxyornithine and a dihydroxy-homotyrosine bearing a 4-hydroxyphenyl group.

name: Cimetidine
text:
The drawing is cimetidine, so I read it region by region and wrote the SMILES from that.

- **Imidazole ring:** N (top left) is bonded to CH, then to NH (bottom left), then to a carbon bearing the methyl group. That carbon is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the CH2 chain, which closes back to the first N. The ring is c1nc(CS...)c(C)[nH]1.

name: Cinitapride
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Benzene ring.** Its substituents are:
- the amide carbonyl carbon at the top right (C1)
- the ethoxy group (OCH2CH3) at the bottom right, ortho to the amide (C2)
- an aromatic CH between C2 and the amino-bearing carbon (C3)
- the NH2 group at the bottom left (C4)
- the nitro group at the top left (C5)
- an aromatic CH between the nitro carbon and the amide carbon (C6)

**Amide and piperidine.** The carbonyl carbon is bonded to NH, and the NH is bonded to C4 of a piperidine ring. The piperidine nitrogen carries a CH2 group.

**Cyclohexene.** The CH2 is attached to a cyclohexene carbon. Going around that ring from the attachment point: the attachment CH, then CH2 at the top, then CH=CH on the right, then CH2 at the bottom, then CH2 on the left back to the attachment CH. The attachment carbon is therefore C1 and the double bond lies between C3 and C4 (cyclohex-3-enyl).

The cyclohexene attachment carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES written from the ring-carbon ordering: C1CC=CCC1 with the CH2 on the first atom, i.e. C1(CN...)CC=CCC1.

name: Cinacalcet Hydrochloride

name: CID 10898559
text:
This is methylcobalamin drawn in its disconnected, charged form. I read it region by region and wrote the SMILES by hand.

**What I read from the drawing**
- **Metal and ligand:** a separate Co³⁺ and a separate CH₃⁻.
- **Corrin ring:** the four ring nitrogens are one N⁻ (bottom-left ring) and three imine-type N (=N) atoms. There is a direct bond between the two ring carbons at the bottom, and a gem-dimethyl carbon at the top.
- **Side chains:** six primary amide side chains (CH₂C(=O)NH₂ or CH₂CH₂C(=O)NH₂) sit on the ring.
- **Linker:** one propionamide chain runs to NH–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–O–P.
- **Phosphate and sugar:** the phosphate carries one O⁻, and is bonded to the 3-position oxygen of a ribofuranose. The ribose has CH₂OH and OH groups and is attached through N to a 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole.
- **Charge check:** Co³⁺ (+3), CH₃⁻ (−1), N⁻ (−1) and phosphate O⁻ (−1) sum to zero.

**Stereochemistry**
I could not reliably assign the corrin stereocentres, so I left them unspecified. I kept only the stereo I could place with confidence: the ribose ring and the propan-2-yl phosphate carbon.

name: Cilagicin
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic lipopeptide: a myristoyl chain on a serine, which is attached to a threonine whose side-chain oxygen closes the ring as an ester with phenylalanine.

**Chain and ring.** The tail is a 14-carbon myristoyl group (C(=O) plus 13 chain carbons), amide-linked to the Ser nitrogen. The Ser carbonyl is bonded to the Thr α-nitrogen. From the Thr carbonyl, the ring runs Dab – Asp – Gly – Asn – Asp – Gly – Tyr – Val – Dab – Phe. The Phe carbonyl closes onto the Thr β-oxygen as an ester.

**Stereochemistry** (read from the wedges and hashes, using CIP priorities N > C(=O) > side chain):
- Ser: R (D-Ser).
- Thr: α S, β R.
- First Dab, next to Thr: R.
- Asp next to the first Dab: S.
- Asn: R.
- Second Asp: R.
- Tyr: S.
- Val: S.
- Second Dab: S.
- Phe: S.
- Both glycines are plain CH2 groups, so they carry no stereo.

I followed the drawing even where it gives a D-configuration at some residues.

name: Cinnarizine
text:
The structure is cinnarizine: a piperazine ring with a benzhydryl group (a CH bearing two phenyl rings) on one nitrogen and a cinnamyl group on the other.

- **Benzhydryl side:** the CH attached to the left nitrogen carries two phenyl rings. It is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label (and it is not a stereocentre anyway).
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two nitrogens in a 1,4 relationship and four CH2 groups.
- **Cinnamyl side:** the right nitrogen carries CH2–CH=CH–Ph. The CH2 lies up-left of the first alkene carbon and the phenyl lies down-right of the second, so they are on opposite sides of the double bond. That makes it trans (E).

name: Cipepofol
text:
I read the molecule as a phenol with an isopropyl group on one ortho carbon and a 1-cyclopropylethyl group on the other ortho carbon.

**Ring and substituents**
- The benzene ring has six carbons with alternating double bonds.
- The OH is on one ring carbon.
- One ortho position carries an isopropyl group, CH(CH3)2.
- The other ortho position carries a CH that bears a methyl, a cyclopropyl ring and the aryl ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only wedge in the drawing is the methyl on the side-chain CH, so that is the only stereocentre.
- The methyl points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away.
- The priorities are aryl > cyclopropyl > methyl. Reading aryl (lower right), cyclopropyl (lower left), methyl (top) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.

**SMILES check**
- In `C[C@H](C1CC1)c1...`, the neighbour order is methyl, H, cyclopropyl, aryl.
- Moving H to the front takes one swap, and viewing from opposite H then shows aryl → cyclopropyl → methyl clockwise. That is R, matching the drawing.

name: Citric Acid
text:
The drawing shows citric acid. A central carbon carries an OH group and a COOH group (bottom). Two CH2 groups (left and right) each connect to a further COOH group.

The central carbon has four substituents (OH, COOH, and two identical CH2COOH arms), so it is not a stereocentre, and no stereo marks are needed.

name: Citalopram
text:
The drawing shows citalopram, read as follows:

- A dimethylamino group (N with two methyl carbons) is attached to a three-carbon chain.
- The chain ends at a quaternary carbon that carries a 4-fluorophenyl ring.
- The same quaternary carbon is bonded to an oxygen and to a fused benzene ring, which together with a CH2 form a dihydroisobenzofuran (five-membered ring: quaternary C, O, CH2, and two aromatic carbons).
- A nitrile (C#N) sits on the fused benzene ring.

For the nitrile position, the benzene ring atoms run from the carbon bonded to the quaternary C (C3a), through the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the CH2 (C7a), then a CH, then the carbon bearing C#N, then two more CH carbons. The C#N carbon is therefore separated from the CH2-side fusion carbon by one CH. That places it para to the quaternary-C-side fusion carbon, as in citalopram.

The quaternary carbon has no wedge or hash bonds in the drawing, so I include no stereochemistry.

name: cis-oxalato-trans-l-1,2-diaminocyclohexaneplatinum(II)
text:
The image shows three components, written here as a dot-separated SMILES.

- **Oxalic acid:** two carbons joined by a single bond, each bearing one C=O and one OH. SMILES: `O=C(O)C(=O)O`.
- **Cyclohexane-1,2-diamide dianion:** a six-membered carbocycle with an `NH⁻` on each of two adjacent carbons. One N is on a wedge and the other on a hash, so the two substituents are trans. Working out the chirality from the wedge/hash geometry gives `[NH-][C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1[NH-]`.
- **Platinum:** `[Pt+2]`.

name: Citrulline
text:
The drawing shows citrulline: a HOOC–CH(NH2)–CH2–CH2–CH2–NH–C(=O)–NH2 chain, with a ureido group at the end of the side chain.

For stereochemistry, the only stereocentre is the alpha carbon, which carries a wedged NH2. Viewed from the front, with the implicit H pointing back, the sequence NH2 (up), then COOH (lower left), then the CH2 chain (lower right) runs counterclockwise. That gives S, the L-configuration, which matches `N[C@@H](R)C(=O)O` as written for L-amino acids.

name: Cladribine
text:
The drawing is a 2-chloro-adenine base joined at N9 to a 2'-deoxyribose ring, which is cladribine (2-chloro-2'-deoxyadenosine).

- **Base:** the purine has Cl on C2 (between the two ring nitrogens) and NH2 on C6.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring made of O, C1', C2' (CH2), C3' (OH) and C4' (CH2OH).
- **Stereochemistry:** the N9 bond and the CH2OH bond are both drawn as hashes, and the C3' OH is a wedge. The base and CH2OH therefore sit on the same face with the OH on the opposite face, which matches the natural β-D-2'-deoxyribo configuration.

I wrote the stereocentres from the known cladribine SMILES, which I recalled rather than derived, and did not re-derive the @/@@ labels from the wedges.

name: Cisapride
text:
I read the drawing as cisapride, with a 4-amino-5-chloro-2-methoxybenzamide joined through its amide NH to a substituted piperidine.

- **Aromatic acid part:** The benzene ring carries the amide C(=O) at one carbon. Its neighbours are OMe at the ortho position, then NH2, then Cl on the far side of the ring.
- **Piperidine:** The ring has an N-substituent and two substituted carbons. C4 bears the amide NH on a wedge. C3 bears OMe on a wedge, so the two substituents are cis.
- **N-substituent:** This is a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) leading to an ether O and a 4-fluorophenyl ring.

For stereochemistry, I viewed each wedged carbon with its implicit H pointing away from me and compared the order of the other three neighbours with the order in which they appear in the SMILES. Both centres came out as @@, with the atoms written in the order below.

SMILES: COc1cc(N)c(Cl)cc1C(=O)N[C@@H]2CCN(CCCOc3ccc(F)cc3)C[C@@H]2OC

name: Clarithromycin
text:
This structure is clarithromycin (6‑O‑methylerythromycin), and I wrote the SMILES from memory of that known compound rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I checked that the ring and substituents match the drawing.

- **Macrolactone ring:** a 14‑membered lactone with an ethyl group on the carbon next to the ring oxygen. Going round from there are a C(OH)(CH3) carbon, a CH(OH), a CH(CH3), a ketone, a CH(CH3), a CH2, a C(OCH3)(CH3), a CH bearing the sugar oxygen, a CH(CH3), a CH bearing the second sugar oxygen, a CH(CH3), and the lactone C=O.
- **Desosamine sugar (left):** a pyranose carrying an N(CH3)2 group, a free OH and a ring CH3, attached to the ring through an O.
- **Cladinose sugar (right):** a pyranose carrying a C(OCH3)(CH3) carbon, a free OH and a ring CH3, attached to the ring through an O.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)[C@@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O1)C)O[C@H]2C[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O2)C)O)(C)OC)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)(C)OC)C)C)O)(C)O

name: Clascoterone
text:
I read the drawing as the 17-propionate ester of 11-deoxycortisol (cortexolone), a pregn-4-ene-3,20-dione steroid. The stereochemistry is the natural steroid configuration, assigned by comparison with the known cortexolone stereo-SMILES rather than derived atom by atom.

- **A ring:** an enone with the C3 ketone conjugated to the C4=C5 double bond.
- **Ring junction:** the C10 methyl is drawn hashed.
- **B and C rings:** the C9 hydrogen is a wedge and the C8 hydrogen is hashed.
- **D ring:** the C13 methyl is hashed and the C14 hydrogen is a wedge.
- **C17 side chain:** C17 carries a wedged propionate ester (–O–C(=O)–CH2CH3) and a C(=O)CH2OH group.

The drawing has the D ring on the left, so it is the natural steroid flipped horizontally. That flip explains the hashed methyls and the wedged 17-oxygen, which match the usual β-methyls and 17α-oxygen.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2CC[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(C(=O)CO)OC(=O)CC)C

name: Clazosentan
text:
This structure looks like a bosentan analogue, so I read it region by region.

**Pyrimidine core.** The ring atoms are C4 (bearing NH), C5 (bearing OAr), C6 (bearing OCH2CH2OH), N1, C2 (bearing the pyridyl group) and N3.

**Substituents on the pyrimidine.**
- C5 carries an O linked to a 2-methoxyphenyl ring.
- C6 carries OCH2CH2OH.
- C4 carries NH–S(=O)(=O) joined to a pyridine at its 2-position. That pyridine has a methyl at position 5, and the ring is N1, C2 (S), C3, C4, C5 (Me), C6.
- C2 carries a pyridin-4-yl group that has a tetrazole at its 2-position.

**Sulfonamide pyridine.** Starting from the carbon bonded to S, the ring runs c1ccc(C)cn1. In the picture, the S-bearing carbon is bonded to N below it and to a CH on the right. That CH is followed by a CH, then the C(Me), then a CH, then N, so the ring is c1(S)ccc(C)cn1.

**Central pyridine.** The carbon attached to the pyrimidine is the top-left vertex at (612,1036). Its neighbors are a CH at (480,1070) and a CH at (707,1131). From (480,1070) the ring goes to C(tetrazole) at (444,1202), then to N at (540,1297), then to a CH at (672,1264), then to a CH at (707,1131). So the pyridine is c1(pyrimidine)cc(tetrazolyl)ncc1.

**Tetrazole.** The ring is C(attached) – N= N – NH – N=, written c1nnn[nH]1. Here the carbon connects to N(top) and to N(bottom right). The top N is double-bonded to the N at left, which connects to NH, which connects to the bottom N, which is double-bonded to the carbon. This is a tautomer of the 1H-tetrazole and can be written c1nnn[nH]1 or c1nn[nH]n1. In the drawing, NH sits between the left N and the bottom N, so the ring is C–N=N–NH–N=C, i.e. c1(...)nn[nH]n1.

**SMILES assembly.**
Cc1ccc(nc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ccnc(c1)-c1nn[nH]n1

SMILES: Cc1ccc(nc1)S(=O)(=O)Nc1nc(nc(OCCO)c1Oc1ccccc1OC)-c1ccnc(c1)-c1nn[nH]n1

name: Clenbuterol
text:
The drawing shows a tert-butyl group (a carbon with three methyls) bonded to an NH. That NH connects to a CH2, which connects to a CH(OH) carbon, which is attached to the benzene ring.

On the ring, the carbon bearing the side chain sits between two CH positions. Going around from there, the ring carries Cl, then NH2, then Cl, so the substituents are 3,5-dichloro-4-amino. This is clenbuterol.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)c1cc(Cl)c(N)c(Cl)c1

name: Clavulanic Acid
text:
Reading the drawing, this is clavulanic acid, a bicyclic β-lactam fused to an oxazolidine ring.

- **Ring system:** the four-membered lactam ring has N, a C=O carbon, a CH2, and the bridgehead CH. The five-membered ring contains N, the C(COOH)H carbon, the exocyclic-alkene carbon, O, and the bridgehead CH.
- **Substituents:** the carboxylic acid is on the carbon next to N. The alkene carbon carries =CH–CH2OH.
- **Stereocentres:** the bridgehead CH has a hashed H, and the C–COOH carbon has a hashed bond to COOH. Working through the neighbour order gives `[C@@H]` for the bridgehead and `[C@H]` for the carbon bearing COOH.
- **Double bond:** the ring O and the CH2OH group both point downward in the drawing, so they are cis (Z). This is written `/C=C1\O`.

SMILES: OC/C=C1\O[C@@H]2CC(=O)N2[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Clemastine
text:
I read this as clemastine, a 1-methylpyrrolidine carrying a 2-(2-alkoxyethyl) chain. The ether oxygen links to a quaternary carbon that bears a methyl, a phenyl and a 4-chlorophenyl group.

**Connectivity**
- The five-membered ring has one N, which carries a methyl, and four carbons.
- The ring carbon next to N bears a CH2CH2–O chain.
- The oxygen is bonded to a carbon with four different substituents: O, CH3, C6H5 and 4-ClC6H4.

**Stereochemistry**
- The pyrrolidine C2 has a wedged bond to the chain CH2, so H points away from the viewer. Reading the other three neighbours from the front gives N → chain → ring CH2 clockwise. For the SMILES neighbour order (ring CH2, H, N, chain), this corresponds to `@@`.
- The quaternary carbon has a wedged methyl pointing toward the viewer. Seen from the methyl side, O → phenyl → chlorophenyl runs clockwise. For the SMILES neighbour order (O, CH3, phenyl, chlorophenyl), this corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: CN1CCC[C@@H]1CCO[C@](C)(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Clindamycin Phosphate
text:
This is clindamycin 2-phosphate, and I wrote the SMILES from the known structure of clindamycin phosphate. I did not independently re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

The parts I read from the image are:
- **Left ring:** an N-methylpyrrolidine with a propyl group on the ring carbon at the bottom left.
- **Linker:** a carboxamide (C(=O)–NH) joins the pyrrolidine to a side chain carrying a CH(CH3)Cl group.
- **Sugar ring:** a pyranose containing the ring oxygen, with an S-methyl thioether on the anomeric carbon. Two ring carbons carry OH groups.
- **Phosphate:** a phosphate monoester, –OP(=O)(OH)2, sits on the ring carbon next to the anomeric carbon.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H]1C[C@H](N(C1)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O2)SC)OP(=O)(O)O)O)O)[C@H](C)Cl

name: Clidinium Bromide
text:
The structure is clidinium bromide: a quaternary N-methyl quinuclidinium (1-azabicyclo[2.2.2]octane) ester of benzilic acid, with a bromide counterion.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Cation core:** The N⁺ carries a methyl group and three ring bonds. The ring carbon labelled "C" is just an explicit carbon. The three N-to-bridgehead paths each contain two carbons, so this is a bicyclo[2.2.2] system with N⁺ as one bridgehead and a CH as the other.
- **Ester position:** The O of the ester is attached to one of the bridge carbons, the one next to the CH bridgehead, in the path through the labelled "C".
- **Acyl group:** The ester is a C(=O) attached to a carbon bearing OH and two phenyl rings, which is the benzilate group.
- **Counterion:** Br⁻ is drawn separately.
- **Stereochemistry:** No wedges or hashes are shown, so none is included.

SMILES: C[N+]12CCC(CC1)C(OC(=O)C(O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)C2.[Br-]

name: Clioquinol
text:
The drawing is a quinoline: a pyridine ring fused to a benzene ring.

**Pyridine ring.** The atoms are N, then C (top right), C, C, and the two fusion carbons. N connects to the fusion carbon at (855,538) and, through a double bond, to the CH at (1345,398).

**Benzene ring.** Going round the ring:
- C8a is the fusion carbon at (855,538), bonded to N.
- C8 is at (570,465) and carries OH.
- C7 is at (365,676) and carries I.
- C6 is at (443,958) and is a CH.
- C5 is at (730,1030) and carries Cl.
- C4a is the fusion carbon at (935,820).

The pyridine ring continues from C4a to C4 at (1220,892), then C3 at (1425,682), C2 at (1345,398), and back to N.

**Double bonds.**
- N=C2
- C3=C4
- C4a=C8a
- C8=C7
- C6=C5

**SMILES.** Starting at N and tracing the ring: N1=CC=CC2=C1C(O)=C(I)C=C2Cl.

Checking the ring closures:
- N1=C is N=C2.
- C=C is C3=C4.
- C4 then connects to C4a, written as C2.
- C4a is double-bonded to C8a, written as =C1, which closes the ring to N.
- C8a connects to C8, written as C(O).
- C8 is double-bonded to C7, written as =C(I).
- C7 connects to C6, written as C, which is double-bonded to C5, written as =C2Cl.
- C5 closes the ring to C4a and carries Cl.

This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: N1=CC=CC2=C1C(O)=C(I)C=C2Cl

name: Clindamycin
text:
This looks like clindamycin, a lincosamide with a 4-propyl-N-methylpyrrolidine-2-carboxamide joined to a 7-chloro-methylthio-sugar. I confirmed only the 4R centre on the propyl-bearing pyrrolidine carbon from the drawing. The other stereocentres follow the standard clindamycin configuration rather than being checked one by one.

- **Pyrrolidine ring:** the ring N carries a methyl, and C4 carries a propyl group on a wedge.
- **Amide link:** a C(=O)–NH amide connects the ring to the side chain.
- **Chloro side chain:** the amide N is bonded to a CH that bears a CH(CH3)Cl group.
- **Sugar ring:** a pyranose ring (O, five carbons) carries an SCH3 at the anomeric carbon and three OH groups.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H]1C[C@H](N(C1)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)Cl)[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O2)SC)O)O)O

name: Clobazam
text:
The drawing shows a 1,5-benzodiazepine-2,4-dione (clobazam-type) skeleton, which I read as follows.

- The seven-membered ring contains N(CH3), C(=O), CH2, C(=O), N(Ph), and two fused aromatic carbons.
- The N-methyl nitrogen is on the left, bonded to the carbonyl carbon at the upper left and to the aromatic carbon at the lower left.
- The N-phenyl nitrogen is on the right, bonded to the carbonyl carbon at the upper right, to the phenyl ring, and to the aromatic carbon at the lower right.
- Chlorine is on the fused benzene ring, on the carbon para to the carbon bearing the N-methyl nitrogen. Going round the ring from the carbon attached to N-phenyl (call it C-a), the next carbon is CH, and the one after that carries Cl.

Writing the SMILES: CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

Checking the ring order: N1 (methyl) is bonded to the aromatic carbon c21, which is the last atom of the fused ring. The fused ring runs c2 (attached to N-phenyl), then c (CH), then c(Cl), then c, then c, then c21 (attached to N-methyl). This matches the drawing, where the carbon bearing N-phenyl is bonded to a CH, which is bonded to C-Cl.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

name: Clodronate
text:
The drawing shows clodronic acid (dichloromethylene bisphosphonic acid).

- A central carbon carries two Cl atoms, one drawn above and one below.
- Left and right of the carbon are two P atoms, each bonded to the carbon.
- Each P has one double-bonded O (=O) and two OH groups.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)C(Cl)(Cl)P(O)(O)=O

name: Clobutinol
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Amine end:** a nitrogen carries two methyl groups and a CH2 (N(C)(C)C).
- **Chain:** that CH2 connects to a CH bearing a methyl, which connects to a quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries a methyl, an OH, and a CH2 that links to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with a chlorine para to the CH2 attachment.

Written as SMILES: CN(C)CC(C)C(C)(O)Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1

Check on the quaternary carbon: it is bonded to the CH, a methyl (the line going down), OH, and the CH2, which gives four substituents. The CH has CH2N, a methyl, the quaternary carbon, and H, which also gives four. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CN(C)CC(C)C(C)(O)Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Clomethiazole
text:
The drawing shows a thiazole ring with three substituent features:

- The ring atoms are S, then CH, then N, then a carbon bearing a methyl group, then a carbon bearing the side chain, which closes back to S.
- The CH between S and N is joined to N by a double bond.
- The two ring carbons that carry substituents are joined by a double bond.
- The side chain on the carbon next to S is CH2CH2Cl.
- The methyl group sits on the carbon next to N.

Written as SMILES, starting from the methyl group: Cc1ncsc1CCCl. This gives the ring c1(C) n c s c1, with the CCCl chain on the carbon that closes the ring next to S. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ncsc1CCCl

name: Clobetasol Propionate
text:
I did not derive the stereocentres atom by atom. The connectivity below follows the drawing, and the stereo descriptors are the ones I recall from the PubChem entry for clobetasol propionate.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- **Core:** a steroid skeleton with a 1,4-dien-3-one A ring, a ketone at C3, and a double bond pair C1=C2 and C4=C5.
- **C9:** fluorine, drawn with a wedge.
- **C11:** hydroxyl, drawn with a hash.
- **C10 and C13:** methyl groups, both hashed.
- **C16:** methyl, hashed.
- **C17:** a propionate ester (–O–C(=O)CH2CH3) drawn with a wedge, plus a chloroacetyl side chain (–C(=O)CH2Cl).

**Stereochemistry check:** The molecule is drawn mirrored relative to the usual steroid orientation, with ring A on the right. In that view the fluorine is opposite the angular methyls, and the 11-OH and the 16-methyl are on the same face as them. The 17-ester is on the opposite face. This matches the 9α-F, 11β-OH, 16β-methyl, 17α-ester pattern of a betamethasone-type steroid, which is clobetasol propionate.

SMILES: CCC(=O)O[C@@]1([C@@H](C[C@@H]2[C@@]1(C[C@@H]([C@]3([C@H]2CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]43C)F)O)C)C)C(=O)CCl

name: Clofazimine
text:
This is clofazimine, a riminophenazine. The structure reads as follows.

- **Phenazine core:** N10 carries a 4-chlorophenyl group and is bonded to the benzo ring and to a carbon of the substituted ring. The other ring nitrogen is N5, which is double-bonded within the ring.
- **Substituted ring:** this ring has a C=N-isopropyl group (an imine carbon) and, on the adjacent carbon, an NH-(4-chlorophenyl) group.

I wrote the SMILES by following the atoms around the ring system.

1. Start with the isopropyl imine: CC(C)N=C1C=C2N(c3ccc(Cl)cc3)c3ccccc3N=C2C=C1Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1
2. Check the ring bonding. C1 (the imine carbon) is bonded to C=C2, where the carbon bearing N10 is C2. The ring then runs C1, C(H)=, C2 (attached to N10), the other fused carbon (=N5), CH=, and C(NHAr), which closes back to C1.
3. Check the double bonds. In the drawing, the imine carbon has a C=N double bond. The carbon next to it (the top CH) is double-bonded to the carbon attached to N10. The carbon attached to N5 is double-bonded to N5. The remaining CH is double-bonded to the C bearing NHAr.
4. The SMILES CC(C)N=C1C=C2N(Ar)c3ccccc3N=C2C=C1NAr satisfies this. The ring runs C1, =C (CH), C2, then through the fused carbon C2' (=N), then CH=C1' (the NHAr carbon), which closes to C1. The valences work out.

SMILES: CC(C)N=C1C=C2N(c3ccc(Cl)cc3)c3ccccc3N=C2C=C1Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Clomipramine
text:
This is clomipramine: an imipramine skeleton with a chlorine on one benzene ring.

**Reading the structure**
- The side chain is N(CH3)2–CH2CH2CH2–N, with the terminal dimethylamino nitrogen at the lower left.
- The ring nitrogen sits between two aromatic rings and carries the propyl chain.
- The two aromatic rings are bridged by a CH2–CH2 unit, making the seven-membered ring.
- Chlorine is on the upper ring, at the carbon para to the ring carbon attached to the CH2 bridge.

**Checking the chlorine position**
The upper ring atoms, with approximate coordinates, are:
- C1 (892,475): bonded to the CH2 bridge
- C2 (795,650): bonded to N
- C3 (595,653)
- C4 (492,480): bears Cl
- C5 (590,305)
- C6 (790,302)

C4 is para to C1 (C1→C2→C3→C4 is three bonds), so Cl is para to the CH2-bearing carbon and meta to the N-bearing carbon, as in clomipramine.

**Writing the SMILES**
Start from the chain: CN(C)CCCN1. The ring N then bonds to C2 of the chlorinated ring, giving c2cc(Cl)ccc2 with C1 as the last atom, which connects to CC (the bridge) and then to the lower ring.

Ring N1, then chlorinated ring: c2cc(Cl)ccc2, where the first c2 is C2 (bonded to N), then c is C3, c(Cl) is C4, then c C5, c C6, and c2 is C1. C1 then bonds to CH2CH2, then the lower aromatic ring: c3ccccc3 closing back to N1.

Full SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2cc(Cl)ccc2CCc2ccccc21

SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2cc(Cl)ccc2CCc2ccccc21

name: Clonazepam
text:
This is a 1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one with a 2-chlorophenyl group on C5 and a nitro group on the fused benzene ring (the drug clonazepam).

Reading the structure atom by atom:
- The seven-membered ring contains NH, a C=O carbon, a CH2, an N, and a C(=N) carbon attached to the 2-chlorophenyl ring. The last two ring members are the two fused benzene carbons.
- The NH is bonded to a fused benzene carbon at about (620, 568). The C5 carbon at about (753, 918) is bonded to the other fused carbon at about (770, 711).
- The nitro group sits on the carbon at about (1019, 451). The path from the carbon bearing NH is (620, 568) → (668, 366) → (868, 308) → (1019, 451, C-NO2) → (970, 653) → (770, 711). So the nitro carbon is para to the NH-bearing carbon: C(NH) → CH → CH → C(NO2) → CH → C(C5). That puts the nitro group para to the nitrogen-bearing carbon, which matches clonazepam.

SMILES: O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1

Check of the SMILES: the fused ring atoms are c2 (attached to C5), then cH, then c(NO2), cH, cH, and finally c2 attached to N1. The nitro carbon is therefore two atoms from the C5-attached carbon (c2, c, c(NO2)), so it is meta to the C5 carbon in the ring path. In the drawing, the C5-attached carbon (770, 711) is bonded to (970, 653), which is bonded to the nitro carbon (1019, 451). That makes the nitro carbon meta to the C5-attached carbon, which agrees with the SMILES.

SMILES: O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1

name: Chloroeremomycin
text:
This is my reading of the drawing as a vancomycin-type glycopeptide, in the chloroeremomycin pattern. It has an N-methyl-leucine at the N-terminus, an asparagine and a seven-residue cross-linked aryl core. The core carries two chlorines and a terminal COOH. A glucose–vancosamine disaccharide sits on the central ring, and a second vancosamine sits on the benzylic oxygen of the lower-right chlorotyrosine. The upper-left chlorotyrosine has a free benzylic OH.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds as drawn, using the 2D geometry around each centre. These assignments are hand-derived and not machine-checked, so they are the most likely source of error.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@@H](NC)C(=O)N[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@H](c4cc(Oc9c(Cl)cc(cc9)[C@H]1O)c(O[C@@H]8O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]8O[C@H]9C[C@](C)(N)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O9)c(Oc9c(Cl)cc(cc9)[C@H]6O[C@H]%12C[C@](C)(N)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O%12)c4)C(=O)N[C@H]5C(=O)N[C@@H]6C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)c7cc(O)cc(O)c7-c8cc5ccc8O

name: Clomiphene
text:
Reading the drawing gives a diethylaminoethoxy group (Et2N–CH2CH2–O–) on a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring is attached to a C=C double bond, whose other carbon carries a chlorine and a phenyl. The first alkene carbon also carries a second, unsubstituted phenyl. This is the clomiphene skeleton.

For the double-bond geometry, the drawing places the Cl and the alkoxyphenyl ring on the same side of the C=C. On the chlorine-bearing carbon, Cl outranks phenyl. On the other carbon, the alkoxyphenyl outranks phenyl because its para carbon bears an O. The two higher-priority groups are therefore cis, so the double bond is Z.

In the SMILES, `Cl/C(...)=C(\Ar)...` puts Cl and the alkoxyphenyl cis.

SMILES: Cl/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccc(OCCN(CC)CC)cc1)c1ccccc1

name: Clonidine
text:
The drawing is clonidine: a 2,6-dichlorophenyl ring joined through an NH to the 2-position of a 4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole (imidazoline) ring.

- **Imidazoline ring:** The ring atoms are NH, a CH2, a second CH2, an N, and a central carbon. The central carbon is double-bonded to the ring N (drawn without H) and single-bonded to the ring NH.
- **Linker:** The central carbon also carries an exocyclic NH that connects to the aromatic ring.
- **Aromatic ring:** The ring carbon bonded to the linker NH has a Cl on each adjacent carbon, which gives the 2,6-dichloro pattern.

Written as SMILES, the imidazoline ring is C1CN=C(N1)N..., and the aryl group is c1c(Cl)cccc1Cl.

SMILES: Clc1cccc(Cl)c1NC1=NCCN1

name: Clorindione
text:
The drawing shows a 1,3-indandione core: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring that carries two C=O groups. The carbon between the two carbonyls (C2) bears a 4-chlorophenyl group. This is chlorindione.

The ring-fusion carbons and the remaining benzo ring carbons are aromatic, and the para-substituted chlorophenyl ring is attached at C2. C2 is drawn with plain bonds and has an H, so it gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: O=C1C(c2ccc(Cl)cc2)C(=O)c2ccccc12

name: Clopidol
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring with one nitrogen, so it is a 4-pyridone.

- The ring atoms are N-H at the bottom, two C(CH3) carbons flanking it, two C(Cl) carbons next to those, and a C=O carbon at the top.
- Each carbon next to the nitrogen carries a methyl group.
- Each carbon next to the carbonyl carbon carries a chlorine.
- The ring has two C=C double bonds: the left C(Cl)=C(CH3) and the right C(Cl)=C(CH3). The top carbon has the C=O double bond.

Writing this out from the carbonyl carbon around the ring gives O=C1C(Cl)=C(C)NC(C)=C1Cl. The drawing shows no stereochemistry, so none is included.

SMILES: O=C1C(Cl)=C(C)NC(C)=C1Cl

name: Clorsulon
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents, plus a trichlorovinyl group.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- C1 at (660, 652) carries a sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)N.
- C2 at (845, 639) is CH.
- C3 at (948, 794) carries a second sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)N.
- C4 at (866, 961) carries NH2.
- C5 at (681, 974) is CH.
- C6 at (578, 819) carries the trichlorovinyl group, C(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl.

Going around the ring from C1, the substituents are:
- C1: SO2NH2
- C2: H
- C3: SO2NH2
- C4: NH2
- C5: H
- C6: C(Cl)=CCl2

The SMILES for this is NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)c(N)cc1C(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl.

Checking the ring: c1 (C1, with the first sulfonamide), c (C2, H), c(S(N)(=O)=O) (C3), c(N) (C4), c (C5, H), c1 (C6, with the vinyl group). This closes the ring and matches the drawing.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)c(N)cc1C(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl

name: Clotrimazole
text:
The drawing is clotrimazole. A central quaternary carbon carries two phenyl rings, a 2-chlorophenyl ring, and an imidazol-1-yl group attached through N.

- **Central carbon:** bonded to the three aryl rings and to the imidazole nitrogen.
- **Chlorophenyl ring:** the ring carbon attached to the central carbon is adjacent to the ring carbon bearing Cl, so the chlorine is ortho.
- **Imidazole:** N1 (the labelled N bonded to the central carbon) connects to a C that is double-bonded to N3, and to a second C that is double-bonded to a third C. Reading the ring, N1–CH=N3–CH=CH–N1 gives the imidazole.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: Clc1ccccc1C(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)n1ccnc1

name: Clozapine
text:
This structure is a dibenzodiazepine: a seven-membered ring fused to two benzene rings. It matches the clozapine skeleton.

**Left ring.** The chlorinated benzene carries Cl at the top left. Its fused carbons connect to the ring N (the imine N= side) and to the NH.

**Seven-membered ring.** The atoms run: aromatic C (upper left ring) – N= – C(piperazinyl) – aromatic C (right ring) – aromatic C (right ring) – NH – aromatic C (left ring).

**Right ring.** An unsubstituted benzene fused to the seven-membered ring.

**Substituent.** The amidine carbon bears an N-methylpiperazine.

**Chlorine position.** The left ring has Cl at the carbon meta to the imine-N-bearing carbon, which is para to the NH-bearing carbon. In the drawing, the ring carbon bonded to N= (at 481,606) is adjacent to the CH at 388,458, which is adjacent to the C–Cl at 214,465. So Cl is meta to the N= carbon and para to the NH carbon (399,760). This matches clozapine, where Cl is para to the NH.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2Nc2ccccc12

name: Clopidogrel
text:
I read this as clopidogrel, the methyl ester of 2-chlorophenyl(6,7-dihydrothieno[3,2-c]pyridin-5-yl)acetic acid.

- **Right side:** a methyl ester (O=C–OCH3) is attached to the stereocentre. The stereocentre also carries a 2-chlorophenyl ring.
- **Left side:** the stereocentre is bonded to the nitrogen of a tetrahydropyridine ring. That ring is fused to a thiophene. The CH2CH2 side of the piperidine ring joins the thiophene carbon next to S, and the N–CH2 side joins the other fusion carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the hashed bond runs from the stereocentre to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are N > C(=O)OMe > aryl > H.
  - In the drawing, N → ester → aryl runs clockwise. The H faces the viewer, so the sense reverses and the centre is S.
  - In SMILES, the neighbour order ester, H, aryl, N with `@` corresponds to S, so I used `[C@H]`.
  - This is the (S)-enantiomer, matching clopidogrel.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](c1ccccc1Cl)N1CCc2sccc2C1

name: Cloxacillin
text:
This structure is cloxacillin, a penicillin carrying a 3-(2-chlorophenyl)-5-methylisoxazole-4-carboxamide side chain.

- **Core:** a penam bicycle made of a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine. The thiazolidine carries a gem-dimethyl carbon next to S and a carboxylic acid on the carbon next to N.
- **Side chain:** an amide NH on the β-lactam carbon, acylated by an isoxazole. The isoxazole has a methyl on the carbon bonded to O and a 2-chlorophenyl on the carbon bonded to N.
- **Stereochemistry:** I checked the carboxylic-acid-bearing carbon against the drawing. With the COOH wedge toward the viewer and H pointing away, the SMILES chirality there matches. I did not check the other two stereocentres independently. I took them from the known natural penicillin configuration, which the drawn wedge and hash pattern appears to follow.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=NO1)C2=CC=CC=C2Cl)C(=O)N[C@H]3[C@@H]4N(C3=O)[C@H](C(S4)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Cobaltocene
text:
The drawing shows a cobalt(II) cation with a radical dot, written Co2+·, and two cyclopentadienyl anions drawn as separate fragments (cobaltocene drawn as ions).

Each ring is a five-membered ring with one C⁻ and four other carbons. Two double bonds are drawn, one on the top edge and one on the bottom edge. The left side of the ring is a single bond, and the bonds to C⁻ are single.

Tracing one ring: the C⁻ connects to the top carbon, which is double-bonded to the upper-left carbon. That carbon is single-bonded down to the lower-left carbon, which is double-bonded to the bottom carbon. The bottom carbon is single-bonded back to C⁻.

This gives the ring SMILES [CH-]1C=CC=C1.

Written as a three-component structure, with the cobalt carrying its charge and radical dot:

[Co+2] . [CH-]1C=CC=C1 . [CH-]1C=CC=C1

The radical dot on Co2+ is hard to encode, so I use [Co+2] without it.

SMILES: [Co+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.[CH-]1C=CC=C1

name: Clocortolone
text:
The drawing is a corticosteroid skeleton: a pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione with a 21-hydroxy-20-ketone side chain.

**Substituents**
- Ring A is a cross-conjugated dienone: C3 carries the C=O, with C1=C2 and C4=C5 double bonds.
- C6 carries F (wedge).
- C9 carries Cl (wedge).
- C11 carries OH (hash).
- C10 and C13 each carry a methyl (both hashed).
- C16 carries a methyl (wedge).
- C17 is a CH bearing the C(=O)CH2OH side chain (hash), so there is no 17-OH.
- C8 has H drawn hashed and C14 has H drawn wedged.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge/hash bonds and the 2D positions of its neighbours. The centres are C6, C8, C9, C10, C11, C13, C14, C16 and C17.

**Check:** I wrote the SMILES in the order side chain → ring D → ring C → ring B → ring A. Ring-closure digits 1 (C17–C13), 2 (C14–C13), 3 (C8–C9) and 4 (C5–C10) each open and close correctly.

SMILES: OCC(=O)[C@H]1[C@H](C)C[C@H]2[C@@H]3C[C@H](F)C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]4(C)[C@@]3(Cl)[C@@H](O)C[C@]12C

name: Codeine
text:
The drawing matches codeine. It shows a methoxy-substituted benzene ring fused to a dihydrofuran ring that carries an ether oxygen. It also has a cyclohexene ring with a wedged OH and a C=C double bond, and an N-methylpiperidine ring bridged across the core. The labelled "C" in the bottom ring is the CH2 benzylic carbon.

I did not derive the stereocentres independently from the wedges and hashes. I took them from the known isomeric SMILES for codeine, which fits the wedged OH and the hashed H atoms in the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4[C@H]1CC5=C2C(=C(C=C5)OC)O[C@H]3[C@H](C=C4)O

name: Cobicistat
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing; the molecule appears to be cobicistat. The stereo assignments come from the three wedge/hash centres in the drawing.

**Fragments read from the image**
- **Right end:** a 2-isopropylthiazol-4-yl group on a CH2, which is attached to N(CH3). That nitrogen carries a C(=O)NH urea.
- **Morpholine arm:** the urea NH sits on a stereocentre bearing CH2CH2–N-morpholine and a C(=O)NH amide.
- **Central chain:** that amide N is on a second stereocentre bearing CH2Ph and CH2CH2. The chain continues to a third stereocentre bearing CH2Ph and NH.
- **Left end:** that NH is a carbamate, NH–C(=O)–O–CH2, attached to a thiazol-5-yl ring (CH2 on the carbon next to S; ring written `c1cncs1`).

**Stereocentres**
- The carbon bearing the morpholinoethyl arm has the CH2 hashed, which gives `[C@@H]` as written.
- The carbon bearing CH2Ph on the amide N has the chain CH2 hashed, which gives `[C@H]`.
- The carbon bearing the carbamate NH has the chain CH2 wedged, which gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC(C)c1nc(CN(C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCN2CCOCC2)C(=O)N[C@H](CC[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)OCc2cncs2)Cc2ccccc2)cs1

name: Cobimetinib
text:
This structure is cobimetinib. I read it region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying iodine at the para position and fluorine at the ortho position relative to the NH link.
- **Central ring:** a benzene ring with the carbonyl carbon on one carbon, the anilino NH on the adjacent carbon, and two adjacent fluorines on the next two ring carbons.
- **Amide and azetidine:** the carbonyl is bonded to the nitrogen of a four-membered azetidine ring. The ring carbon opposite that nitrogen carries both an OH and the piperidine substituent.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring attached through its C2, which is next to the ring NH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is on the bond between the azetidine carbon and the piperidine C2. The azetidine carbon is not a stereocentre, because its two ring CH2 groups are equivalent. The wedge therefore defines the piperidine C2. With priorities N > azetidine C > ring CH2 > H, and the azetidine carbon toward the viewer, the sequence runs counterclockwise, giving S. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]1CCCCN1` with the azetidine carbon as the preceding atom encodes that S centre.

SMILES: O[C]1(CN(C1)C(=O)c1ccc(F)c(F)c1Nc1ccc(I)cc1F)[C@@H]1CCCCN1

I wrote the azetidine carbon as `[C]` by mistake in that line; the valid, corrected SMILES is:

SMILES: OC1(CN(C1)C(=O)c1ccc(F)c(F)c1Nc1ccc(I)cc1F)[C@@H]1CCCCN1

name: Clovibactin
text:
I read the molecule as a linear chain closed into a macrocyclic lactone.

**Chain, from the free N-terminus:**
- Phe: a free NH2 on the α-carbon, which bears a benzyl group (CH2-phenyl).
- Leu with an isobutyl side chain, drawn with a hashed bond.
- Lys with a (CH2)4NH2 side chain, drawn with a hashed bond.
- Ser with a CH2OH side chain, drawn with a wedge.
- A carbon bearing NH and C(=O), joined to a second carbon bearing an ester O and a C(=O)NH2 amide.

**Macrocycle:** The ring runs from the NH-bearing carbon through its C(=O)–NH–Ala(CH3), then C(=O)–NH–Leu, then C(=O)–NH–Leu, and finally C(=O)–O back to the ester-bearing carbon.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash, treating the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent.
- Phe, Ser, Ala and both ring Leu residues come out S.
- The two hashed chain residues (Leu and Lys) come out R.
- The two ring carbons bearing the amide and ester come out R.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closure and atom-for-atom agreement with the drawing.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O[C@H]1C(N)=O

name: Colchicine
text:
This structure is colchicine, read as follows.

- **Left side:** an acetamide group (CH3–C(=O)–NH) is attached to the stereocentre. The N bond is drawn as a wedge.
- **Middle:** a seven-membered ring contains the stereocentre and two CH2 groups. These link to the trimethoxy-substituted benzene ring on the right.
- **Right side:** the benzene ring carries three adjacent OMe groups.
- **Bottom left:** a seven-membered tropolone ring carries one C=O and one OMe. It is joined to the benzene ring by a biaryl bond.

Stereochemistry: the wedge puts N toward the viewer, so H points away. The priorities are N > ring carbon > CH2 > H. Going from N to the ring carbon to the CH2 runs counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S. The SMILES below encodes that with `[C@H]`, and I checked the neighbour order to confirm it gives S.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H]1CCc2cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c2-c2ccc(OC)c(=O)cc21

name: Cocaine
text:
The drawing shows a tropane-type bicycle: a pyrrolidine ring and a piperidine ring share an N-methyl bridge, so this is cocaine, the methyl ester and benzoate ester of ecgonine.

- **Core:** the N-methyl nitrogen bridges the two bridgehead carbons. One side is a two-carbon CH2–CH2 link and the other is a CH2–CH(OBz)–CH(CO2Me) link.
- **Substituents:** the carbon next to the bridgehead carries a methyl ester (C(=O)OCH3). The next carbon carries a benzoate ester (OC(=O)Ph).
- **Stereochemistry:** the four stereocentres come from the drawn hashes, which are the two bridgehead H's, the hashed ester carbon and the hashed benzoate oxygen. I assigned each centre from its drawn geometry and wrote the corresponding @/@@ in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@@H]1[C@H]2CC[C@@H](C[C@@H]1OC(=O)c1ccccc1)N2C

name: Colfosceril Palmitate
text:
I read this as a phosphatidylcholine with two saturated 16-carbon acyl chains (dipalmitoyl), a glycerol backbone, and a phosphocholine head group.

- **Chains:** counting vertices on each chain from the ester carbonyl carbon to the terminal methyl gives 16 carbons, so both are palmitoyl groups.
- **Head group:** the phosphate is drawn as P(=O)(O⁻) with an ester O to the glycerol CH2 and an ester O to the choline CH2CH2N⁺(CH3)3 unit.
- **Stereocentre:** the glycerol C2 carries the only hashed bond, going to the CH2 that bears the acyl ester.
  - The priorities are O-acyl > CH2OP > CH2O-acyl > H.
  - With the hashed CH2O-acyl group pointing away, the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - Reading O → CH2OP → CH2O-acyl on the page goes counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, that reverses to clockwise, which is R.
- **SMILES check:** `OC[C@H](COP…)OC(=O)…` encodes this R configuration when written starting from the CH2O-acyl carbon.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC[C@H](COP(=O)([O-])OCC[N+](C)(C)C)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCC

name: Congo red
text:
The image shows Congo red, the disodium salt of a bis-azo dye.

**Left naphthalene.** C1 carries NH2, C2 carries the azo group (N=N), C3 is CH, and C4 carries SO3⁻. The second ring is fused to this one.

**Centre.** A biphenyl is attached through its para positions to the two azo groups.

**Right naphthalene.** It mirrors the left one: the azo-bearing carbon is flanked by the NH2-bearing carbon (next to the ring fusion) and a CH, and the sulfonate carbon is next to that CH.

**SMILES, left to right.**
- Left naphthalene: `Nc1c(N=Nc2ccc(cc2)-c2ccc(cc2)N=Nc2cc(c3ccccc3c2N)S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(c2ccccc12)S(=O)(=O)[O-]`
- Right naphthalene: ring atoms are c2 (azo), c (CH), c(S) (sulfonate), then the fused benzo ring c3ccccc3, then c2N (the NH2-bearing carbon, bonded back to the azo carbon).
- Check on the right ring: the azo carbon is bonded to the CH and to C(NH2). The CH leads to C(SO3⁻), which joins the fused benzo ring. The benzo ring closes onto C(NH2), which closes back to the azo carbon. This is consistent.
- Check on the left ring: `Nc1c(N=N...)cc(S)c2ccccc12`. C1 has NH2, then the azo carbon, then CH, then C(S), then the fused ring, closing back to C1. This is consistent.

The two sodium ions are written as separate components.

SMILES: Nc1c(N=Nc2ccc(cc2)-c2ccc(cc2)N=Nc2cc(c3ccccc3c2N)S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(c2ccccc12)S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+].[Na+]

name: Copanlisib
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assembled the SMILES from that.

- **Left ring:** a 2-aminopyrimidine joined at C5 to a carbonyl (C=O).
- **Linker:** the carbonyl is bonded to an N that is double-bonded to the amidine carbon of the tricycle, giving an acyl-imine (C(=O)N=C).
- **Tricyclic core:** the amidine carbon is bonded to a ring N and to a second ring N. That second N is double-bonded to a benzo carbon. The ring N is also bonded to a CH2CH2NH bridge, and the NH carbon is double-bonded to the benzo carbon, forming a fused imidazoline ring.
- **Benzo ring substituents:** an OMe sits next to the ring fusion, then an O–CH2CH2CH2–morpholine (attached through N) on the adjacent carbon. The last two ring carbons are CH=CH.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: O=C(N=C1N=C2C(OC)=C(OCCCN3CCOCC3)C=CC2=C2NCCN12)c1cnc(N)nc1

name: Contezolid
text:
I read the molecule as four parts joined together.
