**Stereochemistry:** there are three stereocentres, each with one hashed bond and an implicit H toward the viewer. I worked out the @/@@ label for each from the 2D coordinates:
- the ring carbon bearing the carbonyl is `[C@@H]`
- the ring carbon bearing the vinyl group is `[C@H]`
- the cyano-bearing CH, written as `O[C@H](C#N)c1...`, is `[C@H]`

The SMILES below uses an atom order consistent with these assignments.

SMILES: O=C(O[C@H](C#N)c1cccc(Oc2ccccc2)c1)[C@@H]1[C@H](C=C(Br)Br)C1(C)C

name: Deldeprevir
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing, with stereochemistry taken from the wedges, hashes and the alkene geometry. It has not been checked with a toolkit.

- **Sulfonamide end:** an N-acyl cyclopropanesulfonamide, `C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)C1CC1`, attached to the quaternary cyclopropane carbon.
- **Macrocycle:** that quaternary carbon (which also bears the ring NH) and the neighbouring cyclopropane CH form a spiro-fused cyclopropane. A cis (Z) CH=CH follows, then five CH2 groups, then a stereocentre CH. That CH carries a CH2C(=O)-(3,3-difluoropiperidine) arm and the C(=O) that links to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine:** the ring bears an O-aryl group on one carbon and the C(=O)NH ring closure on the alpha carbon.
- **Aryl group:** a quinoline carrying an 8-methyl and 7-methoxy. Its 2-position is joined to a 4-isopropylthiazol-2-yl, and its 4-position is joined to the pyrrolidine oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned @/@@ at the quaternary cyclopropane carbon, the cyclopropane CH, the chain CH, and both pyrrolidine carbons from the wedge and hash bonds. The alkene is cis, written as `/C=C\`.

SMILES: O=C(NS(=O)(=O)C1CC1)[C@@]12C[C@H]1/C=C\CCCCC[C@H](CC(=O)N1CCCC(F)(F)C1)C(=O)N1C[C@H](Oc3cc(-c4nc(C(C)C)cs4)nc4c(C)c(OC)ccc34)C[C@H]1C(=O)N2

name: Demoxytocin
text:
I read this as deamino-oxytocin (a 3-mercaptopropionyl-capped analogue of oxytocin) with an S–S bridge and L-configured residues. I assigned stereochemistry from the L-amino-acid pattern rather than from each individual wedge or hash.

- **Ring:** the 3-mercaptopropionyl carbonyl (O=C1) connects through CH2–CH2–S–S–CH2 to the Cys α-carbon. The macrocycle then runs Cys → Asn → Gln → Ile → Tyr and closes back on the propionyl carbonyl.
- **Tail on Cys:** the Cys carbonyl is attached to Pro, then Leu, then Gly-NH2 (NCC(N)=O).
- **Side chains:**
  - Asn: CH2C(N)=O
  - Gln: CH2CH2C(N)=O
  - Ile: sec-butyl
  - Tyr: 4-hydroxybenzyl
  - Leu: isobutyl

I checked each stereo tag by permutation against the standard L-residue SMILES for Cys, Pro, Leu, Asn, Gln, Ile and Tyr.

SMILES: O=C1CCSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)NCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)N1

name: Deruxtecan pyrrole-2,5-dione
text:
I read this as a maleimidocaproyl–Gly-Gly-Phe-Gly linker joined through an NH–CH2–O–CH2–C(=O) spacer to an exatecan-type camptothecin core. This is the same layout as deruxtecan.

**Reading by region:**
- **Maleimide end:** a 2,5-dioxopyrrole ring whose nitrogen carries a five-carbon chain, then C(=O)NH (the caproyl amide).
- **Peptide chain:** the caproyl amide continues through Gly, Gly, Phe (benzyl side chain, hashed bond, which I read as L-Phe) and Gly, each joined by amide bonds.
- **Spacer:** the last Gly amide nitrogen is bonded to CH2–O–CH2–C(=O)NH.
- **Core:** the spacer amide nitrogen attaches, through a hashed bond, to the saturated ring carbon of the hexacyclic camptothecin-type system. The core also carries F and CH3 on the aromatic ring, the lactone with an ethyl group and a wedged OH at the quaternary carbon, and the pyridone C=O.

I did not derive the two core stereocentres independently from the wedge geometry. I took their SMILES labels from the known deruxtecan structure. I did check the Phe centre against L-Phe by permuting the neighbour order.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1n(c2=O)Cc2c-1nc1cc(F)c(C)c3c1c2[C@@H](NC(=O)COCNC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)CCCCCN1C(=O)C=CC1=O)CC3

name: Desflurane
text:
The drawing shows a difluoromethyl group (CHF2) on the left, bonded through an oxygen to a CHF carbon. That carbon is bonded to a CF3 group. This is desflurane.

Reading the atoms in order:
- The left carbon carries two fluorines and connects to the oxygen: FC(F)O.
- The oxygen connects to the middle carbon, which carries one fluorine and is attached to CF3: C(F)C(F)(F)F.

All bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included. The middle carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn without stereo marks.

SMILES: FC(F)OC(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Desferrithiocin
text:
The drawing shows the sodium salt of desferrithiocin, a 4-methyl-4,5-dihydrothiazole-4-carboxylate carrying a 3-hydroxypyridin-2-yl group at C2.

- **Thiazoline ring:** the ring runs S–CH2–C(quaternary)–N=C. The C=N double bond is between N and the carbon attached to the pyridine.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it bears the carboxylate (C(=O)[O⁻]), a methyl on a wedge bond, the ring CH2 and the ring N.
- **Pyridine ring:** it is attached through C2, its ring N is adjacent to that carbon, and the OH sits on the next carbon (C3).
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺.

**Stereochemistry:** the methyl is on a wedge, pointing toward the viewer. The other three substituents then run N (upper right), COO⁻ (upper left) and CH2 (down). Seen from the methyl side, N → COO⁻ → CH2 goes counterclockwise, which gives `@` for the neighbour order in the SMILES below.

As a check, the CIP priorities are N > CH2S > COO⁻ > CH3. With the methyl toward the viewer, N → CH2S → COO⁻ appears clockwise, so reversing it gives S, which matches the known (S)-desferrithiocin.

SMILES: [Na+].C[C@]1(C(=O)[O-])CSC(=N1)c1ncccc1O

name: Desipramine
text:
The drawing shows desipramine: a dibenzazepine core (two benzene rings joined by a CH2CH2 bridge and a ring nitrogen), with a three-carbon chain on that nitrogen ending in NHCH3.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Side chain:** a methyl group on NH, then three CH2 groups leading to the ring N. The chain runs from the methyl (75,1127) to NH (225,990), then C (411,1050), C (557,915), C (748,974), and finally N (895,840).
- **Core:** N is bonded to one aromatic carbon on each benzene ring. The upper ring carbon is at (835,648) and the lower ring carbon is at (1080,911).
- **Bridge:** the upper ring's other fusion carbon (947,483) connects through CH2 (1146,468) and CH2 (1282,615) to the lower ring's fusion carbon (1252,812). This makes the central ring 7-membered: N, two aromatic carbons on one side, two on the other, and the two CH2 groups.

SMILES: CNCCCN1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc12

SMILES: CNCCCN1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc12

name: Dersimelagon
text:
I read the molecule as two substituted pyrrolidines joined by an amide, with an aryl group and a piperidine acid on one side.

**Left half**
- The pyrrolidine nitrogen carries a cyclopentyl group.
- One ring carbon bears an aryl group, drawn with a wedge. The aryl is a 4-methoxyphenyl.
- The adjacent quaternary carbon bears a wedged fluorine and the amide carbonyl.

**Right half**
- The amide nitrogen sits in a second pyrrolidine.
- One ring carbon carries a CH2OMe group, drawn with a hash.
- The next ring carbon carries an aryl group, drawn with a wedge.
- That aryl is a benzene ring with a CF3 group para to the pyrrolidine attachment.
- The ring carbon ortho to the attachment bears the nitrogen of a piperidine-4-carboxylic acid.

**Stereochemistry**
I worked out the four stereocentres from the wedges and hashes and checked each against the neighbour order in the SMILES. Reading from the left: the aryl-bearing CH is `@@`, the fluorine-bearing carbon is `@@`, the CH2OMe carbon is `@`, and the right aryl-bearing CH is `@`.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)[C@@H]2CN(C3CCCC3)C[C@@]2(F)C(=O)N4C[C@H](COC)[C@H](C4)c5ccc(cc5N6CCC(CC6)C(=O)O)C(F)(F)F

name: Desoximetasone
Dalbavancin
text:
I read this as a dalbavancin-type lipoglycopeptide and wrote the SMILES by tracing the drawing. The stereocentre assignments come from reading the wedges and hashes by hand and were not machine-checked. The mannose C1 wedge is the least certain, because I assumed its narrow end sits at the ring carbon.

**Backbone.** Seven amino acid residues are linked head to tail.
1. Residue 1 is an N-methyl aryl-glycine whose ring has an OH and an aryl ether.
2. Residue 2 is a CH2-linked para-phenylene that is joined through its oxygen to ring D (residue 4).
3. Residue 3 is a chloro-hydroxyphenylglycine.
4. Residue 4 is a trioxygenated phenylglycine. Its ring carries the aryl ether to residue 2, the aryl ether to the chlorophenyl ring of residue 6, and the O-linked glucuronic acid.
5. Residue 5 is a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine joined by a biaryl bond to residue 7.
6. Residue 6 is a β-hydroxy chlorotyrosine.
7. Residue 7 is a 3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine carrying the O-linked mannose. Its C-terminus is a 3-(dimethylamino)propyl amide.

**Sugars and side chain.**
- The glucuronic acid carries a free COOH and an N-acyl group, the 10-methylundecanoyl chain, whose carbon count I checked on the drawing.
- The mannose is attached through the ring O of residue 7, and its CH2OH is drawn as a hashed bond.

SMILES: CN[C@H](c2ccc(O)c(c2)O%11)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc2ccc(cc2)O%12)C(=O)N[C@@H](c3c(Cl)c(O)cc%11c3)C(=O)N[C@H](c4cc%12c(O[C@@H]%16O[C@H](C(=O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]%16NC(=O)CCCCCCCCC(C)C)c%13c4)C(=O)N[C@H](c5ccc(O)c%14c5)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](O)c6ccc(O%13)c(Cl)c6)C(=O)N[C@@H](c7c%14c(O[C@H]%15O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]%15O)cc(O)c7)C(=O)NCCCN(C)C

name: Deslorelin
text:
Reading the drawing, this is the linear decapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑Trp‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt, with the second Trp (position 6) drawn as the D‑isomer. This is the deslorelin sequence.

**Residues, N‑ to C‑terminus:**
- pyroglutamic acid, drawn as a 5‑membered lactam
- His, with the imidazole attached through the carbon next to the NH
- Trp, an indol‑3‑yl side chain
- Ser
- Tyr, a 4‑hydroxyphenyl side chain
- Trp, an indol‑3‑yl side chain
- Leu
- Arg, with a free guanidine
- Pro, with the C‑terminus as the N‑ethyl amide

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash by checking the N → C(=O) → side‑chain direction.
- pGlu, His, Trp2, Ser, Tyr, Leu, Arg and Pro all come out L.
- Trp6, drawn with a downward wedge, comes out D.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1cnc[nH]1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC

name: Desvenlafaxine Succinate
text:
The image shows three separate components, which I read as follows.

1. **Succinic acid** (top): HO–C(=O)–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–OH, written OC(=O)CCC(=O)O.
2. **Desvenlafaxine** (bottom): a dimethylamino group on CH2, attached to a CH that carries a 4-hydroxyphenyl ring and a 1-hydroxycyclohexyl group. This is CN(C)CC(c1ccc(O)cc1)C1(O)CCCCC1. The cyclohexane ring has 6 vertices: the quaternary carbon plus 5 CH2 groups.
3. **Water**: shown as OH2, written O.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC(=O)O.CN(C)CC(c1ccc(O)cc1)C1(O)CCCCC1.O

name: Deslanoside
text:
This is a digoxigenin-type cardenolide with a four-sugar chain on the 3-OH. I read the stereochemistry from the drawing and then cross-checked it against the known digoxin SMILES, so it is partly from memory rather than fully derived from the wedges and hashes.

- **Aglycone:** a steroid core with a butenolide (the unsaturated five-membered lactone) at C17, 12-OH, 14-OH, and methyls at C10 and C13. This is digoxigenin.
- **Sugar chain at C3:** three 2,6-dideoxy-hexose (digitoxose) units joined in a row through their 4-O positions, each with a free 3-OH.
- **Terminal sugar:** a glucose attached through O to C4 of the outermost digitoxose.

Together these match deslanoside, which is digoxin with a terminal glucose on the sugar chain. I took the digoxin stereodescriptors for the aglycone and the three digitoxoses. For the glucose I rewrote the standard β-D-glucopyranoside stereo so that it starts from the anomeric carbon.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@@H]2[C@H](O[C@H](C[C@@H]2O)O[C@@H]3[C@H](O[C@H](C[C@@H]3O)O[C@H]4CC[C@]5([C@@H](C4)CC[C@@H]6[C@@H]5C[C@H]([C@]7([C@@]6(CC[C@@H]7C8=CC(=O)OC8)O)C)O)C)C)C)O)O[C@@H]9O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]9O

name: Deucravacitinib
text:
This structure matches deucravacitinib (BMS-986165), with a CD3 group on the amide nitrogen.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Cyclopropane amide:** a cyclopropyl ring attached to C(=O)NH, which is bonded to the pyridazine ring.
- **Pyridazine ring:** C(NHC(=O)cPr)=N–N=C(C(=O)NHCD3)–C(NHAr)=CH–. In the image, the carbon at 262,600 carries the amide NH and is bonded to N (at 160,705). That N connects to a second N (at 200,845), which bonds to the carbon at 342,880 bearing the C(=O)NHCD3 group. The next carbon, at 441,775, carries the NH-aryl group, and the CH at 402,635 closes the ring back to the first carbon.
- **Central benzene ring:** the NH is on one carbon, the OMe on the adjacent carbon, and the triazole on the carbon next to that.
- **Triazole:** the ring carbon attached to the benzene is bonded to N (at 1120,805) and to N (at 1180,585). The ring is C3(=N–N(C)–C=N3), so the 1-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl group.

SMILES for the triazole: c1(nn(C)cn1) is written as c1ncn(C)n1 with the attachment at c1. Here the attached carbon is bonded to N=, which bonds to N(CH3), then to CH, then to N, and back to the attached carbon. That gives c1nn(C)cn1.

Full SMILES: O=C(C1CC1)Nc1cc(Nc2cccc(-c3nn(C)cn3)c2OC)c(C(=O)NC([2H])([2H])[2H])nn1

Check on the pyridazine: c1 (NHCO-cPr), then cH, then c(NHAr), then c(C(=O)N...), then n, then n closing to c1. That is 6 atoms: c, c, c, c, n, n. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(C1CC1)Nc1cc(Nc2cccc(-c3nn(C)cn3)c2OC)c(C(=O)NC([2H])([2H])[2H])nn1

name: Desmopressin
text:
I read this as a desmopressin-type cyclic nonapeptide. The ring is closed by a disulfide between a deamino-Cys (S–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–) and a Cys. The ring runs Tyr, Phe, Gln, Asn, then Cys. The tail is Pro, Arg (with a guanidine side chain), then Gly-NH2.

Stereochemistry, read from the wedges and hashes (CIP assignments in parentheses):
- The Arg centre has a bold wedge to the side chain, which gives R, so this is D-Arg.
- The Pro centre is S, as in L-Pro.
- The Cys centre is R, as in L-Cys.
- Tyr, Phe, Gln and Asn each come out S, as in the L-amino acids.

I checked the ring size, side-chain lengths and heteroatom labels against the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H]2CSSCCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc3ccc(O)cc3)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc4ccccc4)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N2

name: Deuruxolitinib
text:
This is ruxolitinib-d8: the (R)-3-(cyclopentyl)-3-(pyrazol-1-yl)propanenitrile core carrying the pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine, with eight deuteriums on the cyclopentyl ring.

- **Heteroaromatic part:** a 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine (pyrimidine fused to a pyrrole with an NH) is attached at its C4 position to C4 of a pyrazole ring.
- **Linker:** the pyrazole N1 is bonded to a stereocentre. That carbon also bears a CH2–C≡N arm, drawn on a wedge, and the cyclopentyl ring.
- **Cyclopentyl ring:** eight ²H labels are shown, two on each of the four CH2 carbons. The ring carbon attached to the stereocentre keeps its ordinary H.
- **Stereochemistry:** the priorities at the stereocentre are N (pyrazole) > cyclopentyl C > CH2CN > H. With the CH2CN on a wedge and H pointing back, N → cyclopentyl → CH2 runs clockwise, so the centre is R. I took the known R-ruxolitinib SMILES `N#CC[C@@H](C1CCCC1)n1cc(cn1)-c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12` as a reference. In my SMILES the pyrazole N and the cyclopentyl C come in the opposite order, so the chirality tag flips to `@`.

SMILES: N#CC[C@H](n1cc(cn1)-c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12)C1C([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])C1([2H])[2H]

name: Deutivacaftor
text:
This is a deuterated ivacaftor (d9): a 4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline-3-carboxamide attached through the amide N to a di-tert-butyl hydroxyphenyl ring. One tert-butyl group is fully deuterated (nine D) and the other is an ordinary tert-butyl.

**Aryl ring.** Reading the ring atoms in order:
- C1 carries the NH.
- C2 carries the plain tert-butyl, on the lower left of C1.
- C3 is an aromatic CH.
- C4 carries the deuterated tert-butyl.
- C5 carries the OH, at the top.
- C6 is an aromatic CH, between C5 and C1.

The OH is therefore ortho to the deuterated tert-butyl and meta to the NH. The plain tert-butyl is ortho to the NH. This matches ivacaftor, whose ring is 5-hydroxy-2,4-di-tert-butylphenyl.

**Quinolone.** The amide carbon attaches to C3 of the quinolone. C4 is the ketone, and C2 is the CH next to the ring NH.

**SMILES.** Written from the amide N: the aryl ring starts at c1 (bearing N), then c(C(C)(C)C) for the plain tert-butyl, then cc for the CH, then the deuterated tert-butyl carbon, then the OH carbon, then the last CH.

Aryl part: `Nc1cc(O)c(C([2H])...)cc1C(C)(C)C`. In this ordering, c1 (N) is followed by a CH, then c(O), then c(tBu-d9), then a CH, then c1 carrying the plain tBu. That puts the plain tBu ortho to N, and the OH meta to N across the CH (N-bearing C1, CH, C-OH), which agrees with the analysis above.

Full SMILES: `O=C(Nc1cc(O)c(C([2H])([2H])... )cc1C(C)(C)C)c1c[nH]c2ccccc2c1=O`, with the deuterated tert-butyl written as `C(C([2H])([2H])[2H])(C([2H])([2H])[2H])C([2H])([2H])[2H]`.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1cc(O)c(C(C([2H])([2H])[2H])(C([2H])([2H])[2H])C([2H])([2H])[2H])cc1C(C)(C)C)c1c[nH]c2ccccc2c1=O

name: Deuterated L-leucine
text:
I read this as leucine with every carbon-bound hydrogen replaced by deuterium (leucine-d10). The nitrogen and the acid OH are drawn as NH2 and OH, so they stay protium.

- **Backbone:** the alpha carbon carries NH2, COOH, a hashed ²H, and a CD2 group.
- **Side chain:** the CD2 is bonded to a CD carbon, which bears two CD3 groups. That gives an isobutyl side chain, so the amino acid is leucine.
- **Deuterium count:** 1 on the alpha carbon, 2 on CD2, 1 on CD and 6 on the two CD3 groups, which totals 10.
- **Stereochemistry:** the ²H on the alpha carbon is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. With the CIP priorities N > COOH > CH2 > ²H, the sequence N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise. That makes the centre S, the same as L-leucine.
- **SMILES:** in L-leucine written as `CC(C)C[C@H](N)C(=O)O`, replacing the implicit H with `[2H]` keeps the neighbour order, so `[C@]([2H])(N)` keeps the S configuration.

SMILES: [2H]C([2H])([2H])C([2H])(C([2H])([2H])[2H])C([2H])([2H])[C@]([2H])(N)C(=O)O

name: Destruxin A
text:
I read the structure as a 19-membered macrocycle containing a depsipeptide (ester plus amide) backbone. Going around the ring, the pieces are:

1. An O-linked CH carrying an allyl group, drawn with a hashed bond.
2. An ester C(=O) leading to a CH2CH2 unit and then an NH. This is a β-alanine-type unit.
3. An N-methyl alanine residue, with its methyl on a wedge.
4. An N-methyl valine residue, with its isopropyl on a wedge.
5. An isoleucine residue whose N is on a wedge and whose sec-butyl CH has a hashed methyl.
6. A proline residue with a hashed H, closing back onto the allyl-bearing CH through its N-acyl carbonyl.

I assigned each stereocentre by working out the clockwise or counterclockwise order of its neighbours in the drawing and converting that to @ or @@ in the SMILES atom order. Because I wrote the SMILES in the opposite direction round the ring from the way I listed the residues above, I checked the connectivity again against the drawing. The sequence is ester O, C(=O), CH2CH2, NH, Ala, N-Me-Val, Ile, Pro, then back to the allyl CH.

SMILES: C=CC[C@H]1OC(=O)CCNC(=O)[C@H](C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@@H]2CCCN2C1=O

name: Dexamethasone
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-diene-3-one steroid (ring A on the right) with 9-fluoro, 11-hydroxy, 17-hydroxy, a 17-hydroxyacetyl side chain (C(=O)CH2OH), and methyl groups at C10, C13 and C16.

The ring system is drawn mirror-flipped relative to the usual steroid layout (ring A on the right, ring D on the left). That reverses the usual wedge/hash reading, so I read the stereochemistry in the flipped frame:

- The C13 and C10 methyls are hashed, which corresponds to β.
- 17-OH, 9-F and the C16 methyl are wedged, which corresponds to α.
- 11-OH and 8-H are hashed (β), and 14-H is wedged (α).

A 16α-methyl with 9α-fluoro and 11β-hydroxy is the pattern of dexamethasone, not its 16β epimer betamethasone. I wrote the SMILES from this assignment, matching it to the known dexamethasone stereochemistry rather than deriving each centre's @/@@ from scratch.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@]1(C(=O)CO)O)C)O)F)C

name: Dexmedetomidine
text:
The drawing shows a 2,3-dimethylphenyl ring and a 1H-imidazol-4-yl ring joined through a CH(CH3) carbon, which is the structure of medetomidine. The stereocentre carries a wedged methyl, so stereochemistry is included.

**Connectivity**
- The benzene ring has two adjacent methyl groups. One is at the carbon next to the ring carbon bearing the side chain, and the other is at the next carbon along.
- The imidazole ring has an NH and a ring N, and it is attached to the stereocentre through a ring carbon next to the NH.
- The stereocentre carries the wedged methyl, the aryl ring, the imidazole ring and an implicit H.

**Stereochemistry**
- CIP priorities: imidazolyl carbon (N,C,C) > aryl carbon (C,C,C) > methyl > H.
- The methyl is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer.
- Viewed from the front, the sequence imidazole (lower left), then aryl (right), then methyl (up) runs counterclockwise. With H at the back, that is S.
- This matches dexmedetomidine, the (S)-enantiomer. I wrote the chirality tag from the known dexmedetomidine SMILES rather than deriving the @ symbol from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](c1cccc(C)c1C)c1cnc[nH]1

name: Dexpanthenol
text:
Reading the drawing, I get the following.

- **Left end:** a quaternary carbon carries two methyl groups and a CH2OH group.
- **Stereocentre:** the quaternary carbon is bonded to a CH carbon with a wedged OH. This is the only stereocentre drawn with a wedge.
- **Amide:** the CH carbon is bonded to a C(=O) that is joined to an NH.
- **Right end:** the NH is bonded to a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) ending in OH.

Together these describe a panthenol-type structure.

For the stereochemistry, I viewed the wedged centre with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer. The neighbours then run quaternary C, then OH, then C=O in a clockwise direction. Writing the SMILES as `CC(C)(CO)[C@@H](O)C(=O)NCCCO`, the neighbour order is quaternary C, H, O, C=O, and `@@` matches that clockwise arrangement.

SMILES: CC(C)(CO)[C@@H](O)C(=O)NCCCO

name: Di((2H3)methyl) sulphoxide
text:
The drawing shows dimethyl sulfoxide with every hydrogen labelled as the ²H isotope, so it is DMSO-d6.

- Sulfur sits in the centre and is double-bonded to an oxygen below it.
- Two carbons are attached to the sulfur, one on each side.
- Each carbon carries three ²H atoms, six in total.

Written as SMILES, each deuterated methyl group is `[2H]C([2H])([2H])`, joined through `S(=O)`.

SMILES: [2H]C([2H])([2H])S(=O)C([2H])([2H])[2H]

name: Detirelix
text:
I read the structure from the N-terminus to the C-terminus as a linear peptide, and assigned each α-carbon from its wedge or hash bond.

**Sequence as drawn:**
1. N-terminal acetyl group on D-2-naphthylalanine (R at the α-carbon).
2. D-4-chlorophenylalanine (R).
3. D-tryptophan, with the indole attached through its 3-position (R).
4. L-serine (S).
5. L-tyrosine (S).
6. A D-lysine-type residue (R) whose side chain is four CH2 groups ending in N=C(NHEt)NHEt, a bis-ethylguanidine.
7. L-leucine (S).
8. L-arginine (S), with its free guanidine.
9. L-proline (S).
10. D-alanine (R) with a C-terminal primary amide.

For the SMILES, an L residue is written `N[C@@H](R)C(=O)` and a D residue `N[C@H](R)C(=O)`. I checked each α-carbon against the drawing by working out the sense of N→C(=O)→side chain relative to the wedge or hash, and each matched the assignment above. Proline was written as `N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)`, which I checked gives S.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCN=C(NCC)NCC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(N)=N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(N)=O

name: Diatrizoate
text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with six substituents, which I read as follows.

Ring atoms, going around: C1 (bottom right, 987,942) carries COOH. C2 (1081,742) carries I. C3 (956,561) carries NHAc. C4 (736,579) carries I. C5 (641,779) carries NHAc. C6 (767,960) carries I.

So the ring runs COOH, I, NHAc, I, NHAc, I. This is a 2,4,6-triiodo-3,5-diacetamidobenzoic acid (diatrizoic acid).

Each NHAc group is drawn as N–C(=O)–CH3.

SMILES, starting from the carboxylic acid carbon:
OC(=O)c1c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c1I

Check: c1 (COOH), then c(I), then c(NHAc), then c(I), then c(NHAc), then c1I. This matches the ring order above.

SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c(I)c(C(=O)O)c1I

name: Dexrazoxane
text:
The drawing shows dexrazoxane: two piperazine-2,6-dione rings, each joined through its ring nitrogen to a CH(CH3)–CH2 linker.

- **Rings:** each ring has a ring N, two C=O groups flanking an NH, and two CH2 groups. This gives N1CC(=O)NC(=O)C1 for each ring.
- **Linker:** one ring N is bonded to the stereocentre CH(CH3), and the other ring N is bonded to the adjacent CH2.
- **Stereocentre:** the methyl group is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CH2N > CH3 > H.
  - On the page, N (upper left) → CH2 (right) → CH3 (lower left) runs clockwise.
  - Because H faces the viewer, the sense reverses, so the centre is S.
- **SMILES chirality:** for the written order C[C?H](CN…)N…, the symbol @@ corresponds to S.

SMILES: C[C@@H](CN1CC(=O)NC(=O)C1)N1CC(=O)NC(=O)C1

name: Diabzi sting agonist-1
text:
I read this as a symmetric-looking dimer: two benzimidazole units joined through an N-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-N linker.

- **Top-right unit:** a benzimidazole with a 7-methoxy group and a 5-carboxamide (CONH2). Its C2 carries an NH-C(=O) amide to a 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazol-5-yl group.
- **Bottom-left unit:** the same benzimidazole and pyrazole amide, but the 7-substituent is O-CH2CH2CH2-morpholine, attached through the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Linker:** the two ring N1 atoms are joined by CH2-CH=CH-CH2. The two CH2 groups sit on opposite sides of the double bond in the drawing, so it is trans (E).

I wrote the SMILES from this reading and checked it atom for atom against the drawing.

SMILES: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OC)c2n1C/C=C/Cn1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCCCN3CCOCC3)c21

name: Diazepam
text:
The drawing shows diazepam, a 1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one core.

- **Seven-membered ring:** N1 carries a methyl group and is bonded to the carbonyl carbon C2 (C=O). C2 connects to the CH2 (C3), then to N4, which is double-bonded to C5. C5 bears the phenyl group and is attached to the fused benzene ring.
- **Fused benzene ring:** The carbon bonded to N1 is C9a. The next ring carbon, going away from the phenyl-bearing C5, is C9, then C8, then C7 (bearing Cl), then C6, then C5a, which is attached to C5. Following the drawing from the carbon bonded to N, the path runs to the lower-left carbon, then the bottom carbon, then the Cl-bearing carbon, then the upper-right carbon, and finally the carbon attached to C5.
- **Pendant phenyl:** An unsubstituted phenyl ring is attached to C5.

SMILES, written as N-methyl, then C(=O), CH2, N=C(Ph), then the fused ring back to N:

CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

Atom-by-atom check of the fused ring: c2 (C5a, attached to C5), c (C6), c(Cl) (C7), c (C8), c (C9), c21 (C9a, closing to N1). This matches the drawing, where the Cl carbon is two atoms from C5a through the CH at the upper right, and the ring-closing carbon bonded to N is next to the lower-left carbon.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

name: Dibenzepin
text:
The drawing shows a dibenzodiazepinone: a seven-membered ring fused to two benzene rings, and containing two nitrogens and one carbonyl carbon.

**Ring atoms.** Starting from the carbonyl carbon C(=O), the seven-membered ring runs: C(=O) → aromatic carbon of the upper benzene ring → the adjacent aromatic carbon of that ring → N(CH3) → aromatic carbon of the lower benzene ring → the neighbouring aromatic carbon of that ring → N(CH2CH2N(CH3)2) → back to C(=O).

**Substituents.**
- The N on the right carries a methyl group.
- The N on the left, next to the carbonyl, carries a CH2CH2N(CH3)2 chain.

**SMILES construction.**
- Chain and ring start: CN(C)CCN1C(=O)c2ccccc2N(C)c2ccccc21
- The carbonyl carbon is attached to the upper benzene ring. Its first ring carbon, c2, bonds to C(=O), and the last ring carbon of that ring, written c2 before N(C), bonds to N-methyl.
- N(C) then attaches to the lower ring carbon c2, which runs ccccc2 and closes on the carbon bonded to N1. I wrote that closing carbon as "c21" so it also closes ring 1 to N1.

I checked the lower ring: the carbon bonded to N-methyl and the carbon bonded to N1 are adjacent, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)CCN1C(=O)c2ccccc2N(C)c2ccccc21

name: Dibenzo-18-crown-6
text:
The drawing is a macrocycle with two benzene rings fused into it and six ring oxygens, which matches dibenzo-18-crown-6.

**Ring oxygens (six):**
- top O at (748, 325)
- upper left O at (380, 540)
- upper right O at (1118, 540)
- lower left O at (380, 965)
- lower right O at (1118, 965)
- bottom O at (748, 1175)

**Connectivity around the macrocycle:**
- The top O joins two CH2 carbons. The left one leads through another CH2 to the upper left O, and the right one leads through another CH2 to the upper right O.
- The upper left O attaches to the left benzene carbon at (330, 675). That ring carbon is bonded to the one at (330, 825), which carries the lower left O. These two are adjacent aromatic carbons.
- The lower left O is followed by CH2, CH2, then the bottom O, then CH2, CH2, then the lower right O.
- The lower right O attaches to the right benzene carbon at (1168, 825). That carbon is bonded to the one at (1168, 675), which carries the upper right O.

**SMILES:** I write the macrocycle starting from the top O, going around the left side, and closing back to the right side.

O1CCOc2ccccc2OCCOCCOc3ccccc3OCC1

Checking this string atom by atom:
- O1, then CC, then O, then the aromatic ring c2ccccc2 (the two attachment carbons are adjacent), then O, CC, O, CC, O, then the second ring c3ccccc3, then O, CC, and ring closure to O1.
- Counting the macrocycle: O1, C, C, O, c, c, O, C, C, O, C, C, O, c, c, O, C, C is 18 atoms, closing to O1. That is correct for an 18-membered ring.
- Ordering around the ring: top O – CC – O(upper left) – Ar – Ar – O(lower left) – CC – O(bottom) – CC – O(lower right) – Ar – Ar – O(upper right) – CC – back to the top O. This matches the string.

SMILES: O1CCOc2ccccc2OCCOCCOc3ccccc3OCC1

name: Dibenzofuran
text:
The drawing shows dibenzofuran. It has a central five-membered ring made of one oxygen and four carbons. The two carbons bonded to oxygen are fused to two benzene rings. The other two carbons of the five-membered ring are joined to each other by a single bond.

Each benzene ring has six carbons, so the molecule has 12 carbons and one oxygen.

I wrote the SMILES by starting at the oxygen, going through the left ring, and closing back through the right ring:

c1ccc2c(c1)oc1ccccc12

Atom-by-atom check:
- c1 is the first ring atom, followed by c and c, then c2, a fusion carbon.
- c(c1) is the other fusion carbon, with c1 closing the left benzene ring. That ring is c1, c, c, c2, c, c1, which is six atoms.
- The fusion carbon c(c1) is bonded to o, and o is bonded to c1 (a new ring label 1), the first carbon of the right ring.
- Continuing c c c c gives four more carbons, and c12 closes both rings. The right ring is c1, c, c, c, c, c12, which is six atoms.
- Ring closure 2 bonds the last carbon to the first fusion carbon, which gives the C–C bond in the five-membered ring. That ring is c2, c, o, c1, c12, which is five atoms.

SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)oc1ccccc12

name: Dibenzothiophene
text:
The drawing shows dibenzothiophene: two benzene rings fused to a central five-membered ring that contains one sulfur atom.

The central ring has S, two aromatic carbons that bond to S (one from each benzene ring), and two carbons joined by the bond between the rings.

Each benzene ring has six carbons, so the molecule has 12 carbons and one sulfur.

Writing it as an aromatic SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)sc1ccccc12.

Checking the ring closures:
- `c1ccc2c(c1)` opens ring 1, then ring 2, and the `(c1)` closes the first benzene ring after six atoms: c1, c, c, c2, c, c1.
- `s` follows the branch carbon, so that carbon bonds to sulfur.
- `c1ccccc12` starts a new ring 1 with six atoms, and the last atom closes ring 1 and ring 2, bonding to the first benzene's c2 atom.

SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)sc1ccccc12

name: Dibrospidium Chloride
text:
The drawing shows a tri-ring system: two piperazine-type rings joined through a central ring, with two spiro quaternary nitrogens, and two chloride counterions (this resembles pipobroman-derived "prospidium"-like structures).

Reading the rings:
- Left ring: N(acyl), CH2, CH2, N+, CH2, CH2, closing back to the acyl N. This is a piperazinium.
- Central ring: the two N+ atoms are linked by two separate CH2CH2 bridges. Top: N+ – CH2 – CH2 – N+ (left N+ to right N+). Bottom: the same. So the central ring is a piperazine-1,4-diium with both nitrogens spiro.
- Right ring: N+, CH2, CH2, N(acyl), CH2, CH2, back to the N+.

Each acyl nitrogen carries C(=O)CCBr, a 3-bromopropanoyl group.

SMILES for the left N-acyl ring and left spiro N+: BrCCC(=O)N1CC[N+]2(CC1)CC[N+]3(CC2)CCN(C(=O)CCBr)CC3

Check: N1 – C – C – [N+]2, then (CC1) closes the left ring with 2 carbons. Next, from [N+]2, CC leads to [N+]3 and then CC2 back to the first N+, which gives the central ring: N+2, C, C, N+3, C, C, back to N+2 (6-membered, correct). Then [N+]3 continues with CCN(...)CC3, which is the right ring.

Chlorides: [Cl-].[Cl-]

SMILES: BrCCC(=O)N1CC[N+]2(CC1)CC[N+]3(CC2)CCN(C(=O)CCBr)CC3.[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Dibekacin
text:
This is my best reading of the drawing. I matched the connectivity to the picture, but I recalled the stereodescriptors from the known compound rather than deriving each one from the wedges and hashes, so they are unverified.

The molecule is a 2-deoxystreptamine core (a cyclohexane carrying two NH2 groups and one OH) with two sugar rings attached through ether oxygens:

- **Left ring:** a pyranose with a ring oxygen, two OH groups, one NH2 and a CH2OH. This is a 3-amino-3-deoxyglucose unit.
- **Right ring:** a tetrahydropyran with a ring oxygen, an NH2 on the carbon next to the anomeric carbon, two CH2 groups, and a CH2NH2 on the carbon next to the ring oxygen. This is a 2,6-diamino-2,3,4,6-tetradeoxyglucose unit.
- **Core attachment:** the right-ring oxygen sits on a core carbon between a C–NH2 and a C–OH. The left-ring oxygen sits on a core carbon between the other C–NH2 and the same C–OH.

This connectivity matches dibekacin (3',4'-dideoxykanamycin B).

SMILES: C1C[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1N)O[C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]2O)O[C@@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)N)O)N)N)CN

name: Dibenzo(ghi,mno)fluoranthene
text:
The drawing shows 20 ring carbons: a central five-membered ring surrounded by five fused six-membered rings. That is corannulene (C20H10). Every carbon sits in a ring, there are no heteroatoms or substituents, and there are no stereocentres.

I labelled the vertices and traced the bonds to confirm the ring fusion. The five-membered ring consists of the five inner carbons, and each of its five edges is shared with one of the five outer hexagons. Neighbouring hexagons share a bond with each other. The drawn double bonds give each carbon exactly one double bond, so a valid Kekulé structure exists and the aromatic SMILES is consistent with it.

I wrote the SMILES in aromatic form. Its ring closures reproduce the central five-membered ring (atoms 16 to 20 in the string) and the five surrounding hexagons.

SMILES: c1cc2ccc3ccc4ccc5ccc1c6c2c3c4c56

name: Dibutyltin dilaurate
text:
The image shows dibutyltin dilaurate: a central tin atom bonded to two n-butyl groups and two laurate (dodecanoate) groups through oxygen.

- **Butyl groups:** each chain attached to Sn has 4 carbons, so each is CCCC.
- **Laurate groups:** counting the left chain from the carbonyl carbon to the terminal methyl gives 12 carbons, with the carbonyl (C=O) bonded to an O that is bonded to Sn. The right chain has the same pattern.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O[Sn](CCCC)(CCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC

name: Dichlorvos
text:
The drawing shows dichlorvos (2,2-dichlorovinyl dimethyl phosphate).

- A phosphorus atom carries one double-bonded O (P=O) and two methoxy groups (OCH3).
- A third oxygen links phosphorus to a CH=CCl2 group. The double bond is between the CH and the carbon bearing both chlorines.
- The CCl2 end of that double bond has two identical substituents, so there is no cis/trans stereochemistry to specify.

SMILES: COP(=O)(OC)OC=C(Cl)Cl

name: Dichlorphenamide
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents: two chlorines and two sulfonamide groups.

Ring atoms, read from the image:
- C1 at (813, 535) carries Cl.
- C2 at (985, 664) carries Cl.
- C3 at (959, 878) carries SO2NH2.
- C4 at (761, 962) is CH.
- C5 at (589, 832) carries SO2NH2.
- C6 at (615, 619) is CH.

Going around the ring, C1 and C2 (both Cl) are adjacent. C3 (sulfonamide) follows, then C4 (CH), then C5 (sulfonamide), then C6 (CH), which closes back to C1. The two sulfonamides are therefore meta to each other, and the two chlorines are ortho to each other.

Written as SMILES starting at C1: Clc1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)cc(S(N)(=O)=O)c1Cl

Checking this against the ring: Cl on C1, then c (C6, CH), then c(SO2NH2) (C5), then c (C4, CH), then c(SO2NH2) (C3), then c1Cl (C2), which closes to C1. This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: Clc1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)cc(S(N)(=O)=O)c1Cl

name: Dextromethorphan
text:
I read the skeleton as a 3‑methoxy‑17‑methylmorphinan, the same ring system as dextromethorphan/levomethorphan, though the drawing is laid out unusually. I traced the atoms and rings one by one, then assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges and hash.

**Skeleton**
- **Aromatic ring:** six carbons with alternating double bonds, carrying an OMe group on the carbon at the top right.
- **Aromatic attachments:** one ring carbon is bonded to the quaternary carbon, and the adjacent aromatic carbon is bonded to a CH2.
- **Piperidine ring:** N(CH3) joins a CH2–CH2 chain that leads to the quaternary carbon. The N also bonds to a CH that carries an H wedge.
- **Middle ring:** the N‑bearing CH is bonded to a CH2 that attaches to the aromatic ring, and to a second CH that carries an H wedge. That second CH is bonded to the quaternary carbon.
- **Cyclohexane ring:** the quaternary carbon and the second CH are joined through four CH2 groups.

**Stereochemistry**
- Both CH–H bonds are drawn as wedges.
- The quaternary carbon has a hashed bond to the CH2 of the CH2–CH2–N chain.
- Working out the chirality from the 2D geometry gives `[C@@]` for the quaternary carbon, `[C@@H]` for the N‑bearing CH and `[C@H]` for the other CH, in the atom order of the SMILES below.

**Check:** the SMILES has three rings besides the aromatic one (piperidine, the ring closed through the CH2 on the aromatic ring, and the cyclohexane), all closed correctly.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)[C@@]34CCN(C)[C@@H](C2)[C@H]3CCCC4

name: Diclofenac sodium
text:
The drawing shows diclofenac sodium.

- **Right ring:** a benzene ring carries a CH2–C(=O)O⁻ group and, on the adjacent carbon, an NH.
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring is attached to the NH through a carbon whose two neighbouring carbons each carry a Cl (2,6-dichloro).
- **Counterion:** a separate Na⁺.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)Cc1ccccc1Nc1c(Cl)cccc1Cl

name: Diclofenac
text:
The drawing shows diclofenac, read as follows:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with a Cl on each carbon next to the carbon bonded to NH, so the substituent pattern is 2,6-dichloro.
- **Linker:** an NH connects the left ring to the right ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring bearing, ortho to the NH, a CH2 group attached to a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH).

SMILES: OC(=O)Cc1ccccc1Nc1c(Cl)cccc1Cl

name: Dichlororuthenium;2-pyridin-2-ylpyridine
text:
The image shows three separate 2,2'-bipyridine molecules and one Cl–Ru–Cl unit, with no bonds between the fragments.

Each bipyridine is drawn in a Kekulé form. Starting at the ring nitrogen, the SMILES is C1=CC=NC(=C1)... Written out as two linked rings, this gives c1ccnc(c1)-c1ccccn1. I use the Kekulé version to match the drawing.

Reading the top-left ring: N is double-bonded to the CH at the upper left (N=C). That CH is single-bonded to the next CH. That CH is double-bonded to the CH at the lower left, which is single-bonded to the CH at the bottom, and so on. The ring atoms in order are N, C(top-left), C(left), C(bottom-left), C(bottom-right), C2 (the carbon attached to the other ring).

- N=C: the double bond between N and the top-left carbon.
- C–C: the bond from the top-left carbon to the left carbon is single.
- C=C: the left carbon is double-bonded to the bottom-left carbon.
- C–C: the bottom-left carbon is single-bonded to the bottom-right carbon.
- C=C: the bottom-right carbon is double-bonded to the carbon attached to the other ring, C2.
- C2–N: that carbon is single-bonded back to N.

The SMILES for one ring is therefore N1=CC=CC=C1-, and the bipyridine is C1=CC=NC(=C1)... Using the explicit form, the ring is C1(=NC=CC=C1)... and the linked unit is:

C1=CC=NC(=C1)C1=NC=CC=C1

Here the second ring is N=C... Checking the right ring: N is double-bonded to the upper-right carbon, and the carbon attached to the other ring (C2) is double-bonded to the bottom-left carbon. So the right ring contributes C2=CC=CC=N2? In that ring C2 is single-bonded to N, with the double bond going to the CH. That gives C1(=CC=CC=N1)... which has N=C and C2=C in the right pattern. This is consistent with the drawing.

The final SMILES for the whole image is three bipyridines plus Cl[Ru]Cl:

SMILES: C1=CC=NC(=C1)C1=NC=CC=C1.C1=CC=NC(=C1)C1=NC=CC=C1.C1=CC=NC(=C1)C1=NC=CC=C1.Cl[Ru]Cl

name: Diclazuril
text:
The drawing shows diclazuril.

- **Nitrile and central carbon:** a nitrile (N≡C) is attached to a CH carbon. That CH carries a 4-chlorophenyl ring and a 2,6-dichlorophenyl ring.
- **Dichlorophenyl ring:** the carbon bonded to the CH sits between two chlorine-bearing carbons. The carbon para to it is bonded to the triazine nitrogen.
- **Triazine ring:** the ring runs N1 (attached to the aryl group), then N=CH, then C(=O), then NH, then C(=O), closing back to N1. This is a 1,2,4-triazine-3,5-dione.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: N#CC(c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1c(Cl)cc(cc1Cl)-n1ncc(=O)[nH]c1=O

I wrote the triazine with an aromatic lowercase "c(=O)" form, which RDKit may or may not accept as valid. A safer Kekulé form is below.

SMILES: N#CC(c1ccc(Cl)cc1)C1=C(Cl)C=C(C=C1Cl)N1N=CC(=O)NC1=O

name: Dicoumarol
text:
The image shows dicoumarol: two 4-hydroxycoumarin units joined through their 3-positions by a CH2 bridge.

Each coumarin unit is a benzene ring fused to a lactone ring. In the lactone ring, C4 carries the OH and is double-bonded to C3. C3 bears the CH2 bridge and is bonded to C2, the carbonyl carbon (C=O), which is attached to the ring oxygen. That oxygen connects to the benzene ring at C8a.

The SMILES for one unit, written from the CH2 bridge, is C3(=C(O)c4ccccc4OC3=O). The full molecule is:

OC1=C(Cc2c(O)c3ccccc3oc2=O)C(=O)Oc2ccccc12

Checking the atoms: C1(O)=C(...)C(=O)Oc2ccccc12 gives C4(OH)=C3–C2(=O)–O–C8a, then the benzene ring closing back to C4a, which matches the drawing. The other half, c2c(O)c3ccccc3oc2=O, is the same coumarin written aromatically: c2 is C3, c(O) is C4, c3ccccc3 is the benzene ring, o is the ring oxygen, and c2=O is the carbonyl carbon. Written aromatically, that half is valid.

SMILES: OC1=C(Cc2c(O)c3ccccc3oc2=O)C(=O)Oc2ccccc12

name: Dicyclohexano-18-crown-6
text:
This is dicyclohexano-18-crown-6. The macrocycle contains 6 oxygens, and two cyclohexane rings are fused to it, one on the left and one on the right.

Reading the macrocycle clockwise from the top O:
- The top O (at 750,325) connects to CH2 CH2, then to the right-upper O (1118,540).
- That O connects to the ring carbon C (1168,675) of the right cyclohexane, which connects to the other ring carbon (1168,825).
- That carbon connects to the lower-right O (1118,965), then CH2 CH2, then the bottom O (750,1175).
- The bottom O connects to CH2 CH2, then the lower-left O (380,965).
- That O connects to the left ring carbon (330,825), then the other left ring carbon (330,675).
- That carbon connects to the upper-left O (380,540), then CH2 CH2, and back to the top O.

The macrocycle has 6 O, 8 CH2 and 4 ring carbons, which makes 18 atoms in total, as expected for an 18-crown-6.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: C1CCC2C(C1)OCCOCCOC3CCCCC3OCCOCCO2

SMILES: C1CCC2C(C1)OCCOCCOC3CCCCC3OCCOCCO2

name: Dicloxacillin
text:
I read this as dicloxacillin: a penicillin core (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring) carrying a gem-dimethyl group and a carboxylic acid. The amide side chain is a 5-methylisoxazole bearing a 2,6-dichlorophenyl group.

I did not independently derive the stereo tags from the wedges and hashes. I used the standard natural-penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R) from the known dicloxacillin SMILES, since the drawing shows a wedged H at the S–CH–N carbon, a hashed amide N at C6, and a wedged COOH at C3. I only partly checked this against the drawing.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=NO1)C2=C(C=CC=C2Cl)Cl)C(=O)N[C@H]3[C@@H]4N(C3=O)[C@H](C(S4)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Dicyclomine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows a diethylaminoethyl ester of a carboxylic acid whose alpha carbon carries two cyclohexyl groups, drawn with HCl as a separate component.

**Amine end:** two ethyl groups on N, then N–CH2–CH2–O. This gives CCN(CC)CCO.

**Ester carbonyl:** O is bonded to C(=O), and that carbon is bonded to a ring carbon.

**Ring system:** the carbon attached to the carbonyl sits in a six-membered ring with 5 other carbons. The vertices at (1143,735), (1035,596), (1100,432), (1273,408), (1383,546) and (1318,710) make up this ring. That carbon also bears a second cyclohexyl group, whose ring vertices at (1198,902), (1370,937), (1424,1105), (1307,1236) and (1135,1200) with (1080,1032) make up a six-membered ring. The first ring is therefore a cyclohexane with a spiro-like quaternary carbon bearing the other ring as a substituent, so the acid part is 1,1'-bi(cyclohexyl)-1-carboxylic acid.

The whole molecule is the hydrochloride salt, written as a second component, Cl.

Quaternary carbon: C1(C(=O)O...)(C2CCCCC2)CCCCC1.

Full SMILES: CCN(CC)CCOC(=O)C1(CCCCC1)C1CCCCC1.Cl

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCOC(=O)C1(CCCCC1)C1CCCCC1.Cl

name: Dideoxycytidine
text:
The drawing shows a cytosine base joined through N1 to a 2′,3′-dideoxyribose ring, which is the structure of zalcitabine (ddC).

- **Base:** the six-membered ring has a C=O at C2, ring N3 double-bonded to C4, C4 bearing NH2, and a C5=C6 double bond leading back to N1.
- **Sugar:** the five-membered ring is O, C1′ (carrying N1), two CH2 groups, and C4′ (carrying CH2OH). It has no hydroxyls on C2′ or C3′.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are two wedges, one on the C1′–N bond and one on the C4′–CH2OH bond. Reading each centre with its implicit H pointing away from the viewer gives @@ for both in the SMILES order used below.

SMILES: OC[C@@H]1CC[C@@H](O1)N2C=CC(N)=NC2=O

name: Didanosine
text:
The drawing shows didanosine (2',3'-dideoxyinosine): a hypoxanthine base attached through N9 to a 2',3'-dideoxyribose ring.

- **Sugar ring:** a five-membered ring with one ring oxygen and three carbons. The CH2OH carbon is C4′, followed by two CH2 groups (C3′ and C2′), then C1′ bonded to the ring oxygen.
- **Base:** a purine. The imidazole ring has N9 attached to the sugar, then CH=N, then the fused carbons. The six-membered ring has C=O and an N–H, with the other N as =N–CH=. This is hypoxanthine.
- **Stereochemistry:** two wedges are drawn, one on the CH2OH bond at C4′ and one on the C1′–N bond. Reading the neighbour order and the wedge direction at each centre gives @@ for both in the SMILES below.

SMILES: OC[C@@H]1CC[C@@H](O1)n1cnc2c1nc[nH]c2=O

name: Diethylpropion Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows a phenyl ketone, PhC(=O)CH(CH3)N(Et)2, drawn together with a separate HCl label.

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with three double bonds, attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- **Chain:** the carbonyl carbon is bonded to a CH that carries a methyl group and the nitrogen.
- **Nitrogen:** N bears two ethyl groups and is neutral. HCl is drawn as a separate component.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all its bonds are plain, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(C)C(=O)c1ccccc1.Cl

name: Diethylstilbestrol
text:
This is diethylstilbestrol, the E isomer of 4,4'-(hex-3-ene-3,4-diyl)diphenol.

- Two para-substituted benzene rings each carry an OH. The OH labels are at the far left and far right of the drawing.
- The central C=C has one ethyl group and one 4-hydroxyphenyl group on each alkene carbon.
- Geometry: the two aryl groups lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the aryls are trans. Because each carbon carries one aryl and one ethyl, the ethyls are trans too. This is the E configuration.

The SMILES below writes the ethyls as trans, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC/C(c1ccc(O)cc1)=C(/CC)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Dienestrol
text:
I read the drawing as a conjugated diene, CH3–CH=C(Ar)–C(Ar)=CH–CH3, where each Ar is a 4-hydroxyphenyl ring. This is the dienestrol skeleton.

- **Aryl rings:** Each ring has six carbons with an OH on the carbon para to the attachment point to the chain.
- **Core:** The two central carbons are joined by a single bond, and each carries one aryl ring.
- **Double bonds:** Each central carbon is double-bonded to a CH that ends in a CH3.
- **Geometry:** From the coordinates, on both double bonds the terminal CH3 and the aryl ring on the neighbouring carbon lie on the same side. The other central carbon is therefore on the opposite side from each CH3.

I encoded this as `C/C=C(\Ar)/C(=C/C)Ar`. I checked that the bond marks agree: the CH3 and the other central carbon are trans on the left double bond, and the same holds on the right one.

SMILES: C/C=C(\c1ccc(O)cc1)/C(=C/C)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Difamilast
Difenacoum
text:
This structure is the 4-hydroxycoumarin core of bromadiolone and difenacoum, here with a 3-substituent. The substituent is a tetralin carrying a biphenyl group, so this is difenacoum.

**Coumarin part:** 4-hydroxycoumarin, with the ring O attached to a benzene ring and a C=O next to it. The C3 carbon bears the tetralin substituent.

**Tetralin part:** the CH attached to C3 of the coumarin is bonded to an aromatic carbon of the fused benzene ring. The ring then runs through the other fused aromatic carbon, a CH2, and a CH that carries the biphenyl-4-yl group, then another CH2 back to the first CH. That gives the six-membered ring C1(coumarin)–CH2–CH(Ar)–CH2–Ar–Ar.

**Stereochemistry:** the drawing uses plain bonds throughout, so no stereo is written.

**SMILES check:**
- Coumarin with tetralin: `O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1C1CC(c2ccc(-c3ccccc3)cc2)Cc2ccccc12`
- Ring closure 1 is reused after the first ring closes, which is valid.
- The tetralin ring is `C1 C C(Ar) C c2ccccc12`. The final aromatic atom closes both the benzene ring (2) and the tetralin ring (1), and it is bonded to the first CH. This is correct.

SMILES: O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1C1CC(c2ccc(-c3ccccc3)cc2)Cc2ccccc12

name: Dictyostatin
text:
I read the structure as a macrolactone ring with a (Z)-buta-1,3-dienyl-bearing side chain on the ring carbon attached to the ring oxygen.

**Ring, starting at the lactone carbonyl and going round:**
1. C(=O), then the ring O closes the lactone at the far end.
2. CH=CH, a cis (Z) double bond.
3. CH=CH, a trans (E) double bond.
4. CH(CH3), methyl on a wedge.
5. CH(OH), OH on a wedge.
6. CH2.
7. CH(OH), OH on a hash.
8. CH=CH, a cis (Z) double bond.
9. CH(CH3), methyl on a hash.
10. CH(OH), OH on a hash.
11. CH(CH3), methyl on a wedge.
12. CH2.
13. CH(CH3), methyl on a wedge.
14. CH2, then CH2.
15. CH(OH), OH on a wedge.
16. CH(CH3), methyl on a hash.
17. CH(O–), the ring-oxygen bond on a hash.

**Side chain on the last ring carbon:** CH(CH3) with the methyl on a hash, then CH=CH (Z), then CH=CH2.

I assigned each @/@@ by reading the wedge or hash at that carbon, with the implicit H on the opposite face. I took the double-bond geometries from the relative positions of the substituents in the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1/C=C\C=C\[C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)C[C@H](O)/C=C\[C@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)C[C@@H](C)CC[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O1)[C@@H](C)/C=C\C=C

name: Difetarsone sodium anhydrous
text:
The drawing shows two para-substituted benzene rings joined through an NH–CH2–CH2–NH linker. Each ring carries an arsonic acid group on the carbon opposite the nitrogen. Each arsenic has one =O, one OH and one O⁻. Two Na⁺ ions are drawn separately.

Reading the pieces:
- Left arsenic: As(=O)(O)[O-]
- Left ring: para-disubstituted benzene, with the arsenic on one end and NH on the other.
- Linker: NH–CH2–CH2–NH, each CH2 plain.
- Right ring and arsenic: the same as the left.
- Counterions: [Na+].[Na+]

The SMILES, written with the sodium ions as separate fragments, is:

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O[As]([O-])(=O)c1ccc(NCCNc2ccc([As](O)([O-])=O)cc2)cc1

name: Dieldrin
text:
I read the structure as a hexachloro-substituted polycyclic skeleton with an epoxide, which matches the dieldrin/endrin framework.

**Atoms and connectivity:**
- The left ring has a C=C double bond, and each alkene carbon carries one Cl.
- Two bridgehead carbons each carry one Cl, drawn with hashed bonds.
- A one-carbon bridge between those two bridgeheads is a CCl2 carbon.
- The centre of the drawing has two CH carbons, each with a hashed H.
- The right side has two further bridgehead CH carbons with wedged H, joined by a CH2 bridge.
- The far right is an epoxide: two CH carbons with hashed H, bridged by an O.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash and its neighbour order in the SMILES string below.

**Check of the string:** Ring-closure labels 1 to 5 are each opened and closed once, and the string accounts for all six Cl atoms, the O, and the C=C double bond.

SMILES: ClC1=C(Cl)[C@]2(Cl)[C@@H]3[C@@H]4C[C@@H]([C@H]5O[C@@H]45)[C@@H]3[C@@]1(Cl)C2(Cl)Cl

name: Diflunisal
text:
The structure is diflunisal: a salicylic acid ring joined to a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring.

**Left ring.** Going around the ring from the carboxylic acid:
- The carbon at (400,727) carries the COOH group.
- The carbon at (350,902) carries OH, ortho to the COOH.
- Next are the carbons at (475,1033) and (652,990).
- The carbon at (703,815) carries the aryl substituent.
- The carbon at (577,684) closes the ring back to the COOH carbon.

The aryl-bearing carbon is therefore para to the OH (the ring positions run COOH-C, OH-C, CH, CH, C-aryl, CH).

**Right ring.** Going around the ring from the biaryl bond:
- The carbon at (880,772) is attached to the left ring.
- The carbon at (1005,903) carries F, ortho to the biaryl carbon.
- The carbon at (1182,860) is CH.
- The carbon at (1233,685) carries F, para to the biaryl carbon.
- The carbons at (1107,554) and (930,597) are CH.

**SMILES.** OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1O)-c1ccc(F)cc1F

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(-c2ccc(F)cc2F)ccc1O

name: Difelikefalin
text:
I read the molecule as a linear pentapeptide-like chain: Phe, Phe, Leu, Lys, then a 4-aminopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid whose ring nitrogen is acylated by the Lys carbonyl.

**Connectivity**
- The top-right Phe has a free NH2 on its alpha carbon and a benzyl side chain. Its carbonyl is bonded to the NH of the second Phe.
- The second Phe carries a second benzyl group and its carbonyl is bonded to the Leu NH.
- Leu has an isobutyl side chain (CH2–CH(CH3)2) and its carbonyl is bonded to the Lys NH.
- Lys has a four-carbon chain ending in NH2, and its carbonyl is bonded to the piperidine nitrogen.
- The piperidine ring has six vertices (one N, five C). The carbon opposite the nitrogen carries both NH2 and COOH.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each alpha carbon from its wedge or hash bond using CIP priorities (N > C=O > side-chain CH2 > H):
- Phe 1 has a wedged NH2 and comes out R.
- Phe 2 has a hashed CH2 and comes out R.
- Leu has a wedged CH2 and comes out R.
- Lys has a hashed CH2 and comes out R.

All four are D-configured. For this atom ordering (N written first, then H, side chain, C=O), R corresponds to `@`. The piperidine quaternary carbon has two identical ring arms, so it is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N1CCC(N)(C(=O)O)CC1

name: Didemnin B
text:
I read the structure as a 25-atom macrocyclic depsipeptide with a lactyl-Pro-N-Me-Leu side chain. I did not identify it by name. I transcribed it atom by atom and assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Macrocycle, starting at the ester O on the CH(CH3) carbon and going around:**
- O–C(=O) of an N-methyl-O-methyltyrosine, whose CH carries a CH2–C6H4–OMe group on a wedge.
- Its N(CH3) is acylated by the proline carbonyl; the proline ring N is acylated by Leu.
- The Leu NH is acylated by C(=O)–CH(CH3)–C(=O), a methyl-bearing carbon with a hashed methyl followed by a ketone.
- Next is CH(iPr)–O, with the isopropyl on a wedge, then O–C(=O)–CH2–CH(OH), with the OH on a wedge.
- Then CH(sec-butyl) with a hashed methyl, then NH–C(=O)–CH(NH–side chain)–CH(CH3)–O, which closes the ring.

**Side chain:** NH–C(=O)–CH(isobutyl)–N(CH3)–C(=O)–proline, with the proline N acylated by lactyl, C(=O)–CH(CH3)OH.

I derived each @/@@ from the drawn coordinates, treating the implicit H as pointing opposite to the wedge or hash on that centre.

SMILES: C[C@H]1OC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(OC)cc2)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H]2CCCN2C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)OC(=O)C[C@H](O)[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@H]1NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@H](C)O

name: Difluprednate
text:
The drawing shows difluprednate, a 6α,9-difluoroprednisolone 17-butyrate 21-acetate. I read these features from the image:

- **A-ring:** a cross-conjugated 1,4-dien-3-one (C=C–C(=O)–C=C) with the C10 methyl drawn as a hashed bond.
- **6-position:** a fluorine on a wedge bond.
- **9-position:** a fluorine on a wedge bond.
- **11-position:** a hydroxyl on a hashed bond.
- **C-ring and D-ring:** the C13 methyl is hashed, the H at C14 is a wedge, and the H at C8 is hashed.
- **C17:** an O-butyrate ester (CCCC(=O)O–) on a wedge bond, plus a C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH3 side chain, which is the 21-acetate.

I did not derive each @/@@ label independently from the wedges. I took the stereo string from my recollection of the standard difluprednate SMILES, so the stereodescriptors rest on that recall rather than on a centre-by-centre check against the drawing.

SMILES: CCCC(=O)O[C@@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(C[C@@H]([C@]3([C@H]2C[C@@H](C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]43C)F)F)O)C)C(=O)COC(=O)C

name: Dihydroartemisinin
text:
The drawing matches dihydroartemisinin, so I wrote its SMILES from the structure's connectivity and took the stereodescriptors from the known compound rather than deriving each one from the wedges.

Reading the image:
- A cyclohexane ring on the left carries a hashed methyl.
- It is fused to a six-membered lactol ring, which has a wedged methyl and a wedged OH next to the ring oxygen.
- A bridging seven-membered ring contains the peroxide O–O and a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl and an ether oxygen.
- The chain C–C–C links the ring-fusion carbon to the methyl-bearing quaternary carbon.

I did not check the wedge/hash directions against each stereocentre independently, so the stereo marks (including the epimeric OH) rest on the known dihydroartemisinin structure.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@H]([C@H](O[C@H]3[C@@]24[C@H]1CC[C@](O3)(OO4)C)O)C

name: Diflucortolone Valerate
text:
I read this as diflucortolone valerate: a 1,4-dien-3-one steroid with 6α,9α-difluoro, 11β-hydroxy, 16α-methyl, a 17-side chain C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)(CH2)3CH3 (a pentanoate ester), and methyl groups at C10 and C13.

The stereochemistry comes from a mix of the drawing and recalled reference structures, so it is not fully derived from the image alone:

- **Ring scaffold and C6:** I took the stereocentres on the ring scaffold from a recalled dexamethasone SMILES. I checked the drawn 6-F wedge, 9-F wedge, 11-OH hash, 10- and 13-methyl hashes, 16-methyl wedge and 17-side-chain hash against that frame, and they are consistent with the natural steroid. I worked out the C6 centre from the drawn wedge and set it to match.
- **C17:** I removed the 17-OH from the dexamethasone SMILES and kept the same configuration at C17.
- **Ester chain:** Counting the drawn chain gives four carbons after the carbonyl, which is a pentanoate (valerate) ester.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3C[C@H](F)C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@H]1C(=O)COC(=O)CCCC)C)O)F)C

name: Dihydroergotamine
text:
This structure is 9,10-dihydroergotamine, an ergot alkaloid. I identified it from the overall skeleton and then wrote the SMILES from memory of the known compound, so the stereodescriptors are taken from that recalled SMILES. I did not independently re-derive each wedge or hash from the drawing.

The parts I read from the image:
- **Ergoline core:** an indole fused to a tetrahydropyridine ring that carries an N-methyl group. The 9,10 bond is saturated, with a hashed H at the carbon next to N and a wedged H at the ring-fusion carbon.
- **Linker:** a carboxamide (C(=O)NH) on the piperidine ring, attached through a hashed bond.
- **Peptide-derived cage:**
  - A quaternary carbon bearing a methyl group, the amide NH and an ether oxygen, and also bonded to a C(=O).
  - That C(=O) is bonded to a ring N.
  - The ring N is bonded to a benzyl-bearing CH.
  - The CH is bonded to a second C(=O), which is bonded to the proline N.
  - A hemiaminal carbon carries the OH (wedged) and the ether O.
  - A pyrrolidine ring is fused through the proline carbon, which has a hashed H.

SMILES: CN1C[C@@H](C[C@H]2[C@H]1CC3=CNC4=CC=CC2=C34)C(=O)N[C@]5(C(=O)N6[C@H](C(=O)N7CCC[C@H]7[C@@]6(O5)O)CC8=CC=CC=C8)C

name: Digoxin
text:
This is a digoxin-type cardiac glycoside. I assigned the constitution from the drawing and the stereochemistry by comparison with digoxin, so the stereo descriptors are inferred rather than read atom by atom from the wedges.

**Constitution**
- The aglycone is a steroid with the usual four fused rings, with a methyl on C10 and on C13.
- There are hydroxyls at C12 and C14.
- C17 carries a butenolide (2(5H)-furanone) ring.
- The C3 oxygen is linked to a chain of three 2,6-dideoxy sugars (digitoxose units). Each unit is a pyranose with a ring CH2 next to the anomeric carbon, a 3-OH and a 5-methyl.
- The two inner sugars are linked through their 4-oxygen. The terminal sugar has free 3-OH and 4-OH groups.

**Stereochemistry**
- Relative to digoxin's natural configuration, every drawn stereocentre is inverted. The C10 and C13 methyls, the C14-OH and the C17 butenolide are hashed, and the C9-H is wedged, which is the opposite of the natural configuration.
- I therefore took the digoxin SMILES and inverted every @/@@. I did not independently verify each sugar centre against the wedges, only the steroid ones.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@@H]([C@@H](C[C@H](O1)O[C@H]2[C@@H](O[C@@H](C[C@H]2O)O[C@H]3[C@@H](O[C@@H](C[C@H]3O)O[C@@H]4CC[C@@]5([C@H](C4)CC[C@H]6[C@H]5C[C@@H]([C@@]7([C@]6(CC[C@H]7C8=CC(=O)OC8)O)C)O)C)C)C)O)O

name: Diisopropyl Fluorophosphate
text:
The drawing shows a phosphorus atom with four substituents: a fluorine, a double-bonded oxygen (P=O), and two oxygens that each carry an isopropyl group (CH(CH3)2). This is diisopropyl fluorophosphate. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)OP(=O)(F)OC(C)C

name: Dimercaprol
text:
The drawing shows a three-carbon chain. Starting from the left, HO is bonded to CH2, then to a central CH carrying an SH group, then to a second CH2 that carries another SH. This is 2,3-dimercaptopropanol (dimercaprol).

The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all bonds are drawn plain, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: OCC(S)CS

name: Dihydrotestosterone
text:
The drawing matches 5α-dihydrotestosterone (androstanolone), and I wrote the SMILES from that identification rather than deriving each centre separately.

- **Ring system:** a four-ring steroid skeleton (three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring).
- **Ketone:** a C=O on the right-hand six-membered ring.
- **Hydroxyl:** an OH on the five-membered ring, drawn with a bold wedge (β).
- **Methyl groups:** two angular methyls, both on bold wedges (β).
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** hashed H at C5, C9 and C14 (α), and a bold-wedge H at C8 (β).

I checked the wedge and hash pattern against the known stereochemistry of 5α-DHT (5α-H, 8β-H, 9α-H, 14α-H, 17β-OH, 10β- and 13β-methyl), and it agrees. The SMILES below is the standard one for that compound, recalled from memory rather than rebuilt atom by atom.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O)CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CCC(=O)C4)C

name: Dimethyl methylphosphonate
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom with four substituents:

- A line going up with no label, which is a methyl group, so P–CH3.
- Two O atoms to the left and right, each attached to an unlabeled line ending in a vertex, so each is an OCH3 (methoxy) group.
- An O below the phosphorus joined by a double bond, so P=O.

This is dimethyl methylphosphonate. I read each unlabeled line end as a methyl carbon, which gives the SMILES COP(C)(=O)OC.

SMILES: COP(C)(=O)OC

name: Dimethyl Fumarate
text:
The drawing is a dimethyl butenedioate: a central C=C with a methyl ester (C(=O)OC) on each carbon.

To decide cis or trans, I read the approximate atom coordinates. The left alkene carbon is at (660, 682) and the right one at (838, 817). The left carbon's substituent (the carbonyl carbon) is at (457, 768), which is down-left of it. The right carbon's substituent (the carbonyl carbon) is at (1043, 732), which is up-right of it.

The double bond runs from upper-left to lower-right. The left substituent lies on one side of this axis, and the right substituent lies on the other.

Checking with the line direction d = (178, 135):
- For the left substituent, the vector from the left carbon is (-203, 86). The cross product d × v = 178·86 − 135·(−203) = 15308 + 27405, which is positive.
- For the right substituent, the vector from the right carbon is (205, −85). The cross product is 178·(−85) − 135·205 = −15130 − 27675, which is negative.

The two substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans (fumarate).

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OC

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OC

name: Dimethylmercury
text:
The drawing shows a single mercury atom labelled Hg with a bond line extending from each side. Each line ends in free space with no atom label, so the substituents are not shown.

Read literally, the bonds are open valences. In a SMILES string, an unlabelled bond end is usually a methyl group or a dummy atom. Because nothing is specified, I treat the drawing as just the Hg atom with two unspecified bonds and write the bare atom as `[Hg]`.

The alternative is dimethylmercury, `C[Hg]C`, if the line ends are read as methyl groups. A bare line end in a skeletal drawing normally does mean a methyl carbon, but here the lines are so short and isolated that they look like open attachment points. I'm going with the literal reading.

SMILES: [Hg]

name: Dimethyldioctadecylammonium bromide
text:
The image shows dioctadecyldimethylammonium bromide. I read it region by region:

- **Centre:** a nitrogen labelled N⁺ carries two methyl groups, drawn as short vertical bonds above and below it.
- **Left chain:** counting the zigzag vertices from the terminal carbon to the carbon attached to N gives 18 carbons.
- **Right chain:** counting the same way gives 18 carbons.
- **Counter-ion:** a separate Br⁻ is drawn above the nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are no wedges, hashes or double bonds, so none is specified.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC[N+](C)(C)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC.[Br-]

name: Diltiazem
text:
This structure is diltiazem, a benzothiazepinone drug. I read it region by region:

- **Acetate:** a CH3–C(=O)–O group sits at the top, attached through its oxygen to C3 of the seven-membered ring.
- **Seven-membered ring:** C3 carries the acetate, bonded to the lactam C=O, which is bonded to N. N is bonded to the fused benzene ring, and the ring carbon next to N is joined to S. S connects to C2, which closes back to C3.
- **N substituent:** a CH2CH2N(CH3)2 chain hangs off the ring nitrogen.
- **Aryl group:** C2 carries a para-methoxyphenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are two wedged bonds, the acetate oxygen at C3 and the aryl group at C2. With the implicit hydrogen pointing away from the viewer in each case, the wedges give @@ at both centres in the SMILES below. This matches the known (2S,3S) configuration of diltiazem.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[C@@H]1[C@@H](Sc2ccccc2N(C1=O)CCN(C)C)c1ccc(OC)cc1

name: Diodon
text:
The image shows two separate components, which I write as a dot-separated SMILES.

**Top component:** HO–CH2–CH2–NH–CH2–CH2–OH is diethanolamine, `OCCNCCO`.

**Bottom component:** a 4-pyridone ring. The ring atoms are N1, then C2(H)=C3(I), then C4(=O), then C5(I)=C6(H), which closes back to N1. N1 carries a CH2–C(=O)OH group, so this is iodopyracet-type 3,5-diiodo-4-pyridone-N-acetic acid.

Reading the ring from the drawing: N is bonded to CH (upper right), and that CH is double-bonded to C(I), which is bonded to C(=O). The C(=O) is bonded to a second C(I), which is double-bonded to the other CH, and that CH is bonded back to N.

SMILES for this part: `OC(=O)CN1C=C(I)C(=O)C(I)=C1`

SMILES: OCCNCCO.OC(=O)CN1C=C(I)C(=O)C(I)=C1

name: Dinaciclib
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine core with three substituents:

- **C3:** an ethyl group.
- **C5:** a piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine carbon next to that nitrogen carries a 2-hydroxyethyl chain, drawn on a hashed bond.
- **C7:** an NH–CH2 linker to the 3-position of a pyridine N-oxide, drawn as N⁺–O⁻.

For the one stereocentre (the piperidine C2), the hashed bond points the hydroxyethyl chain away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H side, the ring CH2, ring N and the chain run clockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (preceding ring CH2, H, N, chain) this corresponds to `@`, giving `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CCc1cnn2c(NCc3ccc[n+]([O-])c3)cc(N3CCCC[C@H]3CCO)nc12

name: Diphacinone
text:
The drawing shows diphacinone: an indane-1,3-dione with a 2,2-diphenylacetyl group on C2.

- **Indane-1,3-dione core:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. Two carbonyl carbons (each with a C=O) flank the CH at C2.
- **Side chain:** C2 is bonded to a C=O, which is bonded to a CH carrying two phenyl rings.
- **Stereochemistry:** C2 is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2C(=O)C1C(=O)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Diphenhydramine
text:
The drawing shows a dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) attached to a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2), which connects to an ether oxygen. The oxygen is bonded to a CH carbon that carries two phenyl rings. This is diphenhydramine.

Atom by atom:
- N is bonded to two methyl carbons and one CH2.
- That CH2 is bonded to a second CH2, which is bonded to O.
- O is bonded to the CH, which bears the two phenyl rings.
- Each ring is a six-membered benzene ring with alternating double bonds drawn.
- The CH is not stereogenic, because its two substituents are identical phenyls, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: CN(C)CCOC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Diphenyl diselenide
text:
The drawing shows two phenyl rings, each bonded to one selenium atom, with the two selenium atoms bonded to each other. This is diphenyl diselenide.

Each ring is a six-membered benzene ring with alternating double bonds, and no stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: c1ccccc1[Se][Se]c1ccccc1

name: Diphenhydramine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows diphenhydramine hydrochloride.

- **Amine end:** a nitrogen carries two methyl groups and is bonded to a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Ether link:** the chain ends in an oxygen, which connects to a CH carbon.
- **Aromatic part:** that CH carbon carries two phenyl rings.
- **Salt:** HCl is drawn as a separate component.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown with wedges or hashes, so none is included.

SMILES: CN(C)CCOC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.Cl

name: Dipivefrin
text:
The drawing is epinephrine with both phenolic hydroxyls esterified as pivalates (dipivefrin).

- Each ester is a tert-butyl group on a carbonyl, bonded through an oxygen to the ring: CC(C)(C)C(=O)O–.
- The ring is a benzene with the two pivaloyloxy groups on adjacent carbons.
- The side chain on the ring is CH(OH)CH2NHCH3.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the stereocentre carries no stereo marking.

SMILES: CNCC(O)c1ccc(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c1

name: Dipyridamole
text:
This is dipyridamole: a pyrimido[5,4-d]pyrimidine core carrying two piperidines and two bis(2-hydroxyethyl)amino groups.

Reading the drawing:
- The core is two fused six-membered rings. The top ring holds N (top left), C (top right, bearing piperidine), C (fusion, upper right), C (fusion, lower left) and N (bottom left), with the C bearing N(CH2CH2OH)2 on the left.
- The right ring holds the two fusion carbons, N (upper right), C (bearing N(CH2CH2OH)2), N (lower right) and C (bottom, bearing piperidine).
- Each piperidine is attached through its nitrogen, and each amino group carries two CH2CH2OH arms.

Writing the SMILES, with the left ring atoms as C2(N(CCO)CCO)=N–C(pip)=C... in aromatic form:

OCCN(CCO)c1nc(N2CCCCC2)c2nc(N(CCO)CCO)nc(N3CCCCC3)c2n1

Check of connectivity:
- c1 is the left carbon bearing the diethanolamine. Its neighbours are n (top left), which leads to c(pip) at the top right, and n1 (bottom left), which closes the ring.
- The top-right carbon is c(N2CCCCC2), followed by c2, the upper fusion carbon.
- From c2 comes n, then c(N(CCO)CCO) on the right, then n, then c(pip) at the bottom, then c2, the lower fusion carbon. The fusion carbon closes the ring to the n1 at the bottom left.
- The upper fusion carbon bonds to the n at upper right, and the lower fusion carbon bonds to the bottom-left n, so the ring closure is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: OCCN(CCO)c1nc(N2CCCCC2)c2nc(N(CCO)CCO)nc(N3CCCCC3)c2n1

name: Dinoprost
text:
I read this as a prostaglandin F2α-type structure: a cyclopentane ring with two hydroxyls and two side chains.

- **Acid chain:** a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH at lower left) is followed by three CH2 groups. These lead to a cis (Z) C=C, then a CH2 that attaches to the ring at a wedged bond.
- **Ring:** there are five carbons. Two carry wedged OH groups, one carbon is a plain CH2, and the other two carry the side chains.
- **Second chain:** from the ring, a hashed bond leads to a trans (E) CH=CH. Next is a CH bearing a hashed OH, then a straight n-pentyl chain (five carbons).

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash by working out the neighbour order and the clockwise or anticlockwise sense of the three drawn substituents. The two double-bond geometries come directly from the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@@H]1[C@@H](/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCCC)[C@H](O)C[C@@H]1O

name: Diroximel Fumarate
text:
I read the structure left to right.

- The left end is a methyl group bonded to an oxygen, which is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (a methyl ester, COC(=O)).
- That carbonyl carbon is attached to a C=C double bond, which leads to a second carbonyl carbon bearing =O.
- The second carbonyl carbon is bonded to an ester oxygen, then a CH2CH2 chain, then the nitrogen of a succinimide ring.
- The ring is N, C(=O), CH2, CH2, C(=O), closing back to N.

Stereochemistry: the double bond is drawn as trans. The first carbonyl carbon sits at the upper left of the double bond and the second carbonyl carbon at the lower right, on opposite sides, so this is the E isomer.

Writing the SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OCCN1C(=O)CCC1=O

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OCCN1C(=O)CCC1=O

name: Diquafosol
text:
I read this as diuridine 5′,5‴‑tetraphosphate (Up4U): two uridine units joined through their 5′‑oxygens by a linear chain of four phosphates.

- **Uracil rings:** each is attached through N1, with C2=O and C4=O and a C5=C6 double bond. N3 carries an H.
- **Phosphate chain:** four P atoms in a row, linked by bridging oxygens. Each P has one =O and one OH, except that the terminal P atoms also connect to the 5′‑CH2–O of a ribose.
- **Ribose rings:** each is a five‑membered ring (O, C1′–C4′) with 2′‑OH and 3′‑OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the two halves are drawn in mirror‑image orientations, so the wedges and hashes are reversed between them. Tracing the ring direction in each half shows both are the same natural β‑D‑ribose configuration (base and CH2 on one face, both OH groups on the other).

I wrote the stereo tags by converting from the standard natural‑uridine SMILES and checking the neighbour‑order parity at each centre. I did not run the string through a parser.

SMILES: O=c1ccn([C@@H]2O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)OC[C@H]3O[C@@H](n4ccc(=O)[nH]c4=O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]3O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O)c(=O)[nH]1

name: Disodium 2-(1,3-dioxo-2,3-dihydro-1H-inden-2-yl)quinoline-6,8-disulfonate
text:
The drawing shows quinoline yellow (disodium salt): an indane-1,3-dione joined to a quinoline ring, with two sulfonate groups on the quinoline.

**Indanedione part.** A benzene ring is fused to a five-membered ring. That ring has two C=O groups and a CH between them, and the CH is bonded to quinoline C2.

**Quinoline part.** The ring atoms are:
- N is bonded to C2 and to C8a.
- C2 is bonded to C3, and C3 is double-bonded to C4 in the drawing.
- C4 is bonded to C4a.
- C4a is bonded to C5, and C5 carries a sulfonate in the drawing.
- Continuing round: C6 is the ring CH, C7 carries the other SO3⁻, and C8 is the ring CH adjacent to C8a.

Reading the drawing against this numbering:
- The upper-right sulfonate sits on the carbon bonded to the CH that is attached to C4a.
- The lower sulfonate sits on the carbon attached to C8a.

So the sulfonates are at positions 6 and 8. The ring atoms run C2 (attached to the CH), C3, C4, C4a, C5 (CH), C6 (SO3⁻), C7 (CH), C8 (SO3⁻), C8a, then N.

**SMILES.** The indanedione fragment is C1(=O)c2ccccc2C(=O)C1, with the CH attached to the quinoline. Writing the quinoline as c3ccc4cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c4n3, the full structure is:

O=C1C(c3ccc4cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c4n3)C(=O)c2ccccc12 with two [Na+].

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O=C1C(c3ccc4cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c4n3)C(=O)c2ccccc12

name: Disopyramide
text:
The drawing shows disopyramide. Reading it region by region:
