- **Central carbon:** a quaternary carbon bonded to four groups: a C(=O)NH2 amide, a phenyl ring, a 2-pyridyl ring, and a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Chain:** the CH2CH2 chain ends at a nitrogen carrying two isopropyl groups, N(C(C)C)C(C)C.
- **Pyridyl ring:** it attaches through the carbon adjacent to the ring nitrogen, so it is a 2-pyridyl group.
- **Phenyl ring:** a plain benzene ring with no substituents.
- **Stereochemistry:** the central carbon is not a stereocentre by connectivity, and no wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: CC(C)N(C(C)C)CCC(C(N)=O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccn1

name: Distearoylphosphatidylcholine
text:
The drawing shows a phosphatidylcholine with two saturated acyl chains, which I read as distearoyl phosphatidylcholine (DSPC).

- **Head group:** a trimethylammonium, N⁺(CH₃)₃, is attached through a CH₂CH₂ link to an oxygen on the phosphorus. The phosphorus carries one P=O, one O⁻ and two ester oxygens.
- **Glycerol backbone:** the phosphate is bonded to a CH₂ of a three-carbon glycerol unit. The central CH and the other CH₂ each carry an acyloxy group (–O–C(=O)–chain).
- **Left chain:** counting vertices from the carbonyl carbon to the terminal methyl gives 18 carbons, so it is a stearoyl group.
- **Right chain:** the same count gives 18 carbons, another stearoyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the central glycerol carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo marks.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC(COC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC)COP(=O)([O-])OCC[N+](C)(C)C

name: Distigmine
text:
The drawing shows a symmetric dication: two 1-methylpyridinium-3-yl carbamate units joined by a hexamethylene chain. This is the structure of demecarium-like compounds, but with a six-carbon chain and N-methyl groups on both carbamate nitrogens (distigmine/hexamethylenebis).

Chain count: the path from the left N to the right N runs through these vertices: (578,858), (655,920), (750,885), (830,946), (922,910), (1003,972). That is 6 carbons, so the chain is hexamethylene.

Left half: the N-methyl pyridinium ring has N+ attached to a CH3, to C2 (the CH at the bottom, 248,705) and to C6 (the upper CH at 183,541). C3 carries the O and is joined to C2 by a double bond. The other ring bonds are C4 (357,568)=C5 (278,505) and C6=N+. In SMILES: C[n+]1cccc(OC(=O)N(C)...)c1, written aromatic.

Full SMILES: C[n+]1cccc(OC(=O)N(C)CCCCCCN(C)C(=O)Oc2ccc[n+](C)c2)c1

SMILES: C[n+]1cccc(OC(=O)N(C)CCCCCCN(C)C(=O)Oc2ccc[n+](C)c2)c1

name: Disulfiram
text:
The drawing shows a disulfide-linked pair of dithiocarbamate units, which is disulfiram.

- Left unit: an N bearing two ethyl groups, bonded to a carbon that is double-bonded to S (C=S) and single-bonded to a bridging S.
- Bridge: that S is bonded to a second S.
- Right unit: the second S is bonded to a C(=S) carbon, which is bonded to an N bearing two ethyl groups.

All bonds are plain, with no stereochemistry shown.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=S)SSC(=S)N(CC)CC

name: DL-selenomethionine
text:
The drawing shows selenomethionine, with plain bonds throughout.

Reading the chain from left to right:

- Se is bonded to a CH2, then a second CH2.
- That CH2 is bonded to the alpha carbon, which carries NH2.
- The alpha carbon is bonded to a carboxylic acid carbon, C(=O)OH.

The alpha carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereochemistry.

name: Dobutamine Hydrochloride
text:

- **Linker:** the chain ends at an NH, which is bonded to a CH carrying a methyl group (the top vertex).
- **Right-hand chain:** from that CH, two CH2 groups lead to a para-hydroxyphenyl ring.
- **Salt:** the HCl is drawn as a separate component.

name: Docusate Sodium
text:
The drawing shows docusate sodium (sodium bis(2-ethylhexyl) sulfosuccinate).

Reading the structure region by region:
- The central chain is a succinate backbone. One carbon carries the sulfonate group, S(=O)(=O)[O-], and is bonded to a carbonyl carbon. The next carbon is a CH2, which is bonded to the second carbonyl carbon.
- Each carbonyl is an ester, C(=O)O–CH2–CH(CH2CH3)–CH2CH2CH2CH3, which is a 2-ethylhexyl group.
- Left chain: O–CH2–CH, with an ethyl branch (CH2–CH3) and a butyl chain (CH2CH2CH2CH3). That makes 6 carbons in the main chain plus the 2-carbon ethyl branch, so 2-ethylhexyl.
- Right chain: the same 2-ethylhexyl group.
- The counterion is Na+.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: Docetaxel
text:
The drawing is docetaxel, a taxane diterpenoid. I identified it from the overall skeleton and the substituents and then wrote the SMILES from memory of docetaxel's standard isomeric form, so the stereodescriptors were not re-derived from each wedge and hash in the image.

The features I matched against the image are:
- the Boc-protected NH on the phenylisoserine side chain, with a phenyl and an OH on the adjacent carbons
- the ester linking that side chain to the ring carbon next to the C=C(CH3) alkene
- the gem-dimethyl carbon bridging the ring system
- the ketone and the two ring OH groups on the large ring
- the benzoate ester and the acetate on the oxetane carbon
- the four-membered ring containing one oxygen (the oxetane)
- the tertiary OH on the carbon bearing the bridging carbon

name: Dofetilide
text:
The drawing is dofetilide.

Reading it region by region:
- Left end: a methylsulfonamide group, CH3-S(=O)(=O)-NH-, attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.

- The chain ends at a tertiary amine nitrogen that bears a methyl group.
- The nitrogen's other substituent is another two-carbon chain (CH2-CH2) running to a second para-substituted benzene ring.
- That ring carries NH-S(=O)(=O)-CH3 on the carbon opposite the chain, matching the left end.

name: Digitoxin
text:
I read this as a cardenolide: a digitoxigenin-type steroid with a butenolide at C17, a 14-hydroxyl, and a chain of three 2,6-dideoxy sugars on the 3-oxygen. The 5-H, 8-H, 9-H, both angular methyls, the 14-OH, the C17 lactone bond and the 3-O bond are all drawn with wedges or hashes, so I assigned chirality at every one of those centres. For each stereocentre I took the wedge/hash geometry from the drawing and converted it to @/@@ by a signed-volume test. This gives the stereochemistry as drawn, which differs from the usual digitoxin configuration at several centres. I did not check it against a reference structure.

**Steroid core.** Ring A is a cyclohexane, ring B a cyclohexane with the 5-H, and ring C a cyclohexane carrying the 14-OH. Ring D is a cyclopentane. There are methyls on C10 and C13. The lactone is C1=CC(=O)OC1 joined at C17.

**Sugar chain.** Each sugar is a tetrahydropyran with a 6-methyl and a ring CH2. The terminal ring carries 3-OH and 4-OH. The two inner rings each carry a 3-OH and a glycosidic oxygen on C4. They are linked 1→4 to each other and to the aglycone's 3-oxygen.

In the SMILES, the sugar rings use digits 1–3. The steroid uses digits 4–8 so that no ring-closure digit is reused while it is still open.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)C[C@H](O[C@@H]2[C@@H](C)O[C@@H](O[C@@H]3[C@@H](C)O[C@@H](O[C@@H]4C[C@H]5CC[C@@H]6[C@@H]([C@@]5(C)CC4)CC[C@@]7(C)[C@]6(O)CC[C@@H]7C8=CC(=O)OC8)C[C@@H]3O)C[C@@H]2O)O1

name: Dolastatin 10
text:
I read this as dolastatin 10, a linear pentapeptide-like chain. From right to left it runs: N,N-dimethylvaline, valine, an N-methyl dolaisoleuine unit carrying a methoxy group and an sec-butyl side chain, a pyrrolidine-containing dolaproine unit with a methoxy and a methyl group, and finally a phenethylamine unit bearing a thiazol-2-yl group.

I wrote the stereochemistry from my recollection of the known natural product rather than deriving each centre from the wedges and hashes. I did check the two valine-type centres: both come out L, which is consistent with the hashed bonds drawn to the nitrogens.

name: Dirithromycin
text:
I read this as dirithromycin, an erythromycin-type 14-membered macrolide with a 9,11-oxazine ring. I assembled the SMILES from the erythromycin A skeleton as I remember it. The drawing confirms the skeleton and substituents, but I took the stereo marks of the unchanged centres from my recollection of erythromycin A rather than re-deriving each from wedges.

**Features read from the drawing**
- The macrolactone runs from C1 (C=O) through C2 (Me), C3 (O-cladinose), C4 (Me), C5 (O-desosamine), C6 (Me, OH), C7 (CH2), C8 (Me), C9 (NH), C10 (Me), C11 (O), C12 (Me, OH) and C13 (ethyl) back to the ring oxygen.
- The oxazine ring is C9–NH–CH(CH2OCH2CH2OCH3)–O–C11.
- The sugar on the left is cladinose, with a 3-OMe, a 3-Me, a 4-OH and a 6-Me.
- The sugar at the bottom is desosamine, with a 3-NMe2 and a 2-OH.

**Stereo assigned directly from the drawing**
- C9 has a hashed H, and the CIP priorities are N > C10 > C8 > H. This gives 9S, written `[C@@H]2` in the SMILES.
- The oxazine C2 carries a hashed CH2 bond, and the priorities are O > N > CH2 > H. This gives R, written `[C@H](COCCOC)N2`.

I checked the bracket and ring-closure counts by hand, but I did not run the string through a parser.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]2[C@@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O1)C)O[C@H]3C[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O3)C)O)(C)OC)C)O[C@H]4[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O4)C)N(C)C)O)(C)O)C)C)O[C@H](COCCOC)N2)(C)O

name: Dolasetron mesylate
text:
This looks like dolasetron mesylate: a dolasetron free base (indole-3-carboxylate ester of a bicyclic amino-ketone) drawn alongside methanesulfonic acid as a separate component.

**Indole ester.** The left part is an indole attached at C3 to an ester carbonyl, C(=O)O. The ring NH is shown explicitly.

**Bicyclic core.**
- The ester oxygen is bonded to a ring CH. That CH sits between two CH2 groups, one leading to each bridgehead CH.
- The top bridgehead CH has a hashed H. It is bonded to N, to the CH2 on the ester-bearing side, and to a CH2 (the drawn "C" label) leading to the CH next to the ketone.
- The N is bonded to both bridgehead CH carbons and to a CH2–C(=O) arm.
- The CH next to the ketone is bonded to a CH2 that leads to the lower bridgehead CH, which carries a wedged H.

**Stereochemistry.** Only the two bridgehead CH carbons have wedge or hash bonds, so only they get stereo marks. I worked out the @@ assignments from the drawn geometry. The top bridgehead has two bonds (to N and to the "C" label) pointing in nearly the same direction, so its assignment is the less certain of the two. The ester-bearing CH and the CH next to the ketone have plain bonds and get no stereo.

**Counter-component.** Methanesulfonic acid is drawn as CH3–S(=O)(=O)–OH.

SMILES: O=C(OC1C[C@@H]2CC3C(=O)CN2[C@@H](C1)C3)c1c[nH]c2ccccc12.CS(=O)(=O)O

name: Domperidone
text:
This structure is domperidone, so I read it as two benzimidazolone units joined through a propyl–piperidine linker.

**Left half.** A benzimidazol-2-one with an NH at the top and a substituted N at the bottom. The substituted N carries a three-carbon chain (CCC) that runs to the piperidine nitrogen.

**Middle.** A piperidine ring. Its nitrogen takes the propyl chain, and the carbon at position 4 (opposite the nitrogen) bonds to the right benzimidazolone N.

**Right half.** A benzimidazol-2-one with Cl on the benzene ring. The N attached to the piperidine is at the upper left of the five-membered ring, and the NH is at the lower right. The ring fusion carbon next to the substituted N (the upper-left carbon) is bonded to the aromatic CH, which leads up to the CH–CH(Cl) side.

Tracing the right benzene ring: the fusion carbon attached to N(piperidinyl) connects to a CH (upper left), then a CH (top), then C–Cl (top right), then a CH (right), then the fusion carbon attached to NH. So Cl is para to the fusion carbon bearing the substituted N… checking against the standard domperidone SMILES, O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C3CCN(CCCn4c5ccccc5[nH]c4=O)CC3, the NH-side fusion carbon is followed by a CH and then C(Cl), and this matches the drawing.

No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C1CCN(CCCn2c3ccccc3[nH]c2=O)CC1

name: Digitonin
Donafenib
text:
This is sorafenib with a CD3 group on the amide nitrogen (d3-sorafenib).

name: Dolastatin 11
text:
I traced the macrocycle atom by atom, starting at the N‑methyl leucine nitrogen and going clockwise around the ring.

**Ring sequence**
1. N‑Me‑Leu: N(CH3), α‑carbon with a wedged isobutyl group, then C=O.
2. NH–CH2–C=O (glycine unit).
3. N‑Me‑Val: N(CH3), α‑carbon with a wedged isopropyl group, then C=O.
4. N‑Me‑Phe(4‑OMe): N(CH3), α‑carbon with a wedged CH2 to a para‑methoxyphenyl ring, then C=O.
5. NH–CH(CH3) with a wedged methyl, then a ketone C=O attached to C(CH3)2. This CMe2 carries the next C=O, which is bonded to NH.
6. NH–CH(CH3) with a wedged methyl, then C=O.
7. NH–CH(ethyl) with a hashed ethyl, then CH(CH3) with a hashed methyl, then C(=O)–O.
8. The ester oxygen bonds to a CH (wedged bond to O) that carries a sec‑butyl group. The sec‑butyl CH has a hashed methyl. This CH is followed by C(=O)–NH–CH2–C(=O), which closes the ring on the first N‑methyl nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry**
I read each centre from its wedge or hash and the positions of its three in‑plane neighbours, then converted that to @/@@ in the order the atoms appear in the SMILES.

name: Dolutegravir
text:
I read this as dolutegravir, drawn with the pyridone as a ketone plus an enol OH.

**Ring system and substituents**
- The left ring is a six-membered 1,3-oxazinane. Its atoms are the methyl-bearing CH, two CH2 groups, O, the ring-fusion CH and N.
- The ring-fusion CH is also bonded to a CH2 that leads to the second N. That N sits in the central ring and carries a C=C–C(=O) unit.
- The lactam C(=O) is attached to the first N, which closes the fused tricyclic core.
- The pyridone ring carries a ketone C=O and an OH on the adjacent carbon.
- A C(=O)NH–CH2 amide leads to a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- Methyl-bearing carbon: the methyl is on a hashed bond and the H is implicit, towards the viewer. Taking neighbours in the SMILES order (methyl, H, N, CH2), this gives `@@`.
- Ring-fusion carbon: the H is hashed. Taking neighbours in the SMILES order (O, H, N, CH2), this gives `@`.

name: Donepezil Hydrochloride
text:

The carbon next to the ketone bears a CH2 link to the 4-position of a piperidine. The piperidine nitrogen carries a benzyl group. The "HCl" label is drawn as a separate component.

name: Donepezil
text:
This structure is donepezil.

- **Indanone core:** a five-membered ring with a ketone (C=O) fused to a benzene ring that carries two methoxy groups.
- **Linker:** a CH2 joins the carbon next to the ketone to the 4-position of a piperidine ring.
- **Piperidine:** the nitrogen carries a benzyl group (CH2 attached to a phenyl ring).
- **Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre at C2 of the indanone is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is included.

name: Dolastatin 15
text:
I read the drawing as a linear depsipeptide with a terminal pyrrolinone, and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Fragments, left to right**
1. N,N-dimethylvaline: a Me2N group on the α-carbon, which carries an isopropyl group and a C=O.
2. Valine, joined through an NH.
3. N-methylvaline.
4. Proline.
5. Proline, whose carboxyl group forms an ester.
6. A 2-hydroxyisovaleric acid unit, bonded through its O to proline 5 and through its C=O to the ring N.
7. A 5-benzyl-4-methoxy-3-pyrrolin-2-one ring, joined through its ring nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned CIP descriptors from the wedges and hashes.
- Both valines and the N-methylvaline are S (L).
- Both prolines are S (L).
- The hydroxyisovalerate carbon is S.
- The benzyl-bearing ring carbon is S.

I then wrote the SMILES chirality tags to reproduce those assignments.

name: Dopamine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying two adjacent OH groups (a catechol) and a two-carbon chain ending in NH2. This is dopamine.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- C1 at (757, 745) bears the CH2CH2NH2 chain.
- C2 at (605, 603) is a plain CH.
- C3 at (407, 663) bears an OH.

The two OH-bearing carbons are adjacent, and the chain carbon sits para to C4 and meta to C3. The drawing shows no stereocentres.

name: Doravirine
text:
This is the doravirine structure, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying Cl, a nitrile (C≡N) and an aryl-O substituent, all in a 1,3,5 pattern.
- **Central ring:** a pyridin-2-one. The ring nitrogen N1 is bonded to C2(=O). C3 carries the aryl-O group, C4 carries CF3, and C5=C6 close the ring back to N1.
- **Linker:** N1 is attached to a CH2 group.
- **Right ring:** the CH2 connects to a triazolone. Its ring atoms are C(=N), N, NH, C(=O) and N-methyl.

N#Cc1cc(Cl)cc(Oc2c(C(F)(F)F)ccn(Cc3n[nH]c(=O)n3C)c2=O)c1

The triazolone ring is C3(=N–NH–C(=O)–N3(CH3)), which matches the drawing: the carbon bonded to CH2 is double-bonded to N, then NH, then C=O, then N-Me closing back to the first carbon.

name: Doxapram
text:
The drawing shows a pyrrolidin-2-one (lactam) ring, which I read as follows.

- The lactam nitrogen carries an ethyl group.
- The carbonyl carbon is bonded to N, to =O, and to the quaternary carbon.
- The quaternary carbon carries two phenyl rings and is bonded to the ring CH.
- That ring CH bears a CH2CH2 chain ending at the nitrogen of a morpholine ring.
- The ring CH is also bonded to a CH2 that closes the ring back to the lactam N.

The five-membered ring is therefore N, C(=O), C(Ph)2, CH, CH2.

The morpholine is N, CH2, CH2, O, CH2, CH2.

name: Doxazosin
text:
This is doxazosin, with no stereochemistry drawn.

The structure breaks into three parts:
- **Quinazoline core:** a 4-amino-6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline, with the piperazine attached at C2.
- **Linker:** a piperazine ring whose second nitrogen is acylated by a carbonyl group.
- **Acyl group:** the carbonyl is attached to C2 of a 2,3-dihydro-1,4-benzodioxine. That carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marker.

name: Doramectin
Dorzolamide
text:
The structure is dorzolamide, a thieno[2,3-b]thiopyran bicyclic sulfonamide, read as follows.

- **Core:** a thiophene ring fused to a six-membered ring that contains a sulfone, S(=O)(=O). The sulfone sulfur is attached directly to the thiophene carbon next to the thiophene sulfur.
- **Sulfonamide:** the other thiophene carbon next to the thiophene sulfur carries S(=O)(=O)NH2.
- **Methyl:** the carbon next to the sulfone sulfur carries a wedged methyl group.
- **Ethylamino:** the carbon on the opposite side of the six-membered ring, attached to the thiophene, carries a hashed NH–CH2CH3 group.
- **Stereochemistry:** I worked out the @/@@ labels from the wedge and hash positions. Both stereocentres are drawn with an implicit hydrogen. The ethylamino carbon comes out as `[C@H]` and the methyl-bearing carbon as `[C@H]` in the SMILES order below. This matches the known (4S,6S) configuration of dorzolamide.

name: Doxylamine
text:
The drawing shows doxylamine. Reading it region by region:

- **Amine end:** a nitrogen carrying two methyl groups (a dimethylamino group).
- **Linker:** the nitrogen is joined to a CH2–CH2 chain, which ends in an oxygen (an ether).
- **Central carbon:** the oxygen attaches to a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl group, a phenyl ring and a 2-pyridyl ring.
- **Pyridine ring:** the carbon bonded to the central carbon sits next to the ring nitrogen, so the ring is attached at its 2-position.
- **Stereochemistry:** the central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all its bonds are drawn plain, so no stereo marks are included.

name: Doxepin
text:
The structure is doxepin: a dibenz[b,e]oxepine tricycle with an exocyclic double bond carrying a 3-(dimethylamino)propylidene chain.

**Connectivity**
- A dimethylamino group, N(CH3)2, is attached to a CH2–CH2–CH= chain.
- The =CH carbon is double-bonded to C11, the ring carbon of the seven-membered ring.
- C11 is bonded to two benzene rings. One ring carries the ring oxygen, and the other carries the ring CH2 that links to the oxygen.
- The oxygen and that CH2 close the seven-membered oxepine ring.

**Double-bond geometry**
- On C11, the aryl ring bearing the oxygen has higher CIP priority than the aryl ring bearing the CH2. At the first point of difference, the carbon bonded to oxygen has substituents (O,C,C), against (C,C,C) on the other ring.
- On the =CH carbon, the CH2 outranks H.
- In the drawing, the chain CH2 lies on the same side as the oxygen-bearing aryl ring, so the double bond is Z.

In the SMILES below, the `/` bonds place the chain CH2 trans to the CH2-bearing aryl ring, which puts it cis to the oxygen-bearing ring. That matches the Z geometry above.

SMILES: CN(C)CC/C=C1/c2ccccc2COc2ccccc21

name: Droloxifene
text:
The drawing shows a 3-hydroxy (meta-hydroxy) tamoxifen analogue, read as follows:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing OH. Counting around the ring, the OH carbon is separated from the carbon attached to the alkene by one ring carbon, so the OH is meta.
- **Central alkene:** one alkene carbon carries the hydroxyphenyl ring and a para-substituted phenyl ring. The other alkene carbon carries an ethyl group and an unsubstituted phenyl ring.
- **Para-substituted ring:** it carries an O–CH2–CH2–N(CH3)2 chain (a dimethylaminoethoxy group).
- **Alkene geometry:** the double bond is drawn roughly vertically. The hydroxyphenyl and the ethyl group both point left, so they are cis. The alkoxyphenyl and the plain phenyl both point right, so they are also cis to each other.

Writing the ethyl group first, then the cis relationship to the hydroxyphenyl, gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1cccc(O)c1)c1ccc(OCCN(C)C)cc1

name: Dronedarone Hydrochloride
text:
This structure is dronedarone hydrochloride.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left chain:** a dibutylamino group, N(CCCC)CCCC, joined to a three-carbon chain (CCC) that ends in an ether oxygen.
- **Middle:** that oxygen is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring, which carries a carbonyl (C=O) on the opposite side.
- **Right:** the carbonyl is bonded to C3 of a benzofuran. C2 carries a butyl group and the ring oxygen is O1. The NHS(=O)(=O)C (methanesulfonamide) group sits at C5 of the benzofuran.
- **Salt:** HCl is drawn as a separate component.

Benzofuran numbering: C3 is attached to C3a, and C4 is the next aromatic carbon, which lies between C3a and C5. The sulfonamide is on the carbon next to that CH, so it is at C5. That matches the drawing, where the C–NHSO2Me carbon is adjacent to the top CH, which is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon C3a.

SMILES written from C2: CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1.Cl

Check of the benzofuran ring: o1 attaches to c2 (C7a), then c (C7), c (C6), c(N...) (C5), c (C4), c2 (C3a), then c1 (C3) closes the furan ring. This is correct.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1.Cl

name: Doxorubicin
text:
I read this as an anthracycline of the doxorubicin type. It has a tetracyclic aglycone with a methoxy-substituted benzene ring, two quinone C=O groups and two phenolic OH groups. The ring carrying C9 has a tertiary OH and a C(=O)CH2OH side chain. The sugar is a 3-amino-3,6-dideoxy pyranose (amino at C3′, OH at C4′, CH3 at C5′) attached through an O-glycosidic bond.

I assigned each stereocentre from the drawn wedges and hashes:
- C5′ (methyl on a bold wedge): `[C@@H]`
- C1′ (hashed bond to the glycosidic O): `[C@@H]`
- C7 (bold wedge to O): `[C@H]`
- C9 (bold wedge to OH): `[C@]`
- C3′ (bold wedge to NH2): `[C@H]`
- C4′ (bold wedge to OH): `[C@@H]`

I also checked the methoxy position. The OMe sits on the benzene carbon next to the one that bears the lower quinone carbonyl, so in the SMILES it comes at the far end of the ring from the upper carbonyl's attachment.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1O[C@@H](O[C@H]2C[C@](O)(C(=O)CO)Cc3c(O)c4C(=O)c5cccc(OC)c5C(=O)c4c(O)c23)C[C@H](N)[C@@H]1O

name: Drospirenone
text:
This structure is drospirenone, and I wrote the SMILES from my recall of its known stereo-SMILES rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I checked only the connectivity against the drawing, not the individual @/@@ assignments.

The drawing matches drospirenone in these features:
- **Ring A:** an enone with a C=C in the ring and a ketone at the far right.
- **Methyl groups:** two angular methyls, drawn as bold wedges at the two quaternary ring-fusion carbons.
- **Upper-right cyclopropane:** a CH2 fused across the 6,7-positions of the steroid core.
- **Left cyclopropane:** a second fused CH2 at the 15,16-positions, next to the D ring.
- **Spiro lactone:** a five-membered ring at C17 containing the ring oxygen and a C=O (the O at the far left).

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1[C@H]3C[C@H]3[C@@H]4[C@@H]2CC[C@]5([C@H]4[C@H]6C[C@H]6[C@@]57CCC(=O)O7)C

name: Dromostanolone Propionate
text:
This is drostanolone propionate, the 17-propionate ester of 2α-methyl-5α-dihydrotestosterone. I read it from the drawing as follows.

- **Skeleton:** the four-ring steroid core has a ketone at C3, a methyl at C2, and angular methyls at C10 and C13.
- **Ester:** C17 carries an O–C(=O)–CH2CH3 group (propionate).
- **Orientation:** the drawing is the usual steroid layout flipped vertically (C5 on top, C10 below). In that flipped view the C10 and C13 methyls and the C9-H are hashed, while the C5-H, C8-H and C14-H are wedged. The C17 oxygen is hashed and the C2 methyl is wedged. Allowing for the flip, this is the natural configuration: 10β- and 13β-methyl, 5α-H, 17β-O and 2α-methyl.

I built the SMILES from the known 5α-dihydrotestosterone stereochemistry. I then set the C2 centre to R, which is the descriptor I recall for drostanolone, and added the propionate on the C17 oxygen. I did not check this against a database, so the C2 assignment rests on that recalled descriptor.

SMILES: CCC(=O)O[C@@H]2CC[C@H]3[C@@H]4CC[C@@H]5[C@@]6(C[C@@H](C)C(=O)C5)C.C

Wait — that line is malformed. The correct single SMILES is below.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2OC(=O)CC)CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(C[C@@H](C)C(=O)C4)C

name: Drotaverine
text:
I read this as drotaverine: a 1-(3,4-diethoxybenzylidene)-6,7-diethoxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline.

- **Left ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring containing NH and two CH2 groups (a tetrahydroisoquinoline). The benzene ring carries two OEt groups on adjacent carbons.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent OEt groups, attached through a CH= unit to C1 of the tetrahydroisoquinoline (the carbon next to NH).
- **Double bond geometry:** the aryl group on the CH and the NH on C1 lie on the same side of the C=C. At C1 the higher priority substituent is N, and at the CH it is the aryl group. Same side means Z.

The SMILES below was checked against this reading and encodes the Z geometry (aryl and N cis).

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(/C=C2\NCCc3cc(OCC)c(OCC)cc32)cc1OCC

name: Dsm-265
text:
This looks like the DSM265 analog: a triazolopyrimidine core with a CF2CH3 group, a methyl group, and an NH-aryl group bearing an SF5.

**Core (read from the drawing):**
- The triazole ring has C2 (bearing CF2CH3), N, N (the bridgehead), C (the fusion carbon) and N.
- C2 is bonded to the top N (N1) and to the left N (N3).
- N1 is bonded to the bridgehead N, which carries the NH-bearing carbon C7.
- N3 is bonded to the fusion carbon C8a.
- The pyrimidine ring runs: bridgehead N, C7 (NH-aryl), CH, C5 (methyl), N4, C8a.

**Bonds:**
- C2=N1 is a double bond, and N3=C8a is a double bond.
- C7=CH is a double bond, and C5=N4 is a double bond.

**SMILES pieces:**
- Substituent on C2: CC(F)(F)
- Triazole and pyrimidine written together: CC(F)(F)c1nc2nc(C)cc(Nc3ccc(S(F)(F)(F)(F)F)cc3)n2n1

**Check of the ring closures:**
- c1 is C2, n is N1... in the string above, the first n after c1 would be N3 (bonded to C2 and to C8a), so the order is c1 (C2), n (N3), c2 (C8a), n (N4), c(C) (C5), c (CH), c(N...) (C7), n2 (bridgehead, closing to C8a), n1 (N1, closing to C2).
- The bridgehead N is bonded to C7, C8a and N1, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(F)(F)c1nc2nc(C)cc(Nc3ccc(S(F)(F)(F)(F)F)cc3)n2n1

name: Droxidopa
text:
The drawing shows droxidopa, with a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring on a CH(OH)–CH(NH2)–COOH chain.

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent OH groups (catechol) at the 3 and 4 positions relative to the chain attachment.
- **Chain:** the ring carbon attaches to a CH carrying an OH on a wedge bond, then to a CH carrying an NH2 on a wedge bond, then to a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH).
- **Stereocentre bearing OH:** the priorities are OH > CH(N) > aryl > H, with H pointing away. Going OH → CH(N) → aryl is clockwise, so this is R.
- **Stereocentre bearing NH2:** the priorities are N > COOH > CH(OH) > H, with H pointing away. Going N → COOH → CH(OH) is counterclockwise, so this is S.

This gives (2S,3R)-2-amino-3-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)-3-hydroxypropanoic acid. In the SMILES below, `@@` at the NH2 carbon encodes S and `@` at the OH carbon encodes R, which I checked by permuting the neighbour order.

SMILES: N[C@@H]([C@H](O)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1)C(=O)O

name: Dromostanolone
text:
I read this as drostanolone (2α-methyl-5α-androstan-17β-ol-3-one), a steroid skeleton with four rings (A–D).

**Skeleton and substituents**
- Ring A carries a ketone (C=O) at C3 and a wedged methyl at C2.
- There are two angular methyls, one at C10 and one at C13, both drawn hashed.
- C17 carries a hashed OH.

**Stereochemistry**
- The ring-fusion hydrogens are shown at C5, C8, C9 and C14.
- I assigned each stereocentre (C2, C5, C8, C9, C10, C13, C14, C17) from the wedge/hash geometry and the neighbour order in the SMILES.

**Atom-by-atom SMILES check**
The SMILES walks C2, C1, C10 (with methyl), C9, C11, C12, C13 (with methyl), C17 (with O), C16, C15, C14, C8, C7, C6, C5, C4, then C3(=O), which closes back to C2. That accounts for all 19 carbons and 2 oxygens in the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@]2(C)[C@H]3CC[C@]4(C)[C@@H](O)CC[C@H]4[C@@H]3CC[C@H]2CC1=O

name: Dotatate
text:
I read the structure as DOTA-D-Phe-Cys-Tyr-D-Trp-Lys-Thr-Cys-Thr, a DOTA-conjugated octreotate-type peptide (DOTA-TATE), with a disulfide between the two Cys residues. I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Regions read from the drawing**
- **Macrocycle:** the left ring is a 12-membered tetra-aza ring (cyclen) with three CH2COOH arms and a fourth CH2C(=O) arm that acylates the Phe nitrogen. This is DOTA.
- **Peptide:** D-Phe is bonded to Cys. Cys is bonded to Tyr, Tyr to D-Trp, D-Trp to Lys, Lys to Thr, and Thr to the second Cys. The second Cys carries a C-terminal Thr acid.
- **Ring:** the two Cys CH2 groups are joined through the S–S bond.

**Stereochemistry from wedges and hashes**
- D-Phe: `[C@H]`
- Cys1 (alpha carbon of the first Cys, attached to Phe): `[C@H]`
- Tyr: `[C@H]`
- D-Trp: `[C@@H]`
- Lys: `[C@H]`
- Thr6: alpha `[C@H]`, side-chain `[C@@H]`
- Cys7 (alpha carbon of the second Cys): `[C@@H]`
- Thr8 (C-terminal Thr): alpha `[C@@H]`, side-chain `[C@@H]`

These tags are in the atom order used in the SMILES below. I checked that the ring closures and the 12-membered DOTA ring close correctly.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)N[C@H]3CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc4c[nH]c5ccccc45)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc6ccc(O)cc6)NC3=O)CC1

name: Duloxetine Hydrochloride
text:
The image shows duloxetine hydrochloride, drawn as the free base plus a separate HCl.

- **Chain:** a secondary amine (N-methyl, with N–H) connects through two CH2 groups to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries an oxygen (to a naphthalene), a thiophene ring and an implicit hydrogen. The hashed bond points to the CH2 on the amine side.
- **Aryl groups:** the oxygen is attached to C1 of the naphthalene. The thiophene is attached at its C2, next to the sulfur.
- **Chirality:** the hashed CH2 is behind the plane, so the implicit H faces the viewer. Viewed from the H side, CH2 → O → thienyl runs clockwise. That corresponds to `[C@H]` when the SMILES is written as `CNCC[C@H](O…)c1cccs1`, which is the (S) configuration.

SMILES: CNCC[C@H](Oc1cccc2ccccc12)c1cccs1.Cl

name: Duloxetine
text:
The drawing shows duloxetine, the (S) enantiomer.

- **Amine end:** a methyl group on an NH, linked to a two-carbon chain (CH3–NH–CH2–CH2).
- **Stereocentre:** the chain reaches a carbon that carries an O-aryl group and a thiophene ring. The CH2 bond to this carbon is drawn as a hashed wedge, so the CH2 sits behind the plane and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **Ether side:** the oxygen is attached to the 1-position of a naphthalene, shown as two fused six-membered aromatic rings.
- **Thiophene:** the five-membered ring contains S and is attached to the stereocentre through the carbon next to S (the 2-position).

For the CIP assignment, the priorities are O > thienyl C (S,C,C) > CH2 (C,H,H) > H. On the page, O to thienyl to CH2 runs clockwise. Because H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, which gives (S).

Written as `CNCC[C@H](Oc1cccc2ccccc12)c1cccs1`, the SMILES lists the neighbours of the stereocentre in the order CH2, H, O, thienyl. That order and the @ symbol give the (S) configuration.

SMILES: CNCC[C@H](Oc1cccc2ccccc12)c1cccs1

name: Dutasteride
text:
I read this as dutasteride, a 4‑azasteroid, and wrote the SMILES from that identification rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

- **Aryl amide:** The benzene ring carries the amide NH on one carbon, a CF3 on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, and a second CF3 on the carbon para to that first CF3. That makes it a 2,5‑bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.
- **Steroid core:** The core has a cyclopentane D‑ring bearing the C(=O)NH amide, a methyl on the ring‑fusion carbon next to it, and two six‑membered rings in the middle. The A‑ring is a lactam with an NH–C(=O) and a C=C double bond, plus a second angular methyl on the A/B ring fusion.
- **Stereochemistry:** The stereo marks in the SMILES come from the known dutasteride structure. I did not re‑derive each @/@@ from the drawing, but the drawing is consistent with it.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2C(=O)NC4=C(C=CC(=C4)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)CC[C@@H]5[C@@]3(C=CC(=O)N5)C

name: Duocarmycin Sa
text:
I read the structure as a duocarmycin SA-type alkylating unit (a cyclopropane-spiro cyclohexadienone fused to a pyrrole carrying a methyl ester). Its ring nitrogen is acylated by a 5,6,7-trimethoxyindole-2-carbonyl group.

**Fragments**
- **Ester and pyrrole:** a methyl ester (`COC(=O)`) sits on C2 of an NH pyrrole. The pyrrole is fused to the six-membered ring.
- **Six-membered ring:** the ring carries a ketone (C=O) next to the pyrrole carbon bearing NH. It continues through a CH=C(N) unit and reaches the spiro carbon.
- **Spiro cyclopropane:** the spiro carbon is bonded to the cyclopropane CH₂, the pyrrole-side ring carbon, the C(N) carbon, and the cyclopropane CH. That CH bears an H and is bonded to the CH₂ that leads to the amide nitrogen.
- **Amide and indole:** the nitrogen bears the C(=O) of the 5,6,7-trimethoxyindole-2-carbonyl group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The wedge on the spiro carbon points to the cyclopropane CH₂. With that bond toward the viewer, the other three neighbours run clockwise (pyrrole-side carbon, then C(N), then CH). That gives `[C@@]`.
- The hashed H on the cyclopropane CH puts H away from the viewer. The remaining neighbours then run counterclockwise (N–CH₂, then spiro carbon, then cyclopropane CH₂). In my SMILES atom order that gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=CC2=C(N1)C(=O)C=C1N(C(=O)c4cc5cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c5[nH]4)C[C@H]3C[C@@]213

name: Durlobactam
text:
I read the structure as a bicyclic urea (a 1,6-diazabicyclo[3.2.1]octene core) carrying an N-sulfooxy group on one nitrogen.

**Connectivity**
- The sulfate group is S(=O)(=O)(OH) linked through an O to the lower nitrogen, N(a).
- N(a) is bonded to the ring C=O carbon, which is also bonded to the right-hand nitrogen, N(b).
- N(b) is bonded to a CH2 and to the carboxamide-bearing CH.
- That CH2 connects to the bridgehead CH, which is also bonded to N(a).
- The six-membered ring runs N(b), CH(CONH2), C(CH3)=CH, bridgehead CH, CH2. It contains one C=C, and the methyl sits on the carbon next to the CH(CONH2).
- The five-membered ring is N(a), C=O, N(b), CH2, bridgehead CH.

**Stereochemistry**
- Two stereocentres are marked: the CH bearing the carboxamide (wedge to the amide carbon) and the bridgehead CH (hashed H).
- Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES against the drawn wedge and hash, both centres come out as `@@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)[C@@H]1N2C[C@@H](C=C1C)N(OS(=O)(=O)O)C2=O

name: E129
text:
This is Allura Red AC, the disodium salt of an azo dye.

**Left ring (benzene):** The ring carbons are:
- C1, bearing the azo N
- C2, bearing OMe (the O at the bottom)
- C3, an aromatic CH
- C4, bearing SO3⁻
- C5, bearing CH3
- C6, an aromatic CH, between C5 and C1

**Right ring system (naphthalene):**
- The azo N is attached to a carbon (C1) that is adjacent to the C-OH carbon (C2).
- C2 is followed by C3 (CH) and C4 (CH), then the fusion carbon C4a.
- From C4a the ring continues to C5 (CH), which is bonded to C6.
- C6 carries SO3⁻, then C7 (CH) and C8 (CH), and then C8a.
- C8a is bonded to C1.

Reading the coordinates, the fusion atom at (1079,750) connects to CH (1084,626) and to CH (1185,818). The CH at 1185,818 connects to C(SO3) at (1180,943). That carbon connects to CH (1070,1000), then CH (963,934), then the fusion carbon (968,808), which bonds to C1 (862,743).

**SMILES:** Start from the methyl on the left ring and write the azo link to the naphthalene.

Cc1cc(N=Nc2c(O)ccc3cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc23)c(OC)cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+].[Na+]

Check on the naphthalene: c2 (C1) bonded to c(O) (C2), then c (C3), c (C4), c3 (C4a), c (C5), c(SO3) (C6), c (C7), c (C8), c23 (C8a). C8a closes to C1 and to C4a, which is correct.

SMILES: Cc1cc(N=Nc2c(O)ccc3cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc23)c(OC)cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+].[Na+]

name: Duvelisib
text:
I read this as duvelisib: an 8-chloro-2-phenylisoquinolin-1-one bearing a 1-(9H-purin-6-ylamino)ethyl group at C3.

- **Purine:** the left fused bicycle is a purine drawn as the 9H tautomer (NH in the five-membered ring). It is attached through its C6 to an exocyclic NH.
- **Side chain:** that NH is bonded to a CH carrying a wedged methyl, and this CH connects to C3 of the isoquinolinone.
- **Isoquinolinone core:** the ring nitrogen carries a phenyl group and is bonded to the C=O carbon. The benzo ring has a Cl on the carbon adjacent to the ring fusion next to the carbonyl (position 8).
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is the only wedged substituent, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > ring carbon > CH3 > H. Going N (lower left), then ring carbon (right), then CH3 (up) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES below, `C[C@H](N...)c...` encodes S.

SMILES: C[C@H](Nc1ncnc2nc[nH]c12)c1cc2cccc(Cl)c2c(=O)n1-c1ccccc1

name: Ebselen
text:
The drawing shows ebselen: a benzisoselenazolone ring system with an N-phenyl group.

- The five-membered ring contains Se, N, a carbonyl carbon (C=O), and two fused aromatic carbons.
- Se is bonded to N and to one fused aromatic carbon of the benzo ring.
- N is bonded to Se, to the carbonyl carbon, and to the phenyl ring.
- The carbonyl carbon is bonded to the other fused aromatic carbon.
- The benzo ring is a six-membered aromatic ring fused to the five-membered ring.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2[Se]N1c1ccccc1

name: Eberconazole
text:
The structure is a dibenzosuberane (10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cycloheptene) with an imidazol-1-yl group on C5 and two chlorines on one benzo ring.

**Seven-membered ring.** Reading around the ring: CH2 (750,282) – CH2 (946,261) – aromatic C (1085,401) of the right benzene – aromatic C (1062,598) – CH (894,702), which carries the imidazole N – aromatic C (708,635) of the left benzene – aromatic C (644,448) – back to the first CH2.

**Left benzene ring.** The atoms are C644,448 (attached to CH2), C708,635 (attached to CH), C579,784 (Cl), C385,747, C321,560 (Cl) and C451,411. The ring fusion carbons are C644 and C708. Both chlorines are on this ring: one on C579, which is adjacent to C708 and so ortho to the CH-bearing carbon, and one on C321.

**Imidazole.** N1 is attached to the CH. The ring runs N1 – CH (770,1030) = N (850,1210) – CH (1046,1189) = CH (1086,996) – N1. This is a normal imidazol-1-yl group.

**SMILES.** Starting from the CH:
C1(n2ccnc2)c3c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc3CCc4ccccc14

Checking the left ring: c3 (C708) – c(Cl) (C579) – c (C385) – c(Cl) (C321) – c (C451) – c3 (C644, bearing the CH2). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Clc1cc(Cl)c2c(c1)CCc1ccccc1C2n1ccnc1

name: Echothiophate
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary ammonium group, N⁺ with three methyls, joined through a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) to a sulfur. The sulfur is bonded to a phosphorus that carries one P=O and two ethoxy groups (OCH2CH3). This is the structure of echothiophate cation.

Reading the SMILES from the drawing: the N⁺ has three methyl groups and the CH2CH2 chain, the chain ends at S, and S attaches to P(=O)(OCC)OCC.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CCSP(=O)(OCC)OCC

name: Dutogliptin
text:
I read the drawing as a pyrrolidine-2-boronic acid whose ring nitrogen is acylated by a glycyl-type unit, C(=O)CH2–NH–(pyrrolidin-3-yl).

**Fragments**
- **Right ring:** a five-membered pyrrolidine with N at the lower left. The carbon next to N carries B(OH)2 on a bold wedge.
- **Linker:** the ring N is bonded to a C=O, then a CH2, then an NH.
- **Left ring:** the NH is attached by a hashed bond to C3 of a second pyrrolidine, whose ring NH is drawn as "HN" at the upper left.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Right stereocentre (carbon bearing B):** the wedge puts B toward the viewer, so H points away. The priorities are N > C > B. N, then ring CH2, then B run clockwise in the drawing, which gives R. In SMILES, `[C@@H]1` written as `OB(O)[C@@H]1CCCN1…` corresponds to R.
- **Left stereocentre (carbon bearing the NH linker):** the hash puts the NH linker away from the viewer, so H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH2 next to the ring NH > CH2 next to CH2. They run counterclockwise in the drawing; because H faces the viewer, the true sense is clockwise, which gives R. In SMILES, `CN[C@@H]1CCNC1` corresponds to R.

SMILES: OB(O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)CN[C@@H]1CCNC1

name: Edetate Calcium Disodium Anhydrous
text:
The drawing shows an EDTA tetra-anion with three counter-ions: Ca²⁺, Na⁺ and Na⁺. This is calcium disodium EDTA.

The EDTA backbone has two nitrogens joined by a CH2CH2 bridge. Each nitrogen carries two CH2COO⁻ arms, giving four carboxylates in total.

The charges balance: the four carboxylate charges (−4) are offset by Ca²⁺ (+2) and two Na⁺ (+2).

The ions are written as separate components in the SMILES, since the drawing shows them unbonded.

SMILES: [Ca+2].[Na+].[Na+].[O-]C(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)CCN(CC([O-])=O)CC([O-])=O

name: Econazole
text:
The drawing shows econazole, built from these parts:

- An imidazole ring attached through N1 to a CH2 group.
- That CH2 is bonded to a CH carbon, which carries the ether oxygen and a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring.
- The oxygen is bonded to a CH2 that leads to a 4-chlorophenyl ring (a 4-chlorobenzyl ether).

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the drawing shows only plain bonds, so I give no stereo marks.

Writing the SMILES from the imidazole outward: Clc1ccc(COC(Cn2ccnc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)cc1.

Atom check on the dichlorophenyl ring: the carbon attached to the CH is the ring carbon at about (1070, 797). Moving around the ring, the carbon at (1033, 946) carries a Cl, which is ortho. The next carbon at (1141, 1051) has no substituent. The carbon at (1288, 1011) carries a Cl, which is para to the attachment point. So the ring is 2,4-dichloro. In the SMILES, c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl starts at the attachment carbon, then goes through c, c, c(Cl), c, and ends on c2Cl, the ortho carbon. That puts the Cl atoms at the para and ortho positions, as drawn.

The imidazole is N1 with a CH2 substituent. Going round the ring: N1 to C2 (the carbon between the two nitrogens), then N3, then C4 and C5. This gives n2cncc2, which is equivalent to the form I wrote above. In the drawing, N(left) connects to the CH at the bottom (1265, 597), which connects to N(right), then to the top-right CH, then the top-left CH, and back to N(left). So the ring is n2cncc2. The earlier form, n2ccnc2, would place the two nitrogens next to a shared carbon in a different order, so I use n2cncc2.

SMILES: Clc1ccc(COC(Cn2ccnc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)cc1

Correction: the ring should be n2cncc2, so the final answer is:

SMILES: Clc1ccc(COC(Cn2cncc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)cc1

name: Edrophonium Chloride
text:
The drawing shows edrophonium chloride, a quaternary ammonium salt.

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with a hydroxyl group (HO) on one carbon. The nitrogen sits on a carbon that is meta to the hydroxyl-bearing carbon. The ring vertices are C(OH) at (355, 953), then (593, 1022), then C(N) at (771, 851). Between C(OH) and C(N) there is one carbon, at (593, 1022), so the substituents are 1,3 (meta).
- **Nitrogen:** N⁺ carries two methyl groups, one ethyl group, and the aryl ring.
- **Counterion:** Cl⁻, drawn separately.

SMILES: CC[N+](C)(C)c1cccc(O)c1.[Cl-]

SMILES: CC[N+](C)(C)c1cccc(O)c1.[Cl-]

name: Ecabet sodium
text:
I read this as the sodium salt of a sulfonated dehydroabietic acid (ecabet sodium type), which is a tricyclic skeleton with an aromatic ring.

- **Aromatic ring:** it carries an isopropyl group, a sulfonate (S(=O)(=O)[O-]), and two ring-fusion carbons. Two ring CH atoms sit between these substituents.
- **Middle ring:** two CH2 groups link the aromatic ring to the ring-fusion CH. The other aromatic fusion carbon attaches to the quaternary carbon bearing a methyl.
- **Saturated outer ring:** it contains three CH2 groups and a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries a methyl and a COOH.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are three stereocentres.
  - The quaternary carbon bearing a methyl, next to the aromatic ring, has a wedged methyl.
  - The CH ring-fusion carbon has a hashed H.
  - The quaternary carbon bearing COOH has a wedged methyl.
  - From the drawn coordinates I assigned them as @@, @@ and @@ in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: CC(C)c1cc2c(cc1S(=O)(=O)[O-])[C@@]1(C)CCC[C@@](C)(C(=O)O)[C@@H]1CC2.[Na+]

name: Efavirenz
text:
The drawing shows efavirenz. I read it as follows:

- **Ring:** a benzoxazinone, i.e. a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring containing a carbamate. The ring atoms in order are the quaternary stereocentre, O, C(=O), NH, and the two fused aromatic carbons.
- **Benzene substituent:** a Cl on the benzene ring, para to the NH-bearing carbon.
- **Stereocentre substituents:** a CF3 group and a cyclopropyl-C≡C– group. The alkyne is drawn on a wedge bond, so it points toward the viewer.

I set the chirality from the wedge. In the SMILES the neighbours of the stereocentre are listed as alkyne, aryl carbon (ring closure 2), CF3, then O. Viewed from the alkyne side, the sequence aryl → CF3 → O runs counterclockwise, which gives `@`.

As a check, the CIP priorities are O > CF3 > aryl > alkyne. With the lowest-priority alkyne toward the viewer, O → CF3 → aryl appears clockwise, so the true sense is counterclockwise. That makes the centre S, which matches efavirenz.

SMILES: C1CC1C#C[C@]2(C(F)(F)F)OC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)cc23

name: Edoxaban
text:
This is edoxaban, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Left end:** a 5-chloropyridin-2-yl group joined through NH to an oxalamide, NHC(=O)C(=O)NH.
- **Centre:** a cyclohexane ring. One ring carbon carries the oxalamide NH on a wedge. The adjacent carbon carries the thiazole-carboxamide NH, also on a wedge. The ring carbon across from these carries a dimethylcarboxamide, C(=O)N(C)C, on a hashed bond.
- **Bottom:** a 5-methyl-4,5,6,7-tetrahydrothiazolo[5,4-c]pyridine, attached to the carboxamide carbonyl at the thiazole C2.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash geometry and the neighbour order in the SMILES below. The result is [C@H] at the oxalamide-bearing carbon, [C@H] at the dimethylamide-bearing carbon, and [C@H] at the thiazole-amide-bearing carbon.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1)C(=O)N[C@H]1CC[C@H](C(=O)N(C)C)C[C@H]1NC(=O)c1nc2CCN(C)Cc2s1

name: Eflornithine
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary carbon bonded to four groups:
- a carboxylic acid, C(=O)O
- an NH2 group
- a CHF2 group
- a chain of CH2CH2CH2 ending in NH2

Reading the chain from the quaternary carbon: it goes to a vertex at (705, 826), then (898, 704), then (1101, 810), and then to NH2. That is three CH2 groups before the terminal NH2.

This matches eflornithine (DFMO), which is 2,5-diamino-2-(difluoromethyl)pentanoic acid. The five-carbon chain counts as the acid carbon, the quaternary carbon, and three CH2 groups.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: NCCCC(N)(C(F)F)C(=O)O

name: Efonidipine
text:
This is a nicardipine-like 1,4-dihydropyridine in which one ester is replaced by a cyclic phosphonate.

**Dihydropyridine core:** N1H is bonded to C2 (methyl) and C6 (methyl). C3 carries the ester, C4 carries the 3-nitrophenyl group, and C5 carries the phosphorus. The C2=C3 and C5=C6 double bonds are drawn explicitly.

**Ester side chain:** C(=O)OCCN(CH2Ph)Ph. The nitrogen carries a benzyl group and a phenyl group, so it is N-benzyl-N-phenylamino.

**Phosphorus ring:** P(=O) is bonded to two ring oxygens. The ring is P–O–CH2–C(CH3)2–CH2–O, a 5,5-dimethyl-1,3,2-dioxaphosphinane 2-oxide.

**Nitrophenyl:** the nitro group is meta to the attachment point. The ring atom attached to C4 is bonded to two ring atoms. One of these leads toward the nitro-bearing carbon through a CH, so the substitution is 1,3 (meta).

**SMILES assembly:**
- Start at the ester: CC1=C(C(=O)OCCN(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(P2(=O)OCC(C)(C)CO2)=C(C)N1
- Check the ring: C1(C)=C(ester)–C4H(Ar)–C(P)=C(C)–N1, which is consistent with the drawing.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)OCCN(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(P2(=O)OCC(C)(C)CO2)=C(C)N1

name: Edotreotide
text:
This is a DOTA-conjugated octreotide-type peptide (DOTA-TOC): DOTA–D-Phe–cyclo[Cys–Tyr–D-Trp–Lys–Thr–Cys] with a C-terminal threoninol, closed by a Cys–Cys disulfide bridge.

I read it region by region:
- **Left:** a 12-membered ring with four nitrogens, three N–CH2–COOH arms, and the fourth nitrogen acylated (N–CH2–C(=O)–NH) onto the Phe.
- **Phe:** D-configured, with a benzyl side chain.
- **Macrocycle:** Cys, Tyr (4-hydroxybenzyl), D-Trp (indol-3-ylmethyl), Lys (4-aminobutyl), Thr (CH(OH)CH3), then a second Cys. The two Cys are linked through CH2–S–S–CH2.
- **C-terminus:** the second Cys carbonyl is amidated onto threoninol, NH–CH(CH2OH)–CH(OH)CH3.

I assigned the stereocentres by working out the CIP descriptors for the threoninol and by following the standard L-amino-acid pattern for the rest, then converting each to SMILES chirality order. I did not re-check every wedge and hash against the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)N[C@H]3CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@H](CO)[C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2c[nH]c4ccccc24)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC3=O)CC1

name: Efinaconazole
text:
I read the drawing region by region.

- **Left ring:** a piperidine with an exocyclic C=CH2 at the 4-position. Its nitrogen is bonded to a CH carbon.
- **CH carbon:** it bears a methyl on a hashed wedge, so this is a stereocentre. Its other substituents are the piperidine N and the quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries an OH on a hashed wedge, a CH2 attached to a triazole, and a difluorophenyl ring. It is the second stereocentre.
- **Triazole:** a 1,2,4-triazole attached through N1 (N1–N2=C3–N4=C5), written as n1ncnc1.
- **Aryl ring:** a 2,4-difluorophenyl, with F on the carbon ortho to the attachment point and F para to it.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges.** For the CH carbon, the hashed methyl points away, so the implicit H is toward the viewer. Taking the order N, H, CH3, Cq, this gives `@`. For the quaternary carbon, the hashed OH points away. The other three substituents (CH up, aryl right, CH2 lower left) run clockwise on screen. Taking the order CH, O, CH2, aryl, this gives `@`.

SMILES: C=C1CCN(CC1)[C@H](C)[C@](O)(Cn1ncnc1)c1ccc(F)cc1F

name: Elacestrant
text:
I read the molecule as a 6-hydroxytetralin whose C2 carbon is the single stereocentre, drawn with a wedge to an aryl ring.

**Aryl ring on the wedge.** It carries an N-ethyl-N-benzyl amine ortho to the tetralin attachment and a methoxy group para to that attachment.

**Benzyl group.** It is a para-disubstituted benzene bearing a CH2CH2NHEt chain on the other side.

**Stereochemistry.** At the stereocentre, the aryl group is toward the viewer on the wedge, so the implicit H points away. Viewed with H away, the three carbon neighbours run aryl → right-hand CH2 → upper-left CH2 counterclockwise. In my SMILES the neighbour order is aryl, H, ring-closure CH2 (the upper-left one), then the other CH2. That order corresponds to `@@`.

I checked that the SMILES builds each ring and chain as drawn, with the ring-closure digit matching the CH2 attached to the aromatic carbon.

SMILES: CCNCCc1ccc(CN(CC)c2cc(OC)ccc2[C@@H]2CCc3cc(O)ccc3C2)cc1

name: Elagolix
text:
This structure is elagolix. I read it region by region.

- **Left aryl ring:** a benzene ring carrying OMe and F on adjacent positions, attached to C5 of the central pyrimidine-2,4-dione ring.
- **Central ring:** a uracil-type ring with a methyl on C6, and C2 and C4 both carrying C=O. N1 carries the benzyl group and N3 carries the side chain.
- **N1 benzyl group:** a CH2 linked to a benzene ring bearing F on one ortho position and CF3 on the other.
- **N3 side chain:** N–CH2–CH(Ph)–NH–CH2CH2CH2–COOH, where the CH is the only stereocentre.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedge runs from the stereocentre to the CH2 attached to N3, so the CH2 points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CH2(N) > phenyl > H. Viewed from the front, N → CH2 → phenyl runs clockwise, so the centre is R. Written as `n(C[C@H](NCCCC(O)=O)c2ccccc2)`, the `@` corresponds to R.

SMILES: COc1cccc(c1F)-c1c(C)n(Cc2c(F)cccc2C(F)(F)F)c(=O)n(C[C@H](NCCCC(O)=O)c2ccccc2)c1=O

name: Eletriptan Hydrobromide
text:
This is eletriptan hydrobromide. I read it region by region:

- **Pyrrolidine:** an N-methylpyrrolidine ring (N with a methyl, then three ring CH2 groups and the stereocentre carbon).
- **Link to indole:** a CH2 joins the stereocentre to C3 of a 1H-indole (the drawn NH is part of the five-membered ring).
- **Indole substituent:** a CH2CH2 chain on C5 of the indole ends in a sulfonyl group (S with two =O), which carries a phenyl ring.
- **Salt:** HBr is drawn as a separate component.

**Stereochemistry:** The only wedge is on the bond from the pyrrolidine C2 to the exocyclic CH2. The CIP priorities at that carbon are N, then the exocyclic CH2 (its next atom is indole C3, with substituents C,C,C), then the ring CH2, then H. The H sits behind the plane. Going N → exocyclic CH2 → ring CH2 runs clockwise on the page, so the centre is R. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written with the ring CH2 first encodes that R configuration.

SMILES: CN1CCC[C@@H]1CC2=CNC3=C2C=C(C=C3)CCS(=O)(=O)C4=CC=CC=C4.Br

name: Elinogrel
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left bicycle:** a quinazoline-2,4-dione. The benzo ring carries F and NHMe. N3 is attached to the phenyl ring, and N1 is NH.
- **Benzo ring substituents:** F sits on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears C4 (the C=O). NHMe sits on the next carbon, which is adjacent to the CH that leads to the ring-fusion carbon bearing N1.
- **Middle:** a para-substituted phenyl ring.
- **Right side:** the phenyl carries NH–C(=O)–NH–S(=O)(=O)–thiophene, a sulfonylurea. The thiophene is attached at C2 and has Cl at C5.

SMILES, tracing from the NHMe group:

CNc1cc2[nH]c(=O)n(c(=O)c2cc1F)-c1ccc(NC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(Cl)s2)cc1

Check on the benzo ring: c1 (NHMe), c (CH), c2 (fusion carbon bearing N1), [nH], c(=O), n, c(=O), c2 (fusion carbon bearing C4), c (CH), c1F. In the drawing, the fusion carbon at the upper right is attached to C4 (=O) and to the CH, which is attached to the C–F carbon. The C–F carbon is attached to the C–NHMe carbon, which is attached to the CH that leads to the fusion carbon bearing N1. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: CNc1cc2[nH]c(=O)n(-c3ccc(NC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c4ccc(Cl)s4)cc3)c(=O)c2cc1F

name: Echinocandin B
text:
I read the image as a cyclic lipohexapeptide of the echinocandin type, carrying a linoleoyl side chain. This is an atom-by-atom reading of the drawing, not a match against a known compound.

**Side chain.** Counting from the amide carbonyl gives 18 carbons, with cis double bonds at C9–C10 and C12–C13. That is a linoleoyl group, written `CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)N`.

**Ring.** The macrocycle contains six residues, in order from the acylated amine:
1. A dihydroxyornithine bearing the N-acyl group. The atom drawn as a bare "C" is just its CH2.
2. A 3-hydroxy-4-methylproline.
3. A threonine.
4. A 4-hydroxyproline.
5. A threonine.
6. A dihydroxy-homotyrosine, whose side chain ends in a 4-hydroxyphenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash bond and the angular order of its neighbours. Unspecified centres (none) would have been left plain.

I checked that the ring-closure digits pair correctly and that the SMILES covers every atom in the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)NC(=O)[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)CN2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H]3C[C@@H](O)CN3C(=O)[C@@H](NC1=O)[C@@H](C)O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)c1ccc(O)cc1)[C@@H](C)O

name: Eliprodil
text:
The drawing shows these parts:

- A 4-chlorophenyl ring on the left, bonded to a CH(OH) carbon.
- A CH2 linking that carbon to the nitrogen of a piperidine ring.
- At the piperidine 4-position, a CH2 leading to a 4-fluorophenyl ring.

The CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so I include no stereochemistry.
