name: Esomeprazole Magnesium
text:
The drawing shows magnesium bis(esomeprazole), i.e. two identical 5-methoxybenzimidazolide–sulfinyl–pyridine units with one Mg²⁺.

**Each ligand:**
- **Pyridine ring:** the CH2 on the carbon next to N, then methyl, methoxy and methyl on the next three ring carbons, and a CH next to the methyl at the far end of the ring.
- **Linker:** the CH2 connects to a sulfoxide S(=O), which is bonded to C2 of the benzimidazole.
- **Benzimidazole:** one ring nitrogen carries the negative charge ([n-]). The benzo ring has an OCH3 group.

**Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the sulfur. The wedge to the CH2 puts that group toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are O > C2 of the benzimidazole > CH2 > lone pair. Viewed from the front, O → C2 → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the sulfur is S, as in esomeprazole. In SMILES, written as `c(...)[S@@](=O)Cc`, this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: [Mg+2].COc1ccc2[n-]c(nc2c1)[S@@](=O)Cc1ncc(C)c(OC)c1C.COc1ccc2[n-]c(nc2c1)[S@@](=O)Cc1ncc(C)c(OC)c1C

name: Estramustine
text:
This is estramustine, which is estradiol with its 3-hydroxyl converted to a bis(2-chloroethyl)carbamate. I read it region by region.

- **Aromatic A ring:** it sits on the right and carries an O–C(=O)–N(CH2CH2Cl)2 group, which is the carbamate ester.
- **Steroid core:** the B and C rings are six-membered and the D ring is a five-membered ring on the left, the usual estra-1,3,5(10)-triene skeleton.
- **D ring substituents:** the 17-OH and the C13 methyl are both drawn with wedges.
- **Ring-junction hydrogens:** H at C8 is a wedge, H at C9 is hashed, and H at C14 is hashed. This matches the natural estradiol configuration (8R, 9S, 13S, 14S, 17S).

I took the stereo SMILES from natural estradiol and replaced the phenol OH with the carbamate.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O)CCC4=C3C=CC(=C4)OC(=O)N(CCCl)CCCl

name: Estriol
text:
The drawing shows the estra-1,3,5(10)-triene steroid skeleton (aromatic A ring, three further fused rings) with three features:

- a phenolic OH on the aromatic ring (C3);
- two OH groups on the five-membered D ring, one hashed and one wedged (C16 and C17);
- a wedged methyl at the ring-fusion carbon (C13), and three ring-fusion hydrogens drawn with wedges or hashes (C8, C9, C14).

The 16-OH is hashed (α) and the 17-OH is wedged (β), and the ring-fusion stereo matches the natural steroid pattern. The molecule is therefore estriol. The drawing is the standard steroid layout rotated 180° in the plane, which does not change the chirality.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the drawing. I wrote the stereo SMILES for estriol from memory and checked it against the drawn wedges and hashes only by the natural-steroid argument above.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1C[C@H]([C@@H]2O)O)CCC4=C3C=CC(=C4)O

name: Etamsylate
text:
The image shows two separate components, diethylamine and 2,5-dihydroxybenzenesulfonic acid, written together as a salt or mixture.

**Diethylamine:** CCNCC, with the NH in the middle of two ethyl groups.

**Aryl component:** a benzene ring carrying a sulfonic acid group (S with two =O and one OH) on one carbon. Going around the ring, the next carbon (lower left) carries an OH, so that OH is ortho to the sulfonic acid. The ring carbon at the upper right carries the other OH.

I numbered the ring atoms as follows:
- C1 (at about 674,838) bears the sulfonic acid.
- C2 (at about 720,1096) bears an OH.
- C3 (at about 965,1185) has no substituent.
- C4 (at about 1167,1017) has no substituent.
- C5 (at about 1120,760) bears an OH.
- C6 (at about 875,669) has no substituent.

The OH groups are therefore at positions 2 and 5 relative to the sulfonic acid at position 1. Both rings and substituents are drawn with plain bonds and no charges, so there is no stereochemistry and the components are written as neutral molecules.

SMILES: CCNCC.O=S(=O)(O)c1cc(O)ccc1O

name: Estrone
text:
The drawing is estrone, a steroid with an aromatic A ring carrying a hydroxyl group and a ketone on the five-membered D ring. I read it as follows:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with an OH substituent at the far right.
- **Middle rings:** two fused six-membered rings, the B ring with two CH2 groups and the C ring with two CH2 groups.
- **Five-membered ring:** it carries a C=O at the lower left and the quaternary carbon bearing the methyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is a wedge, the H at the top ring junction is a wedge, and the H at the ring junction next to the five-membered ring and the H at the lower ring junction are both hashed. This matches natural estrone (8R, 9S, 13S, 14S).

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom. I wrote the SMILES from my recollection of the standard estrone SMILES, and the drawn wedges and hashes agree with natural estrone.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CCC2=O)CCC4=C3C=CC(=C4)O

name: Eritoran
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing as a bisphosphorylated, doubly glycosylated lipid-A-like molecule. The chain lengths are my best estimate from counting zigzag vertices, so those are the least certain parts. I assigned the stereo marks from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing.

**Left (reducing-end) pyranose ring**
- C1 carries an α-phosphate (hashed bond).
- C2 carries an NH-acyl group (hashed bond). The acyl group is 3-oxotetradecanoyl, with 11 carbons after the ketone.
- C3 carries an O-decyl group (wedge).
- C4 carries OH (hashed bond).
- C5 carries a CH2–O link (wedge) to the second ring.

**Right (non-reducing) pyranose ring**
- C1 is joined to that CH2–O through a glycosidic oxygen (hashed bond).
- C2 carries an NH-acyl group (wedge). The acyl group is a 16-carbon chain with a cis double bond at C9=C10 (palmitoleoyl).
- C3 carries O–CH2CH2–CH(OMe)–C6H13 (hashed bond). The stereocentre in this chain is read with the hash starting at that carbon.
- C4 carries a phosphate (wedge).
- C5 carries CH2OMe (hashed bond).

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)CC(=O)N[C@H]1[C@@H](OP(=O)(O)O)O[C@H](CO[C@@H]2O[C@H](COC)[C@@H](OP(=O)(O)O)[C@H](OCC[C@H](OC)CCCCCC)[C@H]2NC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\CCCCCC)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1OCCCCCCCCCC

name: Ethaselen
text:
The drawing shows two benzisoselenazolone units joined through their nitrogen atoms by an ethylene bridge (–CH2–CH2–).

Each unit is a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. That five-membered ring contains Se, N, a C=O carbon, and the two fused aromatic carbons, with an Se–N bond closing the ring. This is the ebselen-type scaffold. Each N carries the CH2 of the linker.

One unit written as SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2[Se]N1R, where R is the linker CH2.

Joining the two units through the two-carbon linker gives:

O=C1c2ccccc2[Se]N1CCN1[Se]c2ccccc2C1=O

Ring-closure check for the second unit: N1 opens ring 1, then [Se], then c2ccccc2 (the benzene ring), then C1=O closes ring 1 back to N. The ring is N, Se, c, c, C, which is five atoms. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2[Se]N1CCN1[Se]c2ccccc2C1=O

name: Ethambutol
text:
I read this as ethambutol, with both stereocentres S.

**Connectivity.** The skeleton is HOCH2–CH(Et)–NH–CH2CH2–NH–CH(Et)–CH2OH. Each end has an ethyl group and a CH2OH on the same carbon as the NH. The two ends are linked through an N–CH2–CH2–N bridge.

**Stereochemistry.** Each stereocentre has a wedge bond to its ethyl carbon, so the implicit H points away from the viewer.
- Priorities at each centre are N > CH2OH > CH2CH3 > H.
- On the left centre, going N (right) → CH2OH (up) → ethyl (lower left) runs counterclockwise on the page. With H at the back, that is S.
- The right centre has the same arrangement (N left, CH2OH down, ethyl upper right), so it is also S.

**SMILES check.** In `CC[C@@H](CO)N…N[C@@H](CC)CO`, the first centre has neighbour order ethyl, H, CH2OH, N. With `@@` this works out to S. The second centre has neighbour order N, H, ethyl, CH2OH. With `@@` this also works out to S. Both match the drawing.

SMILES: CC[C@@H](CO)NCCN[C@@H](CC)CO

name: Ethinylestradiol
text:
This drawing is ethinylestradiol (17α-ethynylestradiol), and I wrote the SMILES from that identification. I did not re-derive each @/@@ symbol from the wedges, so the stereo string comes from my memory of the PubChem entry.

- **Skeleton:** the drawing is a steroid with a fused four-ring core. On the right is an aromatic A ring carrying a phenolic OH. Two six-membered rings follow, then a five-membered D ring on the left.
- **C17 (D ring):** this carbon bears both a tertiary OH, drawn with a bold wedge, and an ethynyl group (C≡CH).
- **C13:** carries a methyl drawn with a bold wedge.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** H at C8 is drawn bold, and H at C9 and H at C14 are drawn hashed.

The wedge pattern is consistent with the natural estradiol configuration, so I used that stereochemistry.

SMILES: C#C[C@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CCC4=C3C=CC(=C4)O)C)O

name: (+-)-Ethopropazine
text:
The drawing shows a phenothiazine core with a side chain on the ring nitrogen. This is ethopropazine (profenamine).

**Side chain:** The ring nitrogen is bonded to a CH2, then a CH that carries a methyl group, then a nitrogen bearing two ethyl groups. This gives N(CC(C)N(CC)CC).

**Ring system:** The ring nitrogen sits between two benzene rings that are also joined through sulfur. The ring is drawn with plain bonds, so there is no stereochemistry to add. The core is c1ccc2c(c1)Sc1ccccc1N2.

**Combined:** CCN(CC)C(C)CN1c2ccccc2Sc2ccccc21

Checking against the drawing:
- The left benzene ring has six carbons, two of them fused to the N and S bridge atoms.
- The right benzene ring is likewise six carbons.
- The chain from ring N is CH2, then CH(CH3), then N(Et)2, which matches.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(C)CN1c2ccccc2Sc2ccccc21

name: Ethosuximide
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered succinimide ring (pyrrolidine-2,5-dione) with one quaternary carbon.

Ring atoms: the quaternary carbon C3 (at about 568,889), a C=O carbon at (535,565) bonded to NH, the NH, a second C=O carbon at (1055,675), and a CH2 at (888,960) that links the second C=O carbon back to C3.

Substituents on the quaternary carbon: an ethyl group (the carbon at (238,889) and the one at (75,605)) and a methyl group (at (533,1217)).

The structure is therefore 3-ethyl-3-methylpyrrolidine-2,5-dione (ethosuximide).

The quaternary carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the drawing uses only plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CCC1(C)CC(=O)NC1=O

name: Ethotoin
text:
The drawing shows a hydantoin ring (imidazolidine-2,4-dione) with these features:

- An ethyl group is attached to the ring nitrogen at the lower left (N-CH2-CH3).
- That nitrogen sits between two carbonyl carbons. One is the upper C=O, which is also bonded to NH (a urea carbonyl). The other is the lower C=O, which is also bonded to the CH carbon (an amide carbonyl).
- The NH is bonded to the CH carbon, which carries a phenyl substituent.
- The CH carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereochemistry.

Writing the SMILES from the ethyl group around the ring: CCN1C(=O)NC(c2ccccc2)C1=O. The ring closure works as follows: N1 bonds to C(=O), then NH, then CH(Ph), then C1(=O), which closes back to N1.

SMILES: CCN1C(=O)NC(c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Ethyl alcohol-d6
text:
The drawing shows ethanol with every hydrogen written as deuterium (²H).

- The oxygen is bonded to one ²H, giving an O–D group.
- The oxygen is also bonded to a carbon (CH2) carrying two ²H atoms.
- That carbon is bonded to a second carbon (CH3) carrying three ²H atoms.
- This gives six deuteriums in total: one on O, two on the first carbon and three on the second.

The SMILES is [2H]OC([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])[2H].

SMILES: [2H]OC([2H])([2H])C([2H])([2H])[2H]

name: Etelcalcetide
text:
I read this as a linear peptide, Ac‑Cys‑Ala‑Arg‑Arg‑Arg‑Ala‑Arg‑NH2, with the N‑terminal Cys joined by a disulfide bond to a free cysteine that carries the C‑terminal acid.

**Connectivity**
- An N‑terminal acetyl group (CH3C(=O)–) caps the first cysteine's nitrogen.
- That cysteine's CH2–S–S–CH2 bridge leads to a second cysteine with a free NH2 and a free COOH.
- The backbone runs Cys, Ala, Arg, Arg, Arg, Ala, Arg.
- Each arginine side chain is CH2CH2CH2–N=C(NH2)2.
- The C‑terminus is a primary amide, C(=O)NH2.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash, using the rule that with H toward the viewer, L amino acids read CO→R→N clockwise.
- The free cysteine, drawn with a wedged NH2, comes out L.
- Every residue in the chain comes out D. These are the first Cys, both Ala and all four Arg.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H](CSSC[C@H](N)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N

name: Ethyl Biscoumacetate
text:
The drawing shows ethyl 2,2-bis(4-hydroxy-2-oxo-2H-chromen-3-yl)acetate, which is two 4-hydroxycoumarin units joined through a central CH that also carries an ethyl ester.

**Left coumarin:** the ring oxygen O1 connects to the benzo ring carbon and to C2, which is a C=O. C3 is double-bonded to C4, which carries the OH. C4 attaches to the benzo carbon C4a. C3 is bonded to the central CH.

**Right coumarin:** the connectivity is the same as the left unit.

**Central CH:** it bears both coumarin C3 atoms and the ester group C(=O)OCC.

Writing the left coumarin as a SMILES fragment: O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1.

The full SMILES, with the central CH joining the two C3 atoms and the ester, is:

CCOC(=O)C(C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O)C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O

Ring check for the first coumarin: C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O. C1 is C3, =C(O) is C4, c2ccccc2 is the benzo ring, O is the ring oxygen, and C1=O closes the ring at C2. This is valid.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C(C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O)C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O

name: Ethyl pyruvate
text:
The drawing shows ethyl pyruvate.

Reading the structure from left to right:
- A methyl carbon at the far left is bonded to a carbon with a double-bonded O (the ketone).
- That ketone carbon is bonded to a second carbon, which carries a double-bonded O (C=O) and a single-bonded O (the ester oxygen).
- The ester oxygen is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a CH3 (the ethyl group).

This gives CC(=O)C(=O)OCC. All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C(C)=O

name: Ethylenediaminetetra(methylenephosphonic acid)
text:
The drawing shows ethylenediamine tetra(methylenephosphonic acid) (EDTMP).

- Two nitrogens are joined by a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2–N).
- Each nitrogen carries two CH2–P(=O)(OH)2 groups.
- That gives four phosphonic acid groups in total: two on the left nitrogen (top and left) and two on the right nitrogen (right and bottom).

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)CN(CP(O)(O)=O)CCN(CP(O)(O)=O)CP(O)(O)=O

name: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic Acid
text:
The drawing shows EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid).

- Two nitrogen atoms are linked by a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2–N).
- Each nitrogen carries two CH2–COOH arms, giving four carboxylic acid groups in total.
- All bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CC(=O)O

name: Etidronic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon with four substituents: a methyl group (the vertical line going up), an OH group (going down), and a phosphonic acid group on each side.

Each phosphorus carries one =O and two OH groups, and is bonded to the central carbon. This is etidronic acid (HEDP).

SMILES: CC(O)(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O

name: Etidocaine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with two methyl groups on the carbons flanking the carbon that bears the NH (a 2,6-dimethylphenyl group).
- **Amide:** the ring carbon is bonded to NH, which is bonded to a C=O carbon.
- **Alpha carbon:** the carbonyl is bonded to a CH that carries an ethyl group (CH2CH3) and a nitrogen.
- **Amine:** that nitrogen is tertiary. One substituent is an ethyl group, drawn as N–CH2–CH3 going right. The other is a propyl group, drawn as N–CH2–CH2–CH3 going up.

No wedges or hashes are shown, so there is no stereochemistry.

Written as SMILES, starting from the ring methyls: Cc1cccc(C)c1NC(=O)C(CC)N(CC)CCC

Atom check: the ring has 6 carbons plus 2 methyls. The chain has C=O, CH, the ethyl group (2 carbons), N-ethyl (2 carbons) and N-propyl (3 carbons). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCN(CC)C(CC)C(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Ethyl p-nitrophenyl benzenethiophosphonate, (-)-
text:
This structure is EPN, O-ethyl O-(4-nitrophenyl) phenylphosphonothioate.

**Connectivity**
- The phosphorus carries four substituents: a P=S double bond, an ethoxy group (O–CH2–CH3), an aryloxy group (O–C6H4–NO2), and a phenyl ring bonded directly to P.
- The aryloxy ring is para-substituted, with the nitro group drawn as N⁺(=O)O⁻.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only stereo marking is the hashed bond from P to the ethoxy oxygen, so P is the single stereocentre.
- Seen from the front, the other three substituents run S → O-aryl → phenyl clockwise.
- The ethoxy group points away from the viewer, so looking from it toward P reverses this to counterclockwise.
- With the neighbour order OEt, S, OAr, Ph in the SMILES, counterclockwise corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: CCO[P@](=S)(Oc1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-])c1ccccc1

name: Eremomycin
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing region by region. It describes a vancomycin/chloroeremomycin-type glycopeptide. I have not run it through a parser, so the stereo tags in particular were assigned by hand from the wedges and hashes and are unverified.

**What I read from the image**
- **Chain:** the peptide runs N-methyl-D-leucine → β-hydroxy-chlorotyrosine → Asn → a central tri-oxygenated aryl-glycine → a hydroxyphenylglycine → a β-hydroxytyrosine → a dihydroxyphenylglycine bearing the free COOH.
- **Chlorinated ring:** the ring on the β-hydroxy residue carries one Cl and is linked through an ether O to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** it carries two aryl ether links (to the chlorinated ring and to the para-phenylene ring) and one O-glycoside.
- **Left sugar:** an amino-methyl deoxy sugar (vancosamine type) sits on the benzylic oxygen of the β-hydroxytyrosine.
- **Right sugar:** a glucose is on the central ring and carries a second amino-methyl deoxy sugar on its 2-position.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each @/@@ from the wedges and hashes at the amino-acid α/β carbons and at every sugar ring centre.

name: Etodolac
text:
This drawing looks like etodolac: a pyrano[3,4-b]indole core with an ethyl group on the quaternary carbon, an ethyl group on the benzene ring, and a CH2COOH side chain.

Reading the atoms and bonds:
- The quaternary carbon (C1) at about (483, 643) carries an ethyl group (CH2 at 285,713, then CH3 at 127,578), a CH2COOH group, the ring oxygen, and the indole C2.
- The ring oxygen connects to CH2 (483,280), then CH2 (692,282), then the indole C3 at (797,462).
- C3 is double-bonded to C2 at (692,643), and C2 bonds to NH.
- NH bonds to C7a at (1022,714), which is part of the benzene ring.
- The benzene ring runs C7a, C7 (1213,800, bearing the ethyl group), C6 (1383,678), C5 (1361,470), C4 (1170,384), and C3a (1001,507).
- C3a bonds to C3.

SMILES, written from the ring-closure labels:
CCC1(CC(=O)O)OCCc2c1[nH]c1c(CC)cccc21

Checking the connectivity of this SMILES:
- C1 is the quaternary carbon, with the ethyl group and CC(=O)O attached.
- O, C, C then lead to c2, the indole C3.
- c1 is the indole C2, closing ring 1 to the quaternary carbon.
- [nH] follows, then c1 (C7a, opening a new ring 1), then c(CC) (C7 with the ethyl group), then ccc for C6, C5, C4.
- The final c21 is C3a, which closes ring 2 to C3 and ring 1 to C7a.

The ring closures are consistent, so this matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCC1(CC(=O)O)OCCc2c1[nH]c1c(CC)cccc21

name: Etomidate
text:
This structure is etomidate, the ethyl ester of a 1-(1-phenylethyl)imidazole-5-carboxylic acid.

- **Ester:** an ethyl group on an oxygen, attached to a C=O, which is bonded to the imidazole ring.
- **Imidazole:** a five-membered ring with two nitrogens. The ester-bearing carbon sits next to the substituted nitrogen. That nitrogen carries the 1-phenylethyl group, and the other nitrogen is the unsubstituted ring N.
- **Side chain:** a stereocentre bonded to the imidazole N, a phenyl ring, a methyl group drawn with a hashed bond, and an implicit H.

For the stereochemistry, the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > phenyl > CH3 > H. The hashed methyl puts the implicit H toward the viewer. On the page, N → phenyl → CH3 runs counterclockwise, so with H toward the viewer the true sense is clockwise, giving R. The SMILES `n1[C@H](C)c1ccccc1`, with neighbours in the order N, H, CH3, phenyl, encodes this R configuration.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)c1cncn1[C@H](C)c1ccccc1

name: Etoposide
text:
This drawing matches etoposide (4'-demethylepipodophyllotoxin 4,6-O-ethylidene-β-D-glucopyranoside). I identified it by its overall features and wrote the SMILES from the known etoposide structure, so I did not re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

- **Aglycone:** a methylenedioxy-fused aromatic ring, a tetralin core and a γ-lactone (C=O with a ring O–CH2).
- **Pendant aryl group:** a 4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl ring.
- **Sugar:** a glucopyranose attached through a glycosidic O, with two free OH groups and a 4,6-O-ethylidene acetal carrying a methyl group.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1OC[C@@H]2[C@@H](O1)[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H](O2)O[C@H]3[C@H]4[C@@H](COC4=O)[C@@H](C5=CC6=C(C=C35)OCO6)C7=CC(=C(C(=C7)OC)O)OC)O)O

name: Etoricoxib
text:
The drawing is an etoricoxib-type structure: a bipyridine core carrying a 4-(methylsulfonyl)phenyl group and a methyl group.

**Ring A (chloropyridine):** Going around the ring, the atoms are C(Cl), CH, C(aryl), C(=N), N, CH. The C bearing Cl sits at about (210, 346). A CH at (398, 354) connects to the C at (485, 522), which carries the phenyl group. That C connects to the C at (384, 680), which is double-bonded to N at (200, 672). N connects to the CH at (109, 504), which closes back to the C(Cl).

**Ring B (methylpyridine):** The C at (384, 680) is bonded to a C at (470, 848) in the second ring. The ring continues through CH (658, 857), CH (743, 1023), C(CH3) (642, 1182), N (455, 1172), and CH (369, 1006), which closes back to (470, 848). The methyl group is on the C at (642, 1182).

**Phenyl ring:** It is attached at (673, 531) and is para-substituted with S(=O)(=O)CH3.

**SMILES:**
- Ring A: c1(Cl)cnc(c(c1)...) with the substituents placed as described above.
- Full molecule: Cc1ccc(cn1)-c1ncc(Cl)cc1-c1ccc(cc1)S(C)(=O)=O

Check on ring A: the aromatic atoms run c1 (the C bearing ring B), n, c (CH), c(Cl), c (CH), c1 (the C bearing the aryl). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cn1)-c1ncc(Cl)cc1-c1ccc(cc1)S(C)(=O)=O

name: Etonogestrel
text:
I did not derive the stereo marks atom by atom. I read the connectivity from the drawing and took the stereo from the known SMILES for etonogestrel, after checking it against the wedges and hashes.

**Connectivity read from the image**
- It is a steroid skeleton with four fused rings.
- The A ring on the right is a 4-en-3-one: a C=O with a C=C in conjugation.
- C11 carries an exocyclic methylene (=CH2).
- C13 carries an ethyl group.
- C17 carries both an OH and an ethynyl group (C≡CH).

**Stereochemistry check**
- The ethyl on C13 and the OH on C17 are both hashed, so they sit on the same face.
- The H on C14 is wedged, so it is trans to the C13 ethyl.
- The H on C8 is hashed and the H on C9 is wedged, so they are trans, as expected for a natural-configuration steroid.
- The H on C10 is hashed.

This relative arrangement matches the ring-fusion pattern of etonogestrel, which is drawn here in a flipped orientation.

SMILES: CC[C@]12CC(=C)[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C#C)O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@H]34

name: Etravirine
text:
This is etravirine, a diarylpyrimidine.

**Pyrimidine ring.** C5 carries Br. C4 carries NH2 and sits between C5 and N3. C2 carries the NH-aryl group and sits between N3 and N1. C6 carries the O-aryl group and sits between N1 and C5.

**Left aryl ring (via O).** The carbon attached to O has a methyl on each neighbouring carbon. The carbon para to O carries the nitrile (C#N). The remaining two ring positions are CH.

**Right aryl ring (via NH).** This is a para-cyanophenyl group.

**SMILES.** Writing the pyrimidine as Nc1nc(Nc2ccc(C#N)cc2)nc(Oc2c(C)cc(C#N)cc2C)c1Br gives the connectivity above.

SMILES: Nc1nc(Nc2ccc(C#N)cc2)nc(Oc2c(C)cc(C#N)cc2C)c1Br

name: Eugenol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents: a hydroxyl group (HO), a methoxy group (OMe) on the adjacent carbon, and an allyl chain (CH2-CH=CH2) on the carbon para to the OH. This is eugenol.

The ring atoms, by approximate position, are:
- C1 at (398, 550), bearing OH.
- C2 at (511, 750), bearing OMe.
- C3 at (738, 750), a CH.
- C4 at (853, 553), bearing the allyl group.
- C5 at (740, 355), a CH.
- C6 at (512, 353), a CH.

The OH carbon and the OMe carbon are adjacent, and the allyl carbon is para to the OH carbon.

The ring bonds are drawn as alternating double bonds: C1=C2, C3=C4 and C5=C6. The allyl chain is CH2 attached to the ring, then CH=CH2.

SMILES: C=CCc1ccc(O)c(OC)c1

SMILES: C=CCc1ccc(O)c(OC)c1

name: Etrasimod
text:
I read the molecule as a tricyclic cyclopenta[b]indole core carrying an acetic acid side chain and a benzyl ether, and the stereocentre was assigned from the wedge bond.

- **Core:** a benzene ring fused to a pyrrole (the NH) and then to a cyclopentane. This is a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydrocyclopenta[b]indole.
- **Acid side chain:** the stereocentre is the cyclopentane carbon next to the NH-bearing carbon. It carries a CH2–COOH group on a wedge bond.
- **Ether:** an O–CH2 link goes from the benzene ring of the core to a second benzene ring.
- **Second benzene ring:** it has a cyclopentyl group at the para position relative to the CH2. A CF3 group sits ortho to the cyclopentyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the acid CH2 is wedged toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Going acid CH2 → N-bearing ring carbon → ring CH2 runs counterclockwise from the front. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order (acid CH2, H, N-bearing carbon via ring closure, ring CH2) gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OC(=O)C[C@H]1CCc2c1[nH]c1ccc(OCc3ccc(C4CCCC4)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)cc21

name: Etretinate
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- **Ester end:** an ethyl group (CH3–CH2) is attached through O to a C=O carbon, so this is an ethyl ester.
- **Chain:** the carbonyl carbon is followed by a four-double-bond polyene (C2=C3, C4=C5, C6=C7, C8=C9). There are methyl branches on C3 and C7.
- **Ring:** C9 attaches to a benzene ring. Going round from the attachment carbon, the ring carries a methyl, a methyl, an OMe, a ring CH, and a methyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** from the coordinates, the chain substituents across each double bond lie on opposite sides, so all four double bonds are E. For C2=C3 and C6=C7, the carbons carrying the main chain are trans to each other, and the methyls sit cis to the preceding chain carbon.

This matches etretinate, ethyl (2E,4E,6E,8E)-9-(4-methoxy-2,3,6-trimethylphenyl)-3,7-dimethylnona-2,4,6,8-tetraenoate.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)/C=C(\C)/C=C/C=C(\C)/C=C/c1c(C)c(C)c(OC)cc1C

name: Esperamicin A1
text:
I read this as a calicheamicin-type enediyne. Its aryl amide carries a 2-methoxyacryloyl group, and the amino sugar carries an isopropylamino group instead of the usual ethylamino. I wrote the SMILES region by region, then assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds as drawn. I did not run a validity check or a structure-to-image comparison, so the stereo assignments rest on my hand reading of the wedges.

**Regions and connectivity**

- **Aryl ester:** a 4,5-dimethoxybenzoate whose ortho NH is acylated by CH2=C(OMe)–C(=O)–. The ester oxygen sits on C3 of the top-right 2,6-dideoxy sugar, which has a 4-OH and a 5-methyl.
- **Core:**
  - A cyclohexenone with a C=C bearing NHCO2Me.
  - A CH–O (glycosidic) carbon next to the ketone.
  - A quaternary C(OH).
  - An exocyclic C=CH–CH2–S–S–S–CH3, drawn with the CH2 cis to the ring C3.
  - A ten-membered ring in the order C≡C–CH=CH–C≡C, with the double bond drawn cis. It closes onto the carbon bearing the long hashed O-glycoside bond.
- **Central pyranose:** carries a 3-OH, a 4-NH–O– linkage to the lower sugar, and a 5-methyl. Its C2 oxygen links to the upper-left sugar.
- **Upper-left sugar:** a 4-OMe, 5-NH-isopropyl pyranose.
- **Lower sugar:** a 4-OH, 3-SMe, 5-methyl pyranose, attached through its anomeric O to the N of the central sugar.

**Stereochemistry:** the wedge and hash bonds fix the sugar centres and the three core stereocentres. I also encoded the cis ring alkene and the cis exocyclic C=C.
