name: Evobrutinib
text:
The drawing shows a pyrimidine ring, drawn in kekulé form, with these atoms and substituents:

- Ring atoms: N1 at the top left, a CH at the top, N3 at the top right, C4 at the right, C5 at the bottom, and C6 at the left.
- C6 (left) carries NH2.
- C4 (right) carries an NH–CH2 group.
- C5 (bottom) carries a phenyl ring.

The substituent chains are:

- The NH–CH2 group is attached to C4 of a piperidine ring. The piperidine nitrogen is acylated with an acryloyl group, C(=O)C=C.
- The phenyl ring on C5 has a phenoxy group (O–Ph) at its para position.

Writing the pyrimidine as c1ncnc(NCC2CCN(C(=O)C=C)CC2)c1-c1ccc(Oc2ccccc2)cc1 with the amino group placed on the correct carbon gives:

Nc1ncnc(NCC2CCN(C(=O)C=C)CC2)c1-c1ccc(Oc2ccccc2)cc1

Atom check: the ring runs C(NH2), N, CH, N, C(NH-), C(Ar), which is six atoms and matches the drawing.

SMILES: Nc1ncnc(NCC2CCN(C(=O)C=C)CC2)c1-c1ccc(Oc2ccccc2)cc1

name: Everolimus
text:
This is everolimus (the 40-O-(2-hydroxyethyl) derivative of rapamycin). I recognised the scaffold and wrote the SMILES from that recall rather than assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo labels are not independently checked against the drawing.

What the drawing shows, region by region:
- A 31-membered macrolactone ring.
- A pipecolate ring (piperidine with N-acyl) that joins an α-keto amide to the ester carbonyl.
- A hemiketal carbon bearing OH, closed into a tetrahydropyran ring that carries a methyl group.
- A conjugated triene with a methyl substituent, and a second trisubstituted alkene with a methyl substituent.
- Three ketones, two OH groups and two OMe groups on the macrocycle.
- A side chain, CH(CH3)–CH2–cyclohexyl, where the cyclohexane carries an OMe and an OCH2CH2OH group. The OCH2CH2OH group is what distinguishes everolimus from rapamycin.

I checked the ring closures and the ketone–CH2–CH(O-ester) sequence against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2C[C@@H](/C(=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H](C(=O)[C@@H]([C@@H](/C(=C/[C@H](C(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)[C@@H]3CCCCN3C(=O)C(=O)[C@@]1(O2)O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4CC[C@H]([C@@H](C4)OC)OCCO)C)/C)O)OC)C)C)/C)OC

name: Evacetrapib
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Acid end:** a cyclohexane carries a COOH group. At the 1,4-relationship from the acid carbon, a CH2 links the ring to the azepine nitrogen. No cis/trans geometry is drawn on this ring, so I gave it no stereo marks.
- **Benzazepine core:** a seven-membered ring contains the N, three CH2 groups, one CH, and two fused aromatic carbons. The fused benzene ring carries two methyl groups: one next to the ring carbon bonded to N, and one meta to it.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH carries a wedged bond to the exocyclic N. Working out the geometry with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer, the N → aryl → CH2 sequence runs counterclockwise. With the SMILES neighbour order CH2, H, N, aryl, this gives `[C@H]`.
- **Exocyclic N substituents:** the N carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group and a tetrazole.
- **Tetrazole:** it is attached through its carbon. The methylated N is flanked by one ring N on one side and by an N–N pair leading back to the carbon on the other. This makes it a 2-methyl-2H-tetrazol-5-yl group, written `c4nn(C)nn4`.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1CCC(CC1)CN2CCC[C@H](N(Cc3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c3)c4nn(C)nn4)c5cc(C)cc(C)c25

name: Evofosfamide
text:
The drawing shows three parts: a 2-nitroimidazole ring, a CH2–O linker, and a phosphorodiamidate bearing two bromoethylamino groups.

**Imidazole ring.** The five ring atoms are N (top left, no substituent), CH, C (bearing CH2), N (bearing methyl) and C (bearing the nitro group). The double bonds are C(nitro)=N and CH=C(CH2).

**Nitro group.** The nitro group is on the carbon between the two ring nitrogens. It is drawn as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Side chain.** The ring carbon next to the N-methyl nitrogen carries CH2–O–P(=O)(NHCH2CH2Br)(NHCH2CH2Br).

Writing the SMILES from the nitro carbon around the ring:
Cn1c(COP(=O)(NCCBr)NCCBr)cnc1[N+](=O)[O-]

Check of ring closure: n1 (N-methyl), c(CH2…) is the substituted carbon, c is the CH, n is the unsubstituted ring N, and c1 is the nitro-bearing carbon, which closes back to the N-methyl nitrogen. The aromatic form is valid.

SMILES: Cn1c(COP(=O)(NCCBr)NCCBr)cnc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Evodiamine
text:
I read this as an evodiamine-type skeleton and wrote the SMILES from that reading.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring that contains the C=O and an N-methyl nitrogen.
- **Centre:** the stereocentre carries H (drawn as a wedge) and is bonded to the N-methyl nitrogen, the amide nitrogen and the indole C2.
- **Right side:** the amide nitrogen is linked through a CH2CH2 bridge to the indole C3, and the indole is a benzene ring fused to a pyrrole bearing NH.

For the stereocentre, I viewed it from the H side, since H is the wedged bond. From there the N(Me) → indole C → amide N sequence runs clockwise. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order (N(Me), H, amide N, indole C) gives `@@`.

SMILES: CN1[C@@H]2c3[nH]c4ccccc4c3CCN2C(=O)c2ccccc21

name: Ezetimibe
text:
This drawing is ezetimibe: an azetidin-2-one (β-lactam) core carrying three substituents.

- **N1:** a 4-fluorophenyl group.
- **C3:** a –CH2CH2–CH(OH)– chain ending in a second 4-fluorophenyl ring, drawn on a hashed bond.
- **C4:** a 4-hydroxyphenyl group, drawn on a wedge.
- **Carbinol carbon:** the OH is on a wedge.

Assigning CIP priorities from the wedges and hashes gives 3R and 4S for the ring carbons and S for the carbinol carbon. This matches ezetimibe, (3R,4S)-1-(4-fluorophenyl)-3-[(3S)-3-(4-fluorophenyl)-3-hydroxypropyl]-4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)azetidin-2-one. I did not check the SMILES string below against these assignments independently. I took it from memory of the known ezetimibe SMILES.

SMILES: O[C@@H](CC[C@@H]1[C@H](N(C1=O)c1ccc(F)cc1)c1ccc(O)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Examorelin
text:
I read the structure as a hexapeptide amide, His–(2‑Me‑D‑Trp)–Ala–Trp–D‑Phe–Lys–NH2, and wrote the SMILES residue by residue from the N‑terminus.

Residues, with stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes at each α‑carbon:
1. **His** (L, S): free NH2 on a hashed bond, side chain CH2 attached to an imidazole.
2. **2‑Methyl‑Trp** (D, R): the indole carries a methyl at C2, and the CH2 is on a hashed bond.
3. **Ala** (L, S): the CH3 is on a hashed bond.
4. **Trp** (L, S): the unsubstituted indole's CH2 is on a hashed bond.
5. **Phe** (D, R): the benzyl CH2 is on a wedge bond.
6. **Lys** (L, S): a four‑carbon chain ending in NH2, with the C‑terminus as a primary amide (C(=O)NH2).

Each residue is written as N[C@@H](R)C(=O) for L and N[C@H](R)C(=O) for D, with the next amide N attached to the preceding C(=O).

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1cnc[nH]1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1c(C)[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N

name: Exemestane
text:
The drawing matches exemestane (6-methylideneandrosta-1,4-diene-3,17-dione), a steroid skeleton with these features:

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, C1=C2 and C4=C5 with the C3 ketone (the O at right).
- **Ring B:** an exocyclic =CH2 at C6.
- **Ring D:** a five-membered ring with a C17 ketone (the O at left).
- **Stereochemistry:** the two methyl groups at C10 and C13 are hashed. The H at C9 and the H at C14 are wedged, and the H at C8 is hashed. This is the natural steroid configuration.

I checked the C13 centre explicitly against the drawing. Seen from the front, the neighbours C14, C17 and C12 run clockwise with the methyl pointing away, which corresponds to `@` in the SMILES below. The other centres I took from the known natural configuration rather than deriving each one.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CCC2=O)CC(=C)C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]34C

name: Ezogabine
text:
This is the structure of ethyl carbamate attached to a substituted benzene (retigabine).

- **Right side:** an ethyl group (CH3-CH2) is bonded to O, which is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to NH. The NH is attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Central ring:** the carbon bearing the carbamate NH is adjacent to the carbon bearing NH2. The ring carbon bearing the NH-benzyl group is para to the carbamate carbon, since it sits at the far left of the ring. The ring vertices run C1 (NHCO) at the upper right of the left-hand side, C2 (NH2) at the lower right, C3 (CH) at the bottom, C4 (NH-benzyl) at the left, C5 (CH) at the top left, and C6 (CH) at the top right. The NH-benzyl group on C4 is therefore para to C1 (carbamate) and meta to C2 (NH2).
- **Left ring:** a 4-fluorobenzyl group is attached through CH2 to the NH.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)Nc1ccc(NCc2ccc(F)cc2)cc1N

SMILES: CCOC(=O)Nc1ccc(NCc2ccc(F)cc2)cc1N

name: Ezlopitant
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-benzhydrylquinuclidin-3-amine whose NH carries a substituted benzyl group.

- **Aryl group on nitrogen:** a benzene ring bears OMe, then (on the adjacent carbon) the CH2 linked to the NH, and an isopropyl group para to the OMe. This gives `COc1ccc(C(C)C)cc1CN…`.
- **Quinuclidine core:** N1 is bonded to C2, which carries the CHPh2 group. C2 is bonded to C3, which bears the NH. C3 is bonded to the bridgehead C4, and two CH2–CH2 bridges run from C4 back to N1, giving the bicyclic ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** only C2 and C3 have hashed H wedges, so only these two get stereo labels. Working from the wedge geometry (H pointing back at each centre), I assigned C3 as `[C@@H]` and C2 as `[C@H]` in the SMILES atom ordering below.
- **Check:** the ring closures are consistent (ring 1 joins C3 and C4, ring 2 joins N1 and the second CH2 bridge), and the atom count matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc(C(C)C)cc1CN[C@@H]1[C@H](C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)N2CCC1CC2

name: Famciclovir
text:
This is famciclovir: a 2-aminopurine attached through N9 to a CH2CH2 chain, which ends in a CH bearing two CH2OAc groups.

Reading the drawing:
- The top acetyl is CH3-C(=O)-O-CH2, attached to the central CH.
- The bottom acetyl is CH3-C(=O)-O-CH2, also attached to the central CH.
- From the central CH, the chain runs CH2-CH2-N, with the N being N9 of the purine.
- The purine has a five-membered ring made of N9, CH, N, and two fusion carbons. The six-membered ring is C4 (fusion carbon, bonded to N9), N3, C2 (bearing NH2), N1, C6 (CH), and C5 (fusion carbon).

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so I added no stereochemistry.

SMILES check: CC(=O)OCC(CCn1cnc2cnc(N)nc12)COC(C)=O

- In n1cnc2cnc(N)nc12, n1 is N9, then c is C8, n is N7, and c2 is C5.
- After C5 come c (C6), n (N1), c(N) (C2 with NH2), n (N3), and c12 (C4, which closes both rings).

This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)OCC(CCn1cnc2cnc(N)nc12)COC(C)=O

name: Falecalcitriol
Famotidine
text:
This is the famotidine skeleton, read as follows.

Left side: a guanidine carbon bearing two NH2 groups is double-bonded to an N (N=C(N)N). That N is attached to C2 of a thiazole ring.

Thiazole ring: C2 is bonded to the ring S and double-bonded to the ring N. The ring N connects to C4, and C4 is double-bonded to C5, which bonds back to the ring S. C4 carries the CH2 substituent.

Chain: from C4, CH2 – S – CH2 – CH2 – C(NH2)=N – S(=O)(=O) – NH2.

The guanidine is drawn as N=C(N)N, with the double bond from the guanidine carbon to the N attached to the ring.

Thiazole SMILES: C2 is written as c1nc(cs1), which gives N=C(N)Nc1nc(CSCCC(N)=NS(N)(=O)=O)cs1. In the drawing the bonds are Kekulé-style, but the aromatic form is equivalent.

SMILES: NC(N)=Nc1nc(CSCCC(N)=NS(N)(=O)=O)cs1

name: Famitinib
text:
I read the molecule as a diethylaminoethyl lactam fused to a methylpyrrole, joined through a methylidene to a 5-fluoro-oxindole.

- **Left side:** an N,N-diethylaminoethyl chain (CCN(CC)CC) is attached to the lactam nitrogen of a 6,7-dihydro-pyrrolo[3,2-c]pyridin-4-one. This bicyclic core has a C=O at position 4, and the pyrrole NH is drawn.
- **Pyrrole:** the carbon next to the pyrrole NH carries the methylidene linker. The adjacent pyrrole carbon carries a methyl group.
- **Right side:** the linker CH is double-bonded to C3 of an oxindole (indolin-2-one) with a lactam NH. The fluorine sits on the benzo ring at position 5, para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the NH.
- **Double-bond geometry:** from the drawn coordinates, the pyrrole substituent and the oxindole C=O lie on the same side of the C=C, so the bond is Z. I encoded this with `/` and `\` marks.

The core is the sunitinib scaffold, but with the lactam-fused ring in place of sunitinib's carboxamide.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCN1CCc2[nH]c(/C=C3\C(=O)Nc4ccc(F)cc43)c(C)c2C1=O

name: Fadh2
text:
This looks like reduced FAD (FADH2): a 1,5-dihydroisoalloxazine (flavin) ring joined to a ribityl chain, a pyrophosphate bridge, and adenosine.

- **Flavin ring:** the benzo ring carries two methyl groups. The central ring has NH at N5 and an N10 substituent, with both C=O groups on the pyrimidine ring (N1H, N3H), so the flavin is in its dihydro form.
- **Ribityl chain:** three stereocentres, each bearing OH. I worked out each centre from the wedges and hashes. The first and third OH groups are on wedges and the middle one is on a hash, which gives `[C@H]` at all three when written from N10 toward the phosphate.
- **Pyrophosphate:** two P(=O)(OH) groups linked by a bridging O, with one end on the ribityl C5 oxygen and the other on the adenosine 5′-oxygen.
- **Adenosine:** the ribose and adenine drawing matches natural D-ribose with an N9-linked adenine bearing NH2. For the sugar's stereo tags I relied on the standard natural-adenosine configuration rather than re-deriving them from the image.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1cc2c(cc1C)N(C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)COP(=O)(O)OP(=O)(O)OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](n3cnc4c(N)ncnc43)[C@H](O)[C@@H]1O)C1=C(N2)C(=O)NC(=O)N1

name: Farxiga
text:
This looks like dapagliflozin co-crystallised with propane-1,2-diol and water (dapagliflozin propanediol monohydrate). I read the three components as follows:

- **Aglycone:** a 4-ethoxyphenyl group joined through a CH2 to a chlorinated benzene ring. The chlorine sits ortho to the CH2 and para to the sugar attachment.
- **Sugar ring:** a C-aryl glucopyranose (tetrahydropyran with a CH2OH and three OH groups), with stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes.
- **Co-formers:** propane-1,2-diol drawn with no stereo marks, so no stereo is given for it, and one water.

I did not independently re-derive each @/@@ label from the wedges. I used the known dapagliflozin configuration, which should match this standard depiction.

SMILES: CCOC1=CC=C(C=C1)CC2=C(C=CC(=C2)[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O)Cl.CC(O)CO.O

name: Fascaplysin
text:
Reading the drawing region by region gives the following structure.

- **Right side:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. One ring carbon carries a C=O, and the adjacent ring carbon is bonded to the N⁺.
- **Centre:** the carbonyl carbon is bonded to a carbon that is double-bonded to the N⁺. The N⁺ is also bonded to a CH=CH unit.
- **Pyridinium-type ring:** the CH=CH leads to a carbon that is double-bonded to the carbon next to the NH, closing a six-membered ring through the N⁺.
- **Left side:** that same carbon is bonded to a benzene ring, and the NH links the other carbon of the double bond to that benzene ring. This forms an indole-type five-membered ring.

I wrote this as a SMILES and checked it against the drawing. The ring closures, the N⁺=C and C=C double bonds, and the single implicit hydrogen on the NH all match. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2[N+]2=C1C1=C(C=C2)c2ccccc2N1

name: Favipiravir
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with these atoms, read in order around the ring:

- C(F), bonded to the fluorine on the left.
- N, drawn with a double bond to the next carbon.
- C, bearing the carboxamide substituent C(=O)NH2.
- C(=O), the ring carbonyl at the lower right.
- NH, at the bottom.
- CH, which closes the ring back to C(F), with a double bond between the CH and C(F).

Bond check:
- C(F)=CH is a double bond (the inner line is drawn on the left side).
- N=C is a double bond.
- C(=O) is a double bond to the ring oxygen.
- The C(F)–N bond is single.
- The CH–NH bond is single.

Writing the SMILES from the carboxamide: NC(=O)C1=NC(F)=CNC1=O

Ring closure check: C1 (the carbon with the amide) =N, then C(F), then =C (the CH), then N (the NH), then C1(=O), which closes the ring. This gives six ring atoms: C1, N, C(F), CH, NH, C(=O). Each atom has a consistent valence.

SMILES: NC(=O)C1=NC(F)=CNC1=O

name: Exatecan
text:
I read this as exatecan, a camptothecin-type structure.

- **Lactone end:** the quaternary carbon carries an ethyl group and an OH drawn as a bold wedge. It is bonded to the lactone C=O and to the pyridone ring, which gives the OCC ring closure. From the 2D geometry I assigned this centre `@@` (in the neighbour order ethyl, ring carbon, OH, C=O).
- **Central rings:** the pyridone N–C(=O) unit is joined through a CH2 to a pyrroloquinoline-type system. It contains one ring N=C, and the double bonds are written in Kekulé form as drawn.
- **Benzo ring:** it carries F and CH3 on adjacent carbons.
- **Cyclohexane ring:** the CH2–CH2 portion is fused to the benzo ring. The carbon bearing NH2 has a hashed bond to N. With the neighbour order (ring carbon, H, N, CH2) I assigned this centre `@@`.

I checked the SMILES for ring-closure numbering and matched it against the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCC2=C1C=C1N(C2=O)CC2=C3[C@@H](N)CCC4=C(C)C(F)=CC(N=C21)=C34

name: Fedratinib
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Pyrimidine core:** The ring atoms are N1, C2, N3, C4, C5, C6. C2 carries the NH-aryl group, C4 carries the NH-aryl group of the sulfonamide ring, and C5 carries the methyl. C6 is the CH next to N1.
- **Upper aryl group:** A para-substituted benzene is attached through NH to C2. At the para position it carries O-CH2CH2-N(pyrrolidine).
- **Lower aryl group:** A meta-substituted benzene is attached through NH to C4 and carries S(=O)(=O)NH-C(CH3)3 (tert-butyl sulfonamide).
  - Ring atoms of the lower benzene: the carbon bearing NH (611,970), then (740,1056), then the carbon bearing S (877,990). Between them is a single carbon, so the substituents are meta.

SMILES: Cc1cnc(Nc2ccc(OCCN3CCCC3)cc2)nc1Nc1cccc(S(=O)(=O)NC(C)(C)C)c1

name: Febuxostat
text:
This structure is febuxostat: a thiazole ring carrying a methyl group and a carboxylic acid, joined at C2 to a benzene ring that bears a cyano group and an isobutoxy group.

**Thiazole ring.** The ring atoms are S, C2 (attached to the benzene), N, C4 (methyl) and C5 (COOH). C4=C5 and C2=N are the double bonds. Written as a SMILES fragment: Cc1nc(-c2...)sc1C(=O)O.

**Benzene ring.** The carbon attached to the thiazole (call it C1) sits next to a CH, then a C bearing the O-isobutyl group at the far end of the ring from C1 (para), and a C bearing the nitrile ortho to the O-isobutyl carbon. This gives c2ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c2.

**Check on positions.** Going around the ring from the thiazole-bearing carbon at (700, 640): a CH at (782, 527), a CH at (922, 542), the C–O carbon at (978, 671), the C–CN carbon at (896, 785), and a CH at (757, 769) back to the start. So the O-isobutyl carbon is para to the thiazole carbon, and the nitrile carbon is meta to it and adjacent to the O-isobutyl carbon, which matches the SMILES above.

SMILES: Cc1nc(-c2ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c2)sc1C(=O)O

name: Felodipine
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine with these features:

- **Ring:** N1(H), C2(CH3)=C3(CO2Et), C4(H)(aryl), C5(CO2Me)=C6(CH3).
- **Left side:** the ester on C3 is drawn as C(=O)OCC, an ethyl ester.
- **Right side:** the ester on C5 is drawn as C(=O)OC, a methyl ester.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring attached at C4 carries Cl on the adjacent ring carbon and a second Cl on the next carbon, so it is 2,3-dichlorophenyl.
- **Ring bonds:** the benzene ring atoms run C1 (attached), C2 (Cl), C3 (Cl), C4, C5, C6. In the image the attached carbon (880,875) is bonded to the C-Cl at (1050,920), then to the C-Cl at (1097,1090), then to (972,1215), (802,1170) and (757,1000).
- **Stereochemistry:** C4 has no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1cccc(Cl)c1Cl

name: Felcisetrag
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- **Methyl carbamate:** a methyl group on an oxygen, attached to a C=O, which is bonded to the nitrogen of piperidine 1 (COC(=O)N).
- **Piperidine 1:** C4 of this ring carries a CH2 linker to the nitrogen of piperidine 2.
- **Piperidine 2:** its C4 carries a CH2–NH–C(=O) group.
- **Benzimidazole:** the amide carbonyl is attached at the 4-position of a benzimidazole. The C2 carbon carries an isopropyl group. The N next to C2 on the top is drawn as =N, and the lower one is NH.

The benzimidazole is written as c1(C(=O)N...)cccc2[nH]c(C(C)C)nc12. In the drawing, the carbon bearing the carbonyl (C4) is bonded to C3a, which is bonded to the =N. The ring-fusion carbon bonded to NH is C7a, and the remaining three CH atoms close the benzene ring.

Full SMILES: COC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)CN1CCC(CNC(=O)c2cccc3[nH]c(C(C)C)nc23)CC1

Check on the benzimidazole fragment: c2cccc3[nH]c(C(C)C)nc23 gives c2 (C4, bearing the carbonyl), then ccc (three CH), then c3 (C7a) bonded to [nH], then c(iPr), then n, then c23 (C3a), which closes to both C4 and C7a. C3a is bonded to the =N, as drawn.

SMILES: COC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)CN1CCC(CNC(=O)c2cccc3[nH]c(C(C)C)nc23)CC1

name: Fenbufen
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl unit, with one phenyl ring attached to a second, para-substituted ring. The para substituent is a ketone, C(=O), followed by two CH2 groups and a terminal carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH.

This is 4-(biphenyl-4-yl)-4-oxobutanoic acid (fenbufen).

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1

name: Felbinac
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl unit: a terminal phenyl ring joined to a para-substituted phenyl ring. The substituent on the second ring is a CH2 group attached to a carboxylic acid, drawn as C(=O)OH. This is 4-biphenylacetic acid (felbinac).

SMILES: OC(=O)Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1

name: Fendiline
text:
The drawing shows a secondary amine, N-(1-phenylethyl)-3,3-diphenylpropylamine (fendiline-like, without the stereo label).

- The nitrogen is drawn as NH.
- On one side, N is bonded to a CH2, then another CH2, then a CH that carries two phenyl rings (the diphenylmethyl carbon).
- On the other side, N is bonded to a CH that carries a methyl group and a phenyl ring.
- All bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(NCCC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Fenfluramine
text:
The drawing shows fenfluramine, which is N-ethyl-1-[3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]propan-2-amine.

- **Ethyl group:** a CH3 and a CH2 attached to NH.
- **Amine side:** the NH connects to a CH carrying a methyl group, then a CH2 that attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the CH2 on one carbon and a CF3 group on the carbon two positions away from it, i.e. meta. The ring atoms in order are C(CH2 attached), CH, C(CF3), CH, CH, CH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo marks are included.

SMILES: CCNC(C)Cc1cccc(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Fenbendazole
text:
The drawing is a benzimidazole carbamate with a phenylthio substituent, which matches the structure of fenbendazole.

- **Carbamate:** a methyl ester (CH3–O–C(=O)) attached to an NH.
- **Imidazole ring:** that NH is bonded to C2 of the ring. C2 is double-bonded to N, which is bonded to the fused benzene carbon (C3a). The other ring nitrogen is NH, bonded to the second fused carbon (C7a).
- **Fused benzene ring:** the carbon attached to S is two bonds away from the fusion carbon on the NH side.
- **Thioether:** S links the benzimidazole to a phenyl ring.

Tracing the fused benzene from the drawing:
- Top-left carbon at (708, 645) is bonded to N= (the fusion carbon C3a).
- Bottom-left carbon at (785, 763) is bonded to NH (C7a).
- From C7a the ring continues to (925, 757), then to (989, 630), which bears S.
- It then continues to (913, 512), then to (773, 519), and back to C3a.

So from C7a (attached to NH), the next carbon is CH, and the one after that bears S. This is the 5(6)-substituted tautomer.

SMILES: COC(=O)NC1=NC2=CC=C(SC3=CC=CC=C3)C=C2N1

Checking the connectivity: C2 is the fusion carbon bonded to N=, then =CC=C(S…) gives CH, CH, then C(S). The ring is C3a, then CH (773,519), CH (913,512), C(S) (989,630), CH (925,757), and C7a. In the SMILES, C2 is C3a, "=CC=C(S...)" gives C(773), C(913)... and C(S) follows. Then "C=C2N1" gives CH (925) and C7a, which is bonded to N1(H). This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: COC(=O)NC1=NC2=CC=C(SC3=CC=CC=C3)C=C2N1

name: Felypressin
text:
I read this as felypressin, the cyclic nonapeptide Cys-Phe-Phe-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Lys-Gly-NH2. A disulfide bridge joins Cys1 and Cys6, and the C-terminus is a primary amide. The drawn chain, ring and side-chain atoms match this sequence. I took the wedges and hashes to be the natural L-configuration at every amino-acid centre and wrote each @/@@ by hand from that assumption.

SMILES: N[C@H]1CSSC[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC1=O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Fenofibrate
text:
The drawing shows fenofibrate, the isopropyl ester of 2-[4-(4-chlorobenzoyl)phenoxy]-2-methylpropanoic acid.

Reading it region by region:
- **Left end:** an isopropyl group (a CH carbon with two methyls) is bonded to an ester oxygen.
- **Ester:** that oxygen is bonded to a carbonyl carbon with a C=O.
- **Quaternary carbon:** the carbonyl carbon is attached to a carbon bearing two methyls and an ether oxygen.
- **First ring:** the ether oxygen connects to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Ketone link:** the other para position of that ring carries a C(=O) group, which joins a second benzene ring.
- **Second ring:** this ring has a chlorine in the para position.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)C(C)(C)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Fenoldopam
text:
This structure is a 3-benzazepine, matching fenoldopam. It has a benzene ring fused to a seven-membered ring that contains one NH, and a 4-hydroxyphenyl group on the carbon next to the fused ring.

**Fused benzene ring.** Reading around the ring from the top:
- C(OH) at the top, bearing OH.
- C(OH) at the upper left, bearing HO.
- C(Cl) at the left.
- The fusion carbon at the lower left, which connects to CH2.
- The fusion carbon at the lower right, which connects to the CH bearing the aryl group.
- An aromatic CH at the right, between the lower-right fusion carbon and the top C(OH).

**Seven-membered ring.** Going around from the lower-left fusion carbon: CH2, CH2, NH, CH2, CH(aryl), then the other fusion carbon. That gives 2 fusion carbons, 2 CH2, N, CH2 and CH, which is 7 atoms.

**Substituent.** The CH carries a phenyl ring with OH at the para position.

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so I have not added stereochemistry.

SMILES: Oc1ccc(cc1)C1CNCCc2c(Cl)c(O)c(O)cc12

name: Fenoterol
text:
This is fenoterol, drawn without stereochemistry.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying two OH groups at the 3 and 5 positions. The ring carbon attached to the side chain sits between them.

**Chain:** from the left ring, a CH(OH) carbon, then a CH2, then NH, then a CH(CH3) carbon, then a CH2 that connects to the right ring.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring with an OH para to the CH2 attachment.

All bonds in the drawing are plain, so I have added no stereochemistry.

SMILES: Oc1cc(O)cc(c1)C(O)CNC(C)Cc1ccc(O)cc1

name: Fenoprofen
text:
The drawing shows fenoprofen, 2-(3-phenoxyphenyl)propanoic acid.

- **Left ring:** a phenyl group bonded to an oxygen atom (an aryl ether).
- **Middle ring:** a benzene ring with the ether oxygen on one carbon and the side chain on another. The ring atoms run from the O-bearing carbon at (652,778) to (637,617) to (767,521) to (915,588) to the side-chain carbon at (932,750) to (800,845). The O-bearing carbon and the side-chain carbon are separated by one ring carbon, so they are meta to each other.
- **Side chain:** a CH(CH3)COOH group. The CH carbon at (1080,817) carries a methyl group and the carboxylic acid carbon, which has a C=O and an OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1cccc(Oc2ccccc2)c1

name: Fentanyl
text:
The drawing shows the following pieces:
- An ethyl group (CH3–CH2) attached to a carbonyl carbon, which carries a C=O oxygen.
- The carbonyl carbon is bonded to an amide nitrogen.
- That nitrogen is also bonded to a phenyl ring and to C4 of a piperidine ring.
- The piperidine nitrogen carries a CH2CH2 chain ending in a second phenyl ring (a phenethyl group).

I recognise this connectivity as fentanyl. The drawing has no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCC(=O)N(c1ccccc1)C1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1

name: Feprazone
text:
The drawing shows a pyrazolidine-3,5-dione ring with two N-phenyl groups and a prenyl side chain, which is the structure of feprazone.

**Ring:** The five-membered ring contains C(=O), then N (bearing a phenyl), then a second N (bearing a phenyl), then C(=O), and finally the CH carbon that closes the ring back to the first C(=O).

**Side chain:** The ring CH carries a CH2, which is attached to CH=C(CH3)2. This is a 3-methylbut-2-enyl (prenyl) group.

**Phenyl groups:** Each N carries an unsubstituted phenyl ring, drawn as a six-membered aromatic ring.

The SMILES below follows the ring from the CH carbon through each carbonyl and nitrogen, and the drawing shows no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)=CCC1C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N(c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Ferric acetylacetonate
text:
The image shows an Fe(3+) ion drawn with a radical dot, together with three acetylacetonate ligands, each drawn as an enolate. Each ligand has a C=O, a CH=C(O⁻) unit and two terminal methyl groups.

Each ligand reads CC(=O)/C=C(/C)[O-]. The drawing shows no stereochemistry that matters here, so I leave the double-bond geometry unspecified and write each ligand as CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].

The iron is drawn as [Fe+3]. The drawing labels it "Fe3+·", which suggests the SMILES [Fe+3]. with a dot separating it from the first ligand. I write it as [Fe+3] followed by the ligands, with dots between all components.

SMILES: [Fe+3].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-]

name: Fenebrutinib
text:
I read the structure in four parts and assembled them into one SMILES.

- **Left tricycle:** a 2,2-dimethylcyclopentane fused to a pyrrole, which is fused to a pyrazinone. The pyrazinone nitrogen carries the C=O and is bonded to the pyridine.
- **Central pyridine:** a 2-pyridyl group bearing a CH2OH at C3 and, at C4, a link to the next ring.
- **Pyridinone:** an N-methyl pyridin-2-one with an NH at C3 joining it to the right-hand pyridine.
- **Right side:** a 2-aminopyridine whose C5 carries a piperazine. The piperazine has a methyl on the carbon next to the pyridine-bound nitrogen, and its other nitrogen carries an oxetan-3-yl group.

The only stereocentre is the piperazine carbon with the wedged methyl. Its substituents rank N (ring nitrogen) > CH2 > CH3 > H. With the methyl wedged toward the viewer and H pointing away, the sequence N → CH2 → CH3 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES as written (`C[C@@H]1C`), `@@` encodes S.

SMILES: CC1(C)Cc2cc3C(=O)N(CCn3c2C1)c1nccc(c1CO)-c1cn(C)c(=O)c(c1)Nc1ccc(cn1)N1CCN(C[C@@H]1C)C1COC1

name: Ferric citrate
text:
The drawing shows a citrate trianion together with an iron(III) cation.

- **Citrate:** A central carbon carries an OH and a carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]). Two CH2 groups lead from it to two more carboxylates, each drawn as C(=O)[O-].
- **Iron:** The label reads Fe with a 3+ charge and a radical dot, which comes from the disconnected fragment notation. As a SMILES atom this is [Fe+3], written here as [Fe+3] after a "." separator. Because the dot appears on the label itself, the drawing may correspond to a radical form, but I am writing it as a plain Fe3+ ion.

The central carbon has four substituents: OH, two CH2 groups and a COO-. It is a stereocentre only by connectivity, and since it is drawn with plain bonds it gets no stereo marking. The two CH2CO2- arms are identical, so it is not actually a stereocentre anyway.

SMILES: [Fe+3].[O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-]

name: Ferrocene
text:
The image shows ferrocene drawn as two separate cyclopentadienyl radicals plus an Fe atom, with no bonds to the metal.

Each ring has five carbons. Two double bonds are drawn, and the fifth carbon carries a radical dot. That carbon is the top-left vertex of each ring, at the position of the dot.

Tracing one ring from the radical carbon: [CH] is bonded to C(top), which is double-bonded to C(right), which is bonded to C(bottom right). That carbon is double-bonded to C(bottom left), which closes back to the radical carbon.

This gives the ring SMILES [CH]1C=CC=C1. Each ring is a separate fragment, and Fe is a separate atom.

SMILES: [CH]1C=CC=C1.[CH]1C=CC=C1.[Fe]

name: Ferric Maltol
text:
The image shows an Fe³⁺ ion with three identical maltolate anions, drawn as separate fragments with no bonds to the metal.

Reading one ligand: the ring is a 4-pyranone. Starting at the ring CH next to O, the atoms are C=C (two CH), then C(=O), then C([O-]) double-bonded to C(CH3), which is bonded to the ring O.

Ring atoms, in order:
- C1: CH attached to O
- C2: CH
- C3: C(=O)
- C4: C(O⁻)
- C5: C(CH3)
- O6: ring oxygen

Each ligand is written as CC1=C([O-])C(=O)C=CO1. The drawing has the C=C between the two CH carbons. This gives the ring O1–C(CH3)=C(O⁻)–C(=O)–CH=CH–O1.

The Fe is drawn as [Fe+3] with a trailing dot, which separates it from the ligands.

SMILES: [Fe+3].CC1=C([O-])C(=O)C=CO1.CC1=C([O-])C(=O)C=CO1.CC1=C([O-])C(=O)C=CO1

name: Ferric Pyrophosphate
text:
The image shows four Fe3+ ions and three pyrophosphate anions, each drawn as a separate fragment.

Each pyrophosphate unit is O=P([O-])([O-])OP(=O)([O-])[O-]. Its charge is 4−, so three units carry 12−, which balances the four Fe3+ ions at 12+. This is iron(III) pyrophosphate, Fe4(P2O7)3.

The Fe atoms are drawn as [Fe+3] with a trailing dot, so they are disconnected fragments. In SMILES this is written as [Fe+3].[Fe+3].[Fe+3].[Fe+3] followed by the three pyrophosphate fragments, each separated by a dot.

SMILES: [Fe+3].[Fe+3].[Fe+3].[Fe+3].O=P([O-])([O-])OP(=O)([O-])[O-].O=P([O-])([O-])OP(=O)([O-])[O-].O=P([O-])([O-])OP(=O)([O-])[O-]

name: Ferrocenecarboxaldehyde
text:
The drawing shows three separate species: Fe2+, a cyclopentadienyl anion, and a formyl-substituted cyclopentadienyl anion (the aldehyde on a cyclopentadienide ring).

**Left ring:** a five-membered ring with the vertices C−, C=C, C–C, and C=C. Written as a SMILES, this is [CH-]1C=CC=C1.

**Right ring:** a five-membered ring with a CHO substituent. The vertices run C(CHO), =C, C, =C, and C−.
- The substituted carbon (at about 1027,875) is double-bonded to the carbon at (1120,648).
- That carbon is single-bonded to the carbon at (1365,664).
- The carbon at (1365,664) is double-bonded to the carbon at (1424,904).
- The carbon at (1424,904) is single-bonded to C− at the bottom, which is single-bonded back to the substituted carbon.

As a SMILES, this is O=CC1=CC=C[CH-]1. The ring carbon bearing the aldehyde has no hydrogen, and the C− carbon keeps one hydrogen.

**Combined:** [Fe+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.O=CC1=CC=C[CH-]1

SMILES: [Fe+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.O=CC1=CC=C[CH-]1

name: Ferrous Fumarate
text:
The drawing shows an Fe²⁺ ion beside a fumarate dianion, so the SMILES has two components.

**Fumarate geometry.** The central C=C runs from about (618, 752) to (840, 946). The left carboxylate carbon at (338, 850) attaches to the upper alkene carbon, and the right carboxylate carbon at (1122, 850) attaches to the lower alkene carbon.

To judge cis or trans, take the direction of the double bond as (222, 194). The substituent on the first alkene carbon points to the lower left, along (−280, 98). The substituent on the second points to the upper right, along (282, −96). These point in opposite directions, so the arrangement is trans (E), which is fumarate.

**SMILES.** The trans geometry is written as `[O-]C(=O)/C=C/C(=O)[O-]`, with the iron as a separate component, `[Fe+2]`.

SMILES: [Fe+2].[O-]C(=O)/C=C/C(=O)[O-]

name: Ferroquine
text:
The image shows three separate species: an Fe2+ ion, an unsubstituted cyclopentadienyl anion, and a substituted cyclopentadienyl anion carrying the side chains. In SMILES they are joined with dots.

**Unsubstituted cyclopentadienyl anion.** This is a five-membered ring with one C⁻ and two double bonds: `[cH-]1cccc1`. Written with explicit Kekulé bonds, it is C1=CC=C[CH-]1.

**Substituted cyclopentadienyl anion.** The ring has five carbons:
- One carbon is C⁻ and bears the CH2NH substituent.
- The adjacent ring carbon bears CH2N(CH3)2.
- The remaining three ring carbons are CH.
- The drawn double bonds are C(CH2N)=CH–CH=CH, with the C⁻ closing the ring.

As SMILES: `[C-]1(CNc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)C(CN(C)C)=CC=C1`. The C⁻ carbon has no hydrogen because it carries a substituent. Its atoms are the C⁻, the C bearing CH2NMe2, and three CH carbons, which makes five in total.

**Quinoline part.** The NH is attached at quinoline position 4. The ring nitrogen is N1, with C2 and C3 between N1 and C4. Cl sits at C7, which is on the benzo ring, meta to the ring fusion carbon next to N (C8a). Reading the drawing, C8a is bonded to C8, which is bonded to C7 (bearing Cl). So the SMILES is c1(NC...)ccnc2cc(Cl)ccc12, where the c2 after n is C8a, then c is C8, then c(Cl) is C7, then cc gives C6 and C5, and c12 is C4a. This matches.

**Full SMILES.** `[Fe+2].c1cc[cH-]c1` would need Kekulé-style aromatic handling, so I use explicit double bonds instead:

[Fe+2].C1=CC=C[CH-]1.[C-]1(CNc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)C(CN(C)C)=CC=C1

SMILES: [Fe+2].C1=CC=C[CH-]1.[C-]1(CNc2ccnc3cc(Cl)ccc23)C(CN(C)C)=CC=C1

name: Fevipiprant
text:
The drawing shows a 7-azaindole (pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine) core with three substituents.

**Core ring system**
- The five-membered ring contains N1, C2 (bearing a methyl), C3 (bearing CH2COOH), C3a and C7a.
- C7a is bonded to N1 and to the pyridine nitrogen N7.
- The pyridine ring runs C3a, C4, C5, C6, N7, C7a.

**Substituents**
- N1 carries a CH2 group attached to a benzene ring.
- On that benzene ring, the carbon attached to the CH2 has a CF3 group on one adjacent carbon.
- The methylsulfonyl group (S(=O)(=O)CH3) sits on the carbon para to the CH2-bearing carbon, which is meta to the CF3-bearing carbon.

**Benzene ring positions**
- Going around the ring from C1, the CH2 carbon, the vertices are: C1 (right-bottom, CH2), C2 (bottom, CF3), C3 (left-bottom), C4 (left-top, SO2Me), C5 (top), C6 (right-top).
- SO2Me is on C4, para to C1, as stated above.

**SMILES assembly**
Starting from the methyl sulfone: CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Cn2c(C)c(CC(=O)O)c3cccnc32)c(C(F)(F)F)c1

Check of the benzene ring: c1 (SO2Me carbon), c, c, c(CH2...) , c(CF3), c1. The CH2 carbon is para to the sulfone carbon (positions 1 and 4), and CF3 is ortho to the CH2 carbon and meta to the sulfone carbon. This matches the drawing.

Check of the azaindole: n2 (N1), c(C) (C2), c(CC(=O)O) (C3), c3 (C3a), ccc (C4, C5, C6), n (N7), c32 (C7a, closing to C3a and N1). This is consistent.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Cn2c(C)c(CC(=O)O)c3cccnc32)c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Fexinidazole
text:
The drawing shows a 1-methyl-5-nitroimidazole ring joined through a CH2–O link to a para-substituted benzene bearing an SMe group.

**Imidazole ring.** The ring atoms are N1 (carrying the methyl group), C2 (carrying the CH2), N3, C4 (CH) and C5 (carrying the nitro group). The drawn double bonds are C2=N3 and C4=C5.

**Substituents.**
- The nitro group is drawn as [N+](=O)[O-] on C5.
- The CH2 on C2 connects to O, which connects to the benzene ring.
- The benzene ring carries a methylthio group (SC) para to the oxygen.

**SMILES.** Writing from the methyl on N1 around the ring gives Cn1c([N+](=O)[O-])cnc1COc1ccc(SC)cc1.

Atom check: the ring is n1, then C5 with the nitro, then c (C4–H), then n (N3), then c1 (C2) with CH2, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1c([N+](=O)[O-])cnc1COc1ccc(SC)cc1

name: Fexofenadine
text:
This structure is fexofenadine. I read it region by region:

- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) attached to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups, which is attached to a benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** para-substituted. One substituent is the dimethyl acid carbon; the other is a CH(OH) carbon.
- **Chain:** CH(OH)–CH2–CH2–CH2–N, four carbons from the ring to the nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the nitrogen is part of a piperidine ring, and the carbon opposite it (C4) carries C(OH)(Ph)2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

SMILES: CC(C)(C(=O)O)c1ccc(cc1)C(O)CCCN1CCC(CC1)C(O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Fertirelin
text:
Reading the drawing, I get a linear decapeptide, pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑Gly‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt, which matches fertirelin. It has the following parts:

- **N‑terminus:** a pyroglutamic acid ring (5‑membered lactam) is acylated by His.
- **Side chains in order:**
  - His carries an imidazole.
  - Trp carries an indole.
  - Ser carries a CH2OH.
  - Tyr carries a para‑hydroxyphenyl.
  - Gly has no side chain.
  - Leu carries an isobutyl.
  - Arg carries a guanidine on a three‑carbon chain.
- **C‑terminus:** a proline ring ending in an N‑ethyl amide.

For stereochemistry, I took every stereocentre with a drawn wedge or hash to be the L‑amino‑acid configuration. I did not check each wedge against the SMILES chirality tags individually. I did check by neighbour‑order permutation that each written centre is the L form, and that the proline and pyroglutamic ring closures keep that configuration.

SMILES: CCNC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1

name: Fexuprazan
text:
The drawing shows a pyrrole ring whose nitrogen carries a sulfonyl group.

**Pyrrole ring:** The ring atoms are N, C2, C3, C4 and C5.
- C2 (upper right of the ring) bears the 2,4-difluorophenyl group.
- C3 bears the methoxy group.
- C4 bears the CH2NHCH3 group.
- C5 is an unsubstituted CH.

**2,4-Difluorophenyl group:** The ring carbon attached to the pyrrole has a fluorine-bearing carbon next to it (ortho). The para position, across the ring from the attachment point, also carries fluorine. This gives c1(...)c(F)cc(F)cc1.

**Sulfonyl group:** The sulfur is double-bonded to two oxygens and attached to a 3-fluorophenyl ring. The ring carbon bonded to sulfur is followed by a CH, then the carbon bearing fluorine, which makes the fluorine meta to the sulfur.

**SMILES:** n1(S(=O)(=O)c2cccc(F)c2)cc(CNC)c(OC)c1-c1ccc(F)cc1F

Atom-by-atom check:
- Pyrrole ring: n1, then c (C5), c(CNC) (C4), c(OC) (C3), c1 (C2), which closes the ring.
- Difluorophenyl ring: c1ccc(F)cc1F. The attachment carbon is followed by c, c, c(F), c, then c1F. The carbon bearing F is para to the attachment carbon (position 4), and the last carbon bearing F is ortho (position 2). This is correct.

SMILES: CNCc1cn(S(=O)(=O)c2cccc(F)c2)c(-c2ccc(F)cc2F)c1OC

name: Fesoterodine Fumarate
text:
This structure is fesoterodine fumarate: the fumaric acid (E-butenedioic acid) salt component plus the fesoterodine free base.

**Fumaric acid:** two carboxylic acids joined through a trans CH=CH, written `OC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)O`.

**Fesoterodine part:**
- A diisopropylamino group (N with two CH(CH3)2) is attached to a CH2CH2 chain.
- The chain ends at a stereocentre that also carries a phenyl ring and a substituted benzene ring.
- On the substituted ring, the carbon ortho to the stereocentre carries an isobutyrate ester, O–C(=O)–CH(CH3)2.
- The ring carbon para to that ester oxygen carries a CH2OH group.

**Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre has a wedge bond to the CH2 of the chain, the substituted aryl group at upper right, the phenyl group below, and the implicit H pointing away from the viewer. Viewed from the front, aryl → chain CH2 → phenyl runs counterclockwise. Writing the neighbours in the order aryl, H, CH2, phenyl, this gives `[C@H]`. This matches the (R) configuration of fesoterodine.

SMILES: OC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)O.CC(C)C(=O)Oc1ccc(CO)cc1[C@H](CCN(C(C)C)C(C)C)c1ccccc1

name: Filgotinib
text:
The structure is a cyclopropanecarboxamide on a [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyridine core, which carries a para-substituted phenyl bearing a CH2-thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide.

**Fragments read from the image**
- Cyclopropyl group attached to C(=O)NH.
- The NH is bonded to C2 of the triazole ring.
- Triazole ring: C2 is double-bonded to N3, and N3 is bonded to the bridgehead N (the label at about 485,885). C2 is also bonded to the other ring N (at about 290,905), which is double-bonded to C8a (at about 395,965). C8a is bonded to the bridgehead N.
- Pyridine ring: the bridgehead N is bonded to C5 (at about 598,921), which carries the aryl group. C5 is double-bonded to C6, then C7, then C8 (double bond C7=C8), then C8a.
- Phenyl ring: para-substituted, with one end bonded to C5 of the pyridine ring and the other to CH2.
- CH2 is bonded to N of thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide: N–CH2CH2–S(=O)(=O)–CH2CH2 back to N.

**SMILES construction**
Starting from the cyclopropyl group: O=C(C1CC1)Nc1nc2cccc(-c3ccc(CN4CCS(=O)(=O)CC4)cc3)n2n1

Check of the fused ring: c1 (C2) n (the ring N bonded to C8a) c2 (C8a) c c c (C8, C7, C6) c(-Ar) (C5) n2 (bridgehead N, closing to C8a) n1 (N3, closing to C2). The bridgehead N is bonded to C5, C8a and N3, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(C1CC1)Nc1nc2cccc(-c3ccc(CN4CCS(=O)(=O)CC4)cc3)n2n1

name: Finasteride
text:
The drawing matches finasteride, a 4-azasteroid. I identified it by recognising the scaffold and then reading the stereochemistry from the drawing's wedges and hashes.

- **Left side:** an N-tert-butyl amide, with the C(=O)NH attached to the five-membered ring by a wedge bond.
- **Ring system:** a fused four-ring skeleton (cyclopentane plus three six-membered rings), with two angular methyl groups on wedge bonds.
- **Right-hand ring:** a lactam containing NH–C(=O)–CH=CH, so the C=C is conjugated with the carbonyl.
- **Stereocentres:** three ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn as hashes or wedges, in addition to the wedged amide carbon and the two wedged methyl-bearing carbons.

I did not re-derive each @/@@ label from the image. I wrote the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the standard finasteride SMILES (as I remember it from PubChem), so the stereo descriptors rest on that recall.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2C(=O)NC(C)(C)C)CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(C=CC(=O)N4)C

name: Fimasartan
text:
The drawing breaks down into five parts.

- **Thioamide:** CN(C)C(=S)C. The dimethylamino nitrogen carries two methyls and is bonded to a C=S carbon, which connects through a CH2 to the pyrimidinone ring.
- **Pyrimidinone ring:** The ring atoms are C5 (bearing the CH2), C4 (bearing a methyl), N3 (=N), C2 (bearing the butyl), N1 (bearing the benzyl), and C6 (=O).
  - C5 is bonded to C4 by a double bond, C4 to N by a single bond, N=C2 by a double bond, C2 to N1 by a single bond, N1 to C(=O) by a single bond, and C(=O) back to C5.
  - SMILES for the ring: CC1=C(CC(=S)N(C)C)C(=O)N(Cc...)C(CCCC)=N1
- **Butyl group:** CCCC on C2.
- **Biphenyl:** The N-CH2 is attached to a para-substituted benzene, whose other para position links to a second benzene ring. That ring carries the tetrazole at the ortho position.
- **Tetrazole:** The drawing shows C(=N–NH–N=N) written as c1nnn[nH]1. The ring is C, N (drawn with a double bond to C), NH, N, N (double bond to the other N). The aromatic form is c1nn[nH]n1 or c1nnn[nH]1, and either works.

Full SMILES: CCCCC1=NC(C)=C(CC(=S)N(C)C)C(=O)N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nnn[nH]1

Checking the tetrazole connectivity: the carbon is bonded to N (bottom left, which connects to NH) and to N (right). The NH connects to the top N, which connects to the right N, which connects back to the carbon. The ring is therefore C–N–NH–N–N, giving c1nn[nH]nn... that is five atoms: C, N(left), NH, N(top), N(right). The SMILES c1nnn[nH]1 reads C, N, N, N, NH, which gives the carbon bonded to NH. In the drawing the carbon is bonded to the left N, which is bonded to NH, so the correct ordering is c1(nn[nH]nn1) with C, N-left, NH, N-top, N-right.

Tetrazole: c1nn[nH]nn1 would have 6 atoms, so the correct form is c1n[nH]nn1. That reads C, N(left), NH, N(top), N(right) closing to C, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCC1=NC(C)=C(CC(=S)N(C)C)C(=O)N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1n[nH]nn1

name: Fingolimod
text:
The drawing shows fingolimod.

Reading the chain from the left, the octyl group has carbons at these approximate x-positions: 75, 153, 251, 329, 427, 505, 603, 681. That is 8 carbons, ending at the ring attachment near x=780.

The benzene ring is para-substituted. On the other side, the ring connects through CH2 (1073) and CH2 (1151) to the quaternary carbon (1247). That carbon carries NH2 and two CH2OH groups.

The SMILES is CCCCCCCCc1ccc(cc1)CCC(N)(CO)CO. No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCc1ccc(cc1)CCC(N)(CO)CO

name: Fipronil
text:
This structure is fipronil.

Reading it region by region:
- **Benzene ring:** it carries two Cl atoms ortho to the point where it joins the pyrazole N, and a CF3 group para to that junction.
- **Pyrazole ring:** N1 is attached to the aryl ring and bonded to C5, which bears NH2. C5 is double-bonded to C4, which carries the S(=O)CF3 group. C4 is bonded to C3, which bears the C≡N group. C3 is double-bonded to N2, and N2 is bonded back to N1.
- **Sulfoxide:** S is double-bonded to O and single-bonded to a CF3 group. No stereochemistry is drawn at S, so none is included.

SMILES: NC1=C(S(=O)C(F)(F)F)C(C#N)=NN1C1=C(Cl)C=C(C(F)(F)F)C=C1Cl

name: Fengycin
text:
I read this as a cyclic lipopeptide: a 3-hydroxyhexadecanoyl chain on a Glu–Orn tail, attached to a macrocycle closed by an ester to a Tyr phenol oxygen. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing. The 3-hydroxy carbon of the fatty chain has plain bonds, so it carries no stereo label.

**Lipid tail.** I counted the chain from the amide carbonyl: C1 is the C=O, C2 is CH2, C3 is CH(OH), and C4–C16 run up to the terminal CH3. That makes a 3-hydroxyhexadecanoyl group.

**Side chain.** The lipid is acylated onto a Glu (free γ-COOH), which is linked to an Orn (free δ-NH2). The Orn carbonyl then forms the amide to the Tyr that closes the ring.

**Macrocycle.** Going around the ring from that Tyr:
- Tyr: its benzylic CH2 is drawn as "C", and the para oxygen forms the ester ring closure.
- Thr: alpha carbon plus a CH(CH3)OH side chain.
- Glu: free γ-COOH.
- Ala.
- Pro.
- Gln: side-chain primary amide.
- Tyr: free para-OH.
- Ile: its carbonyl is esterified by the first Tyr's phenol oxygen.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCC(O)CC(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]1Cc2ccc(cc2)OC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@@H]2CCCN2C(=O)[C@@H](C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(=O)O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](C)O)NC1=O

name: Firocoxib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Lactone ring:** a five-membered ring containing a ring oxygen, a carbonyl carbon (C=O), a carbon bearing the ether oxygen, a carbon bearing the aryl group (joined to the previous carbon by a C=C double bond), and a quaternary carbon carrying two methyl groups. This is a butenolide.
- **Ether substituent:** the carbon next to the carbonyl carries an O–CH2–cyclopropyl group. The cyclopropyl is a three-membered ring.
- **Aryl substituent:** the other alkene carbon is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring. The substituent opposite the ring attachment is a methylsulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O)CH3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the quaternary carbon has two identical methyl groups, so it is not a stereocentre. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES for the lactone: O=C1OC(C)(C)C(c2ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc2)=C1OCC1CC1

Atom check: the ring is C1(=O), O, C(CH3)2, C(aryl)=C(OR), closing back to C1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1OC(C)(C)C(c2ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc2)=C1OCC1CC1

name: Flavoxate
text:
This is flavoxate: a 3-methylflavone-8-carboxylic acid ester of 2-(piperidin-1-yl)ethanol.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Phenyl ring:** a benzene ring at the upper left, attached to C2 of the chromone.
- **Pyranone ring:** C2 is bonded to the phenyl, to the ring oxygen, and by a double bond to C3. C3 carries a methyl group. C4 is a C=O, and C4a and C8a are the ring-fusion carbons.
- **Fused benzene ring:** C8a is bonded to the ring oxygen, and C8 carries the ester group.
- **Ester side chain:** C8 bears C(=O)O–CH2CH2–N, and the nitrogen is part of a piperidine ring.

SMILES, written from the phenyl ring onward: c1ccccc1-c1oc2c(C(=O)OCCN3CCCCC3)cccc2c(=O)c1C

Check on the chromone ring: c1(Ph) o c2 c(ester) c c c c2 c(=O) c1C. The atoms in order are C2(Ph), O1, C8a, C8 (ester), C7, C6, C5, C4a (closing ring 2 back to C8a), C4(=O), and C3(Me) closing ring 1 back to C2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1c(-c2ccccc2)oc2c(C(=O)OCCN3CCCCC3)cccc2c1=O

name: Finerenone
text:
I read the molecule as a 1,4-dihydro-1,6-naphthyridine core, which matches the finerenone skeleton. Working through the drawing region by region:

- **Dihydropyridine ring (left):** it has an NH, a methyl-bearing C=C carbon, and a carbon carrying a primary amide, C(=O)NH2. It also has a stereogenic sp3 carbon (C4).
- **Pyridine ring (lower left):** it is fused to the first ring. It carries a methyl, a ring nitrogen, and an ethoxy group (OCC) on the carbon next to the fusion carbon.
- **Aryl group on C4:** the ring is attached through a wedge bond. Going round from the attachment carbon, it has an OMe-bearing carbon, a CH, a carbon bearing C#N, and two more CH carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** the aryl bond is a wedge (toward the viewer), so the implicit H points away. Viewed from the front, the three carbon neighbours run clockwise from the fusion carbon (C4a), through C3, to the aryl carbon. For the neighbour order C4a, H, C3, aryl in the SMILES below, that corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)C1=C(C)Nc2c(C)cnc(OCC)c2[C@@H]1c1ccc(C#N)cc1OC

name: Flecainide
text:
The drawing shows flecainide, with no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

- **Piperidine ring:** NH followed by five carbons. The substituted carbon is bonded to the NH, to the CH2 that leads to the amide, and to a ring CH2.
- **Amide:** the CH2 connects to an NH, which connects to C(=O) on the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** the carbonyl carbon sits on one ring carbon (position 1). The adjacent carbon (position 2) carries an OCH2CF3 group, shown at the lower left. Going around the ring from position 1 in the other direction, position 6 is a CH, and position 5 carries the second OCH2CF3 group (upper right). The substituents are therefore at positions 2 and 5.

SMILES for the ring: c1(C(=O)NCC2CCCCN2)cc(OCC(F)(F)F)ccc1OCC(F)(F)F

The substituent at position 5 is reached from position 1 via the CH at position 6, then position 5, which agrees with the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(NCC1CCCCN1)c1cc(OCC(F)(F)F)ccc1OCC(F)(F)F

name: Florbetaben (18F)
text:
The drawing shows an N-methylaniline ring joined through a C=C bond to a second benzene ring. That second ring carries a para O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-[18F] chain.

The double bond is drawn in the plane with the two aryl groups on opposite sides, which is the trans (E) geometry. The left ring attaches at its upper right and the right ring at its lower left, and the bond runs from the upper-left carbon (440,718) to the lower-right carbon (500,772). The substituents are at (365,742) on the left and (580,746) on the right. The first alkene carbon sits above the line joining the substituents and the second sits below it, so the substituents are on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES: CNc1ccc(/C=C/c2ccc(OCCOCCOCC[18F])cc2)cc1

name: Florbetapir F-18
text:
This looks like the amyloid PET tracer [18F]AV-45 (florbetapir) or a close analog. It has an N-methylaniline ring, a vinyl linker, and a pyridine bearing a triethylene glycol-type chain ending in 18F.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Left:** a CH3–NH group attached to a benzene ring.
- **Linker:** the para position of that ring carries a CH=CH. The double bond appears to be trans (E), because the drawing shows the two substituents on opposite sides.
- **Pyridine:** the vinyl group is on C5 of the ring. N is adjacent to C2, which carries the O chain (a 2-alkoxy, 5-vinyl pyridine).
- **Chain:** O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–18F, which is three oxygens and three ethylene units.

The SMILES, written from the left, is CNc1ccc(cc1)/C=C/c1ccc(nc1)OCCOCCOCC[18F].

Checking the pyridine: c1ccc(nc1) starts at C5, then C4, C3, C2 (bearing O), then N and C6 closing back to C5. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNc1ccc(cc1)/C=C/c1ccc(nc1)OCCOCCOCC[18F]

name: Florfenicol
text:
I read this as florfenicol, the (1R,2S) isomer.

- **Left side:** a methylsulfonyl group (CH3–SO2, two S=O) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Benzylic carbon:** it carries a wedged OH. The priorities are OH > C2 > aryl > H. With H pointing back, OH (up), C2 (lower right) and aryl (lower left) run clockwise, so this centre is R.
- **Second stereocentre:** it carries a wedged CH2F and an NH below. The priorities are N > CH2F > C1 > H. With H pointing back, N (down), CH2F (upper right) and C1 (upper left) run counterclockwise, so this centre is S.
- **Right side:** the NH is acylated by a dichloroacetyl group, NH–C(=O)–CHCl2.

In the SMILES below, the benzylic carbon is written [C@H] and the CH2F-bearing carbon [C@@H]. I checked each tag against the R/S assignments above.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)[C@H]([C@@H](CF)NC(=O)C(Cl)Cl)O

name: Flomoxef
text:
I read this as the oxacephem antibiotic flomoxef and wrote the SMILES region by region.

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a six-membered ring containing one ring oxygen (the oxacephem skeleton). The ring carries a C=C bearing the carboxylic acid on one carbon and the CH2 linker on the other.
- **C7 of the β-lactam:** it carries both a methoxy group and an acylamino group. The acyl group is NH–C(=O)–CH2–S–CHF2, i.e. a difluoromethylthio-acetamide.
- **Side chain on the ring C=C:** a CH2–S link to a tetrazole carbon. The tetrazole is a five-membered ring of one carbon and four nitrogens, and its N1 bears a CH2CH2OH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows a wedge on the C7–N bond and a hashed H on the ring-fusion carbon (C6). I worked out the @/@@ labels from the 2D coordinates. C7 is `[C@]` with neighbour order O, ring-closure C8 (the β-lactam C=O), N, C6. C6 is `[C@H]` with neighbour order C7, H, N (via the ring closure), O. This assignment was done by hand and has not been checked with software.

SMILES: CO[C@]1(NC(=O)CSC(F)F)[C@H]2OCC(CSc3nnnn3CCO)=C(N2C1=O)C(=O)O

name: Fluciclovine
text:
The drawing shows a cyclobutane ring with four carbon vertices.

- One ring carbon carries both an NH2 group and a carboxylic acid group (C(=O)OH).
- The ring carbon on the opposite side of the ring carries a fluorine.
- All bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: NC1(C(=O)O)CC(F)C1

name: Floxuridine
text:
I read the molecule as 5-fluoro-2'-deoxyuridine (floxuridine): a 5-fluorouracil ring joined through N1 to a 2-deoxyribofuranose ring.

**Base.** The six-membered ring is N1, C2(=O), N3–H, C4(=O), C5(F) and C6, with a C5=C6 double bond. The fluorine sits on C5.

**Sugar.** The five-membered ring is C1', C2' (CH2), C3', C4' and the ring oxygen.
- C3' carries an OH on a wedge bond.
- C4' carries a CH2OH on a hashed bond.
- C1' is bonded to N1 by a hashed bond.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash bond and the 2D positions of its neighbours, with the implicit hydrogen taking the opposite side to the drawn bond.
- C1': `[C@H]2`
- C3': `[C@H](O)`
- C4': `[C@@H](CO)O2`

This gives the natural β-D configuration, consistent with floxuridine. The SMILES uses valid ring closures and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)N(C=C1F)[C@H]2C[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O2

name: Fluconazole
text:
The drawing shows fluconazole: a central carbon bearing an OH, a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring, and two CH2 groups, each linked to a 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl ring.

**Triazole rings.** The upper ring contains N(CH2)–N=C–N=C. Its atoms run from the CH2-bearing N1 to N2 (top), then C3, then N4 (left), then C5 back to N1. So the ring is n1cncn1... written with explicit bonds: N1–N=C–N=C1, which gives C1=NC=NN1C... as the ring closure.

The lower ring is the same: N1 is attached to the CH2, N2 is on the left, C3 is at the bottom left, N4 is at the bottom, and C5 is on the right.

**Aromatic ring.** The ring carbon attached to the central carbon has an ortho F on one side (upper) and a CH on the other (lower). Going around the ring: C1 (attached), C2 (F), C3 (H), C4 (F), C5 (H), C6 (H). This is the 2,4-difluorophenyl pattern.

**Stereochemistry.** The central carbon carries two identical CH2-triazolyl groups, so it is not a stereocentre, and no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: OC(Cn1cncn1)(Cn1cncn1)c1ccc(F)cc1F

name: Flucloxacillin
text:
I read this as flucloxacillin: a penicillin core (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring bearing a gem-dimethyl group and a carboxylic acid) with an acylamino side chain. The side chain is a 5-methylisoxazole-4-carbonyl group carrying a 2-chloro-6-fluorophenyl substituent at the 3-position.

I did not derive the three stereocentres independently from the wedges and hashes. I wrote the stereodescriptors from the known natural penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R) for flucloxacillin, on the assumption that the drawing shows that isomer.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=NO1)C2=C(C=CC=C2Cl)F)C(=O)N[C@H]3[C@@H]4N(C3=O)[C@H](C(S4)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Flucytosine
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with these atoms, going around it:

- C2 is a carbon with a C=O group (O drawn on the left).
- N1 is an NH, drawn at the top.
- C4 is a carbon bearing NH2.
- C5 is a carbon bearing F.
- C6 is a CH.
- N3 is a ring nitrogen with no hydrogen.

The ring bonds are N3=C6 (double), C5=C4 (double), and C2=O (exocyclic double). The remaining ring bonds are single: C2–N3, C2–NH, NH–C4, C5–C6.

This is 5-fluorocytosine, written as a SMILES string: O=C1NC(N)=C(F)C=N1.

Check: C1 (C=O) is bonded to NH, which is bonded to C(N)=, then =C(F), then C(H)=N1, which closes the ring back to C1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1NC(N)=C(F)C=N1

name: Fluindione
text:
The drawing shows an indane-1,3-dione core: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring that carries two C=O groups. The carbon between the two carbonyls (C2) bears a 4-fluorophenyl group. The fluorine sits para to the point of attachment, at the far right of that ring.

C2 is a stereocentre by connectivity only, since its two ring branches are equivalent by symmetry. It is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: O=C1C(c2ccc(F)cc2)C(=O)c2ccccc12

name: Flunarizine
text:
This is flunarizine: a piperazine with a bis(4-fluorophenyl)methyl group on one nitrogen and a cinnamyl group on the other.

The double bond is drawn with the CH2 and the phenyl on opposite sides, so it is trans (E). The chain runs N–CH2 (917,497) – CH= (1010,575) = CH (1123,533) – phenyl (1217,611).

For the geometry, the CH2 at (917,497) is above-left of the first alkene carbon at (1010,575). The phenyl at (1217,611) is below-right of the second alkene carbon at (1123,533). The substituents are therefore on opposite sides of the double bond, which gives E.

SMILES: Fc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccc(F)cc1)N1CCN(CC1)C/C=C/c1ccccc1

name: Flotufolastat
text:
I read the molecule left to right as a chain of linked units, and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond using CIP priorities.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Top left:** an L-glutamate joined through a urea (NC(=O)N) to a second L-glutamate. Both are S, drawn with one hash and one wedge.
- **Ornithine unit:** the second glutamate's side-chain carbonyl forms an amide with an ornithine nitrogen (three CH2 between Cα and Nδ). Its Cα is drawn with a hash and works out as R.
- **Succinyl linker:** the ornithine Nδ is acylated by a succinyl group, N–C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)–N.
- **Lysine unit:** the succinyl group's other end is amidated by a lysine ε-nitrogen (four CH2 chain). Its Cα is R.
- **Diaminopropionic acid unit:** the lysine α-NH is acylated by a diaminopropionic acid whose Cα is R. Its β-NH carries a 4-(di-tert-butylfluorosilyl)benzoyl group.
- **Glutamate–macrocycle unit:** the diaminopropionic acid α-NH is acylated by a glutamate γ-carbonyl. This glutamate's Cα is S and is bonded directly to one nitrogen of a 12-membered ring with four nitrogens (cyclen). The other three ring nitrogens each carry a CH2COOH group.

I converted each wedge/hash reading into @/@@ by permuting neighbour order against a known L-amino-acid SMILES.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC[C@@H](C(=O)O)NC(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)N[C@H](CCCNC(=O)CCC(=O)NCCCC[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)[Si](F)(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)NC(=O)CC[C@H](N2CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CC2)C(=O)O)C(=O)O)C(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Fludrocortisone
text:
I recognised the drawing as a fludrocortisone-type corticosteroid (9-fluoro-11,17,21-trihydroxypregn-4-ene-3,20-dione) and wrote the SMILES from that skeleton, then checked it against the image.

**Structure read from the image:**
- The four-ring steroid core has a C4=C5 double bond conjugated with the C3 ketone (the O at the far right).
- There is a methyl at C10 and a methyl at C13, both drawn as bold wedges.
- There is a hashed fluorine at C9, a wedged hydroxyl at C11, and a hashed hydroxyl at C17.
- The C17 side chain is C(=O)CH2OH.
- H at C8 is wedged and H at C14 is hashed.

**Stereochemistry:** The drawn wedges and hashes match the natural configuration: 8β-H, 9α-F, 10β-Me, 11β-OH, 13β-Me, 14α-H, 17α-OH. I took the chirality tags from the known fludrocortisone SMILES, which I recalled from memory rather than looked up. I then checked the C9 tag by deriving it from the cortisol SMILES with F replacing H. The two agree, so C9 is `[C@@]`.

name: Fludarabine
text:
This structure is fludarabine (2-fluoro-ara-A), read as follows:

- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring (tetrahydrofuran) with a CH2OH on C4′ and OH groups on C3′ and C2′.
- **Stereochemistry:** the N-glycosidic bond is a wedge, the CH2OH is a wedge, the 2′-OH is a wedge and the 3′-OH is hashed.
  - I worked out the anomeric carbon (C1′) from the drawing: viewed from the front with H at the back, N→C2′→O runs clockwise, which gives `[C@@H]`.
  - The remaining centres I took from the known arabinose (vidarabine-type) pattern, which agrees with the drawing: the 2′-OH is on the same face as the CH2OH, and the 3′-OH is trans to the 2′-OH. I did not derive each of these centres separately from the wedges.

name: Flunitrazepam
text:
The drawing shows flunitrazepam, a benzodiazepine, and I read it region by region.

- **Seven-membered ring:** N1 carries a methyl group (the line at the lower left). N1 is bonded to the C=O carbon (C2), which is bonded to a CH2 (C3). The CH2 is bonded to N4, which is double-bonded to C5. C5 carries the 2-fluorophenyl group and is bonded to the fused benzene ring.
- **Fused benzene ring:** it contains the carbon attached to N1, the carbon attached to C5, and the carbon bearing the nitro group. The nitro carbon is the second ring carbon along the path from C5 (C5 → C(ring junction) → CH → C(NO2)). This puts the nitro group para to the carbon bonded to N1.
- **Substituents:** the nitro group is drawn in charge-separated form, [N+](=O)[O-]. The pendant phenyl ring has fluorine on the carbon adjacent to the one attached to C5.

SMILES, built in order:
CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21

Check on the fused ring: c2 (attached to C5), then cH, then c(NO2), then cH, cH, then c21 (attached to N1). The ring junction carbon bonded to C5 is adjacent to a CH, then the nitro carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21

name: Fluorescein
text:
This is fluorescein in its lactone (spiro) form.

The drawing has three parts:
- A benzene ring fused to a five-membered lactone. The lactone ring contains the spiro carbon, an ring O, and a C=O.
- A xanthene core with a ring O. Each of the two outer rings carries an OH.
- A spiro carbon joining the lactone and the xanthene.

The lower-right ring is drawn with double bonds C(OH)=C at the bottom right, so the rings are written as ordinary aromatic rings.

SMILES: O=C1OC2(c3ccccc13)c1ccc(O)cc1Oc1cc(O)ccc12

The atoms check out against the drawing:
- The spiro carbon C2 bonds to the lactone O, the benzo carbon, and the two xanthene carbons.
- The first xanthene ring is c1ccc(O)cc1O…, entered at the carbon attached to the spiro carbon. It then runs through two CH, the C-OH, a CH, and the carbon bearing the ring O.
- The second ring is c1cc(O)ccc12, starting at the carbon bonded to the ring O and ending at the carbon bonded to the spiro carbon.

In the drawing, the ring O connects the carbon adjacent to the CH that sits next to C-OH. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: O=C1OC2(c3ccccc13)c1ccc(O)cc1Oc1cc(O)ccc12

name: Fluorodopa
text:
I read this as 6-fluoro-L-DOPA, an amino acid with a fluorinated catechol ring.

- **Side chain:** A carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) is on the left, bonded to the α-carbon. The α-carbon carries an NH2 on a bold wedge. A CH2 links it to the ring.
- **Ring:** Going around from the CH2-bearing carbon, the substituents are F on the next carbon, then an unsubstituted CH, then OH, then OH, then another unsubstituted CH, and back to the start. The ring therefore has F ortho to the CH2 group and two adjacent OH groups.
- **Stereochemistry:** The wedged NH2 points toward the viewer, so the implicit H is at the back. Viewed with H away, the sequence N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise. With CIP priorities N > COOH > CH2, this is S, which is the L configuration. That matches `N[C@@H](R)C(=O)O` written from N.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1cc(O)c(O)cc1F)C(=O)O

name: Fluoxetine
text:

name: Fluorometholone Acetate
text:
The drawing is a steroid skeleton (four fused rings: three six-membered and one five-membered). I read it as fluorometholone acetate, and I wrote the SMILES partly from my recollection of the known compound rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges.

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with a C=C between C1 and C2, a ketone at C3 and a C=C between C4 and C5.
- **C6:** a methyl group on a bold wedge.
- **C9:** fluorine on a bold wedge.
- **C11:** a hydroxyl on a hashed bond.
- **C10 and C13:** each carries a hashed methyl group.
- **C8 and C14:** these carry the drawn hydrogens (hashed and bold respectively).
- **C17:** carries an acetyl group (C(=O)CH3) and an acetate ester (OC(=O)CH3), with the acetate oxygen on a bold wedge.

The drawing looks like a standard steroid flipped over. The methyls at C10 and C13 are hashed, where they are usually wedged. With that flip, the 6-methyl, 9-fluoro and 17-acetoxy groups are all α, and the 11-hydroxyl is β. That matches fluorometholone (6α-methyl, 9α-fluoro, 11β-hydroxy), so the acetate at C17 gives fluorometholone acetate.

I checked that the SMILES is valid and that the ring closures match the drawing.

name: Fluorometholone
text:
The drawing is a steroid skeleton (four fused rings, A–D) with these features:

- Ring A is a cross-conjugated 1,4-dien-3-one.
- C9 carries F and C11 carries OH.
- C6 carries a methyl, and both ring-junction carbons C10 and C13 carry methyls.
- C17 carries both an OH and an acetyl group (C(=O)CH3).

Taken together, this is fluorometholone (9-fluoro-11,17-dihydroxy-6-methylpregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione).

The methyls on C10 and C13 are hashed, which is the reverse of the usual steroid drawing, so the molecule is shown from the opposite face. Reading every wedge and hash with that in mind gives the natural configuration:

- 9α-F
- 11β-OH
- 6α-methyl
- 17α-OH
- 14α-H
- 8β-H

I did not derive the @/@@ labels independently from the drawing. I wrote them from my memory of the fluorometholone SMILES and checked only that the drawn wedges and hashes correspond to those configurations.

name: Flupirtine
text:
The image shows flupirtine, which I read as follows.

- **Left end:** an ethyl group (CH3–CH2) bonded to an oxygen, then a carbonyl carbon (C=O), then an NH. Together these form an ethyl carbamate, CCOC(=O)N.
- **Pyridine ring:** the carbamate NH is attached to a ring carbon. The adjacent ring carbon bears NH2 and sits next to the ring nitrogen. The carbon on the other side of the ring nitrogen bears the NH–CH2 substituent. The remaining two ring carbons are CH.
- **Right end:** the NH is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a benzene ring carrying fluorine at the para position.

Writing the pyridine ring from the carbamate-bearing carbon: c1(NC(=O)OCC)c(N)nc(NCc2ccc(F)cc2)cc1.

name: Fluphenazine
text:
The drawing is a phenothiazine with a CF3 group on one benzo ring, and its ring nitrogen carries a three-carbon chain to a piperazine bearing a 2-hydroxyethyl group. This is fluphenazine.

**Phenothiazine core.** The left (CF3) ring has its CF3 carbon at (872, 596). Its neighbours are the carbon at (960, 506) and the carbon at (906, 716). The ring carbon at (1028, 746) bonds to N, and the one at (1114, 658) bonds to S. Going around the ring from the CF3 carbon, the order is C(CF3), CH (906, 716), C–N (1028, 746), C–S (1114, 658), CH (1082, 537), CH (960, 506). So the CF3 carbon is separated from the C–N carbon by one CH, which is meta to N and para to S. This matches fluphenazine, with CF3 at position 2.

**Side chain.** From N, three CH2 groups lead to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2CH2OH.

**SMILES.** Written starting from the hydroxyethyl end:
OCCN1CCN(CCCN2c3ccccc3Sc3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc32)CC1

Checking the ring closure in `N2c3ccccc3Sc3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc32`:
- N2 bonds to c3, the first atom of the right benzo ring.
- That ring runs c3ccccc3, and its last atom bonds to S.
- S bonds to the next aromatic carbon, opening ring 3 again (the C–S carbon).
- Then come c, c, and c(CF3), so the CF3 carbon sits two atoms from the C–S carbon, which is para to S.
- Then c and c32 follow, the last atom being the C–N carbon, which closes to N.

This gives CF3 meta to N and para to S, consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: OCCN1CCN(CCCN2c3ccccc3Sc3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc32)CC1

name: Fluoxymesterone
text:

For the stereo check, I looked at C13 in the SMILES. Viewed from its methyl group, the neighbours C14, C17 and C12 run counterclockwise, which matches the `@` in the SMILES and the wedged methyl in the drawing. I did not check the other stereocentres individually.

name: Fluralaner
text:
I read the structure region by region, starting from the left.

- **Left end:** a CF3CH2 group (three F on a carbon, then CH2) is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O). That carbonyl carbon is attached to a CH2, which is bonded to a second NH.
- **Amide link:** the second NH is bonded to another C(=O), which is attached to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** the carbon bearing the C(=O) has a methyl on the adjacent ring carbon. The isoxazoline attaches to the ring carbon para to the carbonyl-bearing carbon.
  - Going around the ring: C1 (carbonyl-bearing, at 700,828), C2 (methyl-bearing, at 762,890), C3 (CH, at 850,868), C4 (isoxazoline-bearing, at 875,783), C5 (CH, at 813,720), C6 (CH, at 725,741).
  - The methyl is therefore ortho to the carbonyl-bearing carbon, and the isoxazoline is at C4, which is para to C1.
- **Isoxazoline ring:** C(=N–O–C(CF3)(Ar)–CH2–), closed back onto the first carbon.
- **Right-hand aryl group:** a 3,5-dichlorophenyl ring on the quaternary carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the quaternary carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

I wrote the SMILES with the CH2 between the two amide groups as "CNC(=O)", which is correct. In the ring closure "C1=NOC(C1)(...)", the first C1 is the C=N carbon and the "(C1)" is the CH2 that closes the ring.

SMILES: O=C(NCC(F)(F)F)CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1C)C1=NOC(C1)(c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Flurbiprofen
text:
This is flurbiprofen. The structure has three parts:

- A phenyl ring on the left, bonded to a central benzene ring.
- On the central ring, a fluorine on the carbon adjacent to the one carrying the phenyl group.
- A CH(CH3)COOH group on the central ring, para to the phenyl group. The fluorine sits ortho to the phenyl and meta to the propanoic acid group.

Tracing the central ring from the carbon bearing the propanoic acid group: C1 carries the CH(CH3)COOH group, C2 is the CH at the bottom right, C3 carries F, C4 carries the phenyl, C5 is CH, and C6 is CH. This places F at C3 and phenyl at C4, which is para to the acid-bearing carbon.

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the stereocentre gets no stereo marks.

name: Fluspirilene
text:
This structure is spiperone-like: 1-phenyl-1,3,8-triazaspiro[4.5]decan-4-one, with the piperidine nitrogen carrying a 4,4-bis(4-fluorophenyl)butyl chain.

**Spiro core.** The spiro carbon is bonded to the C=O carbon, to the N bearing the phenyl group, and to two piperidine CH2 groups. The ring runs C(=O)–NH–CH2–N(Ph)–C(spiro). The piperidine ring is the spiro carbon, CH2, CH2, N, CH2, CH2.

**Side chain.** From the piperidine N the chain is CH2–CH2–CH2–CH(Ar)2, where each Ar is 4-fluorophenyl. That is three CH2 groups and then the CH bearing the two aryl rings.

**SMILES.** Written from the piperidine N: N1(CCCC(c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(F)cc2)CCC3(CC1)C(=O)NCN3c1ccccc1

Ring-closure check: N1 opens ring 1. The piperidine path is CC then C3, the spiro carbon, which opens ring 3. The branch (CC1) closes the piperidine, giving N1, C, C, C3, C, C back to N1, which is six atoms. After the branch, C(=O)NCN3 closes the five-membered ring, and the N carries the phenyl.

SMILES: O=C1NCN(c2ccccc2)C13CCN(CCCC(c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(F)cc2)CC3

name: Flurandrenolide
text:
I read this as the 1,2-dihydro analogue of flunisolide: a 6α-fluoro, 11β,21-dihydroxy, 16α,17-isopropylidenedioxy pregn-4-ene-3,20-dione. Ring A shows only the C4=C5 double bond, with the C3 ketone beside it.
