name: Flutamide
text:
The drawing is flutamide: an isobutyramide on an aromatic ring that also carries a nitro group and a CF3 group.

**Isobutyryl part:** An isopropyl group (two methyls on one CH) attaches to a carbonyl carbon with C=O, and that carbon bonds to NH. This gives CC(C)C(=O)N.

**Ring:** The NH-bearing carbon is the first ring carbon. Going around the ring from there:
- Next is a CH (upper left).
- Then comes the carbon bearing CF3 (top right).
- Then the carbon bearing the nitro group (right).
- Then two CH carbons at the bottom.

So the NH carbon is C1, the CF3 carbon is C3 and the nitro carbon is C4. That makes the ring 4-nitro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl, as in flutamide.

**Nitro group:** Drawn in charge-separated form as [N+](=O)[O-].

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)Nc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Fluticasone Furoate
text:
This drawing matches fluticasone furoate, so I wrote the SMILES from that identification. I did not derive the @/@@ labels atom by atom from the wedges; I took them from the known isomeric SMILES for fluticasone furoate.

- **Core:** a steroid skeleton with a 1,4-dien-3-one in ring A.
- **Fluorines:** one at C6 and one at C9.

The drawn wedges and hashes agree with the known configuration, which has the C6-F, C9-F, C16-methyl and C17-O substituents on one face and the 11-OH on the other. The drawing is flipped relative to the usual steroid orientation, so the methyls at C10 and C13 are hashed rather than wedged.

name: Fidaxomicin
text:
I read this as the macrolide fidaxomicin (tiacumicin B) and built the SMILES from the drawing region by region.

**Macrolactone (18-membered ring)**
- The lactone carbonyl carbon is bonded to the ring oxygen and to C2. C2 carries a CH2–O group and is double-bonded to C3.
- C3 is joined to C4, which is double-bonded to C5. This is followed by a CH2 and then a CH(OH) (wedged OH).
- Next comes C(CH3)=CH, then a CH bearing a wedged ethyl group, then a CH bearing the O-linked sugar (hashed bond).
- After that come C(CH3)=CH and C(CH3)=CH, then a CH2, and finally the CH–O of the lactone. That last carbon carries a CH(OH)CH3 side chain.
- Double-bond geometries were assigned from the drawn positions of the substituents. The two methyl-substituted C=C bonds next to the sugar-bearing carbon are trans along the chain. The C=C bond bearing the ethyl-side methyl is also trans along the chain.

**Sugar on the ring CH2–O**
- This is a six-membered ring with a ring oxygen. The ring carbons carry a wedged methyl, an O-acyl group (hashed), an OH (wedged) and an OMe (wedged).
- The anomeric carbon is bonded to the oxygen of the CH2–O linker.
- The O-acyl group is a 3,5-dichloro-2-ethyl-4,6-dihydroxybenzoate.

**Sugar on the macrocycle oxygen**
- This is a six-membered ring with a ring oxygen and a gem-dimethyl carbon. It carries two OH groups and an isobutyrate ester on the carbon next to the gem-dimethyl.

Stereo marks (@/@@) were assigned from each wedge or hash, taking the narrow end of the wedge as the stereocentre. I did not independently check the final string against a reference structure.

SMILES: O=C1O[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)C/C=C(C)/C=C(C)/[C@H](O[C@H]4[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)C(C)(C)O4)[C@@H](CC)/C=C(C)/[C@@H](O)C/C=C/C=C1\CO[C@@H]5O[C@H](C)[C@@H](OC(=O)c6c(O)c(Cl)c(O)c(Cl)c6CC)[C@H](O)[C@@H]5OC

name: Fluvastatin
text:
I read this as fluvastatin, drawn as the (3S,5R) enantiomer. Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Acid end:** a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH) is attached to a CH2.
- **Diol chain:** the CH2 leads to a carbon bearing a wedged OH (C3), then another CH2, then a second carbon bearing a wedged OH (C5).
- **Alkene:** C5 is attached to a trans CH=CH, which joins the indole at C2.
- **Indole:** the ring nitrogen carries an isopropyl group, and C3 of the indole carries a 4-fluorophenyl ring. The benzo ring is fused in the usual way.

For the stereocentres, the OH groups are wedged up and the implicit H is behind. Applying CIP priorities to the drawing gives C3 = S and C5 = R. That is the mirror image of the marketed (3R,5S) fluvastatin, but I encoded it as drawn. The alkene is trans.

SMILES: OC(=O)C[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)/C=C/c1n(C(C)C)c2ccccc2c1-c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Formaldehyde
text:
The image shows a double bond between an unlabeled atom and an O. Its left half is black, which is the colour RDKit-style drawings use for carbon. The right half is red, matching the O label.

An unlabeled left atom with a double bond to oxygen gives a carbon with only two bonds in total. That is a carbon atom bearing an implicit radical, or a carbene-like carbon, and it is written as [C]=O. Written plainly as C=O, the SMILES would imply formaldehyde, with two implicit hydrogens added. The drawing shows no hydrogens, so the hydrogen-free form is the better fit.

SMILES: [C]=O

name: Formic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a single carbon at the bend of the structure. It carries a double bond to an O on the left and a single bond to an OH on the right. The carbon has no other drawn substituents, so it keeps one implicit hydrogen. That makes the molecule formic acid, HC(=O)OH.

SMILES: O=CO

name: Folic Acid
text:
The structure is folic acid (pteroyl-L-glutamic acid). I read it in three parts:

- **Pterin end (right):** a bicyclic pteridine with a 2-amino group and a 4-oxo group. The ring NH sits between the C=O and the amino-bearing carbon.
- **Linker (middle):** a CH2 joins the pteridine to an NH, which attaches to a para-substituted benzene ring. The ring carries a C(=O)NH amide on the other side.
- **Glutamic acid end (left):** the amide nitrogen is bonded to the stereocentre. That carbon carries a COOH and a CH2CH2COOH chain, with the CH2 drawn on a hashed bond.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. With the CH2 hashed (pointing away), the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page, N (right), then COOH (down), then CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S. This is the natural L-glutamate configuration, and it matches `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O` when N is written first.

SMILES: Nc1nc2ncc(CNc3ccc(cc3)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)nc2c(=O)[nH]1

name: Fluvoxamine
text:
The drawing is fluvoxamine. Reading it region by region:

- **Methoxy chain:** a methyl is bonded to an oxygen, which continues into a four-carbon chain (O–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2) ending at the oxime carbon.
- **Oxime carbon:** this carbon is double-bonded to nitrogen and also carries the aryl ring.
- **Oxime ether:** the nitrogen is bonded to an oxygen, which leads to a CH2–CH2–NH2 group.
- **Aryl ring:** a para-substituted benzene whose far substituent is CF3.

For the C=N geometry I used the drawn coordinates. The oxime O lies on the same side of the C=N bond as the alkyl chain, so it is opposite the aryl ring. Aryl is the higher-priority group on carbon and O is the higher-priority group on nitrogen, so these are on opposite sides, which is the E configuration. In SMILES this is chain/C(=N\O).

SMILES: COCCCC/C(=N\OCCN)c1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1

name: Formoterol
text:
The drawing shows formoterol, with no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying an NH–CHO (formamide) group, an adjacent OH, and the CH(OH)CH2 side chain. The OH and formamide are on neighbouring carbons. The side chain sits on the ring carbon that is meta to the formamide carbon and para to the OH carbon.
- **Linker:** the side chain runs CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH(CH3)–CH2, ending at the right ring.
- **Right ring:** a para-substituted benzene bearing OCH3.

Left ring atom order, going around: C(NHCHO), C(OH), CH, CH, C(side chain), CH, back to C(NHCHO). The ring closure puts the side-chain carbon at the position meta to C(NHCHO) and para to C(OH), which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=CNc1cc(C(O)CNC(C)Cc2ccc(OC)cc2)ccc1O

name: Foscarnet
text:
The drawing shows a phosphorus atom (P) with three substituents and a carbon neighbour:
- a double bond to O (P=O)
- two single-bonded OH groups
- a single bond to a carbon, which carries a C=O and an OH (a carboxylic acid)

This is phosphonoformic acid (foscarnet).

SMILES: OC(=O)P(=O)(O)O

name: Fosfluconazole
text:
The drawing shows fosfluconazole, a fluconazole phosphate prodrug.

**Central carbon:** It carries four substituents: an aryl ring, two CH2 groups and an O–P(=O)(OH)2 group.

**CH2 groups:** Each CH2 is attached to a 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl ring.

**Aryl ring:** It is a 2,4-difluorophenyl group. The ipso carbon is bonded to the central carbon, the ortho carbon bears F, and the para carbon bears F. Going around the ring from the ipso carbon, the top-left carbon has F (ortho), then CH, then the carbon with F (para), then two more CH carbons. The fluorines are therefore at positions 2 and 4.

**Triazole rings:**
- Top ring: N1 (attached to the CH2) is bonded to N2, then C3 (=N), then N4, then C5 back to N1. In the image, N1 connects to the top N, which is double-bonded to a CH, which connects to the left N. The left N is double-bonded to the bottom CH, which connects back to N1. This matches the 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl pattern n1cncn1 written as n1cncn1, i.e. n1ncnc1 (N1, N2, C3, N4, C5).
- Bottom ring: N1 is attached to the CH2 and bonded to the left N (N2), then CH (C3), then the bottom N (N4), then C5 back to N1. This is the same 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl pattern.

**SMILES:** The aryl ring is written as c1ccc(F)cc1F, starting from the ipso carbon.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)OC(Cn1cncn1)(Cn1cncn1)c1ccc(F)cc1F

name: Formocortal
text:
I read the drawing as a triamcinolone-acetonide-type steroid core with four modifications.

- **Ring D side:** a 16,17-acetonide (an isopropylidene ketal bridging the two oxygens), and a 17-C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH3 acetate side chain.
- **Centre of the core:** a 9-fluoro group and an 11-hydroxy group.
- **Ring A:** a 3,5-diene bearing a 3-O–CH2CH2Cl (2-chloroethoxy) ether and a 6-formyl group (CHO).
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedges and hashes match the natural steroid configuration:
  - Both angular methyls, the 16-H, the 17 side chain, the 8-H and the 11-OH are β (wedged).
  - The 14-H and the 9-F are α (hashed).

I adapted the chirality tags from the known triamcinolone acetonide SMILES, keeping the same neighbour order at each stereocentre, and then changed ring A and the side chain to match this drawing.

SMILES: CC1(C)O[C@@H]2C[C@H]3[C@@H]4CC(C=O)=C5C=C(OCCCl)CC[C@]5(C)[C@@]4(F)[C@@H](O)C[C@]3(C)[C@@]2(O1)C(=O)COC(C)=O

name: Flurithromycin
text:
I read this as a fluorinated erythromycin-type 14-membered macrolide, which matches flurithromycin (8-fluoroerythromycin). The SMILES below was built from the drawing, with the ring stereocentres checked against it where I worked them out.

**Macrolactone ring (14 members):**
- Lactone C(=O)–O closes at C13, which carries a hashed ethyl group.
- C12 carries a hashed methyl and an OH.
- C11 carries a hashed OH.
- C10 carries a wedged methyl.
- C9 is a ketone.
- C8 carries F (plain bond) and a hashed methyl.
- C7 is a CH2.
- C6 carries an OH and a hashed methyl.
- C5 carries the hashed O-linked amino sugar.
- C4 carries a wedged methyl.
- C3 carries the hashed O-linked second sugar.
- C2 carries a wedged methyl and is bonded to the lactone carbonyl.

**Sugars:**
- Left sugar is desosamine: a tetrahydropyran with an NMe2 group, an OH and a ring methyl.
- Right sugar is cladinose: a tetrahydropyran with a quaternary C bearing OMe and CH3, an OH, and a ring methyl.

**Stereochemistry:** I worked out C13 and C8 directly from the wedges and hashes. The remaining centres are written to match the erythromycin A stereochemistry. With F placed at C8, I found the same chirality tag as erythromycin gives for that position. I did not independently verify the sugar stereocentres or the other ring centres from the image, so those rely on the erythromycin template.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)[C@@](F)(C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O1)C)O[C@H]2C[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O2)C)O)(C)OC)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)(C)O)C)C)O)(C)O

name: Fosphenytoin
text:
The drawing shows a hydantoin ring (imidazolidine-2,4-dione) with two phenyl groups on C5 and a phosphate group on N3, which makes it fosphenytoin.

- Ring: C5 (the quaternary carbon) is bonded to two phenyl rings, to the C4 carbonyl and to the NH. C4 is bonded to N3. N3 carries the CH2 group and is bonded to the C2 carbonyl, which is bonded to the NH.
- Side chain: N3–CH2–O–P(=O)(OH)OH.
- Stereochemistry: C5 has two identical phenyl substituents, so it is not a stereocentre, and no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: O=C1NC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)C(=O)N1COP(=O)(O)O

name: Fosaprepitant
text:
I read the structure as fosaprepitant, the phosphoryl prodrug of aprepitant. I assembled the SMILES from the drawing in these parts:

- **Triazolone with phosphate:** a 1,2,4-triazol-5-one ring. Its N–P(=O)(OH)₂ nitrogen is bonded to the C=O carbon. The ring carbon opposite is joined through a CH₂ to the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Morpholine:** a six-membered ring with N, a CH bearing the 4-fluorophenyl group, a CH bearing the ether oxygen, a ring O, and two CH₂ groups.
- **Side chain:** the ether oxygen links to a CH(CH₃) carbon, which carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.

I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges. The methyl on the side-chain CH is a wedge, the ether O on the morpholine carbon is a wedge, and the 4-fluorophenyl on the other morpholine carbon is a wedge. I worked each centre out from the viewing direction with the implicit H pointing away. This gave `[C@@H]` for the side-chain carbon and `[C@H]` for both morpholine carbons. I did not check the result against a reference SMILES for the drug.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O[C@H]1OCCN(CC2=NN(P(=O)(O)O)C(=O)N2)[C@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Fosnetupitant
text:
This looks like the netupitant quaternary N-methyl piperazinium phosphonooxymethyl prodrug (fosnetupitant).

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Phosphate end:** an HO–P(=O)(O⁻)–O–CH2 group attached to N⁺.
- **Piperazinium:** N⁺ carries a methyl and the CH2O–P group, and the ring is N⁺1CCN(CC1)…
- **Pyridine:** the piperazine's other nitrogen is bonded to pyridine C2. The ring atoms are C2, N1, C6 (H), C5 (bearing N(Me)C(=O)…), C4 (bearing o-tolyl) and C3 (H).
- **Amide side chain:** N(C)C(=O)C(C)(C)–Ar, where Ar is a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.

SMILES for the pyridine, with C2 attached to the piperazine N: c1(N2CC[N+](C)(COP(=O)(O)[O-])CC2)ncc(N(C)C(=O)C(C)(C)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c3)c(-c3ccccc3C)c1

Checking the pyridine ring connectivity: C2 is bonded to N (drawn at the bottom), then N is bonded to CH (the lower right carbon), then to C5 (bearing N-Me), then to C4 (bearing the aryl), then to CH (C3), and back to C2. This matches the SMILES above.

SMILES: CC1=CC=CC=C1c1cc(N2CC[N+](C)(COP(=O)(O)[O-])CC2)ncc1N(C)C(=O)C(C)(C)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Fosamprenavir
text:
The structure is fosamprenavir. I read it region by region.

- **Sulfonamide end:** a 4-aminophenyl ring is bonded to S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to a tertiary N. That N carries an isobutyl group and a CH2 linking to the next carbon.
- **Phosphate carbon:** the CH2 bond is hashed, and the carbon bears an O–P(=O)(OH)2 group. Working through the CIP priorities gives R.
- **Carbamate carbon:** this carbon carries a wedged benzyl group and an NH–C(=O)–O carbamate. It works out to S.
- **Tetrahydrofuran ring:** a five-membered ring with one O, attached through its 3-position to the carbamate O by a wedged bond. It works out to S.

I checked the chirality tags in the SMILES against these assignments, taking the explicit hydrogen on each centre into account.

SMILES: CC(C)CN(C[C@@H](OP(=O)(O)O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)O[C@H]1CCOC1)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(N)cc1

name: Fospropofol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying three substituents.

- **Ring:** six carbons, with the double bonds drawn between C(iPr) and the next carbon, between the two carbons on the right, and between C(O) and C(iPr) at the bottom.
- **Position 1:** an O–CH2–O–P(=O)(OH)2 chain. The ring oxygen is linked to a CH2, which is linked to another O, which is bonded to P. The phosphorus carries one =O and two OH groups.
- **Positions 2 and 6:** the two ring carbons adjacent to the oxygen-bearing carbon each carry an isopropyl group.

This gives 2,6-diisopropylphenoxymethyl phosphate.

SMILES: CC(C)c1cccc(C(C)C)c1OCOP(=O)(O)O

name: Fosfomycin
text:
This is fosfomycin: an epoxide with a methyl on one ring carbon and a phosphonic acid group, P(=O)(OH)₂, on the other.

- **Ring:** a three-membered ring of one oxygen and two carbons.
- **Substituents:** the left ring carbon carries a methyl, drawn as a hashed bond. The right ring carbon carries the phosphorus, also drawn as a hashed bond. Each ring carbon has an implicit hydrogen pointing toward the viewer.
- **Phosphorus:** one P=O and two P–OH groups.

Working out the chirality from the drawn geometry, with the hydrogens toward the viewer and the hashed substituents away, gives @@ for both ring carbons in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1O[C@@H]1P(=O)(O)O

name: Fostemsavir
text:
This is the fostemsavir structure: a 6-azaindole (pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridine) core carrying the phosphonooxymethyl group on the pyrrole nitrogen.

**Core and substituents**
- The phosphate is OP(=O)(O)O, attached through O–CH2 to the pyrrole nitrogen N1.
- C3 of the pyrrole carries the C(=O)C(=O)N ketoamide. The amide nitrogen is part of a piperazine whose other nitrogen bears a benzoyl group.
- The carbon adjacent to the pyrrole's C3a ring fusion carries OMe.
- The carbon adjacent to C7a (next to the ring nitrogen) carries a 3-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl group.

**Ring connectivity**
- Pyrrole: N1(CH2OP)–CH=C(C3)–C3a–C7a.
- Pyridine: C7a–C7(triazolyl)=N6–C5H=C4(OMe)–C3a.
- Triazole: N1 is attached to C7. Going around the ring, N1 is bonded to C5H, which is bonded to N4, which is bonded to C3(CH3), which is bonded to N2, which closes back to N1. This gives n1cnc(C)n1 with N1 as the attachment point.

**SMILES assembly**
COc1cncc(n2cnc(C)n2)c1... would put the ring atoms in the wrong order, so I wrote the ring in order instead:

c1(OC)cnc(n2cnc(C)n2)c2n(COP(=O)(O)O)cc(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCN(CC3)C(=O)c3ccccc3)c12

Checking the ring closures: c1(OC) is C4, then c is C5, n is N6, c(triazole) is C7, c2 is C7a, n(...) is N1, c is C2, c(...) is C3, and c12 is C3a, which closes to C4 (ring 1) and to C7a (ring 2). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cncc(n2cnc(C)n2)c1-,2 

The line above is malformed, so the correct final answer is:

SMILES: COc1cnc(-n2cnc(C)n2)c2c1c(C(=O)C(=O)N1CCN(C(=O)c3ccccc3)CC1)cn2COP(=O)(O)O

name: Fostamatinib
text:
This structure is fostamatinib, a phosphonooxymethyl prodrug of R406.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Phosphate:** P(=O)(O)(O) with two OH groups, attached through O to a CH2.
- **CH2 link:** the CH2 is bonded to the ring nitrogen N.
- **Oxazinone ring:** N–C(=O)–C(CH3)2–O–c(aromatic). The aromatic carbon next to the N-bearing carbon belongs to a pyridine ring.
- **Pyridine ring:** the carbon bonded to N (in the oxazinone) also bonds to the pyridine nitrogen. The pyridine nitrogen is bonded to a carbon that carries the NH substituent.
- **Pyrimidine:** NH links the pyridine to C4 of the pyrimidine. C5 bears F, C6 is CH, N1 follows, C2 carries the NH-aryl group, and N3 closes the ring.
- **Aryl group:** a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl ring on the second NH.

**SMILES assembly**
Starting from the phosphate:
OP(=O)(O)OCN1C(=O)C(C)(C)Oc2ccc(Nc3nc(Nc4cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c4)ncc3F)nc21

**Check of the fused ring:**
- The ring closure atoms are N1, C(=O), C(C)(C), O, c2 (bonded to O), c, c, c(N…), n, and c21.
- c2 is bonded to O and c21 is bonded to N1, so the oxazinone ring is N1, C=O, CMe2, O, c2 and c21, which is six atoms.
- The pyridine ring is c2, c, c, c(NH), n and c21, which is also six atoms.

SMILES: OP(=O)(O)OCN1C(=O)C(C)(C)Oc2ccc(Nc3nc(Nc4cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c4)ncc3F)nc21

name: Frovatriptan Succinate
text:
The drawing shows three components: frovatriptan, succinic acid and one water molecule.

- **Frovatriptan:** a tetrahydrocarbazole (an indole fused to a cyclohexane ring) with a carboxamide on the benzene ring and an NHMe group on the saturated ring.
- **Stereocentre:** the carbon bearing NHMe has a hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Seen from the H side, the ring CH2 on the right, the CH2 on the upper left and N run counterclockwise. That corresponds to `CN[C@@H]1...C1` in the SMILES atom order. I assigned this by hand and did not run it through a toolkit.
- **Succinic acid:** HOOC-CH2-CH2-COOH.
- **Water:** H2O.

SMILES: CN[C@@H]1CCc2[nH]c3ccc(C(N)=O)cc3c2C1.OC(=O)CCC(=O)O.O

name: Fudosteine
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right, the molecule is HO‑CH2‑CH2‑CH2‑S‑CH2‑CH(NH2)‑COOH. This is a cysteine with a 3‑hydroxypropyl group on the sulfur.

Stereochemistry: only the α‑carbon is drawn with a stereo bond. The NH2 is on a hashed wedge, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

- The CIP priorities at this carbon are N > CH2S > COOH, because S outranks O at the first point of difference.
- Viewed from the front, N (up) → CH2S (lower left) → COOH (lower right) runs counterclockwise.
- The H is toward the viewer, so the sense is reversed and the centre is clockwise, giving R. This matches the L‑cysteine configuration.

Written as SMILES, this stereocentre is `[C@H]` when the carbon is entered from the CH2 side (neighbour order CH2, H, N, COOH).

SMILES: OCCCSC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate
text:
I read the drawing as a five-membered ring (tetrahydrofuran) with one ring oxygen and four ring carbons. The two carbons next to the oxygen each carry a CH2–O–P(=O)(OH)2 group. The two carbons between them each carry an OH.

Stereochemistry from the drawing:
- The left CH2OP is a wedge, which makes the ring carbon it sits on S.
- The right CH2OP is a wedge, which makes its ring carbon R.
- The upper-left OH is a wedge, which makes its carbon S.
- The upper-right OH is a hash, which makes its carbon S.

I assigned these by CIP priorities and then converted them to @/@@ tags in the SMILES atom order by checking neighbour permutations. The CIP labels are by hand, so the tags carry the same risk.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)OC[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Furan
text:
The ring is five-membered: an O at the upper left and four carbons.

Going around the ring from O:
- O to the top carbon C1 (single bond).
- C1 to the right carbon C2, drawn with a double bond (the inner line runs parallel to this bond).
- C2 to the bottom carbon C3 (single bond).
- C3 to the bottom-left carbon C4, drawn with a double bond (the inner parallel line).
- C4 back to O (single bond).

This gives two C=C double bonds, C1=C2 and C3=C4, with O bonded to C1 and C4. That is a furan ring.

SMILES: c1ccoc1

Written in Kekulé form to match the drawing: C1=CC=CO1

SMILES: C1=CC=CO1

name: Furazolidone
text:
This is furazolidone: a 5-nitrofuran joined through a CH=N linkage to an N-amino oxazolidin-2-one.

**Nitrofuran side.** The furan ring has O at the bottom of the upper left, a nitro group (N+ with =O and O−) on the carbon next to the ring O, and the CH=N chain on the other carbon next to the ring O. The ring double bonds are C(NO2)=CH and CH=C(CH=N).

**Linker and oxazolidinone.** The chain runs ring C – CH=N – N(ring). The oxazolidinone ring is N–C(=O)–O–CH2–CH2, closing back to N.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The furan-bearing carbon at (845, 922) has its substituent, the furan carbon, at (665, 907), lower left. The N at (945, 779) carries the other N at (1100, 789) to the right. The C=N axis runs from lower left to upper right. The furan carbon sits on the left side of the axis, and the N substituent on the right. Checking which side of the axis each lies on:

- Axis direction: from C (845, 922) to N (945, 779), so d = (100, −143).
- Furan substituent relative to C: (−180, −15). Cross product d × v = 100·(−15) − (−143)(−180) = −1500 − 25740 = −27240.
- N substituent relative to N: (155, 10). Cross product = 100·10 − (−143)(155) = 1000 + 22165 = 23165.

The two cross products have opposite signs, so the substituents lie on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)c1ccc(o1)/C=N/N1CCOC1=O

name: Fulvestrant
text:
The structure is fulvestrant, an estradiol core with a 7α side chain. I read it region by region from the drawing.

- **Steroid core:** The A ring is aromatic and carries a phenolic OH on the carbon next to C4. Rings B, C and D follow, with a 17-OH on the five-membered D ring. A methyl at C13 is drawn as a wedge, and the ring-fusion hydrogens at C8, C9 and C14 are drawn as wedges or hashes.
- **Side chain:** C7 carries a hashed bond to a chain of nine CH2 groups. The chain ends in a sulfoxide S(=O), then three more CH2 groups, then CF2 and CF3.
- **Stereochemistry:** The core and 17-OH wedges and hashes match the natural estradiol configuration, so I used the estradiol SMILES pattern for those centres. For C7 I worked out the chirality directly from the hashed chain bond, with the implicit H pointing toward the viewer. That gives `@` in the order written below.

The sulfur is also a stereocentre, but it is drawn without a wedge, so I left it unspecified.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O)[C@H](CCCCCCCCCS(=O)CCCC(F)(F)C(F)(F)F)CC4=C3C=CC(=C4)O

name: Furosemide
text:
This structure is furosemide: a benzene ring carrying a carboxylic acid, a furfurylamino group, a chlorine and a sulfonamide.

Reading the ring from the carboxylic acid carbon (C1) around the ring:
- C1 bears the COOH group.
- C2 bears the NH–CH2–furan group.
- C3 is an aromatic CH.
- C4 bears Cl.
- C5 bears the SO2NH2 group.
- C6 is an aromatic CH, which closes back to C1.

The furan is attached through its 2-position: the carbon bonded to the CH2 is adjacent to the ring oxygen, giving c1ccco1 with the attachment at the first atom.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)c(Cl)cc1NCc1ccco1

name: Futibatinib
text:
I read the molecule as a 4-amino-pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine core:

- **Position 3** carries an alkyne linked to a 3,5-dimethoxyphenyl ring.
- **N1** is bonded to the 3-position of a pyrrolidine ring.
- **The pyrrolidine nitrogen** carries an acryloyl group, C(=O)CH=CH2.

The only stereocentre is pyrrolidine C3, drawn with a wedge to the pyrazole N. I took the wedge as having its narrow end at the carbon, so the N points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away.

CIP priorities at that carbon are N > CH2 bonded to the ring N > CH2 bonded to CH2 > H. Viewed with H at the back, N (left), then the CH2 bonded to the ring N (below), then the other CH2 (upper right) run counterclockwise, so the centre is S.

In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` is the writing order that gives S for this neighbour sequence.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CC[C@@H](C1)n1nc(C#Cc2cc(OC)cc(OC)c2)c2c(N)ncnc12

name: Gabapentin
text:
The drawing shows gabapentin: a cyclohexane ring whose one carbon (a quaternary spiro-type centre) carries two substituents.

- One substituent is CH2–NH2 (an aminomethyl group).
- The other is CH2–C(=O)OH (a carboxymethyl group).
- The ring has six carbons: the quaternary carbon plus five others.
- All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: NCC1(CC(=O)O)CCCCC1

name: Gabapentin Enacarbil
text:
This is the gabapentin prodrug with an isobutyryloxyethyl carbamate on the nitrogen.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The left end is an isopropyl group, CH(CH3)2, attached to a C(=O) that is bonded to an O.
- That O is bonded to a CH carrying a methyl group, and the CH is bonded to a second O.
- The second O is bonded to a C(=O), which is bonded to NH.
- The NH is bonded to a CH2 on the quaternary cyclohexane carbon.
- The cyclohexane ring has six vertices, and its quaternary carbon also bears CH2–C(=O)OH.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)OC(C)OC(=O)NCC1(CC(=O)O)CCCCC1

name: Gabexate
text:
This is the structure of gabexate, and I read it region by region.

- **Ethyl ester:** an ethyl group (CH3–CH2) is attached to an oxygen, which is attached to a C=O group.
- **Aromatic ring:** that carbonyl carbon is bonded to a benzene ring. The ring is para-substituted, with the other substituent being an oxygen.
- **Second ester:** this ring oxygen is bonded to a C(=O) group, which continues into a chain.
- **Chain:** counting the carbons after the carbonyl carbon, there are 4 CH2 groups. The chain runs from the carbonyl carbon at (730, 700) through CH2 at (818, 670), CH2 at (890, 727), CH2 at (978, 697), and CH2 at (1050, 752), then a final CH2 at (1140, 720) that attaches to N. That makes 5 CH2 groups in total, so the acid is a 6-carbon acid, hexanoate.
- **Guanidine end:** the last CH2 is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C(N)N, so the terminus is N=C(N)N.

Writing the SMILES from the ethyl end: CCOC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)OC(=O)CCCCCN=C(N)N. The chain after C(=O) has 5 carbons (CCCCC) before N, which matches the count above.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)OC(=O)CCCCCN=C(N)N

name: Friulimicin B
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic lipopeptide, a lipidated peptide with a ring of ten residues. I traced it from the lipid tail around the ring and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Lipid tail:** an iso-branched chain (terminal isopropyl, then 7 CH2) ends in a cis CH=CH, then CH2 and the C(=O) of an amide. This acyl group sits on an Asn residue.

**Ring, in order from the Asn:**
1. Asn: its side chain is CH2C(N)=O, and its backbone C(=O) links to residue 2.
2. 2,3-Diaminobutyric acid (Dab). Its α-N carries the Asn, its C(=O) goes to the pipecolic N, and its β-carbon (with CH3) has an NH that goes to the proline C(=O). This closes the macrocycle.
3. Pipecolic acid (six-membered ring), whose C(=O) links to residue 4.
4. 3-Methylaspartic acid, with the methyl and COOH on its β-carbon.
5. Asp, with a CH2COOH side chain.
6. Gly.
7. Asp, with a CH2COOH side chain.
8. Gly.
9. A second Dab, with its β-carbon bearing CH3 and a free NH2.
10. Val.
11. Pro, whose C(=O) closes back onto the first Dab.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash and from the position of the implicit H. That gives L-Asn, L-Pro and L-Asp. The pipecolic α-carbon comes out with the opposite (D-type) configuration from L-Pro in my reading of the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)CCCCCCC/C=C\CC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N2CCCC[C@@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N3CCC[C@H]3C(=O)N[C@H]1C

name: Gaboxadol
text:
The drawing shows a bicyclic system made of two fused rings.

**Five-membered ring (isoxazolone):** O, NH, C(=O), and two fused carbons. The ring atoms are O1, N2(H), C3(=O), C3a and C7a. The C3a=C7a double bond is the one shared with the six-membered ring.

**Six-membered ring (piperidine):** C7a, a CH2, NH, a CH2, a CH2 and C3a.
- Reading from the top fused carbon (bonded to O): C7a–CH2–NH–CH2–CH2–C3a.
- This gives 6 atoms in total: C7a, CH2, NH, CH2, CH2 and C3a.

**SMILES:** start at the carbonyl carbon, O=C1NOC2=C1CCNC2.
- C1(=O) is bonded to N, then O, then C2 (the fused carbon bearing O).
- C2=C1 closes the five-membered ring through the double bond to the other fused carbon, which is also bonded to the carbonyl carbon.
- That second fused carbon continues CC N C2: CH2, CH2, NH, then CH2 closing back to the O-bearing fused carbon.

Check against the drawing: the O-bearing fused carbon connects to CH2, which connects to NH, then CH2, then CH2, then the carbonyl-side fused carbon. This matches.

SMILES: O=C1NOC2=C1CCNC2

name: Fungichromin
text:
I read the structure as a 28-membered macrolactone ring (a filipin-type polyol with a conjugated pentaene), and wrote the SMILES by walking around the ring from the lactone carbonyl.

**Ring and substituents**
- The lactone is C(=O)–O, and the ring oxygen is attached to a CH bearing a wedged methyl.
- Next is a CH(OH) with a hashed OH, then the pentaene.
- The five C=C bonds are all drawn trans. The last one, C(Me)=CH, has its methyl on the side opposite the polyol chain.
- After the pentaene comes a run of contiguous CH(OH) centres and CH₂ groups: three adjacent CH(OH), then CH₂ / CH(OH) repeated five times, ending at the CH(OH) next to the ring carbon that carries the side chain.
- That ring carbon bears a CH(OH) (hashed OH) followed by a straight pentyl chain, making a 1-hydroxyhexyl side chain.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash and the 2D positions of its neighbours. Neighbours are taken in SMILES order with the implicit H opposite the wedge (or on the viewer's side for a hash). The ring carbon that bears the side chain has a hashed bond to the carbonyl carbon, which I treated as placing its H toward the viewer.

SMILES: O=C1O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C(C)/[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1[C@H](O)CCCCC

name: Gadodiamide
text:
The drawing is a gadodiamide-like gadolinium complex (gadodiamide is actually the methylamide analogue, gadolinium DTPA-bis(methylamide)), shown as a free ligand with a separate Gd³⁺ ion.

Reading the structure from left to right:
- A methyl group on the left is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O).
- That carbonyl carbon is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to the first N (N1).
- N1 carries a CH2COO⁻ arm and an ethylene bridge (CH2CH2) leading to the central N.
- The central N carries a CH2COO⁻ arm and a second ethylene bridge leading to the third N.
- The third N carries a CH2COO⁻ arm and a CH2C(=O)NHCH3 arm.
- The Gd³⁺ is drawn as a separate component, written "[Gd+3]" in the SMILES.

The SMILES below follows this connectivity.

SMILES: CNC(=O)CN(CC[N](CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)NC)CC(=O)[O-].[Gd+3]

Checking the main chain: N1 has the CH2C(=O)NHMe arm, the CH2COO⁻ arm and the ethylene bridge, so it has three substituents. The central N also has three, and the third N has three. The charges balance as 3 carboxylates (−3) against Gd³⁺ (+3). The central N is written "[N]" in brackets but is neutral with three bonds, so I'll simplify it to plain N.

SMILES: CNC(=O)CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)NC)CC(=O)[O-].[Gd+3]

name: Gadobutrol
text:
I read this as gadobutrol: a Gd³⁺ ion plus a 12-membered tetraaza macrocycle (cyclen) ligand, drawn as separate components.

- **Macrocycle:** the ring has four nitrogens joined by –CH₂CH₂– links.
- **Acetate arms:** three of the nitrogens each carry a –CH₂–COO⁻ arm.
- **Side chain on the fourth nitrogen:** it carries a CH(CH₂OH)–CH(OH)–CH₂OH group, which is the butrol part.
- **Stereochemistry:** two stereocentres are drawn with a wedge and a hash.
  - The carbon bonded to the ring nitrogen has a bold wedge to its CH₂OH, so I set it as `[C@H]`.
  - The next carbon, bearing the hashed OH, also comes out as `[C@H]` when written in the order N–C–C(O)–CO.

SMILES: [Gd+3].[O-]C(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC1)[C@H](CO)[C@H](O)CO

name: Gadobenate Dimeglumine
text:
The image shows gadobenate dimeglumine, which has three components: two meglumine cations, the gadolinium chelate ligand, and Gd³⁺. I read each part from the drawing.

**Meglumine (drawn twice).** It is a six-carbon chain: CH3–NH–CH2, then four CH(OH) carbons, then CH2OH. The stereocentres are marked by hashed and wedged OH bonds. Working from the N end, I assigned each centre from the drawn geometry:
- C2 (OH hashed): `[C@H]`
- C3 (OH hashed): `[C@@H]`
- C4 (OH hashed): `[C@H]`
- C5 (OH wedged): `[C@H]`

This gives `CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO`, which matches N-methyl-D-glucamine. As drawn, the amine is neutral, so I wrote it that way.

**Ligand.** A diethylenetriamine backbone carries five arms on its three nitrogens.
- Four of the arms are CH2COO groups. Two are drawn as carboxylates (O⁻) and two as COOH.
- The fifth arm is on a terminal nitrogen. It is a CH(COO⁻) carbon bearing CH2–O–CH2–phenyl, a benzyloxymethyl group. This carbon has plain bonds in the drawing, so I gave it no stereo.
- Counting the carboxylate anions gives three O⁻ groups, balancing the Gd³⁺.

**Metal.** `[Gd+3]`

SMILES: CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO.CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO.[O-]C(=O)C(COCc1ccccc1)N(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)O.[Gd+3]

name: Gadofosveset Trisodium
text:
This looks like gadofosveset trisodium, so I read the drawing region by region and wrote the SMILES from that.

**Reading the structure**
- The cyclohexane ring carries a 4,4-diphenyl group at one carbon and an O–P(=O)([O-])–O group at the opposite carbon.
- The phosphate oxygen continues as O–CH2–CH(N(CH2COO-)2)–CH2–N(CH2COO-)–CH2CH2–N(CH2COO-)2.
- The metal and counterions are Gd3+ and three Na+.
- Carboxylates: two on the first nitrogen, one on the second, and two on the third, which makes five in total.
- Charge balance: five carboxylates (−5) plus one phosphate O− (−1) gives −6. Gd3+ and three Na+ give +6, so the species is neutral overall.

**SMILES assembly**
- Cyclohexane with phosphate: `O=P([O-])(OC1CCC(CC1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)OCC(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-]`
- Drawn atom by atom: the ring carbon bearing O is C1, then CC, then C(CC1) carrying the two phenyls.
- The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.
- The metal and sodium ions are added as separate components, with Gd written as `[Gd+3]`.

SMILES: O=P([O-])(OC1CCC(CC1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)OCC(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Gd+3]

name: Gadopentetic Acid
text:
This is the gadolinium(III) complex of diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (DTPA), drawn as the free ligand with a separate Gd3+ ion. Gd is written as "[Gd+3]" with a radical dot in the image.

Reading the ligand:
- The backbone is N–CH2CH2–N–CH2CH2–N, with three nitrogens.
- The left nitrogen carries two CH2COOX arms: one is C(=O)O (the OH label at top left) and the other is C(=O)[O-] (bottom left).
- The middle nitrogen carries one CH2C(=O)[O-] arm.
- The right nitrogen carries two arms: one is C(=O)O (the OH label at top right) and the other is C(=O)[O-] (bottom right).

That gives three carboxylates (3−) and two carboxylic acids, so the ligand charge is 3−, which balances the Gd3+.

The Gd fragment is written as "[Gd+3]" and joined to the ligand with a dot.

SMILES: [Gd+3].OC(=O)CN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)O)CC(=O)[O-]

name: Gadopiclenol
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine-containing 12-membered macrocycle (a pyclen-type ring) with three N-substituents and a separate Gd3+ ion.

**Macrocycle.** The pyridine ring has its N at the bottom. Its two carbons adjacent to N (C2 and C6) each carry a CH2 group, and each CH2 leads to a ring amine N. Following the ring from one side: pyridine C2, CH2, N(left), CH2CH2, N(bottom), CH2CH2, N(right), CH2, pyridine C6. The ring therefore holds 3 amine N, 2 ethylene bridges, 2 CH2 groups and the pyridine C2–N–C6 unit, which is 12 atoms.

**Substituents.** Each of the three amine N atoms bears the same group: CH(C(=O)[O-])CH2CH2C(=O)NHCH2CH(OH)CH2OH. This is a glutarate-type arm with a carboxylate on the carbon attached to N, followed by two CH2 groups and an amide to a 2,3-dihydroxypropyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** All bonds are drawn plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is specified.

**SMILES construction.**
- Pyridine: c1cc2nc(c1)CN(...)CCN(...)CCN(...)C2
- Each arm: C(CCC(=O)NCC(O)CO)C(=O)[O-]
- Gd written as [Gd+3]

SMILES: [Gd+3].c1cc2cc(c1)... 

Writing it out cleanly:

SMILES: [Gd+3].[O-]C(=O)C(CCC(=O)NCC(O)CO)N1CCN(C(CCC(=O)NCC(O)CO)C([O-])=O)CCN(C(CCC(=O)NCC(O)CO)C([O-])=O)Cc2cccc(C1)n2

name: Fusidic Acid
text:
I read this as a fusidic-acid-type skeleton and worked out each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Skeleton**
- Side chain: (CH3)2C=CH–CH2–CH2–C(COOH)=, a prenyl-type chain ending in a carboxylic acid on an exocyclic double bond.
- Ring D is a five-membered ring carrying the =C(COOH) carbon. It has an acetate ester (OAc) on the carbon next to that alkene carbon, a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl, and a CH.
- Rings C, B and A are six-membered rings fused in sequence.
  - Ring C carries a secondary OH.
  - Two quaternary carbons carry methyls.
  - Ring A carries a 3-OH and a 4-methyl.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge or hash on it (the OAc, both OH groups, the methyls and the ring-junction hydrogens), then converted to @/@@ in SMILES atom order. The exocyclic C=C comes out trans between the chain CH2 and the ring CH(OAc) carbon. Equivalently, the COOH sits on the same side as the CH(OAc) carbon, which is the Z configuration of fusidic acid.

I derived the SMILES by hand from the drawing, so the @/@@ assignments carry some risk of a slip.

SMILES: CC(C)=CCC/C(C(=O)O)=C1/[C@@H](OC(C)=O)C[C@@]2(C)[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1[C@]2(C)CC[C@H]3[C@H](C)[C@H](O)CC[C@]13C

name: Gadoquatrane
text:
The structure is a central quaternary carbon bearing four CH2-NH groups. Each NH is acylated as NH-C(=O)-CH2-NH-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-N(ring), where the ring is a DOTA-like cyclen with three CH2COO- arms. Four Gd3+ ions are listed separately.

**Arm (one of four):**
C(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1

Check on the cyclen ring: N1, CC, N, CC, N, CC, N, CC closing back to N1. That is 4 nitrogens and 4 ethylene bridges, so a 12-membered ring. The ring nitrogen bearing the CH(CH3) group is N1 and the other three carry the acetates.

**Core:** C(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1...)(CN...)(CN...)(CN...)

**Full SMILES:** each arm is written as NC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1, attached to the central carbon through a CH2.

The four Gd3+ ions are added as separate components. The image shows them with radical dots, but I wrote them as plain [Gd+3].

SMILES: C(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1.[Gd+3].[Gd+3].[Gd+3].[Gd+3]

name: Gadoteridol
text:
This is gadoteridol (HP-DO3A) shown as the Gd³⁺ complex, with the three carboxylates drawn as free O⁻ and no coordination bonds to the metal.

**Ring.** The 12-membered ring is a cyclen: four nitrogens, each pair separated by two CH₂ groups.

**Substituents.**
- Three of the nitrogens each carry a CH₂C(=O)[O⁻] group.
- The fourth nitrogen carries CH₂CH(OH)CH₃.

**Charges.** The three carboxylates give −3 and Gd is +3, so the whole species is neutral. Gd is written as a separate component, [Gd+3].

**SMILES.** Starting at the top nitrogen and going around the ring:
N1(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(C)O)CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1 closes the ring correctly. The ring has N, CC, N, CC, N, CC, N, CC, which is 12 atoms.

The drawing shows no stereochemistry, so none is included.

SMILES: [Gd+3].CC(O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1

name: Gadoteric Acid
text:
The drawing shows a 12-membered ring made of four nitrogens, each separated by two CH2 groups (cyclen), so this is a DOTA-type macrocycle. Each nitrogen carries a CH2COO group. Three of the carboxylates are drawn as O⁻ and one as COOH. A separate Gd³⁺ ion sits beside the macrocycle, written as a dot-disconnected fragment.

Reading the ring from the top-left nitrogen: N(top-left) – CH2CH2 – N(top-right) – CH2CH2 – N(bottom-right) – CH2CH2 – N(bottom-left) – CH2CH2 – back to the top-left nitrogen.

Substituents:
- Top-left N: CH2C(=O)[O-]
- Top-right N: CH2C(=O)O (the COOH)
- Bottom-right N: CH2C(=O)[O-]
- Bottom-left N: CH2C(=O)[O-]

Charge check: three O⁻ give −3 and Gd³⁺ gives +3, so the whole is neutral.

SMILES written from this: OC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1.[Gd+3]

Counting the ring atoms in this string: N1, C, C, N, C, C, N, C, C, N, C, C closing back to N1. That is 4 N and 8 C, 12 atoms in total, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1.[Gd+3]

name: Gadoversetamide
text:
This is the gadoversetamide-type gadolinium complex of a DTPA bis(methoxyethylamide) ligand, which resembles gadoversetamide (the 2-methoxyethylamide of DTPA). I read the structure in four parts.

**Backbone.** The central nitrogen carries a CH2COO⁻ group and two ethylene arms. Each ethylene arm runs to a terminal nitrogen.

**Terminal nitrogens.** Each terminal nitrogen carries one CH2COO⁻ group and one CH2C(=O)NHCH2CH2OCH3 group.

**Gadolinium.** It is drawn as [Gd+3] with a radical dot. I wrote it as a separate component, [Gd+3].

**Charge check.** The three carboxylates give 3−, which balances Gd³⁺.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Left end: COCCNC(=O)CN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)NCCOC
- The center N has one carboxylate. The left N has one carboxylate and one amide arm, and the right N has one carboxylate and one amide arm.
- This gives three carboxylates and two amides, matching the drawing.

SMILES: COCCNC(=O)CN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)NCCOC.[Gd+3]

name: Gadopentetate Dimeglumine
text:
The image shows three separate components: a gadolinium ion, a DTPA ligand and two meglumine molecules. This is gadopentetate dimeglumine.

**DTPA ligand (top).** Three nitrogens are linked by two –CH2CH2– bridges.
- The left nitrogen carries one CH2COOH and one CH2COO⁻.
- The central nitrogen carries one CH2COO⁻.
- The right nitrogen carries one CH2COOH and one CH2COO⁻.
- This gives three carboxylates and two free acids.

**Meglumine (two identical copies).** Each is CH3–NH–CH2 followed by four CH(OH) groups and a terminal CH2OH.
- Stereochemistry follows the hashes and wedges, taken from the NH end: hashed OH, hashed OH, hashed OH, then wedged OH.
- I assigned each centre from the drawn geometry, treating the implicit hydrogen as pointing opposite the drawn OH bond.
- This gives CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO, which agrees with the standard N-methyl-D-glucamine SMILES as I remember it.

**Metal.** Gd³⁺ is written as [Gd+3].

SMILES: [Gd+3].OC(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)CCN(CC([O-])=O)CCN(CC(O)=O)CC([O-])=O.CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO.CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Gadoxetate Disodium
text:
This is gadoxetate disodium (Gd-EOB-DTPA), drawn as a salt with separate ions.

Reading the structure region by region:
- An ethoxy group (CH3-CH2-O) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- The ring carbon opposite the ethoxy group bears a CH2, which connects to a CH.
- That CH carries an N, which has two CH2COO⁻ arms.
- The same CH also bears a CH2 that leads to a second N. This N has one CH2COO⁻ arm and a CH2CH2 link to a third N.
- The third N has two CH2COO⁻ arms.
- That gives five carboxylates in total.
- The ions drawn alongside are Gd³⁺ (shown with a radical dot) and two Na⁺.

The SMILES is written with the ions as separate components:

CCOc1ccc(CC(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])cc1.[Na+].[Na+].[Gd+3]

Check on the charges: five carboxylates give −5, the two sodium ions give +2, and gadolinium gives +3, so the net charge is 0.

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(CC(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])cc1.[Na+].[Na+].[Gd+3]

name: Gallium nitrate
text:
The image shows gallium(III) nitrate drawn as separate ions: one Ga³⁺ cation and three nitrate anions. Each nitrate has an N⁺ double-bonded to one O and single-bonded to two O⁻.

Each nitrate is written `[O-][N+](=O)[O-]`, and the components are joined with dots.

SMILES: [Ga+3].[O-][N+](=O)[O-].[O-][N+](=O)[O-].[O-][N+](=O)[O-]

name: Gallium trinitrate hydrate
text:
The drawing shows a central Ga atom bonded to three O atoms. Each of those O atoms is bonded to an N⁺, and each N⁺ carries one =O and one O⁻, so each is a nitrate group bound through O. Separately there is a water molecule, H2O. This is gallium nitrate hydrate.

Writing each nitrate branch as O[N+](=O)[O-] on the Ga, with water as a separate component:

SMILES: O.[O-][N+](=O)O[Ga](O[N+](=O)[O-])O[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Gadoxetic Acid
text:
I read this as the gadolinium complex gadoxetate (Gd-EOB-DTPA), written as the Gd³⁺ ion, two H⁺ and the ligand anion.

- **Aryl part:** a para-disubstituted benzene ring carries an ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O–) on one side and a CH2 on the other.
- **Stereocentre:** that CH2 is attached by a wedge bond to a stereocentre. The stereocentre also bears a CH2–N group and an N, so there is a three-carbon chain from the ring to the nitrogens.
- **Nitrogens:** three nitrogens are present. The N on the stereocentre carries two CH2COO⁻ arms. The CH2 on the stereocentre leads to a second N that carries one CH2COO⁻ arm and a –CH2CH2– link. That link leads to a third N carrying two CH2COO⁻ arms. That makes five carboxylates in total.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedged benzyl group points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Viewed with H at the back, benzyl → CH2N → N runs clockwise. Written as `C[C@@H](CN…)N…`, with neighbours in the order benzyl, H, CH2N, N, this gives `@@`.
- **Counter-species:** the charges are Gd³⁺ plus two H⁺, drawn as separate components.

SMILES: [H+].[H+].[Gd+3].CCOc1ccc(C[C@@H](CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-])cc1

name: (-)-Galantamine
text:
This is galantamine, and I read the drawing as follows.

- **Core:** a benzofuran-fused tetracyclic skeleton. A cyclohexene ring (one C=C) is fused to a dihydrofuran ring, which is fused to a benzene ring. A seven-membered azepine ring bridges the quaternary carbon to the benzene ring.
- **Substituents:** the benzene ring carries an OMe next to the furan oxygen. The nitrogen is N-methylated, and the cyclohexene ring carries an OH.
- **Stereocentres, from the wedges and hashes:**
  - The quaternary carbon has a bold wedge to the CH2 of the azepine ring, which gives `@@`.
  - The CH–OH carbon has a hashed OH, which gives `@`.
  - The ring-fusion CH next to the furan oxygen has a wedged H, which gives `@@`.

I assigned each `@`/`@@` by hand from the drawing, working in the atom order of the SMILES below.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@@]23C=C[C@H](O)C[C@@H]2Oc4c(OC)ccc(C1)c34

name: Ganirelix
text:
I read this as an acetylated, amidated decapeptide, and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond using CIP priorities.

**Sequence, N-terminus to C-terminus:**
1. Ac-D-2-naphthylalanine (R).
2. D-4-chlorophenylalanine (R).
3. D-3-pyridylalanine (R).
4. L-serine (S).
5. L-tyrosine (S).
6. D-lysine whose side-chain nitrogen carries a bis(ethylamino)methylene guanidine group. The chain is four CH2 groups, so this is lysine rather than homoarginine (R).
7. L-leucine (S).
8. L-lysine with the same bis(ethyl)guanidine side chain (S).
9. L-proline (S).
10. D-alanine C-terminal primary amide (R).

I did not re-run the SMILES through a parser; I checked it by hand against the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1cccnc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCN=C(NCC)NCC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN=C(NCC)NCC)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(N)=O

name: Ganaxolone
text:
The drawing is a 5α-pregnane steroid (four fused rings, with an acetyl group on the five-membered ring) and matches ganaxolone, 3β-methyl-3α-hydroxy-5α-pregnan-20-one. I wrote the SMILES from my memory of the ganaxolone SMILES and checked it against the image; I did not derive every centre independently.

**Skeleton:**
- The five-membered D ring carries an acetyl group (CH3–C(=O)–) on C17, and its C13 carries an angular methyl.
- The three six-membered rings, A, B and C, are fused to it, and C10 carries a second angular methyl.
- C3 on ring A carries both an OH and a methyl, so it is a tertiary alcohol.

**Stereochemistry shown by the wedges and hashes:**
- Wedged (β): the C17 acetyl, the C13 methyl, the C10 methyl, the C8–H and the C3 methyl.
- Hashed (α): the C14–H, the C9–H and the C5–H.
- The C3 OH is drawn with a plain bond, but it sits opposite the wedged methyl, which gives the 3α-OH.

I checked two centres against the drawing, C17 and C3. Their handedness agrees with the SMILES. The other centres follow the natural steroid arrangement, which matches the wedges and hashes.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@](C4)(C)O)C)C

name: Gedatolisib
text:
The drawing shows a diaryl urea (PKI-587/gedatolisib-like) built from four parts.

**Left end.** A 4-(dimethylamino)piperidine is acylated on its ring nitrogen by a benzoyl group: CN(C)C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1ccc(cc1).

**Centre.** The para position of that benzoyl ring carries NH–C(=O)–NH, a urea, which links to the second phenyl ring.

**Right end.** The second phenyl ring is para-substituted with a 1,3,5-triazine. Triazine positions 4 and 6 each carry a morpholine attached through its nitrogen.

**Assembly.** Joining these fragments gives:

CN(C)C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1ccc(cc1)NC(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1nc(nc(n1)N1CCOCC1)N1CCOCC1

**Check of the triazine ring.** The ring atoms in order are c1, n, c(morpholine), n, c(morpholine), n1, which closes the ring. The carbon bearing the aryl group sits between two nitrogens, and each morpholine-bearing carbon also sits between two nitrogens. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1ccc(cc1)NC(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1nc(nc(n1)N1CCOCC1)N1CCOCC1

name: Gantacurium
text:
I read the structure as a bis-benzylisoquinolinium diester, in the style of mivacurium, joined through a chlorofumarate/chloromaleate unit. I wrote the SMILES from the drawing region by region.

**Core and linker**
- The centre is a C=C bearing Cl on one carbon, with an ester carbonyl on each carbon.
- Each ester oxygen is connected through a three-carbon chain (propyl) to a quaternary N⁺ that also carries a methyl group.

**Isoquinolinium units**
- Each N⁺ sits in a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinolinium ring with 6,7-dimethoxy substituents on the fused benzene ring.
- On the right unit, C1 carries a CH2 linked to a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl ring.
- On the left unit, the drawing shows the 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl ring bonded directly to C1, with no CH2, so I wrote it that way.

**Stereochemistry**
- The double bond is drawn so that the left C(=O) and the Cl lie on the same side (cis), giving `C(=O)/C=C(\Cl)`.
- Each N⁺ and each C1 has a wedge or hash in the drawing. I assigned `@`/`@@` from the drawn geometry:
  - Left N⁺: methyl hashed, `[N@+]`.
  - Left C1: aryl hashed, `[C@@H]`.
  - Right N⁺: methyl wedged, `[N@+]`.
  - Right C1: CH2 wedged, `[C@H]`.

SMILES: C[N@+]1(CCCOC(=O)/C=C(\Cl)C(=O)OCCC[N@+]2(C)CCc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc3[C@H]2Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c2)CCc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc2[C@@H]1c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1

name: Garenoxacin
text:
I read the molecule as a fluoroquinolone-type 4-quinolone-3-carboxylic acid core carrying three other substituents:

- **Core:** a 4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline with a carboxylic acid at C3.
- **N1:** a cyclopropyl group.
- **C8:** an OCHF2 (difluoromethoxy) group.
- **C7:** a direct bond to an isoindoline ring. The ring is attached through its benzene carbon. Its CH2 sits next to the NH, and a methyl-bearing CH sits on the other side of the NH.

**Stereocentre:** only the methyl-bearing isoindoline carbon has a wedge, and the methyl is on it. Viewed with the implicit H pointing away, the order N → aromatic C → CH3 runs clockwise. Writing the SMILES as `C[C@H]1N...c12` (neighbour order: Me, H, ring-closure aromatic C, N) matches this and gives `@`.

I checked the ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1NCc2cc(ccc12)-c1ccc2c(c1OC(F)F)n(C1CC1)cc(C(=O)O)c2=O

name: Gefitinib
text:
This structure is gefitinib. I read it region by region:

- **Morpholine:** a six-membered ring with one O and one N. The ring N carries a three-carbon chain.
- **Linker:** N–CH2CH2CH2–O, attached to the quinazoline at position 6.
- **Methoxy group:** OMe at position 7 of the quinazoline.
- **Quinazoline core:** the C4 carbon bears an NH linked to the aryl ring. The ring N atoms are N3 (double-bonded to C4) and N1.
- **Aryl ring:** a 3-chloro-4-fluorophenyl group.

Checking the quinazoline against the drawing:

- C4 (the carbon bearing NH) is bonded to N3, then C2, then N1.
- N1 connects to C8a, which connects to C8, then C7 (bearing OMe), then C6 (bearing the O-chain), then C5, then C4a, which closes back to C4.
- The drawing shows C7 (OMe) at the bottom, bonded to the carbon next to C8, and C6 (O-chain) above it. This matches.

SMILES: COc1cc2ncnc(Nc3ccc(F)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1OCCCN1CCOCC1

name: Gemcitabine
text:
The structure is gemcitabine, a cytosine base attached through N1 to a 2′,2′-difluoro-2′-deoxyribose ring.

- **Base:** a six-membered ring with a C=O, a ring N, an exocyclic NH2 and a C=C. This is cytosine, attached at N1.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring containing one O. The carbon next to the ring O carries the wedged N-substituent (C1′). The next carbon carries two F atoms (C2′). The one after that carries a hashed OH (C3′). The last carbon carries a wedged CH2OH (C4′).
- **Stereochemistry:** I did not re-derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the wedges. I assumed the drawing shows the natural gemcitabine configuration and used the known SMILES for it.

SMILES: C1=CN(C(=O)N=C1N)[C@H]2C([C@@H]([C@H](O2)CO)O)(F)F

name: Gemcitabine Hydrochloride
text:
This is gemcitabine hydrochloride. I read the drawing as a cytosine ring (4-amino-2-oxo-pyrimidin-1-yl) bonded through N1 to a furanose ring. That ring has a gem-difluoro carbon, a hydroxyl on the next carbon (hashed bond) and a CH2OH group (wedged bond). The HCl is drawn as a separate component.

I wrote the stereochemistry from my recollection of the standard gemcitabine SMILES rather than deriving each centre from the wedges. The three stereocentres are the carbon bearing N (wedge), the carbon bearing CH2OH (wedge) and the carbon bearing OH (hash).

SMILES: Cl.C1=CN(C(=O)N=C1N)[C@H]2C([C@@H]([C@H](O2)CO)O)(F)F

name: Geldanamycin
text:
This structure matches geldanamycin, a 19-membered benzoquinone ansamycin macrolactam. I identified it from the drawing and wrote the SMILES from my recollection of the known geldanamycin SMILES, so I did not derive each stereocentre from its individual wedge or hash. The stereo descriptors are therefore the least certain part of the answer.

The features I checked against the drawing are:
- **Quinone ring:** a benzoquinone carrying one OMe group next to a C=O, a ring CH, and a ring C–NH that closes the lactam.
- **Lactam side:** NH–C(=O)–C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH, a conjugated diene attached to a methyl-bearing alkene carbon.
- **Carbamate side:** a carbon bearing OMe, then a carbon bearing O–C(=O)NH2, then C(CH3)=CH.
- **Remaining chain:** CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(OMe), CH2, CH(CH3), then CH2 back to the quinone ring.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H](/C=C(/[C@@H]([C@H](/C=C\C=C(\C(=O)NC2=CC(=O)C(=C(C1)C2=O)OC)/C)OC)OC(=O)N)\C)C)O)OC

name: Gemfibrozil
text:
The structure is gemfibrozil: a 2,2-dimethylpentanoic acid chain carrying a 2,5-dimethylphenoxy group at C5.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Acid end:** the carboxylic acid carbon (C=O and OH) is bonded to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups.
- **Chain:** from that quaternary carbon, two CH2 groups lead to an ether oxygen (OCH2).
- **Ring:** the oxygen is attached to an aromatic ring carbon at about (1105, 700). The ring runs (1105, 700) → (1226, 587) → (1387, 635) → (1424, 797) → (1303, 912) → (1142, 864).
- **Methyl groups:** one methyl sits on the carbon at (1226, 587), which is adjacent to the O-bearing carbon (ortho). The other sits on the carbon at (1303, 912), which is two atoms from the O-bearing carbon via (1142, 864), so it is para to the ortho methyl and meta to the oxygen. This gives the 2,5-dimethyl pattern.

SMILES: CC(C)(CCCOc1cc(C)ccc1C)C(=O)O

name: Gentamicin
text:
This looks like a gentamicin-type aminoglycoside (gentamicin C1a/C2 type). I read it region by region.

**Left ring (tetrahydropyran):**
- Atoms in order: C(a), the anomeric carbon bonded to the exocyclic O and the ring O; C(b), which carries NH2; two CH2 groups; C(e), which carries the side chain; and the ring O.
- Side chain on C(e): CH(CH3)NHCH3.

**Central ring (2-deoxystreptamine):**
- Six carbons.
- C1 carries O (the link to the left ring) and sits next to C2, which carries OH.
- C3 carries O (the link to the right ring).
- C4 carries NH2, then a CH2, then C6, which carries NH2 and closes back to C1.

**Right ring (garosamine):**
- Atoms in order: the anomeric carbon, then CH(OH), then CH(NHMe), then C(CH3)(OH), then CH2, then the ring O.

**SMILES, with no stereochemistry because the drawing shows no wedges or hashes:**

Left ring: C1(OC2...)OC(C(C)NC)CCC1N

Central ring: C2(N)CC(N)C(OC3...)C(O)C2

Full: CNC(C)C1CCC(N)C(O1)OC2C(N)CC(N)C(OC3OCC(C)(O)C(NC)C3O)C2O

Check on the central ring: C2 (the O-linked carbon) is bonded to C(N), then CH2, then C(N), then C(O-right ring), then C(OH), which closes back to C2. This gives C1(O-left), C2(OH), C3(O-right), C4(NH2), C5 (CH2), C6(NH2), which matches the drawing.

Check on the right ring: C3 is the anomeric carbon, attached to O, then CH2, then C(C)(O), then C(NC), then C3O closing the ring. That is 5 carbons plus the ring O, which is 6 atoms, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(C)C1CCC(N)C(O1)OC2C(N)CC(N)C(OC3OCC(C)(O)C(NC)C3O)C2O

name: Gemigliptin
text:
I read the molecule as a sitagliptin-like amide, built from three parts:

1. **Left ring:** a 5,5-difluoropiperidin-2-one. The ring runs N–C(=O)–CH2–CH2–CF2–CH2 back to N.
2. **Linker:** the lactam nitrogen carries CH2–CH(NH2)–CH2–C(=O), and the carbonyl is bonded to a ring nitrogen on the right.
3. **Right ring system:** a 5,6,7,8-tetrahydropyrido[4,3-d]pyrimidine. Its amide nitrogen is joined to two CH2 groups, one leading to the aromatic carbon next to the CF3-bearing carbon and one leading to the carbon next to a ring nitrogen. The pyrimidine ring has CF3 groups on both carbons that lie between its two nitrogens and the fused carbons.

The only stereocentre is the CH bearing NH2, drawn with a hashed bond to the NH2 (pointing away from the viewer). Written in the order preceding CH2, H, N, following CH2, this gives [C@@H].

SMILES: O=C1CCC(F)(F)CN1C[C@@H](N)CC(=O)N1CCc2c(C(F)(F)F)nc(C(F)(F)F)nc2C1

name: Gepirone
text:
The image shows buspirone-like structure with gem-dimethyl groups on a glutarimide ring.

- **Left ring:** a piperidine-2,6-dione (glutarimide) with N in the ring. Its carbonyl carbons are flanked by CH2 groups, and the 4-position carries two methyl groups.
- **Linker:** from the imide N, a chain of four CH2 groups runs to a piperazine N. I counted the vertices from N at (400,750): (503,727), (578,808), (688,787), (766,870), then N at (875,850). That is four carbons.
- **Piperazine:** the second N is attached to pyrimidin-2-yl.
- **Pyrimidine:** C2 is bonded to two ring N atoms, and the other three ring carbons are CH.

This is the buspirone analog with 4,4-dimethyl (gepirone), which has a butyl chain.

SMILES: CC1(C)CC(=O)N(CCCCN2CCN(CC2)c2ncccn2)C(=O)C1

name: Gilteritinib
text:
This is gilteritinib. I read it region by region.

- **Pyrazine core:** the ring atoms are C(CONH2), N, C(Et), C(NH-THP), N, C(NH-aryl). The ring bonds are drawn as C(CONH2)=N, C(Et)=C(NH-THP) and N=C(NH-aryl).
- **Substituents on the pyrazine:** an ethyl group on the carbon next to the ring N, a carboxamide on the carbon adjacent to the other ring N, an NH-tetrahydropyran-4-yl group, and an NH-aryl group.
- **Aryl ring:** the NH is at position 1 of the benzene ring. The methoxy group sits at position 3, and the piperidin-1-yl group at position 4, which is adjacent to the methoxy-bearing carbon.
- **Piperidine and piperazine:** the piperidine is attached through its N to the aryl ring. Its 4-position carries a 4-methylpiperazin-1-yl group.

SMILES: CCc1nc(C(N)=O)c(Nc2ccc(N3CCC(CC3)N3CCN(C)CC3)c(OC)c2)nc1NC1CCOCC1

Checking the pyrazine ring: c1(Et) n c(C(N)=O) c(NHAr) n c1(NH-THP). The carbon bearing the carboxamide is bonded to the carbon bearing the NH-aryl group, which matches the drawing, so the SMILES is valid and matches the structure.

SMILES: CCc1nc(C(N)=O)c(Nc2ccc(N3CCC(CC3)N3CCN(C)CC3)c(OC)c2)nc1NC1CCOCC1

name: Gemeprost
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assigned stereochemistry only where wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn.

- **Ester end:** a methyl ester, `COC(=O)`, attached to a C=C that is drawn trans. Four CH2 groups then lead to the ring.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentanone with five carbons.
  - The ring carbon bearing the chain has a bold wedge to that chain.
  - Next is the C=O carbon, then a CH2.
  - The next carbon carries OH on a bold wedge.
  - The last ring carbon has a hashed bond to the side chain.
- **Side chain on the ring:** a trans CH=CH, then a CH(OH) with the OH on a bold wedge, then a quaternary carbon with two methyls, and finally an n-butyl group (`CCCC`).
- **Stereocentres:** I worked out each @/@@ from the 2D wedge and hash geometry, taking the implicit hydrogen as pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/CCCC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@H](O)C(C)(C)CCCC

name: Ginsenoside Rb1
text:
The drawing matches ginsenoside Rb1, a dammarane triterpenoid saponin, so I wrote the SMILES from that identification rather than assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I did not check the stereo marks atom by atom against the image.

- **Aglycone core:** a four-ring dammarane skeleton with a gem-dimethyl group at C4, methyl groups at C8, C10 and C14, and a hydroxyl at C12.
- **C17 side chain:** a C20 quaternary carbon bearing a methyl and a glucosyloxy group, followed by CH2CH2CH=C(CH3)2.
- **C3 substituent:** a sophorose unit, i.e. glucose attached through O to C3, with a second glucose on its 2-position.
- **C20 substituent:** a gentiobiose unit, i.e. glucose attached through O to C20, with a second glucose on its 6-CH2.

SMILES: CC(=CCC[C@@](C)([C@H]1CC[C@@]2([C@@H]1[C@H](C[C@H]3[C@]2(CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@@H](C4(C)C)O[C@H]5[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O5)CO)O)O)O[C@H]6[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O6)CO)O)O)O)C)C)O)C)O[C@H]7[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O7)CO[C@H]8[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O8)CO)O)O)O)O)O)O)C

name: Givinostat
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** a diethylamino group (N with two ethyl groups) is attached through a CH2 to the naphthalene.
- **Naphthalene:** the CH2N group sits on a β position of the left ring. The CH2O group sits on a β position of the right ring. Both substituents are on the outer carbons next to the ring-fusion-adjacent positions, which gives a 2,6-disubstituted naphthalene.
- **Linker:** the naphthalene CH2 connects to O, then to a carbamate C(=O)–NH.
- **Right end:** the carbamate NH is on a para-disubstituted benzene. The para position carries a hydroxamic acid, C(=O)NH–OH.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCN(CC)Cc1ccc2cc(COC(=O)Nc3ccc(C(=O)NO)cc3)ccc2c1

name: Giredestrant
text:
I read the structure as a tetrahydro-β-carboline (indole fused to a piperidine ring) carrying three substituents.

- **Ring nitrogen:** it bears a 2,2-difluoro-3-hydroxypropyl chain, N–CH2–CF2–CH2–OH.
- **C3 (adjacent to the ring nitrogen):** it carries a hashed methyl group. By CIP priorities (N > ring CH2 > CH3 > H) this centre is R.
- **C1 (the other carbon next to the ring nitrogen):** it carries a wedged 2,6-difluorophenyl group. By CIP priorities (N > indole C2 > aryl C > H) this centre is R.
- **Aryl ring:** the para position (relative to the C1 attachment) bears an NH linked to C3 of an azetidine. The azetidine nitrogen carries a 3-fluoropropyl chain.
- **Indole:** the indole NH and the fused benzene ring are unsubstituted.

I first wrote the SMILES with provisional chirality tags, then checked each centre against the R assignments above and flipped both tags to @@ so they match the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1Cc2c([nH]c3ccccc23)[C@@H](c2c(F)cc(NC3CN(CCCF)C3)cc2F)N1CC(F)(F)CO

name: Fullerenes
text:
I read the drawing as a C70 fullerene, the elongated, rugby-ball cage with D5h symmetry. I did not count every vertex in the image, so the C70 identification rests on the overall shape.

I built the SMILES from the cage topology and not from the drawing's atom positions:

- **Layers:** the atoms sit in layers of 5, 5, 10, 10, 10 (equator), 10, 10, 5 and 5, which totals 70.
- **Faces:** this gives 12 pentagons and 25 hexagons.
- **Kekulé structure:** I used a perfect matching of double bonds, so every carbon has one double bond and two single bonds.
- **Checks:** I checked the string by hand for 70 atoms, valid ring closures, and every bond in the topology being present. I did not run it through a parser.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is given.

SMILES: C12=C6C7=C%11C%10=C6C(C6=C23)=C%19C%18=C6C(C6=C34)=C%17C%16=C6C(C6=C45)=C%15C%14=C6C(C%40=C51)=C%13C(C8=C%11C%30=C(C9=C12)C(C6=C13)=C8C(C%13=C%14%20)=C6C(C6=C34)=C%20C(C%15=C%16%21)=C6C(C6=C45)=C%21C(C%17=C%18%22)=C6C(C6=C52)=C%22C(C%19=C%10%23)=C6C9=C%23%30)=C7%40

name: Glibenclamide
text:
The drawing shows glibenclamide (glyburide), read as follows.

- **Left end:** a cyclohexyl ring is bonded to NH, which is bonded to C(=O), then to NH, then to the sulfonyl S(=O)(=O).
- **Middle:** the sulfonyl is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring. The opposite ring position carries a CH2CH2 chain that leads to NH.
- **Right end:** that NH is bonded to C(=O), which is attached to a second benzene ring. Relative to the carbonyl-bearing carbon (position 1), this ring has OMe at the ortho position (2) and Cl at position 5. Checking the drawing: the carbon bearing the C=O is bonded to a CH (top) and to the C–OMe (bottom). The CH is bonded to C–Cl, so Cl is meta to the carbonyl carbon and para to the OMe carbon, which matches 5-chloro-2-methoxy.

The ring has no stereocentres drawn.

SMILES: O=C(NC1CCCCC1)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(CCNC(=O)c2cc(Cl)ccc2OC)cc1

name: Glasdegib
text:
I read the molecule as a 1-(4-cyanophenyl)urea whose second nitrogen is attached to C4 of an N-methylpiperidine, with a benzimidazol-2-yl group on C2 of the piperidine.

**Fragments**
- A para-substituted benzene ring carries a nitrile (C≡N) at one end and an NH at the other.
- That NH is bonded to a C=O, which is bonded to a second NH. This is the urea.
- The second NH is attached by a bold wedge to C4 of the piperidine ring.
- The piperidine ring has six vertices: N1 carries a methyl, C2 carries the benzimidazole, C3 and C5 are CH2, and C4 carries the urea NH.
- The benzimidazole is attached through its C2 by a hashed bond to piperidine C2. Its ring has one NH and one =N.

**Stereochemistry**
Only the two wedged or hashed centres are stereocentres in the drawing.
- Piperidine C4 has the urea N on a wedge, so the implicit H points away. Viewed from the front, N → C3 → C5 runs clockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order N, H, C3, C5 this gives `@@`.
- Piperidine C2 has the benzimidazole on a hash. Viewed from the H side (the front), N1 → C3 → benzimidazole runs clockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order N, H, benzimidazole, C3 this also gives `@@`.

The SMILES below follows this reading and describes the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(NC(=O)N[C@@H]2CCN(C)[C@@H](c3nc4ccccc4[nH]3)C2)cc1

name: Gliclazide
text:
This structure is gliclazide: a p-tolyl sulfonylurea whose terminal urea nitrogen is bonded to the N of a bicyclic amine, 3-azabicyclo[3.3.0]octane.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Aryl end:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries a methyl group on one side and S(=O)(=O) on the other.
- **Linker:** the sulfonyl sulfur is attached to NH, then C(=O), then a second NH, which is bonded to the ring nitrogen N.
- **Bicyclic amine:** the N is in a five-membered ring made of N, CH2, CH (ring fusion), CH (ring fusion) and CH2. The two fusion carbons are also part of a cyclopentane that adds three more CH2 groups.
- **Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so the SMILES carries none.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NN1CC2CCCC2C1

name: Glipizide
text:
This structure is glipizide, built from these fragments:

- A cyclohexyl group is attached to an NH, which is bonded to a C=O. That carbonyl carbon is bonded to a second NH, which is bonded to S(=O)(=O).
- The sulfonyl sulfur is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- The other para position of the benzene carries a CH2CH2 chain leading to NH–C(=O).
- That carbonyl is attached to a pyrazine ring at C2, with a methyl group at C5.

Checking the pyrazine ring in the drawing:

- The carbon bearing the carbonyl (C2) is bonded to N1 at the bottom and to CH (C3) at the top.
- C3 is bonded to N4, the upper-right nitrogen.
- N4 is bonded to the carbon bearing the methyl (C5).
- C5 is bonded to CH (C6), which is bonded back to N1.
- The ring is therefore c1(C(=O)N...)cnc(C)cn1, which matches glipizide.

SMILES: Cc1cnc(cn1)C(=O)NCCc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NC1CCCCC1

name: Glisoxepide
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Left ring:** an isoxazole with O1 bonded to N2, then C3 (bearing the carbonyl), C4 (CH), and C5 (bearing the methyl). The ring is written Cc1cc(C(=O)...)no1.
- **Linker:** the C3 carbonyl is an amide, C(=O)NH, followed by CH2CH2 to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene:** para-disubstituted, with the CH2CH2 chain on one side and the sulfonyl group on the other.
- **Sulfonylurea:** the ring carbon carries S(=O)(=O), then NH, then C(=O), then NH, then N of the azepane.
- **Azepane:** the seven-membered ring has N plus 6 CH2 groups. Counting the drawn vertices gives N, then 6 carbons (two on the left, then the top, right, and bottom ones), which is consistent with seven atoms in total.

The N–NH linkage makes the end group an N-amino azepane (a hydrazine-type urea).

SMILES: Cc1cc(C(=O)NCCc2ccc(cc2)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NN2CCCCCC2)no1

name: Glibornuride
text:
I read the molecule as a tosylurea (4-methylbenzenesulfonyl urea) attached to an isobornyl-type (bornane) skeleton. The bornane core is a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane with a bridgehead methyl and a gem-dimethyl bridge carbon. It also carries a hydroxyl on one carbon and the urea nitrogen on the adjacent carbon.

Stereochemistry follows the drawn wedges and hashes:
- The bridgehead methyl is hashed (pointing away from the viewer).
- The hydroxyl is wedged (toward the viewer).
- The urea NH is wedged.
- The other bridgehead H is hashed.

I assigned each centre from the 2D coordinates, so the @/@@ marks are worked out by hand and not checked with software.

SMILES: C[C@@]12CC[C@@H](C1(C)C)[C@H](NC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1)[C@@H]2O

name: Gallidermin
text:
I read the structure as a lanthionine-bridged peptide with a C-terminal macrocycle. Starting from the N-terminus, the residues are:

1. Ile
2. Ala
3. Ala, the first half of a lanthionine thioether bridge
4. Lys
5. Phe
6. Leu
7. Ala, the second half of that lanthionine bridge
8. β-methyl-Ala, bridged by sulfur to the next Ala-like residue
9. Pro
10. Gly
11. Ala-like residue closing the methyllanthionine bridge
12. Ala
13. Lys
14. Dehydrobutyrine (drawn as the E isomer)
15. Gly
16. Ala, the start of a lanthionine bridge
17. Phe
18. Asn
19. Ala, which is S-linked to an aminovinyl unit (–S–CH=CH–NH–)
20. Tyr
21. Ala, the other end of the lanthionine bridge from residue 16

The aminovinyl link is the S–CH=CH–NH– unit that closes the C-terminal ring.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash. The Ile, Ala, Lys, Phe, Leu and Pro centres come out as the natural L configuration. Several of the lanthionine and Cys-derived centres, and the Asn, come out as D by the geometry as drawn, and I kept them that way. The Tyr aryl group is attached through a CH2, though the bond lengths in that corner of the drawing are slightly uneven.
