name: Glecaprevir
text:
I read the structure as glecaprevir-type: a macrocycle with a quinoxaline, a bridged proline unit, a tert-leucine, a cyclopentane-fused carbamate, a difluoromethylcyclopropane amino acid and a methylcyclopropyl sulfonamide. I wrote the SMILES region by region and checked each wedge/hash against the drawing.

- **Sulfonamide end:** a 1-methylcyclopropyl group on S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to NH, then C(=O), then the cyclopropane quaternary carbon.
- **Cyclopropane:** the quaternary carbon carries the NH (hashed) and the C(=O)NH-sulfonyl group. The adjacent ring carbon carries a CHF2 (wedge).
- **Pyrrolidine:** the ring is N, Cα, CH2, CH(O), CH2. Cα bears the hashed C(=O)NH, and the CH(O) has a hashed H.
- **Amide link:** the pyrrolidine N is acylated by tert-leucine, drawn with a wedged tBu. Its NH forms a carbamate with the cyclopentane oxygen.
- **Cyclopentane:** two adjacent CH carbons, one bearing the carbamate O and one bearing the ether O. Their H's are drawn hashed and wedged respectively.
- **Macrocycle chain:** the ether O is followed by CH2, then CH=CH, then CF2, then the quinoxaline C2. The quinoxaline C3 is bonded to the pyrrolidine O. The drawn chain has only one CH2 between O and the alkene, and the double bond geometry is trans (E).

I assigned @/@@ for each stereocentre by working out the geometry from the wedges and hashes.

SMILES: CC1(CC1)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)[C@]2(C[C@H]2C(F)F)NC(=O)[C@@H]3C[C@@H]4CN3C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)O[C@@H]5CCC[C@H]5OC/C=C/C(F)(F)c6nc7ccccc7nc6O4)C(C)(C)C

name: Glucose 6-phosphate
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose ring with a phosphate ester on the exocyclic CH2. The anomeric carbon (the ring carbon bearing OH next to the ring oxygen) is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo.

**Ring atoms, from the anomeric carbon:**
- C1 carries a plain OH and sits next to the ring oxygen.
- C2 carries an OH on a wedge.
- C3 carries an OH on a hash.
- C4 carries an OH on a wedge.
- C5 is bonded to the ring oxygen and carries a hashed CH2–O–P(=O)(OH)₂ group.

**Stereo assignment** (reading each centre from the wedges and hashes, with the implicit H on the opposite side):
- C5 is `[C@H]`.
- C4 is `[C@@H]`.
- C3 is `[C@H]`.
- C2 is `[C@H]` at the ring closure.

I checked that the SMILES has the six ring atoms (five C and one O), the CH2, and the phosphate with one P=O and two P–OH groups.

SMILES: OC1O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Glycerol
text:
The drawing shows a three-carbon chain with an OH group on each carbon. The left carbon carries HO, the middle carbon carries OH pointing up, and the right carbon carries OH. This is glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol).

The middle carbon has two identical CH2OH substituents, so it is not a stereocentre, and no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: OCC(O)CO

name: Glutaraldehyde
text:
The drawing is a zigzag chain with a C=O at each end. The chain has these atoms:

- O at the far left, double-bonded to the first carbon (about x=315).
- A second carbon (about x=532).
- A third carbon (about x=750).
- A fourth carbon (about x=967).
- A fifth carbon (about x=1185), double-bonded to the O at the far right.

That makes 5 carbons, with an aldehyde group at each end. The molecule is glutaraldehyde, pentanedial.

SMILES: O=CCCCC=O

name: Glycine
text:
The drawing shows H2N attached to a CH2 carbon, which is bonded to a carbon with a double bond to O and a single bond to OH. This is a carboxylic acid with an amino group on the adjacent carbon, which is glycine. No wedges, hashes or charges are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

SMILES: NCC(=O)O

name: Glycobiarsol
text:
The drawing has three separate components.

1. A bismuth cation, drawn as Bi³⁺ with a lone pair: `[Bi+3]`. The colon beside it suggests a lone pair, but I will write it without one.
2. An oxide anion: `[O-2]`.
3. An organic arsonic acid fragment:
   - A para-substituted benzene ring carries an arsenic group on one side. The arsenic is bonded to OH, to O⁻, and double-bonded to O, giving `[As](=O)(O)[O-]`.
   - On the opposite side of the ring, an NH links to a C(=O)CH2OH group, giving `NC(=O)CO`.

The arsenic fragment and ring are written `O[As](=O)([O-])c1ccc(NC(=O)CO)cc1`.

Joining the three components with dots gives the full SMILES.

SMILES: [Bi+3].[O-2].O[As](=O)([O-])c1ccc(NC(=O)CO)cc1

name: Glycolic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a three-carbon-free skeleton of two carbons: a CH2 carbon bearing an HO group, joined to a carbon that has a double bond to O and a single bond to OH. That is a carboxylic acid with a hydroxyl on the adjacent carbon, which is glycolic acid (hydroxyacetic acid). There are no wedges, hashes, charges or stereocentres to encode.

SMILES: OCC(=O)O

name: Glufosfamide
text:
I read this as glufosfamide, the β-D-glucopyranosyl ester of N,N'-bis(2-chloroethyl)phosphorodiamidic acid, and worked out the stereo marks from the drawn wedges and hashes.

**Structure read from the image**
- **Sugar ring:** a six-membered pyranose ring with five carbons and one ring oxygen. It carries a CH2OH group on C5 (wedge), OH groups on C4 (hash), C3 (wedge) and C2 (hash), and an exocyclic O on the anomeric carbon C1 (wedge).
- **Phosphorus group:** the anomeric O is bonded to a P(=O) centre that also bears two NH–CH2CH2Cl arms.

**Stereo assignment:** I derived each @/@@ by hand from the wedge/hash geometry around that carbon, writing the SMILES in the order CH2OH, C5, ring O, C1, C2, C3, C4. I did not check the result against a reference SMILES.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](OP(=O)(NCCCl)NCCCl)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Glycopyrronium
text:
The drawing shows glycopyrronium, which I read as follows.

- **Nitrogen:** a quaternary N⁺ carries two methyl groups and sits in a pyrrolidine ring.
- **Pyrrolidine ring:** N, CH2, CH (bearing the ester oxygen), CH2, CH2, closing back to N. That is five ring atoms.
- **Ester:** the ring CH carries O–C(=O), and the carbonyl carbon attaches to a quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries OH, a cyclopentyl group and a phenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are drawn plain, with no wedges or hashes, so I include none.

SMILES: C[N+]1(C)CCC(C1)OC(=O)C(O)(C1CCCC1)c1ccccc1

name: Glymidine
text:
The drawing shows a methoxyethoxy chain (CH3-O-CH2-CH2-O-) attached to a pyrimidine ring. The ring has two nitrogens flanking the carbon that carries the NH, and the carbon bearing the O-chain sits between two ring CH positions. That makes it a 5-substituted pyrimidin-2-yl. The ring NH connects to a sulfonyl group (S with two =O), which is bonded to a phenyl ring.

SMILES: COCCOc1cnc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccccc2)nc1

name: Glutathione
text:
This structure is glutathione (γ-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinylglycine).

**Chain, left to right:**
- A glycine unit: HOOC–CH2–NH, joined by an amide to the cysteine carbonyl.
- A cysteine unit: C(=O)–CH(CH2SH)–NH. The CH2SH is on a hashed bond.
- A γ-glutamyl unit, linked through its side-chain amide: NH–C(=O)–CH2–CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH. The NH2 is on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:**
- Glutamate α-carbon: the NH2 is wedged, with CH2 to the upper left, COOH to the upper right, and H implied behind. Written as N[C@@H](CCC…)C(=O)O, this gives the L configuration.
- Cysteine α-carbon: the CH2SH is hashed and H is implied toward the viewer. Written as N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)N…, this also matches the drawing.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)NCC(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Glyphosate
text:
The drawing shows glyphosate, read left to right:

- A phosphorus atom (P) carries one double-bonded oxygen (=O) and two hydroxyl groups (OH).
- P is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to an NH.
- The NH is bonded to a second CH2, which leads to a carboxylic acid group, C(=O)OH.

There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: O=P(O)(O)CNCC(=O)O

name: Gold Sodium Thiomalate
text:
The image shows a thiomalate dianion drawn with an S⁻ thiolate, plus three separate cations: Au⁺ and two Na⁺. This is the gold sodium thiomalate salt.

Reading the structure:
- The chain is a carboxylate carbon (O⁻ and =O) bonded to a CH bearing S⁻, then a CH2, then a second carboxylate carbon (=O and O⁻).
- The charges balance: the anion carries three negative charges (S⁻ and two O⁻), and the cations supply three positive charges (Au⁺ and two Na⁺).
- The drawing uses plain bonds at the CH, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: [Au+].[Na+].[Na+].[S-]C(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-]

name: Golvatinib
text:
Reading the structure region by region, from left to right:

- **Left end:** an N-methylpiperazine, written CN1CCN(CC1)…, whose second nitrogen is bonded to C4 of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** its ring nitrogen carries a carbonyl, giving a urea: N–C(=O)–NH–pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** the NH is attached at C2 of the pyridine. The ring nitrogen is next to C2, and the oxygen sits at C4.
  - Ring path: C2 (NH), N1, C6, C5, C4 (O), C3.
  - SMILES fragment: c1(NC(=O)…)cc(O…)ccn1.
- **Central benzene:** the pyridine O connects to this ring. Going around it: C1 (O), C2 (H), C3 (F), C4 (NH), C5, C6. The F is ortho to the NH, so the ring is c1(O…)ccc(NC(=O)…)c(F)c1.
- **Cyclopropane:** the NH is acylated by a cyclopropane-1,1-dicarboxamide, C(=O)C1(CC1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(F)cc1. The second amide nitrogen carries a 4-fluorophenyl group.

Assembled SMILES:

CN1CCN(CC1)C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)Nc1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)C3(CC3)C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)c(F)c2)ccn1

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C1CCN(CC1)C(=O)Nc1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)C3(CC3)C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)c(F)c2)ccn1

name: Gonadorelin
text:
I read this as the decapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑Gly‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑Gly‑NH2 (gonadorelin / LHRH).

- **N‑terminus:** a pyroglutamic acid ring (five‑membered lactam with a C=O).
- **Residues in order:** His (imidazole side chain), Trp (indole), Ser (CH2OH), Tyr (4‑hydroxyphenyl), Gly, Leu (isobutyl), Arg (guanidine chain), Pro (pyrrolidine ring).
- **C‑terminus:** Gly as the primary amide, NH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** I took every wedge/hash centre as the natural L‑configuration (Gly has no stereocentre). I checked that the chirality tags in the SMILES encode L at each residue.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(N)=N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Goserelin
text:
I read this as the decapeptide goserelin: pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Ser(tBu)‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NH‑NH‑C(=O)NH2.

- **Residue order:** pyroglutamic acid, histidine (imidazole), tryptophan (indole), serine (free CH2OH), tyrosine (4‑hydroxybenzyl), O‑tert‑butyl serine, leucine (isobutyl), arginine (guanidine side chain), then proline.
- **C‑terminus:** the proline carbonyl is joined to a semicarbazide group, C(=O)NHNHC(=O)NH2, in place of a free acid or simple amide.
- **Stereochemistry:** the Ser(OH) and Ser(tBu) residues are drawn with opposite wedge types, so Ser(tBu) is D and the free Ser is L. I took the remaining stereocentres from the known configuration of goserelin rather than assigning each wedge independently.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NNC(=O)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](COC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1

name: Glycyrrhizin
text:
I did not derive every stereocentre from the drawing. The structure is glycyrrhizic acid (glycyrrhizin): an 11-oxo-olean-12-ene-30-oic acid (glycyrrhetinic acid) core, a 3-O-linked diglucuronic acid chain, and three carboxylic acids in total.

I checked two quaternary centres directly against the wedges and hashes in the image: the ring-fusion carbon bearing the wedged methyl, and the carbon bearing the hashed methyl and the COOH. Both match the `@` designations in the SMILES below. The remaining centres (the other ring-fusion carbons, the 3-O carbon and the two glucuronic acid rings) come from my recollection of the natural compound's stereochemistry, and the image looks consistent with it.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@](C[C@H]1C3=CC(=O)[C@@H]4[C@]5(CC[C@@H](C([C@@H]5CC[C@]4([C@@]3(CC2)C)C)(C)C)O[C@@H]6[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O6)C(=O)O)O)O)O[C@H]7[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H](O7)C(=O)O)O)O)O)C)(C)C(=O)O

name: Ginkgolide B
text:
I read this as a ginkgolide-type cage: tert-butyl, three lactone C=O groups, three OH groups and a methyl. The connectivity below follows the drawing atom by atom, and the formula comes out as C20H24O10 (20 C, 10 O). The stereo marks come from the drawn wedges and hashes, taken from their narrow ends; I did not check them against a reference structure.

Connectivity as read:
- **Right lactone ring:** CH(CH3) – C(=O) – O – CH – C(OH), closed back to the CH(CH3).
- **Bottom-right lactone:** a quaternary C(ring junction) – C(=O) – O – CH, with the CH bonded to the central quaternary carbon.
- **Left lactone:** CH(OH) – C(=O) – O – acetal CH, with the acetal CH bonded to the central quaternary carbon.
- **Acetal CH:** it also carries a second O, which bridges to the quaternary C next to the CH(CH3) ring.
- **Five-membered carbocycle:** CH(tBu) – CH2 – CH(O) – quaternary C – quaternary C.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C(=O)O[C@@H]2[C@@]1(O)[C@@]36O[C@H]4[C@@]5([C@@H](O)C(=O)O4)[C@H](C(C)(C)C)C[C@@H](OC3=O)[C@]56[C@@H]2O

name: Gozetotide
text:
I read the structure from left to right and wrote each fragment as SMILES.

- **Left end:** a 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)propanoic acid ring carrying a CH2–N(CH2COOH) arm.
- **Linker:** that nitrogen connects through an ethylene bridge (N–CH2CH2–N) to a second N(CH2COOH)–CH2 group on a second hydroxyphenyl ring. This ring also carries a CH2CH2C(=O)NH side chain.
- **Spacer:** the amide NH leads into a five-CH2 chain ending in C(=O) (an aminohexanoyl unit), which is amide-linked to the lysine side-chain NH.
- **Lysine:** four CH2 groups lead to the α-carbon, which bears a COOH and the urea NH.
- **Urea and glutamate:** the urea C(=O) connects to the glutamate NH. Glutamate carries its α-COOH and a CH2CH2COOH side chain.

The chain length of the aminohexanoyl spacer is the least certain count; I estimated it from bond spacing in the drawing.

**Stereochemistry:** both stereocentres are drawn with wedge or hash bonds. I assigned both as S, which corresponds to L-lysine and L-glutamate. The lysine centre is `[C@@H]` and the glutamate centre is `[C@@H]` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCc1ccc(O)c(CN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)Cc2cc(CCC(=O)NCCCCCC(=O)NCCCC[C@@H](C(=O)O)NC(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)ccc2O)c1

name: Gramicidin A
text:
This is gramicidin A, read as a linear pentadecapeptide: an N-formyl group, 15 residues, and a C-terminal ethanolamide (–NH–CH2CH2–OH).

Reading the residues from the formyl end, the drawing shows:

1. Val
2. Gly
3. Ala
4. Leu
5. Ala
6. Val
7. Val
8. Val
9. Trp
10. Leu
11. Trp
12. Leu
13. Trp
14. Leu

name: Grapiprant
text:
I read the structure region by region, starting from the left.

**Tolyl sulfonyl end.** A para-methylphenyl ring is attached to S, which carries two =O groups. S is bonded to NH, which is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to another NH. This is a tosyl urea.

**Linker.** The second NH is bonded to a CH2CH2 chain, and the chain ends on a para-disubstituted benzene ring.

**Bicyclic heteroaromatic.** The benzene ring is bonded to N1 of the fused ring system, which is an imidazo[4,5-c]pyridine. I traced it as follows:
- N1 (attached to the phenyl) is bonded to C2, which carries an ethyl group.
- C2 is double-bonded to N3.
- N3 is bonded to C3a, which is bonded to C4. C4 carries a methyl and is double-bonded to N5.
- N5 is bonded to C6, which carries a methyl, and C6 is double-bonded to C7 (CH).
- C7 is bonded to C7a, which is bonded back to N1 and is double-bonded to C3a.

**SMILES.** The tolyl-sulfonyl-urea part is Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NCCc1ccc(cc1)–, and the bicyclic part is n1c(CC)nc2c(C)nc(C)cc12.

Ring closure check: in n1c(CC)nc2c(C)nc(C)cc21, the atom "c2" after N3 is C3a, and the final "c21" is C7a, which closes ring 2 to C3a and ring 1 to N1. This matches the drawing.

name: Guaifenesin

name: Granisetron hydrochloride
text:
This is granisetron hydrochloride: a 9-methyl-9-azabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane core carrying an amide NH at C3, linked to a 1-methylindazole-3-carbonyl group, with HCl as a separate component.

**Bicyclic amine.** The two bridgehead carbons are joined by the N-methyl nitrogen, a three-carbon bridge on the left, and a CH2–CH(NH)–CH2 bridge on the right. The upper bridgehead has a hashed H and the lower bridgehead has a wedged H, so only these two carbons carry stereo marks. The CH(NH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds and gets no stereo mark.

**Amide and indazole.** The NH is acylated by a C=O whose carbon sits on C3 of the indazole. The indazole N1 carries a methyl group and N2 is the other ring nitrogen, and the benzene ring is fused on the far side.

**Stereo assignment.** I wrote the SMILES with the N-bound bridgehead first and worked out each centre from the 2D geometry and the wedge or hash. Both centres come out as `@` in the string below.

name: Griseofulvin
text:
This structure is griseofulvin, a spiro benzofuranone–cyclohexenone with one Cl and three OMe groups. I read it as follows:

- **Left ring:** a cyclohexenone containing a C=O, a CH=C(OMe) unit, a CH2, and a CH bearing a methyl.
- **Spiro centre:** the carbon shared between the cyclohexenone and the benzofuran-3-one. It is bonded to the ring O and to the ketone C=O of the five-membered ring.
- **Aromatic ring:** it carries two OMe groups and one Cl.

Stereochemistry, assigned from the drawn wedge and hash:

- The spiro carbon has the ring O on a wedge. With priorities O > C(=O) > C(OMe)= > CH, this gives S.
- The methyl-bearing CH has a hashed methyl, which puts H toward the viewer. With priorities spiro C > CH2 > CH3 > H, this gives R.

This matches the known (2S,6'R) configuration of griseofulvin. I checked that the chirality tags in the SMILES below reproduce S at the spiro carbon and R at the CH(CH3).

name: Halobetasol Propionate
text:

The stereo SMILES below was written from my recollection of the known structure of this compound, not derived centre by centre from the image. I did not re-check every stereocentre, and the C6 fluorine descriptor is the least certain.

name: Gramicidin S
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic decapeptide of the gramicidin S type, cyclo(Val‑Orn‑Leu‑D‑Phe‑Pro)₂, with the two halves repeating.

**Sequence.** Walking clockwise from the top Val, each residue's C=O links to the next residue's NH. The order is Val → Orn → Leu → Phe → Pro → Val → Orn → Leu → Phe → Pro, and the last Pro C=O closes back onto the first Val NH.

**Stereochemistry.** For each α‑carbon I took the wedge or hash on the side chain (or on the H for Pro). I then compared the N → C(=O) → side‑chain turn direction with that of an L‑amino acid.
- Val, Orn, Leu (both copies) have wedged side chains in the same arrangement as L residues, so they are L.
- Both Pro residues show a hashed H in the L arrangement, so they are L.
- Both Phe residues have hashed benzyl bonds, which puts the H toward the viewer, so they are D.

For the SMILES, the L residues are written N[C@@H](R)C(=O), D‑Phe as N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O), and L‑Pro as N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O).

I checked that the ring-closure digits are consistent and that every NH and C=O matches the drawing.

name: (+-)-Halofantrine hydrochloride
text:
I read this as halofantrine hydrochloride: a phenanthrene core carrying the side chain, two chlorines and a CF3 group, drawn with an HCl counterion.

- **Side chain:** two n-butyl groups on a nitrogen, which is joined through a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) to a CH(OH) carbon. That carbon is attached to the middle ring of the aromatic system.
- **Aromatic core:** a phenanthrene made of three fused six-membered rings, with all bonds drawn aromatic.
- **Top ring substituents:** one Cl sits on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon, and the second Cl sits on the carbon one position further round (meta to the first).
- **Bottom ring substituent:** a CF3 group.
- **Counterion:** HCl, written as a separate component.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

I traced the atoms around the rings from the drawing. The chain-bearing carbon is followed by a CH, then the fusion carbon next to the C–Cl, the CH, the second C–Cl, a CH, and the second fusion carbon. The bottom ring then runs CH, C–CF3, CH, CH and back to the ring-closing fusion carbon. This matches the SMILES below.

name: Haloperidol
text:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with fluorine at the para position, attached to a ketone carbon (C=O).
- **Chain:** the ketone carbon is followed by three CH2 groups, the last bonded to the nitrogen. That gives a 4-carbon unit counting the C=O: C(=O)CCC–N.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring containing the nitrogen. The carbon opposite the nitrogen (position 4) carries both an OH and a 4-chlorophenyl ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with chlorine at the para position.

name: Haloprogin
text:

name: Harmine
text:
This is harmine, a β-carboline: a pyridine ring fused to a pyrrole ring, which is fused to a benzene ring.

**Pyridine ring.** The atoms run N (left), CH, CH, C (fused, top), C (fused, bottom, attached to the NH carbon), and the C bearing the methyl group. The methyl-bearing carbon is bonded to N through a double bond.

**Pyrrole ring.** The five-membered ring contains the NH, the fused carbon C9a (attached to the methyl-bearing pyridine carbon), the fused carbon at the top of the pyridine ring, and two fused carbons of the benzene ring.

**Benzene ring.** The atoms are the fused carbon at the top, then CH, CH, C(OMe), CH, and the fused carbon bonded to NH. The methoxy group sits on the carbon three positions from the fused carbon that bears the NH.

**SMILES construction.** Starting from the methyl group: Cc1nccc2c1[nH]c1cc(OC)ccc12

- `c1` is the methyl-bearing carbon, followed by `n`, `c`, `c`, and `c2` (the fused carbon).
- The next `c1` closes the pyridine ring; this is the carbon attached to the methyl-bearing carbon and to NH.
- `[nH]` is followed by `c1`, the benzene carbon bonded to N.
- Then `c` (CH), `c(OC)`, `c` and `c`, and finally `c12`, which closes both rings.

Checking the benzene ring: the NH-bearing carbon (c1), then CH, then C(OMe), then CH, CH, and the fused carbon (c12). That is six atoms. The fused carbon c12 bonds to c2, the top pyridine fused carbon, which closes the pyrrole ring. In the drawing, the carbon next to the NH-bearing carbon is a CH and the OMe carbon follows it, which matches the SMILES.

SMILES: Cc1nccc2c1[nH]c1cc(OC)ccc12

name: Grazoprevir
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below.

- **Left side chain:** a cyclopropyl sulfonamide (cyclopropyl–SO2–NH–C(=O)) is attached to a quaternary cyclopropane carbon. That cyclopropane carries a vinyl group and an NH–C(=O) link to the macrocycle.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring (N, CH bearing the amide carbonyl, CH2, CH–O, CH2) with the aryl ether oxygen on the ring CH.
- **Macrocycle:** the pyrrolidine N is acylated by a C(=O) on a tert-butyl-bearing CH. That CH continues through NH–C(=O)–O to a CH of a fused cyclopropane. The adjacent cyclopropane CH leads into a chain of five CH2 groups, which ends on the quinoxaline carbon. The neighbouring quinoxaline carbon carries the O that returns to the pyrrolidine.
- **Quinoxaline:** a fused benzo ring with an OMe group, positioned as drawn.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each wedged or hashed centre from the drawing: the vinylcyclopropane CH, the quaternary cyclopropane carbon, the pyrrolidine alpha-C and O-bearing CH, the tert-butyl CH, and the two fused-cyclopropane CH atoms.

name: HC-toxin
text:
I read this as a cyclic tetrapeptide: an epoxy-ketone amino acid (Aoe-type, with a five-CH2 chain ending in C(=O)-epoxide), proline, and two alanines, closed into a 12-membered ring.

Reading the drawing:
- **Epoxide:** a three-membered ring of one O and two carbons. Its CH carbon carries a hashed bond to the ketone C=O.
- **Chain:** the ketone carbon is followed by five CH2 groups. The last CH2 joins the ring α-carbon through a wedge bond.

name: Henagliflozin
text:
I read this as an ertugliflozin-type bicyclic ketal C-aryl glycoside carrying a fluorine on the ethoxyphenyl ring. Ertugliflozin itself has no fluorine there.

**Aromatic part**

- The bridging oxygen links to the quaternary carbon that carries CH2OH.
- That quaternary carbon is also bonded to the OCH2 carbon.
- Three CH(OH) carbons run from the quaternary carbon round to the anomeric carbon.

- Anomeric carbon (aryl on a wedge): @@
- Quaternary carbon (CH2OH on a wedge): @@
- CH(OH) next to the quaternary carbon (wedge): @@
- Middle CH(OH) (hash): @

text:

name: Heme b

name: Hesperidin

This structure is hesperidin, a flavanone 7-O-rutinoside, so I wrote its SMILES from the known compound. I did not independently re-derive each wedge and hash, so the stereo descriptors rest on that match rather than on a full check against the drawing.

text:

name: Hexaaminecobalt trichloride
text:
The image shows separate, disconnected species: three Cl⁻, one Co³⁺, and several NH3 groups.

The bottom-left label reads "H3NH3NH3NH3NH3N", which is a run of NH3 units drawn together. Reading it as H3N, NH3, NH3, NH3, NH3, N would give 5 NH3 groups plus one extra N. The units are H3N / NH3 / NH3 / NH3 / NH3 / N, so the likely reading is that the string is simply 6 ammonia molecules overlapping in the drawing. Counting the H3 subscripts in that label gives 4 (H3, H3, H3, H3), and the first label begins with "H3N" while the last ends with "N". Written out, that is H3N + NH3 + NH3 + NH3 + NH3 + N, which is 6 N atoms in total, but the final N would carry no H3 and so doesn't fit as a full NH3 unit.

Reading it as hexaammine cobalt(III) chloride, [Co(NH3)6]Cl3, there would be 6 NH3. Two NH3 are drawn separately. The remaining 4 must be in the long label, which would be written H3N.NH3.NH3.NH3.N with the final "N" belonging to the first group of "NH3" overlapped. Counting the labelled pieces: "H3N", "NH3", "NH3", "NH3", "NH3", "N" would be 6 units, with the last N missing hydrogens only because the text overlaps. Counting the H3 subscripts, there are 4 in that label plus 2 separate NH3 groups, giving 6 NH3 in total, which matches [Co(NH3)6]Cl3.

The charges also balance: Co³⁺ with 3 Cl⁻.

SMILES: [Co+3].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].N.N.N.N.N.N

name: Heroin
text:

The drawing shows hashed or wedged bonds at C5, C6, C9, C13 and C14, and I took the @/@@ pattern from the standard heroin SMILES, which I recalled from memory, rather than re-deriving it from the wedges. name: Hexamethylphosphoramide

name: Hexadecyltrimethylammonium Bromide

- **Chain:** the fourth substituent on nitrogen is an unbranched zigzag chain. Counting its vertices from the carbon attached to nitrogen to the terminal methyl gives 16 carbons.
- **Counter-ion:** a separate Br⁻ is shown above the chain.

The SMILES has 16 chain carbons, three N-methyl groups, the N⁺ and the separate bromide. No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

name: Hexamethylenetetramine
text:
This looks like hexamethylenetetramine (urotropine): 4 nitrogens and 6 CH2 groups, with each CH2 bridging two nitrogens.

Atoms in the drawing:
- Nitrogens: N_top (730,385), N_right (1380,710), N_bottom (770,1110), N_left (120,785).
- CH2 groups:
  - C1 (308,411), joining N_top and N_left.
  - C2 (1148,360), joining N_top and N_right.
  - C3 (540,762), joining N_top and N_bottom.
  - C4 (470,556), joining N_left and N_right.
  - C5 (352,1140), joining N_left and N_bottom.
  - C6 (1192,1088), joining N_right and N_bottom.

Each N is bonded to three CH2 groups:
- N_top: C1, C2, C3
- N_left: C1, C4, C5
- N_right: C2, C4, C6
- N_bottom: C3, C5, C6

This matches hexamethylenetetramine, with the six CH2 groups forming the six edges between the four nitrogens.

SMILES: C1N2CN3CN1CN(C2)C3

Checking this SMILES:
- C1 opens ring 1.
- N2 opens ring 2.
- C is followed by N3, which opens ring 3.
- C is followed by N1, which closes ring 1.
- C is followed by N, which carries a branch (C2) closing ring 2, and then C3 closes ring 3.

Atom by atom:
- Ca (ring 1) is bonded to Na and, through the ring-1 closure, to Nc.
- Na (ring 2) is bonded to Ca, Cb, and the C2 that closes ring 2.
- Cb is bonded to Na and Nb (ring 3).
- Nb is bonded to Cb, Cc, and the C3 that closes ring 3.
- Cc is bonded to Nb and Nc (ring-1 closure).
- Nc is bonded to Cc, Ca, and Cd.
- Cd is bonded to Nc and Nd.
- Nd is bonded to Cd, the C2 branch (back to Na), and the C3 closure (to Nb).

Each nitrogen has three carbons, and there are 6 carbons in total, so this is the correct cage.

SMILES: C1N2CN3CN1CN(C2)C3

name: Hexanitrostilbene
text:
The drawing shows a 2,2',4,4',6,6'-hexanitrostilbene: two benzene rings joined by a C=C bond, with each ring carrying three nitro groups.

**Ring and chain layout**
- Left ring: the carbon bonded to the vinyl group (about 567,724) has nitro groups on both neighbouring carbons (ortho). The carbon at about (310,775), para to the vinyl-bearing carbon, carries the third nitro group.
- Right ring: the carbon bonded to the vinyl group (about 914,774) is flanked by two ortho nitro carbons. The carbon at about (1172,724), para to it, carries the third nitro group.
- The two ring carbons are linked by a CH=CH unit.

**Stereochemistry**
- The vinyl carbons sit at about (697,700) and (783,799). The left ring carbon (567,724) is attached to the first vinyl carbon, and the right ring carbon (914,774) to the second.
- The two ring substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond, which makes it trans (E). In SMILES this is `/C=C/`.

**SMILES**
Each nitro group is written in charge-separated form, `[N+](=O)[O-]`.

Left ring, starting at the vinyl-bearing carbon: c1(C=C…)c([N+](=O)[O-])cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1[N+](=O)[O-].

SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1cc([N+](=O)[O-])c(/C=C/c2c([N+](=O)[O-])cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc2[N+](=O)[O-])c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Hexobarbital
text:
The drawing shows a barbiturate ring with a cyclohexenyl substituent, which matches hexobarbital.

**Ring.** The six-membered ring is C5–C4(=O)–N3(CH3)–C2(=O)–N1H–C6(=O), closing back to C5.
- C5 is the quaternary carbon at about (738, 816). It carries a methyl group and the cyclohexenyl group.
- The carbonyl carbon at (775, 585) is bonded to the N-methyl nitrogen.
- The carbonyl carbon at (1175, 650) is bonded to both nitrogens, so it is the urea-type C2.
- The NH is bonded to the carbonyl carbon at (920, 963), which is bonded back to C5.

**Cyclohexenyl group.** The six-membered carbocycle attaches through (517, 739), which is double-bonded to the carbon at (473, 510). The remaining four vertices are CH2 groups.

**SMILES.** The stereocentre at C5 is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)NC(=O)C(C)(C2=CCCCC2)C1=O

name: Hexoprenaline
text:
The drawing shows a symmetric molecule built from two catechol rings joined by a chain.

**Left side:** a benzene ring carries two OH groups on adjacent carbons (the HO labels at the upper left and lower left). The ring is attached to a CH(OH) carbon, which is bonded to a CH2 and then to an NH.

**Chain:** between the two NH groups, I counted the vertices along the zigzag. The path from the left NH runs through vertices at about x = 583, 650, 717, 784, 850 and 917 before reaching the right NH at about x = 985. That gives six CH2 groups, so the linker is a hexamethylene chain.

**Right side:** the second NH is bonded to a CH2, then a CH(OH), then a second benzene ring bearing two adjacent OH groups.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(CNCCCCCCNCC(O)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1

SMILES: OC(CNCCCCCCNCC(O)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1

name: Hexylcaine
text:
The drawing shows a benzoate ester. A phenyl ring is bonded to a C(=O) group, which is bonded to an O. That O is attached to a CH carrying a methyl group, and the CH is attached to a CH2. The CH2 is bonded to an NH, and the NH is bonded to a cyclohexyl ring.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the stereocentre at the CH gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(CNC1CCCCC1)OC(=O)c1ccccc1

name: Histamine
text:
The drawing shows an imidazole ring with a 2-aminoethyl chain, which is histamine.

**Ring.** It is a five-membered ring with these atoms in order:
- NH at the top.
- A substituted carbon at the right, bonded to the chain.
- A CH carbon at the bottom right.
- N at the bottom left.
- A CH carbon at the left, between the two nitrogens.

**Bonds.** There are two double bonds in the ring:
- C=N, drawn between the left CH carbon and the bottom-left N.
- C=C, drawn between the substituted carbon on the right and the bottom-right CH carbon.

**Chain.** The substituted ring carbon carries CH2–CH2–NH2.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring from the substituted carbon: C1(=CN=CN1)CCN. Here the substituted carbon is double-bonded to the bottom CH carbon, which is bonded to N. That N is double-bonded to the left CH carbon, which is bonded to NH, which closes the ring back to the substituted carbon.

SMILES: NCCC1=CN=CN1

name: Hexestrol
text:
The drawing shows hexestrol, the meso (R,S) form: two 4-hydroxyphenyl rings on adjacent carbons of a hexane chain, with an ethyl group on each of those carbons.

- **Skeleton:** a central C–C bond joins two stereocentres. Each carries one 4-hydroxyphenyl ring, one ethyl group (CH2–CH3) and one implicit H.
- **Rings:** both are para-substituted benzene rings with an OH at the position opposite the attachment to the chain.
- **Stereochemistry:** both ethyl groups are on hashed bonds. In the drawing, the left stereocentre is R and the right stereocentre is S. This assignment uses the priority order aryl > other stereocentre > ethyl > H, with H pointing toward the viewer.
- **SMILES chirality tags:** these were worked out from that R/S assignment, giving `[C@@H]` for the left centre and `[C@H]` for the right.

SMILES: CC[C@@H](c1ccc(O)cc1)[C@H](CC)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Histrelin
text:
This structure is the decapeptide histrelin, pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑His(Bn)‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt. I read it residue by residue from the left, and the first six assignments below come from the drawing:

- **pGlu:** a 5‑oxopyrrolidine ring (lactam) whose carbonyl carbon is attached to the His residue.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain with a free NH.
- **Trp:** an indole side chain.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Tyr:** a 4‑hydroxyphenyl side chain.
- **D‑His(Bn):** an imidazole side chain with a benzyl group on one ring nitrogen.
- **Leu:** an isobutyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a guanidine‑terminated propyl side chain.
- **Pro:** a pyrrolidine ring, with the C‑terminus as an N‑ethyl amide (‑C(=O)NHCH2CH3).

For stereochemistry, I took every residue as L except the benzyl‑histidine, which I took as D. I assigned the @/@@ tags from the standard L‑amino‑acid pattern rather than re‑deriving each centre from the wedges and hashes. I adjusted the pGlu and Pro tags for their ring‑closure neighbour order.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1cn(Cc2ccccc2)cn1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC

name: Hmpao
text:
I read the molecule as a symmetric bis-oxime: two HO–N=C(CH3)–CH(CH3)–NH– units joined through a CH2–C(CH3)2–CH2 linker.

**Connectivity**
- Left end: HO–N=C(CH3)–CH(CH3)–NH–
- Centre: –CH2–C(CH3)2–CH2–
- Right end: –NH–CH(CH3)–C(CH3)=N–OH

**Stereochemistry**
- The two oxime C=N bonds are drawn without cis/trans geometry, so I left them unspecified.
- Each CH(CH3) carbon carries a hashed methyl, so both are stereocentres.
- At each one the priorities are N > C(=N) > CH3 > H, and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Reading the drawing from the front, the sequence N → C(=N) → CH3 runs counterclockwise at both centres. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is clockwise, so both centres are R.
- In the SMILES below, the left centre needs `@@` and the right centre needs `@` to give R at each.

SMILES: ON=C(C)[C@@H](C)NCC(C)(C)CN[C@H](C)C(C)=NO

name: Hydralazine
text:
The drawing is a phthalazine ring with a hydrazine group attached, which is hydralazine.

**Ring system.** A benzene ring is fused to a six-membered ring containing two adjacent nitrogens. Going around the second ring:
- The top nitrogen (N) is double-bonded to the CH carbon, which is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon.
- The top nitrogen is single-bonded to the lower nitrogen (N).
- The lower nitrogen is double-bonded to the carbon that bears the NHNH2 group.
- That carbon is bonded to the other ring-fusion carbon.

**Substituent.** The carbon next to the lower ring nitrogen carries NH–NH2, which gives the hydrazine group.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring starting from the hydrazine-bearing carbon gives NNC1=NN=CC2=CC=CC=C12. The benzene ring is aromatic, and the Kekulé form shown above is valid.

SMILES: NNc1nncc2ccccc12

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
text:
The drawing is hydrochlorothiazide, which I read as follows.

- **Benzene ring:** six carbons. One carries the sulfonamide group (S with two =O and NH2). The next carbon carries Cl. The adjacent ring carbon bears the ring NH. The carbon next to that is bonded to the ring S.
- **Fused ring:** S(=O)(=O), then NH, then a CH2, then NH, which attaches to the aromatic carbon.

Writing the SMILES from the sulfonamide nitrogen: NS(=O)(=O)c1cc2c(cc1Cl)NCNS2(=O)=O

Check of the ring closures:
- c1 is the carbon bearing the sulfonamide.
- c is an aromatic CH.
- c2 is the carbon bonded to the ring S, which closes with S2 at the end.
- c( is the carbon bearing the ring NH. Its branch is cc1Cl, a CH followed by the C-Cl carbon, which closes ring 1 back to the sulfonamide carbon.
- Then N, C, N, S2(=O)=O.

The order around the ring is: C(SO2NH2), CH, C(S), C(N), CH, C(Cl), back to C(SO2NH2). In the image the Cl carbon is adjacent to both the sulfonamide carbon and a CH, and that CH is adjacent to the carbon bearing the NH. The sulfonamide carbon is adjacent to a CH, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing the ring S. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1cc2c(cc1Cl)NCNS2(=O)=O

name: Hydrocodone
text:
The drawing matches hydrocodone, a morphinan skeleton. I read it as follows:

- An aromatic ring carries an OMe group, and an adjacent ring oxygen forms the dihydrofuran bridge.
- A ketone (C=O) sits in the cyclohexanone ring, next to the CH–O carbon.
- An N-methyl piperidine ring is bridged by the CH2 drawn with the "C" label.
- Hashed bonds appear at the three ring-fusion C–H centres and at the quaternary carbon, so the stereochemistry is included.

I took the stereo descriptors from my recollection of the known hydrocodone SMILES and did not re-derive each one from the wedges in the image, so the @/@@ assignments are the least certain part.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4C(=O)CC[C@H]2[C@H]1CC5=C3C(=C(C=C5)OC)O4

name: Hydrogen Peroxide
text:
The drawing shows HO–OH: two oxygen atoms joined by a single bond, each carrying one hydrogen. There are no charges, ring atoms or stereo marks. This is hydrogen peroxide.

SMILES: OO

name: Hydrocortisone Aceponate
text:
I read this as hydrocortisone 17-propionate 21-acetate (hydrocortisone aceponate) and wrote the SMILES by adapting the natural hydrocortisone stereochemistry, not by assigning each wedge from scratch.

- **Skeleton:** a four-ring steroid with a C4=C5 double bond conjugated to the C3 ketone in ring A.
- **C11:** a hydroxyl group.
- **C17:** a side chain C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH3 (the 21-acetate), plus an O–C(=O)CH2CH3 propionate ester on the same carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows hashed methyls at C10 and C13, a hashed C11–OH, a wedged H at C9, a hashed H at C8, a wedged H at C14, and a wedged C17–O. The molecule appears rotated 180° about the horizontal axis, with the five-membered ring on the left. That flips every wedge and hash relative to the usual orientation, and the pattern matches the natural hydrocortisone configuration.

I did not re-derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the wedges. I took them from hydrocortisone and kept the neighbour order at C17 unchanged when swapping in the two esters.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(C(=O)COC(C)=O)OC(=O)CC)C)O

name: Huperzine A
text:
I could not read one part of the drawing consistently, so this SMILES is a best-effort reading rather than a certain match.

What I read from the image:
- **Pyridone ring:** a six-membered ring with C(=O), an NH, a C=C fused bond, and a CH=CH unit.
- **Six-membered ring on the right:** it holds a quaternary carbon bearing NH2 (hashed bond), a CH2, a carbon bearing the methyl group, a CH=, and a CH with a hashed H.
- **CH2 bridge:** the CH2 at the bottom links the pyridone ring carbon to the hashed-H carbon.
- **Unclear part:** a small angled arc inside the ring system leaves one carbon looking short of a bond. Bonding it to the pyridone ring carbon would give that carbon five bonds, so I left that arc out and treated the carbon as a plain CH2 bridging the two stereocentres.
- **Stereochemistry:** the @/@@ tags follow the two hashed bonds, but I assigned them by reasoning from the drawing and have not verified them.

SMILES: O=C1C=CC2=C(N1)C[C@@H]3C=C(C)C[C@@]2(N)C3

name: Hydroquinone
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring (six carbons, with three double bonds drawn in alternating positions). Two hydroxyl groups are attached at opposite vertices of the ring, on the left and the right, which is the para (1,4) arrangement. This molecule is hydroquinone (benzene-1,4-diol). There are no wedges, hashes, charges or stereo features to encode.

SMILES: Oc1ccc(O)cc1

name: Hydromorphone
text:
I read the drawing as hydromorphone, a morphinan skeleton, and wrote the SMILES from that identification. I did not re-derive each @/@@ label from the wedges in the image. The stereo labels come from my recollection of the standard isomeric SMILES for hydromorphone, so they are the least certain part.

The features I read from the drawing:
- **Aromatic ring:** a phenol OH sits on one ring carbon, and the neighbouring ring carbon carries the ether oxygen.
- **Ether bridge:** the oxygen links that aromatic carbon to a CH that has a hashed H.
- **Ketone:** a C=O sits next to that CH, followed by two CH2 groups leading to another CH with a hashed H.
- **Piperidine ring:** an N-methyl nitrogen is joined to a CH2–CH2 chain on the quaternary carbon and to a CH with a hashed H. That CH is bonded to the CH2 on the aromatic ring.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries a hashed bond and connects the aromatic ring, the ether CH and the two ring systems.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4C(=O)CC[C@H]2[C@H]1CC5=C3C(=C(C=C5)O)O4

name: Hydroxychloroquine
text:
The drawing is hydroxychloroquine, with plain bonds throughout and no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is written.

**Ring system.** It is a quinoline with Cl on the benzo ring.
- The pyridine ring runs N, CH, CH, C4 (bearing NH), C4a, C8a.
- C8a connects to a CH, which connects to the C–Cl carbon, then CH, CH, and back to C4a.
- The Cl sits on the carbon meta to C8a, which is position 7, as in chloroquine.

**Side chain.** The chain from C4 is NH–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH2–CH2–N(CH2CH3)(CH2CH2OH).

**SMILES assembly.** Written from the side chain into the ring: CCN(CCO)CCCC(C)Nc1ccnc2cc(Cl)ccc12.
- c1 is C4, followed by c c (C3 and C2) and n (N1).
- c2 is C8a, then c (C8), c(Cl) (C7), c c (C6 and C5), and c12 (C4a), which closes both rings.

SMILES: CCN(CCO)CCCC(C)Nc1ccnc2cc(Cl)ccc12

name: Hydroxymethanediphosphonic acid
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon bonded to an OH group and to two phosphorus atoms. Each phosphorus carries one double-bonded O (P=O) and two OH groups. Plain bonds only, so no stereochemistry.

This is a hydroxymethylene bisphosphonic acid.

SMILES: OC(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O

name: Hydroxynorketamine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Cyclohexane ring:** it has six carbons. One is the quaternary carbon bearing NH2 and the aryl group. Next to it is the ketone carbon (C=O). Next to that is the CH bearing OH. Two CH2 groups complete the ring.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring with Cl on the carbon ortho to the point of attachment.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is specified.

The SMILES, written atom by atom:

- Ketone carbon: C1(=O)
- CH(OH): C(O)
- Two CH2 groups: CC
- Quaternary carbon: C1(N)
- Aryl: c1ccccc1Cl

Combined: O=C1C(O)CCCC1(N)c1ccccc1Cl

The ring has C1 (C=O), C(O), C, C, C, C1(N), which is six atoms. In the image, the ring runs C=O, CH(OH), CH2, CH2, CH2, then the quaternary carbon, so there are three CH2 groups. I count the vertices: the C=O carbon at (560,620), CH(OH) at (275,552), a CH2 at (75,765), a CH2 at (157,1045), a CH2 at (441,1112), and the quaternary carbon at (642,900). That is six, with three CH2 groups, which matches the SMILES.

SMILES: O=C1C(O)CCCC1(N)c1ccccc1Cl

name: Hydroxypyridinone
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring made of one nitrogen and five carbons.

- The nitrogen carries an OH group, so it is an N-hydroxy nitrogen.
- The ring carbon next to the nitrogen at the bottom has a C=O (a lactam carbonyl).
- Going around from the nitrogen, the ring carbons are: C(=O), then CH, CH, CH, CH, which closes back onto N.
- The double bonds are in the upper right (CH=CH between the carbon next to N and the next carbon) and in the lower right (CH=CH between the carbon bonded to the lower-right corner and the carbon above it).
- Tracing the carbons: C2 (C=O) – C3 (bottom) – C4 (lower right) – C5 (upper right) – C6 (top, bonded to N).
- The inner double-bond lines sit on the top-right edge (C6=C5) and the bottom-right edge (C4=C3).

This gives 1-hydroxypyridin-2(1H)-one: O=C1C=CC=CN1O.

Atom check: the ring has C1(=O), C=C, C=C, and N1, which is six atoms in total, and the N–OH is included.

SMILES: O=C1C=CC=CN1O

name: Hydroxyzine
text:
The drawing shows hydroxyzine, assembled from these parts:

- A phenyl ring and a 4-chlorophenyl ring are both attached to a single CH carbon.
- That CH carbon is bonded to one nitrogen of a piperazine ring.
- The other piperazine nitrogen carries a CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–OH chain.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: OCCOCCN1CCN(CC1)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Hydroxyurea
text:
The drawing shows hydroxyurea. Reading it from left to right:

- An HO group is attached to an NH.
- That NH is bonded to a central carbon, which carries a double-bonded O below it.
- The same carbon is also bonded to an NH2 on the right.

Written as SMILES, this is a hydroxylamine nitrogen joined to a urea carbonyl: ON–C(=O)–N, giving ONC(N)=O. The structure has no stereochemistry.

SMILES: NC(=O)NO

name: Hypoxanthine
text:
The drawing is a purine skeleton, a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring, which matches hypoxanthine drawn as the 1,9-dihydro tautomer (NH at N1 and at N9).

**Atoms and bonds read from the image:**
- Six-membered ring: C2 (top left carbon) is double-bonded to N3 (top N). N3 is single-bonded to C4 (the fusion carbon, upper right). C4 is bonded to C5 (the lower fusion carbon), and C5 is bonded to C6 (the C=O carbon). C6 is bonded to N1 (the HN at left), and N1 is bonded to C2.
- Five-membered ring: C4 is single-bonded to N9 (the right N with no H, top right), which is double-bonded to C8 (the right-hand carbon). C8 is single-bonded to the NH at the bottom right, which is bonded to C5. The C4=C5 bond is double (the inner line in the drawing).

**SMILES:** Starting from the C=O carbon, O=C1NC=NC2=C1NC=N2.

**Check:**
- C1 (C=O) is bonded to N (NH), then C=N, then C2 (the fusion carbon C4), then =C1 (the other fusion carbon C5, which closes the six-membered ring back to the C=O carbon).
- C5 is then bonded to NH, then C=N, then N closes onto C4 (ring label 2). The N closing onto C4 is the one with no H, and it is double-bonded to C8, as in the drawing.
- Each atom has the right valence.

SMILES: O=C1NC=NC2=C1NC=N2

name: Iberdomide
text:
I read the structure as a lenalidomide-type molecule: a piperidine-2,6-dione (glutarimide) attached through its C3 to the nitrogen of a 1-oxoisoindoline. The isoindoline carries a benzyloxy group at C4, and the benzene ring of that group bears a para-CH2-morpholine.

**Stereocentre:** the only wedge is on the glutarimide C3, pointing to the isoindolinone N, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > C(=O)N > CH2 > H. On the page, N (lower right), C=O (top) and CH2 (left) run counterclockwise, which gives the S configuration.

**SMILES chirality:** in `O=C1CC[C@@H](C(=O)N1)N...` the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, C(=O), N. Working through the permutation, `@@` with this order corresponds to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@@H](C(=O)N1)N1Cc2c(OCc3ccc(CN4CCOCC4)cc3)cccc2C1=O

name: Heparin Pentasaccharide
text:
I read the image as a linear pentasaccharide. It has a methyl glycoside at the top ring and four glycosidic links running down to the bottom ring. The rings, from top to bottom, are:

1. A glucosamine ring (methyl glycoside) carrying an N-sulfate (NHSO3H), a 3-OH and a 6-O-sulfate. Its 4-O is the glycosidic link to ring 2.
2. A uronic acid ring with a COOH, a 3-OH and an O-sulfate on the carbon next to the anomeric carbon.
3. A glucosamine ring with an N-sulfate, an O-sulfate on the ring carbon next to the N-bearing carbon, and a 6-O-sulfate.
4. A uronic acid ring with a COOH and two OH groups, and no sulfate.
5. A terminal glucosamine ring with an N-sulfate, two OH groups and a 6-O-sulfate.

I worked out each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing. Ring 4's COOH bond is drawn as a hash that is partly hidden by the N-hash from ring 5, so that centre is the least certain.

SMILES: CO[C@@H]1[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]([C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O1)O[C@H]1[C@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O)O1)O[C@@H]1[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H]([C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O1)O[C@H]1[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]([C@@H](C(=O)O)O1)O[C@@H]1[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O1

name: Hydroxocobalamin
text:
This is my best reading of the drawing as hydroxocobalamin, with the Co³⁺ and hydroxide drawn as separate ions. The connectivity was traced atom by atom. The stereodescriptors are partly assigned from the known cobalamin pattern rather than read cleanly from every wedge and hash, so some may be wrong. The corrin carbons carrying only plain bonds have no stereo marks.

- **Base:** a 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole attached through N to the ribose C1.
- **Sugar and linker:** the ribose carries a CH₂OH and a 3-phosphate (O⁻). The phosphate is esterified to a 1-aminopropan-2-yl group, which is acylated through an amide to the propionamide side chain on ring D.
- **Corrin ring:**
  - One anionic N⁻ in ring D.
  - Imine-type N atoms in the other rings.
  - Direct ring A–D bond.
  - Gem-dimethyl on ring C.
  - Three meso-methyl groups.
  - Seven amide side chains (CH₂CONH₂ and CH₂CH₂CONH₂).
- **Counter-ions:** a separate Co³⁺ and a separate hydroxide.

name: Ibrutinib
text:
The molecule is ibrutinib, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Acryloyl piperidine:** an acryloyl group (C=C–C(=O)–) is on the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Stereocentre:** the piperidine C3 carries the pyrazole N1 through a wedge bond.
- **Core:** a pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine bears an NH2 group at C4.
- **Aryl group:** the pyrazole C3 is attached to a 4-phenoxyphenyl group.

Stereochemistry at the wedged carbon: the substituent priorities are N (pyrazole) > ring CH2 next to the amide N > ring CH2 on the other side > H. The wedged N points toward the viewer, so H points away. Tracing N → CH2(N) → CH2 goes clockwise in the drawing, which gives R. This is the (R) configuration of ibrutinib, written as `[C@H]` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCC[C@H](C1)n1nc(-c2ccc(Oc3ccccc3)cc2)c2c(N)ncnc21

name: Ibogaine
text:
This structure is ibogaine, the 10-methoxy ibogamine skeleton, and I read the stereochemistry from the four wedge/hash bonds in the drawing.

**Skeleton**
- A 5-methoxyindole unit sits on the right: a benzene ring carrying OMe, fused to a pyrrole ring with an NH.
- The indole C3 carries a CH2CH2 chain that leads to the tertiary amine N.
- The indole C2 is bonded to a CH, which I call C_d. This carbon carries a hashed H.
- C_d also bonds to a CH2 and to the CH next to N, which I call C_b. C_b has a hashed H.
- The CH2 leads to C_c, a bridgehead CH with a wedged H. C_c is bonded to a CH2 that runs to C_a and to another CH2 that goes to N, giving the isoquinuclidine cage.
- C_a is a CH with a hashed H and an ethyl group. It is bonded to C_b.

**Stereocentres**
I assigned each of the four centres from the drawn wedge/hash direction and the neighbour order in the SMILES. Working through them gave C_a as @, C_c as @@, C_d as @@ and C_b as @. I did not cross-check these against a known ibogaine SMILES.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1C[C@@H]2C[C@@H]3[C@H]1N(C2)CCc1c3[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

name: Ibuprofen, (+-)-
text:
The drawing shows ibuprofen. Reading it region by region:

- **Isobutyl group:** two methyl carbons are joined to a CH, which is joined to a CH2, which attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene.
- **Acid side chain:** the opposite ring carbon bears a CH that carries a methyl group and a COOH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** that CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds (no wedges or hashes), so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O

name: Ibuproxam
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an isobutyl group, CH2-CH(CH3)2. The other is a CH(CH3)-C(=O)-NH-OH group, which makes the molecule ibuprofen hydroxamic acid.

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)NO

name: Ibutilide
text:
I read the structure in three parts:

- **Amine end:** the nitrogen carries an ethyl group and an unbranched chain of 7 carbons (heptyl), counted vertex by vertex from the nitrogen to the chain end.
- **Linker:** from the nitrogen, 4 more carbons run toward the ring. The fourth carbon bears the OH and is bonded directly to the benzene ring. It is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marker.
- **Ring end:** the benzene ring is para-substituted. The other substituent is NH–S(=O)(=O)–CH3, a methanesulfonamide.

SMILES: CCCCCCCN(CC)CCCC(O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: Icenticaftor
text:
I read the structure as a pyridine ring carrying four substituents, plus an amide side chain ending in a stereogenic carbinol carbon.

**Ring.** Going around the pyridine ring:
- The ring nitrogen sits next to a carbon bearing OMe.
- Next is a carbon bearing CF3.
- Then comes a CH.
- Then a carbon bearing NH2.
- The last ring carbon carries the carboxamide, C(=O)NH.

**Side chain.** The amide nitrogen connects through CH2 to a quaternary carbon. That carbon bears OH, CH3 (drawn as a wedge) and CF3.

**Stereochemistry.** The wedged methyl points toward the viewer. The other three substituents are OH (upper left), CH2 (lower left) and CF3 (lower right). Viewed from the methyl side, OH → CH2 → CF3 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is written `C[C@](O)(CN…)C(F)(F)F` with methyl first. Rewriting with the CH2 neighbour first (`NC[C@](C)(O)C(F)(F)F`) is an even permutation of the neighbour order, so the `@` is unchanged.

SMILES: COc1nc(C(=O)NC[C@](C)(O)C(F)(F)F)c(N)cc1C(F)(F)F

name: Hypericin
text:
I read this as hypericin drawn as one tautomer, with C30H16O8: six aromatic OH groups, two ring C=O groups and two methyl groups on a fused polycyclic core.

I labelled the 30 carbons by their drawn positions and assigned the double bonds from the image. These are two C=O groups at the lower corners, the visible inner double lines, and the central C=C bonds. I then wrote the SMILES by walking the ring system with ring-closure digits. I checked that every ring carbon carries exactly one double bond.

SMILES: OC1=C2C(O)=C3C(=O)C=C(C)C4=C3C5=C2C(C(O)=C1)=C8C(O)=CC(O)=C9C(O)=C%10C(=O)C=C(C)C4=C%10C5=C89

name: Icotinib
text:
The drawing is a quinazoline with a 3-ethynylanilino group at C4 and a crown ether ring fused across the 6,7-positions (as in erlotinib, but cyclised).

**Quinazoline core:** N1 is the top N (bonded to C8a). C2 is the CH between the two N atoms. N3 is the lower N, bonded to C4. C4 carries the NH-aryl group and is bonded to C4a. C4a is bonded to C8a and C5 (the CH at the bottom). C5 is bonded to C6, which bears an O at the bottom. C6 is bonded to C7, which bears an O at the top. C7 is bonded to C8 (the CH), and C8 is bonded to C8a.

**Macrocycle:** Going from the O on C7 (top) round to the O on C6 (bottom), the chain is:
- O(top)–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O(bottom).
- That gives four ether oxygens in the chain besides the two aryl oxygens on the ring. Looking at the labels: O top (aryl), O right-upper, O lower-right, and O bottom-left (aryl), so there are four O atoms in total.
- The chain from top O: CH2, CH2, O (right), CH2, CH2, O (lower right), CH2, CH2, O (bottom left, aryl).
- Checking the bottom: the bottom-left O is bonded to C6, then CH2 (1050,990), CH2 (1168,1027), then O (1288,1005). So the lower-right O links to the bottom-left O through two CH2 groups.
- The right side runs from the top O through CH2 (1200,548), CH2 (1320,590), O (1400,685), CH2 (1423,805), CH2 (1385,922), to O (1288,1005).

**Full SMILES:** c1(C#C)cccc(c1)Nc1ncnc2cc3OCCOCCOCCOc3cc12 — written out, the ring is O–CCOCCOCCO, i.e. O, 2C, O, 2C, O, 2C, O, which matches the four O atoms.

SMILES: C#Cc1cccc(Nc2ncnc3cc4OCCOCCOCCOc4cc23)c1

name: Idarubicin
text:
This structure matches idarubicin (4-demethoxydaunorubicin). I identified it from the overall scaffold rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo descriptors come from the known idarubicin SMILES.

- **Aglycone:** a tetracyclic anthracyclinone. The aromatic ring is an unsubstituted benzene ring (no methoxy), fused to a quinone ring. Next to that is a hydroquinone-type ring carrying two phenolic OH groups. The last ring is a saturated cyclohexane bearing a tertiary OH and an acetyl group (C(=O)CH3) on one carbon.
- **Sugar:** an amino sugar (daunosamine) attached through a glycosidic O to the cyclohexane ring. It carries a ring methyl, a secondary OH and an NH2.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H]([C@H](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@H]2C[C@@](CC3=C(C4=C(C(=C23)O)C(=O)C5=CC=CC=C5C4=O)O)(C(=O)C)O)N)O

name: Icariin
text:
This is the flavonol glycoside icariin, read as follows.

- **Core:** a chromen-4-one with a 5-OH group, a 4-methoxyphenyl at C2, and a prenyl (3-methylbut-2-enyl) group at C8.
- **C3 substituent:** an O-linked 6-deoxyhexose (rhamnose). It has a CH3 on C5, drawn with a hashed bond.
- **C7 substituent:** an O-linked glucose with a CH2OH group, also drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each sugar stereocentre from its wedge or hash bonds and the implicit H, working through the SMILES neighbour order for each.
- **Connectivity check:** the ring closures in the SMILES give the chromone fusion as drawn, with C8a bonded to O1 and C8 closing back to it.

name: Iclepertin
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-(1,1,1-trifluoropropan-2-yloxy)-5-(methylsulfonyl)benzoyl amide of a 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane. The bicycle carries a 5-(trifluoromethyl)isoxazol-3-yl group at the bridgehead carbon.

**Fragments**
- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring with the amide carbonyl on one carbon. Ortho to it is the ether oxygen, which leads to CH(CH3)CF3. The carbon para to the ether oxygen carries S(=O)(=O)CH3.
- **Amide:** C(=O) bonded to the ring nitrogen of the bicycle.
- **Bicycle:** the N-containing five-membered ring, N–CH2–C(quaternary)–CH(H)–CH2–N, bridged by a cyclopropane CH2 between the quaternary carbon and the CH carbon.
- **Isoxazole:** attached through its C3, which is bonded to the ring N. Going around the ring from C3, the atoms are N, O, C5 (bearing CF3) and C4 (the CH).

**Stereochemistry (from the wedges)**
- **CH(CH3)(CF3)O:** the wedged methyl, with H behind, gives `C[C@@H](O…)C(F)(F)F`.
- **Quaternary bicycle carbon:** the wedge to the isoxazole gives `[C@@]`, with neighbours listed in the order ring CH2, ring closure to the CH carbon, isoxazole, cyclopropane CH2.
- **Bridgehead CH:** the wedged H gives `[C@H]`, with neighbours listed in the order cyclopropane CH2, H, ring closure to the quaternary carbon, ring CH2.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Oc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1C(=O)N1C[C@@]2(c3cc(C(F)(F)F)on3)C[C@H]2C1)C(F)(F)F

name: Idelalisib
text:
I read this as an idelalisib-type molecule: a 5-fluoro-3-phenylquinazolin-4-one with an (S)-1-(purin-6-ylamino)propyl group at C2.

- **Quinazolinone core:** C2 is attached to the side chain. N3 carries the phenyl ring. C4 is the C=O. The benzo ring has fluorine on the carbon next to C4a.
- **Side chain:** a stereocentre bears an ethyl group (wedge bond), an NH linking to the purine, and the quinazolinone C2.
- **Purine:** the NH-bearing carbon is C6. The imidazole N–H sits on the nitrogen next to C5, the carbon bonded to C6, so it is the N7-H tautomer. This differs from the usual idelalisib drawing, so I wrote it as drawn.
- **Stereochemistry:** the ethyl group is on a wedge, so H points away from the viewer. Viewed from the front, ethyl → quinazolinone carbon → NH runs clockwise. That corresponds to `CC[C@H](N…)c1…` in SMILES order.

SMILES: CC[C@H](Nc1ncnc2nc[nH]c12)c1nc2cccc(F)c2c(=O)n1-c1ccccc1

name: Idoxifene
text:
I read the molecule as an idoxifene-type tamoxifen analogue, built from these pieces:

- **Alkene core:** a C=C bond whose first carbon carries an ethyl group and a phenyl ring, and whose second carbon carries a 4-iodophenyl ring and a 4-alkoxyphenyl ring.
- **Side chain:** the alkoxyphenyl ring bears O–CH2–CH2–N, and the nitrogen is part of a pyrrolidine ring (N plus four CH2 groups).
- **Double-bond geometry:** from the drawn coordinates, the ethyl group and the iodophenyl ring both point left, so they sit cis to each other. The phenyl and the alkoxyphenyl rings both point right, also cis.

In the SMILES, `CC/C(...)=C(\Ar)` places the ethyl and the iodophenyl cis, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccc(I)cc1)c1ccc(OCCN2CCCC2)cc1

name: Ifosfamide
text:
The drawing shows cyclophosphamide.

- **Ring:** a six-membered 1,3,2-oxazaphosphinane made of P, O, CH2, CH2, CH2 and N.
- **Phosphorus:** carries a P=O double bond and an exocyclic NH.
- **Substituents:** the exocyclic NH bears a CH2CH2Cl group, and the ring N bears a second CH2CH2Cl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is included.
