name: Iguratimod
text:
The structure is a chromone (4H-chromen-4-one) core with three substituents.

- At C3 (the carbon next to the C=O carbon) there is an NHCHO (formamide) group.
- At C6 there is a phenoxy group (O–Ph), on the benzene carbon adjacent to the ring fusion carbon C4a.
- At C7 there is a methanesulfonamide group (NHSO2CH3), on the carbon adjacent to C6.

Reading the pyranone ring: the ring-fusion carbon C4a (at about 743,803) bonds to the carbonyl carbon C4 (868,710). C4 bonds to C3 (1015,770), which bears the NH. C3 is double-bonded to C2 (1032,928), and C2 bonds to O1 (907,1022). O1 bonds to C8a (762,960). The benzene ring runs C4a–C5 (598,742)–C6 (472,836, bearing OPh)–C7 (490,994, bearing NHSO2Me)–C8 (636,1054)–C8a.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Nc1cc2occ(NC=O)c(=O)c2cc1Oc1ccccc1

name: Ibrexafungerp
text:
I could not read this drawing cleanly, so the SMILES below is a best-effort reading and carries no stereochemistry.

The drawing has overlapping bonds in the lower left and left-hand regions. I made these assignments:

- **Acid ring and side chain:** A cyclohexane ring carries the carboxylic acid next to a quaternary carbon, which bears a methyl and a CH(CH3)–CH(CH3)2 side chain. The neighbouring ring-fusion carbon carries another methyl.
- **Ring B:** This ring contains one C=C double bond.
- **Ring C and bridge:** Ring C is a third six-membered ring. It is bridged by a CH2–O–CH2 link and by a CH–CH2 bridge.
- **Triazole:** A 1,2,4-triazole is attached through N1 to a ring CH. Its C5 carries a pyridin-4-yl group.
- **Ether side chain:** The bridged ring carries an ether O–CH2–C(CH3)(NH2)–C(CH3)2– chain that ends on the pyridine carbon next to the ring N. I read this tail as a tert-butyl-like carbon, but the drawing is ambiguous at that point.
- **Stereochemistry:** I left it out because I could not assign the wedges reliably in the overlapped region.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1C(C)(C(C)C(C)C)CCC2C1(C)CC=C3C2CC(n7ncnc7-c8ccnc(c8)C(C)(C)C(C)(N)CO%13)C45C36COCC4(C)C%13C5C6

name: Ilaprazole
text:
The drawing is a benzimidazole sulfoxide of the ilaprazole type (a proton pump inhibitor scaffold), read as follows:

- **Pyridine ring:** the nitrogen is at the top. The carbon next to it bears the CH2 group, the next carbon bears a methyl, and the next bears the methoxy (OMe). The remaining two carbons are plain CH.
- **Linker:** CH2 then S(=O), which attaches to C2 of the benzimidazole.
- **Benzimidazole:** C2 is bonded to N (the =N) and to NH. The benzo ring carries a pyrrol-1-yl group.
- **Substituent position:** the N–H nitrogen sits at the bottom, attached to the ring-fusion carbon that is adjacent to the CH bearing no substituent. That CH (bottom, at about 1022,808) is bonded to the carbon bearing the pyrrole (1116,735). The pyrrole is therefore at position 5 or 6, and I do not need to fix which for the SMILES.

SMILES, written with the NH tautomer as drawn:

COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(cc3[nH]2)-n2cccc2)c1C

Check on the benzo ring: c3 (the fusion carbon on the =N side) goes to ccc(...)cc3[nH]. The fusion carbon at (892,647) bonds to N; the chain runs to CH (987,571), CH (1099,615), C–pyrrole (1116,735), CH (1022,808), then the fusion carbon (910,768) bonded to NH. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(cc3[nH]2)-n2cccc2)c1C

name: Idoxuridine
text:
This is 5-iodo-2'-deoxyuridine (idoxuridine): an iodouracil base attached through N1 to a 2-deoxyribose ring.

**Base:**
- The six-membered ring has N1, C2(=O), N3–H, C4(=O), C5 bearing iodine, and C6, with a C5=C6 double bond.
- N1 is the nitrogen joined to the sugar.

**Sugar:**
- The five-membered ring is O, C1', C2'(H2), C3', C4'.
- C1' carries the base on a hashed bond.
- C3' carries an OH on a wedge.
- C4' carries CH2OH on a hashed bond.
- C2' has no oxygen substituent, so the sugar is 2'-deoxy.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from the wedge and hash bonds, treating the implicit hydrogen as pointing the opposite way. This gives C1' as @, C3' as @ and C4' as @@, in the SMILES neighbour order below. The result matches the natural β-D-2'-deoxyribonucleoside pattern, with the base and CH2OH on the same face and the 3'-OH on the opposite face.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)N([C@H]2C[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O2)C=C1I

name: Imatinib
text:
The drawing shows imatinib (the free base). I read it region by region:

- **Left ring:** a pyridine attached at its 3-position (the nitrogen sits one carbon away from the attachment carbon).
- **Middle heteroaryl:** a pyrimidine linked to the pyridine at C4. Its C2 carries an NH that connects to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene:** it carries a methyl group ortho to the NH-pyrimidine substituent, and the amide NH sits meta to that NH-pyrimidine group (para to the methyl).
- **Amide:** the NH is acylated by a C=O group attached to the right-hand benzene ring.
- **Right benzene:** it is para-substituted, with a CH2 linking it to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries a methyl group.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds appear, so the SMILES has no stereochemistry.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(CN3CCN(C)CC3)cc2)cc1Nc1nccc(-c2cccnc2)n1

name: Iloperidone
text:
This structure is iloperidone. I read it region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying an acetyl group (CC(=O)), a methoxy group (OC) and an O-propyl chain.
- **Linker:** the ring oxygen leads through three CH2 groups to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** its 4-position bonds to C3 of a benzisoxazole.
- **Benzisoxazole:** the five-membered ring has C=N–O, and the fluorine sits on the benzene ring at the 6-position.

Checking the fluorine position: the five-membered ring atoms are C3, N, O, C7a and C3a. C7a (bonded to O) connects to a CH (C7), which connects to C6 bearing F. C6 then connects to C5 (CH), C4 (CH) and C3a. In the drawing, the carbon bonded to O at about (1235, 715) goes to (1322, 752), then to (1330, 847) with F, then to (1256, 899), then to (1170, 860), then to (1160, 770) at C3a. This matches F at C6.

SMILES: CC(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN2CCC(CC2)c2noc3cc(F)ccc23)c(OC)c1

name: Imidacloprid
text:
This structure is imidacloprid.

- **Pyridine ring:** a 6-chloropyridin-3-yl group. The ring N is bonded to the C bearing Cl, and the ring carbon at the other end of the ring (para to the Cl carbon) carries the CH2 linker.
- **Linker:** a CH2 joins the pyridine ring to the ring N of the imidazolidine.
- **Imidazolidine ring:** the N bonded to the CH2 connects to the central C, which is double-bonded to the exocyclic N. The central C also bonds to the NH. The ring closes through two CH2 groups between the NH and the N.
- **Nitro group:** the exocyclic N carries a nitro group, written N+(=O)[O-].

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)N=C1NCCN1Cc1ccc(Cl)nc1

name: Imidafenacin
text:
The drawing shows imidafenacin: a 2-methylimidazole whose N1 carries a CH2CH2 chain, ending in a quaternary carbon bearing two phenyl groups and a primary amide.

**Imidazole ring:** The ring atoms are N (left, drawn with a double bond to C2), C2 (bearing the methyl group), N1 (bearing the chain), and two CH carbons (C5, then C4) closing the ring back to the left N. The ring SMILES is Cc1nccn1.

**Chain:** N1 connects to CH2, then CH2, then a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries two phenyl rings and the C(=O)NH2 group.

**Assembly:** Cc1nccn1CCC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)C(N)=O

The drawing has no wedges or hashes and the quaternary carbon is not a stereocentre, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: Cc1nccn1CCC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)C(N)=O

name: Imidazo(1,2-a)pyridine
text:
The drawing shows imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine, a fused bicyclic system with a five-membered ring and a six-membered ring.

**Atoms and bonds**
- The bridgehead N (top, at about 710,540) bonds to three atoms: C at upper left (317,415), C at upper right (1067,337), and the bridgehead C at 710,955.
- The five-membered ring runs: N bridgehead, CH (317,415), CH (72,750), N (318,1080), bridgehead C (710,955).
- The five-membered ring double bonds are C(317)=C(72), drawn as an inner line, and N(318)=C(710).
- The six-membered ring runs: N bridgehead, C(1067,337), C(1425,545), C(1425,955), C(1067,1162), C(710,955).
- The six-membered ring double bonds are C(1067,337)=C(1425,545) and C(1425,955)=C(1067,1162).

**SMILES**
Starting at the bridgehead N: n1 ring atoms written in Kekulé form give N1(C=C...) as follows.

N1 bridgehead: `N12C=CN=C1C=CC=C2`

Check: the N bridgehead (ring labels 1 and 2) bonds to C=C, then N, then =C1 (the bridgehead C, closing ring 1 to the N). Then C=C–C=C2 continues around the six-membered ring and closes back to the N.
- The six-membered ring contains N, C1 (bridgehead), C=C, C=C, closing to N, which is 6 atoms. The double bonds are C=C and C=C, with the bridgehead C double-bonded to N in the five-membered ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: C1=CN2C=CC=CC2=N1

name: Imeglimin
text:
Reading the ring atom by atom: the six-membered ring has C(NH2)=N, then C(N(CH3)2)=N, an NH between the two substituted carbons, and a CH carrying a methyl group between the two ring nitrogens.

- The top-left carbon bears the NH2 group and is double-bonded to the left ring nitrogen.
- The top-right ring atom is an NH, linking the NH2-bearing carbon to the right-hand carbon.
- The right-hand carbon bears the dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) and is double-bonded to the bottom-right ring nitrogen.
- The bottom-left carbon carries a hashed methyl and an implicit H. It sits between the left nitrogen and the bottom-right nitrogen, which lead to different environments, so it is a stereocentre and the hash defines its configuration.

For the stereo, I wrote the SMILES with the neighbour order methyl, H, ring-closure N (bottom right), left N. The hashed methyl points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Seen from H, the sequence methyl → left N → bottom-right N runs clockwise. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order takes two swaps, so the parity is unchanged and the tag is `@@`.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1N=C(N)NC(N(C)C)=N1

name: Imidazole
text:
The drawing is a five-membered ring with two nitrogens, which is imidazole.

Reading the ring atoms:
- The top-left N has a double bond to the lower-left carbon, so it is the pyridine-type nitrogen.
- The top-left N also has a single bond to the top carbon.
- The top carbon and the right carbon are joined by a double bond.
- The right carbon is single-bonded to the bottom NH.
- The bottom NH is single-bonded to the lower-left carbon, which closes the ring.

Writing this as SMILES: N1=CNC=C1.

Check: the N1 atom is double-bonded to C, which is bonded to NH, then C=C, and the last C closes the ring back to N1. That gives 5 ring atoms, matching the drawing.

SMILES: C1=CNC=N1

name: Imidapril
text:
I read the molecule as imidapril, an ethyl ester of a phenylpropyl-amino-propanoyl group attached to a 1-methyl-2-oxoimidazolidine-4-carboxylic acid.

- **Ethyl ester and chain:** CH3CH2–O–C(=O)–CH(–CH2CH2–phenyl)–NH–.
- **Alanine unit:** the NH is bonded to a CH(CH3) carbon, which carries a C(=O) that acylates the ring nitrogen.
- **Ring:** a five-membered imidazolidinone with N-methyl, a ring C=O between the two nitrogens, a CH2, and a C4 carrying COOH.

I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes, using CIP priorities with the hydrogen pointing toward the viewer. All three come out as S:

- The methyl-bearing alanine carbon (hashed CH3) is S.
- The carbon bearing the ester and the hashed CH2 is S.
- The ring C4 carrying the hashed COOH is S.

The stereocentre order in the SMILES below matches this assignment.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1[C@@H](CN(C)C1=O)C(=O)O

name: Imipramine
text:
The drawing is imipramine: a dibenzazepine core, with the ring nitrogen carrying a 3-(dimethylamino)propyl chain.

**Core.** Two benzene rings are fused to a seven-membered ring. That ring contains the ring nitrogen, two CH2 groups (the ethylene bridge), and the two carbons of each benzene ring that are bonded to the ring nitrogen or to the CH2 bridge.

**Side chain.** The ring nitrogen is bonded to a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) that ends in N(CH3)2.

**SMILES.** CN(C)CCCN1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc21

**Check against the drawing.**
- The ring nitrogen connects to the upper benzene ring carbon at (836, 648) and to the lower benzene ring carbon at (1080, 911).
- The upper ring carbon at (948, 484) bonds to the CH2 at (1147, 469).
- That CH2 bonds to the CH2 at (1282, 615), which bonds to the lower ring carbon at (1252, 813).
- Seven-membered ring: N, C(836), C(948), CH2, CH2, C(1252), C(1080) — seven atoms, as required.

SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc21

name: Imipenem
text:
I read this as imipenem, the carbapenem antibiotic. The structure has a bicyclic β-lactam fused to a five-membered ring containing a C=C bond. The ring carries a carboxylic acid on the carbon next to N, and a thioether chain –S–CH2CH2–N=CH–NH2 on the other alkene carbon. The β-lactam carbon next to the lactam C=O bears a 1-hydroxyethyl group.

I took the three stereocentres (the two ring-fusion carbons and the CH(OH) carbon) from the known configuration of imipenem rather than deriving each one from the hashed bonds. The N=C double bond has no cis/trans geometry drawn, so I left it unspecified.

SMILES: C[C@H]([C@@H]1[C@H]2CC(=C(N2C1=O)C(=O)O)SCCN=CN)O

name: Imiquimod
text:
This is imiquimod, an imidazo[4,5-c]quinoline carrying an isobutyl group on N1 and an amino group at C4.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Isobutyl group:** two terminal methyls on a CH, then a CH2 attached to the imidazole nitrogen (N1).
- **Imidazole ring:** N1 is bonded to CH=N, and that N is bonded to the fused carbon C3a. C3a is double-bonded to the other fused carbon, which is bonded back to N1.
- **Pyridine ring:** C3a is bonded to C(NH2), which is double-bonded to the ring N. That N is bonded to an aromatic carbon of the benzene ring. The other fused carbon, bonded to N1, attaches to the second benzene fusion carbon.
- **Benzene ring:** four CH carbons plus the two fusion carbons.

Writing this as SMILES: CC(C)Cn1cnc2c(N)nc3ccccc3c12

Check of the ring closures: n1 (N1), c (CH), n, c2 (C3a), c(N) (C4 with NH2), n, c3 (benzene carbon next to N), cccc (four CH), c3 (benzene fusion carbon, closes the benzene ring), c12 (the fusion carbon bonded to N1 via ring closure 1 and to C3a via ring closure 2). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)Cn1cnc2c(N)nc3ccccc3c12

name: Incadronic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon bonded to two phosphonic acid groups, an NH, and an implicit hydrogen. The NH connects to a cycloheptyl ring.

Each phosphorus carries one P=O and two OH groups, so each group is P(=O)(O)O.

Counting the ring vertices one at a time: the attachment carbon at (918,903), then (1078,1063), (1303,1040), (1424,849), (1351,634), (1137,558) and (945,678). That is 7 carbons, so the ring is cycloheptane.

The central carbon has no stereo marks, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: O=P(O)(O)C(NC1CCCCCC1)P(=O)(O)O

name: Indalpine
text:
The drawing shows an indole joined at its C3 position to a two-carbon chain, which ends at C4 of a piperidine ring.

- **Piperidine:** the ring has six vertices: NH, CH2, CH2, CH (the substituted carbon), CH2, CH2. The substituted carbon is therefore C4.
- **Linker:** two CH2 groups, running from the piperidine C4 to the indole C3.
- **Indole:** the pyrrole ring has C3 attached to the chain, C2 as CH, and the NH. The fused benzene ring completes the bicycle.

The SMILES is C1CNCCC1CCc1c[nH]c2ccccc12.

Atom-by-atom check:
- Piperidine: C1, C, N, C, C, C1 gives six atoms, with the last C bearing the chain.
- Chain: CC gives two carbons.
- Indole: c1 (C3), c (C2), [nH], c2 (C7a), cccc (C7, C6, C5, C4), c12 (C3a). This is a valid indole.

SMILES: C1CNCCC1CCc1c[nH]c2ccccc12

name: Indacaterol
text:
I read this as indacaterol, with the (R) configuration at the single stereocentre.

- **Left fragment:** a benzene ring carrying two ethyl groups on adjacent carbons, fused to a five-membered ring (an indane). The indane's C2 carbon bears the secondary amine (NH).
- **Linker:** NH–CH2–CH(OH)–, where the CH(OH) carbon is drawn with a wedged OH.
- **Right fragment:** a quinolin-2(1H)-one. Its ring nitrogen is NH, and C2 is a C=O. C8 carries an OH, and C5 is attached to the CH(OH) carbon.

For the stereocentre, the OH is wedged toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Taking the CIP priorities as OH > CH2N > aryl, the sequence OH → CH2 → aryl runs clockwise, which gives R. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written with the CH2 as the preceding atom and then aryl and OH encodes that same R arrangement.

SMILES: CCc1cc2c(cc1CC)CC(C2)NC[C@@H](c1ccc(O)c2[nH]c(=O)ccc12)O

name: Indenolol
text:
I read the drawing as an indene core (a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring) carrying a β-blocker-style side chain.

- **Ring system:** The five-membered ring has a CH₂, then a CH=CH double bond. The CH₂ is bonded to the aromatic carbon at the lower left of the benzene ring. The CH=CH is bonded to the aromatic carbon next to the one that bears the oxygen.
- **Side chain:** The oxygen on the benzene ring links to CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂–NH–CH(CH₃)₂, an isopropylamino-2-hydroxypropoxy group.
- **Stereochemistry:** The carbon bearing the OH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I assigned no stereo.

I checked the ring closures: the benzene ring has six atoms, and the five-membered ring closes back onto the correct aromatic carbon.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2c1C=CC2

name: Imunofan
text:
I read the drawing as a linear hexapeptide, Arg‑Asp‑Lys‑Val‑Tyr‑Arg, running from the free amino terminus at the lower left to the free carboxylic acid at the upper right.

- **Residues:** Both arginines carry the guanidine side chain (CCCN=C(N)N). Asp has a CH2COOH side chain, Lys has a (CH2)4NH2 chain, Val has an isopropyl group, and Tyr has a CH2‑C6H4‑OH ring (para‑hydroxy).
- **Stereochemistry:** The wedge and hash bonds fix each α‑carbon. I checked the N‑terminal Arg, Asp, Val, Tyr and the C‑terminal Arg by the direction of the substituents around each centre, and all come out as L. Lys (the one residue not checked individually) is also taken as L, so every α‑carbon is written `[C@@H]` in the N→C direction.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)O

name: Indigo
text:
This is a tautomer of indigo. Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left half:** a benzene ring is fused to a five-membered ring containing NH. The ring carbon C2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 carries an OH. C2 is also bonded to the other half of the molecule.
- **Right half:** a benzene ring is fused to a five-membered ring made of C(=O), C(=N), and the ring N. The C=O carbon is bonded to the aromatic carbon and to the C=N carbon. That C=N carbon is bonded to the left-hand C2, and the N attaches to the aromatic carbon.

SMILES for the left half: Oc1c(c2ccccc2[nH]1)... Writing it out in full, with C3 bearing the OH and C2 bonded to the right half:

Left: C3(O)=C2([nH]c4ccccc34)
Right: C2'(=Nc5ccccc5C2'=O)

The combined SMILES is:
OC1=C(NC2=CC=CC=C12)C1=NC2=CC=CC=C2C1=O

I checked it against the drawing. The left ring consists of C3 (=C2, bearing OH), C2, NH, and the two fused aromatic carbons. The right ring consists of C(=N), N, the aromatic carbon, the aromatic carbon, and C(=O). The bonds match.

SMILES: OC1=C(NC2=CC=CC=C12)C1=NC2=CC=CC=C2C1=O

name: Indigo carmine
text:
The drawing shows indigo carmine (indigotine disodium sulfonate) in a tautomeric form. Reading it region by region:

- **Left ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. The five-membered ring has a C=O carbon, then a carbon double-bonded to N (C=N), and the N is bonded to the aromatic carbon. A sulfonate (S(=O)(=O)[O-]) sits on the benzene ring.
- **Right ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. This ring has a C-OH carbon double-bonded to the carbon that is joined to the left unit, and an NH bonded to the aromatic carbon. It carries a second sulfonate on the benzene ring.
- **Link and counterions:** a single bond joins the left C=N carbon to the right C2 carbon. Two Na+ ions are shown.

Writing the left unit: O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)...

The left C=O carbon is attached to the aromatic carbon at the top, which is adjacent to the CH that bears the sulfonate neighbour. The sulfonate-bearing carbon is attached to the top-left CH, which connects to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to C=O. So the sulfonate is para to N's ring-fusion carbon, as in the SMILES above: c2 (attached to N), c, c, c(S), c, c12.

Right unit: C2 (=C(O)c3cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc3N2). The C-OH carbon is attached to the ring-fusion carbon at the top, then the CH, then the carbon bearing S, then two CH, then the ring-fusion carbon bonded to NH.

Full SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)C1=C(O)c2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc2N1

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)C1=C(O)c2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc2N1

name: Indiplon
text:
This is zaleplon-like: a pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine bearing a 3-(N-methylacetamido)phenyl group at position 7 and a thiophene-2-carbonyl group at position 3.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The acetamide is CH3-C(=O)-N(CH3)-Ar.
- The benzene ring is attached to N at one carbon and to the bicyclic core at a meta position.
- The bicyclic core has a bridgehead N (the one bonded to the aryl-bearing carbon), a neighbouring N= and CH, a C3 carrying the carbonyl, a fusion carbon, a ring N, and two CH carbons, with the aryl on C7.
- The carbonyl links C3 to thiophene C2, and the thiophene S sits next to that carbon.

SMILES, built from the core:
- Aryl-bearing carbon: c1(...)ccnc2c(C(=O)c3cccs3)cnn12.
- Full molecule: CC(=O)N(C)c1cccc(c1)-c1ccnc2c(C(=O)c3cccs3)cnn12.

Check of the core ring closure: c1ccnc2c(...)cnn12 gives c1 (C7), c (C6), c (C5), n (N4), c2 (C3a), c(C3) bearing the carbonyl, c (C2), n (N1), n12 (bridgehead N closing to C7 and C3a). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)N(C)c1cccc(c1)-c1ccnc2c(C(=O)c3cccs3)cnn12

name: Indinavir
text:
This structure is indinavir (the HIV protease inhibitor). I recognised the scaffold and wrote its SMILES from memory of the known isomeric form, rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

The drawing matches this scaffold:
- a tert-butyl amide on the piperazine C2 carbon
- a piperazine N4 carrying a pyridin-3-ylmethyl group
- a hydroxyl-bearing chain from N1 to a benzyl-substituted amide carbon
- a cis-aminoindanol amide

I checked one stereocentre against the image: the piperazine carbon bearing the wedged amide. Its configuration agrees with the `[C@@H]` in the SMILES. I did not check the other stereocentres individually.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CN(CCN1C[C@H](C[C@@H](CC2=CC=CC=C2)C(=O)N[C@@H]3[C@@H](CC4=CC=CC=C34)O)O)CC5=CN=CC=C5

name: Indole
text:
The drawing shows indole: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring that contains an NH.

**Six-membered ring.** The vertices are C(432,390), C(73,598), C(73,1010), C(432,1218), C(790,1010) and C(790,598). The double bonds are 432,390–790,598 (inner line), 73,598–73,1010, and 432,1218–790,1010.

**Five-membered ring.** The vertices are C(790,598), N(1180,470), C(1425,803), C(1183,1138) and C(790,1010). The N is bonded to C(790,598) and to C(1425,803). The double bond is C(1425,803)=C(1183,1138). C(1183,1138) is bonded to C(790,1010).

**SMILES.** Starting from the N, the five-membered ring is written as [nH]1ccc2ccccc12. Here C2 (1425,803) and C3 (1183,1138) are the two aromatic carbons, C3a is c2, and C7a is c12.

SMILES: c1ccc2[nH]ccc2c1

name: Indocyanine Green
text:
I read this as a heptamethine cyanine dye. It has two benzo[e]indole end groups, each carrying an N‑(4‑sulfobutyl) chain and a gem‑dimethyl carbon, joined by a seven‑carbon polymethine bridge. The sulfonates are drawn as anions and there is one sodium counter‑ion.

- **Left unit:** a neutral N, with the ring carbon double‑bonded to the first bridge carbon.
- **Bridge:** seven carbons with alternating double bonds. The bonds run =C, C=C, C=C, C=C, then the single bond to the right ring carbon. All the chain double bonds are drawn trans.
- **Right unit:** an iminium N⁺ double‑bonded to its ring carbon.
- **Naphthalene fusion:** the N‑bearing aromatic carbon sits next to the CH=CH of the fused ring. The CMe₂ carbon attaches to the aromatic carbon on the peri side, which gives the benzo[e]indole pattern.
- **Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so the only stereo marked is the chain double‑bond geometry.

I checked the SMILES by counting the bridge carbons (seven) and the ring closures on both naphthalene‑fused units.

SMILES: [Na+].CC1(C)C2=C(C=Cc3ccccc23)N(CCCCS(=O)(=O)[O-])/C1=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C1=[N+](CCCCS(=O)(=O)[O-])c2ccc3ccccc3c2C1(C)C

name: Indolizine
text:
The drawing is a fused bicyclic ring system with a nitrogen at the ring fusion, which is indolizine.

**Atoms and rings**
- The five-membered ring has N, C(a) at the upper left, C(b) at the far left, C(c) at the lower left, and C(d) at the fusion carbon below N.
- The six-membered ring has N, C at the top, C at the upper right, C at the lower right, C at the bottom, and the fusion carbon C(d).

**Double bonds**
- In the five-membered ring: C(a)=C(b) (inner line on the upper left) and C(c)=C(d) (inner line on the bottom).
- In the six-membered ring: top C=upper-right C (inner line on the upper right) and lower-right C=bottom C (inner line on the lower right).
- The N–C(d) bond is single, and N has three connections, so no charge is needed.

**SMILES**
Starting at N: n1 connects to C(a)=C(b)–C(c)=C(d), and C(d) closes back to N. The six-membered ring continues from C(d) to the bottom carbon, then the lower-right and upper-right carbons, then the top carbon, and back to N.

Written with explicit double bonds, this is N1C=CC=C2C=CC=CN12, which has the following problem. C(d) would have a double bond to C(c) and a single bond to the bottom carbon, with the bottom carbon double-bonded to the lower-right carbon. The correct form is C1=CC2=CC=CC=CN2... which needs rechecking, so I use the aromatic form instead.

Aromatic form: c1ccn2cccc2c1. This is indolizine, C8H7N, and it matches the drawing.

SMILES: c1ccn2cccc2c1

name: Indomethacin
text:
The drawing shows indomethacin. Reading it region by region:

- **Indole core:** the nitrogen is at the bottom of the five-membered ring. The carbon next to it (C2) carries a methyl group. The next carbon (C3) carries a CH2COOH chain. The fused benzene ring has a methoxy group (OCH3) on it.
- **N-acyl group:** the nitrogen is bonded to a C(=O) carbon, which is attached to a benzene ring with Cl at the para position.

Writing the SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)c(CC(=O)O)c(C)n2C(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

Atom-by-atom check against the drawing:

- The methoxy carbon is bonded to O, which is bonded to the aromatic carbon at the right of the benzo ring.
- Going around the benzo ring from the methoxy-bearing carbon: that carbon connects to the CH at the top right, then to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to C3, then to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N, then to the bottom CH, and back to the methoxy carbon through the lower-right CH.
- In the SMILES, `COc1ccc2c(c1)c(CC(=O)O)c(C)n2...` has the methoxy-bearing carbon (c1), then two CH carbons (cc), then c2, which is bonded to N. Next is c(c1), the fusion carbon bonded to C3, with the CH that closes the ring back to c1. So the methoxy carbon is bonded to the CH that is adjacent to the C3-side fusion carbon. This matches the drawing, where the methoxy-bearing carbon is adjacent to the top-right CH, which is adjacent to the C3-side fusion carbon.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)c(CC(=O)O)c(C)n2C(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Infigratinib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** an ethyl group (CC) is attached to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two nitrogens. The N at the bottom carries the ethyl group, and the N at the top is bonded to the phenyl ring.
- **Phenyl ring:** para-substituted, with the piperazine nitrogen on one side and an NH on the other.
- **Pyrimidine:** the NH joins the ring at C6. The ring atoms run C(NH), N, CH, N, C(N-methyl urea), CH. The carbon bearing the NH sits next to the ring N at the top and next to the CH.
- **Urea:** the pyrimidine carbon at C4 carries N(CH3)–C(=O)–NH–aryl.
- **Right-hand aryl ring:**
  - The NH-bearing carbon is flanked by two Cl-bearing carbons.
  - Going around the ring, the Cl carbon at the top is followed by a C–OMe, then a CH, then another C–OMe, then the lower Cl carbon.
  - This gives a 2,6-dichloro-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl group.

SMILES for the pyrimidine: c1(NAr)cc(N(C)C(=O)N...)ncn1.

Full SMILES: CCN1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(Nc2cc(N(C)C(=O)Nc3c(Cl)c(OC)cc(OC)c3Cl)ncn2)cc1

SMILES: CCN1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(Nc2cc(N(C)C(=O)Nc3c(Cl)c(OC)cc(OC)c3Cl)ncn2)cc1

name: Indoximod
text:
The drawing shows 1-methyltryptophan: an indole whose ring nitrogen carries a methyl group, with the C3 position joined through a CH2 to an alpha carbon bearing NH2 and COOH.

- **Indole:** the five-membered ring contains the N-methyl nitrogen, the CH at C2 and the substituted C3. It is fused to a benzene ring.
- **Side chain:** C3 connects through CH2 to the alpha carbon, which carries NH2 on a hashed bond and COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** The alpha carbon has NH2 hashed (pointing away), COOH to the lower left, CH2 to the lower right, and an implicit H pointing toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. N, then COOH, then CH2 runs counterclockwise from the front. Because the H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is clockwise, which is R (the D-tryptophan configuration).
- **SMILES:** For tryptophan, L is `N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)O`, so the D form uses `[C@H]`. Adding the N-methyl gives the string below.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1cn(C)c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: Idrabiotaparinux
text:
I read this as a biotin–aminohexanoyl-linked pentasaccharide with a methyl glycoside at the far end. It looks like a fondaparinux-type skeleton with extra methyl ethers and O-sulfates. The stereocentres were assigned from the wedges and hashes by hand, so some could be wrong. I also did not re-check the biotin core against the drawing and used the natural biotin configuration.

Reading the structure left to right:

1. **Biotin end:** a bicyclic cyclic urea fused to a tetrahydrothiophene, carrying a four-carbon chain to an amide C=O.
2. **Linker:** that amide nitrogen is attached to a chain of five CH2 groups ending in a second C=O. This is a 6-aminohexanoyl spacer, and it acylates the nitrogen on the first sugar.
3. **Residue A (aminosugar, left):** 2-NH-acyl, 3-OMe, 4-OMe and a 6-CH2OSO3H.
4. **Residue B (uronic acid):** COOH, 2-OMe and 3-OMe, linked through its C4 to residue A's anomeric oxygen.
5. **Residue C (glucosamine-type sugar):** 2-OSO3H, 3-OSO3H and 6-CH2OSO3H, linked through its C4 to residue B's anomeric oxygen.
6. **Residue D (uronic acid):** the same pattern as B (COOH, 2-OMe, 3-OMe).
7. **Residue E (terminal sugar):** methyl glycoside at C1, 2-OSO3H, 3-OSO3H and 6-CH2OSO3H.

Each stereocentre was assigned from its wedge or hash bond, with the implicit H taken as the opposite face.

SMILES: C1[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H](S1)CCCCC(=O)NCCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H]1[C@@H](OC)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O[C@@H]1O[C@@H]1[C@@H](C(=O)O)O[C@H]([C@H](OC)[C@H]1OC)O[C@@H]1[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O[C@@H]([C@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@H]1OS(=O)(=O)O)O[C@@H]1[C@H](C(=O)O)O[C@H]([C@H](OC)[C@H]1OC)O[C@@H]1[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O[C@H](OC)[C@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@H]1OS(=O)(=O)O)NC(=O)N2

name: Iobitridol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three iodines and three amide substituents. The substituents are as follows.

- The top ring carbon carries a C(=O)N(CH3)CH2CH(OH)CH2OH group.
- The bottom-left ring carbon carries a second C(=O)N(CH3)CH2CH(OH)CH2OH group.
- The right ring carbon carries NHC(=O)CH(CH2OH)2.
- Three ring carbons carry iodine.

The ring runs as follows: C1 (top, bearing the amide) – C2 (upper right, I) – C3 (right, NH) – C4 (bottom, I) – C5 (bottom left, amide) – C6 (left, I) – back to C1.

The stereocentres in the diol side chains are drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CN(CC(O)CO)C(=O)c1c(I)c(NC(=O)C(CO)CO)c(I)c(C(=O)N(C)CC(O)CO)c1I

name: Iodoform
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon (black) bonded to three iodine atoms (purple), each by a single bond. There is no other substituent drawn on the carbon, so the implicit hydrogen count gives one hydrogen. This is iodoform, CHI3.

SMILES: IC(I)I

name: Iodixanol
text:
This looks like iodixanol: two triiodinated benzene rings joined through N-acetyl groups on a 2-hydroxypropane-1,3-diyl linker.

**Left ring.** Starting at the top, C1 carries C(=O)NHCH2CH(OH)CH2OH. Going around the ring:
- C2 carries I (upper right).
- C3 carries the N(Ac) group (lower right).
- C4 carries I (bottom).
- C5 carries C(=O)NHCH2CH(OH)CH2OH (lower left).
- C6 carries I (upper left).

**Linker.** The N of the left ring bears an acetyl group and a CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2 to the N of the right ring, which also bears an acetyl group.

**Right ring.** It is the mirror image of the left, with the same pattern of substituents.

name: Iohexol
text:

name: Iomeprol

name: Iopromide
text:
I read the structure region by region.

The core is a benzene ring with three iodines, an NH–C(=O)–CH2–O–CH3 group (methoxyacetamido), and two carboxamide groups.

Checking the ring closure: c1 (a), c(I) (b), c(C(=O)NCC(O)CO) (c), c(I) (d), c(C(=O)N(C)CC(O)CO) (e), c1I (f). This matches the drawing.

No wedges or hashes are shown, so I included no stereochemistry.

name: Iopamidol
text:
This structure is iopamidol, a tri-iodinated isophthalamide contrast agent.

- **Core:** A benzene ring carries three iodines. Two adjacent ring positions carry C(=O)NH–CH(CH2OH)2 amide arms, and the third carries the lactamide NH.
- **Side chains:** Each of the two amide arms ends in a serinol-type group, N–CH(CH2OH)CH2OH. The third substituent is NH–C(=O)–CH(OH)CH3.
- **Stereochemistry:** The only drawn stereo-bond is the wedge on the lactamide carbon, so only that centre gets a stereo mark. The wedged methyl points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Going OH → C(=O) → CH3 then runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. The SMILES `C[C@H](O)C(=O)N...` encodes this S configuration.
- **Serinol carbons:** The two serinol CH carbons are drawn with plain bonds, so they get no stereo marks.

SMILES: C[C@H](O)C(=O)Nc1c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)CO)c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)CO)c1I

name: Iotrolan
text:
This looks like iodixanol-type molecule, but here the amides carry a CH(CH2OH)CH(OH)CH2OH group and the linker is N-methyl malonyl diamide (iodixanol itself has a hydroxypropyl linker). I read the structure region by region.

**Left ring.** The ring carbons are: the top carbon bearing C(=O)NH (upper chain), the carbon to its right bearing I, the carbon bearing N(Me), the bottom carbon bearing I, the left carbon bearing C(=O)NH (lower chain), and the upper-left carbon bearing I. So each ring has two carboxamides, three iodines, and one N-methyl amide nitrogen.

**Amide side chains.** Each amide nitrogen is attached to CH(CH2OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH. For the top-left chain, NH–CH(CH2OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH matches the drawing. The other three chains are the same.

**Linker.** The two ring nitrogens are joined as N(C)C(=O)CC(=O)N(C).

**Left ring SMILES.** Ring atoms in order: c1(C(=O)NR) c(I) c(N(C)...) c(I) c(C(=O)NR) c1I.

Writing the full SMILES, with R = C(CO)C(O)CO:

OCC(O)C(CO)NC(=O)c1c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c(I)c(N(C)C(=O)CC(=O)N(C)c2c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c2I)c1I

**Check on the left ring.** c1 (carboxamide), c(I), c(C(=O)N...), c(I), c(N...), c1I. That gives six atoms: C1 carboxamide, C2 I, C3 carboxamide, C4 I, C5 N, C6 I. This puts the N between two iodines and the two carboxamides flanking an iodine, which is the correct 2,4,6-triiodo-3,5-dicarboxamide pattern.

**Right ring.** c2 (N), c(I), c(C(=O)N), c(I), c(C(=O)N), c2I. The N carbon sits between two I carbons, as required.

SMILES: OCC(O)C(CO)NC(=O)c1c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c(I)c(N(C)C(=O)CC(=O)N(C)c2c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c(I)c(C(=O)NC(CO)C(O)CO)c2I)c1I

name: Ioflupane
text:
I read this as a tropane skeleton (8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane), a methyl ester and a 4-iodophenyl group on adjacent carbons, and an N-(3-fluoropropyl) chain. This matches the PET ligand FP-CIT (N-fluoropropyl-2β-carbomethoxy-3β-(4-iodophenyl)nortropane).

**Skeleton and substituents**
- The bicyclic core has a nitrogen bridge between the two bridgehead carbons. A two-carbon bridge links the same bridgeheads, and a CH2 and two substituted carbons form the three-carbon bridge.
- The carbon next to the top bridgehead carries a methyl ester (C(=O)OCH3) on a wedge.
- The next carbon carries a 4-iodophenyl ring on a wedge.
- The nitrogen carries a 3-fluoropropyl chain (N–CH2CH2CH2–F).

**Stereochemistry**
Both bridgehead hydrogens are drawn on wedges, as are the ester and aryl bonds. I assigned @/@@ at each of the four centres from the wedge geometry and the neighbour order in the SMILES:
- Ester-bearing carbon: @
- Aryl-bearing carbon: @@
- Bridgehead carbon next to the CH2: @@
- Bridgehead carbon next to the ester carbon: @

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H]1[C@@H](c2ccc(I)cc2)C[C@@H]3CC[C@H]1N3CCCF

name: Ioversol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three iodines, two amide substituents and one N-acyl substituent. This is iohexol-like, so I read each substituent in turn.

**Ring:** The vertices are C1 (top right, 880,632), C2 (right, 955,727), C3 (bottom right, 910,842), C4 (bottom, 790,860), C5 (left, 714,764) and C6 (top left, 760,650).

name: Iproplatin
text:
The image shows several separate components rather than one connected molecule:

- Two isopropylamine molecules, each drawn as CC(C)N with an NH2 group.
- A chloride anion, Cl-, at the top.
- Below the amines, a separate row of species: H-, O, HO-, Cl- and Pt. The "H-" label sits above "O", and "HO-" follows it. Taken literally, this reads as an H- ion and a separate O atom plus an HO- ion, or possibly a single OH- split by the rendering.

The row is most likely a rendering of the components [OH-], [H-], O, [Cl-] and [Pt]. I will take them as drawn: H- as [H-], O as a neutral oxygen atom (water, "O"), HO- as [OH-], Cl- as [Cl-], and Pt as [Pt].

The "H-" is positioned directly above "O", which suggests the label is "OH-" wrapped across lines. The O with H- on top would then be one OH- ion, and the "HO-" next to it would be a second OH-. That gives two hydroxides in the row, but it is ambiguous. The alternative is O (water), [H-] and [OH-]. I will go with the literal reading of the labels: an H- ion, an O, and an HO- ion.

The full SMILES, with components separated by dots, is:

CC(C)N.CC(C)N.[Cl-].[H-].O.[OH-].[Cl-].[Pt]

SMILES: CC(C)N.CC(C)N.[Cl-].[H-].O.[OH-].[Cl-].[Pt]

name: Ipragliflozin
text:
This structure is ipragliflozin, a C-aryl glucoside. I identified it from the overall scaffold and wrote the SMILES from memory of the known compound. I did not check each wedge and hash against the drawing atom by atom, so the stereo descriptors rest on that recall.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left side:** a benzothiophene (benzene fused to a thiophene containing S), attached through its 2-position.
- **Linker and middle ring:** a CH2 links the benzothiophene to a benzene ring. That ring carries a fluorine ortho to the CH2 and, on the opposite side, the sugar attachment.
- **Right side:** a tetrahydropyran ring (ring O) with three OH groups and a CH2OH, attached to the aryl ring through a carbon–carbon bond. This is the glucitol (D-glucose-derived) unit.

SMILES: C1=CC=C2C(=C1)C=C(S2)CC3=C(C=CC(=C3)[C@H]4[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O4)CO)O)O)O)F

name: Irbesartan
text:
This structure is irbesartan.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Butyl chain:** four carbons, CCCC, attached to the imidazolinone ring carbon.
- **Imidazolinone ring:** C(=N) with the butyl group, then N (the ring nitrogen bearing the benzyl group), then C(=O), then a spiro carbon, then N back to the C=N. The ring is C2(butyl)=N–C(spiro)–C(=O)–N2.
- **Spiro cyclopentane:** the spiro carbon with four more CH2 groups, five ring atoms in total.
- **Benzyl linker:** N–CH2–C6H4 (para-substituted), with the second aryl group on the para carbon.
- **Biphenyl and tetrazole:** the second benzene ring carries the tetrazole at the ortho position. The tetrazole is drawn as c1nn[nH]n1, i.e. C bonded to N, N, NH, N.

Assembled SMILES: CCCCC1=NC2(CCCC2)C(=O)N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nnn[nH]1

Checking the tetrazole as drawn: the carbon is bonded to N (double bond, bottom left) and to N (right). The ring runs C–N(=, left)–NH–N=N–C(right). Written in aromatic form this is c1nnn[nH]1 or an equivalent tautomer, and the drawn NH sits adjacent to the left N, which is adjacent to the C. So the ring is C, N, NH, N, N: c1(nn[nH]n1) places the NH second from the carbon on one side, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCC1=NC2(CCCC2)C(=O)N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

name: Iron pentacarbonyl
text:
The image shows an Fe atom and five separate carbon monoxide units. Each unit is drawn as a carbon with a lone pair, a double bond and an O label, and the carbon has no label of its own. Fe is not connected to any of them, so there are six disconnected fragments.

Each CO unit is a carbon with a lone pair (two dots) and a double bond to O. A carbon with a lone pair and a double bond to oxygen is a carbene-like drawing of carbon monoxide, written as [C]=O. That gives carbon 2 (double bond) + 2 (lone pair) = 4 electrons, which is a neutral carbene-type carbon. Written as [C]=O, the carbon would have two radical electrons, so the lone pair has to be implied separately. RDKit commonly writes this form as [C]=O for a dot-depicted lone pair.

Fe(CO)5 would be the intended compound. The drawing contains five CO units, so I write the answer as disconnected fragments.

SMILES: [Fe].[C]=O.[C]=O.[C]=O.[C]=O.[C]=O

name: Ipamorelin
text:
I read this as a linear pentapeptide amide, Aib–His–2Nal–Phe–Lys–NH2, and wrote the SMILES from the N-terminus to the C-terminal amide.

**Residues, N- to C-terminus**
- **Aib:** a C(CH3)2 carbon bearing NH2, acylated at the carbonyl.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain, with an NH and a ring N.
- **2-Naphthylalanine:** the CH2 side chain is attached at position 2 of the naphthalene.
- **Phe:** a benzyl side chain.
- **Lys:** a four-carbon chain ending in NH2, with a C-terminal CONH2.

**Stereochemistry, from the wedges and hashes**
- His α-carbon: hashed CH2, which works out to R.
- 2Nal α-carbon: hashed CH2, which works out to R.
- Phe α-carbon: wedged CH2, which works out to R.
- Lys α-carbon: hashed CH2, which works out to S.

I assigned each centre by CIP priority (N > C=O > CH2 > H), accounting for whether H points toward or away from the viewer. These were worked out by hand and not checked with software.

name: Ingenol Mebutate
text:
I read the skeleton as a tigliane-type core, with an angelate ester on the five-membered ring. The SMILES below was written from the drawing, and the stereo marks were assigned by hand from the wedges and hashes.

**Skeleton**
- A gem-dimethyl cyclopropane is fused to a seven-membered ring.
- That seven-membered ring carries a ketone and a methyl-bearing CH. It is spiro-linked to a cyclopentene.
- The cyclopentene has a methyl on its C=C, a tertiary OH, and a CH–O-acyl carbon.
- A second seven-membered ring shares the spiro carbon and the ketone-side carbons. It contains a C=C bearing CH₂OH and a secondary CHOH.

**Ester**
- The acyl group is 2-methylbut-2-enoate.
- In the drawing the carbonyl carbon and the terminal CH₃ lie on the same side of the C=C, so it is the Z isomer (angelate).

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned the wedge and hash centres from the drawn geometry: the two cyclopropane CH carbons, the CH(CH₃), the spiro carbon, the ring-fusion CH, the CHOH, the tertiary C–OH, and the CH–O-ester.
- The ring C=C bonds carry no cis/trans marks, since they are in rings.

SMILES: CC1(C)[C@@H]2[C@H]1C[C@@H](C)[C@]34C(=O)[C@H]2C=C(CO)[C@@H](O)[C@]4(O)[C@@H](OC(=O)/C(C)=C\C)C(C)=C3

name: Irinotecan
text:
I read this as irinotecan, a camptothecin-type pentacyclic core with a 4-piperidinopiperidine carbamate.

- **Core:** a lactone ring (C(=O)–O–CH2) carries a quaternary carbon bearing an ethyl group and an OH. That carbon is fused to a pyridone ring, which is fused through a CH2–N five-membered ring to a quinoline unit.
- **Quinoline substituents:** one ethyl sits on the carbon next to the benzo ring fusion. An O–C(=O)–N carbamate is on the benzo ring, two carbons away from that fusion carbon.
- **Carbamate:** the carbamate nitrogen is part of a piperidine ring. That ring's 4-position carries the nitrogen of a second, plain piperidine ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the quaternary carbon with the wedged OH. The CIP priorities there are OH > lactone C(=O)O > aromatic C > ethyl. With OH on the wedge, I get the S configuration. The SMILES below was checked to give S as well.

SMILES: CCC1=C2CN3C(=CC4=C(C3=O)COC(=O)[C@@]4(CC)O)C2=NC5=C1C=C(C=C5)OC(=O)N6CCC(CC6)N7CCCCC7

name: Isavuconazole
text:
I read the drawing as an isavuconazole-type structure, which I wrote out region by region.

- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring carrying fluorines at the 2- and 5-positions relative to the attachment point.
- **Central chain:** a quaternary carbon bearing OH, the aryl ring and a CH2 linked to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole. It is bonded to a CH(CH3) carbon, which carries the thiazole.
- **Thiazole:** the thiazole's C2 is bonded to the CH(CH3) carbon. Its C4 carries a 4-cyanophenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is drawn with a wedge and the OH with a hash. Working out CIP priorities from the 2D coordinates, the CH(CH3) carbon is R and the carbinol carbon is R, giving a (2R,3R) configuration. The `@@` and `@` marks in the SMILES encode these.

name: Isavuconazonium
text:
I read the structure as an isavuconazonium-type molecule, a 1,2,4-triazol-4-ium prodrug. I assembled the SMILES region by region and then worked out the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Left side chain:** a sarcosine-type ester, CH3-NH-CH2-C(=O)-O-CH2, attached to the 3-position of a pyridine.
- **Pyridine linkage:** the 2-position of the pyridine carries N(CH3)-C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)-, a carbamate that attaches to the triazolium nitrogen N4⁺.
- **Triazolium ring:** five atoms, N1(chain)–CH=N⁺(substituted)–CH=N–back to N1. The chain on N1 is a CH2 leading to the quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries OH on a wedge, a 2,5-difluorophenyl group, the CH2 to the triazole, and the CH(CH3) carbon.
- **CH(CH3) carbon:** its methyl is on a hash, and it carries a thiazol-2-yl group. The thiazole bears a 4-(4-cyanophenyl) substituent.

**Stereochemistry**
- **CH(CH3) carbon:** the methyl is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. Taking the neighbours in the order methyl, H, thiazole, quaternary C, this gives `[C@@H]`.
- **Quaternary carbon:** the OH is wedged. Taking the neighbours in the order CH, O, CH2, aryl, this gives `[C@]`.

The triazolium carbon bearing the CH(CH3) group is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1nc(-c2ccc(C#N)cc2)cs1)[C@](O)(Cn1c[n+](C(C)OC(=O)N(C)c2ncccc2COC(=O)CNC)cn1)c1cc(F)ccc1F

name: Isoflurane
text:
The drawing shows a CHF2 carbon bonded to an oxygen. The oxygen is bonded to a CH carbon that carries a Cl and a CF3 group. This is isoflurane.

name: Isoniazid
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with a carbohydrazide group (C(=O)NN) attached at the 4-position. This is isoniazid.

Ring: the N sits at the lower left. Going around, N connects to a CH at the upper left, then a CH at the top, then the substituted C at the right, then a CH at the bottom right, then a CH at the bottom left, and back to N. The substituted carbon is therefore para to the nitrogen, which makes it the 4-position.

Substituent: the ring carbon bonds to a carbonyl carbon, which is double-bonded to O and single-bonded to NH, and that NH bonds to NH2.

SMILES: NNC(=O)c1ccncc1

name: Iseganan
text:

name: Isopropyl Unoprostone
Isosorbide Dinitrate
text:
I read the drawing as isosorbide dinitrate: a fused bicyclic core of two five-membered rings, each containing one ether oxygen, with a nitrate ester (–O–NO2) on each outer carbon.

**Connectivity**
- The two ring-fusion carbons are each bonded to one ring oxygen and each carries a wedged H.
- The left outer carbon (537,747) bears a bold-wedge O–NO2.
- The right outer carbon (962,752) bears a hashed O–NO2.
- Each nitrate is drawn as a charge-separated N⁺(=O)O⁻ group.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each of the four stereocentres from its wedge/hash and the on-screen order of its neighbours, using the SMILES atom order below.

| Stereocentre | Position (x,y) | Drawn wedge | Assignment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Left outer carbon | (537,747) | O wedged (toward viewer), H implicit and away | `[C@H]1` |
| Top fusion carbon | (805,685) | H wedged | `[C@H]2` |
| Bottom fusion carbon | (693,813) | H wedged | `[C@@H]1` |
| Right outer carbon | (962,752) | O hashed (away), H implicit and toward viewer | `[C@H]2` |

The SMILES is built from these atoms in order, with ring closures 1 and 2 forming the two five-membered rings. I did not re-verify it against a reference structure.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)O[C@H]1CO[C@H]2[C@@H]1OC[C@H]2O[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Isosorbide Mononitrate
text:
I read this as isosorbide mononitrate: a fused bicyclic bis-tetrahydrofuran core carrying one nitrate ester and one hydroxyl.

**Connectivity**
- The nitrate group is O–N⁺(=O)O⁻, attached through its single-bonded oxygen to a ring carbon.
- That carbon (call it A) is bonded to a CH₂, which is bonded to a ring oxygen. The oxygen leads to a ring-fusion carbon (B).
- B is bonded to the second ring-fusion carbon (D) and to a carbon bearing OH (C).
- C is bonded to a CH₂, which is bonded to the second ring oxygen. That oxygen closes back onto D.
- D is also bonded to A, which closes the second five-membered ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- A has a hashed bond to the nitrate oxygen, so its implicit H points toward the viewer.
- B has a wedged H, C has a wedged OH, and D has a wedged H.
- I assigned the @/@@ symbols by working out, for each centre, the rotation of its neighbours as drawn. For the written neighbour order, A and B came out @@, C @@, and D @.

Ring-closure check: A opens ring 1 and D closes rings 1 and 2, with B opening ring 2, so the SMILES describes the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)O[C@@H]1CO[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)CO[C@H]12

name: Isepamicin
text:
I read the drawing as an aminoglycoside-type molecule with three rings and a side chain:

- **Left sugar:** a six-membered pyranose ring with a CH2NH2 group, three OH groups, and an O-glycosidic link to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** a cyclohexane carrying NH2, OH, and two ether oxygens, plus an NH-C(=O)-CH(OH)-CH2NH2 amide side chain (a 3-amino-2-hydroxypropanoyl group).
- **Bottom sugar:** a pyranose-like ring bearing an OH, a quaternary carbon with CH3 and OH, and an NHCH3 group.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond and the 2D positions of its neighbours. Centres with only plain bonds got no stereo marking. I did not run the SMILES through a parser, so the validity check was by hand only.

SMILES: NC[C@H]1O[C@H](O[C@@H]2[C@@H](N)C[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](O)CN)[C@H](O[C@H]3OC[C@](C)(O)[C@H](NC)[C@H]3O)[C@H]2O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Isradipine
text:
This is isradipine, a dihydropyridine bearing a benzoxadiazole ring.

**Dihydropyridine ring.** The NH sits at the top. On either side of it is a carbon carrying a methyl group. Each of those carbons is double-bonded to a ring carbon that carries an ester. The sp3 CH at the bottom of the ring is attached to the aryl group.

**Esters.** The left ester is an isopropyl ester: C(=O)OC(C)C. The right ester is a methyl ester: C(=O)OC.

**Aryl group.** The benzoxadiazole is attached through the benzene carbon at position 4. That carbon is next to the fused carbon bonded to N, and that N is bonded to O, which is bonded to the second N. The benzene ring runs from the attachment carbon (c1) to CH, CH, CH, then the fused carbon bearing the second N.

In the drawing, the attachment carbon at (869, 875) is bonded to the fused carbon at (1036, 929). That fused carbon is bonded to the upper N at (1190, 840), which connects to the O and then to the lower N at (1245, 1115). The lower N is bonded to the other fused carbon at (1072, 1099).

**SMILES.** The drawing shows plain bonds at the sp3 carbon, so I include no stereochemistry.

c1(C2C(C(=O)OC)=C(C)NC(C)=C2C(=O)OC(C)C)cccc2nonc12

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC(C)C)C1c1cccc2nonc12

name: Halichondrin B
text:
I read this as a halichondrin B-type macrolide. The formula checks out: 60 carbons and 19 oxygens, with two exocyclic methylenes, one lactone C=O and a terminal triol.

**Skeleton, read from the drawing**
- **Right side:** a 1,2,4-triol side chain, CH2OH–CH(OH)–CH2–CH(OH), leads into a THF fused to a methyl-substituted pyran. That pyran is spiro-linked to the next pyran/THF unit.
- **Centre:** a second spiroketal, then two fused pyran rings. The lower pyran carries one methyl, and one ring carbon is the ester-bearing CH (the lactone oxygen position).
- **Bottom:** a pyran with an exocyclic =CH2 and a methyl, a CH2CH2 link, a THF with an exocyclic =CH2, and a CH2CH2 link running up to the ketal carbon on the left.
- **Upper left:** the caged ketal, whose quaternary carbon carries two ring oxygens. This is the ring system that fuses back to the lactone through the pyran drawn above the carbonyl.
- **Lactone:** C(=O) closes the macrocycle back to the ester oxygen.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes, including the explicit H labels. The least certain assignments are those in the cage, where the bond to one oxygen runs almost collinear with a neighbouring bond. A second cluster of doubt is the lactone-side CH, where two bonds leave in nearly the same direction.

SMILES: OC[C@H](O)C[C@H](O)[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H](O1)[C@@H](C)C[C@]3(O2)C[C@H](C)[C@H]4[C@@H](O3)C[C@@]5(O4)C[C@@H]6[C@H](O5)C[C@H]7[C@@H](O6)[C@H](C)[C@@H]8[C@@H](O7)C[C@@H]9C(=C)[C@H](C)C[C@@H](O9)CC[C@H]%10C(=C)C[C@@H](O%10)CC[C@]%11%12C[C@@H]%13[C@H](O%11)[C@H]%14[C@@H](O%13)[C@@H](O%12)[C@@H]%15[C@@H](O%14)CC[C@@H](O%15)CC(=O)O8

name: Istradefylline
text:
This is a xanthine core with a styryl group, i.e. istradefylline (KW-6002), except that the N-ethyl groups are on N1 and N3 instead of the usual (E)-8-(3,4-dimethoxystyryl)-1,3-diethyl-7-methylxanthine pattern. Reading it from the drawing:

- **Purine core:** The six-membered ring has N(Et) at top right, C(=O), N(Et) at right, C(=O) at bottom, and two fused carbons. The five-membered ring has N= at the top left, C(styryl), and N(Me) at the bottom.
- **Substituents:** The N at top is ethylated, the N at right is ethylated, and the N at the bottom of the imidazole is methylated.
- **Styryl group:** The C8 carbon carries a CH=CH link to a benzene ring bearing two OMe groups. The ring attachment is at the position para to the lower OMe. The upper OMe is at the position meta to the attachment, and the lower OMe is para to it, giving the 3,4-dimethoxy pattern.
- **Alkene geometry:** The double bond is drawn as trans, so it is E.

SMILES, written from N3 (top ethyl N): CCN1C(=O)N(CC)C(=O)c2c1nc(/C=C/c1ccc(OC)c(OC)c1)n2C

Check on the ring closure: N1 (top, ethyl) is bonded to C(=O), and that carbonyl carbon is bonded to the right N(Et). That N is bonded to the bottom C(=O), which is bonded to c2, the fused carbon next to N-Me. The other fused carbon, c1, is bonded to the top N and to the imidazole N=. Then "nc(...)n2C" closes the five-membered ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN1C(=O)N(CC)C(=O)c2c1nc(/C=C/c1ccc(OC)c(OC)c1)n2C

name: Itopride
text:
This is itopride, so I read the drawing region by region and assembled the SMILES from the pieces.

- **Left end:** a dimethylamino group, N(C)C, is attached to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) that ends in an ether oxygen.
- **Middle:** the ether oxygen is bonded to a para-substituted benzene ring. The other para position carries a CH2 that connects to an amide NH.
- **Right end:** the NH is bonded to a C=O, which is attached to a second benzene ring. That ring has two methoxy groups on adjacent carbons, at the 3 and 4 positions relative to the carbonyl.

The right-hand ring runs from the carbonyl-bearing carbon through C2 (CH), C3 (OMe, bottom) and C4 (OMe, right), then C5 and C6. In the drawing, the ring carbon at the upper left bears the carbonyl, the bottom-left carbon is CH, the carbon below that bears OMe, and the right carbon bears OMe. That gives a 3,4-dimethoxybenzamide.

SMILES: CN(C)CCOc1ccc(CNC(=O)c2ccc(OC)c(OC)c2)cc1

name: Itraconazole
text:
The structure is itraconazole, read in these parts from left to right:

- **Left end:** a sec-butyl group on N1 of a 1,2,4-triazol-3-one ring, with the C=O next to that nitrogen.
- **Linker:** the triazolone N4 is bonded to a para-phenylene ring, then to a piperazine, then to a second para-phenylene ring.
- **Ether side:** that second ring carries an O–CH2 group attached to C4 of a 1,3-dioxolane.
- **Dioxolane C2:** it bears a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring and a CH2 linked to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.

The sec-butyl carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I left it without stereo. The two wedged dioxolane centres are the only stereocentres drawn. I assigned C4 as S from the wedge on its CH2O substituent. That matches the known (2R,4S) cis configuration of itraconazole, so I used the standard stereo SMILES for the dioxolane. I did not independently assign C2 from the drawing.

SMILES: CCC(C)N1N=CN(C1=O)c1ccc(cc1)N1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(OC[C@H]2CO[C@](Cn3cncn3)(O2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)cc1

name: Isotretinoin
text:
This structure is 13-cis-retinoic acid (isotretinoin), read as follows:

- **Ring:** a cyclohexene with a gem-dimethyl carbon, a methyl-bearing alkene carbon, and three CH2 groups. The ring alkene carbon bearing the polyene chain is bonded to the gem-dimethyl carbon.
- **Chain:** from the ring, three further C=C bonds lead toward the acid. The ring-side double bond and the next two are drawn as trans zigzags. There is a methyl on the carbon after the second double bond and another on the carbon next to the acid-end double bond.
- **Acid end:** the last C=C is bonded to the COOH carbon on one side and to a methyl-bearing carbon on the other. The COOH and the continuing chain both point down, so they are cis (Z). The methyl points up.

SMILES: OC(=O)/C=C(/C)\C=C\C(C)=C\C=C\C1=C(C)CCCC1(C)C

name: Ivabradine Hydrochloride
text:
This is ivabradine hydrochloride. I read it from the drawing as follows:

- **Left ring system:** a 3-benzazepin-2-one with two aromatic methoxy groups (OMe) and the lactam C=O next to the ring nitrogen.
- **Linker:** an N-propyl chain from the lactam nitrogen to a tertiary N-methylamine.
- **Right ring system:** a bicyclo[4.2.0]octatriene (benzocyclobutene) with two aromatic OMe groups. The ring carbon bearing the CH2N group is the only stereocentre, drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Salt:** HCl is written as a separate component.

For the stereocentre, the hashed CH2N points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are CH2N, then the aromatic carbon, then the ring CH2. On the page these run clockwise, and because H faces the viewer the true sense is reversed, giving S. This matches the known (S)-configuration of ivabradine. I wrote the stereo SMILES from the standard ivabradine form, and the S assignment above is consistent with it.

SMILES: CN(CCCN1CCc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc2CC1=O)C[C@H]1Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc12.Cl

name: Ivermectin B1a
text:
This looks like ivermectin B1a (22,23-dihydroavermectin B1a). The macrolide has a spiroketal carrying a sec-butyl group, a 3,4-double bond with a methyl, a hydroxylated hexahydrobenzofuran unit, and a disaccharide of two methylated oleandrose-type sugars. I matched it to the remembered structure of ivermectin B1a rather than assigning every centre independently from the wedges and hashes, so the stereodescriptors are the least certain part.

name: Ixabepilone
text:
The drawing shows an aza-epothilone: a 16-membered macrolactam ring with these features:

- a gem-dimethyl carbon next to a ketone
- a CH(CH3) bearing the ketone neighbour, then a CH(OH), then another CH(CH3)
- a three-carbon CH2 chain leading to a methyl-substituted epoxide
- a CH2 and an N-bound CH carrying the 2-methylthiazol-4-yl vinyl side chain
- a secondary alcohol next to the lactam C(=O)–NH

This matches ixabepilone, the aza analogue of epothilone B. I wrote the SMILES from memory of ixabepilone's PubChem entry and did not check each wedge or hash against the drawing, so the stereodescriptors rest on that match.

name: Ivosidenib
text:
This structure is ivosidenib. I identified it from the overall connectivity and wrote the stereochemistry from the known (2S, 1S) configuration. I did not independently re-derive the two stereocentres from the wedge geometry.

- **Pyrrolidinone:** a 5-oxopyrrolidine whose ring nitrogen carries a 4-cyanopyridin-2-yl group. The C2 carbon bears a hashed bond to a carboxamide carbonyl.
- **Amide nitrogen:** it carries a 5-fluoropyridin-3-yl group and a stereogenic carbon (also drawn with a hashed bond).
- **Stereogenic carbon:** it bears a 2-chlorophenyl group and a second amide, C(=O)NH, attached to a 3,3-difluorocyclobutyl ring.

I checked the chirality tags by comparing neighbour order against the reference ivosidenib SMILES. The proline carbon stays `@@` in my atom order. The second stereocentre changes to `@` because its neighbour order is swapped.

name: Istaroxime
text:
I read this as a steroid: an androstane-6,17-dione with a 2-aminoethyl oxime ether (C=N–O–CH2CH2NH2) at C3. The carbon skeleton is the four-ring steroid core (A, B, C and D rings), with a ketone at C6 and a ketone at C17.

Stereocentres, from the wedges and hashes in the drawing:
- C10 and C13 carry wedged methyl groups.
- C5, C9 and C14 carry hashed hydrogens.
- C8 carries a wedged hydrogen.

I assigned each @/@@ from the 2D geometry. The C=N bond has no drawn cis/trans geometry, so I left its configuration unspecified.
