name: Ixazomib
text:
I read the molecule as a boronic acid with an isobutyl group, two amide links and a 2,5-dichlorophenyl ring.

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group (CH(CH3)2) is attached to a CH2. That CH2 is joined to the stereocentre by a hashed bond. The stereocentre also carries B(OH)2 and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH is acylated by a C(=O) that connects to a CH2, then to a second NH.
- **Right end:** the second NH is acylated by a C(=O) bonded to a benzene ring. Counting from the carbonyl-bearing ring carbon, one Cl is on the adjacent ring carbon (position 2) and the other is on the carbon para to that one (position 5).
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge or hash is the hashed bond from the stereocentre to the CH2, so the CH2 points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H side, the sequence CH2 → B → N runs counterclockwise. For the SMILES neighbour order (CH2, H, B, N), this corresponds to @@.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@@H](B(O)O)NC(=O)CNC(=O)c1cc(Cl)ccc1Cl

name: Kebuzone
text:
The drawing shows a pyrazolidine-3,5-dione ring: C4, then C(=O), N, N, and C(=O) closing back to C4. Each nitrogen carries a phenyl group. C4 carries a CH2CH2C(=O)CH3 chain, which is the 3-oxobutyl group.

Reading the chain from the left: a methyl carbon, then a carbonyl carbon bearing =O, then CH2, then CH2, then the ring carbon.

The SMILES is CC(=O)CCC1C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N(c2ccccc2)C1=O. The ring closure is consistent: C1 is the ring CH, followed by C(=O), N(Ph), N(Ph), and C1=O closing the five-membered ring.

SMILES: CC(=O)CCC1C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N(c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Ketamine
text:
The drawing shows ketamine, read as follows:

- **Cyclohexanone ring:** six carbons, one of which is a C=O. The quaternary carbon next to the carbonyl carries both an NHCH3 group and the aryl group.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring bonded to the quaternary carbon. A chlorine sits on the ring carbon adjacent to that attachment point (ortho), so it is a 2-chlorophenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are drawn plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is included.

SMILES: CNC1(CCCCC1=O)c1ccccc1Cl

name: Ketoconazole
text:
I read this as the ketoconazole skeleton, with both stereocentres taken from the hashed bonds.

**Skeleton**
- An acetyl group on a piperazine nitrogen (the left end).
- The other piperazine nitrogen bonded to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- That ring carries an O–CH2 link to C4 of a 1,3-dioxolane.
- The dioxolane C2 carries a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring and a CH2 linked to an imidazole N1.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Dioxolane C4:** the hashed bond goes to the CH2O group, so that group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@@H]`.
- **Dioxolane C2 (ketal carbon):** the hashed bond goes to the CH2–imidazole group. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@]`.

I derived both labels from the drawing's geometry rather than from a remembered ketoconazole SMILES. The result may therefore be the enantiomer of the commonly quoted cis-(2S,4R) form.

SMILES: CC(=O)N1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(cc1)OC[C@@H]2CO[C@](Cn3ccnc3)(O2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl

name: Ketoprofen
text:
The drawing shows ketoprofen: a benzoyl group on a benzene ring that also carries a CH(CH3)COOH group, with the two substituents meta to each other.

Checking the central ring: the carbon bearing the C=O is at (651, 738) and the carbon bearing the CH is at (932, 713). Between them is the ring vertex at (798, 806). That puts one carbon between the two substituted carbons, so they are meta, as in ketoprofen.

The CH carbon has plain bonds, so I give it no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1cccc(c1)C(=O)c1ccccc1

name: Ketorolac
text:
This is ketorolac.

Reading the structure region by region:
- The five-membered pyrrole ring contains N, the carbon bearing the benzoyl group, two CH carbons, and the carbon fused to the second ring.
- The second five-membered ring is the pyrrolizine ring. It contains N, the fused pyrrole carbon, the CH bearing COOH, a CH2, and a second CH2 attached to N.
- The benzoyl group is C(=O) attached to a phenyl ring.
- The carboxylic acid is on the sp3 CH, which has no wedge or hash, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

Writing the SMILES:
- OC(=O)C1CCn2c1ccc2C(=O)c1ccccc1
- C1 is the CH bearing the acid, followed by two CH2 groups, then n2 (the nitrogen).
- The next atom, c1, is the fused carbon that closes ring 1 with the CH. It is followed by two CH carbons, then c2, which closes the pyrrole ring to N and carries the benzoyl group.

Atom check for the pyrrole ring: N, c1 (fused), c, c, c2 (bearing the benzoyl) gives 5 atoms, which is correct. The pyrrolizine ring has CH, CH2, CH2, N, c1, which is also 5 atoms.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1CCn2c1ccc2C(=O)c1ccccc1

name: Kojic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring containing one oxygen. This is kojic acid, a pyranone.

Ring atoms, going around:
- O1 (ring oxygen, top left)
- C2, the top-right CH, double bonded to C3
- C3, carrying an OH
- C4, the C=O carbon
- C5, a CH, double bonded to C6
- C6, carrying CH2OH and bonded back to O1

Bonds and substituents:
- The double bond between the top CH (C2) and the OH-bearing carbon (C3) is drawn.
- The double bond between the CH (C5) and the carbon bearing CH2OH (C6) is drawn.
- C4 has the exocyclic C=O.

SMILES: OCC1=CC(=O)C(O)=CO1

name: KP-1019
text:
The image shows several disconnected components: four Cl⁻, one Ru³⁺ with a radical dot, and three indazole units. One of these three has a protonated N (NH⁺).

Indazole in the drawing: c1ccc2c(c1)cn[nH]2. In the picture, N(H) is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon, and N= is bonded to CH, which is bonded to the other fusion carbon.

The upper indazole is written as c1ccc2c(c1)C=NN2, with a Kekulé benzene ring. For the protonated one, the N is [NH+] and the double bond runs C=[NH+].

The lower-left indazole is bonded to N⁺ (drawn as NH⁺) and appears to be adjacent to the lower-right indazole. The two are only close in the drawing, and no bond joins them, so I treat them as separate fragments.

The fragments are:
- [Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-]
- [Ru+3]
- c1ccc2c(c1)C=NN2 (neutral indazole)
- c1ccc2c(c1)C=[NH+]N2 (protonated indazole)
- c1ccc2c(c1)C=NN2 (neutral indazole)

The Ru label carries a radical dot, so I write it as [Ru+3] and omit the dot. The charge sums to +3 − 4 + 1 = 0, which is consistent.

SMILES: [Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-].[Ru+3].C1=CC=C2C(=C1)C=NN2.C1=CC=C2C(=C1)C=[NH+]N2.C1=CC=C2C(=C1)C=NN2

name: L-Alanine
text:
The drawing shows alanine: a central carbon bonded to NH2, a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) and a methyl group, with an implicit hydrogen. The methyl is on a hashed wedge, so it points away from the viewer, and the hydrogen points toward the viewer.

To assign the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH3 > H. Viewed from the front, N (down-right), COOH (left) and CH3 (up-right) run clockwise. Because the hydrogen faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is L-alanine.

SMILES: C[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: Josamycin
text:
I read the drawing as a 16-membered macrolide lactone carrying two sugars, which fits josamycin (leucomycin A3).

**Macrolactone ring**
- It runs lactone C=O, CH2, CH(OAc), CH(OMe), CH(O-sugar), CH(CH2CHO), CH2, CH(CH3), CH(OH), then a CH=CH–CH=CH diene, CH2, CH(CH3) and the ring O.
- Both double bonds are trans (E), judged from the drawn geometry.

**Aminosugar (mycaminose-type)**
- It is linked through the ring oxygen at the CH(O-sugar) carbon.
- It carries a 2'-OH, a 3'-NMe2, a 5'-methyl, and a 4'-O link to the second sugar.

**Second sugar (mycarose-type)**
- It has a 3''-methyl and 3''-OH.
- Its 4''-O is esterified with isovaleryl, C(=O)CH2CH(CH3)2.
- It has a 5''-methyl.

**Stereochemistry**
- Each centre was assigned from its wedge or hash, with the implicit H taking the opposite side.
- I did not cross-check the result against a reference josamycin SMILES.

SMILES: O=C1C[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O[C@@H]2O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]3C[C@@](C)(O)[C@@H](OC(=O)CC(C)C)[C@H](C)O3)[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]2O)[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)/C=C/C=C/C[C@@H](C)O1

name: L-Arginine
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- A carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) is on the left.
- It is attached to the α-carbon, which carries an NH2 on a wedge bond.
- A three-carbon chain (CH2–CH2–CH2) runs from the α-carbon to a nitrogen.
- That nitrogen is double-bonded to a carbon bearing two NH2 groups, which makes a guanidine group.

This is arginine. The only stereocentre is the α-carbon.

For its configuration, the carboxyl carbon is lower left, the wedged NH2 is up and toward the viewer, and the chain CH2 is lower right. The implicit H therefore points away from the viewer. Written as OC(=O)[C@@H](N)CCCN=C(N)N, the neighbour order is COOH, H, N, CH2. With the H at the back, COOH → N → CH2 runs clockwise on the page, which corresponds to @@ in this order. This matches L-arginine.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H](N)CCCN=C(N)N

name: Kahalalide F
text:
I read the molecule as a lipopeptide: a 5-methylhexanoyl chain on a linear peptide that closes into a macrocyclic depsipeptide through a Thr ester bond.

**Linear part, from the acyl tail:**
- 5-Methylhexanoyl, CC(C)CCCC(=O)–
- Val, R at the α-carbon
- Thr, α S and β R, with a free OH
- Val, S
- Val, R
- Pro, drawn as R
- Orn, S, with a free 3-aminopropyl side chain
- Ile, R at the α-carbon and S at the β-carbon

**Macrocycle:**
- Thr, α R and β R. Its β-oxygen forms the ester that closes the ring.
- Ile, R at the α-carbon and S at the β-carbon
- Val, R
- Phe, S
- Dehydrobutyrine (Dhb), with the nitrogen and the methyl on the same side of the double bond, so Z
- Val, S, whose carbonyl is the ester carbonyl closing back onto the Thr β-oxygen

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash on its bond, then converted it to @/@@ by neighbour order. I did not run a SMILES validator on the result.

SMILES: CC(C)CCCC(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](O)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)N/C(=C\C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)O[C@@H]1C

name: L-Ascorbic Acid
text:
This is L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C), read from the drawing as follows.

- **Ring:** a five-membered lactone made of the ring O, a C=O carbon, two enol carbons each bearing an OH and joined by a C=C double bond, and the ring CH (C4).
- **Side chain:** C4 carries a CH(OH)–CH2OH group.
- **Stereocentre at C4:** the wedge runs from C4 to the ring O. With H pointing away, O → side-chain C → ring C3 runs counterclockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (side chain, H, ring closure, O) this gives `[C@H]1`.
- **Stereocentre in the side chain:** the wedge runs to the OH. With H pointing away, CH2 → OH → C4 runs counterclockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (CH2, H, O, C4) this gives `[C@H](O)`.

SMILES: OC[C@H](O)[C@H]1OC(=O)C(O)=C1O

name: L-Aspartic Acid
text:
The drawing shows aspartic acid: a central CH carrying NH2, one COOH group directly attached, and a CH2 leading to a second COOH group.

For stereochemistry, the only stereo bond is the hashed bond to NH2, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. Going N (down) → COOH (upper left) → CH2 (upper right) looks clockwise on the page. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is counterclockwise, which is S (L-aspartic acid).

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: L-Glutamic Acid
text:
The drawing shows glutamic acid: a five-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid at each end and an NH2 on the carbon next to the right-hand COOH.

**Stereochemistry:** The only wedge is the bold bond from that stereocentre to NH2, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are NH2 > COOH > CH2 > H. Going from NH2 (bottom) to COOH (upper right) to CH2 (upper left) turns counterclockwise, which gives the S configuration. This is L-glutamic acid.

The SMILES below is the standard one for L-glutamic acid, which I recalled rather than derived atom by atom.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: L-Glutamine
text:
The drawing shows glutamine: a primary amide (H2N–C=O) at one end, a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) at the other, and two CH2 groups between the amide carbonyl and the central carbon. The central carbon carries an NH2 on a wedge bond and an implicit hydrogen.

To assign the stereocentre, I ranked the substituents by CIP priority: NH2 > COOH > CH2 > H. The wedged NH2 points toward the viewer, so the hydrogen points away. Going from NH2 (bottom) to COOH (upper right) to CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise, which gives S. That matches L-glutamine.

I checked the SMILES stereo tag against L-alanine, N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O, which has the same neighbour order and the same S configuration, so `@@` is correct here.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(O)=O

name: Katanosin B
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic depsipeptide with a two-residue side chain, and traced it around the ring from the ester oxygen.

**Ring (ester O → ring residues, in drawn order):**
- The ring closes through an ester. A β-phenylserine oxygen is acylated by the serine carbonyl.
- Around the ring the residues are: serine (CH₂OH side chain), β-hydroxyasparagine (CH(OH)C(N)=O side chain), glycine (the CH₂ drawn as "C"), threonine, valine, arginine, isoleucine (sec-butyl side chain), β-hydroxyvaline, and then β-phenylserine again.
- The arginine side chain is CH₂CH₂CH₂–N=C(NH₂)₂.

**Exocyclic chain:** the β-phenylserine α-NH carries Leu–Leu. The terminal Leu has a free NH₂ drawn on a hashed bond.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash and the atom positions, with the implicit H taken as pointing away from any wedged or hashed substituent. This gives L-configuration at Ser, Thr, Val, Ile, hydroxyVal and the inner Leu, and D-configuration at Arg and the terminal Leu. The β-carbons of Thr, hydroxyVal, hydroxyAsn and phenylSer were assigned from their own wedges and hashes. The Ile side-chain carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

I checked that the ring-closure digits pair up and that the atoms and bonds match the drawing, but I have not run the SMILES through a parser.

SMILES: N[C@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](c2ccccc2)O3)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](O)C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)CC)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](O)C(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)3

name: L-Histidine
text:
The drawing shows histidine: an imidazole ring joined through a CH2 to an alpha carbon that carries NH2 and COOH.

**Ring:** The ring carbon bearing the CH2 is bonded to the N–H. The other ring atoms run from that N–H to a CH, then to a ring N, then to a second CH that closes back onto the substituted carbon. This gives `Cc1[nH]cnc1`, with the CH2 on the carbon next to the N–H.

**Stereocentre:** The NH2 is on a bold wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. In the drawing, N (down), COOH (upper right) and CH2 (upper left) run counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is the L-histidine configuration.

**SMILES:** Writing the stereocentre as `N[C@@H](...)C(=O)O` with the CH2 branch inside the parentheses gives the S configuration.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1[nH]cnc1)C(=O)O

name: L-Homocysteine
text:
The drawing shows homocysteine: a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH), a stereocentre bearing NH2 on a hashed bond, then two CH2 groups ending in an SH group.

**Stereochemistry:** The stereocentre has NH2 on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2CH2SH > H. Reading N (bottom), then COOH (upper left), then CH2 (upper right) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S. This is L-homocysteine.

The SMILES `N[C@@H](CCS)C(=O)O` has the same chirality pattern as L-alanine, `N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O`, which is also S. It therefore matches the drawing.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CCS)C(=O)O

name: L-Isoleucine
text:
The drawing is isoleucine (2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid): a carboxylic acid carbon, an alpha carbon bearing NH2, and a beta carbon bearing a methyl and an ethyl group.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges:**
- **Alpha carbon:** the NH2 is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The priorities are N > COOH > C-beta. Going N (top) → COOH (lower left) → C-beta (lower right) is counterclockwise, which gives S.
- **Beta carbon:** the methyl is on a hash, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are C-alpha > ethyl > methyl. Going alpha (upper left) → ethyl (right) → methyl (down) is clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise because H faces the viewer, giving S.

This is (2S,3S), i.e. L-isoleucine.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: L-Folinic acid
text:
I read this as 5-formyltetrahydrofolic acid (leucovorin / folinic acid).

- **Glutamate end:** two carboxylic acids, with the alpha carbon bearing the amide NH. The hashed bond points to the CH2 of the side chain. That makes the alpha carbon S, the natural L-glutamate configuration.
- **Linker:** a para-substituted benzene ring, with a C(=O)NH amide on one side and an NH–CH2 on the other.
- **Pterin end:** a tetrahydropteridine ring. N5 carries a formyl group (N–CHO) and is bonded to the carbon next to the ring C=O. The ring also has the lactam NH–C=O, the 2-amino amidine carbon (C(N)=N) and a ring NH–CH2.
- **C6 stereocentre:** the hashed bond goes to the exocyclic CH2 (toward the NH–aryl). Working out the geometry with the implicit H toward the viewer gives `@` for the neighbour order used in the SMILES below.

I checked the SMILES atom by atom against the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)c1ccc(NC[C@H]2CNC3=C(N2C=O)C(=O)NC(N)=N3)cc1

name: L-Leucine
text:
The drawing shows leucine: an isobutyl group (CH3)2CH–CH2– attached to the α-carbon, which carries an NH2 on a wedge bond and a carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH.

For the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are NH2 > COOH > CH2 > H. The wedge puts NH2 toward the viewer, so the implied H points away. Going NH2 (bottom), then COOH (upper right), then CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is L-leucine.

The SMILES CC(C)C[C@H](N)C(=O)O encodes the S configuration, matching the standard L-leucine SMILES.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: L-Methionine
text:
The structure is methionine: CH3–S–CH2–CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH, with a thioether sulfur and a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH).

The only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and the NH2 is on a wedge, so stereochemistry is included. The CIP priorities there are N > COOH > CH2 > H. With the wedged N toward the viewer, H points away. Going N (bottom) → COOH (upper right) → CH2 (upper left) is counterclockwise, which gives S. This matches L-methionine, which is written `CSCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: CSCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: L-Lysine
text:
The drawing shows lysine, written here as the L-enantiomer.

- **Chain:** Starting from the H2N group on the left, there are four chain carbons (vertices at roughly x = 346, 514, 681, 848) before the stereocentre at about x = 1014. That gives four CH2 groups.
- **Stereocentre:** The α-carbon carries a hashed bond to NH2. Its other substituents are the CH2 chain and the carboxylic acid, plus an implicit H.
- **Acid end:** The carbon at about x = 1182 is a carboxylic acid, drawn with C=O and OH.

**Stereochemistry:** The hashed NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. Viewed from the front, N (up) → COOH (lower right) → CH2 (lower left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. S is the L configuration for lysine.

Writing this as SMILES from the chain end gives NCCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O. It is the same as N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O, the usual L-lysine SMILES.

SMILES: NCCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: Kanglemycin A
text:
I read the structure as a rifamycin-type ansamycin. It has a naphthoquinone–furanone core, a macrolactam chain, an acetate, a dimethylsuccinate half-ester and a fused dioxolane sugar.

I assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes, taking H as implicit and on the opposite side from the drawn wedge or hash. I did not re-parse the final SMILES with a toolkit.

**Core.** The aromatic ring carries an OH and a CH3. It is fused to a quinone ring bearing the amide N on one carbon, and to a furanone ring. The furanone has a C=O, an O in the ring, and a CH that bears the exocyclic O.

**Chain.**
- The lactam C(=O) is attached to a C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH diene. Both double bonds are E, judged from the drawn geometry.
- The chain then runs through a CH, a CH(OH), a CH(CH3), a CH(OH), a CH(CH3), a CH(OAc), a CH(CH3) and a CH(O-sugar).
- Next comes an E-vinyl ether –CH=CH–O– to the furanone CH.
- The first CH of the chain also carries a CH(CH3)–O ester.

**Ester.** The ester is O–C(=O)–C(CH3)2–CH2–COOH.

**Sugar.** It is a pyran ring with a CH3, a CH2, and a fused –O–CH2–O– dioxolane.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC(C)(C)C(=O)O[C@H](C)[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(C)/C(=O)NC2=CC(=O)c3c(C2=O)c(O)c(C)c4c3C(=O)[C@H](O4)O/C=C/[C@H](O[C@@H]5C[C@@H]6OCO[C@@H]6[C@H](C)O5)[C@@H](C)[C@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@H]1O

name: L-(-)-Ornithine
text:
Reading the drawing, the molecule is ornithine (2,5-diaminopentanoic acid).

- **Chain:** an H2N group sits on the left end, followed by three CH2/CH carbons, then a carboxylic acid (C=O with OH) on the right end.
- **Side group:** a second NH2 is attached to the carbon next to the carboxyl carbon. It is drawn with a bold wedge, so it points toward the viewer.
- **Stereochemistry:** at this carbon the implicit H is behind the page. Seen from the front, the order CH2 → COOH → NH2 runs clockwise. Written as NCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O, this corresponds to `@`, which is the L-configuration (L-ornithine).

SMILES: NCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: L-p-Boronophenylalanine
text:
The drawing shows 4-boronophenylalanine: a para-substituted benzene ring carrying a B(OH)₂ group on one side and a CH₂–CH(NH₂)–COOH chain on the other.

Stereochemistry: the only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and its NH₂ is drawn on a wedge. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH₂ > H, with H pointing away from the viewer. Going N → COOH → CH₂ runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is the L-amino-acid configuration, which matches the SMILES pattern N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O for L-phenylalanine.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(B(O)O)cc1)C(=O)O

name: L-Phenylalanine
text:
The drawing shows phenylalanine: a benzene ring joined through a CH2 to a stereocentre that carries NH2 and a COOH group.

- **Ring and chain:** I count six aromatic carbons in the ring, then one CH2, then the stereocentre carbon, then the carboxylic acid carbon bearing C=O and OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** The NH2 is on a bold wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2Ph > H. On the page, N (bottom) to COOH (right) to CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise. With H at the back, that gives S, which is L-phenylalanine.
- **SMILES check:** `N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O` is the standard SMILES for L-phenylalanine (S), so it matches the drawing.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: L-Selenocysteine
text:
The drawing is selenocysteine: a HOOC–CH(NH2)–CH2–SeH skeleton.

- **Carboxylic acid:** the carbon at the left has a double bond to O and a single bond to HO.
- **Stereocentre:** the alpha carbon carries NH2 on a hashed bond, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **CIP priorities:** N > CH2SeH > COOH > H. The CH2SeH carbon outranks the carboxyl carbon because Se outranks O.
- **Configuration:** viewed from the front, N (down) → CH2Se (upper right) → COOH (upper left) runs counterclockwise. The H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R. This is L-selenocysteine.
- **SMILES check:** this matches the L-cysteine pattern N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O (also R), with S replaced by Se.

SMILES: N[C@@H](C[SeH])C(=O)O

name: L-Methylfolate
text:
I read this as 5-methyltetrahydrofolic acid (levomefolic acid), with a 5-methyl-tetrahydropteridinone, a p-aminobenzoyl linker and a glutamic acid tail.

**Glutamate stereocentre:** the CH2 is on a hashed bond (pointing away). The ordering N, COOH, CH2 runs clockwise on the page. With the implicit H toward the viewer, that makes the centre S, as in L-glutamate. This gives `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O`.

**Pteridine C6 stereocentre:** the exocyclic CH2 is on a wedge (toward the viewer) and the implicit H points away. Seen from the front, N5, then the exocyclic CH2, then the ring CH2 run clockwise. Written as `N1[C@@H](CN…)CN…`, this corresponds to `@@`.

I assigned the C6 centre from the geometry of the drawing alone. I did not run a CIP priority check, and the result differs from the `@` I remembered for the literature SMILES. I kept the drawing-based assignment.

SMILES: CN1[C@@H](CNc2ccc(cc2)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)CNC2=C1C(=O)NC(N)=N2

name: L-Proline
text:
The drawing shows proline: a five-membered ring made of one NH and four carbons, with a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH) on the ring carbon next to nitrogen.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring has N–H at the top, two plain CH2 carbons on the left and bottom, and the substituted carbon at the right.
- The substituted ring carbon carries the COOH group, drawn with a single wedge. This is the only stereocentre.

**Stereochemistry**
- The wedge is narrow at the ring carbon and widens toward the carboxyl carbon, so the COOH points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away.
- CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > COOH > ring CH2 > H.
- On the page, N is at upper left, COOH at right and CH2 at lower left. N → COOH → CH2 therefore runs clockwise with H in the back, which gives R. This is D-proline.

**SMILES check**
- For `OC(=O)[C@H]1CCCN1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is COOH, H, N (via ring closure 1), CH2.
- `@` means H → N → CH2 runs counterclockwise when viewed from COOH. Swapping to put H first turns this into `@@`, so COOH → N → CH2 is clockwise when viewed from H.
- Viewed with H pointing away, that rotation reverses, so N → COOH → CH2 is clockwise, which is R. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H]1CCCN1

name: L-Serine
text:
The drawing is serine, HOOC–CH(NH2)–CH2–OH.

- The left end is a carboxylic acid: a carbon with a C=O (top O) and an HO group.
- That carbon is bonded to the alpha carbon, which carries NH2 on a hashed bond.
- The alpha carbon is also bonded to a CH2 that ends in OH.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are N > COOH > CH2OH > H. The hashed NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Going from N (down) to COOH (upper left) to CH2OH (upper right) reads clockwise on the page. Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S. That makes the molecule L-serine, written as N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O

name: Labetalol
text:
The drawing is labetalol, with no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing a carboxamide (C(N)=O) on one carbon, an OH on the adjacent carbon, and the side chain on the carbon para to the OH. The ring carbons are C1 (carboxamide), C2 (OH), C3, C4, C5 (side chain) and C6. The side chain carbon, drawn at (495, 855), is bonded to the ring carbon at the right of the ring, which is adjacent to the C(C(N)=O) carbon at (440, 745) through the ring bond. So the side chain sits meta to the carboxamide and para to the OH.
- **Side chain:** CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH2–Ph.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cc(C(O)CNC(C)CCc2ccccc2)ccc1O

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cc(C(O)CNC(C)CCc2ccccc2)ccc1O

name: L-Tryptophan
text:
The drawing shows tryptophan: an indole ring (a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing NH) joined at C3 through a CH2 to an alpha carbon. That carbon carries an NH2 and a COOH.

The only stereo marker is the hashed bond from the alpha carbon to NH2, so the alpha carbon is the only stereocentre.

To assign it, the substituents rank N > COOH > CH2 > H. The hashed NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page, N (up) → COOH (lower right) → CH2 (lower left) runs clockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches L-tryptophan.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: L-Threonine
text:
The drawing shows a four-carbon chain with these features:

- A methyl carbon on the left, joined by a wedge bond to a carbon that carries an OH group.
- That carbon is bonded to a second carbon, which carries NH2 on a wedge bond.
- This second carbon is bonded to a carboxylic acid group, C(=O)OH.

This is threonine, so I assigned the stereochemistry from the wedges (hydrogens implicit, pointing away from the viewer).

**Carbon bearing OH:** The priorities are OH, then the carbon bearing N, then CH3, then H. Viewed from the front, OH (up), the N-bearing carbon (lower right) and CH3 (lower left) run clockwise. This gives R.

**Carbon bearing NH2:** The priorities are N, then the carboxyl carbon, then the OH-bearing carbon, then H. Viewed from the front, N (down), the carboxyl carbon (upper right) and the OH-bearing carbon (upper left) run counterclockwise. This gives S.

The molecule is therefore (2S,3R)-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid, which is L-threonine. I checked that the SMILES below encodes R at the OH carbon and S at the NH2 carbon.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O)[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: L-Tyrosine
text:
The drawing shows tyrosine: a para-hydroxyphenyl ring joined through a CH2 to an alpha carbon that carries NH2 and a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH).

The alpha carbon has a bold wedge to NH2, so the amine points toward the viewer and the implicit hydrogen points away. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2. Viewed with H at the back, N (down) → COOH (right) → CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise, which is S. That matches L-tyrosine.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O

name: L-Valine
text:
The drawing shows valine: an isopropyl group on the alpha carbon, which carries an NH2 and a carboxylic acid (C=O and OH).

Stereochemistry: the only stereo marking is the hashed bond from the alpha carbon to NH2, so the nitrogen points away from the viewer and the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer.

- CIP priorities: N > COOH > CH(CH3)2 > H.
- In the drawing, N (up), then COOH (lower right), then isopropyl (lower left) runs clockwise.
- The hydrogen faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S.

This is L-valine, written as CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)O.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: Lactic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a three-carbon chain: a methyl carbon at the upper right, a central carbon bearing an OH group, and a carboxylic acid carbon with a C=O and an OH. This is lactic acid. The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all bonds are drawn plain, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(O)C(=O)O

name: Lacosamide
text:
The drawing shows lacosamide, (R)-2-acetamido-N-benzyl-3-methoxypropanamide.

- **Left end:** a methoxy group (CH3–O) is attached to a CH2 that is drawn as a wedge bond to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries an acetamido group (NH–C(=O)CH3) pointing up, the wedged CH2OMe, and a C(=O)NH–CH2–phenyl amide to the lower right. The remaining substituent is an implicit H.
- **Right end:** the amide nitrogen is bonded to a benzyl group, CH2 attached to a six-membered aromatic ring.

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > C(=O)N > CH2OMe > H. The wedged CH2 is toward the viewer, so the H points away. Reading N (up), then C=O (lower right), then CH2 (lower left) goes clockwise, which gives R.

For the SMILES, `COC[C@@H](NC(C)=O)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1`, viewed from the CH2 neighbour the order H, N, C(=O) is clockwise (@@). That corresponds to R, matching the drawing.

SMILES: COC[C@@H](NC(C)=O)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1

name: Lamotrigine
text:
The drawing is a 1,2,4-triazine ring carrying two amino groups and a dichlorophenyl group. This matches lamotrigine.

**Triazine ring.** Going around the ring from the left:
- A carbon at the left bears NH2 (C3).
- That carbon is double-bonded to the upper N, which is bonded to the upper-right carbon bearing NH2 (C5).
- C5 is double-bonded to the carbon at lower right (C6), which carries the aryl group.
- C6 is single-bonded to the lower-right N, which is double-bonded to the lower-left N.
- The lower-left N is single-bonded back to the left carbon.

This gives the ring Nc(N)... written as: C3(N)=N–C5(N)=C6(Ar)–N=N–C3.

**Aryl ring.** The attachment carbon is bonded to a carbon bearing Cl (ortho), and the next carbon also bears Cl (meta). That is a 2,3-dichlorophenyl group.

**SMILES.** Writing the triazine as aromatic: Nc1nnc(-c2cccc(Cl)c2Cl)c(N)n1.

Checking the ring order: c1 (C3, NH2), n, n, c (C6, aryl), c (C5, NH2), n (the upper N) closing back to c1. This matches the drawing.

For the aryl ring, c2cccc(Cl)c2Cl starts at the attachment carbon. The last atom, c2Cl, is the ortho carbon bearing Cl, and the c(Cl) before it is the meta carbon bearing Cl. This is correct.

SMILES: Nc1nnc(-c2cccc(Cl)c2Cl)c(N)n1

name: Lamivudine
text:
This is lamivudine (3TC): a cytosine ring attached through N1 to a 1,3-oxathiolane ring that carries a CH2OH group.

- **Base:** the six-membered ring has a C=O flanked by N and N, a ring C=N, a C–NH2 carbon, and a CH=CH unit, which makes it cytosine.
- **Sugar ring:** the five-membered ring contains O, S, two CH carbons and a CH2. One CH carbon bears the cytosine N1. The other, between O and S, bears the CH2OH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** both substituents on the ring (the hashed N bond and the hashed CH2OH bond) are shown as hashes, so there are two stereocentres. I checked the chirality at the carbon attached to N by working out the neighbour order from the drawing. It matches the (@) configuration in the known lamivudine SMILES. I did not independently check the second centre, the CH between O and S, and took it from the known lamivudine SMILES.

SMILES: C1[C@H](O[C@@H](S1)CO)N2C=CC(=NC2=O)N

name: Lanifibranor
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Indole part (right):** The nitrogen is bonded to the sulfonyl group. C2 of the indole carries the chain. C3 is CH, and C3a and C7a are the ring-fusion carbons. The chlorine sits on the benzene ring carbon that is bonded to the CH next to C3a, which makes it C5.

**Chain:** From C2 the chain runs CH2, CH2, CH2, then C(=O)OH, so it is a butanoic acid attached at C2.

**Benzothiazole part (left):** The benzene ring carries the sulfonyl group. Its fusion carbons bear N (one side) and S (other side). The thiazole ring is N=CH–S.

Tracing the ring atoms: the carbon bonded to S is bonded to the CH that is bonded to the sulfonyl-bearing carbon. The carbon bonded to N is bonded to the CH=CH on the top, which leads to the sulfonyl carbon. So the sulfonyl-bearing carbon is adjacent to one CH on the S-side ring carbon and one CH on the top. This makes it a benzothiazole with the sulfonyl at C5 or C6.

Coordinates:
- Sulfonyl carbon (595,563) is bonded to the top carbon (513,422) and the bottom carbon (514,705).
- The bottom carbon (514,705) is bonded to the fusion carbon (352,706), which bears S.
- The top carbon (513,422) is bonded to (350,423), which is bonded to the fusion carbon (268,565), which bears N.

The sulfonyl carbon is therefore separated from the S-bearing fusion carbon (C7a) by one CH (C7), so it is C6. The sulfonyl is at position 6.

**SMILES:** Benzothiazole written as c1nc2ccc(cc2s1) places S-bearing C7a followed by C7 and then C6.

Writing it out: O=C(O)CCCc1cc2cc(Cl)ccc2n1S(=O)(=O)c1ccc2ncsc2c1

Check on the sulfonyl-bearing ring: c1ccc2ncsc2c1 starts at the sulfonyl carbon (C6), then c (C5), c (C4), c2 (C3a, bonded to n), then n, c, s, c2 (C7a), then c1 (C7), which closes back to C6. This matches.

Check on the indole ring: c1cc2cc(Cl)ccc2n1 has C2, C3, C3a, C4, C5(Cl), C6, C7, C7a, N. The chlorine is on C5, which is correct, as C4 is the CH next to C3a.

SMILES: O=C(O)CCCc1cc2cc(Cl)ccc2n1S(=O)(=O)c1ccc2ncsc2c1

name: Lactulose
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose ring joined through a glycosidic oxygen to a furanose ring. The pyranose is a glucose-like ring with the CH2OH on C5. The furanose has the glycosidic O on the ring carbon next to the CH(CH2OH)–O carbon, not on the anomeric carbon as in sucrose. The anomeric carbon of the furanose carries an OH and a CH2OH.

**Pyranose ring (left):** ring O, C1 (hashed bond to the glycosidic O), C2 (wedged OH), C3 (hashed OH), C4 (hashed OH), and C5 (hashed CH2OH).

**Furanose ring (right):**
- C_a carries a wedged CH2OH and is bonded to the ring O.
- C_b carries the hashed glycosidic O.
- C_c carries a wedged OH.
- C_d carries a wedged OH and a CH2OH, and is bonded to the ring O.

I assigned each stereocentre (@/@@) by working out the neighbour order and the wedge or hash direction from the drawing's 2D coordinates. I did not run the final string through a SMILES parser.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](O[C@H]2[C@H](O)[C@@](O)(CO)O[C@@H]2CO)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Landiolol Hydrochloride
text:
I read this as the hydrochloride salt of landiolol.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- **Left end:** a 2,2-dimethyl-1,3-dioxolane ring. Its C4 carries a CH2–O ester link, drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Ester and linker:** the ester is –O–C(=O)–CH2CH2– attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Aryl ether side chain:** the ring bears –O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH2CH2–NH–C(=O)–. The OH is on a wedged bond.
- **Right end:** the carbonyl is attached to the nitrogen of a morpholine ring (N, two CH2, O, two CH2).
- **Salt:** HCl is shown as a separate component.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Dioxolane C4 (hashed CH2):** with the implicit H towards the viewer, the neighbours ring CH2, exocyclic CH2 and ring O run counter-clockwise. In the SMILES order (ring CH2, H, exocyclic CH2, ring O) this gives `@@`.
- **Carbinol carbon (wedged OH):** with the implicit H pointing away, the neighbours ArOCH2, OH and CH2N run clockwise. In the SMILES order (ArOCH2, H, OH, CH2N) this also gives `@@`.

I assigned both centres directly from the drawn wedge and hash geometry, not from the known landiolol configuration.

SMILES: CC1(C)OC[C@@H](COC(=O)CCc2ccc(OC[C@@H](O)CNCCNC(=O)N3CCOCC3)cc2)O1.Cl

name: Lactitol
text:
I read this as a glucopyranose-type ring joined through a glycosidic oxygen to a six-carbon open-chain polyol (a hexitol, as in maltitol or lactitol). I did not try to name the sugar from the drawing.

**Ring (left):** a six-membered ring with five carbons and one ring oxygen.
- The anomeric carbon carries the glycosidic oxygen on a hashed bond.
- The next carbon has its OH on a wedge.
- The following two carbons each have an OH on a hashed bond.
- The carbon next to the ring oxygen carries a CH2OH on a hashed bond.

**Chain (right):** six carbons, all bearing OH.
- The first carbon carries the glycosidic oxygen on a hashed bond.
- Going up the chain, the next carbon has its OH on a hash and ends in a CH2OH.
- Going down the chain, the next two carbons have their OH groups on wedges, and the chain ends in a CH2OH.

I assigned each @/@@ by working out the screen orientation of the neighbours at every stereocentre, with the implicit H taken as pointing opposite the wedge or hash.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](O[C@H]([C@H](O)CO)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)CO)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Lansoprazole
text:
The drawing shows lansoprazole, read region by region as follows.

- **Pyridine ring:** the ring nitrogen sits at the top. The carbon next to it bears a CH2 group that leads to the sulfur. The next carbon carries a methyl group. The carbon after that carries the O–CH2–CF3 group (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy).
- **Sulfoxide:** the sulfur is drawn with a double bond to oxygen (S=O) and is bonded to the CH2 and to C2 of the benzimidazole. No wedges or hashes are shown, so I add no stereochemistry.
- **Benzimidazole:** C2 is double-bonded to the ring N (no H) and single-bonded to the NH. The fused benzene ring completes the bicycle.

SMILES: CC1=C(OCC(F)(F)F)C=CN=C1CS(=O)C1=NC2=CC=CC=C2N1

name: Lanthanum carbonate anhydrous
text:
The image shows two La³⁺ ions and three carbonate ions, which is lanthanum carbonate, La2(CO3)3. Each carbonate has one C=O and two O⁻ groups. The charges balance: 2 × (+3) = +6 and 3 × (−2) = −6.

Writing each component as a separate fragment:

SMILES: [La+3].[La+3].[O-]C([O-])=O.[O-]C([O-])=O.[O-]C([O-])=O

name: Lanraplenib
text:
I read the drawing as four connected pieces.

1. **Aminopyrazine:** a six-membered ring with nitrogens at opposite positions (a pyrazine). One carbon carries NH2, and another carbon links to the fused bicycle.
2. **Imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine core:** a fused bicycle with a bridgehead nitrogen. The carbon bearing the pyrazine is adjacent to the ring nitrogen. The carbon on the other side of that nitrogen carries the NH linker.
3. **Linker and phenyl:** the NH connects to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
4. **Piperazine and oxetane:** the benzene's other para position bonds to a piperazine nitrogen. The far piperazine nitrogen bonds to the 3-position of an oxetane (a four-membered ring containing one oxygen).

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry. I checked that the ring closures and atom counts in the SMILES match the drawing.

SMILES: Nc1cncc(n1)-c1cn2ccnc2c(Nc2ccc(cc2)N2CCN(CC2)C2COC2)n1

name: Laninamivir
text:
I read this as a zanamivir analogue in which the C7 hydroxyl is a methyl ether. Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ring:** a six-membered dihydropyran with the ring oxygen at the top right. The C=C sits at the top left, and the ring carbon at the top bears the COOH group.
- **C4 substituent:** a guanidine attached through a wedged bond, written N=C(N)N.
- **C5 substituent:** an acetamide, NHAc, on a hashed bond.
- **C6 substituent:** a side chain on the carbon next to the ring oxygen, which is also drawn with a wedge. The side chain runs CH(OMe), then CH(OH), then CH2OH. The OMe is on a wedge and the middle OH is on a hash.

I assigned each stereocentre (C4, C5, C6, C7, C8) from the wedge/hash geometry, treating the implicit hydrogen as pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1=C[C@H](N=C(N)N)[C@@H](NC(C)=O)[C@@H](O1)[C@H](OC)[C@H](O)CO

name: Lapatinib
text:
This structure is lapatinib, read region by region as follows.

- **Left chain:** a methyl on a sulfonyl group (CS(=O)(=O)), then a two-carbon chain (CC) to an NH, then a CH2 attached to the furan at C2.
- **Furan:** the other α-carbon of the furan (C5) is bonded to the quinazoline at position 6.
- **Quinazoline:** N1 and N3 are the two ring nitrogens, and C4 carries the NH link to the aryl group.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring with Cl ortho to the O-benzyl ether; the benzyl ring bears F at the meta position.

SMILES is built as: CS(=O)(=O)CCNCc1ccc(o1)-c1ccc2ncnc(Nc3ccc(OCc4cccc(F)c4)c(Cl)c3)c2c1

Atom check:
- The quinazoline fused ring is written c1ccc2ncnc(N...)c2c1, with the furan attached at c1. In the drawing, the benzo ring carbon bearing the furan is adjacent to the carbon bonded to C4a (the junction carbon next to C4), which is position 5. The furan-bearing carbon is therefore C6, and my SMILES matches this: c1 (C6), then c (C7), c (C8), c2 (C8a), n (N1), c, n (N3), c(N) (C4), c2 (C4a), c1 (C5).
- In the aryl ring, the NH attaches at c3, then c, c, then c(OBn), then c(Cl), then c3. The Cl is adjacent to the O-bearing carbon and meta to the NH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CCNCc1ccc(o1)-c1ccc2ncnc(Nc3ccc(OCc4cccc(F)c4)c(Cl)c3)c2c1

name: Larotrectinib
text:
I read this as larotrectinib and checked both stereocentres against the drawing.

**Ring system and substituents**
- The core is a pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine. The ring N of the five-membered ring is shared with the six-membered ring, and the five-membered ring carries an N–N bond.
- The carbon next to the ring fusion on the five-membered ring bears an NH–C(=O)– urea linkage.
- The urea nitrogen is part of a pyrrolidine ring. A hashed OH sits on its 3-position.
- On the six-membered ring, the carbon next to the ring nitrogen bears a second pyrrolidine through its nitrogen.
- The 2-position of that pyrrolidine carries a wedged 2,5-difluorophenyl group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The 2-aryl pyrrolidine carbon has the aryl group on a wedge. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `@@`.
- The 3-hydroxypyrrolidine carbon has the OH on a hash. The same check gives `@`.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1cnn2ccc(nc12)N1CCC[C@@H]1c1cc(F)ccc1F)N1CC[C@H](O)C1

name: Lapretolimod ammonium
text:
I read this as a monophosphoryl lipid A ammonium salt: a β(1→6)-linked diglucosamine carrying six acyl chains, one phosphate and one free anomeric OH. I did not verify the stereocentres against the wedges. The ring configurations follow standard D-glucosamine patterns, and the 3-hydroxy carbons are assigned as R, which is the natural lipid A configuration.

- **Left (non-reducing) ring:** a β-glucosamine with a 4-O-phosphate (one P–OH and one P–O⁻) and a free CH₂OH at C6. The 2-N carries a 3-(tetradecanoyloxy)tetradecanoyl group, and the 3-O carries a second 3-(tetradecanoyloxy)tetradecanoyl group.
- **Right (reducing) ring:** an α-glucosamine with a free anomeric OH and a free 4-OH. The 6-CH₂ is linked through O to C1 of the left ring. The 2-N carries a 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl group, and the 3-O carries another 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl ester.
- **Chain lengths:** all acyl chains are C14. A 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl group is written C(=O)CC(O) followed by 11 carbons, and a myristoyl is C(=O) followed by 13 carbons.
- **Counter-ion:** NH₄⁺.

SMILES: [NH4+].OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](OC[C@H]2O[C@H](O)[C@H](NC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H]2O)[C@H](NC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H]1OP(=O)(O)[O-]

name: Lasmiditan
text:
The drawing shows three parts joined in a chain.

- **Piperidine:** an N-methylpiperidine ring, attached at its 4-position to a ketone C=O.
- **Pyridine:** that ketone is bonded to C2 of a pyridine ring. The ring nitrogen sits next to C6, and C6 carries the NH.
- **Benzamide:** the NH is acylated by a benzoyl group, forming an amide. The benzene ring has fluorines at both ortho positions (2 and 6) and at the para position (4), so it is 2,4,6-trifluorophenyl.

Checking the benzene ring: the carbon attached to C=O is bonded to a CF carbon at the top, then a CH, then a CF carbon on the right (para), then a CH, then a CF carbon at the bottom, which closes the ring. This gives fluorines at positions 2, 4 and 6.

Written as SMILES, the pieces combine as:

CN1CCC(CC1)C(=O)c1cccc(NC(=O)c2c(F)cc(F)cc2F)n1

SMILES: CN1CCC(CC1)C(=O)c1cccc(NC(=O)c2c(F)cc(F)cc2F)n1

name: Lanreotide
text:
I read the drawing as lanreotide: D‑2‑Nal‑Cys‑Tyr‑D‑Trp‑Lys‑Val‑Cys‑Thr‑NH2, with a Cys2–Cys7 disulfide ring and a C‑terminal primary amide.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond and checked it against CIP priorities:

- **D‑2‑Nal (N‑terminal, naphthalen‑2‑yl side chain):** R.
- **Cys2:** R (the L form).
- **Tyr:** S (L).
- **Trp:** R (D).
- **Lys:** S (L).
- **Val:** S (L).
- **Cys7:** R (L).
- **Thr:** the α carbon is S and the β carbon (bearing OH and CH3) is R, the L‑Thr configuration.

I then wrote the SMILES from the N‑terminus, closing the macrocycle through the Cys2 α carbon, and rechecked the chirality tags for each atom's neighbour order.

name: Laidlomycin
text:
I read the structure region by region and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

- **Acid end:** a propanoate ester (OC(=O)CC) sits on the carbon next to a CH(CH3)–COOH unit. That carbon is joined to a further CH(CH3), which leads into the left tetrahydropyran.
- **Left tetrahydropyran:** it carries an OH and a CH3, and its other ring carbon is a spiro carbon.
- **Spiro centre:** it is shared with a five-membered ring made of CH2–CH2–C(CH3)–O.
- **Middle:** that quaternary carbon links to a CH of a second tetrahydrofuran (CH2–CH2–C(CH3)–O). This ring's quaternary carbon then links to a third tetrahydrofuran bearing a CH3.
- **Right tetrahydropyran:** it is attached through a ring CH and has two CH3 groups. Its hemiketal carbon bears an OH and a CH2OH.

I worked out each @/@@ by hand from the 2D geometry. I did not run the SMILES through a parser or re-check it against the drawing afterwards.

name: Lasofoxifene
text:
I read the structure as lasofoxifene, a 5,6,7,8-tetrahydronaphthalen-2-ol core carrying a phenyl and a 4-(2-pyrrolidin-1-ylethoxy)phenyl group on adjacent ring carbons.

**Connectivity**
- The left end is a pyrrolidine ring whose nitrogen is joined to a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2–O).
- The oxygen of that chain is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- That benzene ring is bonded to C5 of the tetrahydronaphthalene, which is the stereocentre at the lower wedge.
- The adjacent stereocentre, C6, carries an unsubstituted phenyl ring (the upper wedge) and the CH2–CH2 portion of the saturated ring.
- The fused aromatic ring has a phenolic OH at the far right.

**Stereochemistry**
Both wedges point toward the viewer, so each implicit hydrogen points away. Tracing the three drawn neighbours of each stereocentre from the front gives a clockwise sequence at C5 (aryl → C6 → C4a) and at C6 (phenyl → CH2 → C5). Converting these to SMILES neighbour order gives `@@` for both carbons as written below.

The SMILES below is checked atom for atom against the drawing.

SMILES: C1CCN(C1)CCOc1ccc(cc1)[C@@H]1c2ccc(O)cc2CC[C@@H]1c1ccccc1

name: Larotaxel
text:
I read the structure as a taxane core carrying a cyclopropane ring, an oxetane ring and a Boc-protected phenylisoserine side chain. It resembles docetaxel with a 10-acetyl group, but with a C19 methylene bridging C7 and C8 to form a cyclopropane. The stereo marks were assigned by hand from the wedge and hash bonds, so they are the part most likely to contain an error.

**Core, numbered as in taxanes:**
- C10 carries an OAc group (wedge). C9 is a ketone.
- C8 is quaternary and is bonded to C9, C3, C7 and the C19 methylene (wedge). C19 also bonds to C7, which closes the cyclopropane.
- C7 bears a hashed H and is bonded to C6.
- C5 bears a hashed H and is part of the oxetane (C5–O–C20–C4). C4 carries an OAc group (hashed).
- C3 bears a hashed H. C2 carries an OBz group (hashed).
- C1 carries an OH (wedge). C15 is the gem-dimethyl carbon.
- C11=C12 is the tetrasubstituted double bond, with a methyl on C12. C13 carries the side-chain ester O (hashed).

**Side chain:** the ester C(=O) is followed by C2′ (OH, wedge) and C3′ (NH–Boc, wedge), with a phenyl group on C3′.

Ring closures were checked against the drawing: the cyclopropane is C8–C19–C7, the oxetane is C5–O–C20–C4, and the large ring closes through C3–C8 and C11–C10.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[C@H]1C(=O)[C@]23C[C@H]2C[C@H]4OC[C@@]4(OC(C)=O)[C@H]3[C@H](OC(=O)c5ccccc5)[C@]6(O)C[C@H](OC(=O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)c7ccccc7)C(C)=C1C6(C)C

name: Latanoprost
text:
The drawing matches latanoprost, the isopropyl ester of a 17-phenyl-trinor prostaglandin F2α, and I wrote the SMILES from that reading.

- **Ester end:** an isopropyl ester, `CC(C)OC(=O)`, followed by a chain of three CH2 groups.
- **Alkene:** a cis (Z) double bond, `/C=C\`, then one CH2 leading to the ring.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane carrying two OH groups, both drawn hashed. The upper chain is drawn hashed and the lower chain bold, so the two chains are trans to each other.
- **Lower chain:** CH2CH2, then a CH(OH) drawn hashed, then CH2CH2 and a phenyl ring.
- **Side-chain carbinol:** I worked out its CIP priorities directly from the drawing. The OH ranks first, the phenyl-side branch second and the ring-side branch third. With the hashed OH this gives R, which agrees with latanoprost's 15R centre.

I took the ring stereocentres from the known latanoprost SMILES instead of deriving each one from the wedges, since the wedge pattern matches it.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1CC[C@H](O)CCc1ccccc1

name: Lasalocid A
text:
I read the drawing as lasalocid A: a substituted benzoic acid joined through a chain to a tetrahydrofuran and a tetrahydropyran.

**Aromatic head:**
- The ring carries a methyl, a phenolic OH, a COOH and the chain, in the pattern 2-hydroxy-3-methylbenzoic acid.
- The chain is attached at the ring position next to the COOH carbon.

**Chain from the ring:**
1. Two CH2 groups.
2. CH(CH3), with a hashed methyl.
3. CH(OH), with a wedged OH.
4. CH(CH3), with a hashed methyl.
5. C=O.
6. CH(CH2CH3), with a hashed ethyl.

**Tetrahydrofuran ring:**
- It attaches to the chain through the ring carbon next to O, drawn with a wedged bond to O.
- Next comes a quaternary carbon bearing a wedged ethyl and the pyran ring.
- Then a CH2.
- Then a CH(CH3) with a hashed methyl, which closes the ring.

**Tetrahydropyran ring:**
- Starting at the carbon attached to the THF quaternary carbon, the ring runs through O, CH(CH3) with a wedged methyl, and a quaternary C(OH)(Et) with a hashed OH.
- It then continues through two CH2 groups back to the start.

I assigned each @/@@ by working out the neighbour order around the centre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing, then permuting to the SMILES atom order.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(CC[C@@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](CC)[C@H]2O[C@](CC)([C@H]3CC[C@](O)(CC)[C@H](C)O3)C[C@@H]2C)c(C(=O)O)c1O

name: Lazertinib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Acrylamide:** C=CC(=O)N–, with the NH attached to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** it carries four substituents.
  - C1 bears the acrylamide NH.
  - C2 (adjacent to C1) bears the morpholine N.
  - C3 bears OMe.
  - C4 bears the NH that links to the pyrimidine.
  - The ring runs C1 (NHAc), C2 (morpholine), C3 (H), C4 (OMe), C5 (NH-pyrimidine), C6 (H).
- **Morpholine:** N1CCOCC1, attached through N.
- **Pyrimidine:** C2 carries the NH. N3 lies between C2 and C4, and C4 carries the pyrazole N1. C5 and C6 are CH, and N1 closes the ring back to C2.
- **Pyrazole:** N1 is attached to the pyrimidine. N2 is the adjacent ring nitrogen. C3 bears the phenyl, C4 bears CH2N(CH3)2, and C5 is CH.

SMILES for the core: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(NC...)c(OC)cc1N1CCOCC1. Here the ring order is C1 (NHAc), then cH (C6), then C5 (NH-pyrimidine), C4 (OMe), C3 (H), C2 (morpholine), which is consistent with the ring above.

Full SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-n2cc(CN(C)C)c(-c3ccccc3)n2)c(OC)cc1N1CCOCC1

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-n2cc(CN(C)C)c(-c3ccccc3)n2)c(OC)cc1N1CCOCC1

name: Latanoprostene Bunod
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes. The structure is latanoprostene bunod, a prostaglandin F2α-type ester carrying a nitrooxy-butyl group.

- **Ester end:** a nitrooxy-butyl ester, with the nitrate drawn as O–[N+](=O)[O-] on a four-carbon chain.
- **Upper chain:** the ester carbonyl, then three CH2 groups, then a cis (Z) C=C, then one CH2 joining the cyclopentane. This gives a hept-5-enoate chain.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane with two OH groups, both on hashed bonds. The upper chain is also on a hashed bond. The lower chain is on a bold wedge.
- **Lower chain:** CH2CH2, then a CH(OH) on a hashed bond, then CH2CH2 and a phenyl ring.

I worked out each @/@@ label from the wedge and hash geometry and checked that the result matches the known isomeric form of latanoprostene bunod.

SMILES: O=C(OCCCCO[N+](=O)[O-])CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1CC[C@@H](O)CCc1ccccc1

name: Ledaborbactam
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left side chain:** a CH3–CH2–C(=O)–NH group, so a propanamide attached through N.
- **Stereocentre:** the N is bonded to a ring carbon by a wedge bond. That carbon also bears a CH2 and a boron, with an implicit H.
- **Ring containing boron:** the stereocentre carbon connects to CH2, which connects to an aromatic carbon. The neighbouring aromatic carbon bears an O, which links to B, and B closes back to the stereocentre. B also carries an OH. This gives a six-membered oxaborinine ring fused to the benzene.
- **Benzene ring:** it has six carbons. Two are fused to the oxaborinine ring, and the one next to the O-bearing carbon carries a COOH group.

**Stereo assignment:** the H on the stereocentre is implicit and points away from the viewer. Seen from the front, the neighbours N (wedge, lower left), CH2 (up) and B (lower right) run clockwise. In the SMILES `CCC(=O)N[C@H]1Cc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2OB1O`, the neighbour order at that carbon is N, H, ring-closure B, CH2. That order corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: CCC(=O)N[C@H]1Cc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2OB1O

name: Leflunomide
text:
The drawing shows an isoxazole ring joined through an amide to a para-substituted benzene ring.

**Isoxazole ring.** The atoms run N, O, C(CH3), C, CH, and back to N. N is double-bonded to the CH carbon, and the C(CH3) carbon is double-bonded to the ring carbon that carries the carboxamide. The O sits between the N and the C(CH3) carbon, so the ring is a 5-methylisoxazole with the amide at position 4.

**Amide and aryl group.** The amide carbon has a C=O and an NH, and the NH is bonded to a benzene ring. A CF3 group sits para to the NH on that ring.

This matches leflunomide.

SMILES: Cc1oncc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)C(F)(F)F

name: Lecirelin
text:
I read this as the decapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Tle‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt, a GnRH‑agonist‑type peptide. Tle is tert‑leucine, the residue carrying the tert‑butyl group directly on its α‑carbon. The sequence is built from these pieces, read residue by residue along the backbone:

- **pGlu:** pyroglutamic acid, the 5‑membered lactam with its ring C=O, at the N‑terminus.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain attached through CH2.
- **Trp:** an indole side chain attached through CH2.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Tyr:** a 4‑hydroxybenzyl side chain.
- **Tle:** a tert‑butyl group on the α‑carbon.
- **Leu:** an isobutyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a three‑carbon chain ending in the guanidine group, drawn as N=C(NH2)NH2.
- **Pro‑NHEt:** a proline whose C‑terminus is an N‑ethyl amide.

I assigned stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes at each α‑carbon, using the "CORN" rule. Trp, Ser and the other wedged residues come out as L. The Tle carbon is drawn with a hashed N bond and comes out as D, so it is written with the opposite tag to the L residues. Only the Trp and Ser centres were checked explicitly. The remaining wedged residues (His, Tyr, Leu, Arg, Pro, pGlu) are assumed L, as is typical for this peptide class.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC

name: Lemborexant
text:
I read the structure as lemborexant: a cyclopropane with two substituents on adjacent carbons, plus the aromatic groups below.

**Fragments**
- **Pyrimidine:** the ring is 2,4-dimethylpyrimidine, with methyls on the carbon between the two nitrogens and on the carbon next to the other nitrogen. The oxygen is on C5, and C6 is a plain CH.
- **Linker:** the pyrimidine C5 carries an ether oxygen, which connects to a CH2 group.
- **Cyclopropane:** the CH2 is attached to a quaternary ring carbon. This carbon also carries a 3-fluorophenyl group. The adjacent ring carbon bears a carboxamide, C(=O)NH.
- **Amide substituent:** the amide nitrogen is bonded to C2 of a pyridine ring, with fluorine on C5 of that ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- The CH2O bond on the quaternary carbon is hashed, which gives `[C@@]` in my SMILES atom ordering.
- The C(=O) bond on the other ring carbon is also hashed, which gives `[C@H]` in my SMILES atom ordering.

SMILES: Cc1ncc(OC[C@@]2(c3cccc(F)c3)C[C@H]2C(=O)Nc2ccc(F)cn2)c(C)n1

name: Laulimalide
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote the SMILES with stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes.

**Regions of the molecule**
- **Left ring:** a dihydropyran with a ring oxygen, a CH=C(CH3) double bond and a CH2. Its ring CH carries a wedged (E)-vinyl substituent.
- **Side chain:** the vinyl group leads to a CH(OH) with a wedged OH. That carbon is bonded to the macrolactone carbon bearing the ester oxygen.
- **Macrolactone:** it runs from the ester oxygen through a CH2 and an epoxide (two CH carbons bridged by O). It continues through a CH(OH), a CH2, a C(=CH2), a CH2, a CH(CH3), another CH2, and then the right-hand dihydropyran. The ring closes through a (Z)-CH=CH to the C(=O).
- **Right ring:** a dihydropyran containing a CH=CH, with its two O-bearing CH carbons both drawn as stereocentres.

**Double bonds**
- The CH=CH conjugated to the lactone carbonyl is cis (Z), since both chain substituents lie on the same side.
- The vinyl group on the left ring is trans (E).

**Stereocentres:** I assigned all nine from the wedge and hash bonds.

The SMILES below is hand-written, and I did not run it through a parser.

SMILES: CC1=CCO[C@@H](C1)/C=C/[C@H](O)[C@@H]2C[C@@H]3O[C@H]3[C@@H](O)CC(=C)C[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4CC=C[C@H](O4)C/C=C\C(=O)O2

name: Lenalidomide
text:
The drawing is lenalidomide: a piperidine-2,6-dione ring joined through its C3 carbon to the nitrogen of an isoindolinone, with an amino group on the benzene ring.

**Glutarimide ring (left):** the ring atoms are C(=O), NH, C(=O), CH2, CH2 and the CH that carries the isoindolinone nitrogen. The CH has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.

**Isoindolinone (right):**
- The lactam nitrogen N is bonded to the CH of the glutarimide ring, to a CH2, and to a C=O.
- The CH2 is attached to an aromatic carbon (C3a), which is adjacent to the aromatic carbon bearing NH2.
- The C=O is attached to the other fused aromatic carbon (C7a).
- Going around the benzene ring from C3a: the C–NH2 carbon, then CH, CH, CH, then C7a.

**SMILES:** starting at the glutarimide, `O=C1CCC(N2Cc3c(N)cccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1`.

**Check:**
- Ring closure 1 runs from the first C(=O) through CH2, CH2 and the CH to C(=O) and NH, then back to the start, giving a six-membered ring.
- The isoindolinone ring N2, CH2, c3, c (the aromatic carbon bearing NH2), then c, c, c, c3 and C2=O closes with the aromatic ring. The aromatic atoms are c3, c(N), c, c, c, c3, which makes six, so the benzene ring is complete.
- The five-membered ring is N2, CH2, c3, c3 (the fused carbon) and C2=O.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(N2Cc3c(N)cccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: Laspartomycin
text:
I read the molecule as a cyclic lipopeptide with an acylated Asp tail. I worked out each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds, treating the H on each centre as implicit.

**Lipid tail.** An isopropyl terminus is followed by nine CH2 groups, then a trans CH=CH, then C(=O)–NH on the first Asp.

**First Asp.** Its side chain is CH2COOH, drawn with a wedge. I assigned it the L-like configuration.

**Ring, traced from the Asp acyl nitrogen.**
- The first Asp's C(=O) joins the exocyclic NH of a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit (Dap). Its alpha carbon carries NH (wedge), C(=O) and a CH2 that leads to the ring NH.
- Dap C(=O) goes to the nitrogen of a six-membered pipecolic acid (piperidine) ring, whose alpha H is drawn on a wedge.
- That alpha carbon's C(=O) leads to NH–CH2–C(=O) (a glycine-like unit), then to a second Asp. Its CH2COOH is on a hash.
- That Asp's C(=O) leads to a second NH–CH2–C(=O) unit, then to a third Asp, also hashed.
- That Asp's C(=O) leads to NH–C(=O)–CH2–C(=O) (a malonyl-type unit) and then to a Thr. The Thr NH is hashed, and its CH(OH)CH3 has a hashed methyl.
- The Thr C(=O) leads to an Ile. Its NH is hashed and its side-chain methyl is on a wedge.
- The Ile C(=O) goes to the nitrogen of a five-membered pyrrolidine (proline) ring, whose alpha H is on a wedge.
- The proline C(=O) leads to NH–CH2, which closes back onto the Dap alpha carbon.

**Stereochemistry.** I worked each centre out from the drawn wedges and hashes. The Ile side-chain centre comes out as the drawing shows it, which differs from natural L-isoleucine. I kept it as drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)CCCCCCCCC/C=C/C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N2CCCC[C@H]2C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NC(=O)CC(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@H](C)CC)C(=O)N3CCC[C@H]3C(=O)NC1

name: Lenvatinib
text:
This is lenvatinib, read from the drawing as follows.

**Quinoline core.** The left ring carries a methoxy group (the CH3–O at the far left) and a carboxamide, C(=O)N. The carboxamide sits on the carbon next to the methoxy carbon. The right ring contains the nitrogen, and the aryl ether oxygen attaches at the 4-position, on the carbon adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon.

**Aryl ether side.** The oxygen links the quinoline to a benzene ring. On that ring, the NH is para to the oxygen, and the chlorine is ortho to the NH (meta to the oxygen).

**Urea.** The NH is part of a urea, NC(=O)N, whose other nitrogen carries a cyclopropyl group.

Writing the SMILES from the carboxamide-bearing carbon: COc1cc2nccc(Oc3ccc(NC(=O)NC4CC4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1C(N)=O

Atom check on the quinoline:
- c1 (OMe-bearing carbon), then c (CH), then c2 (the carbon bonded to N), then n, c, c, c(O-aryl), then c2 (the other fusion carbon), then c (CH), then c1 (the carbon bearing C(N)=O).
- This matches the drawing: the carbon bonded to N is next to the CH that is next to the OMe carbon, and the fusion carbon bonded to C4 is next to the CH that is next to the carboxamide carbon.

SMILES: COc1cc2nccc(Oc3ccc(NC(=O)NC4CC4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1C(N)=O

name: Lercanidipine
text:
This structure is lercanidipine, drawn without stereochemistry.

**Reading the drawing, region by region**
- **Left side:** a diphenylpropyl group, with a CH bearing two phenyl rings attached to CH2CH2 and then to N.
- **Amine:** the N carries a methyl group and a CH2 that leads to a quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it has two methyl groups and is bonded to an O.
- **Ester:** that O is part of an ester, O–C(=O), which attaches to the dihydropyridine ring.
- **Dihydropyridine ring:** the ring runs C(C(=O)O…)=C(C)–NH–C(C)=C(C(=O)OC)–CH(Ar), closing back on the first carbon. Both ring carbons next to NH carry methyl groups.
- **Aryl group on the sp3 ring carbon:** a 3-nitrophenyl group.
- **Second ester:** a methyl ester on the other ring alkene carbon.

The sp3 ring carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

**Writing the SMILES**
CN(CCC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)CC(C)(C)OC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

SMILES: CN(CCC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)CC(C)(C)OC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Lenacapavir
text:
I read this structure as lenacapavir and wrote the SMILES region by region from the drawing.

- **Left side:** a methylsulfonyl group on a quaternary carbon bearing two methyls, joined by an alkyne to the 6-position of a pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** its 2-position carries the stereogenic CH, and its 3-position is bonded to the indazole.
- **Stereogenic CH:** it bears a 3,5-difluorobenzyl group (hashed bond) and an NH–C(=O)–CH2 amide. Working through the hashed bond and the implicit H gives `[C@H]` when written with the pyridine carbon first.
- **Indazole:** it has a chloro substituent, an NHSO2CH3 group, and an N-CH2CF3 group.
- **Right side:** the amide CH2 is attached to a pyrazole nitrogen. The pyrazole carries CF3 and is fused to a difluorocyclopentane that is itself fused to a cyclopropane. The two ring-fusion CH carbons have hashed H atoms, which give `[C@@H]1C[C@@H]12` in the order written.

I checked ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)C(C)(C)C#Cc1ccc(c(n1)[C@H](Cc1cc(F)cc(F)c1)NC(=O)Cn1nc(C(F)(F)F)c2c1C(F)(F)[C@@H]1C[C@@H]12)-c1ccc(Cl)c2c(NS(C)(=O)=O)nn(CC(F)(F)F)c12

name: Lesinurad
text:
This is lesinurad: a naphthalene bearing a cyclopropyl group at C4 and a triazole at C1.

**Naphthalene.** The ring on the right (the top ring in the drawing) is fused to the lower ring. The lower ring runs from the fusion carbon at (537,593) to C-cyclopropyl (400,693), then (418,863), (573,931), the carbon bearing the triazole N at (710,831), and the fusion carbon at (692,662).

**Triazole.** The ring is N1 (attached to the naphthalene), C5 (bearing Br), N4, N3 and C2 (bearing S). Reading the labels, N(aryl) connects to C(S) and to C(Br). C(Br) is double bonded to the lower N, which links to the right N. The right N is double bonded to C(S), so the ring is 1,2,4-triazole.

**Side chain.** The S is attached to CH2–C(=O)OH.

**SMILES.** OC(=O)CSc1nnc(Br)n1-c1ccc(C2CC2)c2ccccc12

Checking the naphthalene: the atom c1 (attached to N) is followed by c, c, then c(cyclopropyl), then c2 (fusion), ccccc, and c12 (the other fusion carbon, closing both rings). This matches the drawing, with the triazole on the carbon adjacent to the fusion carbon and the cyclopropyl para to it.

SMILES: OC(=O)CSc1nnc(Br)n1-c1ccc(C2CC2)c2ccccc12

name: Ledipasvir
text:
I read the molecule as a symmetric-looking bis(amide) built around a 9,9-difluorofluorene core, with a different end group on each side.

- **Left end:** a 5-azaspiro[2.4]heptane (cyclopropane spiro-fused to a pyrrolidine). Its C6 carries an imidazol-2-yl group (wedge bond). The ring nitrogen is acylated by an L-valine whose amine is a methyl carbamate (hashed bond).
- **Imidazole link:** the imidazole is attached through C4 to the fluorene at the 2-position.
- **Core:** the fluorene has a CF2 at C9 and is attached at its 7-position to the benzimidazole.
- **Right end:** the benzimidazole C2 carries a 2-azabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane. The bicyclic nitrogen is acylated by a second methyl carbamate-protected L-valine (hashed bond). The wedge bond on the benzimidazole C2 and the two wedged bridgehead H atoms set the bicycle's stereocentres.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge/hash geometry, checking the neighbour order against the SMILES writing order. Both valines come out as the L (S) form.

SMILES: COC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N1CC2(CC2)C[C@H]1c1ncc(-c3ccc4c(c3)C(F)(F)c3cc(-c5ccc6nc([C@@H]7[C@@H]8C[C@@H](CC8)N7C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)C)[nH]c6c5)ccc34)[nH]1

name: Letrozole
text:
The drawing shows letrozole: a central CH bonded to two para-cyanophenyl rings and to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.

Reading the triazole: N1 (bonded to the CH) is connected to N2 on one side and to a CH carbon (C5) on the other. N2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 is single-bonded to N4. N4 is double-bonded to C5, which closes back to N1. This is the 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl pattern.

Each benzene ring carries a nitrile (C≡N) at the para position relative to the CH attachment.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccc(C#N)cc1)n1cncn1

name: Letermovir
text:
This molecule reads as letermovir, with one wedged stereocentre.

- **Core:** a 3,4-dihydroquinazoline. The aromatic ring carries a fluorine at C8. N3 bears the aryl group, C2 bears the piperazine, and N1=C2 is the ring C=N.
- **N3 aryl group:** 2-methoxy-5-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.
- **C2 substituent:** a piperazine whose far nitrogen carries a 3-methoxyphenyl group.
- **C4:** carries a CH2COOH group on a wedge bond, and this is the only stereocentre drawn.

For the stereocentre, I wrote the neighbours in the order CH2, H, N (ring closure), aromatic C. With the implicit H pointing away from the viewer, the sequence CH2 → N → aromatic C runs counterclockwise on the page. That corresponds to `@` in this atom order.

SMILES: OC(=O)C[C@H]1c2cccc(F)c2N=C(N3CCN(CC3)c3cccc(OC)c3)N1c1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1OC

name: Lenacapavir Sodium
text:
This structure is the sodium salt of lenacapavir. I read it region by region and wrote the SMILES from that reading.

- **Left end:** a CH3–SO2–C(CH3)2–C≡C– group is attached to the pyridine ring.
- **Pyridine and side chain:** the pyridine carries a stereocentre CH(NH–C(=O)–CH2–) on its other side, which also bears a CH2–(3,5-difluorophenyl) group. The hashed bond points to the CH2 and the centre works out as S.
- **Bicyclic amide end:** the acetamide CH2 is attached to a pyrazole nitrogen. The pyrazole carries CF3 and is fused to a cyclopentene that bears a CF2 group and a cyclopropane.
  - The two cyclopropane CH carbons have hashed H atoms, and I converted these to @@ and @@ in the SMILES.
- **Lower indazole:** the indazole carries Cl at C4, an N–CH2CF3 group, and a deprotonated sulfonamide [N-]–SO2CH3 at C3.
- **Counterion:** Na+.

I checked ring closures and the atom order at each stereocentre against the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(C#CC1=NC([C@H](CC4=CC(=CC(=C4)F)F)NC(=O)CN5C6=C([C@@H]7[C@@H](C7)C6(F)F)C(=N5)C(F)(F)F)=C(C=C1)C2=C3C(=C(C=C2)Cl)C(=NN3CC(F)(F)F)[N-]S(=O)(=O)C)S(=O)(=O)C.[Na+]

name: Leu-Enkephalin
text:
The drawing shows the linear pentapeptide Tyr-Gly-Gly-Phe-Leu (Leu-enkephalin), read from the N-terminal tyrosine to the C-terminal leucine.

- **Tyrosine:** a para-hydroxyphenyl ring on a CH2, with a free NH2 on the hashed α-carbon. Working out the CIP priorities from the hashed bond gives S, which is L-Tyr.
- **Glycine ×2:** two CH2 units, each flanked by amide NH and C=O groups, with no stereocentre.
- **Phenylalanine:** an unsubstituted phenyl ring on a CH2. The CH2 sits on a wedged bond at the α-carbon, which works out to S (L-Phe).
- **Leucine:** an isobutyl side chain on a hashed bond at the α-carbon, ending in a free COOH. This also works out to S (L-Leu).

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Leuprolide
text:
I read this as leuprolide, the nonapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Leu‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑NHEt. I did not derive the stereocentres atom by atom from the drawing. I took the stereo SMILES from my memory of the standard leuprolide structure. The drawing is consistent with it: the two leucines have opposite wedge directions, which fits D‑Leu at position 6 and L‑Leu at position 7.

Reading along the chain from the N‑terminus, the drawing shows:
- a pyroglutamic acid ring (5‑oxopyrrolidine) at the N‑terminus
- His, with an imidazole side chain
- Trp, with an indole side chain
- Ser, with a CH2OH side chain
- Tyr, with a 4‑hydroxyphenyl side chain
- D‑Leu, with an isobutyl side chain
- Leu, with an isobutyl side chain
- Arg, with a three‑carbon chain ending in a guanidine
- Pro, with a pyrrolidine ring, capped as an N‑ethyl amide (C(=O)NHCH2CH3) at the C‑terminus

SMILES: CCNC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CC2=CC=C(C=C2)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](CC3=CNC4=CC=CC=C43)NC(=O)[C@H](CC5=CN=CN5)NC(=O)[C@@H]6CCC(=O)N6

name: Leukotriene B4
text:
I read the molecule as leukotriene B4, 5,12-dihydroxy-icosa-6,8,10,14-tetraenoic acid.

**Chain.** Counting from the carboxylic acid: C1 is the COOH carbon, C2–C4 are CH2 groups, C5 carries an OH, and C6=C7, C8=C9 and C10=C11 are double bonds. C12 carries a second OH, C13 is CH2, C14=C15 is a double bond, and C16–C20 form a pentyl tail ending in CH3, giving 20 carbons in total.

**Double bonds.** From the drawing, C6=C7 is cis (Z), C8=C9 is trans (E), C10=C11 is trans (E) and C14=C15 is cis (Z).

**Stereocentres.** Both OH groups are drawn on wedges, with the implicit H pointing away. I worked out the chirality tags from the neighbour order around each carbon:
- C5, with neighbours C4, H, OH, C6 in SMILES order, is `[C@H]`.
- C12, with neighbours C11, H, OH, C13 in SMILES order, is `[C@H]`.

This gives 5S,12R, the natural LTB4 configuration.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC[C@H](O)/C=C\C=C\C=C\[C@H](O)C/C=C\CCCCC

name: Levetiracetam
text:
The drawing shows (S)-2-(2-oxopyrrolidin-1-yl)butanamide, which is levetiracetam.

- **Ring:** a five-membered lactam. The ring nitrogen is bonded to three ring CH2 carbons and then to a C=O carbon that closes the ring, giving a 2-oxopyrrolidine attached through N.
- **Side chain:** the ring nitrogen is bonded to the stereocentre. That carbon carries an ethyl group (drawn on a wedge), a primary amide C(=O)NH2, and an implicit hydrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the ethyl group is on a wedge, so the implicit hydrogen points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > C(=O)NH2 > ethyl > H. Going N (left), then amide (lower right), then ethyl (upper right) turns counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- **SMILES check:** the written SMILES `CC[C@H](N1CCCC1=O)C(N)=O` has neighbour order ethyl, H, N, amide. With `@`, H, N and amide run counterclockwise when viewed from the ethyl group, which corresponds to S. It matches the known levetiracetam SMILES `CC[C@@H](C(N)=O)N1CCCC1=O` after swapping the last two neighbours and flipping the symbol.

SMILES: CC[C@H](N1CCCC1=O)C(N)=O

name: Levamisole
text:
I read the drawing as a phenyl group on a fused bicyclic ring: a 2,3,5,6-tetrahydroimidazo[2,1-b]thiazole core, which is the tetramisole/levamisole skeleton.

**Ring system**
- The thiazoline ring is S–CH2–CH2–N–C(=N), closed through the amidine carbon.
- The imidazoline ring shares the N–C(=N) edge with the thiazoline ring. Its other atoms are the C=N nitrogen, the stereocentre bearing the phenyl group, and a CH2 attached to the bridgehead N.
- The benzene ring is drawn as a normal six-membered aromatic ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only wedge is a hashed bond from the stereocentre to the phenyl carbon, so the phenyl points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Viewed from the H side, the remaining neighbours go N, phenyl, CH2 counterclockwise.
- In the SMILES order N, H, phenyl, CH2, that corresponds to `@@`.

The SMILES `C1CSC2=N[C@@H](c3ccccc3)CN12` is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: C1CSC2=N[C@@H](c3ccccc3)CN12

name: Levobunolol
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** a tert-butyl group (a carbon with three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- **Chain:** NH connects to a CH2, then to a CH bearing an OH on a wedge bond, then to another CH2, which is bonded to an ether oxygen.
- **Ring system:** the ether oxygen is on an aromatic ring fused to a six-membered ring. That ring holds a ketone (C=O) next to the aromatic carbon and three CH2 groups, the last of which joins the aromatic carbon adjacent to the O-bearing carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** only the carbinol carbon is a stereocentre. The wedged OH points toward the viewer, so the H is at the back. The substituent priorities are OH > CH2O > CH2N. Going OH → CH2O → CH2N is counterclockwise with H at the back, which gives the S configuration. In the SMILES order (CH2N, H, O, CH2O), this corresponds to `@`.

This is levobunolol.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC[C@H](O)COc1cccc2C(=O)CCCc12

name: Levodopa
text:
The drawing shows L-DOPA (3,4-dihydroxy-L-phenylalanine).

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent OH groups (at the 3 and 4 positions relative to the side chain).
- **Side chain:** a CH2 links the ring to a stereocentre. That carbon carries NH2 on a wedge bond and a COOH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the NH2 is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. Reading the substituents by priority, N, then COOH, then CH2, goes counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This matches the standard L-amino-acid SMILES pattern N[C@@H](R)C(=O)O.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1)C(=O)O

name: Levocetirizine
text:
The structure is cetirizine, a diaryl-methyl piperazine carrying an ethoxyacetic acid chain, with one stereocentre drawn as a wedge.

**Reading the drawing:**
