- **Aryl groups:** an unsubstituted phenyl ring (upper left) and a 4-chlorophenyl ring (lower left) are both attached to one central CH carbon.
- **Piperazine:** the same CH carbon is bonded to one piperazine nitrogen by a wedge bond. The other nitrogen carries the side chain.
- **Side chain:** N–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–C(=O)OH, a 2-ethoxyacetic acid group.

**Stereochemistry:** the central carbon has the wedge to N (toward the viewer), the phenyl up-left, the chlorophenyl down-left, and an implicit H pointing away. Viewed from the front, N → phenyl → chlorophenyl runs counterclockwise. I wrote the SMILES with the neighbour order N, H, phenyl, chlorophenyl, which makes this centre `[C@H]`. I derived this by hand and did not check it against a known SMILES for the named enantiomer.

SMILES: OC(=O)COCCN1CCN(CC1)[C@H](c1ccccc1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Levodropropizine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Aromatic ring:** a six-membered benzene ring (phenyl) on the left.
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two nitrogens para to each other. One nitrogen is bonded to the phenyl ring, and the other carries the side chain.
- **Side chain:** N–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–OH. The stereocentre carries a bold wedge to its OH, which is the only stereo marking in the drawing.

**Assigning the stereocentre:**
- The CIP priorities are OH > CH2OH > CH2N > H.
- The wedged OH points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away.
- On screen, OH is at the bottom, CH2OH at the upper right and CH2N at the upper left. Going OH → CH2OH → CH2N runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.

**Writing the SMILES:** with the chain written as C(N…)[C@H](O)CO, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2N, H, O, CH2OH. Working through the permutation, `@` corresponds to S, so `[C@H]` is correct.

This is levodropropizine, (S)-3-(4-phenylpiperazin-1-yl)propane-1,2-diol.

SMILES: C(N1CCN(CC1)c1ccccc1)[C@H](O)CO

name: Levofloxacin
text:
I read this as levofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone with a fused oxazine ring. The main features I read from the drawing:

- **Core:** a benzene ring fused to a 4-pyridone ring, with a ring C=O and a carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) on the pyridone.
- **Substituents on the benzene ring:** F, and an N-methylpiperazine attached through its nitrogen.
- **Oxazine ring:** an O–CH2–CH(CH3)–N ring fused across the benzene ring and the pyridone nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the CH(CH3) carbon, with a wedge bond to the methyl group. The priorities are N > CH2O > CH3 > H. With H pointing away from the viewer, N (up), CH2 (left) and CH3 (down-right) run counterclockwise, so the centre is S. I chose `@` in the SMILES so that it also comes out as S.

SMILES: C[C@H]1COc2c(N3CCN(C)CC3)c(F)cc3c(=O)c(C(=O)O)cn1c23

name: Levocabastine
text:
I read the image as a 4-cyano-4-(4-fluorophenyl)cyclohexyl group attached through its C1 to the nitrogen of a piperidine ring.

- **Piperidine ring:** the carbon opposite the nitrogen (C4) is quaternary and carries a phenyl group and a COOH group. The COOH is drawn on a wedge. The ring carbon next to C4 on the nitrogen's other side (C3) carries a methyl on a hashed bond.
- **Cyclohexane ring:** one carbon bears the nitrile (C#N) and the 4-fluorophenyl ring, and the carbon opposite it bears the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the two stereocentres from the 2D wedge and hash geometry. In the SMILES atom order, the quaternary C4 comes out as `@@` and the methyl-bearing C3 as `@`.

SMILES: N#CC1(c2ccc(F)cc2)CCC(CC1)N1CC[C@@](c2ccccc2)(C(=O)O)[C@H](C)C1

name: Lidocaine
text:
The drawing shows lidocaine. Reading it region by region:

- **Left:** a diethylamino group, N(CH2CH3)2, with two ethyl chains on the nitrogen.
- **Middle:** that nitrogen is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a C=O. The carbonyl carbon is bonded to NH (an amide).
- **Right:** the NH is attached to a benzene ring. The ring carbons on either side of the attachment point each carry a methyl group (2,6-dimethylphenyl).

SMILES: CCN(CC)CC(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Levosimendan
text:
This structure is levosimendan, the (R)-enantiomer. Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a six-membered ring containing an amide-type NH–C(=O), a CH2, a stereocentre CH bearing a methyl group, and a C=N that closes the ring through an N–N bond.
- **Stereocentre:** the methyl is drawn on a hashed bond. Its neighbours rank C3 (the C=N carbon) > CH2 > CH3 > H. The H points toward the viewer, and C3 → CH2 → CH3 runs counterclockwise from the front, so the configuration is R.
- **Middle:** a para-disubstituted benzene ring, joined to the C=N carbon of the left ring at one end.
- **Right side:** at the other end of the benzene ring, an NH–N= hydrazone linked to a carbon that carries two nitrile groups (C#N).

The SMILES below is written so that its `@@` tag encodes the same R configuration (checked by reordering the neighbours to put H first).

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC(=O)NN=C1c1ccc(NN=C(C#N)C#N)cc1

name: Levothyroxine Sodium
text:
The structure is thyroxine (T4) as its sodium salt, which is levothyroxine sodium.

- **Amino acid end:** a carboxylate (O⁻ and C=O) is attached to a stereocentre bearing NH₂ on a wedge. A CH₂ then links this centre to the first aromatic ring.
- **Inner ring:** it carries two iodines, one at the top and one at the bottom right. A diaryl ether oxygen sits between the two iodines.
- **Outer ring:** the ether oxygen joins it to a ring bearing two iodines flanking an OH, which makes four iodines in total.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺ is drawn separately.
- **Stereochemistry:** with the wedged NH₂ pointing up, CH₂ at lower right, COO⁻ at lower left and H implied behind, N→CH₂→COO⁻ runs clockwise. That gives `N[C@@H](C...)C(=O)[O-]`, the L-amino acid configuration.

SMILES: [Na+].N[C@@H](Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2cc(I)c(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1)C([O-])=O

name: Levonorgestrel
text:
I read this as levonorgestrel: a 13-ethyl gonane skeleton with a 3-keto-4-ene A-ring and a 17-hydroxy-17-ethynyl D-ring. I compared the six wedge/hash centres against the drawing one by one, and each matches the SMILES below.

- **C13:** ethyl is hashed.
- **C17:** OH is hashed.
- **C14:** H is wedged.
- **C8:** H is hashed.
- **C9:** H is wedged.
- **C10:** H is hashed.

SMILES: CC[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C#C)O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@H]34

name: Lifitegrast
text:
I read this as lifitegrast, the (S)-amino acid with a benzofuran-6-carbonyl group.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carries a methylsulfonyl group (CH3SO2) in the meta position. It is joined through a CH2 to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries the hashed CH2, the NH and the COOH. With H pointing toward the viewer, the priorities N > COOH > CH2 run clockwise on the page, so the true configuration is S. The SMILES `C[C@H](N…)C(=O)O` was checked to give S.
- **Centre ring:** the NH is acylated by an amide on a dichlorinated benzene ring, with Cl on both carbons flanking the amide carbon. This benzene is fused to a tetrahydroisoquinoline ring (CH2CH2–N–CH2).
- **Right side:** the ring nitrogen is acylated by a benzofuran. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is next to the CH that touches the O-bearing ring-fusion carbon, so this is the 6-position (benzofuran-6-carbonyl).

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)c1cccc(c1)C[C@H](NC(=O)c1c(Cl)cc2CN(CCc2c1Cl)C(=O)c1ccc2ccoc2c1)C(=O)O

name: Linalool
text:
The drawing shows linalool, with a quaternary carbon bearing OH, a methyl, a vinyl group and a chain.

Reading the atoms from the image:
- The carbon at the right (about 1190,663) carries OH, a methyl (1422,770), a vinyl group (1085,896 = CH, then 1233,1105 = CH2), and a chain carbon at 958,556.
- The chain continues from 958,556 to 750,705 to 517,598. The carbon at 517,598 is double-bonded to 308,746, which carries two methyls (75,638 and 331,1000).

SMILES: CC(C)=CCCC(C)(O)C=C

No wedges or hashes are drawn, and the stereocentre is therefore left unspecified. The trisubstituted double bond has two identical methyl substituents, so it has no cis/trans geometry.

SMILES: CC(C)=CCCC(C)(O)C=C

name: Levorphanol
text:
I read this as an N‑methyl morphinan skeleton with a phenol OH on the aromatic ring, drawn with some bonds crossing.

**Skeleton**
- The nitrogen carries a methyl group. It is bonded to a CH2–CH2 chain that ends at the quaternary carbon C13, and to C9, which has a hashed H.
- C13 is bonded to four atoms: the wedged CH2 (C15), the aromatic carbon at the top of the ring junction, C14 below it, and a CH2 chain going to the right.
- C14 has a hashed H and is bonded to C13, C9 and a CH2 (C8).
- The cyclohexane ring is C13–C14–C8–CH2–CH2–CH2 (C8 to C13), closed back at C13. In the drawing the CH2–CH2 bond on the right crosses an aromatic bond.
- C9 is bonded to a CH2 (C10), which is bonded to an aromatic carbon. The aromatic ring is fused to C13 on the adjacent ring carbon, and a phenolic OH sits para to the C10 attachment.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned @/@@ from the wedge and hash bonds at C13, C14 and C9:
- C13 has the wedged C15 toward the viewer, which gives @.
- C14 has a hashed H, which gives @.
- C9 has a hashed H, which gives @.

This matches the levorphanol‑type morphinan configuration.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23CCCC[C@H]2[C@H]1Cc1ccc(O)cc13

name: Linagliptin
text:
The structure is linagliptin. I read it as a xanthine (purine-2,6-dione) core with these substituents:

- **N7:** a but-2-yn-1-yl group, CH2–C≡C–CH3.
- **C8:** a piperidin-1-yl ring carrying an NH2 at its 3-position.
- **N3:** a methyl group.
- **N1:** a CH2 link to C2 of a 4-methylquinazoline.

**Stereochemistry:** The only drawn stereocentre is the piperidine C3, where the NH2 is on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer). The implicit H therefore points toward the viewer. Reading the priorities N > ring CH2 next to N > ring CH2 next to CH2, the sequence runs counterclockwise from the front. With H toward the viewer this reverses to clockwise, giving R. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written as `C[C@@H](N)C` encodes R.

The SMILES was checked atom for atom against the drawing.

SMILES: CC#CCn1c(N2CCC[C@@H](N)C2)nc2c1c(=O)n(Cc1nc(C)c3ccccc3n1)c(=O)n2C

name: Linifanib
text:
The drawing shows a 3-amino-1H-indazole core with a para-substituted phenyl at C4, and that phenyl carries a urea linked to a 2-fluoro-5-methylphenyl ring.

**Indazole.** The five-membered ring is N=C(N)–C3a...C7a–NH, written as Nc1n[nH]c2cccc(c12)-.... The amino-bearing carbon (C3) is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to it, and to C3a. C3a is fused to the benzene ring, and C4 of that ring carries the aryl group. Its neighbour C7a bonds to the NH.

**Central phenyl.** It is para-substituted, with the indazole at one end and NH–C(=O)–NH at the other.

**Terminal aryl ring.** The carbon attached to the urea NH has fluorine on one adjacent carbon, and the other adjacent carbon is CH. Going around the ring from the NH-bearing carbon (C1): C2 carries F, C3 is CH, C4 is CH, C5 carries the methyl (the lower carbon), and C6 is CH, which sits between C1 and C5. The ring is therefore 2-fluoro-5-methylphenyl.

SMILES: Nc1n[nH]c2cccc(-c3ccc(NC(=O)Nc4cc(C)ccc4F)cc3)c12

name: Linoleic Acid
text:
Reading the drawing from the carboxylic acid end:

- The COOH group is at the left, with the carbonyl carbon as C1.
- Seven more chain carbons follow (C2–C8), then a C9=C10 double bond drawn with cis geometry.
- One CH2 (C11) separates it from a second C12=C13 double bond, also cis.
- Five more carbons (C14–C18) finish the chain, ending in a terminal methyl.

That makes 18 carbons in total with two cis double bonds at positions 9 and 12, which is linoleic acid, (9Z,12Z)-octadeca-9,12-dienoic acid.

SMILES: CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: Linezolid
text:
This structure is linezolid, the (S)-oxazolidinone antibiotic.

- **Left side:** an acetamide (CH3–C(=O)–NH–) is attached through a CH2 to the oxazolidinone ring.
- **Oxazolidinone ring:** a five-membered ring containing O, C(=O) and N. The ring carbon bearing the CH2NHAc group is the only stereocentre. Its bond to the CH2NHAc carbon is drawn as a hash.
- **Aryl group:** the ring nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring. That ring has a fluorine on one carbon and, on the neighbouring carbon, a morpholine nitrogen. The morpholine is a six-membered ring with N and O opposite each other.

For the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are ring O > ring CH2 (leading to N) > CH2NHAc > H. With the hashed CH2NHAc pointing away, the implicit H points toward the viewer. The sequence O → ring CH2 → CH2NHAc runs clockwise on the page. Reversing that for the H pointing toward the viewer gives S.

The SMILES below encodes that configuration.

SMILES: CC(=O)NC[C@H]1CN(C(=O)O1)c1ccc(N2CCOCC2)c(F)c1

name: Liothyronine
text:
The drawing shows 3,3′,5-triiodo-L-thyronine (T3).

- **Inner ring:** a benzene ring carrying the CH2 side chain, two iodines flanking the ring oxygen, and the diaryl ether O at the para position.
- **Outer ring:** a benzene ring joined through the ether O, with a para OH and an iodine ortho to that OH.
- **Side chain:** CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the NH2 is on a wedge. With H pointing away from the viewer, N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S, the L-amino-acid configuration. In the SMILES this is written as N[C@@H](C…)C(=O)O.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2ccc(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1)C(=O)O

name: Lipoic acid
text:
The image shows lipoic acid, a carboxylic acid with a four-carbon chain ending in a five-membered 1,2-dithiolane ring.

- **Acid end:** the left side is a carboxylic acid, with a C=O and an OH on the same carbon.
- **Chain:** after the carboxyl carbon there are four CH2 groups, the last of which is attached by a wedge bond to the ring.
- **Ring:** the five-membered ring contains two adjacent sulfur atoms (S–S), two CH2 carbons and one CH carbon. The CH carbon is the stereocentre, bonded to one S, one ring CH2, the chain CH2 and an implicit H.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedge points toward the viewer, so the H points away. The CIP priorities are S, then the ring CH2 (its neighbour carries S), then the chain CH2, then H. Viewed from the front, S (up), ring CH2 (lower right) and chain CH2 (lower left) run clockwise, so the centre is R.
- **SMILES check:** written as `OC(=O)CCCC[C@@H]1CCSS1`, the neighbour order from the stereocentre is chain, H, S, ring CH2. With `@@` this works out to R, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCC[C@@H]1CCSS1

name: Linaclotide
text:
I read this as a 14-residue peptide with three disulfide bridges. The sequence, from the free-amine N-terminus to the C-terminal acid, is Cys-Cys-Glu-Tyr-Cys-Cys-Asn-Pro-Ala-Cys-Thr-Gly-Cys-Tyr.

- **Termini:** The N-terminal Cys carries a free NH2, and the C-terminal Tyr ends in COOH.
- **Disulfides:** The pairings are Cys1–Cys6, Cys2–Cys10 and Cys5–Cys13. In the SMILES these are ring-closure labels %11, %12 and %13.
- **Side chains:** Glu has a CH2CH2COOH side chain. Asn has CH2C(=O)NH2. Pro is a pyrrolidine ring, and the two Tyr residues carry p-hydroxyphenyl groups.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assumed the natural L configuration at every α-carbon, including Thr (2S,3R). The wedge/hash marks I could read look consistent with this, but I did not check each one individually.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CS%11)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%13)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%11)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%12)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS%13)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O

name: Lithium bis(trimethylsilyl)amide
text:
The drawing shows two silicon atoms, each carrying three methyl groups, joined through a central N that is labeled with one H. A separate lithium atom is drawn at the left with a radical dot, so it is a distinct species and not bonded to the rest.

The two trimethylsilyl groups and the NH make up the amine hexamethyldisilazane. The lithium is written as a neutral radical, [Li].

The SMILES is written with the lithium as a separate component: [Li].C[Si](C)(C)N[Si](C)(C)C

SMILES: [Li].C[Si](C)(C)N[Si](C)(C)C

name: Lithium Carbonate
text:
The image shows a carbonate anion and two lithium cations, so this is lithium carbonate.

- The carbonate is a central carbon bonded to two O⁻ atoms by single bonds and to one O by a double bond.
- Two separate Li⁺ ions are drawn, each with a single positive charge.
- The charges balance: 2 × (+1) from lithium and 2 × (−1) from the two oxide oxygens.
- No stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: [Li+].[Li+].[O-]C([O-])=O

name: Lisaftoclax
text:
I read this as a venetoclax-type structure in which the gem-dimethyl group on the cyclohexene is replaced by a spiro-cyclobutane. Region by region:

- **Left end:** a 4-chlorophenyl group sits on a cyclohexene carbon. That carbon is double-bonded to a second carbon bearing a CH2 that leads to the piperazine. The ring continues through two CH2 groups to a spiro carbon, which carries a four-membered ring (cyclobutane) and links back through one more CH2.
- **Centre:** the piperazine N-aryl nitrogen connects to a benzamide ring. That ring carries a 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridin-5-yloxy group ortho to the carbonyl.
- **Acyl sulfonamide:** the amide C(=O)NH–SO2 links to a second benzene ring. This ring has a nitro group and an NH–CH2 substituent ortho to each other.
- **Right end:** the CH2 attaches to the 2-position of a 1,4-dioxane ring. The hashed bond on this CH2 gives the only stereocentre.

For the stereocentre, the hashed CH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Seen from the H side, the order CH2N → ring O → ring CH2 is clockwise. Written as `NC[C@H]4COCCO4`, with neighbour order CH2N, H, ring-closure O, ring CH2, this corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: Clc1ccc(cc1)C1=C(CN2CCN(CC2)c2ccc(C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c3ccc(NC[C@H]4COCCO4)c([N+](=O)[O-])c3)c(Oc3cnc4[nH]ccc4c3)c2)CCC2(CCC2)C1

name: Lisinopril
text:
This structure is lisinopril. It has a proline ring, a lysine-derived chain ending in NH2, and a 2-phenylethyl group on a carbon that carries a carboxylic acid and an NH.

I checked each wedge against CIP priorities, with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer:
- **Proline α-carbon:** the wedged COOH gives S.
- **Lysine α-carbon:** the wedged CH2 chain gives S.
- **Phenylbutanoic acid α-carbon:** the wedged CH2 gives S.

All three centres are S, which matches lisinopril.

SMILES: NCCCC[C@H](N[C@@H](CCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Lisdexamfetamine
text:
The drawing shows a lysine amide of amphetamine: H2N–(CH2)4–CH(NH2)–C(=O)–NH–CH(CH3)–CH2–phenyl.

- **Chain:** The terminal NH2 is followed by four CH2 carbons, then the alpha carbon bearing a hashed NH2, then the amide C=O.
- **Amide side:** The amide NH is attached to a CH that carries a hashed methyl and a CH2 leading to an unsubstituted benzene ring.
- **Alpha carbon (lysine):** The NH2 is hashed, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities N > C(=O) > CH2 run clockwise on the page, which reverses to counterclockwise because H faces the viewer. This gives S, the L-lysine configuration.
- **Amphetamine carbon:** The methyl is hashed, so H again faces the viewer. The priorities N > CH2Ph > CH3 run clockwise on the page, which reverses to S, matching dextroamphetamine.

I then converted each centre into the matching @/@@ tag for the order in which the neighbours appear in the SMILES.

SMILES: NCCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)Cc1ccccc1

name: Lithium Citrate
text:
The image shows lithium citrate: three Li⁺ cations and a citrate trianion.

The citrate part is a central carbon bearing an OH group and three carboxylate arms. Two arms are CH2–C(=O)[O⁻] and one is a carboxylate attached directly to the central carbon. The central carbon is not a stereocentre, since two of its substituents are identical.

The three lithium ions are written as separate fragments, each [Li+].

SMILES: [Li+].[Li+].[Li+].[O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-]

name: Lithium diisopropylamide
text:
The drawing shows lithium diisopropylamide (LDA) as separate ions.

- **Cation:** Li⁺ is drawn on its own, with no bond to the rest of the molecule.
- **Anion:** a central N⁻ is bonded to two isopropyl groups. Each isopropyl is a CH carbon carrying two methyl carbons. That gives 6 carbons in total: 2 CH and 4 CH3.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown, and none is needed, since the isopropyl carbons are not stereocentres.

SMILES: [Li+].CC(C)[N-]C(C)C

name: Lipid A 504
text:
I read this as an E. coli-type lipid A: a bisphosphate-free disaccharide of two glucosamines (4'-monophosphate, free reducing-end OH) joined by a 1→6 glycosidic bond, carrying six fatty acyl chains. I wrote the SMILES by region and did not independently verify every stereocentre against the wedges and hashes.

**Left (reducing) glucosamine ring**
- C1 carries a free OH.
- C2 carries an N-linked (R)-3-hydroxytetradecanoyl amide.
- C3 carries an O-linked (R)-3-hydroxytetradecanoyl ester.
- C4 carries a free OH.
- C6 is a CH2 linked through O to the other ring.

**Right (non-reducing) glucosamine ring**
- C1' is the glycosidic carbon, bonded to the O of the left ring's C6 CH2.
- C2' carries an N-linked 3-(dodecanoyloxy)tetradecanoyl amide.
- C3' carries an O-linked 3-(tetradecanoyloxy)tetradecanoyl ester.
- C4' carries the phosphate, OP(=O)(O)O.
- C6' is a CH2OH.

**Chain lengths:** I counted the 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl chains as 14 carbons. I assumed the secondary acyl chains are dodecanoyl (12 carbons) and tetradecanoyl (14 carbons) from the drawing and the usual lipid A pattern, not from an exact carbon count.

**Stereochemistry:** The ring stereocentres follow the natural D-glucosamine pattern, α at the reducing end and β at the distal ring. I assigned the (R)-3-acyl centres as `[C@H]` in the SMILES.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O[C@H](CCCCCCCCCCC)CC(=O)N[C@@H]1[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@H](OP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](CO)O[C@H]1OC[C@H]1O[C@H](O)[C@H](NC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H]1O

name: Lobeglitazone
text:
The drawing shows a thiazolidinedione (TZD) core with a benzyl substituent, linked through an ether and an ethyl chain to a pyrimidine.

**Thiazolidinedione end:** The ring is C(=O)–NH–C(=O)–S–CH. The CH carries a CH2 that leads to a para-substituted benzene ring. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marking.

**Linker:** The benzene ring bears an O–CH2–CH2–N(CH3) chain at the para position.

**Pyrimidine ring:** The ring atoms are N1, C2 (CH), N3, C4 (bearing the N-methyl amino group), C5 (CH) and C6 (bearing the aryloxy O). This makes it a 4,6-disubstituted pyrimidine. Reading the ring from the image:
- The top-left N is bonded to the C that carries the O-aryl group.
- That N is also bonded to the CH on the left.
- The CH on the left is bonded to the lower N.
- The lower N is bonded to the C that carries the N(Me) group.
- The C(NMe) is bonded to the CH at the right, which connects back to the C(OAr).

**Methoxyphenyl end:** The pyrimidine C–O is attached to a para-methoxyphenyl ring.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Methoxyphenyl–O–pyrimidine: COc1ccc(Oc2cc(N(C)CCOc3ccc(CC4SC(=O)NC4=O)cc3)ncn2)cc1
- Pyrimidine ring closure check: c2 (C–OAr), then c (CH), then c(N…) (C–NMe), then n, c (CH), n, which closes back to c2. This gives the six-membered ring c2, c, c, n, c, n.

SMILES: COc1ccc(Oc2cc(N(C)CCOc3ccc(CC4SC(=O)NC4=O)cc3)ncn2)cc1

name: Lobenzarit
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

**Left ring.** The ring carbons are C1 (320,595), C2 (495,735), C3 (462,960), C4 (252,1042), C5 (75,902) and C6 (108,678).
- C1 carries a COOH group.
- C2 carries the NH.
- C4 carries Cl.
- C1 is adjacent to C2, so the COOH is ortho to the NH.
- Cl on C4 is para to C1, the carbon bearing the COOH.
- C4 is also meta to C2, the carbon bearing the NH.

**Right ring.** The ring carbons are C1' (882,793), C2' (1093,710), C3' (1270,850), C4' (1237,1075), C5' (1027,1157) and C6' (850,1017).
- C1' carries the NH.
- C2' carries a COOH group, so it is ortho to C1'.

**SMILES.** Writing the left ring starting from the carbon that bears the COOH:
- OC(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1Nc1ccccc1C(=O)O
- Going c1 (C1, COOH), then c (C6), c (C5), c(Cl) (C4), c (C3), c1 (C2, NH), the Cl lands on C4 as drawn.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1Nc1ccccc1C(=O)O

name: Lodoxamide
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents:

- **Ring vertices:** C1 (upper left) bears Cl. C2 (upper right) bears NH–C(=O)–C(=O)OH. C3 (right) is CH. C4 (bottom) bears the C≡N group. C5 (lower left) is CH. C6 (left) bears NH–C(=O)–C(=O)OH.
- **Connectivity:** Going around the ring, Cl sits on the carbon between the two NH-bearing carbons. The nitrile carbon is para to Cl, since C1 and C4 are opposite each other.

The SMILES is N#Cc1cc(NC(=O)C(=O)O)c(Cl)c(NC(=O)C(=O)O)c1.

Checking the ring order: c1 (the nitrile carbon), then cH, then c(NHox), then c(Cl), then c(NHox), then cH closing the ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1cc(NC(=O)C(=O)O)c(Cl)c(NC(=O)C(=O)O)c1

name: Lobaplatin
text:
Reading the drawing as three separate components:

1. **Lactate dianion.** A carboxylate (C(=O)O⁻) is attached to a stereocentre that carries a hashed methyl and an O⁻ (alkoxide). Taking the hashed methyl as pointing away and the implicit H toward the viewer, the stereocentre works out to `C[C@H]([O-])C(=O)[O-]`.

2. **Cyclobutane-1,2-diyl-bis(methylamine).** The four-membered ring has two adjacent substituted carbons, each bearing a CH2NH2 group.
   - The left ring carbon has a wedged CH2NH2, so its H points away.
   - The right ring carbon has a hashed CH2NH2, so its H points toward the viewer.
   - Working through the neighbour order for each centre gives `NC[C@@H]1CC[C@H]1CN`.

3. **Platinum.** It is drawn as a separate Pt²⁺ ion, written `[Pt+2]`.

The charges balance: the two O⁻ groups give −2 and Pt gives +2. I derived the stereo marks by hand from the drawing and did not run them through a toolkit.

SMILES: C[C@H]([O-])C(=O)[O-].NC[C@@H]1CC[C@H]1CN.[Pt+2]

name: Lomitapide
text:
This structure is lomitapide: a fluorene with a 9-carboxamide (N-2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) and a 9-butyl chain, with the chain ending on a piperidine nitrogen. The piperidine 4-position carries an NH-C(=O) amide to a biphenyl bearing a CF3 group.

**Chain length:** From C9 of the fluorene, the drawing shows vertices at about (458,742), (520,818), (618,803) and (681,880), then N. That is four CH2 groups, so a butyl chain.

**Fragments:**
- Fluorene C9 is quaternary: C1(c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12) carrying C(=O)NCC(F)(F)F and the butyl chain.
- Butyl chain to piperidine: CCCCN1CCC(CC1)NC(=O)...
- Benzamide ring: c1ccccc1 with the C(=O) and the aryl group on adjacent carbons (ortho). The aryl group is a para-CF3-phenyl, c1ccc(cc1)C(F)(F)F.

**SMILES assembly:** O=C(NCC(F)(F)F)C1(CCCCN2CCC(CC2)NC(=O)c2ccccc2-c2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

SMILES: O=C(NCC(F)(F)F)C1(CCCCN2CCC(CC2)NC(=O)c2ccccc2-c2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: Lobeline
text:
I read the structure as lobeline: an N-methylpiperidine with a 2-oxo-2-phenylethyl group on one α-carbon and a 2-hydroxy-2-phenylethyl group on the other.

**Connectivity**
- The central ring has one N and five carbons, with an N-methyl group.
- The right α-carbon carries a CH2–C(=O)–phenyl chain.
- The left α-carbon carries a CH2–CH(OH)–phenyl chain.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the drawn wedge or hash, writing the SMILES neighbours in order and checking the sense on screen.
- The right ring carbon has a hashed bond to its CH2, so its H points toward the viewer. The neighbours N → ring CH2 → side CH2 run clockwise, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- The left ring carbon also has a hashed bond to its CH2. Taking the neighbour order H, ring CH2, N, side CH2 gives a clockwise sense, and one swap to the SMILES order gives `[C@H]`.
- The carbinol carbon has a wedged OH, so its H points away from the viewer. The neighbours CH2 → O → phenyl run counterclockwise on screen, so the sense is clockwise from the H side. One swap to the SMILES order gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CN1[C@@H](CC(=O)c2ccccc2)CCC[C@H]1C[C@H](O)c1ccccc1

name: Loperamide
text:
The drawing shows loperamide. Reading it region by region:

- **Amide end:** an N,N-dimethyl amide, where N bears two methyl groups and is bonded to a C=O carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** the carbonyl carbon is attached to a carbon carrying two phenyl rings.
- **Linker:** from that quaternary carbon, a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) leads to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the ring has 6 vertices (N, two CH2, two CH2, and C4). The C4 carbon carries both an OH and a 4-chlorophenyl group.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=O)C(CCN1CCC(O)(CC1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: LN-1-255
text:
I read the drawing as the sodium salt of a penicillanic acid S,S-dioxide (sulfone).

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring. The sulfur carries two =O, and the β-lactam carbonyl is next to the ring nitrogen.
- **C6 substituent:** an exocyclic C=CH–(2-pyridyl) group. The pyridyl and the ring CH (C5) lie on the same side of the double bond, so the pyridyl is trans to the lactam C=O. I encoded this with the `/` markers.
- **C3:** a carboxylate (COO⁻) on a hashed bond, with Na⁺ as the counter-ion.
- **C2:** a hashed methyl and a CH₂–O–C(=O)–CH₂ ester link to a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring.
- **C5:** carries a hashed H.

I worked out the three stereocentres (C3, C5, C2) from the hash positions and neighbour orderings in the drawing.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)[C@@H]1N2C(=O)/C(=C/c3ccccn3)[C@H]2S(=O)(=O)[C@@]1(C)COC(=O)Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1

name: Ljn452
text:
I read the drawing as a 2‑aminobenzothiazole, a tropane‑type bicyclic amine, and an isoxazole carrying a trifluoromethoxyphenyl group, joined through an ether linkage.

**Benzothiazole.** The benzene ring carries a COOH and an F. It is fused to a thiazole whose ring atoms are the aromatic C–N, N=C, C–S and the second aromatic carbon. The thiazole C2 is bonded to the bicyclic amine nitrogen.

**Bicyclic amine.** The nitrogen bridges two bridgehead CH carbons, giving an 8‑azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane skeleton. One bridge is C–C(O–)–C and the other is C–C. The central carbon of the three‑carbon bridge bears an O–CH2 substituent. Both bridgehead hydrogens are drawn as hashed bonds, so both bridgeheads get stereo marks. The central carbon of the three‑carbon bridge has no wedge, so it gets none.

**Isoxazole.** The ring runs C4–C3=N–O–C5. C4 carries the CH2–O chain, C3 carries a 2‑(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl group, and C5 carries a cyclopropyl group.

I assigned the @/@@ marks at the two bridgeheads from the hashed H positions in the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(F)c2nc(sc2c1)N1[C@@H]3CC[C@H]1CC(C3)OCc1c(-c2ccccc2OC(F)(F)F)noc1C1CC1

name: Loratadine
text:
This structure is loratadine, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Ester side chain:** an ethyl group (CH2CH3) is bonded to an O, which is bonded to a C(=O) that is attached to the piperidine nitrogen. This gives CCOC(=O)N.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring containing N, whose carbon opposite the nitrogen is double-bonded to the tricyclic core.
- **Tricyclic core:** a pyridine ring is fused to a seven-membered ring, which is fused to a benzene ring. The seven-membered ring contains two CH2 groups and the exocyclic C=C carbon.
- **Chlorine position:** Cl sits on the benzene ring.

Pyridine ring atoms, going around the ring: N, CH, CH, CH, then the carbon bearing the CH2 (c4), then the carbon bonded to N and to the C=C carbon (c3).

Writing the SMILES:
CCOC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)=C2c3ncccc3CCc4cc(Cl)ccc24

Checking the benzene ring: c4 is the carbon bonded to the CH2, followed by cH, then c(Cl), cH, cH, and finally c24, the carbon bonded to the C=C carbon, which closes ring 2 and ring 4. In the drawing, the benzene carbon attached to the C=C carbon (at 373,799) neighbours a CH (at 489,911). The other fused carbon (at 217,844) neighbours a CH (at 178,1002), which in turn neighbours the carbon bearing Cl (at 295,1114). So Cl is two atoms from the CH2-bearing fused carbon (CH, then C–Cl). The SMILES matches this: c4 (CH2-bearing), c (H), c(Cl), c, c, c24.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)=C2c3ncccc3CCc4cc(Cl)ccc24

name: Lorazepam
text:
The drawing is a benzodiazepine with a 7-chloro-5-(2-chlorophenyl) pattern and a 3-hydroxy-2-one lactam, which is lorazepam without stereochemistry.

**Atoms and connectivity**
- Seven-membered ring: NH, C(=O), CH(OH), N=, C(aryl)=, and the two fused aromatic carbons.
- The NH attaches to a fused aromatic carbon.
- The C=O carbon is bonded to the NH and to the CH(OH).
- The CH(OH) is bonded to the imine N.
- The imine N is double-bonded to the carbon that carries the 2-chlorophenyl group, and that carbon is bonded to the other fused aromatic carbon.
- Chloro-substituted benzo ring: the fused carbon bonded to NH is at (503,623) and the other fused carbon is at (707,689).
  - From (707,689) the ring runs to (866,546), then to the C–Cl carbon at (822,335), then (618,269), then (458,413), and back to (503,623).
  - So the Cl-bearing carbon is two atoms away from the fused carbon (707,689), via (866,546).
- Pendant phenyl ring: the ipso carbon is at (997,910), and the Cl is on the adjacent (ortho) carbon at (1087,1105).

**SMILES construction**
Starting from the lactam carbon: O=C1Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2C(c2ccccc2Cl)=NC1O

Checking the benzo ring: c2 (the fused carbon bonded to N) is followed by c, c, c(Cl), c, then c2 (the fused carbon bonded to the imine carbon).
- Fused carbon (503,623), then (458,413), then (618,269), then C–Cl (822,335), then (866,546), then fused carbon (707,689). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2C(c2ccccc2Cl)=NC1O

name: Lopinavir
text:
This structure is lopinavir, which I identified from the drawing. I worked out the stereochemistry at the carbon bearing the NH–C(=O)CH2OAr group and the hashed benzyl group directly from the wedges. I took the other three stereocentres from my recollection of the known lopinavir SMILES rather than deriving them from the wedges.

- **Left ring:** a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring carries an aryl ether O–CH2–C(=O)–NH.
- **Core chain:** that NH is on a stereocentre bearing a hashed benzyl group. Next is a CH(OH) with a wedged OH, then a CH2, then a stereocentre bearing a benzyl group and an NH.
- **Lower unit:** that NH is acylated by a valine-derived carbon with an isopropyl group (wedged) and a ring nitrogen. The ring is a six-membered cyclic urea, N–CH2CH2CH2–NH–C(=O).

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=CC=C1)C)OCC(=O)N[C@@H](CC2=CC=CC=C2)[C@H](C[C@H](CC3=CC=CC=C3)NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N4CCCNC4=O)O

name: Lonafarnib
text:
I read this as lonafarnib, a tricyclic benzo-cycloheptapyridine core joined to two piperidines.

- **Core:** a pyridine ring carrying Br fused through a CH2–CH2 bridge to a benzene ring carrying Cl and Br. The benzene Br sits next to the stereocentre carbon.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH linking the core to the first piperidine. Its bond to the piperidine carbon is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H faces the viewer. Taking the piperidine, pyridine-side and benzene-side neighbours in turn gives a counterclockwise sense on the page, which works out to `[C@H]` in the SMILES below.
- **Side chain:** the first piperidine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O)CH2, which attaches to the 4-position of a second piperidine. That piperidine's nitrogen carries a primary urea, N–C(=O)NH2.

I checked ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)CC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)[C@H]1c2ncc(Br)cc2CCc2cc(Cl)cc(Br)c12

name: Losartan
text:
This is losartan. The drawing breaks down as follows:

- **Butyl chain:** four carbons, attached to C2 of the imidazole ring.
- **Imidazole ring:** N3 (double-bonded to C2) lies next to the C bearing Cl. That carbon is C4, and it is double-bonded to C5, which carries the CH2OH group. N1 carries the benzyl CH2.
- **Biphenyl:** the CH2 is attached to one benzene ring. The opposite (para) carbon of that ring joins the second benzene ring. On the second ring, the carbon adjacent to the junction carries the tetrazole.
- **Tetrazole:** the ring is C(=N–NH–N=N) as drawn. The ring atoms run from the carbon through N (double bond to C), then NH, then N, then N (double bond), back to C. The drawing shows C=N at the bottom (N double-bonded to C), then NH, then N=N, then N attached to C. In SMILES: c1(nn[nH]n1) in aromatic form, or C1=NNN=N1 in Kekulé form, with the double bonds as drawn.

SMILES: CCCCC1=NC(Cl)=C(CO)N1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

SMILES: CCCCc1nc(Cl)c(CO)n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

name: Lorcaserin Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is lorcaserin hydrochloride, the (R)-8-chloro-1-methyl-2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1H-3-benzazepine salt with HCl.

**Structure read from the image**
- A benzene ring is fused to a seven-membered ring that contains one NH. The ring sequence is aryl C, CH2, CH2, NH, CH2, CH(CH3), aryl C.
- A Cl substituent sits on the benzene ring, meta to the aromatic carbon that bears the CH(CH3).
- The methyl on the CH carbon is drawn as a hashed wedge.
- A separate "HCl" label is drawn, so the answer is the hydrochloride salt.

**Stereocentre**
- The CH(CH3) carbon is the only stereocentre, and its implicit H points toward the viewer because the methyl is hashed.
- CIP priorities are CH2N (highest), then the aromatic carbon, then CH3, then H.
- On the page, CH2N is to the right, the aromatic carbon is upper-left and the methyl is down. This sequence runs counterclockwise.
- With H toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed to clockwise, so the centre is R.
- Writing the SMILES as `C[C@H]1CNCCc2ccc(Cl)cc12` gives R. Its neighbour order is CH3, H, ring closure to the aryl carbon, CH2N, and `@` is the symbol that corresponds to R for that order.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CNCCc2ccc(Cl)cc12.Cl

name: Loxapine
text:
This structure is a dibenz[b,f][1,4]oxazepine bearing an N-methylpiperazine on the imine carbon and a chlorine on one benzene ring. It is the loxapine skeleton.

**Atoms and connectivity read from the drawing**
- Left benzene ring: the carbon bearing Cl connects to a CH that leads to the ring-fusion carbon. That fusion carbon attaches to the imine carbon C(=N).
- The adjacent ring-fusion carbon of the same ring bears the oxygen.
- Seven-membered ring: this ring-fusion carbon, then O, then the right benzene ring carbon. The next carbon of the right ring carries the N, which is double-bonded to the imine carbon. The imine carbon bonds back to the left ring.
- The imine carbon also bears the piperazine nitrogen, and the piperazine's far nitrogen carries the methyl group.

**Writing the SMILES**
CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Oc2ccc(Cl)cc21

**Check of the left ring**
Reading the ring from the oxygen-bearing carbon (c2): `Oc2ccc(Cl)cc21` gives the O-bearing carbon, then CH, CH, C-Cl, CH, and finally the fusion carbon that closes both rings. In the drawing, the O-bearing carbon at (922, 595) is adjacent to the CH at (912, 415). That CH is adjacent to the CH at (752, 333), which is adjacent to the C-Cl at (600, 431). The C-Cl is adjacent to the CH at (610, 612), which is adjacent to the fusion carbon at (770, 693). This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Oc2ccc(Cl)cc21

name: Lorlatinib
text:
This structure is lorlatinib, a macrocyclic compound. I read it region by region:

- **Pyridine ring:** an N=C(NH2) unit, then a carbon bearing the ring oxygen, a CH, a carbon bonded to the pyrazole, and a CH next to the ring nitrogen.
- **Pyrazole:** an N-methyl nitrogen, a carbon bearing the nitrile, a carbon bonded to the pyridine, and a carbon bearing the CH2 linker, with an N=C bond to the ring nitrogen.
- **Linker to the amide:** CH2 to N(CH3), then C(=O) attached to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** a fluorine para to the carbon that bears the C(=O).
- **Stereocentre:** the CH(CH3)–O carbon is attached to the aromatic ring and carries a hashed methyl. Ranking the substituents as O > aryl C > CH3 > H, with the hashed methyl pointing away and the implicit H toward the viewer, gives R. The written SMILES `C[C@H]1O...` encodes this as R.

SMILES: C[C@H]1OC2=C(N)N=CC(=C2)C2=C(C#N)N(C)N=C2CN(C)C(=O)C2=CC=C(F)C=C12

name: Lotilaner
text:
I read the molecule as three connected parts and wrote the SMILES from them.

- **Left side:** a CF3CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2–NH–C(=O) chain ending at C2 of a thiophene.
- **Thiophene:** it carries a methyl group at C3 and is joined at C5 to the isoxazoline ring.
- **Isoxazoline:** a 4,5-dihydroisoxazole ring (C3=N–O–C5–CH2). Its C5 bears a 3,4,5-trichlorophenyl ring and a CF3 group, and only the CF3 is drawn on a wedge.

**Stereocentre.** The only stereocentre is the isoxazoline C5. Its neighbours in the drawing are O (up), the ring CH2 (left), the aryl carbon (right) and the CF3 (wedge, toward the viewer). Viewed from the CF3 side, O → aryl → CH2 runs clockwise. Converting that to the SMILES neighbour order O, CH2, aryl, CF3 gives `@@`.

SMILES: Cc1cc(sc1C(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(F)(F)F)C1=NO[C@@](C1)(c1cc(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Loteprednol Etabonate
text:
I read the drawing as a loteprednol etabonate skeleton, drawn as a mirror image of the usual steroid orientation.

**Skeleton and substituents**
- It is a 1,4-dien-3-one steroid (ring A) with a methyl at C10 and a methyl at C13.
- There is an OH at C11.
- C17 carries an ethyl carbonate (–O–C(=O)–OCH2CH3) and a chloromethyl ester (–C(=O)–OCH2Cl).

**Stereochemistry**
- The ring system is drawn with the D ring on the left, so it is flipped left-to-right relative to the standard steroid layout.
- Compared with the standard orientation, every wedge and hash is inverted. The methyls at C10 and C13 are hashed, the 11-OH is hashed, and the O on C17 is wedged. The H at C9 is wedged, the H at C8 is hashed, and the H at C14 is wedged.
- That makes this the enantiomer of natural-configuration loteprednol etabonate.
- I started from the loteprednol etabonate SMILES as I recall it from PubChem, which I did not look up, and inverted every stereocentre. I did not independently check that recalled SMILES against the drawing centre by centre, so the stereo descriptors are the least certain part of the answer.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)O[C@]1(CC[C@H]2[C@]1(C[C@H]([C@@H]3[C@@H]2CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]34C)O)C)C(=O)OCCl

name: Lumacaftor
text:
This is the lumacaftor structure: 3-[6-({1-[2,2-difluoro-1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl]cyclopropanecarbonyl}amino)-3-methylpyridin-2-yl]benzoic acid.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying a carboxylic acid (C(=O)O). A pyridine is attached at the position meta to the acid.
- **Pyridine:** the nitrogen sits next to the carbon bearing the benzoic acid ring. The adjacent carbon carries a methyl group. The carbon on the other side of the nitrogen carries the NH.
- **Amide:** NH–C(=O) leads to a cyclopropane carbon, which also bears the benzodioxole ring.
- **Benzodioxole:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing O–CF2–O.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1nc(NC(=O)C2(CC2)c2ccc3OC(F)(F)Oc3c2)ccc1C

SMILES: Cc1ccc(NC(=O)C2(CC2)c2ccc3OC(F)(F)Oc3c2)nc1-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1

name: Luotonin A
text:
This looks like the tryptanthrin-like alkaloid batracylin-type scaffold, specifically a quinazolinone fused to a pyrrolo[2,1-b]quinazoline-like ring. I read it from the drawing as follows.

**Left part:**
- A benzene ring is fused to a six-membered ring.
- That six-membered ring contains the aryl carbon bearing C(=O), the carbonyl carbon, N (the bridgehead nitrogen), a C (amidine carbon), and N= (attached to the aryl carbon).

**Middle and right part:**
- The amidine carbon C(a) is bonded to the bridgehead N and double bonded to the left N. It is also bonded to C(b).
- C(b) is double bonded to the right N and bonded to C(c).
- C(c) is bonded to CH2 and double bonded to CH.
- CH2 is bonded to the bridgehead N.
- The five-membered ring is therefore N–C(a)–C(b)–C(c)–CH2.
- The right N is attached to an aryl carbon of the right benzene ring, which carries the CH at its fused position. This gives a quinoline-type ring: C(b)=N–Ar…Ar–CH=C(c).

**SMILES construction:**
O=C1c2ccccc2N=C3N1CC4=Cc5ccccc5N=C34

**Check on ring closures:**
- C1 is the carbonyl carbon.
- c2ccccc2 is the left benzene ring, and its last aromatic atom is bonded to N.
- N=C3 is the left imine nitrogen and C(a).
- N1 closes the ring to the carbonyl and is the bridgehead nitrogen.
- C is the CH2.
- C4 is C(c), and =C is the CH.
- c5ccccc5 is the right benzene ring.
- N=C34 gives the right N double bonded to C(b), which closes ring 3 to C(a) and ring 4 to C(c).

C(c) has a double bond to CH, a single bond to CH2 and a single bond to C(b), so its valence is fine. C(b) has a double bond to N, and single bonds to C(a) and C(c), so it is fine too.

SMILES: O=C1c2ccccc2N=C3N1CC4=Cc5ccccc5N=C34

name: Lurasidone Hydrochloride
text:
The image shows lurasidone hydrochloride. I did not independently derive every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The stereochemistry below is the known lurasidone configuration, which I recalled rather than re-checked against the drawing.

- **Left side:** a norbornane-fused succinimide (a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane carrying a cyclic imide with two C=O groups), with wedge and hash H atoms at the four ring-fusion carbons.
- **Centre:** the imide nitrogen bears a CH2 attached to a cyclohexane. A second CH2 on the adjacent cyclohexane carbon (a 1,2-disubstituted ring) leads to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Right side:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries a 1,2-benzisothiazol-3-yl group (C=N–S in a ring fused to benzene).
- **Salt:** HCl is written as a separate component.

SMILES: C1C[C@@H]2C[C@H]1[C@H]3[C@@H]2C(=O)N(C3=O)C[C@@H]4CCCC[C@H]4CN5CCN(CC5)C6=NSC7=CC=CC=C76.Cl

name: Lumateperone
text:
I read the structure as lumateperone (a tetracyclic indole-fused core with a 4-fluorophenyl butanone chain), and wrote the SMILES from the drawing region by region.

- **Left side:** An N-methyl nitrogen sits in a six-membered ring (N–CH2–CH2–N) fused to a benzene ring. The second nitrogen of that ring is bonded to the stereocentre C_a.
- **Centre:** The five-membered ring runs from that nitrogen through C_a and C_b to the benzene ring. A piperidine ring is fused across C_a–C_b. Its ring nitrogen carries the side chain, and it has two CH2 groups on the C_a side and one CH2 on the C_b side.
- **Stereochemistry:** The two ring-fusion hydrogens, on C_a and C_b, are both drawn as hashed bonds. Working through the neighbour order at each centre gives `[C@@H]` for C_b and `[C@H]` for C_a in the SMILES below.
- **Right side:** A three-carbon chain runs from the piperidine nitrogen to a C=O, which is bonded to a para-fluorophenyl ring.

I checked the ring-closure digits so each ring closes on the intended atoms.

SMILES: CN1CCN2c3c1cccc3[C@@H]4CN(CCCC(=O)c5ccc(F)cc5)CC[C@H]24

name: Lumefantrine
text:
This structure is lumefantrine, read as follows:

- **Fluorene core:** a three-ring system with an exocyclic C9=CH double bond. One benzo ring carries a Cl (position 2) and the CH(OH) side chain (position 4). The other benzo ring carries a Cl at position 7, para to the biaryl bond.
- **Exocyclic alkene substituent:** the =CH– is attached to a 4-chlorophenyl ring.
- **Side chain:** CH(OH)–CH2–N(n-butyl)2, with two straight four-carbon chains on nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the carbinol carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label. The exocyclic double bond is drawn with the aryl group on the same side as the Cl-bearing, side-chain-bearing benzo ring carbon, so I encoded that geometry.

SMILES: CCCCN(CCCC)CC(O)c1cc(Cl)cc2c1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1/C2=C/c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Luliconazole
text:
I read the structure as luliconazole: a 4-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-1,3-dithiolan-2-ylidene carrying a nitrile and an imidazol-1-yl group on the exocyclic alkene carbon.

- **Imidazole:** it is attached through N to the alkene carbon, which also bears the C≡N group.
- **Dithiolane ring:** the alkene carbon is C2 of a five-membered ring containing two S atoms, one CH2 and one CH(aryl).
- **Aryl group:** the benzene ring carries Cl ortho and Cl para to the point of attachment (2,4-dichlorophenyl).
- **Stereocentre:** the aryl bond is drawn hashed, so the hydrogen points toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order (S, H, aryl, CH2) gives `[C@H]`.
- **Alkene geometry:** the imidazole N and the higher-priority ring S (the one bonded to the CH(aryl) carbon) lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so it is E. This is written with `/` and `/`.

SMILES: n1(cncc1)/C(C#N)=C1/S[C@H](c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)CS1

name: Lovastatin
text:
The drawing is lovastatin: a hexahydronaphthalene core carrying a 2-methylbutanoate ester, linked through an ethylene chain to a 4-hydroxy-tetrahydropyran-2-one (lactone) ring.

I read the structure region by region:

- **Core:** two fused six-membered rings. One C=C sits at the ring fusion, running to the CH next to the methyl-bearing carbon. A second C=C sits in the other ring.
- **Substituents on the core:** a wedged methyl on the left ring, a hashed methyl on the upper ring, and an ester oxygen on a wedged carbon.
- **Ester:** C(=O)–CH(CH3)–CH2CH3, with the methyl-bearing carbon drawn hashed.
- **Side chain and lactone:** a CH2CH2 linker leads from a hashed carbon to the ring carbon next to the lactone O, with a wedged bond at that ring carbon. The ring carries a hashed OH and a C=O next to the ring oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each stereocentre (the ring-fusion H is hashed) from the wedge and hash bonds and the 2D positions of its neighbours, then converted each to @ or @@ in SMILES atom order. All nine centres match the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)C(=O)O[C@H]1C[C@@H](C)C=C2C=C[C@H](C)[C@H](CC[C@@H]3C[C@@H](O)CC(=O)O3)[C@@H]12

name: Lycopene
text:
I read this as lycopene, an acyclic C40 carotenoid: a conjugated polyene chain with a 2-methylpent-2-ene end group on each side.

- **Left end:** a Me2C=CH–CH2–CH2– unit, then C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH–.
- **Middle of the chain:** the pattern continues as C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH–, then C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH–CH=C(CH3)–, with methyls drawn up on the left half and down on the right half.
- **Right half:** the polyene continues as CH=CH–CH=C(CH3)–CH=CH–CH=C(CH3)–, then –CH2–CH2–CH=C(CH3)2 at the far right.
- **Counts:** there are 8 chain methyls plus 4 terminal methyls, and 13 C=C bonds in total (11 conjugated plus the 2 terminal ones). This matches lycopene.
- **Stereochemistry:** every internal double bond in the polyene is drawn with trans (E) geometry. The two terminal Me2C=CH bonds have no stereo.

SMILES: CC(=CCC/C(=C/C=C/C(=C/C=C/C(=C/C=C/C=C(/C=C/C=C(/C=C/C=C(/CCC=C(C)C)\C)\C)\C)/C)/C)/C)C

name: Lypressin
text:
I read the drawing as the cyclic nonapeptide lysine vasopressin: Cys1–Tyr–Phe–Gln–Asn–Cys6–Pro–Lys–Gly-NH2, with a disulfide bridge between the two cysteines. The "C" labels in the ring are the cysteine CH2 groups.

- **Ring:** an amide-linked macrocycle with S–S between the two Cys side chains.
- **Side chains:** Tyr has a 4-hydroxybenzyl group, Phe has a benzyl group, Gln has CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 and Asn has CH2C(=O)NH2.
- **Tail:** from Cys6 the chain runs through Pro, then Lys with a free (CH2)4NH2, then Gly, ending in a C-terminal primary amide.
- **Stereochemistry:** I checked the Cys6 centre against the drawing (wedge to the carbonyl, hydrogen implied at the back) and it comes out R, which is L-cysteine. I assumed the other centres are the natural L-configuration as well, without checking each wedge or hash individually.

SMILES: NCCCC[C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H]2CSSC[C@H](N)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc3ccc(O)cc3)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc4ccccc4)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N2)C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Lurtotecan
text:
I read this as a camptothecin-type pentacyclic core with two additions: a 1,4-dioxane ring fused to the benzo ring, and a (4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl group on the pyridine ring carbon next to the benzo ring.

- **Lactone ring (left):** O–CH2 and a C=O, with a quaternary carbon carrying an ethyl and an OH.
- **Stereocentre:** this is the only stereocentre drawn with a hashed bond (to OH). From the 2D coordinates, the neighbour order ethyl, ring-closure carbon, OH, lactone C=O gives `@@` in the SMILES below.
- **Central rings:** a pyridone (N–C=O) fused to a five-membered ring containing N and CH2, then the quinoline-type ring with its imine-type N.
- **Benzo ring:** the dioxane O–CH2–CH2–O sits on the two benzo carbons on the right. Tracing the ring from the quinoline nitrogen side, the order is CH, then the two C–O carbons, then another CH, then the carbon bearing the substituent.
- **Substituent:** CH2 joined to piperazine N, with N-methyl on the far nitrogen.

I checked the ring closures atom by atom: the five-membered ring, the six-membered pyridine ring and the benzo ring each close with the right number of atoms.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCC2=C1C=C1N(C2=O)Cc2c1nc1cc3OCCOc3cc1c2CN1CCN(C)CC1

name: Mabuterol
text:
The drawing shows mabuterol.

- **Left side:** a tert-butyl group (a carbon with three methyls) bonded to NH, then CH2, then CH(OH) attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** the CH(OH) carbon attaches at one ring carbon. Going around the ring from there, the next carbon is a CH, then C-CF3, then C-NH2, then C-Cl, then a CH that closes back to the first carbon. This gives a 4-amino-3-chloro-5-trifluoromethyl pattern.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)c(N)c(Cl)c1

name: Macitentan
text:
The drawing shows a central pyrimidine ring, a 5-bromopyrimidine, a 4-bromophenyl group, and a propyl sulfamide chain.

**Central pyrimidine.** Going around the ring: N at the top left, then a CH at the top, then N at the right. Next comes the carbon bearing the NH–S group, then the carbon bearing the aryl group, then the carbon bearing the O–CH2CH2–O chain. This gives c1ncnc(...)c1... with the substituents placed as follows:
- The carbon bonded to NH is adjacent to the ring N on the right.
- The carbon bonded to O is adjacent to the ring N on the left.
- The carbon bonded to the aryl group lies between those two substituted carbons.

**Sulfamide.** The NH on the ring is bonded to S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to NH–CH2CH2CH3.

**Linker and second pyrimidine.** The ring O connects to CH2CH2 and then to another O. That O is bonded to C2 of a 5-bromopyrimidine, written c1ncc(Br)cn1.

**Aryl group.** The aryl substituent is 4-bromophenyl.

SMILES: CCCNS(=O)(=O)Nc1ncnc(OCCOc2ncc(Br)cn2)c1-c1ccc(Br)cc1

name: Luseogliflozin
text:
I read this as a C-aryl 5-thioglucose, which matches luseogliflozin, and wrote the SMILES from the drawing region by region.

**Aryl side**
- The left ring is a para-disubstituted benzene. One substituent is an ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O–) and the other is a CH2 linker.
- The CH2 links to the central benzene ring.
- Going round the central ring from the CH2-bearing carbon: CH, then the carbon bearing the sugar, then the carbon bearing OMe, then CH, then the carbon bearing the methyl, which closes back to the CH2-bearing carbon.

**Sugar side**
- The six-membered ring contains one sulfur and five carbons.
- C1 carries the aryl group on a hashed bond.
- C2, C3 and C4 each carry an OH, drawn wedge, hash and wedge respectively.
- C5 carries a hashed CH2OH.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned each of the five stereocentres from its wedge or hash and the 2D positions of its neighbours, with the implicit H on the opposite side to the drawn wedge or hash.
- I then converted each to @/@@ in the order the atoms appear in the SMILES.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(Cc2cc([C@@H]3S[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]3O)c(OC)cc2C)cc1

name: (+)-Lysergic acid diethylamide
text:
I read this as LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide): an ergoline tetracycle with an N-methyl piperidine ring, a diethylamide on C8 and an indole NH.

**Skeleton**
- The indole is drawn as a benzene ring fused to a pyrrole carrying an NH.
- A fused six-membered ring links the indole to a second ring. This second ring contains the N-methyl nitrogen, a ring CH2, and a C=C double bond.
- The amide is a C(=O)N(CH2CH3)2 group attached at C8 (the carbon at about (960, 657) in the image).

**Stereocentres**
1. At C8, the bond to the carbonyl carbon is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. From the viewer's side, the carbonyl, vinyl carbon and CH2 appear in clockwise order. With neighbours ordered (C=O, H, vinyl C via ring closure 1, CH2), this corresponds to `@`.
2. At C5 (the carbon at about (620, 601)), the H is hashed (pointing away). From the viewer's side, N, CH2 and the vinyl carbon appear counterclockwise, so from the H side they are clockwise. With neighbours ordered (N, H, vinyl C via ring closure 2, CH2), this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)[C@H]1CN(C)[C@@H]2Cc3c[nH]c4cccc(c34)C2=C1

name: Magnesium Orotate
text:
The image shows magnesium orotate: two orotate anions and one Mg²⁺ cation, drawn as separate fragments.

**Orotate anion.** The ring is a pyrimidine-2,4-dione. Reading around it:
- C6 carries the carboxylate, written C(=O)[O-].
- C6 is bonded to N1 (HN), which connects to C2 (=O).
- C2 connects to N3 (NH), which connects to C4 (=O).
- C4 connects to C5 (CH), which is double-bonded to C6.

This gives the SMILES [O-]C(=O)C1=CC(=O)NC(=O)N1.

**Full structure.** Joining two orotate fragments and the Mg²⁺ ion with dots gives the complete SMILES.

SMILES: [O-]C(=O)C1=CC(=O)NC(=O)N1.[O-]C(=O)C1=CC(=O)NC(=O)N1.[Mg+2]

name: Magnesium Trisilicate
text:
The drawing shows two Mg²⁺ ions and one trisilicate anion.

**Anion connectivity**
- The central Si carries two O⁻ groups (one above, one below). It also bonds to two bridging O atoms, one to the left and one to the right.
- The left bridging O connects to the left Si. That Si is double-bonded to an O and single-bonded to an O⁻.
- The right bridging O connects to the right Si, which has the same substituents: one =O and one O⁻.

**Charge check**
- The anion has four O⁻, so its charge is −4.
- The two Mg²⁺ ions give +4, so the whole drawing is neutral.

**SMILES:** I write the two magnesium ions as separate components, then the anion.
- Central Si: `[O-][Si]([O-])(O[Si](=O)[O-])O[Si](=O)[O-]`

SMILES: [Mg+2].[Mg+2].[O-][Si]([O-])(O[Si](=O)[O-])O[Si](=O)[O-]

name: Magnesium Stearate
text:
The drawing shows magnesium stearate, a Mg²⁺ ion with two identical stearate anions.

- **Chains:** In each chain I counted 18 carbon vertices, with x-positions from about 75 to 1329 in steps of about 74. The last one is the carboxylate carbon, so each chain is a 17-carbon alkyl chain plus the carboxylate carbon.
- **Head groups:** Each chain ends in a C(=O)[O⁻] group, with one C=O and one O⁻ drawn.
- **Metal:** The Mg is labelled 2+, which balances the two carboxylate charges.
- **Stereochemistry:** None is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)[O-].CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)[O-].[Mg+2]

name: Magnesium 2-pyrrolidone-5-carboxylate
text:
The drawing shows magnesium bis(pyroglutamate): two identical 5-oxopyrrolidine-2-carboxylate anions and one Mg²⁺ cation.

- **Each anion:** a five-membered lactam ring made of N–H, a C=O carbon, two CH₂ carbons and the ring CH carbon. The ring CH carbon carries a carboxylate group (C(=O)O⁻).
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge in each anion runs from the ring CH carbon to the carboxylate carbon, so that carbon is the sole stereocentre. With the implicit H pointing away, the priorities N > COO⁻ > CH₂ run counterclockwise, which gives S. This is the L-pyroglutamate configuration, written as `[O-]C(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1`.
- **Cation:** Mg²⁺ is drawn as a separate ion with no bonds to the anions.

SMILES: [Mg+2].[O-]C(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1.[O-]C(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1

name: Mafodotin
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as a maleimidocaproyl‑N‑methylvaline‑valine‑dolaisoleuine‑dolaproine‑phenylalanine chain, which is the mc‑MMAF framework.

- **Left end:** a maleimide ring, N‑linked to a five‑carbon chain (CCCCC) that ends in an amide carbonyl on an N‑methyl nitrogen.
- **First residue:** an N‑methylvaline. I checked its stereocentre against the wedge on the isopropyl group, and it comes out as `[C@H]` in the SMILES order used below.
- **Second residue:** a valine joined through an NH.
- **Next unit:** an N‑methylated carbon bearing a sec‑butyl group, then a CH(OMe) carbon and a CH2–C(=O) group. This is the dolaisoleuine unit.
- **Pyrrolidine unit:** the carbonyl is attached to the ring nitrogen. The ring carbon next to the nitrogen carries a CH(OMe)–CH(CH3)–C(=O) side chain. This is the dolaproine unit.
- **C‑terminus:** an NH‑linked phenylalanine with a free COOH and a phenyl ring.

I checked the first valine's centre directly from the drawing. For the other stereocentres I relied on the known MMAF configuration rather than re‑deriving each one from the wedges.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@@H]([C@@H](CC(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1[C@H](OC)[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(O)=O)OC)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N(C)C(=O)CCCCCN1C(=O)C=CC1=O)C(C)C

name: Malachite Green
text:
The drawing shows malachite green chloride, a triarylmethane dye. Reading it region by region:

- **Central carbon:** it carries a phenyl ring (top), a para-dimethylaminophenyl ring (right), and a double bond to a quinoid ring (left).
- **Left ring:** the quinoid ring has a C=N⁺(CH3)2 iminium at the far end. The double bonds run from the central carbon to the ring carbon, and from the ring carbon bearing N⁺ to that nitrogen.
- **Left ring bonds:** the ring carbon attached to the central carbon is C(=C), the ring has two C=C bonds, and the carbon bearing N⁺ is C(=N⁺).
- **Right ring:** an aromatic ring with an N(CH3)2 substituent.
- **Counterion:** Cl⁻.

The SMILES is written as C(=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccc(N(C)C)cc1.[Cl-]

Checking the quinoid ring: C1 (=C central), C=C, C(=N+), C=C, back to C1. The atoms are C1, C, C, C(=N), C, C, which is 6 atoms. The double bonds are C1=central, then C2=C3, then C4=N, then C5=C6, and C6 closes to C1 by a single bond. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccccc1)=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1.[Cl-]

name: Malathion
text:
The drawing shows malathion: a diethyl succinate backbone with a dimethyl dithiophosphate group attached through sulfur.

Reading the structure region by region:
- Left side: an ethyl group (CH3-CH2) bonded to O, which is bonded to a C=O carbon. This carbon connects to a CH2, which connects to a CH.
- The CH carries the S-P(=S)(OCH3)2 group.
- The same CH also bonds to a second C(=O)O-ethyl group, on the lower right.
- The phosphorus has a double bond to S, two single-bonded OCH3 groups, and a single bond to the bridging S.

The drawing has plain bonds only, so the CH stereocentre gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CC(SP(=S)(OC)OC)C(=O)OCC

name: Manganese(III) acetylacetonate
text:
The image shows Mn(III) tris(acetylacetonate) drawn as separate components: one Mn³⁺ ion and three acetylacetonate anions.

Each ligand has the connectivity CH3–C(=O)–CH=C(O⁻)–CH3. Reading the drawing, the carbonyl carbon is attached to the left methyl and the =O, and the other carbon carries the O⁻ and the right methyl. The CH= is in the middle, with a double bond to the O⁻-bearing carbon. In SMILES this is CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].

The three ligands carry −3 in total, which balances the +3 on Mn.

Stereochemistry: the C=C is drawn in a ring-free zigzag, and a cis/trans label could in principle apply. However, both substituent pairs are drawn in a plain way, so I leave the stereochemistry unspecified.

SMILES: [Mn+3].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-].CC(=O)C=C(C)[O-]

name: Mangafodipir
text:
This is the manganese(II) complex of the ligand known as mangafodipir, with the free acid form shown: N,N'-bis(pyridoxal-5-phosphate-derived) ethylenediamine-N,N'-diacetic acid (DPDP).

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyridine rings:** each ring has N, a methyl group, an OH, a CH2–N substituent and a CH2–O–P substituent.
- **Phosphates:** each is P(=O)(O−)(OH) attached to the ring CH2 through O.
- **Core:** each ring CH2 is attached to an N, the two N atoms are joined by CH2CH2, and each N carries a CH2COOH group.
- **Metal:** Mn2+ is drawn as a separate species.

Writing the left ring: the aromatic ring atoms are c1 (bearing CH2OP), c (the CH), c (bearing CH2N), c (bearing OH), c (bearing CH3) and n.

SMILES for the ligand: OP([O-])(=O)OCc1cc(CN(CCN(CC(O)=O)Cc2cc(COP(O)([O-])=O)nc(C)c2O)CC(O)=O)c(O)c(C)n1

Check of the left ring: c1(COP) c c(CN...) c(O) c(C) n1. In the drawing, the ring carbon bearing CH2OP is adjacent to N and to the CH. The CH is adjacent to the carbon bearing CH2N, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing CH3, which is adjacent to N. This matches.

Right ring, written as c2cc(COP)nc(C)c2O: c2 bears CH2N, then CH, then c(CH2OP), then n, then c(C), then c2(O). This matches the drawing.

The Mn2+ is added as a separate component: [Mn+2].

name: Mangafodipir Trisodium
text:
This is the manganese chelator mangafodipir (Mn-DPDP), drawn as a salt with three H+, three Na+ and one Mn2+.

**Ligand.** An ethylenediamine core carries two N-CH2-COO⁻ arms. Each nitrogen is also bonded to a CH2 that leads to a pyridine ring.

**Each pyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N, C(CH3), C(O⁻), C(CH2N), C(CH2OP) and CH. The ring has a methyl group, a phenolate O⁻, a CH2 to the amine nitrogen, and a CH2-O-PO3²⁻ group.

**Counter-ions.** The drawing shows [H+] ×3, [Mn+2] (drawn with a radical dot) and [Na+] ×3.

**Charge check.** Each ligand half carries a phenolate (−1), a carboxylate (−1) and a phosphate (−2), so −4 per half and −8 in total. The cations add 3 (H⁺) + 3 (Na⁺) + 2 (Mn²⁺) = +8, so the structure is neutral.

**SMILES for one half.** Starting from the ring methyl: Cc1ncc(COP(=O)([O-])[O-])c(CN...)c1[O-]. Here the ring runs N, C(CH3), C(O⁻), C(CH2N), C(CH2OP), CH, which matches the drawing.

**Full SMILES.**
[H+].[H+].[H+].[Mn+2].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].Cc1ncc(COP(=O)([O-])[O-])c(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])Cc2c(COP(=O)([O-])[O-])cnc(C)c2[O-])CC(=O)[O-])c1[O-]

The Mn is drawn as "Mn2+·", so I wrote it as [Mn+2].

SMILES: [H+].[H+].[H+].[Mn+2].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].Cc1ncc(COP(=O)([O-])[O-])c(CN(CCN(CC(=O)[O-])Cc2c(COP(=O)([O-])[O-])cnc(C)c2[O-])CC(=O)[O-])c1[O-]

name: Manidipine
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine with a 3-nitrophenyl group at C4, which matches manidipine.

**Dihydropyridine core.** The ring is NH–C(CH3)=C(CO2Me)–CH(Ar)–C(CO2R)=C(CH3).
- The left ester is a methyl ester: C(=O)OC.
- The right ester is C(=O)OCCN, which links to the piperazine.

**Aryl group.** The ring carries a nitro group meta to the point of attachment, written as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Side chain.** The ester oxygen leads to CH2CH2 and then to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries a CH(Ph)2 group.

**Stereochemistry.** C4 of the dihydropyridine is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OCCN2CCN(C(c3ccccc3)c3ccccc3)CC2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Lurbinectedin
text:
I read this as a trabectedin-type (ecteinascidin 743) skeleton. The scaffold is certain; the stereocentres were assigned from the wedge and hash bonds, so they carry some risk.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Top-right ring:** a benzene ring carrying a methyl, an acetate ester (OAc), and a methylenedioxy bridge (O–CH2–O).
- **Bottom ring:** a benzene ring carrying OH, OMe, a methyl and one aromatic H. It is fused through a CH2 into the bridged bicyclic core, which contains two N atoms (one N-methyl) and a CH–OH carbon.
- **Left unit:** a 5-methoxy-tetrahydro-β-carboline (indole fused to a piperidine ring with NH). Its quaternary carbon bears a CH2–S link to the core and a C(=O)–O ester.
- **Ester bridge:** that ester oxygen connects through a CH2 to the core carbon that also carries the top aryl ring.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond and its neighbour order in the SMILES.

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1c(C)c2OCOc2c3c1[C@H]4SC[C@]5(NCCc6c5[nH]c7ccc(OC)cc67)C(=O)OC[C@@H]3N8[C@@H](O)[C@@H]9Cc%10cc(C)c(OC)c(O)c%10[C@@H](N9C)[C@H]48

name: Mannitol
text:
I read the drawing as a straight six-carbon chain with an OH on every carbon (a hexitol). The two end carbons are CH2OH and the four inner carbons each carry one OH. The inner OH groups are drawn as follows, left to right: wedge, hash, hash, wedge.

I set the stereo for each inner carbon from the wedge or hash on its OH, taking the implicit H as pointing the opposite way. Writing the SMILES from the left-hand CH2OH gives the descriptors below.

- C2 (OH on a wedge): `@@`
- C3 (OH on a hash): `@@`
- C4 (OH on a hash): `@`
- C5 (OH on a wedge): `@`

I did not independently re-verify the chirality assignments beyond this single pass.

SMILES: OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Maprotiline
text:
This looks like maprotiline: a 9,10-dihydro-9,10-ethanoanthracene core with a 3-(methylamino)propyl chain on a bridgehead carbon.

**Core.** Two benzene rings are joined through two bridgehead carbons. One bridgehead (at about 605,633) carries the side chain. The other (at about 297,865) is a CH. Two labelled "C" atoms form the ethano bridge between the bridgeheads. The path is bridgehead 297,865 – C (378,800) – C (517,693) – bridgehead 605,633.

**Top benzene ring.** Its atoms are 430,558; 406,367; 230,290; 75,405; 97,598; 275,673. It is fused to the bridgehead at 605,633 (via 430,558) and to the CH bridgehead at 297,865 (via 275,673).

**Bottom benzene ring.** Its atoms are 629,826; 806,902; 828,1094; 675,1209; 497,1133; 475,941. It is bonded to the bridgehead at 605,633 (via 629,826) and to the CH bridgehead at 297,865 (via 475,941).

**Side chain.** From the quaternary bridgehead the chain runs CH2–CH2–CH2–NH–CH3.

**SMILES.** Writing the quaternary bridgehead as C1 (ring-bond labels 1 and 2):
- C12(CCCNC) opens the bridgehead with the side chain.
- c3ccccc3 is the top benzene ring, and its last aromatic atom closes onto the CH bridgehead.
- The bottom ring is opened from the quaternary carbon via ring label 2.

Full string: CNCCCC12CCC(c3ccccc31)c1ccccc12

Check: C12 is the quaternary carbon. The two bridge carbons CC follow, then C(...) is the CH bridgehead. Its first branch, c3ccccc31, is an aromatic ring that closes ring 3 within itself and closes ring 1 back to the quaternary carbon. After the branch, c1ccccc12 is the second aromatic ring, whose last atom closes ring 2 back to the quaternary carbon. Ring label 1 is reused after it was closed, which is valid. Both benzene rings are fused to both bridgeheads, as drawn.

SMILES: CNCCCC12CCC(c3ccccc31)c1ccccc12

name: Maribavir
text:
I read the drawing as a 5,6-dichlorobenzimidazole carrying an isopropylamino group at C2 and a ribofuranose on N1. This matches maribavir.

- **Benzimidazole:** The fused bicycle has two ring nitrogens, one of which is substituted (N1, bonded to the sugar). Two Cl atoms sit on adjacent carbons of the benzene ring.
- **C2 substituent:** The NH is bonded to a CH that carries two methyls. One methyl is at the lower left, and the other is drawn upward and overlaps the lower OH label, so it is an isopropyl group.
- **Sugar:** The five-membered ring has one ring O, with CH2OH at C4' and OH groups at C2' and C3'.
- **Stereochemistry:** The N1 bond at C1' and the CH2OH bond at C4' are both hashed, so they lie on the same face, which makes it β. Both OH groups are wedged, on the opposite face.
- **Handedness:** Going C1'→C2'→C3'→C4'→O is clockwise on the page. In the standard D-ribose Haworth view the base and CH2OH point toward the viewer, but here they point away. So this is the L-sugar, the mirror image of the D-ribonucleoside pattern.

I wrote the SMILES as the mirror image of the usual D-ribonucleoside pattern. I took that pattern from my recollection of the adenosine SMILES and cross-checked it against the PubChem form.

SMILES: CC(C)Nc1nc2cc(Cl)c(Cl)cc2n1[C@H]1O[C@@H](CO)[C@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Malacidin A
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic lipopeptide with an N-acylated, branched-chain exocyclic amino acid. It resembles the amphomycin/friulimicin family, but I did not identify it by name, so the SMILES below comes from tracing the drawing.

**Lipid tail.** An 8-methylnona-2,4-dienoyl group, CC(C)CCC=CC=CC(=O), with C2=C3 drawn trans and C4=C5 drawn cis.

**Exocyclic residue.** A 3-methylaspartic acid unit, N-acylated by the lipid and linked through its carbonyl to the ring.

**Ring residues, in order:**
1. 2,3-diaminobutyric acid. Its α-NH carries the exocyclic residue and its β-NH closes the ring. Only the α-carbon has a wedge, so the β-carbon is left unspecified.
2. Valine.
3. Lysine, with a free (CH2)4NH2 side chain.
4. β-Hydroxyaspartic acid. Only the α-carbon is taken as stereo-defined, because I assumed the hashed bond starts there; the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is left unspecified.
5. Aspartic acid.
6. Glycine, drawn as a plain "C".
7. 3-Methylaspartic acid. The carbon bearing the CH3 is drawn plain, so it is unspecified.
8. Valine.
9. 4-Methylproline, with stereo at the α-carbon (H wedge) and at C4 (methyl wedge).

The chirality marks come from the wedges and hashes at each α-carbon, reading the neighbours in SMILES order.

SMILES: CC(C)CC/C=C\C=C\C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(O)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N2C[C@H](C)C[C@H]2C(=O)NC(C)1

name: Maropitant
text:
I read the structure as a 2-benzhydryl-quinuclidin-3-amine whose nitrogen carries a 5-tert-butyl-2-methoxybenzyl group.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with OMe on one carbon, a CH2 linker to the NH on the adjacent carbon, and a tert-butyl group para to the OMe.
- **Centre:** an NH joined to a stereocentre (C3 of the bicyclic amine). C3 bears a hashed H and is bonded to the ring carbon C2 and to the bridgehead C4.
- **Bicycle:** a quinuclidine (1-azabicyclo[2.2.2]octane). The nitrogen is bonded to C2 and to two CH2 bridges that run to the bridgehead C4.
- **C2:** it carries a hashed H and a CH(Ph)2 group (two phenyl rings on one carbon).

**Stereochemistry**
- At C3, with the hashed H pointing back, N → C4 → C2 runs clockwise on the page. That gives `[C@H]` for the neighbour order N, H, C2 (ring closure), C4.
- At C2, with the hashed H pointing back, N → C3 → CHPh2 runs counterclockwise on the page. That gives `[C@H]` for the neighbour order N, H, C3 (ring closure), CHPh2.

I used distinct ring-closure digits so the quinuclidine ring (1, 2) and the phenyl rings (3, 4) do not clash.

SMILES: COc1ccc(C(C)(C)C)cc1CN[C@H]1C2CCN(CC2)[C@H]1C(c3ccccc3)c4ccccc4

name: Manganese phthalocyanine
text:
I read the drawing as manganese phthalocyanine: a 16-membered macrocycle of four isoindole units joined by bridging aza nitrogens. Two of the inner nitrogens carry a negative charge, and the Mn²⁺ is drawn as a separate ion, so I wrote it as a separate component.

I wrote the SMILES by tracing the macrocycle from the upper-left isoindole unit, with each fused benzene ring in an explicit Kekulé form. I checked ring closures and bond orders, and every carbon comes out with valence four.

I left out the radical dot shown next to Mn²⁺ in the image.

name: Marcellomycin
text:
I read the molecule as an anthracycline glycoside: a tetracyclic aglycone carrying a trisaccharide at C-7. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing, and I have not run the SMILES through a parser to confirm it is valid.

- **Aglycone:** a 1,4-dihydroxy-anthraquinone ring system fused to a cyclohexane ring, with a phenolic OH on the central aromatic ring. The cyclohexane ring has a quaternary carbon bearing OH (hashed) and an ethyl group, an adjacent CH bearing a methyl ester (wedged), and the glycosylated CH at the other end.
- **Sugar 1:** a 2,3,6-trideoxy sugar with a wedged NMe2 at C-3 and a wedged glycosidic O at C-4, attached to C-7 through a hashed O.
- **Sugar 2:** a 2,6-dideoxy sugar with a wedged OH at C-3 and a wedged glycosidic O at C-4, linked to sugar 1 through a hashed O.
- **Sugar 3:** a terminal 2,6-dideoxy sugar with OH groups at C-3 and C-4, both wedged, linked to sugar 2 through a hashed O.

name: Mavacamten
text:
I read the molecule as a uracil-type ring (a pyrimidine-2,4-dione) with three substituents:

- **Ring:** N3 carries an isopropyl group and sits between two C=O carbons. The ring then continues through a CH=C bond to N1–H, which closes the ring through the other C=O.
- **Amino side chain:** the ring carbon next to N1–H bears an NH, which is bonded to a CH(CH3)–phenyl group.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH carbon has a wedged methyl, so the hydrogen points away from the viewer. Seen from the front, methyl → phenyl → N runs clockwise. Written as N[C@@H](C)c…, this order (N, H, CH3, phenyl) corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: CC(C)N1C(=O)C=C(N[C@@H](C)c2ccccc2)NC1=O

name: Maxacalcitol
text:
This looks like the vitamin D analogue maxacalcitol (22‑oxacalcitriol). I identified it by recognising the overall skeleton rather than by working out each stereocentre from the wedges. The stereo tags below come from the known calcitriol pattern, so they are not independently checked against the drawing.

- **Side chain:** a CH(CH3) carbon carrying an ether oxygen, followed by CH2CH2C(CH3)2OH.
- **Ring system:** a bicyclic hydrindane core with an angular methyl, joined through a conjugated diene to a cyclohexane ring.
- **A‑ring:** the cyclohexane ring carries an exocyclic =CH2 and two OH groups.

name: Maytansine
text:
I read this as maytansine, a maytansinoid macrolide. The ring system and substituents are:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring carrying the OMe, the Cl, the ring N-methyl amide nitrogen and the CH2 link to the diene.
- **Macrocycle:** it contains the N-methyl lactam, the epoxide, the cyclic carbamate (NC(=O)O), a tertiary C–OH, a C–OMe next to the E,E-diene, and a methyl-bearing carbon.
- **Ester side chain:** an N-acetyl-N-methyl-alanine ester on the carbon next to the epoxide.

I did not derive every wedge and hash independently. The stereodescriptors and the diene geometry come from my recollection of the known maytansine isomeric SMILES, so the stereochemistry is the least certain part.
