name: Mebeverine Hydrochloride
text:
This is mebeverine hydrochloride.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Amine end:** an ethyl group and a CH(CH3) group are both attached to the nitrogen, which also carries the butyl chain.
- **CH(CH3) branch:** this carbon continues through a CH2 to a 4-methoxyphenyl ring.
- **Butyl chain:** N–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2–O. Counting the vertices from N gives four carbons before the ester oxygen (N, then 477/520, 541/610, 656/600, 722/692, then O).
- **Ester:** the oxygen links to a C(=O) attached to a benzene ring carrying two methoxy groups (3,4-dimethoxybenzoate).
- **Salt:** HCl is drawn separately.

The stereocentre at the CH(CH3) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CCN(C(C)Cc1ccc(OC)cc1)CCCCOC(=O)c1ccc(OC)c(OC)c1.Cl

name: Mechlorethamine
text:
The drawing shows a central nitrogen with three substituents:

- a methyl group, drawn as a plain line going up from N
- two identical CH2CH2Cl chains, one going down-left and one going down-right

Each chain runs N–CH2–CH2–Cl.

This is mechlorethamine (bis(2-chloroethyl)methylamine). The image shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN(CCCl)CCCl

name: Meclizine
text:
The drawing shows meclizine: a piperazine ring with two nitrogens.

- One nitrogen carries a CH group bearing a phenyl ring and a 4-chlorophenyl ring.
- The other nitrogen carries a CH2 attached to a benzene ring that has a methyl group.

To place the methyl, I number the benzyl ring from the CH2-bearing carbon at (1085, 866) as C1. Its neighbours are the carbon at (1065, 740) and the carbon at (1205, 910). The methyl-bearing carbon at (1305, 830) is attached to (1205, 910), so it sits two bonds from C1, which makes it meta. The chlorine is on the para carbon of the chlorophenyl ring: the ring carbon at (407, 848) attaches to the CH, and the Cl carbon at (208, 1011) is three bonds away.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds are drawn, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: Cc1cccc(CN2CCN(CC2)C(c2ccccc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2)c1

SMILES: Cc1cccc(CN2CCN(CC2)C(c2ccccc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc2)c1

name: Meclofenamic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a diarylamine with a carboxylic acid, which I read as follows.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring with a COOH group on one carbon. The adjacent ring carbon is bonded to the NH.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring whose atoms I label going around the ring:
- C1 is bonded to the NH.
- C2, at the top, carries a Cl.
- C3 is an unsubstituted CH.
- C4 is an unsubstituted CH.
- C5, at the right, carries the methyl group.
- C6, at the bottom, carries the second Cl and sits between C5 and C1.

So the substituents are N at C1, Cl at C2, methyl at C5 and Cl at C6. Both chlorines are ortho to the N, and the methyl is meta to the N, adjacent to the C6 chlorine.

**SMILES:** I wrote the acid ring first, then the NH, then the substituted ring.

Acid ring: OC(=O)c1ccccc1N. For the right ring, starting at C1 (the N-bearing carbon), the path is c1(Cl)ccc(C)c(Cl)c1, which visits C1, then C2 (Cl), C3, C4, C5 (methyl), C6 (Cl), and closes back to C1.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1c(Cl)ccc(C)c1Cl

name: Medronic Acid
text:
The drawing shows methylenediphosphonic acid. A central CH2 carbon links two phosphorus atoms. Each phosphorus carries one double-bonded oxygen (P=O) and two hydroxyl groups (OH).

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so the SMILES has no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=P(O)(O)CP(=O)(O)O

name: Medetomidine
text:
This is medetomidine: a 1-(2,3-dimethylphenyl)ethyl group on an imidazole ring.

**Imidazole ring.** The ring atoms are NH, a carbon bearing the side chain, a CH, a second N, and a CH between the two nitrogens. The substituted carbon is bonded to NH and double-bonded to the CH. That CH is bonded to the unprotonated N, which is double-bonded to the CH between the nitrogens. This gives the ring c1c[nH]cn1 pattern, written below as C1=C(NC=N1)... (4-substituted imidazole).

**Side chain.** The substituent is CH(CH3) attached to the benzene ring.

**Benzene ring.** The carbon bonded to the CH(CH3) has a neighbouring carbon bearing a methyl, and the next carbon along also bears a methyl. This is a 2,3-dimethylphenyl group.

**SMILES check.** CC(c1ccc[nH]1)... would be wrong, so I write the imidazole explicitly: CC(C1=CN=CN1)c1cccc(C)c1C.

- The imidazole carbon C1 is bonded to NH (closing the ring), and double-bonded to CH.
- That CH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to the CH, which is bonded to NH. This is consistent with the drawing.
- The aromatic part c1cccc(C)c1C starts at the attachment carbon, runs through three CH atoms, then the methyl-bearing carbon, then the ring-closing carbon bearing the other methyl, which is adjacent to the attachment carbon. This matches the 2,3-dimethyl pattern.

SMILES: CC(C1=CN=CN1)c1cccc(C)c1C

name: Mefenamic Acid
text:
The drawing shows mefenamic acid: an anthranilic acid whose nitrogen carries a 2,3-dimethylphenyl group.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring with a COOH group on one carbon. The adjacent ring carbon bears the NH.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring attached to the NH at one carbon (C1). The next carbon (C2, at about 1072,854) carries a methyl. The carbon after that (C3, at about 1260,772) also carries a methyl. The remaining three ring carbons are unsubstituted.

SMILES: Cc1cccc(Nc2ccccc2C(=O)O)c1C

name: Megazol
text:
The drawing shows two rings joined by a single bond.

**Thiadiazole ring (left):** The ring atoms are S, C(NH2), N, N and C. The C(NH2) carbon is double-bonded to the first N, the two N atoms are joined by a single bond, and the second N is double-bonded to the last C. That last C is bonded back to S, which closes a 1,3,4-thiadiazole. The NH2 group sits on the carbon next to S.

**Imidazole ring (right):** The ring atoms are C2, N3, CH, C(NO2) and N1(CH3). C2 is double-bonded to N3, N3 is single-bonded to the CH, and the CH is double-bonded to the C bearing the nitro group. That carbon is single-bonded to N1, which carries the methyl, and N1 is single-bonded back to C2. This is a 1-methyl-5-nitroimidazole attached at C2 to the thiadiazole carbon.

**Nitro group:** Drawn in the charge-separated form, [N+](=O)[O-].

SMILES written ring by ring:
- Thiadiazole: Nc1nnc(s1)
- Linked imidazole: -c1ncc([N+](=O)[O-])n1C

Full SMILES: Nc1nnc(s1)-c1ncc([N+](=O)[O-])n1C

SMILES: Nc1nnc(s1)-c1ncc([N+](=O)[O-])n1C

name: Medroxyprogesterone
text:
The drawing shows a pregn-4-ene-3,20-dione steroid skeleton (four fused rings, with the enone in ring A). It carries a 17-hydroxy group, a 17-acetyl group (the C(=O)CH3 on the left) and a 6-methyl group, plus the two angular methyls at C10 and C13. That is medroxyprogesterone (6α-methyl-17-hydroxyprogesterone).

The drawing is flipped vertically relative to the usual steroid orientation. The C13 and C10 methyls are hashed, the 6-methyl and 17-OH are wedged, and the ring-junction hydrogens are drawn the opposite way to the usual depiction. Every wedge and hash is inverted together, so this is the natural stereochemistry viewed from the other face.

I took the stereo SMILES from my recall of the standard medroxyprogesterone SMILES and checked it only by this reasoning, not by building the structure from the drawing atom by atom.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@@H]2[C@H](CC[C@]3([C@H]2CC[C@@]3(C(=O)C)O)C)[C@@]4(C1=CC(=O)CC4)C

name: Maytansinol
text:
I recognised the drawing as a maytansinol-type ansa macrolide: a chloro-methoxy aromatic ring, an N-methyl amide, an epoxide, a cyclic carbamate and a methoxy diene. I wrote the SMILES from the connectivity I could read off the drawing. The stereo descriptors for the ring stereocentres are recalled from the known maytansinol structure, not derived from the wedges, so they are the least certain part. The two double-bond geometries I checked against the drawing: the CH=CH is E, and the CH2 and the diene chain sit trans across the trisubstituted double bond.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2C[C@]([C@@H](/C=C/C=C(/Cc3cc(OC)c(Cl)c(c3)N(C)C(=O)C[C@@H]([C@@]4([C@H]1O4)C)O)\C)OC)(NC(=O)O2)O

name: Mefloquine Hydrochloride
text:
This structure is mefloquine hydrochloride: a quinoline bearing a CF3 group at C2 and another at C8, with the C4 carbon attached to a CH(OH) group that links to a piperidin-2-yl ring. The HCl is written as a separate component.

I read the stereochemistry from the two stereocentres:

- **Carbinol carbon:** the OH is on a hashed bond (pointing away), with the quinoline to the upper right, the piperidine carbon to the upper left, and an implicit H toward the viewer. Written in the order O, H, quinoline, piperidine, this gives `@@`.
- **Piperidine C2:** the ring CH2 is on a wedge (toward the viewer), with N above, the carbinol carbon to the lower right, and an implicit H pointing away. Written in the order carbinol, H, N (ring closure), CH2, this gives `@`.

I did not re-parse the final SMILES with software.

SMILES: Cl.O[C@@H](c1cc(C(F)(F)F)nc2c(C(F)(F)F)cccc12)[C@H]1CCCCN1

name: Melamine
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring that alternates carbon and nitrogen. Each of the three ring carbons carries an NH2 group, which makes this melamine (1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triamine).

Reading the ring atoms and bonds:
- Top-left carbon (bearing NH2) has a double bond to the top-right ring N.
- Right carbon (bearing NH2) is bonded to the top-right N by a single bond and has a double bond to the bottom-right N.
- Bottom-left carbon (bearing NH2) is bonded to the bottom-right N by a single bond and has a double bond to the left N.
- The left N is bonded to the top-left carbon by a single bond.

Each carbon has exactly one double bond within the ring, so the alternation is consistent.

SMILES: Nc1nc(N)nc(N)n1

name: Meglumine Antimoniate
text:
I read the drawing as two separate components, written below as a dot-separated SMILES.

**Antimony component:** an Sb atom carries two double-bonded oxygens and one OH, which gives `O[Sb](=O)=O`.

**Organic component:** the chain is HO–CH2–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH3. I wrote it from the HO end as `OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)CNC`. Each stereocentre's tag comes from its drawn bond (wedge or hash) and its implicit hydrogen:

| Carbon (from left) | OH bond | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| C2 | wedge | `@@` |
| C3 | hash | `@@` |
| C4 | hash | `@` |
| C5 | hash | `@@` |

SMILES: O[Sb](=O)=O.OC[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)CNC

name: Mannopeptimycin alpha
text:
I read the structure as a cyclic hexapeptide carrying three sugar units. This resembles the mannopeptimycin family, though I worked from the drawing rather than from that match.

**Macrocycle (six residues, in ring order):**
1. Serine, with a CH2OH side chain; its Cα is drawn with a hashed bond, giving L-Ser.
2. Glycine.
3. β-Methylphenylalanine, with a phenyl and a methyl on the β-carbon. The wedges give (2S,3S).
4. Tyrosine, whose para-phenol oxygen carries a disaccharide. The wedge on its Cα gives the D configuration.
5. A β-hydroxy cyclic-guanidine amino acid (a 2-amino-imidazoline ring bearing a CH(OH) group). Its Cα is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo.
6. A second residue of the same type, but with the imidazoline ring nitrogen bonded to a hexopyranose. All of its stereocentres are wedged.

**Sugars:**
- A hexopyranose is attached to the ring N of residue 6.
- Two hexopyranoses are linked in a chain: the first is bonded through O to the tyrosine phenol, and the second is bonded through O at the 4-position of the first.

I assigned the @/@@ marks centre by centre from the wedge and hash bonds. I wrote the SMILES by hand and checked it against the drawing, but I did not run it through a parser.

SMILES: N1[C@@H](CO)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)c2ccccc2)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc2ccc(O[C@H]3O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O[C@H]4O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]4O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]3O)cc2)C(=O)NC([C@@H](O)[C@@H]2CN=C(N)N2)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](O)[C@@H]2CN=C(N)N2[C@H]3O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]3O)C1=O

name: Melagatran
text:
This looks like melagatran, and I read it as follows.

- **Left side:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries an amidine group (C(=NH)NH2) on one side and a CH2–NH–C(=O) group on the other.
- **Azetidine:** the amide carbonyl attaches to a four-membered ring carbon, drawn with a hashed bond, next to the ring nitrogen. That nitrogen is acylated by the C=O on the right.
- **Right side:** the acyl carbon is bonded to a stereocentre drawn with a wedge to NH. That centre also carries a cyclohexyl ring. The NH continues to CH2–COOH.

I assigned the two stereocentres from the hash and wedge geometry, with the implicit H on each carbon pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent.

- **Azetidine carbon:** @@ in the SMILES order below.
- **Cyclohexyl-bearing carbon:** @ in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: NC(=N)c1ccc(CNC(=O)[C@@H]2CCN2C(=O)[C@H](NCC(=O)O)C2CCCCC2)cc1

name: Melarsoprol
text:
The drawing shows three parts, read from left to right.

1. A five-membered 1,3,2-dithiarsolane ring made of As, S, CH2, CH and S. The CH carries a CH2OH group, drawn as HO–CH2.
2. A para-substituted benzene ring. One end is bonded to As and the other to an NH group.
3. A 1,3,5-triazine ring. The NH is attached to one ring carbon, and the other two ring carbons each carry an NH2.

The triazine has alternating bonds, so I wrote it as the aromatic ring c1nc(N)nc(N)n1.

The full SMILES is OCC1CS[As](S1)c1ccc(Nc2nc(N)nc(N)n2)cc1.

Checking the ring closures:
- In the dithiarsolane, C1 is the CH, followed by CH2, S, As, and then S closing back to C1. That gives 5 atoms: CH, CH2, S, As, S.
- The benzene ring is c1ccc(...)cc1, which has 6 atoms.
- The triazine is c2nc(N)nc(N)n2, which has 6 atoms: 3 carbons and 3 nitrogens.

SMILES: OCC1CS[As](S1)c1ccc(Nc2nc(N)nc(N)n2)cc1

name: Melatonin
text:
This structure is melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine), read region by region as follows.

- **Acetamide:** a methyl group is attached to a C=O, which is bonded to NH.
- **Linker:** the NH is followed by two CH2 groups, then the indole C3.
- **Indole:** the five-membered ring contains the NH at the top. C2 is the CH next to that NH, C3 carries the side chain, and C3a and C7a are the fusion atoms.
- **Benzene ring:** going from C3a (at about 1018,704), the next atom is C4, a CH at 1117,862. After that comes C5 at 1302,856, which carries the OMe. Then come C6 (1390,692) and C7 (1292,535), and finally C7a (1106,540), which is bonded to the NH.
- **Methoxy:** the OMe sits on C5, which is the position para to C7a... checking against the ring, C5 is meta to C3a and para to C7a, which is correct for 5-methoxy.

SMILES: CC(=O)NCCc1c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

name: Melitracene
text:
The drawing shows melitracen, a tricyclic compound with these parts:

- **Amine chain:** a dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) attached to a three-carbon chain, N–CH2–CH2–CH=.
- **Central ring:** a six-membered ring fused to two benzene rings, one on each side.
- **Ring substituents:** the ring carbon at the top bears the exocyclic C=C to the chain. The ring carbon at the bottom is a quaternary carbon carrying two methyl groups.
- **Stereochemistry:** the exocyclic double-bond carbon is attached to two equivalent aryl branches, so the double bond has no E/Z geometry. No stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: CN(C)CCC=C1c2ccccc2C(C)(C)c2ccccc21

name: Meloxicam
text:
This is meloxicam. I read the structure region by region.

- **Thiazole ring:** a methyl group is attached to a ring carbon that also bonds to S. That S bonds to the C2 carbon, which carries the NH and is double-bonded to the ring N. The ring N bonds to a CH, and the CH is double-bonded to the methyl-bearing carbon. This gives Cc1cnc(s1)N.
- **Amide:** the NH is attached to a C(=O), which is attached to the ring carbon C3.
- **Benzothiazine ring:** C3 is double-bonded to C4, which carries the OH. C3 is also bonded to N, which carries a methyl group and is bonded to S(=O)(=O). The sulfonyl S is bonded to an aromatic carbon, and C4 is bonded to the adjacent aromatic carbon, which closes the benzene ring.

SMILES: Cc1cnc(s1)NC(=O)C1=C(O)c2ccccc2S(=O)(=O)N1C

name: Melevodopa
text:
This structure is the methyl ester of DOPA (3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine), with the stereochemistry read from the single wedge.

- **Ester end:** a methyl group sits on an oxygen, which is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), giving COC(=O).
- **Stereocentre:** the alpha carbon carries an NH2 on a bold wedge, a hydrogen that is implicit and therefore pointing away, and a CH2 chain.
- **Side chain:** the CH2 links to a benzene ring carrying two adjacent OH groups. One is on the carbon next to the ring-attachment carbon's neighbour, and the other is one carbon further round, so the ring is a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl.
- **Configuration:** with the wedged NH2 toward the viewer and H behind, the sequence NH2 → CH2 → C(=O) runs clockwise. This corresponds to `[C@@H]` when written as COC(=O)[C@@H](N)C…, which is the L (S) configuration.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@@H](N)Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1

name: Menadione
text:
The drawing shows menadione (2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone).

- **Quinone ring:** C1 is a carbonyl carbon (top O). C2 carries the methyl group and is double-bonded to C3, which is a CH. C4 is the second carbonyl carbon (bottom O). C4a and C8a are the fusion carbons.
- **Benzene ring:** the fused ring is aromatic and drawn with alternating double bonds.

SMILES: CC1=CC(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: Melphalan
text:
This structure is melphalan (L-phenylalanine mustard).

- **Ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene.
- **Ring substituents:** one is an N,N-bis(2-chloroethyl)amino group, N(CH2CH2Cl)2. The other is a CH2 leading to the amino-acid carbon.
- **Side chain:** CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the α-carbon, with a wedge to NH2, so the NH2 points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. Tracing N → COOH → CH2 in the drawing runs counterclockwise with H at the back, which gives S. That matches the L-amino-acid pattern N[C@@H](R)C(=O)O.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(N(CCCl)CCCl)cc1)C(=O)O

name: Memantine
text:
The drawing is an adamantane cage with an NH2 group on one bridgehead carbon and a methyl group on each of two other bridgehead carbons. The fourth bridgehead carbon is an unsubstituted CH. This is 3,5-dimethyladamantan-1-amine (memantine).

I checked the connectivity against the drawing:

- The amine-bearing carbon (at about 450,866) bonds to N and to three cage CH2 carbons.
- The two methyl-bearing bridgeheads (at about 804,633 and 1182,820) each bond to a methyl group and to three cage CH2 carbons.
- The remaining bridgehead (at about 829,1054) bonds to three CH2 carbons.

The formula comes to 12 carbons plus one nitrogen. The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES has no stereochemistry.

SMILES: NC12CC3CC(C)(C1)CC(C)(C3)C2

name: Megestrol
text:
I read the drawing as a pregnane steroid (a megestrol-type skeleton). It has a 3-ketone, 4,6-diene, 6-methyl, 17-hydroxy and 17-acetyl groups, and methyls at C10 and C13.

- **Rings and substituents:** The A ring runs C1–C2–C3(=O)–C4=C5–C10. The B ring contains C6(CH3)=C7, then C8 and C9. C11 and C12 link C9 to C13 in the C ring. The five-membered D ring is C13–C14–C15–C16–C17, and C17 carries the OH and the acetyl group.
- **Stereocentres:** I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash bonds as drawn. The OH on C17 is wedged, and the H atoms on C9 and C14 are wedged. The H on C8 is hashed, and the methyls on C10 and C13 are hashed.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@@]1(O)CC[C@H]2[C@@H]3C=C(C)C4=CC(=O)CC[C@]4(C)[C@H]3CC[C@]12C

name: Menthol
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered carbon ring with three substituents, all drawn with plain bonds.

Ring atoms, going around the ring:
- C1 (at about 372, 645) carries a methyl group (the line going left).
- C2 (506, 380) is a plain CH2.
- C3 (802, 362) is a plain CH2.
- C4 (965, 611) carries an isopropyl group (the CH at 1262, 595, with two methyl carbons).
- C5 (831, 877) carries the OH.
- C6 (535, 895) is a plain CH2.

The OH carbon is adjacent to the isopropyl-bearing carbon, and the methyl-bearing carbon is separated from the OH carbon by one CH2 (C6). This is the menthol skeleton: 2-isopropyl-5-methylcyclohexanol.

There are no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES written from the ring: CC1CCC(C(C)C)C(O)C1

SMILES: CC1CCC(C(C)C)C(O)C1

name: Menadione Sodium Bisulfite
text:
The drawing shows a sodium salt (Na+) of a sulfonate (S with two =O and one O−).

The sulfonate sulfur is attached to a quaternary carbon that carries a methyl group. That carbon is bonded to a C=O carbon and to a CH2 group. The CH2 is bonded to a second C=O carbon. Both carbonyl carbons are fused to a benzene ring. This gives a 2-methyl-1,4-dioxo-tetralin-2-sulfonate, which is the menadione sodium bisulfite structure.

The ring is C2(CH3)(SO3−), C1(=O), the aromatic fusion carbons, C4(=O), and C3H2. The aromatic ring has six carbons, two of which are the fusion carbons.

SMILES: [Na+].CC1(S(=O)(=O)[O-])CC(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: [Na+].CC1(S(=O)(=O)[O-])CC(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: Meperidine
text:
The drawing shows an ethyl ester (CH3-CH2-O-C(=O)-) attached to a quaternary carbon. That carbon is part of a piperidine ring and also carries a phenyl group. The piperidine nitrogen bears a methyl group.

Reading the ring: the quaternary carbon connects to CH2, CH2 and then N(CH3), and back through CH2, CH2 to the quaternary carbon. This makes it a 4-substituted piperidine with 6 ring atoms (the quaternary carbon, 4 CH2 groups and N).

The structure is ethyl 1-methyl-4-phenylpiperidine-4-carboxylate (pethidine/meperidine). No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1(CCN(C)CC1)c1ccccc1

name: Mephobarbital
text:
The drawing shows a barbiturate ring (pyrimidine-2,4,6-trione) with these features:

- The ring is C5(quaternary)–C(=O)–N(CH3)–C(=O)–NH–C(=O) back to C5.
- C5 carries an ethyl group and a phenyl group.
- The phenyl ring is drawn in Kekulé form with three double bonds.
- The N-methyl group is on the nitrogen between the two carbonyls, adjacent to the top carbonyl.

This is mephobarbital (5-ethyl-1-methyl-5-phenylbarbituric acid).

C5 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CCC1(c2ccccc2)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)NC1=O

name: Mepivacaine
text:
The drawing shows mepivacaine: an N-methylpiperidine ring carrying a 2-carboxamide, with the amide nitrogen attached to a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring.

**Piperidine ring.** The ring atoms are N, the carbon bearing the carbonyl, and four further CH2 carbons, six in total. The ring nitrogen carries a methyl group.

**Amide.** The ring carbon is bonded to a C(=O) group, which is bonded to NH.

**Aryl ring.** The NH is attached to a benzene ring that has methyl groups on both carbons adjacent to the attachment point (positions 2 and 6).

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the ring carbon that is a stereocentre by connectivity gets no stereo marker.

SMILES: CN1CCCCC1C(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Meprylcaine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Chain on the left:** a propyl group (CH3–CH2–CH2) is attached to an NH.
- **Central carbon:** the NH is bonded to a quaternary carbon that carries two methyl groups and a CH2.
- **Ester:** that CH2 is bonded to an O, which is bonded to a C(=O) that carries a phenyl ring (a benzoate ester).

This is 2-methyl-2-(propylamino)propyl benzoate (the compound known as meprylcaine). All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCCNC(C)(C)COC(=O)c1ccccc1

name: Mercuric Chloride
text:
The drawing shows a linear Cl–Hg–Cl molecule: one mercury atom with a single bond to a chlorine on each side. No charges, stereochemistry or abbreviations appear. This is mercury(II) chloride.

SMILES: Cl[Hg]Cl

name: Melogliptin
text:
I read the structure in three parts and worked out each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Fragments**
- **Left:** a 1,2,4-triazole attached through N1 to a CH2 group.
- **Middle:** a cyclopentane substituted at positions 1 and 3. One carbon bears the CH2–triazole, drawn hashed. The other bears the NH, also drawn hashed.
- **Linker:** NH–CH2–C(=O), connecting the cyclopentane to the pyrrolidine nitrogen as an amide.
- **Right:** a pyrrolidine whose nitrogen is acylated. The carbon next to nitrogen carries a wedged C≡N. The carbon at position 4 carries a wedged F.

**Stereo assignment**
For each centre I took the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent. I then read the rotation of the remaining neighbours in the written SMILES order.
- The CN-bearing pyrrolidine carbon is `@@`.
- The CF carbon is `@`.
- The cyclopentane carbon bearing NH is `@@`.
- The cyclopentane carbon bearing CH2–triazole is `@`.

I checked that ring closures and atom counts match the drawing.

SMILES: N#C[C@@H]1C[C@H](F)CN1C(=O)CN[C@@H]1CC[C@H](Cn2cncn2)C1

name: Mersalyl
text:
The drawing is a multi-component structure: Na+, HO-, and an organomercury cation paired with a carboxylate anion. This looks like mersalyl sodium.

Reading the main fragment from the left:
- Hg+ is bonded to a CH2.
- That CH2 is bonded to a CH, which carries a methoxy group (the O at the top left, with a methyl).
- The CH is bonded to another CH2, then to NH.
- NH is bonded to a C(=O), which is attached to the benzene ring.
- On the adjacent ring carbon (ortho position) there is an O-CH2-C(=O)[O-] group.

The SMILES for the cation and anion part is [Hg+]CC(OC)CNC(=O)c1ccccc1OCC(=O)[O-].

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so there is no stereochemistry. The counterions are written as separate components.

SMILES: [Na+].[OH-].[Hg+]CC(OC)CNC(=O)c1ccccc1OCC(=O)[O-]

name: Merbromin
text:
This is merbromin (mercurochrome) written as separate ions, with two Na+, one HO-, and an Hg+ bonded to the ring carbon.

**Left ring.** The atoms are C(Hg) at (408,686), C(O-) at (290,809), C(Br) at (337,974), CH at (503,1014), C at (621,891), and C at (574,727), which bears the ring O. The bonds are:
- C(Hg)=C(574,727), a double bond
- C(O-)=C(Br), a double bond
- CH=C(621,891), a double bond

**Central ring.** The atoms are O, C(574,727), C(621,891), C9 at (787,933), C(905,810), and C(858,645).
- C9=C(905,810) is a double bond.

**Right ring.** The atoms are C(858,645), CH at (977,522), C(=O) at (1143,564), C(Br) at (1189,727), CH at (1071,850), and C(905,810).
- C(858,645)=CH(977,522) is a double bond.
- C(Br)=CH(1071,850) is a double bond.
- C=O is a double bond.

**Benzoate.** C9 is attached to a phenyl ring, which carries the carboxylate C(=O)[O-] on the adjacent carbon.

**SMILES assembly.** I write the ions as separate fragments, starting with the three non-organic pieces and then the organic fragment:

[Na+].[Na+].[OH-].[Hg+]c1c([O-])c(Br)cc2c1Oc1cc(=O)c(Br)cc1=C2c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]

**Check on the ring closures.** The left ring is c1(Hg) c([O-]) c(Br) c c2 c1 O. Here c1(Hg) is the atom at 408,686, then C(O-), C(Br), CH, and c2 at 621,891. The next atom, written c1 at 574,727, closes ring 1 with the Hg-bearing carbon. In my string, "cc2c1O" gives CH, then c2 (621,891), then c1 (574,727) closing to the Hg carbon, then O. This is correct.

Then O connects to c1 at 858,645 (new ring label 1), followed by "c" for CH(977,522), "c(=O)", "c(Br)", "c" for CH(1071,850), and "c1" for C(905,810). The closure to 858,645 is correct. The double bond "=C2" goes from C(905,810) to C9, and C9 closes ring 2 with c2 at 621,891. This is correct.

Kekulé validity: in the right ring, c1(858) = c(977), then c(=O), then c(Br) = c(1071), then c1(905), which has the exocyclic double bond to C9. This is consistent.

The Hg+ is a single-bonded cation, as drawn.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[OH-].[Hg+]c1c([O-])c(Br)cc2c1Oc1cc(=O)c(Br)cc1=C2c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]

name: Mescaline
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with a 2-aminoethyl chain (H2N–CH2–CH2–) on one ring carbon and three methoxy groups on the other side of the ring.

Reading the ring: the ring carbon attached to the chain is at (708, 768). Going around from there, the next carbon (765, 578) is a CH. After it come the three carbons bearing OMe at (958, 532), (1095, 678) and (1037, 868). The last ring carbon, (845, 913), is a CH. The methoxy groups are therefore at positions 3, 4 and 5 relative to the chain, which makes this mescaline.

SMILES: NCCc1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1

name: Mesna
text:
The drawing shows sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (mesna), written as two separate ions.

- **Sodium:** a separate Na⁺ label.
- **Sulfonate group:** a sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens and one single-bonded O⁻.
- **Chain:** the sulfur is attached to a two-carbon chain (CH₂–CH₂) that ends in an SH group.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)CCS

name: Mertansine
text:
This structure looks like DM1 (mertansine), a maytansinoid with a 3-mercaptopropanoyl-N-methylalanine ester side chain. I identified it from the overall scaffold and wrote the SMILES largely from memory of the known maytansine/DM1 string. I did not independently re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo descriptors are the least certain part.

Features read from the drawing:
- **Aromatic ring:** it carries Cl and OMe, and the ring nitrogen is N-methyl.
- **Macrocycle:** it contains a lactam C=O, an epoxide, and a diene with a methyl-substituted alkene.
- **Carbamate bridge:** a cyclic carbamate (NH–C(=O)–O) sits alongside a tertiary OH and an OMe.
- **Side chain:** an ester links to N-methylalanine, whose nitrogen is acylated by 3-mercaptopropanoyl (C(=O)CCS).

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2C[C@]([C@@H](/C=C/C=C(/CC3=CC(=C(C(=C3)OC)Cl)N(C(=O)C[C@@H]([C@]4([C@H]1O4)C)OC(=O)[C@H](C)N(C)C(=O)CCS)C)\C)OC)(NC(=O)O2)O

name: Mesoridazine
text:
This is a phenothiazine bearing a methylsulfinyl group, with a 2-(1-methylpiperidin-2-yl)ethyl chain on the ring nitrogen. That matches mesoridazine.

**Reading the structure**
- The sulfoxide is S(=O) with a methyl group, attached to the upper benzene ring.
- The phenothiazine core has N10 and S5 bridging the two benzene rings. The upper ring carries the sulfoxide, and the lower ring is unsubstituted.
- The N-substituent runs N–CH2–CH2–C2 of a piperidine ring. The piperidine nitrogen carries a methyl group.
- The piperidine ring has six vertices: C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and N.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I add no stereochemistry.

**Building the SMILES**
Start from the sulfoxide methyl and go through the upper ring: CS(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCC3CCCCN3C)c2c1.

Checking the upper ring:
- The sulfoxide-bearing carbon is c1 (at 825,443).
- Next come the ring carbons at 1002,366 and 1158,481, then the carbon at 1135,673 bonded to S (c2).
- The carbon at 959,749 is bonded to N, and the one at 804,635 is the CH that closes the ring back to c1.

SMILES: CS(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCC3CCCCN3C)c2c1

name: Meropenem
text:
I read the drawing as meropenem, the carbapenem antibiotic. Its structural parts are:

- a carbapenem core, a β-lactam fused to a five-membered ring containing a C=C
- a carboxylic acid on the alkene carbon next to the ring nitrogen
- a methyl group on the ring carbon next to the alkene
- a 1-hydroxyethyl side chain on the carbon next to the lactam carbonyl
- a thioether linking the alkene carbon to a pyrrolidine ring
- a dimethylamide (C(=O)N(CH3)2) on the pyrrolidine

I did not check every wedge and hash against the picture. Instead I assigned CIP descriptors to the stereocentres in the SMILES below and compared them with the known meropenem configuration, (4R,5S,6S) with 8R on the side chain and (3S,5S) on the pyrrolidine. They match.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2[C@H](C(=O)N2C(=C1S[C@H]3C[C@H](NC3)C(=O)N(C)C)C(=O)O)[C@@H](C)O

name: Metahexamide
text:
The drawing shows a cyclohexyl group bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a C=O, then another NH, then a sulfonyl group (S with two =O) attached to a benzene ring.

On the ring, the sulfonyl carbon is at position 1. Going around from there, the next ring carbon is CH (position 6, upper right), then CH (position 5), then the carbon bearing the methyl (position 4), then the carbon bearing NH2 (position 3), then CH (position 2), which closes back to position 1.

So the ring is 3-amino-4-methylbenzenesulfonyl, and the whole molecule is a sulfonylurea.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1N)S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NC1CCCCC1

name: Metamizole
text:
This is metamizole (dipyrone) in its sulfonic acid form.

**Pyrazolone ring.** The ring atoms are:
- N1, which carries a methyl group.
- N2, which carries the phenyl group.
- C3, which is the C=O carbon.
- C4, which bears the N(CH3)CH2SO3H substituent.
- C5, which bears a methyl group.

The ring has a C4=C5 double bond.

**Side chain.** C4 is bonded to N(CH3)–CH2–S(=O)(=O)OH.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring as CN1C(C)=C(N(C)CS(=O)(=O)O)C(=O)N1c1ccccc1 gives:
- N1 (methyl), then C5 (methyl) double-bonded to C4 (side chain), then C3 (=O), then N2 (phenyl), which closes back to N1.

This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CN1C(C)=C(N(C)CS(=O)(=O)O)C(=O)N1c1ccccc1

name: Mestranol
text:
The drawing is mestranol, the 3-methyl ether of ethinylestradiol. I read it as a steroid skeleton with these features:

- **Ring A:** an aromatic ring carrying a methoxy group (O–CH3) at the right-hand end.
- **Rings B and C:** two fused six-membered rings. They carry a hashed H at C9, a bold-wedge H at C8 and a hashed H at C14.
- **Ring D:** a five-membered ring. C13 carries a bold-wedge methyl, and C17 carries a bold-wedge OH and an ethynyl group (C≡CH).

The wedge pattern matches the natural estrane configuration (8β-H, 9α-H, 14α-H, 13β-methyl, 17β-OH, 17α-ethynyl).

I did not derive the stereodescriptors atom by atom from the wedges. The SMILES below is the standard isomeric SMILES for mestranol as I remember it, and it fits this wedge pattern.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C#C)O)CCC4=C3C=CC(=C4)OC

name: Metformin
text:
The drawing shows metformin, drawn as a tautomer.

- On the left, a nitrogen carries two methyl groups (the two lines going up and down-left from it) and is bonded to a carbon.
- That carbon has a double bond to an NH (drawn at the bottom) and a single bond to the central N.
- The central N is double-bonded to the right-hand carbon.
- The right-hand carbon carries two NH2 groups.

Written out, the connectivity is CN(C)C(=N)N=C(N)N.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=N)N=C(N)N

name: Metaproterenol
text:
The drawing shows orciprenaline (metaproterenol).

- **Isopropyl group:** a CH carbon with two methyl groups, bonded to an NH.
- **Chain:** the NH connects to a CH2, then to a CH(OH), which attaches to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the side chain at one carbon and OH groups at the two meta positions, giving a 3,5-dihydroxyphenyl pattern.

Checking the ring positions:
- The ring-attachment carbon is at (885, 842).
- Going around the ring: (910, 657), then (1082, 587), which carries OH, then (1228, 702), then (1204, 886), which carries OH, then (1032, 956), then back to the attachment carbon.
- The OH carbons at (1082, 587) and (1204, 886) are each separated from the attachment carbon by one ring carbon, so they are meta to it and to each other (3,5).

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)c1cc(O)cc(O)c1

name: Metformin Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows metformin hydrochloride.

- The left nitrogen carries two methyl groups (CN(C)).
- It is bonded to a carbon that has a C=NH group and a single bond to the middle nitrogen.
- The middle nitrogen is double-bonded to the right carbon, which bears two NH2 groups.
- HCl is drawn as a separate component.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=N)N=C(N)N.Cl

name: Methadone
text:
The drawing shows methadone: an ethyl ketone (CH3CH2–C(=O)) attached to a quaternary carbon that carries two phenyl rings. That carbon is also bonded to a CH2, which leads to a CH bearing a methyl and an N(CH3)2 group.

Reading the structure atom by atom:
- Top chain: CH3–CH2–C(=O)–.
- The carbonyl carbon is bonded to the quaternary carbon, which carries two phenyl rings.
- The quaternary carbon is also bonded to CH2–CH(CH3)–N(CH3)2.

The CH(CH3) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CCC(=O)C(CC(C)N(C)C)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Merotocin
text:
I read the molecule as a head-to-tail-style macrocyclic thioether peptide, traced around the ring and then along the side chain.

**Ring.** Starting from the ring carbonyl, the atoms run C(=O)–CH2–CH2–CH2–S–CH2 into the Cys α-carbon. This gives three CH2 groups between the carbonyl and S. From the Cys α-carbon the ring continues through four more residues, each linked by an amide:

1. Asn, with a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain
2. Gln, with a CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain
3. Ile, with a sec-butyl side chain
4. Tyr, with a 4-hydroxybenzyl side chain

The Tyr NH closes the ring onto the first carbonyl.

**Side chain off the Cys carbonyl.** The Cys C(=O) is bonded to a tertiary amide N that carries a 4-fluorobenzyl group and a CH2C(=O)– arm. That arm continues as NH–Leu–C(=O)–NH–CH2–C(=O)NH2.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows wedges or hashes at six α-carbons and at the Ile β-carbon. I assigned each from its wedge or hash and neighbour order. The Cys, Asn, Gln, Ile, Tyr and Leu α-centres all come out with the natural L-configuration, and the Ile β-centre matches natural L-Ile.

SMILES: O=C1CCCSC[C@@H](C(=O)N(Cc2ccc(F)cc2)CC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)NCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)N1

name: Methanol-13C
text:
The drawing shows a carbon atom labeled with the isotope ¹³C, joined by a single bond to an OH group. This is methanol with a ¹³C label. The carbon has three implicit hydrogens.

SMILES: [13CH3]O

name: Methanol-D4
text:
The drawing shows methanol with every hydrogen labelled as deuterium (²H).

- The central carbon has three bonds to ²H and one bond to oxygen.
- The oxygen is bonded to the carbon and to a fourth ²H, the hydroxyl hydrogen.

Written with explicit isotope labels, the SMILES is [2H]C([2H])([2H])O[2H].

SMILES: [2H]OC([2H])([2H])[2H]

name: Methaqualone
text:
The drawing shows methaqualone, a quinazolin-4-one core, built up as follows.

- **Quinazolinone core:** a benzene ring is fused to a six-membered ring. That ring contains the C=O carbon, the N bearing the aryl group, a C(CH3)= carbon, and a ring N double-bonded to that carbon.
- **C2 substituent:** the carbon between the two nitrogens carries a methyl group and is double-bonded to the lower N.
- **N3 substituent:** the upper N carries a 2-methylphenyl (o-tolyl) group. The methyl sits on the ring carbon adjacent to the one attached to N.

SMILES: Cc1ccccc1N1C(C)=Nc2ccccc2C1=O

name: Methamphetamine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left chain:** a methyl group is bonded to an NH, so the amine is a secondary N-methyl amine.
- **Stereocentre:** the NH is bonded to a carbon that carries a hashed methyl (pointing back) and a CH2 that leads to the ring.
- **Ring:** the CH2 is attached to a benzene ring drawn with three alternating double bonds, so it is a phenyl group.

Together this is N-methyl-1-phenylpropan-2-amine (methamphetamine).

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CH2Ph > CH3 > H.

1. The hashed methyl points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
2. In the drawing, N is up, CH2 is lower right and CH3 is lower left. Going N → CH2 → CH3 is clockwise as drawn.
3. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S.

I wrote `CN[C@@H](C)Cc1ccccc1` and checked it: with the neighbour order N, H, CH3, CH2, `@@` means H, CH3, CH2 run clockwise when viewed from N. Moving H to the front of the list flips the symbol to `@`. Viewed from the side opposite H, N → CH2 → CH3 then runs counterclockwise, which is S, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CN[C@@H](C)Cc1ccccc1

name: Methimazole
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered ring with these atoms:

- A thione carbon (C=S) at the upper left of the ring, with S drawn double-bonded to it.
- An NH at the upper right, bonded to the thione carbon.
- Two CH carbons on the right and bottom right, joined by a double bond.
- An N at the bottom left, carrying a methyl group and bonded back to the thione carbon.

This is methimazole (1-methyl-imidazole-2-thione).

Ring bonds, starting from the thione carbon: C(=S) – NH – CH=CH – N(CH3) – back to C(=S).

SMILES: CN1C=CNC1=S

name: Mesterolone
text:
I read the drawing as a 5α-androstane skeleton with a 3-ketone, a 17-hydroxyl and a methyl on C1, which is the mesterolone-type pattern.

**Ring skeleton and substituents**
- The four fused rings are the usual steroid A, B, C and D, with D as the five-membered ring.
- The ketone sits on the carbon at the right of ring A. Its two neighbours are CH2 groups, C2 and C4.
- C1 is the carbon next to C2 and carries a wedged methyl.
- C10 and C13 each carry a hashed (back) angular methyl.
- C17 carries a hashed OH.

**Stereochemistry**
- Wedged hydrogens are drawn at C5, C9 and C14, and a hashed hydrogen at C8.
- I assigned each centre from the 2D coordinates and wedge/hash directions, then adjusted for the order in which the neighbours appear in the SMILES.

**SMILES atom order**
The string runs C1(Me), C2, C3(=O), C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C14, C15, C16, C17(OH), C13(Me), C12, C11, C9, C10(Me). Ring closures 1 and 2 meet at C10, closure 3 joins C8 to C9, and closure 4 joins C14 to C13.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CC(=O)C[C@@H]2CC[C@H]3[C@@H]4CC[C@H](O)[C@@]4(C)CC[C@@H]3[C@@]12C

name: Methisazone
text:
The drawing shows a thiosemicarbazone-type azo tautomer of N-methylisatin 3-thiosemicarbazone, built from an indole core with substituents at positions 1, 2 and 3.

**Substituents on the five-membered ring**
- The ring nitrogen carries a methyl group.
- The carbon next to that nitrogen carries an OH and is double-bonded to the ring carbon at position 3 (C2=C3).
- The C3 carbon is bonded to N=N–C(=S)NH2, an azo group leading to a thioamide.

**Fused benzene ring**
- It is drawn as an aromatic ring fused to the five-membered ring, with the C3a–C4 and C5=C6 double bonds shown in the image.

**SMILES construction**
- Writing the azo chain first: NC(=S)N=NC1=C(O)N(C)c2ccccc12.
- The ring closure at the end connects C3a back to C3.

SMILES: NC(=S)N=NC1=C(O)N(C)c2ccccc12

name: Methocarbamol
text:
The drawing shows methocarbamol: a benzene ring carrying an ortho-methoxy group and an aryl ether, linked through a CH2–CH(OH)–CH2 chain to a carbamate.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent substituents. One is OCH3 (the methyl is drawn at the bottom left). The other is an O–CH2 ether oxygen.
- **Chain:** the ether oxygen connects to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2.
- **Carbamate:** the last CH2 is bonded to O, which is bonded to C(=O)NH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: COc1ccccc1OCC(O)COC(N)=O

name: Methohexital
text:
The drawing shows a barbiturate ring, a six-membered ring of C(=O)–NH–C(=O)–N(CH3)–C(=O)–C5, where C5 is the quaternary carbon.

C5 carries two substituents:
- An allyl group: CH2–CH=CH2.
- A hexynyl-type chain: CH(CH3)–C≡C–CH2–CH3, which is a 1-methylpent-2-ynyl group.

This matches methohexital. The structure has no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

Chain check, tracing from the left of the drawing: CH3, then CH2, then C≡C, then CH(CH3), then the quaternary ring carbon. That gives CCC#CC(C)C1(CC=C)....

Ring SMILES: C1(=O)NC(=O)N(C)C(=O)C1(...), with the substituents on the quaternary carbon.

Full SMILES: CCC#CC(C)C1(CC=C)C(=O)NC(=O)N(C)C1=O

SMILES: CCC#CC(C)C1(CC=C)C(=O)NC(=O)N(C)C1=O

name: Methoxyflurane
text:
The drawing shows a CHCl2 carbon joined to a CF2 carbon. The CF2 carbon also carries an O, which connects to a CH3 at the end of the chain. This is methoxyflurane.

SMILES: COC(F)(F)C(Cl)Cl

name: Methicillin
text:
This structure is methicillin, a penicillin with a 2,6-dimethoxybenzamide side chain. I read it region by region.

- **Side chain:** a benzene ring carries two OMe groups ortho to the carbon that bears the C(=O)NH group, so it is a 2,6-dimethoxybenzoyl amide.
- **β-lactam ring:** the amide nitrogen attaches to a ring carbon through a hashed bond. That carbon is bonded to the lactam C=O, which is bonded to the ring N. The ring N is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon, which carries an H on a wedge.
- **Thiazolidine ring:** the ring N is bonded to a carbon that carries the COOH on a wedge. That carbon is bonded to C(CH3)2, which is bonded to S, and S is bonded back to the ring-fusion carbon.
- **Stereocentres:** I assigned the three stereocentres (the amide-bearing carbon, the COOH-bearing carbon and the ring-fusion carbon) from the wedge and hash bonds. In the SMILES they are the first, second and third `@@`/`@` centres, written `[C@@H]`, `[C@@H]` and `[C@H]`.

SMILES: COc1cccc(OC)c1C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N2[C@@H](C(=O)O)C(C)(C)S[C@H]12

name: Mersacidin
text:
I read the drawing as a lanthipeptide-type macrocycle and wrote it as one SMILES. Only the connectivity is checked atom by atom against the drawing. The stereo marks are only approximate: I assigned them mostly by assuming natural L-amino acids rather than reading every wedge and hash, so the stereocentres may not match the image exactly.

**N-terminal ring:** a seven-membered 1,4-thiazepane, in order S, CH2, CH(NH2), C(=O), NH, CH, CH(CH3). The ring CH carries the chain, which continues through Phe.

**Chain order:**
1. Phe.
2. A methyllanthionine residue that is bridged by sulfur through a CH2 to a Cys.
3. That Cys, followed by Val.
4. Four Gly residues.
5. Pro.
6. Leu, which closes back onto the methyllanthionine residue.

**Second part:**
1. A second methyllanthionine residue, bridged by sulfur to the CH2 of another Cys.
2. Leu.
3. An Abu-type residue whose β-carbon is joined through sulfur to an S–CH=CH–NH aminovinyl unit.
4. Ile.
5. The Cys that closes the second sulfur bridge.
6. Glu, with a free CO2H side chain.
7. Dehydroalanine, which closes the macrocycle.

SMILES: N[C@H]1CS[C@H](C)[C@@H](NC1=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]2[C@@H](C)SC[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)NC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)[C@H]3CCCN3C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC2=O)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)S4)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]5[C@H](C)SC=CNC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC(=O)[C@H](CS4)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(=O)O)NC(=O)C(=C)NC5=O

name: Methyl Aminolevulinate
text:
The drawing, read from left to right, shows:

- A methyl carbon bonded to an oxygen, which is bonded to a carbon with a C=O. Together these form a methyl ester.
- Two CH2 groups follow the ester carbon.
- A ketone carbon (C=O) comes next.
- A CH2 attached to NH2 ends the chain.

This is methyl 5-amino-4-oxopentanoate (the methyl ester of 5-aminolevulinic acid).

The molecule has no stereocentres, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: COC(=O)CCC(=O)CN

name: Methyl magnesium bromide
text:
The image shows three separate ionic species with no bonds drawn between them: Br⁻, H₃C⁻ and Mg²⁺. This is methylmagnesium bromide written in its ionic form.

- Bromide: [Br-]
- Methyl carbanion: [CH3-]
- Magnesium: [Mg+2]

The charges balance: −1 −1 +2 = 0.

SMILES: [Br-].[CH3-].[Mg+2]

name: Methotrexate
text:
This structure is methotrexate. I read it in four parts:

- **Pteridine core:** a 2,4-diaminopteridine ring, bearing a CH2 substituent at C6.
- **Linker:** the CH2 is bonded to an N-methyl nitrogen, which is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Amide:** the benzene ring carries a C(=O)NH group that links to the glutamate unit.
- **Glutamate unit:** a CH stereocentre bearing the amide N, a COOH, and a CH2CH2COOH chain.

For the stereocentre, the wedge bond points to the side-chain CH2, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The substituent priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. Going N → COOH → CH2 in the drawing runs counterclockwise with H at the back, which gives S, the L-glutamate configuration. I wrote the SMILES with the matching `@@` tag in the order N, H, CH2 chain, COOH.

SMILES: CN(Cc1cnc2nc(N)nc(N)c2n1)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Methyl Parathion
text:
The drawing shows methyl parathion.

- Phosphorus is double-bonded to sulfur (P=S).
- Phosphorus carries two methoxy groups (two O–CH3).
- Phosphorus also carries an O-aryl group, where the oxygen is bonded to a benzene ring.
- The ring has a nitro group para to that oxygen, drawn as [N+](=O)[O-].

The SMILES is COP(=S)(OC)Oc1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]. It is valid, and it accounts for every atom in the drawing.

SMILES: COP(=S)(OC)Oc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1

name: Methylcymantrene
text:
The image shows several separate fragments:

- A manganese atom drawn as a radical, [Mn].
- Three carbon monoxide ligands, each drawn as [C-]#[O+].
- A methylcyclopentadienyl anion. It is a five-membered ring with C- at the left, then a CH=C(CH3) double bond, then C(CH3), then CH=CH.

Tracing the ring: the C- atom bonds to the top CH, which is double-bonded to the C bearing the methyl group. That carbon bonds to the lower-right CH, which is double-bonded to the lower-left CH, and that CH closes the ring back to C-.

Ring SMILES: [C-]1C=C(C)C=C1. The ring atoms are C-, CH=, C(Me), CH=, CH, which makes five, and the double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5, so it is valid.

The fragments are separated by dots:

SMILES: [Mn].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].CC1=CC=C[C-]1

Checking the last fragment against the drawing: the methyl carbon is on the ring carbon, which is double-bonded to the top CH and single-bonded to the lower-right CH. The ring path is C(Me)=CH–[C-]–CH=CH–back to C(Me). In the drawing the C- is bonded to the top CH and to the lower-left CH, which is double-bonded to the lower-right CH, and that CH is bonded to C(Me). This matches CC1=CC=C[C-]1 only if the atoms are in the order C(Me), =CH, then CH, =CH, then C-. That is not the drawn order, so I rewrite it as CC1=C[C-]C=C1. Here C1(Me)=CH–[C-]–CH=CH–back to C1, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: [Mn].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].[C-]#[O+].CC1=C[C-]C=C1

name: Methscopolamine bromide
text:
I read this as methscopolamine bromide, the N-methyl quaternary salt of scopolamine, and wrote the SMILES from the drawing.

- **Cation core:** a tropane-type bicycle with an N⁺ carrying two methyl groups, and an epoxide bridging the two adjacent ring carbons.
- **Ester side chain:** the ring carbon bearing the oxygen is acylated as O–C(=O)–CH(CH₂OH)–phenyl.
- **Counter-ion:** Br⁻.
- **Stereochemistry:** wedges and hashes are drawn on the two bridgehead carbons, the two epoxide carbons and the CH(CH₂OH) carbon, so these carry @/@@ tags. The ester-bearing ring carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo tag.

I took the tag assignments from the known scopolamine stereo-SMILES rather than deriving each one from the wedge geometry, so the @/@@ tags are the least certain part of this answer.

SMILES: C[N+]1(C)[C@@H]2CC(C[C@H]1[C@H]3[C@@H]2O3)OC(=O)[C@H](CO)c4ccccc4.[Br-]

name: Methenolone
text:
I read the drawing as a 1-methyl-androst-1-en-3-one steroid skeleton with a 17-hydroxyl. I worked out each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Skeleton**
- The four fused rings are the usual steroid A/B/C/D system: three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring.
- Ring A carries a ketone at C3, a C1=C2 double bond, and a methyl on C1.
- There are angular methyls on C10 and C13, and an OH on C17.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes**
- The methyls on C10 and C13 are both hashed.
- The 17-OH is hashed.
- The H on C9 is wedged.
- The H on C8 is hashed.
- The H on C14 is wedged.
- The H on C5 is wedged.

This is the reverse of the usual natural-steroid depiction in every stereocentre, so the drawing shows the enantiomeric series. I assigned each @/@@ directly from the drawn geometry.

**SMILES check:** it contains 20 skeleton carbons (19 ring and methyl carbons plus the C1 methyl), one carbonyl O and one hydroxyl O. That matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@@H](CC[C@H]4CC(=O)C=C(C)[C@]34C)[C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O

name: Methyldopa
text:
I read this as methyldopa, (S)-2-amino-3-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl)-2-methylpropanoic acid.

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent OH groups (a catechol), at the 3 and 4 positions relative to the CH2 attachment.
- **Side chain:** the ring carries a CH2 that joins a quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it bears NH2, a hashed methyl, the CH2 and a COOH group.

**Stereochemistry:** the methyl is hashed, so it points away from the viewer. The remaining substituents rank N > COOH > CH2Ar, and with the methyl pointing away they run counterclockwise in the drawing. That gives the S configuration.

In the SMILES, the neighbours of the stereocentre are written in the order CH3, N, CH2, COOH. Viewed from the methyl side, N → CH2 → COOH runs counterclockwise, which is `@`.

SMILES: C[C@](N)(Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1)C(=O)O

name: Methylene Blue
text:
This is methylene blue chloride: a phenothiazinium core with a dimethyliminium group on one side and a dimethylamino group on the other, plus a chloride counterion.

Reading the drawing:
- The left ring carries the iminium, N⁺(C)(C)=C. The carbon bearing it is bonded to a CH that leads to the carbon attached to S, and to another CH that continues around the ring.
- The central ring contains N, written N=C, and S, bonded to the two ring-fusion carbons on each side.
- The right ring is aromatic and carries N(C)C.
- Cl⁻ is a separate ion.

Writing the SMILES from the left side:
- C[N+](C)=C1C=CC2=NC3=CC=C(N(C)C)C=C3SC2=C1
- Left ring: C1(=N+) – C=C – C2(=N) – C2'(S) = C1. The atoms are C1 (bearing N⁺), then CH=CH, then C2 (fusion carbon bonded to N by a double bond), then the other fusion carbon C(S), then CH back to C1.
- In the drawing, the left ring has a C=C at the top left, the N⁺=C bond, and a C=C at the bottom (CH=C–S). This gives C1(=[N+])C=CC2=NC3=CC=C(N(C)C)C=C3SC2=C1.
- Check the left ring: C1, C, C, C2, C(S) (the closing C2), and C= (CH) back to C1. That is six atoms.
- Right ring: C3 (bonded to N), =C, C, C(NMe2), C, C3 (bonded to S). The ring closure uses C3 for the carbon bonded to S.

Full SMILES: C[N+](C)=C1C=CC2=NC3=CC=C(N(C)C)C=C3SC2=C1.[Cl-]

Double-bond check: C1(=N+), C=C, C2=N, C3=C (C3 then =CH), C(NMe2) with its neighbouring C=C, C3 closing, S, then C2=C1. The ring closure C2=C1 gives C(S)=CH, and the CH is bonded to C1 by a single bond. C1 already has its double bond to N⁺, so this is consistent.

SMILES: C[N+](C)=C1C=CC2=NC3=CC=C(N(C)C)C=C3SC2=C1.[Cl-]

name: Methyldigoxin
text:
I read this as digoxin with the terminal sugar's 4-OH replaced by a methoxy group. I started from the known digoxin stereo-SMILES and adjusted it to match the drawing.

- **Aglycone:** a steroid core with a butenolide (C8=CC(=O)OC8) at C17, hydroxyls at C12 and C14, and methyl groups at C10 and C13.
- **Orientation check:** the C17 substituent and both ring-junction methyls are drawn hashed, so the page shows the molecule from the opposite face. The C8-H, C9-H and C5-H wedges are consistent with natural 5β-digoxin stereochemistry on that basis.
- **Sugar chain:** three 2,6-dideoxy sugars (digitoxose type) are linked through glycosidic oxygens to C3 of the steroid.
- **Terminal sugar:** the top-left ring carries a free OH at C3 and an OMe at C4, which is the change from digoxin.

I took the sugar stereocentres from the digoxin SMILES rather than re-deriving each one from the wedges.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@H](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@@H]2[C@H](O[C@H](C[C@@H]2O)O[C@@H]3[C@H](O[C@H](C[C@@H]3O)O[C@H]4CC[C@]5([C@@H](C4)CC[C@@H]6[C@@H]5C[C@H]([C@]7([C@@]6(CC[C@@H]7C8=CC(=O)OC8)O)C)O)C)C)C)O)OC

name: Methyllithium
text:
The image shows two separate ionic species: a lithium cation, Li⁺, and a methyl carbanion, CH₃⁻. This is methyllithium drawn as an ion pair, with no bond between them.

Writing each ion in SMILES gives [Li+] for lithium and [CH3-] for the methyl anion. Joining them with a dot shows they are separate components.

SMILES: [Li+].[CH3-]

name: Methylone
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring fused to a five-membered 1,3-dioxole ring (a methylenedioxy bridge: O–CH2–O). The other ring carbon carries a ketone, C(=O), which is bonded to a CH bearing a methyl group and an NHCH3 group. This is methylone.

The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(NC)C(=O)c1ccc2OCOc2c1

name: Methylparaben
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an ester: a methyl group bonded to an O, which is bonded to a C that carries a C=O and is attached to the ring. The other substituent, opposite it on the ring, is an OH. This is methyl 4-hydroxybenzoate (methylparaben).

SMILES: COC(=O)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Methylphenidate
text:
The drawing shows a methyl ester (CH3–O–C(=O)–) attached to a central CH. That CH also carries a phenyl ring and a piperidin-2-yl ring (a six-membered ring containing NH). This is the structure of methylphenidate.

All bonds are plain lines with no wedges or hashes, so I have included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: COC(=O)C(c1ccccc1)C1CCCCN1

name: Methylergometrine
text:
I read this as methylergometrine (methylergonovine), the lysergic acid amide of (S)-2-aminobutan-1-ol. I assigned the side-chain stereocentre from the drawing and took the two ring stereocentres from the known compound rather than working them out separately from the wedges.

- **Core:** an ergoline ring system with an indole NH, an N-methyl piperidine ring, and a C=C in the D ring conjugated to the aromatic ring.
- **Amide:** a carboxamide on the D ring, with its carbon on a hashed bond.
- **Side chain:** the amide N bears CH(CH2OH)CH2CH3, with the ethyl group on a hashed bond. Reading the drawing, this carbon is S, and the SMILES `CC[C@@H](CO)N` also works out to S.
- **Ring stereocentres:** the hashed H at the ring-fusion carbon and the hashed amide bond at C8 follow the known configuration of methylergometrine.

SMILES: CC[C@@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H]1CN([C@@H]2CC3=CNC4=CC=CC(=C34)C2=C1)C

name: Methylnaltrexone Bromide
text:
This structure is methylnaltrexone bromide: the N-methyl quaternary ammonium salt of naltrexone, with a cyclopropylmethyl group on nitrogen and a bromide counter-ion.

- **Core:** a morphinan skeleton with a phenol OH on the aromatic ring, an ether bridge (the O in the furan ring), a ketone (C=O) in the cyclohexanone ring, and a tertiary OH on the ring-fusion carbon.
- **Nitrogen:** drawn as N⁺ with four carbon substituents: the methyl, the cyclopropylmethyl, and two ring carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** I took the carbon stereocentres from the wedges in the drawing and matched them to the naltrexone configuration. The N⁺ is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it has no wedge, so I left it unspecified.

I checked the SMILES for validity and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: C[N+]1(CC2CC2)CC[C@]34[C@@H]5C(=O)CC[C@]3([C@H]1CC6=C4C(=C(C=C6)O)O5)O.[Br-]

name: Methylprednisolone
text:
The drawing is a 6-methyl pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione steroid. It has 11-OH, 17-OH and a 21-hydroxy ketone side chain (C(=O)CH2OH), which matches methylprednisolone.

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with C=C at C1–C2, the C3 ketone, and C4=C5.
- **Methyl groups:** one at C10, one at C13, and one at C6.
- **Orientation and stereochemistry:** the drawing is a left-right mirror of the usual steroid layout. The hashed 10- and 13-methyls and the hashed 11-OH therefore correspond to the natural β face. The wedged 6-methyl, 17-OH and 14-H correspond to the α face.

I wrote the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the standard methylprednisolone (6α-methyl) string rather than by assigning each centre from the wedges, so the @/@@ marks are not independently checked.

SMILES: C[C@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CC[C@@]([C@]3(C[C@@H]([C@@H]2[C@@]4(C1=CC(=O)C=C4)C)O)C)(C(=O)CO)O

name: Methylselenocysteine
text:
The drawing shows a methyl group bonded to selenium, then a CH2, then a stereocentre carrying NH2 and a carboxylic acid (C=O with OH). This is Se-methylselenocysteine, CH3–Se–CH2–CH(NH2)–COOH.

The NH2 is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer, and the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer.

CIP priorities at the stereocentre are:
1. N
2. CH2Se (Se outranks O)
3. COOH
4. H

Viewed from the front, N (bottom) → CH2Se (upper right) → COOH (upper left) runs counterclockwise. Because H points toward the viewer, the sense is reversed, so the centre is R. This is the L-configuration, as in L-cysteine.

For the SMILES, I compared against L-cysteine, N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O. Writing the neighbours in the order CH2, H, N, COOH swaps N and CH2 relative to that string, which flips the chirality tag. The result is C[Se]C[C@H](N)C(=O)O, which is the R/L form.

SMILES: C[Se]C[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: Methylprednisolone Aceponate
text:
This is a 6‑methyl prednisolone‑type steroid, which matches methylprednisolone aceponate (the 17‑propionate, 21‑acetate ester). I read it as follows:

- **Ring A:** a cross‑conjugated 1,4‑dien‑3‑one, with the ketone at the right of the drawing.
- **Ring B:** a methyl at C6, drawn as a bold wedge.
- **Angular methyls:** hashed methyl groups at C10 and C13.
- **Ring C:** a hashed OH at C11.
- **Ring D:** C17 carries an O‑propionate (bold wedge) and a C(=O)CH2‑O‑acetyl side chain.

The drawing is turned over relative to the usual steroid orientation (ring A on the right). That is why the angular methyls appear hashed and the 6‑methyl appears as a wedge, so the stereochemistry is the natural one. I took the stereo descriptors from the known SMILES for this compound, as I remember it, and did not re‑derive each centre from the wedges.

SMILES: CCC(=O)O[C@@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(C[C@@H]([C@H]3[C@H]2C[C@H](C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]34C)C)O)C)C(=O)COC(C)=O

name: Methyltestosterone
text:
This is 17α-methyltestosterone (17β-hydroxy-17α-methylandrost-4-en-3-one). It is a steroid with the usual four fused rings: three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring.

- **Ring A:** a cyclohexenone, with the ketone C=O at the right and the C=C at the top of the ring.
- **Angular methyls:** two methyl groups are drawn with wedges, one at each of the two ring-fusion carbons next to the A and D rings.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** three H labels are drawn. One is wedged and two are hashed.
- **Five-membered ring:** the quaternary carbon on the left carries an OH and a hashed methyl.

The drawing is the standard steroid layout rotated 180° in the plane, so the wedge and hash assignments match the natural configuration. I took the stereo SMILES from the known natural isomer rather than deriving each centre from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C)O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C

name: Metoclopramide
text:
The drawing is metoclopramide, which I read as follows.

- **Amine end:** a diethylamino group, N(CC)CC, attached to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) that ends in an amide NH.
- **Amide:** the NH bonds to C(=O), which is attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring substituents:** going around the ring from the carbonyl-bearing carbon, the next carbon carries OMe. After it comes a CH, then the carbon with NH2, then the carbon with Cl, then a CH that closes back to the first carbon. So the ring has C(=O) at position 1, OMe at 2, NH2 at 4 and Cl at 5.

Written as SMILES, the chain is CCN(CC)CCNC(=O) and the ring is c1cc(N)c(Cl)cc1 with the substituents placed as above:

CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1cc(Cl)c(N)cc1OC

Checking the ring order in this string: c1 (bearing C=O), then cc(Cl), which gives CH and then C-Cl, then c(N), then c (CH), then c1OC (the carbon bearing OMe, bonded back to c1). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1cc(Cl)c(N)cc1OC

name: Metixene
text:
The drawing shows an N-methylpiperidine ring joined through a CH2 to a thioxanthene (9,10-dihydro) system.

**Piperidine ring.** Going around the ring from N: N, then a CH2 at the bottom (403,1073), then the CH at (547,945) that carries the substituent, then a CH2 at (509,756), then a CH2 at (325,695), then a CH2 at (180,823), and back to N. That is 6 atoms, so it is a piperidine with the substituent at C3. The N-methyl is at the lower left.

**Linker.** The ring CH is bonded to a CH2 at (730,1006), which is bonded to the CH at (875,878). That CH is C9 of the thioxanthene.

**Thioxanthene.** C9 is bonded to two aromatic carbons, one in each benzene ring. The two rings are bridged by S, giving a central six-membered ring made of C9, two aromatic carbons, S, and two more aromatic carbons.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Piperidine and linker: CN1CCCC(C1)CC2
- Thioxanthene: C2c3ccccc3Sc3ccccc23

The full string is CN1CCCC(C1)CC2c3ccccc3Sc3ccccc23.

**Check.** C9 is written as C2, followed by the first benzene ring c3ccccc3. S follows, then the second ring c3ccccc23, whose last atom closes to C9 through ring label 2. The ring-closure labels are consistent.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN1CCCC(C1)CC2c3ccccc3Sc3ccccc23

name: Metoprolol
text:
The drawing shows metoprolol, read as follows:

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group (CH3, CH, CH3) attached to NH.
- **Side chain:** NH is bonded to CH2, then to CH(OH), then to CH2, then to O, which attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene. The other substituent is CH2CH2-O-CH3, which gives the methoxyethyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing has no wedges or hashes, so the stereocentre at CH(OH) gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(CCOC)cc1

name: Metoprolol Succinate
text:
The image shows metoprolol succinate: two metoprolol molecules and one succinic acid, drawn as separate components.

- **Succinic acid:** OC(=O)CCC(=O)O
- **Metoprolol (each of the two):** CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(CCOC)cc1

The ring is para-substituted. One ring carbon carries the O–CH2 chain and the carbon opposite it carries CH2CH2OCH3. The drawing shows plain bonds with no wedges or hashes, so I added no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(CCOC)cc1.CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(CCOC)cc1.OC(=O)CCC(=O)O

name: Metrizoic Acid
text:
The structure is a benzene ring carrying six substituents, which I read as follows.

Ring atoms, going around from the carboxylic acid carbon:
- C1 (right, at about 960,744) bears COOH.
- C2 (top right, 837,534) bears I.
- C3 (top left, 594,537) bears N(CH3)C(=O)CH3.
- C4 (left, 474,748) bears I.
- C5 (bottom left, 597,958) bears NHC(=O)CH3.
- C6 (bottom right, 841,956) bears I.

This is a 2,4,6-triiodo-3,5-diamido benzoic acid, with an N-methylacetamido group at C3 and an acetamido group at C5. It matches metrizoic acid (3-acetamido-5-(N-methylacetamido)-2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid).

SMILES: CC(=O)N(C)c1c(I)c(C(=O)O)c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c1I

name: Metronidazole
text:
The drawing shows metronidazole, an imidazole ring carrying a nitro group, a methyl group and a hydroxyethyl chain.

**Ring (five-membered):**
- N1 (bottom) carries the CH2CH2OH chain.
- C2, at the lower right, carries the methyl group.
- N3, at the right, is double-bonded to C2.
- C4, at the top, is double-bonded to C5.
- C5 carries the nitro group and is bonded to N1.

**Substituents:**
- The nitro group is drawn as [N+](=O)[O-], attached to C5.
- The chain on N1 is CH2–CH2–OH.

**Writing the SMILES:** Starting from the chain, OCCn1c(C)ncc1[N+](=O)[O-] gives the aromatic form. In Kekulé form this is OCCN1C(C)=NC=C1[N+](=O)[O-].

**Atom-by-atom check:**
- N1 is bonded to C2 and C5, and N1 also carries the chain.
- C2 is bonded to the methyl group and has a double bond to N3.
- N3 is bonded to C4.
- C4 has a double bond to C5.
- C5 is bonded to the nitro group and closes the ring to N1.

This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OCCN1C(C)=NC=C1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Methyl O-2,3,4-tri-O-methyl-6-O-sulfo-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-(1->4)-O-2,3-di-O-methyl-beta-D-glucopyranuronosyl-(1->4)-O-2,3,6-tri-O-sulfo-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-(1->4)-O-2,3-di-O-methyl-alpha-L-idopyranuronosyl-(1->4)-alpha-D-glucopyranoside 2,3,6-tris(hydrogen sulfate)
text:
I read the molecule as a linear tetrasaccharide of five-membered-chain pyranose units joined by 1→4 glycosidic bonds, running left to right.

1. **Residue A (left end):** a glucose methyl glycoside with a wedged anomeric OMe. It carries sulfates (OSO3H) at C2 and C3, a CH2OSO3H at C5, and its C4 oxygen links to residue B.
2. **Residue B:** a uronic acid with OMe at C2 and C3 and a hashed COOH at C5. Its C4 oxygen links to residue C.
3. **Residue C:** a glucose unit with sulfates at C2 and C3 and a CH2OSO3H at C5. Its C4 oxygen links to residue D.
4. **Residue D:** a uronic acid with OMe at C2 and C3. Its COOH at C5 is drawn with a bold wedge, unlike B's hashed one, so the C5 configuration differs. Its C4 oxygen links to residue E.
5. **Residue E (right end):** a glucose unit with OMe at C2, C3 and C4 and a CH2OSO3H at C5.

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge or hash bonds and the 2D positions of the neighbours, with the implicit H placed opposite the wedged or hashed substituent. I did not run the final string through a SMILES parser.

SMILES: CO[C@@H]1[C@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@H](O[C@H]2[C@H](OC)[C@@H](OC)[C@H](O[C@@H]3[C@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@@H](OS(=O)(=O)O)[C@H](O[C@H]4[C@H](OC)[C@@H](OC)[C@H](O[C@@H]5[C@H](OC)[C@@H](OC)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O5)[C@@H](C(=O)O)O4)[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O3)[C@H](C(=O)O)O2)[C@@H](COS(=O)(=O)O)O1

name: Mexiletine
text:
The structure is a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ether of 2-aminopropanol, which is mexiletine.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The left end is a methyl group attached to a CH that carries NH2.
- That CH is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to O.
- The O is bonded to an aromatic carbon of a benzene ring.
- The two ring carbons on either side of that carbon each carry a methyl group.
- The remaining three ring carbons are unsubstituted.
- All bonds are plain lines with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CC(N)COc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Mezlocillin
text:
The molecule is mezlocillin: a penicillin core (a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring carrying gem-dimethyl groups and a carboxylic acid) with a phenylglycine amide side chain.

The side-chain nitrogen is acylated by a 2-oxoimidazolidine-1-carbonyl group. The other nitrogen of that imidazolidinone ring carries a methylsulfonyl group (S(=O)(=O)CH3).

The drawing shows a hashed bond at C6 (to the NH), a wedged H at C5, a wedged carboxylic acid at C3, and a hashed bond at the phenylglycine carbon. I assigned the stereodescriptors by matching this to the natural penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R, with the D-phenylglycine side chain), not by deriving each centre independently from the wedges. The ring-stereocentre pattern is the same as in ampicillin's SMILES.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)[C@@H](C3=CC=CC=C3)NC(=O)N4CCN(C4=O)S(=O)(=O)C)C(=O)O)C

name: Mezigdomide
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Glutarimide:** a piperidine-2,6-dione ring (NH between two C=O groups). Its C3 carbon carries a wedge bond to the isoindolinone nitrogen.
- **Isoindolinone:** a lactam with one C=O and one CH2 on the nitrogen, fused to a benzene ring. The ring carbon next to the CH2-bearing ring fusion carries an O–CH2 ether.
- **Linker:** the ether CH2 connects to a para-disubstituted benzene, whose other substituent is a CH2 attached to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Aryl end:** the other piperazine nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring that has an ortho fluorine and a para nitrile (C≡N) relative to the piperazine.

**Stereochemistry:** the only drawn stereocentre is the glutarimide C3, with the wedge pointing to the isoindolinone N. Its neighbours are the ring CH2 (left), the C=O (up), the wedged N (lower right) and an implicit H pointing away. Seen from the front, CH2 → C=O → N runs clockwise. Writing the neighbours in SMILES order (CH2, H, N, C=O) then gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N2Cc3c(cccc3OCc3ccc(CN4CCN(CC4)c4ccc(C#N)cc4F)cc3)C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: Metrizamide
text:
I read the molecule as a metrizamide-type structure: a 2,4,6-triiodobenzamide core carrying an acetamido group and an N-methylacetamido group, with the amide nitrogen attached to a 2-amino-2-deoxy pyranose ring.

- **Aromatic ring:** six carbons, with three iodines on alternating positions. The other three positions carry the C(=O)NH amide, the NHC(=O)CH3 group and the N(CH3)C(=O)CH3 group.
- **Pyranose ring:** ring oxygen, an anomeric carbon bearing OH, then a ring carbon bearing the amide NH, a ring carbon bearing OH, a ring carbon bearing OH, and a ring carbon bearing CH2OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the four ring stereocentres from the wedges and hashes: NH wedge, CH2OH hash, one OH wedge and one OH hash. The anomeric carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

SMILES: CC(=O)N(C)c1c(I)c(C(=O)N[C@H]2C(O)O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]2O)c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c1I

name: Metra
text:
I read this as phenmetrazine tartrate, drawn as two separate components.

**Tartaric acid component (top).** It is a four-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid at each end and two CH(OH) carbons between them. Both OH groups are on wedge bonds.
- Starting from the left carboxyl, the lower-left stereocentre has its OH on a wedge pointing down, which gives `[C@H]`.
- The upper-right stereocentre has its OH on a wedge pointing up, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- This gives `O=C(O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(=O)O`.

**Phenmetrazine component (bottom).** It is a morpholine ring with the atoms in the order O, CH2, CH2, N(CH3), CH(CH3), CH(Ph).
- The CH bearing the methyl group has the methyl on a wedge, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- The CH bearing the phenyl group has the phenyl on a hashed bond, which gives `[C@H]`.
- The N carries a methyl group, and the phenyl is an ordinary six-carbon aromatic ring.
- This gives `C[C@@H]1N(C)CCO[C@H]1c1ccccc1`.

I worked out each @/@@ assignment by hand from the wedge and hash geometry, so the stereo marks are the part most open to error.

SMILES: O=C(O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(=O)O.C[C@@H]1N(C)CCO[C@H]1c1ccccc1

name: Miconazole Nitrate
text:
This structure is econazole-type, but with two chlorines on each ring it is miconazole nitrate. It has two components: nitric acid and miconazole.

**Nitric acid:** drawn as O=[N+](O)[O-], with the N bearing HO, O⁻ and =O.

**Miconazole:**
- Left ring: the attachment carbon is bonded to the CH(O) carbon. The ring has Cl ortho to that attachment and a second Cl para to it.
- Chain: the CH carbon carries an O–CH2–aryl group and a CH2–N(imidazole) group.
- Right ring: the CH2 attaches to a ring carbon that has Cl ortho and Cl para.
- Imidazole: N1 is attached to the CH2. The ring is n1ccnc1, with N1–CH=N–CH=CH.

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES for miconazole: Clc1ccc(c(Cl)c1)C(Cn1ccnc1)OCc1ccc(Cl)cc1Cl

Combined with the nitrate component:

SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])O.Clc1ccc(C(Cn2ccnc2)OCc2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)c(Cl)c1

name: Mibefradil
text:
I read this as mibefradil, with the stereochemistry taken from the two drawn wedges.

**Fragments read from the image**
- **Left:** a benzimidazole (an N–H and a pyridine-type N) joined at C2 to a three-carbon chain. The chain leads to a tertiary N that carries a methyl, then a two-carbon chain going to the quaternary carbon.
- **Right:** a tetralin ring. Its aromatic ring bears F on the carbon para to the ring-fusion carbon attached to the CH(iPr) carbon. The saturated ring holds a quaternary C bearing the ester oxygen and the chain, then a CH2CH2, and a CH carrying isopropyl.
- **Ester:** O–C(=O)–CH2–OCH3, a methoxyacetate.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Quaternary carbon:** the CH2 chain is on a hashed bond (pointing back). Viewed from the front, O, the CH(iPr) carbon and the ring CH2 run clockwise. This gives `[C@]` for the SMILES neighbour order O, ring closure, chain, ring CH2.
- **CH(iPr) carbon:** the isopropyl is on a wedge (toward the viewer), so the implicit H points back. This gives `[C@@H]` for the neighbour order aromatic C, H, ring closure, iPr.

name: Midazolam
text:
This structure is midazolam, which I identified from the drawing and then wrote out atom by atom.

**Imidazole ring (left):**
- A methyl group is attached to a carbon (C2) that is double-bonded to N (N3) and single-bonded to the bridgehead N.
- N3 connects to CH (C4), which is double-bonded to C5.
- C5 bonds to the bridgehead N and to the CH2 carbon.

**Diazepine ring:**
- The bridgehead N bonds to a benzene carbon.
- The two fused benzene carbons are joined to C(=N), which bears the fluorophenyl group.
- The N of C=N bonds to the CH2, which bonds back to C5.

**Chlorobenzene ring:**
- Going around the ring from the fusion carbon bonded to N (ring atom a): a, then CH, then CH, then C-Cl, then CH, then the fusion carbon bonded to C=N.
- In the image, the fusion carbon at (549,765) bonds to N, and the fusion carbon at (743,804) bonds to the C=N carbon.
- Cl sits on the carbon at (811,469), which is attached to (874,656), and that carbon attaches to (743,804). So Cl is on the carbon meta to the fusion carbon bearing C=N, reached via one CH.

**SMILES:**
Cc1ncc2CN=C(c3ccccc3F)c3cc(Cl)ccc3-n12

Checking the benzene ring in this SMILES: c3 (fusion, bonded to C=N), then cH (874,656), then c(Cl), then cH, then cH, then c3 (fusion, bonded to N). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ncc2CN=C(c3ccccc3F)c3cc(Cl)ccc3-n12

name: Midodrine Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows midodrine hydrochloride.

- **Left chain:** an H2N–CH2–C(=O)–NH–CH2– fragment (a glycine amide).
- **Stereocentre:** the CH2 connects to a CH(OH) carbon, which is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.
- **Aromatic ring:** the CH(OH) carbon attaches to a benzene ring carrying two methoxy groups. One methoxy is on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, and the other is para to it, on the carbon two positions further around the ring.
- **Ring order:** starting at the ring carbon bearing the CH(OH) group (call it C1), the next carbon (C2) bears OMe at the top. Going around the ring: C3 is CH (top right), C4 is CH (right), C5 is the carbon bearing OMe at the lower right, and C6 is CH (bottom).
- **Substituent positions:** the OMe groups are on C2 and C5, which gives the 2,5-dimethoxy pattern.
- **Salt:** HCl is written as a separate component.

SMILES: NCC(=O)NCC(O)c1cc(OC)ccc1OC.Cl

name: Micafungin
text:
I read this as micafungin, a cyclic hexapeptide carrying the pentyloxyphenyl-isoxazolyl-benzoyl side chain and the sulfated dihydroxyhomotyrosine residue. I assembled the SMILES from the drawing's connectivity, but the stereo tags are partly from memory of micafungin rather than derived wedge by wedge, so they are unverified.

Connectivity read from the image:
- **Side chain:** a pentyloxy group on a phenyl ring, linked to a 3,5-disubstituted isoxazole, then a para-substituted benzamide on the ring nitrogen.
- **Ring residue 1:** the benzamide nitrogen sits on an α-carbon bearing a CH2 (the vertex labelled "C"), then CH(OH)–CH(OH)–NH, a dihydroxy-ornithine unit.
- **Ring residue 2:** a 3-hydroxy-4-methylproline.
- **Ring residue 3:** a residue whose side chain is CH(OH)CH2C(=O)NH2.
- **Ring residue 4:** a dihydroxyhomotyrosine, CH(OH)–CH(OH)–aryl, where the aryl ring carries a free OH and an OSO3H.
- **Ring residue 5:** a 4-hydroxyproline.
- **Ring residue 6:** a threonine that closes the macrocycle back to the first residue's carbonyl.
