name: Mifepristone
text:
The drawing is a mifepristone-type steroid. I wrote the SMILES from the PubChem SMILES for mifepristone and checked it against the drawing; I did not rederive the stereo tags from the wedges independently.

- **Core:** a 4,9-dien-3-one steroid skeleton. The C=O sits at the top right, and the C4=C5 and C9=C10 double bonds are both drawn.
- **C11:** a bold wedge to a para-substituted phenyl ring carrying N(CH3)2.
- **C13:** a bold wedge to a methyl group.
- **C17:** a bold wedge to OH, with a propynyl group (–C≡C–CH3) on the same carbon.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** one H is hashed on C14 and one is bold on C8.

name: Midostaurin
text:
The drawing is midostaurin (PKC412), a staurosporine analogue with an N-benzoyl-N-methylamino group on the sugar ring. I read the structure in three parts and set the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- The core is an indolocarbazole. Two indole units are fused to a central benzene ring, which also carries a lactam (CH2–NH–C=O).
- Both indole nitrogens are bridged to a seven-membered sugar-type ring. One nitrogen is attached to a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl, and the other to an acetal CH. These two carbons are joined through an oxygen bridge.
- The sugar ring has an OMe carbon, an N(CH3)C(=O)Ph carbon, and a CH2.

**Stereocentres**
I assigned each centre by working out the orientation of its neighbours in the drawing, treating a hashed bond as pointing away from the viewer and a wedge as pointing toward it.
- The quaternary C–CH3 has a hashed methyl, which gives `[C@@]`.
- The C–OMe carbon has a wedged OMe, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- The C–N(Me)Bz carbon has a wedged N, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- The acetal CH has a hashed H, which gives `[C@@H]`.

**SMILES check**
Ring closure 1 is the oxygen bridge, ring closure 2 is the N–C(quaternary) bond, and the remaining digits close the aromatic rings. The string follows the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: C[C@@]12[C@@H]([C@@H](C[C@@H](O1)N3C4=CC=CC=C4C5=C6C(=C7C8=CC=CC=C8N2C7=C53)CNC6=O)N(C)C(=O)C9=CC=CC=C9)OC

name: Mifamurtide anhydrous
text:
This is mifamurtide sodium hydrate (L-MTP-PE), a muramyl tripeptide phosphatidylethanolamine. I read it as a dipalmitoyl glycerophosphate linked through ethanolamine to the tripeptide. The count of 16 carbons per acyl chain is an estimate from the chain length in the drawing, matching palmitoyl.

The stereochemistry follows the known natural configurations, which I assumed to match the drawing rather than reading every wedge and hash:

- The glycerol centre is the natural R form, as in DPPC.
- The alanines are L, the isoglutamine is D, and the lactyl ether is R.
- The open-chain acetamido sugar is the D-gluco form (MurNAc).

The sodium counter-ion and the water of hydration are included as separate components.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC[C@H](COP(=O)([O-])OCCNC(=O)[C@H](C)NC(=O)CC[C@H](C(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](C)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)O[C@H]([C@@H](NC(C)=O)C=O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCC.O.[Na+]

name: Microcystin-lr
text:
I read the structure as a microcystin-type cyclic peptide and wrote the SMILES by going around the macrocycle from the Leu residue.

**Residues, in ring order:**
1. Leu: isobutyl side chain, wedged CH2.
2. β-Methyl-Asp: free CO2H on the α-carbon, with a hashed methyl on the β-carbon.
3. Arg: the side chain ends in a guanidine, drawn as N=C(N)N.
4. Adda: the α-carbon carries a wedged vinyl and is followed by a CH(CH3) that is part of the ring. The side chain is a trans CH=CH, then C(CH3)=CH (E), then CH(CH3), then CH(OMe)CH2Ph.
5. Glu: free CO2H on the α-carbon, with the γ-carbon forming an amide to the N-methyl nitrogen of the next residue (the two atoms labelled "C" in the drawing are the CH2CH2).
6. N-Methyl-dehydroalanine: N(CH3)–C(=CH2)–C(=O).
7. Ala: hashed methyl, closing the ring back to Leu.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash by comparing the neighbour order in the SMILES with their arrangement on the page. The Leu, Arg and Glu centres come out as the usual L-configuration patterns, and both Adda double bonds are E.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)O)[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@@H](/C=C/C(C)=C/[C@H](C)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)OC)[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)O)CCC(=O)N(C)C(=C)C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(=O)N1

name: Migalastat
text:
I read the drawing as a six-membered piperidine ring with a hydroxymethyl group and three hydroxyls, which is the 1-deoxynojirimycin skeleton.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring contains one NH and five carbons: N, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6.
- C2 carries a CH2OH group, drawn with a bold wedge.
- C3 carries an OH, drawn with a bold wedge.
- C4 carries an OH, drawn with a bold wedge.
- C5 carries an OH, drawn with a hashed bond.
- C6 is a plain CH2 bonded to N and C5.

**Stereo assignment**
I wrote the SMILES in the order OC–C2–N–C6–C5–C4–C3, closing the ring from C3 back to C2. For each stereocentre I took the implicit H as pointing away from the viewer, except at C5, where the hashed OH puts H toward the viewer. I then read the rotation of the other three neighbours from the drawn angles, and swapped H into first position to get the @/@@ symbol.
- C2: `[C@H]`
- C5: `[C@H]`
- C4: `[C@@H]`
- C3: `[C@H]`

SMILES: OC[C@H]1NC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Miglitol
text:
Reading the drawing, I get a six-membered piperidine ring with an N-(2-hydroxyethyl) group, a CH2OH on the carbon next to N, and three ring OH groups. This is the structure of miglitol.

- **Ring:** N, then CH2, then three CH(OH) carbons, then the CH bearing CH2OH, which closes back to N.
- **N substituent:** –CH2CH2OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each of the four stereocentres from the wedge and hash positions, using the 2D bond directions around each carbon.
  - The carbon next to the ring CH2 has a hashed OH, which gives @.
  - The next carbon has a wedged OH, which gives @@.
  - The next carbon has a hashed OH, which gives @.
  - The carbon bearing CH2OH has a wedged CH2OH, which gives @.

SMILES: OCCN1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1CO

name: Miglustat
text:
I read the structure as N-butyl-1-deoxynojirimycin (miglustat): a piperidine ring bearing an N-butyl group, three hydroxyls and a CH2OH.

**Connectivity**
- The N-butyl chain has four carbons: CCCC–N.
- The ring is N, CH2, CH(OH), CH(OH), CH(OH), CH(CH2OH), closing back to N.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes**
I took each centre in SMILES neighbour order (previous atom, H, substituent, next atom), with the implicit H pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash.
- C bearing the top OH (hashed): `[C@H]`
- C bearing the right OH (wedge): `[C@@H]`
- C bearing the lower OH (hashed): `[C@H]`
- Ring C bearing the CH2OH (wedge): `[C@H]`

I checked the chirality tags by hand from the 2D coordinates rather than with software, so a tag could be flipped.

SMILES: CCCCN1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1CO

name: Milataxel
text:
This looks like a 10-deacetyl docetaxel analog. It has the taxane core, a C13 side chain carrying a 2-furyl group instead of phenyl, and a propionate ester at C7.

I built the SMILES from the docetaxel framework and checked each region against the drawing:

- **Side chain (left):** the N-Boc amide (NHC(=O)OC(CH3)3) sits on a carbon bearing the 2-furyl ring. The next carbon has an OH and is attached to the ester C=O, which links to C13 of the core.
- **Core, top:** the C11=C12 double bond carries a methyl. C10 bears an OH, so there is no acetate there, and C9 is a ketone.
- **Core, right:** C7 carries an O-propionyl group (OC(=O)CC), where docetaxel has an OH.
- **Core, bottom:** C4 bears an acetate and the oxetane ring is fused at C4/C5. C2 carries a benzoate, and C1 carries an OH.
- **Gem-dimethyl:** the C15 gem-dimethyl bridge is drawn.

For stereochemistry I took the docetaxel configuration and assumed the wedges and hashes match it. I did not re-derive each centre independently from the drawing.

name: Milrinone
text:
This is milrinone: a 2-pyridone ring carrying a methyl, a 4-pyridyl group and a nitrile.

**Pyridone ring** (six atoms):
- C(=O) at the lower right, bonded to the ring NH.
- The NH is bonded to the C bearing the methyl.
- That methyl-bearing C is double-bonded to the C bearing the pyridyl group.
- The pyridyl-bearing C is bonded to a CH.
- The CH is double-bonded to the C bearing C#N.
- The C#N-bearing C closes the ring back to the C=O.

**Pyridyl substituent:** a 4-pyridyl ring attached through its para carbon, with the ring N at the far left.

Reading the pyridyl ring from the attachment carbon (522,739): it connects to the carbon at (462,529), then to (250,477), then to N (100,635), then to (158,844), then to (371,896), and back to the attachment carbon. The ring N is therefore para to the attachment point, which makes it a 4-pyridyl.

SMILES: Cc1[nH]c(=O)c(C#N)cc1-c1ccncc1

name: Milnacipran Hydrochloride
text:
I read this as milnacipran hydrochloride: a cyclopropane carrying a phenyl and a diethylamide on one carbon and a CH2NH2 on the adjacent carbon, with HCl as a separate component.

**Connectivity**
- The cyclopropane has three ring carbons. The quaternary one bears the phenyl ring and the C(=O)N(Et)2 group. The neighbouring ring CH bears CH2NH2. The third ring carbon is a CH2.
- The amide nitrogen carries two ethyl groups.
- HCl is drawn separately, so I wrote it as a second component.

**Stereochemistry**
- Two wedges are drawn: the carbonyl carbon on the quaternary ring carbon is hashed, and the CH2NH2 carbon on the adjacent ring CH is hashed.
- For the quaternary carbon, the neighbours in SMILES order are carbonyl C, ring CH, phenyl, ring CH2. The carbonyl points away from the viewer, and the other three run clockwise on screen. That gives `@`.
- For the ring CH, the neighbours in SMILES order are ring CH2, H, quaternary C, CH2N. The CH2N points away, so the implicit H points toward the viewer, and the other three run counterclockwise from the H side. After reordering to the SMILES sequence, this gives `@@`.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)[C@]1(c2ccccc2)C[C@@H]1CN.Cl

name: Micrococcin
Minodronic Acid
text:
This is minodronic acid: an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine ring joined through a CH2 to a carbon that carries an OH and two phosphonic acid groups.

**Ring system.** The five-membered ring has these atoms:
- C3, the carbon bearing the CH2 substituent.
- C2, the CH next to C3, with a double bond between C2 and C3.
- N1, the imine-type nitrogen, which is double-bonded to C8a.
- C8a, the fusion carbon.
- N4, the bridgehead nitrogen bonded to C3.

The six-membered ring contains N4, C5, C6, C7, C8 and C8a, with double bonds C5=C6 and C7=C8. This accounts for all the ring bonds drawn, including the double bond from N1 to C8a.

**Side chain.** C3 is attached to CH2, which connects to C(O)(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O.

**SMILES check.** Writing the ring starting at C3: `c1cn...` would be aromatic, so I use the aromatic form `c1(CC(O)(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O)cnc2ccccn12`. The ring closure `n12` links N4 back to C3 (ring 1) and to C8a (ring 2). The atoms are: C3, then c (C2), n (N1), c2 (C8a), cccc (C8, C7, C6, C5), and n12 (N4). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(Cc1cnc2ccccn12)(P(=O)(O)O)P(=O)(O)O

name: Milvexian
text:
I read the structure as a macrocyclic lactam fused around a pyridine and a pyrazole, with a pyrimidinone carrying a chloro-aryl triazole substituent.

**Macrocycle.** The ring runs: a CH(CH3) carbon, then C(=O), then NH. The NH attaches to the pyrazole, which connects to the pyridine. The pyridine carbon next to its ring nitrogen bonds to a CH that sits at the end of a three-carbon CH2 chain leading back to the CH(CH3).

**Pyrazole.** It has an N-CHF2 group. Its carbon bearing the NH is adjacent to a CH, and the ring is C(NH)–CH=N–N(CHF2)–C(pyridyl).

**Pyrimidinone.** The ring nitrogen N3 bonds to the stereocentre CH. The ring continues N3–CH=N–C(aryl)=CH–C(=O).

**Aryl and triazole.** The aryl ring carries a Cl para to the triazole nitrogen attachment. The triazole is a 1,2,3-triazole bonded through N1 and has a Cl on C4.

**Stereochemistry.** Two wedges are drawn.
- The methyl-bearing carbon has a wedged methyl, which gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order below.
- The CH attached to the pyrimidinone nitrogen has a wedged N, which gives `[C@H]`.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CCC[C@H](n2cnc(cc2=O)-c2cc(Cl)ccc2-n2cc(Cl)nn2)c2cc(ccn2)-c2n(C(F)F)ncc2NC1=O

name: Minoxidil
text:
The drawing is a minoxidil tautomer: a pyrimidine ring with an N-hydroxy group, an exocyclic imine, an amino group and a piperidine substituent.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- C2 carries the =NH group and is bonded to N1 and N3.
- N1 carries the OH group and is bonded to C6.
- C6 carries the NH2 group and is double-bonded to C5.
- C5 is a CH bonded to C4.
- C4 is double-bonded to N3 and carries the piperidine nitrogen.
- N3 closes the ring back to C2.

Piperidine: the nitrogen is attached to C4 and to five CH2 groups, which close a six-membered ring.

SMILES, written from N1: ON1C(=N)N=C(N2CCCCC2)C=C1N

Check: N1 is bonded to O, C2 and C6. C2 is =NH and bonded to N3. N3=C4 is a double bond. C4 carries the piperidine and is bonded to C5. C5=C6 is a double bond, and C6 carries NH2 and closes the ring to N1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: ON1C(=N)N=C(N2CCCCC2)C=C1N

name: Milademetan
text:
I read the structure as follows.

- **Oxindole:** a 6-chloro-oxindole (lactam NH–C=O), spiro-fused at C3.
- **Spiro carbon:** this carbon is also a ring carbon of the pyrrolidine and is bonded to a second spiro carbon.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring containing NH. One carbon carries a 2-chloro-3-fluoropyridin-4-yl group (bold wedge). The next carbon carries a carboxamide C(=O)NH (hashed bond).
- **Cyclohexane:** the second spiro carbon, next to the NH, belongs to a 4,4-dimethylcyclohexane ring.
- **Amide substituent:** the amide N bears a tetrahydropyran-3-yl group (ring O, wedge on the N-bearing carbon). The carbon next to the ring O carries a primary carboxamide, C(=O)NH2, on a hashed bond.

I assigned the @/@@ marks from the wedges and hashes. The wedge between the two spiro carbons I took as starting at the oxindole spiro carbon. The cyclohexane spiro carbon is not a stereocentre, because its two ring branches are identical.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2cc(Cl)ccc2[C@@]13[C@@H](c4ccnc(Cl)c4F)[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H]5CC[C@@H](C(N)=O)OC5)NC36CCC(C)(C)CC6

name: Minocycline
text:
I read this as a minocycline-type tetracycline skeleton, with the hydroxyl-bearing aromatic ring on the right. The SMILES below was assembled region by region from the drawing.

**Ring system and substituents**
- **Left ring:** a carboxamide (C(=O)NH2) sits on a C=C(OH) unit, which is followed by the quaternary C(OH), the CH–NMe2 carbon and a ring ketone.
- **Middle ring:** a ketone is conjugated to a C=C(OH) unit.
- **Right ring:** an aromatic ring carries one OH and one NMe2.
- **Bridge:** two CH2 groups link the rings, and the two ring-fusion CH carbons are drawn with hashed H.

**Stereochemistry**
There are four drawn stereocentres:
- the quaternary C–OH (hashed OH),
- the CH carbon bearing the hashed NMe2,
- the ring-fusion CH with hashed H next to it,
- the other ring-fusion CH with hashed H.

I converted each hashed bond into @/@@ using the neighbour order in the SMILES string.

**Ring closures**
- Digit 1: left ring.
- Digit 2: the quaternary C(OH) to the adjacent ring-fusion CH.
- Digit 3: middle ring.
- Digit 4: aromatic ring.

SMILES: NC(=O)C1=C(O)[C@@]2(O)C(=O)C3=C(O)c4c(O)ccc(N(C)C)c4C[C@H]3C[C@H]2[C@H](N(C)C)C1=O

name: Mirabegron
text:
I read this as mirabegron, which has an (R) stereocentre.

- **Left end:** a phenyl ring attached to a stereocentre CH that carries the wedged OH.
- **Chain:** CH2 – NH – CH2CH2, linking the stereocentre to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Right end:** the benzene ring bears an NH–C(=O)–CH2 amide. The CH2 is attached to C4 of a 2-aminothiazole (ring atoms S, C–NH2, N, and two CH/C carbons).
- **Stereochemistry:** the OH is drawn on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are OH > CH2N > phenyl > H. In the drawing, OH (up), CH2N (right) and phenyl (down-left) run clockwise, which gives (R). I wrote the SMILES with the OH written first from the stereocentre and set the chirality tag to match (R) by checking the neighbour order.

SMILES: O[C@@H](CNCCc1ccc(NC(=O)Cc2csc(N)n2)cc1)c1ccccc1

name: Minaxolone
text:
I read this as a pregnane (steroid) skeleton and wrote the SMILES ring by ring, assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Substituents**
- C17 carries an acetyl group (CC(=O)–).
- C13 and C10 each carry an angular methyl, drawn hashed.
- C11 carries an N(CH3)2 group on a wedge.
- C2 carries an ethoxy group (OCC) on a hash.
- C3 carries an OH on a wedge.

**Ring-fusion hydrogens**
- H at C9: wedge.
- H at C8: hash.
- H at C14: wedge.
- H at C5: wedge.

I derived the @/@@ symbols by hand from the 2D coordinates and have not run the string through a SMILES parser.

name: Mirex
text:
I read the drawing as a cage of 10 carbons and 12 chlorines (C10Cl12), which matches mirex. I labelled each carbon by position and listed the bonds between them.

- **Carbons:** two carry two Cl each (top-left and bottom-right), and the other eight carry one Cl each, giving 12 Cl in total.
- **C–C bonds:** I counted 14, including the long diagonal from the upper-right carbon to the left-hand carbon and the near-vertical bond through the middle.
- **Check:** every carbon comes out with four bonds once its Cl atoms are counted.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows only plain bonds, so I added no stereo marks.

name: Mitapivat
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline-8-sulfonamide whose nitrogen is attached to a para-substituted benzene. That benzene carries an amide to a piperazine, and the piperazine bears a cyclopropylmethyl group.

- **Quinoline:** the ring nitrogen sits next to the fused carbon, which is adjacent to the C8 carbon bearing the sulfonyl group. This gives the 8-sulfonyl quinoline.
- **Sulfonamide:** S(=O)(=O) links C8 to an NH.
- **Benzene:** the NH-bearing carbon is para to the carbonyl-bearing carbon.
- **Piperazine:** the amide nitrogen is joined by C(=O) to the benzene, and the opposite nitrogen carries CH2–cyclopropyl.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2cccc3cccnc23)cc1)N1CCN(CC2CC2)CC1

name: Mirtazapine
text:
This structure is mirtazapine, and I read it from the drawing as follows.

**Pyridine ring (left):** The atoms are N, CH, CH, CH and two fused carbons. The ring nitrogen is bonded to a fused carbon (533,760) that also carries the other ring nitrogen. The other fused carbon (503,511) is bonded to the CH2 bridge.

**Benzene ring (upper right):** Two of its carbons are fused to the central seven-membered ring. One is bonded to the CH2 bridge and the other to the CH carbon (980,805).

**Central seven-membered ring:** Its atoms are CH2, the benzene carbon at (926,358), the benzene carbon at (1061,569), the CH at (980,805), N (the tertiary ring nitrogen), the pyridine carbon at (533,760), and the pyridine carbon at (503,511).

**Piperazine ring:** Its atoms are N, CH, CH2, N(CH3), CH2 and CH2. The CH is bonded to the central-ring N, to the benzene carbon at (1061,569), and to a CH2 that leads to N-methyl. From the N-methyl, the chain goes through CH2, CH2 and back to the central-ring N.

**SMILES:** Starting from the methyl group, CN1CCN2C(C1)c1ccccc1Cc1cccnc12. Checking the ring closures:
- N1 is the N-methyl nitrogen, followed by CH2 and CH2 to N2.
- C(C1) is the CH, and its CH2 closes ring 1 back to the N-methyl nitrogen.
- c1ccccc1 is the benzene ring. The first aromatic carbon attaches to the CH, and the last one, which is ortho to the first, carries the CH2 bridge.
- Cc1cccnc12 follows: the aromatic carbon c1 is bonded to the CH2 bridge, then come three CH carbons and the pyridine N. The final carbon closes ring 1 with c1 and ring 2 with N2.

The pyridine ring order is c1 (503,511), then CH, CH, CH, N, and the carbon at (533,760), which closes the ring. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CCN2C(C1)c1ccccc1Cc1cccnc12

name: Mirogabalin
text:
I read the structure as a bicyclo[3.2.0]heptene core, which matches the drug mirogabalin.

- **Core:** A cyclopentene is fused to a cyclobutane through two bridgehead CH carbons, each drawn with a wedged H. The ring C=C sits next to one bridgehead and carries an ethyl group on its other carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** The cyclobutane carbon beside the other bridgehead bears an aminomethyl group (CH2NH2) and a hashed CH2COOH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned @/@@ at the two bridgehead carbons and the quaternary carbon from the wedge and hash geometry, and they are consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: CCC1=C[C@@H]2[C@H](C1)C[C@]2(CN)CC(=O)O

name: Misoprostol
text:
I read the structure as a methyl ester of a heptanoic acid chain attached to a cyclopentanone ring, which also carries a hydroxy group and a hydroxy-methyl-octenyl side chain. This is a misoprostol-type skeleton.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Ester chain:** a methyl ester (O–CH3, C=O) is followed by six CH2 groups, giving a heptanoate chain attached to the ring.
- **Ring:** a five-membered ring with a ketone, a CH2, a CH bearing OH (wedge), a CH bearing the alkenyl chain (hashed), and a CH bearing the ester chain (wedge).
- **Side chain:** a trans CH=CH, then CH2, then a quaternary carbon bearing OH and CH3, then a butyl group (four carbons).

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned the three ring stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds as drawn, giving `[C@H]`, `[C@@H]` and `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order below.
- The side-chain double bond is drawn trans, so it is written `/C=C/`.
- The quaternary carbinol carbon has plain bonds in the drawing, so I left it without stereo.

SMILES: COC(=O)CCCCCC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/CC(C)(O)CCCC

name: Mitotane
text:
The drawing is o,p'-DDD: a CHCl2 carbon attached to a CH, which carries two aryl rings.

- **Top chain:** the carbon bearing two Cl atoms (CHCl2) connects to the central CH.
- **Central CH:** it bonds to both rings and has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.
- **Left ring:** it attaches to the central CH at one carbon. The adjacent carbon bears Cl, so the ring is 2-chlorophenyl (ortho).
- **Right ring:** it attaches to the central CH at one carbon. Going round the ring (attachment carbon, then the top carbon, the upper-right carbon, the carbon bearing Cl), the Cl sits on the carbon opposite the attachment carbon. This is 4-chlorophenyl (para).

SMILES: ClC(Cl)C(c1ccccc1Cl)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Mitiglinide
text:
I read the drawing as mitiglinide, (2S)-2-benzyl-4-[(3aR,7aS)-octahydroisoindol-2-yl]-4-oxobutanoic acid. This is how I read it, region by region:

- **Acid end:** a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) is attached to a stereocentre. That carbon also carries a CH2–phenyl group (benzyl) and a CH2–C(=O)–N chain.
- **Chain:** the CH2 next to the stereocentre is joined by a wedge bond and leads to a carbonyl whose carbon is bonded to the ring nitrogen, forming an amide.
- **Bicyclic amine:** the nitrogen sits in a five-membered ring fused to a six-membered carbocycle, an octahydroisoindole. Both ring-fusion carbons carry hashed H atoms on the same face, so the fusion is cis.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are COOH, then CH2C(=O)N, then CH2Ph, then H. With H pointing away, that sequence runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is encoded as `[C@@H]` in the written order.

For the two ring-fusion carbons, I assigned the tags from the hashed H atoms, which gives `[C@@H]` at each fusion carbon in the SMILES order used.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)CC(=O)N1C[C@@H]2CCCC[C@@H]2C1

name: Mitoxantrone
text:
This is mitoxantrone, an anthraquinone core with the following substituents.

- The top ring carries an OH at each of its two upper corners, with two CH carbons between them.
- The two carbonyls (C=O) sit in the middle ring.
- The bottom ring carries an NH at each lower corner, and each NH is attached to a CH2CH2NHCH2CH2OH chain.

Writing the SMILES from the top ring down: OC1=CC=C(O)C2=C1C(=O)C1=C(NCCNCCO)C=CC(NCCNCCO)=C1C2=O

Checking the ring closures:
- The first ring is C1(O)=CC=C(O)C2=C1…, so the atoms are C1(OH), CH, CH, C(OH), C2 and C1′, which makes 6 atoms.
- C2=C1 gives the fusion atoms. The first fusion atom, C2, is bonded to C(OH) and the next fusion atom is bonded to C1(OH).
- After C1 (the ring-closing atom) comes C(=O), then C1=C(N…)C=CC(N…)=C1, then C2=O.

The second ring is C1=C(N)C=CC(N)=C1, where the first atom C1 is bonded to the carbonyl and the last atom C1 closes the ring to the first and bonds onward to C2=O. This is consistent. The final C2=O closes to the first fusion atom, C2.

SMILES: OC1=CC=C(O)C2=C1C(=O)C1=C(NCCNCCO)C=CC(NCCNCCO)=C1C2=O

name: Mitomycin C
text:
This drawing is mitomycin C. I wrote its SMILES from my recall of the standard PubChem SMILES for this compound, not by building it up from the picture. I then checked one stereocentre against the drawing and the other stereocentres were not checked.

The structure has these parts:
- a 2-amino-3-methyl-1,4-benzoquinone ring fused to a pyrrolidine (the quinone carbons carry the NH2, CH3 and two C=O groups)
- a fused aziridine ring (NH) with two hashed hydrogens
- a methoxy group on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen, drawn with a hashed bond
- a carbamate side chain, CH2–O–C(=O)–NH2, on a wedged bond

The check was at the methoxy-bearing carbon. With the OMe pointing away from the viewer, the other three neighbours (the aziridine-side carbon, the ring N and the CH(CH2O) carbon) run clockwise in that order. That matches the `@@` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: CO[C@@]12[C@H](COC(N)=O)C3=C(N1C[C@H]1N[C@@H]12)C(=O)C(C)=C(N)C3=O

name: MK 1775
text:
This is the Wee1 inhibitor adavosertib (AZD1775).

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Bicyclic core:** a pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-3-one. The C=O carbon is bonded to N(allyl), and that N is bonded to the second N, which carries the pyridyl group. The second N is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon C7a, which is double-bonded to a pyrimidine N. The pyrimidine ring runs C7a=N–C(NHAr)=N–CH=C3a.
- **N-allyl:** N–CH2–CH=CH2.
- **Pyridyl substituent:** a pyridin-2-yl attached to the second N, with a C(C)(C)O group at the 6-position.
- **Anilino group:** an NH-linked para-substituted phenyl bearing a 4-methylpiperazin-1-yl group.

SMILES, written as the lactam ring first:
C=CCN1N(c2cccc(C(C)(C)O)n2)C2=NC(Nc3ccc(N4CCN(C)CC4)cc3)=NC=C2C1=O

Check of the ring closures:
- N1 (allyl) – N(pyridyl) – C2 (C7a) =N–C(NHAr)=N–C=C2 (C3a)–C1(=O) closes back to N1.
- C2 is opened at the fusion carbon C7a, and the later "C=C2" closes it at C3a. C7a=N, then C(NHAr)=N, then CH=C3a. So the pyrimidine ring is C7a, N, C, N, CH, C3a, which is six atoms.
- C3a is bonded to C(=O), which closes ring 1 to N1. The five-membered ring is N1, N, C7a, C3a, C(=O), which is correct.

SMILES: C=CCN1N(c2cccc(C(C)(C)O)n2)C2=NC(Nc3ccc(N4CCN(C)CC4)cc3)=NC=C2C1=O

name: Miocamycin
text:
I read the drawing as a 16-membered macrolide (a midecamycin/leucomycin-type structure). It has a lactone ring with a CH2CHO side chain, an OMe group, and propionate and acetate esters on the ring. Two sugars hang off it: an amino sugar carrying a dimethylamino and a free OH, and a second sugar carrying a C-methyl, an acetate and a propionate.

**Macrolactone ring, traced from the CH(CH3)–O carbon:**
- The ring starts at CH(CH3)–O, with a wedged methyl.
- It continues through CH2 and two E (trans) C=C bonds, forming a conjugated diene.
- Next is CH(OAc) with a wedged O, then CH(CH3) with a wedged methyl, then CH2.
- Then comes CH bearing a wedged CH2CHO, then CH(O-sugar) with a wedged O, then CH(OMe) with a wedged O.
- Next is CH(OC(=O)Et) with a wedged O, then CH2, then the lactone C(=O) closing back to the ring oxygen.

**Amino sugar (attached at the CH(O-sugar) carbon):**
- It is a pyranose with a ring O, a methyl at C5 (wedged), a hashed O-glycoside at C4, a wedged NMe2 at C3, and a hashed OH at C2.
- The hashed O at C4 links to the second sugar.

**Second sugar:**
- It is a 2,6-dideoxy pyranose.
- C3 is quaternary, carrying a wedged methyl and an OAc.
- C4 carries a hashed O-propionyl, and C5 carries a wedged methyl.

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry, taking the implicit H as the opposite face to the wedged or hashed substituent. I did not run the SMILES through a parser to check it.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](OC(C)=O)[C@H](C)C[C@H](CC=O)[C@H](O[C@@H]2O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]3C[C@@](C)(OC(C)=O)[C@@H](OC(=O)CC)[C@H](C)O3)[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]2O)[C@@H](OC)[C@H](OC(=O)CC)CC(=O)O1

name: Mobocertinib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ester:** an isopropyl group, CC(C)O, is attached to a C(=O) that sits on the pyrimidine ring.
- **Pyrimidine:** the ring atoms in order are C5 (bearing the ester), C4 (bearing the indole), N3, C2 (bearing the NH), N1, and C6 (the CH). C4 and C2 are joined through N3, and C2 and C6 through N1.
- **Indole:** the pyrimidine C4 is bonded to indole C3. The indole nitrogen carries a methyl group, and the benzene ring is fused to the five-membered ring.
- **Central benzene ring:**
  - C1 carries the NH that links to pyrimidine C2.
  - C2 carries the OMe.
  - C3 is a CH.
  - C4 carries N(Me)CH2CH2N(Me)2.
  - C5 carries NHC(=O)C=C.
  - C6 is a CH.

SMILES, written from the ester end:

CC(C)OC(=O)c1cnc(Nc2cc(NC(=O)C=C)c(N(C)CCN(C)C)cc2OC)nc1-c1cn(C)c2ccccc12

Checking the benzene ring: c2 (the NH-bearing carbon), then cH, then c(NHacryl), then c(NMe...), then cH, then c(OMe), closing the ring. In the drawing the NH-bearing carbon is bonded to the OMe carbon and to a CH. The OMe carbon is also bonded to a CH, which connects to the carbon bearing N(Me). That carbon is next to the carbon bearing the acrylamide NH, which connects through a CH back to the NH-bearing carbon. This matches the SMILES, in which the acrylamide carbon is adjacent to the N(Me) carbon.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)c1cnc(Nc2cc(NC(=O)C=C)c(N(C)CCN(C)C)cc2OC)nc1-c1cn(C)c2ccccc12

name: Moclobemide
text:
The drawing shows three connected parts:

- **Morpholine ring:** a six-membered ring with O and N at opposite positions, giving O1CCN(CC1).
- **Linker:** the ring nitrogen carries a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2), which ends at an NH.
- **Amide and aryl group:** the NH is bonded to a C=O, which is attached to a benzene ring. The ring carries Cl at the para position, which matches the drawing, where Cl sits on the carbon opposite the carbonyl-bearing carbon.

This is 4-chloro-N-(2-morpholin-4-ylethyl)benzamide.

SMILES: O=C(NCCN1CCOCC1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Mivacurium Chloride
text:
I read this as the bis-benzylisoquinolinium diester with an (E)-oct-4-enedioate linker, which matches mivacurium chloride. This is a reading of the drawing, not a database lookup.

- **Isoquinolinium units (two, identical):** each is a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinolinium with 6,7-dimethoxy groups. The nitrogen is quaternary (N⁺) and carries a methyl and a 3-carbon propyl linker. C1 carries a 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzyl group.
- **Linker:** each propyl chain ends in an ester oxygen. The two esters are joined through a C8 diacid chain, –C(=O)CH2CH2CH=CHCH2CH2C(=O)–, with the double bond drawn trans (E).
- **Counter-ions:** two Cl⁻.
- **Stereochemistry:** both C1 centres are drawn with a bold wedge to the benzyl CH2. In each case the neighbours N, aryl carbon and benzyl CH2 run counterclockwise when viewed with H at the back. The SMILES order aryl–[C@H]–(ring closure to N)–CH2 encodes that, so I wrote both centres as `[C@H]`.

SMILES: C[N+]1(CCCOC(=O)CC/C=C/CCC(=O)OCCC[N+]2(C)CCc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc3[C@H]2Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c2)CCc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc2[C@H]1Cc1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1.[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Modafinil
text:
The drawing shows modafinil: a primary amide (H2N–C(=O)) attached to a CH2 group, which is bonded to a sulfoxide sulfur (S=O). The sulfur is bonded to a CH carbon carrying two phenyl rings.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry. The sulfur is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds.

SMILES: NC(=O)CS(=O)C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Molindone
text:
The drawing shows a tetrahydroindol-4-one core with a morpholinylmethyl substituent.

**Pyrrole ring:** NH is bonded to C2, which carries a methyl group, and to C7a. C2 is double-bonded to C3, which carries an ethyl group. C3 is bonded to C3a, and C3a is double-bonded to C7a.

**Six-membered ring:** C3a is bonded to the C=O carbon (C4). C4 is bonded to C5, which carries the CH2–morpholine substituent. C5 is bonded to C6 (CH2), then C7 (CH2), then C7a.

**Morpholine:** N is bonded to CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2 and closes the ring.

SMILES: CCc1c(C)[nH]c2CCC(CN3CCOCC3)C(=O)c12

SMILES: CCc1c(C)[nH]c2c1C(=O)C(CN1CCOCC1)CC2

name: ML RR-S2 CDA Sodium Salt
text:
I read this as a cyclic di-adenosine bisphosphorothioate disodium salt, with mixed 2',5' and 3',5' linkages (an analogue of 2'3'-c-di-AMP).

**Structure read from the drawing**
- Both bases are adenine, drawn as 6-aminopurines attached through N9 to C1' of a ribose. The N9 bonds are hashed.
- **Left ribose:** C3' carries a free OH and C2' carries an O–P bond. C5' is linked through O to the upper phosphorus.
- **Right ribose:** C2' carries a free OH and C3' carries an O–P bond. C5' is linked through O to the lower phosphorus.
- **Upper phosphorus:** P(=S)(O⁻), joining the left C5' oxygen to the right C3' oxygen.
- **Lower phosphorus:** P(=O)(S⁻), joining the left C2' oxygen to the right C5' oxygen.
- Two Na⁺ counterions are shown.

**Stereochemistry**
- I took the sugar stereocentres to be those of natural D-ribo adenosine, which is consistent with the wedges and hashes shown.
- The phosphorus atoms have no wedges or hashes, so I gave them no stereo.
- I wrote the two nucleosides as separate fragments joined by ring-closure digits (%10, %11). The neighbour order around each stereocentre is the same as in the adenosine template, so the chirality tags carry over. The SMILES was not run through a parser.

SMILES: Nc1ncnc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=S)([O-])O%10)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1OP%11(=O)[S-].Nc1ncnc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](CO%11)[C@@H]%10[C@H]1O.[Na+].[Na+]

name: Molnupiravir
text:
This structure matches molnupiravir, the 5'-isobutyryl ester of N4-hydroxycytidine. I read it region by region:

- **Ester side chain:** an isopropyl group (CH3)2CH attached to a C=O, which is bonded through O to the 5'-CH2. This is an isobutyrate ester.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring made of one ring O and four carbons. The 4' carbon carries the CH2O-ester on a bold wedge. The 1' carbon carries the ring nitrogen N on a bold wedge. The 2' and 3' carbons each carry an OH on a hashed bond. This is the β-D-ribofuranose pattern.
- **Base:** a six-membered pyrimidinone ring. N1 is attached to the sugar, followed by C2(=O), then N3 double-bonded to C4, which carries NH–OH (a hydroxylamine). The ring closes through C5=C6 back to N1.

I took the stereodescriptors from the known molnupiravir SMILES, and they agree with the wedges and hashes drawn here.

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)OC[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@H]([C@@H](O1)N2C=CC(=NC2=O)NO)O)O

name: Moexipril
text:
I read the structure as moexipril, with the ethyl ester, the alanine-type amide and the 6,7-dimethoxy-tetrahydroisoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid.

- **Left side:** an ethyl ester, C(=O)OEt, sits on a carbon that also carries a CH2CH2-phenyl chain and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH is attached to a CH(CH3) carbon, which carries an amide C(=O) joined to the ring nitrogen.
- **Right side:** the ring is a tetrahydroisoquinoline. N–CH(COOH)–CH2 is fused to a benzene ring bearing two OMe groups.

Stereochemistry, assigned from the wedges and hashes by CIP priority (N > C(=O) > CH2 or CH3 > H):

- The ester-bearing carbon (CH2 wedge) is S.
- The alanine carbon (CH3 wedge) is S.
- The ring carbon bearing COOH (hashed bond, H toward the viewer) is S.

I then checked that the chirality tags in the SMILES below reproduce S, S, S at these three centres.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc2C[C@H]1C(O)=O

name: Momelotinib
text:
This is momelotinib. I read it region by region:

- **Left end:** a morpholine ring (O at the far left, N at the right) attached through its nitrogen to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** that benzene carries an NH on the opposite side, which connects to C2 of a pyrimidine.
- **Pyrimidine:** N1 and N3 flank C2, and C4 bears the aryl group.
- **Right end:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries a C(=O)NH group, which is attached to CH2–C≡N.

Written as SMILES: N#CCNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccnc(n1)Nc1ccc(cc1)N1CCOCC1

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

SMILES: N#CCNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccnc(n1)Nc1ccc(cc1)N1CCOCC1

name: Molsidomine
text:
This looks like molsidomine, drawn as the sydnonimine with an N-ethoxycarbonyl group.

Reading the drawing:
- The ethyl group is CH3–CH2–O, attached to a carbon that carries O⁻ and a double bond to N (C(=N)[O-]).
- That N is bonded to a ring carbon.
- The ring is a five-membered 1,2,3-oxadiazole: O1, N2, N3⁺, C4, C5. The drawn atoms are O (top left), N (top), N⁺ (right), CH (bottom), and C (left).
- Ring bonds: O–N single; N=N⁺ double; N⁺–CH single; CH=C double; C–O single.
- N⁺ is bonded to the morpholine nitrogen, and the morpholine ring is N1CCOCC1.

SMILES: CCOC([O-])=Nc1c[n+](N2CCOCC2)=no1

Check: c1 is bonded to the exocyclic N and to the ring O. The ring is written c1 c [n+] (=n) o1, so the aromatic form has c1, c, [n+], n, o1, which is five atoms. In the aromatic SMILES the [n+] is bonded to the neighbouring n, and the ring closes through o1 back to c1. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOC([O-])=Nc1c[n+](N2CCOCC2)no1

name: Monobenzone
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring bonded to a CH2 group, which is bonded to an ether oxygen. The oxygen is attached to a second benzene ring, and that ring carries an OH group para to the ether oxygen. This is 4-(benzyloxy)phenol.

SMILES: Oc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)cc1

name: Mometasone Furoate
text:
The drawing shows mometasone furoate, a corticosteroid. I identified it from the following features and wrote the SMILES from that identification, taking the stereodescriptors from the recalled PubChem entry for mometasone furoate. I did not re-derive each wedge and hash from the picture.

- **Core:** a steroid with a 1,4-dien-3-one A-ring.
- **Ring-junction substituents:** a chlorine at C9 and a hydroxyl at C11. There are methyl groups at C10 and C13 and a methyl at C16.
- **C17 substituents:** a 2-chloroacetyl group (C(=O)CH2Cl) and a furan-2-carboxylate ester (OC(=O) attached to a furan ring).

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]4([C@]3([C@H](C[C@@]2([C@]1(C(=O)CCl)OC(=O)C5=CC=CO5)C)O)Cl)C

name: Monomethyl Fumarate
text:
The drawing shows a methyl ester at one end and a carboxylic acid at the other, joined by a carbon–carbon double bond: CH3–O–C(=O)–CH=CH–C(=O)OH.

For the double bond geometry, I compared the positions of the two carbonyl carbons relative to the C=C axis. The ester carbon and the acid carbon lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the alkene is trans (E).

This is the monomethyl ester of fumaric acid.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)O

name: Monensin
text:
This structure matches monensin A, a polyether ionophore, and I wrote the SMILES from that recognition rather than assigning every stereocentre independently from the wedges and hashes. I did not re-derive each @/@@ label against the drawing, so the stereochemistry is taken from my recollection of the known monensin A structure.

These features of the drawing fit monensin A:
- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid with an adjacent methoxy group and methyl branches.
- **Ring system:** five rings in a row. They are a tetrahydropyran carrying an OH and a methyl, a spiro-fused five-membered ring, two further tetrahydrofurans, and a terminal hemiketal pyran.
- **Substituents:** an ethyl group on one tetrahydrofuran, and a CH2OH plus an OH on the terminal hemiketal carbon.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(CC[C@@H](O1)[C@@]2(CC[C@@]3(O2)C[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O3)[C@@H](C)[C@H]([C@H](C)C(=O)O)OC)C)O)C)[C@@H]4[C@H](C[C@@H](O4)[C@@H]5[C@H](C[C@H]([C@](O5)(CO)O)C)C)C

name: Monomethylauristatin E
text:
The drawing matches monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). I read it as five connected units, left to right:

- **Norephedrine unit:** a phenyl ring on a carbon bearing OH (hashed bond), then a carbon with a methyl (wedge) and an amide NH.
- **Dolaproine unit:** a methyl-bearing carbon (hashed methyl) next to the amide C=O, then a methoxy-bearing carbon (hashed O) attached to the 2-position of a pyrrolidine ring.
- **Dolaisoleuine unit:** the pyrrolidine nitrogen acylated by a C(=O)CH2 group, then a methoxy-bearing carbon, then a carbon carrying an N-methyl amide nitrogen (wedge) and a sec-butyl group (ethyl plus wedged methyl).
- **Valine unit:** an isopropyl-bearing carbon (hashed NH) with a C=O linked to the N-methyl nitrogen.
- **N-methylvaline unit:** a terminal isopropyl-bearing carbon (hashed NHMe) linked to the valine NH through its C=O.

I wrote the stereodescriptors from the known MMAE structure rather than deriving each one from the wedges and hashes, so they are not independently checked against the drawing.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@@H]([C@@H](CC(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1[C@@H]([C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)[C@H](C2=CC=CC=C2)O)OC)OC)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)NC

name: Mithramycin
text:
I read the structure as an aureolic-acid-type glycoside (olivomycin/chromomycin family): a tricyclic aglycone carrying two sugar chains and a polyoxygenated side chain.

**Aglycone**
- A naphthalene-derived core with an aromatic methyl, two aromatic OH groups and one aromatic O-glycoside.
- The third ring is partly saturated. It contains a ketone, a CH bearing an O-glycoside (wedge), a CH2, and a CH bearing the side chain (hashed bond to the CH2).
- The side chain is CH(OMe), then C=O, then CH(OH), then CH(OH)CH3. The first CH(OMe) is a hash bond, the next CH(OH) is a wedge, and the CH3 on the last carbon is a wedge.

**Sugars**
- Left chain, on the aromatic oxygen: a 2,6-dideoxy sugar (ring CH2, 4-OH, 5-CH3), O-linked at C3 to a second 2,6-dideoxy sugar that carries 3-OH and 4-OH.
- Right chain, on the ring oxygen next to the ketone: a 2,6-dideoxy sugar (4-OH), linked at C3 to a second 2,6-dideoxy sugar, which is linked at C3 to a third sugar. The third sugar is a 2,6-dideoxy sugar with a C3 methyl and OH (a quaternary carbon) and a 4-OH.

I derived each stereocentre's @/@@ from the wedge or hash bond and the 2D geometry at that carbon. The SMILES below has valid ring closures, and every ring and substituent matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1c(O[C@H]2C[C@@H](O[C@H]3C[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O3)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O2)cc2cc3C[C@@H]([C@H](OC)C(=O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)C)[C@H](O[C@H]4C[C@@H](O[C@H]5C[C@@H](O[C@H]6C[C@](C)(O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O6)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)O5)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O4)C(=O)c3c(O)c2c1O

name: Montelukast
text:
This structure is montelukast, and I read it region by region.

- **Left side:** a benzene ring is ortho-substituted with a C(CH3)2OH group (the HO-bearing carbon with two methyls) and a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Stereocentre:** the chain leads to a carbon bearing S, a 1,3-disubstituted benzene ring and an implicit H. The bond to the CH2 is hashed.
- **Sulfur side chain:** S–CH2–(cyclopropane-1,1-diyl)–CH2–COOH.
- **Right side:** the 1,3-disubstituted benzene carries a trans CH=CH linked to C2 of a 7-chloroquinoline.

For the stereochemistry, the priorities at the stereocentre are S, then aryl, then CH2, then H. The CH2 is hashed (pointing away), so H points toward the viewer. S (lower left), aryl (lower right) and CH2 (top) run counterclockwise from the front. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving R.

In the SMILES I write the neighbours of the stereocentre in the order CH2, H, S, aryl. For R in that order, the tag is @@.

SMILES: CC(C)(O)c1ccccc1CC[C@@H](SCC2(CC2)CC(=O)O)c1cccc(c1)/C=C/c1ccc2ccc(Cl)cc2n1

name: Montelukast Sodium
text:
The image shows montelukast as its sodium salt. I read it region by region:

- **Left aryl group:** an ortho-disubstituted benzene carrying a C(CH3)2OH group and a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Stereocentre:** a carbon bonded to sulfur, the CH2 chain (hashed bond), a 1,3-disubstituted benzene, and an implicit H.
- **Thioether side:** S–CH2 attached to a cyclopropane carbon that also bears CH2–COO⁻.
- **Right side:** the benzene's other substituent is a trans CH=CH linked to the 2-position of a 7-chloroquinoline.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are S > aryl > CH2 > H. The hashed CH2 points away, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page, S (lower left) → aryl (lower right) → CH2 (top) runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R.

In the SMILES, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, S, aryl. Checking this ordering gives `@@` for R, so that is the tag used below.

SMILES: CC(C)(O)c1ccccc1CC[C@@H](SCC1(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)c1cccc(/C=C/c2ccc3ccc(Cl)cc3n2)c1.[Na+]

name: Morantel Tartrate
text:
The structure is a two-component salt drawn as two separate fragments: morantel and tartaric acid.

**Morantel fragment (bottom):**
- A thiophene ring carries a methyl group on the carbon next to the carbon that bears the vinyl chain.
- A trans (E) CH=CH links the thiophene to C2 of a 1-methyl-1,4,5,6-tetrahydropyrimidine ring.
- That ring has an N-methyl nitrogen, three CH2 groups, and a C=N double bond.
- The trans geometry follows from the drawing: the thiophene and the ring lie on opposite sides of the double bond.
- SMILES: `CN1CCCN=C1/C=C/c1sccc1C`

**Tartaric acid fragment (top):**
- It has two CH(OH) carbons between two COOH groups, and both OH groups are drawn with wedge bonds.
- For the upper stereocentre, the priorities are OH > COOH > CH(OH) > H. The hydrogen points away from the viewer, and OH → COOH → CH(OH) runs clockwise, so it is R.
- For the lower stereocentre, the same priority order runs clockwise, so it is also R.
- This is the (R,R) form, which is L-(+)-tartaric acid.
- SMILES: `O=C(O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(=O)O`. I checked that this string encodes R,R.

SMILES: CN1CCCN=C1/C=C/c1sccc1C.O=C(O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(=O)O

name: Moroxydine
text:
The drawing shows a morpholine ring: O, CH2, CH2, N, CH2, CH2, closed back to O. The ring nitrogen is bonded to a carbon that carries a C=NH group and a single bond to an N. That N is double-bonded to a second carbon bearing two NH2 groups. This is moroxydine.

Written as a SMILES string, starting from the ring oxygen: O1CCN(CC1)C(=N)N=C(N)N.

Check of the connections:
- The ring nitrogen is bonded to C(=N), the imine carbon.
- That carbon is single-bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C(N)N.

SMILES: N=C(N=C(N)N)N1CCOCC1

name: Morphine 6-glucuronide
text:
This is morphine-6-glucuronide: a morphine core carrying a glucuronic acid unit on the C6 oxygen. I assigned the stereochemistry by matching the drawing to the natural morphine skeleton and a β-D-glucuronide. I did not derive each wedge and hash independently, and the SMILES below is from memory of the PubChem entry.

- **Aromatic ring:** a phenol OH sits on the aromatic ring next to the furan-type ether oxygen.
- **Morphinan core:** the ether oxygen bridges to the carbon that carries the hashed H. A CH=CH double bond runs through the cyclohexene ring. The N-methyl nitrogen is bridged to the carbon bearing the hashed H at the bottom, and the atom labelled "C" is the CH2 linking that carbon to the aromatic ring.
- **Glucuronide:** the C6 oxygen is bonded to the anomeric carbon of a pyranose ring. That ring carries three OH groups and a terminal COOH, which makes it glucuronic acid.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4[C@H]1CC5=C2C(=C(C=C5)O)O[C@H]3[C@H](C=C4)O[C@H]6[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O6)C(=O)O)O)O)O

name: Morphine Sulfate
text:
This drawing is morphine sulfate: two identical morphine molecules plus one sulfuric acid, written as three dot-separated components.

- **Morphine core:** a phenanthrene-derived pentacyclic skeleton with a phenol OH on the aromatic ring and an ether oxygen bridge. It has a cyclohexene ring carrying a secondary alcohol (the wedged OH) and an N-methylpiperidine ring.
- **Sulfuric acid:** S with two =O and two OH groups.
- **Stereochemistry:** the five stereocentres are marked by wedges and hashes. I did not derive the @/@@ labels from the drawing. I wrote them from my recall of the standard morphine SMILES, so they are not independently confirmed against the wedges.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4[C@H]1CC5=C2C(=C(C=C5)O)O[C@H]3[C@H](C=C4)O.CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4[C@H]1CC5=C2C(=C(C=C5)O)O[C@H]3[C@H](C=C4)O.OS(=O)(=O)O

name: Morphine
text:
The drawing is morphine: a 3-hydroxy, 6-hydroxy, N-methyl morphinan with a 7,8-double bond and a 4,5-epoxy (ether) bridge. I wrote the SMILES from my recall of the standard morphine string and checked it against the drawing's connectivity. I did not independently derive the @/@@ descriptors from the individual wedges and hashes.

- **Aromatic ring:** a phenol OH on one carbon, with the neighbouring carbon bonded to the ether oxygen.
- **Ether bridge:** the oxygen links the aromatic ring to the carbon that carries a hashed H.
- **Cyclohexene ring:** a wedged OH sits on the carbon next to the C=C.
- **Nitrogen bridge:** an N-methyl group, with the nitrogen joined to a CH2–CH2 chain on the quaternary carbon and to the benzylic CH2 through a CH. Hashed H's mark the ring-fusion carbons.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4[C@H]1CC5=C2C(=C(C=C5)O)O[C@H]3[C@H](C=C4)O

name: Mosapride
text:
This is mosapride, and I read it from the drawing as follows.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with an amide carbonyl, an ethoxy group (OCH2CH3), a chlorine and an NH2. The carbonyl carbon is attached to the ring carbon at about (402, 725). The adjacent ring carbon at (440, 830) carries the OEt. Going around the ring, the next carbons are (372, 920), then (258, 902) carrying NH2, then (218, 796) carrying Cl, then (290, 707), which closes back to the carbonyl-bearing carbon.
- **Amide link:** C(=O)NH–CH2 leads to the morpholine C2.
- **Morpholine:** C2 is bonded to O, to CH2 (C3) and to the exocyclic CH2. C3 connects to N, N connects to C5, C5 to C6, and C6 to O, closing the ring. The ring nitrogen carries a 4-fluorobenzyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows only plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CCOc1cc(N)c(Cl)cc1C(=O)NCC1CN(Cc2ccc(F)cc2)CCO1

name: Mosliciguat
text:
I read the drawing as follows.

- **Core:** a 5,6,7,8-tetrahydroquinoline with a carboxylic acid at C2. C5 carries the tertiary amine nitrogen through a hashed bond.
- **Nitrogen substituents:** besides C5, the nitrogen carries two CH2CH2 arms.
  - One arm ends in a para-carboxyphenyl ring.
  - The other ends in an ortho-disubstituted benzene. Its oxygen is linked through OCH2 to a chlorobiphenyl: the first ring has Cl ortho to the CH2, and the second ring has a para-CF3.
- **Stereochemistry:** only C5 is marked, with the hashed bond to N, so N points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - The CIP priorities are N > C4a (aromatic) > C6 > H.
  - Viewed from the front, N → C4a → C6 runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S.
  - In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at that carbon is N, H, ring-closure to C4a, then C6. This order with `@` corresponds to S.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(CCN(CCc2ccccc2OCc2ccc(cc2Cl)-c2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)[C@H]2CCCc3nc(C(=O)O)ccc32)cc1

name: Mosnodenvir
text:
I read the structure as a 3-acylindole carrying a 5-OCF3 group, with the carbonyl bonded to a single stereocentre.

- **Indole:** The NH indole has the C(=O) group at C3 and OCF3 at C5.
- **Stereocentre:** The CH is bonded to the carbonyl carbon, an NH-aryl group, a chloro-methoxyphenyl ring, and an implicit H. The hashed bond points to the NH.
- **NH-aryl ring:** This benzene ring has the NH, an OMe and a methylsulfonyl group (SO2CH3) in a 1,3,5 pattern.
- **Chloro-methoxyphenyl ring:** The ring is attached to the stereocentre. It carries OMe ortho to that attachment and Cl para to it.

For the stereo, I took the hashed N as pointing away from the viewer, which puts the implicit H toward the viewer. Viewed from the front, N → C(=O) → aryl runs clockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (C=O, H, N, aryl) this gives `@@`.

SMILES: O=C(c1c[nH]c2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc12)[C@@H](Nc1cc(OC)cc(S(C)(=O)=O)c1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1OC

name: Monophosphoryl Lipid A
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing atom by atom, and the stereo flags were worked out from the wedge and hash geometry. The molecule is a lipid A-type disaccharide of two glucosamine-like rings joined by a CH2–O–C1 linkage.

**Left (non-reducing) ring**
- It has a CH2OH on C5 and a phosphate (OP(=O)(O)O) on C4.
- C3 carries an O-acyl group, (R)-3-(tetradecanoyloxy)tetradecanoyl.
- C2 carries an N-acyl group of the same type.
- C1 is the anomeric carbon, linked through O to the CH2 of the right ring.

**Right (reducing) ring**
- Going round from the ring oxygen, the ring carbons carry:
  - OH on C1 (hashed).
  - OH on C2 (hashed).
  - NH-acyl on C3, no stereo drawn.
  - O-acyl on C4 (wedged).
  - The CH2–O link on C5.
- The N-acyl and O-acyl groups are both 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl, each with a hashed OH at C3.

I followed the drawing for the right ring even though it differs from natural lipid A, which has the amine at C2 and a free OH at C4. The wedge at C5 of the right ring is read as starting at the ring carbon and pointing to the CH2. This is the one place where the drawing is ambiguous.

Chain lengths are taken as tetradecanoyl (14 C) for the ester acyl groups and 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl for the rest. These counts come from reading the drawing and assuming standard lipid A chains.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@@H](OC[C@H]2O[C@H](O)[C@H](O)C(NC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@H]2OC(=O)C[C@H](O)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@H](NC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC)CCCCCCCCCCC)[C@H]1OP(=O)(O)O

name: Moxalactam
text:
I read this as latamoxef (moxalactam), an oxacephem β-lactam, and built the SMILES region by region.

- **Left ring:** a 1-methyltetrazole attached through its carbon to S, then CH2, which leads to the ring alkene carbon.
- **Central bicycle:** a six-membered ring containing O, CH2, C(CH2S…)=C(COOH) and N, fused to the four-membered β-lactam ring (N–C=O, a quaternary carbon bearing OMe and NH, and a CH).
- **Right side:** the NH is acylated by C(=O)–CH(COOH)–C6H4–OH (para-hydroxyphenyl). That CH has plain bonds in the drawing, so I gave it no stereo.
- **Stereocentres:** only the two ring-fusion carbons are drawn with wedge/hash bonds.
  - The quaternary carbon has the hashed bond to NH.
  - The CH has the wedged H.
  - I assigned @ to the quaternary carbon and @ to the CH from the drawn geometry, using the neighbour order in the SMILES below.

SMILES: CO[C@]1(NC(=O)C(C(=O)O)c2ccc(O)cc2)[C@H]2OCC(CSc3nnnn3C)=C(C(=O)O)N2C1=O

name: MM 47761
text:
I read this as a vancomycin-type glycopeptide and wrote the SMILES from the drawing. Because the drawing has no wedges or hashes, I included no stereochemistry.

- **Side chain:** an N-methylleucine (CNC(CC(C)C)C(=O)N–) is attached to the β-hydroxy chloro-aryl residue. The chlorinated ring is linked through an aryl ether oxygen to the central ring.
- **Asparagine:** the Asn side chain is CH2C(N)=O.
- **Central ring:** this ring carries the glucose O-link, the O-links to the chloro-aryl ring and to the lower ring, and the ring-to-chain bond. Its other two positions are CH.
- **Left side:** there is a carboxylic-acid-bearing residue with the 3,5-dihydroxyphenyl ring, which is joined by a biaryl bond to a second ring carrying one OH. A para-substituted lower ring is joined to the central ring through an ether oxygen. The adjacent CH carries the O-linked vancosamine sugar, whose ring has a quaternary C(NH2)(CH3) and a CH(OH).
- **Disaccharide:** the glucose carries CH2OH and two OH groups. Its C2 oxygen links to a 6-deoxyhexose with a CH3 and three OH groups.

I checked the ring closures and the atom counts of each ring against the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(CC(C)C)C(=O)NC(C(O)c8cc(Cl)c(O%11)cc8)C(=O)NC(CC(N)=O)C(=O)NC(c6cc%11c(OC%14OC(CO)C(O)C(O)C%14OC%15OC(C)C(O)C(O)C%15O)c(O%12)c6)C(=O)NC3C(=O)NC(C(OC%13CC(C)(N)C(O)C(C)O%13)c9ccc%12cc9)C(=O)NC(C(=O)O)c5cc(O)cc(O)c5-c5c(O)ccc3c5

name: Motexafin lutetium
text:
The drawing shows a lutetium(III) texaphyrin complex (motexafin lutetium type). It has five components: the macrocycle, Lu³⁺, one water, and two acetate anions.

**Macrocycle, read region by region:**
- **Top pyrrole:** a 3-hydroxypropyl group and a methyl group on the β-carbons. Its nitrogen is a plain imine-type N.
- **Left pyrrole:** two ethyl groups on the β-carbons. Its nitrogen carries the negative charge, [N-].
- **Bottom pyrrole:** a methyl group and a 3-hydroxypropyl group on the β-carbons. Its nitrogen is also a plain imine-type N.
- **Benzene unit:** it is joined to the rest of the macrocycle through two C=N bonds. Each of its two remaining ring carbons carries an O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH3 chain (triethylene glycol monomethyl ether).
- **Bridges:** CH= links join the pyrroles to each other and to the imine nitrogens.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so the SMILES has no stereo marks.

**Kekulé form I used:**
- The two benzene double bonds that remain in the ring are the one next to each ether carbon.
- The two benzene carbons attached to the imine nitrogens carry exocyclic C=N bonds instead.

I assembled the SMILES by hand and traced it atom by atom against the drawing, but did not run it through a parser.

SMILES: C1(CCCO)=C(C)C2=CN=C3C=C(OCCOCCOCCOC)C(OCCOCCOCCOC)=CC3=NC=C4C(C)=C(CCCO)C(=N4)C=C5C(CC)=C(CC)C(=CC1=N2)[N-]5.[Lu+3].O.CC(=O)[O-].CC(=O)[O-]

name: Moxifloxacin
text:
This structure is moxifloxacin. I read it region by region:

- **Core:** a 4-quinolone (quinolin-4-one) with a carboxylic acid at C3, a ketone at C4, and an N-cyclopropyl group on the ring nitrogen.
- **Benzo ring substituents:** fluorine at C6, the bicyclic amine at C7, and a methoxy group at C8.
- **Bicyclic amine:** a pyrrolidine fused to a piperidine (octahydropyrrolo[3,4-b]pyridine). The pyrrolidine nitrogen is attached to the aromatic ring. The piperidine NH sits next to one ring-fusion carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the two ring-fusion CH carbons each carry a hashed H, so both are stereocentres. The H on the upper one points up and the H on the lower one points down, both hashed (away from the viewer). Working out the neighbour order for each centre gives `@@` for both in the SMILES below.

SMILES: COc1c(N2C[C@@H]3CCCN[C@@H]3C2)c(F)cc2c1n(C1CC1)cc(C(=O)O)c2=O

name: Mupirocin
text:
This drawing is mupirocin (pseudomonic acid A), and I wrote the SMILES from memory of its known structure rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

The parts I read from the image:
- **Left side chain:** a 3-hydroxybutan-2-yl group attached to an epoxide.
- **Linker:** the epoxide connects through a CH2 to the tetrahydropyran ring.
- **Pyran ring:** a six-membered ring with one ring oxygen and two adjacent hydroxyls.
- **Unsaturated ester:** a CH2–C(CH3)=CH–C(=O)O unit, drawn with E geometry, hangs off the ring.
- **Acid chain:** the ester oxygen is attached to a nine-carbon chain ending in COOH (nonanoic acid).

SMILES: C[C@H]([C@H]1[C@@H](O1)C[C@H]2CO[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]2O)O)C/C(=C/C(=O)OCCCCCCCCC(=O)O)/C)[C@H](C)O

name: Mufemilast
text:
I read the molecule as an apremilast-type structure: a thieno[3,4-c]pyrrole-4,6-dione carrying an acetamido group, with the imide nitrogen attached to a stereogenic carbon.

- **Left heterocycle:** a thiophene fused to a cyclic imide (two C=O around the N). The thiophene carbon next to S carries an NHAc group (NH–C(=O)CH3). The other thiophene carbon next to S is a plain CH.
- **Stereocentre:** it bears the imide N, a CH2–S(=O)(=O)CH3 group drawn on a hashed bond, the aryl ring and an implicit H. By CIP priority, N > CH2SO2 > aryl > H. With the CH2 pointing back, the H points toward the viewer, so the apparent clockwise sequence N → CH2 → aryl reverses to counterclockwise. This gives (S), which matches apremilast.
- **Aryl ring:** the attachment carbon, then a CH, then C–OEt, then C–OMe, then two CH. This is a 3-ethoxy-4-methoxyphenyl ring.
- **SMILES stereo tag:** in `[C@@H]` the neighbours are written in the order aryl, H, CH2, N. I checked that `@@` corresponds to (S) for this ordering.

SMILES: CCOc1cc([C@@H](CS(C)(=O)=O)N2C(=O)c3csc(NC(C)=O)c3C2=O)ccc1OC

name: Muraglitazar
text:
This is a glycine N-substituted with a carbamate and a benzyl group (the muraglitazar structure).

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Top left: a methoxy group (CH3–O) on a para-substituted benzene ring. The ring's other para position carries O–C(=O), so this is a 4-methoxyphenyl ester of a carbamate.
- Carbamate: the C(=O) is bonded to N, and N carries both a CH2COOH group and a CH2 attached to a second para-substituted benzene ring.
- Second benzene ring: its para position carries an O–CH2CH2 chain leading to an oxazole.
- Oxazole: C4 bears the CH2CH2 chain and is bonded to N3. C5 bears the methyl and is bonded to O1. C2 bears the phenyl group and lies between N3 and O1.
- Far right: an unsubstituted phenyl ring on oxazole C2.

SMILES: COc1ccc(OC(=O)N(CC(=O)O)Cc2ccc(OCCc3nc(-c4ccccc4)oc3C)cc2)cc1

name: Murabutide
text:
This is the open-chain form of muramyl dipeptide (MDP) as its butyl ester: an N-acetylmuramic acid aldehyde, linked through its lactyl ether to L-Ala, then D-isoglutamine with a butyl ester.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Butyl ester:** the four-carbon chain at the top right is bonded to O, then to C(=O) (`CCCCOC(=O)`).
- **Isoglutamine unit:** the α-carbon carries a bold wedge to the CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain and an NH to the alanine. Reading the wedge gives the D configuration.
- **Alanine unit:** the methyl is on a hashed bond, which gives L-Ala.
- **Lactyl ether:** the lactyl carbon has a wedged methyl and is bonded to the sugar O.
- **Sugar chain:** it runs CHO, then C(NHAc), then C(O-lactyl), then CH(OH), then CH(OH), then CH2OH. The NHAc and the lower OH are hashed, while the O-lactyl and the upper OH are wedged.

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge/hash geometry and the order the neighbours appear in the SMILES.

SMILES: CCCCOC(=O)[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](C)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)O[C@H]([C@H](C=O)NC(C)=O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Mycophenolate Mofetil
text:
This structure is mycophenolate mofetil, so I read it region by region and then checked the alkene geometry.

**Aromatic core:** The benzene ring carries these substituents:
- OH on the upper-left carbon.
- The side chain on the upper-right carbon.
- OMe on the right carbon.
- Methyl on the lower-right carbon.
- The fused lactone on the lower-left and left carbons.

**Lactone:** The ring carbon next to the OH-bearing carbon is attached to C(=O), which connects to O and then CH2, and that CH2 joins the ring carbon next to the methyl-bearing carbon.

**Side chain:** From the ring, the chain runs CH2–CH=C(CH3)–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–O–CH2CH2–N(morpholine).

**Alkene geometry:** In the drawing, the ring-side CH2 at (480,658) attaches to the alkene carbon at (585,662). The methyl at (593,482) and the CH2 at (745,577) attach to the other alkene carbon at (640,573).

The double bond runs from (585,662) to (640,573). The CH2 substituent on the lower carbon sits to the left of the bond. On the upper carbon, the methyl points up-left and the CH2 points right.

Taking the bond direction as lower-left to upper-right, the ring CH2 is on the left side of the lower carbon, which is the upper-left side relative to the bond. The methyl on the upper carbon is also on the upper-left side. These two are therefore on the same side, so the chain CH2 (the higher-priority group on that carbon) is on the opposite side to the ring CH2, giving E. This matches mycophenolate, which is E.

SMILES, written with E geometry: `C(/C=C(\C)CCC(=O)OCCN1CCOCC1)` attached to the ring carbon, giving the full string below.

Checking the geometry in this string: the ring-attached CH2 is written before `/C=`, so it is "below" the first alkene carbon. In `\C`, the methyl is "below" the second alkene carbon, so the methyl and the CH2 are on opposite sides... To work this out, `/C=C(\C)CC` with the preceding atom X written as X/C=C(\C)CC places X and the methyl on opposite sides of the double bond. X is therefore trans to the methyl and cis to the chain CH2. The ring CH2 and the chain CH2 would then be cis, which is Z. I need E, so I use `/C=C(/C)CC` instead, which puts X and the methyl cis and the chain CH2 trans to X.

SMILES: COc1c(C)c2COC(=O)c2c(O)c1C/C=C(/C)CCC(=O)OCCN1CCOCC1

name: Muramyl Dipeptide

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge or hash and the 2D positions of its neighbours, with the implicit H taken as the opposite side from the drawn wedge or hash. I did not independently re-check the resulting @/@@ marks, for example against a known MDP SMILES.

text:

The SMILES encodes this with `C/C=C(\C)CCC(=O)O`, where the first CH2 and the methyl are both "below" the double bond.

text:

- Ring B is the other spiro tetrahydropyran. Its atoms run: spiro carbon, CH2, CH–O (the lactone oxygen), CH2, CH, ring O.
- The macrocycle runs from the lactone C(=O)O through ring B to a CH2–CH=C(CH3)–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH=CH–CH=C diene unit.
- That diene ends on a carbon in the fused dihydrofuran. The furan ring is C=C–CH2–O–CH–C(quaternary, OH).
- The cyclohexene ring carries a C(CH3)=CH, a CH(OH) and the CH bearing the lactone carbonyl.

**Stereochemistry and double-bond geometry**
- Each stereocentre was assigned from its wedge or hash bond, including the implicit H where the drawing shows one.
- The oxime OMe is cis to the ring CH2 and trans to the CH(CH3).
- In the side chain, the ring CH and the isopropyl group are trans.
- The ring-bound CH2 is cis to the methyl on the trisubstituted macrocycle alkene.
- The CH=CH in the diene is trans.
- The last diene C=C is cis to the furan CH2 and trans to the quaternary carbon.

I checked that the ring closures, atom counts and bond orders match the drawing.

text:

The only stereocentre is the α‑carbon, and the wedge bond runs from it to the CH2SH group. The hydrogen is therefore pointing away from the viewer. In the drawing, N sits at the upper right, CH2SH at the bottom and COOH at the upper left, so tracing N → CH2SH → COOH goes clockwise. name: N-Acetylcysteine amide
text:
Reading the drawing from right to left:

- The methyl carbon on the right is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), which is bonded to an NH. This is an N-acetyl group.
- The NH is bonded to the central stereocentre carbon.
- The stereocentre carries a CH2–SH group on a wedge bond (pointing toward the viewer), so the implicit H points away.
- The stereocentre's remaining substituent is a carbonyl carbon (C=O) bearing an NH2, which is a primary amide.

The molecule is N-acetylcysteinamide.

**Stereochemistry:** The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CH2SH > C(=O)NH2 > H. The CH2SH group outranks the amide carbon because S beats O at the first point of difference. With H pointing away, the sequence N (upper right), CH2SH (bottom), C(=O)NH2 (upper left) runs clockwise, so the centre is R (the L-cysteine configuration).

For the SMILES `CC(=O)N[C@@H](CS)C(N)=O`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is N, H, CH2S, C(=O). The `@@` tag means H → CH2S → C(=O) runs clockwise when viewed from N. Moving H to the front is one swap, giving `@`, which corresponds to R. This matches the drawing.

name: Nabumetone
text:

Continuing from C4a, C5 is (1092,819), C6 is (1173,675) with OMe, C7 is (1088,532), and C8 is (922,533). The substituents are therefore at C2 and C6.

**SMILES:** CC(=O)CCc1ccc2cc(OC)ccc2c1

name: Nabilone
