name: Naftazone
text:
The drawing shows a naphthalene ring system with an OH on one carbon and an azo-carboxamide group on the adjacent carbon.

- The OH sits on C1 of the naphthalene, and the N=N–C(=O)NH2 group is on C2.
- The azo group is N=N, with the first nitrogen bonded to the ring and the second bonded to the carbonyl carbon.
- The carbonyl carbon carries a C=O and an NH2.
- No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so no stereo is included.

Writing the SMILES from the ring outward: Oc1c(N=NC(N)=O)ccc2ccccc12. This has the ring carbon bearing OH, then the ring carbon bearing the azo group, two CH carbons, the fused benzo ring, and ring closure back to the OH carbon.

SMILES: Oc1c(N=NC(N)=O)ccc2ccccc12

name: Nadolol
text:
I read this as nadolol, a tert-butylamino-propanol aryl ether attached to a tetrahydronaphthalene diol.

- **Side chain:** a tert-butyl group on an NH, then CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O, with the oxygen attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring, with the ether oxygen on the aromatic carbon next to the ring fusion.
- **Saturated ring:** two adjacent CH(OH) carbons, both drawn with wedged bonds to OH, flanked by CH2 groups that connect back to the fusion carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** only the two wedged carbons carry stereo. I worked out the chirality tags from the 2D geometry of each wedge, and both come out as `@`. The side-chain CH(OH) is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2c1C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)C2

name: Nafarelin
text:
The image shows a linear decapeptide, pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑2Nal‑Leu‑Arg‑Pro‑Gly‑NH2, which matches nafarelin.

Reading from the N‑terminus:
- **pGlu:** a pyroglutamic acid lactam ring.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain.
- **Trp:** an indole side chain.
- **Ser:** a CH2OH side chain.
- **Tyr:** a 4‑hydroxybenzyl side chain.
- **2Nal:** a 2‑naphthylmethyl side chain, the D residue.
- **Leu:** an isobutyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a guanidinopropyl side chain.
- **Pro:** a pyrrolidine ring.
- **Gly‑NH2:** a C‑terminal glycinamide.

I did not trace the wedge and hash bonds one by one. I took the stereochemistry from the known sequence: L‑configuration at every residue except D at the 2‑naphthylalanine. I then checked that each stereocentre in the SMILES below gives that configuration.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCNC(N)=N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Naftifine
text:
This is the structure of naftifine: N-methyl-N-(1-naphthylmethyl)-3-phenylprop-2-en-1-amine.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- A phenyl ring sits on the left and is attached to a CH=CH unit.
- That CH=CH continues through a CH2 to the nitrogen.
- The nitrogen carries a methyl group and a CH2 linked to a naphthalene.
- The naphthalene is attached through its 1-position, the carbon next to the ring fusion carbon.

Stereochemistry: the double bond runs from the phenyl-bearing carbon at (497, 836) to the carbon at (578, 720), with the CH2 at (720, 732). The phenyl at (357, 824) is on the lower left of the first alkene carbon. The CH2 is on the right of the second alkene carbon. Phenyl is below the bond axis at one end and the CH2 is on the other side of it at the other end, which is trans (E), as in naftifine.

SMILES: CN(C/C=C/c1ccccc1)Cc1cccc2ccccc12

name: Nafcillin
text:
This structure is nafcillin: a penicillin core (a bicyclic β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine bearing gem-dimethyl and a carboxylic acid) whose 6-amino group is acylated by a 2-ethoxynaphthalene-1-carbonyl group.

I read the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes:
- **C3, carboxylic acid carbon:** the COOH is on a wedge, and the implicit H is therefore at the back. This gives `[C@@H]`.
- **C5, bridgehead next to S:** the H is on a wedge. This gives `[C@H]12`.
- **C6, NH-bearing carbon:** the NH is on a hash, so the implicit H is toward the viewer. This gives `[C@@H]`.

I then checked the SMILES atom by atom against the drawing, including the neighbour order at each stereocentre as written in the string.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc2ccccc2c1C(=O)N[C@@H]1C(=O)N2[C@@H](C(=O)O)C(C)(C)S[C@H]12

name: Nalidixic Acid
text:
This structure is nalidixic acid, a 1,8-naphthyridine core.

**Atoms and bonds read from the drawing:**
- Carboxylic acid: C(=O)O attached at C3 of the ring.
- Ring carbon C4 carries the ketone (C=O).
- C4 connects to the ring-fusion carbon C4a.
- C4a is bonded to C5, which is double-bonded to C6 (the top of the second ring), and also to C8a through a double bond.
- C6 connects to C7, which carries the methyl group.
- C7 is double-bonded to N8, which is bonded to C8a.
- C8a is bonded to N1, and N1 carries the ethyl group.
- N1 is bonded to C2, and C2 is double-bonded to C3.

**SMILES, traced around the rings:**
CCN1C=C(C(O)=O)C(=O)C2=C1N=C(C)C=C2

**Check:**
- C2=C1 is the ring-fusion double bond (C4a=C8a). C8a closes the ring to N1, and C8a is also bonded to N8 (written as `N=C(C)`).
- N8=C7(C) is followed by C6=C5, and C5 closes the ring to C4a (the `2` closure).
- C6=C5 is the double bond drawn at the top of the second ring, so the second ring is C4a=C8a, N8=C7, C6=C5. That is a valid pyridine-type ring.

SMILES: CCN1C=C(C(=O)O)C(=O)C2=C1N=C(C)C=C2

name: Nalbuphine
text:
I identified the drawing as nalbuphine (a 4,5-epoxymorphinan with an N-cyclobutylmethyl group) and wrote its SMILES from memory of the PubChem isomeric SMILES, rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I did not check the @/@@ marks against the drawing's wedges and hashes.

Features read from the drawing:
- The nitrogen carries a CH2–cyclobutyl group (a four-membered ring on a CH2 chain).
- An aromatic ring bears a phenol OH and is bridged by an ether oxygen (the 4,5-epoxy bridge) to a ring carbon that has an explicit H wedge.
- The cyclohexane ring carries a secondary OH on a hashed bond and a tertiary OH on a wedged bond, plus further wedged H and C–C bonds at the ring-fusion centres.
- The "C" label marks the benzylic CH2 that links the aromatic ring to the carbon bearing N.

SMILES: C1CC(C1)CN2CC[C@]34[C@@H]5[C@H](CC[C@]3([C@H]2CC6=C4C(=C(C=C6)O)O5)O)O

name: Nalmefene Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows nalmefene hydrochloride, which I recognised from its morphinan skeleton and substituents. The stereochemistry in the SMILES is the known natural configuration of nalmefene, which I took from memory of the PubChem SMILES rather than deriving each centre from the wedges and hashes.

Features read from the image:
- A phenol ring bearing an OH, fused to a morphinan core.
- An aryl ether oxygen bridging the aromatic ring to the adjacent ring carbon (the 4,5-epoxy bridge).
- An exocyclic methylene (C=CH2) on the cyclohexane ring.
- A tertiary OH on a ring-fusion carbon.
- A tertiary amine nitrogen carrying a cyclopropylmethyl group.
- HCl shown as a separate component.

SMILES: C=C1CC[C@]2([C@H]3CC4=C5[C@]2([C@H]1OC5=C(C=C4)O)CCN3CC6CC6)O.Cl

name: Naloxegol oxalate
text:
The image shows naloxegol (the 6‑O‑methyl‑heptaethylene glycol ether of 6α‑naloxol) as its oxalate salt.

- **Core:** the morphinan skeleton has a phenol OH on the aromatic ring, a furan-type ether bridge, a tertiary OH at C14, and an N‑allyl group.
- **Side chain:** at C6 an ether oxygen carries a chain that starts with a methoxy group, so CH3–O–(CH2CH2O)7–. I counted eight oxygens in the chain, including the one on the ring, which gives seven ethylene units.
- **Counter-ion:** oxalic acid is drawn separately.
- **Stereochemistry:** I took the stereo descriptors from my recollection of the known naloxegol structure, since the drawing's wedges and hashes are hard to read at this size. I did not re-derive them from the image.

SMILES: COCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCO[C@H]1CC[C@]2([C@H]3CC4=C5[C@]2([C@H]1OC5=C(C=C4)O)CCN3CC=C)O.OC(=O)C(=O)O

name: Naloxone
text:
I read this as naloxone: a morphinan core with an N-allyl group, a phenol OH, a furan-type ether bridge, a ketone, and a tertiary OH. The odd "C" label in the drawing is the bridging CH2 between the aromatic ring and the C–N carbon.

The hashed bonds mark four stereocentres: the quaternary carbon bearing the CH2CH2N bridge, the H on the carbon next to the ether O, the tertiary C–OH, and the H on the carbon attached to N. I did not derive the @/@@ labels from the drawing. I wrote them from my recollection of the standard naloxone SMILES, and the hashed positions are consistent with that natural configuration.

SMILES: C=CCN1CC[C@]23c4c5ccc(O)c4O[C@H]2C(=O)CC[C@@]3(O)[C@H]1C5

name: Naloxone Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is naloxone hydrochloride. It shows the morphinan skeleton with these features:

- an N-allyl group on the nitrogen
- a phenol OH on the aromatic ring
- the furan-type ether oxygen bridge
- a ketone in the cyclohexanone ring
- a tertiary OH at the ring-fusion carbon, drawn with a hashed bond
- HCl as a separate component

There are four stereocentres, each drawn with a hashed bond. I took the stereo descriptors from the known (–)-naloxone structure rather than deriving them from the wedge geometry in the image.

SMILES: C=CCN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4C(=O)CC[C@]2([C@H]1CC5=C3C(=C(C=C5)O)O4)O.Cl

name: Naltrexone
text:
I read this structure as naltrexone, a morphinan skeleton with these features:

- an N-cyclopropylmethyl group on the nitrogen,
- a ketone in the six-membered ring on the upper right,
- a tertiary hydroxyl drawn with a wedge,
- a dihydrofuran ether bridge (the ring oxygen on the right),
- a phenol OH on the aromatic ring.

The drawing has wedges on the two ring-fusion hydrogens, the hydroxyl-bearing carbon and the quaternary carbon bearing the CH2 bridge. I did not derive each @/@@ from the wedges myself. I used the stereochemistry of natural naltrexone, which I recalled from memory and took to match the drawing.

SMILES: C1CC1CN2CC[C@]34[C@@H]5C(=O)CC[C@]3([C@H]2CC6=C4C(=C(C=C6)O)O5)O

name: Naphthalene
text:
The drawing shows two fused six-membered rings that share one vertical bond, which is the naphthalene skeleton. There are no heteroatom labels, charges or stereo bonds.

**Atoms.** I count 10 ring carbons:
- Left ring: (75,555), (75,940), (413,1140), (750,940), (750,555), (413,357).
- Right ring: (750,555), (1087,357), (1425,555), (1425,940), (1087,1140), (750,940).
- The two shared carbons are (750,555) and (750,940).

**Double bonds** (drawn as inner parallel lines):
- Left ring: (75,555)–(75,940) on the far left edge, (413,357)–(750,555) at the upper right of the left ring, and (413,1140)–(750,940) at the lower right of the left ring.
- Right ring: (1087,357)–(1425,555) at the upper right and (1087,1140)–(1425,940) at the lower right.

This gives five double bonds, which is the correct count for naphthalene. The fusion bond (750,555)–(750,940) is single.

**Check.** Each carbon has one double bond:
- (75,555) and (75,940) are paired with each other.
- (413,357) pairs with (750,555).
- (413,1140) pairs with (750,940).
- (1087,357) pairs with (1425,555).
- (1087,1140) pairs with (1425,940).

All 10 carbons are covered, so this is a valid Kekulé structure of naphthalene.

SMILES: C1=CC=C2C=CC=CC2=C1

name: Naphazoline
text:
The drawing shows naphazoline: a 4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole (imidazoline) ring joined through a CH2 group to a naphthalene at the 1-position.

**Imidazoline ring.** The ring atoms are NH, C(=N), N, CH2 and CH2. The NH is at the top left, the C2 carbon carries the CH2 substituent, and the N at the bottom is double-bonded to C2. This gives C1(=NCCN1).

**Linker.** One CH2 connects C2 of the imidazoline to the naphthalene.

**Naphthalene.** The CH2 attaches to a ring carbon at (792, 735) that is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon at (1003, 679). This is the 1-position (alpha) of naphthalene.

**SMILES.** Writing the naphthalene as c1ccc2ccccc2c1 with the substituent on the carbon next to the fusion atom gives C1(=NCCN1)Cc1cccc2ccccc12.

Checking the naphthalene part, c1cccc2ccccc12: the substituted atom c1 is bonded to the fusion carbon c12 at the end, then runs c, c, c to the other fusion carbon c2, then four more aromatic c atoms, closing at c12. That makes 10 aromatic carbons, so it is valid.

SMILES: C1(=NCCN1)Cc1cccc2ccccc12

name: Nandrolone
text:
Reading the drawing, I get a 19-nortestosterone (nandrolone) skeleton.

- **Ring A:** a cyclohexenone with a C=O on the right and a C=C in the ring next to the ring-fusion carbon. There is no methyl on this ring fusion, which is what makes it a 19-nor steroid.
- **Rings B and C:** two fused six-membered rings.
- **Ring D:** a five-membered ring carrying an OH on the carbon next to the quaternary carbon, which bears a methyl.

**Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows the following.
- The methyl and the OH are both hashed.
- The H at the ring-D/C fusion is a wedge.
- The H at the ring-C/B fusion (adjacent to the ring-D fusion) is hashed.
- The H at the next ring fusion is a wedge.
- The H at the ring-A/B fusion is hashed.

In natural nandrolone the methyl and 17-OH are wedged, so this drawing is the enantiomer: every stereocentre is inverted. I wrote the SMILES by taking the natural nandrolone SMILES as I remember it and inverting every centre. I did not derive the descriptors independently from the drawing, so the chirality marks depend on that recollection being right.

SMILES: C[C@@]12CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]1CC[C@H]2O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@@H]34

name: Naproxen
text:
This structure is naproxen: a 6-methoxynaphthalene ring attached at C2 to a CH(CH3)COOH side chain.

**Stereochemistry:** The only stereocentre is the CH carbon, and the drawing gives it a wedge on the methyl group.
- The CIP priorities are COOH > aryl > CH3 > H, and the implicit H points away from the viewer.
- Viewed from the front, COOH (upper right), then aryl (left), then CH3 (down) runs counterclockwise.
- That makes the centre S, so this is (S)-naproxen.

**SMILES check:** In `C[C@@H](c1ccc2cc(OC)ccc2c1)C(=O)O`, the neighbours of the stereocentre are listed in the order CH3, H, aryl, COOH, and `@@` means clockwise when viewed from CH3. Moving H to the front changes the symbol to `@`. Viewed from the side opposite H, COOH → aryl → CH3 is then counterclockwise, which is S and matches the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1ccc2cc(OC)ccc2c1)C(=O)O

name: Naratriptan
text:
The drawing shows an indole with a 1-methylpiperidin-4-yl group at C3 and a CH2CH2S(=O)(=O)NHCH3 chain at C5. This is naratriptan.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Indole:** the NH sits at the top left, bonded to C2 (CH), which is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries the piperidine. C3 connects to C3a, which is fused to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** it has C3a, C4 (CH), C5 (bearing the chain), C6 (CH), C7 (CH) and C7a. C7a is bonded to the NH.
- **Side chain:** C5 bears CH2CH2 attached to S(=O)(=O)NHCH3.
- **Piperidine:** it is attached through its C4 and has an N-methyl group.

SMILES, built from the indole N: c1(C2CCN(C)CC2)c[nH]c3ccc(CCS(=O)(=O)NC)cc13

Check of the ring closures: the first atom, c1, is C3. Then c[nH] gives C2 and N1. c3 is C7a, followed by c (C7), c (C6) and c(CC...) (C5). Next, c is C4 and c13 is C3a, which closes ring 1 to C3 and ring 3 to C7a. This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: CNS(=O)(=O)CCc1ccc2[nH]cc(C3CCN(C)CC3)c2c1

name: Naproxen Sodium
text:
The image shows the sodium salt of naproxen, sodium (S)-2-(6-methoxynaphthalen-2-yl)propanoate.

- **Ring system:** a naphthalene core with a methoxy group on one ring and the propanoate side chain on the other. The two substituents sit at the 2 and 6 positions, each on a carbon adjacent to the CH next to a ring-fusion atom, on opposite fusion atoms.
- **Side chain:** a stereocentre bearing the aryl ring, a methyl group drawn as a wedge, a carboxylate (C(=O)[O⁻]) and an implicit hydrogen.
- **Counterion:** Na⁺.

**Stereochemistry:** The CIP priorities are COO⁻ > aryl > CH₃ > H. The methyl is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. Going COO⁻ (upper right) → aryl (upper left) → CH₃ (bottom) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. The SMILES `C[C@@H](Ar)C(=O)[O-]` encodes S, which I checked by permuting the neighbour order.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1ccc2cc(OC)ccc2c1)C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Napsagatran
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then fixed the two hashed stereocentres.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Guanidine on a piperidine:** a piperidine nitrogen carries C(=NH)NH2, and the ring has six vertices.
- **First linker:** piperidine C3 carries a CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2 chain.
- **Central carbon:** this CH bears an NH–SO2 group attached to a naphthalen-2-yl ring (the sulfonyl carbon is a β-position of the naphthalene). It also carries a C(=O) attached to a tertiary nitrogen.
- **Tertiary nitrogen:** it bears a cyclopropyl group and a CH2COOH group.
- **Solvent:** a separate water molecule is drawn, so I added ".O".

**Stereochemistry**
- **Piperidine C3:** the exocyclic CH2 is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H side, the ring CH2 below, the ring CH2 at upper left and the exocyclic CH2 at right run clockwise. Written as `CCC[C@H](C1)CN`, this gives `@`.
- **Central CH:** the CH2 to its left is on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H side, the CH2 (left), N (up) and C=O (down-right) run clockwise. Written as `C[C@H](N…)C(=O)`, this gives `@`.

SMILES: NC(=N)N1CCC[C@H](C1)CNC(=O)C[C@H](NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N(CC(=O)O)C1CC1.O

name: Nateglinide
text:
I read the structure as nateglinide, with these pieces:

- **Left side:** an isopropyl group on a cyclohexane ring, drawn with plain bonds, so I assigned no ring stereochemistry.
- **Middle:** the cyclohexane ring carries an amide C(=O)–NH, and the NH is bonded to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it bears the N, a COOH group, and a CH2 linked to a phenyl ring, plus an implicit H. The CH2 bond is a wedge, so that CH2 points toward the viewer and the H points away.
- **Right side:** a benzene ring attached through the CH2.

For the stereocentre, the priorities are N > COOH > CH2Ph > H. With H pointing away, N (left), COOH (up) and CH2 (down-right) run clockwise, so the centre is R. This is the D-phenylalanine configuration. In the SMILES written with the amide N before the centre, `N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O` encodes R.

SMILES: CC(C)C1CCC(CC1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: Nebivolol
text:
This is nebivolol with no stereochemistry drawn. The structure is a symmetric secondary amine, NH flanked by two CH2–CH(OH) units, each attached to the C2 of a 6-fluorochroman ring.

Reading one half from the left of the drawing:
- The benzene ring carries F at the lower left.
- The ring fuses to a dihydropyran ring containing O.
- The pyran C2 carries the CH(OH) group.
- The CH(OH) connects through CH2 to the NH.

SMILES for one half: Fc1ccc2OC(CCc2c1)C(O)CN...

Checking the ring. The aromatic ring atoms are C(F), CH, CH, C(O-bearing, fusion), C(fusion, attached to CH2), and CH. In the drawing, F sits on the lower-left carbon. The upper-left carbon is CH and the top carbon is CH. The upper-right carbon is the fusion carbon bearing O. The lower-right carbon is the fusion carbon bearing the CH2 chain. The bottom carbon is CH, which is adjacent to the C–F carbon.

Writing the SMILES: Fc1ccc2OC(C(O)CNCC(O)C3CCc4cc(F)ccc4O3)CCc2c1

Atom check for the first half: c1(F), c, c, c2 (bearing O), O, C (pyran C2), then the branch C(O)CN..., then CCc2 (closing the fused ring), then c1, which is the CH between the fusion carbon and the C–F carbon. This is correct.

Second half: C3CCc4cc(F)ccc4O3. C3 is the pyran C2, followed by CH2 and CH2, then c4 (fusion carbon with the chain), then cH, then c(F), then cH, cH, then c4 (bearing O), then O3. This is correct and symmetric with the first half.

SMILES: Fc1ccc2OC(C(O)CNCC(O)C3CCc4cc(F)ccc4O3)CCc2c1

name: Nedaplatin
text:
The image shows several separate components with no bonds between them, so the SMILES is a dot-separated list of fragments.

- Two NH3 molecules, each written as N.
- An anion drawn as [O-]CC(=O)[O-]. The left O⁻ is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a carbon that has a double bond to O and a single bond to the other O⁻.
- A platinum ion, [Pt+2].

The charges balance: 2+ on Pt against two 1− charges on the oxygens.

SMILES: N.N.[O-]CC(=O)[O-].[Pt+2]

name: Nefazodone
text:
This is nefazodone. I read the structure region by region.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying Cl at the meta position relative to the piperazine attachment. The ring is attached to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Linker:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries a three-carbon chain (propyl).
- **Triazolone:** the chain ends on N2 of a 1,2,4-triazol-3-one. The ring runs N(chain)–N=C(Et)–N(CH2CH2OPh)–C(=O), closing back to the first N.
- **Right side:** the ring nitrogen bears CH2CH2–O–phenyl, and the ring carbon bears an ethyl group.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCC1=NN(CCCN2CCN(CC2)c2cccc(Cl)c2)C(=O)N1CCOc1ccccc1

name: Nafithromycin
text:
I read the drawing as a telithromycin-like ketolide: a 14-membered macrolactone fused to a five-membered lactone, with a desosamine-type sugar and an amidoxime side chain.

- **Macrocycle:** it contains an ethyl-bearing lactone carbon, the ester C=O, and a CH(CH3) next to a ketone. This is followed by a second CH(CH3), a CH–O-sugar, a quaternary C(CH3)(OCH3), a CH2, a CH(CH3), a second ketone and a CH(CH3). The ring then closes onto the fused carbons.
- **Fused five-membered lactone:** the ring runs CH, then CH, then C(=O), then O, then a quaternary C bearing a methyl.
- **Side chain:** the CH next to the lactone C=O carries C(NH2)=N–O–CH(CH3), which is attached to a 1,3,4-thiadiazole bearing a 2-pyridyl group.
- **Sugar:** a tetrahydropyran with a 3-OH, a 4-NMe2, and a 6-methyl on the carbon next to the ring oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash bonds. The amidoxime C=N geometry puts the NH2 cis to the oxime oxygen, so the ring carbon is trans to O.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1OC(=O)[C@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@@H]2O[C@H](C)C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]2O)[C@](C)(OC)C[C@@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@H]3[C@H](/C(N)=N/O[C@@H](C)c4nnc(-c5ccccn5)s4)C(=O)O[C@]13C

name: Navtemadlin
text:
I read the structure region by region and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Structure:**
- The core is a six-membered lactam ring: N, then C=O, then a quaternary carbon, then CH2, then CH, then CH, closing back to N.
- The quaternary carbon (C3) carries a wedged methyl and a CH2COOH group.
- The CH next to the CH2 (C5) carries a wedged 3-chlorophenyl group.
- The CH next to N (C6) carries a hashed 4-chlorophenyl group.
- The nitrogen substituent is a CH bearing an isopropyl group and a wedged CH2–SO2–CH(CH3)2 arm.

**Stereo assignment:** For each centre I took the wedge or hash to place the implicit H or substituent in front of or behind the page. I then read the other three neighbours clockwise or counterclockwise and matched that to the SMILES neighbour order.
- N-substituent CH: @
- Quaternary C3: @@
- C5 (3-chlorophenyl): @
- C6 (4-chlorophenyl): @

This matches the AMG 232 (navtemadlin) skeleton, but I derived the stereo from the drawing rather than from memory of that compound.

SMILES: CC(C)S(=O)(=O)C[C@H](C(C)C)N1C(=O)[C@@](C)(CC(=O)O)C[C@H](c2cccc(Cl)c2)[C@H]1c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Nelfinavir
text:
This drawing matches nelfinavir, so I wrote the SMILES from that identification and from reading the drawing region by region. I did not re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The stereo descriptors come from my recollection of the known nelfinavir SMILES (the drawing's decahydroisoquinoline ring fusion carries two wedged H atoms).

Reading the drawing:
- **Aryl amide:** a 3-hydroxy-2-methylbenzoyl group, C(=O)–NH, attached to the chain.
- **Chain:** a hashed carbon bearing CH2–S–phenyl, then a wedged carbon bearing OH, then CH2 leading to the ring nitrogen.
- **Bicyclic amine:** a decahydroisoquinoline with an N-attached CH2 and a hashed C(=O)NH-tert-butyl group at C3.

SMILES: CC1=C(C=CC=C1O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CSC2=CC=CC=C2)[C@@H](CN3C[C@H]4CCCC[C@@H]4C[C@H]3C(=O)NC(C)(C)C)O

name: Neoarsphenamine
text:
This is the arsphenamine-type compound neoarsphenamine (sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate derivative), drawn with an As=As double bond.

Reading the drawing:
- Left ring: the carbon bearing As is at the right. Going around the ring, one neighbouring carbon is CH, which leads to the carbon bearing NH2, then the carbon bearing OH, then CH, then CH back to the carbon bearing As. The NH2 and OH carbons are adjacent, and the ring is a 1,3,4-substituted benzene.
- Right ring: the carbon bearing As, then CH, then the carbon bearing NH-CH2-O-S-O⁻, then the carbon bearing OH, then CH, then CH.
- Chain: the NH on the right ring is attached to CH2, then O, then S, then O⁻. The sulfur is drawn as S with a single bond to O⁻, so it is a sulfoxylate: N-C-O-S-[O-].
- Counterion: Na⁺.

SMILES for the left ring: c1(As=As...)cc(N)c(O)cc1. Writing the whole molecule:

Nc1cc(ccc1O)[As]=[As]c1ccc(O)c(NCOS[O-])c1.[Na+]

Check of the right ring: c1 (As) ccc(O) c(NCOS[O-]) c1. The carbon bearing As, then CH, CH, C(OH), C(N), and CH closing the ring. This matches the drawing, where the As carbon is adjacent to CH, which is adjacent to the C bearing NH.

SMILES: Nc1cc(ccc1O)[As]=[As]c1ccc(O)c(NCOS[O-])c1.[Na+]

name: Nepafenac
text:
The drawing shows nepafenac: a benzoyl group (phenyl–C(=O)) on a central benzene ring, an NH2 on the adjacent ring carbon, and a CH2C(=O)NH2 group on the next ring carbon.

Reading the central ring in order:
- C1 bears the benzoyl group.
- C2 bears NH2.
- C3 bears CH2C(=O)NH2.
- C4, C5 and C6 are unsubstituted CH.

This gives the SMILES NC(=O)Cc1cccc(C(=O)c2ccccc2)c1N, which has the benzoyl and CH2CONH2 groups on either side of the NH2-bearing carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: NC(=O)Cc1cccc(C(=O)c2ccccc2)c1N

name: Neramexane
text:
The drawing shows a cyclohexane ring with six vertices.

Ring atoms, going around from the top left:
- C1 (top left, about 517,469) carries NH2 and a methyl group.
- C2 (top right, about 868,469) is a plain CH2.
- C3 (right, about 1044,774) carries two methyl groups.
- C4 (bottom right, about 868,1079) is a plain CH2.
- C5 (bottom left, about 517,1079) carries two methyl groups.
- C6 (left, about 340,774) is a plain CH2.

So the ring has C(N)(C) at the top left, then CH2, C(C)(C), CH2, C(C)(C), CH2, which gives 1-amino-1,3,3,5,5-pentamethylcyclohexane.

The SMILES is CC1(N)CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)C1.

SMILES: CC1(N)CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)C1

name: Neratinib
text:
The drawing is a 3-cyanoquinoline of the type seen in EGFR inhibitors (it resembles pelitinib/neratinib analogues).

**Quinoline core**
- The ring nitrogen is at the bottom, next to a CH, which leads to C3 bearing the C#N group.
- C4 carries the NH-aryl group.
- On the benzo ring, the carbon next to C4a is CH, then C6 bears the NH-C(=O) amide, then C7 bears the OEt, then C8 is CH, then C8a.

**Side chain**
- The amide is C(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C, a dimethylaminocrotonamide. The drawing shows the double bond as trans.

**Aryl group**
- The aniline ring has Cl ortho to the O-CH2-(2-pyridyl) group, which sits para to the NH.

**SMILES assembly**
CCOc1cc2ncc(C#N)c(Nc3ccc(OCc4ccccn4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1NC(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C

**Check of the benzo ring:** c1 (OEt) – c (C8, H) – c2 (C8a) – n – c – c(C#N) – c(N…) (C4) – c2 (C4a) – c (C5, H) – c1 (NHC(=O)…). The ring closure is correct: C6 bonds back to C7.

**Check of the aniline ring:** c3 (N-attached), c, c, c(O), c(Cl), c3. Cl is adjacent to the O-bearing carbon and meta to the NH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOc1cc2ncc(C#N)c(Nc3ccc(OCc4ccccn4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1NC(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C

name: Netarsudil
text:
I read the molecule as a 2,4-dimethylbenzoate ester of a 4-substituted benzyl alcohol, with the substituent carrying an amide to isoquinolin-6-yl.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with methyl groups at positions 2 and 4 relative to the ester carbonyl carbon (C1), giving a 2,4-dimethylbenzoyl group.
- **Linker:** the carbonyl is bonded to an ester oxygen, then a CH2, then a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Stereocentre:** this carbon carries the aryl ring, a CH2NH2 group drawn on a hashed bond, a C(=O)NH group, and an implicit H.
- **Right ring system:** an isoquinoline with N at the top. Following the ring atoms, the nitrogen-bearing ring has C1 next to the ring fusion carbon, and the NH is attached to C6. So the amide nitrogen is on isoquinolin-6-yl.

For the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are C(=O)N, then CH2NH2, then the aryl ring, then H. The hashed CH2NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page, the order C(=O)N (upper right), then CH2NH2 (bottom), then aryl (left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S.

For the SMILES `...c2ccc(cc2)[C@H](CN)C(=O)N...`, the neighbour order at this carbon is aryl, H, CH2N, C(=O). Working through this order, `@` gives R, so S requires `@@`.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(C(=O)OCc2ccc(cc2)[C@@H](CN)C(=O)Nc2ccc3cnccc3c2)c(C)c1

name: Neticonazole
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then assembled them.

- **Chain:** the left-hand chain has five carbons before the oxygen, so it is a pentyloxy group (CCCCCO–).
- **Benzene ring:** the pentyloxy group sits on one ring carbon, and the vinyl substituent is on the adjacent ring carbon (ortho).
- **Imidazole:** an imidazole is attached through its N1 to the first alkene carbon.
- **Alkene:** the second alkene carbon carries a hydrogen and an S–CH3 group (methylthio).

Stereochemistry: in the drawing, the aryl group and the SMe group lie on the same side of the C=C bond. The imidazole nitrogen therefore sits opposite the sulfur. N outranks C and S outranks H, so higher-priority groups are on opposite sides, which is the E configuration. In SMILES this is written `aryl/C(n…)=C\SC`.

SMILES: CCCCCOc1ccccc1/C(n1ccnc1)=C\SC

name: Natamycin
text:
I read this as a natamycin-type 26-membered macrolide with a mycosamine sugar, and wrote the SMILES from the drawing.

**Macrocycle (clockwise from the CH–CH₃)**
- A CH(CH₃) carries a wedged methyl and is bonded to the lactone oxygen.
- The lactone O–C(=O) is followed by a trans CH=CH, then an epoxide, then CH₂, CH(OH) (hashed), and CH₂.
- Next is a hemiketal carbon bearing OH (wedged) and a ring O, which closes a six-membered tetrahydropyran. That ring also contains CH₂, CH(OH), CH(COOH) and a CH.
- From that CH, a CH₂ leads to the carbon that carries the sugar O (wedge).
- A conjugated tetraene follows, with all four double bonds trans by the drawn geometry, and then a CH₂ returns to the CH(CH₃).

**Sugar**
- The sugar is a 3-amino-3,6-dideoxy pyranose (mycosamine): ring O, anomeric C–O (hashed), 2-OH, 3-NH₂ (hashed), 4-OH (wedge), and a 5-CH₃ (hashed).

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds and the drawn positions of its neighbours. I did not independently check the string against a database entry.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](O[C@H]4[C@@H](O)[C@@H](N)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O4)C[C@@H]2O[C@@](O)(C[C@H](O)[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@@H](O)C[C@H]3O[C@@H]3/C=C/C(=O)O1

name: Nevirapine
text:
This is nevirapine, which I recognised from the drawing and then checked atom by atom.

**Left ring:** a pyridine with N at the top. Its atoms run N, C (top left), C, C(CH3), then C (bottom right, bonded to NH) and C (bonded to the central N). The methyl is on the carbon next to the carbon bearing NH.

**Right ring:** a pyridine with N at the top right. Going round from the carbon attached to the central N: C(=N), N, CH, CH, CH, then C bearing the C=O, which closes back to the first carbon.

**Central ring:** a seven-membered ring made of the carbon attached to the central N on the left, the central N (carrying cyclopropyl), the carbon on the right ring, the right-ring carbon bearing C(=O), the C=O, the NH, and the left-ring carbon bearing NH.

**SMILES:** Cc1ccnc2c1NC(=O)c1cccnc1N2C1CC1

Checking the left ring: c1(C) is bonded to ccnc2 and to c1N. The atoms are C(Me), CH, CH, N, C2 (attached to the central N), then the carbon bearing NH, which closes ring 1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ccnc2c1NC(=O)c1cccnc1N2C1CC1

name: Netupitant
text:
This structure is netupitant, and I read it region by region.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with CF3 groups at the 3 and 5 positions. It attaches through a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups, C(C)(C), which is bonded to the amide carbonyl (C=O).
- **Amide nitrogen:** N-methylated, and bonded to the pyridine ring.
- **Pyridine ring:** the nitrogen-bearing carbon is C(piperazinyl), with the ring nitrogen next to it. Going around the ring, the atoms are C(N-amide), then CH, then N, then C(piperazine), then CH, then C(aryl). The amide N sits on C3. C4 carries the o-tolyl group. C6 carries the 4-methylpiperazine.
- **Tolyl and piperazine:** the o-tolyl is a benzene with a methyl ortho to the bond to the pyridine. The piperazine is N-methylated at the far nitrogen.

SMILES, written with the pyridine as c1(N(C)C(=O)...)cnc(N2CCN(C)CC2)cc1-c1ccccc1C:

CN1CCN(CC1)c1cc(-c2ccccc2C)c(cn1)N(C)C(=O)C(C)(C)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1

Check on the pyridine: n1 is bonded to the C bearing the piperazine (c1) and to the CH (cn1). The ring runs c1(pip), c (CH), c(tolyl), c(N-amide), c (CH), n1. That gives six atoms with the nitrogen adjacent to both the piperazinyl carbon and a CH, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)c1cc(-c2ccccc2C)c(cn1)N(C)C(=O)C(C)(C)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Neomycin
text:
I read the drawing as a tetrasaccharide with the following units:

- **Left ring:** a 2,6-diamino-2,6-dideoxy-pyranose with two OH groups, attached through its anomeric carbon to the ribose.
- **Centre-left ring:** a ribofuranose with a CH2OH group, linked at C3 to the left ring and at its anomeric carbon to the central ring.
- **Central ring:** a 2-deoxystreptamine (a cyclohexane carrying two NH2 groups, one OH and two glycosidic O atoms).
- **Top-right ring:** a second 2,6-diamino-2,6-dideoxy-pyranose with two OH groups, attached through its anomeric carbon to the central ring.

Each stereocentre was assigned from the wedge or hash bond drawn at it, using the implicit hydrogen as the opposite-side neighbour. I did not re-check the finished string beyond that per-centre derivation.

SMILES: NC[C@@H]1O[C@H](O[C@H]2[C@@H](O)[C@H](O[C@H]3[C@H](O[C@H]4O[C@H](CN)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]4N)[C@@H](N)C[C@@H](N)[C@@H]3O)O[C@@H]2CO)[C@H](N)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Nickel tetracarbonyl
text:
The image shows one Ni atom with no bonds and four separate carbon monoxide units. Each unit is drawn as O+ triple-bonded to C−, written [O+]#[C-]. The Ni and the four CO units are disconnected fragments, so they are separated by dots in the SMILES.

SMILES: [Ni].[O+]#[C-].[O+]#[C-].[O+]#[C-].[O+]#[C-]

name: Narasin
text:
I read this as a polyether ionophore of the salinomycin type. I did not match it against a known SMILES; I wrote it atom by atom from the drawing and assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Left side**
- A carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) is attached to a CH that carries an ethyl group.
- That CH is bonded to a tetrahydropyran ring with two methyl substituents.

**Chain**
- The pyran ring continues into a chain containing a methyl-bearing CH, a CH–OH, another methyl-bearing CH and a ketone.
- The ketone is followed by a CH bearing an ethyl group.

**Spiro core**
- That CH joins a second methyl-substituted tetrahydropyran ring.
- This ring is spiro-fused to a dihydropyran that contains a C=C and a CH–OH.
- The same spiro system also includes a tetrahydrofuran ring bearing a methyl group.

**Right end**
- The tetrahydrofuran carries a final tetrahydropyran ring.
- That ring has a methyl group and a quaternary carbon bearing both an ethyl group and an OH.

I checked the SMILES for balanced parentheses and ring-closure digits.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CC)[C@@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](CC)[C@H]2O[C@]3(C=C[C@@H](O)[C@]4(CC[C@](C)(O4)[C@H]5CC[C@@](CC)(O)[C@H](C)O5)O3)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]2C)[C@@H](C)C[C@@H]1C

name: Nicardipine
text:
This structure is nicardipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine drawn without stereochemistry.

**Dihydropyridine core.** The ring contains an NH, two methyl-bearing carbons (C2 and C6), two ester-bearing carbons (C3 and C5), and the sp3 C4 carrying the aryl group.

**Aryl group.** C4 bears a 3-nitrophenyl ring. The nitro group sits at the meta position, written as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Ester arms.**
- The left ester is a methyl ester, C(=O)OC.
- The right ester is C(=O)OCCN(C)Cc1ccccc1, a 2-(N-benzyl-N-methylamino)ethyl ester.

**Stereochemistry.** C4 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Start with the methyl ester: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1)C(=O)OCCN(C)Cc1ccccc1.
- The ring closure is correct: C1 (C3, bearing the methyl ester) is double-bonded to C(C) (C2), which connects to N, then C(C) (C6), double-bonded to C (C5) bearing the second ester, then C4 closing back to C3.
- C4 is written as C1 with the aryl group attached, so the C4 ring closure to C3 is valid.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OCCN(C)Cc2ccccc2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Nickelocene
text:
The image shows three separate species: a Ni²⁺ cation and two identical cyclopentadienyl anions.

Each anion is a five-membered ring. The ring has two C=C double bonds and one carbon bearing a negative charge. Reading around the ring from that charged carbon, the bonds are: single bond to the top-right carbon, then a double bond to the top-left carbon, a single bond down the left side, a double bond along the bottom, and a single bond back to the charged carbon.

The SMILES for one anion is [CH-]1C=CC=C1. The charged carbon carries one hydrogen, so it is written [CH-].

Combining the two anions with the nickel cation, as separate components, gives the answer below.

SMILES: [Ni+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.[CH-]1C=CC=C1

name: Niclosamide
text:
The drawing is niclosamide: a 5-chloro-2-hydroxybenzamide (salicylamide) core with an amide N attached to a 2-chloro-4-nitrophenyl ring.

Left ring: the carbon bearing OH sits at the top and is adjacent to the carbon carrying the C(=O) group. Going round the ring from there, the carbons are C(OH), CH, CH, C(Cl), CH, then C(C=O). The Cl carbon is para to the C(OH) carbon, so the ring is 5-chloro-2-hydroxybenzoyl.

Right ring: the carbon bonded to NH has an adjacent C(Cl), then a CH, then C(NO2), then two CH carbons back to the start. The NO2 is therefore para to the N-bearing carbon and the Cl is ortho to it.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1Cl)c1cc(Cl)ccc1O

name: Nicorandil
text:
The drawing shows nicorandil: a pyridine ring with a carboxamide at the 3-position, where the amide nitrogen carries a two-carbon chain ending in a nitrate ester.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Left end:** a nitro group drawn as [N+](=O)[O-], attached through an oxygen to the chain (a nitrate ester, O–NO2).
- **Chain:** O–CH2–CH2–NH, two carbons between the ester oxygen and the amide nitrogen.
- **Amide:** NH–C(=O), with the carbonyl carbon bonded to the ring.
- **Ring:** six atoms, one of them N. The carbon bearing the amide is bonded to a CH that is bonded to the ring N, so the substituent sits at the 3-position (meta to N), as in nicotinamide.

SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])OCCNC(=O)c1cccnc1

name: Nicotinamide
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with a carboxamide (C(=O)NH2) substituent.

Ring: the N at the top right is bonded to the top-left carbon at (925, 460) and to the right carbon at (1425, 748). The ring then continues through the bottom-right carbon (1257, 1038) and the bottom-left carbon (925, 1038) to the substituted carbon at (757, 748), which closes back to the top-left carbon at (925, 460). That is six ring atoms: N, CH, C(substituted), CH, CH, CH.

The substituted carbon is separated from N by one CH, so the amide sits at the 3-position of the pyridine. The amide carbon carries a C=O (red O) and an NH2.

This is nicotinamide.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cccnc1

name: Nicotinic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered aromatic ring containing one nitrogen, with a carboxylic acid group attached.

**Ring.** Going around the ring from the nitrogen, the atoms are N, then CH, then CH, then CH, then the carbon bearing the substituent, then CH, and back to N. The substituted carbon is therefore separated from N by one CH, which puts the substituent at position 3.

**Substituent.** The carbon attached to the ring has a C=O (drawn as a double bond to O) and an OH, so it is a carboxylic acid (–COOH).

**Check.** The ring has 5 carbons and 1 nitrogen, which makes a pyridine. With the acid at position 3, the molecule is nicotinic acid (pyridine-3-carboxylic acid).

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccnc1

name: Nicotine
text:
This structure is nicotine: an N-methylpyrrolidine ring joined at its C2 carbon to the 3-position of a pyridine ring.

- **Pyrrolidine ring:** the ring has five vertices, one N and four carbons. The N carries a methyl group.
- **Pyridine ring:** the ring has six vertices with one N, and it is attached through the carbon meta to that N.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the pyrrolidine C2, drawn with a hashed wedge to the pyridine, so the pyridyl group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **CIP assignment:** the priorities are N > pyridyl C > ring CH2 > H. On screen, N (upper left) → pyridyl (right) → CH2 (lower left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is counterclockwise, which is S.

This matches natural (S)-nicotine.

SMILES: CN1CCC[C@H]1c1cccnc1

name: Nifedipine
text:
This is a nifedipine-type 1,4-dihydropyridine, so I read it region by region.

- **Dihydropyridine ring:** NH, then C(CH3)=C(CO2CH3), then the sp3 CH carrying the aryl group, then C(CO2CH3)=C(CH3), closing back to NH.
- **Esters:** both are methyl esters. The top one is C(=O)OC on the upper ring carbon. The bottom one is C(=O)OC on the lower ring carbon.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring attached at the sp3 CH, with a nitro group (drawn as [N+](=O)[O-]) on the adjacent ring carbon. The ring is therefore 2-nitrophenyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the sp3 CH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1ccccc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Nicomorphine
text:
The drawing matches nicomorphine, which is morphine esterified with nicotinic acid at both the 3-phenol and the 6-alcohol. Each ester carbonyl carries a pyridin-3-yl ring. I did not derive the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes myself. I took them from the heroin SMILES I remember, swapping acetyl for nicotinoyl, and assumed the drawing shows natural morphine stereochemistry.

I checked the SMILES for validity: the ring-closure labels are reused only after they are closed. The first stereocentre has the same neighbour order as in the heroin SMILES, so its chirality tag carries over unchanged.

SMILES: O=C(O[C@H]1C=C[C@H]2[C@H]3Cc4ccc(OC(=O)c6cccnc6)c5O[C@@H]1[C@]2(CCN3C)c45)c1cccnc1

name: Nifuroxazide
text:
The drawing shows a 4-hydroxybenzoyl hydrazone of 5-nitrofurfural (nifuroxazide).

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with an OH at the far-left carbon (para position) and the carbonyl attached at the opposite carbon.
- **Linker:** C(=O)–NH–N=CH–, with the CH attached to the furan ring.
- **Right ring:** a furan with the CH at C2 and the nitro group at C5. The nitro group is drawn charge-separated, as [N+](=O)[O-].

Stereochemistry: the C=N bond is drawn without explicit cis/trans geometry markers, so I left the double bond unspecified.

SMILES: O=C(NN=Cc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])o1)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Nifenazone
text:
The drawing shows a 4-aminoantipyrine core acylated with nicotinic acid, so the molecule is N-(1,5-dimethyl-3-oxo-2-phenylpyrazol-4-yl)nicotinamide.

**Pyrazolone ring.**
- The ring atoms are C(CH3)=C(NH...)–C(=O)–N(Ph)–N(CH3), closed back to the first carbon.
- The top carbon bears a methyl and is double-bonded to the carbon carrying the NH.
- That NH carbon is single-bonded to the C=O carbon.
- The C=O carbon is bonded to N, which carries the phenyl group.
- That N is bonded to the N that carries the N-methyl, and this N closes the ring to the methyl-bearing carbon.

**Amide and pyridine.**
- The NH is bonded to a C(=O) group, which is attached to a pyridine ring.
- The pyridine attachment carbon is adjacent to a CH that is bonded to N, so the ring is substituted at the 3-position (nicotinoyl).

**Assembled SMILES.** CC1=C(NC(=O)c2cccnc2)C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N1C

SMILES: CC1=C(NC(=O)c2cccnc2)C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N1C

name: Nifekalant
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** a para-substituted benzene ring carrying a nitro group, drawn as [N+](=O)[O-].
- **Linker to the central nitrogen:** from the ring, a chain of three CH2 groups (propyl) leads to a tertiary nitrogen.
- **Central nitrogen substituents:** besides the propyl chain, it carries a CH2CH2OH group and a CH2CH2NH group.
- **Right end:** the NH is attached to C6 of a uracil ring.
  - The ring runs N1(Me)–C2(=O)–N3(Me)–C4(=O)–C5H=C6.
  - The N bearing the lower methyl is bonded to C6 and to the lower C=O.
  - The N bearing the upper methyl is bonded to both carbonyl carbons.
  - So this is a 6-amino-1,3-dimethyluracil.

Writing this as SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(CCCN(CCO)CCNC2=CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)N2C)cc1

Check on the ring closure: C2=CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)N2C opens at C6 (C2), then =C is C5, C(=O) is C4, N(C) is the upper N-methyl, C(=O) is the lower carbonyl, and N2C is the lower N-methyl closing back to C6. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(CCCN(CCO)CCNC2=CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)N2C)cc1

name: Nilotinib
text:

- **Left end:** a pyridin-3-yl ring is attached to C4 of a pyrimidine.
- **Pyrimidine:** C2 carries an NH link to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** it has a methyl group ortho to the NH-bearing carbon, and a C(=O)NH amide at the position meta to the NH.
- **Amide nitrogen:** it is bonded to a second benzene ring that carries CF3 and a 4-methylimidazol-1-yl group, both meta to the amide attachment.
- **Imidazole:** N1 is attached to the ring. C5 is a CH and C4 carries the methyl. N3 is the other ring nitrogen, and C2 is a CH between N1 and N3.

Writing the SMILES from the left pyridine: c1cncc(c1)-c1ccnc(n1)Nc1cc(ccc1C)C(=O)Nc1cc(cc(c1)n1cnc(C)c1)C(F)(F)F

Checks:
- The central ring is c1cc(ccc1C)…, where the first atom bears the NH, the next is CH, the next bears the carbonyl, then two CH, and the ring-closing carbon bears the methyl. This puts the methyl ortho to the NH carbon and the carbonyl meta to it, matching the drawing.
- The imidazole n1cnc(C)c1 has N1, C2, N3, C4 (methyl) and C5, as drawn.

SMILES: Cc1cn(cn1)-c1cc(NC(=O)c2ccc(C)c(Nc3nccc(n3)-c3cccnc3)c2)cc(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Nikkomycin X
text:
This looks like a nikkomycin-type structure, and I read it region by region.

**Left ring (imidazolone):** An aldehyde O=CH is attached to a ring carbon. That carbon is bonded to NH, which connects to C(=O), then to N (ring), then to CH=, which closes back to the aldehyde-bearing carbon. In SMILES: O=CC1=CN(...)C(=O)N1.

**Furanose ring:** The ring N is attached to C1', which is bonded to the ring O. The ring O connects to C4'. C4' connects to C3' (OH), which connects to C2' (OH), which closes to C1'. In SMILES: C1(N...)OC(...)C(O)C1O.

**Side chain from C4':** C4' bears a CH that carries both COOH and NH. The NH is acylated: NC(=O)C(N)C(C)C(O)c1ccc(O)cn1.

**Pyridine ring:** The ring N is bonded to a carbon that carries the CH(OH) substituent. Going around the ring from that carbon: C2 (substituted), C3, C4, C5 (OH), C6, then N. In the drawing, C5 (bearing OH) is bonded to the CH that is bonded to N, so it is c1ccc(O)cn1. This matches.

**Assembled SMILES (no stereo, since the drawing shows no wedges):**

O=CC1=CN(C(=O)N1)C1OC(C(NC(=O)C(N)C(C)C(O)c2ccc(O)cn2)C(=O)O)C(O)C1O

I checked the ring closures. The imidazolone is C1(CHO)=C–N(...)–C(=O)–N1, which gives a 5-membered ring. The furanose ring is C1 (anomeric), O, C4', C3', C2', closing back to C1, which is 5-membered. This is consistent.

SMILES: O=CC1=CN(C(=O)N1)C1OC(C(NC(=O)C(N)C(C)C(O)c2ccc(O)cn2)C(=O)O)C(O)C1O

name: Niguldipine
text:
I read this as a niguldipine-type 1,4-dihydropyridine with these parts:

- **Dihydropyridine core:** a 2,6-dimethyl-1,4-dihydropyridine ring.
- **C3 substituent:** a methyl ester.
- **C5 substituent:** a propyl ester whose chain ends in a 4,4-diphenylpiperidine nitrogen (O–CH2CH2CH2–N).
- **C4 substituent:** a 3-nitrophenyl group, drawn on a hashed bond. This is the only stereocentre.

For the stereocentre at C4, the aryl group points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. On screen, C5 is to the right, the aryl is up, and C3 is lower-left. Viewed from the H side, C5→aryl→C3 runs counterclockwise. In the SMILES below the neighbour order at C4 is C5, H, C3, aryl, which corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OCCCN2CCC(CC2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)[C@H]1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Niludipine
text:
The drawing shows a 1,4-dihydropyridine ring with these parts:

- **Ring:** NH at the top, flanked by two carbons that each carry a methyl group. Each of these carbons is double-bonded to the ring carbon below it (C2=C3 and C5=C6). The sp3 C4 sits at the bottom.
- **C4 substituent:** a 3-nitrophenyl group. The nitro group is drawn as N⁺ with an O⁻ and a =O, on the meta carbon relative to the attachment point.
- **C3 and C5 substituents:** each carries an ester, C(=O)OCH2CH2OCH2CH2CH3, i.e. a 2-propoxyethyl ester.
- **Left chain:** from the carbonyl, O, then CH2CH2, then O, then CH2CH2CH3. The drawn path is CH3–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–O, which is propoxyethyl.
- **Right chain:** the same group, mirrored.

All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included. C4 is a stereocentre by connectivity but is not drawn with a wedge or hash.

name: Nilvadipine
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine, which I read region by region.

**Ring (six-membered):**

**Aryl group:** The phenyl ring is attached to C4 at one carbon. The nitro group sits on the carbon two positions along the ring, so the ring is meta-substituted. The nitro group is drawn as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Stereochemistry:** C4 is drawn with plain bonds, so I include no stereo marks.

**SMILES assembly:** I start at the methyl on C2 and go around the ring: CC1=C(C(=O)OC(C)C)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC)=C(C#N)N1

name: Nimesulide
text:
This is nimesulide: a methanesulfonamide (CH3-SO2-NH-) attached to a benzene ring that carries a phenoxy group ortho to the NH and a nitro group.

Reading the central ring vertex by vertex:
- The NH-bearing carbon is at (662, 1054).
- The phenoxy-bearing carbon is at (614, 837), adjacent to it.
- The next carbon is at (778, 688), a CH.
- The nitro-bearing carbon is at (990, 755).
- Then come the CH at (1037, 972) and the CH at (873, 1122), which closes the ring back to the NH-bearing carbon.

The nitro group sits para to the NH-bearing carbon: the NH carbon is C1, the phenoxy carbon is C2, the CH is C3, the nitro carbon is C4, and the nitro is on C4. The ring is therefore 1-NHSO2Me, 2-OPh, 4-NO2.

The upper-left ring is an unsubstituted phenyl attached through the ether oxygen.

name: Nimodipine
text:
This is nimodipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine drug. I read it from the drawing as follows.

- The C4 carbon carries a 3-nitrophenyl group. The nitro group is drawn as N+ with a double-bonded O and an O−.
- The left ester at C3 is C(=O)OCCOC, a 2-methoxyethyl ester.
- The right ester at C5 is C(=O)OC(C)C, an isopropyl ester.

name: Nipradilol
text:
The drawing shows a chroman (benzopyran) ring system carrying an isopropylamino-hydroxypropoxy side chain and a nitrate ester.

**Side chain:** An isopropyl group (CH(CH3)2) is bonded to NH, then CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then O, which attaches to the aromatic ring.

**Ring system:**
- The benzene ring has six carbons. One carbon bears the side-chain O (position 8). The adjacent carbon (C8a) bears the ring oxygen. Another fusion carbon (C4a) is bonded to CH2 (C4).
- The pyran ring runs O1, C2 (CH2), C3 (CH–ONO2), C4 (CH2), C4a, C8a.
- The nitrate is O–[N+](=O)[O-].

**SMILES:** CC(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2c1OCC(C2)O[N+](=O)[O-]

**Check:**
- c1 is the aromatic carbon bearing the side chain, followed by ccc for three CH carbons.
- c2 is C4a, and the next c1 closes the benzene ring and is C8a. This carbon bonds to O, then CH2 (C2), then CH (C3) with branch (C2), where C2 is the C4 CH2 closing back to C4a, and then the nitrate.
- The benzene ring is c1, c, c, c, c2, c1, which is six atoms.
- All bonds are plain in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: Nintedanib esylate
text:
The image shows two components: ethanesulfonic acid and a nintedanib-like free base drawn in a tautomeric form.

**Ethanesulfonic acid:** CCS(=O)(=O)O

**Main molecule, traced region by region:**
- Indole core: the C2 carbon carries an OH, the C3 carbon is double-bonded to C2, and the ring is aromatic with an NH. The C6 position carries a methyl ester.
- C3 substituent: a carbon attached to C3 by a single bond, with a phenyl group and a C=N double bond to the aryl nitrogen.
- Central aryl ring: a para-substituted benzene bearing the N= on one side and N(CH3)C(=O)CH2-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl) on the other.

Writing the indole as an aromatic system with an OH on C2: Oc1[nH]c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2c1C(c1ccccc1)=Nc1ccc(cc1)N(C)C(=O)CN1CCN(C)CC1

**Aromaticity check of the indole:** The pyrrole ring atoms are C2(OH), N–H, C7a, C3a and C3. In the drawing, C2=C3 is a double bond, C3a=C7a is a double bond, and N–H is a single-bonded nitrogen. This is a valid aromatic 2-hydroxyindole.

**Benzo ring:** C7a is bonded to C7, then C6 (carrying the ester), C5, C4 and C3a. The ester sits on the carbon that is para to C3a... in the image, C7a connects to the CH at the lower right, then to the C bearing the ester. So the ester carbon is C6, which matches the SMILES above (c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2 reads from C7a through C7 to C6).

**Stereochemistry:** The C=N bond has no explicit cis/trans geometry marked, so none is included.

**Final SMILES, with the two components separated by a dot:**

SMILES: CCS(=O)(=O)O.Oc1[nH]c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2c1C(c1ccccc1)=Nc1ccc(cc1)N(C)C(=O)CN1CCN(C)CC1

name: Nirmatrelvir
text:

name: Niraparib
text:
The structure is niraparib, with the (S) configuration at the piperidine stereocentre.

Seen from the front, C2 → aryl → C4 runs counterclockwise, which gives S. In the SMILES below, the neighbour order at that carbon (aryl, H, C2 via the ring closure, C4) with `@@` also corresponds to S.

name: Nitazoxanide

name: Nitisinone
text:

name: Nitramine
text:

CN(C1=C(C=C(C=C1[N+](=O)[O-])[N+](=O)[O-])[N+](=O)[O-])[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Nitrazepam
text:
The drawing shows nitrazepam, a 1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one.

name: Nitrendipine

name: Nikkomycin Z
text:
This drawing appears to be nikkomycin Z. I built the SMILES from the image region by region and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Fragments**
- **Uracil:** an N1-linked pyrimidine-2,4-dione ring, written `O=C1C=CN(C(=O)N1)`.
- **Ribose-type ring:** a five-membered ring with one oxygen. C1' carries the uracil N on a hashed bond, C2' and C3' each carry a wedged OH, and C4' is joined to the ring O by a hashed bond.
- **Exocyclic carbon (C5'):** it bears a free COOH and an NH on a hashed bond. That NH is the amide N of the chain.
- **Chain:** the amide C=O leads to a CH(NH2) with a wedged NH2. Next is a CH with a wedged methyl, then a CH(OH) with a wedged OH.
- **Pyridine:** a 5-hydroxypyridin-2-yl ring attached to the CH(OH) carbon, written `c3ccc(O)cn3`.

**Stereochemistry:** I worked out each centre from the wedge/hash drawn at it and the 2D positions of its neighbours. I took the narrow end of each hashed bond to be at the stereocentre. The ring and chain centres came out as `[C@@H]2`, `[C@H]`, `[C@@H](O)`, `[C@H]2O`, `[C@H]`, `[C@@H](N)`, `[C@H](C)` and `[C@H](O)` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: O=C1C=CN(C(=O)N1)[C@@H]2O[C@H]([C@H](NC(=O)[C@@H](N)[C@H](C)[C@H](O)c3ccc(O)cn3)C(=O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O

The ring has six vertices. The nitro-bearing carbon is at the left, and the other five carbons each have one ²H substituent, so this is nitrobenzene-d5.

name: Nitrofurazone

name: Nitroglycerin
