name: Nitrous Oxide
text:
The drawing shows a linear chain of three atoms: N, N⁺ and O.

- The left N carries a negative charge, shown as a minus sign above the bond. It is joined to the central N⁺ by a double bond.
- The central N⁺ is joined to O by a double bond.

This is nitrous oxide, written as [N-]=[N+]=O.

Charge check: the left N has two bonds plus two lone pairs, which makes it N⁻. The central N⁺ has four bonds. The O has two bonds. The total charge is zero.

SMILES: [N-]=[N+]=O

name: Nitrofurantoin
text:
This is nitrofurantoin: a 5-nitrofuran linked through a CH=N bond to the N-amino group of a hydantoin ring.

**Furan ring.** The ring atoms are O, C5 (bearing the nitro group), C4, C3 and C2. C2 carries the CH=N substituent. The nitro group is drawn charge-separated, as [N+](=O)[O-].

**Linker and hydantoin ring.** The CH=N unit connects to N1 of the hydantoin. N1 is bonded to C2(=O), which is bonded to NH. NH is bonded to C4(=O), which is bonded to CH2, closing back to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with plain bonds, but its geometry is visible. Going left to right, the furan attaches to the CH carbon at about (620, 903) and the CH is at about (783, 908). The N is at about (868, 772) and the next N at about (1010, 775). The furan substituent on the CH sits lower-left of the CH, while the N1 substituent on the imine N continues to the right at roughly the same height as that N. The furan is therefore at the bottom-left and N1 at the upper-right, which are on opposite sides of the C=N bond. This is the E configuration, matching nitrofurantoin.

In SMILES, `/C=N/N` means the substituents before the C and after the N are trans. I write the furan carbon as `c1.../C=N/N1...`, which gives the E isomer.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)c1ccc(o1)/C=N/N1CC(=O)NC1=O

name: Nizatidine
text:
The structure reads, from left to right, as follows.

- **Nitroethene end:** a nitro group, drawn as [N+](=O)[O-], is attached to a CH that is double-bonded to a carbon.
- **Amidine-type carbon:** that carbon carries NHCH3 and NH-CH2CH2-S.
- **Thioether link:** the sulfur connects to a CH2 that leads to the thiazole ring.
- **Thiazole ring:** C4 bears the CH2S group and is bonded to N3. N3 is double-bonded to C2, which bears CH2N(CH3)2. C2 is also bonded to the ring S1, which bonds to C5, and C5 is double-bonded to C4.

Written as SMILES, this is CNC(=C[N+](=O)[O-])NCCSCc1csc(CN(C)C)n1.

Checking the ring: c1 (C4), c (C5), s, c(CN(C)C) (C2), n1 (N3). C4 is bonded to N3 through the ring closure, which matches the drawing.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CNC(=C[N+](=O)[O-])NCCSCc1csc(CN(C)C)n1

name: Nemadectin
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing by hand. I assigned the stereocentres and double-bond geometry from wedge/hash directions and bond coordinates, so those are the most likely places for an error. The structure is a macrocyclic lactone of the milbemycin type.

- **Side chain:** a trans-configured isobutenyl group, CH(CH3)2–CH=C(CH3)–, is attached to the carbon next to the ring oxygen of the left tetrahydropyran ring.
- **Spiroketal:** the left tetrahydropyran carries a methyl and a hydroxyl and is spiro-fused to a second tetrahydropyran (two ring oxygens on the spiro carbon).
- **Macrocycle:** the second pyran is bridged to an ester oxygen, then C(=O), then a cyclohexene bearing a methyl and a hydroxyl. The cyclohexene is fused to a tetrahydrofuran that carries a tertiary OH. The ring continues through a trisubstituted alkene with a methyl, a CH(CH3) centre, and a conjugated diene (trans, then cis to the furan CH2) back to the pyran.

SMILES: CC(C)/C=C(/[C@H]1O[C@]2(C[C@H](O)[C@H](C)1)C[C@@H]7C[C@H](O2)C/C=C(C)/C[C@@H](C)/C=C/C=C8\CO[C@@H]9[C@H](O)C(C)=C[C@@H](C(=O)O7)[C@@]98O)C

name: Norelgestromin
text:
I read this as the 3-oxime of levonorgestrel. This is a norgestrel-type 19-nor steroid skeleton with these features:

- a 13-ethyl group
- a 17-hydroxy-17-ethynyl group
- a 4-ene
- a 3-position C=N–OH oxime in place of the ketone

I took the ring-fusion stereocentres, the hashed ethyl and the hashed OH to match the natural levonorgestrel configuration, as in its known SMILES, rather than deriving each one from the wedges. In the drawing the oxime OH points down, on the same side as the C4 carbon, so I set the C=N geometry accordingly.

SMILES: CC[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@@H](CCC4=C/C(=N\O)CC[C@H]34)[C@@H]1CC[C@]2(O)C#C

name: Norepinephrine
text:
The drawing shows norepinephrine (noradrenaline): a catechol ring (benzene with two adjacent OH groups) attached to a CH(OH)–CH2–NH2 side chain.

For the stereocentre, the OH is on a wedge. The CIP priorities are OH > CH2NH2 > aryl > H. With H pointing away from the viewer, the sequence OH (top), CH2NH2 (lower right), aryl (lower left) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.

Checking the SMILES `NC[C@H](O)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1`: from the CH2 neighbour, H → O → aryl runs counterclockwise (@). This works out to R, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC[C@H](O)c1ccc(O)c(O)c1

name: Norethandrolone
text:
I read this as 17α-ethyl-17β-hydroxy-estr-4-en-3-one (norethandrolone), a 19-nor steroid with an ethyl and a hydroxyl on C17. The SMILES below is written from the known SMILES for this compound rather than derived independently from the wedges, so I only checked the drawn stereochemistry against it by eye.

- **Ring system:** the four fused rings have the A/B/C/D steroid layout.
- **Ring A:** a C3 ketone (C=O on the right) conjugated with the C4=C5 double bond.
- **C10:** there is no methyl here, only a hashed H, so it is a 19-nor steroid.
- **C13:** a hashed methyl group.
- **C17:** a hashed OH and an ethyl chain.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:**
  - hashed at C8 and C10
  - wedged at C9 and C14
- **Consistency check:** this pattern matches the natural steroid configuration (8β-H, 9α-H, 10β-H, 14α-H, 13β-methyl).

SMILES: CC[C@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@H]34)C)O

name: Nortriptyline
text:
The drawing shows nortriptyline: a dibenzo-fused seven-membered ring carrying an exocyclic alkylidene side chain that ends in a secondary N-methylamine.

- **Side chain:** a methyl on NH, then two CH2 groups, then a CH that is double-bonded to the ring carbon (CNCCC=C1).
- **Central ring:** the double-bonded ring carbon connects to two benzene rings. The two benzene rings are linked on the far side by a CH2–CH2 bridge, which closes the seven-membered ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is included. The two aryl groups on the double-bonded ring carbon are equivalent by connectivity because of the symmetric CH2CH2 bridge, so the double bond has no E/Z designation. There are no wedges or hashes.

SMILES: CNCCC=C1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc12

name: Norethindrone
text:
I read this as norethisterone (norethindrone), a 19‑nor steroid, and took its stereochemistry from the PubChem SMILES for that compound after checking the wedges against it.

**Skeleton and substituents**
- It has the four fused steroid rings. Ring A is a cyclohexenone, with a C=O at the right edge and a C4=C5 double bond. Rings B and C are cyclohexanes, and ring D is a cyclopentane on the left.
- At C17 on ring D there is a tertiary alcohol (OH) and an ethynyl group (C≡CH).
- There is a methyl group on C13, and no methyl on C10, which is why this is a 19‑nor steroid.

**Stereochemistry**
- The drawing shows a hashed methyl at C13, a hashed OH at C17, and a wedged H at C14. It also shows a wedged H at C9, and hashed H at C8 and C10.
- Relative to the usual steroid drawing, every wedge is reversed. The ring system is also drawn mirrored, with ring A on the right and ring D on the left. The two changes cancel, so the drawing matches the natural configuration of norethindrone. I did not independently derive each @/@@ from the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C#C)O)CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@H]34

name: Nonactin
text:
I read this as a 40-membered macrocycle with four 2,5-disubstituted tetrahydrofuran rings. It has four ester linkages, and the ring carbons that carry a methyl group are marked with wedges or hashes. The connectivity and stereochemistry are consistent with nonactin.

I traced the ring from the top-left CH and assigned each stereocentre (@/@@) from its wedge or hash, with the implicit H taken as pointing to the opposite face. The four repeating units fall into two alternating stereochemical types, with units 1 and 3 identical and units 2 and 4 identical, which matches the symmetric look of the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1OC(=O)[C@H](C)[C@H]2CC[C@H](O2)C[C@H](C)OC(=O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H]2CC[C@@H](O2)C[C@@H](C)OC(=O)[C@H](C)[C@H]2CC[C@H](O2)C[C@H](C)OC(=O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H]2CC[C@@H](O2)C1

name: Noscapine
text:
This is a noscapine-type skeleton: a methylated tetrahydroisoquinoline carrying a methylenedioxy group and a methoxy group, linked to a dimethoxy-substituted phthalide (lactone) ring.

**Connectivity, region by region**
- Left ring system: a benzene ring fused to a methylenedioxy ring (O–CH2–O) and to a six-membered ring containing N-CH3 and a CH2CH2 bridge. One methoxy group sits on the benzene ring next to the stereocentre.
- Right ring system: a benzene ring with two adjacent OMe groups, fused to a five-membered lactone (C(=O)–O–CH).
- The two ring systems are joined by a single bond between the CH next to N and the CH bearing the lactone oxygen.

**Stereochemistry**
- The CH next to N has a wedge to N. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@@H]`.
- The lactone CH has a hashed bond to O. The same analysis gives `[C@H]`.

I derived the chirality tags by hand from the wedge and hash geometry. The remembered SMILES for noscapine (S,R) has `[C@@H]` at the second centre, which differs from my derived `[C@H]`, so that centre is the least certain.

SMILES: CN1CCc2cc3OCOc3c(OC)c2[C@@H]1[C@H]1OC(=O)c2c1ccc(OC)c2OC

name: Nogalamycin
text:
I read the structure as a nogalamycin-type anthracycline. It has a tetramethoxy deoxy-sugar (nogalose) on the left and a bridged aminosugar ring on the right.

**Left side**
- The sugar ring is a six-membered pyranose. Its anomeric carbon is hashed to the aglycone oxygen.
- Going round the ring: a methyl-bearing carbon (wedge), then OMe (hash), then a quaternary C(CH3)(OMe), then OMe (wedge).

**Aglycone**
- A cyclohexane ring carries, in order: C–O-sugar (hash), CH2, C(OH)(CH3) (methyl hashed), and CH–CO2Me (wedge).
- This ring is fused to the aromatic ring that bears a phenolic OH.
- A quinone-like ring with two C=O groups links that ring to a second aromatic ring. The second ring has a phenolic OH, an aryl–O bond to the acetal carbon, and a bond to the quaternary methyl carbon.

**Right side**
- A bicyclic ketal bridge links the quaternary C(CH3) and the acetal CH through an O bridge, with the aryl O on the same acetal CH.
- The ring carbons are C(OH), C(NMe2) (wedge) and C(OH).

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry in the drawing. Plain-bond centres get no stereo.

SMILES: CO[C@@H]1[C@](C)(OC)[C@@H](OC)[C@H](C)O[C@H]1O[C@H]2C[C@](C)(O)[C@H](C(=O)OC)c3cc4c(c(O)c23)C(=O)c5c(O)cc6c(c5C4=O)O[C@@H]7O[C@@]6(C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](N(C)C)[C@@H]7O

name: Noxiptiline
text:
The drawing shows a dibenzosuberone-type oxime ether: a 10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cycloheptene core with a C=N–O–CH2CH2–N(CH3)2 side chain (noxiptiline).

**Chain:** Two methyls sit on the nitrogen (N), which connects to CH2–CH2–O–N=C.

**Seven-membered ring:** The C=N carbon is bonded to two aromatic carbons, one in each benzene ring. Each benzene ring also carries a carbon bonded to one of two CH2 groups, and those two CH2 groups are bonded to each other.

**SMILES construction:** Starting from the side chain, CN(C)CCON=C1 opens the seven-membered ring at the oxime carbon. Then c2ccccc2 gives the first benzene ring, with its last atom bonded to CH2. CCc2ccccc12 then gives the two CH2 groups and the second benzene ring, which closes back to the oxime carbon.

Checking the first benzene ring: the atom written as c2 attaches to C1, and the closing atom c2 attaches to the CH2. These are ortho neighbours, which matches the drawing. In the second ring, the first atom attaches to the CH2 and the last atom (c12) closes ring 1 to the oxime carbon and ring 2 to the first atom of that ring, so those two are ortho as well.

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included. The C=N geometry is not specified by wedges or cis/trans marks.

SMILES: CN(C)CCON=C1c2ccccc2CCc2ccccc12

name: Norucholic Acid
text:
I read this as a 3,7-dihydroxy bile acid on a steroid skeleton, with a short side chain at C17 of CH(CH3)–CH2–COOH. That makes it a nor-bile acid, consistent with norursodeoxycholic acid (3α,7β-dihydroxy).

**Skeleton and substituents**
- Four fused rings: three six-membered and one five-membered.
- Hydroxyl groups at C3 and C7.
- Methyl groups at C10 and C13.
- The side chain from C17 is CH(CH3)–CH2–C(=O)OH.

**Stereochemistry from the drawing**
- C20: methyl on a wedge.
- C17: wedge bond to the ring carbon C16.
- C14: hashed H.
- C8: wedge H.
- C7: wedge OH.
- C5: wedge H.
- C3: hashed OH.
- C10 and C13: wedge methyls.
- C9: hashed H.

I assigned each centre by reading the neighbour positions and wedge or hash directions in the image and converting them to @/@@ in the SMILES atom order.

SMILES: C[C@H](CC(=O)O)[C@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@@H]3[C@@H](O)C[C@@H]4C[C@H](O)CC[C@]4(C)[C@H]3CC[C@]12C

name: Nocathiacin I
text:
I read the drawing region by region and wrote the SMILES below. I did not run it through a validator.

**Reading of the structure**
- **Tail:** an acrylamide unit, C=C(C(N)=O)NC(=O), joined to a thiazole that is attached to the central pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** it carries an OH. Its other two substituent positions each bear a thiazole, giving the macrocycle.
- **Upper arc:** thiazole, then C(=O)–NH–threonine (with its CH(OH)CH3 side chain), then NH–C(=C(CH3)OCH3) (the methoxy-vinyl unit), then a second thiazole.
- **Lower ring:** that second thiazole is followed by C(=O)–NH–CH, a third thiazole, C(=O)–NH–CH(CH2–O–C(=O)–) and a fourth thiazole, which closes back onto the pyridine.
- **Indole core:** an N-hydroxy indole. The ester carbonyl sits on C2, and a CH2–O ether sits on C3. The benzene ring carries a CH2–O–C(=O) group.
- **Sugar:** a 2,6-dideoxy sugar linked through a hashed glycosidic bond. Its ring has a 6-methyl (wedge), a 4-NMe2 (wedge) and a 3-methyl-3-OH (hashed methyl).

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned stereo from the wedges and hashes at the threonine α and β carbons, the two ring CH carbons next to the thiazoles, the ether-bearing CH, the CH bearing CH2O, and the four sugar stereocentres.
- The CH carrying the sugar oxygen has only plain bonds in the drawing, so I left it unspecified.
- The methoxy-vinyl double bond is drawn with fixed geometry. The NH and the CH3 are on the same side, so I encoded it as `N/C(=C(\C)OC)`.

SMILES: C=C(C(N)=O)NC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1nc2c(cc1O)-c1nc(cs1)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N/C(=C(\C)OC)c1nc(cs1)C(=O)N[C@@H]3c1nc(cs1)C(=O)N[C@@H](COC(=O)c4n(O)c5cccc6c5c4CO[C@@H]3C(O[C@H]3C[C@](C)(O)[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H](C)O3)C(=O)OC6)c1nc2cs1

name: O-Acetylpsilocin
text:
The drawing shows an indole core. The NH sits at the top, bonded to the benzene ring fusion carbon and to the C2 carbon. C2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 carries the side chain.

Side chain: C3 is bonded to CH2, then CH2, then N(CH3)2.

Benzene ring: the ring fusion carbon C3a is bonded to C4, which bears the O-acetyl group (OC(=O)C). The ring then continues C4–C5=C6–C7=C7a, with C7a bonded to N.

Bond check against the drawing:
- C7a=C3a is drawn as a double bond (the inner line between 400,412 and 500,600).
- C7=C6 is a double bond (the inner line near 190,405 to 75,585).
- C5=C4 is a double bond (the line near 175,773 to 388,780).
- C2=C3 is a double bond.

Written as SMILES, starting from the acetyl group:

CC(=O)Oc1cccc2[nH]cc(CCN(C)C)c12

This is the atom-for-atom reading: c1 is C4, then C5, C6, C7, c2 is C7a, [nH], C2, C3 with the side chain, and c12 is C3a closing both rings. This is psilocin acetate (4-AcO-DMT).

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1cccc2[nH]cc(CCN(C)C)c12

name: Npc209773
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Bicyclic amine:** it is a tropane (8-methyl-8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane). The N carries a methyl group and bridges the two bridgehead carbons. One bridge is a two-carbon CH2–CH2 unit on the left, and the other is a three-carbon CH2–CH(O)–CH2 unit on the right.
- **Ester:** the carbon at the middle of the three-carbon bridge bears an O–C(=O) ester group.
- **Acyl part:** the carbonyl carbon is bonded to a CH that carries a phenyl ring and a CH2OH group (a tropic acid ester).
- **Stereochemistry:** both bridgehead hydrogens are drawn as wedges, so those two centres get @/@@ labels. The ester-bearing carbon and the CH(CH2OH)Ph carbon are drawn with plain bonds, so they get no stereo marks.

I worked out each bridgehead's @/@@ from the drawn geometry, with the H wedged toward the viewer, and wrote the SMILES with the ring closures noted below.

The SMILES has the following layout:

- `CN1` is the N-methyl nitrogen.
- `[C@@H]2` is the first bridgehead, and the ring-closure digit 2 links it to the CH2 on the three-carbon bridge.
- `CC` is the two-carbon bridge.
- `[C@H]1` is the second bridgehead, which closes the ring back to N.
- `CC(C2)` is the three-carbon bridge, with the ester-bearing carbon in the middle.
- `OC(=O)C(CO)c1ccccc1` is the ester and tropic acid side chain.

SMILES: CN1[C@@H]2CC[C@H]1CC(C2)OC(=O)C(CO)c1ccccc1

name: Nosiheptide
text:
I read the drawing as a nosiheptide-type thiopeptide macrocycle: a central 3-hydroxypyridine carrying several thiazoles, a 3-methylindole acid linked through a thioester and an ester, and a dehydroalanine amide tail. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry. The cis/trans geometry of the two C=C bonds is also left unspecified.

Building the SMILES region by region:

1. **Tail:** a primary amide on a dehydroalanine (`NC(=O)C(=C)N...`), acylated through an amide to a thiazole C4. That thiazole's C2 is bonded to the pyridine.
2. **Pyridine:**
   - C2 bears the tail thiazole.
   - C3 bears OH.
   - C5 bears the upper-right thiazole.
   - C6 bears the thiazole that closes the ring at the lower right.
3. **Upper-right thiazole:** its C4 is acylated by the amide-linked threonine (`NC(C(C)O)C(=O)N`).
4. **Dehydrobutyrine unit:** the threonine's C-terminal amide NH is attached to `C(=CC)`, which links to the top-left thiazole.
5. **Top-left thiazole:** its C4 carries a C(=O)NH group that leads to a CH bearing a CH2–CH(OH)–C(=O)–O chain.
6. **Ester and indole:** the ester oxygen connects through CH2 to C4 of the 3-methylindole. The indole C2 carries C(=O)S.
7. **Thioester and cysteine unit:** the S–CH2–CH(NH…) segment connects through the middle-left thiazole, closing the macrocycle at the CH bearing the CH2–CH(OH) chain.
8. **Lower thiazole:** attached to the cysteine-derived CH, it closes onto the pyridine C6.

The ring-closure digits were checked so that the pyridine, each thiazole, the indole and the macrocycle close correctly.

SMILES: NC(=O)C(=C)NC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1nc2c(cc1O)-c1nc(cs1)C(=O)NC(C(C)O)C(=O)NC(=CC)c1nc(cs1)C(=O)NC3CC(O)C(=O)OCc4cccc5[nH]c(c(C)c45)C(=O)SCC(NC(=O)c6csc3n6)c7nc2cs7

name: Novolimus
text:
This reads as 16‑O‑demethylrapamycin (sirolimus with a free OH in place of one methoxy), and I wrote the SMILES by adapting the known rapamycin SMILES to what the drawing shows. I did not re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes; I kept rapamycin's.

Reading the macrocycle from the pyran ring:
- **Pyran ring:** an O‑bridged ring carries a methyl on a wedge, and the hemiketal carbon bears an OH.
- **Amide/ester section:** the hemiketal carbon is followed by two adjacent C=O groups, then the piperidine N. The piperidine carbon next to N bears a hashed H and is bonded to a C(=O)–O ester.
- **Ester side:** the ester O leads to a CH that carries the side chain and the ring CH2 leading to a ketone.
- **Side chain:** CH(CH3)–CH2 leads to a cyclohexane ring bearing OMe and OH.
- **Ketone to alkene:** the ketone is followed by CH(CH3) and a trisubstituted C=C(CH3).
- **Hydroxyl and methoxy carbons:** next come CH(OH) and CH(OMe), then a C=O.
- **Methylated section:** this C=O is followed by CH(CH3), CH2 and CH(CH3).
- **Triene:** CH(CH3) leads into a conjugated triene, whose last carbon is the C(CH3)= that meets the next CH(OH).
- **Closure:** CH(OH) then CH2 closes onto the pyran carbon.

The carbon next to the pyran CH2 carries a free OH, not the OMe that rapamycin has at that position. So I changed the terminal `OC` of the rapamycin SMILES to `O`.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2C[C@@H](/C(=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H](C(=O)[C@@H]([C@@H](/C(=C/[C@H](C(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)[C@@H]3CCCCN3C(=O)C(=O)[C@@]1(O2)O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4CC[C@H]([C@@H](C4)OC)O)C)/C)O)OC)C)C)/C)O

name: Obidoxime Chloride
text:
The drawing shows obidoxime chloride: two pyridinium rings joined through their nitrogens by a CH2–O–CH2 bridge, each ring carrying an oxime at the 4-position, with two chloride counterions.

**Left ring.** The nitrogen N+ is bonded to a ring carbon by a double bond, and the 4-position carries CH=N–OH.

**Bridge.** Each N+ is attached to a CH2, and the two CH2 groups are linked through one oxygen.

**Right ring.** It mirrors the left ring, with the same 4-substituted CH=N–OH group.

**Counterions.** Two Cl⁻ are drawn separately.

**Stereochemistry.** The oxime C=N bonds are drawn without explicit cis/trans geometry, so I include no stereo marks.

The SMILES below was written from this reading and not run through a validator.

SMILES: ON=Cc1cc[n+](COC[n+]2ccc(C=NO)cc2)cc1.[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Oclacitinib
text:
The drawing shows a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine core (the 7-deazapurine of oclacitinib) with an N-methyl-N-cyclohexylamino group at C4. The cyclohexane carries a CH2–SO2–NHCH3 group. This matches oclacitinib.

**Core.** The pyrrole NH is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to N (pyrimidine). That N goes to CH, then to N, then to C4 (bearing the amino group), then to C4a, and back to C7a. C4a is also bonded to the pyrrole CH=CH that returns to the NH.

SMILES for the core: c1nc2[nH]ccc2c(N(C)...)n1

**Substituent.** The chain is N(C)C1CCC(CS(=O)(=O)NC)CC1. The cyclohexane has 6 ring vertices: C1 (N-attached), then two CH2, then C4 (bearing CH2S), then two CH2.

**Stereochemistry.** All cyclohexane bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CNS(=O)(=O)CC1CCC(CC1)N(C)c1ncnc2[nH]ccc12

name: Obicetrapib
text:
I read the molecule as a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline core, with these substituents:

- **N1:** an ethyl carbamate, N–C(=O)OCH2CH3.
- **C2:** an ethyl group on a hashed bond.
- **C4:** a tertiary amine nitrogen on a hashed bond. That nitrogen carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group and a pyrimidin-2-yl group.
- **Benzo ring:** a CF3 group at C6.
- **Pyrimidine:** an O–CH2CH2CH2–COOH chain at C5.

For the two stereocentres, I treated the hashed substituent as pointing away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Reading the remaining three neighbours around each centre from the H side gave clockwise at both C2 and C4. Writing the neighbours in SMILES order gives [C@H] for both centres.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)N1[C@H](CC)C[C@H](N(Cc2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c2)c2ncc(OCCCC(=O)O)cn2)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc21

name: Octenidine Hydrochloride
text:
The image shows octenidine dihydrochloride.

- **Core:** two 1,4-dihydropyridine rings, each with an exocyclic C=N double bond at the 4-position (a 4-ylidene imine). Each ring nitrogen is substituted.
- **Linker:** an unbranched chain of 10 CH2 groups joins the two ring nitrogens.
- **End groups:** each imine nitrogen carries an n-octyl chain (8 carbons).
- **Salt:** two separate HCl labels are drawn, so I wrote them as two Cl atoms after the main molecule.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

I counted the chain vertices one by one from the drawing: 10 in the linker and 8 in each octyl group.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCN=C1C=CN(C=C1)CCCCCCCCCCN1C=CC(=NCCCCCCCC)C=C1.Cl.Cl

name: Octogen
text:
The drawing shows an eight-membered ring that alternates N and CH2: four ring nitrogens and four CH2 carbons. Each ring nitrogen carries a nitro group, drawn as N+ with one =O and one O−. This is HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine).

Ring atoms, going round: N (top left), CH2 (top), N (top right), CH2 (right), N (bottom right), CH2 (bottom), N (bottom left), CH2 (left), and back to the top-left N.

I read this as a ring with a nitro on every N, written as the SMILES below.

SMILES: O=[N+]([O-])N1CN([N+](=O)[O-])CN([N+](=O)[O-])CN([N+](=O)[O-])C1

name: Obeticholic Acid
text:
This is obeticholic acid, which is 6α‑ethyl‑chenodeoxycholic acid. The drawing shows a steroid core with a 3‑OH, a 7‑OH, a 6‑ethyl group, two angular methyls and a pentanoic acid side chain.

Reading the stereochemistry:
- The drawing is rotated and flipped relative to the usual steroid orientation, which swaps wedges and hashes.
- The two methyls are hashed in this view, which corresponds to β.
- The 3‑OH, 7‑OH and 6‑ethyl are wedged, which corresponds to α.
- The H at C5 is hashed, which corresponds to 5β, as in bile acids.
- The 8‑ and 9‑H and the other ring‑fusion H atoms are shown in the usual steroid configuration.

I did not derive every stereocentre independently from the picture. I built the SMILES from the chenodeoxycholic acid skeleton and added the 6α‑ethyl group. The configuration at C6 comes from my recollection of the obeticholic acid SMILES rather than from a separate check against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](CCC(=O)O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@H](CC)[C@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)O)C

name: Octreotide Acetate
text:
The drawing is octreotide as its diacetate salt. The peptide is D-Phe-Cys-Phe-D-Trp-Lys-Thr-Cys-Thr(ol), with a Cys–Cys disulfide bridge forming the ring, and two acetic acid molecules are drawn separately.

I did not derive the stereo marks from the wedges and hashes one by one. I wrote the peptide part from the known octreotide structure and checked that its connectivity matches the drawing: the two benzyl groups, the indole, the lysine chain, the threonine and threoninol hydroxyls, and the S–S bridge.

SMILES: C[C@H]([C@@H](CO)NC(=O)[C@H]1CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N1)[C@@H](C)O)CCCCN)CC2=CNC3=CC=CC=C32)CC4=CC=CC=C4)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC5=CC=CC=C5)N)O.CC(=O)O.CC(=O)O

name: Oglemilast
text:
The drawing shows a dibenzofuran core, a 3,5-dichloropyridin-4-yl amide, a difluoromethoxy group and a methanesulfonamide.

**Dibenzofuran core.** The upper benzene ring has these vertices:
- C1 (at 737,690) carries the C(=O)N group.
- C2 (825,572) and C3 (972,590) are plain CH positions.
- C4 (1029,726) carries OCHF2.
- C4a (940,845) is bonded to the furan O.
- C9b (794,827) is the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the lower ring.

The lower benzene ring has these vertices:
- C9a (732,961) is bonded to C9b.
- C9 (590,1003) is a CH.
- C8 (558,1148) carries the NHSO2Me group.
- C7 (665,1248) is a CH.
- C6 (807,1206) is a CH.
- C5a (838,1061) is bonded to the furan O.

**Substituents.**
- The amide is C(=O)NH attached to the pyridine at its 4-position, which sits between two C–Cl carbons. The pyridine is therefore 3,5-dichloropyridin-4-yl.
- The upper ring carries OC(F)F.
- The lower ring carries NS(=O)(=O)C.

**SMILES assembly.**
Start with the amide and pyridine: O=C(Nc1c(Cl)cncc1Cl)c1ccc(OC(F)F)c2oc3ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc3c12

Checking the ring closures: c1 (C1) is followed by c (C2), c (C3), c(OC(F)F) (C4), and c2 (C4a), which opens ring 2. Then o, then c3 (C5a), c (C6), c (C7), c(NHSO2Me) (C8), c (C9), and c3 (C9a), which closes the lower ring. Finally c12 (C9b) bonds to C1 and to C4a. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1c(Cl)cncc1Cl)c1ccc(OC(F)F)c2oc3ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc3c12

name: Olanzapine
text:
This structure is the thienobenzodiazepine olanzapine.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Piperazine:** an N-methylpiperazine. The methyl sits on the left nitrogen, and the right nitrogen attaches to the amidine carbon.
- **Amidine carbon:** it carries a double bond to the ring N, which is bonded to the benzene ring, and a single bond to the thiophene carbon.
- **Thiophene:** this carbon is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the NH and S. The ring then continues through CH= to C(CH3), which is bonded to S.
- **Benzene:** it is fused to the seven-membered ring, with one carbon bonded to N= and the adjacent carbon bonded to NH.

SMILES written from this reading: CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Nc2sc(C)cc12

Checking the atoms against the drawing: the thiophene ring is c2 (bonded to NH), s, c(C), c, c12. The last atom, c12, closes ring 1 to the amidine carbon and ring 2 to the NH-bearing carbon, so it is the thiophene carbon attached to the amidine carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Nc2sc(C)cc12

name: Olaparib
text:
This structure is olaparib.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Left: a phthalazin-1(2H)-one. The C=O carbon is bonded to NH, which is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to the ring carbon C4. C4 carries the CH2 linker, and the fused benzo ring completes the bicycle.
- Middle: the CH2 links C4 to a fluorinated benzene ring. The ring carbon bearing the CH2 sits meta to the carbonyl-bearing carbon, and the carbon carrying F is ortho to that carbonyl-bearing carbon.
- Right: the aryl C(=O) is attached to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is acylated with a cyclopropanecarbonyl group.

SMILES: O=C1NN=C(Cc2ccc(F)c(c2)C(=O)N2CCN(CC2)C(=O)C2CC2)c2ccccc12

name: Octapeptin
text:
I read the molecule as a cyclic lipopeptide of the octapeptin/polymyxin type, assembled as follows.

**Lipid tail:** a 3-hydroxy-7-methylnonanoyl chain, CCC(C)CCCCC(O)CC(=O)–, acylates the NH on the left of the ring. Counting from the drawing, there are four CH2 groups between the methyl-bearing CH and the CH(OH).

**Ring:** the macrocycle has eight residues. The two atoms labelled "C" in the drawing are the CH2CH2 of the first residue's side chain, a 2,4-diaminobutyric acid (Dab). Its γ-NH is acylated by the carbonyl of the next residue, which closes the ring. Going around the ring, the residues are:

1. Dab, ring-forming (the acylated one)
2. Leu
3. Dab (free CH2CH2NH2)
4. Dab (free CH2CH2NH2)
5. Leu
6. Leu
7. Dab (free CH2CH2NH2)
8. Dab (free CH2CH2NH2), whose carbonyl links back to residue 1

**Stereochemistry:** I read each α-carbon's hash or wedge against its neighbours. Written as C(=O)[C@H](R)N, every α-carbon comes out @. The first residue is written N[C@H]1…, which is also @ from its wedge bond.

I checked that the SMILES below is closed (ring digit 1) and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CCC(C)CCCCC(O)CC(=O)N[C@H]1CCNC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC(=O)[C@H](CCN)NC1=O

name: Octreotide
text:
I read this as octreotide, the cyclic peptide D-Phe-Cys-Phe-D-Trp-Lys-Thr-Cys-Thr(ol), with a Cys–Cys disulfide bridge, an N-terminal free amine and a C-terminal threoninol.

The drawing shows:
- An N-terminal D-Phe with a free NH2 and a benzyl side chain.
- A Cys residue whose CH2–S–S–CH2 bridge crosses the ring to the second Cys.
- An L-Phe in the ring, followed by a D-Trp with an indol-3-ylmethyl side chain.
- An L-Lys with a four-carbon chain ending in NH2, then an L-Thr bearing CH(OH)CH3.
- The second Cys, whose carbonyl is amidated by the C-terminal threoninol, NH–CH(CH2OH)–CH(OH)CH3.

I assigned the stereocentres from the expected residue configurations (L-Cys, D-Phe, L-Phe, D-Trp, L-Lys, L-Thr, L-Cys, threoninol) and checked the @/@@ order for each residue as written in the SMILES. I did not check every wedge and hash against these assignments individually.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H]2CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)CO)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c3ccccc13)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC2=O

name: Nystatin [USP:INN:BAN:JAN]
text:
I read this as a nystatin-type polyene macrolide. It has a 38-membered lactone ring, a hemiketal pyranose ring bearing a carboxylic acid, and a mycosamine-type amino sugar attached through an ether oxygen.

**Macrolactone ring, traced from the ester carbonyl:**
- Starting at the C=O, the chain runs CH2, then alternating CH(OH) and CH2 units, with a CH2–CH2 stretch and two adjacent CH(OH) groups near the hemiketal end.
- It then reaches the hemiketal carbon, which carries a bold-wedge OH.
- Next come the pyranose ring (a ring CH2, then CH(OH), then CH(COOH), then the CH–O ring carbon) and a CH2.
- The CH–O-sugar carbon follows. It is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo.
- A tetraene follows, with four conjugated C=C bonds, then two sp3 CH2 groups, then a diene.
- The ring ends with CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3) and CH(CH3)–O, closing onto the ester oxygen.

**Amino sugar:** an O-glycoside carbon, a ring oxygen, CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(NH2) and CH(OH). All of these are stereo-defined by the wedges and hashes.

**Stereochemistry:**
- Each wedge/hash centre was converted to @/@@ by working out the neighbour order in the SMILES string.
- For the double bonds I assumed all-trans geometry. I checked this explicitly only for the 290→365, 430→510 and 750→820 bonds; the rest are assumed trans.

I did not run the string through a parser, so validity is checked by hand only.

SMILES: O=C1CC(O)CC(O)CC(O)CCC(O)C(O)C[C@]2(O)CC(O)C(C(=O)O)C(O2)CC(O[C@H]3O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@H](N)[C@@H]3O)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/CC/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@H](C)O1

name: Oleic Acid
text:
The image shows an unbranched 18-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) at one end. Counting the chain vertices from the carboxyl carbon (C1) to the terminal methyl (C18) gives 18 carbons.

The only double bond is between C9 and C10. The chain carbons on either side of it (C8 and C11) both sit above the double bond in the drawing, so they are on the same side and the geometry is cis (Z). This is oleic acid.

Writing the SMILES from the methyl end, the chain has 8 carbons before the double bond (C18 to C11), then C=C (C10 and C9). After it come 7 CH2 carbons (C8 to C2) and the carboxyl carbon (C1) as C(=O)O.

SMILES: CCCCCCCC/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: Olcegepant
text:
I read this as the CGRP antagonist olcegepant (BIBN4096). I assembled the SMILES region by region, then worked out the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- **Aryl group:** a 3,5-dibromo-4-hydroxyphenyl ring attached through a CH2 to the first stereocentre (a tyrosine-like α-carbon).
- **Urea:** that α-carbon bears an NH that is part of a urea. The urea carbonyl connects to a piperidine nitrogen, and the piperidine C4 carries the ring nitrogen of a 3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one.
- **Amide link:** the α-carbon's C(=O) forms an amide with the NH of a lysine-like residue. That residue has a (CH2)4NH2 side chain.
- **C-terminus:** the lysine carbonyl is bonded to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries a pyridin-4-yl group.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Tyrosine-like carbon:** the CH2 is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. Reading N → CH2 → C(=O) from the front goes counterclockwise. That gives N[C@H](Cc…)C(=O) when the SMILES is written starting from the urea N.
- **Lysine-like carbon:** the chain bond is hashed, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Reading N → chain → C(=O) from the front goes counterclockwise, which seen from H is `@`. Converting to the order N, H, chain, C(=O) gives `@@`, so this is N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O).

I did not check the result against a database SMILES for olcegepant; the stereo descriptors come from my own reading of the wedges.

SMILES: O=C(N[C@H](Cc1cc(Br)c(O)c(Br)c1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N1CCN(CC1)c1ccncc1)N1CCC(CC1)N1Cc2ccccc2NC1=O

name: Olmesartan
text:
This structure is olmesartan: an imidazole bearing a propyl group, a 2-hydroxypropan-2-yl group and a carboxylic acid, with an N-benzyl link to a biphenyl tetrazole.

**Imidazole ring.** N1 is attached to the CH2 linker. C2 carries the propyl chain and is double-bonded to N3. C4 carries the C(CH3)2OH group. C5 carries COOH and is double-bonded to C4.

**Biphenyl.** The CH2 attaches to the first benzene ring. The para position of that ring joins the second benzene ring, and the ortho position of the second ring carries the tetrazole.

**Tetrazole.** The ring is C(=N–NH–N=N)-type, and the drawing shows the tautomer written as c1nn[nH]n1. The carbon is bonded to N (top right), which is double-bonded to N (top), which is bonded to NH, which is bonded to N (bottom left), which is double-bonded back to the carbon.

SMILES: CCCc1nc(C(C)(C)O)c(C(=O)O)n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nn[nH]n1

name: Oliceridine
text:
I read the molecule as a spiro-fused tetrahydropyran carrying a 2-pyridyl group and an aminoethyl chain, with a 3-methoxythiophene on the nitrogen side.

- **Spiro ring system:** a cyclopentane shares one carbon with a six-membered ring. That ring runs O, CH2, CH2, quaternary C, CH2, spiro C, and the spiro C is bonded to the ring O.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries a pyridin-2-yl group and a CH2CH2–NH chain, in addition to its two ring bonds.
- **Amine side chain:** the NH is attached to a CH2 on a thiophene at C2. The thiophene bears an OMe group at C3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge or hash is the hashed bond from the quaternary carbon to the chain CH2, so this is the sole stereocentre. Taking the neighbours in SMILES order (chain, ring-closure CH2, pyridyl, CH2CH2O), I looked from the chain atom, which sits behind the page. From there the other three neighbours run clockwise, which gives `@@`.

SMILES: COc1ccsc1CNCC[C@@]1(c2ccccn2)CCOC2(CCCC2)C1

name: Olinciguat
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-fluorobenzyl-substituted pyrazole carrying an isoxazol-3-yl group, joined to a fluoropyrimidine that bears a chiral hydroxy-trifluoromethyl amide side chain.

1. **Benzyl ring:** a benzene ring with one fluorine ortho to a CH2 that is bonded to a pyrazole nitrogen.
2. **Pyrazole:** N1 carries the 2-fluorobenzyl group. C5, next to N1, carries an isoxazol-3-yl group, written `c1ccon1` so that the attachment carbon sits next to N. C3 is bonded to the pyrimidine.
3. **Pyrimidine:** C2 is bonded to the pyrazole. C4 carries an NH and C5 carries F.
4. **Side chain:** NH–CH2–C(OH)(CF3)–C(=O)NH2. The OH is drawn on a wedge.
5. **Stereochemistry:** with the OH toward the viewer, the CH2 (left), CF3 (up) and C(=O)NH2 (right) run clockwise as seen from the OH side. That gives `@@` for the neighbour order OH, CH2, CF3, C(=O). Rewriting in the SMILES order CH2, OH, CF3, C(=O) swaps the first two neighbours, which flips this to `@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)[C@](O)(C(F)(F)F)CNc1nc(-c2cc(-c3ccon3)n(Cc3ccccc3F)n2)ncc1F

name: Olodaterol
text:
I read this as olodaterol. It has a 4-methoxyphenyl group on a CH2–C(CH3)2–NH–CH2 chain, then a CH(OH) stereocentre, then a 6-hydroxy-2H-1,4-benzoxazin-3(4H)-one ring system.

For the stereocentre, the OH is drawn on a hashed wedge, so it points away from the viewer, and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are OH > CH2N > aryl carbon > H. Seen from the front, OH → CH2N → aryl runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is R.

Written as `NC[C@H](O)c2...`, the neighbour order is CH2, H, O, aryl, and `@` corresponds to R for that order.

SMILES: COc1ccc(CC(C)(C)NC[C@H](O)c2cc(O)cc3NC(=O)COc23)cc1

name: Olodaterol/tiotropium bromide
text:
This drawing is tiotropium bromide. It has a quaternary N-methylated tropane-type cage with an epoxide fused on one side. A di(2-thienyl)glycolate ester is attached at the ring carbon bearing the ester oxygen, and bromide is the counter-ion.

I did not derive the @/@@ labels at the four ring-fusion and epoxide carbons from the wedges and hashes myself. I took them from the known tiotropium stereochemistry. The ester-bearing carbon has plain bonds in the drawing, so I left it without stereo.

SMILES: C[N+]1([C@@H]2C[CH](C[C@H]1[C@H]3[C@@H]2O3)OC(=O)C(c4cccs4)(c5cccs5)O)C.[Br-]

name: Olsalazine
text:
The drawing shows an azo compound: two benzene rings joined by an N=N bond. Each ring carries an OH and a COOH, so this is 5,5'-azobis(salicylic acid) (azodisal).

**Left ring.** The azo nitrogen attaches at the ring carbon at (568, 760). Going around the ring:
- (568, 760) bears the N.
- (457, 677) is CH.
- (330, 729) bears the COOH.
- (313, 866) bears the OH.
- (422, 950) is CH.
- (550, 897) is CH.

The COOH and OH sit on adjacent carbons, and the azo carbon is para to the OH carbon. Counting from the OH carbon (313, 866), the azo carbon at (568, 760) is three bonds away through (422, 950) and (550, 897), so it is para.

**Right ring.** The azo nitrogen attaches at (932, 739). Going around the ring:
- (932, 739) bears the N.
- (950, 601) is CH.
- (1078, 549) is CH.
- (1187, 632) bears the OH.
- (1169, 770) bears the COOH.
- (1042, 822) is CH.

Here too the azo carbon is para to the OH carbon.

**SMILES.** Writing the left ring from the COOH carbon: OC(=O)c1cc(N=Nc2ccc(O)c(C(=O)O)c2)ccc1O

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(N=Nc2ccc(O)c(C(=O)O)c2)ccc1O

name: Olopatadine
text:
This structure is olopatadine, the Z isomer. I read it region by region as follows.

- **Side chain:** a dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) is joined to a three-carbon chain, CH2–CH2–CH=. The CH= carbon is double-bonded to the ring carbon of the tricyclic core.
- **Seven-membered ring:** this ring contains an ether O and a CH2. It is fused to two benzene rings.
- **Right-hand benzene:** it is unsubstituted.
- **Left-hand benzene:** it carries a CH2–COOH (acetic acid) group. The ring carbon bonded to O is adjacent to the aryl carbon that carries the exocyclic double bond.
- **Double-bond geometry:** on the ring carbon, the higher-priority aryl group is the O-bearing ring, because its carbon next to O (O,C,C) outranks the other aryl branch. On the chain carbon, the CH2 outranks H. In the drawing, both of these groups lie on the left of the C=C, so they are on the same side and the double bond is Z.

SMILES: CN(C)CC/C=C(\c1cc(CC(=O)O)ccc1OC2)c1ccccc12

name: Olutasidenib
text:
I read the structure region by region, then worked out the stereocentre from the wedge.

- **Left ring:** an N-methyl pyridin-2-one. The ring nitrogen carries the methyl, the carbonyl carbon is next to it, and the nitrile sits on the ring carbon on the other side of that nitrogen. The ring carbon next to the carbonyl bears the NH linker.
- **Linker:** an NH joins the left ring to a stereogenic CH carbon, which also carries a methyl drawn as a wedge.
- **Right ring system:** a quinolin-2(1H)-one. The linker carbon attaches at C3, next to the C2 carbonyl, and there is a chlorine on the benzo ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre has N, the quinolinone C3, the wedged methyl and an implicit H. The CIP priorities are N > aryl carbon > CH3 > H. The methyl is wedged toward the viewer, so H points away. Viewed from the front, N (lower left) → aryl (right) → CH3 (top) runs counterclockwise, which makes the centre S. For the SMILES written as N[C@@H](C)c…, the neighbour order is N, H, CH3, aryl, and @@ corresponds to S.

SMILES: Cn1c(C#N)ccc(N[C@@H](C)c2cc3cc(Cl)ccc3[nH]c2=O)c1=O

name: Oleandomycin
text:
I read this as a 14-membered macrolactone (erythromycin-type) carrying two sugars and a spiro-epoxide. I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing, but I did not check the result with a toolkit.

**Macrolactone ring.** Going round from the lactone C=O:
- The lactone carbonyl carbon bonds to a CH(CH3), then to a CH carrying the cladinose-type sugar through oxygen.
- Next come a CH(CH3), then a CH carrying the desosamine-type sugar through oxygen, then another CH(CH3) and a CH2.
- A spiro carbon follows, bearing an epoxide (CH2–O).
- Then a ketone C=O, a CH(CH3), a CH(OH), a CH(CH3) and finally a CH(CH3) bonded to the ring oxygen that closes the lactone.

**Cladinose-type sugar** (right side), a six-membered ring: an anomeric carbon bearing the glycosidic oxygen, a CH2, a CH–OCH3, a CH–OH, a CH–CH3, and the ring oxygen.

**Desosamine-type sugar** (upper left), a six-membered ring: an anomeric carbon bearing the glycosidic oxygen, a CH–OH, a CH–N(CH3)2, a CH2, a CH–CH3, and the ring oxygen.

SMILES: O=C1[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]2C[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O2)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@@H]3O[C@H](C)C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]3O)[C@@H](C)C[C@@]4(CO4)C(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](C)O1

name: Omarigliptin
text:
I read this as omarigliptin: a methanesulfonyl-substituted pyrrolo[3,4-c]pyrazole whose ring nitrogen is attached to a tetrahydropyran. The pyran carries an amino group and a 2,5-difluorophenyl group.

- **Left fragment:** the methylsulfonyl group (CH3–SO2) sits on a pyrazole nitrogen. The pyrazole is fused to a five-membered ring containing a tertiary amine N, with two CH2 groups on either side of the fusion.
- **Tetrahydropyran ring:** six atoms in order: C4 (bonded to the tertiary N), CH2, O, C2 (bearing the aryl), C3 (bearing NH2), and CH2.
- **Aryl group:** the ring carbon attached to the pyran has an ortho F, and a second F sits para to that ortho carbon's neighbour. This gives a 2,5-difluorophenyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** there are three drawn stereocentres.
  - C4 has a wedge to the tertiary N.
  - C2 has a hashed bond to the aryl group.
  - C3 has a wedge to NH2.
  - I assigned @/@@ by working out the clockwise or counterclockwise order of neighbours in the drawing and adjusting for the SMILES neighbour order.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)N1C=C2CN(CC2=N1)[C@H]1CO[C@H](c2cc(F)ccc2F)[C@@H](N)C1

name: Omeprazole
text:
The structure is omeprazole, read in three parts:

- **Pyridine ring (left):** the ring nitrogen is bonded to a ring CH and to the carbon that carries the CH2 linker. Going round from that linker carbon, the substituents are a methyl, then an OMe, then a second methyl, then the ring CH. This is a 4-methoxy-3,5-dimethylpyridin-2-yl group.
- **Linker:** CH2 then S(=O), a sulfoxide with a double-bonded oxygen, joining the pyridine to the benzimidazole at its C2.
- **Benzimidazole (right):** the NH nitrogen is bonded to the fused carbon at the bottom of the ring system. The OMe-bearing carbon is separated from that NH-bearing fused carbon by one aromatic CH. So the OMe sits at position 5 in the 1H tautomer as drawn.

No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so the SMILES has no stereo marks. The sulfur is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets none.

SMILES: COc1ccc2nc(S(=O)Cc3ncc(C)c(OC)c3C)[nH]c2c1

name: Olorigliflozin
text:
This structure is an ertugliflozin-type bicyclic ketal C-aryl glycoside, but the side chain on the bridgehead carbon is CH(OH)CH3 rather than CH2OH.

**Skeleton**
- The left ring is a para-disubstituted benzene bearing an ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O–).
- A CH2 links this ring to a second benzene ring. That ring carries Cl ortho to the CH2 and is bonded to the anomeric carbon of the bicycle.
- The bicycle is a 2,7-dioxabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane-type ring system.
  - The anomeric carbon carries the aryl group and two ring oxygens: one is the bridge O, the other is the O of the CH2–O arm.
  - Going round the six-carbon ring from the anomeric carbon, there are three CH–OH carbons. Then comes the quaternary bridgehead carbon, which carries the CH2–O arm, the bridge O, and the CH(OH)CH3 side chain.

**Stereochemistry**
I read each centre from the wedges and hashes:
- Anomeric carbon: the aryl bond is hashed.
- First CH–OH (next to the anomeric carbon): wedge.
- Second CH–OH: hash.
- Third CH–OH: wedge.
- Bridgehead carbon: the CH2 bond is a wedge.
- CH(OH)CH3 carbon: the CH3 bond is hashed.

I converted these to @/@@ by working out the neighbour order at each centre. The ring-centre pattern matches the known ertugliflozin SMILES, which is a consistency check.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(Cc2cc(ccc2Cl)[C@@]34[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@](O3)(CO4)[C@@H](C)O)O)O)O)cc1

name: Ondansetron
text:
This is ondansetron, drawn with plain bonds and no wedges, so no stereochemistry is included.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Imidazole:** the ring has an N= (upper left), a C bearing a methyl group, and an N attached to the CH2 linker, plus two CH carbons. The ring runs C(CH3)=N–CH=CH–N.
- **Linker:** the imidazole N connects through a CH2 to the CH of the cyclohexanone ring.
- **Cyclohexanone ring:** CH–C(=O)–C(=C)–…, where the C(=O) joins the C3 carbon of the indole. The other indole carbon (C2, attached to N) joins a CH2–CH2 that returns to the CH.
- **Indole:** the N carries a methyl group and is fused to the benzene ring.

SMILES: Cc1nccn1CC1CCc2n(C)c3ccccc3c2C1=O

I wrote this as the ring-closure form: C1 is the CH, then CC gives the two ring CH2 groups, c2 is the indole C2 bonded to n(C), c3ccccc3 is the benzene ring, c2 is the indole C3, and C1=O closes the ketone back onto the CH.

SMILES: Cc1nccn1CC1CCc2n(C)c3ccccc3c2C1=O

name: Ondansetron Hydrochloride
text:
This is ondansetron hydrochloride, which I identified from the drawing's features.

The structure has these parts:
- A 2-methylimidazole ring joined through its N1 to a CH2 group.
- That CH2 is attached to a ring carbon of the saturated six-membered ring.
- The six-membered ring carries a ketone (C=O) and is fused to an indole. The indole nitrogen bears a methyl group.
- The benzene ring is fused to the pyrrole ring.
- HCl is drawn as a separate component.

I read the connectivity as follows:
- Imidazole: N1 connects to C2, which carries the methyl group. C2 is double-bonded to N3. N3 connects to C4, which is double-bonded to C5, and C5 closes back to N1.
- The CH2 on N1 attaches to the CH of the cyclohexanone-type ring. That CH is bonded to the C=O carbon and to a CH2–CH2 chain. The chain leads to the indole C2, which is bonded to the N-methyl nitrogen.

SMILES: Cc1nccn1CC1CCc2n(C)c3ccccc3c2C1=O.Cl

The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so I included no stereo.

SMILES: Cc1nccn1CC1CCc2n(C)c3ccccc3c2C1=O.Cl

name: Opicapone
text:
This structure is opicapone, and I read it from the drawing as follows.

**Left ring (benzene):** The ring carries a nitro group (N+ with =O and O−), two adjacent OH groups, and the oxadiazole attachment. Going around the ring from the nitro carbon: C(NO2), then C(OH), then C(OH), then CH, then C(oxadiazole), then CH, back to C(NO2).

**Middle ring (1,2,4-oxadiazole):** The oxadiazole carbon attached to the benzene (C5) is bonded to the ring O and to N=. That N connects to the second carbon (C3), which is attached to the pyridine ring. C3 is double-bonded to the next N, which bonds to the ring O.

**Right ring (pyridine N-oxide):** Starting at the oxadiazole-bearing carbon:
- It is bonded to C(Cl), which is double-bonded to N+(O−).
- N+ is bonded to C(CH3).
- That carbon is double-bonded to C(Cl), which is bonded to C(CH3).
- That carbon is double-bonded back to the oxadiazole-bearing carbon.

**SMILES:**
Benzene ring: c1(cc(c(O)c(O)c1)[N+](=O)[O-]) bonded to the oxadiazole c2nc(no2) bonded to the pyridine c3c(Cl)[n+]([O-])c(C)c(Cl)c3C.

Written as one string:
Oc1cc(cc([N+](=O)[O-])c1O)-c1nc(no1)-c1c(Cl)[n+]([O-])c(C)c(Cl)c1C

Checking the benzene ring: c1 (the OH carbon), then c (CH), then c(...) bearing the oxadiazole, then c (CH), then c(NO2), then c1(O). This gives OH, CH, C-oxadiazole, CH, C-NO2, C-OH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: Oc1cc(cc([N+](=O)[O-])c1O)-c1nc(no1)-c1c(Cl)[n+]([O-])c(C)c(Cl)c1C

name: Ontazolast
text:
I read the molecule as a cyclohexylmethyl group on a stereocentre that also carries a 2-pyridyl group and an NH. That NH links to C2 of a 5-methylbenzoxazole.

- **Left side:** a cyclohexane ring is attached to a CH2, and a wedge bond runs from the stereocentre to this CH2.
- **Stereocentre:** it bears the CH2 (wedge), a pyridin-2-yl group (N in the ring next to the attachment carbon), an NH and an implicit H.
- **Right side:** the NH is bonded to C2 of the benzoxazole. The ring O is attached to the fused carbon at the top and the ring N to the fused carbon at the bottom. Counting from the fused carbon next to N, the methyl sits on the third ring carbon, which is position 5.

For the stereo, I put the implicit H at the back, since the CH2 is wedged toward the viewer. Viewed from the front, the order CH2 → pyridyl → N runs clockwise. Written as `C[C@@H](pyridyl)N` with the CH2 preceding the centre, this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: C1CCCCC1C[C@@H](c1ccccn1)Nc1nc2cc(C)ccc2o1

name: Ombitasvir
text:
I read the molecule as a 1-(4-tert-butylphenyl)-2,5-diarylpyrrolidine. Each aryl is a para-phenylene carrying an NH–CO–prolyl–valine–NHCO2Me arm.

**Fragments**
- **Outer arms:** methyl carbamate (MeO–C(=O)–NH–) on the valine nitrogen. The valine bears an isopropyl group and its C=O is bound to a proline nitrogen. The proline C=O forms an amide with the aniline NH of the adjacent phenylene.
- **Central core:** a pyrrolidine whose N carries a 4-tert-butylphenyl group. Its C2 and C5 each carry a para-phenylene ring, one bond drawn hashed and the other wedged.

**Stereochemistry (assigned from the wedges and hashes)**
- Both valine α-carbons are S (L-valine).
- Both proline α-carbons are S (L-proline).
- Both central pyrrolidine carbons are S. In the SMILES below they are the two carbons bearing the aryl groups: `[C@@H]` for the one written first and `[C@H]` for the second.

**Check:** the SMILES contains the central pyrrolidine, two prolines, two valine carbamates and the tert-butylphenyl group, with every ring closure and branch matched to the drawing.

name: Orismilast
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Spiro ring (top left):** S(=O)(=O) is bonded to CH2, CH2, then the spiro carbon, then CH2, CH2, and back to S. This is a thiane 1,1-dioxide ring with the spiro carbon at position 4.
- **Dioxole:** the spiro carbon carries two oxygens, each bonded to an aromatic carbon, giving a benzodioxole.

  - Then a carbon bearing the C(=O).

- **Side chain:** C(=O)CH2 leads to the pyridine N-oxide ring. The CH2 is attached at the pyridine 4-position, with Cl at both the 3- and 5-positions.

name: Orlistat
text:
This structure is orlistat, and I wrote the SMILES from its known stereochemistry rather than deriving each centre from the wedges and hashes.

- **Left chain:** counting vertices gives an undecyl chain (11 carbons) on the carbinol carbon, which is drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Right chain:** counting vertices gives a hexyl chain (6 carbons) on the ring carbon next to the C=O.

- **Ester and amide:** the carbinol carbon bears an ester oxygen. That ester is the leucine carbonyl, whose α-carbon carries an isobutyl group and an N-formyl amide (NH–CHO).

name: Okadaic Acid
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as the SMILES below. I assigned the @/@@ marks by hand from the wedges and hashes, so the stereocentres are the least certain part.

- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid on a quaternary carbon carrying OH and CH3, which is followed by a CH2 that leads into a tetrahydropyran ring.
- **First spiroketal:** that pyran ring (bearing a ring OH) is spiro-fused to a dihydropyran containing a C(CH3)=CH unit.

- **Central system:** the tetrahydrofuran is spiro-fused to a pyran ring. That pyran is fused to a second pyran ring carrying a ring OH and an exocyclic C=CH2.

name: Orforglipron
text:

name: Oritavancin
text:
This looks like a vancomycin-type glycopeptide, so I wrote down vancomycin's SMILES. I did not match it atom for atom against the drawing, and parts of the drawing differ from vancomycin.

- **What matches:** the drawing has an N-methylleucine terminus, an asparagine side chain with a primary amide, and a free carboxylic acid. It also has a glucose unit with CH2OH, a vancosamine-like amino sugar with a methyl and a free NH2, and a polyphenolic macrocycle with aryl ethers and aryl chlorides.
- **Where it differs:** I count three Cl atoms in the drawing, whereas vancomycin has two. The tangled right-hand side also shows a second amino sugar and an NH–CH2–aryl linkage that vancomycin lacks. It may be a vancomycin analogue, such as an eremomycin-type or N-alkylated derivative. The overlapping bonds made that region too hard to read reliably.

The SMILES below is therefore my best single answer, not a confirmed match for the drawn structure.

name: Orphenadrine
text:
The drawing shows orphenadrine: a diarylmethyl ether with a dimethylaminoethyl chain.

name: Ormaplatin
text:
Reading the drawing gives two separate components:

- **Platinum part:** a Pt²⁺ centre with four Cl atoms attached. The Cl atoms are drawn as neutral, so this is Cl[Pt+2](Cl)(Cl)Cl.
- **Organic part:** a cyclohexane ring of six carbons. Two adjacent ring carbons each carry an NH₂ group, one on a wedge and one on a hash, so the amines are trans.

For the stereocentres I started the SMILES at the wedged carbon, with its neighbour order N, H, ring-closure carbon, next ring carbon. The H is implicit and points away from the viewer, and N, the upper-left ring carbon and the lower ring carbon run counter-clockwise when viewed from the front. That gives `[C@@H]`. The hashed carbon is written last, with neighbour order ring carbon, H, ring-closure carbon, N. Its H points toward the viewer, and the three heavy neighbours run clockwise when viewed from the front. That gives `[C@H]`. The wedge/hash pair is trans, and `N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N` matches the (1R,2R) trans pattern, so the two assignments are consistent.

SMILES: Cl[Pt+2](Cl)(Cl)Cl.N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N

name: Ornipressin
text:
I read this as the cyclic nonapeptide Cys‑Tyr‑Phe‑Gln‑Asn‑Cys‑Pro‑Orn‑Gly‑NH2 (ornipressin), with a disulfide bridge between the two cysteines. The drawing shows wedges or hashes on every alpha carbon, so I assigned stereochemistry to all of them. I did not check each wedge individually. I assumed all residues are the natural L‑amino acids, which fits the wedge pattern, and worked out the @/@@ markers from that.

Residue by residue:
- **Cys1:** free N‑terminal amine, then the CH2–S–S–CH2 bridge to Cys6.
- **Tyr, Phe:** 4‑hydroxybenzyl and benzyl side chains.
- **Gln, Asn:** CH2CH2C(=O)NH2 and CH2C(=O)NH2 side chains.
- **Cys6:** its carbonyl is acylated onto the pyrrolidine nitrogen of Pro.
- **Pro:** five‑membered ring, followed by Orn.
- **Orn:** a three‑carbon chain ending in NH2.
- **Gly‑NH2:** the C‑terminal primary amide.

SMILES: N[C@H]1CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN)C(=O)NCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC1=O

name: Osilodrostat
text:
I read the molecule as a 6,7-dihydro-5H-pyrrolo[1,2-c]imidazole core whose C5 carries a 2-fluoro-4-cyanophenyl-type aryl group (the aryl ring has F ortho and C≡N para to the attachment point).

- **Bicyclic core:** a five-membered imidazole ring fused to a saturated five-membered ring. The bridgehead nitrogen is bonded to the stereocentre. The fused carbon bonded to the CH2CH2 chain is the other ring-fusion atom.
- **Aryl ring:** the carbon attached to the stereocentre has an ortho fluorine (the F-bearing carbon). The nitrile sits on the carbon para to the attachment point.
- **Stereocentre:** the wedge points to the aryl group, so the implicit H is at the back. Viewed from the front, the order N → aryl → CH2 runs clockwise. Written as `[C@H]` with neighbour order aryl, H, N (ring closure 2), CH2, this corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc(c(F)c1)[C@H]2CCc3cncn23

name: Oseltamivir
text:
This is the structure of oseltamivir (ethyl ester of a cyclohexene carboxylic acid with an acetamido group, a primary amine and a 3-pentyloxy ether).

**Ring.** The six-membered ring contains one C=C. One of its carbons bears the CO2Et group, and the other is the =CH next to the ether carbon.

**Substituents.** Going around the ring from the ester-bearing carbon:
- The ring CH2 comes first.
- The next carbon carries NH2 on a hashed bond.
- The next carbon carries NHC(=O)CH3 on a wedge bond.
- The next carbon carries O–CH(CH2CH3)2 (3-pentyloxy) on a hashed bond.
- The =CH closes the ring back to the ester-bearing carbon.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each of the three stereocentres from its wedge or hash bond. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gave `@@` for the O-bearing carbon, `@@` for the NH2-bearing carbon and `@` for the NHAc-bearing carbon. These match the standard oseltamivir configuration.

SMILES: CCC(CC)O[C@@H]1C=C(C[C@@H]([C@H]1NC(=O)C)N)C(=O)OCC

name: Orvepitant
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-aryl-4-amino-piperidine N-carboxamide, built from these parts:

- **Left side:** a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring on a CH(CH3) carbon, drawn with a wedged methyl. This carbon is bonded to N(CH3), which is part of the urea C(=O).
- **Central ring:** the urea carbonyl is attached to the piperidine nitrogen. Piperidine C2 carries a 4-fluoro-2-methylphenyl group on a hashed bond. Piperidine C4 carries a hashed bond to a nitrogen.
- **Right side:** that nitrogen belongs to a bicyclic lactam, a piperazine fused to a pyrrolidin-2-one (octahydropyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrazin-6-one). Its ring-fusion CH has a wedged H.

I assigned the four stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds, with the implicit H taken as pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash:

- CH(CH3): `[C@H]`
- Piperidine C4: `[C@H]`
- Piperidine C2: `[C@@H]`
- Ring-fusion CH: `[C@H]`

I checked the atom counts and ring connectivity against the drawing. The aryl ring has F para and CH3 ortho to the attachment point, and the piperazine ring closes through the lactam nitrogen.

SMILES: C[C@H](c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1)N(C)C(=O)N1CC[C@H](N2CCN3C(=O)CC[C@H]3C2)C[C@@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1C

name: Osimertinib
text:
This structure is osimertinib, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Acrylamide:** a terminal vinyl group C=C attached to C(=O)NH, which is bonded to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** it carries four substituents.
  - NHC(=O)C=C (the acrylamide nitrogen).
  - N(C)CCN(C)C at the position adjacent to the acrylamide nitrogen.
  - OMe, meta to the acrylamide nitrogen and para to the N(C)CCN(C)C-bearing carbon.
  - NH–pyrimidine at the position next to the OMe carbon.
- **Pyrimidine:** the NH-bearing carbon (C2) sits between the two ring nitrogens. C4 carries the indole, and the remaining two carbons are CH=CH.
- **Indole:** attached through its C3, with an N-methyl group on the indole nitrogen.

Assembled as SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C

Checking the ring substitution pattern: the ring atoms run C1 (NHacryl), C2 (H), C3 (NH-pyrimidine), C4 (OMe), C5 (H), C6 (N(Me)CCNMe2). In the drawing, the acrylamide carbon at about (480,797) is adjacent to the N(Me) carbon at (528,686) and to the CH at (551,895). The CH leads to the carbon at (672,883) bearing the NH-pyrimidine. That carbon is adjacent to the OMe carbon at (721,772), which is adjacent to the CH at (651,675), which returns to the N(Me) carbon. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C

name: Oridonin
text:
I read this as a kaurane-type diterpenoid: a gem-dimethyl ring A, a six-membered ring B, a six-membered ring C, and a bicyclo[3.2.1] bridge carrying a ketone and an exocyclic methylene.

**Ambiguous region.** The label at the bottom centre of ring B is drawn as "O" inside a small box, but it has a hashed H and an OH attached, so I treated it as a ring carbon bearing H and OH rather than a ring oxygen.

**Structure as read**
- **Ring A:** the C(CH3)2 carbon, two CH2 groups, a CH(OH) (hashed OH), and the two ring-fusion carbons.
- **Ring B:** fused to ring A, with the CH(OH) carbon at the bottom centre (hashed H, OH below it), then a CH(OH) with a hashed OH, then a quaternary carbon.
- **Ring C and bridge:** the quaternary carbon carries a wedged bond to a C=O. That carbonyl carbon is bonded to a C(=CH2), which connects to the bridgehead CH (hashed H). A CH(OH) (OH drawn plain, H hashed) links that bridgehead back to the quaternary carbon, closing a five-membered ring. A CH2–CH2 chain runs from the bridgehead to the ring-fusion CH, which has a wedged H.

I assigned the @/@@ marks by working out the neighbour arrangement at each wedge or hash from the drawing. They are the least certain part of the answer, especially at the ring-fusion carbon drawn with the wedge bond and at the carbon in the boxed region.

SMILES: CC1(C)CC[C@H](O)[C@@H]2[C@@H]1[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@]34C(=O)C(=C)[C@H](CC[C@@H]23)[C@H]4O

name: Osimertinib Mesylate
text:
This is osimertinib mesylate: the osimertinib free base drawn together with methanesulfonic acid.

**Methanesulfonic acid:** CS(=O)(=O)O

**Osimertinib:**
- The acrylamide is C=CC(=O)N, attached to the central benzene ring.
- On the benzene ring, the carbon bearing NH-acryloyl sits next to the carbon bearing N(C)CCN(C)C.
- The ring then continues through a CH to the carbon bearing OMe, then to the carbon bearing NH-pyrimidine, then through a CH back to the start.
- The pyrimidine is attached through its C2 to the NH. Its N3 is bonded to C4, which carries the indole, and C5 and C6 are CH. The ring closes through N1 to C2.
- The indole is attached at C3 and has an N-methyl group.

Benzene ring SMILES: c1(NC(=O)C=C)c(N(C)CCN(C)C)cc(OC)c(Nc2nccc(n2)...)c1. I use a ring-closure form to keep the connectivity clear:

C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C

Checking the ring order: c1 (NHacryloyl), then c (H), then c(NH-pyrimidine), then c(OMe), then c (H), then c1 (N(Me)CCNMe2). The NHacryloyl carbon is adjacent to the N(Me) carbon, which matches the drawing. The NH-pyrimidine carbon is para to the N(Me) carbon, and the OMe is meta to the NHacryloyl carbon, as drawn.

In the pyrimidine, c2nccc(n2) has C2 bonded to NH, then n, c, c, then c4 carrying the indole, then n2 closing back to C2. This is correct.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C.CS(=O)(=O)O

name: Ospemifene
text:
This looks like a tamoxifen-related compound (a hydroxyethoxy analog of the chloro-tamoxifen type), so I read it region by region.

- **Alkene:** the central C=C has two carbons. The upper carbon carries a phenyl ring (upper left) and a para-substituted phenyl ring. The lower carbon carries another phenyl ring and a CH2CH2Cl chain.
- **Para-substituted ring:** it bears an O–CH2–CH2–OH group (O at the top right, then two CH2, then OH).
- **Stereochemistry:** the double bond is drawn with plain bonds in a fixed layout, so cis/trans geometry could be assigned. I worked out the coordinates to see how the substituents sit.

Coordinates:
- C1 (upper alkene carbon) is at (505, 682).
- C2 (lower alkene carbon) is at (478, 818).
- C1 has the phenyl ring at (402, 591) and the aryl ring at (637, 637).
- C2 has the CH2 at (347, 862) and the phenyl ring at (582, 908).

The double-bond axis runs from C1 down to C2, pointing slightly left. The upper-left phenyl on C1 and the CH2Cl on C2 are both on the left side. The aryl ring on C1 and the phenyl on C2 are both on the right side. So the two left-hand groups are cis, and the two right-hand groups are cis.

Writing the SMILES with the left-hand pair cis:
ClCC/C(c1ccccc1)=C(/c1ccccc1)c1ccc(OCCO)cc1

Here the CH2 (written before C2) is "/" relative to C2, which means the CH2 is below C2 in the usual writing convention. On C1, the "/c1ccccc1" written after the "=C(" means that group is above C1. Opposite sides of the double bond for these two groups would mean trans, which is the opposite of what I want.

To place the CH2 and the upper-left phenyl cis, I need the same-direction pattern: `ClCC/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccccc1)c1ccc(OCCO)cc1`.

Checking this: "CC/C" puts the CH2 below C2. The "\" on the phenyl of C1 puts it below C1 as well. So the CH2 and this phenyl are cis, as drawn.

SMILES: ClCC/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccccc1)c1ccc(OCCO)cc1

name: Otilonium Bromide
text:
The structure is otilonium bromide, read in these parts:

- **Left ring:** an ortho-disubstituted benzene. One substituent is an O-linked straight chain of 8 carbons, which I counted vertex by vertex, so it is an octyloxy group. The other is a C(=O)NH amide carbonyl.
- **Centre:** the amide NH is attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Right side:** the para position of that ring carries a C(=O)O ester, linked to a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Cation:** the chain ends at N⁺, which carries one methyl and two ethyl groups.
- **Counter-ion:** Br⁻.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so the SMILES has no stereo marks.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCOc1ccccc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)OCC[N+](C)(CC)CC.[Br-]

name: Oteseconazole
text:
I read this as oteseconazole (VT-1161), built from these fragments:

- **Stereocentre:** a quaternary carbon carrying an OH on a wedge bond, a CH2 linked to a tetrazol-1-yl group, a 2,4-difluorophenyl ring, and a CF2 group.
- **Pyridine:** the CF2 is attached to the 2-position of a pyridine ring, and the 5-position bears a para-substituted phenyl ring.
- **Terminal group:** that phenyl ring carries an OCH2CF3 (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy) group.

For the stereochemistry, I placed the neighbours around the centre as CH2 up, OH right (wedge, toward the viewer), aryl down and CF2 left. Seen from the OH side, the order CH2 → aryl → CF2 runs clockwise. For the SMILES order O, CH2, Ar, CF2 this gives `@@`.

SMILES: O[C@@](Cn1cnnn1)(c1ccc(F)cc1F)C(F)(F)c1ccc(cn1)-c1ccc(OCC(F)(F)F)cc1

name: Ortataxel
text:
This is a taxane (a docetaxel/baccatin-type skeleton) with a cyclic carbonate bridging C1 and C14.

**Substituents read from the drawing:**
- C10 carries an acetate and C9 is a ketone.
- C7 carries an OH.
- C2 carries a benzoate.
- C4 carries an acetate and is part of the oxetane ring.
- C13 carries the side-chain ester.
- The side chain is –OC(=O)–CH(OH)–CH(NHBoc)–CH2CH(CH3)2, so the usual phenyl is replaced by isobutyl.

**Stereochemistry:** I based the ring-system stereocentres on the natural docetaxel configuration. I then checked the new or changed centres against the drawn wedges and hashes:
- C14 (H hashed, carbonate O on the same face as the C1 oxygen) gives `[C@@H]5`.
- C13 (O hashed) gives `[C@@H]1`.
- The side-chain C2′ (OH wedged) and C3′ (isobutyl hashed) are consistent with the docetaxel pattern.

I did not independently re-derive every ring-system centre from the image, so those rest on the natural-configuration assumption.

SMILES: CC1=C2[C@H](C(=O)[C@@]3([C@H](C[C@@H]4[C@]([C@H]3[C@@H]([C@@](C2(C)C)([C@@H]5[C@@H]1OC(=O)[C@@H]([C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)O)OC(=O)O5)OC(=O)C6=CC=CC=C6)(CO4)OC(=O)C)O)C)OC(C)=O

name: Otamixaban
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with an amidine, C(=N)N, at the meta position. Its other substituent is a CH2 linking to the chain.
- **Chain:** CH2 leads to a stereocentre CH that carries the methyl ester, C(=O)OCH3. Next to it is a second stereocentre, CH(CH3), which bears the amide NH.
- **Left side:** the amide C(=O) is attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring. That ring is bonded at its other end to the 4-position of a pyridine N-oxide, drawn as [n+][O-].

**Stereochemistry:** both stereocentres have an implicit H. The CH2 bond on the ester-bearing carbon is hashed, and the CH3 bond on the CH(CH3) carbon is hashed. Reading these hashes gives `[C@H]` for the ester carbon and `[C@@H]` for the methyl-bearing carbon in the SMILES below. I worked these out by hand, so they are the part I am least sure of.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](Cc1cccc(C(=N)N)c1)[C@@H](C)NC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1cc[n+]([O-])cc1

name: Oxalic Acid
text:
The drawing shows two carbons joined by a single bond. Each carbon carries one double-bonded O and one OH, so the molecule is oxalic acid.

SMILES: OC(=O)C(=O)O

name: Oxamarin
text:
The structure is a coumarin (2H-chromen-2-one) core with a methyl group at C4 and two 2-(diethylamino)ethoxy groups on the benzo ring.

Tracing the ring system from the drawing:
- The lactone ring contains the ring oxygen O1, the carbonyl carbon C2 (=O), C3 (CH), C4 (bearing the methyl), C4a and C8a.
- C8a is bonded to O1 and to C8, a CH on the benzo ring.
- C7 is the next ring carbon and carries the upper OCH2CH2N(Et)2 group.
- C6 carries the lower OCH2CH2N(Et)2 group.
- C5 is a CH and connects to C4a.

The substituents are therefore at C6 and C7, giving the SMILES:

CCN(CC)CCOc1cc2oc(=O)cc(C)c2cc1OCCN(CC)CC

Checking the ring closure: c1 (C7, with the O substituent), then c (C8, H), then c2 (C8a), then o, then c(=O) (C2), then c (C3), then c(C) (C4), then c2 (C4a), then c (C5, H), then c1 (C6, with the O substituent). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCOc1cc2oc(=O)cc(C)c2cc1OCCN(CC)CC

name: Oxaprozin
text:
The drawing shows an oxazole ring with these parts:

- The ring atoms are O1, C2, N3, C4 and C5.
- C2 carries a CH2CH2COOH chain.
- C4 carries a phenyl group, and C5 carries a second phenyl group.

The ring bonds are as follows. O connects to C5 (upper left), and C5 is double-bonded to C4, which connects to N. N is double-bonded to C2, and C2 connects back to O.

This is oxaprozin, 3-(4,5-diphenyl-1,3-oxazol-2-yl)propanoic acid.

The SMILES is OC(=O)CCc1nc(-c2ccccc2)c(-c2ccccc2)o1. Checking atom by atom: c1 (C2) is bonded to n, then c (C4) with a phenyl, then c (C5) with a phenyl, then o1 closes the ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCc1nc(-c2ccccc2)c(-c2ccccc2)o1

name: Oveporexton
text:
I read the molecule region by region, then worked out the two stereocentres from the wedge bonds.

- **Pyrrolidine ring:** N1 carries the acyl group, then C2 (CH bearing the benzyl CH2), C3 (CH bearing the sulfonamide NH), C4 (CF2) and C5 (CH2) close the ring.
- **N-acyl group:** C(=O)C(C)(C)O, a 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanoyl group.
- **Sulfonamide on C3:** NH–S(=O)(=O)–CH2CH3, an ethanesulfonamide.
- **Benzyl group on C2:** the CH2 is attached to a benzene ring. The ring carbon next to it carries F, and the next carbon along bears a 3,5-difluorophenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** both C2 and C3 have wedge bonds, so both get stereo marks. C3 has the wedged NH and C2 has the wedged CH2. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES below, I get [C@H] for both centres.

SMILES: CCS(=O)(=O)N[C@H]1C(F)(F)CN(C(=O)C(C)(C)O)[C@H]1Cc1cccc(-c2cc(F)cc(F)c2)c1F

name: Oxacillin
text:
This is oxacillin, a penicillin carrying a 5-methyl-3-phenylisoxazole-4-carboxamide side chain on the 6-amino position of the penam core. I read the structure in three parts:

- **Side chain:** a 5-methyl-3-phenylisoxazole ring (O1, N2, C3 bearing the phenyl, C4 bearing the amide carbonyl, C5 bearing the methyl) joined through C(=O)NH to the core.
- **Penam core:** a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring. The thiazolidine carbon next to sulfur carries two methyls, and the carbon next to the ring nitrogen carries a COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows a wedged COOH at C3, a wedged H at the bridgehead C5, and a hashed NH at C6. I checked the C6 centre against the drawing explicitly. From the implicit H (toward the viewer), the substituents N, C5 and C7 run counterclockwise, which corresponds to `[C@H]` in the SMILES below. I did not derive the C5 and C3 symbols independently from the drawing. I took them from the natural penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R), as I remember the standard oxacillin SMILES.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=NO1)C2=CC=CC=C2)C(=O)N[C@H]3[C@@H]4N(C3=O)[C@H](C(S4)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Oxeladin
text:
The drawing shows a phenyl ring attached to a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries two ethyl groups and a C(=O)O ester carbon. The ester oxygen leads into a chain O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N, and the nitrogen bears two ethyl groups.

This reads as 2-(2-(diethylamino)ethoxy)ethyl 2,2-diphenylbutanoate-type structure, specifically 2-ethyl-2-phenylbutanoate (the ester of 2,2-diethylphenylacetic acid), i.e. the drug pentoxyverine-like compound. All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCC(CC)(c1ccccc1)C(=O)OCCOCCN(CC)CC

name: Oxcarbazepine
text:
The drawing shows oxcarbazepine: a dibenzazepine core with a central seven-membered ring.

- **Seven-membered ring:** N, aromatic carbon (left ring), aromatic carbon (left ring), C=O, CH2, aromatic carbon (right ring), aromatic carbon (right ring), and back to N.
- **N substituent:** a carboxamide, N–C(=O)NH2.
- **Left benzene ring:** it is fused to the seven-membered ring through the carbon bonded to N and the carbon bonded to the ketone.
- **Right benzene ring:** it is fused through the carbon bonded to N and the carbon bonded to the CH2.

SMILES: NC(=O)N1c2ccccc2CC(=O)c2ccccc12

Check on the ring closures: N1 is bonded to the left-ring carbon c2, which runs around the ring (c2ccccc2) with its last atom bearing the CH2.

That gives N1–c2ccccc2–C–C(=O)–c2ccccc12. Here the left ring's first carbon is bonded to N and its last carbon to CH2, so CH2 is attached to the left ring and C(=O) to the right ring. In the image, the ketone is on the left ring and the CH2 on the right ring, so the string should be written the other way round. The ring-fusion connectivity is mirror-symmetric except for that placement, so I rewrite it to match the drawing:

NC(=O)N1c2ccccc2C(=O)Cc2ccccc12

Check: N1, then c2ccccc2, where the first carbon is bonded to N and the last carbon to C(=O). Next come CH2, then the right ring c2ccccc12, whose last carbon closes to N1 and whose first carbon is bonded to CH2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)N1c2ccccc2C(=O)Cc2ccccc12

name: Oxfendazole
text:
The drawing shows oxfendazole's sulfoxide analogue, which is the structure of fenbendazole sulfoxide (oxfendazole): methyl N-(5-(phenylsulfinyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Left:** a methyl group on an oxygen, bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), which is bonded to an NH. This is a methyl carbamate, COC(=O)N.
- **Centre:** the NH attaches to C2 of a benzimidazole. C2 is double-bonded to N, which is attached to the benzene ring, and single-bonded to an NH that is attached to the other ring-fusion carbon.
- **Benzo ring:** the sulfur sits on the ring carbon on the right, at the position para to the fused carbon bonded to the N= atom, as drawn.
- **Right:** the sulfur carries an =O and is bonded to a phenyl group, so it is a sulfoxide (S(=O)c1ccccc1).

SMILES: COC(=O)Nc1nc2ccc(S(=O)c3ccccc3)cc2[nH]1

SMILES: COC(=O)Nc1nc2ccc(S(=O)c3ccccc3)cc2[nH]1

name: Oxprenolol
text:
This is oxprenolol. I read the drawing in three parts.

- **Amine end:** an isopropyl group (CH3, CH, CH3) is bonded to NH.
- **Linker:** the NH connects to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then an ether O that attaches to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring carries two adjacent substituents. One is the ether O from the linker. The other is an O-allyl group, O–CH2–CH=CH2.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccccc1OCC=C

name: Oxiconazole Nitrate
text:
This is oxiconazole nitrate. The structure has two parts: the oxiconazole cation-free base and nitric acid drawn as a separate component.

**Oxiconazole.** The imidazole ring is attached through its N1 to a CH2 group. That CH2 is bonded to a C(=N–O–CH2–Ar) carbon, which also carries a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring. The oxime oxygen is linked through CH2 to a second 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring.

**Imidazole ring.** Reading the drawing, N1 connects to C2, which is double-bonded to N3. N3 connects to C4, which is double-bonded to C5, and C5 closes back to N1. This gives n1ccnc1 written in aromatic form, or C1=CN=CN1 in Kekulé form, with N1 bearing the CH2.
