**Left aryl ring.** The ring carbon attached to the C=N carbon has an adjacent carbon bearing Cl (ortho). Going around the ring, the next carbon is CH, then the carbon bearing Cl (para to the attachment point), then two CH carbons. This is c1ccc(Cl)cc1Cl, starting from the attachment carbon.

**Right aryl ring.** The CH2-bearing carbon has an ortho Cl, and the carbon para to the CH2 also has Cl. This is also a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring.

**Nitric acid.** It is drawn as the charge-separated form O[N+](=O)[O-].

**Oxime geometry.** The drawing shows no explicit stereo bonds, so I leave the C=N geometry unspecified.

SMILES: C(n1ccnc1)C(=NOCc1ccc(Cl)cc1Cl)c1ccc(Cl)cc1Cl.O[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Oxybutynin
text:
The drawing shows oxybutynin, which I read as follows.

- **Amine end:** a nitrogen carries two ethyl groups. It is bonded to a CH2, which leads into a C≡C triple bond.
- **Linker to the ester:** the alkyne is followed by another CH2, then an ester oxygen, then a C=O.
- **Acyl side:** the carbonyl carbon is attached to a quaternary carbon bearing an OH, a cyclohexyl ring (6 carbons) and a phenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CC#CCOC(=O)C(O)(C1CCCCC1)c1ccccc1

name: Oxybuprocaine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents.

- **Ester side:** the ring carbon at the upper right carries a C(=O)O group, an ester. The ester oxygen is bonded to CH2CH2N(CH2CH3)2, a 2-(diethylamino)ethyl group.
- **Amino group:** the ring carbon at the upper left carries NH2.
- **Butoxy group:** the ring carbon at the lower left carries an O-butyl group (OCCCC). I counted the chain from the oxygen: O to CH2, CH2, CH2, then the terminal CH3, which makes four carbons.

The ring positions relative to the ester carbon (C1, upper right) are:
- C2, the top-right vertex, is CH.
- C3, the top-left vertex, is CH.
- C4, the left vertex, carries NH2.
- C5, the bottom-left vertex, carries the butoxy group.
- C6, the bottom-right vertex, is CH.

The ester carbon sits on the right vertex of the ring. The ring runs from the C(=O) carbon to the CH at the bottom right, then to the carbon bearing OBu, then to the carbon bearing NH2, then to two CH carbons at the top. So the amino group is para to the ester and the butoxy group is meta to it.

This corresponds to oxybuprocaine (benoxinate).

SMILES: CCCCOc1cc(C(=O)OCCN(CC)CC)ccc1N

name: Oxitropium bromide
text:
I read this as the N-ethyl, N-methyl quaternary ammonium salt of scopolamine, with bromide as the counter-ion (the ethyl analogue of butylscopolamine bromide).

- **Core:** a tropane-type bicycle with an epoxide (the O bridging two adjacent carbons) and a positively charged nitrogen bearing one methyl and one ethyl group.
- **Ester:** the ring carbon bearing the ester oxygen is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo label. The O–C(=O) carbon is attached to a CH carrying a CH2OH group and a phenyl ring; that carbon is drawn with a wedge, so it carries a stereo label.
- **Stereo marks:** the two bridgehead carbons and the two epoxide carbons carry the wedge/hash H atoms, so they carry stereo labels.
- **Source of the labels:** I did not derive the @/@@ assignments from the drawing. They are adapted from my recollection of the PubChem SMILES for butylscopolamine bromide, with butyl replaced by ethyl and the unmarked ring carbon left unspecified, so the stereo descriptors are the least certain part of the answer.

SMILES: CC[N+]1(C)[C@@H]2CC(C[C@@H]1[C@H]3[C@@H]2O3)OC(=O)[C@H](CO)c1ccccc1.[Br-]

name: Oxandrolone
text:
I read the skeleton as a four-ring system: a cyclopentane fused to two cyclohexanes and then to a six-membered lactone.

- **Cyclopentane:** The ring carries a quaternary C(OH)(CH3) with a hashed methyl, and the neighbouring ring-fusion carbon carries a wedged methyl.
- **Two cyclohexanes:** These are fused through carbons bearing H atoms (one wedged, three hashed), plus a second quaternary carbon with a wedged methyl.
- **Lactone ring:** This ring contains C(=O)–O–CH2, with a CH2 between the carbonyl and the ring-fusion CH.

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry, taking the neighbour order as it appears in the SMILES string. I did not run the string through a parser, so it has not been checked mechanically.

SMILES: C[C@]1(O)CC[C@@H]2[C@]1(C)CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@H]4CC(=O)OC[C@]34C

name: Oxymetazoline
text:
This structure is oxymetazoline, read from the drawing as follows.

**Benzene ring.** The ring atoms, going around, are:
- C1 bears the tert-butyl group.
- C2 bears the OH.
- C3 bears a methyl group.
- C4 bears the CH2 that links to the imidazoline.
- C5 bears a methyl group.
- C6 is an unsubstituted CH.

**Side groups.**
- The tert-butyl group is a quaternary carbon carrying three methyls.
- The CH2 links the ring to C2 of the imidazoline ring.
- The imidazoline ring is C(=N–CH2–CH2–NH–), closed back onto the same carbon.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring starting from the OH carbon:
Oc1c(C(C)(C)C)cc(C)c(CC2=NCCN2)c1C

The atoms in this string match the drawing:
- The OH-bearing carbon is bonded to the tert-butyl carbon, then to the CH, then to the C-methyl.
- That C-methyl is followed by the carbon carrying the CH2 group.
- The last ring carbon, closing the ring, bears the methyl that sits next to the OH carbon.

SMILES: Oc1c(C(C)(C)C)cc(C)c(CC2=NCCN2)c1C

name: Oxycodone
text:
The drawing matches the oxycodone skeleton: a 4,5-epoxymorphinan with a 3-methoxy aromatic ring, a 6-ketone, a 14-hydroxyl, an N-methyl group and a two-carbon bridge from nitrogen. I read it region by region:

- **Aromatic ring:** one carbon bears OMe, the next carbon bears the furan-type ether oxygen, and there are two aromatic CH atoms. The ring carbons next to the bridge carbons close the ring.
- **Furan ring:** the ether O links the aromatic carbon to the CH carbon (drawn with an H wedge) that sits next to the C=O.
- **Cyclohexanone ring:** C=O, then two CH2 groups, then the quaternary carbon bearing the hashed OH.
- **Nitrogen bridge:** N carries a methyl group, a CH2–CH2 arm leading to the hashed quaternary carbon, and the CH (H wedge) that connects through CH2 to the aromatic ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedges and hashes shown correspond to the natural oxycodone configuration. I took the stereo descriptors from the known oxycodone SMILES rather than deriving each one from the drawing, so the @/@@ assignments are the least certain part.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4C(=O)CC[C@]2([C@H]1CC5=C3C(=C(C=C5)OC)O4)O

name: Oxycodone Hydrochloride
text:
I read this as oxycodone hydrochloride: a morphinan skeleton with a 4,5-epoxy bridge, a 3-methoxy group, a 6-ketone, a 14-hydroxyl and an N-methyl amine, plus HCl as a separate component. I did not derive the stereo marks independently. I used the standard oxycodone configuration and checked that its ring connectivity and substituents match the drawing atom for atom. I recalled that SMILES from memory and did not re-derive its stereodescriptors against the wedges.

Connectivity check:
- The aromatic ring carries the OMe and the ether oxygen of the furan ring, and is joined to the quaternary carbon and to the CH2 on the right.
- The cyclohexanone ring contains the C=O, two CH2 groups, the C–OH quaternary carbon and the CH–O carbon.
- The piperidine ring contains the N-methyl nitrogen, the CH2CH2 bridge and the CH that bears the drawn H.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23C4=C5C(=C(C=C4)OC)O[C@H]2C(=O)CC[C@]3([C@H]1C5)O.Cl

name: Oxypurinol
text:
Reading the drawing atom by atom:

- **Six-membered ring:** C(=O) at the left, then NH at the top, then a carbon (C7a) at the top right. That carbon is double-bonded to C3a at the lower right. C3a connects to the C(=O) at the bottom, which connects to HN at the lower left and back to the left C(=O).
- **Five-membered ring:** C7a bonds to NH at the top right, then N, then =CH. The CH bonds to C3a, which closes the ring.
- **Double bonds:** C7a=C3a is drawn as a double bond. The N=CH bond is also double. Both carbonyls are C=O.

SMILES, written ring by ring:

- Start with O=C1NC2=C(C=N2)... but the pyrazole has NH, so write it as C2 (C7a) bonded to the NH.
- O=C1NC2=C(C=NN2)C(=O)N1 gives C7a bonded to N(H), then N, then =CH. Here C2=C(...) puts C7a double-bonded to C3a. C3a is bonded to CH, which is double-bonded to N, then NH, which closes back to C7a. This matches the drawing.
- The ring closures work out: C1 is the left carbonyl, N is the top NH, C2 is C7a, and C( is C3a. The branch C=NN2 runs CH=N–NH and closes to C7a. Then C(=O)N1 is the bottom carbonyl and the lower-left NH, closing to C1.

SMILES: O=C1NC2=C(C=NN2)C(=O)N1

name: Oxymorphone
text:
The drawing is a morphinan skeleton, and I read it as oxymorphone, with the stereochemistry written from memory of the known compound's SMILES rather than derived from the wedges and hashes.

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring carries a phenolic OH and is fused to a dihydrofuran ring through the ether oxygen.
- **Ketone ring:** a cyclohexanone ring contains the C=O, two CH2 groups, a quaternary carbon bearing a tertiary OH (shown with a hashed bond), and the carbon next to the ether oxygen (H on a hashed bond).
- **Piperidine ring:** an N-methyl nitrogen is bridged through a CH2–CH2 chain to the quaternary carbon. It is also bonded to the CH (H on a hashed bond) that connects through a CH2 to the aromatic ring.

I checked that the SMILES contains the same atoms and ring closures as the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@]23[C@@H]4C(=O)CC[C@]2([C@H]1CC5=C3C(=C(C=C5)O)O4)O

name: Ozone
text:
The image shows three oxygen atoms in a bent chain. The left oxygen carries a negative charge and is joined to the central oxygen by a single bond. The central oxygen carries a positive charge and is joined to the right oxygen by a double bond. This is ozone.

SMILES: [O-][O+]=O

name: Paclitaxel
text:
This is paclitaxel (Taxol). I identified it from the overall scaffold and substituents and wrote its SMILES from memory of the standard isomeric form, not by assigning each wedge and hash from the image. I did not check the stereo marks one by one against the drawing, so the stereochemistry is the standard 2'R,3'S paclitaxel configuration.

What the drawing shows, region by region:
- **Core:** a taxane skeleton with the 6-8-6 ring system and a gem-dimethyl bridge carbon. It carries a C=C bearing a methyl group, a ketone, and a free OH on the six-membered ring.
- **Oxetane:** a four-membered ring containing one oxygen, with an acetate on the adjacent carbon.
- **Core esters:** an acetate on the carbon next to the ketone, and a benzoate ester on the ring carbon next to the oxetane-bearing carbon.
- **Side chain:** an ester linking to a phenylisoserine unit. It has a 2'-OH, a 3'-phenyl group, and an N-benzoyl amide.

SMILES: CC1=C2[C@H](C(=O)[C@@]3([C@H](C[C@@H]4[C@]([C@H]3[C@@H]([C@@](C2(C)C)(C[C@@H]1OC(=O)[C@@H]([C@H](C5=CC=CC=C5)NC(=O)C6=CC=CC=C6)O)O)OC(=O)C7=CC=CC=C7)(CO4)OC(=O)C)O)C)OC(=O)C

name: Ozanimod
text:
I read the structure as an ozanimod-type molecule: a 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene whose C1 carries an NH–CH2CH2OH group. Its C4 is joined to C3 of a 1,2,4-oxadiazole, and the oxadiazole C5 is joined to a benzene ring bearing an isopropoxy group and a nitrile on adjacent carbons.

**Stereochemistry.** The only stereocentre is indane C1, drawn with a wedge to the NH group, so the hydrogen points away from the viewer. The priorities are N > aromatic ring-fusion carbon > CH2. In the drawing these three run counterclockwise, which gives the (S) configuration.

**SMILES check.** In `[C@H]1`, the neighbour order is N, H, ring-fusion carbon (ring closure 1), then CH2. The `@` symbol corresponds to (S) for that order. The ring closures put the oxadiazole on C4 of the indane, next to the ring-fusion carbon C3a. In the oxadiazole, N2–O1–C5 and the remaining ring nitrogen N4 are connected as in the drawing.

SMILES: OCCN[C@H]1CCc2c1cccc2-c1noc(n1)-c1ccc(OC(C)C)c(C#N)c1

name: Ouabain
text:
This is a cardenolide glycoside with the ouabain skeleton: a butenolide on C17, a steroid core carrying OH groups at C1, C5, C11 and C14 and a CH2OH at C10, and a 6-deoxyhexose (rhamnose-type) sugar on the C3 oxygen.

I built the SMILES region by region from the drawing:

- **Lactone:** the ring is O–C(=O)–CH=C–CH2, attached through its alkene carbon to C17.
- **Steroid core:** the four fused rings carry the OH, CH2OH and methyl substituents listed above.
- **Sugar:** a pyranose bearing a methyl, three OH groups and the glycosidic O to C3.

I assigned each @/@@ centre from the wedge and hash bonds and the 2D positions of the neighbours. I did not check the result against a database entry, so the stereo marks come only from my reading of the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1C=C(CO1)[C@H]2CC[C@]3(O)[C@@H]4CC[C@]5(O)C[C@@H](O[C@@H]6O[C@@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]6O)C[C@@H](O)[C@]5(CO)[C@H]4[C@H](O)C[C@]23C

name: Pacritinib
text:
I read this as the macrocyclic pyrimidine-based structure of pacritinib.

- **Left side:** a meta-disubstituted benzene. One substituent is a CH2–O link into the macrocycle. The other is a bond to C4 of a pyrimidine.
- **Pyrimidine:** C2 carries an NH that links to the second benzene ring. The ring has two adjacent CH carbons and two N atoms, which fits a pyrimidine.
- **Second benzene ring:** it carries the NH, a CH2–O group on the carbon next to the ring CH between them, and an O–CH2CH2–pyrrolidine side chain.
- **Macrocycle bridge:** ArCH2–O–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–O–CH2–Ar. The drawn alkene looks trans, so I wrote it as E.
- **Side chain:** the aryl-O–CH2CH2 unit ends on the nitrogen of a five-membered saturated pyrrolidine ring.

I checked that the aromatic ring closures and the macrocycle closure in the SMILES match the drawn connectivity.

SMILES: C1CCN(C1)CCOc2ccc3cc2COC/C=C/COCc4cccc(c4)-c5ccnc(n5)N3

name: Oxytocin
text:
This is oxytocin (Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2). The two cysteine CH2 groups, drawn as "C" labels, are joined through the S–S disulfide bridge to form the 20-membered ring. The molecule runs from the free N-terminal amine on Cys1 through the ring to the Gly primary amide at the C-terminus.

I took the sequence from the drawing and assigned each stereocentre as the natural L-amino acid. I did not check each wedge or hash individually against the drawing. The Ile side-chain carbon also follows the natural configuration, and I checked each centre's @/@@ against the L-amino-acid convention.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)[C@@H]1NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC(=O)[C@@H](N)CSSC[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC1=O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Palbociclib
text:
This structure is palbociclib.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Acetyl group: CH3-C(=O)- attached to the ring carbon at the lower left.
- Pyridone ring: the carbon bearing the acetyl is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the methyl. The next carbon is C(=O), which connects to N, and that N carries the cyclopentyl group.
- Pyrimidine ring: it is fused to the pyridone. The shared carbons are C4a (attached to the methyl-bearing carbon) and C8a (attached to the ring N). The remaining ring atoms are N=C(NH-aryl)-N=C8a, plus CH=N back to C4a.
- Aryl substituent: the NH links to a pyridine whose carbons run C2 (NH), C3H, C4H and C5 (bearing the piperazine), then C6H, then N back to C2.
- Piperazine: attached through N1, with an NH at the far end.

SMILES, written from the acetyl group around the rings:
CC(=O)C1=C(C)c2cnc(Nc3ccc(cn3)N3CCNCC3)nc2N(C2CCCC2)C1=O

Check of the ring-closure labels: ring 1 opens at C1 (the acetyl-bearing carbon) and closes at C1=O. The fused aromatic ring uses label 2 for c2…nc2, and the cyclopentyl reuses 2 after it closes, which is valid. The pyridine uses 3 and closes at n3. The piperazine reuses 3 afterward, also valid.

SMILES: CC(=O)C1=C(C)c2cnc(Nc3ccc(cn3)N3CCNCC3)nc2N(C2CCCC2)C1=O

name: Palifosfamide
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom with four substituents:
- a double bond to O (P=O)
- a single bond to OH
- two single bonds to NH groups

Each NH is attached to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) ending in Cl, so each arm is NCCCl.

This is N,N'-bis(2-chloroethyl)phosphorodiamidic acid. There are no stereocentres and no stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: O=P(O)(NCCCl)NCCCl

name: Padsevonil
text:
I read the molecule as an imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole core carrying three substituents.

- **Fused core:** the five-membered ring with S, the bridgehead N and the N=C is a 1,3,4-thiadiazole, fused to an imidazole. Starting from the CH2OMe carbon, the ring path is C(CH2OMe)=N–N(bridgehead)–C(=C–CF3)… with the second bridgehead carbon bonded to S.
- **Substituents on the core:**
  - A CH2OCH3 group on the thiadiazole carbon.
  - A CF3 group on the imidazole carbon.
  - A CH2 linking the neighbouring imidazole carbon to the lactam nitrogen.
- **Lactam:** a pyrrolidin-2-one ring (N, CH2, CH, CH2, C=O).
- **Stereocentre:** the ring CH at position 4 of the lactam carries a CH2CF2Cl group on a wedge bond.

For the stereocentre, I wrote the neighbours in the order: ring CH2 toward N, H, wedge CH2, ring CH2 toward C=O. The wedge puts H behind the page. Viewed from the front, the ring CH2 toward N, the wedge CH2 and the ring CH2 toward C=O run clockwise. That corresponds to @@ in this atom order.

SMILES: COCc1nn2c(CN3C[C@@H](CC(F)(F)Cl)CC3=O)c(C(F)(F)F)nc2s1

name: Paliperidone
text:
This is paliperidone, drawn without stereochemistry.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Benzisoxazole:** a benzene ring carries F. It is fused to an isoxazole ring made of C3, N, O and the two fusion carbons, and C3 is attached to the piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** the 4-position is bonded to C3 of the benzisoxazole, and the ring nitrogen carries the ethylene linker.
- **Linker:** N–CH2–CH2– runs to the pyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidinone core.
- **Pyrimidinone core:**
  - The carbon bearing the linker is C3.
  - It is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the methyl group (C2).
  - C2 is bonded to N=, and that N is double-bonded to the ring-fusion carbon (C9a).
  - C3 is also bonded to the C=O carbon, which is bonded to the ring nitrogen.
- **Saturated ring:** the ring nitrogen connects through CH2CH2CH2 to CH(OH), and CH(OH) connects to C9a.

SMILES:
Fc1ccc2c(c1)onc2C1CCN(CC1)CCC1=C(C)N=C2C(O)CCCN2C1=O

Check on the benzisoxazole: c1 (F-bearing) ccc2 c(c1) o n c2. The atom "c2" after "ccc" is the fusion carbon bonded to C3, and the next "c(c1)" is the fusion carbon bonded to O. The drawing shows C3a attached to the CH of the benzene ring and C3, while C7a bears O. Writing it as Fc1ccc2c(c1)onc2… would give a different pattern, so I rewrote it as:

Fc1ccc2c(c1)onc2 means: c1(F), c, c, c2 (fusion, ring-opening 2), c(c1) (the other fusion carbon, closing the benzene ring), o, n, c2 (closing to the first fusion carbon). That puts O on the fusion carbon next to the CH adjacent to C–F, and C3 on the other fusion carbon, which matches the drawing: F-bearing carbon, CH, then C7a (bonded to O).

The final string is the same as above.

SMILES: Fc1ccc2c(c1)onc2C1CCN(CC1)CCC1=C(C)N=C2C(O)CCCN2C1=O

name: Paliperidone Palmitate
text:
This is paliperidone palmitate. I read it as three parts:

- **Ester chain:** a straight chain of 16 carbons including the C=O, which is a palmitoyl group. I counted this from the zigzag spacing (about 15 bonds from the terminal methyl to the carbonyl), so the count is an estimate rather than an exact vertex-by-vertex tally.
- **Core:** a tetrahydropyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one bearing the ester oxygen on the saturated ring carbon next to the ring fusion, a methyl group, and a two-carbon linker at the 3-position.
- **Side group:** the linker ends at the nitrogen of a piperidine whose 4-position carries a 6-fluoro-1,2-benzisoxazol-3-yl group.

The ester-bearing carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC1CCCN2C(=O)C(CCN3CCC(CC3)c3noc4cc(F)ccc34)=C(C)N=C12

name: Palmitic Acid
text:
The drawing is an unbranched zigzag chain ending in a carboxylic acid group (C=O and OH on the last carbon).

Counting the vertices along the chain from the left end gives 16 carbons, with the 16th being the carboxyl carbon. That makes 15 chain carbons followed by C(=O)O. The molecule is palmitic acid (hexadecanoic acid). The drawing has no wedges, hashes or double bonds in the chain, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: Palmatine
text:
This SMILES describes the molecule drawn, which appears to be the palmatine cation. I read it from the drawing as follows:

- **Left benzene ring:** it carries two adjacent OMe groups, at the carbons drawn at about (358,721) and (293,848). The two CH carbons of this ring sit at the bottom.
- **Pyridinium ring:** it is fused to the left ring and contains N⁺. N⁺ is bonded to a CH on the left side, to the CH₂CH₂ chain, and (by a double bond) to the carbon that joins the right aromatic ring. That carbon is also bonded to a CH, which is attached to the left ring.
- **Right ring:** the CH₂CH₂ chain leads into a second benzene ring, which carries two adjacent OMe groups at the far right. The ring carbon next to the N⁺=C carbon closes the ring back to it.

Walking the atoms in order gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: COc1ccc2cc3[n+](cc2c1OC)CCc1cc(OC)c(OC)cc1-3

name: Palonosetron Hydrochloride
text:
This structure is palonosetron hydrochloride. I identified it from the overall skeleton and wrote the stereochemistry from memory of the known (3S,3aS) drug, not by independently assigning the two wedged H centres in the drawing.

- **Quinuclidine unit:** The bicyclic amine on the left has a bridgehead N, and the bridging carbon is drawn with an explicit "C" label. Its C3 carbon carries a wedged H and is bonded to the lactam N.
- **Lactam core:** The amide N is attached to a C=O, which is attached to a benzene ring. An N–CH2–CH(H wedge) unit links back to the ring, and a CH2CH2 bridge completes a hexahydrobenzo[de]isoquinolin-1-one.
- **Salt:** HCl is shown as a separate component.

SMILES: C1CN2CCC1[C@@H](C2)N3C[C@@H]4CCC5=C4C(=CC=C5)C3=O.Cl

name: Paltusotine
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline core with three substituents.

- **Quinoline ring:** N1 is at the top. C2 is the CH next to it, C3 carries the aryl group, and C4 carries the piperidine. C4a and C8a are the fusion carbons, and C5 is the CH adjacent to C4a. C6 carries the second aryl group, followed by C7 (CH) and C8 (CH) back to C8a.
- **Position 3:** a 3,5-difluorophenyl group.
- **Position 4:** a 4-aminopiperidin-1-yl group, attached through its ring nitrogen.
- **Position 6:** a phenyl ring bearing OH at the carbon next to the attachment point and CN on the carbon next to that. The ring is therefore 2-hydroxy-3-cyanophenyl.

Writing the SMILES from the quinoline ring: N1=CC(Ar)=C(N2CCC(N)CC2)c3cc(Ar')ccc13.

- Ar is c1cc(F)cc(F)c1.
- Ar' is c1cccc(C#N)c1O.

Full SMILES: N#Cc1cccc(c1O)-c1ccc2ncc(-c3cc(F)cc(F)c3)c(N3CCC(N)CC3)c2c1

Check on the quinoline ring: c1ccc2ncc(...)c(...)c2c1 starts at C6 (the attachment atom c1), then C7 (c), C8 (c), C8a (c2), N, C2 (c), C3 (c(...)), C4 (c(...)), C4a (c2), and C5 (c1). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1cccc(c1O)-c1ccc2ncc(-c3cc(F)cc(F)c3)c(N3CCC(N)CC3)c2c1

name: Palovarotene
text:
The drawing shows a tetramethyltetrahydronaphthalene core, a stilbene-type linker to a benzoic acid, and a pyrazol-1-ylmethyl substituent.

**Tetralin core.** The saturated ring has a C(CH3)2 group at the top left, two CH2 groups, and a second C(CH3)2 group at the bottom left. The aromatic ring is fused to it. Its two ring-fusion carbons are at about (362, 545) and (316, 666). The other four aromatic carbons are:
- CH at (489, 525)
- C at (571, 625), which carries the vinyl group
- C at (525, 746), which carries the CH2–N group
- CH at (398, 766)

**Linker and acid.** The vinyl group is CH=CH, running from (700, 605) to (780, 704). It joins a para-substituted benzene ring that ends in COOH.

**Pyrazole.** The CH2 at (607, 846) connects to N1 of the pyrazole. The ring is N1–N=CH–CH=CH back to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The double bond is drawn with the aryl groups on opposite sides, so it is trans (E). The two substituents on the double bond, the aryl carbon at (571, 625) and the aryl carbon at (909, 683), sit on opposite sides of the line from (700, 605) to (780, 704), which confirms E.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Start at the tetralin: CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)c2cc(CN3C=CC=N3)c(/C=C/c3ccc(C(=O)O)cc3)cc21
- Check the ring closure: C1(C)(C) is the top quaternary carbon, then CC, then C(C)(C) at the bottom, then c2 (the ring-fusion carbon at (316, 666)). Next is cc, the CH at (398, 766), then c(CH2N) at (525, 746). After that comes c(vinyl) at (571, 625), then c, the CH at (489, 525), and finally c21 at (362, 545), which closes both rings.
- This matches the drawing: the CH2N carbon is adjacent to the CH at (398, 766), and the vinyl carbon is adjacent to the CH at (489, 525).
- Pyrazole written as N3C=CC=N3 gives N1–CH=CH–CH=N–N1, which is the correct ring.

SMILES: CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)c2cc(Cn3cccn3)c(/C=C/c3ccc(C(=O)O)cc3)cc21

name: Pantoprazole
text:
This structure is pantoprazole, a benzimidazole sulfoxide. I read it region by region.

**Pyridine ring (left).** The ring atoms are N, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6.
- C2 carries the CH2 that leads to the sulfoxide.
- C3 carries an OMe.
- C4 carries an OMe.
- C5 and C6 are plain CH.

**Linker.** The CH2 is bonded to a sulfoxide S, written S(=O), which is bonded to C2 of the benzimidazole.

**Benzimidazole (right).** C2 is bonded to N (imine) and to NH. The fused benzene ring bears an OCHF2 group.

**Assembled SMILES.** COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(OC(F)F)cc3[nH]2)c1OC

**Atom check on the benzimidazole.**
- The ring N (no H) is attached to the fused carbon at the upper left of the benzene ring (around 880,640). From there the benzene runs to the top carbon (955,543), then 1075,560, then 1122,675, which bears the O, then 1047,770, then 925,755, which is bonded to NH.
- In the SMILES, c3 (bonded to n) is followed by c, c, c(OC(F)F), c, c3[nH]. This gives the fused carbon, CH, CH, C–O, CH and the fused carbon bonded to NH.
- The O-bearing carbon is therefore the third ring atom from the N-side fusion carbon, and it is adjacent to the CH that sits next to the NH-side fusion carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(OC(F)F)cc3[nH]2)c1OC

name: Pamiparib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Pyrrolidine ring:** an N and three CH2 groups close onto a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries a hashed methyl.
- **Seven-membered ring:** the pyrrolidine N is attached to a CH2. This CH2 leads to a C=N, then to an NH, then to a C=O, and the C=O is bonded to the benzene ring. The ring closes through the indole carbons.
- **Indole core:** a fluorinated benzene ring is fused to a pyrrole ring that contains an NH. The quaternary carbon is bonded to the indole C2 position.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is hashed, so it points away from the viewer. The other three neighbours of the stereocentre, in the order N, indole carbon, CH2, run clockwise when seen from the front. Seen from the methyl side, as SMILES reads them, that order is counterclockwise, which gives `@`.

The SMILES, with the stereocentre neighbours ordered methyl, N (ring closure 1), indole carbon (ring closure 2), CH2, is:

SMILES: C[C@]12CCCN1CC1=NNC(=O)c3cc(F)cc4[nH]c2c1c34

name: Pancuronium Bromide
text:
This is pancuronium bromide: a steroid core carrying two N-methylpiperidinium groups and two acetate esters, with two bromide counter-ions.

I identified the skeleton from the drawing. The structure is a four-ring steroid with a methyl at each of the two ring junctions (C10 and C13). An acetoxy group and an N-methylpiperidinium group sit on adjacent carbons of ring A (C3 and C2) and of ring D (C17 and C16). Two Br⁻ ions are shown separately.

The stereo descriptors in the SMILES are not derived atom by atom from the wedges and hashes. The drawing is rotated about 180° from the usual steroid orientation, so I could not check each centre reliably. I wrote the SMILES from the known configuration of pancuronium and took that to be what the drawing shows.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1C[C@@H]([C@@H]2OC(=O)C)[N+]4(CCCCC4)C)CC[C@@H]5[C@@]3(C[C@@H]([C@H](C5)OC(=O)C)[N+]6(CCCCC6)C)C.[Br-].[Br-]

name: Pantothenic Acid
text:
The drawing shows pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) as its D-(R) enantiomer.

- **Left end:** a quaternary carbon carries two methyl groups and a CH2OH, and is bonded to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries an OH on a wedge bond and is bonded to the amide carbonyl carbon.
- **Amide link:** C(=O) joins to NH.
- **Right end:** NH is followed by CH2CH2 and a terminal carboxylic acid, C(=O)OH.

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are OH, then C(=O)N, then C(CH3)2CH2OH, then H. With the OH wedged toward the viewer, H points away. Going from OH (top) to C=O (lower right) to the quaternary carbon (lower left) is clockwise, so the centre is R. I checked that `[C@@H]`, written after the quaternary carbon as `CC(C)(CO)[C@@H](O)C(=O)...`, encodes R.

SMILES: CC(C)(CO)[C@@H](O)C(=O)NCCC(=O)O

name: Paramethadione
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered oxazolidine-2,4-dione ring. Going around the ring: O1, then C2 (C=O), then N3 (bearing a methyl), then C4 (C=O), then C5. C5 is quaternary and carries both an ethyl group and a methyl group. This is trimethadione-like, with an ethyl at C5 in place of a methyl.

C5 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CCC1(C)OC(=O)N(C)C1=O

name: Papaverine
text:
This structure is papaverine: an isoquinoline carrying a 3,4-dimethoxybenzyl group at C1 and methoxy groups at C6 and C7.

**Isoquinoline core.** The pyridine ring contains N, C1 (attached to the CH2), and the two CH carbons next to N, joined to the fused benzene ring. C1 is bonded to the fused carbon C8a, which is bonded to C8 (CH), then C7 (OMe), C6 (OMe), C5 (CH), and C4a. C4a is bonded to C4 (CH), then C3 (CH), then N.

**Benzyl ring.** The CH2 connects to a benzene ring bearing two OMe groups on adjacent carbons, at the meta and para positions relative to the CH2.

**SMILES check.** Writing from the methoxy on the benzyl ring: COc1ccc(Cc2nccc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc23)cc1OC

- c2 is C1 of the isoquinoline, followed by n and then cc (C3 and C4).
- c3 is C4a, followed by c (C5), c(OC) (C6), c(OC) (C7), and c (C8).
- c23 is C8a, which closes both rings.

The drawing shows OMe on the carbon after C5, and then OMe on the next carbon, which matches this.

SMILES: COc1ccc(Cc2nccc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc23)cc1OC

name: Paraquat
text:
The drawing shows two pyridinium rings joined by a single bond between their 4-positions. Each ring nitrogen carries a positive charge and a methyl group, so the molecule is the paraquat dication (1,1'-dimethyl-4,4'-bipyridinium).

Reading the left ring from the bonds drawn: N+ is double-bonded to the upper carbon, which is single-bonded to the next carbon. That carbon is double-bonded to the ring-junction carbon (the one attached to the other ring). The junction carbon is single-bonded to the lower carbon, which is double-bonded to the next carbon, and that carbon is single-bonded back to N+.

The right ring is read the same way. The junction carbon is double-bonded to the lower carbon (the lower inner line) and single-bonded to the upper carbon. The upper carbon is double-bonded to the next carbon, which is single-bonded to N+. N+ is double-bonded to the lower carbon, which is single-bonded to the junction carbon.

Written out, the left ring is C[N+]1=CC=C(C=C1)… and the right ring is …C2=CC=[N+](C)C=C2. Each ring has alternating double bonds in a valid pattern, so the SMILES below is consistent with the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: C[N+]1=CC=C(C=C1)C1=CC=[N+](C)C=C1

name: Paroxetine
text:
The structure is paroxetine, a 4-(4-fluorophenyl)piperidine carrying a 3-(1,3-benzodioxol-5-yloxymethyl) group.

**Skeleton**
- The top-right ring is a para-substituted fluorobenzene, with F at the top and the piperidine attached at the bottom.
- The right-hand ring is a piperidine containing one NH.
- The piperidine C4 carries the aryl group and C3 carries the CH2–O group.
- The CH2–O links to the 1,3-benzodioxole through its 5-position (a benzene ring fused to an O–CH2–O five-membered ring).

**Stereochemistry**
- C4 has the aryl bond drawn as a hash, so the aryl group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Taking the neighbour order aryl, H, C3, C5 as written in the SMILES, this gives `[C@@H]`.
- C3 has the CH2O bond drawn as a wedge, so the CH2O group points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Taking the neighbour order C2, H, C4, CH2 as written, this gives `[C@H]`.

Together these correspond to the (3S,4R) configuration.

SMILES: Fc1ccc(cc1)[C@@H]1CCNC[C@H]1COc1ccc2OCOc2c1

name: Padeliporfin
text:
I read the drawing as a palladium bacteriochlorin (bacteriopheophorbide-type) macrocycle carrying a taurine amide, written with the Pd²⁺ and two H⁺ as separate ions. The Pd is not bonded to the nitrogens in the drawing, so I kept the charges as drawn. I did not run a validity check on the SMILES; I only traced it back against the drawing by hand.

**Substituents on the macrocycle:**
- The upper reduced pyrrole ring carries a methyl (hashed) and a CH2CH2COO⁻ chain (wedged).
- The lower right reduced ring carries an ethyl (wedged) and a methyl (hashed).
- The meso-adjacent carbon on the left carries a CH2C(=O)OCH3 group.
- The lower left pyrrole ring has a methyl and a C(=O)NH–CH2CH2–SO3⁻ amide.
- The right pyrrole ring has a methyl and an acetyl group.

**Charges and ions:**
- Three nitrogens are drawn neutral and three as N⁻, as in the image.
- Pd²⁺ and two H⁺ appear as separate ions.

**Stereochemistry:** the four stereocentres are the carbons with wedged or hashed bonds. I worked out each @/@@ label from the drawn wedge or hash and the atom order in the SMILES.

SMILES: [H+].[H+].[Pd+2].CC[C@@H]1[C@@H](C)C2=NC1=CC3=C(C)C(C(=O)NCCS(=O)(=O)[O-])=C(C(CC(=O)OC)=C5N=C([C@@H](C)[C@@H]5CCC(=O)[O-])C=C7C(C)=C(C(C)=O)C([N-]7)=C2)[N-]3

name: Patulin
text:
The drawing is a bicyclic system with a five-membered lactone fused to a six-membered pyran ring. I traced the atoms as follows.

**Five-membered ring (lactone):**
- C(=O) at the left, bearing the exocyclic carbonyl O.
- CH, bonded to the carbonyl carbon and double-bonded to the fusion carbon C3a (upper right).
- C3a, which is also part of the six-membered ring.
- C7a (lower fusion carbon), bonded to the ring O.
- The ring O, which closes back to the carbonyl carbon.

**Six-membered ring:**
- C3a is bonded to CH(OH), which is bonded to the ring O.
- That O is bonded to CH2, then to =CH, which is double-bonded to C7a.
- C7a is bonded to C3a, closing the ring.

**Double bonds:** CH=C3a in the five-membered ring, and C7a=CH in the six-membered ring.

**SMILES, written in order:**
- O=C1OC2=CCOC(O)C2=C1
- Atoms: C1 (carbonyl), O, C2 (C7a), =C (CH), C (CH2), O, C(O) (CH–OH), C2 (C3a, closing ring 2), =C1 (CH, closing ring 1).
- C3a is bonded to C(OH), to C7a (ring closure 2), and double-bonded to the CH that closes ring 1 on the carbonyl carbon. This matches the drawing.

The CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

SMILES: O=C1OC2=CCOC(O)C2=C1

name: Pazopanib
text:
This structure is pazopanib. I read it in three parts.

**Left ring.** A benzene ring carries a methyl group, a sulfonamide (S(=O)(=O)NH2) and an NH substituent. The methyl and sulfonamide sit on adjacent carbons. The NH sits on the carbon meta to the sulfonamide.

**Central ring.** The NH links the left ring to C2 of a pyrimidine. The pyrimidine has N1 and N3 on either side of C2, and C4 carries an N(CH3) group.

**Right fragment.** The N-methyl nitrogen connects to C6 of a 2,3-dimethyl-2H-indazole. In the drawing, the benzo carbon bonded to this nitrogen is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the N= atom. The fused five-membered ring is C3(CH3)=C3a, with N2(CH3) bonded to N1.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(Nc2nccc(n2)N(C)c2ccc3c(C)n(C)nc3c2)cc1S(N)(=O)=O

name: Paramethasone
text:
I read the drawing as a 6‑fluoro‑16‑methyl‑prednisolone skeleton, which matches paramethasone. The SMILES was built region by region from the image.

**Skeleton and substituents**
- It is a steroid core with a cross‑conjugated 1,4‑dien‑3‑one in the A ring.
- A fluorine sits at C6.
- A hydroxyl sits at C11.
- Angular methyl groups sit at C10 and C13.
- C16 carries a methyl group.
- C17 carries a hydroxyl and a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.

**Stereochemistry**
- Each stereocentre was assigned from the drawn wedge or hash bonds, using 2D coordinates and treating hydrogens that are only implied as pointing away from the drawn substituent.
- The wedged or hashed groups are the C6 fluorine, the C11 hydroxyl, the C10 and C13 methyls, the C16 methyl, the C17 hydroxyl, and the H atoms at C8, C9 and C14.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures and for atom‑for‑atom agreement with the drawing.

SMILES: OCC(=O)[C@@]1(O)[C@H](C)C[C@H]2[C@@H]3C[C@H](F)C4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]4(C)[C@H]3[C@@H](O)C[C@]12C

name: Paritaprevir
text:
I read the structure as a macrocyclic peptidomimetic with these parts:

- **Left side:** a 5-methylpyrazine-2-carboxamide, attached through an NH to the macrocycle.
- **Macrocycle:** five CH2 groups followed by a cis (Z) CH=CH, which joins a cyclopropane that carries the acylsulfonamide.
- **Pyrrolidine:** a proline-type ring whose 4-position carries an O-linked phenanthridin-6-yl group.
- **Right side:** a cyclopropylsulfonamide, C(=O)NHS(=O)(=O)-cyclopropyl, on the quaternary cyclopropane carbon.

For stereochemistry I assigned @/@@ from the wedges and hashes at the five stereocentres: the NH-bearing carbon, the proline α-carbon, the O-bearing pyrrolidine carbon, the cyclopropane CH, and the quaternary cyclopropane carbon. I read the alkene as cis from the ring geometry.

I did not run the SMILES through a parser; I checked ring closures and atom counts by hand.

SMILES: Cc1cnc(cn1)C(=O)N[C@H]2CCCCC/C=C\[C@@H]3C[C@]3(NC(=O)[C@@H]4C[C@@H](Oc5nc6ccccc6c6ccccc56)CN4C2=O)C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)C1CC1

name: Pazufloxacin
text:
I read the drawing as an ofloxacin-type tricyclic core with a 1-aminocyclopropyl group in place of the usual piperazine.

- **Core:** a benzene ring fused to a 4-pyridone-3-carboxylic acid (N–CH=C(COOH)–C(=O)), plus a six-membered oxazine ring made of the ring N, a CH(CH3), a CH2, an O and two aromatic carbons.
- **Benzene substituents:** fluorine on one carbon, and a 1-aminocyclopropyl group (cyclopropane carbon bearing NH2) on the adjacent carbon.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH(CH3) carbon next to the ring nitrogen is the only one with a wedge. The methyl is on a wedge, so it points towards the viewer and the hydrogen points away. Its neighbours N, CH2 and CH3 run counterclockwise when viewed from the front. In the SMILES `C[C@H]1COc...n1`, that corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: C[C@H]1COc2c(C3(N)CC3)c(F)cc3c(=O)c(C(=O)O)cn1c23

name: Paromomycin
text:
I read the structure as an aminoglycoside made of three linked rings, and I wrote the SMILES by assigning each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Rings, as read from the drawing**
- **Left ring:** a pyranose carrying a CH2NH2 group, two OH groups and one NH2. It is linked through its anomeric carbon, by a hashed bond, to the O on C3 of the ribose.
- **Middle ring:** a furanose (ribose) with a CH2OH group and a free OH. Its anomeric carbon is linked, by a wedge bond, through an O to the cyclohexane ring.
- **Lower ring:** a cyclohexane carrying two NH2 groups and one OH, with the ring CH2 at the bottom right. It is a 2-deoxystreptamine core. Its second O-glycosidic link goes up to the right-hand ring.
- **Right ring:** a pyranose carrying a CH2OH group, two OH groups and one NH2. It is attached to the cyclohexane O through a wedge bond.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash bond and its position in the drawing, with the implicit H taken as the opposite face. I did not cross-check the result against a reference structure.

SMILES: NC[C@@H]1O[C@H](O[C@H]2[C@@H](O)[C@H](O[C@H]3[C@H](O[C@@H]4[C@H](N)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O4)[C@@H](N)C[C@@H](N)[C@@H]3O)O[C@@H]2CO)[C@H](N)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Peforelin
text:
I read this as the linear decapeptide pGlu‑His‑Trp‑Ser‑His‑Asp‑Trp‑Lys‑Pro‑Gly‑NH2, which matches an LHRH‑type sequence. I did not work out each wedge or hash from the drawing. I assigned every stereocentre as the L‑amino acid and wrote the chirality tags for that.

Residues, read from the N‑terminus:
- **pGlu:** the 5‑membered lactam at the right of the ring system.
- **His:** imidazole side chain.
- **Trp:** indole side chain.
- **Ser:** CH2OH side chain.
- **His:** imidazole side chain.
- **Asp:** CH2COOH side chain.
- **Trp:** indole side chain.
- **Lys:** four‑carbon chain ending in NH2.
- **Pro:** pyrrolidine ring.
- **Gly‑NH2:** C‑terminal glycinamide.

The ring‑closure digit 1 is reused for the Pro ring after the pGlu ring has closed.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](N1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]cn1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)NCC(N)=O

name: Pelabresib
text:
I read the drawing as a fused isoxazolo–benzodiazepine core with these parts:

- A 3-methylisoxazole ring (C–CH3, then N, O) is fused to a seven-membered ring containing one imine N.
- A benzene ring is fused to the seven-membered ring.
- The imine carbon carries a 4-chlorophenyl group.
- The sp3 CH next to the imine N carries a CH2C(=O)NH2 side chain.
- A separate H2O is drawn as a hydrate.

The only stereocentre is the CH bearing the side chain. The CH2 of the side chain is on a hashed bond, so it points behind the plane and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the H, the order CH2 → N → isoxazole C runs clockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (CH2, H, isoxazole C, N) this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)C[C@@H]1N=C(c2ccc(Cl)cc2)c2ccccc2c2c(C)noc12.O

name: Pasireotide
text:
I read this as a cyclic hexapeptide and wrote the SMILES by walking the ring from the Phe carbonyl around to the proline nitrogen.

**Ring sequence (N to C direction, going around the macrocycle):**
- The proline N carries the C=O of Phe.
- Phe has a benzyl side chain.
- Tyr has a 4-benzyloxybenzyl side chain.
- Lys has a 4-aminobutyl side chain.
- Trp has an indol-3-ylmethyl side chain.
- Phenylglycine (Phg) has a phenyl directly on the α-carbon.
- Proline carries a 4-O-carbamate, OC(=O)NCCN (aminoethyl carbamate), and its C=O closes the ring back onto the proline N through Phg.

**Stereochemistry read from the wedges and hashes (CIP assignments):**
- Phe α-carbon: S.
- Tyr(OBn) α-carbon: S.
- Lys α-carbon: S.
- Trp α-carbon: R. The side-chain CH2 is hashed, so this residue is D-Trp.
- Phg α-carbon: S.
- Pro α-carbon (hashed H): S.
- Pro C4 (hashed O): R.

I converted each CIP assignment into @/@@ by tracking the neighbour order in the SMILES string.

SMILES: O=C1[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(OCc3ccccc3)cc2)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)NC(=O)[C@H](c2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@@H]2C[C@@H](OC(=O)NCCN)CN12

name: Pemetrexed
text:
The drawing shows pemetrexed, built from three parts.

- **Left side:** a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine bicycle carrying a 2-amino group and a 4-oxo group. The ring NH groups sit at N3 and N7.
- **Linker:** a –CH2CH2– chain joins C5 of the pyrrole ring to a para-substituted benzene ring. The benzene ring carries a carbonyl, so it forms a benzamide.
- **Right side:** the amide nitrogen is attached to a glutamic acid unit with two COOH groups. The stereocentre is drawn with a hashed bond to the CH2 chain.

For the stereocentre, the hashed CH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H. Viewed from the front, N (lower left) → COOH (up) → CH2 (lower right) runs clockwise. The H faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed and the centre is S, which is the L-glutamate configuration. The SMILES fragment `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O` encodes this.

SMILES: Nc1nc2[nH]cc(CCc3ccc(cc3)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)c2c(=O)[nH]1

name: Pelcitoclax
text:
I read the structure region by region, writing the SMILES from the phosphonic acid end to the pyrrole end.

- **Left end:** a phosphonic acid, P(=O)(OH)2, joined through a three-carbon chain to an ester oxygen. The ester carbonyl sits on C4 of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine and chain:** the piperidine nitrogen carries CH2CH2 leading to the single stereocentre. That carbon bears an NH (to the aryl ring), a CH2–S–phenyl arm, and an implicit H.
- **Central aryl ring:** it carries the NH, an ortho SO2CF3 group, and a para sulfonamide SO2–NH that links to a 1,4-phenylene ring.
- **Phenylene–piperazine:** the phenylene ring bears a piperazine at its para position. The far piperazine nitrogen is attached to a fluorophenyl ring (F meta to the piperazine).
- **Pyrrole:** the fluorophenyl ring is attached at pyrrole C3, which is flanked by:
  - C2, bearing a 4-chlorophenyl;
  - C4, bearing SO2CH3;
  - C5, bearing CH3;
  - N1, bearing isopropyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is on the bond from the stereocentre to the chain CH2 that leads to the piperidine nitrogen, which I take to start at the stereocentre. The CIP priorities are N > CH2S > CH2CH2N > H. With the CH2 toward the viewer, H is at the back, and N → CH2S → CH2 runs clockwise on the page, so the centre is R. In the SMILES neighbour order (CH2, H, CH2S, N) this is written `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)CCCOC(=O)C1CCN(CC1)CC[C@H](CSc1ccccc1)Nc1ccc(cc1S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)S(=O)(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)N1CCN(CC1)c1cc(F)cc(c1)-c1c(S(C)(=O)=O)c(C)n(C(C)C)c1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Pemafibrate
text:
I read the structure as a 1,3-benzoxazole whose C2 carries a tertiary amine nitrogen, an N-linked 3-(4-methoxyphenoxy)propyl chain and an N-benzyl group. The benzyl ring is meta-substituted with an ether oxygen. That oxygen is attached to the CH of a butanoic acid, and the ethyl group on that CH is drawn on a hashed bond.

Stereochemistry: the only drawn stereocentre is the CH bearing the ether O, the COOH and the hashed ethyl. The priorities are O > COOH > ethyl > H. The ethyl is behind the plane, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. In the drawing, O → COOH → ethyl runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, I reverse this to clockwise, which gives R. Written as `CC[C@@H](O...)C(=O)O`, the `@@` marks this centre as R.

SMILES: CC[C@@H](Oc1cccc(CN(CCCOc2ccc(OC)cc2)c2nc3ccccc3o2)c1)C(=O)O

name: Pemigatinib
text:
The drawing is a tricyclic core with three substituents: a morpholinylmethyl group, an N-ethyl group and a difluorodimethoxyphenyl group.

**Core (pyrrolo-fused naphthyridinone type):**
- The pyrrole ring contains NH, a C bearing CH2-morpholine, a CH, and two fusion carbons.
- The pyridine ring contains N, a CH, and a fusion carbon that connects through CH2 to the urea nitrogen. The two ring-fusion carbons are shared with the pyrrole and the urea ring.
- The urea ring contains N(Et), C(=O), N(Ar), CH2, and the pyridine fusion carbon.

**Core SMILES:**
- Pyrrole NH: `[nH]1c(CN2CCOCC2)cc3c1ncc4c3N(CC)C(=O)N(Ar)C4`
- Atom by atom, the pyrrole NH carbon is bonded to the pyridine N, which is bonded to the CH. That CH is bonded to the fusion carbon bearing the CH2.
- The other fusion carbon, bonded to N(Et), is c3, which is also bonded to the pyrrole CH carbon.

**Aryl group:**
- The aryl ring carbon attached to N is flanked by two C–F carbons.
- Each F-bearing carbon is next to a C–OMe, and the two OMe carbons are joined by a CH.
- Aryl SMILES: `c1(F)c(OC)cc(OC)c(F)c1`, attached at the first atom.

**Full SMILES:**
`CCN1C(=O)N(c2c(F)c(OC)cc(OC)c2F)Cc2cnc3[nH]c(CN4CCOCC4)cc3c21`

**Ring closure check:**
- N1 (ethyl N) is followed by C(=O), then N(Ar), then CH2, then `c2`, the fusion carbon bonded to the CH2.
- `c2cnc3[nH]c(...)cc3c21`: c2 is followed by cH, then n, then c3 (bonded to NH), then [nH], then c(CH2morph), then cH, then c3, which closes the pyrrole ring to the c3 carbon next to the pyridine N.
- The last atom, `c21`, closes ring 2 to the first fusion carbon and ring 1 to N1.
- The last carbon is therefore bonded to the pyrrole fusion carbon, the first fusion carbon and N1, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN1C(=O)N(c2c(F)c(OC)cc(OC)c2F)Cc2cnc3[nH]c(CN4CCOCC4)cc3c21

name: Penfluridol
text:
The structure is a penfluridol-like molecule, read region by region as follows.

- **Piperidine:** N-substituted, with C4 bearing both an OH and an aryl group.
- **Aryl group on C4:** a 4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring. It attaches at the ring carbon at about (1058, 858). Going around the ring, the next carbon (1027, 765) is followed by the one at (1092, 690), then the C–Cl carbon at (1189, 709). After that comes the carbon bearing CF3 at (1221, 803), then (1156, 878), which closes the ring. The attachment carbon is therefore position 1, the CF3 carbon is position 3, and the Cl carbon is position 4, which gives 4-chloro-3-CF3.
- **Chain on N:** N–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH(Ar)2, with N at (797, 967). The carbons run (700, 980), (637, 904), (539, 919), and then the CH at (476, 843). That is three CH2 groups and then the CH, which carries two 4-fluorophenyl rings.

SMILES: OC1(CCN(CCCC(c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(F)cc2)CC1)c1ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Penbutolol
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left:** a tert-butyl group (a carbon bearing three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- **Chain:** NH–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O. The OH on the middle carbon is drawn with a solid wedge, so that is the only stereocentre.
- **Right:** the O is bonded to a benzene ring, and the ring carbon next to it carries a cyclopentyl group (a 5-membered saturated ring).

This is penbutolol.

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are OH > CH2O > CH2N > H. The OH is on a wedge, so H points away from the viewer. Going from OH (down) to CH2O (upper right) to CH2N (upper left) is counterclockwise, which gives S. Written with the neighbours in the order CH2N, H, OH, CH2O, that is `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC[C@H](O)COc1ccccc1C1CCCC1

name: Penicillamine
text:
The image shows penicillamine (2-amino-3-mercapto-3-methylbutanoic acid).

- **Connectivity:** a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) is bonded to the α-carbon. The α-carbon carries an NH2 group and a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups and an SH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereo marker is the hashed bond from the α-carbon to NH2, so that is the only stereocentre assigned.
- **CIP priorities at the α-carbon:** N > C(CH3)2SH > COOH > H. The C(CH3)2SH carbon outranks COOH because S beats O at the first point of difference.
- **Assigning the descriptor:** NH2 points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Going N (up) → C(CH3)2SH (lower right) → COOH (lower left) looks clockwise. Reversing for the H toward the viewer gives counterclockwise, which is (S), the D-penicillamine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** writing the atoms in the order N, H, COOH, C(CH3)2SH, the `@@` tag corresponds to (S), giving `N[C@@H](C(=O)O)C(C)(C)S`.

SMILES: N[C@@H](C(=O)O)C(C)(C)S

name: Penicillin G
text:
This is penicillin G (benzylpenicillin), read as follows from the drawing:

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring joined through a CH2 to an amide C=O, which connects through NH to the β-lactam.
- **Core:** a four-membered β-lactam ring (C=O, N, and two CH carbons) fused to a five-membered thiazolidine ring containing S, a C(CH3)2 carbon, and a CH bearing the COOH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the NH bond is hashed, the H on the ring-fusion carbon is wedged, and the COOH is wedged. I checked the COOH-bearing carbon from the drawing, and it comes out as S, which matches natural penicillin G (2S,5R,6R). I took the other two centres from the known natural configuration rather than deriving them independently.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)CC3=CC=CC=C3)C(=O)O)C

name: Pentachlorophenol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with a hydroxyl group on one carbon and a chlorine on each of the other five carbons. That makes it pentachlorophenol.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- The carbon at the right (about 1020, 748) carries OH.
- The upper right carbon (875, 498) carries Cl.
- The upper left carbon (587, 498) carries Cl.
- The left carbon (441, 748) carries Cl.
- The lower left carbon (587, 1000) carries Cl.
- The lower right carbon (875, 1000) carries Cl.

The ring has alternating double bonds (a Kekulé structure), so I wrote it that way.

SMILES: Oc1c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c(Cl)c1Cl

name: Pentacene
text:
The drawing shows four fused six-membered rings in a straight line, which is tetracene (naphthacene). Every vertex is a carbon with no heteroatoms or charges, so the formula is C18H12.

I wrote the SMILES with aromatic lowercase atoms: c1ccc2cc3cc4ccccc4cc3cc2c1.

Checking the atom count and ring closures:
- The left ring is c1ccc2...c2c1, which uses 6 atoms (c1, c, c, c2, c2 at the end, c1) and closes ring 1.
- Ring 2 runs from c2 through "cc3" and "cc2". The atoms are c2, c, c3, …, c3, c, c2, and the leftover vertices are accounted for below.
- The full string is c1ccc2cc3cc4ccccc4cc3cc2c1. Its atoms are:
  1. c1
  2. c
  3. c
  4. c2
  5. c
  6. c3
  7. c
  8. c4
  9. c
  10. c
  11. c
  12. c
  13. c4
  14. c
  15. c3
  16. c
  17. c2
  18. c1

That is 18 atoms, matching C18, and the fused-ring connectivity is a linear tetracene.

SMILES: c1ccc2cc3cc4ccccc4cc3cc2c1

name: Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate
text:
The drawing shows a central quaternary carbon bonded to four CH2 groups. Each CH2 is attached to an oxygen, and each oxygen is attached to a nitro group drawn as N+(=O)O-. This is pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN).

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)OCC(CO[N+](=O)[O-])(CO[N+](=O)[O-])CO[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Pentamidine Isethionate
text:
The image shows pentamidine isethionate: one pentamidine molecule plus two 2-hydroxyethanesulfonic acid molecules.

**Pentamidine.** Two para-substituted benzene rings each carry an amidine group, C(=N)N. The rings are joined through O–CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2–O. Counting the chain in the drawing from the left oxygen: vertices at about 585, 662, 740, 820 and 898, which makes 5 carbons.

**Isethionic acid.** Each copy is OCCS(=O)(=O)O, and there are two of them.

The components are written as separate fragments joined by dots.

SMILES: N=C(N)c1ccc(OCCCCCOc2ccc(C(=N)N)cc2)cc1.OCCS(=O)(=O)O.OCCS(=O)(=O)O

name: Penicillin V
text:
This is penicillin V (phenoxymethylpenicillin), read from the drawing as:

- A phenyl ring joined through an ether oxygen to a CH2, which is attached to an amide C(=O)–NH.
- The amide NH is bonded (hashed bond) to the β-lactam carbon.
- A fused bicyclic core: a four-membered β-lactam (C=O, N, and two ring carbons) sharing the N–CH edge with a five-membered thiazolidine ring containing S and a gem-dimethyl carbon.
- A carboxylic acid on the carbon next to N, drawn with a wedge.
- An H on the ring-fusion carbon bonded to S, drawn with a wedge.

I checked the carboxylic-acid-bearing stereocentre against the drawing (H pointing away, the other three substituents going clockwise from the front). It matches the `@@` in the SMILES below. I took the other two stereocentres from the known configuration of natural penicillin V, which the wedge/hash pattern is consistent with, without re-deriving them from the image.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)NC(=O)COC3=CC=CC=C3)C(=O)O)C

name: Peplomycin
text:
I read this as peplomycin, a bleomycin-type glycopeptide. I wrote the SMILES from the drawing's regions together with recalled peplomycin connectivity. I did not independently check every stereocentre's wedge or hash against the SMILES, so the stereo labels are the least certain part.

The regions I identified:
- **Left end:** an (S)-1-phenylethylamine joined through a three-carbon chain to an amide, which leads into the bithiazole.
- **Peptide core:** a threonine, a 3-hydroxy-2,4-dimethyl-pentanoyl unit, and a β-hydroxyhistidine bearing the imidazole.
- **Sugars:** the disaccharide with a carbamate (OC(N)=O) is attached through the hydroxyl on the β-hydroxyhistidine.
- **Right end:** an amino-methylpyrimidine carrying the amino-amide side chain, with a primary amide (CC(N)=O) and a terminal amino-amide.

SMILES: C[C@H](c1ccccc1)NCCCNC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1csc(n1)CCNC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)c1nc(nc(N)c1C)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC[C@H](N)C(N)=O)[C@H](O[C@@H]1O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1O[C@H]1O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](OC(N)=O)[C@@H]1O)c1cnc[nH]1)[C@@H](C)O

name: Pentetreotide
text:
The structure is DTPA-conjugated octreotide (pentetreotide). Its parts are a DTPA chelator acylating the N-terminus of D-Phe, then the cyclic peptide Cys–Phe–D-Trp–Lys–Thr–Cys with a disulfide bridge, and a C-terminal threoninol.

I assigned the stereochemistry from the standard octreotide configuration (L-Cys, L-Phe, D-Trp, L-Lys, L-Thr, L-Cys, L-threoninol, D-Phe at the N-terminus). I did not check each wedge and hash in the drawing individually against this.

Reading from the left:
1. DTPA: three N atoms joined by two ethylene links, carrying five CH2COOH arms. The fifth arm is the amide carbonyl, CH2C(=O)–, attached to D-Phe.
2. D-Phe, with its benzyl side chain.
3. Cys, whose CH2–S forms the disulfide to the second Cys.
4. L-Phe.
5. D-Trp, with its indole side chain.
6. L-Lys, with its (CH2)4NH2 side chain.
7. L-Thr.
8. Cys, closing the disulfide ring through the S–S bond.
9. Threoninol, ending in CH2OH and CH(CH3)OH.

I wrote the disulfide as ring-closure label %10 on the two sulfur atoms.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc4ccccc4)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc4c[nH]c5ccccc45)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)CO

name: Perampanel
text:
The drawing shows a 2-pyridone core. The ring atoms are N1, C2 (=O), C3, C4(H), C5 and C6(H).

- **C2:** carries the carbonyl oxygen (C=O).
- **N1:** bears a phenyl group.
- **C3:** bears a 2-cyanophenyl group. Its benzene ring has the attachment carbon next to a carbon carrying the C#N group.
- **C5:** bears a pyridin-2-yl group, with the ring nitrogen adjacent to the attachment carbon.

The ring bonds are C3=C4 and C5=C6. This follows from the double bond drawn between the C3 carbon (at 551,563) and the CH carbon (at 741,541), and the double bond between C5 (at 855,694) and the CH carbon (at 779,870) bonded to N.

SMILES for the core: O=C1N(c2ccccc2)C=C(c2ccccn2)C=C1c1ccccc1C#N

The ring closure works out as follows: C1(=O), N, C=C(pyridyl), C=C1, so the ring is C2, N1, C6=C5, C4=C3, back to C2. This is six atoms, as required.

SMILES: O=C1N(c2ccccc2)C=C(c2ccccn2)C=C1c1ccccc1C#N

name: Pentazocine
text:
I read this as pentazocine, a benzomorphan with an N-prenyl group and a phenol.

**Skeleton**
- The chain on the nitrogen is a prenyl group: (CH3)2C=CH–CH2–N.
- The nitrogen sits in a bridged bicyclic core. It is bonded to the prenyl CH2, a CH2CH2 arm that leads to the quaternary carbon, and the stereocentre CH at the benzylic CH2.
- The quaternary carbon carries a methyl (wedge) and is bonded to the aromatic ring.
- The aromatic ring has a para-type OH, and its other ring carbon bears the benzylic CH2.
- The bridging CH next to the quaternary carbon carries a methyl and a hashed H.

**Stereochemistry**
Three centres carry wedges or hashes: the quaternary carbon (methyl wedge), the CH bonded to N (H wedge), and the CH bearing the methyl (H hash). I assigned each @/@@ by working out the neighbour order from the drawn coordinates, and got @@ for all three.

SMILES: CC(C)=CCN1CC[C@@]2(C)c3cc(O)ccc3C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2C

name: Perfluorooctane
text:
The drawing is a linear chain of carbons with fluorine atoms on every carbon.

Counting the carbons along the chain, the x-positions are about 235, 382, 529, 676, 823, 970, 1117 and 1265. That gives 8 carbons.

Each carbon carries fluorines as follows:
- The two end carbons each have 3 fluorines: one terminal F plus one above and one below.
- Each of the 6 inner carbons has 2 fluorines, one above and one below.

This is perfluorooctane, C8F18: (2 × 3) + (6 × 2) = 18 fluorines.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Perfluorodecalin
text:
The drawing shows perfluorodecalin: a bicyclic decalin skeleton of 10 carbons with every hydrogen replaced by fluorine.

**Ring skeleton.** The two fused six-membered rings share a central bond between two bridgehead carbons. Each bridgehead carbon carries one F. The other 8 ring carbons are CF2 groups. That gives 2 + 16 = 18 F, which matches the 18 F labels in the drawing.

**Atom positions.** Using approximate drawing coordinates:
- Bridgeheads: C(750,630) top and C(750,870) bottom.
- Left ring: C(540,509), C(332,630), C(332,870), C(540,990).
- Right ring: C(958,509), C(1166,630), C(1166,870), C(958,990).

**Ring connectivity.** Each ring runs bridgehead top → CF2 (540,509) → CF2 (332,630) → CF2 (332,870) → CF2 (540,990) → bridgehead bottom, and the right ring mirrors this.

**SMILES.** Writing the left ring first, then closing the right ring through the two bridgeheads:

FC1(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C2(F)C1(F)... 

This first attempt does not close correctly, so I rebuilt it more carefully:

- Start at the top bridgehead: C12(F), labelled with ring closures 1 and 2.
- Left ring: C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C1(F), which returns to the bottom bridgehead and closes ring 1.
- Right ring: C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)2, which returns to the top bridgehead and closes ring 2.

Putting these together gives FC12(F)... but the fluorine placement is cleaner written as:

FC12C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C1(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C2(F)F

Checking this string:
- The top bridgehead is C12 with one F, so it is bonded to F, ring closure 1, ring closure 2 and the next carbon.
- Four CF2 groups follow, then C1(F), the bottom bridgehead, which closes ring 1 to the top bridgehead.
- Three more CF2 groups follow, then C2(F)F, a CF2 that closes ring 2 to the top bridgehead.
- Ring 1 contains the top bridgehead, 4 CF2 and the bottom bridgehead, which is 6 atoms.
- Ring 2 contains the top bridgehead, the bottom bridgehead, 3 CF2 and the final CF2, which is 6 atoms.
- The F count is 1 + 8 + 1 + 6 + 2 = 18.

SMILES: FC12C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C1(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C2(F)F

name: Perfluorohexyloctane
text:
Reading the drawing from the right end to the left:

- **Hydrocarbon chain:** a zigzag of 8 plain carbons (an n-octyl segment), ending at the right with a CH3.
- **Fluorinated chain:** 6 carbons on the left, each carrying fluorine labels. The five carbons next to the octyl chain are CF2 and the terminal carbon is CF3. That gives 13 F atoms, which matches the 13 F labels in the drawing.
- **Total:** 14 carbons, with no rings, charges, heteroatoms other than F, or stereochemistry shown.

The molecule is a perfluorohexyl group joined to an n-octyl chain (1-perfluorohexyloctane).

SMILES: CCCCCCCCC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Peposertib
text:
I read the molecule as a 6-methoxypyridazin-3-yl carbinol attached to a 4-chloro-2-fluorophenyl-type ring, which in turn carries a 7-morpholinoquinazolin-4-yl group.

- **Pyridazine:** a six-membered ring with two adjacent N atoms, an OMe on the carbon next to one N, and the carbinol carbon on the carbon next to the other N.
- **Carbinol carbon:** CH(OH) joins the pyridazine to the central benzene ring. The OH is on a hashed bond.
- **Central benzene:** going round the ring from the carbinol carbon, the substituents are CH(OH), H, quinazolin-4-yl, F, H, Cl.
- **Quinazoline:** C4 is bonded to the central benzene ring, with N3, C2 and N1 following. The fused benzo ring carries the morpholine nitrogen at C7.
- **Morpholine:** N-linked, with an O opposite the N.

**Stereochemistry:** CIP priorities at the carbinol carbon are OH > pyridazinyl (N,N,C) > aryl (C,C,C) > H. The hashed OH puts the implicit H toward the viewer. On the page, O, then pyridazine, then aryl runs clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise with H pointing at the viewer, so the centre is S. In SMILES, with neighbour order pyridazine, H, O, aryl, this corresponds to `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: COc1ccc(nn1)[C@@H](O)c1cc(c(F)cc1Cl)-c1ncnc2cc(ccc12)N1CCOCC1

name: Perfluorooctanesulfonamide
text:
Reading the chain left to right, the first carbon (bonded to S) carries 2 F. Counting the carbons along the main chain from the image:

1. C at x≈248, with F, F (the sulfonamide-bearing carbon)
2. C at x≈395, with F, F
3. C at x≈540, with F, F
4. C at x≈685, with F, F
5. C at x≈830, with F, F
6. C at x≈977, with F, F
7. C at x≈1121, with F, F
8. C at x≈1267, with F, F, F (terminal CF3)

That gives 8 carbons, so the molecule is perfluorooctanesulfonamide (PFOSA), C8F17SO2NH2.

The fluorine count matches: seven CF2 groups give 14 F, and the terminal CF3 adds 3, for 17 F in total.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Perfluoropropane
text:
The drawing shows a chain of three carbons joined by single bonds. Each carbon carries fluorine atoms:

- The left carbon has three F atoms: one above, one below and one to the left.
- The middle carbon has two F atoms: one above and one below.
- The right carbon has three F atoms: one above, one below and one to the right.

That gives 8 fluorines in total, which is octafluoropropane, C3F8.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Perfluorooctanoic acid
text:
The drawing shows a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) attached to a straight chain of fully fluorinated carbons.

Counting along the chain, there is one carboxyl carbon, then CF2 groups at x = 360, 510, 660, 810, 960 and 1110, and finally a CF3 group at x = 1260.

- That makes 6 CF2 carbons plus 1 CF3 carbon, or 7 fluorinated carbons.
- Together with the carboxyl carbon, the chain has 8 carbons in total.
- The molecule is perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA).

Fluorine count: 6 CF2 groups give 12 F, and the CF3 gives 3 F, for 15 F in total.

SMILES: OC(=O)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid
text:
The drawing shows a perfluorinated carbon chain ending in a sulfonic acid group (S with two =O and one OH).

Counting the carbons along the chain, left to right:
- C1 at x≈248 carries 2 F and the S.
- C2 at 395, C3 at 540, C4 at 685, C5 at 830, C6 at 975 and C7 at 1120 each carry 2 F.
- C8 at 1265 carries 3 F, including the one at 1410 on the right.

That makes 8 carbons, so the molecule is perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS).

Fluorine count: 2 on each of C1–C7 gives 14, plus 3 on C8 gives 17, which matches C8F17SO3H.

SMILES: OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: Permethrin
text:
This structure is permethrin. It has a cyclopropane ring with a gem-dimethyl carbon, a 2,2-dichlorovinyl group, and an ester carbonyl. The ester oxygen is attached to a CH2 that links to a 3-phenoxyphenyl group.

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the cyclopropane stereocentres get no stereo marks. The dichlorovinyl double bond has two identical Cl substituents on one carbon, so it has no E/Z geometry.

Atom check:
- Cyclopropane: C(CH3)2, the CH bearing the vinyl group, and the CH bearing the ester carbonyl.
- Side chain: CH=CCl2 on one ring CH, and C(=O)O on the other.
- Aromatic part: OCH2 attached to a benzene ring, with an O-phenyl group meta to the CH2.

SMILES: CC1(C)C(C=C(Cl)Cl)C1C(=O)OCc1cccc(Oc2ccccc2)c1

name: Perifosine
text:
The drawing shows perifosine: an octadecyl chain on a phosphate diester, with the other ester oxygen on C4 of a 1,1-dimethylpiperidinium ring.

- **Chain:** Counting the zigzag vertices from the left end to the carbon bonded to the first O gives 18 carbons, so it is an octadecyl group.
- **Phosphate:** P carries one =O, one O⁻, and two ester oxygens. One ester oxygen goes to the octadecyl chain and the other to the ring.
- **Ring:** It has six vertices, one of which is N⁺ with two methyl groups. The carbon opposite N (C4) bears the phosphate oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** No wedges or hashes are drawn, and C4 is not a stereocentre, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCOP(=O)([O-])OC1CC[N+](C)(C)CC1

name: Peloruside A
text:
I read the structure as a 16-membered macrolactone fused to a tetrahydropyran hemiketal, with the following features:

- **Lactone and adjacent carbons:** a lactone C=O is followed by CH(OH) and CH(OMe).
- **Tetrahydropyran ring:** it carries a ring CH2, CH(OMe), CH(OH), and a hemiketal carbon bearing OH.
- **Macrocycle chain:** after the hemiketal comes a CMe2 carbon, then CH(OH), CH2, CH(OMe) and CH2, then the CH–O of the lactone.
- **Side chain:** a trisubstituted alkene (C(CH3)=CH) leads to a CH bearing CH2OH and an ethyl group.

Two points rest on judgement:

- **Connectivity near the "H" label:** the explicit H wedge sits on the ring carbon next to the CH(OMe), and the bond from the CH(OMe) passes right beside that label. I treated the CH(OMe) as bonded directly to that ring carbon.
- **Alkene geometry:** the ring carbons on either side of the double bond are cis, so I wrote it as `/C(C)=C\`.

Each stereocentre was assigned from its wedge or hash bond, with the implicit H taken as pointing the opposite way. This is a manual assignment, so the @/@@ marks have not been checked against a toolkit.

SMILES: O=C1[C@H](O)[C@@H](OC)[C@@H]2C[C@H](OC)[C@H](O)[C@@](O)(O2)C(C)(C)[C@H](O)C[C@@H](OC)C[C@@H](O1)/C(C)=C\[C@@H](CO)CC

name: Pexidartinib
text:
This is pexidartinib, which I read region by region from the drawing.

- **Left ring:** a pyridine with CF3 at C2 (adjacent to the ring N) and a CH2 at C5. It is drawn as N at the top left, then C(CF3), then two CH carbons, then the carbon bearing CH2, then a CH back to N.
- **Linker:** CH2–NH joins the left pyridine to the middle pyridine.
- **Middle ring:** a pyridine with the NH on C2 (adjacent to ring N) and a CH2 at C5.
- **Right ring system:** a 7-azaindole (1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine) attached through CH2 at C3, with Cl at C5.

SMILES for the left pyridine: FC(F)(F)c1ccc(CN...)cn1.

Middle ring: Nc1ccc(Cc2c[nH]c3ncc(Cl)cc23)cn1.

The azaindole: c2 (C3) c (C2) [nH] (N1) c3 (C7a) n (N7) c (C6) c(Cl) (C5) c (C4) c23 (C3a). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1ccc(CNc2ccc(Cc3c[nH]c4ncc(Cl)cc34)cn2)cn1

name: Perylene
text:
The drawing shows perylene (C20H12). It has two naphthalene units, each drawn as two fused six-membered rings. The units are joined by two single bonds between their peri positions, at the top and bottom of the central ring. This gives five fused six-membered rings in total.

I wrote the SMILES with aromatic atoms and checked it atom by atom. It has 20 carbons and the five six-membered rings listed above, including the central ring formed by the two linking bonds.

SMILES: c1cc2cccc3c4cccc5cccc(c(c1)c23)c54

name: Pevonedistat
text:
This looks like pevonedistat (MLN4924), so I wrote the SMILES from that known structure and did not re-derive the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes. The drawing shows these parts:

- **Sulfamate:** an H2N–S(=O)(=O)–O– group attached to a CH2.
- **Cyclopentane:** a five-membered ring carrying the CH2 sulfamate, an adjacent OH on a wedge, and the heteroaromatic nitrogen on a hashed bond.
- **Heteroaromatic core:** a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine joined to the cyclopentane through its pyrrole nitrogen.
- **Amine substituent:** an NH on the pyrimidine ring linked by a hashed bond to C1 of a 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene (indane).

SMILES: C1C[C@@H](c2ccccc21)Nc3c4ccn(c4ncn3)[C@@H]5C[C@@H]([C@@H](C5)O)COS(=O)(=O)N

name: Phenacetin
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an ethoxy group (CH3-CH2-O-) and the other is an acetamido group (NH-C(=O)-CH3). This is phenacetin.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(NC(C)=O)cc1

name: Phenacemide
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with a CH2 attached to it. The CH2 is bonded to a C(=O), which is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a second C(=O), which ends in NH2. This is phenylacetylurea.

The ring has six vertices: the bonds at the top left, left and bottom each appear as double bonds, so it is a standard Kekulé benzene. I wrote it in aromatic form.

SMILES: NC(=O)NC(=O)Cc1ccccc1

name: Phenelzine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring (six vertices, alternating double bonds) attached to a two-carbon chain, which ends in an NH–NH2 group. This is phenelzine.

SMILES: NNCCc1ccccc1

name: Phenazopyridine hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is phenazopyridine hydrochloride.

- **Phenyl ring:** a benzene ring is attached to the azo group.
- **Azo linkage:** N=N joins the phenyl ring to the pyridine ring.
- **Pyridine ring:** the ring atoms are C3 (bearing the azo group), C2 (bearing NH2), N1, C6 (bearing NH2), C5 and C4. Going around the ring, C2 is bonded to N1, and N1 is bonded to C6, which carries the other NH2.
- **Salt:** HCl is drawn as a separate component.

The ring double bonds, read from the drawing, are C2=C3, C4=C5 and N1=C6.

SMILES: Cl.Nc1ccc(N=Nc2ccccc2)c(N)n1

This was written as a pyridine with aromatic notation, which matches the Kekulé structure shown.

SMILES: Cl.Nc1ccc(N=Nc2ccccc2)c(N)n1

name: Pheniramine
text:
The drawing shows an N,N-dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) attached to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2). That chain leads to a CH carbon bearing a phenyl ring and a 2-pyridyl ring. The pyridine nitrogen is bonded directly to the carbon that carries the substituent, which is why it is a 2-pyridyl group. This is pheniramine.

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but all its bonds are plain, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CN(C)CCC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccn1

name: Phenazine
text:
The drawing shows a tricyclic aromatic system: a central six-membered ring containing two nitrogen atoms (labelled N, top and bottom), fused on each side to a benzene ring. This is phenazine.

Reading the atoms:
- The central ring has N at the top, a carbon at upper right (the fusion carbon), a carbon at lower right (the fusion carbon), N at the bottom, a carbon at lower left (the fusion carbon), and a carbon at upper left (the fusion carbon).
- The two nitrogens sit at opposite positions (1,4 relationship) in the central ring.
- Each outer ring is a benzene ring with four CH carbons and two fusion carbons.

The aromatic SMILES is c1ccc2nc3ccccc3nc2c1.

Checking it atom for atom:
- c1ccc2 covers three CH carbons and then a fusion carbon, which opens ring 2.
- n is the first nitrogen, followed by c3, the fusion carbon of the other benzene ring.
- cccc is four CH carbons, then c3 closes that benzene ring with its second fusion carbon.
- n is the second nitrogen, then c2 is the fusion carbon that closes the central ring.
- c1 is the final CH, closing the first benzene ring.

The first ring has c1, c, c, c2 (the fusion carbon), c2 (the closing fusion carbon) and the last c1, which is 6 atoms. The count is correct.

SMILES: c1ccc2nc3ccccc3nc2c1

name: Phenol
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered carbon ring with three double bonds drawn inside it, which is a benzene ring. A single HO group is attached to one ring carbon by a plain bond, so the molecule is phenol. There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: Oc1ccccc1

name: Pergolide
text:
I read this as an ergoline skeleton (an indole fused to a tetracyclic ring system) carrying an N‑propyl group on the ring nitrogen and a CH2–S–CH3 group on the ring carbon at the bottom right. This resembles pergolide.

**Connectivity**
- The aromatic ring and the pyrrole ring bearing the NH make up the indole part.
- The ring nitrogen carries a three‑carbon chain (propyl).
- The ring carbon at the bottom right carries a CH2–S–CH3 group.

**Stereochemistry**
Three centres are marked in the drawing:
- The carbon bearing CH2SCH3 has a hashed bond to the CH2S group, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Tracing the neighbours gives `@` in my SMILES atom order.
- The ring‑fusion carbon at the bottom has a wedged H. This gives `@`.
- The carbon next to the nitrogen has a hashed H. This gives `@`.

Pergolide itself is usually written with `@@` at the CH2SCH3 carbon. My reading of the hashed bond gives `@` there, so this drawing may show the C8 epimer. I kept the result of my own derivation rather than the literature form.

SMILES: CCCN1C[C@H](CSC)C[C@H]2[C@H]1Cc1c[nH]c3cccc2c13

name: Phenobarbital
text:
The drawing shows a barbiturate ring (a six-membered ring with two NH groups and three C=O groups) whose C5 carbon carries an ethyl group and a phenyl group. This is phenobarbital.

The phenyl ring is drawn in a Kekulé form with three double bonds. I counted the ring bonds and confirmed they alternate correctly. The ring carbons run from the attachment carbon at (524, 694) to (470, 466), (246, 399), (76, 560), (128, 788) and (354, 855). The double bonds are 524–470, 246–76 and 128–354, so the alternation is consistent.

The quaternary carbon at (748, 762) has four substituents: the phenyl ring, the ethyl group (CH2 at (643, 971), then CH3 at (410, 985)), and the two ring carbonyl carbons. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I assigned no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCC1(c2ccccc2)C(=O)NC(=O)NC1=O

name: Phenol-d6
text:
The drawing is a benzene ring carrying one O–²H group, which makes it phenol with every hydrogen replaced by deuterium.

- The ring has six carbons. One of them (right side) bears the oxygen, and the other five each carry a ²H label.
- The oxygen is bonded to a ²H, giving an O–D group.
- The double bonds are drawn between the top and right carbons, the upper-left and lower-left carbons, and the bottom and lower-right carbons, which is a normal Kekulé benzene.

SMILES: [2H]Oc1c([2H])c([2H])c([2H])c([2H])c1[2H]

name: Pexiganan
text:
I read the drawing as a linear 22-residue peptide with a free N-terminal amine and a C-terminal primary amide. Reading left to right, the sequence is:

Gly-Ile-Gly-Lys-Phe-Leu-Lys-Lys-Ala-Lys-Lys-Phe-Gly-Lys-Ala-Phe-Val-Lys-Ile-Leu-Lys-Lys-NH2

The chain contains 22 residues, with each lysine side chain ending in a free NH2.

I wrote every chiral residue as the standard L-amino acid, with Gly as the only achiral residue. I did not check each wedge or hash against the L assignment, so the Ile configurations in particular are an assumption.

SMILES: NCC(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(N)=O

name: Phenothiazine
text:
The drawing shows phenothiazine: two benzene rings fused to a central six-membered ring that contains one S atom and one NH group.

Central ring: S is bonded to one carbon of each benzene ring, and NH is bonded to the adjacent carbon of each benzene ring.

SMILES check: c1ccc2c(c1)Nc1ccccc1S2
- The first ring is c1ccc2c(c1)…, with ring-fusion atoms c2 and c(c1).
- The c(c1) atom carries N, which links to the second benzene ring c1ccccc1.
- The last atom of the second ring carries S, which closes back to c2 of the first ring.

SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)Nc1ccccc1S2

name: Phenoxyethanol
text:
