The drawing shows a benzene ring (six vertices, alternating double bonds) attached to an oxygen. That oxygen connects to a two-carbon chain ending in OH, so the molecule is 2-phenoxyethanol. There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: OCCOc1ccccc1

name: Phenoperidine
text:
The drawing shows an ethyl ester (CH3CH2–O–C(=O)–) attached to C4 of a piperidine ring. C4 also carries a phenyl group. The ring nitrogen bears a three-carbon chain, CH2–CH2–CH(OH)–, which ends in a second phenyl group.

All bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so I included no stereochemistry. The carbon bearing the OH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn without stereo marking.

Written atom by atom: the ethyl group is CC, then O, then C(=O), then the quaternary ring carbon C1(c2ccccc2) with the phenyl. The ring continues CCN(CC1) with the side chain CCC(O)c3ccccc3 on the nitrogen.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1(c2ccccc2)CCN(CCC(O)c2ccccc2)CC1

name: Phenprocoumon
text:
The drawing is a 4-hydroxycoumarin core carrying a 1-phenylpropyl group at C3.

- **Coumarin core:** the lactone C(=O) is bonded to the ring O, which is bonded to the fused benzene ring. C3 (double bond to C4) carries the side chain, and C4 carries the OH.
- **Side chain:** the CH attached to C3 bears an ethyl group (CH2–CH3) and a phenyl ring, so it is a 1-phenylpropyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CCC(c1ccccc1)C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O

name: Phenoxazine
text:
The drawing shows a phenoxazine skeleton: two benzene rings fused to a central six-membered ring that contains one O and one NH, at opposite positions.

- The central ring has O at the top and NH at the bottom.
- Each benzene ring is attached to both heteroatoms through two adjacent ring carbons.
- Each benzene ring is drawn with three double bonds, so the SMILES uses aromatic lowercase atoms.

Writing it out: `c1ccc2c(c1)Nc1ccccc1O2`. The ring-closure digit 1 is reused for the second benzene ring after the first closes, which is valid.

Atom check:
- The first ring is c1ccc2c(c1): atoms c1, c, c, c2, c(, c1), which is six carbons. The c2 carbon bonds to O through ring closure 2, and the next carbon bonds to N.
- N then connects to c1ccccc1, a second benzene ring. Its last carbon bears O, closing ring 2 with the first ring.

This gives 12 carbons, 1 N and 1 O, matching the drawing.

SMILES: c1ccc2c(c1)Nc1ccccc1O2

name: Phentermine
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary carbon bearing an NH2 group, two methyl groups, and a CH2 that connects to a benzene ring. This is phentermine, 2-methyl-1-phenylpropan-2-amine.

The central carbon has four substituents: NH2, two methyls and the CH2. The benzene ring has six carbons with alternating double bonds and is attached through the CH2. Because the central carbon carries two identical methyls, it is not a stereocentre, so no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: CC(C)(N)Cc1ccccc1

name: Phensuximide
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered succinimide ring with an N-methyl group, two carbonyl oxygens, and a phenyl group on the ring carbon next to one carbonyl. This is N-methyl-2-phenylsuccinimide (3-phenyl-1-methylpyrrolidine-2,5-dione).

Reading the ring atoms:
- The nitrogen carries a methyl group (the line going up-left).
- One carbonyl carbon (top) is double-bonded to O and bonded to N and to the CH that carries the phenyl group.
- The other carbonyl carbon (bottom left) is double-bonded to O and bonded to N and to the CH2.
- The CH2 connects to the CH bearing the phenyl group, closing the five-membered ring.
- The phenyl ring is drawn as a benzene with three double bonds.

All bonds at the CH carbon are plain lines, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)CC(c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Phentolamine
text:
This structure is phentolamine.

- **Imidazoline ring:** a five-membered ring made of NH, CH2, CH2, N and a C that is double-bonded to N. That C also carries a CH2 substituent.
- **Linker:** the CH2 connects to a tertiary N.
- **Aryl groups on N:** a 4-methylphenyl (p-tolyl) group and a 3-hydroxyphenyl group.
- **Hydroxyphenyl substitution:** the ring carbon bonded to N is C1. Going around the ring, the next carbon (top-left) is C2, and the one after it carries OH, so OH is at C3 (meta). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)N(CC1=NCCN1)c1cccc(O)c1

name: Phenylbutazone
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered pyrazolidine-3,5-dione ring with the following parts:

- **Ring:** C(=O)–N(Ph)–N(Ph)–C(=O)–CH, where the CH closes back onto the first carbonyl carbon.
- **Substituents:** each nitrogen carries a phenyl group, and the CH carries a straight n-butyl chain.
- **Butyl chain:** the vertices run from the CH at (657, 890) to (489, 937) to (365, 816) to (199, 862) to (75, 742), which is four carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

This is phenylbutazone.

SMILES: CCCCC1C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N(c2ccccc2)C1=O

name: Phenylmercuric Acetate
text:
The drawing shows phenylmercuric acetate. It has three parts:

- A benzene ring with a single bond from one ring carbon to Hg.
- An Hg–O single bond.
- An acetate group, where O is bonded to a carbon that carries a C=O and a CH3.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[Hg]c1ccccc1

name: Phenytoin
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered hydantoin ring with two phenyl groups on the same carbon. This is 5,5-diphenylimidazolidine-2,4-dione (phenytoin).

Ring atoms, read from the image:
- A quaternary carbon at about (760, 652) carries both phenyl groups.
- Going around the ring from it: a C=O carbon at the top (O at top left), then NH, then a second C=O carbon (O at right), then NH, which closes back to the quaternary carbon.

The two phenyl rings are drawn as plain six-membered rings with alternating double bonds. The quaternary carbon is not a stereocentre, since its two substituents are identical phenyls, and no wedges or hashes are drawn.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)N1

name: Phenylmercuric Nitrate
text:
The drawing shows phenylmercuric nitrate: a benzene ring bonded to Hg, which is bonded to an oxygen of a nitrate group.

- **Ring:** six carbons with three double bonds. The Hg-bearing carbon sits at the lower left of the ring, and the double bonds are drawn from that carbon to the next one down, from the top vertex to the upper right, and from the right vertex to the bottom.
- **Nitrate:** Hg–O–N⁺(=O)–O⁻, with the nitrogen carrying the plus charge and the single-bonded terminal oxygen carrying the minus charge.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown, so none is included.

The SMILES is written as a Kekulé benzene ring, with the Hg attached at the first ring carbon.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)O[Hg]C1=CC=CC=C1

name: Phosphocreatine
text:
This is phosphocreatine. Reading the drawing region by region:

- A methyl group is attached to a nitrogen.
- That nitrogen carries a CH2 that leads to a carboxylic acid, drawn as C(=O)OH.
- The same nitrogen is bonded to a central carbon, which bears an NH2 group and a double bond to a second nitrogen (C=N).
- That second nitrogen is bonded to phosphorus, which carries one P=O and two OH groups.

SMILES: CN(CC(=O)O)C(N)=NP(=O)(O)O

name: Phosphoric Acid
text:
The image shows a central phosphorus atom with four oxygen substituents. One oxygen is joined by a double bond (P=O), and the other three are hydroxyl groups (OH). This is phosphoric acid, H3PO4.

SMILES: O=P(O)(O)O

name: Phosphoenolpyruvate
text:
The drawing shows phosphoenolpyruvic acid, read as follows:

- A terminal CH2 is double-bonded to a carbon.
- That carbon is bonded to an oxygen, which is bonded to a phosphorus carrying one P=O and two OH groups (a phosphate group).
- The same carbon is also bonded to a carboxylic acid carbon, C(=O)OH.

There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry applies.

SMILES: C=C(OP(=O)(O)O)C(=O)O

name: Phenylephrine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left chain:** a methyl group is attached to an NH, which is attached to a CH2.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH2 joins a carbon that carries an OH on a bold wedge and a bond to the ring. The wedge is the only stereo information in the drawing.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the chain attached at one carbon and an OH on the ring carbon two positions away, so the two substituents are meta to each other.
- **Identity:** this is phenylephrine.

Assigning the stereocentre with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer, the CIP priorities are OH, then CH2N (N beats C), then the aryl carbon. On screen the OH (bottom), CH2N (upper left) and aryl (right) run clockwise, so the centre is R.

Checking the SMILES `CNC[C@H](O)c1cccc(O)c1`: the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, O, aryl. With `@`, viewing from the CH2, the sequence H, O, aryl runs counterclockwise. Working this through gives R, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNC[C@H](O)c1cccc(O)c1

name: Phytate
text:
The drawing shows a cyclohexane ring with six carbons. Each ring carbon carries an O–P(=O)(OH)2 group, so the molecule is a hexakis(dihydrogen phosphate) of cyclohexane (phytic acid skeleton). All bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: OP(O)(=O)OC1C(OP(O)(O)=O)C(OP(O)(O)=O)C(OP(O)(O)=O)C(OP(O)(O)=O)C1OP(O)(O)=O

name: Physostigmine
text:
This structure is physostigmine (eserine), a tricyclic pyrroloindoline carrying an N-methylcarbamate on the benzene ring. I assigned the stereocentres from the two wedges in the drawing.

**Connectivity**
- The benzene ring has a carbamate oxygen at the right-hand carbon. The O–C(=O)–NH–CH3 group is on the right.
- The ring-fusion carbon attached to the benzene ring (C3a) bears a wedged methyl. Its other neighbours are a CH2 and the aminal carbon (C8a).
- The five-membered ring on the left runs C3a, CH2, CH2, N(CH3), C8a.
- C8a also bonds to the indoline N(CH3), which is attached to the benzene ring. C8a carries a wedged H.

**Stereochemistry**
- For the SMILES atom order aromatic C, ring closure to C8a, methyl, CH2, I found C3a to be `[C@]`. The wedged methyl points toward the viewer.
- For the atom order N(CH3) of the pyrrolidine, H, C3a, indoline N, I found C8a to be `[C@@H]`. The wedged H points toward the viewer.

SMILES: CNC(=O)Oc1ccc2c(c1)[C@]3(C)CCN(C)[C@@H]3N2C

name: Piclamilast
text:
The drawing shows a benzamide (this resembles roflumilast, but with a cyclopentyloxy group and a methoxy group in place of roflumilast's cyclopropylmethoxy and difluoromethoxy groups).

**Benzene ring:** The carbonyl-bearing carbon sits at the top right of the ring. The cyclopentyloxy group is on the adjacent meta carbon (upper left), and the methoxy group is on the next carbon (lower left, para to the carbonyl carbon).

**Cyclopentyl ether:** A five-membered carbon ring is attached through an oxygen to the benzene ring.

**Amide and pyridine:** The carbonyl carbon is bonded to an NH, which is attached to the 4-position of a pyridine. Chlorines are on the 3- and 5-positions of that pyridine, flanking the NH-bearing carbon. The ring nitrogen sits between the two CH carbons.

**SMILES:** COc1ccc(cc1OC1CCCC1)C(=O)Nc1c(Cl)cncc1Cl

Checking the ring atoms: the pyridine is c1 (bearing N), c(Cl), c, n, c, c1Cl, which gives six atoms, and the aromatic benzene ring is also complete.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1OC1CCCC1)C(=O)Nc1c(Cl)cncc1Cl

name: Pibrentasvir
text:
This is my reading of the drawing, written as SMILES. It describes a symmetric molecule with the following parts:

- **Central core:** a pyrrolidine whose nitrogen carries a 3,5-difluoro-4-[4-(4-fluorophenyl)piperidin-1-yl]phenyl group. The 2- and 5-positions of this pyrrolidine each carry a fluorobenzimidazole.
- **Each arm:** the benzimidazole C2 is bonded to a pyrrolidine. That pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by an O-methyl-threonine residue, whose amine is capped as a methyl carbamate.

The drawing is the same molecule on both sides, mirrored, so the wedges on one side appear as hashes on the other. The overall structure matches pibrentasvir, and I wrote the stereocentres from that known configuration and not from the wedges and hashes alone. I then checked that the two arms are written consistently:

- The threonine residues are L-configured (2S,3R).
- Both arm pyrrolidines are S.
- The central pyrrolidine is drawn with the same stereo pattern at both of its substituted carbons.

SMILES: COC(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)OC)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1c1nc2cc(F)c(cc2[nH]1)[C@@H]1CC[C@H](N1c1cc(F)c(N2CCC(CC2)c2ccc(F)cc2)c(F)c1)c1cc2[nH]c(nc2cc1F)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)[C@@H](C)OC

name: Phylloquinone
text:
This is phylloquinone (vitamin K1): a 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone carrying a phytyl side chain at C3.

**Ring.** The quinone ring is fused to a benzene ring. Its two C=O carbons sit at the positions drawn with the O labels, and one ring carbon beside them carries a methyl group. The adjacent ring carbon carries the side chain.

**Side chain.** Reading from the ring outward, I counted:
- a CH2, then a CH= double-bonded to a carbon bearing a methyl;
- three CH2 groups, then a stereocentre with a hashed methyl;
- three CH2 groups, then a stereocentre with a wedged methyl;
- three CH2 groups, then a terminal isopropyl group.

**Double bond.** The methyl on the quaternary alkene carbon and the ring-side CH2 on the other alkene carbon both point up. So the two main-chain CH2 groups are on opposite sides, which makes the double bond E.

**Stereocentres.** I assigned each centre from the wedge or hash and the implicit H, writing the SMILES from the isopropyl end:
- The wedged-methyl carbon comes out as `[C@@H]`.
- The hashed-methyl carbon also comes out as `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: CC(C)CCC[C@@H](C)CCC[C@@H](C)CCC/C(C)=C/CC1=C(C)C(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: Picoplatin
text:
The image shows four separate components with no bonds between them:

- A platinum(II) cation, Pt²⁺.
- Two chloride anions, Cl⁻. One sits to the right of the ring at the end of a line, but the line ends at an unlabelled vertex, so that vertex is a methyl carbon and the Cl⁻ is a separate ion.
- A free ammonia molecule, NH₃.
- A six-membered ring with one nitrogen, which is pyridine. It has a C=N double bond at the top and two further double bonds in the Kekulé drawing. The carbon next to the ring nitrogen, at the lower right, carries the methyl group. This is 2-methylpyridine.

Counting the ring vertices gives N, the top-left C, the left C, the bottom-left C, the bottom-right C, and the methyl-bearing C, which makes six atoms.

SMILES: [Pt+2].[Cl-].[Cl-].N.CC1=CC=CC=N1

name: Picotamide
text:
The structure is a benzene ring carrying three substituents, with two pyridin-3-ylmethyl amide arms.

**Central benzene ring.** Reading the vertices: C1 at (597,826) bears the amide C(=O)NH on the left. C2 at (649,938) bears OMe. C3 at (771,949) is CH. C4 at (843,849) is CH. C5 at (791,738) bears the right amide C(=O)NH. C6 at (668,727) is CH.

The ring order is C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6. C1 (left amide) and C5 (right amide) are both adjacent to C6, so they are meta to each other. OMe on C2 is ortho to C1 and para to C5.

**Left arm.** C1 is attached to C(=O)NHCH2-pyridin-3-yl. In the pyridine, N sits at (268,367), with a CH at (147,355) on one side and a CH at (320,478) on the other. The carbon at (320,478) is bonded to the substituted carbon (250,578), so the substituent is on the 3-position.

**Right arm.** C5 is attached to C(=O)NHCH2-pyridin-3-yl. The pyridine here has N at (1352,683), a CH at (1231,672), then the substituted carbon (1180,560). The substituted carbon is separated from N by one CH, so this is also a 3-pyridyl group.

**SMILES.** Starting from the OMe carbon:
COc1ccc(C(=O)NCc2cccnc2)cc1C(=O)NCc1cccnc1

Checking connectivity: c1 (the OMe carbon) → c → c → c(C(=O)N...) is C5 → c is C6 → c1 closes the ring at C1 with its amide. The amide on C1 is ortho to OMe and the other amide is para to OMe, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc(C(=O)NCc2cccnc2)cc1C(=O)NCc1cccnc1

name: Phthalocyanine
text:
I read this as metal-free phthalocyanine, drawn in one particular tautomer with two NH groups on opposite isoindole units. I did not run the SMILES through a validator; I checked it by hand against the drawing.

The macrocycle has four benzo-fused five-membered rings (isoindole units) joined by four bridging aza nitrogens. Two of the ring nitrogens carry H (the labelled NH groups at upper right and lower left). The other two ring nitrogens are plain imine-type N. I wrote the double bonds as drawn, then closed the rings to give the SMILES below.

SMILES: C12=NC(c3ccccc31)=NC4=C5C=CC=CC5=C(N4)N=C6N=C(N=C7NC(=N2)c8ccccc87)c9ccccc69

name: Pimavanserin
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** an isobutyl group, (CH3)2CH-CH2, joined through an oxygen to a benzene ring (isobutoxy group).
- **Left ring:** a para-substituted benzene. One para position carries the isobutoxy oxygen, and the other carries a CH2 that leads to NH.
- **Centre:** the NH is bonded to a C=O, which is bonded to a second nitrogen, so this is a urea.
- **Second nitrogen:** it carries a 4-fluorobenzyl group (CH2 attached to a para-fluorophenyl ring) and a 1-methylpiperidin-4-yl group.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen bears a methyl group, and the ring carbon at position 4 is bonded to the urea nitrogen.

There are no wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds, so no stereochemistry is written.

SMILES: CC(C)COc1ccc(CNC(=O)N(Cc2ccc(F)cc2)C2CCN(C)CC2)cc1

name: Pimobendan
text:
This is a 4,5-dihydropyridazin-3(2H)-one with a methyl group at C5, joined at C6 to a benzimidazole that carries a 4-methoxyphenyl group at its 2-position (the pimobendan scaffold).

**Dihydropyridazinone ring.** Starting from the carbonyl: O=C1CC(C)C(=NN1)–. The ring atoms are C(=O), CH2, CH(CH3), C(=N), N, and NH.

**Benzimidazole.** The ring carbon attached to the pyridazinone is bonded to the benzene ring carbon at (535,712). Going around the benzene ring: (535,712) → (555,596) → (667,557) → (756,632) → (735,749) → (624,788) → back to (535,712). The atoms at (756,632) and (735,749) are the fusion carbons. (756,632) bonds to N (873,620), the =N, which is double-bonded to C2 at (922,724). C2 bonds to NH (836,805), which bonds to (735,749). C2 also carries the aryl group.

**Aryl group.** C2 attaches to a benzene ring bearing OCH3 at the para position.

**SMILES assembly.** Writing the benzimidazole as c1ccc2nc(-c3ccc(OC)cc3)[nH]c2c1, the pyridazinone attaches at the benzene carbon that is meta to the fusion carbon next to the =N and para to the fusion carbon next to the NH.

- The attachment carbon (535,712) is adjacent to (624,788), which is adjacent to the fusion carbon (735,749) that bears the NH.
- So the attachment carbon is separated from the NH-bearing fusion carbon by one CH, making it meta to that carbon.
- It is separated from the N=-bearing fusion carbon (756,632) by two CH atoms, (555,596) and (667,557), making it para to that carbon.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)-c1nc2ccc(cc2[nH]1)C1=NNC(=O)CC1C

name: Pilocarpine
text:
I read the molecule as pilocarpine: a γ-butyrolactone ring carrying an ethyl group and a (1-methylimidazol-5-yl)methyl group.

**Skeleton**
- The five-membered lactone ring consists of the ring oxygen, a CH2, two CH carbons and the C=O carbon.
- The ethyl group is attached to the CH next to the carbonyl.
- The CH–CH2 link carries the imidazole, which is bonded through its carbon next to the N-methyl nitrogen. That nitrogen bears the methyl group, and the second ring nitrogen is drawn with a double bond to its neighbouring carbon.

**Stereochemistry**
Both ring CH centres have a hashed bond, one to the ethyl CH2 and one to the CH2 of the imidazolylmethyl group, with the implicit H pointing toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES string for each centre, both come out as `@@`.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1C(=O)OC[C@@H]1Cc1cncn1C

name: Pidotimod
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a five-membered thiazolidine, with S and N in the ring and three ring carbons. The ring carbon next to N (bottom left) carries a COOH group on a hashed bond.
- **Linker:** the ring N is acylated by a C=O group, which is attached on a wedged bond to the stereocentre of the right-hand ring.
- **Right ring:** a five-membered pyrrolidin-2-one (5-oxopyrrolidine) with an NH and a ring C=O. This is the pidotimod skeleton.

Stereochemistry, with the implicit H at each centre:

- **Thiazolidine C4:** COOH is hashed (away from the viewer), so H points toward the viewer. This gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order OC(=O)[C@@H]1CSCN1, which is the R configuration.
- **Pyrrolidinone C2:** the carbonyl is on a wedge (toward the viewer), so H points away. This gives `[C@@H]` in the order C(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H]1CSCN1C(=O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)N1

name: Pimozide
text:
This structure is pimozide-like, but the chain has only three CH2 groups between the CH(Ar)2 carbon and the piperidine nitrogen, so I counted the chain atoms from the drawing.

Chain: the CH carbon at (480, 878) bonds to a carbon at (562, 943), then (660, 907), then (743, 973), then N at (843, 937). That gives CH–CH2–CH2–CH2–N, which is three CH2 groups, as in pimozide.

Fragments:
- Two 4-fluorophenyl groups on the CH carbon.
- Piperidine, with N bonded to the chain and C4 bonded to the benzimidazolone N.
- Benzimidazol-2-one: N1 attached to the piperidine C4, C2 as C=O, N3 as NH, fused to a benzene ring.

SMILES: O=C1Nc2ccccc2N1C1CCN(CCCC(c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(F)cc2)CC1

name: Pimecrolimus
text:
This is the structure of pimecrolimus, an ascomycin-type 23-membered macrolide with a chlorinated methoxycyclohexyl side chain. I identified it from the drawn connectivity and then wrote the stereocentres and double-bond geometry from my memory of the known pimecrolimus SMILES, not by working them out from the wedges. The stereo marks are therefore the least certain part of the answer.

What I read from the drawing:
- **Ring-bearing side chain:** a cyclohexane with a Cl on one carbon and an adjacent OMe, joined through a CH=C(CH3) alkene to the macrocycle.
- **Macrocycle, top left:** a CH bearing an ethyl group, then CH=C(CH3), then CH2, CH(CH3), CH2, and a CH(OMe) carbon.
- **Macrocycle, top right:** a ketone, a CH2, then CH(OH) and CH(CH3), leading to the lactone O.
- **Bottom:** a pipecolate ring (piperidine with N) carrying the lactone C=O, then an N–C(=O)–C(=O) α-keto amide.
- **Tetrahydrofuran ring (left):** a hemiketal carbon bearing OH, a CH(CH3), a CH2, a CH(OMe), and a ring CH–O.

I checked the parentheses in the SMILES by hand and they close correctly.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1C=C(C[C@@H](C[C@@H]([C@@H]2[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@](O2)(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCCC[C@H]3C(=O)O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H](CC1=O)O)C)/C(=C/[C@@H]4CC[C@H]([C@@H](C4)OC)Cl)/C)O)C)OC)OC)C)/C

name: Pinazepam
text:
The drawing shows a benzodiazepine core, which matches a 1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one skeleton.

- **Seven-membered ring:** N1 is bonded to the C2 carbonyl (C=O), then to a CH2 (C3), then to N4, which is double-bonded to C5. C5 carries a phenyl group and is attached to the fused benzene ring.
- **N1 substituent:** a propargyl group, CH2–C≡CH.
- **Fused benzene ring:** it carries a Cl. Starting from the carbon bonded to N1 and going around the ring, the next carbon is the CH at the bottom left, then another CH at the bottom, then the C–Cl carbon, then a CH, then the carbon bonded to C5.

SMILES: C#CCN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

In this SMILES, ring atom c2cc(Cl)ccc21 starts at the carbon bonded to C5, then goes to CH, C–Cl, CH, CH, and finally the carbon bonded to N1. This places the Cl on the carbon that is two atoms from the C5-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing. The compound is the known benzodiazepine pinazepam.

SMILES: C#CCN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

name: Pheophorbide a
text:
I read the structure as a pheophorbide-type chlorin macrocycle drawn in its enol form, and I wrote the SMILES by walking around the four pyrrole-type rings.

- **Ring A:** a vinyl group and a methyl group.
- **Ring B:** an ethyl group and a methyl group.
- **Ring C:** a methyl group, fused to the five-membered ring that carries the enol OH and the methyl ester.
- **Ring D:** the reduced ring bearing the NH, with a methyl and a CH2CH2COOH side chain.
- **Stereocentres:** three, each drawn with a wedge or hash. These are the ring D methyl carbon (hashed methyl), the ring D carbon bearing the propionic acid (wedged), and the carbon bearing the CO2Me (hashed).

I assigned @/@@ by working out the geometry around each of the three stereocentres from the drawing. I did not run the SMILES through a validator.

SMILES: C=CC1=C(C)C2=NC1=CC1=NC(C(CC)=C1C)=CC3=C(C)C4=C(O)[C@H](C(=O)OC)C(=C5NC(=C2)[C@@H](C)[C@@H]5CCC(=O)O)C4=N3

name: Pindolol
text:
The drawing is pindolol: an indole with a 2-hydroxy-3-(isopropylamino)propoxy chain at position 4, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Indole:** the NH sits at the lower left and is bonded to a CH=CH unit (the five-membered ring). The fused benzene ring carries the ether oxygen on the carbon adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon, which is position 4.
- **Side chain:** O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH(CH3)2.

I wrote the SMILES starting from the side chain and then closed the indole ring, checking the connectivity: c1(OCC(O)CNC(C)C)cccc2[nH]ccc12.

- The ring-fusion carbon bearing the NH is c2, and it closes with the other fusion carbon through the labels 2 and 1.
- The first aromatic atom (bearing O) is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon c12, which is also bonded to the CH= carbon of the five-membered ring (C3).
- This matches the drawing: the bottom fusion carbon connects to the C3 CH, then C2 CH, then NH, then the top fusion carbon.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2[nH]ccc12

name: Pindone
text:
The drawing shows pindone, 2-pivaloyl-1,3-indandione.

- **tert-Butyl group:** a quaternary carbon at the left carries three methyl groups.
- **Side-chain carbonyl:** the quaternary carbon is bonded to a C(=O) group, which connects to the CH at the ring (C2 of the indane).
- **Five-membered ring:** the CH is bonded to two C=O carbons, and each of these is bonded to one of the two fused aromatic carbons.
- **Benzene ring:** fused to the five-membered ring, with alternating double bonds drawn.

I wrote the SMILES by tracing these connections. The CH carries no stereo marks, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(=O)C1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: Pinaverium Bromide
text:
I read the structure as a bromide salt of a morpholinium cation, with these parts:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with two adjacent OMe groups. The Br sits on the ring carbon next to the CH₂ that carries the nitrogen, and it is para to one of the OMe-bearing carbons' neighbours in the pattern drawn (OMe, OMe, H, C–CH₂N, C–Br, H).
- **Morpholinium:** the benzylic CH₂ is attached to the N⁺ of a morpholine ring. The ring is N⁺, CH₂CH₂, O, CH₂CH₂, with N⁺ bonded to four carbons.
- **Side chain on N⁺:** N⁺–CH₂CH₂–O–CH₂CH₂–, ending on the pinane unit.
- **Pinane unit:** a bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane carrying a gem-dimethyl carbon as the one-carbon bridge between the two bridgeheads. The chain is attached to the three-carbon bridge at the carbon adjacent to a bridgehead (the 2-position of pinane). The drawing shows only plain bonds, so I give no stereochemistry.
- **Counter-ion:** Br⁻.

SMILES: COc1cc(Br)c(C[N+]2(CCOCCC3CCC4CC3C4(C)C)CCOCC2)cc1OC.[Br-]

name: Pimodivir
text:
I read this as pimodivir (VX-787), a 5-fluoro-7-azaindole joined to a 5-fluoropyrimidine, with a bicyclo[2.2.2]octane carrying a carboxylic acid and an amino link.

- **Right side:** a 5-fluoro-1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine (7-azaindole) is bonded at its 3-position to C2 of a pyrimidine. That pyrimidine has fluorine at C5 and an NH at C4.
- **Left side:** the drawn cage is a bicyclo[2.2.2]octane in perspective. It has eight carbons, with bridgeheads joined by three two-carbon bridges. The COOH sits on a carbon next to one bridgehead, and the NH sits on the neighbouring carbon next to the other bridgehead. The wedged H and hashed H mark these two adjacent stereocentres.
- **Stereochemistry:** I could not fully resolve the wedge and hash geometry from the drawing. I took the stereo tags from my recollection of the published (2S,3S) pimodivir SMILES, so they are not independently confirmed against the image.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H]1[C@@H](Nc2nc(-c3c[nH]c4ncc(F)cc34)ncc2F)C2CCC1CC2

name: Pioglitazone
text:
This structure is pioglitazone, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Left end:** an ethyl group is attached to a pyridine ring at the position para to the ring carbon that carries the side chain. The ring nitrogen sits next to the carbon bearing the CH2CH2O chain.
- **Linker:** the pyridine carbon next to N connects through CH2–CH2–O to a benzene ring.
- **Middle:** the benzene ring is para-substituted. The O is on one side, and a CH2 leading to the thiazolidinedione is on the other.
- **Right end:** the thiazolidinedione ring runs CH(–S)–C(=O)–NH–C(=O)–S. The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

Ring positions on the pyridine: N is bonded to the carbon carrying the side chain and to a CH. That CH is bonded to the carbon carrying the ethyl group, which is then bonded to two more CH atoms and back to the side-chain carbon. This puts the ethyl group at position 5 and the side chain at position 2.

SMILES: CCc1ccc(CCOc2ccc(CC3SC(=O)NC3=O)cc2)nc1

name: Piperacillin
text:
This drawing matches piperacillin, so I wrote the SMILES from that identification and from memory of its published SMILES. I did not independently verify each stereocentre against the wedges and hashes.

- **Core:** a penicillin bicyclic ring system, with a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine that carries a gem-dimethyl group and a carboxylic acid.
- **Side chain:** the 6-amino group is acylated by a phenylglycine unit, drawn with a hashed bond at its stereocentre.
- **Terminal group:** the phenylglycine nitrogen is linked through a urea carbonyl to a 4-ethyl-2,3-dioxopiperazine ring.

name: Piperaquine
text:
The drawing shows a symmetric molecule: two 7-chloroquinolin-4-yl groups, each attached to a piperazine nitrogen, with the two piperazines joined by a three-carbon chain (propane-1,3-diyl) between their other nitrogens. This is piperaquine.

Left quinoline: the ring nitrogen N1 is bonded to C2 and C8a. C8a is bonded to C8, which is bonded to C7, and C7 carries the Cl. C7 is bonded to C6, then C5, then C4a, and C4a is bonded to C4, which bears the piperazine.

Chain check: the piperazine N–CH2–CH2–CH2–N chain shows three carbons between the nitrogens. Counting vertices from the left N at (607,850), the chain goes (680,890), (753,850), (826,890) and then N at (900,850). That is three carbons.

Full SMILES: Clc1ccc2c(N3CCN(CCCN4CCN(CC4)c4ccnc5cc(Cl)ccc45)CC3)ccnc2c1

name: Piperazine
text:
The ring has six vertices, going around: NH (top right), CH2 (right), CH2 (bottom right), NH (bottom left), CH2 (left), CH2 (top left), and back to the first NH. The order is N–C–C–N–C–C, with the two nitrogens opposite each other (1,4 positions). This is piperazine. All bonds are plain single bonds, so there is no stereochemistry.

name: Pipotiazine
text:
This structure is a phenothiazine, which is the drug thioproperazine-like scaffold carrying a piperidine side chain (it resembles pipotiazine).

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Sulfonamide:** the dimethylamino group N(C)C is bonded to S(=O)(=O), and that sulfur is attached to the aromatic carbon at the upper left of the left ring.
- **Phenothiazine core:** the left benzene ring has a carbon bearing the sulfonamide, a CH next to it, and then the carbon attached to the ring nitrogen N10. The other fusion carbon is attached to S. The right benzene ring is unsubstituted.
- **Linker:** the ring nitrogen carries a three-carbon chain (CCC) that ends at the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** the ring has a 2-hydroxyethyl substituent (CCO) at the 4-position.

Writing the SMILES, starting from the sulfonamide:

CN(C)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN3CCC(CCO)CC3)c2c1

Atom-by-atom check on the left ring: c1 (bearing S), c, c, c2 (bonded to S), then c2 closing at the carbon bonded to N, and finally c1, the CH between the S-bearing carbon and the N-bearing carbon. In the image the sulfonamide carbon is at upper left, with the CH to its right leading to the carbon attached to N. The carbon attached to S lies at the bottom right, so the order is consistent.

SMILES: CN(C)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN3CCC(CCO)CC3)c2c1

name: Piretanide
text:
This is a bumetanide analogue in which the butylamino group is replaced by pyrrolidine.

The central benzene ring carries four substituents:
- A carboxylic acid, C(=O)O.
- A sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)N, on the carbon two positions away from the acid-bearing carbon.
- A phenoxy group, O-Ph, on the carbon between the sulfonamide carbon and the pyrrolidine carbon.
- A pyrrolidine nitrogen on the next ring carbon.

Going around the ring from the acid: C1 (COOH), C2 (H, top right), C3 (pyrrolidinyl), C4 (OPh), C5 (SO2NH2), C6 (H, bottom). So the acid and the pyrrolidine are meta to each other, and the acid and the sulfonamide are also meta to each other.

name: Pirfenidone
text:
The drawing shows a 2-pyridone ring with an N-phenyl group and a methyl substituent.

**Ring atoms (6-membered):**

**Substituents:**

name: Piroctone Olamine
text:
The image shows two components: ethanolamine (2-aminoethanol) and a pyridone, which is the piroctone salt (piroctone olamine).

**Ethanolamine:** HO-CH2-CH2-NH2, written as NCCO.

**Pyridone ring:** N-hydroxy-2-pyridone.
- The ring nitrogen carries an OH.
- C2 is the carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- C3 is CH, C4 bears a methyl, C5 is CH, and C6 bears the side chain.
- The ring bonds are C3=C4 and C5=C6.

**Side chain on C6:** CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-C(CH3)3, which is the 2,4,4-trimethylpentyl group.

In the drawing, the ring carbon at about (638, 735) connects to CH2 at (783, 592). That connects to CH at (980, 644), which carries a methyl at (1122, 500). The CH then connects to CH2 at (1032, 841), then to the quaternary carbon at (1228, 893), which has three methyls.

The ring SMILES is ON1C(=O)C=C(C)C=C1CC(C)CC(C)(C)C.

name: Piroxicam
text:
The drawing shows piroxicam.

Reading it region by region:
- **Right side:** a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring that contains S(=O)(=O), N-CH3, a C=C, and a C-OH.
- **Sulfonamide part:** the sulfur carries two =O groups and is bonded to N(CH3) and to an aromatic carbon of the benzene ring.
- **Enol part:** the N-bearing carbon is double-bonded to the carbon carrying OH, and that carbon is bonded to the other fused benzene carbon.
- **Left side:** the N-bearing ring carbon carries a C(=O)NH group, and the NH is attached to a pyridin-2-yl ring.

Writing the SMILES from the N-methyl group: CN1C(C(=O)Nc2ccccn2)=C(O)c2ccccc2S1(=O)=O

Atom check:
- The ring is N1, C(=C), C(O), then the aromatic carbons c2…c2, S1. This closes as a six-membered ring: N, C, C, c, c, S.
- The pyridine ring is c2ccccn2, with the N adjacent to the attachment carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1C(C(=O)Nc2ccccn2)=C(O)c2ccccc2S1(=O)=O

name: Pitolisant
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a piperidine, with the nitrogen at a ring vertex and five ring carbons.
- **Chain from nitrogen:** N–CH2–CH2–CH2–O. The bonds from N go to vertices at about x=378, 483 and 583 before reaching O, so there are three carbons.
- **Chain from oxygen:** O–CH2 (786), CH2 (889), CH2 (990), then the aromatic carbon at 1095. That is three carbons between O and the ring.

name: Pirarubicin
text:
I read this as pirarubicin, which is doxorubicin carrying a tetrahydropyranyl group on the 4'-oxygen of the sugar. I wrote the SMILES from the known doxorubicin skeleton and confirmed each region against the drawing.

- **Aglycone:** a tetracyclic anthracyclinone with a methoxy group on the aromatic ring and two quinone carbonyls. It has two phenolic OH groups and a tertiary C–OH carrying a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.
- **Sugar:** a daunosamine-type ring with an NH2 group and a methyl group, joined to the aglycone through a glycosidic O.
- **Extra ring:** a six-membered tetrahydropyran (five carbons and one ring O) attached through an acetal carbon to the sugar's 4'-oxygen.

Most stereocentres follow the wedges and hashes as I recall them in the doxorubicin SMILES. For the tetrahydropyran acetal carbon I worked out the configuration from the wedge to the sugar oxygen and got `@@`. That differs from my recollection of the database entry, which I recalled as `@`. I went with my own reading of the drawing for that centre, so it is the least certain part of the answer.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H]([C@H](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@H]2C[C@@](CC3=C(C4=C(C(=C23)O)C(=O)C5=C(C4=O)C=CC=C5OC)O)(C(=O)CO)O)N)O[C@@H]6CCCCO6

name: Pitavastatin
text:
This is pitavastatin, (3R,5S,6E)-7-[2-cyclopropyl-4-(4-fluorophenyl)quinolin-3-yl]-3,5-dihydroxyhept-6-enoic acid.

- **Ring system:** the quinoline core has a cyclopropyl group on C2 (next to N) and a 4-fluorophenyl group on C4. C3 carries the side chain.
- **Side chain:** an E-configured CH=CH leads from the quinoline C3 to C5, which bears an OH. A CH2 then connects to C3, which also bears an OH, followed by CH2 and the COOH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** both OH groups are drawn on hashed bonds, and the alkene is drawn trans.
  - At C3, the priorities are OH > CH2–COOH > CH2–CH(OH). With H toward the viewer, the sequence reads clockwise, so it is R.
  - At C5, the priorities are OH > vinyl carbon > CH2. With H toward the viewer, the sequence reads counterclockwise, so it is S.

I took the chirality tags in the SMILES below from the known pitavastatin string, not by deriving @/@@ from my own atom ordering. My R/S assignments from the drawing match that known (3R,5S) configuration.

SMILES: C1CC1C2=NC3=CC=CC=C3C(=C2/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H](CC(=O)O)O)O)C4=CC=C(C=C4)F

name: Pirtobrutinib
text:
I read the molecule as a 1,3,4,5-substituted pyrazole carrying a chiral trifluoroisopropyl group, with a para-phenylene linker leading to a benzamide.

- **Pyrazole core:** N1 carries the CH(CH3)CF3 group. The ring continues N2=C3, C4, C5, with the C5 carbon bearing NH2.
- **C4 substituent:** a primary carboxamide, C(=O)NH2.
- **C3 substituent:** a para-disubstituted benzene ring. Its other end carries CH2–NH–C(=O)–Ar.
- **Terminal aryl group:** a benzamide ring with OCH3 ortho to the carbonyl and F para to the OCH3, which puts F meta to the carbonyl, a 5-fluoro-2-methoxyphenyl group.
- **Stereocentre:** the only wedge or hash in the drawing is the hashed methyl on the CH(CF3) carbon, so only that carbon gets stereochemistry.
  - The priorities are N > CF3 > CH3 > H.
  - With the methyl pointing away, the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - Viewed from the front, N → CF3 → CH3 runs clockwise, so the true configuration is counterclockwise, which is S.
  - Written as `C[C@H](n1...)C(F)(F)F`, the neighbour order (CH3, H, N, CF3) gives S.

SMILES: C[C@H](n1nc(-c2ccc(CNC(=O)c3cc(F)ccc3OC)cc2)c(C(N)=O)c1N)C(F)(F)F

name: Pivmecillinam
text:
I read this as pivmecillinam (the pivaloyloxymethyl ester of mecillinam), a penicillin-type β-lactam.

- **Left:** a saturated seven-membered ring (azepane) with one nitrogen. That nitrogen is bonded to a CH= carbon, which is double-bonded to an exocyclic N (an amidine, N=CH–N).
- **Centre:** a fused bicyclic β-lactam–thiazolidine core. The four-membered ring holds the lactam C=O and N, and the five-membered ring holds S, a gem-dimethyl carbon and the carboxylate-bearing carbon.
- **Right:** the carboxylate is esterified as C(=O)–O–CH2–O–C(=O)–C(CH3)3, a pivaloyloxymethyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the three stereocentres are the ring-fusion CH (H wedge), the amidine-bearing CH (hashed bond to N) and the carboxylate-bearing CH (wedge to C=O). I checked the carboxylate-bearing centre against the drawn wedge and the SMILES (@@). The other two I took from the known pivmecillinam configuration rather than re-deriving them.

SMILES: CC1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1)[C@@H](C2=O)N=CN3CCCCCC3)C(=O)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C)C

name: Platinum(II),1-cyclobutanedicarboxylato)diammine-, cis-
text:
The drawing shows three separate components:

1. A cyclobutane ring with four carbons. One ring carbon carries two carboxylic acid groups, C(=O)O each, so this is cyclobutane-1,1-dicarboxylic acid.
2. An isolated NH2⁻ drawn at the top.
3. NH2⁻ attached to Pt²⁺, shown as "NH2⁻Pt2+".

The labels read as separate species, so I wrote them as separate components. The first NH2⁻ is a free ion, and the second is written next to Pt²⁺ with no drawn bond, so I treated it as an ion pair rather than a bonded unit.

Fragment SMILES:
- Acid: OC(=O)C1(CCC1)C(=O)O
- Amides: [NH2-] and [NH2-]
- Platinum: [Pt+2]

The charges balance: two NH2⁻ (−2) and Pt²⁺ (+2).

SMILES: OC(=O)C1(CCC1)C(=O)O.[NH2-].[NH2-].[Pt+2]

name: Plerixafor
text:
I read the image as a benzene ring with a para-substituted pair of CH2 groups, each CH2 attached to one nitrogen of an identical 14-membered tetraaza macrocycle (a cyclam-type ring).

**Central ring.** The benzene ring has two substituents, in the 1,4 (para) positions. Each substituent is a CH2 group leading to a macrocycle nitrogen.

**Macrocycle (left, counted atom by atom).** Starting from the substituted N and going round the ring, the sequence is N, CH2, CH2, CH2, NH, CH2, CH2, NH, CH2, CH2, CH2, NH, CH2, CH2, then back to N. That is 14 ring atoms with 4 nitrogens. The nitrogens are separated alternately by three and two carbons, and only the benzyl-bearing nitrogen is tertiary. This is a 1,4,8,11-tetraazacyclotetradecane (cyclam) ring.

**Macrocycle (right).** The right-hand ring has the same 14-atom pattern, with the same alternating 3- and 2-carbon spacing. Its tertiary nitrogen is attached to the other benzylic CH2.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

The SMILES below has the ring closures checked against this count.

SMILES: c1cc(CN2CCCNCCNCCCNCC2)ccc1CN1CCCNCCNCCCNCC1

name: Plinabulin
text:
I read the structure as three parts joined together.

- **Imidazole:** a ring bearing a tert-butyl group on the carbon next to the NH. The ring carbon next to the ring N (the one without H) carries a =CH– link.
- **Central ring:** a piperazine-2,5-dione with two C=O groups and two NH groups. One ring carbon is double-bonded to the CH from the imidazole. The other ring carbon is double-bonded to a CH attached to a phenyl group.
- **Geometry of the two exocyclic C=C bonds:**
  - On the imidazolyl-methylidene bond, the imidazole and the adjacent ring NH lie on the same side, which gives Z.
  - On the benzylidene bond, the phenyl and the adjacent ring NH also lie on the same side, which gives Z.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C1=C(/C=C2\NC(=O)C(\NC2=O)=C\c3ccccc3)N=CN1

name: Plecanatide
text:
I read this as a linear 15-residue peptide with one β-alanine insert and two disulfide bridges. I traced the backbone from the N-terminal amine to the C-terminal acid, and I checked the Asn1 centre against its wedge. I did not check the other centres individually; I assumed they are all L (natural) amino acids.

**Sequence, N-terminus to C-terminus:**
Asn – Asp – Glu – Cys – Glu – Leu – Cys – Val – Asn – Val – Ala – Cys – Thr – β-Ala – Cys – Leu-COOH

**Points that needed care:**
- Near the bottom right, two bonds cross. One is the Cys(7) C(=O) → NH → Val(8) α-carbon link. The other is the Thr C(=O)–NH–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–NH–Cys link, which makes a β-alanine unit.
- The disulfide bridges join the 1st and 3rd Cys (Cys4–Cys12) and the 2nd and 4th Cys (Cys7–Cys14).

**Stereochemistry:** the Asn1 wedge reads as S (L-Asn). I wrote the other residues as L-amino acids, and L-Thr includes its β-carbon.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS2)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS1)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)NCCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS2)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: Plocabulin
text:
I read the structure in four parts and assigned stereochemistry from the wedges, hashes and cis/trans geometry in the drawing.

**Left ring.** A 6-membered α,β-unsaturated lactone with a methoxy group on the alkene carbon next to the ring C=O. The ring carbon bonded to the ring oxygen has a hashed bond to the ring CH2, which I assigned S.

**Polyene chain.** The ring carbon is attached to a CH(CH3) drawn with a hashed methyl (S). This leads to a trisubstituted alkene with a methyl branch (E), then two further alkenes (both Z), ending in an amide C=O.

**Central residue.** The amide N is bonded to a tert-leucine-type carbon bearing a tert-butyl group and a hashed N bond (S). Its C=O continues as a second amide.

**Right chain.** The second amide N is attached to a CH=CH (Z), then CH2, then a carbamate-bearing carbon (OC(N)=O) with a bold wedge (S). The chain ends with CH2–CH=CH–CH3 (Z).

SMILES: COC1=CC[C@H](OC1=O)[C@@H](C)/C=C(\C)/C=C\C=C/C(=O)N[C@H](C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N/C=C\C[C@@H](OC(N)=O)C/C=C\C

name: Plitidepsin
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic depsipeptide that looks like a didemnin analogue. I wrote the SMILES by following the chain from the pyruvyl-proline tail around the macrocycle.

**Side chain (left to right in the drawing):**
- A pyruvyl group, CH3C(=O)C(=O)–, is attached to the nitrogen of a proline ring.
- That proline is bonded through its carbonyl to an N-methyl-leucine, which has a wedged isobutyl group.
- The N-methyl-leucine carbonyl is bonded to the NH of a threonine-type residue, which is also part of the macrocycle.

**Macrocycle, starting at the threonine α-carbon and going around:**
1. The threonine α-carbon carries the side-chain NH (hashed bond). Its β-carbon bears a hashed methyl and the ring ester oxygen.
2. That oxygen is esterified to the carbonyl of an N-methyl-O-methyltyrosine (4-methoxybenzyl side chain).
3. The N-methyl-tyrosine nitrogen is acylated by a proline, whose nitrogen is in turn acylated by a leucine.
4. The leucine NH is acylated by a CH(CH3) carbon, which is bonded to a ketone carbon.
5. The ketone carbon is bonded to a CH carrying an isopropyl group, which bears the ester oxygen.
6. That oxygen is esterified to a carbonyl, followed by the CH2 that the drawing labels "C".
7. The CH2 is followed by CH(OH), then a CH bearing a sec-butyl group (hashed methyl) and the NH.
8. That NH closes the ring onto the threonine carbonyl.

I assigned the @/@@ marks from each wedge or hash and the neighbour order in the SMILES. The proline, tyrosine and leucine centres came out as the usual L configuration and the N-methyl-leucine in the tail as D. I did not run the string through a parser.

SMILES: CC(=O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N(C)[C@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H]3[C@@H](C)OC(=O)[C@H](Cc4ccc(OC)cc4)N(C)C(=O)[C@@H]4CCCN4C(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)C(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)OC(=O)C[C@H](O)[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)NC3=O

name: Pomalidomide
text:
The drawing shows pomalidomide: a glutarimide ring joined through its N-substituted carbon to a phthalimide that carries an NH2 on the benzene ring.

**Glutarimide ring:** NH is bonded to two C=O carbons. One C=O is bonded to CH2, which is bonded to CH2, which is bonded to the CH. That CH is bonded to the other C=O and to the phthalimide N. The ring has six members: N, C(=O), CH, CH2, CH2, C(=O).

**Phthalimide:** The N is bonded to two C=O carbons, each attached to the benzene ring at adjacent positions.

**Amino position:** The NH2 sits on the benzene carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the lower C=O (the one bonded to the bottom carbonyl carbon). This is the 4-amino position.

**Stereochemistry:** The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES written from the lower carbonyl: O=C1NC(=O)CCC1N1C(=O)c2cccc(N)c2C1=O

Checking the benzene ring: c2cccc(N)c2 starts at the fusion carbon attached to the first C=O, goes through three CH, then C(N), then the fusion carbon attached to the last C=O. So the NH2 is adjacent to the fusion carbon on the C1=O side, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)CCC1N1C(=O)c2cccc(N)c2C1=O

name: Ponatinib
text:
This structure is ponatinib: an imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine joined through an alkyne to a tolyl amide, with a CF3-substituted aryl bearing a 4-methylpiperazinylmethyl group.

**Imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine.** The five-membered ring contains a bridgehead N, C3 (bearing the alkyne), a CH, an N and the fusion carbon. The six-membered ring contains the bridgehead N, an N, and three CH carbons that close back to the fusion carbon. Written as SMILES: C#Cc1cnc2cccnn12.

**Central benzene ring.** The alkyne-bearing carbon is adjacent to the methyl-bearing carbon. The amide carbonyl sits meta to the alkyne, which gives: Cc1ccc(C(=O)N...)cc1C#C...

**Right-hand aryl ring.** The NH-bearing carbon is C1. Going around the ring from it, the next carbon is CH, then the CF3-bearing carbon, then the CH2N-bearing carbon, then CH, then CH back to C1. Written as SMILES: c1cc(CN2CCN(C)CC2)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1 attached at the NH carbon.

**Check of the right-hand ring against the drawing.** The ring atoms are N-attached C (1025,945), top-left CH (1030,835), top CH (1127,783), the CH2-bearing carbon (1220,843), the CF3-bearing carbon (1215,953) and the bottom CH (1118,1005). The NH carbon is therefore bonded to a CH, which leads to the CH2-bearing carbon, and to another CH, which leads to the CF3-bearing carbon. This puts CF3 meta to the amide N and the CH2 group para to it, which matches the SMILES above.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(CN3CCN(C)CC3)c(C(F)(F)F)c2)cc1C#Cc1cnc2cccnn12

name: Ponazuril
text:
The drawing shows a 1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione ring. It has an N-methyl, an NH, and an N bearing an aryl group.

**Triazine ring.** Going around the ring: N(CH3), then C(=O), then N(aryl), then C(=O), then NH, then C(=O), back to N(CH3).

**Aryl group on the ring N.** This is a benzene ring carrying a methyl and an aryloxy group. Numbering from the ring carbon attached to N (C1), the ring runs through C2 (CH), C3 (C–CH3), C4 (C–O) and C5, C6 (both CH). So the methyl sits ortho to the oxygen, and the oxygen is para to the N attachment.

**Aryloxy substituent.** The oxygen connects to a second benzene ring. Para to the oxygen on that ring is the S(=O)(=O)CF3 group.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)NC(=O)N(C1=O)c1ccc(Oc2ccc(cc2)S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)c(C)c1

name: Podophyllotoxin
text:
I read this as podophyllotoxin, a lignan lactone, and assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Ring systems**
- A γ-lactone: O=C–O–CH2 closed onto two adjacent ring-fusion carbons.
- A central six-membered ring carrying a secondary alcohol (HO, hashed bond) and a trimethoxyphenyl group (hashed bond).
- A methylenedioxy-fused benzene ring (the O–CH2–O bridge at lower left).
- A 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl ring on the right (three OMe groups).

**Stereocentres**
There are four, all marked in the drawing:
- The lactone-side ring-fusion carbon with the hashed H.
- The ring-fusion carbon next to C=O with the wedged H.
- The CH–OH carbon with the hashed OH.
- The CH–aryl carbon with the hashed aryl bond.

I converted each to @/@@ by working out the clockwise or anticlockwise order of its neighbours in the drawing and adjusting for the neighbour order in the SMILES. I did not cross-check the result against the known podophyllotoxin SMILES.

SMILES: O=C1OC[C@H]2[C@H]1[C@H](c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1)c1cc3OCOc3cc1[C@@H]2O

name: Pneumocandin B(0)
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic hexapeptide lipopeptide of the echinocandin type, with a 10,12-dimethylmyristoyl tail. I worked out each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds, with hydrogens treated as implicit.

**Side chain.** The acyl chain runs C(=O), then eight CH2 groups, then CH(CH3) (hashed methyl), CH2, CH(CH3) (wedged methyl), and an ethyl end. That is 10,12-dimethylmyristoyl, attached to the ring through an amide NH.

**Ring residues, in order around the ring:**
1. A 4,5-dihydroxyornithine. Its α-carbon carries the acylated NH, followed by CH2, CH(OH) and CH(OH)–N. The label "C" in the drawing is that CH2.
2. A 3-hydroxyproline.
3. A 3-hydroxy-glutamine side chain, CH(OH)CH2C(=O)NH2, on the next α-carbon.
4. A 3,4-dihydroxy-homotyrosine. Its side chain is CH(OH)–CH(OH)–C6H4–OH, with a para-hydroxyphenyl group.
5. A 4-hydroxyproline.
6. A threonine, with CH(OH)CH3 on its α-carbon, which closes the ring back onto the ornithine carbonyl.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures and for the chain length, and then assigned each @/@@ centre by hand from the drawn geometry.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)C[C@H](C)CCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H]1C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)NC(=O)[C@@H]2[C@@H](O)CCN2C(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)[C@@H](O)c3ccc(O)cc3)NC(=O)[C@@H]3C[C@@H](O)CN3C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC1=O

name: Potassium Citrate
text:
The drawing shows tripotassium citrate monohydrate. It has three K⁺ ions, one water molecule, and a citrate trianion.

The citrate core is a central carbon bearing an OH group and three substituents: two CH2–COO⁻ arms and one directly attached COO⁻ group. The central carbon is not a stereocentre, since two of its substituents are identical.

Each component is written as a separate fragment, joined with dots:

- Citrate: [O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-]
- Potassium ions: [K+] three times
- Water: O

SMILES: O.[K+].[K+].[K+].[O-]C(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)[O-])C(=O)[O-]

name: Potassium Ferrocyanide
text:
The image shows separate disconnected species: four K+ ions, one Fe2+ ion, and six cyanide anions drawn as [C-]#N.

Counting from the drawing, the cyanides are at y=580, 748, 915, 1083, and 1250, and there is a sixth beside the last one at the bottom. The K+ ions are two at the top and two at the bottom right, so four in total.

Charge check: 4 K+ gives +4 and Fe2+ gives +2, for +6 in total. Six cyanide anions give −6, so the whole thing is neutral. This is potassium ferrocyanide.

SMILES: [K+].[K+].[K+].[K+].[Fe+2].[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N

name: Posaconazole
text:
I read this as posaconazole. I worked out the two stereocentres in the left-hand side chain from the drawing and took the tetrahydrofuran stereocentres from the known posaconazole structure rather than deriving them from the wedges.

**Regions read from the drawing**
- **Left side chain:** an ethyl group on a CH that carries the triazolone N, next to a CH(OH)CH3.
- **Triazolone:** a 1,2,4-triazol-3-one ring with a C=O. Its other N is bonded to a para-phenylene.
- **Linker:** the phenylene connects through a piperazine to a second para-phenylene, which carries an O–CH2 group.
- **Tetrahydrofuran:** the O–CH2 attaches to a tetrahydrofuran ring. The ring carbon next to the ring oxygen bears a 2,4-difluorophenyl group and a CH2 linked to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.

**Stereochemistry**
- The ethyl-bearing CH has a hashed bond to the ethyl group, which puts the implicit H toward the viewer. With priorities N > CH(OH) > ethyl > H, this gives S.
- The CH(OH) carbon has a wedged methyl, which puts H at the back. With priorities OH > C(N) > CH3 > H, this also gives S.
- Both match the (2S,3S)-2-hydroxypentan-3-yl group of posaconazole, and I checked that the SMILES chirality tags reproduce these assignments.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]([C@H](C)O)n1ncn(c1=O)c1ccc(cc1)N1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(OC[C@H]2C[C@@](Cn3cncn3)(OC2)c2ccc(F)cc2F)cc1

name: Pnu-159682
text:
I read this as a doxorubicin-type anthracycline whose sugar nitrogen carries a fused methoxy-oxazolidine/morpholine ring system.

**Aglycone**
- The tetracyclic core has a 4-methoxy group on the terminal benzene ring.
- Both quinone C=O groups are present, and the two phenol OH groups sit on the middle ring.
- C9 carries a wedged OH and a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.
- C7 carries the wedged glycosidic O.

**Sugar and fused rings**
- The sugar is a pyranose with the anomeric carbon (C1′) bonded to the glycosidic O, plus a hashed C5′ methyl.
- C3′ is bonded to N, and C4′ is bonded to an oxazolidine O.
- That oxazolidine O leads to a carbon bonded to N and to a CH(OMe), which closes through O–CH2–CH2 back to N, forming the morpholine ring.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the drawn wedges and hashes by working out the geometry of its four neighbours.

SMILES: OCC(=O)[C@]1(O)Cc2c(O)c3C(=O)c4cccc(OC)c4C(=O)c3c(O)c2[C@@H](O[C@H]2C[C@@H]3N4CCO[C@H](OC)[C@@H]4O[C@@H]3[C@H](C)O2)C1

name: Potassium Iodide
text:
The image shows two separate ions: a potassium cation (K⁺, in black) and an iodide anion (I⁻, in purple). There are no bonds between them, so this is potassium iodide written as two disconnected components.

SMILES: [K+].[I-]

name: Potassium hexachloroplatinate(IV)
text:
The drawing shows potassium hexachloroplatinate(IV), K2PtCl6. It contains two K+ ions and one Pt center with a 2− charge. Six Cl atoms are drawn bonded to Pt, each with a single bond.

Charge check: Pt carries 2−, and the six Cl atoms are drawn as neutral. The two K+ ions give +2, so the whole formula is neutral.

I wrote the SMILES as three dot-separated parts: the two K+ ions and the PtCl6 anion with Pt written as [Pt-2].

SMILES: [K+].[K+].Cl[Pt-2](Cl)(Cl)(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Potassium Perchlorate
text:
The drawing shows a central Cl carrying a 3+ charge, bonded by single bonds to four O atoms that each carry a minus charge. A separate K⁺ sits to the right.

Charge check: Cl³⁺ plus four O⁻ gives −1, and K⁺ brings the total to 0.

The SMILES is written with the potassium ion as a separate component.

SMILES: [K+].[O-][Cl+3]([O-])([O-])[O-]

name: Potassium Permanganate
text:
The image shows potassium permanganate, drawn as a K⁺ cation beside an Mn centre.

- Mn has three double bonds, each to an O: one at the upper left, one at the upper right and one at the lower right.
- Mn has one single bond to an O at the lower left, which carries a negative charge.
- The K is drawn as a separate K⁺ ion, so the two parts are written as a dot-separated pair.

SMILES: [K+].[O-][Mn](=O)(=O)=O

name: Ponesimod
text:
This structure matches ponesimod. I read it region by region:

- **Core ring:** a thiazolidin-4-one with C=O at C4, S at position 1, and ring N (position 3) bearing an o-tolyl group.
- **C2 substituent:** an exocyclic C=N–propyl (propylimino) group.
- **C5 substituent:** a benzylidene (=CH–aryl). The aryl ring carries Cl ortho to an ether O, and the ether chain is OCH2–CH(OH)–CH2OH.
- **Glycerol stereocentre:** the OH is on a hashed bond. The priorities are OH > CH2OAr > CH2OH > H. With H toward the viewer, the sequence OH → CH2OAr → CH2OH runs counterclockwise, so reversing gives R. In SMILES, `OC[C@H](O)CO` encodes R.
- **Benzylidene C=C:** the ring S and the aryl group lie on the same side of the double bond, so it is Z.
- **C2=N bond:** in the drawing the propyl group sits on the same side as the ring N3 and opposite the S, so I encoded it as drawn (E by CIP, since S outranks N3). This differs from the 2Z descriptor I recall for ponesimod, but I followed the drawing.

SMILES: CCC/N=C1/S/C(=C\c2ccc(OC[C@H](O)CO)c(Cl)c2)C(=O)N1c1ccccc1C

name: Potassium trichloro(ethylene)platinate(II) hydrate
text:
The image shows several separate components: a trichloroplatinate anion, water, ethene, and a potassium cation. This matches Zeise's salt hydrate.

- **Anion:** Pt carries a negative charge and is bonded to three Cl atoms, written [Pt-](Cl)(Cl)Cl.
- **Water:** O.
- **Ethene:** a C=C double bond with no hydrogens drawn, written C=C.
- **Cation:** [K+].

The components are joined with dots: O.C=C.[K+].Cl[Pt-](Cl)Cl

SMILES: O.C=C.[K+].Cl[Pt-](Cl)Cl

name: Practolol
text:
This structure reads as practolol: a para-disubstituted benzene ring carrying an acetamido group (NHC(=O)CH3) on one side and an aryloxypropanolamine chain on the other.

The chain runs from the ring oxygen: O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–NH–CH(CH3)2. The carbon bearing the OH is drawn with plain bonds, so I have given it no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(NC(C)=O)cc1

name: Pracinostat
text:
The drawing shows a benzimidazole core with three substituents.

- **C2 substituent:** a butyl chain (4 carbons), CCCC–.
- **N1 substituent:** a CH2CH2 linker leading to N(CC)CC, a diethylamino group.
- **Benzene ring substituent:** an acrylohydroxamic acid, –CH=CH–C(=O)NHOH. The double bond is drawn as trans (E): the ring attaches at the upper-left of the alkene and the carbonyl at the lower-right, on opposite sides.

For the ring, the N1 carbon (call it C7a) is bonded to the lower-left benzene carbon at (722, 883). The benzene ring runs C3a (692, 683), then C4 (808, 665), then C5 (882, 757) bearing the substituent, then C6 (840, 866), then C7 (722, 883), then C7a (650, 792).

The SMILES is written in this order:

CCCCc1nc2cc(/C=C/C(=O)NO)ccc2n1CCN(CC)CC

Ring closure check: c1 (C2), n (N3), c2 (C3a), c (C4), c(...) (C5 with substituent), c (C6), c (C7), c2 (C7a), n1 (N1). C7a is bonded to C3a through the closure 2, and N1 closes to C2 through closure 1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCc1nc2cc(/C=C/C(=O)NO)ccc2n1CCN(CC)CC

name: Pralidoxime Chloride
text:
The drawing shows pralidoxime chloride (2-PAM chloride), which has three parts.

- **Ring:** a pyridinium ring with N+ bearing a methyl group. The ring has six vertices: N+, then C2 (carrying the side chain), C3, C4, C5 and C6.
- **Side chain:** at C2, a CH=N–OH oxime group. The bonds are drawn plainly, so no E/Z geometry is specified.
- **Counter-ion:** Cl⁻, drawn separately.

Ring bonds as drawn:
- N+ is double-bonded to C6 (the lower-left carbon).
- C5 and C4 are joined by a double bond.
- C3 is double-bonded to C2.

Writing the ring atoms in order gives the Kekulé form C[n+]... which I write explicitly as C[N+]1=CC=CC=C1C=NO. Checking the ring: N1+(=C6), C6–C5 single, C5=C4 double, C4–C3 single, C3=C2 double, C2–N1 single. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: C[N+]1=CC=CC=C1C=NO.[Cl-]

name: Povorcitinib
text:
I read the structure in four parts:

- **Left pyrazole:** a 3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazol-4-yl group, joined at C4 to a second pyrazole.
- **Middle:** the second pyrazole is attached through its C4 and N1. Its N1 bonds to C3 of an azetidine, and that same carbon also carries a CH2C≡N group. The azetidine nitrogen bonds to the aryl ring.
- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring bearing the azetidine nitrogen, a fluorine on each side of it (at the two ortho positions), and the carboxamide para to the nitrogen.
- **Amide side chain:** C(=O)NH on a single stereocentre that carries CH3 (hashed bond), CF3, the amide N and an implicit H.

For the stereocentre, the CIP priorities are N > CF3 > CH3 > H. With the methyl hashed (away from the viewer), the implicit H points toward the viewer. Tracing N → CF3 → CH3 in the drawing goes clockwise, and flipping that for the H facing the viewer gives S. In the SMILES order N, H, CH3, CF3, S corresponds to `@@`, so the fragment is `N[C@@H](C)C(F)(F)F`.

SMILES: Cc1n[nH]c(C)c1-c1cnn(c1)C1(CC#N)CN(C1)c1cc(F)c(cc1F)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(F)(F)F

name: Pralatrexate
text:
I read the molecule as an L-glutamic acid amide of a para-substituted benzoic acid, with a 2,4-diaminopteridine at the far end.

- **Glutamate end:** The α-carbon carries a free carboxylic acid, an NH amide, and a CH2CH2COOH side chain. The side-chain bond is a wedge. With H pointing away, N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S, as in L-glutamic acid.
- **Linker:** The amide nitrogen is acylated by a C=O attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Para substituent:** The other ring position carries CH(CH2C≡CH)CH2–, a propargyl branch on a carbon that is a stereocentre by connectivity. It is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Pteridine:** The CH2 is bonded to C6 of a pteridine. C7 is CH, and the amino groups are at C2 and C4, giving the 2,4-diaminopteridin-6-yl group.

To write the stereocentre, I started from L-glutamic acid, N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O. Starting instead from the side-chain CH2 swaps the order of the first and third neighbours, so the tag becomes @.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC[C@H](NC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C(CC#C)Cc1cnc2nc(N)nc(N)c2n1)C(=O)O

name: Pranidipine
text:
This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine in the cilnidipine family, with a methyl ester on one side and a cinnamyl ester on the other.

**Dihydropyridine core:** NH, then C2 (methyl), C3 (carrying the cinnamyl ester), C4 (sp3, carrying the aryl group), C5 (carrying the methyl ester), and C6 (methyl). The ring bonds are C2=C3 and C5=C6.

**Substituents:**
- The aryl group on C4 is 3-nitrophenyl.
- The ester on C3 is C(=O)OC/C=C/c1ccccc1, a cinnamyl ester.
- The ester on C5 is C(=O)OC, a methyl ester.

**Stereochemistry:** The cinnamyl double bond is drawn trans. Going from the CH2 at (888, 802) to the CH at (1000, 845), then to the CH at (1093, 771) and the phenyl carbon at (1205, 813), the CH2 and the phenyl lie on opposite sides, so it is E. C4 is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

**SMILES:** `COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC/C=C/c2ccccc2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1`

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC/C=C/c2ccccc2)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Pranlukast
text:
This is pranlukast, a chromone (4-oxo-4H-chromene) carrying a tetrazole and an amide-linked aryl ether.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Tetrazole:** a five-membered ring with an NH. Its carbon is attached to C2 of the chromone.
- **Chromone core:** the pyranone ring has O1, C2 (bearing the tetrazole), C3 (=CH) and C4 (=O). The fused benzene ring carries the NH at C8, next to the ring oxygen.
- **Amide:** the chromone C8 is bonded to NH, then C(=O), then a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- **Side chain:** on the para position of that benzene ring, O–CH2CH2CH2CH2–Ph. Counting from the oxygen, the chain has four CH2 groups before the terminal phenyl.

**Assembling the SMILES**
- Tetrazole: c1nnn[nH]1 (written as C1=NN=NN1 in the drawn tautomer; the aromatic form is used below).
- Chromone with substituents: O=c1cc(-c2nnn[nH]2)oc2c(NC(=O)c3ccc(OCCCCc4ccccc4)cc3)cccc12

The drawing shows N=N and C=N bonds with an NH on the ring, which fits the aromatic tetrazole written this way.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1cccc2c(=O)cc(-c3nnn[nH]3)oc12)c1ccc(OCCCCc2ccccc2)cc1

name: Pramipexole
text:
The drawing shows pramipexole, a 2-amino-4,5,6,7-tetrahydrobenzothiazole with an N-propylamino group on the saturated ring.

- **Chain:** a three-carbon propyl chain (CH3–CH2–CH2) is attached to an NH.
- **Stereocentre:** that NH sits on a ring carbon by a wedge bond.
- **Saturated ring:** six-membered, with two CH2 groups on one side of the stereocentre and one CH2 on the other. The CH2 on the lower side leads to the ring-fusion carbon bearing S. The other CH2 leads to another CH2, then to the ring-fusion carbon bearing N.
- **Thiazole ring:** fused to the saturated ring, with S at the bottom and N at the top. The carbon between S and N carries an NH2.

CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N first, then the CH2 on the sulfur side, then the other CH2, then H. The wedged N points toward the viewer, so H points away. Reading N → S-side CH2 → other CH2 on the screen runs counterclockwise, which gives (S).

In the SMILES `CCCN[C@H]1CCc2nc(N)sc2C1`, the neighbours of the stereocentre are listed as N, H, the ring closure (the S-side CH2), then the other CH2. For that order, `@` corresponds to (S), which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCN[C@H]1CCc2nc(N)sc2C1

name: Prasugrel
text:
The drawing is prasugrel, which I read region by region as follows.

- **Acetate:** a methyl group on a C(=O) that is bonded to an O, giving CC(=O)O–.
- **Thiophene ring:** the acetate O is on a thiophene carbon. That carbon is bonded to S and, through a double bond, to a CH. The CH connects to a ring-fusion carbon, which is double-bonded to the other fusion carbon, and that carbon is bonded to S.
- **Saturated ring:** one fusion carbon connects through CH2 to N. The other fusion carbon connects through CH2–CH2 to N.
- **N substituent:** N is bonded to a CH that carries the 2-fluorophenyl group and a C(=O)-cyclopropyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CC(=O)OC1=CC2=C(S1)CCN(C2)C(C(=O)C1CC1)c1ccccc1F

name: Pranoprofen
text:
This is pranoprofen: a 5H-chromeno[2,3-b]pyridine core carrying a 2-propanoic acid group.

Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Side chain:** a methyl group on a CH, which carries a COOH (drawn with C=O and HO). It is attached to the benzene ring. The CH has no wedge or hash, so no stereochemistry is assigned.
- **Benzene ring:** six carbons. One bears the side chain, one is bonded to O, and one is bonded to the CH2. The ring runs from the side-chain carbon (523,677) through the carbon at 569,511, then 735,469, then 853,592 (bonded to O), then 808,757 (bonded to CH2), then 643,798, and back.
- **Central ring:** the benzene carbon bearing O links to O, which links to the pyridine carbon at 1139,672. That carbon is bonded to N and is double-bonded to the carbon at 1093,837, which is bonded to the CH2 at 927,879. The CH2 connects back to the benzene carbon at 808,757.
- **Pyridine ring:** N, then the carbon at 1424,753, then 1379,917, then 1213,959, then 1093,837, then 1139,672. The double bonds are N=C(1424), C(1379)=C(1213) and C(1093)=C(1139).

SMILES, written from the side chain through the benzene ring and then the pyridine:

CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc2Oc3ncccc3Cc2c1

Check on ring closure: c1 is the side-chain carbon, c, c, then c2 (the carbon bonded to O), O, c3 (bonded to N), n, c, c, c, c3 (bonded to CH2), C, then c2 (closing onto the O-bearing carbon's ring partner), and c1 closing the benzene ring.

This ordering gives a ring closure problem: the "c2" after CH2 would close with the O-bearing carbon, which is wrong. Rewriting so the ring closure is correct:

c1 (side-chain carbon), c, c, c2 (O-bearing), then O, c3 n c c c c3 C, c2 (CH2-bearing, closing the central ring to c2), c1.

In the written SMILES, the atom "c2" after the CH2 closes ring 2 with the O-bearing carbon. These two carbons are adjacent in the benzene ring, so the closure is valid. The benzene ring has c1, c, c, c2(O), c2(CH2), c1, which is six atoms.

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc2Oc3ncccc3Cc2c1

name: Pralmorelin
text:
I read this as a linear hexapeptide amide, D-Ala–D-2Nal–L-Ala–L-Trp–D-Phe–L-Lys–NH2, and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Residues, N-terminus to C-terminus:**
1. Ala: the methyl is on a wedge. I assign R, so this is D-Ala.
2. 2-Naphthylalanine: the CH2 is on a hash. I assign R, so this is D-2Nal. The side chain is a 2-naphthyl group, written `c1ccc2ccccc2c1`.
3. Ala: the methyl is on a hash. I assign S, so this is L-Ala.
4. Trp: the CH2 to the indol-3-yl group is on a hash. I assign S, so this is L-Trp.
5. Phe: the benzyl CH2 is on a wedge. I assign R, so this is D-Phe.
6. Lys: the chain is on a hash. I assign S, so this is L-Lys, ending in a primary amide (C(N)=O). The side chain is (CH2)4NH2.

I derived the @/@@ marks by hand from the drawing; the SMILES was not run through a parser.

SMILES: N[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(N)=O

name: Praziquantel
text:
This is praziquantel, drawn without stereochemistry.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The cyclohexane ring on the left is attached to a C(=O) group, which is bonded to the lower nitrogen (N).
- From the lower N, one CH2 leads up to the lactam carbonyl C(=O), and another CH2 leads to the ring-fusion CH.
- The lactam carbonyl is bonded to the upper N.
- The upper N is bonded to the ring-fusion CH and to a CH2CH2 chain that runs to the benzene ring.
- The ring-fusion CH is also bonded directly to the benzene ring.

The ring-fusion CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: O=C(C1CCCCC1)N1CC(=O)N2CCc3ccccc3C2C1

name: Pravastatin
text:
I recognised this structure as pravastatin and wrote the SMILES from that recognition. I did not independently check each stereocentre against the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

What the drawing shows:
- **Ring system:** a bicyclic core with two ring double bonds, a hydroxyl on the left ring, and a methyl on the right ring.
- **Ester:** the ring oxygen carries a 2-methylbutanoate group, drawn as O–C(=O)–CH(CH3)–CH2CH3.
- **Side chain:** a chain of two CH2 groups leads to two hydroxylated carbons, one more CH2, and then the carboxylic acid. Both side-chain OH groups are drawn with hashed bonds.

The stereochemistry in the SMILES is the known one for pravastatin.

SMILES: CC[C@H](C)C(=O)O[C@H]1C[C@@H](C=C2[C@H]1[C@H]([C@H](C=C2)C)CC[C@H](C[C@H](CC(=O)O)O)O)O

name: Prazosin
text:
This structure is prazosin: a 4-amino-6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline with a piperazine at C2, and that piperazine N-acylated with a 2-furoyl group.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Quinazoline core:** the benzene ring carries two OMe groups, on the two adjacent carbons at the left. The pyrimidine ring has N3 at the bottom, C4 bearing NH2, and N1 at the top. C2 sits between the two nitrogens and bonds to the piperazine N.
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two N atoms. One N joins quinazoline C2, and the other N is acylated.
- **Furoyl group:** a C=O attached to the C2 of a furan ring (the furan O is adjacent to the carbonyl-bearing carbon).

There are no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: COc1cc2nc(nc(N)c2cc1OC)N1CCN(CC1)C(=O)c1ccco1

name: Pramiconazole
text:
I read the molecule as an itraconazole-like analogue. An N-isopropyl imidazolidin-2-one replaces the triazolone, and there is no sec-butyl group.

**Regions, left to right**
- An isopropyl group is on N1 of an imidazolidin-2-one (5-membered ring with a C=O), and N3 of that ring is bonded to a para-disubstituted benzene.
- That benzene carries a piperazine through one of its nitrogens, and the other piperazine nitrogen bonds to a second para-disubstituted benzene.
- The second benzene bears an O–CH2 link to C2 of a 1,3-dioxolane.
- The other dioxolane carbon (C4) is quaternary and bears a 2,4-difluorophenyl group and a CH2–(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl) group. The triazole attaches through N1, which is bonded to both a ring carbon and a ring nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry**
- Both stereocentres are on the dioxolane ring, and each has one wedge bond.
- The CH2OAr carbon (C2) has a wedge to its CH2 substituent. Applying the CIP priorities to the drawing gives S, which is `[C@H]` in the SMILES below.
- The quaternary carbon (C4) has a wedge to its CH2-triazole. This gives R, which is `[C@]` in the SMILES below.

I derived both tags by hand from the drawing rather than checking them with software.

SMILES: CC(C)N1CCN(C1=O)c1ccc(cc1)N1CCN(CC1)c1ccc(cc1)OC[C@H]1OC[C@](Cn2cncn2)(c2ccc(F)cc2F)O1

name: Pregabalin
text:
The drawing is pregabalin, (S)-3-(aminomethyl)-5-methylhexanoic acid.

- **Chain:** an isopropyl group (the two left methyls on one CH) is joined by a CH2 to the stereocentre. From the stereocentre, one branch is CH2–C(=O)OH and the other is CH2–NH2.
- **Stereocentre:** the only wedge is the bond from the stereocentre to the isobutyl CH2, so the implicit H points away from the viewer.
- **CIP priorities:** CH2NH2 ranks first. CH2COOH ranks second, because its next carbon carries (O,O,O) against (C,C,H) for the isobutyl CH. The isobutyl CH2 ranks third and H fourth.
- **Direction:** on the page the sequence CH2NH2 (down), CH2COOH (upper right), isobutyl (upper left) runs counterclockwise. With H at the back, that is S.
- **SMILES:** I set the chirality tag by converting the known PubChem pregabalin SMILES, CC(C)C[C@@H](CC(=O)O)CN, rather than deriving it from first principles. Swapping the last two neighbours flips @@ to @, giving the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](CN)CC(=O)O

name: Prednisolone
text:
The drawing shows a pregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione skeleton, which is prednisolone. It has these features:
- ring A: a cross-conjugated dienone (C=C–C(=O)–C=C),
- two angular methyl groups,
- an 11-hydroxyl,
- a 17-hydroxyl and a 17-side chain of C(=O)CH2OH.

The ring system is drawn mirrored left-to-right relative to the usual steroid orientation. The hashed methyls and the other wedge/hash marks are therefore consistent with the natural stereochemistry. I wrote the SMILES from the standard prednisolone stereochemistry rather than deriving each centre separately from the wedges.

name: Prednisone
text:
The drawing is prednisone (17,21-dihydroxypregna-1,4-diene-3,11,20-trione), and the SMILES below is the standard recalled one for it. I did not rebuild each stereocentre from the wedges.

- **Rings:** the standard four-ring steroid skeleton, with ring A on the right and ring D on the left.
- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated 1,4-dien-3-one, with C=C at C1–C2 and C4–C5 and a ketone at C3.
- **Ring C:** a ketone at C11.
- **Ring D and side chain:** C17 carries a tertiary OH and a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.
- **Methyls:** two angular methyls, at C10 and C13.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing is a left-right mirror of the usual steroid orientation, and every wedge and hash is inverted relative to the usual depiction (both methyls hashed, the H at C9 wedged, and so on). The mirrored layout and the inverted marks cancel, so it is the natural configuration.

SMILES: C[C@]12C=CC(=O)C=C1CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2C(=O)C[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]4(C(=O)CO)O)C

name: Planosporicin
text:
I read this as a 24-residue polycyclic peptide with five thioether bridges, and wrote it residue by residue from the N-terminus. I could not read every part of the drawing with confidence, so some choices below are assumptions.

**Sequence as read, N to C:**
1. Ile
2. Z-dehydrobutyrine, with the CH3 cis to the N as drawn
3. Cys-type residue with a two-carbon arm to S (bridged to residue 11)
4. Val
5. Dehydroalanine
6. Trp
7. Cys (S-bridged to residue 18)
8. Residue with a two-carbon arm to S (bridged to residue 9)
9. Cys (S-bridged to residue 8)
10. Thr
11. Cys (S-bridged to residue 3)
12. Glu
13. Gly
14. Gly
15. Gly
16. Cys (S-bridged to residue 19)
17. Gly
18. Cys (S-bridged to residue 7)
19. Cys (S-bridged to residue 16)
20. His
21. Cys (S-bridged to residue 22)
22. Cys (S-bridged to residue 21)
23. Pro
24. Gly-OH

**Uncertain readings:**
- Several bonds in the drawing are overlapped or stretched, so some connections are inferred from topology rather than read directly. This applies most to the Gly-Gly-Gly stretch and the right-hand ring system.
- Residues 3 and 8 are written with two carbons between the α-carbon and sulfur, because the drawing shows two vertices there. The other bridging residues have one carbon.
- I did not work out the wedge and hash directions one by one. I assumed L-configuration at every stereocentre, which gives the natural L-Ile and L-Thr and L-Pro. The stereo marks are therefore an assumption, not a reading of the wedges.
