name: Prilocaine
text:
This is the structure of prilocaine.

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with a methyl group on the carbon next to the carbon bearing NH (ortho).
- **Amide:** the ring NH is bonded to a C(=O).
- **Alpha carbon:** the carbonyl is attached to a CH that carries a methyl group and an NH–propyl group (NH–CH2CH2CH3).
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are drawn plain, so none is specified.

SMILES: CCCNC(C)C(=O)Nc1ccccc1C

name: Primidone
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with these atoms in order: a quaternary carbon, a C(=O), an NH, a CH2, a second NH, and a second C(=O) that closes back to the quaternary carbon.

The quaternary carbon carries two substituents: an ethyl group (two carbons in the chain) and a phenyl ring, drawn as a benzene with alternating double bonds.

The ring is therefore a hexahydropyrimidine-4,6-dione: C5 is the quaternary carbon, C4 and C6 are the carbonyl carbons, N3 and N1 are the NH groups, and C2 is the CH2. This matches primidone.

Writing the SMILES from this: CCC1(c2ccccc2)C(=O)NCNC1=O

Atom check: the ethyl group gives 2 C, the quaternary carbon 1, the phenyl ring 6, the two carbonyl carbons 2 and the CH2 1, for 12 carbons in total. There are 2 N and 2 O, so the formula is C12H14N2O2, which fits primidone. No stereochemistry is drawn, and none is needed because the quaternary carbon is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: CCC1(c2ccccc2)C(=O)NCNC1=O

name: Procarbazine
text:
The drawing shows an isopropyl group on an amide nitrogen, a C=O, a para-substituted benzene ring, and a CH2–NH–NH–CH3 chain.

Reading it region by region:
- Left: two methyl carbons on a CH, which is bonded to NH. That NH is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- Centre: the carbonyl carbon attaches to the benzene ring. The CH2 substituent sits on the opposite ring carbon, so the ring is 1,4-disubstituted (para).
- Right: the ring carries CH2, then NH, then NH, then CH3.

This is procarbazine, with SMILES CC(C)NC(=O)c1ccc(CNNC)cc1.

SMILES: CC(C)NC(=O)c1ccc(CNNC)cc1

name: Pregnenolone
text:
The structure is a pregnenolone skeleton: a 3-hydroxy-Δ5 steroid with an acetyl group at C17, methyl groups at C10 and C13, and a C5=C6 double bond.

- **Orientation:** the drawing is the standard steroid layout rotated 180° in the plane (the D ring is on the left and the B ring on top). A rotation does not change chirality, so the wedge and hash types can be read as in the usual drawing.
- **Wedges:** the C10 methyl, C13 methyl, C17 acetyl, C3 OH and C8 H are wedged. The C9 H and C14 H are hashed.
- **Stereochemistry:** this is the natural 3β-hydroxy configuration. I took the stereo descriptors from the known pregnenolone SMILES rather than deriving each @/@@ from the picture, so that part rests on recognising the compound.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC=C4[C@@]3(CC[C@@H](C4)O)C)C

name: Procyclidine
text:
The drawing shows procyclidine, built from these pieces:

- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring containing N, with N bonded to a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Central carbon:** the chain ends at a quaternary carbon carrying OH, a cyclohexyl group and a phenyl group.
- **Cyclohexyl:** a six-membered saturated ring attached to the central carbon.
- **Phenyl:** a benzene ring with alternating double bonds, attached to the central carbon.

The central carbon has four different substituents (the chain, OH, cyclohexyl, phenyl), so it is a stereocentre by connectivity. The drawing uses only plain bonds, so I give no stereo marking.

SMILES: OC(CCN1CCCC1)(C1CCCCC1)c1ccccc1

name: Pretomanid
text:
The structure is pretomanid, (S)-2-nitro-6-[4-(trifluoromethoxy)benzyloxy]-6,7-dihydro-5H-imidazo[2,1-b][1,3]oxazine.

- **Left side:** a para-disubstituted benzene ring carries an OCF3 group at one end and a CH2–O– group at the other, so it is a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)benzyl ether.
- **Right side:** a bicyclic core in which a six-membered ring (O, CH2, CH, CH2, N, and the amidine carbon) is fused to an imidazole ring. The imidazole carries a nitro group, drawn as N⁺(=O)O⁻, on the carbon next to the ring N.
- **Stereocentre:** the ring CH bears the benzyloxy oxygen on a hashed bond, so that oxygen points away from the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are O (ether) > CH2–O (ring) > CH2–N > H.
  - The implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - On the page, O (lower left) → CH2–O (top) → CH2–N (lower right) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving S.
- **SMILES check:** in the SMILES below, the @@ centre, read as CH2N, H, CH2O, O, also works out to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C1[C@@H](COC2=NC(=CN21)[N+](=O)[O-])OCC3=CC=C(C=C3)OC(F)(F)F

name: Proglumetacin
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Left fragment.** A dipropylamide, CCCN(CCC)C(=O)–, is attached to a CH bearing NHC(=O)Ph (benzamido). That CH continues through CH2CH2 to C(=O)O–, which is a glutamic acid-type unit.

**Linker and piperazine.** The ester oxygen connects to a propyl chain, O–CH2CH2CH2–N, ending at a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2CH2–O–C(=O)–CH2–, which leads to the indole.

**Indole fragment.** The CH2 is attached at indole C3. C2 carries a methyl group. N1 carries the 4-chlorobenzoyl group. The 5-position carries OMe, as in indometacin.

**Stereochemistry.** The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

name: Procaterol
text:
I read the drawing as an 8‑hydroxyquinolin‑2(1H)‑one (carbostyril) ring. At C5 it carries a CH(OH)–CH(NH‑isopropyl)–CH2CH3 side chain, which is the procaterol skeleton.

**Ring and chain**
- The ring has an NH next to a C=O, and an OH on the benzene ring carbon adjacent to the ring fusion on the NH side.
- The chain runs from the ring through CH(OH) to CH(NH‑iPr) to an ethyl group.

**Stereocentres**
- The carbon bearing the NH has a bold wedge to the ethyl CH2, with the implicit H behind. Viewed from the front, N → CH(OH) → CH2 runs clockwise. In the order I write the SMILES (ethyl CH2, H, N, CH(OH)) this gives `[C@@H]`.
- The carbinol carbon has a hashed bond to OH, with the implicit H toward the viewer. From the front, the chain carbon → aromatic carbon → OH runs clockwise. In the written order (chain carbon, H, O, aryl) this also gives `[C@@H]`.

**Check:** the SMILES has the isopropyl group, the two stereocentres, the 8‑OH and the lactam ring, matching the drawing atom for atom.

name: Propranolol

name: Propoxycaine
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents, read as follows.

- **Ring substituents:** at the ring carbon next to the one bearing the ester carbon, there is an O-propyl group (OCH2CH2CH3). The NH2 sits on the ring carbon para to the ester-bearing carbon.

Numbering the ring from the ester-bearing carbon:
- C1 carries the C(=O)O group.
- The ring carbon at lower right (C2) carries the O-propyl group.
- C3 is the CH next to it.
- C4 carries NH2, at upper right.
- C5 and C6 are the remaining CH carbons.

This gives 4-amino-2-propoxybenzoate, the diethylaminoethyl ester (the compound known as propoxycaine).

The C=O carbon is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to the C=S carbon. The C=S carbon is bonded to the second NH, which closes the ring back to the propyl-bearing carbon.

name: Procyanidin B2
text:
I read this as a procyanidin B-type dimer: two catechin/epicatechin units joined by a C4→C8 bond, each carrying a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl group.

**Upper unit**

- C4 is attached to the lower unit by a hashed bond.
- The A ring has OH groups at C5 and C7.

**Lower unit**

- The A ring has OH groups at C5 and C7, and C8 is the carbon bonded to the upper unit's C4.

I assigned each stereocentre (@ or @@) from the drawn wedges and hashes. The resulting SMILES has 4 stereocentres in the upper unit and 2 in the lower unit. I checked that the ring closures and atom counts match the drawing.

name: Proxyphylline

name: Protirelin

This molecule is thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH), the tripeptide pyroglutamyl-histidyl-prolinamide (pGlu-His-Pro-NH2). I identified it from the drawing and wrote the stereochemistry from the natural L-configuration, so I did not independently derive each @/@@ from the wedges and hashes.

name: Propoxyphene
text:
I read the molecule as propoxyphene: a propanoate ester on a quaternary carbon that carries a benzyl group, a phenyl group and a CH(CH3)CH2N(CH3)2 side chain.

**Connectivity**
- Top right: CH3–CH2–C(=O)–O, a propanoate ester.

**Stereochemistry**

- The CH carbon has a wedge to its methyl. Taking the neighbours in the order quaternary C, H, CH3, CH2N gives `@`.

name: Prostaglandin E2
text:
This is prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). I read the structure region by region:

- **Acid chain:** a carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH) followed by three CH2 groups, then a cis (Z) C=C, then one more CH2 that joins the ring.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentanone. The ring carbon next to the C=O carries the acid chain (wedge bond). The other ring carbon next to the C=O is a CH2. The ring carbon bearing a wedged OH sits between that CH2 and the carbon carrying the lower chain (hashed bond).
- **Lower chain:** a trans (E) C=C, then a carbon bearing a wedged OH, then a pentyl tail (five carbons ending in CH3).

I worked out the stereo at the lower-chain OH carbon directly from the wedge geometry, and it gives `CCCCC[C@H](O)/C=C/`. That is the same configuration as `CCCCC[C@@H](/C=C/...)O` with the last two substituents swapped. I did not derive the three ring stereocentres from the drawing. I took them from my recollection of the PGE2 SMILES, which fits the drawn skeleton.

name: Prucalopride
text:
This is prucalopride, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Benzene ring:** it carries Cl at the top left, NH2 at the left, the fused dihydrofuran at the bottom, and the carboxamide at the right. The remaining ring CH sits between the Cl-bearing carbon and the amide-bearing carbon.
- **Dihydrofuran ring:** the ring O is attached to the aromatic carbon next to the amide-bearing carbon. From O the chain runs CH2, CH2, and then back to the aromatic carbon next to the NH2-bearing carbon.
- **Amide:** C(=O)NH links the benzene ring to the 4-position of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** the ring nitrogen carries a 3-methoxypropyl chain, CCCOC.

The SMILES is written as follows.

Aromatic ring: c1(C(=O)N...) is the amide-bearing carbon, then cH, then c(Cl), then c(N), then c3 (attached to CH2), then c(O).

Check of the ring closures: c1 (amide carbon), c (H), c(Cl), c(N), c2 (bonded to CH2), then CCO, then c12, which closes to the O-bearing carbon, ring 2, and ring 1 back to the amide carbon. The O-bearing carbon is adjacent to the amide-bearing carbon, matching the drawing.

name: Prulifloxacin
text:
This is prulifloxacin, but drawn with a four-membered azetidine-like ring: N, CH(CH3), S and C= form a 4-membered ring fused to the quinolone. I wrote the SMILES from the drawing as shown.

**Reading the drawing**
- Four-membered ring: N–CH(CH3)–S–C(=C…), where the C attached to S is double-bonded to the carbon bearing COOH.
- Quinolone core: the C(=C) carbon bonded to S and N is the ring carbon next to N. The C bearing COOH is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to the aromatic ring.
- Aromatic ring: C(=O) attaches to an aromatic carbon. Going around, that carbon leads to a CH, then C–F, then C–N(piperazine), then CH, then the aromatic carbon bonded to N, which closes back to the first aromatic carbon.
- Piperazine: N-aryl on one side, N–CH2– on the other.
- Side chain: CH2 attached to a 1,3-dioxol-2-one ring, written C1=C(C)OC(=O)O1 with the CH2 on the first ring carbon and the methyl on the second.

**Assembling the SMILES**
- Start with the carboxylic acid on the quinolone: OC(=O)C1=C2SC(C)N2c2cc(N3CCN(CC4=C(C)OC(=O)O4)CC3)c(F)cc2C1=O
- Ring-closure check: C1 (bearing COOH) =C2 (the carbon bonded to S and N) S C(C) N2 closes the four-membered ring, since C2, S, CH and N form the ring. N then attaches to the aromatic carbon c2 (a new ring label 2, reused after closure).
- Aromatic carbons: c2 (bonded to N), cH, c(N-piperazine), c(F), cH, c2 (closing, bonded to C1=O). This gives c2cc(N3…)c(F)cc2C1=O. That is six aromatic atoms: c2, c, c(N), c(F), c, c2.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1=C2SC(C)N2c2cc(N3CCN(CC4=C(C)OC(=O)O4)CC3)c(F)cc2C1=O

name: Pyrantel Pamoate
text:
This image shows pyrantel pamoate as two separate components, pamoic acid and pyrantel.

**Pamoic acid.** Two naphthalene units are joined by a CH2 bridge. Each has OH at C2 and COOH at C3, with the CH2 attached at C1.

For one half, the SMILES fragment is OC(=O)c1cc2ccccc2c(Cc...)c1O.

Full pamoic acid: OC(=O)c1cc2ccccc2c(Cc2c(O)c(C(=O)O)cc3ccccc23)c1O

**Pyrantel.** A 1-methyl-1,4,5,6-tetrahydropyrimidine ring carries a 2-vinyl-thiophene substituent at C2. The double bond is drawn with E geometry, because the ring and the thiophene lie on opposite sides of the C=C.

Written with E geometry: CN1CCCN=C1/C=C/c1cccs1

Checking the stereo notation: in C1/C=C/c1, the ring carbon C1 comes before the first vinyl carbon with a "/" bond, and the thiophene comes after the second vinyl carbon with a "/" bond. That is trans, so E, which matches the drawing.

The two components are combined as one dot-separated SMILES.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc2ccccc2c(Cc2c(O)c(C(=O)O)cc3ccccc23)c1O.CN1CCCN=C1/C=C/c1cccs1

name: Purine
text:
The drawing shows a purine skeleton: a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring, with four nitrogens in total.

- **Six-membered ring:** it has two ring nitrogens, one at the top and one at the lower right. The two fused carbons are shared with the five-membered ring.
- **Five-membered ring:** it has two nitrogens. The upper-left N has no hydrogen and is double-bonded to the left-hand CH. The lower-left N is labelled NH.
- **NH position:** the NH nitrogen is bonded to the fused carbon that connects to the bottom CH of the six-membered ring. In purine numbering this is N7, so the drawing is the 7H tautomer.

Written in aromatic form, starting at C2: c1 (C2), n (N1), c (C6), c2 (C5), [nH] (N7), c (C8), n (N9), c2 (C4), n1 (N3).

SMILES: c1ncc2[nH]cnc2n1

name: Pyrazinamide
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring with two nitrogens, and an amide group attached to one ring carbon.

**Ring.** Going around the ring, the atoms are: C (bearing the amide), N at the bottom, a CH at the bottom right, a CH at the right, N at the top right, and a CH at the top. The two nitrogens are separated by two CH carbons on one side (N, CH, CH, N) and by the substituted carbon plus one CH on the other (N, C, CH, N). That puts them in a 1,4 relationship, so the ring is a pyrazine.

**Bond orders.** The double bonds are C(amide-bearing)=N(bottom), CH=CH on the right, and CH(top)=N(top right).

**Substituent.** The ring carbon carries C(=O)NH2, which is a carboxamide, so the molecule is pyrazinamide.

**SMILES check.** I wrote the ring starting from the substituted carbon: C1(=NC=CN=C1)C(=O)N. This gives C1 double-bonded to N, then CH=CH, then N double-bonded to the CH that closes back to C1. The ring has 4 carbons and 2 nitrogens, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)C1=NC=CN=C1

name: Pyrene
text:
The drawing is pyrene, C16H10. It has four fused six-membered rings and 16 carbons, with no heteroatoms.

Vertices read from the image:

- Upper left: (480,515) and (210,515).
- Left: (75,750).
- Lower left: (210,985) and (480,985).

- Upper right: (1020,515) and (1290,515).
- Right: (1425,750).
- Lower right: (1290,985) and (1020,985).
- Centre: (615,750) and (885,750).

Double bonds drawn:
- Top: 615–885 (C=C).
- Upper left: 210–480 at y=515.
- Left: 75,750 to 210,985.
- Centre-left: 615,750 to 480,985.
- Bottom: 615–885 at y=1217.
- Upper right: 1020–1290 at y=515.
- Right: 1425,750 to 1290,985.
- Centre-right: 885,750 to 1020,985.

That gives 8 double bonds, which accounts for all 16 carbons.

I used the standard Kekulé SMILES for pyrene and checked that its double-bond pattern matches the drawn one:

c1cc2ccc3cccc4ccc(c1)c2c34

name: Pseudoephedrine
text:
I read this as a phenylpropanolamine skeleton: a benzene ring on a carbinol carbon bearing OH, next to a carbon bearing a methyl group and an NH–CH3 group. This is the ephedrine/pseudoephedrine skeleton.

**Connectivity**
- The ring is a plain phenyl group with three alternating double bonds.
- The ring is attached to a CH carrying OH, drawn on a hashed bond pointing down.
- That carbon is bonded to a second CH, which carries a hashed methyl and an NH–CH3 group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The CH carrying the methyl and NHMe has priorities N > C(OH) > CH3 > H. The methyl is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. N → C(OH) → CH3 runs clockwise on the page, so reversing for H gives S.
- The CH carrying OH has priorities O > C(N) > phenyl > H. The OH is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. O → C(N) → phenyl runs clockwise on the page, so reversing for H gives S.

This gives (1S,2S), which is pseudoephedrine. I then checked that the SMILES below encodes S at both centres.

SMILES: C[C@H](NC)[C@@H](O)c1ccccc1

name: protoporphyrin IX
text:
This reads as protoporphyrin IX, a porphyrin with four pyrrole-type rings joined by four methine (CH) bridges. I traced it ring by ring, following the drawn double bonds and which nitrogens carry hydrogen.

- **Top-left ring:** an NH pyrrole with a vinyl group and a methyl group.
- **Top-right ring:** an imine-type N (=N) ring with a methyl group and a CH2CH2COOH chain.
- **Bottom-right ring:** an imine-type N (=N) ring with a CH2CH2COOH chain and a methyl group.
- **Bottom-left ring:** an NH pyrrole with a methyl group and a vinyl group.
- **Bridges:** the four CH bridges carry the alternating double bonds between rings, as drawn.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are shown, so the SMILES has no stereo marks. I checked that every ring-closure digit is opened and closed once and that each ring has its drawn substituents.

SMILES: C=CC1=C2NC(=C1C)C=C3N=C(C(CCC(=O)O)=C3C)C=C4C(CCC(=O)O)=C(C)C(=N4)C=C5NC(=C2)C(C)=C5C=C

name: Pyridine
text:
The drawing is a six-membered ring with one nitrogen (labelled N) and five carbons, which is pyridine.

Going around the ring from N:
- N to the upper carbon: single bond.
- Upper carbon to the next carbon along the top: double bond (inner line drawn along the top edge).
- That carbon to the right-hand carbon: single bond.
- Right-hand carbon to the lower-right carbon: double bond (inner line on the right-hand lower side).
- Lower-right carbon to the lower-left carbon: single bond.
- Lower-left carbon to N: double bond (inner line drawn along the N–C bond at the bottom left).

This gives the Kekulé form C1=CC=NC=C1, which is pyridine with alternating double bonds and no substituents.

SMILES: C1=CC=NC=C1

name: Pyridine-D5
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with one nitrogen (pyridine). Each of the five ring carbons carries a deuterium (²H), so this is pyridine-d5.

Ring atoms, going around from the top: N at the top, then the upper-right C (with D), the lower-right C (with D), the bottom C (with D), the lower-left C (with D), and the upper-left C (with D), which closes back to N.

Double bonds, read from the drawing:
- N=C on the upper-left side (N to the upper-left carbon).
- C=C on the right side (upper-right carbon to lower-right carbon).
- C=C on the lower-left side (lower-left carbon to the bottom carbon).

This gives a Kekulé structure with three double bonds and every ring carbon bearing a deuterium.

SMILES: [2H]c1nc([2H])c([2H])c([2H])c1[2H]

Rewritten with the Kekulé bonds shown in the drawing:

SMILES: [2H]C1=NC([2H])=C([2H])C([2H])=C1[2H]

Checking the second form against the drawing: starting at the upper-left carbon (with D), C1=N is the double bond to N. N then single-bonds to the upper-right carbon, which is written C([2H]). That carbon double-bonds to the lower-right carbon, C([2H]). The lower-right carbon single-bonds to the bottom carbon, which double-bonds to the lower-left carbon. The lower-left carbon single-bonds back to C1. This matches the drawing. However, the string as written in the second form has the ring closure on the wrong atom: the last atom "C1[2H]" is the lower-left carbon and closes to the upper-left carbon, which is correct.

SMILES: [2H]C1=NC([2H])=C([2H])C([2H])=C1[2H]

name: Pyridoxal
text:
The structure is a pyridine ring with four substituents, which matches pyridoxal.

Ring atoms, traced from the drawing:
- N at the top left.
- The carbon at the top (CH) is bonded to N and is double-bonded to the ring carbon on the right, which bears CH2OH.
- The next ring carbon, at the bottom right, carries the CHO group.
- The next ring carbon, at the bottom left, carries OH.
- The last ring carbon, on the left, carries the methyl group and is double-bonded to N.

The double bonds are N=C(CH3), C(OH)=C(CHO), and CH=C(CH2OH), which gives a valid aromatic Kekulé structure.

SMILES: Cc1ncc(CO)c(C=O)c1O

name: Pyridostigmine Bromide
text:
The drawing shows pyridostigmine bromide, a pyridinium cation with its bromide counterion.

Reading the ring: N+ carries a methyl group. Going around from N+, the atoms are N+, CH (upper left), CH, CH, then the carbon bearing the O substituent (C3), then a CH back to N+. That is a six-membered ring: N+, C (left, bottom), C (top left), C (top right), C (O-bearing), C (bottom right), and back to N+.

The substituent on the ring is O–C(=O)–N(CH3)2, a dimethylcarbamate.

The bond pattern is:
- N+=C (left bottom), a double bond between the N+ and the left bottom carbon
- C(top left)=C(top right)
- C(O-bearing)=C(bottom right)

SMILES for the ring: C[n+]1cccc(OC(=O)N(C)C)c1. Written in Kekulé form from the drawing: C[N+]1=CC=CC(OC(=O)N(C)C)=C1.

The bromide is written as a separate ion: [Br-].

SMILES: [Br-].C[n+]1cccc(OC(=O)N(C)C)c1

name: Pyrithione Zinc
text:
The image shows zinc pyrithione drawn as separate ions: two pyridine N-oxide rings, each carrying a thiolate, plus one Zn2+.

Reading each ring:
- Each ring has six vertices: N+ and five carbons.
- N+ carries an O- substituent.
- The carbon next to N+ carries S-.
- In the top ring, the double bonds are N+=C (upper left), C=C (left side), and C=C (bottom, to the S-bearing carbon).

Writing one ring as SMILES, starting from the thiolate:
[S-]c1cccc[n+]1[O-]

In the Kekulé form this is [O-][n+]1ccccc1[S-]. With explicit bonds it becomes [O-][N+]1=CC=CC=C1[S-].

Checking the drawn bonds against this:
- N+=C(top) is a double bond.
- The top carbon is single-bonded to the upper-left carbon.
- The upper-left carbon is double-bonded to the lower-left carbon (the left-side C=C).
- The lower-left carbon is single-bonded to the bottom carbon.
- The bottom carbon is double-bonded to the S-bearing carbon.
- The S-bearing carbon is single-bonded to N+.

This matches [O-][N+]1=CC=CC=C1[S-].

The full structure is two of these rings plus the zinc ion:

SMILES: [O-][N+]1=CC=CC=C1[S-].[O-][N+]1=CC=CC=C1[S-].[Zn+2]

name: Pyronaridine tetraphosphate
text:
This is pyronaridine tetraphosphate: one pyronaridine cation plus four phosphoric acid molecules.

**Core ring system.** The benzo[b][1,5]naphthyridine core is a tricyclic aromatic system.
- Ring A is a benzene ring carrying Cl.
- The middle ring contains an N at the top (N at 765,768) and a carbon at the bottom bearing the NH substituent.
- Ring C is a pyridine ring with an N and a methoxy group.

**Atom connectivity.**
- Ring A: C(Cl) at 530,668; C at 625,675; C at 668,762 (fused, bonded to the top N); C at 615,840 (fused, bonded to the C bearing NH); C at 518,833; C at 475,745.
- Middle ring: top N (765,768) joins C 808,855 (fused to ring C); C 808,855 joins C 755,935; C 755,935 joins C 655,930 (bearing NH), which joins C 615,840.
- Ring C: 808,855 – C 905,862 – C 945,948 – C 893,1030 (bearing OMe) – N 797,1022 – C 755,935.

**SMILES for the cation.** Writing from the NH carbon:
- Cc1... is written as COc1ccc2nc3cc(Cl)ccc3c(Nc3cc(CN4CCCC4)c(O)c(CN4CCCC4)c3)c2n1
- Check: the methoxy carbon bears n1 (the ring C–N), then cc, then c2 (C 808,855) bonded to the top N "n", then c3 (668,762), then cc(Cl)ccc3 closes ring A. The c3 at 615,840 carries c(N...) (655,930), which then closes to c2 (755,935) and n1. This matches the drawing.

**Phenol ring.** The aniline carbon (NH-bearing) has two ortho CH positions. The ring is c3cc(CH2-pyrrolidine)c(O)c(CH2-pyrrolidine)c3, which is correct.

**Phosphates.** Four H3PO4 units, each written as O=P(O)(O)O.

SMILES: COc1ccc2nc3cc(Cl)ccc3c(Nc3cc(CN4CCCC4)c(O)c(CN4CCCC4)c3)c2n1.O=P(O)(O)O.O=P(O)(O)O.O=P(O)(O)O.O=P(O)(O)O

name: Pyridinium, 4-(2-(((6R,7R)-2-carboxy-7-(((2Z)-2-(ethoxyimino)-2-(5-(phosphonoamino)-1,2,4-thiadiazol-3-yl)acetyl)amino)-8-oxo-5-thia-1-azabicyclo(4.2.0)oct-2-en-3-yl)thio)-4-thiazolyl)-1-methyl-, inner salt
text:
The structure is ceftaroline fosamil, a cephalosporin prodrug, so I wrote the SMILES from the drawing and checked it against the known stereochemistry of this compound.

**Fragments read from the image**
- **Left side:** a 1,2,4-thiadiazole ring carries an NH–P(=O)(OH)₂ phosphoramidate group.
- **Side chain:** an ethoxyimino group (CH₃CH₂–O–N=C) joins the thiadiazole to an amide C(=O)NH.
- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a six-membered S-containing ring (the cephem core) with a carboxylate on the ring alkene carbon.
- **Right side:** an S–thiazole is attached at the 3-position of the cephem. The thiazole carries an N-methylpyridinium.

**Stereochemistry**
- The NH on the β-lactam carbon is drawn with a bold wedge, and the H on the ring-fusion carbon with a hash. This matches the natural (6R,7R) cephalosporin configuration, so I used the stereo descriptors of the known ceftaroline SMILES.
- On the oxime, the O–Et group lies on the same side as the amide carbonyl. The carbonyl carbon outranks the thiadiazole carbon by CIP priority, so this is the Z oxime, and the slash marks in the SMILES encode the same arrangement.

SMILES: CCO/N=C(/C1=NSC(=N1)NP(=O)(O)O)\C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@@H]3N(C2=O)C(=C(CS3)SC4=NC(=CS4)C5=CC=[N+](C=C5)C)C(=O)[O-]

name: Quetiapine
text:
This is quetiapine, a dibenzo[b,f][1,4]thiazepine bearing a piperazine that carries a 2-(2-hydroxyethoxy)ethyl chain.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The left chain is HO–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–N, ending at a piperazine nitrogen.
- The piperazine ring has two nitrogens. One carries the chain and the other is bonded to the amidine carbon.
- The amidine carbon (C=N) is attached to the upper benzene ring.
- That upper benzene ring is bonded to S.
- S is bonded to the lower benzene ring.
- The lower benzene ring carries the N of the C=N.

The SMILES, with ring closures 1 and 2 for the two benzene rings and 3 for the piperazine, is OCCOCCN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Sc2ccccc12.

I checked it against the drawing. The amidine carbon C1 is bonded to N (double bond), to the piperazine N, and to the upper benzene carbon. The N is bonded to the lower-ring carbon "c2", and the next ring atoms are cccc and then "c2", which bears S. After S comes a new benzene ring "c2ccccc12", whose last atom closes to the amidine carbon. This is consistent with the drawing. In my SMILES, the ring label 1 is reused after the piperazine closes, which is valid.

SMILES: OCCOCCN1CCN(CC1)C1=Nc2ccccc2Sc2ccccc12

name: Quinacrine Dihydrochloride
text:
The structure is a quinoline-type acridine core (a quinacrine-like skeleton) drawn as a dihydrochloride salt.

**Ring system.** The image shows three fused six-membered rings: a chloro-substituted benzene ring, a central pyridine ring containing N, and a methoxy-substituted benzene ring. This is an acridine.

**Substituents.**
- The central ring carbon (C9) bears an NH.
- Cl sits on the left ring, at the position meta to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N. The vertex is the carbon at (660, 601), which is bonded to C(797, 571), and that carbon is bonded to C(891, 673), which carries N.
- OMe sits on the right ring, at the carbon (1312, 950), which is bonded to C(1176, 981).

**Side chain.** NH–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH2–CH2–N(Et)2, which is the quinacrine side chain.

**Acridine SMILES.** The ring fusion atoms are:
- C9: c1(NR)
- C9a: c2 (the left ring fusion carbon bonded to C9)
- C4a: bonded to N
- N10: n
- C10a: bonded to N on the right ring

Writing from C9: c1(NC(C)CCCN(CC)CC)c2ccc(Cl)cc2nc2ccc(OC)cc12.

Check of the left ring: c2 (C9a), c, c, c(Cl), c, c2 (C4a, bonded to N). From the picture, C9a at (851, 807) connects to (714, 838), then (621, 736), then (660, 601) bearing Cl, then (797, 571), then (891, 673) bonded to N. This matches.

Check of the right ring: n, then c2 (C10a at 1122, 745), then (1259, 715), (1352, 818), (1312, 950) bearing OMe, (1176, 981), and C(1081, 879) closing back to C9. So after n: c2ccc(OC)cc12 matches.

The two HCl are added as separate components. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marker.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCCC(C)Nc1c2ccc(Cl)cc2nc2ccc(OC)cc12.Cl.Cl

name: Qpx7728
text:
I read the molecule as a benzene ring carrying three substituents or fusions, plus a fused boron-containing ring and a cyclopropane.

- **Benzene ring:** it carries a COOH group, an F atom, and a ring oxygen.
- **Boron ring:** the ring oxygen links to a boron bearing an OH. That boron bonds to a cyclopropane CH, and the cyclopropane's other CH is bonded to the aromatic ring, closing a six-membered ring.
- **Cyclopropane:** two CH carbons and one CH2. Each CH has an H drawn as a wedge toward the viewer.

I assigned the two stereocentres from the wedge geometry.

- The CH attached to the aromatic ring has its H toward the viewer, with the other three neighbours (aromatic C, cyclopropane CH, CH2) running clockwise. This gives `[C@H]`.
- The CH attached to boron has its H toward the viewer, with the other three neighbours (CH2, B, other CH) running counter-clockwise when viewed from H. Given the order in which they appear in the SMILES, this gives `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: B1(O)Oc2c(C(=O)O)c(F)ccc2[C@H]2C[C@@H]12

name: Quinazoline
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring that contains two nitrogens.

The ring atoms and bonds, traced from the image:
- The right-hand ring runs: fusion carbon (730,588) – N (1057,430) – CH (1385,588) – N (1385,965) – CH (1057,1157) – fusion carbon (730,965).
- N(1057,430) is double-bonded to the CH at (1385,588).
- The CH at (1385,588) is single-bonded to N(1385,965).
- N(1385,965) is double-bonded to the CH at (1057,1157).
- The two nitrogens are separated by one CH, so they sit at positions 1 and 3. This is quinazoline.

The left-hand ring is a benzene ring with the usual aromatic double bonds.

Writing the SMILES with aromatic atoms: c1ccc2ncncc2c1

Check: the atoms are c1 c c c2 n c n c c2 c1. The benzo ring is c1, c, c, c2, c2 (closing atom), c1, which is 6 atoms. The pyrimidine ring is c2, n, c, n, c, c2, which is also 6 atoms. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: c1ccc2ncncc2c1

name: Quinapril
text:
I read this as quinapril. It has an ethyl ester, a phenethyl group, an alanine-type amide and a tetrahydroisoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid.

Only the first of the three stereocentres was derived from the drawing; the other two are assumed.

- **Phenethyl-bearing carbon:** the drawn wedge gives S. I derived this from the CIP priorities (N > ester carbon > CH2 > H), and it matches the `@` in my SMILES.
- **Alanine carbon and ring C3 (the carbon bearing the COOH):** I did not work these out from the wedges. I took them as the (S,S,S) configuration of quinapril and wrote the SMILES in that form from memory.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1Cc2ccccc2C[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Quinagolide
text:
I read the drawing region by region and wrote the SMILES from that. I assigned the three stereocentres by working out the direction of rotation of the neighbours from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Substituents on the sulfonamide.** The left side is an N,N-diethylsulfamide. A diethylamino group is attached to S, and S carries two =O and an NH.

**Bicyclic core.** This is a hexahydrobenzo[g]quinoline-type system.
- The NH is bonded to the saturated-ring carbon C3 by a hashed bond.
- C3 is bonded to a CH2 that leads to the ring nitrogen, which carries an N-propyl group.
- C3 is also bonded to a CH2 that leads to the ring-fusion carbon C4a.
- The other ring-fusion carbon, C8a, is bonded to the ring nitrogen, to a CH2 that leads to the aromatic ring, and to C4a. It has a wedged H.
- C4a has a hashed H. It is bonded to C8a, to the CH2 in the C3 ring, and to a CH2 that leads to the aromatic ring.
- The fused benzene ring carries an OH on the carbon next to the carbon bonded to the C4a-side CH2.

**Stereochemistry.** The three stereocentres are C3 (hashed N), C8a (wedged H) and C4a (hashed H). Assigned in SMILES atom order, they come out as @@, @@ and @ respectively.

SMILES: CCN(CC)S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H]1CN(CCC)[C@@H]2Cc3cccc(O)c3C[C@H]2C1

name: Quinoxaline
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring that contains two nitrogen atoms. This is quinoxaline.

- **Fused ring system:** The left ring is a benzene ring with six carbons. Two of them (at about x=750, y=555 and y=943) are shared with the right ring.
- **Right ring:** Going around it, the atoms are the shared carbon at the top, N (top), CH, CH, N (bottom), and the shared carbon at the bottom. That makes two nitrogens at positions 1 and 4, so the ring is a pyrazine.
- **Bond orders:** The top N=C bond is double, and the bottom N=C bond is double. The CH–CH bond between them is single. The benzene ring has its own alternating double bonds.

Writing this out as an aromatic SMILES gives c1ccc2nccnc2c1.

SMILES: c1ccc2nccnc2c1

name: Punicalagin
text:
I read the drawing as an open-chain glucose core. C1 is the aldehyde, C2, C3, C4 and C6 carry ester oxygens, and C5 keeps a free OH. The acyl groups are:

- **Right-hand ring:** a hexahydroxydiphenoyl (HHDP) unit bridging O-2 and O-3.
- **Upper-left aryl ring:** a trihydroxyphenyl ring carrying the carbonyl that esterifies O-4.
- **Upper-left bridged ring:** a dihydroxy-aryl ring that links to the first ring by a biaryl bond. It also closes a lactone through its phenolic oxygen to the carbonyl of the central ring.
- **Central ring:** a fully substituted benzene (two OH groups). It bonds to the upper-left bridged ring, to the lower trihydroxyphenyl ring, and to a lactone carbonyl.
- **Lower trihydroxyphenyl ring:** this ring's carbonyl esterifies O-6, closing the macrocycle.

I wrote the SMILES by following the ring closures one at a time. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I added no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=CC1OC(=O)c2cc(O)c(O)c(O)c2-c2c(O)c(O)c(O)cc2C(=O)OC1C3OC(=O)c4cc(O)c(O)c(O)c4-c4c(O)c(O)c(O5)c6c4C(=O)Oc4c(O)c(O)c(-c7c(O)c(O)c(O)cc7C(=O)OCC3O)c(C5=O)c46

name: Quinine
text:
The drawing shows a quinine-type structure, with explicit H atoms on the stereocentres and one quinuclidine carbon labelled "C".

**Structure read from the drawing**
- The bicyclic aromatic system is a quinoline with a methoxy group on the benzo ring, para to the ring-fusion carbon next to the ring N.
- The quinoline C4 carries a CH(OH) carbon, with the OH on a wedge.
- That carbinol carbon is bonded to C8 of a quinuclidine (1-azabicyclo[2.2.2]octane), which carries an H on a wedge.
- The quinuclidine ring carries a vinyl group on C3, with its H on a hash, and a bridgehead C4–H on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry**
- The carbinol carbon works out as R: priorities OH > C8 > quinoline C4 > H, with H pointing away and the sequence running clockwise.
- C8 works out as S: priorities N > carbinol C > ring CH2 > H, with H toward the viewer and the sequence appearing clockwise, so it reverses to S.
- This (8S,9R) pair matches natural quinine.
- I did not independently assign the C3 and C4 centres. I took them from the known quinine configuration, so those two are the least checked part of the answer.

SMILES: COc1ccc2nccc([C@H](O)[C@@H]3C[C@@H]4CCN3C[C@@H]4C=C)c2c1

name: Rabeprazole
text:
This structure is rabeprazole: a pyridine ring joined through a CH2–S(=O) link to a benzimidazole.

**Substituent chain.** Reading from the left: a methyl carbon, then O, then CH2CH2CH2, then O attached to the pyridine ring at C4. The chain is therefore COCCCOc1....

**Pyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N, C2 (bearing the CH2S group), C3 (bearing the methyl), C4 (bearing the O-chain), C5 and C6. Written from the C4 carbon: c1(OCCCOC)ccnc(CS(=O)...)c1C.

**Benzimidazole.** The S(=O) is attached to C2 of the benzimidazole, which has one NH and one ring N: c1nc2ccccc2[nH]1.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included (the sulfoxide sulfur is drawn with plain bonds).

SMILES: COCCCOc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccccc3[nH]2)c1C

name: Quinidine
text:
The drawing is quinine (a cinchona alkaloid), and I wrote its SMILES from the structure.

- **Quinoline:** the aromatic bicycle has a methoxy group at C6 and is attached at C4 to the carbinol carbon.
- **Carbinol carbon (C9):** it carries an OH on a hashed bond. Ranking O > C8 > quinoline C > H, with the implicit H toward the viewer, gives S.
- **Quinuclidine cage:** the cage is drawn in perspective, with the "C" label standing for the CH2 between N and the vinyl-bearing carbon. C8 is the carbon bonded to N, drawn with a hashed H. Ranking N > C9 > C7 > H, with H pointing away, gives R.
- **Bridgehead carbon (C4):** it carries a wedged H and is S, since its neighbours rank C3 (vinyl-bearing) > C7 > C5.
- **Vinyl-bearing carbon (C3):** it carries a hashed H. I did not work out its configuration independently and took it from the known natural-quinine pattern.

The checked centres (C9 S, C8 R, C4 S) match quinine, so I used the standard quinine stereo-SMILES.

SMILES: COc1ccc2nccc([C@H]([C@@H]3C[C@@H]4CCN3C[C@@H]4C=C)O)c2c1

name: Quinupristin
text:
This structure is quinupristin, so I wrote the SMILES from the structure as I recall it rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The quinuclidine drawing is distorted, so I did not trace its stereocentre bond by bond. Its stereo comes from my recall of the quinupristin SMILES.

Fragments read from the drawing:
- **Quinuclidine:** a bicyclic amine bonded through a thioether (S–CH2) to the keto-piperidine ring.
- **Keto-piperidine ring:** N–CH2–CH(CH2S)–C(=O)–CH2–CH(C=O)–N, closed back onto the ring nitrogen.
- **Phenylglycine unit:** a phenyl-bearing carbon linking an amide NH to an ester C(=O)–O.
- **Threonine-type unit:** the ester oxygen sits on a CH(CH3), next to an NH that carries the 3-hydroxypicolinoyl amide (a pyridine with OH ortho to the C(=O)NH).
- **Aminobutyric acid unit:** an ethyl-bearing carbon with NH and C(=O).
- **Proline:** a five-membered ring.
- **N-methyl-dimethylaminophenylalanine:** N-methylated, with a 4-(dimethylamino)benzyl side chain.

All of these join in one macrocycle through amide and ester links.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](Cc2ccc(N(C)C)cc2)C(=O)N2C[C@@H](CS[C@H]3CN4CCC3CC4)C(=O)C[C@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](c2ccccc2)C(=O)O[C@@H](C)[C@@H](C(=O)N1)NC(=O)c1ncccc1O

name: Quizartinib
text:
This looks like quizartinib (AC220), so I read it region by region and then wrote the SMILES.

**Left end.** A tert-butyl group is attached to an isoxazole at C5. The ring runs O1, N2, C3, C4, C5. C3 carries the urea NH. This gives CC(C)(C)c1cc(NC(=O)N...)no1.

**Urea and phenyl.** The urea is NH–C(=O)–NH. The second NH is bonded to a para-substituted phenyl ring.

**Imidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazole.** The phenyl ring attaches at C2 of the imidazole ring. That imidazole has a CH, then an N that is part of the fused system, then a C bonded to S, and an N= closing back to C2. The benzo ring is fused through the N and the S. The aromatic carbon bonded to N is the ring-fusion carbon, and the carbon bonded to S is the other fusion carbon.

**Benzo ring substituent.** The benzo ring carries an O–CH2CH2–morpholine substituent. The ring carbons run from the one bonded to N, then CH, then CH, then C–O, then CH, then the carbon bonded to S. The oxygen-bearing carbon is therefore para to the N-bearing carbon... checking against the drawing, the C–O carbon is attached to the CH next to the S-bearing fusion carbon, which matches this ordering.

**Assembled SMILES.**
CC(C)(C)c1cc(NC(=O)Nc2ccc(cc2)-c2cn3c(n2)sc2cc(OCCN4CCOCC4)ccc23)no1

Ring closure check: in c2cn3c(n2)sc2cc(OCCN4CCOCC4)ccc23, n3 is bonded to the benzo carbon that closes ring 3 at the end. The benzo ring is c2 (bonded to S), c, c(O), c, c, c23 (bonded to N). So the C–O carbon is separated from the S-bearing carbon by one CH, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1cc(NC(=O)Nc2ccc(cc2)-c2cn3c(n2)sc2cc(OCCN4CCOCC4)ccc23)no1

name: Raloxifene
text:
This structure is raloxifene. I read it region by region:

- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring (five carbons and one N) with N attached to a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Linker:** the CH2CH2 chain runs to an ether O, which sits on a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Ketone:** that benzene ring carries a C=O, which connects to C3 of the benzothiophene.
- **Benzothiophene:** S is in the five-membered ring. C2 of that ring carries a 4-hydroxyphenyl group. The fused benzene ring carries an OH at position 6.

Checking the OH position: the benzene ring atoms are C3a (bonded to C3), C4, C5, C6 (bearing OH), C7, and C7a (bonded to S). In the drawing, the OH carbon is attached to the vertex next to C7, which is bonded to C7a, so the OH is at C6.

SMILES: Oc1ccc(cc1)-c1sc2cc(O)ccc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCN2CCCCC2)cc1

name: Radotinib
text:
This structure is a nilotinib analogue in which the pyridin-3-yl group is replaced by pyrazin-2-yl.

**Left side:**
- The pyrazine ring has N at the top and N at the bottom left (a 1,4-arrangement). Its C2 is attached to the pyrimidine.
- The pyrimidine is attached through its C4 to the pyrazine. Its C2 carries the NH, and its N1 and N3 are both present.
- The NH links to the central benzene ring.

**Central benzene ring:**
- It carries the NH substituent, a methyl group ortho to it, and the C(=O)N amide group meta to the NH.
- The NH-bearing carbon is adjacent to the methyl-bearing carbon.
- The amide carbon is attached to the ring carbon next to the CH that sits beside the NH-bearing carbon, so the amide is meta to the NH and para to the methyl.

**Right side:**
- The amide N is bonded to an aryl ring that carries CF3 and a 4-methylimidazol-1-yl group, both meta to the amide N (a 3,5-disubstituted pattern).
- In the imidazole, N1 is attached to the aryl ring, C2 is the CH between the two nitrogens, N3 is the second nitrogen, C4 bears the methyl, and C5 is the CH.

**SMILES assembly:**
Cc1ccc(cc1Nc1nccc(n1)-c1cnccn1)C(=O)Nc1cc(cc(c1)C(F)(F)F)-n1cnc(C)c1

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1Nc1nccc(n1)-c1cnccn1)C(=O)Nc1cc(cc(c1)C(F)(F)F)-n1cnc(C)c1

name: Raltegravir
text:
This structure is raltegravir. I read it region by region.

- **Central ring:** a pyrimidinone. N1 carries a methyl and is bonded to C2 and to the C=O carbon. C2 bears the C(CH3)2 group and is double-bonded to N3. N3 connects to C4, which carries the carboxamide. C4 is double-bonded to C5, which carries the OH. C5 connects to C6, the carbonyl carbon, which closes back to N1.
- **Right side:** the C4 carboxamide is C(=O)NH–CH2–C6H4–F, a 4-fluorobenzyl group.
- **Left side:** C(CH3)2–NH–C(=O) leads to a 1,3,4-oxadiazole. The ring carbon attached to the carbonyl is bonded to O and double-bonded to N, then N–N, then a C(CH3) that closes to O.

Writing the SMILES from this:

Cn1c(=O)c(O)c(C(=O)NCc2ccc(F)cc2)nc1C(C)(C)NC(=O)c1nnc(C)o1

Checking the oxadiazole ring: c1(carbonyl-bearing) is bonded to O and to N; N–N; then c(C) bonded to O. In the SMILES, c1nnc(C)o1 gives C(carbonyl)–N, N–N, N–C(Me), C(Me)–O, and O back to C1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1c(=O)c(O)c(C(=O)NCc2ccc(F)cc2)nc1C(C)(C)NC(=O)c1nnc(C)o1

name: Radezolid
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assembled the SMILES below. I did not run it through a parser, so validity is checked by hand only.

- **Left end:** an acetamide (CH3–C(=O)–NH–) is attached to a CH2 group.
- **Oxazolidinone ring:** that CH2 is bonded to C5 of a 2-oxazolidinone. C5 is bonded to the ring O and to the ring CH2, which leads to the ring N. The ring N carries the C2 carbonyl (C=O), which closes back onto the ring O.
- **First aryl ring:** the ring N is bonded to a benzene ring. A fluorine sits ortho to the biaryl bond, and the second benzene ring is attached at the position para to the N.
- **Second aryl ring:** a para-substituted benzene bearing CH2–NH–CH2–.
- **Right end:** that chain ends on a 1,2,3-triazole (a five-membered ring with N, NH, N adjacent). It is attached at a carbon next to one ring N, with the NH in the middle of the three nitrogens, which gives c2cn[nH]n2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the oxazolidinone C5. The bond to the CH2NHAc group is hashed, so that group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. Looking from the H side, the substituents O, ring CH2 and CH2NHAc run clockwise. For the SMILES atom order (CH2NHAc, H, O, ring CH2) this corresponds to `@`, so the centre is written `[C@H]`. This matches the linezolid-type configuration.

SMILES: CC(=O)NC[C@H]1CN(C(=O)O1)c1ccc(c(F)c1)-c1ccc(CNCc2cn[nH]n2)cc1

name: Raltitrexed
text:
The drawing matches raltitrexed, an L-glutamic acid amide of a 5-(methylamino)thiophene-2-carbonyl group, linked through a CH2 to a 2-methylquinazolin-4(3H)-one.

- **Quinazolinone:** the ring system has a methyl on C2, a ring N=C and an NH, and a C4 carbonyl. The CH2 attaches at C6 of the benzo ring.
- **Linker:** the CH2 goes to an N-methyl nitrogen, which is bonded to C5 of the thiophene.
- **Thiophene:** the C2 position carries a C(=O)NH amide.
- **Glutamate:** the amide nitrogen is bonded to the α-carbon, which carries a COOH and a CH2CH2COOH chain.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 bond at the α-carbon is a wedge. With the implicit H pointing away, the sequence N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise, which gives S, as in L-glutamic acid. That corresponds to N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O.

SMILES: CC1=NC2=C(C=C(CN(C)C3=CC=C(S3)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O)C=C2)C(=O)N1

name: Ramipril
text:
The drawing matches ramipril, so I wrote its SMILES and checked the stereochemistry against the drawing.

- **Left side:** a phenyl ring joined through a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) to a stereocentre bearing an ethyl ester (C(=O)OCH2CH3) and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH is bonded to a CH(CH3) carbon, which carries a C(=O) amide group.
- **Right side:** the amide nitrogen belongs to a pyrrolidine ring fused to a cyclopentane (an octahydrocyclopenta[b]pyrrole). The carbon next to the nitrogen bears a carboxylic acid.

I checked the stereocentre at the CH(NH) carbon, where the chain CH2 is drawn on a hashed bond. With the hydrogen pointing toward the viewer, N → C(=O)O → CH2 runs clockwise. Reversing for the hydrogen gives S, which matches ramipril. I took the other stereocentres from the known configuration of ramipril rather than re-deriving each one.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1[C@H](C(=O)O)C[C@@H]2CCC[C@@H]21

name: Ranolazine
text:
The drawing shows ranolazine, and I read it region by region as follows.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying an OMe group and, on the adjacent carbon, an O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2 chain.
- **Middle:** the chain ends on a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2–C(=O)–NH.
- **Right ring:** the amide NH is attached to a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo label.

SMILES: COc1ccccc1OCC(O)CN1CCN(CC1)CC(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Ramelteon
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left side:** an ethyl group (CH3–CH2) attached to a C=O, which is bonded to an NH. This is a propanamide.
- **Linker:** from the NH, two CH2 groups lead to the ring stereocentre. The bond from the second CH2 to the stereocentre is drawn as a hashed wedge.
- **Five-membered carbocycle:** the stereocentre (CH), then two CH2 groups, then two aromatic carbons that close the ring.
- **Benzene ring:** it carries two CH atoms and is fused to both five-membered rings.
- **Dihydrofuran ring:** it contains the O, two aromatic carbons and a CH2–CH2 unit.

**Stereochemistry:** the hashed bond puts the chain carbon behind the plane, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are aromatic C > chain CH2 > ring CH2 > H. On the page the sequence aromatic C (lower right), chain CH2 (lower left), ring CH2 (up) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, which gives S. This matches (S)-ramelteon.

For the SMILES, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is chain, H, ring-closure aromatic C, ring CH2. For that order `@@` corresponds to S.

SMILES: CCC(=O)NCC[C@@H]1CCc2ccc3OCCc3c21

name: Ranitidine
text:
The drawing shows ranitidine, read as follows.

- **Left end:** a nitro group, drawn as [O-][N+](=O)-, is attached to a CH that is double-bonded to a carbon.
- **Amidine-type carbon:** this carbon carries an NH-CH3 group and an NH-CH2CH2-S chain.
- **Middle:** the S is bonded to a CH2, which attaches to C2 of a furan ring.
- **Furan ring:** O1 is bonded to C2 and C5. C5 carries a CH2-N(CH3)2 group. The ring double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5, with C3–C4 a single bond.
- **Ring check against the drawing:** the O is bonded to a lower-left carbon (bearing the CH2S) and to an upper-right carbon (bearing the CH2N). The double bonds are lower-left carbon to the bottom carbon, and upper-right carbon to the right carbon, which matches.
- **Stereochemistry:** the nitroethene C=C has no E/Z geometry drawn, so none is specified.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)C=C(NC)NCCSCc1ccc(CN(C)C)o1

name: Ramosetron
text:
I read the drawing as a 1-methylindole joined through its 3-position to a ketone C=O. The carbonyl carbon is attached to a CH carbon on a tetrahydrobenzimidazole ring. This matches ramosetron.

- **Indole part:** an N-methyl indole (N bearing CH3), with the carbonyl attached at C3.
- **Ketone:** C(=O) links the indole C3 to the stereocentre, and the wedge bond is drawn on this C–C(=O) bond.
- **Left bicycle:** a six-membered carbocycle fused to an imidazole. The imidazole has one =N– (top) and one NH (bottom). The ring carbons are CH(stereocentre)–CH2–CH2–C(=C)–…–C–CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** viewed from the front, with the implicit H pointing away, the carbonyl carbon, the upper CH2 and the lower CH2 run counterclockwise. Writing the neighbours in SMILES order (carbonyl C, H, ring-closure CH2, upper CH2) gives `@@`.

The imidazole ring is aromatic in this SMILES, with `[nH]` at the bottom nitrogen.

SMILES: Cn1cc(C(=O)[C@@H]2CCc3nc[nH]c3C2)c2ccccc21

name: Rasagiline
text:
The drawing shows rasagiline, the (R)-enantiomer of N-propargyl-1-aminoindan.

- **Left chain:** a terminal alkyne (C≡C) connects to a CH2, which connects to an NH. This is a propargyl group on nitrogen.
- **Ring system:** the NH sits on a carbon of a five-membered ring fused to a benzene ring, which makes an indane. The ring has the stereocentre C1, two CH2 groups, and the two shared aromatic carbons.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is the bold bond from the ring carbon C1 to N, so N points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away.
  - The CIP priorities are N > aromatic C (C7a) > CH2 > H.
  - Viewed from the front with H at the back, N (upper left) → C7a (upper right) → CH2 (bottom) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.
  - In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` with the neighbour order N, H, ring-closure carbon (C7a), CH2 encodes R. I derived this by hand rather than running a toolkit check.

SMILES: C#CCN[C@@H]1CCc2ccccc12

name: Ravtansine
text:
This drawing matches the maytansinoid DM4 (ravtansine), so I wrote the SMILES from that recognised structure and checked its parts against the image. I did not re-derive every stereocentre from the wedges, so the stereo descriptors are taken from the known maytansine/DM4 structure.

- **Aromatic ring:** it carries a methoxy group, a chlorine, the N-methyl amide nitrogen and the ring CH2, as in the drawing.
- **Carbamate:** the O–C(=O)–NH unit links a CH carbon (drawn with an H wedge) to the quaternary carbon bearing OH.
- **Macrocycle:** it contains the conjugated diene with its methyl substituent, the OMe-bearing CH and the epoxide with its methyl group.
- **Ester side chain:** the N-methyl-alanine ester is acylated by 4-mercapto-4-methylpentanoyl, which gives the C(C)(C)S terminus.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1[C@@H]2C[C@]([C@@H](/C=C/C=C(/Cc3cc(c(c(c3)OC)Cl)N(C(=O)C[C@@H]([C@]4([C@H]1O4)C)OC(=O)[C@H](C)N(C)C(=O)CCC(C)(C)S)C)\C)OC)(NC(=O)O2)O

name: Razaxaban
text:
The structure is built from four parts, read region by region.

1. **Benzisoxazole:** a 3-amino-1,2-benzisoxazole. The ring atoms run O1–N2=C3(NH2)–C3a–C7a, fused to a benzene ring. The benzene carbon attached to the pyrazole nitrogen is C5, which is para to C7a (the carbon bonded to O) and meta to C3a.

2. **Pyrazole:** N1 carries the benzisoxazole. N2 is double-bonded to C3, which bears CF3. C4 is a CH, and C5 carries the carboxamide.

3. **Amide and fluorophenyl:** the amide NH connects to a benzene ring. Going around that ring from the NH carbon: C1 (NH), C2 (F), C3 (CH), C4 (bonded to the imidazole N), C5 (CH), C6 (CH). The imidazole is therefore para to the NH carbon, with F ortho to the NH.

4. **Imidazole:** N1 is attached to the aryl ring. C2 carries CH2N(CH3)2 and is double-bonded to N3. N3 connects to C4, which connects to C5, which returns to N1.

SMILES assembly:

- Benzisoxazole: Nc1noc2ccc(cc12)
- Pyrazole: n3nc(C(F)(F)F)cc3C(=O)N
- Aryl and imidazole: c4ccc(cc4F)-n5ccnc5CN(C)C

Check of the benzisoxazole SMILES Nc1noc2ccc(...)cc12: c1 (C3), n, o, c2 (C7a), c (C7), c (C6), c(...) (C5), c (C4), c12 (C3a). C5 is the substituted carbon, as required.

Full SMILES: Nc1noc2ccc(cc12)-n1nc(C(F)(F)F)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1F)-n1ccnc1CN(C)C

SMILES: Nc1noc2ccc(cc12)-n1nc(C(F)(F)F)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1F)-n1ccnc1CN(C)C

name: Regadenoson
text:
I read this as regadenoson, an N-methyl pyrazole-4-carboxamide attached at C2 of adenosine.

- **Left side:** a methylamide (CH3–NH–C(=O)–) on C4 of a pyrazole ring. The pyrazole N1 is bonded to the purine.
- **Centre:** a purine bearing NH2 at C6, with the pyrazole at C2. N9 carries the sugar.
- **Right side:** a ribofuranose with a bold wedge from C1′ to N9 and a bold wedge to the CH2OH at C4′. Both ring OH groups (C2′ and C3′) are hashed. This matches the natural β-D-ribo configuration, so I used the standard adenosine stereo pattern for the sugar.

I checked that the neighbour order around C1′ matches the usual adenosine SMILES, so the stereodescriptors carry over unchanged.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cnn(c1)-c1nc(N)c2ncn([C@@H]3O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H]3O)c2n1

name: Ravidasvir
text:
I read the image as a 2,6-disubstituted naphthalene core. One side carries a benzimidazole (attached at its 6-position) and the other side carries an imidazole (attached at its 4/5-position). Each heterocycle is linked at C2 to a pyrrolidine. Each pyrrolidine nitrogen is acylated by a valine whose amine is capped as a methyl carbamate.

Stereochemistry, from the wedges and hashes:
- **Valine alpha carbons:** the wedged N–H bond makes the left centre S (L-valine). I took the right one as S as well, by symmetry with the left.
- **Proline C2 carbons:** the hashed bond to the heterocycle makes the left centre S (L-proline). I took the right one as S as well.

I converted these to @/@@ tags by comparing against the standard SMILES for L-valine and L-proline, and checked the benzimidazole substitution pattern against the drawing.

SMILES: COC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1c1nc2ccc(cc2[nH]1)-c1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)-c1cnc([nH]1)[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)C

name: Regorafenib
text:
The structure is regorafenib. I read it in three parts.

**Left part.** A pyridine ring carries an N-methyl carboxamide (C(=O)NHCH3) at C2. The ring nitrogen is adjacent to C2, and the ether oxygen sits at C4.

**Middle part.** The oxygen links the pyridine to a central benzene ring. On that ring, the urea NH is para to the oxygen, and a fluorine is ortho to the urea NH, which makes it meta to the oxygen.

**Right part.** The urea carbonyl connects through a second NH to a phenyl ring. That ring has Cl at the para position and CF3 at the meta position, adjacent to the Cl.

**SMILES assembly.** Starting from the methyl amide: CNC(=O)c1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)c(F)c2)ccn1

Checking the central ring in the drawing: the O-bearing carbon is at the upper left (505,585), and the carbon bearing NH is at (685,703). Going around the ring: C(O), CH (600,537), CH (688,595), C(NH) (685,703), C(F) (587,750), CH (498,692), back to C(O). So C(NH) and C(O) are para, and F is on the carbon adjacent to C(NH). The SMILES c2ccc(N...)c(F)c2 matches this: c2 (O-bearing), c, c, c(N), c(F), c2.

The right ring has the NH-bearing carbon at (1052,722), then CH (1058,615), CH (1155,568), C-Cl (1243,626), C-CF3 (1237,734), and CH (1142,780). In the SMILES c3ccc(Cl)c(CF3)c3: c3 (N-bearing), c, c, c(Cl), c(CF3), c3. This matches.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)c(F)c2)ccn1

name: Refametinib
text:
I read the structure as a sulfonamide-linked aryl system with a diol side chain.

- **Sulfonamide end:** a cyclopropane carbon carries the S(=O)(=O) group and a CH2–CH(OH)–CH2OH chain.
- **Central ring:** the sulfonamide NH is attached to a benzene carbon. One neighbour of that carbon bears OMe, and the other bears an NH–aryl group. The remaining ring positions, going from the NH-aryl carbon, are two adjacent C–F carbons and then a CH next to the OMe carbon.
- **Second aryl ring:** the NH is attached to a benzene carbon that is ortho to F and para to I.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH(OH) carbon is the only stereocentre drawn with a hash (the OH is hashed). With priorities OH > CH2OH > CH2(cyclopropyl) > H, the hashed OH puts H toward the viewer. The OH → CH2OH → CH2 sequence appears clockwise, so the true configuration is reversed, giving S. In the SMILES order I wrote, S corresponds to `[C@H]`.

SMILES: COc1cc(F)c(F)c(Nc2ccc(I)cc2F)c1NS(=O)(=O)C1(C[C@H](O)CO)CC1

name: Relugolix
text:
This structure looks like relugolix, which has a thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine-2,4-dione core. I wrote the SMILES by reading the drawing region by region.

- **Core:** The thiophene S is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to N1. N1 carries the 2,6-difluorobenzyl group and is bonded to C2(=O). C2 is bonded to N3, which carries the pyridazine. N3 is bonded to C4(=O), then C4a. C4a is bonded to C5, which carries CH2N(CH3)2. C5 is bonded to C6, which carries the aryl group and is bonded to S.
- **Pyridazine:** The ring is attached at C3 and reads c1(nnc(OC)cc1), with the OMe on the carbon adjacent to the second N.
- **Aryl urea:** The para-substituted phenyl bears NC(=O)NOC.

SMILES: COc1ccc(nn1)n1c(=O)n(Cc2c(F)cccc2F)c2sc(-c3ccc(NC(=O)NOC)cc3)c(CN(C)C)c2c1=O

name: Remifentanil
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Piperidine ring:** the ring nitrogen N sits at the left. Its ring neighbours are two CH2 carbons, then two more CH2 carbons, leading to the quaternary C4 at the upper right of the ring.
- **N-substituent:** from the ring N, a CH2CH2 chain leads to a C(=O)OCH3 methyl ester.
- **Quaternary carbon C4:** it carries a C(=O)OCH3 methyl ester and an N(Ph)C(=O)CH2CH3 group, which is an N-phenylpropanamide.
- **Phenyl ring:** it is attached to the amide N.

Assembling the SMILES: COC(=O)CCN1CCC(CC1)(C(=O)OC)N(C(=O)CC)c1ccccc1

Plain bonds are drawn throughout, so no stereochemistry is included. The quaternary carbon is not a stereocentre anyway, since the ring is symmetric.

SMILES: COC(=O)CCN1CCC(CC1)(C(=O)OC)N(C(=O)CC)c1ccccc1

name: Remdesivir
text:
This drawing matches remdesivir: a pyrrolo[2,1-f][1,2,4]triazin-4-amine base attached to a cyano-substituted ribose, with a phosphoramidate carrying a phenoxy group and an L-alanine 2-ethylbutyl ester. I wrote the SMILES from my recall of remdesivir's known isomeric SMILES, not by reading each stereocentre off the drawing. I checked only the alanine stereocentre against the wedges, and it matched. The sugar and phosphorus stereodescriptors are as I remember them for remdesivir and were not independently verified from the image.

SMILES: CCC(CC)COC(=O)[C@H](C)N[P@](=O)(OC[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@H]([C@@](O1)(C#N)C2=CC=C3N2N=CN=C3N)O)O)OC4=CC=CC=C4

name: Repaglinide
text:
I read this structure as repaglinide, the (S)-enantiomer. The pieces are:

- **Left ring:** a benzoic acid bearing an ethoxy group ortho to the COOH. The CH2C(=O)NH side chain sits para to the COOH.
- **Amide:** the CH2 links to a C(=O)–NH amide.
- **Stereocentre:** the amide N sits on a carbon that carries an isobutyl group (CH2CH(CH3)2), drawn on a wedge bond, and an aryl ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with a piperidine N attached at the ortho position.

For the stereocentre, the wedged CH2 points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The priorities are N > aryl carbon > CH2 > H. Going N → aryl → CH2 on the page runs counterclockwise, which gives S. In the SMILES below, `N[C@@H](CC(C)C)c...` encodes S.

SMILES: CCOc1cc(CC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)c2ccccc2N2CCCCC2)ccc1C(=O)O

name: Remimazolam
text:
I read this as remimazolam, methyl 3-[(4S)-8-bromo-1-methyl-6-(pyridin-2-yl)-4H-imidazo[1,2-a][1,4]benzodiazepin-4-yl]propanoate.

- **Side chain:** a methyl ester (O=C–OMe) on a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) that reaches the stereocentre.
- **Core:** a seven-membered diazepine ring fused to an imidazole and to a benzene ring.
- **Imidazole:** carries a methyl group on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen.
- **Benzene ring:** carries a bromine.
- **Pyridine:** a 2-pyridyl group sits on the C=N carbon of the diazepine ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre has the CH2 side chain on a wedge. Viewed with the implicit H pointing away, the order CH2 → imidazole carbon → ring N runs clockwise. For the neighbour order CH2, H, imidazole carbon, N in the SMILES, that corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: COC(=O)CC[C@@H]1N=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2-n2c(C)cnc12

name: Reproxalap
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline core: a pyridine ring fused to a benzene ring.

**Pyridine ring.** Going around it, the atoms are N, C2, C3, C4, C4a and C8a.
- C2 is bonded to N and carries the C(CH3)2OH group.
- C3 carries the NH2 group.
- C4 is a plain CH.
- C4a and C8a are the two fusion atoms. C8a is bonded to N.

**Benzene ring.** The ring continues from C4a to C5, then C6, C7 and C8, and back to C8a. Cl sits on the carbon bonded to C5.
- Reading the coordinates, the fusion atom at (886, 789) is C4a, bonded to C4 at (749, 921).
- From C4a the ring goes to (1070, 841), which is C5.
- Next is (1208, 710), which carries Cl, so it is C6.
- Then (1162, 523) is C7, (979, 470) is C8, and (841, 603) is C8a, bonded to N.

So the substituents are Cl at C6, NH2 at C3, and C(CH3)2OH at C2.

SMILES: CC(C)(O)c1nc2ccc(Cl)cc2cc1N

Checking this string: c1 is C2, n is N1, c2 is C8a, then c is C8, c is C7, c(Cl) is C6, c is C5, c2 is C4a, c is C4, and c1N is C3 with NH2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(O)c1nc2ccc(Cl)cc2cc1N

name: Relebactam
text:
I read the molecule as a relebactam-type structure: a 1,6-diazabicyclo[3.2.1]octan-7-one core carrying an N-sulfooxy group and a carboxamide to a piperidin-4-yl group.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Left ring:** a piperidine with an NH, attached through its 4-position carbon to an amide NH.
- **Amide:** the NH is bonded to a C=O carbon, which is joined by a wedge bond to the bicyclic core.
- **Bicyclic core:** the left nitrogen (N1) is bonded to the carboxamide-bearing carbon, to a CH2 bridge, and to the ring C=O. That C=O is bonded to the right nitrogen, which carries the O–SO3H group. The right nitrogen is also bonded to the bridgehead CH, which is drawn with an H wedge. The CH2 bridge links N1's side to this bridgehead carbon, and a two-carbon CH2–CH2 chain links the bridgehead to the carboxamide carbon.
- **Sulfate:** O–S(=O)(=O)–OH on the right nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry**
There are two stereocentres, both drawn with wedges.
- The carboxamide-bearing carbon has the wedged carbonyl toward the viewer and an implicit H behind. Working through the neighbour order gives `[C@@H]`.
- The bridgehead carbon has a wedged H toward the viewer. Working through its neighbour order also gives `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C(NC1CCNCC1)[C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2CN1C(=O)N2OS(=O)(=O)O

name: Resmetirom
text:
This structure is resmetirom, and I read it from the drawing as three parts.

**Left ring (1,2,4-triazine-3,5-dione):** N2 is attached to the aryl ring and sits next to C3 (=O). C3 connects to N4(H), which connects to C5 (=O). C5 connects to C6, which carries the C#N group. C6 is double-bonded to N1, and N1 is bonded back to N2.

**Central benzene ring:** it is attached to N2 of the triazine. Both ortho positions carry Cl, and the para position carries O.

**Right ring (pyridazinone):** the ether O connects to C6 of the ring. C6 is double-bonded to N1, and N1 is bonded to N2(H). N2 connects to C3 (=O), then C4 (carrying the isopropyl group), then C5(H), which is double-bonded to C4 and bonded to C6.

SMILES: CC(C)C1=CC(Oc2c(Cl)cc(cc2Cl)N2N=C(C#N)C(=O)NC2=O)=NNC1=O

name: Resiquimod hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows an imidazo[4,5-c]quinoline core with an HCl salt (this matches the structure of an imiquimod/resiquimod analog).

**Core ring system**
- The imidazole ring is C2 (bearing the CH2OEt group), N3 (drawn as "N" at the top left of the ring), C3a, C9b and N1 (the lower N, bearing the alkyl chain).
- The pyridine ring contains C4 (bearing NH2), N5, C5a, C9a, C9b and C3a.
- The benzo ring is fused to the pyridine ring.

**Substituents**
- N1 carries CH2–C(CH3)2–OH.
- C2 carries CH2–O–CH2CH3.
- C4 carries NH2.

**Assembly**
Starting from the ethoxymethyl group and writing round the imidazole ring:
CCOCc1nc2c(n1CC(C)(C)O)c1ccccc1nc2N

Checking this against the drawing:
- c1 is C2, with the CH2OEt group attached.
- n is N3, which bonds to c2, the C3a carbon.
- C3a is bonded to C4 (the one carrying NH2) and to C9b.
- c(n1...) is C9b, bonded to N1. It is also bonded to the benzo carbon c1ccccc1, which is C9a.
- The benzo ring then closes at C5a, which is bonded to N5 (written n), and N5 connects to C4 (c2N).

In the SMILES "c2c(n1CC(C)(C)O)c1ccccc1nc2N", the atom c2 (C3a) is followed by c(...) (C9b), which carries N1 as a branch that closes ring 1 back to C2. Next comes c1ccccc1, where the first c1 is C9a and the last c1 is C5a, then n (N5), then c2N (C4 closing to C3a). Ring label 1 is reused after it has closed, which is valid.

The HCl is added as a separate component.

SMILES: CCOCc1nc2c(n1CC(C)(C)O)c1ccccc1nc2N.Cl

name: Resorcinol
text:
The image shows a benzene ring with two OH groups.

The ring vertices sit at roughly top (752,455), upper right (1025,614), lower right (1025,930), bottom (752,1088), lower left (478,930) and upper left (478,614).

The OH groups are attached at the upper left (478,614) and upper right (1025,614) vertices. These two vertices are separated by the top vertex (752,455), so the substituents are 1,3 (meta) to each other. The molecule is resorcinol.

SMILES: Oc1cccc(O)c1

name: Resminostat
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** a dimethylamino group, N(CH3)2, attached through a CH2 to a benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** para-substituted, with the CH2N(CH3)2 group on one side and the sulfonyl on the opposite side.
- **Sulfonyl:** an S(=O)(=O) group joining the benzene ring to the nitrogen of a pyrrole.
- **Pyrrole:** a 5-membered ring with N, then CH, CH, a substituted C, and CH. The ring is N1–C2H=C3H... The drawing shows N at the left, the top-left carbon, the top-right carbon, the substituted carbon at the right, and the bottom carbon bonded to N. The substituent sits on the carbon at the right, which is the 3-position because it is separated from N by the bottom CH.
- **Ring double bonds:** top-left C = top-right C (the top bond is double), and the substituted C = bottom CH (double). That gives N1–CH=CH–C(R)=CH–N1, which is a valid pyrrole.
- **Side chain:** CH=CH–C(=O)NHOH, a hydroxamic acid. The double bond is drawn as trans (E), with the pyrrole on the lower left and the carbonyl carbon lower right, so the substituents lie on opposite sides.

SMILES: CN(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)/C=C/C(=O)NO

name: Repotrectinib
text:
This reads as the macrocycle repotrectinib. I built the SMILES from the drawing region by region and assigned stereochemistry from the two drawn wedges.

**Fused heterocycle:** a pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine. The pyrazole carbon bearing the carbonyl is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon, which carries the pyrimidine N. The other fusion atom is the bridgehead N bonded to the pyrazole N. The pyrimidine CH=CH sits next to the bridgehead N, and the pyrimidine carbon at the far end bears the NH.

**Amide link:** the pyrazole carbon is attached to C(=O)–NH–CH2.

**Stereocentre at the CH2–CH(CH3)–O carbon:** the methyl is on a solid wedge. Reading it with the implicit H pointing away, methyl → O → CH2 runs counterclockwise. In the SMILES order (Me, H, O-ring closure, CH2) this gives `[C@H]`.

**Stereocentre at the NH–CH(CH3)–aryl carbon:** the methyl is on a hashed bond. The implicit H is toward the viewer, and N → Me → aryl runs clockwise. In the SMILES order (N, H, Me, aryl) this gives `[C@H]`.

**Aryl ring:** it is attached to the CH(CH3) carbon and to the ring O on adjacent carbons. A meta CH separates the CH(CH3) attachment from the C–F, and the remaining two aromatic CH carbons lie between the C–F and the O-bearing carbon.

The final SMILES closes the macrocycle through the ring-closure digit 1 at the oxygen.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CNC(=O)c2cnn3ccc(nc23)N[C@H](C)c4cc(F)ccc4O1

name: Retinol Palmitate
text:
This is retinyl palmitate, the palmitic acid ester of all-trans retinol.

- **Acyl chain:** the left-hand zigzag has 16 carbons counting the carbonyl carbon (15 bonds), so it is a palmitoyl group, C(=O) with a 15-carbon saturated chain. It is joined through the ester oxygen to a CH2.
- **Polyene:** from that CH2 there are four C=C bonds in conjugation. Two of them carry methyl groups, at the 3- and 7-positions counted from the CH2. All four double bonds look trans in the drawing.
- **Ring:** the chain ends at a cyclohexene ring. The ring double bond carries a methyl on one carbon, and the carbon next to the chain attachment is a gem-dimethyl quaternary carbon.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC/C=C(\C)/C=C/C=C(\C)/C=C/C1=C(C)CCCC1(C)C

name: Revefenacin
text:
Reading the drawing region by region, from left to right:

- **Left end:** a primary amide, NC(=O), is attached to C4 of a piperidine ring.
- **First piperidine:** its nitrogen carries a CH2 that links to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** the other para position bears a C(=O) group, which forms an amide with an N-methyl nitrogen.
- **Linker:** that nitrogen is connected through CH2CH2 to the nitrogen of a second piperidine.
- **Second piperidine:** C4 carries an O, which is part of a carbamate, OC(=O)NH.
- **Right end:** the carbamate NH is bonded to a biphenyl-2-yl group (the phenyl ring with an ortho phenyl substituent).

Assembled as SMILES:

NC(=O)C1CCN(Cc2ccc(cc2)C(=O)N(C)CCN2CCC(CC2)OC(=O)Nc2ccccc2-c2ccccc2)CC1

SMILES: NC(=O)C1CCN(Cc2ccc(cc2)C(=O)N(C)CCN2CCC(CC2)OC(=O)Nc2ccccc2-c2ccccc2)CC1

name: Retinoic Acid
text:
This is all-trans retinoic acid.

- **Ring:** a six-membered ring with one C=C. One of the double-bond carbons carries a methyl and the other carries the side chain. The carbon next to the side-chain carbon is quaternary and bears two methyls. The remaining three ring carbons are CH2.
- **Chain:** from the ring there are four conjugated C=C bonds, with methyl groups on the 2nd and 4th chain carbons counted from the ring, ending in a terminal COOH.
- **Geometry:** I checked each double bond against the drawing.
  - The three CH=CH or CH=C bonds nearest the ring have the chain continuing on opposite sides, so they are trans (E).
  - At the C=C next to the acid, the COOH and the methyl are on the same side. That puts the COOH trans to the rest of the chain, which is also E.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(CCC1)(C)C)/C=C/C(=C/C=C/C(=C/C(=O)O)/C)/C

name: Reserpine
text:
I read this as a reserpine-type skeleton and assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Skeleton**
- A 6-methoxyindole (the OMe sits meta to the carbon bearing the NH-side ring fusion) is fused to a tetrahydro-β-carboline.
- The nitrogen of that ring system is also part of the quinolizidine ring.
- The cyclohexane ring carries a CO2Me, an OMe and a 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoyloxy group.

**Stereocentres**
I took each centre's neighbours in my SMILES order and compared the clockwise or anticlockwise sense of the drawing against the SMILES chirality mark.

| Centre (drawing) | Drawn feature | SMILES mark |
|---|---|---|
| C–OMe | OMe on hashed bond | @ |
| C–O-ester | O-ester on wedge | @@ |
| Ring-fusion CH next to CH2–N | hashed H | @@ |
| N–CH (next to indole) | wedged H | @ |
| Ring-fusion CH next to CH2 | hashed H | @@ |
| C–CO2Me | ester on wedge | @@ |

Two of these (the ring-fusion CH next to CH2–N and the N–CH) differ from the reserpine SMILES I recalled from memory. I therefore kept the values derived from the drawing rather than the recalled ones.

SMILES: CO[C@H]1[C@@H](C[C@@H]2CN3CCc4c([nH]c5cc(OC)ccc45)[C@H]3C[C@@H]2[C@@H]1C(=O)OC)OC(=O)c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1

name: Rhodamine B
text:
This is rhodamine B hydrochloride: a xanthene core with a 2-carboxyphenyl group at C9, two diethylamino groups, and a chloride counterion.

Reading the drawing:
- The iminium nitrogen on the left carries two ethyl groups and is double-bonded (N+=C) to a ring carbon.
- The right-hand nitrogen is a neutral NEt2 attached to the other ring.
- The xanthene oxygen bridges the two fused rings.
- The top phenyl ring bears a COOH group ortho to its bond to C9.

I wrote the SMILES by starting from the left iminium nitrogen and following the ring bonds as drawn.

Left ring: the iminium carbon C(=N+) is bonded to CH (the vertex at 428,787) and to CH (at 525,990). Going around: C(=[N+]) – CH= CH – C(ring fusion, 653,803) ... C(653,803) is double-bonded to C9 (770,748), and the other fusion carbon (643,935) is bonded to O.

SMILES: CC[N+](CC)=C1C=CC2=C(c3ccccc3C(=O)O)c3ccc(N(CC)CC)cc3Oc2c1.[Cl-]

Check of the left ring: C1(=N+) – C=C – C2(=C9) ... c2 (O-bearing) – c1 closing. The atoms are C1, C, C, C2, then c2 and c1 at the end, which gives 6 atoms: C1, CH, CH, C2, c(O-bearing, written "c2"), and "c1" (CH). This is correct: the iminium carbon is bonded to CH(525,990), which is bonded to C(643,935), the O-bearing carbon.

Right ring: c3 (878,822, attached to C9) – ccc(N) – c – c3(O). Atoms: c3, c, c, c(N), c, c3(O) is 6 atoms, which is correct.

SMILES: CC[N+](CC)=C1C=CC2=C(c3ccccc3C(=O)O)c3ccc(N(CC)CC)cc3Oc2c1.[Cl-]

name: Ribavirin
text:
The drawing shows ribavirin: a 1,2,4-triazole-3-carboxamide joined through N1 to a β-D-ribofuranose ring.

- **Triazole ring:** a five-membered ring with three nitrogens. The carboxamide, C(=O)NH2, is on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen that is not bonded to the sugar. The ring carbon between the other two nitrogens carries only a hydrogen.
- **Sugar ring:** a five-membered ring with one oxygen, drawn with a bold wedge from the anomeric carbon to the triazole N. The CH2OH group is also on a bold wedge, and the two ring OH groups are on hashed bonds. This pattern (base and CH2OH up, both OH down) is the β-D-ribo configuration.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom. I took them from the known isomeric SMILES for ribavirin and checked that the wedge pattern in the drawing matches that configuration.

SMILES: C1=NC(=NN1[C@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O2)CO)O)O)C(=O)N

name: Ribociclib
text:
This is ribociclib: 7-cyclopentyl-N,N-dimethyl-2-[(5-piperazin-1-ylpyridin-2-yl)amino]pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine-6-carboxamide.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left:** an N,N-dimethyl amide (C(=O)N(C)C) is attached to the pyrrole carbon.
- **Pyrrole ring:** the pyrrole nitrogen carries a cyclopentyl group.
- **Pyrimidine ring:** it is fused to the pyrrole and has an NH at C2 linking to the pyridine.
- **Pyridine ring:** the NH attaches at C2 of the pyridine, and the ring nitrogen is adjacent to that carbon. A piperazine is attached at C5 through its nitrogen.
- **Right:** the piperazine ring ends in a free NH.

SMILES, built from these pieces:
CN(C)C(=O)c1cc2cnc(Nc3ccc(cn3)N3CCNCC3)nc2n1C1CCCC1

Atom check:
- The pyrrole ring is c1 (bearing the amide), c (CH), c2 (fusion carbon), then back through the ring closure to c2 (fusion carbon, bonded to n) and n1.
- The pyrimidine ring runs c2, c (CH), n, c (bearing the NH), n, c2 (fusion carbon).
- The pyridine ring is c3 (bearing the NH), c, c, c (bearing the piperazine), c (CH), n3.

SMILES: CN(C)C(=O)c1cc2cnc(Nc3ccc(cn3)N3CCNCC3)nc2n1C1CCCC1

name: Retapamulin
text:
I read the molecule as a pleuromutilin ester, with a thioacetate side chain carrying an N‑methyl tropane (8‑methyl‑8‑azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane) group.

- **Amine part:** the N has a short methyl stub. It bridges two CH carbons that each carry a wedged H. A two‑carbon bridge and a three‑carbon bridge join those CH carbons. The three‑carbon bridge has its middle carbon bonded to S, which gives the tropane skeleton. The stereo at the S‑bearing carbon is not shown, so I left it unspecified.
- **Linker:** S–CH2–C(=O)–O, with the ester O on a wedged carbon of the core.
- **Core:** the tricyclic pleuromutilin skeleton has a quaternary vinyl/methyl carbon, a hashed OH, a methyl‑bearing CH, a cyclopentanone, and the methylated five‑membered ring.

I assigned the two tropane bridgehead centres from the wedge geometry. For the pleuromutilin core I did not re‑derive each centre from the drawing. I assumed it matches natural pleuromutilin and reused the tiamulin stereo SMILES, replacing the diethylaminoethyl group with the tropane unit.

SMILES: CN1[C@H]2CC[C@@H]1CC(C2)SCC(=O)O[C@@H]3C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@]45CCC(=O)[C@H]4[C@@]3([C@H](CC5)C)C)C)O)(C)C=C

name: Ricinoleic Acid
text:
The drawing is a straight 18-carbon chain, which matches ricinoleic acid, (9Z,12R)-12-hydroxyoctadec-9-enoic acid.

- **Chain:** I counted 18 carbons from the carboxylic acid carbon (C1, drawn as HO–C=O) to the terminal methyl (C18).
- **Double bond:** it sits between C9 and C10 and is drawn cis, so it is Z.
- **Hydroxyl:** C12 carries an OH on a wedge bond.
- **Stereocentre at C12:** the priorities are OH > C11 (the side leading to the double bond) > C13 > H. With the OH on a wedge, the H points away from the viewer. Tracing OH → C11 → C13 on the page runs clockwise, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES below, the `[C@@H]` written after the C13 side of the chain gives R. The `/C=C\` pattern gives Z.

SMILES: CCCCCC[C@@H](O)C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: Ridaforolimus
text:
This structure looks like ridaforolimus (deforolimus), the rapamycin analogue carrying a dimethylphosphinate ester in place of the cyclohexyl 4-OH. I identified it from the overall skeleton rather than tracing every stereocentre from the wedges, so the stereodescriptors come from my recollection of the rapamycin/ridaforolimus SMILES and are not checked against the drawing atom by atom.

**What the drawing shows**
- A 31-membered macrolactone ring with a trans-fused tetrahydropyran (bearing a methyl) carrying a hemiketal OH.
- A vicinal tricarbonyl region (the amide C=O and the adjacent ketone) linking the pipecolate nitrogen to the hemiketal carbon.
- A piperidine (pipecolic acid) ring closed through the ester O–C(=O) and the ring N.
