- A conjugated triene, several ring methyl and methoxy groups, two ring ketones, and one secondary OH.
- A side chain running from the ester oxygen through CH(CH3) and CH2 to a cyclohexane ring. That ring carries an OMe and an O–P(=O)(CH3)2 group.

**Not confirmed from the image**
- The triene's E/Z geometry.
- The R/S assignment at each wedged or hashed centre.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2C[C@@H](/C(=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H](C(=O)[C@@H]([C@@H](/C(=C/[C@H](C(=O)C[C@@H](OC(=O)[C@@H]3CCCCN3C(=O)C(=O)[C@@]1(O2)O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4CC[C@H]([C@@H](C4)OC)OP(=O)(C)C)C)/C)O)OC)C)C)/C)OC

name: Riboflavin
text:
The drawing shows riboflavin (vitamin B2): a dimethyl-substituted isoalloxazine ring system with a ribityl side chain on the ring nitrogen.

**Ring system:**
- The benzene ring carries two methyl groups.
- It is fused to a central ring containing two nitrogens.
- That ring is fused to a pyrimidinedione ring with two C=O groups and an N–H between them.
- The central-ring nitrogen on the right carries the side chain.

**Side chain:** The chain is N–CH2–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH. The three stereocentres are drawn with a bold wedge, a hashed bond and a bold wedge, in that order from the ring. Working out each centre from the wedge or hash and the positions of the neighbouring atoms gives [C@H], [C@H], [C@H] when the chain is written starting from the CH2 on nitrogen. This matches natural D-ribityl riboflavin.

SMILES: Cc1cc2nc3c(=O)[nH]c(=O)nc-3n(C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO)c2cc1C

name: Rifampicin
text:
This is rifampicin, which I identified from the drawing and wrote out as the SMILES below.

- **Aromatic core:** a naphthalene-type system carrying two OH groups, a methyl, and a fused furanone with a ketone.
- **Spiro carbon:** it carries a methyl and is bonded to two oxygens, one in the furanone ring and one linking to the enol ether CH=CH–O of the macrocycle.
- **Hydrazone side chain:** a CH=N–N bond leads to an N-methylpiperazine.
- **Amide link:** an NH–C(=O) amide connects the aromatic ring to the ansa chain.
- **Ansa chain from the amide:** C(CH3)=CH (cis) – CH=CH (trans) – CH(CH3) – CH(OH) – CH(CH3) – CH(OH) – CH(CH3) – CH(OAc) – CH(CH3) – CH(OMe) – CH=CH–O.

I wrote the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes as I read them. I cross-checked it against the commonly cited rifampicin SMILES from memory, not against a database, so the stereo descriptors are the part most worth verifying.

SMILES: CO[C@H]1/C=C/O[C@@]2(C)Oc3c(C)c(O)c4c(c3C2=O)c(O)c(/C=N/N2CCN(C)CC2)c(NC(=O)/C(C)=C\C=C\[C@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H]1C)c4O

name: Rezafungin
text:
I read the structure as an echinocandin-type cyclic lipohexapeptide, closely resembling rezafungin. Its lipophilic side chain is a para-terphenyl bearing a pentyloxy group, and it carries a choline-type O‑CH2CH2‑N⁺Me3 ether. I did not attempt a systematic match against rezafungin's stereochemistry; I assigned each centre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Side chain.** A pentyloxy-substituted terphenyl is joined through a benzamide C(=O)–NH to the ring. The first ring residue is an ornithine α‑carbon (wedged NH). Its CH2, labelled "C" in the drawing, runs to a CH(OH) (wedged OH) and then to the CH bearing O‑CH2CH2‑N⁺(CH3)3 (wedged O) and the ring NH.

**Ring residues, in order around the macrocycle:**
1. A 3‑hydroxy‑4‑methylproline: its α‑H is wedged, the OH is wedged and the methyl is wedged.
2. A threonine, with hashed α‑N and hashed methyl.
3. A 4,5‑dihydroxy‑homotyrosine: the ring N–H is hashed at the α‑carbon, both OH groups are hashed, and it carries a 4‑hydroxyphenyl group.
4. A 4‑hydroxyproline: the α‑H is wedged and the OH is wedged.
5. A second threonine, with hashed α‑N and hashed methyl, which closes the ring back onto the ornithine C(=O).

I converted each wedge or hash into an @/@@ tag by working out the neighbour order around that carbon.

SMILES: CCCCCOc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)N[C@H]4C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](OCC[N+](C)(C)C)NC(=O)[C@@H]5[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)CN5C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@H](O)[C@@H](O)c6ccc(O)cc6)NC(=O)[C@@H]1C[C@@H](O)CN1C(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC4=O

name: Rifabutin
text:
I read this as rifabutin, a rifamycin-type macrocycle. The drawing shows the following parts:

- **Aromatic core:** a naphthalene-derived core carrying two OH groups and one methyl group.
- **Furanone:** a ring fused to the core, containing the quaternary C–CH3 carbon, an O atom and a C=O.
- **Spiro-imidazole:** an imidazole ring fused to the core and joined by a spiro carbon to an N-isobutyl piperidine.
- **Ansa chain:** an amide NH–C(=O) linked through a diene, a run of CH(CH3) and CH(OH) centres, an OAc group, an OMe group and an enol ether to the furanone.

I did not read the chain stereochemistry and alkene geometry independently from the wedges. I took them from the known stereochemistry of the rifamycin ansa chain (as in rifampicin), and the drawn wedges and hashes look consistent with that. I wrote the aromatic and imidazole part from my own reading of the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(\C(=O)NC2=C(O)C3=C(O)C(C)=C4C(=C3C5=NC6(CCN(CC(C)C)CC6)N=C25)C(=O)[C@](O4)(O/C=C/[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]1O)C)O)C)OC(=O)C)C)OC)C)\C

name: Rifamycin B
text:
This looks like rifamycin B: a naphthofuranone core carrying an O‑CH2‑COOH group, bridged by an ansa chain with an amide NH. I identified it from the overall scaffold and wrote the SMILES from that recognition and from my recollection of the known structure, not by independently deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The stereo descriptors are therefore the least certain part of the answer.

I checked the connectivity against the drawing and it matches. The ansa chain runs from the CH(CH3) next to the diene through CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OH), CH(CH3), CH(OAc), CH(CH3) and CH(OMe). It then continues through the CH=CH–O enol ether to the quaternary acetal carbon, which carries a methyl. The aromatic ring has a methyl, two OH groups and the OCH2COOH substituent, and the diene is attached to a C(CH3) next to the amide C=O.

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(\C(=O)NC2=CC(=C3C(=C2O)C(=C(C4=C3C(=O)[C@](O4)(O/C=C/[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]1O)C)O)C)OC(=O)C)C)OC)C)C)O)OCC(=O)O)/C

name: Rilmenidine
text:
The drawing shows a 2-amino-4,5-dihydrooxazole (2-oxazoline) ring. The ring atoms are O, a CH2, a second CH2, N, and the C2 carbon, which is double-bonded to N. C2 also carries an NH substituent.

The NH is attached to a CH that bears two cyclopropyl groups.

Writing this as SMILES gives C1COC(=N1)NC(C2CC2)C3CC3. The CH carries two identical cyclopropyl groups, so it is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: C1COC(=N1)NC(C2CC2)C3CC3

name: Rifapentine
text:
I read this as rifapentine, a rifamycin-type ansa macrolide. I wrote the SMILES from a recalled rifampicin SMILES rather than reading each stereocentre off the drawing, so the stereo descriptors are inferred from the natural rifamycin series and not independently checked against the wedges.

- **Naphthalene core:** the ring system carries the hydroxyls, a methyl, and the fused furanone with its ketone and quaternary methyl carbon.
- **Ansa chain:** it runs from the amide NH through the diene, the hydroxyl- and methyl-bearing carbons, the acetate ester, the methoxy carbon and the enol ether back to the furanone oxygen.
- **Side chain:** the aromatic ring bears a CH=N–N link to a piperazine, whose far nitrogen carries a cyclopentyl group. In rifampicin this nitrogen carries a methyl instead, so I swapped the methyl for cyclopentyl.

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(\C(=O)NC2=C(C3=C(C4=C(C(=C3O)C)O[C@@](C4=O)(O/C=C/[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]1O)C)O)C)OC(=O)C)OC)C)C(=C2/C=N/N5CCN(CC5)C6CCCC6)O)O)/C

name: Rilpivirine
text:
This is rilpivirine. The drawing shows a pyrimidine ring with two NH substituents.

- **Pyrimidine:** C2 carries an NH linked to a 4-cyanophenyl group. C4 carries an NH linked to the 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring.
- **Dimethylphenyl ring:** the 4-position bears a CH=CH–C≡N group.
- **Double bond geometry:** the vinyl chain runs from the ring carbon at about (330, 865) to the carbon at about (225, 847), and then to the nitrile carbon at about (150, 920). The ring carbon and the nitrile carbon sit on opposite sides of the double bond (one below-right, one below-left), so the geometry is trans (E).

For the SMILES, I write the chain from the nitrile end as N#C/C=C/c1cc(C)c(Nc2ccnc(Nc3ccc(C#N)cc3)n2)c(C)c1. This is the E form, as in rilpivirine.

SMILES: N#C/C=C/c1cc(C)c(Nc2ccnc(Nc3ccc(C#N)cc3)n2)c(C)c1

name: Riluzole
text:
The drawing shows riluzole, a 2-aminobenzothiazole with a trifluoromethoxy group on the benzene ring.

Thiazole ring:
- C2 carries the NH2 group and is bonded to S1 and to N3 by a double bond.
- N3 is bonded to C3a, a fused carbon.
- S1 is bonded to C7a, the other fused carbon.

Benzene ring (aromatic, alternating double bonds as drawn):
- C7a (at 640,658) is connected to a CH carbon at (805,585), which is bonded to the carbon at (950,692) that bears the OCF3 group.
- That carbon connects to the CH carbon at (932,873), then to the CH carbon at (767,945), and then to C3a at (621,839).

The OCF3 group is on the carbon para to C3a. Positions on the ring: C3a is attached to N, C4 is (767,945), C5 is (932,873), C6 is (950,692), which bears the OCF3, and C7 is (805,585). This is the 6-position, as in riluzole.

SMILES: Nc1nc2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc2s1

name: Rimantadine Hydrochloride
text:
This is rimantadine hydrochloride: an adamantane with a 1-aminoethyl group on one bridgehead carbon, plus HCl.

**Side chain:** a methyl carbon is bonded to a CH that carries NH2, and that CH is bonded to the adamantane. The bonds are all plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

**Adamantane core:** I read the ring atoms from the drawing as follows.
- C1 (748,757) is the quaternary carbon bearing the side chain. It bonds to C2 (900,455), C3 (597,1060) and C4 (935,1040).
- C2 (900,455) bonds to C5 (1238,435).
- C5 (1238,435) bonds to C6 (1425,717) and to C7 (763,1004), the long diagonal.
- C6 (1425,717) bonds to C8 (1270,1018).
- C8 (1270,1018) bonds to C4 (935,1040) and to C9 (1122,1322).
- C9 (1122,1322) bonds to C10 (783,1342).
- C10 (783,1342) bonds to C3 (597,1060) and to C7 (763,1004).

The ten core carbons are C1 to C10, each with three ring bonds or two as appropriate:
- C1 is a bridgehead.
- C5, C8 and C10 are bridgeheads (CH).
- C2, C3, C4, C6, C7 and C9 are CH2. Checking C7: it bonds to C5 and C10 only, so it is CH2.

This matches the adamantane skeleton, with four bridgeheads (C1, C5, C8, C10) and six CH2 groups.

**SMILES:** I write the adamantane as C1 (substituted bridgehead) with the three arms C2, C3 and C4.

CC(N)C12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2 is the standard rimantadine SMILES. Adding the HCl as a separate component gives the final string.

SMILES: CC(N)C12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2.Cl

name: Rimexolone
text:
I read this as a 1,4-dien-3-one steroid skeleton (four fused rings) with these substituents:

- an 11-hydroxyl (hashed bond),
- 10- and 13-methyl groups (both hashed),
- a 16-methyl (wedged),
- a 17-methyl (wedged) and a 17-propanoyl group (CH3CH2C(=O)–) on the same carbon.

The three ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn as H at C8 (hashed), C9 (wedge) and C14 (wedge).

I assigned each stereocentre (C8, C9, C10, C11, C13, C14, C16, C17) from the wedge/hash bonds and the drawn positions of its neighbours. I did not run the SMILES through a validator; I only checked that the ring-closure digits pair up and that the atom count matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCC(=O)[C@@]1(C)[C@H](C)C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)C=C[C@]4(C)[C@H]3[C@@H](O)C[C@]12C

name: Rimonabant
text:
This drawing is rimonabant, which I identified from the layout and checked against the drawn atoms.

**Pyrazole core:** N1 carries the 2,4-dichlorophenyl group. N2 is double-bonded to C3. C3 carries the carboxamide. C4 carries the methyl group. C5 carries the 4-chlorophenyl group.

**Dichlorophenyl ring:** The ring carbon attached to N1 has a Cl on the adjacent (ortho) carbon. Going around the ring, the next carbon is CH, then the carbon bearing the second Cl. This puts the second Cl para to the attachment point, giving a 2,4-dichlorophenyl group.

**Amide side chain:** C3 is bonded to C(=O)NH–N, and that N is part of a piperidine ring (N1CCCCC1).

SMILES: Cc1c(C(=O)NN2CCCCC2)nn(-c2ccc(Cl)cc2Cl)c1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Rintatolimod
text:
The image shows three separate nucleoside 5'-monophosphates, so the SMILES is three dot-separated fragments. Each has a β-D-ribose ring with 2',3'-diol, a 5'-O-phosphate and a base on C1'.

1. **Top: uridine 5'-monophosphate (UMP).** The base is uracil, attached through N1, with C2=O, N3–H and C4=O.
2. **Bottom left: cytidine 5'-monophosphate (CMP).** The base is cytosine, attached through N1, with C2=O and a C4 amino group.
3. **Bottom right: inosine 5'-monophosphate (IMP).** The base is hypoxanthine, a purine attached through N9, with a C6=O and an N1–H.

For stereochemistry, all three sugars are drawn with the same wedge/hash pattern. I used the stereo pattern of the standard D-ribonucleotides (as in AMP), `[C@@H]…[C@H](COP…)[C@@H](O)[C@H]…O`, for each fragment. I matched it to the drawing from memory of that pattern rather than by tracing each wedge individually.

SMILES: O=c1ccn([C@@H]2O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O)c(=O)[nH]1.Nc1ccn([C@@H]2O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]2O)c(=O)n1.O=c1[nH]cnc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=O)(O)O)[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O

name: Rifamycin
text:
I read the structure as an ansa-macrolide of the rifamycin type. A naphthalene core carries four substituents: a methyl, three OH groups and a fused furanone. The furanone has an acetal carbon next to its C=O. The macrocycle runs from the acetal O through a CH=CH–O–, a CH(OMe), and a CH(Me)–CH(OAc)–CH(Me)–CH(OH)–CH(Me)–CH(OH)–CH(Me) sequence. It then continues through a trans CH=CH, a cis C(Me)=CH, and a C(=O)NH amide that closes onto the aromatic ring.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge or hash drawn on its H or O. The two ring-adjacent double bonds are E, and the diene is trans then cis relative to the amide carbonyl. The SMILES is hand-checked for valid ring closures but not parsed or computed.

SMILES: [C@@H]1(O/C=C/[C@H](OC)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@H](C)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)/C=C/C=C(C)\C(=O)N9)Oc2c(C)c(O)c3c(O)c9cc(O)c3c2C1=O

name: Rintodestrant
text:
The drawing shows a benzothiophene core with three substituents, plus an acrylic acid side chain.

- **Left ring:** a 4-fluoro-2,6-dimethylphenyl ring, attached through its C1 to a ketone, C(=O).
- **Benzothiophene:** the ketone is bonded to C2 of the benzothiophene, which is next to S. C3 carries an aryl ether oxygen. The benzo ring carries an OH at position 6. This is the carbon para to C3a, which sits meta to the S-bearing C7a.
- **Right ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene linked through the ether O. Its other substituent is a CH=CH–COOH chain.
- **Alkene geometry:** the double bond is drawn as trans. The aryl-bearing carbon sits at the lower left and the COOH-bearing carbon at the upper right. The substituents point to opposite sides, so the bond is E.

SMILES for the left ring and ketone: Cc1cc(F)cc(C)c1C(=O)c2sc3cc(O)ccc3c2Oc4ccc(cc4)/C=C/C(=O)O

Check on the benzothiophene ring fusion: S is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to C7 (CH), then C6 (bearing OH), then C5 and C4, then C3a. In the SMILES, c2 (C2) is followed by s, then c3 (C7a), then c (C7), then c(O) (C6), then c (C5), then c (C4), then c3 (C3a), then c2 (C3) with the ether O. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1cc(F)cc(C)c1C(=O)c1sc2cc(O)ccc2c1Oc1ccc(cc1)/C=C/C(=O)O

name: Riociguat
text:
This is the riociguat skeleton, but the pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine is drawn with N1 bearing the benzyl group, so it is a 1-(2-fluorobenzyl)-1H-pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridin-3-yl group attached to a pyrimidine.

**Pyrazolopyridine core.** The pyridine N sits at the top left, bonded to C (top, 465,372) and to the ring-fusion carbon C7a (449,598). The pyridine carbons run N–CH–CH–CH–C3a–C7a. The pyrazole ring is C7a–N1(benzyl)–N2=C3–C3a, with C3 bonded to the pyrimidine.

**Pyrimidine.** C2 is attached to the pyrazole C3 and sits between two ring nitrogens. The ring continues C2–N=C(NH2)–C(N(Me)CO2Me)=C(NH2)–N=, closing back to C2.

**Benzyl group.** N1 carries CH2, which is bonded to a benzene ring with fluorine on the ortho carbon.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Pyrazolopyridine with benzyl: n1(Cc2ccccc2F)nc(c3cccnc13)
- Pyrimidine: c4nc(N)c(N(C)C(=O)OC)c(N)n4

Full SMILES: COC(=O)N(C)c1c(N)nc(nc1N)-c1nn(Cc2ccccc2F)c2ncccc12

The ring closures check out. In c1nn(Cc2ccccc2F)c2ncccc12, c1 is C3, then n (N2), then n(Bn) (N1), then c2 (C7a), then n, c, c, c, and finally c12 (C3a), which closes to both C7a and C3.

SMILES: COC(=O)N(C)c1c(N)nc(nc1N)-c1nn(Cc2ccccc2F)c2ncccc12

name: Rimocidin
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Structure read from the image**
- **Sugar:** a mycosamine-type ring (3-amino-3,6-dideoxy sugar). It has a ring O, a C-methyl, an NH2 and two OH groups, and it is attached to the macrocycle through a glycosidic O.
- **Macrolactone:** an ester C(=O) leads to a CH bearing an ethyl group, then CH(OH), CH2, a ketone C=O, three CH2 groups and a CH(OH). A CH2 then joins a hemiketal carbon (OH, ring O) in a tetrahydropyran ring.
- **Tetrahydropyran ring:** besides the hemiketal carbon, it has CH2, CH(OH), CH(COOH) and a CH next to the ring O. That last CH continues to a CH2 and then to the CH–O–sugar carbon.
- **Polyene:** from the CH–O–sugar carbon, four conjugated double bonds, all drawn trans, run to a CH2 and then to the ester CH bearing a propyl group, which closes the ring through the ester O.

I checked the final string for validity and for a match to the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H]1C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](O[C@@H]3O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@H](N)[C@@H]3O)C[C@@H]2O[C@@](O)(C[C@H](O)[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@@H](O)CCCC(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@H](CC)C(=O)O1

name: Rifalazil
text:
This SMILES is my best reading, and one part of the drawing is uncertain. The central core is drawn in a distorted, perspective-like way, so I resolved its bonding by chemical sense and the closest known relatives. Those are rifamycin-type compounds, specifically a benzoxazino-rifamycin with an isobutylpiperazine on the benzo ring. I took the stereocentres and double-bond geometry of the ansa chain from the rifamycin (rifampicin) pattern. I did not check each centre independently against the drawn wedges and hashes.

**Ansa chain (left and top of the macrocycle)**
- Starting from the amide: C(=O)–C(CH3)=CH–CH=CH–CH(CH3)–CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–CH(OAc)–CH(CH3)–CH(OMe)–CH=CH–O.
- The chain ends on a quaternary spiro carbon that carries a methyl group.
- The acetate is written as OC(=O)C and the methoxy as OC.

**Core (bottom right)**
- The spiro carbon sits in a five-membered furan ring fused to the aromatic ring.
- That aromatic ring carries an OH and a CH3.
- A second OH sits on the carbon next to the spiro carbon.
- The ring fused beyond it carries the amide NH and a C=O.
- An oxazine ring (O and N=) joins this ring system to a cyclohexadienone, which is the quinone-imine part.
- A piperazine bearing an isobutyl group (N–CH2–CH(CH3)2) is attached to the cyclohexadienone ring.

**Uncertain point:** which core carbons bear the OH groups and the C=O.

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(\C(=O)NC2=C3OC4=CC(N5CCN(CC(C)C)CC5)=CC(=O)C4=NC3=C6C2=O)... 

Corrected final SMILES below (the line above was cut off while drafting):

SMILES: C[C@H]1/C=C/C=C(\C(=O)NC2=C3OC4=CC(N5CCN(CC(C)C)CC5)=CC(=O)C4=NC3=C6C(C2=O)=C(O)C(C)=C7C6=C(O)[C@@](C)(O/C=C/[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]1O)C)O)C)OC(=O)C)C)OC)O7)/C

name: Ripretinib
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Right-hand bicycle (1,6-naphthyridin-2-one core):**
- The lactam ring contains N1 (bearing an ethyl group), C2 (=O), C3 (bearing the aryl group), C4 (CH), C4a and C8a.
- The pyridine ring is fused at C4a–C8a. It runs C4a, then C5 (CH), N6, C7 (bearing NHMe), C8 (CH), and back to C8a.
- Bond orders: N6=C7 is a double bond, C5=C4a is a double bond, and C8=C8a is a double bond. C3=C4 is also a double bond.

**Central benzene ring:** it carries three substituents.
- One carbon bears the naphthyridinone.
- The adjacent carbon bears Br.
- The next carbon (CH) leads to the carbon bearing F.
- The carbon next to F bears the NH of the urea.
- The remaining carbon, between the urea-bearing carbon and the naphthyridinone-bearing carbon, is CH.

**Urea:** the central ring NH–C(=O)–NH links to a phenyl group.

**SMILES assembly:**
CCn1c(=O)c(cc2cnc(NC)cc12)-c1cc(NC(=O)Nc2ccccc2)c(F)cc1Br

I checked the aryl ring in this SMILES: c1 (attached to the naphthyridinone), then cH, then c(NHurea), then c(F), then cH, then c(Br), which closes back to c1. This matches the drawing, where the Br carbon is adjacent to the naphthyridinone-bearing carbon, and F is adjacent to the urea-bearing carbon.

SMILES: CCn1c(=O)c(cc2cnc(NC)cc12)-c1cc(NC(=O)Nc2ccccc2)c(F)cc1Br

name: Ripasudil
text:
I read the molecule as 4-fluoro-5-[(2S)-2-methyl-1,4-diazepan-1-yl]sulfonylisoquinoline, which matches ripasudil.

- **Isoquinoline core:** The bicyclic aromatic system has one ring nitrogen. Fluorine sits on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon. The sulfonyl group sits on the benzo-ring carbon adjacent to that same fusion carbon.
- **Sulfonamide:** The sulfur carries two double-bonded oxygens and links the aromatic carbon to a ring nitrogen.
- **Diazepane ring:** This is a seven-membered ring containing N(SO2), a CH(CH3) carbon, a CH2, an NH, and then three CH2 groups closing back to the sulfonamide nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** The methyl on the CH carbon is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. With the implicit hydrogen toward the viewer, the sequence methyl → CH2 → N runs counterclockwise on the page. For the SMILES atom order Me, H, N (ring closure), CH2, this corresponds to `@`, giving `C[C@H]1CNCCCN1...`.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CNCCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cccc2cncc(F)c12

name: Risdiplam
text:
This looks like the risdiplam scaffold: a pyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one core carrying a 2,8-dimethylimidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine and a 4,7-diazaspiro[2.5]octane.

**Left bicycle (imidazo[1,2-b]pyridazine)**
- Imidazole ring: N= C(ring fusion) – N(bridgehead) – CH= C(CH3) – back to N.
- Pyridazine ring: the bridgehead N is bonded to a ring N, which is bonded to a C that carries the pyrimidinone. That C connects to CH, then C(CH3), then the fusion carbon.
- SMILES for this part: Cc1cn2nc(cc(C)c2n1)-

**Central pyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one**
- Substituent-bearing carbon C2, bonded to N1 (=N–), then the fusion carbon C9a, then N5 (bridgehead).
- C2=C3, then C4(=O) attached to the bridgehead N.
- Pyridine ring: bridgehead N–CH=C(N-substituent)–CH=CH–C9a.
- SMILES: c1(...)cc(=O)n2cc(N...)ccc2n1

**Right-hand amine**
- The N is attached to CH2, then the spiro carbon (part of a cyclopropane), then NH, then CH2CH2 back to N.
- SMILES: N1CC2(CC2)NCC1

**Assembled SMILES**
Cc1cn2nc(cc(C)c2n1)-c1cc(=O)n2cc(N3CCNC4(CC4)C3)ccc2n1

Checking the piperazine ring: N3–C–C–NH–C4(spiro)–CH2–back to N3. This gives N, CH2, CH2, NH, C(spiro), CH2, which is 6 atoms, matching the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1cn2nc(cc(C)c2n1)-c1cc(=O)n2cc(N3CCNC4(CC4)C3)ccc2n1

name: qs-21-apiose isomer
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing region by region. It is not machine-checked, and several stereo assignments rest on partly ambiguous wedges and natural-product conventions.

**Aglycone.** It is an oleanane triterpenoid, quillaic acid: a 12-ene, a 3-O-glycoside, a 16-OH, a 23-CHO, and a 28-carboxylate that carries an ester sugar chain. I derived the ring stereocentres from the usual natural configuration and the drawn wedges.

**C-3 chain.** The sugar on C-3 is a β-glucuronic acid carrying a β-galactose on O-2 and a β-xylose on O-3.

**C-28 ester chain.** The ester sugar chain is β-D-fucose, which is acylated on O-4. Its O-2 carries α-L-rhamnose, whose O-4 carries β-D-xylose. That xylose's O-3 carries β-D-apiofuranose, which has a quaternary C-3 with OH and CH2OH.

**Acyl group on fucose O-4.** It is a dimer of 3,5-dihydroxy-6-methyloctanoic acid. The 5-OH of the first unit is acylated by the second unit. The 5-OH of the second unit is glycosylated by an α-L-arabinofuranose.

**Stereochemistry.** The β/α sugar configurations come from the wedge and hash pattern. Where a wedge was ambiguous (the rhamnose C-3 OH and the glucuronic acid anomeric bond), I used the natural configuration, which matches the other drawn bonds.

SMILES: C[C@@]12C[C@@H](O)[C@]3(CCC(C[C@H]3C1=CC[C@H]4[C@]2(CC[C@@H]5[C@@]4(CC[C@H](O[C@H]6[C@H](O[C@H]7[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](CO)O7)[C@@H](O[C@H]8[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)CO8)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C(=O)O)O6)[C@@]5(C)C=O)C)C)(C)C)C(=O)O[C@H]1[C@H](O[C@H]2[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O[C@H]3[C@H](O)[C@@H](O[C@H]4[C@H](O)[C@@](O)(CO)CO4)[C@H](O)CO3)[C@H](C)O2)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](OC(=O)C[C@@H](O)C[C@H](OC(=O)C[C@@H](O)C[C@H](O[C@H]5[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](CO)O5)[C@@H](C)CC)[C@@H](C)CC)[C@@H](C)O1

name: Risperidone
text:
This structure is a risperidone-type molecule, here with a 3,4,6,7,8,9-hexahydro-pyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one core (no hydroxyl, so it is not paliperidone).

**Benzisoxazole part:** a fluorine sits on the benzene ring. The ring fuses to an isoxazole made of O, N and C3, and C3 carries the piperidine substituent. This is 6-fluoro-1,2-benzisoxazol-3-yl, written as `Fc1ccc2c(c1)onc2`.

**Linker:** the piperidine is attached at its 4-position to C3 of the benzisoxazole. Its nitrogen carries a CH2CH2 chain that runs to the bicyclic core.

**Bicyclic core:**
- The ring atoms are C(=O), N, C(=N), N=, C(CH3) and the carbon bearing the chain.
- The pyrimidinone ring is C(CH3)=C(chain)–C(=O)–N–C(=N–) closing back to C(CH3).
- The fused six-membered ring is N–CH2CH2CH2CH2–C, giving four CH2 groups.

Written as SMILES: `Cc1nc2CCCCn2c(=O)c1CCN1CCC(CC1)c1noc2cc(F)ccc12`

Check on the benzisoxazole: `c1noc2cc(F)ccc12` has c1 (C3), n, o, c2 (C7a), then c (C7), c(F) (C6), c (C5), c (C4), and c12 (C3a), which closes to both C3 and C7a. F is on C6, the carbon next to C7, which is attached to C7a, which is attached to O. This agrees with the drawing, where F-bearing carbon is two bonds from the O-bearing carbon.

SMILES: Cc1nc2CCCCn2c(=O)c1CCN1CCC(CC1)c1noc2cc(F)ccc12

name: Ritlecitinib
text:
I read the molecule as a 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine whose 4-position carries an NH link to C3 of a piperidine. The piperidine nitrogen is acylated with an acryloyl group (C=CC(=O)), and C2 of the piperidine bears a methyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** Two wedges are drawn.
- **C3 (carries the NH):** the wedge bond to NH puts the hydrogen at the back. The sequence NH → ring CH2 next to N → ring CH2 on the other side runs clockwise, so this centre is R.
- **C2 (carries the methyl):** the wedge bond to the methyl puts the hydrogen at the back. The sequence N → ring CH2 → CH3 runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S.

I then matched these to the SMILES chirality marks: `[C@H]` at C3 gives R and `[C@@H]` at C2 gives S.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1C[C@H](Nc2ncnc3[nH]ccc23)CC[C@@H]1C

name: Ritodrine
text:
I read the drawing as ritodrine, with 1R,2S stereochemistry.

- **Left ring:** a para-substituted phenol, with an OH on one end and an ethylene chain (CH2CH2) on the other.
- **Linker:** that chain ends in an NH, which is bonded to a stereocentre carrying a hashed methyl.
- **Right side:** the next carbon carries a wedged OH and is bonded to a second para-substituted phenol ring.

Stereochemistry:

- **The N-bearing carbon:** the methyl is hashed, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH(OH) > CH3 > H. Read from the front, N → C1 → CH3 runs clockwise, and reversing for the H gives S.
- **The OH-bearing carbon:** the OH is wedged, so the implicit H points away. The priorities are OH > CH(N) > aryl > H. OH → CH(N) → aryl runs clockwise, which gives R.

Writing these as SMILES tags gives `C[C@H](NCCc1ccc(O)cc1)[C@H](O)c1ccc(O)cc1`.

SMILES: C[C@H](NCCc1ccc(O)cc1)[C@H](O)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Ritobegron
text:
I read the molecule as a 4-hydroxyphenyl ring joined to a CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH2CH2 chain. That chain leads to a 2,5-dimethylphenyl ring carrying an OCH2COOH group para to the ethyl chain.

**Skeleton**
- Left ring: a para-substituted phenol, with an OH at one end and the CH(OH) carbon at the other.
- Chain: aryl–CH(OH)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH2–CH2–aryl.
- Right ring: six aromatic carbons.
  - The ethyl chain is on one carbon.
  - A methyl group is on each of the two ring carbons adjacent to the O-bearing carbon.
  - The ring carbon opposite the ethyl chain bears O–CH2–C(=O)OH.

**Stereochemistry**
- The CH(CH3)N carbon has a hashed methyl. The implicit H therefore points toward the viewer.
  - The priority order is N > CH(OH) > CH3 > H.
  - As drawn this runs clockwise, and reversing for the H gives S.
- The CH(OH) carbon has a hashed OH. Its implicit H also points toward the viewer.
  - The priority order is OH > CH(N) > aryl > H.
  - As drawn this runs counterclockwise, and reversing for the H gives R.
- Writing the SMILES in the order methyl, N-bearing carbon, carbinol carbon, the tag `[C@H]` gives S at the first centre and `[C@H]` gives R at the second.

SMILES: C[C@H](NCCc1cc(C)c(OCC(=O)O)cc1C)[C@H](O)c1ccc(O)cc1

name: Risuteganib
text:
I read the drawing as a linear hexapeptide, Gly‑Arg‑Gly‑cysteic acid‑Thr‑Pro. It is drawn from the N‑terminal glycine (bottom left) to the C‑terminal proline acid (bottom centre).

**Residues read from the image**
- **Gly:** H2N‑CH2‑C(=O)‑, with the carbonyl bonded to the Arg NH.
- **Arg:** the α‑carbon carries a wedged CH2CH2CH2 chain ending in N=C(NH2)NH2 (a guanidine). Its C=O bonds to the NH of the second Gly.
- **Gly:** NH‑CH2‑C(=O)‑, with the carbonyl bonded to the NH of the next residue.
- **Cysteic acid:** the α‑carbon carries a wedged CH2‑SO3H (S with two =O and one OH). Its C=O bonds to the Thr NH.
- **Thr:** the α‑carbon is drawn with a wedge to N. The β‑carbon carries OH and a wedged CH3. The Thr C=O is bonded to the proline nitrogen.
- **Pro:** a five‑membered ring (N plus four carbons) with the α‑carbon bearing a hashed bond to COOH.

**Stereochemistry**
I worked out each wedged or hashed centre from the drawn geometry. The Arg, cysteic acid and Thr α‑carbons all match the L‑amino acid pattern, and Thr's β‑carbon matches L‑Thr. The proline α‑carbon matches L‑Pro. The glycines have no stereocentre.

SMILES: NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS(=O)(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Rivaroxaban
text:
This structure is rivaroxaban, read region by region from the drawing:

- **Left ring:** a morpholin-3-one, with the ring N attached to the benzene ring and the C=O next to that N.
- **Centre:** a para-disubstituted benzene linking the morpholinone N to the N of an oxazolidin-2-one.
- **Oxazolidinone:** the ring carbon C5 carries a CH2–NH group on a hashed bond, so this is the one drawn stereocentre.
- **Right side:** the NH is acylated by a thiophene-2-carbonyl group, with Cl on thiophene C5.

**Stereocentre:** the CIP priorities are ring O > ring CH2 (attached to N) > CH2NH > H.

- The hashed bond points the CH2NH group away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Viewed from the front, O (down) → ring CH2 (upper left) → CH2N (upper right) runs clockwise.
- Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving S.

I wrote the SMILES so that `[C@H]` has the neighbour order CH2N, H, ring-closure O, ring CH2, which encodes this S configuration.

SMILES: O=C(NC[C@H]1CN(c2ccc(cc2)N2CCOCC2=O)C(=O)O1)c1ccc(Cl)s1

name: Rivastigmine
text:
Reading the drawing gives rivastigmine:

- **Carbamate end:** an N-ethyl-N-methyl carbamate, CCN(C)C(=O)O–, attached to the aromatic ring through the ester oxygen.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring substituted at two meta positions.
- **Side chain:** a CH(CH3)N(CH3)2 group on the other ring position. Its methyl is drawn on a wedge bond.

**Stereocentre:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > aryl carbon > CH3 > H. The wedged methyl points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Traced from the front, N (upper right), then aryl (upper left), then CH3 (down) runs counterclockwise. With H pointing away, that gives S.

I checked the SMILES chirality tag against this. In `...c(c1)[C@H](C)N(C)C`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is aryl, H, CH3, N. That order corresponds to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(C)C(=O)Oc1cccc(c1)[C@H](C)N(C)C

name: Ritonavir
text:
This structure is ritonavir. I read it region by region and checked the stereocentres against the wedges and hashes.

**Fragments**
- A 2-isopropylthiazol-4-yl group is attached through a CH2 to an N-methyl nitrogen.
- That nitrogen carries a urea C=O, which links through NH to a valine unit (isopropyl side chain).
- The valine C=O forms an amide with an NH on a chain carbon that bears a benzyl group.
- The chain continues through CH2 to a CH(OH), then to a second CH bearing another benzyl group.
- That last carbon carries an NH-C(=O)-O-CH2 carbamate, attached to a thiazol-5-yl ring.

**Stereochemistry**
- The valine α-carbon has the N on a hashed bond. I worked this out as `N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)` in the SMILES atom order.
- The benzyl-bearing carbon next to the amide NH has a wedged benzyl bond. This gives `N[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C` in the SMILES atom order.
- The CH(OH) and the carbamate-bearing carbon have hashed bonds. I took these two from the known ritonavir configuration and rewrote them into my atom order. I did not derive them independently from the image.

SMILES: CC(C)c1nc(CN(C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C[C@H](O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)OCc2cncs2)cs1

name: Rizatriptan
text:
This is rizatriptan: an indole with a 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl chain at C3 and a CH2–(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl) group at C5.

**Side chain.** The dimethylamino group is N with two methyls, attached through two CH2 groups to the indole C3 (the carbon that is part of the five-membered ring and not bonded to NH).

**Indole core.** The five-membered ring runs NH–CH=C3–C3a, with C7a closing back to NH. C3 is bonded to the chain. In the six-membered ring, C3a is bonded to C4, which is bonded to C5, and C5 carries the CH2 substituent. The drawing is consistent with this: the carbon bonded to the CH2 is the one two bonds from C3a, through the bottom vertex.

**Triazole.** The ring is N1(CH2)–N2=C3–N4=C5–N1. In the drawing, N1 (top) is bonded to N (left), which is double-bonded to a CH at the bottom, which is bonded to N (bottom right). That N is double-bonded to the CH at the right, which closes back to N1. This is a 1,2,4-triazole attached through N1.

**SMILES:** CN(C)CCc1c[nH]c2ccc(Cn3cncn3)cc12

Check on the triazole writing: n3cncn3 gives N1–C–N–C–N1, which has the wrong arrangement. The drawing has N1 bonded to N2, then C3, N4, C5, so the ring should be written n3ncnc3. Here N1 is bonded to N, then CH, then N, then CH, which closes to N1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)CCc1c[nH]c2ccc(Cn3ncnc3)cc12

name: Robenacoxib
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying three substituents.
- An ethyl group (CH3-CH2) is attached at the lower left.
- A CH2COOH group is attached at the upper position.
- An NH is attached at the position adjacent (ortho) to the CH2COOH carbon.
- The ethyl carbon and the CH2COOH carbon are separated by one ring CH, so they are meta to each other.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring bonded to the NH through its carbon at about (965, 795).
- Going around from that carbon, the next ring carbon (1117, 716) carries F.
- The next (1260, 807) carries F.
- The next (1253, 977) is a CH.
- The next (1102, 1056) carries F.
- The last (958, 965) carries F and closes back to the NH-bearing carbon.
- This gives a 2,3,5,6-tetrafluorophenyl ring (F on four carbons, one CH).

**SMILES:** Starting from the ethyl group, I wrote CCc1ccc(Nc2c(F)c(F)cc(F)c2F)c(CC(=O)O)c1.

**Check on the left ring:**
- c1 carries the ethyl group.
- The next two atoms, "cc", are CH, CH.
- The following c bears the N.
- The next c bears the CH2COOH.
- The final c1 is a CH that closes the ring.
- The N-bearing carbon is therefore adjacent to the CH2COOH carbon, and the CH2COOH carbon is adjacent to the ring CH that sits next to the ethyl carbon, which matches the drawing.

**Check on the right ring:** c2 (attached to N), c(F), c(F), cH, c(F), c2F gives F on four carbons and one CH, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CCc1ccc(Nc2c(F)c(F)cc(F)c2F)c(CC(=O)O)c1

name: Rocuronium Bromide
text:
The drawing is rocuronium bromide, a steroid-type neuromuscular blocker. I identified it from its features rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges, and I wrote the SMILES from the known structure of that compound.

- **Quaternary nitrogen:** an N-allyl pyrrolidinium on the five-membered D ring.
- **Acetate:** an acetoxy group on the carbon next to the ring-fusion methyl.
- **Steroid core:** a four-ring skeleton with two angular methyl groups.
- **A-ring substituents:** a morpholine on one carbon and a hydroxyl on the adjacent carbon.
- **Counter-ion:** bromide.

I did not independently check each @/@@ label against the wedges and hashes, so the stereochemistry rests on that recognition.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[C@H]1[C@H](C[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(C[C@@H]([C@H](C4)O)N5CCOCC5)C)C)[N+]6(CCCC6)CC=C.[Br-]

name: Rofecoxib
text:
The drawing is rofecoxib (Vioxx), a butenolide ring carrying a phenyl group and a 4-(methylsulfonyl)phenyl group.

**Ring:** The five-membered lactone ring contains an O, a CH2, a C=C and a C(=O). Going round it: O, then CH2, then the ring carbon bearing the methylsulfonylphenyl group, which is double-bonded to the carbon bearing the phenyl group. That carbon is bonded to the carbonyl carbon (C=O), which closes the ring back to O.

**Substituents:** The phenyl group is on the carbon next to the carbonyl. The para-substituted aryl group is on the carbon next to the CH2, and its substituent is S(=O)(=O)CH3.

**SMILES:** O=C1OCC(=C1c1ccccc1)c1ccc(cc1)S(C)(=O)=O

I checked the connectivity against the drawing. The carbonyl carbon C1 is bonded to O and to the phenyl-bearing carbon, and ring closure 1 joins it to that carbon. The ring is therefore C1(=O), O, CH2, C(aryl)=C(Ph), back to C1, which gives five atoms.

SMILES: O=C1OCC(=C1c1ccccc1)c1ccc(cc1)S(C)(=O)=O

name: Roflumilast
text:
This structure is roflumilast, and I read it from the drawing as follows.

- **Left side:** a cyclopropylmethoxy group (cyclopropane–CH2–O) is attached to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** it carries the cyclopropylmethoxy group at one position and an OCHF2 group on the adjacent carbon. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is the third position, so the two oxygen substituents sit at positions 3 and 4 relative to the carbonyl.
- **Amide:** the ring carbon bears C(=O)NH, and the NH is bonded to the pyridine ring.
- **Pyridine ring:** the NH attaches at the 4-position, with chlorines at both adjacent carbons (3 and 5). The ring nitrogen sits opposite the NH-bearing carbon.

Checking the pyridine connectivity in the drawing: the C bearing NH connects to the C(Cl) at the top, which connects to the CH, then to N, then to another CH, then to the lower C(Cl), and back to the C bearing NH. This is a 3,5-dichloropyridin-4-yl group.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1c(Cl)cncc1Cl)c1ccc(OC(F)F)c(OCC2CC2)c1

name: Riviciclib
text:
I read this as a flavone (chromen-4-one) core carrying a 2-chlorophenyl group at C2, hydroxyls at C5 and C7, and an N-methylpyrrolidine at C8.

- **Core and substituents:** The chromen-4-one has a ring oxygen and a C4 carbonyl. The aryl group at C2 is a benzene ring with Cl on the carbon next to the attachment point.
- **Pyrrolidine ring:** It has N-methyl, a CH2OH on the carbon next to N, and a bond from the next ring carbon to C8 of the chromenone.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - The pyrrolidine carbon bonded to the chromenone (C3) has a wedge to the aromatic carbon. By CIP priorities, this centre is R.
  - The carbon bearing CH2OH (C2) has a hashed bond to the CH2OH. This centre is S.
  - I converted both assignments into @ labels in the SMILES atom order below.

SMILES: CN1CC[C@H](c2c(O)cc(O)c3c(=O)cc(-c4ccccc4Cl)oc23)[C@H]1CO

name: Rolapitant Hydrochloride
text:
This is rolapitant hydrochloride monohydrate. The skeleton is a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group on a CH(CH3)–O–CH2 chain. The CH2 is attached to a quaternary carbon that carries a phenyl ring and sits in a piperidine. That piperidine is spiro-fused to a γ-lactam (a pyrrolidin-2-one). HCl and H2O are drawn as separate components.

Stereochemistry was read from the three drawn wedge or hash bonds:
- **CH(CH3)–O carbon:** the methyl is on a wedge, which gives `[C@@H]`.
- **Quaternary carbon bearing phenyl:** the CH2O bond is hashed, which gives `[C@@]`.
- **Spiro carbon:** the ring CH2 bond is wedged, which gives `[C@]`.

SMILES: C[C@@H](OC[C@@]1(c2ccccc2)CC[C@]2(CCC(=O)N2)CN1)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1.Cl.O

name: Romidepsin
text:
I read this as romidepsin (FK228), a bicyclic depsipeptide with a disulfide bridge, and wrote the SMILES from the drawing.

**Ring components, traced around the drawing**
- Cys: the CH with the hashed H, its CH2–S–S link, its C(=O) and its NH.
- Dehydrobutyrine: a C(=CH–CH3) unit bonded to a C(=O) and an NH.
- Val: the upper CH with the bold-wedge H, bearing an isopropyl group.
- Val: the right-hand CH with the hashed isopropyl, bonded to the ester C(=O).
- Acyl unit: –O–CH(–CH=CH–CH2CH2–S)–CH2–C(=O)–NH–, with a trans ring alkene.

**Connectivity and geometry**
- The ring alkene has its two chain substituents on opposite sides, so it is trans (`/C=C/`).
- On the ethylidene double bond, the methyl lies on the same side as the NH, so I wrote it as Z (`C/C=C1\N`).

**Stereocentres (assigned from the wedges and hashes)**
- Cys CH: `[C@H]2`
- Val CH with the bold wedge: `[C@H]` in `N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)`
- Ester CH with the hashed H: `[C@H]`
- Val CH with the hashed isopropyl: `[C@H]` in `OC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)N`

I did not run the SMILES through a validator, but I checked the ring closures and atoms against the drawing.

SMILES: C/C=C1\NC(=O)[C@H]2CSSCC/C=C/[C@H](CC(=O)N[C@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N2)OC(=O)[C@H](C(C)C)NC1=O

name: Ristocetin A
text:
I read the image as a glycopeptide-antibiotic-type aglycone (a ristocetin/teicoplanin-like heptapeptide) carrying four sugar groups. I did not match it to a named compound, and the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES has no stereochemistry.

**Aglycone**
- The backbone is a chain of seven amino-acid units joined by amide bonds, starting from a methyl ester at one end and ending at a free NH2 at the other.
- Aryl rings are cross-linked by diaryl ethers, and one aryl–aryl bond joins the top-right pair of rings.
- The top-left benzene ring carries a benzylic CH bearing the amino-sugar.
- The lower-left benzene ring carries a CH(OH) next to the peptide chain.

**Sugars**
- A 4-amino-5-hydroxy-6-methyl-oxane (vancosamine-like) is attached through a benzylic ether.
- A glucose-type hexose is attached through a phenolic ether on the top-right ring, with a free CH2OH.
- A trisaccharide sits on the central ring: a hexose carrying a pentose through its C2-oxygen via another hexose, and a 6-deoxyhexose on its CH2 through an ether.

**Checks**
- The ring-closure labels are paired one-to-one.
- Each diaryl-ether oxygen is opened once and closed on the carbon at the other end, so no O–O bonds are created.
- The parentheses balance.
- I did not recount the finished string atom by atom against the drawing.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1NC(=O)C(C(OC%13CC(N)C(O)C(C)O%13)c%12ccc(cc%12)O%11)NC(=O)C(c%15cc(-c%16c1cc(O)cc(OC%20OC(CO)C(O)C(O)C%20O)%16)c(O)cc%15)NC(=O)C(c%21cc(O%22)c(OC%40OC(COC%50OC(C)C(O)C(O)C%50O)C(O)C(O)C%40OC%60OC(CO)C(O)C(O)C%60OC%30OCC(O)C(O)C%30O)c%11c%21)NC(=O)C(c%70cc(O)c(C)c(O%71)c%70)NC(=O)C(C(O)c%80ccc%22cc%80)NC(=O)C(N)c%90ccc(O)c%71c%90

name: Ronifibrate
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring with Cl at the top (para) and an O attached at the bottom.
- **Linker from the ring:** the ring O connects to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups, which connects to a C(=O).
- **Propyl chain:** that carbonyl carbon is joined through O to a chain of three CH2 groups (vertices at 690,925, 783,842 and 900,880). The chain then goes through O to a second C(=O).
- **Right ring:** this carbonyl is attached to a pyridine ring. The attachment carbon is at 1200,752. The ring runs from that carbon to 1320,790, then N (1410,710), then 1385,587, then 1268,548, then 1177,630, and back to the attachment carbon. N is therefore separated from the attachment carbon by one CH, so the substituent is at the 3-position (a nicotinate).

SMILES: CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)OCCCOC(=O)c1cccnc1

Checking the propyl chain: the carbons between the two O atoms are 690,925, 783,842 and 900,880, which is three carbons, so OCCCO is correct.

SMILES: CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)OCCCOC(=O)c1cccnc1

name: Ropinirole
text:
The drawing shows ropinirole: an oxindole (indolin-2-one) core carrying a 2-(dipropylamino)ethyl chain on the benzene ring.

**Ring system:**
- The benzene ring is drawn with its atoms at (385,395), (537,468), (548,636), (409,731), (257,658) and (245,489).
- The NH is attached to the ring carbon at (257,658).
- The NH connects to the C=O carbon at (220,928).
- A CH2 at (386,899) joins that carbonyl carbon to the ring carbon at (409,731).
- The five-membered ring is therefore N–C(=O)–CH2–C(ar)–C(ar), which is an oxindole.

**Side chain:**
- The ring carbon at (548,636) bears CH2 (700,710), then CH2 (841,616), then N.
- The nitrogen carries two propyl groups.

**SMILES:** starting at the carbonyl, O=C1Cc2c(CCN(CCC)CCC)cccc2N1. This has the ring-fusion carbon bearing CH2, the adjacent aromatic carbon bearing the side chain, three aromatic CH, and the final ring-fusion carbon bonded to N.

SMILES: O=C1Cc2c(CCN(CCC)CCC)cccc2N1

name: Rokitamycin
text:
I read the molecule as a 16-membered macrolide carrying a disaccharide, with an aldehyde side chain, a methoxy group, two free hydroxyls and a conjugated diene. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing, but I could not check the result with software.

**Macrolactone ring (16 atoms)**
- C1 is the lactone C=O, followed by CH2 (C2).
- C3 carries OH (wedge).
- C4 carries OMe (hash).
- C5 carries the sugar oxygen (wedge).
- C6 carries a CH2CHO side chain (wedge).
- C7 is a CH2.
- C8 carries a methyl (wedge).
- C9 carries OH (wedge).
- C10=C11 and C12=C13 are two double bonds. Both are drawn trans (E).
- C14 is a CH2.
- C15 carries a methyl (wedge) and is bonded to the ring oxygen.

**Amino sugar (mycaminose-type) on C5**
- It is a six-membered pyranose with a ring oxygen.
- Its substituents are a 2'-OH, a 3'-NMe2 and a 5'-methyl.
- Its 4'-oxygen is linked to the second sugar.

**Second sugar (mycarose-type) on the 4'-oxygen**
- It is a 2,6-dideoxy pyranose.
- C3'' carries a methyl and a propanoate ester.
- C4'' carries a butanoate ester.
- C5'' carries a methyl.

name: Romurtide
text:
I read this as an open-chain N-acetylmuramic acid (an aldehyde with a free polyol tail) linked through its lactyl ether to L-Ala, then isoglutamine, then a lysine whose side-chain amine carries a stearoyl group. I counted 18 carbons in the fatty acyl chain, including the carbonyl, from the zigzag spacing, which is an estimate.

Stereocentres were assigned from the wedges and hashes as drawn:
- **Sugar C2 (NHAc):** wedged N.
- **Sugar C3 (ether O):** hashed O.
- **Sugar C4 (OH):** wedged OH.
- **Sugar C5 (OH):** hashed OH.
- **Lactyl carbon:** hashed methyl.
- **Ala α-carbon:** wedged methyl.
- **isoGln α-carbon:** wedged CH2.
- **Lys α-carbon:** hashed CH2.

name: Rosiglitazone
text:
The drawing shows rosiglitazone, read in these pieces:

- **Left end:** a pyridine ring whose ring nitrogen sits next to the carbon bearing an N(CH3) substituent, so it is a 2-pyridyl group.
- **Linker:** that substituent nitrogen carries a methyl and a CH2CH2 chain, which ends in an O attached to a benzene ring.
- **Middle:** the benzene ring is para-substituted, with the ether oxygen on one side and a CH2 on the other.
- **Right end:** the CH2 attaches to C5 of a thiazolidine-2,4-dione ring. C5 connects to S and to a C(=O), which connects to NH, which connects to the second C(=O), which connects back to S.
- **Stereochemistry:** C5 is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: CN(CCOc1ccc(CC2SC(=O)NC2=O)cc1)c1ccccn1

name: Ropivacaine
text:
The drawing is ropivacaine, (S)-N-(2,6-dimethylphenyl)-1-propylpiperidine-2-carboxamide.

- **Left ring:** a piperidine (one N and five carbons) with an N-propyl chain running down from the nitrogen.
- **Stereocentre:** the ring carbon next to N carries the amide carbon C(=O) on a wedge bond.
- **Right side:** the C(=O) is bonded to an NH, which is attached to a benzene ring. That ring has methyl groups on both carbons adjacent to the N-bearing carbon (2,6-dimethylphenyl).

For the stereocentre, the priorities are N > C(=O) > ring CH2 > H. The wedge puts the amide carbon toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. On the page, N (south) → C(=O) (east) → CH2 (northwest) runs counterclockwise, which gives S. Writing the SMILES as `CCCN1CCCC[C@H]1C(=O)N...` and working through the neighbour order gives S for `@`, so `@` is correct here.

SMILES: CCCN1CCCC[C@H]1C(=O)Nc1c(C)cccc1C

name: Roscovitine
text:
This looks like roscovitine, and I read the structure in these parts:

- **Purine core:** a fused imidazole and pyrimidine ring.
- **N9 substituent:** an isopropyl group.
- **C6 substituent:** a benzylamino group (NH–CH2–phenyl).
- **C2 substituent:** an NH attached to a stereocentre that carries an ethyl group, a CH2OH group and one implicit H.

The ethyl bond at the stereocentre is hashed, so ethyl points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N, then CH2OH, then ethyl, then H. Viewed from the front, N (left) → CH2OH (lower right) → ethyl (upper right) runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, I reverse this, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES written as CC[C@H](CO)N..., the `@` tag corresponds to R. I checked this by working out the chirality order from the ethyl carbon, and it matches the known SMILES form of (R)-roscovitine.

SMILES: CC[C@H](CO)Nc1nc(NCc2ccccc2)c2ncn(C(C)C)c2n1

name: Roxarsone
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents:

- An arsonic acid group, As(=O)(O)O, attached at one ring carbon.
- A nitro group, drawn as [N+](=O)[O-], on the ring carbon at the upper left.
- A hydroxyl group (HO) on the ring carbon below the nitro-bearing carbon.

Ring layout, with approximate coordinates:

- C1 (900,826) bears As.
- C2 (719,681) is the top vertex, an unsubstituted CH.
- C3 (502,767) bears the nitro group.
- C4 (468,996) bears OH.
- C5 (650,1141) is an unsubstituted CH.
- C6 (866,1056) is an unsubstituted CH.

So the ring is C1(As), C2(H), C3(NO2), C4(OH), C5(H), C6(H). The nitro and hydroxyl groups are adjacent, and As is meta to the nitro group and para to the hydroxyl group. This is 3-nitro-4-hydroxyphenylarsonic acid (roxarsone).

SMILES: O=[As](O)(O)c1ccc(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Rodorubicin
text:
I read the molecule as an anthracycline-type tetracyclic aglycone carrying three sugar units. The stereocentres were assigned from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Aglycone**
- Ring D is an aromatic ring with one phenolic OH, attached to a quinone ring bearing two C=O groups.
- The central ring is aromatic with two OH groups.
- Ring A is a cyclohexane bearing a quaternary C(OH)(Et) and two O-glycosylated CH centres.

**Sugars**
- Lower sugar: a 2,3,6-trideoxy-3-(dimethylamino) pyranose with a 4-OH and a 5-methyl, attached at the lower ring-A carbon (C10).
- Upper sugar: the same type of aminosugar, but with the 4-oxygen glycosylated instead of free, attached at the upper ring-A carbon (C7).
- Terminal unit: a tricyclic bis-pyran fused through a 1,4-dioxane ring. It carries a ketone and two methyl-bearing carbons and is attached through the upper sugar's 4-oxygen.

I did not run a validity check on the SMILES. I checked the ring-closure digits by hand, using different digits inside the branches so none are reused while still open.

SMILES: O=C1c2c(O)cccc2C(=O)c2c(O)c3c(c(O)c12)[C@@H](O[C@H]4C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H](O[C@H]5C[C@@H]6O[C@H]7CC(=O)[C@H](C)O[C@H]7O[C@@H]6[C@H](C)O5)[C@H](C)O4)C[C@](O)(CC)[C@@H]3O[C@H]1C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)O1

name: Roxatidine
text:
The drawing contains these parts:

- **Benzene ring:** a meta-disubstituted ring. One substituent is O (an ether) and the other is CH2 attached to a piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** N plus 5 carbons, giving 6 ring vertices (N, then 5 CH2 groups).
- **Chain from the ether O:** O–CH2–CH2–CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2–OH.

The ring substitution is meta. Counting around the ring, the carbon bearing O (at 370,462) connects to the carbon at 323,607, which connects to the carbon bearing CH2 at 175,637. That makes the two substituents 1,3 to each other.

SMILES: OCC(=O)NCCCOc1cccc(CN2CCCCC2)c1

name: Rosuvastatin Calcium
text:
The drawing shows two rosuvastatin anions with one Ca²⁺, i.e. rosuvastatin calcium.

Each anion has these parts:
- **Pyrimidine core:** the 2-position carries N(CH₃)SO₂CH₃, the 4-position carries a 4-fluorophenyl group, and the 6-position carries an isopropyl group.
- **Side chain:** the 5-position carries an E-alkene (–CH=CH–) leading to a 3,5-dihydroxyheptenoate chain that ends in a carboxylate (COO⁻).
- **Stereochemistry:** the two hydroxyl-bearing carbons are drawn with wedge bonds, and the alkene is trans.

I assigned the @/@@ marks from my recollection of the standard rosuvastatin (3R,5S,6E) isomeric SMILES, re-ordering the neighbours to fit my atom order. I did not independently re-derive the wedge directions from the image.

SMILES: CC(C)c1nc(N(C)S(C)(=O)=O)nc(-c2ccc(F)cc2)c1/C=C/[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)CC(=O)[O-].CC(C)c1nc(N(C)S(C)(=O)=O)nc(-c2ccc(F)cc2)c1/C=C/[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)CC(=O)[O-].[Ca+2]

name: Rotigotine
text:
This structure is rotigotine, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Left side:** a thiophene ring (S in a five-membered ring) is attached at C2 to a CH2CH2 chain, which leads to the nitrogen.
- **Nitrogen:** a tertiary amine carrying an n-propyl group, the thienylethyl chain, and the ring carbon below.
- **Right side:** a tetrahydronaphthalene (a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring) with an OH on the aromatic carbon next to the ring fusion.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the ring carbon bearing N, which is joined to N by a hashed bond, so N points away from the viewer.
  - The CIP priorities are N, then the CH2 on the aromatic side, then the other CH2, then H.
  - With H toward the viewer, the sequence runs clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise (S) for the true configuration.
  - In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` with neighbour order N, H, ring-closure CH2, chain CH2 gives S.

SMILES: CCCN(CCc1cccs1)[C@H]1CCc2c(C1)cccc2O

name: Roxithromycin
text:
I recognised this as roxithromycin (the 9-oxime O-[(2-methoxyethoxy)methyl] ether of erythromycin) and wrote its SMILES from memory. I then checked it against the drawing only in part: connectivity, the oxime geometry and the substituents. I did not re-derive every wedge and hash centre from the image.

- **Macrolide ring:** a 14-membered lactone with the ethyl group on the carbon bearing the ring oxygen, plus the ring methyls and hydroxyls.
- **Oxime side chain:** the C=N–O–CH2–O–CH2CH2–OCH3 group on the ring carbon at the lower left.
- **Desosamine sugar:** the amino sugar at the top, carrying the dimethylamino group and a hydroxyl.
- **Cladinose sugar:** the sugar at the right, carrying an OMe, a methyl and a hydroxyl.
- **Oxime geometry:** in the drawing the oxime oxygen sits on the same side as the CH(CH3)CH2 carbon and opposite the other ring neighbour. That is the E configuration, which the `/C(=N/O...)/` notation encodes.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H](/C(=N/OCOCCOC)/[C@@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)O1)C)O[C@H]2C[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O2)C)O)(C)OC)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)(C)O)C)C)O)(C)O

name: Rucaparib
text:
This structure is rucaparib, a tricyclic indole–azepinone with a fluorine, a para-substituted phenyl ring and a CH2NHCH3 side chain.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Benzene ring of the indole: it carries F at the left, and its remaining atoms are two CH carbons, the carbon bonded to the carbonyl, a fused carbon (C3a) and the fused carbon bonded to NH (C7a).
- Pyrrole ring: C7a bonds to NH, NH to C2, C2 to C3 (double bond), and C3 to C3a. C2 also carries the phenyl ring.
- Seven-membered lactam ring: C3 connects to CH2, then CH2, then NH, then C(=O), which attaches to the benzene carbon next to C3a.
- Side chain: the phenyl ring is para-substituted with CH2–NH–CH3.

SMILES, written as the aromatic indole core with the lactam fused on:
O=C1NCCc2c([nH]c3cc(F)cc1c23)-c1ccc(CNC)cc1

Atom check:
- Ring closure 1: C1(=O), N, C, C, then c2 (C3), c (C2), [nH], c3 (C7a), c (CH), c(F), c (CH), c1 (the carbon bonded to the carbonyl, closing ring 1), then c23 (C3a, closing rings 2 and 3).
- C3a bonds to C3 (ring 2), to C7a (ring 3), and to the carbonyl-bearing carbon, which is the preceding atom.
- The benzene ring is then c3, c, c(F), c, c1, c23, which is six atoms.
- C3a bonds to the carbonyl-bearing carbon, and this carbon bonds to C(=O). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1NCCc2c([nH]c3cc(F)cc1c23)-c1ccc(CNC)cc1

name: Rubrene
text:
The drawing shows a linear tetracene core made of four fused six-membered rings in a row, with one phenyl group on each of the four carbons flanking the two central rings. This is 5,6,11,12-tetraphenyltetracene (rubrene).

- The outer left and right rings are plain benzo rings.
- The two middle rings each carry one phenyl at the top and one at the bottom. The top phenyls sit at the 645,628 and 855,628 vertices, and the bottom phenyls at the 645,873 and 855,873 vertices.
- All bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry applies.

I checked the SMILES by tracing the rings. The first middle ring closes through the two substituted carbons that bear phenyls para to each other, and the second middle ring closes through the last carbon. Both middle rings therefore carry two phenyls, and the benzo rings sit at the two ends.

SMILES: c1ccc(cc1)-c1c2ccccc2c(-c2ccccc2)c2c(-c3ccccc3)c3ccccc3c(-c3ccccc3)c12

name: Ruboxistaurin
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocyclic bisindolylmaleimide, close to the ruboxistaurin type.

- **Core:** a maleimide ring (C(=O)NC(=O) with a C=C between the two carbons) carries an indol-3-yl group on each alkene carbon.
- **Left indole:** its nitrogen carries the chain N–CH2–CH2–O.
- **Right indole:** its nitrogen carries the chain N–CH2–CH2–CH(…)–.
- **Macrocycle closure:** the CH bearing the oxygen of the first chain is the same CH that ends the second chain, and it also carries a CH2–N(CH3)2 side group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2NMe2 bond is hashed. The substituents rank O > CH2N > CH2C > H. With the hashed CH2N pointing away, H points toward the viewer. On the page, O, CH2N and CH2C run clockwise, so the real configuration is reversed, giving S. In the SMILES, with neighbours written in the order CH2N, H, ring-closure to O, CH2, this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: CN(C)C[C@@H]1CCn2cc(c3ccccc32)C2=C(C(=O)NC2=O)c2cn(CCO1)c1ccccc21

name: Rubitecan
text:
This is 9-nitrocamptothecin (rubitecan): the camptothecin pentacyclic core with a nitro group on the benzo ring.

- **Core:** the E-ring lactone (O–C(=O)–C(OH)(Et)) is fused to the pyridone, which is fused through the N–CH2 to the pyrroloquinoline portion.
- **Nitro group:** it sits on the benzo-ring carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that is bonded to the CH. That puts it peri to the C7–H, which is position 9.
- **Stereocentre:** the quaternary carbon carries a hashed bond to OH, with ethyl, the lactone carbonyl carbon and the ring alkene carbon as its other neighbours. Reading the neighbours in the order Et, ring carbon, OH, C(=O) in my SMILES and working out the geometry from the hashed OH gives `@@`.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1-c3nc4cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c4cc3Cn1c2=O

name: Rufinamide
text:
This is rufinamide: a 1,2,3-triazole carrying a carboxamide, with an N-benzyl group bearing two ortho fluorines.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Benzene ring:** it has fluorines on the two carbons flanking the carbon that bears the CH2 group, so the ring is 2,6-difluorophenyl.
- **Linker:** a single CH2 joins the ring to N1 of the triazole.
- **Triazole:** N1 (attached to the CH2) is bonded to a ring CH and to N2. N2 is double-bonded to N3. N3 is bonded to C4, which carries the amide, and C4 is double-bonded to the CH (C5), which closes back to N1.
- **Amide:** C4 bears C(=O)NH2.

Writing this as SMILES: NC(=O)c1cn(Cc2c(F)cccc2F)nn1

Atom check: the ring c1 (C4) – c (C5) – n (N1, with the benzyl) – n (N2) – n1 (N3) closes back to C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cn(Cc2c(F)cccc2F)nn1

name: Ruthenocene
text:
The image shows two cyclopentadienyl radicals and a ruthenium atom (ruthenocene drawn without bonds to the metal).

Each ring has five carbons. Two double bonds are drawn, and the radical dot sits on the one carbon that has no double bond. Each ring is therefore [CH]1C=CC=C1, written with the radical carbon bonded to its two ring neighbours. Checking the drawing: the left ring has a vertex at the top right and another at the right, joined by a double bond. The bottom vertex and the bottom-left vertex are also joined by a double bond. The upper-left vertex carries the dot.

The ring path is as follows:
- Upper-left carbon (radical), bonded to the top carbon.
- Top carbon, double bonded to the right carbon.
- Right carbon, bonded to the bottom carbon.
- Bottom carbon, double bonded to the lower-left carbon.
- Lower-left carbon, bonded back to the radical carbon.

This gives [CH]1C=CC=C1 for each ring. The three components are disconnected, so the SMILES separates them with dots.

SMILES: [Ru].[CH]1C=CC=C1.[CH]1C=CC=C1

name: Saffan
text:
I read the image as two separate molecules, written as a dot-separated SMILES. They are probably alfadolone acetate (top) and alfaxalone (bottom), the two components of the anaesthetic mixture Saffan. Both are 5α-pregnane steroids with a 3-hydroxy group (hashed bond), an 11-ketone and a C20 ketone side chain on C17.

- **Top molecule:** the side chain is a 21-acetoxy-20-ketone, –C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)CH3, so it is the 21-acetate of the bottom molecule.
- **Bottom molecule:** the side chain is a plain methyl ketone, –C(=O)CH3.

The drawn stereochemistry follows the natural steroid pattern:
- **Wedges:** the two methyls at C10 and C13, the C17 side chain, and the C8 hydrogen.
- **Hashes:** the C3 hydroxyl and the hydrogens at C5, C9 and C14.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks centre by centre. I took them from the stereo-SMILES I recall for these two compounds and checked only that they agree with the natural-steroid pattern above.

SMILES: CC(=O)OCC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC(=O)[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)C.CC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC(=O)[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)C

name: Safinamide
text:
I read this as safinamide, the (S)-enantiomer.

- **Left end:** a primary amide, C(N)=O, attached to a stereocentre. The stereocentre carries a methyl group (hashed bond) and an NH.
- **Middle:** the NH links through a CH2 to a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring carries an O–CH2 group at the position opposite the NH–CH2.
- **Right end:** the O–CH2 leads to a second benzene ring with fluorine in the meta position relative to the CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is hashed, so it points away and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > C(=O)N > CH3 > H. Reading N, then C(=O), then CH3 on the page runs clockwise. With H toward the viewer, the true configuration is the reverse, giving S.
- **SMILES check:** in `C[C@H](N...)C(N)=O` the neighbour order is CH3, H, N, C. This `@` notation works out to S, matching the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](NCc1ccc(OCc2cccc(F)c2)cc1)C(N)=O

name: Salicylanilide
text:
The drawing shows salicylanilide (2-hydroxy-N-phenylbenzamide).

- The right ring is a benzene ring carrying an OH on the carbon next to the carbon that bears the carbonyl.
- The carbonyl carbon is double-bonded to O and single-bonded to NH.
- The NH is attached to a phenyl ring on the left.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1ccccc1O

name: Salbutamol
text:
The drawing shows salbutamol (albuterol).

- **Left side:** a tert-butyl group (a quaternary carbon with three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- **Chain:** the NH connects to a CH2, then to a CH carrying an OH, which is bonded to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** the carbon bearing the OH-bearing chain is para to the ring OH. The CH2OH group sits ortho to the phenol OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is assigned.

Ring atoms, traced from the chain attachment: C1 (chain), C2 (CH), C3 (bearing CH2OH), C4 (bearing OH), C5 (CH), C6 (CH).

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)c1ccc(O)c(CO)c1

name: Runcaciguat
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-cyclopropyl-propanoic acid whose C3 carries a 4-chloro-3-amidophenyl ring. The amide nitrogen is acylated by a 2-(4-chlorophenyl)-4,4,4-trifluoro-3-methylbutanoyl group.

**Skeleton**
- The carboxylic acid is HOOC–CH2–CH, and that CH carries a cyclopropyl ring and the aryl ring.
- The aryl ring has the CH attached at one carbon. Going round the ring from there, the next two carbons are CH, then C–Cl, then C–NH, then a CH that closes the ring.
- The amide is NH–C(=O)–CH(4-chlorophenyl)–CH(CH3)–CF3.

**Stereocentres**
I assigned each from the wedges and hashes, treating the implicit H as pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash.
1. The benzylic CH next to the cyclopropyl ring has a hashed bond to the CH2, giving `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used below.
2. The CH alpha to the amide carbonyl has a wedged bond to the C=O, giving `[C@H]`.
3. The CH bearing CH3 and CF3 has a wedged bond to the CH3, giving `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C(O)C[C@@H](C1CC1)c1ccc(Cl)c(NC(=O)[C@H](c2ccc(Cl)cc2)[C@@H](C)C(F)(F)F)c1

name: Sacubitril
text:
This structure is sacubitril, the ethyl ester of an N-succinyl biphenylalanine-derived amino acid. I read it in four parts:

- **Ester end:** an ethyl ester, CCOC(=O), attached to a carbon bearing a methyl group drawn on a bold wedge.
- **Backbone:** that carbon connects through a CH2 to a second stereocentre, which carries the amide NH and is drawn with a hashed bond to the CH2.
- **Aryl group:** from the second stereocentre, a benzyl CH2 leads to a biphenyl, a para-substituted benzene ring linked to a plain phenyl ring.
- **Acid end:** the NH is acylated by a succinic acid half-amide, NC(=O)CCC(=O)O.

I assigned the stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds using CIP priorities:

- **Methyl-bearing carbon:** priorities are ester carbon, then CH2, then CH3, then H. With the methyl on a wedge the H points away, and the ester → CH2 → CH3 sequence runs clockwise on the page, so this centre is R.
- **N-bearing carbon:** priorities are N, then the benzyl CH2, then the lower CH2, then H. The lower CH2 is hashed, so the H points toward the viewer. The N → benzyl → lower CH2 sequence runs clockwise on the page, which reverses to S.

This gives (2R,4S), matching sacubitril. I then checked that the @/@@ tags in the SMILES below reproduce R at the methyl-bearing carbon and S at the N-bearing carbon.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H](Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1)NC(=O)CCC(=O)O

name: Salicylic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two adjacent substituents. One is a hydroxyl group (OH). The other is a carboxylic acid group, drawn as a carbon double-bonded to O and single-bonded to OH. Two adjacent substituents of this kind make the molecule salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccccc1O

name: Salmeterol
text:
The drawing shows salmeterol. I read it region by region:

- **Left end:** a monosubstituted benzene ring, joined to a chain of 4 CH2 groups that ends at an ether oxygen (O).
- **Middle:** after the ether oxygen, a chain of 6 CH2 groups leads to an NH. From the NH, a CH2 connects to a CH bearing an OH.
- **Right end:** a benzene ring attached at the CH(OH) carbon. It carries an OH on the carbon para to that attachment, and a CH2OH on the carbon next to the OH-bearing one.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: OCc1cc(C(O)CNCCCCCCOCCCCc2ccccc2)ccc1O

name: Salacinol
text:
I read the molecule as a sulfonium salt of the salacinol type: a thiolane ring with a side chain bearing a sulfate.

**Ring (five-membered, S⁺ plus four carbons):**
- The S⁺ is bonded to a ring CH2 and to a ring CH.
- That ring CH carries a hashed CH2OH.
- The next ring carbon carries a wedged OH.
- The next carbon carries a hashed OH.
- The ring closes back through the CH2 to S⁺.

**Side chain on S⁺:**
- S⁺–CH2–CH(OH), with the OH on a wedge.
- That carbon is bonded to a second CH, which carries a hashed CH2OH and an O–SO3⁻ group.
- The sulfate has two S=O bonds and one O⁻.

I assigned @/@@ at each of the five stereocentres from the drawn wedges and hashes, with implicit H counted in the SMILES neighbour order.

SMILES: [O-]S(=O)(=O)O[C@@H](CO)[C@H](O)C[S+]1C[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1CO

name: Saquinavir
text:
This drawing matches saquinavir, so I wrote the SMILES from the known structure of that drug and did not re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

- **Left end:** a quinoline ring attached through its 2-position to an amide carbonyl (C(=O)–NH).
- **Asparagine-type unit:** that NH is on a stereocentre bearing a CH2–C(=O)NH2 side chain, followed by a second amide C(=O)–NH.
- **Hydroxyethylene core:** the NH sits on a carbon bearing a benzyl group (CH2–phenyl). The next carbon bears the OH, and then a CH2 leads to a ring nitrogen.
- **Right end:** a decahydroisoquinoline (fused 6/6 ring system with a ring N). Its carbon next to N carries a C(=O)NH–tert-butyl group.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC(=O)[C@@H]1C[C@@H]2CCCC[C@@H]2CN1C[C@H]([C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)c1ccc2ccccc2n1)O

name: Sarcosine
text:
The drawing shows a methyl group attached to an NH, which is bonded to a CH2. That CH2 is bonded to a carboxylic acid carbon, drawn with a C=O and an OH. This is sarcosine (N-methylglycine), with no stereocentres.

SMILES: CNCC(=O)O

name: Saracatinib
text:
This is saracatinib (AZD0530), and I read the structure region by region.

- **Quinazoline core:** N1 and N3 sit at the bottom, with C2 between them. C4 carries the NH. The benzo ring has the tetrahydropyranyloxy group at C5 and the OCH2CH2-(4-methylpiperazine) chain at C7.
- **Aniline part:** The NH links to a benzodioxole ring (a 1,3-benzodioxole). The carbon bearing NH is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the O, and the chlorine is on the next carbon. This gives a 5-chloro-1,3-benzodioxol-4-yl group.
- **Tetrahydropyran:** It is a six-membered ring (O plus five carbons) attached through its C4 to the ether oxygen.

Writing the SMILES in order:
- Benzodioxole: c1(N...)c(Cl)ccc2OCOc12. The NH-bearing carbon is bonded to the fusion carbon that carries the O at the top of the drawing.
- Full molecule: CN1CCN(CC1)CCOc1cc(OC2CCOCC2)c2c(c1)ncnc2Nc1c(Cl)ccc2OCOc12

Checking the quinazoline: c1 (the C7 bearing O) is followed by cc(OC2CCOCC2), which is C8 and then C6. Here "cc(...)" means c1, then c (C8), then c(O-THP) (C6). In the drawing, the carbon bearing the THP oxygen is the one bonded to the ring-fusion carbon C4a, which is adjacent to C4. So the carbon labelled C6 above is really C5. The ring then runs C7(O-chain), C6 (CH), C5 (O-THP), C4a, C8a, C8 (CH). The SMILES c1cc(OTHP)c2c(c1)ncnc2N has C7, C6H, C5(OTHP), C4a (c2), then c(c1) as C8a with C8 closing the ring, then n, c, n, c2(N) as C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CCN(CC1)CCOc1cc(OC2CCOCC2)c2c(c1)ncnc2Nc1c(Cl)ccc2OCOc12

name: Samuraciclib
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine core with three substituents, one of which is a piperidinol carrying the two drawn stereocentres.

- **Core:** the five-membered ring has two adjacent nitrogens, one of them the ring-fusion nitrogen. It is fused to a pyrimidine ring through that nitrogen and one shared carbon.
- **Isopropyl:** it sits on the pyrazole carbon next to the shared carbon.
- **Benzylamino:** an NH–CH2–phenyl group is on the pyrimidine carbon next to the bridgehead nitrogen.
- **Piperidinylmethylamino:** an NH–CH2 group on the other pyrimidine carbon leads to C4 of a piperidine ring. The ring NH is drawn at the top right, and C3 carries an OH on a wedge.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 on C4 is drawn on a hash, so C4 is R. The OH on C3 is drawn on a wedge, so C3 is R. In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` for C4 and `[C@@H]` for C3 encode these two R centres.

SMILES: CC(C)c1cnn2c(NCc3ccccc3)cc(NC[C@H]3CCNC[C@@H]3O)nc12

name: Saruparib
text:
The drawing breaks into three parts: a bicyclic core, a piperazine linker, and a pyridine carboxamide.

**Bicyclic core (1,5-naphthyridin-2-one).**
- The left ring contains an ethyl-bearing carbon, a C=O carbon, and an NH, and it fuses with the right ring.
- The right ring contains an aromatic N, a CH, a carbon bearing CH2, and another CH.
- Reading the left ring: the ethyl-substituted carbon (C3) is bonded to the C=O carbon (C2), which is bonded to NH (N1). N1 is bonded to the fusion carbon C8a, which is bonded to the other fusion carbon C4a.
- C4a is bonded to the aromatic N and also to the CH (C4) that closes the ring back to C3.
- The right ring runs: C8a, a CH, the carbon bearing CH2, a CH, N, and C4a.
- So the core is a 1,5-naphthyridin-2(1H)-one carrying the ethyl group.

**Linker.** The CH2 on the right ring connects to a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is bonded to the pyridine.

**Pyridine carboxamide.**
- The pyridine ring has the piperazine at C5 and C(=O)NHCH3 at C2, next to the ring nitrogen.
- The ring runs: the carbon attached to the piperazine N, a CH, the ring N, the carbon bearing the amide, a CH, and a CH.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Core: CCC1=Cc2ncc(CN3...)cc2NC1=O
- Check of the core: C1 (ethyl-bearing) =C (C4), then c2 (C4a), n, c (CH), c(CH2...), c (CH), c2 (C8a), N, C1=O.
- Full molecule: CCC1=Cc2ncc(CN3CCN(CC3)c3ccc(C(=O)NC)nc3)cc2NC1=O

The ring-3 atoms in the pyridine fragment c3ccc(...)nc3 read as: c3 (attached to the piperazine N), c, c, c(amide), n, c3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCC1=Cc2ncc(CN3CCN(CC3)c3ccc(C(=O)NC)nc3)cc2NC1=O

name: Sarpogrelate
text:
This structure is sarpogrelate, which I read from the drawing in three parts.

- **Amine end:** a dimethylamino group, N(C)C, is attached to a CH2. That CH2 connects to a CH bearing an O-succinate ester.
- **Ether side:** the same CH is attached to a CH2–O–aryl group. The aryl ring is a benzene with the ether oxygen at one position and a CH2CH2 linker at the adjacent (ortho) position. The linker runs to a second benzene ring that carries OMe at the meta position.
- **Succinate ester:** the CH–O–C(=O)CH2CH2C(=O)OH chain.

I checked the second ring. The ring carbon attached to the linker is at (710, 417). Going around the ring, the next carbon is (840, 485), then the carbon bearing OMe at (965, 407). Those two substituted carbons are separated by one carbon, so the substitution is meta.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I give no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CN(C)CC(COc1ccccc1CCc1cccc(OC)c1)OC(=O)CCC(=O)O

SMILES: CN(C)CC(COc1ccccc1CCc1cccc(OC)c1)OC(=O)CCC(=O)O

name: Satraplatin
text:
The image shows several disconnected components, which I wrote as dot-separated fragments in SMILES:

- Two chloride anions, each [Cl-].
- Ammonia, N (drawn as NH3).
- Two acetate anions, each CC(=O)[O-].
- Cyclohexylamine, NC1CCCCC1.
- A platinum cation, [Pt+4].

The charges balance: Pt is +4, and the two Cl⁻ and two acetate ions give −4, with the neutral ammonia and amine contributing nothing.

SMILES: [Cl-].[Cl-].N.CC(=O)[O-].NC1CCCCC1.CC(=O)[O-].[Pt+4]

name: Sapropterin
text:
I read this as tetrahydrobiopterin (the 6R, L-erythro form). I assigned the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes, taking each carbon in turn.

**Skeleton**
- A pyrimidinone ring: C(=O)–NH–C(NH2)=N–C=C. The C=C is the fusion bond.
- A saturated ring fused to it: the fusion carbons, then NH, a stereocentre CH, CH2, and NH.
- A side chain on that stereocentre: CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH3.

**Stereocentres**
- **Methyl-bearing carbon:** the methyl is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. This gives S, written `C[C@H](O)...`.
- **Middle carbon:** the OH is on a wedge, so it points toward the viewer. This gives R, written `[C@H](O)`.
- **Ring carbon:** the CH2 is on a wedge. This gives R, written `[C@H]1`.

These agree with the (1'R,2'S) side chain and 6R ring centre of natural tetrahydrobiopterin.

SMILES: C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]1CNC2=C(N1)C(=O)NC(N)=N2

name: Sarolaner
text:
I read the structure as a 3,5-dichloro-4-fluorophenyl and CF3-bearing dihydroisoxazole linked to a spiro isobenzofuran–azetidine, which carries an N-acyl methylsulfonylacetyl group.

- **Left end:** a benzene ring with Cl at both meta positions and F at the para position. It is attached to C5 of a 4,5-dihydroisoxazole (O1, N2=C3, CH2 at C4). C5 also carries CF3 on a wedge bond.
- **Centre:** C3 of the isoxazoline bonds to a benzene ring. This ring is fused to a five-membered ring containing a CH2 and an O, and the ring carbon attached to O is a spiro carbon.
- **Spiro junction:** that spiro carbon is also part of an azetidine ring (spiro[isobenzofuran-1,3'-azetidine]). The isoxazoline-bearing aryl carbon is para to the aryl carbon attached to the spiro carbon.
- **Right end:** the azetidine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O)CH2S(=O)(=O)CH3.
- **Stereochemistry:** only the isoxazoline C5 is drawn with a wedge. The CIP priorities are O > CF3 > aryl > CH2. Taking the neighbours in SMILES order (O, CH2, aryl, CF3) with CF3 toward the viewer, the geometry works out to `@@`.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CC(=O)N1CC2(C1)OCc1cc(ccc12)C1=NO[C@@](C1)(c1cc(Cl)c(F)c(Cl)c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Saxagliptin Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing shows saxagliptin hydrochloride. The structure has these parts:

- A 2-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane ring (a cyclopropane fused to a pyrrolidine) with a nitrile on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen.
- An amide linking the ring nitrogen to a carbon that bears an NH2 group.
- A 3-hydroxyadamantan-1-yl group attached to that same carbon.
- HCl drawn as a separate component.

I did not assign the @/@@ marks from the wedges and hashes myself. I wrote them from the known saxagliptin SMILES, (1S,3S,5S)-2-[(2S)-2-amino-2-(3-hydroxyadamantan-1-yl)acetyl]-2-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-3-carbonitrile, on the assumption that the drawing shows the marketed drug.

SMILES: C1[C@@H]2[C@H]1N([C@@H](C2)C#N)C(=O)[C@H](C34CC5CC(C3)CC(C5)(C4)O)N.Cl

name: Savolitinib
text:
I read this as a 1H-[1,2,3]triazolo[4,5-b]pyrazine core, which appears to be savolitinib.

- **Core:** the triazole N1 carries the stereogenic CH(CH3). The pyrazine carbon adjacent to the ring-fusion nitrogen carries the pyrazole.
- **Substituent on the pyrazine:** a 1-methylpyrazol-4-yl group.
