- **Substituent on the stereocentre:** an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridin-6-yl group, attached through the pyridine-ring carbon next to the bridgehead nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is drawn on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. Viewed from the front, the methyl, triazole N and aryl carbon run counterclockwise in that order. That gives `@@` when the SMILES is written as C[C@@H](aryl)N.

I checked the final SMILES atom by atom against the drawing, including the ring fusions and every nitrogen position.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1ccc2nccn2c1)n1nnc2ncc(-c3cnn(C)c3)nc12

name: Seladelpar
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methylphenoxyacetic acid carrying a thioether at the 4-position of the ring.

- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid (HO–C=O) attached to a CH2, which is bonded to an aryl ether oxygen.
- **First ring:** a benzene ring with the ether oxygen at one position and a methyl group on the adjacent carbon. A sulfur is on the carbon para to the oxygen.
- **Linker:** S–CH2–CH(OEt)–CH2–O, where the ethoxy group (O–CH2–CH3) hangs off the middle carbon.
- **Right end:** the linker's terminal oxygen is bonded to a second benzene ring, which carries a CF3 group para to that oxygen.

**Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is on the CH(OEt) carbon, on its bond to the CH2–OAr group.
- CIP priorities at that carbon are OEt > CH2S > CH2OAr > H.
- The wedged bond points toward the viewer, so the implicit hydrogen points away.
- Viewed from the front, OEt (bottom) → CH2S (upper left) → CH2OAr (upper right) runs clockwise, so the centre is R.
- In the SMILES below, written with the neighbour order CH2S, H, OEt, CH2OAr, `[C@H]` encodes R.

SMILES: OC(=O)COc1ccc(SC[C@H](OCC)COc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)cc1C

name: Selatogrel
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then assigned the two stereocentres from the hashed bonds.

- **Left end:** a butyl carbamate (n-butyl–O–C(=O)–) on one nitrogen of a piperazine. The other piperazine nitrogen is acylated by a C(=O).
- **Central carbon:** the acyl carbon is attached to a stereocentre that carries a CH2–P(=O)(OH)2 group on a hashed bond and an NH. That NH is acylated by the carbonyl on the pyrimidine ring.
- **Pyrimidine:** the carboxamide sits at C4 and a phenyl group at C2. A pyrrolidin-1-yl group is at C6, with a methoxy group on its 3-position carbon, drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned both centres from the hashed bonds, with the implicit H pointing toward the viewer in each case. Working through the neighbour order in the SMILES gives `[C@H]` for the phosphonate-bearing carbon and `[C@H]` for the methoxy-bearing pyrrolidine carbon.

SMILES: CCCCOC(=O)N1CCN(CC1)C(=O)[C@H](CP(=O)(O)O)NC(=O)c1cc(N2CC[C@H](OC)C2)nc(-c2ccccc2)n1

name: Selenium disulfide
text:
The drawing shows a central Se atom joined to two S atoms. Each Se–S connection is drawn as a double bond, so the molecule is S=[Se]=S.

SMILES: S=[Se]=S

name: Selenium sulfide (SeS)
text:
The image shows two atom labels, S on the left and Se on the right, joined by a double bond (two parallel lines). Each atom carries no charge and no hydrogens, so the molecule is the sulfur–selenium double-bonded species, S=[Se].

SMILES: S=[Se]

name: Seglitide
text:
I read the structure as a cyclic hexapeptide with the ring sequence Lys, Val, Phe, N‑Me‑Ala, Tyr, Trp. Each residue's carbonyl carbon is bonded to the next residue's nitrogen, and the Trp carbonyl closes the ring onto the Lys NH.

- **Lys:** a 4‑aminobutyl side chain on a wedged carbon.
- **Val:** an isopropyl group on a wedged carbon.
- **Phe:** a benzyl group on a wedged carbon.
- **N‑Me‑Ala:** the amide nitrogen carries a methyl group, and the alanine methyl is wedged.
- **Tyr:** a 4‑hydroxybenzyl group on a wedged carbon.
- **Trp:** an indol‑3‑ylmethyl group on a hashed carbon.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash, taking the implicit hydrogen as pointing the opposite way. The result is @ for Lys, @@ for Val, Phe, Ala and Tyr, and @ for Trp.

SMILES: NCCCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)N(C)[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)C(=O)N1

name: Selegiline
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Alkyne end:** a terminal C≡C attached to a CH2, which is attached to the nitrogen (a propargyl group).
- **Nitrogen:** a tertiary amine carrying that propargyl group, a methyl group, and the stereocentre carbon.
- **Stereocentre:** it bears the N, a wedged methyl, a CH2 leading to the phenyl ring, and an implicit H.
- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with three alternating double bonds, attached through the CH2.

This is selegiline, N-methyl-N-propargyl-1-phenylpropan-2-amine.

For the stereochemistry, the wedged methyl points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The priorities are N > CH2Ph > CH3 > H. Going N (up), then CH2 (right), then CH3 (lower left) is clockwise with H at the back, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES `C#CCN(C)[C@H](C)Cc1ccccc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is N, H, CH3, CH2. The `@` tag means that, viewed from N, the sequence H → CH3 → CH2 runs counterclockwise. Working this through gives R, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C#CCN(C)[C@H](C)Cc1ccccc1

name: Selexipag
text:
This is the selexipag structure. I read it region by region:

- **Sulfonamide end:** a methyl group on S(=O)(=O), then NH, then C(=O).
- **Linker:** the carbonyl carbon is attached to CH2, then O, then four CH2 groups (the chain between O and N is drawn as 4 carbons), then N.
- **Amine:** this N carries an isopropyl group and the pyrazine ring.
- **Pyrazine ring:** the ring atoms are C(N-substituted), CH, N, C(Ph), C(Ph), N. Starting at the amine-bearing carbon, the ring runs C2 (bearing N), then C3H, then N4, then C5 (Ph), then C6 (Ph), then N1 back to C2. The drawing agrees: the carbon attached to the amine N is bonded to CH and to a ring N, and the CH is bonded to a ring N, which in turn is bonded to the C bearing a phenyl.

Chain count from the drawing: C(=O)–CH2 (406,802), O (490,760), then CH2 (573,810), CH2 (657,767), CH2 (741,818), CH2 (826,775), then N. That gives 4 CH2 groups between O and N.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)NC(=O)COCCCCN(C(C)C)c1cnc(-c2ccccc2)c(-c2ccccc2)n1

name: Selenocystine
text:
This is selenocystine, two selenocysteine units joined through a Se–Se bond.

- **Chain:** each half is HOOC–CH(NH2)–CH2–Se, and the two CH2–Se units are linked Se–Se. That gives two carboxylic acids, two primary amines, two CH2 groups and two selenium atoms.
- **Stereochemistry:** both α-carbons carry a hashed NH2, so both are stereocentres. For the left one, the priorities are N > CH2Se > COOH > H. Viewed with H toward the viewer, N (down), then CH2 (upper right), then COOH (upper left), runs counterclockwise on screen, so the true sense is clockwise. That makes the centre R, the L-configuration for selenocysteine. The right-hand centre is the same by symmetry.
- **SMILES:** the first centre is written as N[C@@H](C[Se]...)C(=O)O. In the second centre the neighbour order is CH2, H, N, COOH, which swaps N and CH2. The same configuration is therefore written [C@H].

SMILES: N[C@@H](C[Se][Se]C[C@H](N)C(=O)O)C(=O)O

name: Satoreotide
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic heptapeptide held by a disulfide bridge. Each stereocentre was assigned from its wedge or hash, and the SMILES has not been checked by software.

**Residues, N- to C-terminus:**
1. The N-terminal residue is 4-chlorophenylalanine, with a free NH2 and a 4-ClC6H4–CH2 side chain.
2. The first cysteine carries its CH2–S, which closes the disulfide, and its C=O closes the macrocycle onto residue 3.
3. A 4-aminophenylalanine has its aryl nitrogen acylated by an L-hydroorotyl ring (the 2,6-dioxo-hexahydropyrimidine-4-carbonyl group).
4. A second 4-aminophenylalanine has a urea (NH–C(=O)–NH2) on the aryl nitrogen.
5. A lysine has a free terminal NH2 on a four-carbon chain.
6. A threonine has an OH on the side-chain carbon, which is also a stereocentre.
7. The second cysteine is bonded through S–S to the first, and its carbonyl continues to the C-terminal tyrosine amide, Tyr–C(=O)NH2.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]2CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N[C@H](Cc3ccc(O)cc3)C(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc4ccc(NC(N)=O)cc4)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc5ccc(NC(=O)[C@@H]6CC(=O)NC(=O)N6)cc5)NC2=O

name: Sematilide
text:
The drawing shows a diethylamino group (two ethyl groups on N) joined by a two-carbon chain to an amide NH. The amide C=O is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring. The other ring substituent is an NH-SO2-CH3 (methanesulfonamide) group.

Reading it from left to right gives CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: Selinexor
text:
I read the structure as a (Z)-configured prop-2-enehydrazide, matching the known drug selinexor.

- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring carrying two CF3 groups at the 3 and 5 positions (meta to each other).
- **Triazole:** a 1,2,4-triazole attached to the benzene at C3, with N1 bonded to the vinyl chain.
- **Chain:** N1–CH=CH–C(=O)–NH–NH–, a prop-2-enehydrazide. In the drawing, the triazole N and the carbonyl carbon both sit below the C=C bond, so they are cis and the alkene is Z.
- **Terminal ring:** the second NH is bonded to C2 of a pyrazine ring (ring order C2, C3, N4, C5, C6, N1).

I checked the ring closures against the drawing, and the `/C=C\` pattern in the SMILES gives the cis arrangement.

SMILES: O=C(/C=C\n1cnc(n1)-c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1)NNc1cnccn1

name: Seletalisib
text:
I read the molecule as three linked parts and wrote the SMILES from them.

- **Left fragment:** a pyrido[3,2-d]pyrimidine whose C4 carries an NH. The pyrimidine ring has two nitrogens, and the fused pyridine ring has one nitrogen next to the ring-fusion carbon.
- **Centre:** the NH is attached to a stereocentre bearing CF3 and a quinoline C3. The NH bond is drawn as a hashed wedge, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **Quinoline:** it has Cl at C8 and, at C2, a pyridin-3-yl group present as the N-oxide (`[n+]([O-])`).

For the stereocentre, viewed from the H (the viewer's side), N → quinoline C3 → CF3 runs clockwise. Writing the neighbours in the order CF3, H, N, C3 then gives `@`, so the centre is `[C@H]`.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)[C@H](Nc1ncnc2cccnc12)c1cc2cccc(Cl)c2nc1-c1ccc[n+]([O-])c1

name: Selpercatinib
text:
This structure matches selpercatinib (LOXO-292), so I read it region by region and wrote the SMILES from that.

**Left side:** a 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropoxy group, CC(C)(O)CO–, attached to the pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyridine core.

**Core:** the pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyridine carries a nitrile on the pyrazole carbon C3, the aryl group on C4, and the alkoxy group on C6. Atoms in the drawing:
- The bridgehead N is bonded to the CH next to it (C7) and to the pyrazole N.
- C7 is double-bonded to C6, which bears the O-alkyl group.
- C5 is the CH between C6 and C4.
- C4 bears the pyridyl ring and is bonded to C3a, which is bonded to C3 (C#N).
- The pyrazole ring closes through C2 (CH) and N.

Core SMILES: N#Cc1cnn2cc(OCC(C)(C)O)cc(c12)-Ar

**Middle ring:** a pyridine bearing the core at one position and the diazabicycle at the 2-position, i.e. c1ccc(nc1)N.

**Diazabicycle:** 3,6-diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptane.
- N3 is bonded to the pyridine, to CH2 (a), and to CH2 (b).
- CH2 (a) leads to bridgehead C1.
- CH2 (b) leads to bridgehead C5.
- C1 and C5 are joined by a one-carbon bridge (CH2) and by N6.
- N6 carries the CH2 linker.

The ring SMILES is N1(CC2CC(C1)N2Cc...)... Checking against the drawing: N3 connects to CH2 (a, upper left) to C1 (upper), and to CH2 (b, lower) to C5. C1 connects to N6 and to the CH2 bridge. C5 connects to N6 and to the same CH2 bridge. So the bicycle is N3(CC1CC(C2)N1R)... which I write as N1(CC2CC(C1)N2R) with ring labels adjusted.

**Right side:** the N6 substituent is CH2–(6-methoxypyridin-3-yl), i.e. Cc1ccc(OC)nc1.

**Full SMILES:**
N#Cc1cnn2cc(OCC(C)(C)O)cc(-c3ccc(nc3)N3CC4CC(C3)N4Cc3ccc(OC)nc3)c12

Check of the diazabicycle: N3 is followed by C, then C4 (bridgehead), then C (bridge CH2), then C(C3) (the other bridgehead, with its CH2 closing back to N3), then N4, which closes to the first bridgehead. This gives bridgeheads joined by CH2, by N, and by the N3–CH2 paths on each side, which is correct.

SMILES: N#Cc1cnn2cc(OCC(C)(C)O)cc(-c3ccc(nc3)N3CC4CC(C3)N4Cc3ccc(OC)nc3)c12

name: Semaxanib
text:
The drawing shows a 3,5-dimethylpyrrole joined through a =CH– linker to the 3-position of an oxindole (indolin-2-one). This is the semaxanib (SU5416) skeleton.

- **Pyrrole ring:** an NH-pyrrole with a methyl on the carbon next to NH and another methyl on the next ring carbon. The ring carbon bearing the linker is the other carbon adjacent to NH.
- **Linker:** the pyrrole C2 is bonded to a CH, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole.
- **Oxindole:** C3 is attached to the C=O carbon and to the fused benzene ring. The lactam N–H is attached to the benzene ring carbon.
- **Double-bond geometry:** the pyrrole carbon and the C=O carbon lie on the same side of the C=C bond in the drawing. On the CH, the pyrrole outranks H. On C3, the C=O carbon (O,O,N) outranks the aromatic carbon (C,C,C). The higher-priority groups are on the same side, so the bond is Z.

In SMILES, a `/` followed by a `\` across the double bond puts the pyrrole and the C=O carbon cis, which gives Z.

SMILES: Cc1cc(C)c(/C=C2\C(=O)Nc3ccccc32)[nH]1

name: Sempervirine
text:
I read the structure as a fused ring system and wrote a Kekulé SMILES for it.

**Rings**
- A saturated cyclohexane ring with four CH₂ groups, fused at its two non-CH₂ carbons to a six-membered ring containing N.
- That N-containing ring has a ring-fusion N (the upper N, no H) and is fused to a second six-membered ring.
- Next comes a five-membered ring containing the lower N, which is drawn as an imine-type N (C=N).
- A benzene ring at the right end is fused to that five-membered ring.

**Double bonds**
- In the central rings: C=C in the cyclohexane-fused ring (two), C=C between the ring-fusion carbons next to the upper N, and C=C in the upper vinyl CH=CH.
- In the five-membered ring: the lower N is double-bonded to the benzene-fused carbon, and the adjacent fusion carbon is double-bonded into the benzene ring.
- Benzene: two further C=C bonds.

I checked the SMILES atom by atom against the drawing. It has the four CH₂ groups, 2 N atoms and 4 fused rings, and no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: C1CCCC2=CC3=C4N=C5C=CC=CC5=C4C=CN3C=C21

name: Serotonin
text:
This is serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine): an indole ring with an aminoethyl chain at C3 and a hydroxyl on the benzene ring.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Side chain:** H2N is bonded to a CH2, then a second CH2, which attaches to the indole carbon at about (693, 754). This is C3 of the indole.
- **Pyrrole ring:** C3 is double-bonded to the carbon at (660, 963), which is C2. C2 bonds to NH at the bottom. NH bonds to C7a at (998, 908). C7a is also bonded to C3a at (902, 720), which closes the five-membered ring back to C3.
- **Benzene ring:** C3a is bonded to the carbon at (1016, 543), which is C4. C4 is double-bonded to C5 at (1227, 553), and C5 carries the OH. C5 bonds to C6 at (1324, 741), C6 is double-bonded to C7 at (1210, 919), and C7 bonds to C7a. The C3a=C7a bond is the remaining double bond in the aromatic ring.

SMILES: NCCc1c[nH]c2ccc(O)cc12

name: Sertindole
text:
This structure is sertindole, which I identified from the drawing and then checked region by region.

- **Imidazolidin-2-one:** a five-membered ring made of C(=O), NH, CH2, CH2 and N. The ring nitrogen N is attached to a two-carbon chain.
- **Linker and piperidine:** the chain is N–CH2–CH2–N(piperidine). The piperidine carbon opposite its nitrogen (C4) bonds to the indole C3.
- **Indole:** the indole nitrogen N1 carries the 4-fluorophenyl group. Chlorine sits on the benzo ring at C5. This position is meta to the C3a ring-fusion carbon, on the carbon bonded to the CH between C3a and C5, which is C4.

SMILES: O=C1NCCN1CCN1CCC(CC1)c1cn(-c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc12

I wrote this by tracing the ring connectivity in the drawing. The indole portion is c1cn(Ar)c2ccc(Cl)cc12: C3, C2, N1, C7a, C7, C6, C5(Cl), C4, C3a. That matches the image, where Cl is on the carbon bonded to the CH that leads to C3a.

There are no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: O=C1NCCN1CCN1CCC(CC1)c1cn(-c2ccc(F)cc2)c2ccc(Cl)cc12

name: Serlopitant
text:
I read the structure as an N-substituted 3-aminocyclopent-2-enone attached to a fused bicyclic amine (an octahydroisoindole). The cyclohexane ring of that bicycle carries a 4-fluorophenyl group and an ether side chain.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Cyclopentenone:** C(=O)–CH2–CH2–C(=CH), with the ring carbon at the C=C attached to the nitrogen.
- **Bicyclic core:** the nitrogen sits in a five-membered ring fused to a cyclohexane. The ring-fusion carbons are both drawn with H labels, one hashed and one wedged.
- **Aryl group:** a 4-fluorophenyl on the cyclohexane carbon next to the ring fusion, attached by a hashed bond.
- **Ether side chain:** the next cyclohexane carbon bears an O on a wedge. That O is bonded to a CH(CH3) with a hashed methyl, and the CH carries a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.

**Stereocentres:** I assigned the @/@@ marks by working out the geometry at each of the five centres from the wedge and hash bonds. These are the two ring-fusion carbons, the aryl-bearing carbon, the O-bearing carbon, and the side-chain CH(CH3). I did this by hand, so the stereo marks are the part most open to error.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(=C1)N1C[C@H]2[C@H](c3ccc(F)cc3)[C@@H](O[C@H](C)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c3)CC[C@@H]2C1

name: Senna
text:
This is the bis-anthrone C-glycoside skeleton of sennoside B. It has two 10-glucosyloxy-1-hydroxy-9-oxo-anthracene units, each carrying a carboxylic acid, joined through their C10 carbons. I read it as follows:

- **Anthrone units:** Each has a carbonyl at C9, a phenolic OH, and a COOH on the same ring as that OH. The other ring carries an O-glucosyl group.
- **Sugars:** Each is a β-D-glucopyranosyl unit with a CH2OH group. I took the sugar stereo from the SMILES I recalled for the sennosides rather than re-deriving every centre from the wedges.
- **Central carbons:** I assigned both from the wedges. At the upper C10, the wedge runs to the COOH-bearing ring, which gives `@@` in my atom ordering. At the lower C10′, the wedge runs to the sugar-bearing ring, which also gives `@@`. The two central centres are therefore not related by a 180° rotation of the drawing. That points to the meso-type (R,S) isomer, sennoside B, rather than sennoside A.

I did not verify the CIP labels or the glucose centres independently, so the sugar stereo and the sennoside B identification rest partly on recall.

SMILES: C1=CC2=C(C(=C1)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)O)O)C(=O)C4=C([C@@H]2[C@@H]5C6=C(C(=CC=C6)O[C@H]7[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O7)CO)O)O)O)C(=O)C8=C5C=C(C=C8O)C(=O)O)C=C(C=C4O)C(=O)O

name: Setipiprant
text:
The drawing shows a tetrahydro-γ-carboline core (a pyrido[4,3-b]indole) with three substituents.

**Core.** An indole nitrogen (N, right side) carries a CH2COOH group. The benzene ring carries F. The six-membered ring contains a second N, which is acylated and bonded to two CH2 groups.

**Ring connectivity.**
- The indole N is bonded to C2 (the carbon at about 1020,913), which is also bonded to the CH2 at about 958,1044.
- That CH2 connects to the CH2 at about 813,1052, which connects to N (730,935).
- N connects to the CH2 at about 795,803, which connects to C3 (941,794).
- C3 is double-bonded to C2 and bonded to the benzo carbon at about 1030,680.
- The other benzo carbon (1165,730) is bonded to the indole N.

**Benzene ring.** The atoms run 1030,680 → 1007,538 → 1118,445 (bearing F) → 1252,494 → 1277,637 → 1165,730. The F carbon is therefore meta to the C3-attached carbon, which gives a 6-fluoro pattern on the tetrahydro-γ-carboline.

**Acyl group.** N–C(=O)– is attached to the naphthalene at its 1-position, since the attachment carbon is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon (363,831).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Indole N: n1(CC(=O)O)
- Writing the core as non-aromatic notation: OC(=O)CN1C2=C(CN(CC2)C(=O)c2cccc3ccccc23)c2cc(F)ccc12
- C2 is the carbon attached to the CH2CH2 side, and C3 is the carbon attached to the CH2 that leads to N. In the SMILES, C2 (written "C2=") closes ring 2 with the CC2 end, and "C(CN(CC2)...)" is C3 with its CH2–N. This matches the drawing.
- Naphthalene: c2cccc3ccccc23 gives a 1-naphthyl group. The attachment atom c2 is followed by cccc, then c3 (the fusion carbon), then ccccc23 closing the ring back to the attachment carbon, so the attachment carbon is adjacent to the fusion carbon. This is correct.
- Benzo ring: c2cc(F)ccc12. The first c2 is attached to C3, then c (CH), then c(F), then cc, then c12 bonded to N. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN1C2=C(CN(CC2)C(=O)c2cccc3ccccc23)c2cc(F)ccc12

name: Sertraline
text:
The structure is a tetralin (a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring) carrying three substituents:

- **Amine carbon:** a secondary N-methylamine (NHCH3) on one benzylic carbon, drawn with a hashed bond to N.
- **Aryl carbon:** a 3,4-dichlorophenyl group on the other benzylic carbon, also on a hashed bond. Counting around that ring from the attachment point, the two Cl atoms sit at the meta and para positions.
- **Linking carbons:** two CH2 groups join the two benzylic carbons.

This is the sertraline skeleton.

For stereochemistry, I worked out each centre from the hashed bond and the implicit H, which points toward the viewer.

- **Amine carbon:** N is hashed. Viewed from the H side, N, CH2 and the aromatic carbon run counterclockwise. Written in the SMILES neighbour order N, H, ring-closure aromatic C, CH2, this gives `[C@H]`.
- **Aryl-bearing carbon:** the aryl group is hashed. Viewed from the H side, CH2, aryl and the fused aromatic carbon run counterclockwise. Written in the SMILES neighbour order CH2, H, aryl, fused C, this gives `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: CN[C@H]1CC[C@@H](c2ccc(Cl)c(Cl)c2)c2ccccc21

name: Sertraline Hydrochloride
text:
The drawing is sertraline hydrochloride.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying two adjacent chlorines (3,4-dichlorophenyl). It is attached to the saturated ring through a hashed bond.
- **Middle and right rings:** a tetralin core, which is a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring.
- **Amine:** the other saturated ring carbon bears an NH–CH3 group, attached through a hashed bond.
- **Salt:** a separate HCl is drawn above the molecule.

I worked out each stereocentre from the hashed bonds, with the implicit hydrogen pointing toward the viewer. That gives `[C@H]` for the carbon bearing nitrogen and `[C@@H]` for the carbon bearing the aryl group. This matches the known (1S,4S) configuration of sertraline.

SMILES: CN[C@H]1CC[C@@H](c2ccc(Cl)c(Cl)c2)c2ccccc21.Cl

name: Sevoflurane
text:
The drawing shows a fluoromethyl ether: F–CH2–O–CH(CF3)2.

- On the left, F is bonded to a CH2 carbon.
- That CH2 is bonded to O.
- O is bonded to a central CH carbon.
- The central CH carbon carries two CF3 groups, one at the upper right and one below.

This is sevoflurane. All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry. The central carbon is not a stereocentre because its two CF3 groups are identical.

SMILES: FCOC(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: Setiptiline
text:
I read the drawing as a tetracyclic skeleton and traced the atoms around it.

**Atoms and rings**
- Right benzene ring: C1042,137; C1290,126; C1425,337; C1310,558; C1061,569; C927,359.
- Left benzene ring: C504,511; C274,413; C75,564; C105,811; C335,909; C533,760.
- Central seven-membered ring: CH2 at 679,333; C927,359 (right ring); C1061,569 (right ring); C981,805 (alkene); C746,890 (alkene); C533,760 (left ring); C504,511 (left ring). This is 7 atoms.
- Piperidine-like ring: C981,805; C1171,967; N; C892,1297; C701,1135; C746,890. This is 6 atoms, and the C=C between 746,890 and 981,805 is shared with the seven-membered ring.
- N-methyl group on the nitrogen.

**SMILES construction**
- Start at the N-methyl group and the nitrogen: CN1CCC2=C(C1)...
- C2 is C746,890, which bonds to C533,760 of the left ring. The other alkene carbon, C981,805, bonds to C1061,569 of the right ring.
- Left ring from C533: c3ccccc3 with the CH2 attached at C504.
- Written out: CN1CCC2=C(C1)c1ccccc1Cc1ccccc12
  - C2 is the alkene carbon at 746,890, and C(C1) is the carbon at 981,805 bearing the CH2 that closes onto N.
  - Then c1ccccc1 is the right ring, starting at C1061 and ending at C927, which bears the CH2. Ring closure 1 is reused, which is fine because the earlier ring 1 closed at C1.
  - After that CH2 comes the left ring, c1ccccc1 with its last atom closing to C2.
- In this string the right ring's first aromatic atom (C1061) is bonded to C981 and its ortho atom (C927) to the CH2, which matches the drawing.
- The left ring begins at C504 (attached to the CH2) and ends at C533, which closes to C2 (746,890). This also matches.

SMILES: CN1CCC2=C(C1)c1ccccc1Cc1ccccc12

name: Selamectin
text:
I read the drawing as a selamectin-type avermectin and built the SMILES region by region. I assigned the stereocentres and double-bond geometries from the wedges, hashes and bond angles, and I did not check the result against a database record.

- **Spiroketal end:** a cyclohexyl-bearing tetrahydropyran carries a methyl group and is spiro-fused to a second tetrahydropyran.
- **Macrolide ring:** the second tetrahydropyran carries the ester oxygen. From there the ring runs through a trisubstituted alkene, the sugar-bearing carbon, a methyl-bearing carbon, a diene, and then into the fused ring system.
- **Fused rings:** a tetrahydrofuran is fused to a cyclohexene. The tertiary OH carbon, the lactone carbonyl and the ring C=N–OH oxime sit on this system.
- **Sugar:** a 2,6-dideoxy pyranose joined through an oxygen, bearing OMe, OH and a methyl.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CC[C@]2(C[C@@H]3C[C@H](O2)C/C=C(C)/[C@@H](O[C@H]6C[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O6)[C@@H](C)/C=C/C=C4\CO[C@H]5[C@]4(O)[C@H](C(=O)O3)C=C(C)/C5=N/O)O[C@@H]1C1CCCCC1

name: Sibutramine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Amine:** the nitrogen carries two methyl groups (the two lines to the upper left and lower left) and is bonded to a CH carbon.
- **Central CH:** this carbon connects to the nitrogen, to a quaternary carbon, and to a CH2.
- **Isobutyl chain:** the CH2 leads to a CH that carries two methyl groups, so the chain is CH2–CH(CH3)2.
- **Cyclobutane:** the quaternary carbon is a vertex of a four-membered ring. The ring atoms are the quaternary carbon, the carbon at (318, 418), the carbon at (404, 204), and the carbon at (618, 291).
- **Aryl group:** the quaternary carbon is also bonded to a benzene ring. The ring has a chlorine on the carbon para to this attachment point.

Putting these together gives CN(C)C(CC(C)C)C1(CCC1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1. There are no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CN(C)C(CC(C)C)C1(CCC1)c1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Silica
text:
The image shows a central Si atom with a double bond to an O on each side, so the molecule is O=Si=O (silicon dioxide drawn as a linear molecule). I read the bond orders and atom labels directly from the drawing. There are no charges and no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=[Si]=O

name: Sildenafil
text:
This drawing is sildenafil, and I read it region by region as follows.

- **Pyrazole ring:** N1 carries a methyl group and is bonded to N2. N2 is double-bonded to C3, which carries the propyl chain. C3 connects to the fused carbon C3a, which is double-bonded to C7a, and C7a bonds back to N1.
- **Pyrimidinone ring:** C7a is bonded to the carbonyl carbon C(=O), which is bonded to NH. NH is bonded to C(aryl)=N, and that N bonds to C3a.
- **Aryl group:** The ring carbon attached to the pyrimidinone has an ortho OEt group. The sulfonyl group sits para to the OEt, which is meta to the attachment carbon.
- **Sulfonamide:** The sulfonyl group is bonded to a piperazine N, and the other piperazine N carries a methyl.

SMILES: CCCc1nn(C)c2c1nc([nH]c2=O)-c1cc(ccc1OCC)S(=O)(=O)N1CCN(C)CC1

name: Silperisone
text:
The drawing shows three parts joined through a silicon atom.

- **Piperidine ring:** a six-membered ring containing one N and five carbons.
- **Linker and silicon:** the ring N is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to Si. Si carries two methyl groups (the two plain lines going down and up-right), and it is also bonded to a benzylic CH2.
- **Aromatic ring:** the benzylic CH2 is attached to a benzene ring, and the carbon para to that attachment bears F.

Written as SMILES: C[Si](C)(CN1CCCCC1)Cc1ccc(F)cc1

SMILES: C[Si](C)(CN1CCCCC1)Cc1ccc(F)cc1

name: Silver(I) trifluoromethanesulfonate
text:
The image shows silver(I) triflate (silver trifluoromethanesulfonate), drawn as two separate ions.

- **Cation:** Ag⁺ is drawn on its own.
- **Anion:** a sulfur atom carries two double-bonded oxygens (one above, one below) and one singly bonded O⁻ on the left. On the right, S is bonded to a carbon that carries three fluorines.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is shown, so none is included.

The two ions are written as separate components joined by a dot.

SMILES: [Ag+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: Shr0302
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-methoxy-1,2,4-thiadiazol-5-yl urea. The urea nitrogen is the ring nitrogen of a cis-fused bicyclic octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole. On the cyclopentane carbon of that bicycle sits an N-methyl-N-(7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4-yl)amino group.

- **Left ring:** a 1,2,4-thiadiazole carrying OMe on one carbon and the NH–C(=O) link on the other.
- **Bicycle:** the urea nitrogen is part of a pyrrolidine ring that shares its two fusion carbons with a cyclopentane ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** both ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn as wedges, so the fusion is cis. Working out the neighbour order for each fusion carbon gives `@@` for both. The carbon bearing the N-methylamino group has only plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Right ring system:** the pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine is attached through its C4 to the N-methyl nitrogen.

SMILES: COc1nsc(NC(=O)N2C[C@@H]3CC(N(C)c4ncnc5[nH]ccc45)C[C@@H]3C2)n1

name: Silver Sulfadiazine
text:
The drawing is silver sulfadiazine: a silver cation, and a sulfadiazine anion with the deprotonated sulfonamide nitrogen.

- **Silver:** Ag with a + charge, drawn as a separate species.
- **Sulfonamide:** S with two double-bonded O atoms. S is bonded to N⁻ and to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** para-substituted, with NH2 opposite the sulfur.
- **Pyrimidine ring:** N⁻ is attached to the C2 carbon, which sits between the two ring nitrogens. The ring reads N=C(N⁻)–N=C–C=C–, closing back on the first N.

Reading the pyrimidine from the drawing: the top-left N is double bonded to C2, C2 is single bonded to the lower N, and that N is double bonded to the bottom carbon. The bottom carbon is single bonded to the left carbon, which is double bonded to the carbon next to the top-left N. The ring closes through a single bond to the top-left N.

SMILES: [Ag+].Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)[N-]c1ncccn1

SMILES: [Ag+].Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)[N-]c1ncccn1

name: Silodosin
text:
This structure is silodosin, an indoline-7-carboxamide drawn with a single wedge at the side-chain stereocentre.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- Indoline core: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing N, with CH2CH2 closing the ring. The ring nitrogen carries a 3-hydroxypropyl chain (CCCO).
- The benzene carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears N carries a primary amide, C(=O)NH2.
- The benzene carbon on the other side of that amide-bearing carbon carries a CH2–CH(CH3)–NH side chain.
- The NH continues as CH2CH2–O–aryl. The aryl ring is a benzene with an ortho OCH2CF3 group.

**Stereocentre**
The only stereocentre is the CH bearing the methyl, drawn with a wedge to the methyl, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CH2(aryl) > CH3 > H. Reading N (down) → CH2 (left) → CH3 (upper right) goes clockwise with H at the back, so the centre is R. This matches the known configuration of silodosin.

For the SMILES, `C[C@H](CAr)N` with neighbours in the order CH3, H, CH2, N gives R, consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](Cc1cc(C(N)=O)c2c(c1)CCN2CCCO)NCCOc1ccccc1OCC(F)(F)F

name: Simfibrate
text:
The drawing shows a symmetric diester: propane-1,3-diyl bis[2-(4-chlorophenoxy)-2-methylpropanoate].

Each end of the molecule has a 4-chlorophenyl ring joined through an ether oxygen to a quaternary carbon carrying two methyl groups. That carbon is bonded to a C(=O) that forms an ester with O. The two ester oxygens are joined by a three-carbon chain (CH2–CH2–CH2). I counted three carbons in the chain: the two lower vertices and the apex between them.

The quaternary carbons carry two identical methyls, so there are no stereocentres and no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: CC(C)(Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)OCCCOC(=O)C(C)(C)Oc1ccc(Cl)cc1

name: Sincalide
text:
I read this as the sulfated CCK-8 octapeptide, H-Asp-Tyr(SO3H)-Met-Gly-Trp-Met-Asp-Phe-NH2. The chain runs from the free amine of the N-terminal Asp, through the sulfated Tyr, Met, Gly, Trp, Met and Asp, to a C-terminal Phe amide.

I checked the stereo at the N-terminal Asp alpha carbon, where the NH2 is hashed. Using CIP priorities (N > C(=O)N > CH2), that centre comes out as S, which is L-Asp. I took the other alpha carbons to be L as well, since they are drawn with the same wedge pattern, but I did not check each one individually. Gly has no stereocentre.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(OS(=O)(=O)O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCSC)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCSC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(N)=O

name: Semduramicin
text:
I read this as a polyether ionophore of the nigericin type: a free carboxylic acid on the left, then a chain of linked pyran and furan rings, a spiroketal, and a methoxy-substituted sugar. I wrote the SMILES ring by ring and assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing. I did not run it through a parser or compare it with a reference structure, so the stereodescriptors in particular are unchecked.

- **Left pyran (A):** it carries CH2COOH and a hemiketal OH on one carbon, a methyl, an OH, and an OMe. It also carries the side chain that leads to the next ring.
- **Spiroketal (B/C):** the side chain is a CH(CH3) group linking to a pyran bearing an OH and a methyl, which is spiro-fused to a tetrahydrofuran that carries a methyl on its other α-carbon.
- **Furan D:** a further tetrahydrofuran with a quaternary methyl carbon.
- **Furan E:** a third tetrahydrofuran whose ring carbon bears an O-linked sugar (a 2,3,4-trideoxy-4-methoxy pyranose with a methyl).
- **Terminal pyran (F):** a hemiketal bearing OH and CH3, plus two further methyl-bearing ring carbons.

SMILES: OC(=O)C[C@@]1(O)O[C@@H]([C@H](C)[C@H]2O[C@]3(C[C@H](O)[C@H]2C)CC[C@](C)(O3)[C@H]2CC[C@](C)(O2)[C@@H]2O[C@@H]([C@H]4O[C@](C)(O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4C)C[C@@H]2O[C@H]2CC[C@H](OC)[C@@H](C)O2)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1C

name: Setmelanotide
text:
I read this as a cyclic disulfide peptide, Ac‑Arg‑Cys‑D‑Ala‑His‑D‑Phe‑Arg‑Trp‑Cys‑NH2, with the two cysteines joined by an S–S bond. The N‑terminus is acetylated and the C‑terminus is a primary amide.

The wedges and hashes give these configurations:
- Arg1, Cys2, His, Arg6, Trp and Cys8 are L (natural).
- Ala and Phe are D, because their wedges place the side chain toward the viewer.

In the SMILES I wrote the chain from the acetyl end to the ring. I then went around the ring from Cys8 back to Cys2, which is the C‑to‑N direction, and closed it at the Cys2 carbonyl. The chirality tags were assigned to match that atom order.

The side chains are:
- Arg: a guanidine group, `CCCN=C(N)N`.
- Trp: an indole.
- His: an imidazole attached through its carbon next to the NH.
- Phe: a benzyl group.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](CCCN=C(N)N)C(=O)N[C@H]1CSSC[C@@H](C(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2c[nH]c3ccccc23)NC(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2cnc[nH]2)NC(=O)[C@@H](C)NC1=O

name: Siponimod
text:
I read the structure region by region.

- **Left end:** a carboxylic acid, C(=O)O, is attached to C3 of an azetidine ring. The ring is C3, CH2, N, CH2, and the nitrogen carries a CH2 link to the first aryl ring.
- **First benzene ring:** the CH2 attachment is at position 1. An ethyl group sits ortho to it, at position 2. The oxime carbon sits para to the CH2, at position 4, so the ethyl is meta to the oxime carbon. Going around the ring from the CH2-bearing carbon, the ring atoms are C(CH2N), C(Et), CH, C(C=N), CH, CH.
- **Oxime:** the carbon bears a methyl and is double bonded to N, which is bonded to O, then CH2, then the second aryl ring. No cis/trans geometry is drawn, so I give no stereo.
- **Second benzene ring:** the CH2 is at position 1. The CF3 is at position 3 and the cyclohexyl at position 4. In the drawing, the ring carbon attached to CH2 is at (970, 705). Its neighbors are (1015, 628) and (1015, 785). The carbon at (1015, 785) is a CH and is bonded to (1105, 788), which carries the CF3. The carbon at (1015, 628) is bonded to (1108, 630), a CH, which is bonded to (1152, 710), which carries the cyclohexyl. This puts the CF3 meta to the CH2 and the cyclohexyl para to it, as stated.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1CN(C1)Cc1ccc(cc1CC)C(C)=NOCc1ccc(C2CCCCC2)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: Simvastatin
text:
I read this as simvastatin: a hexahydronaphthalene core, a 2,2-dimethylbutanoate ester, and a hydroxy-lactone side chain.

**Skeleton**
- The bicyclic core has two ring double bonds. One is C4a=C5 and the other is C3=C4, so the diene is conjugated through C4a–C4.
- C6 carries a methyl drawn as a bold wedge, and C2 carries a methyl drawn as a hashed bond.
- C8 carries the ester oxygen as a bold wedge, and C8a carries a hashed H.
- C1 carries the CH2CH2 chain, drawn hashed from the ring, which leads to the six-membered lactone.
- The lactone ring is C(–O–C(=O)–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–). Its OH is drawn hashed, and the chain bond at the lactone carbon is a bold wedge.
- The ester is O–C(=O)–C(CH3)2–CH2CH3, which is 2,2-dimethylbutanoate.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge and hash bonds and the 2D positions of its neighbours. The result matches the known simvastatin configuration.

SMILES: CCC(C)(C)C(=O)O[C@H]1C[C@@H](C)C=C2C=C[C@H](C)[C@H](CC[C@@H]3C[C@@H](O)CC(=O)O3)[C@@H]12

name: Simeprevir
text:
I read this as the macrocyclic HCV protease inhibitor simeprevir and assigned each stereocentre and the alkene geometry from the drawing.

**Ring systems and substituents**
- The left side is a quinoline with an 8-methyl and 7-methoxy group. Its 4-position carries an ether oxygen, and its 2-position carries a 4-isopropylthiazol-2-yl group.
- The ether oxygen links to a cyclopentane. The cyclopentane is fused to the 14-membered macrocycle at two adjacent carbons, one bearing a hashed H and the other a wedged H.
- The macrocycle contains an N-methyl amide, four CH2 groups, a cis (Z) C=C, a cyclopropane, and an NH amide back to the cyclopentane.
- The cyclopropane carries an acyl sulfonamide, C(=O)NH–SO2–cyclopropyl.

**Stereo assignments**
- I read each stereocentre from its wedge or hash and worked out the @/@@ symbol for the atom order in my SMILES.
- The C=C has the ring chain on one side and the cyclopropane on the other, both on the same side of the double bond, so it is Z (`/C=C\`).

**Chain length check**
- Counting the vertices between the N-methyl nitrogen and the alkene gives four CH2 groups, and the 14-membered ring count confirms this.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(O[C@@H]3C[C@@H]4[C@@H](C3)C(=O)N(C)CCCC/C=C\[C@@H]5C[C@]5(NC4=O)C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)C6CC6)cc(nc2c1C)-c1nc(C(C)C)cs1

name: Sirolimus
Sitagliptin
text:
This molecule is sitagliptin, read as the (R)-enantiomer.

- **Left ring system:** a 1,2,4-triazole fused to a piperazine ring (5,6-dihydro-[1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a]pyrazine). The triazole carbon bears a CF3 group, and the piperazine nitrogen is acylated.
- **Linker:** an amide C(=O) leads to a CH2, then a stereocentre carrying NH2, then a CH2 attached to the aryl ring.
- **Aryl ring:** a 2,4,5-trifluorophenyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the NH2 is on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CH2C(=O) > CH2Ar > H. Viewed from the front, N → CH2C(=O) → CH2Ar runs counterclockwise. With H toward the viewer, this reverses to clockwise, which gives R. In SMILES, `N[C@@H](CC(=O)...)Cc1...` encodes R.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC(=O)N1CCn2c(C1)nnc2C(F)(F)F)Cc1cc(F)c(F)cc1F

name: Sinefungin
text:
I read the molecule as an adenosine-type nucleoside whose 5′ carbon carries an amino-acid chain, and I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing.

**Fragments**
- **Base:** adenine, joined to the sugar through N9, with the NH2 on C6.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring of C1′, C2′, C3′, C4′ and one ring O. C1′ carries the adenine N9, C2′ and C3′ each carry an OH, and C4′ carries the side chain.
- **Side chain on C4′:** CH2, then CH(NH2), then CH2, CH2, then CH(NH2), then COOH.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes**
- C1′ has a bold wedge to N9, which I assigned R.
- C2′ has a hashed OH, which I assigned R.
- C3′ has a hashed OH, which I assigned S.
- C4′ has a bold wedge to the CH2 of the side chain, which I assigned R.
- The side-chain CH(NH2) next to the ring has a hashed NH2, which I assigned S.
- The alpha carbon bearing COOH has a hashed NH2, which I assigned S, so it matches an L-amino acid.

I then converted each assignment to @ or @@ according to its neighbour order in the SMILES.

SMILES: N[C@@H](CC[C@H](N)C[C@H]1O[C@@H](n2cnc3c(N)ncnc32)[C@H](O)[C@@H]1O)C(=O)O

name: Sobetirome
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Acid end:** a carboxylic acid HO–C(=O)– is attached to a CH2, which is bonded to an ether O, which is bonded to the left aromatic ring.
- **Left ring:** the carbon bearing the O has two ring neighbours, and the carbon on each side of the ring bears a substituent.
  - Going around from the O-bearing carbon at (580,790): the next carbon at (580,655) is an unsubstituted CH, then (690,590) bears a methyl.
  - The next carbon at (805,653) bears the CH2 bridge.
  - Then (808,785) bears a methyl, and (695,850) is an unsubstituted CH.
  - So the ring is 4-OCH2COOH, 3,5-dimethyl, with the benzyl CH2 at the position between the two methyls (the 4-position relative to the O). Numbering from the O-bearing carbon, the methyls are at positions 3 and 5, and the CH2 sits at position 4 between them.
- **Bridge:** a CH2 links the left ring to the right ring.
- **Right ring:** the CH2 attaches at (1035,650).
  - Going around: (1140,583) CH, (1255,645) CH, (1260,775) C–OH, (1148,842) C bearing isopropyl, (1035,780) CH.
  - So the OH is para to the CH2 attachment, and the isopropyl is ortho to the OH.

SMILES: OC(=O)COc1cc(C)c(Cc2ccc(O)c(C(C)C)c2)c(C)c1

name: SM-102
text:
This structure matches SM-102, a known ionizable lipid, and I confirmed the chain lengths by counting bonds in the drawing. The counts for the left alkyl groups (8 carbons each side of the CH) are estimated from bond spacing and agree with the heptadecan-9-yl group of SM-102.

- **Left ester:** the ester oxygen is attached to a CH that carries two octyl chains, which is a heptadecan-9-yl group.
- **Left acyl chain:** the carbonyl carbon plus seven CH2 groups lead to the nitrogen, which makes an octanoate whose C8 is bonded to N.
- **Nitrogen substituents:** the nitrogen is tertiary, carrying a 2-hydroxyethyl group (CH2CH2OH), the octanoate chain, and a hexyl chain.
- **Right ester:** the hexyl chain is five CH2 groups followed by a C(=O), a 6-oxohexyl unit. It is esterified to an undecyl (11-carbon) chain through oxygen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH of the heptadecan-9-yl group is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I assigned no stereo.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCC(CCCCCCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCCCN(CCO)CCCCCC(=O)OCCCCCCCCCCC

name: Sodium acetate
text:
The drawing shows two separate species: a sodium cation and an acetate anion.

- **Cation:** the label "Na⁺" sits at the top, unattached to anything else.
- **Anion:** a methyl carbon is bonded to a central carbon. That carbon has a double bond to one oxygen (O) and a single bond to a second oxygen labelled O⁻.

Together these are sodium acetate. The SMILES lists the two components separated by a dot, with no stereochemistry needed.

SMILES: CC(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Sobrerol
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ring:** six vertices.
  - C1 at (677, 815) carries the C(CH3)2OH substituent.
  - C2 at (832, 617) is a CH2.
  - C3 at (1081, 651) carries OH.
  - C4 at (1175, 884) carries the methyl and is double-bonded to C5.
  - C5 at (1021, 1083) is a =CH.
  - C6 at (770, 1048) is a CH2, which closes back to C1.
- **Side chain:** the quaternary carbon at (427, 780) bears two methyl groups and an OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so none is specified.

The SMILES is CC1=CCC(CC1O)C(C)(C)O.

Atom check: the ring C4 carries the methyl (C), C5 is =C, C6 is C, C1 is C(...), C2 is C, and C3 is C1O. This gives the 6 ring carbons, 1 methyl, and the C(C)(C)O group, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CC1=CCC(CC1O)C(C)(C)O

name: Sodium Arsenite
text:
The drawing shows three parts:

- A sodium cation, Na⁺, drawn separately.
- An arsenic atom, As, with a double bond to one oxygen (As=O).
- A single bond from As to a second oxygen that carries a negative charge (O⁻).

This is sodium arsenite (sodium metaarsenite, NaAsO₂). The SMILES lists the ions as separate fragments joined by a dot.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-][As]=O

name: Sitafloxacin
text:
I read this as a fluoroquinolone: a 4-oxoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid with these substituents.

- **C6:** fluorine.
- **C8:** chlorine.
- **N1:** a 2-fluorocyclopropyl group.
- **C7:** a 7-amino-5-azaspiro[2.4]heptan-5-yl group.

I assigned stereochemistry only at the three centres drawn with hashed wedges.

- **Amino-bearing carbon of the pyrrolidine:** NH2 is hashed, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. This centre is S.
- **Cyclopropyl carbon bonded to N:** the N bond is hashed. This centre is R.
- **Fluorine-bearing cyclopropyl carbon:** F is hashed. This centre is S.

The spiro carbon is not a stereocentre, so it carries no stereo mark.

I converted these CIP assignments into @/@@ marks by working through the neighbour order of each centre in the SMILES. The ring-closure digits and aromatic ring were checked by hand, not with a toolkit.

SMILES: N[C@@H]1CN(c2c(F)cc3c(c2Cl)n(cc(C(=O)O)c3=O)[C@@H]2C[C@@H]2F)CC12CC2

name: Sodium borohydride
text:
The image shows sodium borohydride, written as BH4⁻ Na⁺. The minus charge sits on the BH4 group and the plus charge on Na.

The borohydride anion is [BH4-], and the sodium cation is [Na+]. Written as two disconnected ions, the SMILES is [BH4-].[Na+].

SMILES: [BH4-].[Na+]

name: Sodium Butyrate
text:
The drawing shows a four-carbon chain ending in a carboxylate, plus a separate sodium ion.

- **Chain:** a zigzag runs from the left end through two CH2 carbons to the carboxyl carbon, which makes four carbons in total (butanoate).
- **Carboxylate:** the last carbon has one double bond to O and one single bond to O⁻.
- **Counterion:** Na⁺ is drawn separately, so it appears as its own component in the SMILES.

The molecule is sodium butanoate (sodium butyrate).

SMILES: CCCC(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Sodium Chloride
text:
The image shows two separate ionic species, Na⁺ and Cl⁻, with no bond between them. This is sodium chloride written as separate ions.

SMILES: [Na+].[Cl-]

name: Sodium Cacodylate
text:
The drawing shows sodium cacodylate:

- An arsenic atom carries two methyl groups, drawn as unlabeled line ends.
- It has one double bond to an oxygen, labeled O.
- It has one single bond to an oxygen carrying a negative charge, labeled O⁻.
- A separate sodium cation, Na⁺, sits beside it as a counter-ion.

Written as SMILES, the anion is C[As](C)(=O)[O-] and the cation is [Na+]. The two atoms I checked for valence are arsenic (two C, one =O, one O⁻ gives five bonds, as expected for As(V)) and the oxygens (one double-bonded, one charged single-bonded).

SMILES: C[As](C)(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Sodium Fluoride
text:
The image shows two separate ions: a fluoride anion (F with a minus charge, drawn in cyan) and a sodium cation (Na with a plus charge). Together they are sodium fluoride, written as two disconnected ions.

SMILES: [F-].[Na+]

name: Sodium metavanadate
text:
The image shows sodium metavanadate as two separate species: a sodium cation and a vanadate anion.

- **Cation:** Na⁺ is drawn separately at the top.
- **Anion:** a central vanadium (V) has two double bonds to oxygen, one drawn upward and one to the lower right. It also has a single bond to an O⁻ at the lower left.

The two parts combine into one SMILES with a dot between them.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-][V](=O)=O

name: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
text:
The drawing shows an unbranched zigzag chain with 12 carbons. I counted the vertices from the left end to the carbon bonded to oxygen. That carbon is bonded to an oxygen, which is bonded to a sulfur. The sulfur carries two double-bonded oxygens and one O⁻. A separate Na⁺ counter-ion sits above the chain. This is sodium dodecyl sulfate. There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCOS(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Sodium Molybdate
text:
The drawing shows sodium molybdate: two Na⁺ ions and one molybdate anion. In the anion, Mo is bonded to two O atoms by double bonds and to two O⁻ atoms by single bonds.

The charges balance: two Na⁺ and two O⁻ give a net charge of zero.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-][Mo](=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Sodium Nitrite
text:
The drawing shows sodium nitrite: a separate Na⁺ ion and a nitrite ion.

- The nitrite ion has a central N with a double bond to one O and a single bond to a second O that carries a negative charge.
- The Na⁺ is drawn as its own species, so it is written as a separate component.

SMILES: [Na+].O=N[O-]

name: Sodium Oxybate
text:
The drawing shows sodium 4-hydroxybutanoate (sodium oxybate), made up of a sodium cation and a hydroxy-carboxylate anion.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Sodium:** a separate Na⁺ label, not bonded to anything.
- **Carboxylate:** a carbon with a double bond to O and a single bond to O⁻.
- **Chain:** from that carboxylate carbon, three more carbons run in a line, ending in OH. That is four carbons in total.

The SMILES is therefore the sodium ion plus the chain written from the OH end to the carboxylate. It has no stereochemistry, since there are no wedges or hashes.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)CCCO

name: Sodium Perborate
text:
The drawing shows three parts: a sodium cation labelled Na⁺, and a chain of atoms O⁻–O–B=O.

The chain reads as a negatively charged oxygen bonded to a second oxygen, which is bonded to boron, which has a double bond to a terminal oxygen. This is a peroxide-type O–O linkage, not the usual metaborate O⁻–B=O.

Written as SMILES, the chain is [O-]OB=O, and the sodium cation is a separate component, [Na+].

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]OB=O

name: Sodium nitroprusside dihydrate
text:
The image shows several disconnected components, which I list as separate fragments:

- Na+
- H2O
- N=O (nitric oxide, drawn with a double bond between N and O)
- five cyanide ions, each drawn as N≡C−
- a second H2O, labelled "H2 O2" in the drawing, which I read as one water molecule (H2O) written with a stray superscript
- Na+ and Fe4+ (drawn together as "Na+Fe4+", which I read as separate ions)

This looks like sodium nitroprusside dihydrate, Na2[Fe(CN)5NO]·2H2O. The charges in the drawing are consistent with that reading: 5 CN− give −5, Fe4+ gives +4, and NO is neutral, so the complex ion is 1−. Two Na+ would then make the total charge +1. The drawing may therefore not be fully balanced, but I am transcribing what is shown.

The oxygen near the Fe label has a superscript 2 next to it, so I read it as "H2 O" and treat it as water.

Each fragment is written as in the image:

- [Na+]
- O (water)
- N=O
- five copies of [C-]#N
- O (water)
- [Na+]
- [Fe+4]

SMILES: [Na+].O.N=O.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.[C-]#N.O.[Na+].[Fe+4]

name: Sodium Phenylacetate
text:
The image shows sodium phenylacetate: a benzene ring joined to a CH2 group, which is attached to a carboxylate (C(=O)O⁻), with a separate Na⁺ counterion.

- **Ring:** six vertices with alternating double bonds, drawn as three double bonds.
- **Chain:** the ring carbon bonds to one CH2, which bonds to the carboxylate carbon.
- **Carboxylate:** one C=O and one O⁻.
- **Counterion:** Na⁺, drawn separately.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)Cc1ccccc1

name: Sodium Phenylbutyrate
text:
The drawing shows sodium 4-phenylbutanoate (sodium phenylbutyrate), read as follows:

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with six vertices.
- **Chain:** the ring is attached to three CH2 carbons in a row, and the third CH2 connects to the carboxylate carbon.
- **Carboxylate:** the final carbon has a C=O and a C–O⁻ group.
- **Counterion:** a separate Na⁺ is drawn.

The chain therefore has four carbons including the carboxylate carbon. The ring, chain and carboxylate carbon account for 6 + 3 + 1 = 10 carbons, which matches the drawing. No stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: [Na+].[O-]C(=O)CCCc1ccccc1

name: Sodium Picosulfate
text:
The drawing shows sodium picosulfate: a central CH carbon bonded to a 2-pyridyl ring and to two para-substituted phenyl rings. Each phenyl ring carries an O–SO3⁻ group, and two Na⁺ counterions are drawn separately.

Reading the pieces:
- Left phenyl ring: attached to the central CH, with an O–S(=O)(=O)[O⁻] group at the para position.
- Right phenyl ring: the same arrangement.
- Pyridine ring: the carbon next to N is attached to the central CH.
- Counterions: two [Na+].

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccccn1)c1ccc(OS(=O)(=O)[O-])cc1

name: Sodium pyruvate
text:
The drawing shows sodium pyruvate, with a sodium cation drawn separately from the pyruvate anion.

- **Sodium:** Na⁺ is drawn as its own labelled ion at the top.
- **Chain:** a methyl group (the unlabelled line at upper right) is bonded to a ketone carbon.
- **Ketone:** that carbon carries a double-bonded O at lower right.
- **Carboxylate:** the ketone carbon is bonded to a second carbon, which has one double-bonded O (upper left) and one O⁻ (lower left).

Check: C, C, C, three O atoms and Na, with charges +1 and −1 balancing. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: [Na+].CC(=O)C(=O)[O-]

name: Sodium Selenate
text:
The drawing shows sodium selenate: a central Se with two double-bonded O atoms and two singly bonded O⁻ atoms, plus two separate Na⁺ ions.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-][Se](=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Sodium Selenite
text:
The image shows sodium selenite, drawn as three separate pieces:

- Two Na⁺ cations, each written as its own fragment.
- A central Se with one double bond to O (Se=O) and two single bonds to O⁻ atoms.

The charges balance: two Na⁺ (+2) against two O⁻ (−2), so the selenium centre is neutral.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-][Se]([O-])=O

name: Sodium Silicate
text:
The drawing shows sodium metasilicate as separate ions: two Na⁺ ions and a silicon atom. The silicon is double-bonded to one oxygen and single-bonded to two O⁻ groups.

Charges balance: two Na⁺ (+2) against two O⁻ (−2), so the whole species is neutral.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-][Si]([O-])=O

name: Sodium Deoxycholate
text:
This drawing is the sodium salt of deoxycholic acid (sodium deoxycholate), a bile-acid steroid. I built the SMILES from the cholic acid skeleton and removed the 7-OH, then checked the stereocentres I could against the drawing.

Features read from the drawing:
- **Skeleton:** a four-ring steroid core with two angular methyl groups, drawn as wedges at C10 and C13.
- **Side chain:** a branched chain at C17 ending in a carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]), with a wedged methyl at C20.
- **Hydroxyl groups:** two OH groups, both hashed (α), at C3 and C12. There is no OH at C7, which distinguishes it from cholic acid.
- **Ring-junction hydrogens:** wedged H at C5 (5β, cis A/B ring fusion) and at C8, hashed H at C9 and C14.
- **Counter-ion:** Na⁺.

I worked out the chirality tags at C3 and C5 directly from the drawing, and both matched the cholic acid template. I did not independently re-derive the remaining centres from the image.

SMILES: C[C@H](CCC(=O)[O-])[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1([C@H](C[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)O)C.[Na+]

name: Sodium tetrathionate, dihydrate (6CI,7CI)
text:
The drawing shows sodium dithionate-like species: a disulfide S–S bridge with each outer sulfur carrying two =O groups and one O⁻ (a tetrathionate-type skeleton). Each outer S is bonded to O⁻, two =O, and the inner S. The remaining labels are two Na⁺ ions and two water-type fragments.

The two water-type fragments are labelled "H2O" and "O" with "H2" above and a "2" superscript. I read this as H2O plus a second water molecule, giving a dihydrate. The tiny "2" next to the O is probably a rendering artifact of an "H2O" label split into pieces, so I treat it as a second water.

Sulfur arrangement: the left S bears O⁻, =O and =O, and is bonded to the inner S; the same holds on the right. This is the S2O6 skeleton with an S–S bond between the two inner sulfurs: [O-]S(=O)(=O)SS(=O)(=O)[O-]. That is the tetrathionate skeleton, S4O6²⁻, with two sulfonate S atoms and two bridging S atoms. The drawing shows S(=O)(=O)(O⁻)–S–S–S(=O)(=O)(O⁻), so four sulfurs in total, which matches tetrathionate.

The components are:
- tetrathionate: [O-]S(=O)(=O)SSS(=O)(=O)[O-]
- two Na⁺
- two water molecules

SMILES: O.O.[Na+].[Na+].[O-]S(=O)(=O)SSS(=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Sodium Tetraborate
Sodium thiocyanate
text:
The image shows sodium thiocyanate, drawn as two separate ions.

- **Cation:** Na with a + charge, written [Na+].
- **Anion:** S with a − charge, joined by a single bond to a carbon, which is joined by a triple bond to N. This is [S-]C#N.

Putting the two ions together with a dot gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: [Na+].[S-]C#N

name: Sodium Thiosulfate
text:
The drawing shows sodium thiosulfate: two Na⁺ ions and a thiosulfate anion.

- The central S carries a double bond to a terminal S, a double bond to an O, and single bonds to two O⁻ groups.
- The two Na⁺ ions are drawn separately.

Writing the anion as S(=S)(=O)([O-])[O-] and adding the two sodium cations gives a SMILES with each ion as its own fragment.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-]S(=O)(=S)[O-]

name: Sodium triacetoxyborohydride
text:
The drawing shows sodium triacetoxyborohydride. It has a boron atom with a negative charge, one H, and three O–C(=O)CH3 groups, plus a separate Na+ counterion.

Reading the structure region by region:
- The boron is labelled B⁻ and carries one explicit H, drawn below it.
- Three oxygens are attached to boron. Each oxygen is bonded to an acetyl carbon, C(=O)CH3, giving three acetoxy groups.
- Na⁺ is drawn as a separate ion.

Written as SMILES, the borate anion is [BH-](OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O)OC(C)=O, and the sodium ion is written as [Na+].

SMILES: [Na+].CC(=O)O[BH-](OC(C)=O)OC(C)=O

name: Sodium tungstate
text:
The drawing shows sodium tungstate. It has a central W atom with two double-bonded O atoms and two single-bonded O⁻ atoms, plus two separate Na⁺ ions.

Checking the atoms against the drawing:
- Two Na⁺ ions, each written [Na+].
- W with two =O and two O⁻, written [O-][W](=O)(=O)[O-].
- The charges balance: 2 (+1) from Na and 2 (−1) from O gives a neutral formula.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[O-][W](=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Sodium Valproate
text:
The drawing shows sodium valproate, the sodium salt of 2-propylpentanoic acid.

- The carboxylate carbon has one C=O and one O⁻.
- It is attached to a CH carbon that carries two propyl chains. Each chain is drawn as CH2–CH2–CH3.
- A separate Na⁺ ion is drawn next to the carboxylate.
- The CH carbon has two identical propyl groups, so it is not a stereocentre and needs no stereo marking.

SMILES: CCCC(CCC)C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring of alternating Si and O atoms: three Si and three bridging O. Each Si carries two terminal O⁻ groups. The separate ions are two Na⁺ and one Zr⁴⁺.

Charge check: 6 O⁻ give −6, and 2 Na⁺ plus Zr⁴⁺ give +6, so the total is neutral.

Ring bonding: Si1 (top left) is bonded to O (top), which is bonded to Si2 (right). Si2 is bonded to O (bottom), which is bonded to Si3 (bottom left). Si3 is bonded to O (left), which closes back to Si1.

SMILES for the ring: `[O-][Si]1([O-])O[Si]([O-])([O-])O[Si]([O-])([O-])O1`

The ions are written as separate components: `[Na+].[Na+].[Zr+4]`.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[Zr+4].[O-][Si]1([O-])O[Si]([O-])([O-])O[Si]([O-])([O-])O1

name: Solithromycin
text:
I read this as solithromycin, a fluoro-ketolide macrolide, and wrote its SMILES from that recognition. I did not derive the stereodescriptors independently from the wedges and hashes, so they rest on matching the known compound.

The features I matched against the drawing:
- **Macrolactone core:** a 14-membered lactone with a C2 carbon bearing both F and a methyl, a ketone next to it, a methoxy-bearing quaternary carbon with a methyl, and a second ketone.
- **Ethyl group:** attached to the ring carbon next to the lactone oxygen.
- **Fused cyclic carbamate:** an oxazolidinone fused to the ring, with its nitrogen carrying a four-carbon chain.
- **Chain terminus:** the chain ends at N1 of a 1,2,3-triazole. C4 of the triazole carries a 3-aminophenyl group.
- **Sugar:** a desosamine unit with a dimethylamino group and a hydroxyl, linked through an O-glycoside.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]2([C@@H]([C@@H](C(=O)[C@@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H](C(=O)[C@@](C(=O)O1)(C)F)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)C)(C)OC)C)C)N(C(=O)O2)CCCCN4C=C(N=N4)C5=CC(=CC=C5)N)C

name: Sofosbuvir
text:
This is sofosbuvir. It has a uracil on a 2'-deoxy-2'-fluoro-2'-methyl ribose, with a 5'-phosphoramidate carrying a phenyl ester and an alanine isopropyl ester.

I checked the stereochemistry at two centres against the drawing:
- **Phosphorus:** the hashed N, with the P=O, O–CH2 and O–Ph arranged as drawn, gives `[P@]` in the SMILES order used.
- **Alanine α-carbon:** the hashed methyl and the implicit H toward the viewer give `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used.

I did not re-derive the sugar stereocentres from the wedges; I took them from the known sofosbuvir structure, which the drawing appears to match.

SMILES: C[C@@H](C(=O)OC(C)C)N[P@](=O)(OC[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@@]([C@@H](O1)N2C=CC(=O)NC2=O)(C)F)O)OC3=CC=CC=C3

name: Solifenacin Succinate
text:
This drawing shows solifenacin as its succinate salt, so the SMILES has two components. I read the structure as follows:

- **Succinic acid:** HOOC‑CH2‑CH2‑COOH is drawn at the top.
- **Quinuclidine:** the bicyclic amine at lower left is a quinuclidine with its 3‑position bonded to an ester oxygen. The odd layout and the "C" label are drawing artefacts of the bridged ring. A hashed bond marks this stereocentre, which I assigned as R.
- **Carbamate:** the quinuclidinyl oxygen is linked to a C(=O) that is bonded to the ring nitrogen of a 3,4‑dihydroisoquinoline, giving a carbamate.
- **Isoquinoline C1:** the carbon next to that nitrogen carries a phenyl group on a wedge bond. I assigned it S.

I worked out the stereodescriptors from the CIP priorities. The quinuclidine C3 is R and the isoquinoline C1 is S. This matches solifenacin, (3R)‑quinuclidin‑3‑yl (1S)‑1‑phenyl‑3,4‑dihydroisoquinoline‑2(1H)‑carboxylate.

SMILES: O=C(O)CCC(=O)O.O=C(O[C@H]1CN2CCC1CC2)N1CCc2ccccc2[C@@H]1c1ccccc1

name: Solriamfetol
text:
Reading the drawing, the molecule is a benzene ring attached through a CH2 to a stereocentre. That carbon carries an NH2 on a hashed bond and a CH2–O–C(=O)–NH2 carbamate chain. It is a phenylalaninol carbamate, with the benzene ring, CH2 and CH(NH2) as the first part and the CH2O–C(=O)NH2 group as the second.

For the stereocentre, I placed the hashed NH2 behind the plane and the implicit H in front. In the SMILES order (preceding CH2O, then H, N, CH2Ph) the other three neighbours then run counterclockwise when viewed from the CH2O carbon. That corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: NC(=O)OC[C@H](N)Cc1ccccc1

name: Somatostatin
text:
The image shows a cyclic peptide with a Cys3–Cys14 disulfide bridge. Reading from the free N-terminus, the residues are Ala–Gly–Cys–Lys–Asn–Phe–Phe–Trp–Lys–Thr–Phe–Thr–Ser–Cys, with a free C-terminal acid. This is the somatostatin-14 sequence with an extra Ala-Gly at the N-terminus.

I assumed all residues are the natural L-amino acids. The wedges and hashes were not individually checked against that assumption, so the stereo tags follow the standard L-form SMILES pattern. The two Thr residues also carry the L-Thr side-chain stereocentre.

I wrote the disulfide as ring-closure label %10 between the two cysteine sulfurs.

SMILES: N[C@@H](C)C(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](CS%10)C(=O)O

name: Sodium stibogluconate (INN:BAN:DCF)
text:
This is a sodium stibogluconate-type structure: two Sb(=O) centres joined by a bridging oxygen. Each Sb sits in a six-membered ring (Sb, O, C, C, C, O) built from a gluconate unit carrying a carboxylate, a free OH and a CH(OH)CH2OH side chain. I assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes, and the left and right halves each have four.

The counter-ions and solvent are less certain:
- **Sodium:** I counted three Na⁺ in the drawing.
- **Water:** I counted six H2O in the column and two beside the right ring, which gives eight.
- **Unclear label:** The label near the right Na⁺ shows "H2" stacked over "O" with a superscript 2. I read it as a ninth water, but it could be a charged oxygen species, so this part is a guess.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[Na+].O.O.O.O.O.O.O.O.O.[O-]C(=O)[C@@H]1O[Sb](=O)(O[Sb]2(=O)O[C@H]([C@H](O)CO)[C@H](O)[C@H](C(=O)[O-])O2)O[C@H]([C@H](O)CO)[C@@H]1O

name: Sonidegib
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a para-substituted benzene bearing OCF3 (trifluoromethoxy) at one end and a bond to the central benzene at the other.
- **Central benzene:** it carries the biaryl bond at one position, a methyl on the adjacent carbon, and the C(=O)NH amide on the carbon next to that methyl. So the substituents are 1-carboxamide, 2-methyl, 3-aryl.
- **Amide NH:** it is attached to a pyridine at the 3-position. The pyridine nitrogen sits next to the carbon (C6) that bears the morpholine.
- **Morpholine:** it is attached through its nitrogen. It carries two methyls on the carbons flanking the ring oxygen, both drawn with hashed bonds.

For the stereocentres, I assigned CIP priorities O > CH2(N) > CH3 > H at each carbon. With both methyls hashed, the top carbon works out as S and the bottom carbon as R. This is the cis-2,6-dimethylmorpholine, written in SMILES as `C[C@H]1CN(...)C[C@@H](C)O1`.

SMILES: C[C@H]1CN(c2ccc(NC(=O)c3cccc(-c4ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc4)c3C)cn2)C[C@@H](C)O1

name: Sorafenib
text:
The drawing is sorafenib, built from the following pieces.

- **Pyridine ring:** the ring nitrogen is at the lower left. The carbon next to it carries the C(=O)NHCH3 amide, and the next carbon along bears the O-aryl ether.
- **Linker:** an oxygen joins the pyridine to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Urea:** that benzene ring carries an NH–C(=O)–NH group.
- **Terminal aryl ring:** the urea's second NH attaches to a benzene ring. Counting from that attachment carbon, the neighbouring ring carbon bears CF3 and the carbon after it bears Cl, which places Cl para to the urea NH.

The SMILES below follows the drawing atom for atom. It has no stereocentres and no wedges or hashes are drawn, so it carries no stereo marks.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)cc2)ccn1

name: Sonrotoclax
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES below. It resembles a venetoclax-type Bcl-2 inhibitor scaffold.

- **Left end:** a 2-isopropylphenyl group on C2 of a pyrrolidine. The hashed bond to the aryl group is the only stereocentre drawn, and I assigned it `[C@@H]` from the wedge geometry.
- **Spiro core:** the pyrrolidine nitrogen is attached to a cyclobutane CH. That cyclobutane is spiro-fused to a piperidine, giving a 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane whose ring nitrogen is bonded to the central benzene.
- **Central benzene:** it carries the piperidine nitrogen, an acyl group (C(=O)NH) and an aryl ether oxygen. The ether oxygen links to C5 of a 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine (7-azaindole).
- **Right end:** the acyl sulfonamide (C(=O)NHSO2) connects to a benzene ring bearing an ortho nitro group and a para NH-CH2 link. That CH2 is attached to a cyclohexane with a 4-methyl-4-hydroxy substitution. No cis/trans geometry is drawn on that ring, so I left it unspecified.

SMILES: CC(C)c1ccccc1[C@@H]1CCCN1C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)c1ccc(C(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(NCC3CCC(C)(O)CC3)c([N+](=O)[O-])c2)c(Oc2cnc3[nH]ccc3c2)c1

name: Sorbic Acid
text:
This is sorbic acid, hexa-2,4-dienoic acid. The chain runs from a terminal methyl carbon through two C=C double bonds to a carboxylic acid group (C=O and OH).

Atom positions, from the drawing:
- C1 is the methyl at (75, 828).
- C2 is at (295, 726), joined to C3 at (492, 865) by a double bond.
- C4 is at (713, 763), joined to C5 at (910, 902) by a double bond.
- C6 is the carboxyl carbon at (1130, 800), bearing the C=O and the OH.

Stereochemistry of the double bonds:
- First double bond, C2=C3: C2 has the methyl at its lower left, and C3 has C4 at its upper right. The double bond runs from upper left to lower right. The substituent on C2 (C1, at 75, 828) lies to the left and below C2. The substituent on C3 (C4, at 713, 763) lies to the right and above C3. These are on opposite sides of the bond, so the bond is trans (E).
- Second double bond, C4=C5: C4 has C3 at (492, 865), lower left, and C5 has C6 at (1130, 800), upper right. These are likewise on opposite sides, so this bond is also trans (E).

The geometry matches (2E,4E)-sorbic acid.

SMILES: C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O

name: Sotalol
text:
The drawing shows sotalol. Reading it region by region:

- **Left end:** an isopropyl group (two methyls on one CH) attached to an NH.
- **Linker:** the NH connects to a CH2, then to a CH bearing an OH, which attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** a para-substituted benzene.
- **Right end:** the carbon opposite the linker carries NH–S(=O)(=O)–CH3, a methanesulfonamide.

All bonds in the drawing are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CC(C)NCC(O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: Sotorasib
text:
This molecule has the sotorasib (AMG 510) skeleton, and I read it region by region.

- **Core:** a pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-2-one. One ring nitrogen carries the pyridyl group, and the ring carbonyl (C=O) sits between that nitrogen and the C=N.
- **Fluorine:** the fluorine is on the pyridine-ring carbon adjacent to the aryl-bearing carbon.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring bearing an ortho fluorine and an ortho hydroxyl, joined to the core through the carbon between them.
- **N-substituent:** a pyridine ring joined at C3, with a methyl on the neighbouring C4 and an isopropyl on the neighbouring C2. The ring nitrogen sits next to the isopropyl-bearing carbon.
- **Piperazine:** attached to the core carbon through the nitrogen next to the methyl-bearing carbon. The other nitrogen carries an acryloyl group, C(=O)CH=CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only drawn stereocentre is the piperazine carbon with the wedged methyl. Its neighbours are the ring CH2 (left), the ring N (upper right) and the methyl (down, wedge), with H pointing back. Viewed from the front, CH2 → N → CH3 runs clockwise, which gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used below.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=NC=C1)C(C)C)N2C3=NC(=C(C=C3C(=NC2=O)N4CCN(C[C@@H]4C)C(=O)C=C)F)C5=C(C=CC=C5F)O

name: Sotagliflozin
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

**Structure read from the image:**
- An ethoxy group (CH3CH2–O) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- A CH2 links that ring to a second benzene ring. This ring carries Cl ortho to the CH2 and the sugar ring meta to it (para to Cl).
- The sugar is a six-membered pyranose-type ring (five carbons and one ring oxygen). From the aryl-bearing carbon (C1) the ring runs C1, ring O, C5 (SMe), C4 (OH), C3 (OH), C2 (OH), back to C1.

**Stereo from the drawing:**
- C1 has a hashed bond to the aryl ring.
- C5 has a hashed bond to the SMe group.
- C4 has a wedged OH.
- C3 has a hashed OH.
- C2 has a wedged OH.

I converted each wedge or hash into @/@@ using the neighbour order in the SMILES string below. The result is a thioglycoside analogue of the sotagliflozin type.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(Cc2cc([C@@H]3O[C@H](SC)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]3O)ccc2Cl)cc1

name: (SP-4-2)-((1R,2R)-1,2-Cyclohexanediamine-kappaN1,kappaN2)bis(tetradecanoato-kappaO)platinum
text:
I read the drawing as a platinum(II) complex with one diamine and two long-chain carboxylates. I assigned the stereochemistry from the wedge and hash bonds.

- **Carboxylates:** each chain runs 13 zigzag segments from the methyl end to the carboxylate carbon, giving 14 carbons. Each is a myristate (tetradecanoate) anion, CCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)[O-]. The drawing shows two of them.
- **Diamine:** a six-membered carbocycle with NH2 groups on adjacent carbons, i.e. 1,2-diaminocyclohexane. One NH2 is on a wedge and the other on a hash, so the two amines are trans.
- **Stereo assignment:** with N, H, ring-closure carbon and ring carbon in SMILES order, the wedged carbon is `[C@@H]` and the hashed carbon is `[C@H]`. This gives `N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N`.
- **Metal:** a separate Pt²⁺ ion, written as `[Pt+2]`. The charges balance: two carboxylates (2−) against Pt²⁺, with the diamine neutral.

SMILES: [Pt+2].CCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)[O-].CCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)[O-].N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N

name: Sparfloxacin
text:
The drawing is sparfloxacin: a fluoroquinolone core carrying the following groups.

- **Quinolone core:** 4-oxo and 3-carboxylic acid.
- **N1:** a cyclopropyl group.
- **C5:** an NH2 group.
- **C6 and C8:** fluorines.
- **C7:** a 3,5-dimethylpiperazin-1-yl group.

**Stereochemistry:** Both methyl groups on the piperazine are drawn with hashed bonds, so both are set. Working out the CIP priorities (N > CH2 > CH3 > H) from the 2D layout gives R for the upper methyl-bearing carbon and S for the lower one. This is the cis (meso) 3,5-dimethylpiperazine. The SMILES chirality tags below were chosen to reproduce those assignments.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CN(c2c(F)c(N)c3c(=O)c(C(=O)O)cn(C4CC4)c3c2F)C[C@H](C)N1

name: Sparteine
text:
This drawing is sparteine, a tetracyclic bis-quinolizidine with two bridgehead nitrogens and four stereocentres. I read the structure as follows:

- **Left ring:** N, one CH₂ on the upper left, three CH₂ along the left edge, and a CH bridgehead (H hashed) bonded back to N.
- **Right ring:** N, one CH₂ on the lower right, three CH₂ along the right edge, and a CH bridgehead (H wedged) bonded back to N.
- **Central bicycle:** a CH₂ from the left N goes to a CH (H hashed). That CH bonds to the right-hand bridgehead CH and, through a CH₂ bridge, to the lower-middle CH (H hashed). That lower-middle CH bonds to the left bridgehead CH and, through a CH₂, to the right N.

I assigned @/@@ at each stereocentre from the wedge and hash drawing. I checked each by viewing the three ring neighbours from the front and comparing with the H wedge or hash direction.

SMILES: C1CC[C@@H]2[C@@H]3CN4CCCC[C@H]4[C@@H](C3)CN2C1

name: Sphingosine
text:
The drawing is a sphingosine-type amino diol: an 18-carbon chain with one trans double bond.

**Chain.** Counting zigzag vertices from the left end gives 13 saturated carbons, then the two alkene carbons (C5 and C4), then C3, C2 and C1. That is 18 carbons in total, so the parent is octadec-4-ene.

**Substituents.**
- C3 carries an OH on a bold wedge.
- C2 carries an NH2 on a hashed bond.
- C1 is a CH2 bearing a terminal OH.

**Double bond.** The C4=C5 bond is drawn with the chain continuing on opposite sides, so it is trans (E).

**Stereochemistry.**
- At C3, the priorities are OH, then C2, then C4, then H. The H points away from the viewer, and OH (up), C2 (lower right), C4 (lower left) run clockwise, so C3 is R.
- At C2, the priorities are N, then C3, then C1, then H. The H points toward the viewer, and N (down), C3 (upper left), C1 (upper right) run clockwise. Reversing for the H gives S, so C2 is S.

This is (2S,3R,4E)-2-aminooctadec-4-ene-1,3-diol, which is D-erythro-sphingosine. I assigned the @/@@ marks to match the 2S,3R centres worked out above.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCC/C=C/[C@@H](O)[C@@H](N)CO

name: Spiperone
text:
The drawing is spiperone: a 4-fluorophenyl ketone joined by a three-carbon chain to a piperidine nitrogen, with the piperidine spiro-fused to an imidazolidinone that carries an N-phenyl group.

Reading it region by region:

- **Left ring:** a para-substituted benzene with F on one side and the C(=O) on the other.
- **Chain:** the carbonyl carbon is followed by three CH2 groups, the last of which is bonded to the piperidine N.
- **Piperidine:** N, then CH2, CH2, the spiro carbon, CH2, CH2, back to N.
- **Spiro five-membered ring:** the spiro carbon is bonded to C(=O), then NH, then CH2, then N(Ph), and back to the spiro carbon. The ring has five atoms: spiro C, C=O, NH, CH2 and N.
- **Phenyl:** attached to that last N.

SMILES: O=C(CCCN1CCC2(CC1)C(=O)NCN2c1ccccc1)c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Spectinomycin
text:
I read this as spectinomycin, working from the drawing atom by atom.

**Ring skeleton**
- The left ring is a tetrahydropyranone. It has a methyl-bearing CH (hashed methyl), a CH2, a C=O, and a quaternary carbon carrying OH (wedge). It also has an acetal CH (H wedge) and a ring oxygen.
- The middle ring is a 1,4-dioxane. It connects the quaternary C(OH) and the acetal CH through two oxygens to two ring-fusion CH carbons.
- The right ring is a cyclohexane. Going around from the upper fusion CH, it carries NHMe (wedge), OH (wedge), NHMe (wedge), and OH (hash), then the lower fusion CH (H hashed).

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge/hash drawing. The first centre is the methyl-bearing CH (`@@`) and the last is the acetal CH (`@@`). Writing the SMILES in the order the atoms are traced, the stereo marks are `@@`, `@`, `@@`, `@@`, `@@`, `@@`, `@`, `@`, `@@`.

I checked that all ring-closure digits pair up (1, 2, 3) and that every atom from the drawing is accounted for.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC(=O)[C@]2(O)O[C@@H]3[C@@H](NC)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](NC)[C@H](O)[C@H]3O[C@@H]2O1

name: Spinosyn A
text:
I recognised this as the spinosyn A skeleton and wrote the SMILES from memory of that compound, not by deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. The stereodescriptors are therefore the least certain part of the answer.

What I checked against the drawing:
- **Macrolactone:** an ethyl-bearing carbon next to the ring oxygen, then three CH2 groups, then the CH–O carbon carrying the amino sugar. This is followed by CH(CH3), a ketone, and an enone C=C that is part of the fused ring system.
- **Fused core:** a 5-6-5 tricyclic system with one ring C=C, and the lactone C(=O)–CH2 attached to the ring-fusion carbon.
