- **Cyclopentane sugar link:** the cyclopentane carries an O-glycoside to a 2,3,4-tri-O-methyl-6-deoxyhexose (three OMe groups and a C-methyl).
- **Amino sugar:** a tetrahydropyran carrying an N(CH3)2 group and a methyl, attached through its anomeric carbon to the macrolide oxygen.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1CCC[C@H]([C@H](C(=O)C2=C[C@H]3[C@@H]4C[C@@H](C[C@H]4C=C[C@@H]3[C@H]2CC(=O)O1)O[C@H]5[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O5)C)OC)OC)OC)C)O[C@H]6CC[C@@H]([C@H](O6)C)N(C)C

name: Spironolactone
text:
The drawing shows spironolactone, a steroid with these features:

- **A ring:** a 4-en-3-one, with a ketone on the right and a C=C in the ring.
- **C10 and C13:** each carries an angular methyl, drawn as hashed bonds.
- **C7:** carries an S–C(=O)CH3 thioacetyl group, drawn with a wedge.
- **C17:** a spiro carbon that closes a γ-lactone (O–C(=O)–CH2–CH2) onto the five-membered D ring.
- **C8, C9 and C14:** each carries an H, shown as a wedge or hash.

I did not derive the stereodescriptors independently from the wedges and hashes. I wrote the SMILES from my recollection of spironolactone's standard isomeric SMILES and checked its connectivity against the drawing. The stereo marks therefore rest on that recollection.

SMILES: C[C@]12CCC(=O)C=C1C[C@H]([C@@H]3[C@@H]2CC[C@]4([C@H]3CC[C@@]45CCC(=O)O5)C)SC(=O)C

name: Spirapril
text:
The drawing matches spirapril, which I identified from its overall structure and then checked against the image.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- An ethyl ester (CH3CH2–O–C(=O)–) sits on a stereocentre drawn with a hashed bond to a CH2CH2 chain, which ends in a phenyl ring.
- That stereocentre also carries an NH, which links to an alanine-type CH(CH3) drawn with a hashed methyl.
- This alanine carbon is attached to a C(=O) amide, which bonds to the ring nitrogen.
- The ring is a pyrrolidine whose C4 is a spiro carbon bearing two sulfur atoms joined by a CH2CH2 bridge (a 1,3-dithiolane).
- The ring carbon next to the nitrogen carries a wedged COOH.

**Stereochemistry**
- I checked the proline carbon, the one carrying the wedged COOH, directly against the drawing. With the COOH toward the viewer, the priorities N > COOH > CH2 run counterclockwise with H pointing away, so it is S.
- I did not re-derive the other two stereocentres from the hashed bonds. I took them from the enalapril-type pattern (all S) that spirapril follows.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1CC2(C[C@H]1C(=O)O)SCCS2

name: Spiroplatin
text:
The drawing shows three separate components: a sulfate dianion, a platinum(2+) cation, and a diamine ligand.

- **Sulfate:** a sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens and two O⁻ groups, written `O=S(=O)([O-])[O-]`.
- **Platinum:** a free Pt²⁺ ion, written `[Pt+2]`.
- **Ligand:** a cyclohexane ring in which one ring carbon carries two CH2NH2 groups. The ring has six vertices, and the quaternary carbon is the one bearing both substituents. This is 1,1-bis(aminomethyl)cyclohexane, written `NCC1(CN)CCCCC1`.

The components are not joined by bonds in the drawing, so I write them as dot-separated fragments.

SMILES: NCC1(CN)CCCCC1.O=S(=O)([O-])[O-].[Pt+2]

name: Siomycin A
text:
This SMILES is a best-effort reading of the drawing. The structure looks like thiostrepton, and I assembled the connectivity partly from that recognition. Several parts of the drawing overlap, so some of the reading is inferred:

- **Central ring:** I could not resolve its atoms from the drawing. I wrote it as a six-membered ring with an imine and two CH2 groups that are not clearly drawn.
- **Dehydroalanine tail:** I assigned the dehydroalanine units to the chain by the most consistent reading of the overlapping bonds.
- **Stereochemistry:** The @/@@ tags are my best guesses from the wedges and hashes, and some may be wrong.

The pieces I read from the drawing are:

- A dehydrobutyrine (Dhb) unit attached to a thiazoline.
- A threonine residue linked to the top thiazole.
- A second thiazole carrying a dihydroxy side chain.
- A third thiazole attached to a CH(CH3)–O ester carbon.
- A fused hydroxyethyl-substituted pyridine with a partially unsaturated carbocycle (the quinaldic acid-type unit).
- A valine residue and an alanine residue.
- Dehydroalanine units, ending in a dehydroalanine amide tail (–C(=O)NH2).

I have not been able to run a validity check on the SMILES.

name: Stanozolol
text:
This is stanozolol, a 17α-methyl-17β-hydroxy androstane steroid with a pyrazole fused to the A ring.

- **Pyrazole ring:** it has an N= at the top, bonded to a CH=, and an NH at the bottom. The NH sits on the carbon next to the CH2 that links to C5, and the CH= sits on the carbon next to the CH2 that links to C10.
- **D ring:** it carries a tertiary carbon with OH and a hashed methyl, which gives 17α-methyl and 17β-OH.
- **Methyl groups:** there is a wedged methyl at C13 and a wedged methyl at C10.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** the H atoms at the ring fusions are drawn with wedges or hashes in the standard steroid arrangement.

I wrote the stereocentres from my recollection of the known stanozolol SMILES and only partly checked them against the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@]2(C)O)CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(Cc5c(C4)[nH]nc5)C

name: Squalene
text:
The drawing is squalene, a C30 chain with six trisubstituted double bonds that are all drawn trans (E).

Reading the chain from the left, the pattern is:

- Me₂C=CH–CH₂CH₂–C(Me)=CH–CH₂CH₂–C(Me)=CH–CH₂CH₂–CH=C(Me)–CH₂CH₂–CH=C(Me)–CH₂CH₂–CH=CMe₂.
- The central CH₂CH₂ link is flanked by CH= on both sides, so the two halves join tail to tail.
- The chain has 24 carbons in the main chain plus 6 methyl branches, which gives 30 carbons in total.

I wrote the SMILES from memory of the standard squalene string rather than deriving every E/Z marker from the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=CCC/C(=C/CC/C(=C/CC/C=C(/CC/C=C(/CCC=C(C)C)\C)\C)/C)/C)C

name: Stavudine
text:
I read this as stavudine (d4T): a thymine ring joined through N1 to a 2′,3′‑didehydro‑2′,3′‑dideoxyribose ring.

- **Base:** a six‑membered ring with C5 carrying a methyl group, a C5=C6 double bond, N1 bonded to the sugar, C2=O, N3–H and C4=O.
- **Sugar:** a five‑membered ring containing O, C1′ (bonded to N1 by a wedge), a C2′=C3′ double bond, and C4′, which carries a wedged CH2OH group.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the chirality of each wedged centre by taking the implicit H as pointing away from the viewer and reading the order of the other three substituents on the page. This gives @ at C1′ and @@ at C4′ in the SMILES order below.

SMILES: CC1=CN([C@H]2C=C[C@@H](CO)O2)C(=O)NC1=O

name: Stevioside
text:
I identified this as stevioside, a steviol glycoside, and wrote the SMILES from memory of that compound's standard form rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I did check the connectivity against the drawing.

- **Aglycone:** the central core is the tetracyclic ent-kaurane skeleton of steviol. It has an exocyclic methylene (C=CH2) on the bridged ring, a methyl on the ring-fusion carbon, and a second methyl on the carbon that carries the carboxyl group.
- **Bridgehead check:** the oxygen-bearing carbon is bonded to the O, the ring CH2, the bridging CH2 and the C(=CH2) carbon. The bridging CH2 and the CH2 next to the methylene carbon both connect back to the same quaternary ring-fusion carbon. This matches the drawing.
- **Left side:** the C13 oxygen carries a glucose that bears a second glucose at its 2-position, forming a sophorosyl disaccharide.
- **Right side:** the carboxyl group forms an ester with a single glucose.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedge pattern is consistent with the natural stevioside configuration, but I did not re-derive each stereodescriptor from the image.

SMILES: C[C@@]12CCC[C@@]([C@H]1CC[C@]34[C@H]2CC[C@](C3)(C(=C)C4)O[C@H]5[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O5)CO)O)O)O[C@H]6[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O6)CO)O)O)O)(C)C(=O)O[C@H]7[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O7)CO)O)O)O

name: Stibophen
text:
The drawing shows an antimony(III) bis-catecholate complex, essentially stibophen: five sulfonate groups, five Na+ ions and six waters. I read it as follows.

**Components**
- Na+ appears three times at the top, plus two more at the right ("Na+Na+"), giving 5 Na+.
- H2O appears 6 times.
- Charges: five sulfonates (5−) plus one phenolate O− (1−) gives 6−, against 5 Na+. The Sb centre must therefore carry the balancing +1 charge in the intended formula, but as drawn Sb is neutral with no charge label. I follow the drawing and leave Sb uncharged.

**Right-hand ring (catechol bound to Sb through two O atoms)**
- Sb is bonded to O (top), O (bottom) and the O on the left ring.
- The ring atoms, with the two Sb-bound oxygens on adjacent carbons:
  - c1: carries O (top), fused
  - c2: carries O (bottom), fused
  - c3: CH
  - c4: C(SO3−)
  - c5: CH
  - c6: C(SO3−), attached to c1
- Written as SMILES: O1[Sb]...Oc2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c12

**Left ring**
- A phenolate carbon bears O−, with a sulfonate on the adjacent carbon.
- The next carbon bears the O–Sb link.
- The ring then continues through a CH, a carbon with a sulfonate, and a CH.
- Written as SMILES: c1(O[Sb])c([O-])c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c1

**Assembled SMILES**
[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].O.O.O.O.O.O.[O-]c1c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc1O[Sb]1Oc2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c2O1

Checking the left ring in this string: c1([O-]) is bonded to c(SO3) and to c1(O–Sb) at ring closure. The sequence is C(O−), C(SO3), CH, C(SO3), CH, C(OSb), which is 6 carbons, so the ring is consistent.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].O.O.O.O.O.O.[O-]c1c(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc1O[Sb]1Oc2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])c2O1

name: Stiripentol
text:
The drawing shows a benzodioxole (methylenedioxy-benzene) ring joined to a CH=CH unit, then a CH(OH) carbon, then a tert-butyl group. This is stiripentol.

The double bond is drawn with plain bonds, but its geometry is visible. The ring attachment at (667,741) goes to the vinyl carbon at (833,675), then to the next carbon at (975,783), then to the CH(OH) carbon at (1140,716). The ring substituent sits at the upper left and the CH(OH) group at the upper right of the bond, so the two substituents are on opposite sides of the double bond. The double bond is therefore trans (E), which matches stiripentol.

The CH(OH) carbon has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(O)/C=C/c1ccc2OCOc2c1

name: Stop
text:
The drawing shows a tin atom (Sn) bonded to two fluorine atoms (F), with a lone pair drawn as two dots beside Sn. This is tin(II) fluoride, SnF2. The lone pair is written in SMILES as a divalent tin with no hydrogens, `[Sn]`, so the two-fluorine form is F[Sn]F.

SMILES: F[Sn]F

name: Strontium Ranelate
text:
This is strontium ranelate: a thiophene ring carrying a nitrile, two carboxymethyl groups on N, a carboxylate and a CH2COO− group, with two Sr2+ counterions.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- S is bonded to C2 (the carbon bearing the N atom) and to C5 (the carbon bearing the COO−).
- C2 is double-bonded to C3, which carries the C≡N group.
- C3 is single-bonded to C4, which carries CH2COO−.
- C4 is double-bonded to C5, which carries COO−.

SMILES, written with the ring atoms in the order S–C5–C4–C3–C2:

[Sr+2].[Sr+2].[O-]C(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)c1sc(C([O-])=O)c(CC([O-])=O)c1C#N

Check: c1 (C2, with N) – s – c (C5, with the COO−) – c (C4, with CH2COO−) – c1 (C3, with C#N). The ring closes back to C2, so this is a valid thiophene. There are four carboxylates (4−) balanced by two Sr2+ (4+).

SMILES: [Sr+2].[Sr+2].[O-]C(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)c1sc(C([O-])=O)c(CC([O-])=O)c1C#N

name: Streptomycin
text:
The drawing shows streptomycin, so I wrote the SMILES from the known structure of that antibiotic rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges. I did not check every wedge and hash against the SMILES atom by atom.

The drawing matches streptomycin's three units:
- **Streptidine core:** a cyclohexane ring with two guanidine groups (N=C(N)N) and several hydroxyls, joined through an ether oxygen to the central sugar.
- **Streptose unit:** a five-membered ring containing O, with a methyl group, a tertiary C–OH carrying a CHO (aldehyde), and a glycosidic O linking it to the third unit.
- **N-methyl-glucosamine unit:** a pyranose ring bearing CH2OH, two OH groups and an NHCH3 group.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@@]([C@H]([C@@H](O1)O[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]2O)O)N=C(N)N)O)N=C(N)N)O[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H](O3)CO)O)O)NC)(C=O)O

name: Succinylcholine Chloride
text:
The drawing shows succinylcholine chloride, which I read as follows.

- Each end carries a trimethylammonium group, N⁺(CH3)3.
- Each nitrogen is joined to a CH2CH2 unit that leads to an ester oxygen.
- Each ester oxygen is bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), and the two carbonyls are linked by a CH2CH2 bridge, giving the succinate core.
- Two chloride ions, Cl⁻, are drawn as separate counterions.
- No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are shown, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CCOC(=O)CCC(=O)OCC[N+](C)(C)C.[Cl-].[Cl-]

name: Substance P
text:
This sequence reads as substance P, Arg-Pro-Lys-Pro-Gln-Gln-Phe-Phe-Gly-Leu-Met-NH2. It is a C-terminal primary amide with a free N-terminal arginine whose side chain ends in a guanidine group.

I assigned the stereocentres as the natural L-amino acids and did not check each wedge and hash against that assignment. The stereo marks on the SMILES below are written to give L-configuration at every residue.

name: Sucrose
text:
The drawing shows a disaccharide with two rings joined by a glycosidic oxygen.

- **Left ring:** a six-membered pyranose with a ring oxygen. It carries three OH groups and one CH2OH, so it is a glucose unit. Its anomeric carbon is linked through the bridging oxygen.
- **Right ring:** a five-membered furanose with a ring oxygen. Its anomeric carbon is quaternary, bearing the bridging O, a CH2OH and the ring oxygen. It also has one OH on the ring and one CH2OH on the other side of the ring, so it is a fructose unit.

Together these make sucrose, an α-D-glucopyranosyl β-D-fructofuranoside. I did not check each wedge and hash against the stereo descriptors one by one. I took the stereochemistry from the standard sucrose SMILES, on the assumption that the drawing is the natural isomer.

SMILES: C([C@@H]1[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)O[C@]2([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O2)CO)O)O)CO)O)O)O)O

name: Sufentanil
text:
This structure is a sufentanil-type molecule, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Thiophene:** The sulfur is bonded to two carbons. One is the ring carbon that carries the substituent, and it is double-bonded to the next ring carbon. The ring then continues through a second C=C and closes back to S.
- **Linker:** The thiophene C2 connects through a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** The ring has N plus five carbons. The carbon at position 4 is quaternary and carries both a CH2OCH3 group and an N(phenyl)C(=O)CH2CH3 group, a propanamide on a nitrogen that also bears the phenyl ring.
- **Stereochemistry:** No wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CCC(=O)N(c1ccccc1)C1(COC)CCN(CCc2cccs2)CC1

name: Succimer
text:
The drawing shows 2,3-dimercaptosuccinic acid: a four-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid (COOH) at each end and an SH group on each of the two middle carbons.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges:**
- The left stereocentre has a wedged SH, so its implicit H points away from the viewer. Its priorities are S > C3 > COOH. Going S → C3 → COOH from the front is clockwise, so this centre is R.
- The right stereocentre has a hashed SH, so its implicit H points toward the viewer. Its priorities are S > C2 > COOH. Going S → C2 → COOH is clockwise, and reversing for the H pointing toward the viewer gives S.
- The result is (R,S), the meso form.

**Writing the SMILES:** For `OC(=O)[C@@H](S)[C@@H](S)C(=O)O`, I worked out the chirality symbols from the neighbour order at each centre. The `@@` at the first centre gives R and the `@@` at the second gives S, matching the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@@H](S)[C@@H](S)C(=O)O

name: Sulfamethoxazole
text:
The drawing shows sulfamethoxazole, read as follows.

- The benzene ring carries an NH2 group at one end and an S(=O)(=O) group at the para position.
- The sulfonyl sulfur is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a ring carbon of the isoxazole.
- In the isoxazole, that carbon is double-bonded to N, and N is bonded to O.
- Going around the ring from O, the next atom is a carbon bearing a methyl group, then a CH, then back to the carbon attached to the sulfonamide NH.
- The ring double bonds are C=N and C=C (the methyl-bearing carbon to the CH), which matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1cc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(N)cc2)no1

name: Sulfasalazine
text:
This is sulfasalazine. The drawing shows three parts:

- A pyridin-2-yl group on the left, attached through NH to a sulfonyl group (S with two =O).
- A para-disubstituted benzene ring carrying the sulfonyl group and, on the opposite side, an azo group (N=N).
- A second benzene ring bearing the azo group, a hydroxyl and a carboxylic acid. The OH sits on the carbon next to the one carrying COOH, and the azo group is on the carbon para to the OH.

The drawing shows no cis/trans geometry for the azo bond, so I leave it unspecified.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(N=Nc2ccc(cc2)S(=O)(=O)Nc2ccccn2)ccc1O

name: Sulfathiazole
text:
This is sulfathiazole: a 4-aminobenzenesulfonamide whose sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the 2-position of a thiazole ring.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Benzene ring:** a six-membered ring with an NH2 group on one carbon and the sulfonyl group on the carbon opposite it (para).
- **Sulfonyl group:** a sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens, joined to the benzene ring and to an NH.
- **Thiazole ring:** the NH connects to the ring carbon that sits between S and N. That carbon is double-bonded to the ring N (C=N). The ring then runs N–CH=CH–S back to the carbon, giving a five-membered ring of S, C2, N, C, C.

SMILES: Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)NC1=NC=CS1

name: Sugammadex
text:
The drawing is a cyclodextrin with eight glucose units in the ring. Each unit carries a –CH2–S–CH2CH2–COOH group at C6, and I counted eight such sulfur chains. This matches the γ-cyclodextrin derivative sugammadex, a per-6-deoxy-6-(2-carboxyethylthio) γ-cyclodextrin.

I wrote the SMILES largely from recall of the sugammadex structure rather than deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I checked the connectivity (eight units, eight thioether acid chains) against the image. I did not verify the stereo descriptors centre by centre.

SMILES: C(CSC[C@@H]1[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)O[C@@H]3[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]3O)O)O[C@@H]4[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]4O)O)O[C@@H]5[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]5O)O)O[C@@H]6[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]6O)O)O[C@@H]7[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]7O)O)O[C@@H]8[C@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]8O)O)O[C@@H]9[C@H](O[C@H](O2)[C@@H]([C@H]9O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)CSCCC(=O)O)O)O)C(=O)O

name: Sulbactam
text:
The drawing shows sulbactam, a penicillanic acid sulfone: a β-lactam fused to a five-membered ring that contains the sulfone.

**Connectivity**
- A gem-dimethyl carbon is bonded to the sulfone sulfur (S(=O)=O) and to the carbon that carries the carboxylic acid (C(=O)OH).
- That carboxyl-bearing carbon is bonded to the ring nitrogen.
- The nitrogen is part of the four-membered β-lactam ring: N, C=O, CH2, and the ring-fusion CH.
- The ring-fusion CH is also bonded to the sulfur.

**Stereochemistry**
- The ring-fusion CH has a hashed H (pointing away from the viewer). Its other substituents are S (up), N (lower right) and CH2 (lower left). Viewed from the front, S → N → CH2 runs clockwise. In the SMILES atom order S, H, N, CH2 this is `[C@@H]`.
- The carboxyl-bearing carbon has a hashed COOH, so its implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the front, CMe2 → COOH → N runs clockwise. In the SMILES atom order N, H, CMe2, COOH this is `[C@H]`.

SMILES: CC1(C)S(=O)(=O)[C@@H]2CC(=O)N2[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: Sulfinpyrazone
text:
The drawing shows sulfinpyrazone: a pyrazolidine-3,5-dione ring with N,N'-diphenyl substitution and a 2-(phenylsulfinyl)ethyl chain on the C4 carbon.

- Ring: N1(Ph)–N2(Ph), with C3(=O) bonded to one N, C5(=O) bonded to the other, and C4 between the two carbonyl carbons.
- C4 carries a CH2CH2 chain ending in S(=O) attached to a phenyl ring.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn. The sulfoxide sulfur and C4 are stereocentres by connectivity, but they get no stereo marks.

SMILES: O=C1C(CCS(=O)c2ccccc2)C(=O)N(c2ccccc2)N1c1ccccc1

name: Sulfur Hexafluoride
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur atom (S) with six fluorine atoms (F) attached by single bonds. This is sulfur hexafluoride, SF6.

SMILES: FS(F)(F)(F)(F)F

name: spiramycin II
text:
I read the molecule as a 16-membered macrolide lactone carrying three sugars, and I wrote the SMILES by walking around the ring and assigning each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Macrolactone ring (16 atoms), in order:**
- The lactone carbonyl C(=O) is followed by a CH2.
- Next comes CH(OAc) with a hashed bond, then CH(OMe) with a wedge.
- Then CH(O-sugar) with a hashed bond, then CH(CH2CHO) with a hashed bond to the CH2CHO.
- A CH2 follows, then CH(CH3) with a hashed methyl, then CH(O-aminosugar) with a hashed bond.
- The diene is CH=CH–CH=CH, with both double bonds read as trans (E).
- A CH2 follows, then CH(CH3) with a hashed methyl, which bears the lactone oxygen and closes the ring.

**Sugars:**
- The sugar at the CH(O-sugar) position is a mycaminose-type pyranose carrying NMe2, an OH, and a ring methyl.
- At its 4-position it carries a mycarose-type 2,6-dideoxy pyranose with a tertiary C(CH3)(OH), a secondary OH and a ring methyl.
- The sugar on the left of the drawing is a forosamine-type tetrahydropyran carrying NMe2 and a ring methyl.

I checked the SMILES for balanced rings and branches, with the digits 1–4 each opened and closed once.

SMILES: O=C1C[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@H](OC)[C@@H](O[C@@H]2O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]3C[C@@](C)(O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)O3)[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H]2O)[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]4CC[C@H](N(C)C)[C@@H](C)O4)/C=C/C=C/C[C@@H](C)O1

name: Sulfuric Acid
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur atom with four oxygen substituents:
- Two oxygens are attached by double bonds (the doubled lines to the O at the top and the O at the bottom right).
- Two oxygens are attached by single bonds and carry hydrogens (OH at the upper right and HO at the lower left).

This is sulfuric acid. There are no charges and no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OS(=O)(=O)O

name: Sulpiride
text:
This structure is sulpiride: 5-(aminosulfonyl)-N-[(1-ethylpyrrolidin-2-yl)methyl]-2-methoxybenzamide.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Ethyl group:** a CH3–CH2 chain attached to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine ring:** five vertices, N plus four carbons. The carbon next to N carries the CH2 linker.
- **Linker and amide:** the CH2 leads to NH, then to C(=O), which attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** the carbonyl-bearing carbon has the OMe on the adjacent ring carbon. The SO2NH2 group sits on the ring carbon meta to the carbonyl carbon, which is the one next to the CH between the two substituted positions.
- **Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre in the pyrrolidine ring is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CCN1CCCC1CNC(=O)c1cc(S(N)(=O)=O)ccc1OC

name: Sumatriptan
text:
The drawing is sumatriptan: an indole with a 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl chain at C3 and a CH2-SO2-NHCH3 group at C5.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Dimethylamino chain:** the N bears two methyls and connects through two CH2 groups to the indole C3.
- **Pyrrole ring:** NH, then CH (C2) double-bonded to C3, which carries the chain. C3 joins the ring-fusion carbon C3a, which connects to the other fusion carbon C7a, and C7a is bonded back to NH.
- **Benzene ring:** C3a connects to the lower vertex (C4), then to C5, which carries the CH2SO2NHMe group. Next come C6 and C7, then C7a. The C7a=C3a bond is drawn as a double bond, and the double bonds at C4=C5 and C6=C7 complete the aromatic ring.
- **Sulfonamide:** CH2 is bonded to S, which has two =O and an NH–CH3.

SMILES: CNS(=O)(=O)Cc1ccc2[nH]cc(CCN(C)C)c2c1

name: Sunitinib
text:
The structure is sunitinib, which I read as follows:

- **Left side:** a diethylamino group (N with two ethyls) joined by a two-carbon chain to an amide NH, which is attached to a C=O.
- **Pyrrole ring:** the amide C=O sits on a 2,4-dimethylpyrrole (an NH ring with a methyl on each of two carbons).
- **Linker:** the pyrrole carbon next to the NH carries a CH= that forms an exocyclic double bond to C3 of the oxindole.
- **Oxindole:** a lactam (NH–C=O) fused to a benzene ring carrying one fluorine.
- **Double-bond geometry:** the pyrrole carbon on the CH and the lactam C=O carbon on the oxindole C3 lie on the same side of the C=C. That is the Z isomer, so I encoded it with `/` and `\` marks.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(/C=C2\C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc23)=C1C

name: Sulindac
text:
I read this as the sulindac skeleton: an indene core with a CH2COOH group, a methyl, a fluorine, and an exocyclic benzylidene bearing a para methylsulfinyl group.

- **Five-membered ring:** a C=C carries the methyl on one carbon and the CH2C(=O)OH group on the other. The ring is fused to a benzene ring, and the exocyclic carbon is attached at the ring fusion.
- **Fluorine:** it sits on the benzo ring, meta to the carbon that bears the CH2COOH-side ring fusion (one CH between them).
- **Exocyclic alkene:** it links the ring carbon to a CH that bears a para-substituted phenyl ring, and that phenyl carries S(=O)CH3.
- **Alkene geometry:** from the coordinates, the aryl group on the exocyclic CH lies on the same side as the benzo-ring carbon. It is therefore trans to the methyl-bearing carbon. I wrote the SMILES to match this drawn geometry rather than the literature configuration of sulindac.
- **Stereo notation:** with `/` on the ring-fusion carbon, the `\` after `C1=C` puts the aryl group cis to the benzo carbon.
- **Sulfoxide:** it is drawn with plain bonds, so I assigned no stereo to the sulfur.

SMILES: CC1=C(CC(=O)O)c2cc(F)ccc2/C1=C\c1ccc(S(C)=O)cc1

name: Suramin
text:
This drawing is suramin, a symmetric polysulfonated urea. I read it in three parts and joined them.

- **Terminal groups:** each end is a naphthalene bearing three sulfonic acids. The carbon carrying the amide NH is C8, and the SO3H groups sit at C1 (peri to the NH carbon), C3 and C5, giving an 8-aminonaphthalene-1,3,5-trisulfonic acid.
- **Middle units:** each naphthylamine is acylated by a 4-methylbenzoyl ring. The methyl carbon is adjacent to the ring carbon bearing the second NH, and the carbonyl-bearing carbon is meta to that NH carbon. That second NH is acylated by a meta-substituted benzoyl ring.
- **Centre:** the two meta-substituted benzoyl rings are joined through their ring carbons by a urea, NH–C(=O)–NH.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1NC(=O)c1cccc(NC(=O)Nc2cccc(c2)C(=O)Nc2cc(ccc2C)C(=O)Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)O)c3cc(S(=O)(=O)O)cc(S(=O)(=O)O)c23)c1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)O)c2cc(S(=O)(=O)O)cc(S(=O)(=O)O)c12

name: Sutezolid
text:
The drawing shows the thiomorpholine analogue of linezolid. I read it as follows:

- **Left side:** an acetamide, CH3–C(=O)–NH–CH2–.
- **Centre:** a 2-oxazolidinone ring. Its ring O sits next to the C=O carbon, which is bonded to the ring N. The stereocentre bears the CH2NHAc arm and the ring CH2 that leads to N.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring on the oxazolidinone N, with F ortho to the thiomorpholine nitrogen.
- **Right side:** a thiomorpholine ring (N, CH2, CH2, S, CH2, CH2) attached through its N.

For stereochemistry, the CH2NHAc bond at the oxazolidinone stereocentre is hashed, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are ring O, then the ring CH2 (attached to N), then the exocyclic CH2N, then H. Seen from the front, O (up) to ring CH2 (lower right) to exocyclic CH2N (lower left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S, as in linezolid. The SMILES neighbour order matches the standard linezolid SMILES, so `[C@H]` gives the same S configuration.

SMILES: CC(=O)NC[C@H]1CN(c2ccc(N3CCSCC3)c(F)c2)C(=O)O1

name: Suvorexant
text:
This molecule is suvorexant, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Left aryl ring:** a benzene ring carrying a 2H-1,2,3-triazol-2-yl group (N-linked) and a methyl group. The carbonyl-bearing carbon sits ortho to the triazole, and the methyl is para to the triazole.
- **Amide:** a C=O links this ring to a ring nitrogen of the central 1,4-diazepane.
- **Diazepane ring:** seven members, N–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH2–N–CH2–CH2. The methyl-bearing carbon is next to the amide nitrogen and carries the only wedge in the drawing, a bold wedge to the methyl.
- **Right side:** the other diazepane nitrogen is bonded to C2 of a 5-chlorobenzoxazole.
- **Stereochemistry:** the methyl is toward the viewer, so the hydrogen points away. Reading the substituents with the hydrogen away gives N, then ring CH2, then CH3, which runs clockwise in the drawing. That is the R configuration. I converted this to `[C@@H]` for the atom order written in the SMILES below.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CCN(c2nc3cc(Cl)ccc3o2)CCN1C(=O)c1cc(C)ccc1-n1nccn1

name: Tafamidis
text:
The drawing shows a benzoxazole core with a 3,5-dichlorophenyl group on C2 and a carboxylic acid on the benzo ring.

**Dichlorophenyl ring:** The ring attaches to the oxazole C2 at its lower-right vertex. Going around from there, the carbons are the attachment carbon, a CH at the top, a C–Cl at upper left, a CH at left, a C–Cl at lower left, and a CH at the bottom. The two Cl atoms therefore sit meta to the attachment point, which makes it a 3,5-dichlorophenyl group.

**Oxazole ring:** C2 is bonded to O and, through a double bond, to N. The ring then continues through C3a (bonded to N) and C7a (bonded to O).

**Benzo ring:** Its atoms are C7a (bonded to O), then C7 (top CH), then C6 (bearing COOH), then C5 (CH), C4 (CH), and C3a (bonded to N).

The COOH carbon attaches to the ring vertex at the right (1100,776). That vertex is adjacent to the top CH at (979,687), which in turn is adjacent to C7a at (839,747), the carbon bonded to O. So the acid sits on the carbon meta to C7a, which is position 6 of the benzoxazole (para to C3a–N).

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc2nc(oc2c1)-c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1

name: Tadalafil
text:
The image shows tadalafil, a β-carboline-fused piperazinedione. I read the structure in these parts:

- **Piperazinedione ring:** N-methyl (N-CH3), a CH2, and two C=O groups. One C=O is bonded to the ring N and the other to the stereocentre carbon.
- **Core:** the stereocentre carbon with a hashed H, then a CH2 leading to the indole C3. The indole NH and the fused benzene ring follow, and the indole C2 connects to the second stereocentre.
- **Second stereocentre:** it carries the 1,3-benzodioxole (methylenedioxyphenyl) group on a wedge bond.

For the stereochemistry, I worked out the chirality symbols from the 2D geometry of each centre:

- **C12a** has a hashed H, so the H sits behind the plane. Viewed from the front, N, then C=O, then CH2 runs clockwise. With neighbour order N, H, C(=O), CH2, this gives `[C@@H]`.
- **C6** has the aryl group on a wedge, with the implicit H behind. Viewed from the front, the order indole C, then N, then aryl runs counterclockwise. With neighbour order indole C, H, N (ring closure), aryl, this gives `[C@H]`.

I checked that the SMILES below is valid and accounts for every atom in the drawing.

SMILES: CN1CC(=O)N2[C@@H](C1=O)Cc1c([nH]c3ccccc13)[C@H]2c1ccc2OCOc2c1

name: Suzetrigine
text:
I read the molecule as a tetrahydrofuran core carrying four substituents, plus the two aromatic fragments:

- **Ring:** O1, C2, C3, C4 and C5.
- **C2:** a wedged amide, C(=O)NH, attached to the 4-position of a pyridine. The pyridine carries a primary carboxamide, C(N)=O, at its 2-position.
- **C3:** a hashed bond to a benzene ring. Going around that ring from the attachment carbon, the substituents are OMe, F, F, then H, H. So it is a 2-methoxy-3,4-difluorophenyl group.
- **C4:** a hashed methyl.
- **C5:** a wedged methyl and a CF3 group.

I assigned @/@@ at each of the four ring stereocentres from the wedge and hash drawing and the 2D positions of their neighbours. I checked the neighbour order in the SMILES against each centre. This was done by hand, not with a toolkit.

SMILES: C[C@@]1(C(F)(F)F)O[C@@H](C(=O)Nc2ccnc(C(N)=O)c2)[C@H](c2ccc(F)c(F)c2OC)[C@@H]1C

name: Talabostat
text:
I read the structure as Val-boroPro (talabostat): a valine residue joined by an amide to a pyrrolidine ring that carries a boronic acid, B(OH)₂, at C2.

**Skeleton**
- The left side is an isopropyl group (two CH₃ on one CH). That CH is bonded to the α-carbon, which carries NH₂ and a C(=O) group.
- The C(=O) is bonded to the ring nitrogen. The ring is N, CH₂, CH₂, CH₂, then the CH that bears B(OH)₂ (five atoms in all).

**Stereochemistry (two wedged centres)**
- The α-carbon has NH₂ on a hashed bond (pointing back), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order iPr, H, N, C(=O) gives `[C@H]`. This matches L-valine.
- The ring CH has a bold wedge to boron (pointing toward the viewer), so its H points back. Working through the neighbour order CH₂, H, N, B gives `[C@H]` when the ring is written as `N1CCC[C@H]1B(O)O`.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1B(O)O

name: Talinolol
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- A tert-butyl group (a carbon with three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- The NH connects to a CH2, then a CH(OH), then a CH2, then an O (ether).
- The ether O attaches to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- The opposite ring carbon bears an NH–C(=O)–NH urea linkage.
- The far NH is bonded to a cyclohexyl ring.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1ccc(NC(=O)NC2CCCCC2)cc1

name: Tafluprost
text:
I read the structure as tafluprost, an isopropyl ester prostaglandin analogue, and wrote the SMILES region by region.

- **Ester end:** an isopropyl group is attached through O to a C=O, followed by a chain of three CH2 groups.
- **Heptenoate chain:** a cis (Z) C=C leads to a CH2, which joins the cyclopentane at a carbon drawn with a hashed bond.
- **Cyclopentane ring:** five carbons carry, in order, the heptenoate chain (hashed), the vinyl side chain (wedge), an OH (hashed), a CH2, and a second OH (hashed).
- **Side chain on the ring:** a trans (E) CH=CH leads to a CF2 group, then CH2–O–phenyl (a phenoxy group).

I assigned the four ring stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds by working out each carbon's neighbour order in the SMILES. The Z and E double-bond geometries come directly from the drawing. I also checked the result against my recollection of tafluprost's (1R,2R,3R,5S) configuration.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@@H]1[C@@H](/C=C/C(F)(F)COc2ccccc2)[C@H](O)C[C@@H]1O

name: Sorangicin A
text:
I read the drawing as a 32-membered macrolactone with a 2-methyl-6-methyl-alkenoic acid side chain. I traced the ring atom by atom and then assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Ring and side chain**
- The side chain is HOOC‑(CH2)4‑CH(CH3)‑CH=C(CH3)‑, attached to a dihydropyran ring. That ring is C–O–C–CH=CH–C, and its last carbon carries the lactone oxygen.
- The lactone C(=O) leads into a conjugated triene, which runs into the bicyclic region at the lower right.
- Going the other way round the macrocycle from the dihydropyran: CH2, CH=CH, CH2, CH2, CH=CH, CH(OH), CH(OH).
- That chain ends in a tetrahydropyran ring (O, CH2, CH(OH), CH(CH3), two ring CH carbons). It continues through CH2 and CH=CH to the bicyclic region.

**Bicyclic region**
- It contains a THF ring and a six-membered ring that share a CH2 bridge, and one ring carbon bears a methyl.
- The long bond running from the upper ring carbon down to the lower one crosses other bonds, and the CH(CH3) carbon sits on it. I read that carbon as bonded to both ring carbons, which is the least certain part of the connectivity. Stereo at this bridged centre is also less certain.

**Double bonds (from drawn geometry)**
- The three chain double bonds are E.
- In the triene, the first two double bonds are Z and the last is E.
- The side-chain alkene is E.

The stereocentres were assigned from the wedge and hash bonds. I did not re-check the final string with a parser.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCC[C@@H](C)/C=C(C)/[C@@H]1O[C@@H]2C=C[C@@H]1OC(=O)/C=C\C=C/C=C/[C@H]5O[C@@H]6C[C@H]5O[C@H]([C@H]6C)/C=C/C[C@@H]8[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O8)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](O)/C=C/CC/C=C/C2

name: Talazoparib
text:
I read this as talazoparib, a tricyclic phthalazinone-fused core carrying two fluorine atoms. The SMILES below is built from that reading, with the stereocentres assigned from the drawn wedge and hash.

**Structure read from the image**
- **Triazole:** a 1-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-5-yl ring, with N-methyl at the top and its carbon attached to the core through a wedged bond.
- **Core:** a fused ring system containing a C=N–NH–C(=O) lactam (the phthalazinone part), an aromatic ring bearing one fluorine, and an NH in the ring that joins to the benzylic carbon.
- **Aryl group:** a 4-fluorophenyl ring attached to the carbon next to the ring NH, through a hashed bond.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Triazole-bearing carbon:** the triazole is wedged (towards the viewer), so the hydrogen points away. The neighbours in SMILES order (triazole, H, ring-closure carbon, C=N carbon) give `[C@H]`.
- **Aryl-bearing carbon:** the aryl is hashed (away), so the hydrogen points towards the viewer. The neighbours in SMILES order (N, H, ring-closure carbon, aryl) give `[C@@H]`.

I checked ring closures and the atom count against the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1ncnc1[C@H]1c2n[nH]c(=O)c3cc(F)cc(c23)N[C@@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1

name: Tamoxifen
text:
This structure is tamoxifen, read as follows:

- **Left end:** an N,N-dimethylamino group (N with two methyls) connected through a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2) to an oxygen.
- **Aryl ether:** that oxygen is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Alkene:** the para-substituted ring is bonded to one carbon of a C=C double bond. That carbon also carries an unsubstituted phenyl ring.
- **Other alkene carbon:** it carries an ethyl group and a second unsubstituted phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry:** the ethyl group and the unsubstituted phenyl on the far alkene carbon both point to the right, so they are cis. The aminoethoxyphenyl ring and the other phenyl ring are on the left side of the double bond.

By CIP priorities, the aminoethoxyphenyl ring outranks the plain phenyl on one carbon, and the phenyl outranks ethyl on the other. These two higher-priority groups are on the same side, so the double bond is Z.

SMILES: CC/C(=C(\c1ccccc1)c1ccc(OCCN(C)C)cc1)c1ccccc1

name: Tamsulosin
text:
This structure is tamsulosin, and the SMILES below is read from the drawing.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carries an ethoxy group (O–CH2–CH3) and, on the adjacent carbon, an O–CH2–CH2–NH chain.
- **Stereocentre:** the NH is attached to a CH that carries a methyl on a hashed bond and a CH2 leading to the second ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring is substituted with a methoxy group and, on the adjacent carbon, a sulfonamide (SO2NH2). The CH2 from the stereocentre is attached at the position para to the methoxy.

**Stereochemistry:** the hashed methyl points away from the viewer, so the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH2(aryl) > CH3 > H. Reading N → CH2 → CH3 on the page runs counterclockwise. Reversing this because H faces the viewer gives clockwise, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES written as `N[C@H](C)C`, the `@` symbol corresponds to R at this centre.

SMILES: CCOc1ccccc1OCCN[C@H](C)Cc1ccc(OC)c(S(N)(=O)=O)c1

name: Taniborbactam
text:
I read the drawing as a benzoxaborine core (a benzene ring fused to a six-membered ring containing O and B) carrying three substituents.

1. **Left chain:** H2N–CH2–CH2–NH– is attached to a cyclohexane ring. The ring's 1,4-position carries a CH2–C(=O)–NH– group, which links to the stereocentre of the core.
2. **Fused ring:** the ring runs C(H)(NHC=O)–CH2–aromatic C, then the aromatic C bearing the ring oxygen, then O, then B(OH), and back to the C(H).
3. **Aromatic ring:** a COOH sits on the aromatic carbon next to the one bearing the ring oxygen.
4. **Stereochemistry:** the C–N bond at the ring carbon next to boron is a wedge. The cyclohexane has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marks. Looking with the implicit H pointing away, N (wedge), CH2 and B run N → CH2 → B clockwise. Written as N[C@H]1C…B1, this corresponds to `[C@H]`.

SMILES: NCCNC1CCC(CC1)CC(=O)N[C@H]1Cc2cccc(C(=O)O)c2OB1O

name: Tapinarof
text:
The drawing shows a stilbene: a phenyl ring joined through a CH=CH bridge to a dihydroxy-isopropyl-substituted benzene ring.

**Substituted ring.** Starting from the carbon that carries the vinyl bridge, the ring runs: C(vinyl), CH, C(OH), C(iPr), C(OH), CH, back to the start. This is a 3,5-dihydroxy-4-isopropyl pattern, so the isopropyl group sits between the two OH groups.

**Alkene geometry.** The double bond is drawn with the two ring substituents on opposite sides, which is trans (E). The first ring attaches at the upper-left end of the double bond, at about (668, 697) leading to (830, 672). The bond then goes down to (935, 800), which connects onward to the phenyl at (1098, 774). The ring carbon sits to the left of the first alkene carbon and the phenyl to the right of the second, with one up and one down, so this is the zigzag trans arrangement.

**SMILES.** Writing the first ring, then the E double bond, then the phenyl: `CC(C)c1c(O)cc(/C=C/c2ccccc2)cc1O`

SMILES: CC(C)c1c(O)cc(/C=C/c2ccccc2)cc1O

name: Tartrazine
text:
The drawing shows tartrazine as drawn, in its azo/keto tautomer, with three Na+ counterions.

**Pyrazolone ring.** The five-membered ring is C(COO-)=N–N(Ar)–C(=O)–CH(N=N–Ar). The carbon bearing the azo group is an sp3 CH with no stereo shown.

**Substituents.** The azo group (N=N) is attached to a 4-sulfonatophenyl ring. The ring nitrogen is attached to a second 4-sulfonatophenyl ring. The carboxylate is on the ring carbon that is double-bonded to N.

**Counterions.** Three Na+ are drawn separately.

SMILES assembled from this reading:

[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[O-]C(=O)C1=NN(c2ccc(cc2)S(=O)(=O)[O-])C(=O)C1N=Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)[O-]

Check on the ring closure: C1(COO-)=N–N(Ar)–C(=O)–C1(H)(N=N...) closes correctly as a five-membered ring.

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[O-]C(=O)C1=NN(c2ccc(cc2)S(=O)(=O)[O-])C(=O)C1N=Nc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)[O-]

name: Tatb
text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with six substituents, alternating amino and nitro groups, which matches 1,3,5-triamino-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene (TATB).

Ring vertices as drawn:
- Top-left carbon: NH2
- Top-right carbon: NO2
- Right carbon: NH2
- Bottom-right carbon: NO2
- Bottom-left carbon: NH2
- Left carbon: NO2

Going around the ring, the substituents alternate NH2 and NO2, so the ring is fully substituted. Each nitro group is drawn in charge-separated form, N+(=O)O-.

The ring bonds are drawn as double bonds between top-left and top-right, between right and bottom-right, and between bottom-left and left, which is a valid Kekulé structure.

Writing the SMILES from the top-left carbon: C1(N)=C([N+](=O)[O-])C(N)=C([N+](=O)[O-])C(N)=C1[N+](=O)[O-]

Checking the ring bonds: C1=C (top-left to top-right), then C(N) single-bonded to the top-right carbon and double-bonded to the next carbon, C([N+]...), then C(N)=C1. This gives double bonds at top-left/top-right, right/bottom-right, and bottom-left/left, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C1(N)=C([N+](=O)[O-])C(N)=C([N+](=O)[O-])C(N)=C1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: Tapentadol
text:
I read this as tapentadol, the (R,R) isomer of 3-[1-(dimethylamino)-2-methylpentan-3-yl]phenol.

- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with an OH on one carbon and the side chain on the carbon two positions away (meta).
- **Side chain:** the ring carbon is attached to a stereocentre (C3) that carries an ethyl group on a bold wedge. C3 is bonded to a second stereocentre (C2) that carries a methyl on a hashed bond. C2 is bonded to a CH2–N(CH3)2 group.
- **C3 configuration:** the priorities are aryl > C2 > ethyl > H. With H pointing away, aryl → C2 → ethyl runs clockwise on the page, so C3 is R.
- **C2 configuration:** the priorities are CH2N > C3 > methyl > H. The methyl is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. CH2N → C3 → methyl runs counterclockwise on the page, which reverses to clockwise for the true view, so C2 is R.
- **SMILES chirality marks:** written as CC[C@H]([C@@H](C)CN(C)C)c1cccc(O)c1, the marks give R at C3 and R at C2, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CC[C@H]([C@@H](C)CN(C)C)c1cccc(O)c1

name: Taurine
text:
The drawing shows a sulfonic acid group (S bearing two =O and one OH) attached to a two-carbon chain that ends in NH2. This is 2-aminoethanesulfonic acid, which is taurine.

Reading the atoms in order: NH2 is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to a second CH2, which is bonded to S. The S carries two double-bonded O atoms and one OH. There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: NCCS(=O)(=O)O

name: Tavaborole
text:
The image shows a benzoxaborole: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing B, O and CH2, with an OH on boron and a fluorine on the benzene ring.

**Atoms and bonds**
- The five-membered ring is B, O, CH2 and the two fused aromatic carbons.
- B carries an OH and is bonded to the aromatic carbon at about (617, 655).
- CH2 at (510, 1070) is bonded to the aromatic carbon at (713, 902).
- The benzene ring runs: C1 (617, 655, attached to B), C2 (780, 449), C3 (1043, 487), C4 (1140, 734, attached to F), C5 (975, 940), C6 (713, 902, attached to CH2).
