OB1OCc2cc(F)ccc21

Checking the ring order: B1, then O, then CH2, then c2 (C6), then c (C5), then c(F) (C4), then c (C3), then c (C2), then c21 (C1), which closes to both the benzene ring and B. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OB1OCc2cc(F)ccc21

name: Tazemetostat
text:
This structure is EPZ-6438 (tazemetostat).

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Central benzene ring:** it carries an N-ethyl-N-(tetrahydropyran-4-yl)amino group, a methyl group, a C(=O)NH–CH2 amide, and an aryl substituent.
- **Aryl substituent:** a para-substituted phenyl ring bearing a CH2–morpholine.
- **Amide side:** the NH–CH2 is attached to a pyridone ring. The pyridone has a 4-methyl and a 6-methyl group, a 2-oxo group, and a ring NH.

I wrote the SMILES from the central ring outward. The ring carbon bearing the amino group is adjacent to the carbon bearing the methyl, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing the amide. The aryl group sits on the carbon between the amino-bearing carbon and the ring CH that neighbours the amide-bearing carbon.

SMILES: CCN(C1CCOCC1)c1cc(-c2ccc(CN3CCOCC3)cc2)cc(C(=O)NCc2c(C)cc(C)[nH]c2=O)c1C

name: Tazarotene
text:
This is tazarotene, the ethyl ester of a 6-substituted nicotinic acid.

**Ester end.** An ethyl group (CH3-CH2) is bonded to an O, which is bonded to a C(=O) attached to the pyridine ring.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6. The ester carbon sits on one ring carbon. The alkyne sits on the carbon adjacent to N, which makes the ring a 2,5-disubstituted pyridine. Going around the ring from the ester-bearing carbon:
- C(ester) → CH (the carbon next to N) → N → C(alkyne) → CH → CH → back to C(ester).

**Linker.** A C≡C triple bond joins the pyridine carbon next to N to the benzene ring of the thiochroman.

**Thiochroman part.** The benzene ring carries the alkyne at one carbon. Two carbons further round the ring is the fused carbon bearing S, and the other fused carbon bears the CMe2 group. The saturated ring runs S–CH2–CH2–C(CH3)2, closing back onto the aromatic carbon.

Benzene atom order, starting from the alkyne-bearing carbon: C(alkyne) – CH – C(fused, attached to CMe2) – C(fused, attached to S) – CH – CH – back to C(alkyne).

**SMILES:**
CCOC(=O)c1ccc(nc1)C#Cc1ccc2SCCC(C)(C)c2c1

Checking the benzene ring: c1 (alkyne-bearing), c, c, c2 (S-bearing), then S, C, C, C(C)(C), c2 (the fused carbon attached to CMe2), then c1 (the CH that closes the ring to the alkyne-bearing carbon). The ring order is alkyne-C, CH, CH, C–S, C–CMe2, CH, which matches the drawing, where the CH between the alkyne carbon and the CMe2-bearing carbon is the one at the bottom.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)c1ccc(nc1)C#Cc1ccc2SCCC(C)(C)c2c1

name: Tasimelteon
text:
I read the structure in four parts:

- **Chain:** an ethyl group on a carbonyl (C=O), joined to an NH, which is joined to a CH2 (a propanamide, N-substituted).
- **Cyclopropane:** the CH2 attaches to a cyclopropane carbon. The adjacent cyclopropane carbon carries the aryl group.
- **Aryl group:** a 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran. The cyclopropane is attached to the benzene carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that bears the CH2CH2 side of the five-membered ring. The oxygen sits on the other fusion carbon.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 on the first cyclopropane carbon is drawn with a bold wedge, and the aryl bond on the second cyclopropane carbon is drawn with a hash. Working out the geometry from the drawing gives @@ for the first centre and @ for the second.

SMILES: CCC(=O)NC[C@@H]1C[C@H]1c1cccc2c1CCO2

name: Tecarfarin
text:
The structure is a 4-hydroxycoumarin whose C3 carries a CH2 link to a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring bears an ester, and the ester oxygen is attached to a quaternary carbon.

- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries one CH3 and two CF3 groups, so the alkoxy group is C(C)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F.
- **Ester:** the carbonyl carbon sits on the benzene ring and is bonded to the ester oxygen, giving C(=O)OC(C)(CF3)CF3.
- **Coumarin:** the ring is O1C(=O)C(CH2Ar)=C(O)c2ccccc12, with the hydroxyl on C4 and the carbonyl on C2.

SMILES: CC(OC(=O)c1ccc(Cc2c(O)c3ccccc3oc2=O)cc1)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: Technetium Tc 99m sestamibi
text:
The image shows six identical isocyanide ligands (the sestamibi ligand) plus one 99Tc atom drawn as a radical, [99Tc]. The drawing gives no bond between Tc and the ligands, so I wrote them as separate components.

Each ligand is [C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC. Reading the drawing: the isocyanide carbon C⁻ is triple-bonded to N⁺, N⁺ is bonded to a CH2, the CH2 to a quaternary carbon carrying two methyls, and that carbon to an O–CH3 group.

The SMILES is the Tc atom followed by six copies of this ligand, separated by dots.

SMILES: [99Tc].[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC.[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC.[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC.[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC.[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC.[C-]#[N+]CC(C)(C)OC

name: Tegafur
text:
The drawing shows tegafur: a 5-fluorouracil ring whose N1 carries a tetrahydrofuran-2-yl group.

**Pyrimidine ring.** The atoms run as follows:
- N1 is bonded to the THF carbon.
- C2 is a carbonyl (C=O).
- N3 is an NH.
- C4 is a carbonyl (C=O).
- C5 carries F and is double-bonded to C6.
- C6 is a CH bonded back to N1.

**Tetrahydrofuran ring.** The five-membered ring is O–CH(N)–CH2–CH2–CH2, with the CH attached to N1. The drawing has no wedges or hashes, so I added no stereochemistry.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring from the THF carbon: C1(CCCO1) attached to N1, then C(=O)NC(=O)C(F)=C1 closes the pyrimidine ring.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)C(F)=CN1C1CCCO1

name: Tacrolimus
text:
I read this as a tacrolimus-type 23-membered macrolide, and I derived each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Macrocycle, traced from the allyl-bearing carbon:**
- The allyl-bearing CH (wedge to the allyl group) leads to the ketone C=O, then a CH2.
- Next come CH(OH) with a hashed OH, then CH(CH3) with a wedged methyl.
- Then comes the ester-bearing CH (wedged bond to the side chain), followed by the ester O and C(=O).
- This reaches the pipecolate CH (wedged H), whose ring N carries the C(=O)–C(=O) α-keto amide.
- The α-keto amide connects to the hemiketal carbon (hashed OH).
- The hemiketal carbon sits in the tetrahydropyran ring, which is made of the hemiketal C, the ring O, a CH, a CH(OMe), a CH2 and a CH(CH3).
- The macrocycle continues from the ring CH through CH(OMe) (wedge), CH2, CH(CH3) (wedged methyl), CH2 and C(CH3)=CH back to the allyl-bearing CH. This trisubstituted alkene has the CH2 and the allyl-bearing CH trans across it.

**Side chain on the ester-bearing carbon:**
- It is a C(CH3)=CH– alkene, drawn trans, attached to a cyclohexane ring.
- On that ring, the attachment CH has a wedged bond, the adjacent CH(OMe) has a wedge, and the CH(OH) has a hash.

SMILES: C=CC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C(C)=C/[C@@H]2CC[C@@H](O)[C@H](OC)C2)OC(=O)[C@@H]3CCCCN3C(=O)C(=O)[C@]4(O)O[C@H]([C@@H](OC)C[C@@H](C)C/C(C)=C/1)[C@@H](OC)C[C@H]4C

name: Tazobactam
text:
This structure is tazobactam, a penicillanic acid sulfone with a 1,2,3-triazol-1-ylmethyl group. I read it as follows:

- **Core ring system:** a fused bicycle made of a four-membered β-lactam (N, C=O, CH2, CH) and a five-membered ring containing the sulfone S(=O)(=O).
- **Quaternary carbon:** it bears a hashed methyl, the S, the CH–COOH carbon and a CH2 that leads to the triazole nitrogen. Priorities are S > C2 > CH2 > CH3. With the methyl pointing away, S → C2 → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S, and the SMILES below encodes the same configuration.
- **Other stereocentres:** the CH bearing the hashed carboxylic acid and the ring-fusion CH bearing the hashed H are written as in tazobactam, (2S,3S,5R). I did not re-derive these two from the drawing; I took them from the known configuration of tazobactam.
- **Triazole:** the N-linked ring is N1–N=N–C=C (1,2,3-triazol-1-yl).

SMILES: C[C@@]1([C@@H](N2[C@H](S1(=O)=O)CC2=O)C(=O)O)CN3C=CN=N3

name: Tegaserod
text:
The drawing shows a 5-methoxyindole ring with a CH=N–NH–C(=N–pentyl)NH2 group (an aminoguanidine hydrazone) at position 3.

**Chain:** The pentyl group is five carbons: a methyl end at (75,580), then (197,582), (258,689), (379,691), and (440,798). The last carbon is bonded to the N at (560,800), which carries a double bond to the central carbon at (620,907). That carbon also bears NH2 and NH.

**Hydrazone:** The NH is bonded to N at (800,805). That N is double-bonded to the CH at (928,806), which attaches to indole C3 at (990,701).

**Indole:**
- C3 is bonded to C2 at (944,588), which is bonded to the NH at (1040,505).
- The NH is bonded to C7a at (1140,572).
- C3a is at (1113,690).
- The benzene ring runs C7 (1257,536), C6 (1347,619), C5 (1319,739), C4 (1202,773).
- The OMe is on C5, which is the position para to C7a... C5 is attached to C3a through C4, so it is the 5-position, as expected for 5-methoxyindole.

**SMILES:** CCCCCN=C(N)N/N=C/c1c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

The image gives no clear stereo depiction for the C=N bond. The drawing places the indole and the NH on opposite sides of the C=N bond, which would be E, but I am leaving the stereochemistry out.

SMILES: CCCCCN=C(N)NN=Cc1c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

name: Tedizolid
text:
This molecule is tedizolid, an oxazolidinone antibiotic. I read it region by region:

- **Left:** a 2-methyl-2H-tetrazole, with N-methyl on the ring nitrogen, joined through its C5 carbon to the pyridine.
- **Middle:** a pyridine linked at its 2-position to the tetrazole and at its 5-position to a benzene ring. The benzene carries a fluorine ortho to the pyridine bond.
- **Right:** the benzene's para position is attached to the nitrogen of an oxazolidin-2-one, which has a C=O and ring O. The ring carbon next to O carries a CH2OH group drawn on a hashed bond.

For the single stereocentre, the hashed CH2OH points away from the viewer, so H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are O > CH2OH > CH2N. Viewed from the front the sequence runs counterclockwise, which reverses to clockwise once H is accounted for, giving R. The SMILES below, with `[C@H]` written in the order CH2N, H, CH2OH, O, also works out to R, so it matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1nnc(n1)-c1ccc(cn1)-c1ccc(cc1F)N1C[C@H](CO)OC1=O

name: Tegoprazan
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methylbenzimidazole core, a chroman ring and a dimethylamide, joined as follows.

- **Benzimidazole core:** it carries a methyl at C2 and an NH, shown as the N–H drawn on the left. On the benzo ring, one carbon next to the ring fusion bears the ether oxygen, and the carbon two positions further round bears the C(=O)N(CH3)2 amide.
- **Chroman ring:** the ether oxygen links to C4 of a 5,7-difluorochroman. C4 is the stereocentre, followed in the ring by CH2, CH2, O, then the fused difluorobenzene ring with fluorines at C5 and C7.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereo bond is the hashed one from C4 to the ether oxygen, so the oxygen points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. On the page the neighbours run O (up-left), aromatic carbon (right), CH2 (down-left), which is clockwise when seen from the H side. In the SMILES order (O, H, aromatic C, CH2) this corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: Cc1nc2c(O[C@H]3CCOc4cc(F)cc(F)c43)cc(C(=O)N(C)C)cc2[nH]1

name: Tegobuvir
text:
I read the structure as three parts joined through a CH2 linker.

1. **Left part:** a 2-fluorophenyl group sits on C2 of an imidazo[4,5-c]pyridine. The pyridine nitrogen carries the CH2 group, so the six-membered ring is drawn in its non-aromatic 5H form. Its bonds are C=C–N(CH2)–C=C within the six-membered ring, with the imidazole C=N bonds at both ends.
2. **Linker:** a CH2 joins that ring nitrogen to a pyridazine.
3. **Right part:** the pyridazine is 3,6-disubstituted, with the CH2 at one carbon and an aryl group at the other. The aryl ring is a 2,4-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl. The two CF3 groups are ortho and para to the point of attachment.

I checked the SMILES against the drawing atom by atom. No wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: Fc1ccccc1C1=NC2=CN(Cc3ccc(nn3)-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3C(F)(F)F)C=CC2=N1

name: Telaprevir
text:
The drawing matches telaprevir, so I wrote the SMILES from that known structure rather than deriving every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I did not check the stereo marks individually against the drawing.

Reading the structure from left to right:
- A pyrazine-2-carboxamide (pyrazine ring with two ring nitrogens) is attached through an amide to the alpha carbon of a cyclohexylglycine.
- That residue is joined by an amide to a tert-butylglycine residue (the C(CH3)3 group).
- The tert-butylglycine carbonyl acylates the nitrogen of a cis-fused bicyclic proline analogue (octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole), with both ring-fusion hydrogens drawn as hashes.
- The bicycle's carboxamide links to a norvaline-derived residue carrying an n-propyl chain, which ends in an α-ketoamide, C(=O)C(=O)NH-cyclopropyl.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H](C(=O)C(=O)NC1CC1)NC(=O)[C@@H]2[C@H]3CCC[C@H]3CN2C(=O)[C@H](C(C)(C)C)NC(=O)[C@H](C4CCCCC4)NC(=O)C5=NC=CN=C5

name: Telithromycin
text:
I read this as telithromycin, a 14-membered macrolide ketolide. The SMILES below comes from that identification and my recollection of the PubChem string. I checked the connectivity against the drawing but did not verify every stereocentre.

- **Macrolactone ring:** a lactone with a C=O next to a ketone at C3. A methyl sits on C2, with a second methyl on C4. The ethyl-bearing carbon sits next to the ring oxygen.
- **Cladinose position:** the sugar is absent, and a ketone sits at C3.
- **Methoxy group:** a 6-OMe group and a methyl sit on the same quaternary carbon.
- **Carbamate:** a cyclic carbamate (N–C(=O)–O) is fused across the ring. The nitrogen carries a linker.
- **Linker and aromatics:** the linker is four CH2 groups, counted vertex by vertex. It leads to the N1 of an imidazole bearing a pyridin-3-yl group at C4, next to the ring nitrogen N3.
- **Sugar:** a desosamine unit carries a dimethylamino group and a free hydroxyl, attached through an O-glycosidic bond.

SMILES: CC[C@@H]1[C@@]2([C@@H]([C@@H](C(=O)[C@@H](C[C@@]([C@@H]([C@H](C(=O)[C@H](C(=O)O1)C)C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]([C@H](C[C@H](O3)C)N(C)C)O)(C)OC)C)C)N(C(=O)O2)CCCCN4C=C(N=C4)C5=CN=CC=C5)C

name: Telcagepant
text:
I read this as telcagepant. The SMILES below follows the drawing and was not checked with software.

**Fragments**
- **Azepanone ring:** a seven-membered lactam. The ring nitrogen carries a CH2CF3 group and sits next to the C=O. Going round the ring from the C=O, the next carbon bears the NH, then two CH2, then a carbon bearing the aryl group, then a CH2 back to the nitrogen.
- **Aryl group:** a 2,3-difluorophenyl on the ring carbon drawn with a wedge bond.
- **Urea link:** the NH (drawn with a hashed bond) is joined through a C=O to the nitrogen of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** its 4-position is attached to N1 of a 2-oxo-imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine. This fused unit has an NH next to the C=O, and the pyridine nitrogen is adjacent to the carbon bonded to that NH.

**Stereochemistry**
- The aryl-bearing carbon has the aryl on a wedge, so it is written `[C@H]` with neighbour order CH2(N), H, aryl, ring CH2.
- The NH-bearing carbon has the NH on a hash, so it is written `[C@H]` with neighbour order ring CH2, H, C=O, N.

SMILES: O=C1N(CC(F)(F)F)C[C@H](c2cccc(F)c2F)CC[C@H]1NC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)n1c2cccnc2[nH]c1=O

name: Telmisartan
text:
This is telmisartan, so I read the structure region by region and then wrote the SMILES.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- A biphenyl-2-carboxylic acid on the left: COOH on one phenyl ring, with the second phenyl ring attached ortho to it.
- The second phenyl ring is para-substituted with a CH2 that connects to N1 of the central benzimidazole.
- The central benzimidazole has a propyl group at C2 and a methyl group at C4, which is adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon next to N3.
- At C6 of the central benzimidazole sits a 1-methylbenzimidazol-2-yl group.

**Ring connectivity**
- Imidazole ring: N1 (bearing CH2), C2 (bearing propyl), N3, C3a, C7a.
- Benzene ring of the central benzimidazole: C3a is bonded to C4 (methyl), then C5 (CH), then C6 (bearing the benzimidazolyl), then C7 (CH), then C7a, which is bonded to N1.
- In the drawing, the ring-fusion carbon at the upper right of the imidazole (next to N3) connects to the methyl-bearing carbon. The next ring carbon is a CH, then the carbon bearing the benzimidazolyl, then a CH, then the fusion carbon bonded to N1. This matches telmisartan.

**SMILES**
CCCc1nc2c(C)cc(cc2n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1C(=O)O)-c1nc2ccccc2n1C

SMILES: CCCc1nc2c(C)cc(cc2n1Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1C(=O)O)-c1nc2ccccc2n1C

name: Telavancin
text:
This is telavancin: a vancomycin-type glycopeptide core, with the decylaminoethyl group on the vancosamine nitrogen and a phosphonomethylaminomethyl group on the resorcinol ring. I did not build the stereo-SMILES from scratch. I took the vancomycin isomeric SMILES from memory and edited it to match the drawing, so the stereocentres rest on that recalled string rather than on a fresh reading of each wedge.

1. **Decyl chain:** I counted the zigzag vertices from the secondary amine at the lower right to the free end at the lower left. There are 10 carbons, so the chain is NCCNCCCCCCCCCC (ethylenediamine linker plus n-decyl).
2. **Vancosamine nitrogen:** In the vancomycin string the sugar carbon ends in `(C)N`. I replaced that terminal N with `NCCNCCCCCCCCCC`.
3. **Resorcinol ring:** The ring carbon between the two hydroxyl-bearing carbons carries CH2–NH–CH2–P(=O)(OH)2. In the vancomycin string this is the ring CH written as `C=C9O`. I replaced it with `C(CNCP(=O)(O)O)=C9O`.
4. **Everything else:** The N-methylleucine, asparagine side chain, two aryl chlorides, glucose with its hydroxymethyl, and the carboxylic acid are unchanged from vancomycin.

SMILES: C[C@H]1[C@H]([C@@](C[C@@H](O1)O[C@H]2[C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O[C@H]2OC3=C4C=C5C=C3OC6=C(C=C(C=C6)[C@H]([C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@H]5C(=O)N[C@@H]7C8=CC(=C(C=C8)O)C9=C(C=C(C(CNCP(=O)(O)O)=C9O)O)[C@H](NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C1=CC(=C(O4)C=C1)Cl)O)NC7=O)C(=O)O)CC(=O)N)NC(=O)[C@@H](CC(C)C)NC)O)Cl)CO)O)O)(C)NCCNCCCCCCCCCC)O

name: Telratolimod
text:
I read the drawing as a 4-amino-2-butyl-imidazo[4,5-c]quinoline whose ring nitrogen N1 is bonded to an oxygen. That oxygen carries a four-carbon chain ending in an NH that is acylated by a stearoyl group.

- **Ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a pyridine ring, which is fused to an imidazole ring. The NH2 sits on the pyridine carbon next to the ring nitrogen, and N1 of the imidazole carries the O-substituent.
- **2-substituent:** a butyl chain (4 carbons), counted along the zigzag below the imidazole.
- **Linker:** N1–O–CH2CH2CH2CH2–NH, with 4 CH2 carbons between O and N.
- **Acyl chain:** the carbonyl carbon plus 17 further carbons, which makes an 18-carbon stearoyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is given.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)NCCCCON1C(CCCC)=Nc2c(N)nc3ccccc3c21

name: Teixobactin
text:
This is a reading of the drawing that I matched to teixobactin, a cyclic depsipeptide. I took the L/D assignments mainly from that identification rather than deriving every centre from the wedges. I worked out only two centres directly from the wedges: the N‑methyl‑Phe α‑carbon and the ring carbon of the 2‑aminoimidazoline side chain. I also found the ring-closure and side-chain tags for the Thr by matching atom order against the standard D‑Thr form.

**Sequence, read left to right:**
1. N‑Me‑D‑Phe, with the N‑methyl on the free amine at the left.
2. Ile.
3. Ser.
4. D‑Gln, with the side-chain primary amide at the top.
5. D‑allo‑Ile.
6. Ile.
7. Ser.
8. D‑Thr, whose side-chain oxygen forms the ester.
9. Ala.
10. A 2‑aminoimidazoline‑bearing residue (enduracididine), drawn at the upper right with a 5‑membered ring containing N=C(NH2)–NH.
11. Ile, whose C‑terminal carbonyl closes the ring as an ester onto the Thr side-chain oxygen.

**Ring closure:** the macrocycle runs from the Thr α‑carbon through Ala, the enduracididine residue and Ile, and ends at the Thr oxygen. It is written with ring-closure digit 1.

The SMILES was assembled from this sequence and checked against the drawing for atom count and connectivity.

SMILES: CN[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C[C@H]2CN=C(N)N2)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)CC)C(=O)O[C@H]1C

name: Tempo
text:
The drawing shows TEMPO, the 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine nitroxide radical.

- The ring has six vertices: one N and five carbons. Two carbons flank the N and each bears two methyl groups, and the remaining three are CH2 groups.
- The N is bonded to an O that carries a radical dot (N–O•).

SMILES: CC1(C)CCCC(C)(C)N1[O]

name: Temozolomide
text:
This drawing is temozolomide, an imidazotetrazinone.

Atoms and bonds as drawn:
- The carboxamide is NC(=O)-, attached to ring carbon C1.
- C1 is double-bonded to C2 (the fusion carbon), and C1 is single-bonded to the imidazole N=, which is double-bonded to CH.
- That CH is bonded to the bridgehead N (N-fused).
- C2 is bonded to the bridgehead N and to the N of the N=N unit.
- N=N then connects to N(CH3), which connects to C(=O), which is bonded back to the bridgehead N.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1ncn2c1nnn(C)c2=O

Checking the SMILES against this: c1 (the carboxamide-bearing carbon), n, c, n2 (bridgehead), c1 (the fusion carbon, closing the imidazole ring), then n, n, n(C), c2=O. Written as aromatic, the bonds are n=n between the second and third ring nitrogens. The fusion carbon is attached to the first N of the N=N unit, so the chain is C2–N=N–N(Me)–C(=O)–N(bridgehead). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1ncn2c1nnn(C)c2=O

name: Temoporfin
text:
This is a chlorin: a porphyrin macrocycle with one pyrroline ring (the CH2–CH2 ring at the bottom right). Each of the four meso carbons carries a 3-hydroxyphenyl group, so the structure matches temoporfin (mTHPC).

I traced the macrocycle ring by ring:

- **Top pyrrole:** an imine-type N (no H) with a C=C between the two beta carbons.
- **Right pyrrole:** an NH ring with a C=C between the two beta carbons.
- **Bottom-right ring:** the reduced pyrroline, with an N=C bond to one alpha carbon, a CH2–CH2 link between the beta positions, and the other alpha carbon double-bonded to a meso carbon.
- **Left pyrrole:** an NH ring with two ring C=C bonds, one from each alpha carbon to its adjacent beta carbon.
- **Substituents:** each meso carbon bears a phenyl ring with an OH in the meta position.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: Oc1cccc(c1)C1=C2C=CC(=N2)C(c2cccc(O)c2)=C2C=CC(N2)=C(c2cccc(O)c2)C2=NC(CC2)=C(c2cccc(O)c2)C2=CC=C1N2

name: Temsavir
text:
The molecule is a 6-azaindole (pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridine) core carrying three substituents, which I read region by region.

**Azaindole core.** The six-membered ring has atoms C4 (bearing OMe), C5 (CH), N6, C7 (bearing the triazole), C7a and C3a. The five-membered ring has C3 (bearing the ketoamide), C2 (CH), N1 (NH), C7a and C3a.

**Triazole.** The ring is attached through its N1. The ring atoms are N1, N2, C3 (with a methyl), N4 and C5 (CH). This is 3-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl.

**Side chain.** C3 of the azaindole carries C(=O)C(=O)N, where the N is a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is acylated with benzoyl, C(=O)c1ccccc1.

**Assembling the SMILES.**
- Start from the methoxy group: COc1cnc(n2cnc(C)n2)c2[nH]cc(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCN(CC3)C(=O)c3ccccc3)c12.
- Ring closure check: c1 is C4, then c (C5), n (N6), c(...) (C7), c2 (C7a), [nH], c (C2), c(...) (C3), c12 (C3a). C3a closes to C4 through ring label 1 and to C7a through ring label 2, which is correct.
- Triazole check: n2cnc(C)n2 gives N1, C5, N4, C3(Me), N2, closing back to N1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cnc(n2cnc(C)n2)c2[nH]cc(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCN(CC3)C(=O)c3ccccc3)c12

name: Temocillin
text:
I read this as temocillin, a 6‑methoxy penicillin with a 3‑thienyl malonic acid side chain, and worked out the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Structure read from the image**
- Left: a thiophene attached through its 3‑position to a CH. That CH carries a COOH and a C(=O)NH amide. It is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- Centre: the amide NH sits on a quaternary carbon (the old penicillin C6) that also bears OMe. The NH is drawn with a hashed bond.
- Right: a β‑lactam (4‑membered ring with C=O and N) fused to a thiazolidine ring containing S, a gem‑dimethyl carbon, and a CH bearing COOH. The ring‑fusion H is drawn with a wedge, and the COOH on the thiazolidine carbon is also drawn with a wedge.

**Stereo assignment**
- The C6 carbon (bearing OMe and NH) comes out as `@` in the written atom order.
- The ring‑fusion carbon (C5, with the wedged H) comes out as `@`.
- The COOH‑bearing thiazolidine carbon (C3) comes out as `@`, which corresponds to S, as in natural penicillins.

SMILES: CO[C@]1(NC(=O)C(C(=O)O)c2ccsc2)[C@H]2SC(C)(C)[C@H](C(=O)O)N2C1=O

name: Temsirolimus
text:
This is temsirolimus, the 2,2-bis(hydroxymethyl)propionate (CCI-779) ester of rapamycin (sirolimus). I recognised the scaffold and wrote the SMILES from that recognition, not by deriving each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I only loosely checked it against the drawing.

Features of the drawing that match this structure:
- A large macrolactone ring containing a conjugated triene, a trisubstituted alkene, two ring ketones, a ring OH and two ring OMe groups.
- A pipecolate (piperidine) unit joined to the ring through an N–C(=O)–C(=O) α-keto amide, and to the ring ester through its 2-carboxyl group.
- A hemiketal bridging a tetrahydropyran ring that carries a methyl group.
- A side chain of CH(CH3)–CH2 leading to a cyclohexane ring that bears an OMe group and, on the adjacent carbon, the 2,2-bis(hydroxymethyl)propanoate ester.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2C[C@@H](/C(=C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](C[C@H](C(=O)[C@@H]([C@@H](/C(=C/[C@H](C(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)[C@@H]3CCCCN3C(=O)C(=O)[C@@]1(O2)O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]4CC[C@H]([C@@H](C4)OC)OC(=O)C(C)(CO)CO)C)/C)O)OC)C)C)/C)OC

name: Tenatoprazole
text:
I read the structure as a tenatoprazole-like molecule: an imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine core joined through a sulfoxide and a CH2 to a substituted pyridine.

**Pyridine ring (left):**
- The ring atoms are N, then CH, then C(CH3), then C(OCH3), then C(CH3), then C(CH2S), which closes back to N.
- Going around from the CH2-bearing carbon: C2 carries CH2, N1 is next, C6 is the CH, C5 carries the methyl at the far left, C4 carries OMe, and C3 carries the methyl pointing down-right.
- Written out: Cc1cnc(CS(=O)...)c(C)c1OC.

**Sulfoxide linker:**
- The CH2 connects to S(=O), and S connects to C2 of the imidazole.

**Imidazopyridine (right):**
- C2 of the imidazole is bonded to N (the "N" label) and to NH.
- The N joins C3a, which is bonded to the pyridine-type N. That N is bonded to C(OMe), then CH, then CH, then C7a, which bears the NH.
- Written out: c1nc2nc(OC)ccc2[nH]1, with the sulfoxide attached at c1.

**Full SMILES:**
Cc1cnc(CS(=O)c2nc3nc(OC)ccc3[nH]2)c(C)c1OC

Checking the ring closures: c2 (imidazole C2), n, c3 (C3a), n, c(OC), c, c, c3 (C7a, closing the ring at C3a), [nH], and the closure back to c2. The fused ring system is consistent.

SMILES: Cc1cnc(CS(=O)c2nc3nc(OC)ccc3[nH]2)c(C)c1OC

name: Temurtide
text:
I read this as an open-chain N-acetylmuramic acid (an aldehyde) whose lactyl ether is joined by an amide to a threonine. That threonine is in turn amide-linked to an isoglutamine, which has a free γ-carboxylic acid and a primary amide.

Stereochemistry was assigned only at the wedge or hash centres. I worked each centre out from the 2D drawing, with the implicit H taken as the opposite face to the wedge or hash.

- The sugar chain runs from the acetamido carbon, bearing the CHO and hashed NH, through three further carbons. The ether O (wedge) is on the second, a hashed OH on the third, and a wedged OH on the fourth, followed by CH2OH.
- The lactyl carbon has a wedged methyl.
- The threonine α carbon has a wedged NH, and its β carbon has a wedged methyl.
- The isoglutamine α carbon has a wedged CH2.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@@H](C=O)[C@@H](O[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)O)C(=O)N[C@H](CCC(=O)O)C(N)=O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: Teneligliptin
text:
I read this as teneligliptin: a pyrrolidine carrying a thiazolidine amide at C2 and a piperazine at C4. The piperazine's other nitrogen is attached to a 3-methyl-1-phenylpyrazol-5-yl group.

**Regions of the drawing**
- **Left:** a phenyl ring is attached to N1 of a pyrazole. The pyrazole has a methyl at C3 and is bonded through C5 to the piperazine nitrogen.
- **Centre:** a piperazine links the pyrazole to C4 of the pyrrolidine. The pyrrolidine ring contains an NH.
- **Right:** C2 of the pyrrolidine bears a C(=O) bonded to the nitrogen of a thiazolidine ring (N–CH2–CH2–S–CH2).

**Stereochemistry**
- Both stereocentres are drawn with wedges: the C=O wedge at pyrrolidine C2 and the piperazine-N wedge at C4.
- Working from the wedge geometry, with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer at each centre, I assigned C2 as `[C@@H]` and C4 as `[C@H]` in the SMILES below.

SMILES: O=C(N1CCSC1)[C@@H]1C[C@H](N2CCN(CC2)c2cc(C)nn2-c2ccccc2)CN1

name: Tenapanor
text:
I read the molecule as a symmetric bis-urea. Each end is a 6,8-dichloro-2-methyl-tetrahydroisoquinolin-4-yl group attached at the meta position of a benzenesulfonamide. The two ends are linked through the following chain:

- sulfonamide NH, then CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2
- NH–C(=O)–NH
- (CH2)4
- NH–C(=O)–NH
- CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2, then the second sulfonamide NH

**Stereochemistry:** each tetrahydroisoquinoline C4 carries a wedge or hash to the phenyl ring. The left end uses a hashed bond and the right end a bold bond, but the right end is also the mirror image of the left, so the two flips cancel and both centres have the same configuration.

I assigned CIP priorities at C4 as C3 (attached to N) > C4a > phenyl > H. On the left, the hashed phenyl points away, so H points toward the viewer. Tracing C3, C4a, phenyl then runs clockwise on the page, and with H toward the viewer that reverses to counterclockwise, giving S. Both centres are therefore S. In the SMILES below, this corresponds to `[C@@H]` when the neighbours are written in the order phenyl, H, ring closure to C4a, C3.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(NCCOCCOCCNC(=O)NCCCCNC(=O)NCCOCCOCCNS(=O)(=O)c1cccc(c1)[C@@H]1CN(C)Cc2c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc12)c1cccc(c1)[C@@H]1CN(C)Cc2c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc12

name: Tenofovir
text:
The drawing shows tenofovir, an adenine (6-aminopurine) attached through N9 to a propan-2-yl chain that carries a phosphonomethoxy group.

- **Purine:** a fused six- and five-membered ring system with an NH2 on the six-membered ring. The five-membered ring nitrogen next to the CH2 chain is N9, which is substituted.
- **Chain:** N9–CH2–CH(CH3)–O–CH2–P(=O)(OH)2.
- **Stereocentre:** the methyl is drawn on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are O > CH2N > CH3 > H. Seen from the front, O → CH2 → CH3 runs counterclockwise, so with H toward the viewer the true configuration is clockwise, giving R.
- **SMILES check:** writing the centre as `C[C@H](Cn...)O...` encodes the R configuration for this neighbour order.

SMILES: C[C@H](Cn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)OCP(=O)(O)O

name: Tenofovir Disoproxil
text:
The drawing shows tenofovir disoproxil (the bis-isopropyl carbonate prodrug of tenofovir).

- **Base:** an adenine (6-aminopurine) attached through N9 to a CH2.
- **Stereocentre:** the CH2 leads to a CH that carries a hashed methyl, an ether O and an implicit H. Ranking O > CH2N > CH3 > H, the O → CH2 → CH3 sequence runs counterclockwise with the hashed methyl pointing away, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Reversing for the H gives R, which I wrote as `C[C@H](CN…)O…`.
- **Phosphonate:** the ether O connects through OCH2 to a P(=O) centre.
- **Side chains:** P carries two identical –O–CH2–O–C(=O)–O–CH(CH3)2 groups (isopropyl carbonates).

SMILES: C[C@H](Cn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)OCP(=O)(OCOC(=O)OC(C)C)OCOC(=O)OC(C)C

name: Tenofovir Alafenamide
text:
This molecule is tenofovir alafenamide, read region by region from the drawing.

- **Ester end:** an isopropyl group on an ester oxygen, then C(=O) attached to an alanine α-carbon.
- **Alanine centre:** the methyl is on a wedge, and the centre is attached to NH. Working through the priorities gives the S (L-alanine) configuration.
- **Phosphorus:** P is bonded to =O, the NH, an O-phenyl group, and a CH2 on a hashed bond. Treating the hashed CH2 as pointing away gives `[P@]` when written in the order N, =O, CH2, OPh.
- **Linker:** CH2–O–CH(CH3)–CH2, where the methyl is on a hashed bond. This stereocentre works out as R, which is `[C@H]` when written with the oxygen first.
- **Base:** the CH2 is bonded to N9 of an adenine (6-aminopurine) ring.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)[C@H](C)N[P@](=O)(CO[C@H](C)Cn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)Oc1ccccc1

name: Tepotinib
text:
The drawing shows tepotinib, built from these fragments:

- **Benzonitrile:** a benzene ring carrying a C#N group, attached at the meta position to the pyridazinone.
- **Pyridazinone:** the ring runs C(=O)–N(CH2Ar)–N=C(Ar)–CH=CH, with the carbonyl carbon bonded to the ring N that bears the benzyl group.
- **Central benzene:** a meta-disubstituted ring carrying the CH2 link to the pyridazinone N and the pyrimidine.
- **Pyrimidine:** attached through its C2 position, with N1 and N3 on either side. The carbon at position 5 carries the O–CH2 group.
- **Piperidine:** the O–CH2 group is bonded to C4 of an N-methylpiperidine ring.

Writing these out as SMILES:

- Benzonitrile with pyridazinone: N#Cc1cccc(c1)-c1ccc(=O)n(Cc2cccc(c2)-c2ncc(OCC3CCN(C)CC3)cn2)n1
- Check of the pyridazinone ring: c1(Ar)=N–N(CH2Ar)–C(=O)–C=C, which gives atoms c1, c, c, c(=O), n, n, six in total.

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: N#Cc1cccc(c1)-c1ccc(=O)n(Cc2cccc(c2)-c2ncc(OCC3CCN(C)CC3)cn2)n1

name: Terazosin
text:
The drawing is terazosin: a 4-amino-6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline whose C2 carries a piperazine. The piperazine's other nitrogen is acylated by a tetrahydrofuran-2-carbonyl group.

Reading the regions:
- **Quinazoline:** the benzene ring carries two OMe groups, and the pyrimidine ring has N1, C2 (bearing the piperazine), N3 and C4 (bearing NH2).
- **Piperazine:** one nitrogen is attached to C2 of the quinazoline, and the other nitrogen is bonded to the C=O.
- **Tetrahydrofuran:** a five-membered ring (O plus four carbons) whose C2 bonds to the carbonyl carbon. The carbonyl carbon sits between the piperazine N and the THF C2, and the C2 stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: COc1cc2nc(N3CCN(CC3)C(=O)C3CCCO3)nc(N)c2cc1OC

name: Terbutaline
text:
The drawing is terbutaline, read as follows:

- A tert-butyl group (a quaternary carbon with three methyls) is attached to an NH.
- The NH connects to a CH2, which connects to a CH bearing an OH.
- That CH is bonded to a benzene ring carrying two OH groups, in a 3,5-pattern relative to the chain attachment.

I checked the ring positions by going around it. The ring atom attached to the chain is at (875, 843). Its neighbours are (899, 656) and (1025, 958). Moving from (899, 656) to (1073, 583), that carbon carries an OH. The next ring atom is (1224, 697), then (1200, 885), which carries the second OH, and then (1025, 958) closes the ring. So the two OH carbons sit at positions 3 and 5 relative to the chain carbon, which is consistent with terbutaline.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I included no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)c1cc(O)cc(O)c1

name: Terbinafine
text:
This structure is terbinafine: a tert-butyl group joined to an alkyne, then a trans alkene, a CH2, and an N-methyl tertiary amine. The nitrogen also carries a CH2 linked to the 1-position of naphthalene.

Reading the chain from the left: the tert-butyl carbon (at about 200,800) is bonded to the alkyne (330 to 455), which leads to the alkene carbon at (585,830). That carbon is double-bonded to the carbon at (657,725), which connects through CH2 (787,735) to N.

For the double bond geometry, the substituents are the alkyne on the carbon at (585,830) and the CH2 on the carbon at (657,725). The alkyne lies to the left and below the bond, while the CH2 lies to the right and slightly below. The bond runs from (585,830) up to (657,725). The alkyne carbon at (455,820) is to the left of the first alkene carbon, and the CH2 at (787,735) is to the right of the second. These sit on opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans (E).

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C#C/C=C/CN(C)Cc1cccc2ccccc12

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C#C/C=C/CN(C)Cc1cccc2ccccc12

name: Terfenadine
text:
The drawing shows the terfenadine skeleton, and I read it region by region as follows.

- **Left end:** a tert-butyl group is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Chain:** the ring carries CH(OH), followed by CH2, CH2 and CH2, which connects to the piperidine nitrogen. The chain is CH(OH)–CH2–CH2–CH2–N, so there are three CH2 groups between the carbinol carbon and N.
- **Piperidine:** N and five carbons make up the six-membered ring. The carbon at position 4 carries C(OH)(Ph)2.
- **Right end:** the carbinol carbon bears two phenyl rings and an OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)C(O)CCCN1CCC(CC1)C(O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Terodiline
text:
The drawing shows a tert-butyl group on an NH, which is bonded to a CH(CH3) carbon. That carbon connects through a CH2 to a CH carrying two phenyl rings. This is terodiline.

All bonds are plain lines with no wedges or hashes, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(CC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)NC(C)(C)C

name: Tert-Butyllithium
text:
The image shows two separate species.

- On the left is a lithium atom with a dot, which is a lithium radical: [Li].
- On the right is an isopropyl skeleton: a central carbon with three bonds to carbons, one up, one lower left and one lower right. Hmm, the central carbon carries a dot, so it is a radical. Its three bonds are the two methyl groups plus the upward carbon. That gives a central carbon bonded to three methyl groups, with one unpaired electron: the tert-butyl radical.

Counting the atoms: the vertical line goes up to a terminal carbon, and the two lower lines each go to a terminal carbon. The central carbon therefore has three carbon neighbors and one radical dot, so it is C(C)(C)C with a radical, written [C](C)(C)C.

The two pieces are drawn as separate components, so I write them with a dot between them:

SMILES: [Li].C[C](C)C

name: Tertatolol
text:
The drawing shows a tert-butyl group on an NH, which connects to a CH2, then a CH(OH), then a CH2, then an O attached to an aromatic ring. This is the tertatolol skeleton.

**Side chain:** tert-butyl–NH–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–O–aryl. There are no wedges or hashes, so the CH(OH) carbon gets no stereo.

**Ring system:** The benzene ring is fused to a six-membered ring that contains S. Going around the benzene ring:
- C(O) is the aromatic carbon bearing the ether oxygen, at about (1012, 722).
- The next ring atom is the fusion carbon bonded to S, at about (1150, 792).
- The next is the second fusion carbon, at about (1278, 708), which bears a CH2.
- Then come the two aromatic CH atoms at (1270, 553) and (1133, 484).
- The last is a CH at (1004, 568), which closes back to C(O).

The saturated ring runs S, CH2 (1296, 1016), CH2 (1424, 932), CH2 (1416, 778), then the fusion carbon at (1278, 708), and back to the other fusion carbon bonded to S. That gives a thiochroman with the ether oxygen at position 8.

**SMILES:** CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2CCCSc12

Checking the ring closure: c1 (C–O), then c, c, c for the three aromatic CH atoms. Next is c2, the fusion carbon bearing the CH2, followed by CCC, then S, then c12, the fusion carbon bonded to S that closes both rings. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)COc1cccc2CCCSc12

name: Terlipressin
text:
I read this as the peptide Gly‑Gly‑Gly‑Cys‑Tyr‑Phe‑Gln‑Asn‑Cys‑Pro‑Lys‑Gly‑NH2 (terlipressin), with a disulfide bridge between the two cysteines.

- **N‑terminal tail:** three glycines (H2N‑CH2‑CO‑ repeated) lead into the first cysteine's nitrogen.
- **Macrocycle:** Cys, Tyr (4‑hydroxybenzyl side chain), Phe (benzyl), Gln (‑CH2CH2CONH2), Asn (‑CH2CONH2), then Cys again. The two cysteine CH2 groups are joined through the S–S bond.
- **C‑terminal tail:** from the second cysteine's carbonyl, Pro (pyrrolidine), Lys (4‑aminobutyl side chain), and Gly‑NH2.

For stereochemistry, I did not check each wedge and hash against the picture. I assumed all residues are the natural L‑amino acids and worked out the @/@@ labels from the atom order in my SMILES. The proline carbon, for example, is written with the preceding ring CH2 first, then H, then the ring‑closure N, then the carbonyl carbon.

SMILES: NCC(=O)NCC(=O)NCC(=O)N[C@H]1CSSC[C@@H](C(=O)N2CCC[C@H]2C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)NCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](CCC(N)=O)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)NC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccc(O)cc2)NC1=O

name: Testosterone Enanthate
text:
The drawing shows testosterone enanthate (testosterone heptanoate), with the steroid core flipped left to right compared with the usual orientation.

- **Ester chain:** counting from the free methyl end to the carbonyl carbon gives 7 carbons, so the acyl group is heptanoyl, attached through the ester oxygen to C17.
- **Ring A:** an enone, with a C=O at C3 and a C4=C5 double bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** both methyl groups (C18 and C19) are hashed, the C9 and C14 hydrogens are wedged, and the C8 hydrogen and the C17 oxygen are hashed. In the usual orientation this pattern is the natural testosterone configuration (17β-ester, 8β-H, 9α-H, 14α-H, β-methyls). Flipping the drawing swaps wedges and hashes, so I used the natural configuration.

SMILES: CCCCCCC(=O)O[C@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]4(C)[C@H]3CC[C@]12C

name: Testosterone
text:
I read the skeleton as a four-ring steroid core (three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring) with an enone, a hydroxyl and two methyl groups.

**Ring skeleton and substituents**
- The ketone O is on C3, which sits in the left-hand-side six-membered ring at the right of the drawing. It is conjugated with a C4=C5 double bond.
- The OH is on the five-membered ring, on the carbon next to the ring-fusion carbon that carries a methyl (C17 next to C13).
- A second methyl sits on the other quaternary ring-fusion carbon (C10).

**Stereochemistry as drawn**
- Both methyls are hashed.
- The OH is hashed.
- The H on C9 is a wedge.
- The H on C14 is a wedge.
- The H on C8 is hashed.

I assigned @/@@ at each of these centres from the 2D coordinates and the wedge or hash direction.

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@@H](CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C)[C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O

name: Testosterone, undecanoate
text:
The drawing shows testosterone undecanoate: the testosterone steroid core esterified at the 17-oxygen with a straight-chain undecanoyl group.

- **Ester chain:** the carbonyl carbon plus ten more carbons to the left makes an 11-carbon (undecanoyl) acyl chain, attached through the ester O to C17.
- **Steroid core:** the four fused rings carry an enone in ring A (C=O at C3 with the C4=C5 double bond). There are two methyl groups, one at C10 and one at C13.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedges and hashes on C13 methyl, C10 methyl, C17–O and the ring-fusion hydrogens are all drawn. In this image the hash/wedge pattern looks flipped relative to the usual steroid drawing, which is consistent with the same molecule drawn in a different orientation. I therefore wrote the natural testosterone configuration (17β-O, 13β-methyl, 10β-methyl). I took this from the known PubChem SMILES for testosterone undecanoate rather than deriving each centre from the wedges.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCC(=O)O[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]34C)C

name: Tesirine
text:
I read the molecule left to right, as a maleimide–PEG–Val-Ala–PABC linker carrying two pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) units joined by a pentyl diether.

- **Maleimide end:** the maleimide N is attached to CH2CH2C(=O)NH, followed by a PEG chain of 8 ether oxygens (each O separated by CH2CH2) ending in CH2CH2C(=O)NH.
- **Peptide:** the chain continues as valine (isopropyl side chain) then alanine, then an NH-aryl amide onto a para-substituted benzyl ring (PABC). I assumed L-Val and L-Ala, since the image gives no way to confirm this.
- **Carbamate PBD:** the benzyl CH2–O–C(=O) is a carbamate on N10 of the first PBD, which is in the carbinolamine form with C11–OH. Its stereocentres are (11S,11aS): the OH wedge and the H wedge both give S.
- **Imine PBD:** the second PBD is in the imine form (N=CH), with the 11a stereocentre also S, as read from the hashed H.
- **Linkage:** the two PBDs are connected through their C8 oxygens by an O–(CH2)5–O linker. Each PBD carries a methoxy at C7 and a 2-methyl C=C in the pyrrolidine ring.

I checked the aromatic substitution pattern on both PBD rings against the drawing. The OR carbon sits next to the CH that is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon, and the OMe carbon sits next to the CH that is adjacent to the C=O-bearing carbon.

SMILES: O=C1C=CC(=O)N1CCC(=O)NCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCOCCC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)Nc1ccc(COC(=O)N5c6cc(OCCCCCOc7cc8c(cc7OC)C(=O)N7C=C(C)C[C@H]7C=N8)c(OC)cc6C(=O)N6C=C(C)C[C@H]6[C@@H]5O)cc1

name: Testosterone Propionate
text:
I read this as the testosterone propionate skeleton, drawn with every stereocentre inverted relative to natural testosterone propionate.

**Skeleton**
- The left side is a propionate ester: CH3-CH2-C(=O)-O- attached to C17 of the five-membered ring.
- The steroid core is the usual four-ring system. The right-hand ring is a cyclohexenone with a C3 ketone and a C4=C5 double bond. A methyl sits on C10 and another on C13.
- Counting the vertices gives the 19 core carbons of the steroid plus the 3-carbon propionyl group.

**Stereochemistry as drawn**
- The C17–O bond, both methyls (C10 and C13) and the H on C8 are hashed.
- The H on C9 and the H on C14 are wedged.
- In natural testosterone propionate, with this same ring orientation, the O and methyls are wedged and the C9 and C14 hydrogens are hashed. Every stereo bond here is therefore the opposite of the natural compound.
- I started from the SMILES for natural testosterone propionate and inverted each centre (swapping @ and @@) to match the drawing. I did this by reasoning from the natural compound's configuration, not by running a SMILES checker.

SMILES: CCC(=O)O[C@@H]1CC[C@H]2[C@]1(CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@@]34C)C

name: Tetomilast
text:
The drawing shows three connected ring systems.

- **Pyridine ring:** the carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) sits on the carbon next to the ring nitrogen. The carbon on the other side of that nitrogen carries the thiazole.
- **Thiazole ring:** its C4 attaches to the pyridine. The ring runs C4, then N, then C2 (which bears the aryl group), then S, then C5 (CH), and back to C4.
- **Benzene ring:** it is attached to thiazole C2 and carries two ethoxy groups. Numbering the attachment carbon as 1, the ethoxy groups are at positions 3 and 4, so it is a 3,4-diethoxyphenyl.

Writing the SMILES from the acid end: OC(=O)c1cccc(n1)-c1csc(n1)-c1ccc(OCC)c(OCC)c1

Checking the thiazole: c1csc(n1) starts at C4 (attached to the pyridine), then C5 (cH), then S, then C2 (attached to the aryl group), then N closing back to C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(n1)-c1csc(n1)-c1ccc(OCC)c(OCC)c1

name: Tetrabutylammonium Bromide
text:
The drawing shows a central N⁺ bonded to four identical unbranched chains, with a separate Br⁻ ion.

Counting carbons in one chain, for example the upper left: N to the carbon at (607,467), then (413,520), (270,377), and (75,430). That is 4 carbons, so each chain is a butyl group. The other three chains look the same.

This is tetrabutylammonium bromide.

SMILES: CCCC[N+](CCCC)(CCCC)CCCC.[Br-]

name: Tetraethyllead
text:
The drawing shows a central Pb atom with four bonds, each leading to a two-carbon chain. Each chain is a CH2 attached to Pb followed by a terminal CH3, so each is an ethyl group.

Four ethyl groups on lead is tetraethyllead.

SMILES: CC[Pb](CC)(CC)CC

name: Tetrafluoroethylene
text:
The drawing shows two carbons joined by a double bond. Each carbon carries two fluorine atoms, so the molecule is tetrafluoroethylene. Since each carbon has two identical substituents, there is no cis/trans geometry to specify.

SMILES: FC(F)=C(F)F

name: Tetrahydrofuran
text:
The drawing shows a five-membered ring made of four carbon vertices and one oxygen labelled "O". Every bond is a single bond, and no wedges, hashes, charges or substituents are drawn. This is tetrahydrofuran.

SMILES: C1CCOC1

name: (+-)-Tetrahydrozoline
text:
The drawing shows tetrahydrozoline: a 2-imidazoline ring attached to C1 of a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene.

**Imidazoline ring:** The NH is at the top left, bonded to a CH2 on the left. That CH2 connects to a second CH2 at the bottom, which bonds to the N at the bottom. This N is double-bonded to the C at the right of the ring, and that C bonds back to the NH. The ring has five atoms: C, NH, CH2, CH2, N.

**Tetralin part:** The ring-junction aromatic carbon (at 965,803) is bonded to the CH (at 749,645), which carries the imidazoline substituent. From that CH the saturated ring continues through three CH2 groups to the other aromatic junction carbon (at 1209,695). The benzene ring is fused at these two junction carbons, with the double bonds as drawn.

**SMILES:** C1CN=C(N1)C2CCCc3ccccc23

The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: C1CN=C(N1)C2CCCc3ccccc23

name: Tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium
text:
The image shows tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0). It has four triphenylphosphine units, each with a phosphorus bonded to three phenyl rings, and a separate Pd atom. No bonds are drawn between Pd and the phosphorus atoms, so I write them as separate components.

name: Tesetaxel
text:
I read the structure as a taxane core (a docetaxel/cabazitaxel-type skeleton) with these features:

- **Side chain:** an N-Boc amino acid ester whose aryl group is a 3-fluoropyridin-2-yl ring, with a 2-hydroxy group on the chain.
- **Core substituents:** a benzoate on C2, an acetate on C4, an oxetane ring (C4–CH2–O–C5), and a tertiary OH on C1.
- **Ring and substituent features:** the C11=C12 double bond carries a methyl, C15 carries a gem-dimethyl, and C8 carries a wedged methyl.
- **Dioxolane:** a five-membered ring bridges C9 and C10 through two oxygens. Its acetal carbon bears a CH2N(CH3)2 group.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge/hash bonds and the implicit hydrogens. I did not run the SMILES through a parser, so the validity check and the stereo assignments are by hand.

name: Tetraphenylphosphonium Chloride
text:
The drawing shows tetraphenylphosphonium chloride. A central P⁺ is bonded to four phenyl rings (top, left, right, bottom), and a separate Cl⁻ counterion sits to the right.

Each ring is a six-membered aromatic ring drawn with alternating double bonds, and each is attached to phosphorus through one ring carbon.

SMILES: [Cl-].c1ccc(cc1)[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: Tetrofosmin
text:
The drawing shows two phosphorus atoms joined by a CH2CH2 bridge. Each phosphorus also carries two CH2CH2OCH2CH3 (2-ethoxyethyl) arms.

Reading the arms:
- Left phosphorus: one arm goes up to O and then an ethyl group (CH2CH2–O–CH2CH3). The other arm goes down to O and then an ethyl group.
- Right phosphorus: one arm goes up to O and then an ethyl group. The other arm goes right to O and then an ethyl group.
- The bridge between the two phosphorus atoms is P–CH2–CH2–P.

Each phosphorus therefore has three substituents, which makes the molecule a bis(diphosphine): (EtOCH2CH2)2P–CH2CH2–P(CH2CH2OEt)2.

SMILES: CCOCCP(CCOCC)CCP(CCOCC)CCOCC

name: Thalidomide
text:
The drawing shows thalidomide: a phthalimide group (a benzene ring fused to an imide ring) attached through its nitrogen to the 3-position of a glutarimide (piperidine-2,6-dione) ring.

Glutarimide ring: the NH sits between two carbonyl carbons. One carbonyl carbon is bonded to the CH that carries the phthalimide nitrogen. The other carbonyl carbon is bonded to a CH2, which connects through a second CH2 to that same CH.

The CH is drawn with plain bonds, so I assign no stereochemistry.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(N2C(=O)c3ccccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: Tetrahydrocannabinol
text:
I read the drawing as a tricyclic cannabinoid skeleton, the tetrahydrocannabinol type, and wrote the SMILES from that.

**Structure read from the image**
- **Aromatic ring:** a benzene ring with an n-pentyl chain (5 carbons) on the left and an OH at the bottom.
- **Pyran ring:** a ring oxygen joins the aromatic ring to a quaternary carbon bearing two methyl groups.
- **Cyclohexene ring:** it contains one C=C double bond and a methyl on the alkene carbon at the far right.
- **Ring-fusion stereocentres:** the two carbons where the rings join carry explicit H atoms. One H is drawn with a wedge (C6a) and the other with a hash (C10a), so the H atoms are trans.

**Stereo assignment**
I worked out each centre from the 2D coordinates. In the SMILES atom order, C6a has neighbours C6, H, C10a, C7. C10a has neighbours C10, H, C10b (aromatic), C6a. Both centres work out to `@@` in the string below.

SMILES: CCCCCc1cc(O)c2c(c1)OC(C)(C)[C@@H]1CCC(C)=C[C@@H]21

name: Tetraphenylporphyrin
text:
I read this as 5,10,15,20-tetraphenylporphyrin, drawn as the tautomer with two NH pyrroles (top and bottom) and two imine-type N= pyrroles (left and right). I assigned each bond order as drawn.

- **Macrocycle:** four meso carbons, each carrying a phenyl ring, link four pyrrole rings.
- **Top pyrrole (NH):** C=C on the outer carbons, with both alpha carbons joined to N by single bonds. Each alpha carbon is double-bonded to a neighbouring meso carbon.
- **Right pyrrole (N=):** the C=N double bond lies on the upper-left side of the ring, and the outer C=C is at the right. The lower alpha carbon is double-bonded to the bottom meso carbon.
- **Bottom pyrrole (NH):** double bonds are drawn on both outer sides (Cβ=Cα and Cβ=Cα'), so the NH is flanked by two single bonds.
- **Left pyrrole (N=):** the C=N double bond lies on the upper side, and the outer C=C is at the left. The lower alpha carbon is double-bonded to the left meso carbon.

I checked the SMILES by walking the ring closures through all four pyrroles and four phenyls. There are no stereocentres or wedges.

SMILES: C1(c2ccccc2)=C3C=CC(N3)=C(c4ccccc4)C5=NC(C=C5)=C(c6ccccc6)C7=CC=C(N7)C(c8ccccc8)=C9C=CC1=N9

name: Teverelix acetate
text:
I read this as the acetate salt of a decapeptide: Ac‑D‑2Nal‑D‑4Cpa‑D‑3Pal‑Ser‑Tyr‑D‑Cit‑Leu‑Lys(iPr)‑Pro‑D‑Ala‑NH2. The residue order and the aromatic side chains come from the drawing; the stereochemistry follows the standard residue configuration for this sequence and was not re-derived from each wedge or hash.

Residues, N‑terminus to C‑terminus:
1. N‑acetyl‑D‑3‑(2‑naphthyl)alanine.
2. D‑4‑chlorophenylalanine.
3. D‑3‑(3‑pyridyl)alanine.
4. L‑serine.
5. L‑tyrosine.
6. D‑citrulline, with the side chain ending in an NH–C(=O)NH2 urea.
7. L‑leucine.
8. L‑lysine with an isopropyl group on the side‑chain nitrogen.
9. L‑proline.
10. D‑alanine as the C‑terminal primary amide.

Acetic acid is drawn separately, so it is added as a second component.

I checked the stereo tags against the SMILES convention: D residues written N[C@H](R)C(=O) and L residues written N[C@@H](R)C(=O). The proline centre, written N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O), is L.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc2ccccc2c1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccc(Cl)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1cccnc1)C(=O)N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCNC(N)=O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCNC(C)C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)N[C@H](C)C(N)=O.CC(=O)O

name: Theophylline
text:
The drawing is a purine-dione core, which matches theophylline (1,3-dimethylxanthine).

**Atoms and bonds read from the image:**
- Top-right N carries a methyl and is bonded to the fusion carbon at upper left and to the C=O carbon at right (C2, with O at upper right).
- Bottom-right N carries a methyl and is bonded to C2 and to the lower C=O carbon (C6, with O at the bottom).
- C6 is bonded to the lower fusion carbon, which is double-bonded to the upper fusion carbon.
- The upper fusion carbon is bonded to the imidazole N (no H) at upper left. That N is double-bonded to the CH on the left, and the CH is bonded to the NH at lower left, which closes onto the lower fusion carbon.

**SMILES:** Cn1c(=O)c2[nH]cnc2n(C)c1=O

**Check against the drawing:**
- Ring 1: n1 (methyl), c(=O), c2 (lower fusion), then [nH], c, n, c2 (upper fusion), n(C), c1=O. The six-membered ring is N1, C6, C5, C4, N3, C2, which is correct.
- The image shows the double bond between the two fusion carbons, and the C=N in the five-membered ring is between the upper N and the CH. In my SMILES the aromatic form places the NH next to the lower fusion carbon (c2), and the =N-type nitrogen is next to the upper fusion carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cn1c(=O)c2[nH]cnc2n(C)c1=O

name: Thiamine
text:
This is the thiamine cation.

**Thiazolium ring:** S is bonded to C5 and to C2. C5 carries the CH2CH2OH chain. C5=C4, and C4 carries a methyl group. C4 is bonded to N+, and N+=C2, with C2 bonded back to S.

**Linker:** N+ is bonded to a CH2, which is bonded to C5 of the pyrimidine.

**Pyrimidine ring:** C5 (attached to the CH2) is bonded to C6 (an aromatic CH) and to C4 (bearing NH2). C6 is bonded to N1. N1=C2, and C2 carries a methyl group. C2 is bonded to N3, and N3=C4.

Written as SMILES, the thiazolium part is OCCc1sc[n+](c1C)Cc2cnc(C)nc2N.

Check against the drawing: C5 (with the chain) is bonded to S and double-bonded to C4 (with the methyl), C4 is bonded to N+, and N+ is bonded to C2, which is bonded to S. The pyrimidine ring is c2 c n c(C) n c2N, which gives six atoms: C5, C6, N1, C2, N3, C4.

SMILES: OCCc1sc[n+](Cc2cnc(C)nc2N)c1C

name: Thiamine Pyrophosphate
text:
This is thiamine diphosphate (thiamine pyrophosphate), drawn with one phosphate oxygen as O⁻.

**Pyrimidine ring.** Going around: C(CH3)=N–C(NH2)=C(CH2–)–CH=N. The ring atoms are N (top), C bearing the methyl, N (right), C bearing NH2, C bearing the CH2 linker, and CH.

**Thiazolium ring.** N⁺ is bonded to the CH2 linker and to a C that carries a methyl. That carbon is double-bonded to the C bearing the side chain, which connects to S. S connects to CH, and CH=N⁺ closes the ring.

**Side chain.** The ring carbon bears CH2CH2–O–P(=O)(O)–O–P(=O)([O-])O.

SMILES, written in order:
- Pyrimidine: Cc1ncc(c(N)n1)C[n+]2...
- Thiazolium: c[s]c(CCO...)c2C

Full SMILES: Cc1ncc(C[n+]2csc(CCOP(=O)(O)OP(=O)([O-])O)c2C)c(N)n1

Check of the pyrimidine ring: c1(C) n c c(CH2...) c(N) n1 gives six atoms: C, N, CH, C, C(NH2), N. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ncc(C[n+]2csc(CCOP(=O)(O)OP(=O)([O-])O)c2C)c(N)n1

name: Thiethylperazine
text:
The drawing shows a phenothiazine core with an ethylthio group on one benzo ring and an N-(3-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)propyl) chain on the ring nitrogen. This is thiethylperazine.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Ethylthio group:** CH3-CH2-S, attached to the upper-left benzo ring.
- **Substituted benzo ring:** the carbon bearing S-Et sits next to a CH that leads to the carbon bonded to N. That ring-fusion carbon is also bonded to the other ring-fusion carbon, which carries the ring S. The remaining two CH carbons close the ring.
- **Central ring:** N and S bridge the two benzo rings. The unsubstituted benzo ring is drawn at the lower right.
- **Side chain:** N-CH2CH2CH2-N, leading to a piperazine ring whose far nitrogen carries a methyl group.

SMILES, written from the ethylthio group onward:
CCSc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN3CCN(C)CC3)c2c1

Check on the substituted ring: c1 (bearing SEt), c, c, c2 (bonded to the ring S), then the ring closes through c2 (bonded to N) and c1 (the CH between them). In the drawing, the S-Et carbon is bonded to the CH that leads to the N-bearing carbon, and also to the CH–CH path toward the S-bearing carbon. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: CCSc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCCN3CCN(C)CC3)c2c1

name: Thiamphenicol
text:
This drawing is thiamphenicol, and the SMILES below was read from the image and checked against it.

- **Left side:** a methylsulfonyl group (CH3–SO2, two S=O) is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Side chain:** from the ring comes a CH(OH) carbon, then a CH carbon that carries a CH2OH group and an NH. The NH is acylated by a dichloroacetyl group, NC(=O)CHCl2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the first stereocentre (CH–OH) has the OH drawn on a wedge. The second (CH–N) has the CH2OH drawn on a wedge. Assigning CIP priorities from the drawing gives R at both centres.
- **Check:** I wrote the SMILES with @@ at both centres and confirmed it also comes out as (R,R).

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](CO)NC(=O)C(Cl)Cl

name: Thimerosal
text:
The image shows thimerosal, the sodium salt of 2-(ethylmercuriothio)benzoic acid.

- **Ethyl group:** two carbons, with the CH2 bonded to Hg.
- **Hg–S link:** Hg is bonded to S, and S is bonded to a ring carbon.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the S-bearing carbon adjacent to the carbon carrying the carboxylate (ortho substitution).
- **Carboxylate:** C(=O)[O-], with Na+ as the counterion.

SMILES: CC[Hg]Sc1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

SMILES: CC[Hg]Sc1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: Thebaine
text:
I read the drawing as a morphinan-type skeleton and wrote it atom by atom.

- **Aromatic ring:** six carbons, bearing an OMe on the left. One neighbouring aromatic carbon carries the ether O, and another carries the CH2 drawn as the explicit "C".
- **Dihydrofuran ring:** the aromatic ether O links to the stereocentre carbon with the hashed H.
- **Cyclohexadiene ring:** it has two C=C bonds and an OMe on the carbon next to that stereocentre. It also contains the quaternary carbon carrying the hashed CH2.
- **Nitrogen bridge:** the quaternary carbon continues through CH2–CH2 to an N-methyl nitrogen. That nitrogen bonds to the second H-bearing stereocentre (hashed H), which also bonds to the diene ring and to the aromatic CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** all three stereocentres have wedges or hashes in the drawing. I assigned @/@@ for each from the 2D coordinates and hash directions.

I checked that the ring-closure digits pair up correctly and that every atom in the drawing is accounted for.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c3c1O[C@H]1C(OC)=CC=C4[C@@H](C2)N(C)CC[C@]341

name: Theaflavin
text:
I read the structure as a benzotropolone core (a benzene ring fused to a seven-membered ring) carrying two flavan-3-ol units, each with a 5,7-dihydroxy-chroman ring system.

**Core**
- The seven-membered ring contains a C=O, then a C(OH)=CH–C(flavan)=CH sequence, and is fused to the benzene ring.
- The benzene ring carries two adjacent OH groups, one CH, and one carbon bearing the left flavan.

**Flavan units**
- Each unit is C2(–aryl)–O–C8a, with C3 bearing an OH and C4 as CH2.
- Each A-ring is a benzene ring with OH at C5 and C7.
- The right flavan is attached to the core at the seven-membered ring through a wedged bond. Its C3–OH is a wedge.
- The left flavan is attached to the benzene ring through a hashed bond. Its C3–OH is a hash.

**Stereochemistry**
- I assigned the four stereocentres (@/@@) from the wedge and hash bonds by working out the neighbour order at each centre.
- I did not re-check the assignments with a toolkit, so the @/@@ marks are the least certain part of the answer.

SMILES: O=C1C(O)=CC([C@H]2Oc3cc(O)cc(O)c3C[C@H]2O)=Cc2c1c(O)c(O)cc2[C@@H]1Oc2cc(O)cc(O)c2C[C@H]1O

name: Thioguanine
text:
This looks like thioguanine drawn as a tautomer.

Atoms and bonds read from the drawing:
- C6 (top) carries a C=S double bond and is bonded to N1 and to C5.
- N1 (right) is double-bonded to C2.
- C2 carries the NH2 group and is also bonded to N3, which is an NH.
- N3 bonds to C4.
- C4 is double-bonded to C5 and bonded to N9 (the lower-left "N" label, drawn without an H).
- C5 is bonded to the NH at the upper left.
- Imidazole ring: that upper-left NH links to a CH, and the CH is double-bonded to the lower-left N, which closes back to C4.

SMILES: S=C1N=C(N)NC2=C1NC=N2

Check on the five-membered ring: C5 is bonded to NH, which is bonded to CH, which is double-bonded to N, which is bonded to C4. C4=C5 closes the ring, so the ring is C5, NH, CH, N, C4.

In the SMILES, "S=C1N=C(N)NC2=C1NC=N2" starts at C6 (ring label 1). It goes to N1, then =C2 with the NH2, then N3(H), then C4 (ring label 2). C4=C5 follows, and C5 closes ring 1 to C6. Then NH, CH=N, and the N closes ring 2 to C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: S=C1N=C(N)NC2=C1NC=N2

name: Thiopental
text:
The drawing shows thiobarbituric acid with two substituents on C5, which is thiopental.

**Ring:** a six-membered ring made of C5 (quaternary), C4(=O), N3H, C2(=S), N1H and C6(=O).

**Substituents on C5:**
- An ethyl group, drawn as the bond from C5 down to the CH2 and then to the CH3 on the left.
- A 1-methylbutyl group (pentan-2-yl). Starting from the ring carbon, the chain runs CH, then CH3 (the vertical methyl), then CH2, CH2, CH3 toward the left.

**Chain check:** the image has the chain from C5 to a CH. That CH carries a methyl pointing up and continues to a CH2 at about (433, 744), then a CH2 at about (255, 637), then a CH3 at about (75, 738). This gives CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH3, which is 1-methylbutyl.

**Stereochemistry:** no wedges or hashes are drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCC(C)C1(CC)C(=O)NC(=S)NC1=O

name: Thiophene
text:
The drawing is a five-membered ring made of one sulfur and four carbons.

Going around the ring from S: S connects to the top carbon, and that bond is plain. The top carbon is double-bonded to the right carbon, as shown by the inner parallel line. The right carbon is single-bonded to the bottom carbon. The bottom carbon is double-bonded to the bottom-left carbon, again shown by an inner line. The bottom-left carbon is single-bonded back to S.

That gives S1C=CC=C1, which is thiophene.

SMILES: C1=CSC=C1

name: Thiotepa
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom (P) double-bonded to sulfur (S) and single-bonded to three nitrogen atoms. Each nitrogen sits in an aziridine ring, which is a three-membered ring made of one N and two CH2 carbons. The structure is tris(aziridin-1-yl)phosphine sulfide, also known as thiotepa.

Each ring is drawn as a triangle: N joined to two carbons that are also joined to each other. No stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: S=P(N1CC1)(N1CC1)N1CC1

name: Thioridazine
text:
This is thioridazine: a phenothiazine core with an SMe group and an N-CH2CH2-(1-methylpiperidin-2-yl) side chain.

**Piperidine ring.** The ring atoms are C2 (the attachment point at about 445,915), then C3 (305,783), C4 (120,838), C5 (75,1027), C6 (216,1160), and N (400,1100). N carries a methyl group.

**Side chain.** From C2 the chain runs to a CH2 at (631,860), then a CH2 at (771,993), then the phenothiazine N.

**Phenothiazine core.** The N attaches to two aromatic carbons. One is at (1002,749), which belongs to the substituted ring. The other is at (1099,1071), which belongs to the unsubstituted ring. S is bonded to (1188,694) on the substituted ring and to (1284,1016) on the unsubstituted ring.

**Substituted ring.** Going around: C(1002,749) → C(862,617) → C(906,428), which carries SMe → C(1092,373) → C(1232,506) → C(1188,694) → back to C(1002,749). The SMe group is therefore on the carbon meta to the N-bearing carbon (one carbon removed from C862), which matches thioridazine's 2-position.

**SMILES.** Written starting from the SMe group:
CSc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCC3CCCCN3C)c2c1

Check on the substituted ring: c1 (C-SMe), c (1092), c (1232), c2 (1188, bonded to S), then the S-linked benzo ring, then N, then c2 (1002, bonded to N) and c1 (862). This closes the ring correctly.

The piperidine C2 is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: CSc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CCC3CCCCN3C)c2c1

name: Thiothixene
text:
I read this as thiothixene, a thioxanthene bearing an N,N-dimethylsulfonamide.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying SO2N(CH3)2 at the top left.
- **Central ring:** a thioxanthene core with S at the top right. Its C9 carbon carries an exocyclic C=C.
- **Side chain:** C9=CH–CH2–CH2–N, ending in an N-methylpiperazine. The piperazine is a six-membered ring with two N atoms, one of which bears a methyl group.
- **Double bond geometry:** Taking the pixel coordinates of the drawing, the chain CH2 lies on the same side of the C=C as the ring carbon of the sulfonamide-bearing ring. The chain is therefore cis to that ring carbon, which I encoded as `/C(=C\C...)`.

SMILES: CN(C)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc2c(c1)/C(=C\CCN1CCN(C)CC1)c1ccccc1S2

name: Thymol
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents: an isopropyl group, a hydroxyl group on the adjacent ring carbon, and a methyl group.

Ring atoms, going around the ring:
- A: (535, 610), bearing the isopropyl group.
- B: (668, 877), bearing OH.
- C: (965, 893), bearing H.
- D: (1128, 645), bearing the methyl group.
- E: (995, 380), bearing H.
- F: (697, 363), bearing H.

The OH carbon (B) is adjacent to the isopropyl carbon (A). The methyl carbon (D) is para to B, since B→C→D is only two steps but D lies opposite A... checking the positions: A–B–C–D gives D three bonds from A, so D is para to A, not B. Relative to B, D is meta (B→C→D).

So the substituents are: OH at B, isopropyl at A (ortho to OH), and methyl at D (meta to OH, para to the isopropyl). This is thymol, 2-isopropyl-5-methylphenol.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(C(C)C)c(O)c1

SMILES: Cc1ccc(C(C)C)c(O)c1

name: Teicoplanin A2-2
text:
This is a teicoplanin-type glycopeptide (an A2-2-like structure). I read it off as a seven-residue aglycone with three sugars and an acyl chain, and the SMILES below describes it.

**Peptide core, N- to C-terminus**
1. Residue 1 is a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine with a free NH2. Its ring is linked by an ether to residue 3.
2. Residue 2 is a 3-chlorotyrosine-type unit whose β-carbon is drawn as CH2. Its ring is linked by an ether to residue 4.
3. Residue 3 is a 3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine whose ring carries the ether to residue 1.
4. Residue 4 is a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine whose ring bears three oxygens. It has an ether to residue 2, an ether to residue 6, and the O-glycoside.
5. Residue 5 is a 4-hydroxyphenylglycine joined by a biaryl C–C bond to the ring of residue 7.
6. Residue 6 is a 3-chloro-β-hydroxytyrosine unit. Its β-O carries a GlcNAc, and its ring bears the ether to residue 4.
7. Residue 7 is a 3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine with a free C-terminal COOH. It carries the α-mannose and the biaryl bond to residue 5.

**Sugars and acyl chain**
- The acylated glucosamine is a β-N-(8-methylnonanoyl)glucosamine on the O of residue 4's ring.
- The GlcNAc is a β-N-acetylglucosamine on the β-O of residue 6.
- The mannose is an α-mannose on the O of residue 7's ring.
- I counted the chain as C(=O), six CH2 and an isopropyl terminus, which is 8-methylnonanoyl.

**Uncertainties**
- Several wedge/hash readings are ambiguous because the long ring-crossing bonds overlap the drawing. This applies especially to residue 2's α-H, so the stereo assignments are my best reading.
- The sugar stereodescriptors were set to β-D-glucosamine, β-D-N-acetylglucosamine and α-D-mannose.

SMILES: N[C@H](c1ccc(O)c(c1)O%10)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc2ccc(O%12)c(Cl)c2)C(=O)N[C@@H](c3cc(O)cc(c3)%10)C(=O)N[C@H](c8cc%12c(O[C@@H]9O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]9NC(=O)CCCCCCC(C)C)c%13c8)C(=O)N[C@H](c5ccc(O)c%14c5)C(=O)N[C@H]([C@@H](O[C@@H]9O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]9NC(C)=O)c6ccc(O%13)c(Cl)c6)C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)c7c%14c(O[C@H]9O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@@H]9O)cc(O)c7

name: Thymopentin
text:
I read this as the linear pentapeptide Arg‑Lys‑Asp‑Val‑Tyr (the sequence of thymopentin), joined by four amide bonds. The chain runs from the N‑terminal arginine to the C‑terminal tyrosine with a free carboxylic acid.

- **Arg:** the side chain is a three‑carbon chain ending in a guanidine group, N=C(N)N. The α‑NH2 is drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Lys:** the side chain is a four‑carbon chain ending in NH2.
- **Asp:** the side chain is CH2COOH.
- **Val:** the side chain is an isopropyl group.
- **Tyr:** the side chain is a benzyl group carrying a para OH, and the C‑terminus is COOH.

The wedges and hashes on the five α‑carbons are consistent with all five residues being the natural L (S) configuration. I assigned the @/@@ marks to match that rather than deriving each one from the drawing.

SMILES: NC(N)=NCCC[C@H](N)C(=O)N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O

name: Threonyl muramyl dipeptide
text:
I read the image as a muramic acid derivative: an N-acetylmuramic acid (a pyranose ring with an NHAc group, a hashed anomeric OH and a CH2OH) joined through its lactyl ether to a threonine–isoglutamine dipeptide. That is a muramyl dipeptide analogue with threonine in place of alanine.

**Regions**
- **Sugar ring:** a six-membered ring of five carbons and one oxygen.
  - C1 carries a hashed OH.
  - C2 carries a wedged NHC(=O)CH3.
  - C3 carries a hashed O link to the lactyl group.
  - C4 carries a wedged OH.
  - C5 carries a wedged CH2OH.
- **Lactyl linker:** O–CH(CH3)–C(=O)–NH, with the methyl hashed.
- **Threonine:** NH–CH(C(=O)…)–CH(CH3)OH. The α-carbon N is wedged and the β-carbon methyl is hashed.
- **Isoglutamine:** NH–CH(CH2CH2COOH)–C(=O)NH2, with the CH2 hashed.

**Stereo assignment:** I worked out each centre from the wedge/hash drawing, including the implicit hydrogen, and converted each to @ or @@ in SMILES atom order. I did not independently verify the resulting SMILES with software.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H](O)O[C@@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O[C@H](C)C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@H](CCC(=O)O)C(N)=O)[C@@H](C)O

name: Thyroxine
text:
The image shows thyroxine (T4), an iodinated diaryl ether amino acid.

- **Left side:** a carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) is attached to the α-carbon, which carries an NH2 group on a wedge bond. A CH2 links that carbon to the first benzene ring.
- **First ring:** it has iodines at both positions next to the ether oxygen, so the ring is 3,5-diiodo-substituted. The CH2 sits para to the ether oxygen.
- **Ether bridge:** an oxygen joins the first ring to the second ring.
- **Second ring:** it carries a para OH, with iodines on both carbons next to that OH, so it is also 3,5-diiodo-substituted.
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedged NH2 points up, COOH lies lower left, CH2 lies lower right, and the implicit H points away from the viewer. With CIP priorities N > COOH > CH2, the sequence runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S, which is the L-configuration. This corresponds to `N[C@@H](...)C(=O)O` in the SMILES.

SMILES: N[C@@H](Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2cc(I)c(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1)C(=O)O

name: Tiaprofenic Acid
text:
The drawing shows a thiophene ring with two substituents on the carbons next to sulfur.

- **Side chain:** a CH(CH3)COOH group, a propanoic acid attached through its alpha carbon. The alpha carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.
- **Other substituent:** a benzoyl group, C(=O) bonded to a phenyl ring.
- **Ring:** the thiophene runs S, C2 (bearing the propanoic acid), C3, C4, C5 (bearing the benzoyl). This matches the drawing, with a double bond between C2 and C3 and another between C4 and C5.

The compound is 2-(5-benzoylthiophen-2-yl)propanoic acid (tiaprofenic acid).

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc(s1)C(=O)c1ccccc1

name: Tiapride
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Amine end:** a diethylamino group, N(CC)CC, joined to a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2).
- **Amide:** the chain ends at an NH, which is bonded to a C=O carbon that attaches to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the carbonyl carbon on one carbon. The adjacent ring carbon carries OCH3 (methoxy). The ring carbon para to the methoxy carbon carries the methylsulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O)CH3.

Checking the substituent positions by ring vertex:
- C1 (945,812) bears the C(=O)N group.
- C2 (960,668) bears OMe.
- C3 (1092,610) is CH.
- C4 (1207,694) is CH.
- C5 (1192,836) bears the sulfonyl group.
- C6 (1062,894) is CH.

The sulfonyl carbon C5 is para to C2 (the OMe carbon) and meta to C1 (the carbonyl carbon).
