name: Tiagabine
text:
The structure is tiagabine, (R)-1-[4,4-bis(3-methylthiophen-2-yl)but-3-enyl]piperidine-3-carboxylic acid.

- **Thiophenes:** two 3-methylthiophen-2-yl rings, both attached to the same alkene carbon.
- **Chain:** that alkene carbon is double-bonded to a CH, which continues through two CH2 groups to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** a six-membered ring with the nitrogen at position 1 and a carboxylic acid on C3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the C3 stereocentre has a hashed bond to the COOH group, so that group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are COOH > CH2–N > ring CH2 > H.
  - Seen from the front, COOH (up) → CH2N (left) → ring CH2 (lower right) runs counterclockwise.
  - With H toward the viewer this reverses, so the centre is R.
  - Writing the stereocentre as `CCC[C@H](C2)C(=O)O` gives R in SMILES order.
- **Alkene:** the two substituents on one end are identical thienyl groups, so no E/Z label is needed.

SMILES: CC1=C(SC=C1)C(=CCCN2CCC[C@H](C2)C(=O)O)C3=C(C=CS3)C

name: Ticlopidine
text:
This is ticlopidine, a 4,5,6,7-tetrahydrothieno[3,2-c]pyridine carrying a 2-chlorobenzyl group on nitrogen.

**Thiophene ring:** S is bonded to CH=CH, which connects to a fused carbon C3a (at about 388,702). C3a is double-bonded to C7a (at about 374,902), and C7a is bonded back to S. The ring is therefore S–CH=CH–C=C(–S), with C3a and C7a as the two fusion atoms.

**Piperidine ring:** C3a is bonded to a CH2 (at 569,615), which is bonded to N. N is bonded to CH2 (at 720,927), then to CH2 (at 540,1014), then to C7a.

**Benzyl group:** N is bonded to a CH2 (at 914,640), which is bonded to the aromatic carbon at 1079,752. The adjacent aromatic carbon at 1260,665 carries Cl, so the chlorine is ortho to the CH2.

SMILES, written from the fusion carbon C3a:
- C3a: `C1=C...` is awkward here, so I start from the thiophene CH instead: `Clc1ccccc1CN1CCc2sccc2C1`.
- Check of the thiophene fragment: `c2sccc2` places C7a bonded to S, then S–CH=CH–C3a, with C3a closing the ring back to C7a. C3a is then bonded to the CH2 `C1`, which closes onto N. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Clc1ccccc1CN1CCc2sccc2C1

name: Thiocillin
text:
I read the drawing as a thiopeptide-type macrocycle: a central 2,3,6-trisubstituted pyridine with a ring of thiazoles, amino acids and a dehydrobutyrine, plus a bithiazole side chain.

**Macrocycle**
- The pyridine C3 carries thiazole A through its C2. Thiazole A's C4 carries a C(=O) amide to the NH of a threonine residue.
- The threonine alpha carbon is hashed to its NH and carries a CH(OH)CH3 group with a hashed methyl. Its C=O leads to a dehydrobutyrine NH, where the C=C–CH3 has the NH cis to the CH3.
- The dehydrobutyrine carbon attaches to thiazole B at its C2. Thiazole B's C4 carries a C(=O)–NH to a valine-type CH, which has a wedged isopropyl group.
- That CH attaches to thiazole C at its C2. Thiazole C's C4 carries a C(=O)–NH to a second valine-type CH, which has a hashed isopropyl group.
- That second CH attaches to thiazole D at its C2. Thiazole D's C4 attaches to the pyridine C2, which closes the ring.

**Side chain**
- The pyridine C6 carries a 2,4'-linked bithiazole (thiazoles E and F). The terminal thiazole F carries a C(=O)NH group attached to a dehydrobutyrine, again with NH cis to CH3.
- The dehydrobutyrine's C=O is an amide, NH–CH2–CH(OH)CH3, with a hashed methyl on the carbinol carbon.

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash, with the implicit H on the opposite side from the drawn wedge or hash, and then worked out @/@@ for the atom order in the SMILES. The two double bonds are encoded with / and \ markers matching the drawn geometry.

SMILES: C[C@H](O)CNC(=O)/C(=C/C)NC(=O)c1csc(n1)-c1nc(sc1)-c1ccc2c(n1)-c1csc(n1)[C@H](C(C)C)NC(=O)c1csc(n1)[C@@H](C(C)C)NC(=O)c1csc(n1)/C(=C/C)NC(=O)[C@H]([C@@H](C)O)NC(=O)c1csc2n1

name: Timolol
text:
This structure is timolol, read from the drawing as follows.

- **Left side:** a tert-butyl group is attached to an NH, which connects to a CH2.
- **Stereocentre:** the next carbon carries an OH on a hashed bond and continues to a CH2–O. Working through the neighbours in SMILES order (CH2N, H, OH, CH2O) with the OH pointing back and the implicit H toward the viewer gives `[C@H]`.
- **Right side:** the O is bonded to a 1,2,5-thiadiazole ring. The ring runs C(O)=N–S–N=C, and the second ring carbon bears a morpholine attached through its nitrogen.

name: Tilidine
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ester:** an ethyl group is attached to an O, which is attached to a C=O. The carbonyl carbon is joined to a quaternary ring carbon by a wedge bond.
- **Ring:** a six-membered carbocycle. Going round from the quaternary carbon, the atoms are the quaternary C, a CH bearing the NMe2 group (hashed bond), a CH=CH double bond, and two CH2 groups back to the quaternary C.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it also carries a phenyl ring, drawn as a benzene with three double bonds.
- **Amine:** the nitrogen carries two methyl groups.

Stereochemistry, assigned from the wedge and hash bonds:

- **Quaternary carbon:** the carbonyl carbon is on the wedge (toward the viewer). I wrote the neighbours in the order carbonyl, ring-closure carbon (the CH–N), phenyl, ring CH2. Seen from the carbonyl, the other three run counterclockwise, which gives `@`.
- **CH–N carbon:** the NMe2 group is on the hash (away from the viewer), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. I wrote the neighbours in the order alkene carbon, H, ring-closure carbon (the quaternary C), N. Seen from H, the alkene carbon, quaternary carbon and N run clockwise. Swapping H and the alkene carbon in the SMILES order flips this to `@`.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@]1(c2ccccc2)CCC=C[C@H]1N(C)C

name: Tiopronin
text:
The drawing shows a chain: CH3 – CH(SH) – C(=O) – NH – CH2 – C(=O)OH.

This is tiopronin (N-(2-mercaptopropionyl)glycine). The central carbon bearing the SH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: Tipifarnib
text:
I read this as tipifarnib, (R)-6-[amino(4-chlorophenyl)(1-methylimidazol-5-yl)methyl]-4-(3-chlorophenyl)-1-methylquinolin-2(1H)-one. The fragments are:

- **Core:** an N-methyl quinolin-2-one, with the carbonyl at C2 and N1 carrying the methyl.
- **C4 substituent:** a 3-chlorophenyl group.
- **C6 substituent:** a quaternary carbon bearing NH2 (drawn on a hashed bond), a 4-chlorophenyl group and a 1-methylimidazol-5-yl group.

For the stereocentre, the hashed NH2 points away from the viewer. Seen from the front, the 4-chlorophenyl, quinolinyl and imidazolyl groups run clockwise. Seen from the N side, that order is counterclockwise, which gives `N[C@](aryl)(quinolinyl)(imidazolyl)`.

I checked the ring closures and atom counts of the SMILES against the drawing.

name: Tirapazamine
text:
This is tirapazamine, a 1,2,4-benzotriazine 1,4-dioxide carrying an amino group at C3.

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- The top N⁺ carries an O⁻ and has a double bond to the neighbouring N (the N without a charge).
- That N is single-bonded to the carbon bearing NH2.
- The NH2-bearing carbon has a double bond to the bottom N⁺, which carries the second O⁻.
- The bottom N⁺ is single-bonded to a benzene carbon, and the top N⁺ is single-bonded to the adjacent benzene carbon, completing the fused ring.

The benzene ring has three double bonds. One is the top-left C–C bond, one is the left-hand C–C bond, and one is the bottom-right C–C bond.

SMILES written from the top N⁺ around the ring: [O-][N+]1=NC(N)=[N+]([O-])c2ccccc12

Check on the fused carbons: c2ccccc12 closes the benzene ring, and the last atom bonds back to N1 (the top N⁺). The first aromatic atom c2 is attached to the bottom N⁺. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: [O-][N+]1=NC(N)=[N+]([O-])c2ccccc12

name: Tipranavir
text:
I read this as tipranavir, a 5,6-dihydro-4-hydroxy-2-pyranone (lactone) with a sulfonamide side chain.

**Structure read from the drawing:**
- **Lactone ring:** a six-membered ring containing O, a C=O carbon, a C=C bearing the OH, a CH2 and a quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries a phenethyl group (CH2CH2Ph) and an n-propyl group, drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Side chain on the ring C=C:** a CH(ethyl) stereocentre, drawn with a wedged ethyl, attached to a meta-substituted benzene.
- **Sulfonamide:** the benzene carries NH–SO2 linked to a pyridine, joined at C2 (next to the ring N), with CF3 at C5.

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned CIP priorities from the wedges and hashes for both centres.
- The quaternary carbon, with the propyl on the hashed bond pointing away, comes out R.
- The CH(ethyl) carbon, with the ethyl on the wedge and the implicit H pointing away, also comes out R.

I checked the quaternary centre against my SMILES directly and it gives R. For the second centre I did not fully re-derive the @@ writing; I matched it to the known tipranavir SMILES, which is also R.

name: Tiratricol
text:
The drawing shows a diaryl ether with an acetic acid side chain, which is the thyroid-hormone-like skeleton of tiratricol-type compounds (here, 3,3',5-triiodothyroacetic acid).

**Right ring.** Starting from the carbon bearing the CH2COOH group (the para position), the ring has an H-bearing carbon, then a carbon bearing I, then the carbon bearing the ether O, then a second carbon bearing I, then another H-bearing carbon. The ether O sits para to the CH2COOH group and is flanked by the two iodines.

**Left ring.** The carbon attached to the ether O has an H-bearing carbon on one side and a ring CH on the other. Going around the ring: the carbon bearing I, then the carbon bearing OH, then two CH carbons back to the start. So the OH is para to the ether O, with one iodine ortho to the OH.

**Side chain.** CH2 then C(=O)OH.

Written as SMILES:

OC(=O)Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2ccc(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1

Atom check: the right ring c1 (bearing CH2), c (H), c(I), c(O-aryl), c(I), c1 (H) gives 6 carbons. The left ring c2 (bearing O), c (H), c (H), c(O) (bearing OH), c(I), c2 (H) gives 6 carbons. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2ccc(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1

name: Tirbanibulin
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- **Morpholine:** a six-membered ring with one O and one N. The N carries a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Linker:** the chain ends in an O that attaches to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Pyridine:** the benzene's para carbon bonds to a pyridine ring at the position meta to N, which is C5 of the pyridine (the ring N is at the bottom right). C2 of the pyridine, next to N, carries a CH2.
- **Amide:** that CH2 connects to C(=O)NH, and the NH bears a benzyl group (CH2 on a phenyl ring).

Pyridine ring atoms: C2 (bearing CH2), N1, C6 (an aromatic CH), C5 (bearing the aryl group), C4 and C3.

In the image, the ring runs from the carbon bonded to the aryl group (left, at about 735,640), up to the top-left carbon (778,567), across to the top-right carbon (865,570), and down to the carbon bearing the CH2 (905,646). From there it goes to N (860,720), then to the bottom-left carbon (778,718), and back to the aryl-bearing carbon. So the aryl carbon is bonded to the CH next to N (C6) and to a CH (C4). The aryl carbon is therefore C5 and the CH2-bearing carbon is C2, which matches the assignment above.

SMILES: O=C(Cc1ccc(cn1)-c1ccc(OCCN2CCOCC2)cc1)NCc1ccccc1

name: Tildipirosin
text:
I read this as a 16-membered macrolide lactone (a tylosin/desmycosin-type skeleton). It carries a glycosidic amino sugar and two piperidine groups.

**Macrolide ring**, numbered from the lactone carbonyl:
- C1 is the lactone C=O, closing through the ring O to C15.
- C2 is a CH2.
- C3 is CH–OH (hashed OH).
- C4 is CH–CH3 (wedged methyl).
- C5 is CH–O–sugar (hashed O).
- C6 is CH bearing a CH2CH2–piperidine chain (hashed).
- C7 is a CH2.
- C8 is CH–CH3 (hashed methyl).
- C9 is a ketone.
- C10=C11 is a trans (E) double bond.
- C12(CH3)=C13 is a trisubstituted double bond; C11 and C14 are trans across it.
- C14 is CH bearing a CH2–piperidine group (wedged).
- C15 is CH bearing an ethyl group (hashed) and the ring oxygen.

**Sugar:** a six-membered ring with a ring oxygen, a C5′ methyl (wedge), 4′-OH (hash), 3′-N(CH3)2 (wedge) and 2′-OH (hash). C1′ is linked to the macrolide C5 oxygen.

I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry, and checked that the atom count matches the drawing.

name: Titanium dioxide
text:
The image shows titanium in the centre with an oxygen at each end. Each Ti–O link is drawn as a double bond, which is titanium dioxide, O=[Ti]=O. There are no charges, rings or stereochemistry to add.

SMILES: O=[Ti]=O

name: Titanocene dichloride
text:
The image shows titanocene dichloride drawn as separate ions: one Ti⁴⁺, two Cl⁻, and two cyclopentadienide rings.

Each ring has five carbons. One carbon carries the negative charge and has only single bonds to its two neighbours. The other four carbons form two C=C double bonds. Written from the charged carbon, the ring is [CH-]1C=CC=C1.

The labels give the total charge as 4 + 2(−1) + 2(−1) = 0, so the species is neutral overall.

name: Tirofiban hydrochloride anhydrous
text:
This is tirofiban hydrochloride. Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left chain:** a butyl group (4 carbons) is attached to a sulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to an NH.
- **Stereocentre:** the NH is bonded to an α-carbon carrying a COOH group and a CH2 that links to the benzene ring. The CH2 bond is a wedge, so the hydrogen points away from the viewer. The substituents run N (up), COOH (lower left), CH2 (lower right). Priorities are N > COOH > CH2 > H, and that sequence runs counter-clockwise, so the centre is S.
- **Aromatic ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene, with the CH2 on one side and an ether oxygen on the other.
- **Ether chain:** O followed by 4 CH2 groups, ending at C4 of a piperidine ring (6-membered, with one NH).
- **Counter-ion:** HCl, written as a separate component.

I checked that the SMILES chirality tag matches the S configuration read from the wedge.

SMILES: CCCCS(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(OCCCCC2CCNCC2)cc1)C(=O)O.Cl

name: Tizanidine
text:
This structure is tizanidine: a 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole core carrying a chlorine and an NH-linked 4,5-dihydroimidazol-2-yl group.

**Benzothiadiazole ring.** The five-membered ring contains S, N, C, C, N. S is bonded to both ring nitrogens. The upper N is double-bonded to the fused carbon at the top (the one bonded to the carbon bearing NH). The lower N is double-bonded to the other fused carbon.

**Benzene ring.** The fused carbon at the top (C3a) is bonded to the carbon bearing the NH substituent. That carbon is double-bonded to the carbon bearing Cl. Next come two CH carbons, one double-bonded to the other, and the second CH is bonded to the lower fused carbon.

**Side chain.** The NH is attached to C(=N–CH2–CH2–NH), which is the imidazoline ring.

**SMILES.** Writing this out from the lower ring nitrogen: Clc1ccc2nsnc2c1NC1=NCCN1. Checking this against the drawing:
- c1 (Cl-bearing) → c → c, the two CH carbons.
- c2 is the fused carbon bonded to the lower N, written n s n, then c2 is the other fused carbon.
- c1 is the NH-bearing carbon, which closes the benzene ring back to the Cl-bearing carbon.

This gives the correct connectivity: the Cl-bearing carbon is adjacent to the NH-bearing carbon, and the NH-bearing carbon is adjacent to the fused carbon at the top, which is bonded to the upper N. The SMILES is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: Clc1ccc2nsnc2c1NC1=NCCN1

name: Tixocortol Pivalate
text:
I read this as a cortisol-type steroid whose C21 hydroxyl is replaced by a pivaloyl thioester. I took the stereochemistry from the drawn wedges and hashes and matched it to the natural cortisol configuration rather than assigning each centre independently.

- **Side chain:** the left end is a tert-butyl group on a C(=O) that is bonded to S. The S connects through a CH2 to a ketone carbon, which is attached to C17. This gives the pivaloyl thioester of a 21-thiol.
- **D ring (five-membered):** C17 carries a hashed OH and the C20 ketone side chain. C13 carries a wedged methyl (C18).
- **C ring:** C11 carries a wedged OH (11β).
- **A ring:** there is a C4=C5 double bond and a C3 ketone, with a wedged methyl (C19) on C10.
- **Ring-fusion hydrogens:** H-8 is wedged, H-9 is hashed and H-14 is hashed, as in natural cortisol.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(=O)SCC(=O)[C@@]1(O)CC[C@H]2[C@@H]3CCC4=CC(=O)CC[C@]4(C)[C@H]3[C@@H](O)C[C@@]21C

name: Tofenacin
text:
The drawing shows an ortho-methylphenyl (tolyl) ring and a plain phenyl ring, both attached to one CH carbon. That CH carbon is also bonded to an oxygen, which continues as O–CH2–CH2–NH–CH3. This is tofenacin (N-desmethylorphenadrine).

Reading the structure region by region:
- The lower-left ring has the CH attached at one vertex and a methyl on the adjacent vertex, so it is ortho-substituted.
- The upper ring is an unsubstituted phenyl.
- The central CH carbon has no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

SMILES: CNCCOC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1C

name: Tobramycin
text:
The drawing matches tobramycin, and I wrote the SMILES from that identification and from memory of the PubChem isomeric SMILES. I did not rebuild each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereodescriptors are the least certain part.

- **Central ring:** a 2-deoxystreptamine cyclohexane carrying two NH2 groups, one OH and two glycosidic oxygens.
- **Left ring:** a pyranose bearing CH2NH2, OH, a ring CH2, NH2 and the anomeric carbon. This is the 2,6-diamino-2,3,6-trideoxy sugar.
- **Right ring:** a pyranose bearing the anomeric carbon, OH, NH2, OH and CH2OH. This is the 3-amino-3-deoxyglucose unit.

SMILES: C1[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]1N)O[C@@H]2[C@@H](C[C@@H]([C@H](O2)CN)O)N)O)O[C@@H]3[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O3)CO)O)N)O)N

name: Tolazoline
text:
The drawing shows a 4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole (imidazoline) ring joined through a CH2 to a benzene ring. This is tolazoline.

**Imidazoline ring:** it has five atoms: an NH, a C(=N) carbon, the ring N, and two CH2 carbons. The C=N double bond runs between the ring carbon and the lower N. The ring closes through the two CH2 groups, which link the NH to the lower N.

**Linker and aryl group:** the ring carbon (C2) carries a CH2, which is attached to a phenyl ring drawn as a Kekulé benzene.

**SMILES:** C1CN=C(N1)Cc1ccccc1

There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: C1CN=C(N1)Cc1ccccc1

name: Tofacitinib
text:
I read this as tofacitinib. The structure has a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine bearing an N-methylamino group at C4. That nitrogen is attached to a piperidine ring, whose ring nitrogen carries a cyanoacetyl group (C(=O)CH2C≡N). The piperidine also has a methyl group on the carbon next to the amino-bearing carbon.

Both stereocentres are drawn with hashed bonds, one to the N-methylamino nitrogen and one to the ring methyl. Assigning CIP priorities with the implicit hydrogen pointing toward the viewer, I get R at the amino-bearing carbon (C3) and R at the methyl-bearing carbon (C4). This matches the (3R,4R) configuration of tofacitinib.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CCN(C[C@@H]1N(C)c2ncnc3[nH]ccc23)C(=O)CC#N

name: Tolbutamide
text:
The drawing shows tolbutamide, read as follows:

- **Left side:** a para-substituted benzene ring with a methyl group at one end.
- **Middle:** a sulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O), on the other ring carbon, bonded to an NH.
- **Urea link:** that NH connects to a carbonyl carbon, C(=O), which is bonded to a second NH.
- **Right side:** the second NH carries a straight n-butyl chain. Counting from the NH, the carbons run up, down, up, then right, which makes four.

There are no wedges, hashes or charges, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCCCNC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1

name: Thiostrepton
text:
I could not read the central pyridine/thiazole junction in the drawing, so that part of this SMILES is a best guess. Three other regions are also uncertain:

- **Thiazole D substituent:** the C(OH)(CH3)CH(CH3)OH group near the top is overlapped in the image and was read approximately.
- **Urea link:** the carbonyl-bearing linker beside the lower-left thiazole did not resolve cleanly, so I joined the two units with a C(=O)N linkage that may not match the drawing.
- **Terminal chain:** the Dha tail ending in C(=C)C(N)=O is a similar approximate reading.

The SMILES below is valid in form, but it is not a confirmed atom-for-atom match to the drawing.

No stereochemistry is included, because the drawing shows no wedges or hashes.

SMILES: CCC(C)C1NC2C=CC3=C(C2O)N=C(C=C3C(C)O)C(=O)OC(C)C%11NC(=O)C4=CSC(=N4)C(NC(=O)C5CSC(=N5)C(=CC)NC(=O)C6=CSC(=N6)c9c(-c%10csc%11n%10)nc(-c%12nc(C(=O)NC(=O)NC(=C)C(=O)NC(=C)C(N)=O)cs%12)c(NC(=O)C(C)NC(=O)C(=C)NC(=O)C(C)NC1=O)c9)C(C)(O)C(C)O

name: Tolcapone
text:
The drawing shows a benzophenone core. A p-tolyl ring (methyl at the para position) is joined through a C=O group to a second ring.

On the second ring, going around from the carbonyl-bearing carbon:
- C1 carries the carbonyl.
- C2 is CH.
- C3 carries OH (the upper right OH).
- C4 carries OH (the lower right OH).
- C5 carries the nitro group (N+ with =O and O−).
- C6 is CH.

This ring is therefore 3,4-dihydroxy-5-nitrophenyl, which is the same substitution pattern as tolcapone.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c1cc(O)c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: Tolfenamic Acid
text:
The drawing shows an anthranilic acid core, with a benzoic acid ring whose carboxylic acid is ortho to an NH linker.

The NH connects to a second aromatic ring. Starting from the ring carbon bonded to N, one neighbour carries a methyl group. The next carbon after that carries Cl. This gives a 3-chloro-2-methylphenyl group, which is the structure of tolfenamic acid.

Reading the SMILES from the acid end: OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1cccc(Cl)c1C

Atom check:
- Left ring: c1 (bearing COOH), then c, c, c, c, then c1 (bearing N). That is 6 carbons, which is correct.
- Right ring: c1 (bearing N), c, c, c, c(Cl), c1(C). That is 6 carbons, with the methyl on the carbon adjacent to the N-bearing carbon and Cl on the next carbon.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1cccc(Cl)c1C

name: Tolperisone
text:
The drawing shows a para-substituted benzene ring (methyl at the para position) bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O). The carbonyl carbon is attached to a CH that carries a methyl group, and that CH connects through a CH2 to the nitrogen of a piperidine ring (N plus five carbons). The ring is unsubstituted.

This is tolperisone. The CH stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)C(C)CN1CCCCC1

name: Tolnaftate
text:
The drawing shows a thiocarbamate: an O-aryl N-methyl-N-aryl carbamothioate, with C(=S) bonded to both N and O.

- **Nitrogen:** it carries a methyl group and a 3-methylphenyl ring. The ring carbon bonded to N sits next to a CH, and the methyl-bearing carbon is one further CH along (meta). The ring runs from the N-bearing carbon (447,763) to (297,766) to (225,899, methyl-bearing), so the methyl is meta to N.
- **Oxygen:** it is bonded to a naphthalen-2-yl group. The attachment carbon (897,750) is adjacent to (975,878) and (968,618). Carbon 975,878 is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon (1125,875), so the attachment carbon is separated from the fusion carbon by one CH. That makes it a 2-naphthyl group.

SMILES: CN(c1cccc(C)c1)C(=S)Oc1ccc2ccccc2c1

name: Tilmicosin
text:
I read this as a tilmicosin-type 16-membered macrolide and worked out each stereocentre from its wedges and hashes. I did not check the result against a reference SMILES.

**Macrolactone ring.** Going round the ring, I read:
- a lactone C(=O)–O, with the ring carbon next to the O bearing an ethyl group;
- the adjacent ring carbon bearing a CH2–O–sugar arm;
- a trisubstituted C=C with a methyl group, then a trans CH=CH, then a ketone;
- CH(CH3), then CH2, then CH carrying a CH2CH2–N side chain;
- CH–O–desosamine, then CH(CH3), then CH(OH), then CH2 back to the lactone C=O.

The two double bonds are drawn trans, so I wrote them as `/C=C/` and `C(C)=C/`.

**Substituents.**
- The side-chain amine is a 3,5-dimethylpiperidine. Both methyls are wedged, so they are cis.
- The glycoside on the ring is a desosamine-type sugar. It has a ring O, a C-methyl, two OH groups and an NMe2.
- The CH2–O sugar is a 6-deoxy sugar bearing two OMe groups, one OH and a C-methyl.

I assigned each @/@@ by working out the neighbour order around the stereocentre from the wedge and hash drawing.

SMILES: CC[C@H]1OC(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O[C@H]2[C@H](O)[C@@H](N(C)C)[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)O2)[C@@H](CCN2C[C@@H](C)C[C@@H](C)C2)C[C@@H](C)C(=O)/C=C/C(C)=C/[C@@H]1CO[C@@H]1O[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)[C@@H](OC)[C@H]1OC

name: Toluene
text:
The drawing shows a six-membered ring with three double bonds, so it is a benzene ring. A single line extends from the right-hand vertex, which is one carbon (a methyl group) because the line ends with no label.

The double bonds are drawn on the top edge, the lower-left edge and the lower-right edge. The ring vertices are:

- Top-left (300, 360) and top-right (750, 360), joined by the top double bond.
- Right (975, 750), which carries the substituent.
- Bottom-right (750, 1140) and bottom-left (300, 1140).
- Left (75, 750).

The lower-left double bond joins the left vertex and the bottom-left vertex. The lower-right double bond joins the right vertex and the bottom-right vertex. The bottom edge is a single bond. This gives a valid Kekulé structure.

The molecule is toluene, a methyl group on a benzene ring.

SMILES: Cc1ccccc1

name: Toltrazuril
text:
The drawing shows a 1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione ring (a triazinetrione) attached to a substituted diaryl ether.

**Triazinetrione ring.** The ring atoms, going around, are:
- N(CH3)
- C(=O), reached from the N-methyl nitrogen and bonded to the aryl-bearing nitrogen
- N(aryl)
- C(=O), bonded to N(aryl) and NH
- NH
- C(=O), bonded to NH and closing back to N(CH3)

**Aryl group.** The ring nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring. Going around that ring from the nitrogen attachment:
- C1, attached to the triazine N
- C2, an aromatic CH
- C3, bearing the methyl group
- C4, bearing the oxygen of the ether
- C5, an aromatic CH
- C6, an aromatic CH

The methyl and the ether oxygen are on adjacent carbons (C3 and C4). The ether oxygen is therefore para to the triazine nitrogen and ortho to the methyl.

**Second aryl ring.** The ether oxygen links to a para-substituted benzene ring that carries S-CF3 at the position opposite the oxygen.

**SMILES.** Written starting from the N-methyl nitrogen:

CN1C(=O)N(c2ccc(Oc3ccc(SC(F)(F)F)cc3)c(C)c2)C(=O)NC1=O

Checking the ring order: N1(Me), C(=O), N(aryl), C(=O), NH, C1(=O) closing the ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)N(c2ccc(Oc3ccc(SC(F)(F)F)cc3)c(C)c2)C(=O)NC1=O

name: Tomatine
text:
This SMILES is not read atom by atom from the drawing. I recognised the molecule as α-tomatine, the tomatidine glycoalkaloid with a lycotetraose chain at C-3. I then wrote its SMILES from memory and checked only the connectivity against the image. The stereo descriptors are as I recalled them and I did not re-derive them from the wedges and hashes.

- **Aglycone:** a 5α-spirosolane steroid, with the spiro N-containing piperidine ring (NH, methyl-substituted) and the fused furan ring (O) at the left of the drawing.
- **Sugar 1:** a galactose attached through O at C-3 of the steroid.
- **Sugar 2:** a glucose linked at the 4-position of the galactose.
- **Sugars 3 and 4:** a second glucose on the 2-position and a xylose on the 3-position of that glucose.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1CC[C@@]2([C@H]([C@H]3[C@@H](O2)C[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H]5[C@H]4CC[C@@H]6[C@@]5(CC[C@@H](C6)O[C@H]7[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@H](O7)CO)O[C@H]8[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O8)CO)O)O[C@H]9[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H](CO9)O)O)O)O[C@H]%10[C@@H]([C@H]([C@@H]([C@H](O%10)CO)O)O)O)O)O)C)C)NC1

name: Tolterodine Tartrate
text:
The image shows two components, tolterodine and tartaric acid, written as a salt with a dot.

**Tolterodine (lower component).** It has a 4-methylphenol ring joined at the carbon next to the OH to a stereogenic CH. That CH also carries a phenyl ring and a CH2CH2N(iPr)2 chain, with the CH2 attached by a wedge bond.
- CIP priorities at the stereocentre are phenol-ring carbon > phenyl > CH2 > H.
- With the wedge CH2 toward the viewer and H pointing away, the order phenol-ring carbon → phenyl → CH2 runs clockwise, so the centre is R.
- The SMILES `Cc1ccc(O)c(c1)[C@H](CCN(C(C)C)C(C)C)c1ccccc1` encodes R. I checked the neighbour order and the @ symbol against these priorities.

**Tartaric acid (upper component).** It has two CH(OH) centres, each drawn with a wedged OH.
- Working through the priorities (OH > COOH > CH(OH)COOH > H), both centres come out R, which is L-(+)-tartaric acid.
- The SMILES `OC(=O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(O)=O` encodes (R,R). I checked each @/@@ by the same priority analysis.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(O)c(c1)[C@H](CCN(C(C)C)C(C)C)c1ccccc1.OC(=O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)C(O)=O

name: Tofogliflozin
text:
I read the structure as a spiro-fused isobenzofuran–pyran C-glycoside carrying a 4-ethylbenzyl group, which has the tofogliflozin skeleton.

**Connectivity**
- The left ring is a para-disubstituted benzene bearing an ethyl group (CC–). Its other substituent is a CH2 linker to the bicyclic aromatic ring.
- The bicyclic aromatic ring is a benzene fused to a five-membered ring made of ArC–CH2–O–C(spiro)–ArC.
- The spiro carbon is also part of a six-membered pyran ring: spiro C, ring O, CH(CH2OH), CH(OH), CH(OH), CH(OH), back to the spiro carbon.
- The benzyl-bearing aromatic carbon is meta to the CH2–O carbon of the fused ring. It sits next to the aromatic CH that is adjacent to the spiro-bearing carbon.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing, working through the signed-volume (chirality) sense at each one.
- The spiro carbon has a wedge to the furan oxygen, giving `[C@]`.
- The pyran ring carbons, in SMILES order from the ring oxygen, are:
  - C5′ (hashed CH2OH): `[C@H]`
  - C4′ (wedged OH): `[C@@H]`
  - C3′ (hashed OH): `[C@H]`
  - C2′ (wedged OH): `[C@H]`

SMILES: CCc1ccc(Cc2ccc3c(c2)[C@]2(OC3)O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]2O)cc1

name: Topotecan
text:
I read this as topotecan, a camptothecin core carrying a 9-dimethylaminomethyl and a 10-hydroxy group on the quinoline ring.

- **Left ring system:** the benzene ring carries a CH2N(CH3)2 group and an OH on adjacent carbons. It is fused to the pyridine-type ring that contains the aromatic N.
- **Middle rings:** a CH2 links the quinoline to the lactam nitrogen, which bears the C=O. That nitrogen sits in a pyridone ring.
- **Right lactone:** the pyridone is fused to a six-membered lactone (CH2–O–C(=O)).
- **Stereocentre:** the quaternary carbon bears the ethyl, a wedged OH, the lactone C=O and a ring carbon. Working through the wedge geometry (OH toward the viewer, with ethyl, lactone C=O and ring carbon running counterclockwise from that side) gives `@@` for the atom order written below.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCC2=C1C=C1N(C2=O)CC2=CC3=C(CN(C)C)C(O)=CC=C3N=C12

name: Torasemide
text:
This is torsemide, a pyridine sulfonylurea. I read it region by region.

- **Pyridine ring:** The ring nitrogen is at the top. Going around the ring, N connects to a CH, then to the carbon bearing the sulfonyl group (C3). Next is the carbon bearing the NH-aryl group (C4), then two CH carbons that close the ring back to N.
- **Sulfonylurea chain:** The sulfonyl sulfur carries two =O groups and is bonded to NH. That NH connects to C(=O), then to NH, then to an isopropyl group.
- **Aryl group:** The pyridine C4 is bonded to an NH, which attaches to a benzene ring. The benzene has a methyl group meta to the NH attachment. Tracing the ring: the carbon attached to NH (call it a1) is bonded to a CH (a2), then to the carbon bearing the methyl (a3), then through three more ring carbons back to a1. The methyl is therefore at the meta position, a 3-methylphenyl group.

SMILES: Cc1cccc(Nc2ccncc2S(=O)(=O)NC(=O)NC(C)C)c1

name: Topiramate
text:
I read the drawing as topiramate: a fructopyranose core carrying two isopropylidene ketals and a CH2‑O‑SO2NH2 sulfamate group.

**Skeleton**
- The pyranose ring has a spiro carbon, a ring oxygen, a CH2, and two CH carbons (one next to the CH2, one in the middle), plus a further CH carbon next to the spiro carbon.
- The spiro carbon carries a CH2O–S(=O)(=O)NH2 group.
- One isopropylidene ketal bridges the spiro carbon and its neighbouring CH through two oxygens, forming a five‑membered dioxolane.
- A second isopropylidene ketal bridges the other two CH carbons through two oxygens, forming another dioxolane.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from its wedge or hash bonds, using the atom order in the SMILES below:
- The spiro carbon has a wedged CH2O bond and comes out as `@@`.
- The CH next to the ring CH2 has a hashed H and comes out as `@`.
- The middle CH has a hashed H and comes out as `@`.
- The CH next to the spiro carbon has a wedged H and comes out as `@@`.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)OC[C@@]12OC[C@H]3OC(C)(C)O[C@H]3[C@@H]1OC(C)(C)O2

name: Tradipitant
text:
The drawing breaks down into five parts.

1. **Benzyl group:** a benzene ring carries two CF3 groups at the 3 and 5 positions and a CH2 at position 1. The CH2 is bonded to a triazole nitrogen.
2. **Triazole:** the ring is N1(CH2Ar)–N2=N3–C4=C5. Reading around the ring, the CH2-bearing N is bonded to a second N, which is double-bonded to a third N. The third N is bonded to a carbon (C4), which is double-bonded to C5, and C5 closes back to the first N.
3. **C5 substituent:** C5 (the carbon bonded to the CH2-bearing N) carries a pyridin-4-yl group.
4. **C4 substituent:** C4 (the carbon next to N=N) is bonded to the 2-position of a pyridine ring. That pyridine has a ring nitrogen next to the attachment carbon, and its 3-position carries a C(=O)-aryl group.
5. **Aryl ketone:** the carbonyl is attached to a 2-chlorophenyl ring.

Assembling these pieces gives:

O=C(c1ccccc1Cl)c1cccnc1-c1nnn(Cc2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c2)c1-c1ccncc1

Atom check: in the pyridine ring, C2 is bonded to the ring nitrogen N1 and to C3, which bears the carbonyl. The ring runs N1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and closes back to N1. In the SMILES, c1cccnc1- starts at C3 (which bears the carbonyl), then C4, C5, C6, N1 and C2. C2 is the closing atom and carries the triazole substituent, so this matches.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1Cl)c1cccnc1-c1nnn(Cc2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c2)c1-c1ccncc1

name: Tovorafenib
text:
I read the structure as three parts joined by two amide links.

- **Left ring:** a pyrimidine carrying the amide carbonyl on one carbon, a Cl on the next, and an NH2 on the one after. As a fragment this is c1ncnc(N)c1Cl, with the carbonyl attached at the first atom.
- **Centre:** a stereocentre bearing a hashed methyl, the amide NH, a thiazole C2 and an implicit H. The thiazole has its second carbon attached to the stereocentre and its fifth carbon attached to a second carbonyl.
- **Right ring:** a pyridine joined through the amide NH at its C2. It has CF3 at C4 and Cl at C5.

For the stereocentre, the hashed methyl points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Looking from the H side, methyl, N and thiazole run counterclockwise. That corresponds to `C[C@@H](N…)c` when the SMILES is written starting from the methyl.

SMILES: C[C@@H](NC(=O)c1ncnc(N)c1Cl)c1ncc(s1)C(=O)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)c(Cl)cn1

name: Torcetrapib
text:
I read the drawing as a tetrahydroquinoline, the torcetrapib scaffold, and assembled the SMILES region by region.

- **Core ring:** a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring that contains N1. N1 carries an ethyl carbamate (N–C(=O)–O–CH2CH3). The benzo ring bears a CF3 group.
- **C2 (next to N1):** carries an ethyl group on a hashed bond.
- **C4:** carries a hashed bond to an exocyclic nitrogen. That nitrogen bears a methyl carbamate (C(=O)OCH3) and a benzyl group. The benzyl ring is 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.
- **Stereochemistry at C2:** only the two hashed bonds, at C2 and C4, show stereochemistry. For C2 I took the hashed ethyl as pointing away from the viewer, with H toward the viewer. Reading the neighbours N1, C3, ethyl then gives `[C@H]` in the SMILES order.
- **Stereochemistry at C4:** I took the hashed N as pointing away, with H toward the viewer. Reading the neighbours C4a, N, C3 then gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)N1c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2[C@@H](N(Cc2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c2)C(=O)OC)C[C@H]1CC

name: Toremifene
text:
The drawing is toremifene, with the double bond geometry read from the image as Z.

**Connectivity**
- The left end is an N,N-dimethylamino group joined by CH2CH2 to an ether oxygen, which is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- That ring is attached to one carbon of a C=C double bond. This carbon also carries a phenyl ring.
- The other alkene carbon carries a second phenyl ring and a CH2CH2Cl chain.

**Double bond geometry**
The drawing fixes the geometry, so I assigned CIP priorities from the atom positions.
- On the first alkene carbon, the 4-alkoxyphenyl group outranks the plain phenyl, because oxygen appears at the para position.
- On the second alkene carbon, the phenyl outranks CH2CH2Cl.
- In the drawing, the 4-alkoxyphenyl group and the phenyl on the second carbon lie on the same side of the double bond. That makes the configuration Z.

**SMILES check**
In my SMILES, the aryl group sits below the first alkene carbon and the phenyl sits below the second alkene carbon, so they are cis. This matches the Z assignment.

SMILES: CN(C)CCOc1ccc(cc1)/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccccc1)CCCl

name: trans-Diamminedichloroplatinum
text:
The drawing shows Cl–Pt(2+)–Cl as a single connected unit, with two separate NH3 molecules drawn beneath it and not bonded to anything.

The Pt carries a 2+ charge, and the two Cl atoms are each attached to it by a single bond. Both NH3 groups are neutral, so the charge is not balanced by them.

Written as a multi-component SMILES, the three pieces are the Cl–Pt–Cl unit, then each NH3 separated by a dot:

Cl[Pt+2]Cl.N.N

SMILES: Cl[Pt+2]Cl.N.N

name: Trametinib
text:
This structure is trametinib, a pyridopyrimidine-trione core. I read it region by region.

**Core.** The bicyclic system is a pyrido[4,3-d]pyrimidine-trione:
- The pyrimidine ring has N1 bearing the aryl group, then C2(=O), N3 bearing the cyclopropyl, then C4(=O), then C4a and C8a.
- The pyridone ring runs C4a=C5(NHAr)–N6(Me)–C7(=O)–C8(Me)=C8a.
- C5 carries the NH-aryl group and N6 carries a methyl.
- C7 is the carbonyl and C8 carries a methyl.

**Substituents.**
- The N-aryl group is a phenyl ring bearing an NHC(=O)CH3 group at the meta position.
- The anilino group is 2-fluoro-4-iodophenyl, attached through NH.

**Assembling the SMILES.**
- Start with the acetamide: CC(=O)Nc1cccc(c1)
- Attach N1: n1 (written as N in a Kekulé-style SMILES)
- Then C2(=O), N3 with cyclopropyl, C4(=O), C4a, and so on.

CC(=O)Nc1cccc(c1)N1C(=O)N(C2CC2)C(=O)C2=C1C(C)=C(... wait, the ring order needs care. C8a is attached to N1 and C8, and C4a is attached to C4 and C5. The order is C8a=C8(C)–C7(=O)–N6(C)–C5(Nar)=C4a.

Written out: CC(=O)Nc1cccc(c1)N1C(=O)N(C2CC2)C(=O)C2=C1C(C)=C... this is incorrect, because C8a is double-bonded to C8 while C4a is double-bonded to C5. The corrected form is:

N1C(=O)N(C2CC2)C(=O)C2=C(Nc3ccc(I)cc3F)N(C)C(=O)C(C)=C12

Here C4a (C2=) is double-bonded to C5, and C8a (=C12) is double-bonded to C8 and closes rings 1 and 2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)Nc1cccc(c1)N1C(=O)N(C2CC2)C(=O)C2=C(Nc3ccc(I)cc3F)N(C)C(=O)C(C)=C12

name: Tranylcypromine
text:
The drawing shows a cyclopropane ring and a benzene ring.

- **Cyclopropane:** three carbons. One carries an NH2 group, and the adjacent one is bonded to the benzene ring. The third carbon is a plain CH2.
- **Benzene ring:** six carbons with three alternating double bonds, attached to the cyclopropane at a single position.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain lines, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo marks are included.

This is 2-phenylcyclopropan-1-amine (tranylcypromine skeleton).

SMILES: NC1CC1c1ccccc1

name: Trapidil
text:
The drawing shows a [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine core with a diethylamino group and a methyl group.

**Atoms and bonds read from the image**
- Diethylamino group: CCN(CC) attached to a ring carbon C7.
- C7 is bonded to ring N (the bridgehead, N8).
- C7=C6, where C6 is a CH.
- C6 is bonded to C5, which carries the methyl group.
- C5=N4.
- N4 is bonded to C3a, the fused carbon.
- C3a is bonded to the bridgehead N, and C3a=N3.
- N3 is bonded to C2, a CH, drawn as N–C.
- C2=N1, and N1 is bonded to the bridgehead N.

**Ring bonds**
- Six-membered ring: C7, C6, C5, N4, C3a and the bridgehead N.
- Five-membered ring: bridgehead N, N1, C2, N3 and C3a.

**SMILES construction**
Start at the ethyl groups and the amine nitrogen, then go around the rings:
CCN(CC)c1cc(C)nc2ncnn12

Check of the ring closures:
- c1 is C7.
- c is C6.
- c(C) is C5 with the methyl.
- n is N4.
- c2 is C3a.
- n is N3.
- c is C2.
- n is N1.
- n12 is the bridgehead N, which closes to C7 (ring 1) and to C3a (ring 2).

This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cc(C)nc2ncnn12

name: Tranimilast
text:
I read the structure as a 3,5-dichloropyridine N-oxide linked through a CH2 to a stereogenic carbon. That carbon carries an ester oxygen, which acylates a benzoic acid bearing a methanesulfonamide and a cyclopropylmethoxy group. Its aryl substituent is a 3-(cyclopropylmethoxy)-4-(difluoromethoxy)phenyl ring.

The only drawn stereocentre is the carbon with the hashed CH2 bond. Its neighbours are the ester O (lower left), the hashed CH2 (lower right) and the aryl ring (up), with H implied toward the viewer. Working through the neighbour order O, H, CH2, aryl gives `[C@@H]` when written with the ester O preceding it.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1OCC1CC1)C(=O)O[C@@H](Cc1c(Cl)c[n+]([O-])cc1Cl)c1ccc(OC(F)F)c(OCC2CC2)c1

name: Trazodone
text:
This is trazodone: a 3-chlorophenyl group on a piperazine, a three-carbon chain, and a triazolopyridinone.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Chlorophenyl ring:** Cl sits on a carbon, and the piperazine nitrogen is attached to the ring carbon meta to it, giving Clc1cccc(c1)N.
- **Piperazine:** a six-membered ring with two N atoms. The aryl-bearing N is bonded to two CH2 groups, and the other N carries the chain.
- **Chain:** three CH2 groups run from the second piperazine N to the triazole N.
- **Triazolopyridinone:** the chain N is bonded to C(=O), which is bonded to the ring-fusion N. That fusion N is bonded to the pyridine CH and to the fusion carbon. The fusion carbon is double-bonded to the other triazole N (=N), and that N is bonded back to the chain N.

The SMILES below writes the ring-fusion carbon as C(=N2) and closes the triazole ring through the chain N.

SMILES: O=C1N(CCCN2CCN(CC2)c2cccc(Cl)c2)N=C2C=CC=CN12

name: Travoprost
text:
The drawing matches travoprost, the isopropyl ester of a prostaglandin F2α analogue. I wrote the SMILES from the structure, but I took the stereodescriptors from the known stereochemistry of travoprost rather than re-deriving each wedge and hash from the image.

- **Ester end:** an isopropyl group on the ester oxygen, then the carbonyl.
- **Upper chain:** three CH2 groups, then a cis (Z) C=C, then one more CH2 that joins the cyclopentane through a hashed bond. This gives the hept-5-enoate chain.
- **Cyclopentane:** two ring OH groups, drawn with hashed bonds, and a ring CH2 between them.
- **Lower chain:** a trans (E) CH=CH attached to the ring by a wedged bond. Next comes a CH(OH) with a hashed bond, then CH2–O–aryl.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring bearing CF3 meta to the ether oxygen.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@H](C[C@H]([C@@H]1/C=C/[C@H](COC2=CC=CC(=C2)C(F)(F)F)O)O)O

name: Tramadol
text:
The image shows tramadol, with a 3-methoxyphenyl ring and a dimethylaminomethyl group on a cyclohexanol ring.

**Structure read from the drawing:**
- **Cyclohexane ring:** six carbons. One carbon (call it C1) carries both the OH and the aryl group. The adjacent carbon (C2) carries the CH2–N(CH3)2 side chain.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring with an OCH3 substituent meta to the ring carbon bonded to C1.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing has two wedges. The OH on C1 is a bold wedge. The CH2N bond on C2 is also a bold wedge.

**Assigning the stereocentres (CIP):**
- **C2:** the priorities are C1 > CH2N > ring CH2, with H pointing away. C1 (upper right) → CH2N (bottom) → ring CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise, so C2 is R.
- **C1:** the priorities are OH > aryl > C2 > ring CH2. A triple-product check using the wedged OH gives R.

This is (1R,2R)-tramadol. Writing the SMILES as `CN(C)C[C@H]1CCCC[C@]1(O)c1cccc(OC)c1` and checking each neighbour order, the tags `[C@H]` for C2 and `[C@]` for C1 reproduce R at both centres.

SMILES: CN(C)C[C@H]1CCCC[C@]1(O)c1cccc(OC)c1

name: Trelagliptin
text:
I read this structure as trelagliptin, which is the alogliptin skeleton with a fluorine on the benzonitrile ring.

- **Pyrimidinedione core:** a six-membered ring with two C=O groups. One ring N carries a methyl group. The other ring N carries the benzyl CH2. A C=C links the carbon bearing the piperidine to the CH between the carbonyls.
- **Piperidine:** attached through its ring N to the pyrimidinedione carbon. The carbon three atoms round the ring from that N carries NH2 on a hashed bond.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring bearing a C≡N and the CH2 on adjacent carbons. The fluorine sits para to the nitrile carbon.

**Stereochemistry:** The NH2 is on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from that H, the three other neighbours (the upper CH2, the NH2, the lower CH2) run counterclockwise. In the SMILES order below (upper CH2, H, N, lower CH2), this corresponds to `@@`.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)C=C(N2CCC[C@@H](N)C2)N(Cc2cc(F)ccc2C#N)C1=O

name: Treprostinil Diolamine
text:
I read this as treprostinil with diethanolamine as the salt partner. I took the stereochemistry from the known stereo-SMILES of treprostinil rather than re-deriving each centre from the wedges and hashes. I did check that the connectivity matches the drawing.

- **Core:** a cyclopenta[g]naphthalene (benzene fused to a six-membered ring, which is fused to a cyclopentane). The ring-fusion carbons carry the two hashed H atoms.
- **Cyclopentane:** one carbon carries a wedged OH. The adjacent carbon carries a hashed bond to the side chain.
- **Side chain:** a 3-hydroxyoctyl chain, with the OH on a hashed-bond carbon.
- **Aromatic ring:** an O–CH2–COOH group (oxyacetic acid) on the benzene carbon next to the ring fusion.
- **Second component:** HN(CH2CH2OH)2, diethanolamine, drawn separately above the main structure.

SMILES: CCCCC[C@@H](CC[C@@H]1[C@H](C[C@H]2[C@@H]1CC3=C(C2)C(=CC=C3)OCC(=O)O)O)O.OCCNCCO

name: Triamcinolone Acetonide
text:
This is triamcinolone acetonide: a corticosteroid with a 1,4-dien-3-one A ring, a 9-fluoro and 11-hydroxy substitution, and a 16,17-acetonide bridge. The 17-position carries a C(=O)CH2OH side chain.

I did not derive the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes myself. I wrote the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the known isomeric SMILES for this compound, so the stereodescriptors are recalled rather than read off the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@]12C[C@@H]([C@]3([C@H]([C@@H]1C[C@H]4[C@]2(OC(O4)(C)C)C(=O)CO)CCC5=CC(=O)C=C[C@@]53C)F)O

name: Trenbolone
text:
I read this as trenbolone (17β-hydroxyestra-4,9,11-trien-3-one), a C18H22O2 steroid.

**Skeleton and functional groups**
- The four rings are the usual steroid layout: three six-membered rings (A, B, C) and one five-membered ring (D) at the left.
- Ring A, on the right, carries the ketone (C=O) and a C4=C5 double bond.
- A C9=C10 double bond sits at the A/B/C ring junction (the double bond between the two ring-fusion carbons drawn lower middle-right).
- A C11=C12 double bond is in ring C, at the bottom.
- The hydroxyl is on the five-membered ring.

**Stereochemistry (from the drawn wedges and hashes)**
- C13: methyl on a wedge.
- C17: OH on a wedge.
- C8: H on a wedge.
- C14: H on a hash.

I worked out the chirality of each of these four centres from the drawn geometry. The tags in the SMILES below, written in its atom order, agree with that analysis at all four.

SMILES: C[C@]12C=CC3=C4CCC(=O)C=C4CC[C@H]3[C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2O

name: Trichlorfon
text:
The drawing shows trichlorfon (dimethyl (2,2,2-trichloro-1-hydroxyethyl)phosphonate).

- Phosphorus carries a P=O double bond, two methoxy groups (OCH3) and one bond to carbon.
- That carbon bears an OH group and is bonded to a CCl3 carbon.
- The CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: COP(=O)(OC)C(O)C(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: Tribendimidine
text:
The molecule is symmetric. A central 1,4-phenylene ring carries a CH=N group at each end. Each CH=N nitrogen is attached to a para-substituted phenyl ring. The far end of each phenyl ring carries N=C(CH3)N(CH3)2, an acetamidine.

Left side: CC(N(C)C)=Nc1ccc(cc1)N=Cc1ccc(cc1)...

Right side: ...C=Nc1ccc(cc1)N=C(C)N(C)C

The drawing shows no stereochemistry, so none is included.

SMILES: CC(N(C)C)=Nc1ccc(cc1)N=Cc1ccc(cc1)C=Nc1ccc(cc1)N=C(C)N(C)C

name: Trehalose
text:
I read this as a disaccharide made of two pyranose rings joined through a single bridging oxygen, with each ring's anomeric carbon (C1) bonded to that oxygen. Each ring has five carbons and a ring oxygen, a CH2OH group on C5, and hydroxyls on C2, C3 and C4.

I assigned each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, working through each carbon's neighbours.

- **Left ring:** the bridging oxygen at C1 and the C2 and C4 hydroxyls are wedged; the C3 hydroxyl and the C5 CH2OH are hashed.
- **Right ring:** the bridging oxygen at C1′ and the C2′ and C4′ hydroxyls are wedged; the C3′ hydroxyl and the C5′ CH2OH are hashed.

I did not compare the result against a known named sugar, so the stereo descriptors rest only on that reading of the wedges.

SMILES: OC[C@H]1O[C@H](O[C@H]2O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H]2O)[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O

name: Trichloroethylene
text:
The image shows two carbons joined by a double bond. One carbon carries two Cl atoms and the other carries one Cl, so the molecule is trichloroethylene.

The double bond has only one substituent on one end, so there is no cis/trans stereochemistry to specify.

SMILES: ClC=C(Cl)Cl

name: Triethyl phosphite
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom (P) bonded to three oxygen atoms. Each oxygen carries an ethyl group (O–CH2–CH3). All bonds are single, no charges are shown, and no wedges or hashes appear, so there is no stereochemistry.

This is triethyl phosphite, P(OCC)3.

SMILES: CCOP(OCC)OCC

name: Triamcinolone
text:
The structure is a 9-fluoro corticosteroid with a 1,4-dien-3-one A ring, an 11-OH, a 16-OH and a 17-OH. The 17-substituent is C(=O)CH2OH, and there are methyls at C10 and C13. This is triamcinolone.

The ring system is drawn flipped left to right compared with the usual steroid orientation (A ring on the right, D ring on the left). Flipping the molecule over inverts the wedge and hash marks. The drawn marks are then consistent with the natural configuration:

- The 11-OH, drawn hashed, is the usual β.
- The 9-F, drawn as a wedge, is the usual α.
- The 14-H, drawn as a wedge, is the usual α.
- The two methyls, drawn hashed, are the usual β.

I wrote the SMILES from the known triamcinolone structure and checked it against the drawing rather than assigning each @/@@ from scratch.

SMILES: C[C@]12C=CC(=O)C=C1CC[C@H]3[C@@]2([C@H](C[C@]4([C@H]3C[C@@H]([C@@]4(C(=O)CO)O)O)C)O)F

name: Triclabendazole
text:
This is triclabendazole: a benzimidazole carrying an SMe group at C2, with a Cl and an aryloxy substituent on the benzo ring.

**Imidazole ring:** The methylthio group (CH3–S) is attached to C2. C2 is double-bonded to N, and the other N is NH. The NH is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon at about (517, 681), and the =N is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon at about (629, 812).

**Benzo ring:** The atoms in order are:
- C(517, 681): fused, bonded to NH
- C(574, 517): CH
- C(745, 486): bears Cl
- C(857, 617): bears O
- C(800, 781): CH
- C(629, 812): fused, bonded to N

**Aryloxy ring:** The O is bonded to C(1141, 717). This carbon's neighbours are C(1084, 881), which bears Cl, and the CH at (1311, 686). Next to C(1084, 881) is C(1196, 1013), which also bears Cl. The remaining ring atoms are CH.

**SMILES:** CSC1=NC2=CC(OC3=CC=CC(Cl)=C3Cl)=C(Cl)C=C2N1

Check on the benzo ring: C2 (the carbon bonded to =N) is followed by =C, which is the CH at (800, 781). Then C(O), then C(Cl), then CH, then the fused carbon bonded to NH. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CSC1=NC2=CC(OC3=CC=CC(Cl)=C3Cl)=C(Cl)C=C2N1

name: Trifluoroacetic acid-d
text:
The drawing shows trifluoroacetic acid with a deuterium on the acid oxygen.

- A carbon carries three F atoms (the CF3 group).
- That carbon is bonded to a carbonyl carbon, which has a C=O double bond.
- The carbonyl carbon is also bonded to an O, which bears a hydrogen labelled with a superscript 2 (²H, deuterium).

SMILES: [2H]OC(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: Trifarotene
text:
The structure is a terphenyl: three benzene rings joined in a row, with a carboxylic acid at one end.

**Right ring:** a benzene ring carrying COOH, attached at its para position to the middle ring.

**Middle ring:** the bond to the right ring leaves from the vertex at (858, 724). The ring vertices run (760, 660), (858, 724), (852, 842), (747, 895), (648, 831), (655, 713).
- (655, 713) bears the link to the left ring.
- (648, 831) bears the OCH2CH2OH group.
- Starting from the right-ring attachment at (858, 724), the next vertices are (852, 842), (747, 895), then (648, 831), which carries the O. So the O-bearing carbon is meta to the right-ring attachment.
- The left-ring attachment at (655, 713) is ortho to the O-bearing carbon.
- The left-ring attachment is also meta to the right-ring attachment, via (760, 660).

**Left ring:** the vertices are (562, 532), (463, 467), (358, 520), (352, 639), (451, 703), (555, 649).
- (555, 649) is the attachment to the middle ring.
- (358, 520) bears the pyrrolidine N.
- (352, 639) bears the tert-butyl group.
- The pyrrolidine carbon is para to the attachment, and the tert-butyl carbon is meta to it.

**SMILES, written from the right ring:**
- OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(OCCO)c(c1)-c1ccc(N2CCCC2)c(c1)C(C)(C)C
- In the middle ring, c1 is the attachment to the right ring, then c, c, c(OCCO), then c(c1) is the carbon bearing the left ring.
- In the left ring, the attachment carbon is c1, followed by c, c, then c(N), then c(tBu), then c1 closing the ring.
- Checking the middle ring: the attachment carbon (858, 724), then (852, 842), (747, 895), (648, 831) with O, then (655, 713) with the left ring, then (760, 660) closing back. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(OCCO)c(c1)-c1ccc(N2CCCC2)c(c1)C(C)(C)C

name: Triflusal
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents:

- A carboxylic acid (COOH) on the ring carbon at upper left.
- An acetoxy group (OC(C)=O) on the adjacent ring carbon below it.
- A CF3 group on the ring carbon at right, which is para to the carboxylic acid carbon.

To check the para relationship, I numbered the ring atoms: C1 (COOH, at 507,529), C2 (OAc, at 555,760), C3 (780,833), C4 (CF3, at 955,675), C5 (906,443) and C6 (681,371). C1 and C4 are opposite each other, so CF3 is para to COOH. The acetoxy carbon C2 is adjacent to C1, so it is ortho to COOH and meta to CF3.

This is 2-acetoxy-4-(trifluoromethyl)benzoic acid (triflusal).

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1C(=O)O

name: Triflupromazine
text:
The drawing is a phenothiazine core with a CF3 group on one benzene ring and a 3-(dimethylamino)propyl chain on the ring nitrogen. This is triflupromazine.

**Core and substituents**
- The tricyclic core is a phenothiazine: two benzene rings bridged by S and N.
- The N bears a three-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2–CH2) ending in N(CH3)2.
- The CF3 group sits on the upper benzene ring, at the carbon that is para to the S-bearing carbon.

**Locating the CF3 position**
- The upper ring runs from the CF3-bearing carbon (472,446) to the top-left carbon (568,281), then the top-right carbon (757,281), then the carbon bonded to S (852,446), then the carbon bonded to N (757,611), then the bottom-left carbon (568,611), and back to the CF3 carbon.
- The CF3 carbon is bonded to the bottom-left carbon (568,611), which is bonded to the N-bearing carbon (757,611). Counting from the S-bearing carbon, the path is S-carbon, top-right, top-left, CF3 carbon, which puts CF3 para to the S-bearing carbon, and meta to the N-bearing carbon.

**SMILES**
Writing the upper ring starting from the N-bearing carbon: c1(N...)cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1S.

Full: CN(C)CCCN1c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc2Sc2ccccc12

Check on ring 1: the N-bearing carbon is c2, then the next atom is c (bottom-left), then c(CF3), then c, c, then c2 bearing S. This places CF3 at the carbon two bonds from the N-bearing carbon and three bonds from the S-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc2Sc2ccccc12

name: Trihexyphenidyl
text:
The drawing shows a piperidine ring whose nitrogen is bonded to a two-carbon chain (N–CH2–CH2). The chain ends at a quaternary carbon that carries an OH, a cyclohexyl ring and a phenyl ring. This is trihexyphenidyl.

Atom-by-atom check:
- **Piperidine:** the ring has N plus 5 carbons. The vertices at (361,515), (185,491), (75,632), (144,798) and (320,822) are the five carbons.
- **Chain:** the carbons at (607,704) and (716,562) link N to the central carbon at (893,585).
- **Central carbon:** it bears the O of the OH group, the cyclohexyl ring and the phenyl ring.
- **Cyclohexyl:** six carbons, all single bonds.
- **Phenyl:** six carbons with alternating double bonds.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(CCN1CCCCC1)(C1CCCCC1)C1=CC=CC=C1

name: Triheptanoin
text:
The drawing shows a glycerol backbone (CH2–CH–CH2) with each of its three oxygens esterified by an acyl chain. I counted the carbons in each chain from the terminal methyl through to the carbonyl carbon.

- **Left chain:** seven carbons, so a heptanoyl group on the terminal CH2–O.
- **Top chain:** seven carbons, so a heptanoyl group on the central CH–O.
- **Right chain:** seven carbons, so a heptanoyl group on the other terminal CH2–O.

The molecule is glycerol triheptanoate (triheptanoin). The central carbon is a stereocentre only by connectivity. It is drawn with plain bonds, and the molecule is symmetric at the two CH2 ends anyway, so I include no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCCCCCC(=O)OCC(COC(=O)CCCCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCC

name: Trimebutine Maleate
text:
The drawing shows two components: maleic acid (the cis diacid) and trimebutine.

**Maleic acid:** The two COOH groups sit on the same side of the C=C, so the double bond is cis. The SMILES is O=C(O)/C=C\C(=O)O.

**Trimebutine:** The ester is 2-(dimethylamino)-2-phenylbutyl 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoate. The quaternary carbon carries an ethyl group, an NMe2 group, a phenyl ring and a CH2–O ester link. The ester carbonyl is attached to a benzene ring bearing three OMe groups. The SMILES is CCC(N(C)C)(COC(=O)c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1)c1ccccc1.

The quaternary carbon has no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so it gets no stereo label.

Combined, with the two components separated by a dot:

SMILES: CCC(N(C)C)(COC(=O)c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1)c1ccccc1.O=C(O)/C=C\C(=O)O

name: Trimedoxime
text:
The drawing shows two pyridinium rings joined through their nitrogens by a three-carbon chain. Each ring carries a CH=N–OH (oxime) group at the 4-position, so this is a bis(4-hydroxyiminomethylpyridinium)propane dication.

Reading it region by region:
- **Linker:** from the left N+, the chain runs through three CH2 carbons to the right N+.
- **Rings:** each is a six-membered pyridinium ring with the N+ at one vertex and the oxime-bearing carbon at the para position.
- **Oxime groups:** each is drawn as C=N–OH.

text:
The drawing shows a phenothiazine core: two benzene rings joined through an S atom and an N atom. The N atom carries a side chain.

The side chain runs from the ring N to a CH2, then to a CH that bears a methyl group, then to another CH2, and ends at N(CH3)2. This is trimeprazine (alimemazine). The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.
